prs.title: fix(cli): preserve quota-interrupted sessions and stop on Escape
prs.body:
## Summary

Keep the latest user prompt and completed tool rounds when a request stops for quota or cancellation, so normal quit/signout cleanup does not erase resumable conversation history. One Escape stops the quota retry dialog.

## Details

Preserve history for terminal/retryable quota errors and cancellation, and recompute its prompt-token estimate instead of rolling back those turns. Other request failures retain the existing rollback behavior. Escape in the quota dialog chooses Stop and consumes the key once.

Regressions write real JSONL, run normal session cleanup, reload the record, and rebuild the client history. They also cover a completed tool call/result and signout's account-specific thought-signature cleanup. No authentication, public settings-schema, model-catalog, or package-version additions.

## Related Issues

User-reported regression; no linked issue.

## How to Validate

Validated final head `3ed37a028bf6267cd8a9b97dfe967160a8d1721f`, based on upstream `ed96faedfd5571f055c44f2c9509d62321d1138d`.

- Core: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --root packages/core src/core/geminiChat.test.ts src/core/geminiChat.quota.test.ts src/core/geminiChat_network_retry.test.ts src/services/chatRecordingService.test.ts src/utils/sessionUtils.test.ts src/utils/delay.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false --maxWorkers=1 --minWorkers=1` passes 230/230 on Linux Node 24.21.0 and native Windows Node 24.14.1.
- CLI: the same Vitest invocation with `--root packages/cli` and `src/ui/components/ProQuotaDialog.test.tsx src/ui/hooks/useQuotaAndFallback.test.ts src/ui/commands/authCommand.test.ts src/ui/commands/quitCommand.test.ts` passes 60/60 on both platforms.
- A separate probe imports compiled production `GeminiChat`, uses real `Config`/storage/recording with a fake content generator, and passes three real-file scenarios against source builds and installed core tarballs on Linux and native Windows: terminal quota then normal quit cleanup/resume; retryable quota then cleanup/resume; completed tool round then abort/signout signature cleanup/resume.
- Actual Linux source and isolated packed-npx terminal launches use a localhost backend returning a 429 with a simulated 3,600-second reset. One Escape stops the request, normal `/quit` exits 0, and the prompt remains in JSONL. Native Windows actual offline npm-exec from an isolated installed prefix passes the same product assertions, including CLI exit 0 and the saved prompt. Package smoke version/help checks are recorded separately from these feature assertions.
- Native Windows uses an isolated NTFS checkout and native dependencies. Resolution from the actual compiled CLI entry points to its own core build; its `GeminiChat` hash matches the intended history change. Packed CLI/core tarballs and resolved paths are checked separately. Native packages use extracted local tarballs and matching native dependency junctions after a bounded registry-install timeout; this does not claim a successful fresh registry installation.
- Linux build, affected core/CLI typechecks, changed-file ESLint/Prettier, and whitespace checks pass. Native core/test-utils/devtools/CLI build stages and affected focused tests pass; native `npm run start -- --version` and `--help` also exit 0 in the isolated checkout. The built artifact image `gemini-history-pr29799:3ed37a0` passes all three JSONL cases and the actual npx Escape/quit flow under Linux Node 20.20.2 with external networking disabled. Repeating through native Windows -> WSL Docker also passes; these are Linux containers.
- Full `npm run preflight` completed on this head in a disposable Linux checkout under Node 20.19.0 with two Vitest workers. Install/format/build/full lint/all typechecks pass; tracked source remains clean. CLI reports 10 failed, 7,401 passed, 4 skipped; core reports 76 failed, 8,300 passed, 57 skipped. prs.title: fix(core): drop tool calls streamed by failed attempts on retry
prs.body:
## Summary

On a mid-stream retry, `GeminiChat` has already yielded the failed attempt's chunks, while only the successful attempt's model turn is written to history. Every front end collected `ToolCallRequest` events from both attempts, executed both calls and answered both. A side-effecting command therefore ran twice, and the extra `functionResponse` no longer matched the model turn, so the next request failed with `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT` and every later request in the session was rejected too.

This implements the existing `RETRY` contract ("The UI should discard any partial content from the attempt that just failed") for tool calls in every consumer.

## Details

- `core/Turn`: reset `pendingToolCalls` when a retry is signalled, so calls that never entered history are not reported as pending.
- ACP (`acpSession`), interactive UI (`useGeminiStream`, including `pendingToolCallRequestsRef`), headless (`nonInteractiveCli`), a2a-server (`executor`) and the subagent `LocalAgentExecutor`: drop the collected tool call requests on `Retry`.
- No behavior change when a turn is not retried; clearing only happens when the backend signals a retry.
- Out of scope (unchanged): partial text from a failed attempt is still displayed, and headless stream-json may still emit a `tool_use` event for a call that is dropped.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30014

## How to Validate

Each new test streams a tool call, then `Retry`, then a second call, and asserts that exactly one call is executed and answered. All of them fail without the source change.

```bash
cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/core/turn.test.ts src/agents/local-executor.test.ts
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp/acpSession.test.ts src/nonInteractiveCli.test.ts src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.test.tsx
cd packages/a2a-server && npx vitest run src/agent/executor.test.ts
```

Additional checks:

- `tsc --noEmit` (core/cli/a2a), `eslint --max-warnings 0` and `prettier --check` pass.
- Full `@google/gemini-cli-core` suite: 8555 passed. The single failure is the pre-existing macOS-only `/dev/ttys001` test from #30008.
- Full a2a-server suite: 183 passed.
- Affected suites also pass in a Linux Docker container (`node:22-bookworm`, linux/arm64) after a clean `npm ci` + `npm run build`.

## 中文说明

修复 #30014。流式中途重试时，失败 attempt 的 tool call 已经发给前端但不会进入 history，导致同一命令被执行两次，且多余的 functionResponse 与 history 不匹配，后续请求持续 400。现在各前端在收到 `Retry` 时丢弃失败 attempt 收集到的调用，并清空 `Turn.pendingToolCalls`；无重试时行为不变。

prs.title: fix(core): fall back across model tiers only when Auto quota is exhausted
prs.body:
### Summary

Auto quota routing currently dead-ends a session after a hard quota exhaustion, and capacity-shaped failures are recorded as permanent unavailability. This PR rebuilds the terminal-quota handling so that **Auto mode** immediately routes across model tiers (Pro ↔ Flash) on true quota exhaustion, while **manual selections** always stay on the user's chosen model.

The behavior this restores was last healthy around 0.53. The regression chain, in upstream history:

- #28599 (Jul 30) — capacity messages introduced a delay-less `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` path that classified terminal.
- #28716 (Aug 6) — capacity reason codes classify as `terminal` even with `RetryInfo`; the prompt-on-attempt-1 behavior and the a2a `retry_always → stop` wiring landed here.
- #28730 (Aug 11) — added the false "usage limit" wording plus quota-bucket `modelId` normalization.
- #28790 (Aug 13) — added three silent capacity retries and the 30s TTL, but only for reason `'capacity'`.
- #28761 — maintainer/user-confirmed fallout thread: *"MODEL_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED is definitely not terminal"*, *"0.53.1 seems to be the last version with retries"*; closes "in #28790" but the terminal-marking mismatch survived.

The concrete interlock today:

1. `DEFAULT_STATE` maps every failure kind → `'terminal'` (`policyCatalog.ts`), and `applyAvailabilityTransition` derives the terminal reason from the failure kind instead of the error: `failureKind === 'terminal' ? 'quota' : 'capacity'` (`policyHelpers.ts`). Capacity-shaped `TerminalQuotaError`s therefore get a **permanent `'quota'`** mark, while the `'capacity'` TTL from #28790 only applies to errors already classified as capacity — the TTL and the error's permanence are inverted.
2. Marking only happens after a fallback intent is accepted (`handleFallback`), never during silent retries.
3. After one exhausted-quota outcome, both chain models can be marked in a single turn (`failedModel` + the alternate it is about to silently try). `selectFirstAvailable` then has no candidates, `lastResort === failedModel`, and `handleFallback` returns `null` — the request fails with no retry, no dialog, and no reset-until-session-restart path that a user can influence.

### What this changes

- **Classification split (`googleQuotaErrors.ts`)** — new `isQuotaExhaustedError()` returns `true` only for errors driven by an exhausted usage entitlement. It excludes `MODEL_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED`/`MODEL_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED` (reason or message), `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (`ErrorInfo` reason), per-minute `QuotaFailure` violations, insufficient-credit errors, and 5xx statuses. Transient conditions keep their existing retry rules.
- **Reason-aware terminal marking (`policyHelpers.ts`, `handler.ts`)** — `applyAvailabilityTransition` takes an optional terminal reason computed from the error. Capacity failures land in the #28790 TTL bucket; true exhaustion is a permanent `'quota'` mark, recorded through `markQuotaExhausted()` for every alias/backend ID that maps to the exhausted model so the same backend is never retried under another name.
- **Quota-aware selection (`policyHelpers.ts`)** — `resolveQuotaFallbackModel()` picks the other tier for Auto selections. It skips models whose quota is advertised as zero (`remainingFraction`/`remainingAmount`, including the legacy Code Assist Flash bucket), honors no-Pro-access and preview/Gemini 3.1 access flags when resolving the tier candidates, keeps distinct API-key backend IDs separate from Code Assist aliases, skips candidates whose runtime override resolves back to an exhausted model, and consults availability health. Zero-quota knowledge is applied *before* a request is sent (`selectModelForAvailability`), so a known-exhausted model is not even attempted.
- **Immediate cross-tier switch (`retry.ts`, `baseLlmClient.ts`)** — new `onQuotaExhausted` retry hook. When a hard-quota error arrives and the current model is an Auto selection, `handleFallback` marks exhaustion, rotates the session ID, sets the active model to the selected alternate, and the retry loop continues with the attempt counter reset. This is silent (no dialog) in both interactive and unattended Auto use, and stops with an enriched error when no eligible model remains, instead of waiting for a reset.
- **Manual selections stay manual** — a manual selection whose own quota is exhausted keeps the selected model (availability never substitutes another model for it), and the existing same-model retry / stop / upgrade affordances are unchanged. Temporary model activation during fallback preserves exhaustion marks; an explicit model selection still clears availability state except for exhaustion marks.
- Preserved by design: the three-objective behavior from #28716 (fail-fast prompts, silent capacity retries from #28790, launch-flag chain behavior) and `isOriginallyGemini3` manual wrap-around semantics are unchanged.

### Behavior

| Scenario | Auto | Manual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hard quota exhausted (e.g. daily limit) | Immediately switches to the other tier, no prompt; marks the exhausted model and all its aliases/IDs | Stays on the selected model; same-model retry / stop / upgrade dialog unchanged |
| Both tiers exhausted | Stops with an enriched quota error instead of waiting for a reset | Stays on the selected model |
| Known zero quota on the requested model | Skips to the alternate before sending a request | Stays on the selected model |
| Capacity exhaustion (`MODEL_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED`) | 3 silent in-turn retries (interactive) / bounded retries (unattended); TTL-bucketed availability per #28790 | Unchanged behavior |
| Per-minute rate limits, credits, 5xx | Unchanged (existing retry/backoff) | Unchanged |

### a2a-server

The a2a-server intentionally returns `stop` from its in-request fallback handler (per #28716); future requests still fall back through `activateFallbackMode`. This PR's scope is core Auto quota routing, so that behavior is unchanged — noting it here because the terminal-marking change touches the shared `handleFallback` path.

### Tests

All tests live in the existing upstream test files (no new test files), extending:
- `googleQuotaErrors.test.ts` — exhaustion vs capacity / rate-limit / credits / per-minute violations / 5xx classification.
- `policyHelpers.test.ts` — cross-tier selection, zero-quota skip (including legacy Code Assist buckets), alias/backend mapping, no-Pro-access + runtime override resolution, access-flag refinement, manual fixedness under exhaustion.
- `modelAvailabilityService.test.ts` — `reset({ preserveQuota })` keeps exhaustion marks only.
- `config.test.ts` — `activateFallbackMode` in Auto keeps the user's Auto selection while routing the active model; manual activations preserve exhaustion marks.
- `retry.test.ts` — `onQuotaExhausted` hook fires only for true exhaustion, resets attempts, falls back to the enriched error otherwise.
- `handler.test.ts` + `baseLlmClient.test.ts` — Auto silently switches with no handler invocation; manual keeps the dialog; the hook is only wired for eligible Auto selections; already-exhausted alternates route to `null` rather than switching.
- `geminiChat.test.ts` / `geminiChat_network_retry.test.ts` — resolved-config refresh during the persistent-429 path and real-retry coverage, including a renamed manual Gemini-3 case (upstream previously re-routed manual Gemini-3 models on quota; this PR intentionally fixes those fixtures to the new no-switch behavior).

### Pre-submission checklist

- [x] Core `typecheck` (tsc) clean; CLI and a2a-server `typecheck` clean.
- [x] Core `npm run build` and CLI build succeed.
- [x] Full core vitest suite green (420 files) plus all touched focused suites, run serially (`--maxWorkers=1`).
- [x] `eslint` on every changed file; `prettier --check` on every changed file; `git diff --check` clean.
- [x] Behavior documented in `docs/cli/model.md`.
- [x] Linux: Docker offline-intercept fixture (`node:20-slim`, mock Code Assist backend via `CODE_ASSIST_ENDPOINT`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_ACCESS_TOKEN` auth) — real HTTP flow: router classifies → `gemini-2.5-pro` turn returns `429` + `ErrorInfo(QUOTA_EXHAUSTED)` + `RetryInfo(3600s)` → classified `TerminalQuotaError` → silent Auto switch ("Usage limit reached on gemini-2.5-pro. Switching to gemini-3.5-flash." in debug output) → second `:streamGenerateContent` request on flash returns SSE and the user turn completes with the flash answer, exit 0, no dialog, no forced wait.
- [ ] Linux: Podman + the same fixture. *Blocked on host sudo — pending install.*
- [x] Linux: `npx` smoke via `npm pack` of the fixed workspace (CLI + core tarballs installed into a scratch project, `npx --no-install gemini --version` → `0.66.0-nightly.g204db94ae`).
- [x] Windows (native `node.exe` v24.14.1 on an NTFS checkout of this head): `npm ci` clean; core + CLI `typecheck` clean (exit 0); CLI package `npm run build` clean (exit 0, `dist/index.js` produced); root `npm run bundle` clean; version probes: `node bundle\gemini.js --version` and `node packages\cli\dist\index.js --version` → `0.66.0-nightly.g204db94ae`. Focused vitest across the same 12-suite set as Linux (quota classification, retry, handler, policy helpers, config, availability service, baseLlmClient, both integration files, network-retry, useQuotaAndFallback, ProQuotaDialog): 300 tests ran, 267 pass; the only failures are 33 `config.test.ts` cases in Windows-specific areas (path normalization, ripgrep discovery, GitService/initialize) that reproduce **byte-identically on unmodified upstream `main`** (baseline checkout of `main` on the same NTFS volume: same 33 failures, verified with a name-by-name diff; this PR adds 50 tests to that file and all 50 pass on Windows). Known upstream-environment quirk, also baseline-reproduced: core's `npm run build` under the npm lifecycle aborts with a native `0xC0000409` (STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN, npm exit 3221226505) after the browser-mcp bundling step — identical crash point and code on unmodified `main`; every individual step (`tsc --build`, browser-mcp bundle, `copy_files.js`, docs `cpSync`) passes standalone on both checkouts, `tsc` output completes before the crash on both, and the CLI workspace build is unaffected. Note: `npx --no-install gemini --version` is not usable as a workspace probe on this host because it resolves to a pre-existing global install (0.63.0), so that specific sub-check is intentionally left unchecked; the built artifacts were invoked directly instead.
- [ ] macOS (Seatbelt sandbox). *Not available in this environment — leaving unchecked.*

### Review notes

- The protected-1-4 conflict surface is `handler.ts` + `policyHelpers.ts` — both files' changes are additive; existing shapes (chain resolution, policy catalog, `SILENT_ACTIONS`) are untouched.
- `applyModelSelection` now throws a `TerminalQuotaError` when the selection finds no eligible model (Auto behavior: stop instead of waiting for a reset). It only throws for Auto selections; manual selections return the backup model exactly as before.
- One upstream test was intentionally renamed: `should fallback for Gemini 3 models even if config is NOT in AUTO mode` → `keeps a manually selected Gemini 3 model fixed after exhausting quota` — this records the behavioral change the PR makes (manual Gemini-3 selections previously re-routed to Flash on quota).
- `modelAvailabilityService.reset()` gained an optional `{ preserveQuota }` argument (default behavior unchanged: clear everything).
- The retry hook (unlike `onPersistent429`) is not gated behind `isInteractive`: interactive gating stays only where a user prompt can be shown; exhaustion routing works in unattended contexts.

### What changed?

This PR fixes image pasting (`Alt+V`) in WSL2 and non-standard Linux environments where `XDG_SESSION_TYPE` is unset and the clipboard exposes `image/bmp`:

1. **Display Server Detection Fallback**:
   - `getUserLinuxClipboardTool()` now checks `process.env["WAYLAND_DISPLAY"]` (maps to `wl-paste`) and `process.env["DISPLAY"]` (maps to `xclip`) when `XDG_SESSION_TYPE` is not set.
   - If the preferred tool is not installed, it falls back to check if the alternative tool is available under an active display.

2. **Dynamic Image MIME Type Detection & Non-PNG Support**:
   - Instead of strictly requesting `--type image/png`, `getWlPasteImageFormat()` and `getXclipImageFormat()` inspect available clipboard targets.
   - Supported clipboard formats now include `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/webp`, and `image/bmp` (common on Windows clipboard bridge in WSL2).
   - Images are saved with their matching extension (`.png`, `.jpg`, `.webp`, `.bmp`).
   - Added `.bmp` to `IMAGE_EXTENSIONS` so temporary clipboard cleanup handles BMP files.

3. **Unit Tests**:
   - Added unit tests in `clipboardUtils.test.ts` for:
     - `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` fallback when `XDG_SESSION_TYPE` is unset.
     - `DISPLAY` fallback when `XDG_SESSION_TYPE` is unset.

prs.title: feat(cli): report working, blocked and idle status to the terminal (OSC 7501)
prs.body:
## Summary

The interactive TUI now reports its status to the terminal with OSC 7501 Program Status reports: working, blocked (permission, question, or auth), done or error, and idle. With several sessions open in different tabs, a supporting terminal can show which one needs you without anyone parsing screen text.

## Details

- State comes from the existing streaming state: responding is working; tool confirmation, ask-user and auth dialogs are blocked; a finished turn is done or error; otherwise idle. Reports are sent only when the status changes, and idle is sent on exit.
- Uses the same tmux/screen passthrough as the existing terminal notifications.
- Interactive TTY only. Nothing is written in `-p`, JSON / stream-JSON output, ACP, or when stdout isn't a TTY.
- `ui.programStatus` (default on) turns it off. Terminals that don't support the sequence ignore it.

## Related Issues

Closes #29710

## How to Validate

1. In a terminal that supports OSC 7501, run `gemini`, send a prompt, and watch the tab go working → done → idle. Ask for a shell command and the tab shows blocked while the confirmation is up.
2. `gemini -p "hi" --output-format json | xxd | grep 1b5d` finds no OSC sequence.
3. `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- programStatus`.

prs.title: fix(core): strip trailing punctuation and unbalanced brackets from web_fetch URLs
prs.body:
## Summary

- `parsePrompt()` in `packages/core/src/tools/web-fetch.ts` split the prompt on whitespace and passed each token straight to `new URL()`, which accepts a trailing comma. A comma-separated list of URLs therefore produced polluted URLs (e.g. `https://example.com/,`) that failed downstream in confirmation, the `<authorized_urls>` block and the fallback fetch.
- Added `cleanUrlToken()`, which strips trailing sentence punctuation (`. `, `,`, `;`, `:`) and unbalanced closing brackets from each token before validation. `?` and `!` are kept intact since they can be meaningful query/path characters, and balanced brackets (e.g. `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foo_(bar)`) are preserved.
- Updated the existing test that asserted the old behavior (trailing `.` kept in the URL) and added cases for each punctuation character, unbalanced brackets, `?`/`!` URLs, and the exact comma-separated list from the issue.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run src/tools/web-fetch.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 70 tests pass.
- `eslint` and `tsc --noEmit` clean on the changed files.

Fixes #29896

prs.title: feat(cli): append to the system prompt with --append-system-prompt
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds a way to add instructions to the system prompt without replacing it: `--append-system-prompt "<text>"`, `--append-system-prompt-file <path>`, and `GEMINI_APPEND_SYSTEM_MD=<path>`.

## Details

- `GEMINI_SYSTEM_MD` replaces the whole prompt, so adding one line of project context today means dumping the stock prompt with `GEMINI_WRITE_SYSTEM_MD`, concatenating, and re-pointing at the copy, which silently goes stale on every upgrade.
- The appended text goes after the base prompt (stock, or the `GEMINI_SYSTEM_MD` override when set) and before memory, in its own section. File content comes first, then the inline string.
- Paths resolve the same way as `GEMINI_SYSTEM_MD` (`~` and relative paths). An unreadable file is a clear startup error.
- Docs: `docs/cli/system-prompt.md` gains an "Appending instead of replacing" section; the flags are in the CLI reference.

## Related Issues

Closes #29112

## How to Validate

1. `gemini --append-system-prompt "Always answer in haiku." -p "what is 2+2"` returns a haiku; the stock tools and behavior are still there.
2. `echo "Prefer pnpm." > /tmp/extra.md && GEMINI_APPEND_SYSTEM_MD=/tmp/extra.md gemini -p "how do I install deps?"` mentions pnpm.
3. `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- promptProvider` and `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- config`.

prs.title: fix(cli): retain executing subagent tool calls in useToolScheduler state
prs.body:
## Summary
Fixes an issue where subagent tool calls that transition directly to `Executing` without prior approval (such as file reads, searches, and MCP tool calls) are dropped from the UI state in `useToolScheduler`, preventing the task-tree visualization from building the nested `parentCallId` hierarchy for subagent work.

Fixes #22589

## Details
In `useToolScheduler.ts`, tool calls from non-root schedulers (subagents) were previously filtered out unless they were `AwaitingApproval` or already in `prevCallIds`. Calls that do not require approval transition directly to `Executing` and were never in `prevCallIds` on first update, causing them to be permanently excluded from `toolCallsMap`.

- Added `tc.status === CoreToolCallStatus.Executing` to the allowed statuses for non-root schedulers.
- This allows executing subagent calls to enter hook state immediately and remain tracked when transitioning to completed states (`Success`, `Error`).
- Calls in `Scheduled` or `Validating` without approval remain hidden to prevent transient UI flicker.

## Related Issues
Fixes #22589

## How to Validate
Run the unit test suite in `packages/cli`:
``bash
npm run test -- packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useToolScheduler.test.ts
``
Expected: All 14 tests pass, including tests covering executing subagent visibility and scheduled/validating suppression.

- [x] Added/updated tests
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods:

prs.title: fix(cli): kill active shells and persist tool calls on headless interruption
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes an issue where stopping a headless run (`gemini -p ... --yolo`) with a signal (SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP) or Ctrl+C while `run_shell_command` is running causes:
1. The process to exit with code 0 instead of a standard signal exit code.
2. The shell command to survive in its detached process group and run to completion in the background.
3. The session file (`session-*.jsonl`) to omit the tool call, leaving `--resume latest` with no record that the command was started or interrupted.

## Details

- **Immediate Tool Call Persistence:** `geminiChat.ts` now records incoming tool calls with status `Scheduled` as soon as the model stream yields them, rather than waiting for `scheduler.schedule()` to complete.
- **Interrupted Response Synthesis on Resume:** `convertSessionToClientHistory()` synthesizes an interrupted `functionResponse` for any uncompleted tool call. This prevents Gemini API 400 errors (unpaired function calls) and informs the model that execution was interrupted so it can inspect state before re-running.
- **Process Group Termination:** Added `ShellExecutionService.cleanupAllActiveProcesses()` to `runExitCleanup()` to terminate active child processes and PTY process groups across platforms (via `taskkill` on Windows and group signals on POSIX).
- **Signal Exit Codes:** Wired SIGHUP handling into non-interactive CLI runners and ensured graceful shutdowns return standard POSIX exit codes (130 for SIGINT, 143 for SIGTERM, 129 for SIGHUP) instead of 0.
- **Shared Helpers:** Extracted `createCancelledToolCall` and `CANCELLED_TOOL_ERROR_MESSAGE` into `@google/gemini-cli-core` (`tool-utils.ts`) so both interactive and headless runners record cancellation consistently.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30007

## How to Validate

1. **Unit tests:**
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/nonInteractiveCli.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/utils/cleanup.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/sessionUtils.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/core/geminiChat.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/services/shellExecutionService.test.ts

prs.title: feat(acp): let clients steer a running turn
prs.body:
## Summary

Lets ACP clients (Zed, JetBrains, VS Code extensions, and others that run `gemini --acp`) add a user message to a running `session/prompt` turn without cancelling it, the same way `experimental.modelSteering` works in the terminal.
Today an ACP client can only send `session/cancel` or a new prompt, and both throw away the work in progress. This is an opt-in protocol extension: a client that doesn't use it only sees one extra `_meta` key in the `initialize` response.

## Details

**Protocol** (constants in `acpUtils.ts`)

- `initialize` advertises the extension under `agentCapabilities._meta["geminicli.com"].steering` with `version`, `content: ["text"]`, `maxPending: 20`, `maxChars: 8000`, and `enabled`.
- Steering is enabled when the client sends `clientCapabilities._meta["geminicli.com"].steering: true`, or when the user has `experimental.modelSteering` on.
- New request `_geminicli.com/session/steer` with `{ sessionId, content }`. It returns `{ status: "queued", steerId, pending }`, or `{ status: "no_active_turn" }` when no model loop is running.
- When a message reaches the model, the client gets a `user_message_chunk` with the user's text and `_meta["geminicli.com"].steering = { steerId, state: "delivered" }`.
- Messages still queued when the turn ends (cancel, replacement prompt, or turn limit) come back in the `session/prompt` response as `_meta["geminicli.com"].undeliveredSteering`. If the turn throws, each one is sent as a `user_message_chunk` with `state: "undelivered"` before the error.

**Behavior in `Session.prompt()`**

- Queued messages are added at the start of each loop iteration, after the turn-limit and cancel checks, in front of the tool results.
- They're joined and wrapped with `buildUserSteeringHintPrompt`, the same as the terminal UI does for hints sent after tool calls (`useGeminiStream.ts`). Each message still gets its own `delivered` update on the client.
- If the model finishes without tool calls while a message is queued, the loop sends one more request in the same turn, like the terminal UI auto-submits leftover hints.
- Running tools and open permission requests are not interrupted. Slash commands get `no_active_turn`. A second `session/prompt` still cancels the first, and the replaced turn reports its queue as undelivered.
- Messages are also passed to `InjectionService` with source `user_steering`, so running local subagents see them, as in the terminal. This is a no-op unless `experimental.modelSteering` is on.
- Loading a session replays stored steering as the user's own text, not the wrapped prompt.

**Dispatcher**

- `GeminiAgent.extMethod` routes the steer method and returns `-32601` for unknown methods. `GeminiAgent.extNotification` ignores unknown notifications, as the ACP spec advises.

No core changes. Terminal behavior and the `experimental.modelSteering` default are unchanged. No breaking changes.

**Open questions for maintainers** (see #29900): the `_geminicli.com/` method prefix, gating on client opt-in or the setting, reporting undelivered messages in the response versus a notification, and whether a `session/unsteer` method is needed.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29900

## How to Validate

1. Unit tests:

   ```bash
   npm run build
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/acp/
   ```

For the full suite, run `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true npm run preflight`, as CI does. Without that variable, 9 tests in `gemini.test.tsx` fail on `main` too.

New cases in `acpSession.test.ts` cover delivery, ordering, continuation when the model ends, `no_active_turn`, cancel, open permission requests, turn limits, replacement prompts, errors, validation, injection, and history replay. `acpRpcDispatcher.test.ts` covers capability advertisement and routing.

2. Protocol smoke test against the built CLI (no model call needed): send `initialize` and check `agentCapabilities._meta["geminicli.com"].steering`; steer an unknown session and expect `-32602`; call an unknown `_` method and expect `-32601`.
3. End to end with an ACP client: start a prompt that runs a tool, send `_geminicli.com/session/steer` while it runs, then check that the next model request contains the hint, the client gets a `delivered` chunk, and the turn finishes without being cancelled.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any)

prs.title: fix(core): keep oversized and boundary lines in read_background_output
prs.body:
## Summary

`read_background_output` reads the last 64KB of a log and always dropped the first line of that window when it didn't start at byte 0. A log that is one line longer than 64KB came back as `Full Log Output:` with nothing after it, a complete first line was lost when the window started right after a newline, and truncated output was still labelled "Full Log Output".

## Details

- read one extra byte before the window to tell whether it starts mid line
- drop the partial first line only when other lines follow; when it's the only line, keep it as a fragment
- skip the continuation bytes of a UTF-8 character cut by the cap, so the fragment doesn't start with U+FFFD
- the header says when earlier output was truncated
- the read stays bounded at 64KB plus one byte, and the session ownership check is unchanged

## Related Issues

Fixes #29944

## How to Validate

```
cd packages/core
npx vitest run src/tools/shellBackgroundTools.test.ts
```

New tests cover a 70,000 character single line, a window that starts right after a newline, a partial first line followed by a full one, and an "é" split by the cap. Against main's source all 4 fail; with this change the file passes 14/14 (macOS, Node 25). I didn't run the CLI end to end.

issues.title: Context window rollover still fails after #5205 closed as completed: checkpoint.md absent recurs on 1.0.105
issues.body:
Filing this as a new issue because #5205 — which carries the original report, an independent reproduction, and my 1.0.105 reproduction — was closed as completed on 2026-10-30 with no closing comment, no linked PR or commit, and no release containing a fix. The latest release is still 1.0.105 (2026-10-28), and no changelog entry in any version mentions checkpoint.md or the rollover refusal. Only the author or maintainers can reopen #5205, so the post-closure evidence also lives here. (Reopen request with the same evidence: https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/5205#issuecomment-6543292385; my original reproduction: https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/5205#issuecomment-6485623208)

**Environment:** Copilot CLI 1.0.105 (current latest release), Windows 11.

**Failure:** "Failed to start a fresh context window: checkpoint.md is absent for this agent; write it before requesting rollover"

**Recurrences since the #5205 closure, both on 1.0.105:**

1. **2026-10-30 ~18:44 UTC** — resuming a parked long-running session: the rollover was refused with the exact error above. The session had zero compaction events and its checkpoints/ folder held only the stub index.md, so no checkpoint existed to satisfy the gate.
2. **2026-10-31T03:05:38Z** — a delegated agent launch died at startup with the same refusal delivered as a session.error event ("Execution failed: Failed to start a fresh context window: checkpoint.md is absent for this agent; write it before requesting rollover"), aborting the parent run's shutdown records mid-sequence.

**Pattern (unchanged across all reports):** in a session where no compaction has run, no checkpoint is ever registered — automatic compaction does not create one — and any fresh-context rollover in that session is then refused. The agent cannot create the checkpoint itself, and no documented mechanism lets it; the only workaround is a manual /compact by the user before the rollover point.

**Expected:** either rollover does not require a checkpoint the system never created, or the checkpoint is created by the automatic path the documentation describes. If a fix has shipped somewhere not visible in the releases or on #5205, a pointer to the PR or release would settle both issues.

issues.title: Allow users to cancel or remove enqueued messages before they are executed

labels.name: area:input-keyboard
labels.description: Keyboard shortcuts, keybindings, copy/paste, clipboard, mouse, and text input

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

There is no way to cancel or remove a message or slash command that has been queued (via `Ctrl+Q` / `Ctrl+Enter`) while the agent is busy or during `/compact`. Once enqueued, messages are automatically processed in order when the agent finishes — even if the user has changed their mind or made a mistake.

### Proposed solution

Add a mechanism to view and selectively cancel queued messages before they are executed. This could take the form of:
- A `/queue` command to list pending messages, with `/queue cancel <n>` to remove a specific entry.
- An interactive UI overlay (e.g., triggered by a keybinding) showing the queue with the ability to navigate and delete items.
- A keybinding (e.g., `Ctrl+Shift+Q`) to clear the entire queue at once.

This would benefit Copilot CLI users by:
- Preventing accidental or unwanted actions from queued messages the user no longer intends to send.
- Complementing existing cancellation behavior (`Ctrl+C` for active operations, `Escape` for specific commands like `/compact`) with control over *pending* operations.
- Improving confidence in the queueing workflow, encouraging users to queue more freely knowing they can course-correct.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. **Accidental queue during compaction** — User sends a message during `/compact` (auto-queued per v0.0.389), then realizes it was wrong. They want to remove it before compaction finishes and the message is sent to the model.
2. **Multiple queued commands** — User queues several slash commands with `Ctrl+Q` while the agent is working, then decides the third one is no longer needed. They run `/queue` to see the list and `/queue cancel 3` to drop it.
3. **Clear entire queue** — User has queued several messages but the agent's response changes their plan entirely. They press `Ctrl+Shift+Q` (or run `/queue clear`) to discard all pending messages and start fresh.
4. **Review before execution** — User wants to double-check what's queued before the agent finishes. They press a keybinding to see a transient overlay of queued items, then dismiss it or remove specific entries.

### Additional context

- Current queueing was introduced in v0.0.394 (`Ctrl+D`) and the keybinding was later changed to `Ctrl+Q` / `Ctrl+Enter` in v0.0.407.
- Auto-queueing during `/compact` was added in v0.0.389.
- Existing cancel mechanisms (`Ctrl+C`, `Escape`) only affect the *currently running* operation, not messages waiting in the queue.

issues.title: ACP: expose the model list as a category:model config option (session/new returns only mode and allow_all)
issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Over `copilot --acp`, a client has no way to list the models available to the signed-in account or to pick one for a session.

Measured on GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.85 (macOS arm64):

- `session/new` returns `sessionId`, `modes` and `configOptions` only. `configOptions` holds exactly two `select` options, `mode` and `allow_all`. There is no option with `category: "model"`.
- `session/load` returns the same set.
- Sending `/model` as a prompt answers: *"The model-picker dialog is only available in the interactive CLI."*
- `--model <id>` accepts any string. `copilot --acp --model=not_a_real_model_xyz` starts, creates a session and completes a prompt with no error, no stderr, and nothing on the wire reports which model actually ran.

So an ACP client (an editor or a desktop app embedding Copilot) can only offer a single "Copilot default" row. It cannot show the models the user's plan allows, and if it hard-codes ids it cannot tell when one silently fell back.

### Proposed solution

Advertise the model list the way the ACP spec already provides for it:

1. Include a `SessionConfigOption` with `type: "select"` and `category: "model"` in `session/new` and `session/load` responses, listing the ids the account can use and `currentValue` set to the active model. Grouping by vendor via `SessionConfigSelectGroup` is fine.
2. Accept `session/set_config_option` for that option and emit `config_option_update` on change, so a client can switch models mid-session without respawning.
3. Ideally, reject an unknown `--model` value (or at least log it to stderr) instead of silently running the default.

This is the same shape the interactive `/model` picker already has; it just needs to be exposed on the ACP surface.

### Example prompts or workflows

An ACP client starts `copilot --acp`, calls `session/new`, reads the `model` config option, shows its values in a picker, and calls `session/set_config_option` with the user's choice. Today step 3 yields nothing to show.

### Additional context

Minimal reproduction (Node 24):

```js
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
const c = spawn('copilot', ['--acp', '--no-auto-update'], { stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'inherit'] })
const send = (o) => c.stdin.write(JSON.stringify(o) + '\n')
let buf = ''
c.stdout.on('data', (d) => {
  buf += d
  for (const line of buf.split('\n').slice(0, -1)) {
    const m = JSON.parse(line)
    if (m.id === 1) send({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 2, method: 'session/new', params: { cwd: process.cwd(), mcpServers: [] } })
    if (m.id === 2) { console.log(Object.keys(m.result), m.result.configOptions.map((o) => o.id)); c.kill() }
  }
  buf = buf.slice(buf.lastIndexOf('\n') + 1)
})
send({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 1, method: 'initialize', params: { protocolVersion: 1, clientCapabilities: { fs: { readTextFile: false, writeTextFile: false } }, clientInfo: { name: 'probe', version: '0' } } })
```

Prints `[ 'sessionId', 'modes', 'configOptions' ] [ 'mode', 'allow_all' ]`.

Version: `GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.85`. ACP SDK used by the client: `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` 1.4.0.

issues.title: Regression (1.0.88 → 1.0.89): MCP OAuth authorization page opens on every ACP session instead of the challenge being resolved silently

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
## Describe the bug

An OAuth-protected HTTP MCP server that has a **valid, unexpired** access token in
`~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config` is answered with HTTP 401 on every new `--acp`
session, and the CLI responds by opening the OAuth authorization page again.
Because the browser SSO session is already established, the flow self-approves
and the tab closes — so the user sees an unrequested sign-in page flash open on
*every single session start*, with no way to suppress it.

This is a **regression**: `1.0.88` connects the same server, with the same token,
and resolves the identical OAuth challenge silently — no page, no interaction.

Critically, the stored token has **no refresh token** (the tokens file contains
only `accessToken`, `expiresAt`, `scope`), so there is no silent renewal path —
the CLI appears to fall straight through to the interactive flow rather than
using the access token it already holds.

## Affected version

- **Last known good: `1.0.88`**
- **Broken: `1.0.89`**

A single version bump. Both were tested on the same machine, minutes apart, against
the same MCP server and the same on-disk token.

| Installed | Size | SHA-256 (first 16) | `--no-auto-update --version` | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Aug 14 | 152.1 MB | `4F590F1F60F3F2BD` | 1.0.80 | works — challenge resolved silently |
| Sep 23 | 144.2 MB | `E2160809894BA950` | **1.0.88** | **works** — challenge resolved silently |
| Sep 29 | 144.8 MB | `155778DD92A2171A` | **1.0.89** | **broken** — page opens every session |

**Secondary reporting bug worth fixing on its own:** plain `copilot --version`
reported `1.0.89` for *all three* binaries, including the 1.0.80 one. Only
`copilot --no-auto-update --version` reveals the real built-in versions above.
That made this regression very hard to characterise — it looked like one version
behaving two different ways. If `--version` is reporting a cached/candidate
package rather than the running build, it should say so.

- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200)
- Mode: `copilot --acp` (ACP server), 4 × `--plugin-dir`
- MCP protocol negotiated: `2025-11-25`

## Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure an OAuth-protected HTTP MCP server in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`:
   `https://mcp.internal.example.com/servers/REDACTED-MCP/mcp`
2. Complete its OAuth flow once. Confirm `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config` now holds a
   registration with `"isStatic": false` and a paired `*.tokens.json` whose keys are
   exactly `accessToken`, `expiresAt`, `scope` — i.e. **no `refreshToken`**, and
   `expiresAt` comfortably in the future (mine was ~3 days out).
3. Start `copilot --acp` and drive `initialize` → `authenticate` → `session/new`,
   passing that server in `mcpServers`.
4. Observe: the authorization page opens even though the token is still valid.
5. Repeat step 3. It opens again, every time.

## Expected behavior

With a valid unexpired access token on disk, `session/new` should connect the MCP
server using that token and open nothing. If the server genuinely rejects the
token with 401, the CLI should surface an actionable error rather than silently
launching a browser authorization flow on every session — that behaviour is
unusable for headless or unattended ACP clients.

## Actual behavior — CLI log

From `~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log` on the **Sep 29** build (hostnames redacted):

```
[ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed,
        when Client(OAuthChallenge {
          www_authenticate_header: "******\"https://mcp.internal.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/servers/REDACTED-MCP/mcp\"",
          response: McpOAuthHttpResponse { status_code: 401, header_count: 6, has_body: true } })

[INFO]  [rust:acp::mcp_oauth] opened the MCP OAuth authorization page {"server_name":"REDACTED-MCP"}

[WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::session::mcp::agent_host] HTTP 401 challenge
        (WWW-Authenticate: ******"https://mcp.internal.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/servers/REDACTED-MCP/mcp")
        {"server":"REDACTED-MCP"}
```

Possibly the same root cause — the new discovery call is rejected for lack of a
bearer token, then falls back:

```
[WARNING] [rust:mcp::client] server/discover failed; retrying with legacy initialize
        {"error":"unexpected server response: HTTP 400 Bad Request: {\"error\":\"Invalid or missing bearer token\"}"}
```

## A/B isolating the build

Same machine, same 3-minute window, **same on-disk token** (issued earlier that day,
`expiresAt` 3 days out), identical client invocation and identical MCP server list.
Only the `copilot.exe` binary was swapped between runs:

| Run | Version | `opened the MCP OAuth authorization page` | `401 challenge` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15:29 | 1.0.80 (`4F590F1F…`) | **0** | **0** |
| 15:32 | 1.0.89 (`155778DD…`) | **1** | **2** |
| 20:33 | **1.0.88** (`E2160809…`) | **0** | **0** |

Because the token was unchanged and still valid across all three runs, token expiry
is ruled out as the cause; the binary is the only variable. 1.0.88 passing puts the
regression squarely in the 1.0.88 → 1.0.89 change.

On 1.0.88 and 1.0.80 the server issues the **same** OAuth challenge — the log still shows
`worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed, when Client(OAuthChallenge {…})`
— but it is then resolved without any user interaction:

```
[ERROR] Successfully authenticated with co-design
[INFO]  [rust:rmcp::service] Service initialized as client { … }
[ERROR] Handling tools refresh for co-design
```

So the regression is not "the server started returning 401". It is that 1.0.89 no
longer completes that challenge silently and instead falls back to opening the
interactive authorization page. (Those two lines are also logged at `ERROR` level
on success in 1.0.80, which looks like a separate log-level mistake.)

## Impact

Every new ACP session pops a browser window the operator did not ask for. For any
non-interactive ACP client (our case: a local web UI and scheduled agent runs)
this is disruptive, and on a headless host the flow has nobody to approve it.

issues.title: Context window rollover fails: "checkpoint.md is absent for this agent; write it before requesting rollover"

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

issues.body:
# Context window rollover fails: "checkpoint.md is absent for this agent; write it before requesting rollover"

### Describe the bug
Long-running agent sessions crash when the context window fills and the runtime attempts a rollover:

```
Execution failed: Failed to start a fresh context window: checkpoint.md is absent for this agent; write it before requesting rollover
```

The turn ends and the session (or sub-agent) is effectively dead; it recurs on subsequent turns in the same session.

### What we observed
- The agent **had** written a `checkpoint.md` to the session's `files/` folder (via a normal file write / patch) ~7 minutes before the first failure, yet the runtime still reported it as absent "for this agent".
- The native runtime contains related errors ("Replacing checkpoint.md requires expected_revision; read or stat it first, or use append", "Stale checkpoint writer…"), which suggests checkpoints must be written through a runtime-managed store/tool rather than a plain file write. In our sessions the model did not appear to have any tool exposed for that store, so it could never satisfy the precondition.
- Seen repeatedly across multiple sessions/sub-agents (custom agents and the main agent), mostly in long tool-heavy sessions (builds, test runs, large tool outputs).

### Expected behavior
Either the runtime writes/derives the checkpoint itself before rollover, or the agent is given (and prompted to use) the tool needed to create it. Failing that, it should fall back to normal compaction instead of terminating the turn.

### Environment
- GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.100 (also seen on 1.0.98)
- Windows 11 x64, PowerShell
- Models: GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 sessions

### Workaround
Manual `/compact` before the context fills avoids it.

issues.title: High CPU and repeated "gh auth token" failures when not signed in (worse without gh)

labels.name: area:authentication
labels.description: Login, OAuth, device auth, token management, and keychain integration

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When Copilot CLI runs without a usable GitHub credential, the background auth probe `copilot_runtime::auth::gh` (i.e. `gh auth token`) is retried in a tight loop **with no backoff**. I hit this in a normal interactive session using a BYOK provider, with no GitHub account signed in: the process sat with a CPU core pegged while I was working in that session, and signing in (`/login`) brought it back to idle immediately. The faster the probe fails, the worse it gets — where `gh` is not resolvable on `PATH` every attempt fails in microseconds and the process busy-spins at **~145 % of one core**; with `gh` installed but signed out it still spins at ~19 %.

Every attempt logs:

```
[WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::auth::gh] Failed to run `gh auth token` {"error":"program path has no file name","program":""}
```

Note `"program":""` — the probe is invoked with an empty program path, so no process is spawned and the caller retries at once. The warning rate equals the retry rate: **274 lines/s** in the reproduction below (inter-arrival median 3 ms, min 0 ms).

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.101.

Windows standalone binary via winget (`GitHub.Copilot`). `gh` was absent from `PATH` when variant A was measured, and installed but signed out (2.103.2) for variant B.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior


**How I ran into it:** a normal interactive session using a BYOK provider, with no GitHub account signed in. CPU sat with one core pegged for as long as the session was open, and `%USERPROFILE%\.copilot\logs\process-*.log` filled up with the warnings above. Signing in via `/login` brought CPU back to idle.

**Isolated experiment (measurement only, not the trigger):** the essential condition is just *a session with no GitHub credential*. Without one the CLI would exit immediately, so to keep such a session alive on demand I pointed the BYOK provider at a port that refuses connections and ran it headless (`-p`). This setup exists only to make the spin measurable — it is not the scenario in the report.

```powershell
$env:COPILOT_HOME              = "C:\temp\cp-empty"        # empty dir => no credentials
$env:COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:9/v1"   # refuses connections
$env:COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY  = "sk-test"

copilot -p "say hi" -s --model gpt-4o-mini --no-auto-update
```

1. Run the block above with `gh` **not** on `PATH` (variant A).
2. Run it again with `gh` installed but **not signed in** (variant B).
3. Sample CPU per second: `Get-Process copilot | Select-Object CPU`.
4. Inspect `%USERPROFILE%\.copilot\logs\process-*.log` (or point `--log-dir` at a directory).

Result:

| Variant | CPU | `auth::gh` warnings |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A: `gh` not on PATH | **~145 % of one core**, sustained for the whole run | **9,921 lines in 36.2 s → 274 /s**; inter-arrival median **3 ms**, min 0 ms, p90 6 ms |
| B: `gh` on PATH, not signed in | ~19 % of one core | 0 lines |

Three consecutive lines from variant A:

```
2026-10-26T07:23:17.891Z [WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::auth::gh] Failed to run `gh auth token` {"error":"program path has no file name","program":""}
2026-10-26T07:23:17.896Z [WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::auth::gh] Failed to run `gh auth token` {"error":"program path has no file name","program":""}
2026-10-26T07:23:17.899Z [WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::auth::gh] Failed to run `gh auth token` {"error":"program path has no file name","program":""}
```


### Expected behavior

CPU should stay near idle during a session that has no GitHub credential — interactive or not — and an unresolvable `gh` binary should be treated as "gh unavailable": probed once, or on a backoff schedule, instead of being re-probed on every call.

### Additional context


**Environment**

* OS: Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 10.0.19044, x64
* Observed in an interactive session with a BYOK provider, no GitHub account signed in
* The figures come from the headless experiment above: same log signature, easier to sample
* No proxy configured

**Earlier occurrence, same signature** (first launch on this machine, 1.0.101, no login): 4,459 warnings in 37.0 s = **120.5 /s**, median gap 7 ms, flat until the user signed in.

**Notes on the mechanism**

* The probe fails without spawning anything (`"program":""`), so retry latency is ~0 and the loop period collapses to microseconds.
* Failures appear to be retried immediately — no backoff, and the 0 ms inter-arrival gaps suggest overlapping attempts.
* Other auth probes settle at a ~1.1 s cadence while network-bound (`auth::manager_orchestration`: `Failed to fetch GitHub CLI user login (401)` ↔ `Failed to fetch PAT user login (401)`), so the gh-probe path is the outlier.
* With `gh` installed the loop is only slower (~19 % CPU), not gone.

**Workaround**

Signing in (`/login`) or exporting `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` / a fine-grained PAT stops the loop; installing `gh` only lowers the severity.

**Possibly related (different root causes)**

* #4415 High CPU usage in copilot-cli
* #5148 Idle CLI sessions pin one CPU core at 100 % (`notify-rs` debouncer loop busy-spins)
* #3700 [High severity] 1.0.60 WSL2 regression: CLI MainThread spins at ~215 % CPU while idle

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.88 on Linux, a  userPromptSubmitted  command hook can finish successfully in milliseconds, but Copilot does not recognize its completion until the configured timeout expires and the thread waiting for child process completion is woken up.

Starting copilot using "COPILOT_SETUP_TERMINAL=false copilot" avoid the issue. 

We traced this to a process-wide SIGCHLD handler conflict between Copilot’s in-process native runtime and Node.js/libuv:

1. The native runtime installs a SIGCHLD handler.
2. Automatic terminal-setup detection invokes Node’s  child_process.exec  to run:
ps -Ao pid=,ppid=,comm=
3. libuv’s  uv_spawn  replaces the native runtime’s SIGCHLD handler.
4. After that subprocess completes, libuv cleanup through  uv_signal_stop  resets SIGCHLD to  SIG_DFL , rather than restoring the native runtime’s handler.
5. A subsequently launched prompt-hook process exits successfully, but its completion does not promptly wake the native runtime’s child waiter.
6. Copilot collects the already-available exit status at our configured 300-second boundary for our hook processor and continues normally.

This is not a hook script taking five minutes to execute, nor a slow model response.

Environment

• GitHub Copilot CLI: 1.0.88
• Node.js version reported by CLI: v24.20.0
• Copilot runs on a remote Linux host.
• Two users connected to the same Linux host using the same remote account, through SSH:
• An SSH session from macOS consistently received fast responses with SSH sessions established using iTerm on the Mac.
• An SSH session from Windows reproduced the delay when using mobaxterm or putty.
• The configured  UserPromptSubmit  command hook had a 300-second timeout.
• The hook was loaded from the user-level hook configuration.

In the affected session:

• Copilot emits  hook.start  for  userPromptSubmitted .
• The hook process exits with status 0 in approximately 274 ms.
• SIGCHLD is delivered to the parent, but no corresponding signal handler runs.
• The child remains a zombie, parented to Copilot.
• Copilot remains active, but the prompt does not progress to a model request.
• Approximately 300 seconds after hook start (our set timeout), Copilot calls  wait4  again and collects the successful exit status.
• Copilot then emits  hook.end  with  success: true  and proceeds to the model.

### Affected version

1.0.88

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure a user-level  UserPromptSubmit  command hook with a 300-second timeout.
2. Start interactive Copilot CLI 1.0.88 on Linux from the affected Windows-origin SSH session.
3. Submit a simple text prompt that does not require a tool call.
4. Observe  hook.start , but no timely  hook.end  or model response.
5. Inspect the hook child: it has already exited and remains a zombie.
6. Wait for the configured timeout boundary; Copilot recognizes the successful exit and responds.

Control tests:

• Removing the user-level hooks eliminated the prompt delay.
• With hooks enabled, the macOS-origin SSH session responded promptly.
• In the fast capture, the native runtime’s SIGCHLD handler remained effective and the hook child was reaped immediately.
• In the delayed capture, the terminal-detection  ps  subprocess ran and the parent’s SIGCHLD handler was subsequently reset to default.

Use this strace command to see the replacement of the SIGCHLD handler for 

 strace -ff -k -ttt -T \
  -e trace=%process,%signal \
  -e signal=all \
  -o /tmp/copilot-startup-stack-affected \
  copilot --log-level debug

### Expected behavior

After a  userPromptSubmitted  hook process exits, Copilot should promptly collect its exit status, emit  hook.end , and proceed with the model turn.

Startup subprocesses launched through Node/libuv should not leave the native runtime’s child-exit notification mechanism disabled.

### Additional context

_No response_
