issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When using Claude Opus, it will occasionally `cd` into a lower directory and then access a sibling directory using the relative parent directory shortcut (`..`). This will inevitably be flagged by Copilot CLI as going outside of the project directory, which is clearly incorrect. Rather than assuming `..` is going out of the project directory, Copilot CLI should be getting the absolute directory and checking that.



### Affected version

Copilot v1.0.80

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Example issue:

1. Start Copilot CLI in `/work`.
2. Ask Claude to review code with a deep directory structure.
3. Claude will use something like the following command: `cd subfolder/subfolder3/subfolder5 && grep -rn "searching for text" ../subfolder4`
4. The CLI incorrectly "warns" me that it's accessing a directory outside my workspace. And then wants me to add `../subfolder4` to my "allowed" directories, which is not secure. If it was added to the "allowed" directories, it actually *could* do it at the top level.

### Expected behavior

The CLI should be converting relative addressing to absolute addressing and checking the full path.

### Additional context

_No response_

issues.title: Managed-settings interim fail-closed uses an empty allow list ([[]]) and permanently drops user MCP servers that register inside the window — reproduces via the desktop app, on an account with no managed policy

labels.name: area:enterprise
labels.description: GitHub Enterprise (GHE/GHES) support, org policies, and enterprise settings

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

While the CLI resolves managed settings, it installs an **interim "deny everything" MCP policy**
(`managedAllowedMcpServerLists: [[]]` — one list, containing nothing). Any user-configured MCP server
that happens to register during that window is rejected with:

```
[ERROR] Skipping MCP server "<name>": not permitted by enterprise managed allow list
```

Two things make this a real bug rather than a benign transient:

1. **It fires even when there is no managed policy at all.** In my logs the resolution completes in
   5–65 ms with `source=none`, `serverFetchFailed=false`, and
   `[managedSettings] applied: no bypass restriction in force (managed policy absent)`. Nothing failed,
   and there is no enterprise policy on this account. The deny is purely pre-emptive.
2. **Servers denied during that window are never restored.** The "policy relaxed" restore loop replays
   only servers captured in `policyRemovedConfigs`, and the startup deny paths never write there. Those
   servers stay dead for the entire life of the session.

Net effect: opening a session while any session is resolving managed settings silently produces a
session with **no user MCP servers**, permanently. Built-in servers are exempt (the trusted-first-party
check keeps entries whose `source === "builtin"`), so it presents as "my servers are broken" rather than
"a policy was applied".

### Important scope note

**The defect is in the CLI, but it is only reachable when the CLI is driven by a client that sets
`enableManagedSettings: true`.** The GitHub Copilot desktop app sets it on every `session.create` and
`session.resume`. A CLI launched by hand does not, so **this cannot be reproduced from a bare terminal
invocation** — please see the warning at the top of the repro steps before trying.

This is provable from both sides of the interface:

- **CLI side** (`app.js`, 1.0.79-5): 21 occurrences of `enableManagedSettings`, and **not one assigns it
  `true`**. Both `enableManagedSettings=!0` and `enableManagedSettings:!0` are absent from the entire
  bundle. The field initialises to `!1` and is thereafter only read from the client payload
  (`this.enableManagedSettings = n.enableManagedSettings ?? !1`). Every managed-settings entry point is
  gated on it, including `refreshManagedSettings()`, which opens with
  `if(!this.enableManagedSettings)return;`.
- **App side** (`copilot-sdk/index.js`, app 1.1.6): passes
  `enableManagedSettings: config.enableManagedSettings` into both `session.create` and `session.resume`.

That is why the same binary produces 257 deny events under the app and 0 when launched directly.

### Impact

- Sessions silently lose all user MCP tooling. There is no `tools_changed` notification, no banner, and
  no error surfaced in the UI — only an `[ERROR]` line in a process log the user has no reason to read.
- The message names a cause (`enterprise managed allow list`) that **does not exist on the account**,
  sending users to hunt for a nonexistent policy. At least one upstream reporter (#4392) read it as a
  genuine corporate whitelist.
- Agents and skills that depend on those servers fail in ways that look like the servers are
  misconfigured, so users edit working configuration trying to fix it.
- MCP child processes are spawned and then discarded, so the startup cost is paid for no benefit.

## Affected Version

**Reproduced on CLI payload 1.0.79-5**, driven by desktop app 1.1.6 (`commit=a9706b2`); also observed
under app 1.1.5 (`f459745`). Windows 11 x64.

The mechanism is present in every payload from **1.0.72** onward. Marker counts taken directly from each
shipped `app.js`:

| CLI payload | `managedAllowedMcpServerLists:[[]]` | host-wide fan-out to active sessions | `managedSettingsResolutionInFlight` |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1.0.71** | **absent** | **0** | **0** |
| 1.0.72 | present | 0 | 0 |
| 1.0.73 | present | 0 | 0 |
| **1.0.78-2** | present | **1** | **4** |
| 1.0.79-5 | present | 1 | 4 |
| 1.0.79-9 | present | 1 | 4 |

- **1.0.72** introduced the empty-allow-list interim state, behind a narrow session-local guard.
- **1.0.78-2** made it routine: it added fan-out to every active session and widened the trigger guard at
  the same time (diff in Additional context).
- **1.0.71 does not contain the mechanism at all** and is the basis of the workaround.

Install timeline on this machine, from `~/.copilot/logs/github-app.*.log`:

```
2026-08-04T07:42:36Z  Detected Copilot CLI version at startup version=Copilot binary version: 1.0.78-2 source=Some(Bundled)
2026-08-07T15:03:37Z  Detected Copilot CLI version at startup version=Copilot binary version: 1.0.79-5 source=Some(Bundled)
```

**The desktop app version is a precondition, not the cause.** `copilot-sdk/index.js` is byte-identical
between app 1.1.5 and 1.1.6 (SHA-256 `648CD26BA299…`, 449,504 bytes in both), and the app has passed
`enableManagedSettings` since 1.1.0 — so nothing changed on the app side across the window in which the
symptom appeared.

> Note on reading versions: `copilot.exe --version` self-resolves to the newest *installed* payload and
> will misreport which payload is actually running. Use `--no-auto-update --version`, or inspect the
> loaded module path of a live process.

### Affected version

CLI payload 1.0.79-5+. See the bottom of description for details on affected version

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

> ⚠️ **A hand-launched CLI will not reproduce this, and the clean log it produces is not evidence the
> build is fine.** Running `copilot --server --stdio --no-auto-update` directly produced **0**
> `[managedSettings]` lines and **0** deny events, while the app-spawned *same binary* in the same hour
> produced **823** and **257** respectively. The reason is in the scope note above: such a process is
> never sent `enableManagedSettings: true`, so it never enters the managed-settings path at all — and
> that holds **even if you authenticate it**. Reproduce through the desktop app.

1. Install the desktop app (1.1.5 or 1.1.6) with a CLI payload of **1.0.78-2 or later**.
2. Sign in with an account that has **no** enterprise managed policy. Confirm with the process log — a
   clean resolution on such an account looks like this:

```
2026-08-09T15:19:40.754Z [INFO] [managedSettings] self-fetch starting for account https://github.com/<user>
2026-08-09T15:19:40.755Z [INFO] [managedSettings] device MDM: no policy present on this device
2026-08-09T15:19:40.915Z [INFO] [managedSettings] server policy: none for this account (404/empty) from https://github.com
2026-08-09T15:19:40.916Z [INFO] [managedSettings] effective policy resolved: source=none, bypassDisabled=false, serverFetchFailed=false
2026-08-09T15:19:40.916Z [INFO] [managedSettings] applied: no bypass restriction in force (managed policy absent)
```

3. Configure 2 or more user MCP servers in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`. Transport does not matter —
   stdio, http and local all fail together. Do not rely on the built-in GitHub server to show the
   failure; it is exempt.
4. **Open several app sessions in quick succession**, or open a new session while another is still
   starting. Opening a single session already issues `session.create` and then `session.resume` roughly
   2 s later, so one open produces two overlapping option updates; several opens make a collision
   near-certain.
5. Search the CLI process logs for the denial:

```powershell
Select-String -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.copilot\logs\process-*.log" `
  -SimpleMatch 'not permitted by enterprise managed allow list' |
  Where-Object { $_.Line -match '^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T' -and $_.Line.Length -lt 300 }
```

> **The `^\d{4}-…` anchor and the length filter are both necessary.** Conversation transcripts and
> fetched page text are written into these same logs, so an unanchored search matches quoted copies of
> the message and overcounts badly. This produced false positives twice during the investigation.

**Output — the denial, with the surrounding lifecycle.** From
`~/.copilot/logs/process-1786241789611-38652.log`. Note the ordering and the millisecond deltas: the
skips land **inside** the fetch, and the fetch **succeeds**:

```
2026-08-09T02:16:45.131Z [INFO]  [managedSettings] self-fetch starting for account https://github.com/<user>
2026-08-09T02:16:45.136Z [ERROR] Skipping MCP server "ado-skype": not permitted by enterprise managed allow list
2026-08-09T02:16:45.136Z [ERROR] Skipping MCP server "ado-domoreexp": not permitted by enterprise managed allow list
2026-08-09T02:16:45.136Z [ERROR] Skipping MCP server "mcp_windbg": not permitted by enterprise managed allow list
2026-08-09T02:16:45.136Z [ERROR] Skipping MCP server "obsidian-vault-coding-brain": not permitted by enterprise managed allow list
2026-08-09T02:16:45.196Z [INFO]  [managedSettings] self-fetch complete for https://github.com/<user>: bypassDisabled=false, serverFetchFailed=false, serverCacheFallback=false, deviceLoadFailed=false
2026-08-09T02:16:45.634Z [WARNING] Failed to refresh persisted MCP tools for mcp_windbg; continuing with cached tools: Error: MCP server "mcp_windbg" is not connected
```

- deny window here = **65 ms**; the servers were denied at **+5 ms**
- `serverFetchFailed=false` — the policy fetch worked
- the MCP child processes had **already been spawned**
  (`MCP server stderr {"server_name":"ado-domoreexp", ...}` at `02:16:45.079`), so the work is done and
  then thrown away

6. To see the window itself and every trigger, pull the whole lifecycle:

```powershell
Select-String -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.copilot\logs\process-*.log" -SimpleMatch '[managedSettings]'
```

**Output — a tighter variant**, in which a server is denied **1 ms after the fetch already completed**,
showing the interim policy is not cleared synchronously with completion:

```
2026-08-09T02:18:14.600Z [INFO]  [managedSettings] self-fetch starting for account https://github.com/<user>
2026-08-09T02:18:14.605Z [ERROR] Skipping MCP server "ado-skype": not permitted by enterprise managed allow list
   ... (ado-domoreexp, mcp_windbg, obsidian-vault-coding-brain, same millisecond)
2026-08-09T02:18:14.619Z [INFO]  [managedSettings] self-fetch complete for https://github.com/<user>: ... serverFetchFailed=false ...
2026-08-09T02:18:14.620Z [ERROR] Skipping MCP server "obsidian-vault-coding-brain": not permitted by enterprise managed allow list
```

**Output — additional trigger sources**, each of which opens its own deny window:

```
2026-08-09T02:18:18.068Z [INFO] [managedSettings] self-fetch starting for account device-only
2026-08-09T02:18:18.076Z [INFO] [managedSettings] self-fetch starting for account https://github.com/<user>
2026-08-09T02:18:18.079Z [INFO] [managedSettings] self-fetch result for device-only discarded: account changed while the fetch was in flight
```

**Reproduction rate.** Over the surviving log-retention window (2026-08-08T22:46Z – 2026-08-09T02:18Z),
during ordinary multi-session use: **42 skip records in 9 bursts across 2 CLI processes** —
`obsidian-vault-coding-brain` ×15, `ado-skype` ×9, `ado-domoreexp` ×9, `mcp_windbg` ×9. The built-in
GitHub server was never skipped. Not every session is affected; which sessions lose servers permanently
is decided by the timing rule described in Additional context.

### Expected behavior

On an account with **no** enterprise managed policy, all servers configured in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`
should start and remain available for the life of the session. Concretely:

1. **No deny while the policy is merely undetermined.** "We have not resolved the policy yet" should not
   be encoded as "a policy exists and it permits nothing." With `source=none`, `serverFetchFailed=false`
   and `managed policy absent`, zero servers should be filtered.
2. **If a pre-emptive deny is genuinely required, it must be reversible.** A server denied during the
   interim window should be restored when the window closes, exactly as a server stopped by a real
   policy tightening already is. Today the two cases behave differently and only one of them recovers.
3. **Registration should wait for the policy rather than race it.** The gate that exists for this purpose
   should be in force during startup registration.
4. **A resolution that has not failed should not disturb sessions that are already running.** Servers
   already connected should not be torn down for a routine re-resolution in another session.
5. **If servers are withheld, say so where the user will see it.** The failure is currently silent in the
   UI, and the message that does exist blames an enterprise policy that is not present on the account.

### Additional context

### Where the code is

All references are to the shipped bundle:

```
%LOCALAPPDATA%\copilot\pkg\win32-x64\1.0.79-5\app.js      (9,317,686 chars, 6,135 lines)
```

The file is bundled one module per line, so the relevant lines are 100–150 KB wide (line 2345 is 147,313
chars; line 2398 is 114,363). **A line number alone will not locate anything — use line:col, or the byte
offset.** Both are given; either can be re-derived by searching for the symbol name, which is unminified.

| # | What | Symbol | line:col | byte offset |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Producer emits the empty allow list | `composedManagedMcpHostOptions` | 2398:44941 | 2147203 |
| 1a | The literal itself | `managedAllowedMcpServerLists:[[]]` | 2398:45016 | 2147278 |
| 2 | Consumer's `length > 0` test | `managedMcpPolicyPlan` | 2345:75295 | 1893804 |
| 3 | Tighten + relax, both halves | `enforceManagedMcpPolicy` | 2345:76770 | 1895279 |
| 3a | **The only `.set()` in the bundle** | `policyRemovedConfigs.set(` | 2345:77656 | 1896165 |
| 4 | Deny path A — bulk start loop | after `managedMcpPolicyBlockReasonForBulk` | 2345:79639 | 1898148 |
| 5 | Deny path B — first check | `startServerOnce` | 2345:93949 | 1912458 |
| 6 | Deny path C — second check | `startServerOnce` | 2345:94664 | 1913173 |
| 7 | The gate that opts itself out | `expectManagedMcpPolicy` | 2398:43337 | 2145599 |
| 8 | Host-wide fan-out | `beginManagedSettingsResolution` | 2398:42842 | 2145104 |
| 9 | The trigger | `updateOptions` | 2402:67610 | 2284349 |
| 10 | Client-supplied flag default | `enableManagedSettings ?? !1` | 2402:40113 | 2256852 |

To re-derive line:col from an offset (`[regex]::Matches` over a 9 MB string hangs — use `IndexOf`):

```powershell
$s = [IO.File]::ReadAllText("$env:LOCALAPPDATA\copilot\pkg\win32-x64\1.0.79-5\app.js")
$off = $s.IndexOf('policyRemovedConfigs.set(', [StringComparison]::Ordinal)
$line = 1; $i = $s.IndexOf("`n"); $last = 0
while ($i -ge 0 -and $i -lt $off) { $line++; $last = $i + 1; $i = $s.IndexOf("`n", $i + 1) }
"line $line col $($off - $last + 1)  offset $off"
```

There is a fourth `mcpHostStateAddFiltered(...)` call at 2345:93083 / offset 1911592, inside
`applyConfigFilterToServer`. **It is not part of this defect** — it is the separate config-filter path
and logs `MCP server "X" filtered: <reason>`, not the allow-list message. Noted so the count is not
mistaken for four managed-policy deny sites; there are three.

### Root cause

#### 1. The producer emits "a policy exists and it allows nothing"

```js
composedManagedMcpHostOptions() {
  if (this.managedMcpInterimFailClosed)
    return { managedAllowedMcpServerLists: [[]] };          // <-- one list, containing nothing
  let e = this.composeManagedMcpPolicy();
  return {
    managedAllowedMcpServerLists: e.allowedLists.length > 0 ? e.allowedLists : void 0,
    managedDeniedMcpServers:      e.denied.length      > 0 ? e.denied      : void 0
  };
}
```

Note the asymmetry with the normal path directly below it: when there is genuinely no policy the normal
path returns `void 0`, but the interim path returns `[[]]`.

#### 2. The consumer's "is a policy configured?" test cannot tell `[[]]` from a real policy

```js
async managedMcpPolicyPlan(e, n) {
  let r = this.managedAllowedMcpServerLists ?? [],
      o = r.length > 0,                                     // [[]].length === 1  -> true
      s = (this.managedDeniedMcpServers?.length ?? 0) > 0;
  return !o && !s
    ? { removeNames: [], logMessages: [] }
    : await h.mcpHostManagedMcpPolicyActions(/* ... */);
}
```

`[[]]` is truthy for `length > 0`, so the native policy engine runs against an empty allow list and
removes everything not exempt. The user-visible string comes from `o.logMessages[0]`, produced by the
native addon — which is why grepping `app.js` for `not permitted by enterprise managed allow list` finds
nothing.

Exemption set — why built-ins survive and every user server dies together regardless of transport:

```js
isRegisteredServerTrustedFirstParty(e) {
  return this.trustedDynamicStartServerNames.has(e)
      || this.trustedDefaultServerNames.includes(e)
      || this.trustedExternalServerNames.has(e);
}
// trustedDefaultServerNames keeps only entries whose source === "builtin"
```

#### 3. The bug's teeth: the startup deny paths are not restorable

`enforceManagedMcpPolicy` contains both halves of the policy transition. On tighten it stops the server
**and stashes its config**; on relax it replays **only** what was stashed:

```js
// tighten: stop + stash
try { await this.stopServer(l); } catch (d) { /* ... */ }
this.policyRemovedConfigs.set(l, c);            // <-- the ONLY .set() in the file (2345:77656)
delete this.config.mcpServers[l];

// relax: restore
for (let [l, c] of [...this.policyRemovedConfigs])
  if (!s.has(l)) {
    if (this.config.mcpServers[l]) { this.policyRemovedConfigs.delete(l); continue; }
    try { await this.startServer(l, c); } catch (d) { /* ... */ continue; }
    this.config.mcpServers[l] && (this.policyRemovedConfigs.delete(l), a = !0);
  }
```

But a server denied **while starting** never reaches that stash. `startServerOnce` checks the policy
twice and both times just marks the server filtered and returns:

```js
async startServerOnce(e, n, r, o, s = !1) {
  let a = this.currentServerStopVersion(e);
  if (!this.validateServerConfig(e, n)) return;
  let l = await this.managedMcpPolicyBlockReason(e, n, s);
  if (l) { h.mcpHostStateAddFiltered(this.hostStateHandle, e); this.logger.log(l); return; }   // 2345:93949
  /* ... gate plan, config filtering ... */
  let g = await this.managedMcpPolicyBlockReason(e, d, s);
  if (g || this.currentServerStopVersion(e) !== a) {
    g && (h.mcpHostStateAddFiltered(this.hostStateHandle, e), this.logger.log(g)); return;      // 2345:94664
  }
  this.config.mcpServers[e] = d;      // only reached when NOT blocked
  /* ... connect ... */
}
```

and the bulk path additionally **deletes the config outright**:

```js
let d = await this.managedMcpPolicyBlockReasonForBulk(l, c);
if (d) {
  this.logger.log(d);
  h.mcpHostStateAddFiltered(this.hostStateHandle, l);
  delete this.config.mcpServers[l];       // <-- dropped, never stashed for restore  (2345:79639)
  return;
}
```

**There is exactly one `policyRemovedConfigs.set(...)` in the bundle, and none of the three
managed-policy deny paths is it.** Therefore:

| when the window opens | outcome |
|---|---|
| server **already registered** | stopped, stashed, **restored automatically** when the policy clears |
| server **registering right now** | filtered + config dropped, **never restored** — dead for the life of the session |

A fresh session registers its MCP servers at session start, which is exactly when the window opens, so
the common case is the non-restorable one. This single asymmetry is why the failure looks
non-deterministic, and why "it fixed itself after a minute" and "it was dead for the whole session" are
both accurate reports of the same defect.

Servers in the second row can still come back if a later full MCP client rebuild happens to re-register
them from the original config — the teardown/rebuild described in #4392. That is incidental rather than
the restore path, and it can be denied again: I measured 4 consecutive bursts on the same 4 servers
within 90 s.

#### 4. What opens the window, and why it opens so often

```js
beginManagedSettingsResolution() {
  if (this.lastManagedSettingsLayers) {
    this.managedSettingsResolutionInFlight = !0;
    this.managedSettingsPolicyGeneration++;
    for (let n of this.activeSessions.values())
      n.beginManagedSettingsResolution({ permissions: !1 });   // fan-out to EVERY live session
  }
}
```

`{permissions:false}` skips the permissions half, but the session-level handler still always calls
`beginInterimManagedMcpFailClosed()`. A session that joins while a resolution is in flight is
immediately fail-closed too:

```js
applyCurrentManagedSettingsPolicy(e, n, r) {
  /* ... */ this.managedSettingsResolutionInFlight
      ? e.beginManagedSettingsResolution({ permissions: !1 })
      : /* ... */
}
```

There is a gate intended to make MCP registration wait for the policy, but it opts itself out whenever
the host already exists, so registration proceeds against the interim `[[]]`:

```js
expectManagedMcpPolicy() {
  if (this.managedMcpPolicyApplied || this.mcpHost || this.managedMcpPolicyGate) return;
  /* ...create gate... */
}
// consumer:
this.managedMcpPolicyGate && await this.managedMcpPolicyGate.promise;   // no gate -> awaits nothing
```

### The 1.0.78-2 trigger-guard change

```js
// 1.0.73 — narrow: authInfo present AND identity defined AND identity changed; session-local effect
if (e.authInfo !== void 0 && this.enableManagedSettings) {
  let l = YX(this.authInfo);
  l !== void 0 && l !== this.managedSettingsFetchIdentity && (
    this.managedSettingsFetchIdentity = l,
    this.beginInterimManagedMcpFailClosed(),          // this session only
    /* ... */);
}

// 1.0.78-2 and later — broad: key merely present, undefined identity no longer suppresses,
// plus a generation check; effect is now host-wide
if (this.enableManagedSettings && ("authInfo" in e || e.enableManagedSettings === !0)) {
  let c = ene(this.authInfo);
  (c !== this.managedSettingsFetchIdentity ||
   this.managedSettingsAuthGeneration !== this.managedSettingsFetchGeneration) && (
    this.managedSettingsFetchIdentity   = c,
    this.managedSettingsFetchGeneration = this.managedSettingsAuthGeneration,
    this.beginManagedSettingsResolution(),            // fan-out to ALL sessions
    /* ... */);
}
```

Three widenings at once: `e.authInfo !== void 0` became `"authInfo" in e`; the `l !== void 0` guard was
dropped; and a generation disjunct was added. `managedSettingsAuthGeneration++` (new in 1.0.78-2, fired
on `auth_info_updated`) means each auth refresh arms the next options update to re-trigger the cycle.

The **hourly** `refreshManagedSettings()` timer does *not* call `beginManagedSettingsResolution()` — only
`updateOptions` does. So the window is tied to session churn, not to the timer.

### Suggested fixes (any one breaks the chain)

1. **Do not use `[[]]` as a sentinel.** Represent "policy undetermined" as a distinct flag, or make the
   consumer test `r.some(list => list.length > 0)` instead of `r.length > 0`.
2. **Make the deny paths restorable** — have the `startServerOnce` and bulk deny paths record the config
   into `policyRemovedConfigs` (or an equivalent) so the "policy relaxed" loop can replay them. This is
   the smallest change that removes the permanent-loss case.
3. **Fix the gate** — drop `|| this.mcpHost` from `expectManagedMcpPolicy()` so registration waits for
   the resolution instead of racing it.
4. **Do not fan out to already-running sessions**, or at minimum do not tear down servers that are
   already connected for a resolution that has not failed.

### Workaround (verified)

Pin the CLI to **1.0.71**, which does not contain the mechanism at all:

```powershell
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable(
  'COPILOT_CLI_PATH',
  "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\github-copilot-sdk\cli\1.0.71\copilot.exe",
  'User')
# then fully exit and restart the app
```

Confirmed applied — note that the reported version string is unreliable here; the **path** is ground truth:

```
2026-08-09T05:01:55Z  Detected Copilot CLI version at startup version=GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.79-9
                      source=Some(Local) path="...\github-copilot-sdk\cli\1.0.71\copilot.exe"
                      bundled_version="1.0.79-5"
```

All 8 running `copilot.exe` processes load their payload from `pkg\win32-x64\1.0.71\`, and there have
been **zero** deny events in the ~11 h since, across continued multi-session use.

### What we could not determine

- **Whether the interim state is ever legitimately needed.** If the intent is to fail closed only when
  the policy genuinely cannot be determined, then the `serverFetchFailed=false` / `managed policy absent`
  case observed here should never have entered it at all.
- **Exact first occurrence.** `process-*.log` files rotate; the oldest surviving one starts
  2026-08-08T22:24Z. Earlier deny events were observed during this investigation but those files are now
  gone. The version matrix is the reliable dating, not the logs.
- **Why the perceived onset was 2026-08-08** when 1.0.78-2 shipped on 08-04. Best explanation: the
  fan-out only bites when sessions overlap, and concurrent multi-session usage began on 08-08. **Not
  proven** — offered as a hypothesis, not a finding.

### Related issues

- **#4378** — *"…registry policy fetch fails with 401/403 on GHEC data residency, silently blocking all
  user-configured MCP servers"* — same symptom, different cause (fetch **fails**). Here the fetch
  **succeeds** and there is no policy, so this is a distinct defect that #4378's fix would not cover.
- **#4349** — *"Managed settings policy fetch fails closed on valid enum value…"* — another fail-closed
  input-handling variant. Also fetch-side.
- **#4392** — post-auth MCP client teardown/rebuild. Relevant twice over: it is the incidental mechanism
  behind the observed silent recoveries, and its author also read the allow-list message as a real
  corporate policy.

**Please do not close this as a duplicate of the fetch-failure family.** The discriminator is one field
in the resolved line: every filed variant has `serverFetchFailed=true`; this one has
`serverFetchFailed=false` with `source=none` / `managed policy absent`. Relatedly, the **v1.0.78 release
note** advertises a fail-closed → fail-open change, but that covers the *fetch-failure* path only. This
variant is untouched by it and in fact reproduces on 1.0.79-5, which postdates it.

A third-party report quoting `Skipping MCP server "umacs-build-bridge"` dated 2026-08-03 matches the
1.0.72/1.0.73 era, consistent with the mechanism landing in 1.0.72.

issues.title: apply_patch stores deleted binary in session history, permanently exceeding CAPI 5 MB limit

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When `apply_patch` deletes a large binary file, its `tool.execution_complete` event stores the entire deleted binary as a textual diff in `result.detailedContent`.

This result remains in conversation history. Subsequent requests exceed CAPI Responses' 5 MB limit, and `/compact` fails for the same reason, leaving the session unrecoverable through the CLI.

### Affected configuration

- GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.71-0
- Linux
- Model: GPT-5.6 Sol (`gpt-5.6-sol`)
- Context window: 1.1M
- Reasoning effort: high
- Interactive session later resumed with `copilot --resume=<session-id>`

The model, context-window size, and reasoning effort may affect when compaction runs, but the persisted binary tool output appears to be the direct cause of the 5 MB transport failure.

### Observed sequence

1. Copilot used `apply_patch` to delete a large ELF executable.
2. The persisted event contained:
   - `result.detailedContent`: 22,810,594 characters
   - Serialized JSONL record: 72,155,553 bytes
   - Tool telemetry: 111,879 removed lines
3. `events.jsonl` grew to 118,622,622 bytes.
4. Further requests failed with:

   > The request is too large to send through CAPI Responses. Try shortening the conversation or prompt. (5.0 MB request; 5.0 MB limit)

5. Automatic/manual compaction failed with the same error.

### Expected behavior

Binary content should not be persisted as a textual patch. The CLI should retain deletion metadata while omitting or capping oversized `detailedContent`.

After a request-size failure, oversized tool output should be evicted so compaction can recover the session.

### Workaround and root-cause confirmation

After backing up the session, I replaced the oversized `detailedContent` with a short marker. This reduced the event log from 118.6 MB to 46.5 MB and eliminated the CAPI request-size failure.

### Related issues

This resembles #3767, but that issue covered inline attachments and was fixed in v1.0.62. This report concerns persisted `apply_patch` output in v1.0.71.

The session also developed malformed JSONL records that prevented resume, reported separately in #4098. The shared root cause is not proven, although the unusually large write may have widened the failure window.

I have not attached `events.jsonl` because it contains conversation and tool history.

---

Investigated and filed with assistance from GitHub Copilot CLI.

issues.title: Copilot CLI SEA binary hangs when IPv6 is unroutable — no fallback to IPv4

labels.name: area:networking
labels.description: Proxy, SSL/TLS, certificates, corporate environments, and connectivity issues

issues.body:
## Description

Copilot CLI v1.0.12 hangs on startup (and on any prompt/init) when DNS returns an IPv6 AAAA record for `api.individual.githubcopilot.com` that has no route. The bundled Node.js SEA binary's `fetch` (undici) does not fall back to IPv4, unlike system Node.js which handles this gracefully via Happy Eyeballs.

The CLI appears to work (login succeeds, Octokit API calls return 200), but the MCP server connection and model listing retry with exponential backoff (5s → 10s → 20s → 40s → 80s) across 5 attempts, making the CLI unusable for ~2.5 minutes before failing.

## Root cause

1. DNS returns both A (IPv4) and AAAA (IPv6) records for `api.individual.githubcopilot.com`
2. IPv6 is unroutable on the current network (e.g. mobile hotspot)
3. `curl -6 https://api.individual.githubcopilot.com/` → `No route to host`
4. `curl -4 https://api.individual.githubcopilot.com/` → works (404, as expected)
5. System Node.js `fetch('https://api.individual.githubcopilot.com/...')` → works (falls back to IPv4)
6. Copilot CLI SEA binary → `TypeError: fetch failed` (no fallback)

Because the binary is a Node.js Single Executable Application, `NODE_OPTIONS="--dns-result-order=ipv4first"` has no effect.

## Environment

- **OS:** macOS 15 (Darwin 25.3.0), Apple Silicon
- **Copilot CLI:** 1.0.12 (Homebrew cask)
- **Bundled Node.js:** v24.11.1
- **Network:** iPhone hotspot (no IPv6 routing) + DNS resolver that returns AAAA records

## Logs

From `~/.copilot/logs/`:

```
[ERROR] Starting remote MCP client for github-mcp-server with url: https://api.individual.githubcopilot.com/mcp/readonly
[ERROR] Creating MCP client for github-mcp-server...
[ERROR] Connecting MCP client for github-mcp-server...
[ERROR] Error making GitHub API request: AggregateError
[WARNING] Retrying request to GitHub API in 5 seconds. Attempt 1/5
[ERROR] MCP transport for github-mcp-server closed
[ERROR] Failed to start MCP client for remote server github-mcp-server: TypeError: fetch failed
```

Note: Octokit requests to `api.github.com` succeed (200) in the same session — only `fetch()`-based requests to `api.individual.githubcopilot.com` fail.

## Workaround

Disable any DNS resolver that returns AAAA records for the Copilot API endpoint (in my case, disabling Tailscale MagicDNS).

Adding an `/etc/hosts` entry for IPv4 does **not** help because `getaddrinfo` still returns the IPv6 address from DNS alongside the `/etc/hosts` IPv4 entry.

## Suggested fix

The SEA binary should use Happy Eyeballs (RFC 6555/8305) or `--dns-result-order=ipv4first` so that an unroutable IPv6 address doesn't prevent connection over IPv4. System Node.js v24 already handles this correctly — the issue is specific to the bundled undici in the SEA build.

Writing good prompt and predicting how the model is going to interpret them is hard

The prompt enhancer from Augment Code is fantastic.

Pro Tip: I had "Question?" to the input to the prompt enhancer and it often asks questions that will help it understand your intent better

For our basline http over ssh performance, I think it would be better to use openssh's local forwaring instead of a raw http session. Let's make that change

questons?
```

Prompt enhancer ->
```
For our baseline HTTP-over-SSH performance testing, I want to modify the test implementation to use OpenSSH's built-in local port forwarding (`ssh -L`) instead of our current approach that creates raw HTTP sessions through SSH tunnels programmatically.

issues.title: Support `/rename` in VS Code agent sessions, and let the agent invoke it

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
## Problem

`/rename` (added in #1776) works in the terminal CLI, but not for Copilot CLI sessions hosted in VS Code's Agents window:

- Typing `/rename` in an agent session's chat has no effect there — renaming is only available through the VS Code UI (verified 2026-07-23).
- There is no way for the **agent itself** to rename its session — no tool, and no slash-command it can run.

## Proposal

1. **Honor `/rename NEW_NAME` in VS Code agent sessions**, matching the terminal CLI behavior.
2. **Expose rename to the agent** (a tool, or agent-invocable `/rename`), so workflows can set titles programmatically.

## Use case

Session-hygiene rituals: I keep many long-running agent sessions and prefix titles with a status word as threads settle — `DONE …`, `PARKED …`, `CONT'D …` — so the session picker doubles as a work board. Today every close-out ends with manual rename homework; an agent-invocable rename would let the close-out workflow set the title itself (and lower-stakes: agents could title sessions descriptively from the start, cf. #3365 on auto-naming).

## Notes from poking at the internals

- A UI rename syncs into `~/.copilot/session-state/UUID/workspace.yaml` (`name:` + `user_named:`), so agents can already *read* current titles (verified 2026-07-24).
- Writing `workspace.yaml` directly doesn't work as a workaround: VS Code caches session labels elsewhere (workspace `state.vscdb`, `agentSessions.model.cache`) and doesn't notice the change.

## Related

- #1776 — added `/rename` (terminal CLI)
- #3365 — auto-generated session names not working
- #3415 — show session name at all times
- #2966 — broader session-management tooling

issues.title: `--available-tools` with an empty value exposes all tools instead of none

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

`--available-tools` is documented to disable every tool not listed, but an empty value (`--available-tools=` or `--available-tools ''`) sends all 21 built-in tools, the same as omitting the flag. There's no documented way to run `copilot -p` with no tools.


| Flag | Tools sent to the model |
|---|---|
| `--available-tools=` | 21 |
| `--available-tools ''` | 21 |
| `--excluded-tools '*'` | 21 |
| `--available-tools __none__` (a name that matches no tool) | 0 |

The workaround in the last row works, but it relies on unknown tool names being silently ignored.


### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. In an empty directory, run:
   ```
   copilot -p "Reply with the word ok." -s --model claude-haiku-5.5 \
     --available-tools= --disable-builtin-mcps --no-custom-instructions --no-ask-user
   ```
2. Read the tool count from the newest session's events:
   ```
   EVENTS=$(ls -t ~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl | head -1)
   jq -rn 'first(inputs | select(.type == "session.usage_checkpoint"))
     | .data.promptCacheBreakState[0].models[]
     | "\(.model): tool_count=\(.tool_count) tool_tokens=\(.tool_tokens)"' "$EVENTS"
   ```
   Output: `claude-haiku-5.5: tool_count=21 tool_tokens=10439`
3. Repeat steps 1 and 2 with `--available-tools __none__`.
   ```
   copilot -p "Reply with the word ok." -s --model claude-haiku-5.5 \
     --available-tools='__none__' --disable-builtin-mcps --no-custom-instructions --no-ask-user
   ```
   Output: `claude-haiku-5.5: tool_count=0 tool_tokens=0`


### Expected behavior

An empty `--available-tools` exposes no tools, or there's a documented way to disable all tools and an empty value is rejected with an error.

### Additional context

For text-only `copilot -p` calls in CI, the unwanted tool definitions add about 10,000 tokens per call. Related: #4596 (system prompt still references removed tools), #407 (list available tools).

issues.title: Hook event for slash-command / skill invocation (like Claude Code's UserPromptExpansion), and async command hooks

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Add a hook event that fires when a slash command or skill is invoked, with a matcher on its name

### Proposed solution

We ship skills as plugins for both Claude Code and Copilot CLI and log their use from plugin hooks. A skill the user types (/my-skill) doesn't go through the model's skill tool, so the only way to see it today is a userPromptSubmitted hook. That hook starts a process on every prompt and blocks it (~0.3 s), just to check whether the prompt starts with /.
 
Claude Code solves this with a UserPromptExpansion event. It fires when a typed command expands, carries command_name (plugin:skill) and command_source, and supports a matcher on the command name, so the hook only runs for matching commands.

Requests:
1. A hook event (e.g. skillInvoked / userPromptExpansion) that fires when a typed slash command or skill expands, with the plugin and skill name in the payload and a matcher on the name.
2. Support for "async": true on command hooks, so a logging hook doesn't delay the prompt (Claude Code runs async hooks in the background; Copilot CLI 1.0.105 currently waits for them).

The skill name and plugin are already available as the github.copilot.skill.invoked OTel span and the SDK SKILL_INVOKED event; exposing the same to plugin hooks would cover it.

### Example prompts or workflows

 User types /my-plugin:my-skill (or /my-skill). A hook configured as "skillInvoked": [{ "type": "command", "command": "...", "matcher": "^my-plugin:" }] runs with { "skillName": "my-plugin:my-skill", "source": "slash_command"}; ordinary prompts run no hook.

### Additional context

Copilot CLI 1.0.105, Windows 11. Claude Code already offers this as UserPromptExpansion

issues.title: `/keep-alive` in WSL2 does not prevent the Windows host from sleeping

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When Copilot CLI runs inside WSL2, `/keep-alive` does not prevent the Windows host from sleeping. WSL is treated as Linux, so the CLI attempts to use `systemd-inhibit`; that does not create a Windows host power request visible through `powercfg -requests`.

This means long-running Copilot tasks can be suspended when the Windows host sleeps, even though keep-alive is enabled.

### Affected version

1.0.105

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Run Copilot CLI inside WSL2 on Windows.
2. Enable `/keep-alive on` or the busy-mode equivalent.
3. From Windows, run `powercfg -requests`.
4. Observe that Copilot CLI has not registered a Windows host power request.
5. Allow the Windows host's configured idle timeout to expire.
6. Observe that the host can sleep and suspend the WSL2/Copilot workload.

### Expected behavior

Enabling `/keep-alive` inside WSL2 should prevent the Windows host from sleeping, just as running Copilot CLI natively on Windows does.

The implementation could detect WSL2 and invoke an appropriate Windows-host mechanism, or clearly expose a supported integration that creates and releases the host power request for the lifetime of the Copilot task.

### Additional context

The original implementation uses `systemd-inhibit` on Linux and Windows power APIs only for native Windows processes:
https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/5669

A later fix explicitly handles WSL as an environment where the Linux inhibitor may fail, but does not forward sleep inhibition to the Windows host:
https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/13161

WSL2 is important for file-heavy Rust, Go, and similar development because working on its Linux filesystem can be substantially faster than working directly on NTFS. Requiring a separate Windows keep-awake utility makes `/keep-alive` ineffective for this common workflow.

Originating discussion:
https://github.slack.com/archives/C093WSH3L8J/p1793378606869279

issues.title: Autopilot: assistant says its answer is "above", but no text was output before task_complete

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In autopilot, the agent often ends a turn with `task_complete` whose summary refers to a deliverable "above" (e.g.
"The Discord post is above, ready to copy"). The user sees no such text, because none was output: the
`assistant.message` before the call has `content: ""`. The user has to ask again, and the agent then insists it
already wrote it.

From my local session logs (`~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl`, last 21 days, deduplicated by tool-call ID):

- 544 `task_complete` calls; 489 had no assistant text before the call (often fine, the summary is the answer).
- 31 summaries refer to something "above"; in 27 of them (12 sessions) no text was output in that turn. Some may
  point to an earlier turn, so 27 is an upper bound.

One verified example (session log, 2026-10-30T15:55:32Z): the summary says "The shorter, casual Discord post is
above". The message content is empty, and the post text appears nowhere in the log, not even in the stored
reasoning summary, which only says "I've drafted a short, casual forum post…". Non-reasoning output was 151 tokens
for 342 characters of tool-call arguments, so no separate draft was emitted as visible output.

This is not #5150 (ACP clients got the summary only as a tool call; fixed in 1.0.102). Here the TUI shows everything
it received; the referenced text was never output. A second model (GPT-6.1 Sol) checked the log independently and
confirmed the counts.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105, TUI (not ACP). Windows 11, PowerShell 7. Model claude-opus-5.5, autopilot mode on.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Intermittent; it happens most when the deliverable is text the user will copy (a draft, an explanation):

1. Turn on autopilot (`/autopilot` or Shift+Tab).
2. Ask: `Draft a short, casual forum post asking how others keep their CMS sites updated.`
3. Then ask: `Make it shorter and less formal.`
4. Check the final message: often only the `task_complete` summary appears, saying the post is "above", with no
   post shown.
5. Confirm in `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl`: the `assistant.message` with the `task_complete` tool
   request has `"content": ""`, and the post text is not in the file.

### Expected behavior

When the agent ends a turn with `task_complete`, every deliverable the user asked for is visible: either as message
text before the call or inside the summary. The summary never refers to text ("above") that was not output in this
or an earlier turn. Possible guardrails:

- the `task_complete` tool description could say "put the deliverable in the summary, or output it before calling";
- the CLI could flag a summary that refers to "above" when the turn has no visible text.

### Additional context

- Workaround: an instruction in `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` to put every deliverable inside the
  `task_complete` summary. That shouldn't be needed for every autopilot user.
- I searched github/copilot-cli issues ("autopilot task_complete summary", "message not shown", "task_complete
  hides") and found only #5150, which is a different problem.
- Root cause not proven: the token counts show the text wasn't emitted as visible output, but the stored reasoning
  is a summary (`reasoningSummary: "detailed"`), so I can't tell whether the model wrote it only in its reasoning.

issues.title: Agent writes invalid PowerShell on Windows (recurring patterns)

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When running on Windows, the Copilot CLI agent often writes PowerShell commands that fail to parse or run, so it has to retry. Each retry is an extra tool call plus a model turn. From 3 weeks of my session logs (2,164 unique shell calls), these patterns recur:

- Substring with IndexOf = -1, no bounds check (7 calls / 4 sessions)
- "$var: text" in a double-quoted string → ParserError; needs "${var}: text" (4/3)
- multi-line if/else joined into "}; elseif" → 'elseif' is not recognized (2/2)
- ConvertFrom-Json on package-lock.json without -AsHashtable, which fails on the empty "" key (2/2)
- bash-style \" escaping inside a single-quoted jq filter → jq parse error (1/1)

Expected: the agent writes valid PowerShell 7 for the powershell tool: no bash-isms, braces around a variable before ":", if/elseif blocks on separate lines, IndexOf results checked before Substring, and -AsHashtable for package-lock.json.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105. Windows 11, PowerShell 7.6.9, model claude-opus-5.5.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior


Each line below is a command of the kind the agent generated. Run each one in `pwsh -NoProfile`:

1. `$s="x"; "$s: y"` → ParserError: Variable reference is not valid
2. `if ($false) { 1 }; elseif ($true) { 2 }` → 'elseif' is not recognized
3. `'{"":1}' | ConvertFrom-Json` → "property whose name is an empty string … only supported using the -AsHashTable switch"
4. `"abc".Substring(0, [Math]::Min("abc".IndexOf("z"), 10))` → ArgumentOutOfRangeException (length -1)

### Expected behavior

On Windows, the agent writes valid PowerShell 7 for the powershell tool: no bash-style escaping ("), braces around a variable before a colon ("${var}:"), if/elseif/else kept on one block instead of joined with ";", IndexOf results checked before Substring, and ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable for files such as package-lock.json. The command should work on the first try, without a retry turn.

### Additional context

 - Counts come from my local session logs (~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl), 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-30. Calls were deduplicated by tool-call ID, because resumed sessions copy their history.
 - 11% of shell calls were flagged with a shell_error_category, but most of those were environment issues or real build failures. The patterns above are the ones caused by the generated command itself.
 - I searched the github/copilot-cli issues and found no existing report for these patterns.
 - Workaround: I added PowerShell rules to ~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md. That shouldn't be needed for every Windows user.

### Describe the bug

The built-in `web_search` tool fails intermittently (more than half of calls over the last ~9 days) with:

```
MCP server 'github-mcp-server': MCP request failed: Transport send error: Transport [...StreamableHttpClientWorker<...RawCapturingReqwestClient>...] error: unexpected server response: HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout: [HTML error page omitted]
```

Every failure happens at **~121s**. Successful calls take between 32s and 115s. This points to a fixed **120s gateway timeout** in front of the remote MCP endpoint (`https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/mcp/readonly`). The web search backend (Bing searches plus answer synthesis) often runs longer than that limit.

### Evidence (from local `~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl`, `tool.execution_start` → `tool.execution_complete`)

| Start (UTC)              | Duration (s) | Result |
|--------------------------|-------------:|--------|
| 2026-10-22T00:53:58Z     | 42.7  | OK  |
| 2026-10-22T00:58:11Z     | 42.4  | OK  |
| 2026-10-22T12:39:50Z     | 121.2 | 504 |
| 2026-10-22T12:42:42Z     | 121.0 | 504 |
| 2026-10-23T18:04:13Z     | 109.2 | OK  |
| 2026-10-26T17:13:55Z     | 87.1  | OK  |
| 2026-10-27T17:06:36Z     | 120.9 | 504 |
| 2026-10-28T19:36:13Z     | 120.9 | 504 |
| 2026-10-28T19:38:52Z     | 114.8 | OK  |
| 2026-10-28T19:38:52Z     | 120.8 | 504 |
| 2026-10-28T19:40:56Z     | 120.9 | 504 |
| 2026-10-28T19:49:43Z     | 121.1 | 504 |
| 2026-10-28T19:57:28Z     | 42.3  | OK  |
| 2026-10-28T19:59:53Z     | 32.1  | OK  |
| 2026-10-29T17:59:24Z     | 120.9 | 504 |
| 2026-10-30T13:58:26Z     | 121.0 | 504 |

That is 9 failures out of 16 calls, all at 120.8–121.2s.

### Client-side causes ruled out

- No HTTP(S) proxy configured (env vars and `scutil --proxy` are empty).
- No TLS interception: the endpoint certificate is `CN=*.business.githubcopilot.com`, issued by Sectigo.
- Traffic is routed directly via the local network, not through the corporate VPN.
- The endpoint responds normally from the GitHub edge (`x-github-edge-region: iad`, `x-github-backend: Kubernetes`).
- Copilot CLI is on the latest version (1.0.105). It has no configurable timeout for this tool.

### Expected behavior

`web_search` should complete reliably. Possible fixes:
- Raise the gateway/proxy timeout for the `web_search` tool on the remote MCP server above 120s.
- Bound the backend search/synthesis time so it finishes and returns a (possibly partial) answer before the gateway limit.
- Stream progress or keep-alives over the streamable HTTP transport so the gateway does not close idle long-running requests.

### Environment

- Copilot CLI 1.0.105, macOS (Apple Silicon), installed via Homebrew cask
- Plan: Copilot Business (`api.business.githubcopilot.com`)
- Remote MCP endpoint: `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/mcp/readonly`

issues.title: Support repository-level, version-controlled command permissions (allow / ask / deny)

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

While preparing a developer workshop, I wanted to commit a shared set of Copilot CLI command permissions alongside the repository's instructions, skills, and agents. Everyone cloning the repository should be able to review and adopt the same defaults, without individually configuring their home directory, repeatedly approving identical commands, or copying CLI flags.

The missing capability is **repository-level, version-controlled allow / ask / deny rules for commands**, not just saving one user's approvals for a project on their own machine.

Copilot CLI already supports `.github/copilot/settings.json`, but the [documented repository settings](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-config-dir-reference#repository-settings-githubcopilotsettingsjson) do not include command permission rules. Saved project permissions under `~/.copilot/permissions-config.json` are local to each user, rather than a portable configuration shared through the repository.

### Proposed solution

Support a committed repository permission configuration, ideally by extending `.github/copilot/settings.json`, with:

- **Allow:** preapprove specific commands or command patterns without repeated prompts.
- **Ask:** require explicit approval for matching commands, even when a broader allow rule matches.
- **Deny:** block matching commands, with deny taking precedence over ask and allow.

Reuse Copilot CLI's existing permission pattern syntax where practical, and document matching and precedence. Rules should be repository-scoped and portable across collaborators' machines.

Repository-provided approvals should require explicit user review and opt-in, not silently apply just because a repository was cloned. Changes that expand approvals should be surfaced for review. Repository rules must not weaken organization restrictions or explicit user deny rules.

Named or switchable permission profiles are not required for this use case: a committed, team-shared permission file would be sufficient.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. **Workshop setup:** the organizer commits approvals for the workshop's test and lint commands. Participants review and accept those rules instead of configuring identical permissions individually.
2. **Team onboarding:** new contributors clone the repository and can adopt the same reviewed command defaults as the rest of the team.
3. **Team standards:** setting up team standards for permissions corresponding to committed instruction files and skills would allow better collaboration.
4. **Mixed approval levels:** allow `npm run test` and `npm run lint`, ask before `git push`, and deny `git reset --hard`.
5. **Reviewable permission changes:** a pull request adds a new command approval alongside the script or workflow that needs it.

This avoids requiring broad `--allow-all` access simply to reduce repetitive approvals.

### Additional context

Claude Code supports repository-level `.claude/settings.json` files with `permissions.allow`, `permissions.ask`, and `permissions.deny`. I would like an equivalent native Copilot CLI capability.

Related issues:

- #3176 proposes a broader system of named, switchable permission profiles, including per-repository profiles. This request focuses specifically on committed, team-shared rules without requiring a profile system.
- #2398 requests a default permission configuration file, primarily at the user level.
- #5083 requests remembering approvals across sessions.
- #2338 reports that permissions in `.claude/settings.json` are not applied.

releases.body:
**Fixed**
- With --screen-reader, failed and rejected tool calls, errors such as an unknown command, and warnings now begin with "Error:" or "Warning:" instead of reading like any other message.
- /resume <session-id> foregrounds an already running background session instead of showing it twice on exit
- An HTTP MCP server that accepts connections but never answers now holds startup for its connection timeout once, instead of three times over
- Saving MCP server changes preserves symlinked mcp-config.json files and updates the symlink target.

**Fixed**

### Description

A Go subscription's usage meters report **lower** limits than the documented ones for `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, by a constant factor of 0.6.

`GET /console/api/go/status` (with `x-org-id`) returns:

```
fiveHour  limitMicroCents 1200000000   ($12)
week      limitMicroCents 3000000000   ($30)
month     limitMicroCents 6000000000   ($60)
```

The Console renders those as 0% / 30% / 15%, so the percentages are computed from the $60 base.

Docs (`opencode.ai/docs/go`) and the Console's own model table both say `deepseek-v4.1-flash` on Go has a monthly limit of **$100** — and the docs state `5-hour: 20% / weekly: 50% / monthly: 100%`, i.e. $20 / $50 / $100.

So the three reported limits are exactly **0.6×** the documented ones ($12/$20, $30/$50, $60/$100): same shape, different base.

Additionally, `opencode.ai/go` still shows "Previously $15; now $60" (4x Usage badge) for this model.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Subscribe to Go, then call `GET /console/api/go/status` with the `x-org-id` header.
2. Compare `access.meters.{fiveHour,week,month}.limitMicroCents` against the `deepseek-v4.1-flash` monthly limit on `opencode.ai/docs/go`.
3. Ratios come out at 0.6 for all three windows.

Account: org `org_01M4X9X4AZE94DACXTR7CZ5BFZ`, Go plan, period 2026-10-26T02:51:59Z → 2026-11-26T02:51:59Z.

### Expected

Either the meters report $20 / $50 / $100, or the docs and console table report $12 / $30 / $60. Right now a user planning against the documented $100 hits the wall at 60% of it.

Related context: PR #60532 noted that a docs change could ship while "the registry and the Console are back at the old limits", so docs/registry drift seems to be a known failure mode here.

### Operating System

Windows 11

### OpenCode version

Using the Go API from a custom agent (Hermes), not the OpenCode CLI, so billing was checked via the Console UI and the endpoint above.

issues.title: tui: plan/build mode state desyncs between UI and agent, causing unauthorized or refused work
issues.body:
# opencode: Plan/Build mode state desyncs between UI and agent

## Summary

The system-reminder blocks injected into the conversation toggle between "You are in Plan
mode" and "You are NO LONGER in Plan mode" at points that do not match the user's actual
mode selection in the UI. This causes the agent to refuse modifications when the user
believes they are in Build mode, or to execute modifications when the user believes they
are in Plan mode. The confusion is recurring across sessions.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.5
- OS: Linux 7.0.0-42-generic (Ubuntu, x64)
- Terminal: Guake (TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor)
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: latest (release)
- Active plugins: None found in config
- Default agent: `"default_agent": "plan"` (set in ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json)

## Reproduction

1. Start a session. The default agent is `plan`, so the session begins in Plan mode.
2. Switch to Build mode in the UI (or via agent switch).
3. Continue working. At various points, system-reminder blocks are injected stating
   "You are in Plan mode" even though the user selected Build mode.
4. Conversely, after the user switches back to Plan mode, reminders may say
   "You are NO LONGER in Plan mode."
5. The agent follows the reminder, not the user's stated mode, leading to either
   refused work or unauthorized modifications.

## Expected Behavior

The agent's mode should always match the user's current selection in the UI. Mode
transitions should be unambiguous and not fire spuriously mid-conversation.

## Actual Behavior

- System-reminder blocks toggle between Plan and Build mode independently of user
  actions, sometimes mid-conversation and sometimes after a single user message.
- The agent cannot verify the true mode state beyond these blocks.
- In this session alone, the mode flipped at least 6 times, including:
  - Plan mode active while user said "we're in build mode here, please continue"
  - Plan mode active immediately after a user message asking to commit changes
  - Build-mode actions (file writes, git commits, docker restarts) executed while
    the reminder said Plan mode, because the user explicitly requested them

## Additional Context

- The config has `"default_agent": "plan"`, which means every new session starts in
  Plan mode. This default may contribute to confusion — a new user or a user who
  expects Build mode on startup will immediately be in Plan mode without realizing it.
- **Session database investigation (privacy-safe):** Each session in
  `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` has an `agent` column (values: `plan`,
  `build`, `explore`). The mode is stored per-session, not per-message. When the
  user "switches agents" in the UI, it likely creates a new session or updates the
  `agent` field. The system-reminder blocks reference the mode of the *current*
  session, but the reminder text can lag behind the user's actual selection,
  especially when multiple sessions are open or the user switches mid-conversation.
- **Database evidence (this session, `ses_e6cefdd06ffe7nncEAts4aJCIa`):** The session's
  `agent` field in `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` is `"plan"` and never changes.
  However, the synthetic system-reminder messages within the session toggle between
  "You are in Plan mode" and "You are NO LONGER in Plan mode" **13 times** in a
  single session. The timestamps of these toggles do not correlate with any user
  agent-switch action — they appear to fire on their own schedule.
- **Observed in this session:** The mode reminder toggled at least 13 times during
  a single long session, including:
  - "You are in Plan mode" appearing immediately after the user said "we're in
    build mode here, please continue" and asked me to commit changes.
  - "You are NO LONGER in Plan mode" appearing after the user asked to clean up
    lahhost (which was already done in a prior turn).
  - "You are in Plan mode" appearing after the user said "let's get it done!"
    requesting implementation of the ZFS backup.
  - "You are NO LONGER in Plan mode" appearing after the commit succeeded.
  - "You are in Plan mode" appearing after the user asked to "note and document"
    the session work.
  - "You are in Plan mode" appearing after the user said "yes, install gh."
  - The agent executing file writes, docker restarts, git commits, and apt installs
    while the reminder said Plan mode, because the user explicitly requested them.
  - The agent refusing a commit while the reminder said Plan mode, even though
    the user said "we're in build mode."
- The `report` skill's runtime diagnostics snapshot (captured at skill registration)
  shows the same mode-state ambiguity.
- Suggested improvements:
  1. Make the default agent configurable or default to Build (with Plan as opt-in).
  2. Ensure system-reminder mode blocks only fire on actual mode transitions, not
     spuriously.
  3. Provide a visible, persistent mode indicator in the TUI/status bar that both
     the user and agent can reference.
  4. When the user explicitly states their mode ("we're in build mode"), the agent
     should trust the user's statement over a stale reminder.
  5. Consider storing mode per-message rather than per-session, so mid-session
     switches are tracked accurately.
- The user has consented to include this context. No secrets or project-specific
  confidential data are included.
EOF

issues.title: project: session list returns empty in a directory that became a git repo after first open
issues.body:
### Description

`opencode session list` returns nothing for a directory that opencode first opened *before* it became a git repo, even though sessions exist.

The project registry ends up with two entries for the same directory:

- `9ed4d1ef…` — registered pre-git (no `vcs`), and still the identity that CLI invocations resolve and mark active
- `efe4468c…` — registered on the next session after `git init` + first commit (`vcs: git`, id equals `git rev-parse HEAD`)

All sessions are stored under the newer VCS identity, but `session list` resolves the stale pre-git entry and finds zero sessions. Resuming by explicit ID (`opencode -s <id>`) and `GET /api/session?directory=<dir>` both work, which points at project resolution rather than storage.

A session started *after* `git init` also reported `Is directory a git repo: no` in its harness environment snapshot, so the stale identity appears to win in more places than just `session list`.

Expected: the CLI should resolve the same project identity the sessions are stored under — prefer the VCS entry once the directory has a repo, or deduplicate identities that share a canonical directory.

Workarounds: `opencode api get "/api/session?directory=$(pwd)"`, or resume explicitly with `opencode -s <sessionID>`.

### Plugins

None — user config only contains `{"$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json"}`.

### OpenCode version

v2.2.2 (channel: latest)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open opencode in a plain, non-git directory and create a session. This registers project A (id = directory hash, no VCS).
2. `git init && git commit` in that directory.
3. Open opencode again and create a session. This registers project B (`vcs: git`, id = HEAD commit hash); sessions are now stored under B.
4. Run `opencode session list` in the directory → empty (`--format json` → `[]`).
5. `opencode api get "/api/session?directory=$(pwd)"` → the sessions exist, all with `projectID` = B.

Consistently reproducible. Control: in a directory that was a git repo before first being opened, `session list` shows all 44 sessions.

Observed data (Linux; timestamps are epoch ms):

issues.title: web: unrecognised post-login redirect URL crashes createSessionRetention with "can't access property "type", e is undefined
issues.body:
### Description

The web app is unbootable when the SPA mounts while the address bar holds a URL outside the router's list. The crash fires in the session-retention effect and kills the app.

`packages/app/src/shell/state/layout.tsx` `currentRoute()` **throws** `Unrecognised route!` for any path that isn't `/`, `/settings`, `/connect`, `/components`, `/new-session`, `/server/:key/session/:id`. Solid catches the throw, leaves the `useCurrentRoute()` memo value `undefined`, and defers the rethrow. `createSessionRetention` (`packages/app/src/runtime/server/runtime.tsx:232`) then evaluates its `current` callback, which reads the memo **unguarded**:

```tsx
current: () => {
  const route = currentRoute()
  return route.type === "session" && route.server === connKey ? route.sessionId : undefined
},
```

→ `TypeError: can't access property "type", e is undefined`.

This is auth-agnostic: any gateway that completes login by returning the browser to a URL under the app origin (forward-auth / OAuth2 proxies: oauth2-proxy, Authelia, Cloudflare Access, authentik, corporate SSO outposts) mounts the SPA on a path outside the router's list, and the app dies on every login. Pairing authenticates the user *to* the server; it doesn't replace a network-level auth gate in front of the web app, which is why many self-hosters put an SSO proxy in front — and that flow currently makes the web UI unbootable.

Suggested fix: return a fallback (e.g. `{ type: "home" }`) from `currentRoute()` instead of throwing, and/or guard with `route?.type` in `createSessionRetention` and other unguarded readers.

### Plugins

None.

### OpenCode version

2.2.5 (verified: deployed chunk hashes match the v2.2.5 release binary; the bug is also present on `dev` at `packages/app/src/shell/state/layout.tsx:91`)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Serve `opencode serve` behind any auth proxy that completes login via a redirect to a URL under the app origin (e.g. oauth2-proxy's `/oauth2/callback`, Authelia's, authentik's `/outpost.goauthentik.io/callback`) with the SPA served for that path.
2. Complete login; the SPA boots while the address bar shows the callback URL.
3. Console shows the TypeError and the app never renders.

### Screenshot and/or share link

```
TypeError: can't access property "type", e is undefined
    current https://app.example.com/_assets/current-CS21lgrW.js:6:46336
    L/<@https://app.example.com/_assets/solid-eTxPEHmU.js:1:41974
    Me/q/Y/Ie/Ne/X@https://app.example.com/_assets/solid-Csl37FmM.js (reactive update frames)
    S@https://app.example.com/_assets/web-C8KihOh2.js:1:7296
    @https://app.example.com/_assets/index-BDq5uAY5.js:35:14189
```

Decoded from the shipped bundle, `current-CS21lgrW.js:6:46336` is exactly the `createSessionRetention` `current` callback quoted above.

### Operating System

Server: Linux x64; client: Firefox (reproducible on any browser).

### Terminal

Not applicable (web app).

### Additional context

Even absent any proxy, the throwing parser plus unguarded memo read is one deep link away from bricking the app — the parser should degrade to a fallback route and `createSessionRetention` should guard, regardless of deployment auth.

issues.title: desktop: SSH remote reports "running OpenCode 1" for a patch-version mismatch
issues.body:
## Summary

The desktop app's SSH remote connection refuses to connect when the remote service runs a different patch version of OpenCode 2, and reports it as "running OpenCode 1". The displayed `1` is a fallback value, not the real server version.

## Environment

- opencode version: Desktop 2.2.5; remote service 2.2.0
- OS: macOS (desktop), Linux (remote)
- Terminal: Not applicable (desktop app)
- Shell: zsh (remote)
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: None

## Reproduction

1. On a remote Linux host, run an OpenCode 2.2.0 background service (`service.json` reports `"version":"2.2.0"`).
2. In OpenCode Desktop 2.2.5, add an SSH remote connection to that host and try to connect.
3. The connection is marked incompatible and shows: `This server is running OpenCode 1, which isn't compatible with this app. Upgrade it to OpenCode V2 to continue.`
4. Click "Update and reconnect": the desktop installs its matching CLI version, restarts the remote service, and connects successfully.

## Expected Behavior

The message should report the actual version mismatch (2.2.0 vs 2.2.5), or offer the update action directly. A patch-level mismatch should not be presented as an OpenCode 1 server that must be upgraded to V2.

## Actual Behavior

The connection is presented as an incompatible OpenCode 1 server. Both sides are OpenCode V2; only the patch version differs. The message hides the real cause and the recovery action.

## Additional Context

- The SSH bootstrap compares the remote service registration version with the desktop app's bundled CLI version using strict equality. On mismatch it fails with a `version` error and marks the connection incompatible.
- The row message uses `server.row.incompatible` with `version: health?.version ?? "1"`. For an SSH target that never reaches the connected state, `health.version` is unavailable, so the UI displays the hardcoded fallback `1`.
- Frequency: consistent.
- Workaround: "Update and reconnect" resolves it.

issues.title: Free tier issues: read this first, then post your report here

labels.name: zen
labels.description: Relates to Zen

issues.body:
This is the **main issue for free tier problems**. If you see any of these, you're in the right place:

- `Free usage exceeded, subscribe to Go`
- `Free usage limit reached`
- `You've used today's free messages. They reset at ...` and the reset never happens
- `This version of OpenCode Desktop no longer supports free models`
- `OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode`
- `OpenCode 1.18.0 or newer is required to use the free tier`

**Please comment here instead of opening a new issue.** We're closing duplicates and pointing them here so everything is in one place.

## 1. Make sure you're on the latest OpenCode v2

Most free tier reports come from **OpenCode v1** (versions `0.x` and `1.x`, for example Desktop or CLI `1.19.5`). v1 no longer supports free models and only gets fixes for critical bugs. Updating to v2 has fixed this for many people.

Check your version:

- **Terminal:** `opencode --version`
- **Desktop:** Settings → About

The latest v2 release is **2.2.1**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The v1 Desktop app's built-in updater keeps you on `1.x`. Download v2 manually from **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**.

### Desktop

Download v2 Desktop for macOS, Windows or Linux from **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**, or on macOS:

```sh
brew install --cask opencode-desktop
```

### Terminal (TUI / CLI)

All install options are listed at **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**. The quickest on macOS and Linux:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash
```

Or use a package manager:

```sh
npm install -g @opencode/cli
bun install -g --trust @opencode/cli
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2
paru -S opencode-beta
```

v1 and v2 both use the `opencode` command. If you installed v1 with a package manager, remove it first, for example `npm uninstall -g opencode-ai`. Windows package managers (Chocolatey, Scoop) don't support v2. On Windows, use the Desktop app, npm, or a [standalone binary](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/).

### Useful docs

- [Install OpenCode v2](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/)
- [Migrate from v1](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1/)
- [Free models, limits and privacy](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/models/#free-models)
- [OpenCode Go](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go/)
- [Troubleshooting](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting/)

## 2. Other things to check

- **Free models only work inside OpenCode.** Other clients, proxies and direct API calls can't use them. Use a paid model or [Go](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go/) there instead.
- **Subscribed to Go but still seeing free limits?** Run `/connect`, sign in with **OpenCode Console** in your browser (make sure you authorize the workspace with your Go subscription, or choose **OpenCode Go** if you use a Go API key), then pick a Go model (`opencode-go/...`) with `/models` rather than a free model (`opencode/...-free`).
- **Hit the real daily limit?** Wait for the reset time shown, subscribe to [Go](https://opencode.ai/go), or connect another provider with `/connect`.

## 3. Still broken on the latest v2? Comment with:

- OpenCode version, and whether you use Desktop, TUI, CLI or web
- Operating system
- The free model you used
- The exact error message (a screenshot is fine)
- When it started and the reset time you were shown
- Whether you have Go or Console credits

> [!WARNING]
> Don't post email addresses, payment details or other account information here. This issue is public.

## 4. Still don't know what's going on?

If you're on the latest v2 and none of the above helps, or the problem is about your account, billing or Go subscription, email **help@anoma.ly** with the details from step 3. Billing and account issues can't be fixed in GitHub issues.
