### What does this PR do?

Supersedes #48730, which was closed by the automated PR cleanup while waiting for review. Complements #59399: that PR keeps a location alive while a terminal socket is attached; this one keeps it alive while a terminal is still running after its client detached (panel closed, tab switched away, app restarted, connection dropped), which is the case in #48691. The two checks compose, and this branch is rebased onto #59399 now that it has landed.

Since #57416 the inactivity sweep keeps a location alive while a running session or a background job owns it. A running terminal counts as neither: terminals produce no session events, so a location whose only activity is an open terminal is still evicted on schedule and the Pty finalizer kills every terminal in it. That is the blank pane and "PTY session not found" in #48691, which the triage bot reproduced on v2.2.0 and current `dev`.

Before evicting an expired location, the sweep now also asks that location's Pty service for running terminals and refreshes the timer while any exist, the same way it already treats active sessions and background jobs. The probe uses `contextEffectOption`, so it only reads the cached graph and never boots a location; a graph that failed to build counts as having no terminals, so failed locations are cleaned up as before.

- New case in `packages/core/test/location-activity.test.ts`: a location whose graph is the real `Pty` node, with a running `cat` terminal, stays cached when its deadline passes, and is evicted by the next sweep after the terminal is removed. The case fails without the fix.

prs.title: feat(core): trace each request and session turn on its own, with session, tool and model details
prs.body:
**OpenCode's traces can now answer "what happened in this session?": every HTTP request and every session turn gets its own trace, and spans name the session, the tool and the model.**
Before this, almost every span from a running server ended up inside one giant startup trace, and nothing said which session, tool or model it belonged to. Nothing users see changes; only exported telemetry does.

❌ **Before**
1. Route handlers and background fibers captured the server's startup span when the server booted.
2. ❌ Every request, tool call and model call for the life of the process nested under that one trace (millions of spans in one trace after a day).
3. ❌ No span carried a session id, tool spans carried no attributes, and model-call spans carried only the URL.
4. Per-event and file-path plumbing spans made up about a sixth of all spans.

✅ **After**
1. The server builds its routes without the startup span, so each request's handler spans nest under that request.
2. Each session turn (`SessionRunner.drain`) starts its own trace, and every span inside it carries `session.id`.
3. Tool spans carry the tool name, call id and session; failures already mark the span as an error.
4. Model-call spans carry provider, model, finish reason, input, output and cache-read tokens, time to first output, and the error type on failure (OpenTelemetry `gen_ai.*` names).
5. Three high-volume plumbing spans are no longer traced: per-LLM-event publishing, path resolving and the credential list.

```diff
- server boot span ─┬─ every request ─ handler spans
-                   └─ every session turn ─ tools, model calls (no ids, no attributes)
+ request span ─ handler spans                          (one trace per request)
+ session turn {session.id} ─ tool {name, call id}     (one trace per turn)
+                           └─ model call {provider, model, tokens, first output ms}
```

📊 **Numbers**: one day of a single desktop server's exported spans, before this change

| Measure | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Spans inside the two largest traces | 97% of 6.5M | one trace per request or turn (tests) |
| Spans with a session id | 0 | every span in a turn (tests) |
| Tool spans with any attribute | 504 of 70,193 | all |
| Spans removed as plumbing | – | ~16% of recent volume (39k of 250k in 30 min) |

The two new tests fail without the change: `request-tracing.test.ts` (a request's handler span shared the startup trace) and `session-runner-recorded.test.ts` (the turn had a parent, and 51 spans in it had no session id). 413 targeted tests pass.

👀 **Read:** `process.ts` and `fetch.ts`, where routes are built without the parent span. The cause is that the HTTP API builder captures the whole build-time context, including the current span, and provides it to every handler; dropping the span there fixes every handler at once. Side effect: the layer-building spans at boot are now separate roots instead of children of `ServerProcess.start`. A session turn is a new root, so it isn't linked to the request that queued it; `session.id` joins them. The rest is routine.

<sub>Found by reading a day of the desktop app's exported traces · no user reports · "after" verified by tests, not yet on a live day</sub>

<details><summary>Checks run</summary>

- `bun check --no-script -b -p tsconfig.tests.json` in `packages/core`: no type errors
- `bun check --no-script -b` in `packages/server`, `bun check --no-script` in `packages/util`: no type errors
- `bun test` in `packages/core`: credential, session-execution, session-run-coordinator, session-runner (message, recorded, retry, tool-events, main), session-step, tool-execute, tool-write, location-filesystem: 406 pass
- `bun test` in `packages/server`: process, request-tracing, session-create: 7 pass

</details>

### Problem

Warming pings every model on the same fixed interval (4 minutes by default), whatever its prompt cache lifetime. That's too often for long caches and wasted on models that don't cache at all.

### Change

`warming.interval` accepts `"auto"`: ping at 90% of the model's `cache.ttl`, and skip models without one.

```jsonc
"warming": { "interval": "auto", "duration": "2 hours" },
"providers": { "anthropic": { "settings": { "cache": { "ttl": "1h" } } } }
```

```text
interval "auto" + cache.ttl "5m"  → ping every 4.5 minutes
interval "auto" + no cache.ttl    → not warmed
interval unset / a duration       → unchanged
```

Additive: existing configs behave the same. Only `cache.ttl` you set yourself counts for now; per-model defaults can come from models.dev later. The warming docs explain `"auto"` and that `duration` must exceed the interval for long TTLs.

prs.title: feat(ai): accept Standard Schema for tool input and schema
prs.body:
### Problem

Tool `input` and structured-output `schema` only took an Effect Schema or a raw JSON Schema, so Zod, Valibot or ArkType users had to convert by hand and lost typed arguments.

### Change

Both now also take a [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev), in both clients, with no new runtime dependency (the spec interfaces are copied into `src/standard-schema.ts`, as the spec recommends).

```
tool({ input: schema })            // or ai.generate({ schema })
  Effect Schema    -> decode, JSON Schema from Effect          (unchanged)
  "~standard" in   -> validate: schema["~standard"].validate(args)
                      execute args: StandardSchemaV1.InferOutput<schema>
                      model JSON Schema: schema["~standard"].jsonSchema.input({ target: "draft-2020-12" }), minus $schema
                      no jsonSchema export -> throws at tool() with how to fix
  otherwise        -> raw JSON Schema, args unknown            (unchanged)
```

The JSON Schema comes from [Standard JSON Schema](https://standardschema.dev/json-schema), the companion spec Zod 4.2+ and ArkType implement on every schema, and Valibot implements through `toStandardJsonSchema` from `@valibot/to-json-schema` (which keeps validation). A schema without it fails with a clear error instead of taking a separate `jsonSchema` field: the major libraries already export one, and a second field could drift from what is validated.

### Out of scope

- A `success` schema for Standard Schema tools; results pass through as with raw JSON Schema tools (with an optional `outputSchema`).

prs.title: refactor(ai): rename tool parameters to input
prs.body:
### Problem

A tool's arguments had two names. You passed `parameters` for an Effect Schema or `jsonSchema` for a raw JSON Schema. Everywhere else the package calls them `input`: `tool-call` events, `ToolDefinition.inputSchema`, and structured output's `schema`, which already takes either kind.

### Change

`tool({...})` takes `input` in both clients. There is no alias for the old names.

```diff
 tool({
   name: "weather",
-  parameters: Schema.Struct({ city: Schema.String }),   // or: jsonSchema: mcpTool.inputSchema
+  input: Schema.Struct({ city: Schema.String }),        // or: input: mcpTool.inputSchema
   success: Schema.Struct({ forecast: Schema.String }),
   execute: ({ city }) => ...,
 })
```

- `input` takes an Effect Schema, which decodes the arguments and types them, or a plain JSON Schema object, whose arguments arrive as `unknown`. At runtime the tool tells them apart with `Schema.isSchema`, the same check `schema` uses for structured output.
- The result schema still depends on the kind of input. An Effect `input` pairs with `success`, which validates and encodes the result. A JSON `input` pairs with `outputSchema`, which is only advertised to the model. Mixing them is a type error.
- Renamed to match the new option:
  - `Tool.parameters` is now `Tool.input`. For a JSON tool it now holds the JSON Schema you passed, not `Schema.Unknown`.
  - `toModelOutput` now receives `{ id, input, output }` instead of `{ id, parameters, output }`.
  - The generic type parameter is now `Input`.
- New exported types: `ToolInput` (an Effect Schema or a JSON Schema) and `ToolInputType<Input>` (the value `execute` receives).
- Structured output in `llm.ts` builds its hidden tool with `input: schema` and no longer branches on the schema kind.
- Updated the README, tutorial and tests. New type tests cover JSON `input` typed as `unknown`, rejection of the old `parameters` and `jsonSchema` keys, and rejection of mixed `success`/`outputSchema`.

### Out of scope

Provider wire fields named `parameters` or `jsonSchema` (Chat Completions `function.parameters`, Bedrock `jsonSchema`) are unchanged. Core does not call `tool()`.

prs.title: fix(core): coordinate MCP token refreshes with the credential lock
prs.body:
MCP OAuth refreshes ran outside the per-credential lock other integrations use. The in-memory map that shared a refresh request let go before the new tokens were saved, so with rotating refresh tokens a second connection could replay the old one, get `invalid_grant`, and delete the saved credential, signing everyone out. The per-URL connect queue hid this at connect time in one process, but not for mid-session 401s or across processes.

Now the provider's fetch handles refresh requests under `Credential.lock`, the same way `Integration.connection.resolve` does since https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/54023:

```
send(token request with refresh R):
  lock(credential):                  # in-process share + file lock
    row = re-read credential
    if row.access != token this connection's 401 rejected: return row   # someone already refreshed
    response = POST token endpoint   # 30s timeout
    if not ok: fail with response    # the SDK reads the rejection as usual
    save new tokens; return new row
  answer the SDK from the row
```

All SDK refresh paths send their token request through the transport fetch, so this covers connect, live requests, the SSE stream, reconnects and the refresh branch of step-up. The provider's own `saveTokens` and `saveClientInformation` no longer write the row, so a late save can't undo a newer rotation.

Rejected refreshes no longer delete the sign-in. `invalidateCredentials` just stops that connection from offering its refresh token, so the SDK's one retry ends in `needs_auth`. A live connection whose refresh is rejected also goes to `needs_auth` (that used to happen only because the delete reconnected every Location).

Not handled on purpose:
- A dead credential costs one refresh request per connect attempt, per connection.
- After `invalid_client`, signing in again reuses the saved client, and signing in adds a new credential instead of replacing the dead one.
- The per-URL `endpointLoads` queue stays; removing it is a follow-up. With it removed locally, the 10-Location experiment still sends one refresh with no sign-outs.

Every `ai` call already takes plain input, so the separate `request` builders are gone from the public `ai` surface. `ai.compact` and `ai.canCompact` now take the same plain input as `generate` and build the request themselves.

**Before**

```ts
const request = ai.request({ model, prompt: "hello" })
yield* ai.compact(request)
```

**After**

```ts
yield* ai.compact({ model, prompt: "hello" })
```

A built `LLMRequest` is still accepted everywhere. Code that needs one directly, such as `LLMClient`, `compileRequest` or `LLMRequest.update`, now builds it with `LLMRequest.from(input)`.

**Removed** (in both `@opencode/ai` and `@opencode/ai/effect`)

- `ai.request`
- `ai.image.request`
- `ai.decision.request`
- `ai.experimental.speech.request`, `ai.experimental.transcription.request`, `ai.experimental.video.request`. These are also gone from the `Speech`, `Transcription` and `Video` namespaces exported by `@opencode/ai/experimental`.

**Added**

- `LLMRequest.from(input)`, which normalizes plain input into an `LLMRequest` (what `ai.request` used to do).

Callers in core, the tests, the README and the tutorial are updated. The Promise/Effect parity check passes.

issues.title: durable: MCP extension for Harness hosts

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

A durable MCP extension, next to `@earendil-works/pi-durable/codemode` and `/tool-search`: it connects MCP servers and registers their tools as `ToolRegistration`s, so a Harness can offer MCP tools the way the coding agent does.

- Tools as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`, deferred or `callers: ["tools"]` by exposure, with a codemode namespace per server carrying its instructions.
- Replay policy from annotations: `readOnlyHint` or `idempotentHint` tools are `replay: "safe"`, everything else unsafe.
- Connections owned by the extension, opened on first use, with reconnects and `McpOAuthStateStore` for credentials.
- The resource tools (`list_mcp_resources`, `read_mcp_resource`, ...).
- `mcp.json` loading shared with the coding agent, so hosts honor the same files and project trust.

### Why?

Agents in [pi-agents](https://github.com/mavam/pi-agents) run on pi-durable and can't use MCP servers. pi-durable already has the pieces: nested calls, `callers`, deferred tools, `tool_search`, and codemode namespaces, and its README mentions an "MCP bridge". But the bridge itself lives only in the coding agent's `AgentSession` extension. Each durable host would otherwise rebuild config loading, exposure, OAuth, and the tool mapping, and Pi's own durable session will need the same.

### How? (optional)

Port the coding agent's MCP extension the way codemode and tool search were ported, as `@earendil-works/pi-durable/mcp` or a durable entry point in `pi-mcp`, e.g., `createMcpExtension({ servers, exposure?, auth? })`. The Harness core stays MCP-agnostic, as with codemode.

Short of that, exporting `loadMcpConfig` (or moving it to `pi-mcp`) would let hosts build the bridge on the same `mcp.json` files and project trust.

Sharing a client with the host's own connections would let pi-agents avoid a second `stdio` process per server, but isn't required.

issues.title: pi-durable: expose non-persisting native prompt preparation for candidate model admission

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Request

Expose a public, non-persisting pi-durable prompt-preparation API backed by the implementation used by generation. Hosts need to estimate a candidate model request without submitting input, changing the persisted model, triggering compaction or copying the private prompt planner.

Inspected published `@earendil-works/pi-durable` 1.4.0 and current root exports (`packages/durable/src/index.ts` Git blob `9d35a93785197f0026d6bc36e05f0119614e5c98`). `Conversation.context()` exposes committed context and `agent()` exposes the resolved agent. `renderSections` and `planSystemEntries` remain private. `beforeRequest` observes an actual generation and is unsuitable for a non-persisting capacity query; application hooks can also write.

## Reproduced downstream failure

https://github.com/rcarmo/piclaw/issues/1843 tracks a host that adds all current instructions, sections and schemas to the SDK estimate. Offline native generations show why that is incorrect:

- An unchanged section produces no new system entry, but the host charges its rendered payload again.
- `Agent.sections` already includes `instructions`; charging the field separately doubles it.
- Applicable provider usage already includes the unchanged selected tool catalogue.
- After a compaction head with no later baseline, equal-looking retained sections still require native baseline rebuilding and omission of old system contributions. A simple equality check cannot replace native planning.

The reproduction uses disposable MemoryStorage and recorded synthetic model requests. Three duplication tests fail; the compaction boundary control passes. No live-provider requests or history rewrites are involved.

## Required semantics

- Return the prospective provider-facing model messages after native section/tool planning, context edits and post-head baseline handling, or a native context estimate derived from those same messages.
- Use the same implementation and ordering semantics as generation; avoid a separate preview planner.
- Resolve candidate model/thinking overrides without persisting them or mutating a prepared request.
- Do not append entries, admit submissions, run generation, invoke providers or compact.
- Make renderer, environment and hook boundaries explicit. Do not invoke arbitrary write-capable `beforeRequest` hooks under a read-only promise. A pure planner that accepts already rendered sections is also useful if its projection includes native context-edit semantics.
- Expose a frontier/revision or sufficient provenance so callers can reject changed history, agent configuration, registry/default extensions and cancellation before committing selection.
- Specify failure behaviour and whether returned estimates include output/reserve policy. Keep byte-size limits separate from token estimates.

## Regression cases

Unchanged/changed/removed/re-added/reordered sections; instructions as sections; unchanged and same-name-replaced selected schemas; measured prefix plus unmeasured suffix; reset/compaction invalidation; pending post-head baseline; model-dependent rendering; abort and concurrent configuration/registry/history changes. Preview must preserve exact durable history and accepted input and must not create provider or accounting effects.

Downstream work: https://github.com/rcarmo/piclaw/issues/1857. This request does not propose a silent SDK upgrade or a private-import workaround.

issues.title: Models.refresh returns empty errors when a newer refresh supersedes it

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Problem

`Models.refresh()` can return `errors.size === 0` while every provider's catalog is failing, if another refresh of the same provider overlaps it.

In `packages/ai/src/models.ts`, each per-provider operation calls `beginProviderRefresh`, which bumps the provider generation and aborts the previous operation's controller. The catch block only records an error when `!signal.aborted`, so an aborted (superseded) operation reports nothing. Its caller gets an empty success even though the newer refresh fails for the same reason.

## Concrete trace

1. `models-store.json` is corrupt (`{"catalog":`).
2. Caller C runs `refreshModelCatalogs()` (the model selector's shared refresh) and reaches `Models.refresh()`.
3. An unjoined `ModelRuntime.refresh()` (the `void this.refresh(...)` calls after register/unregister/credential changes) reaches `Models.refresh()` after C started. It bumps the generation and aborts C's operations.
4. C's operations are dropped, C returns `{ aborted: false, errors: <empty> }`, and the selector shows no error. The newer refresh fails with the parse error, but nobody receives it.

Observed in a Nix CI sandbox (offline test `tests/test-pi-sol61-native.mjs`: `assert.ok(refresh.errors.size > 0)` false, once in about 12 hours; passes on retry). Reproduces on 1.1.0 and 1.4.0 with the forced order below.

## Forced-order reproduction (no timing dependence)

```ts
const models = createModels();
let release: () => void;
const gate = new Promise<void>((r) => { release = r; });
models.setProvider(testProvider({ id: "dynamic", refreshModels: async () => { await gate; throw new Error("corrupt catalog"); } }));
const joined = models.refresh({ allowNetwork: false });      // C
const superseding = models.refresh({ allowNetwork: false }); // X supersedes C
release();
const [c, x] = await Promise.all([joined, superseding]);
// x.errors.get("dynamic") is set; c.errors is empty (expected: also "corrupt catalog")
```

## Proposed fix

A superseded caller joins the latest refresh of that provider and returns its outcome. Supersession without a successor (`setProvider`, `deleteProvider`, `clearProviders`) and the caller's own abort keep reporting nothing. A patch with three regression tests is on a fork branch and can be sent as a PR if wanted.

This issue is AI-generated by w28:p2Y

issues.title: 0.99.x: terminal color query replies leak into the prompt and BEL opens the external editor (mintty on Windows, ConPTY)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: inprogress
labels.description: Issue is being worked on

issues.body:
### What happened?

On startup pi opens the external editor. The prompt contains `;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000;1;rgb:d4d4/2c2c/3a3a;…`.
The query runs regardless of theme.

**Versions:** 0.99.x are affected. 0.87.1 is fine. Windows Terminal is fine.
**Terminal:** mintty on Windows, native node.exe, `TERM=xterm`, `EDITOR=vim` (I am using GitBash for Windows environment)

## Cause

0.87.1 sent a single `ESC]11;?BEL` query. 0.99.x sends OSC 10, OSC 11, OSC 4 for indices 0–15, and DA1 (`ESC[c`) as the end marker (`TERMINAL_COLOR_QUERY` in `packages/tui/src/tui.ts`). In this terminal:

1. The DA1 reply arrives first, before any color reply. `consumeTerminalColorResponse` then drops the pending query, so later replies are no longer consumed.
2. The OSC replies arrive without their `ESC]4` prefix, in fragments (`;0`, `;rgb:0000/0000/0000`, `BEL`, `;1`, …). The reply regex cannot match them anyway.
3. `StdinBuffer` splits non-escape input into single characters, so they land in the editor as text. Each stray BEL is Ctrl+G and opens the external editor.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run pi under GitBash (Windows).
2. The prompt contains `;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000;1;rgb:d4d4/2c2c/3a3a;…`.
3. External editor opens, containing the prompt.

### Expected behavior

Prompt is empty and external editor is not opened at the startup. Worked in 0.87.1.

### Version

0.99.0, 0.99.1, 0.99.2,
1.0.0 (tui-mode regular; see my comment below)

issues.title: Windows (pwsh/ConPTY): loader line suddenly paints at the top of the screen (autowrap drift in main-screen renderer)
issues.body:
## What happened?

In regular (main-screen) mode on Windows, the loader/spinner line at the bottom of the screen occasionally jumps to the very top of the screen and stays misaligned. It happens occasionally in pwsh (Windows Terminal / ConPTY), not on xterm-style terminals.

## Root cause

This is the same root cause as #8484 (closed without review), with a different visible symptom.

`TuiMainScreen` paints with relative cursor moves (`CSI n A/B`) and tracks the cursor row itself (`hardwareCursorRow`). ConPTY commits line wraps **eagerly** instead of holding xterm's deferred "pending wrap" state. Whenever a painted line's visible width exactly equals the terminal width (editor borders, separators, long tool output), the real cursor ends up one row below the tracked position. The drift accumulates across frames until the renderer's move-up to the loader row clamps at the top of the screen, and the loader gets painted there.

It is occasional because drift only accrues when full-width lines are painted since the last full redraw.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run pi in regular mode in pwsh / Windows Terminal.
2. Let the agent produce output containing lines that exactly fill the terminal width (borders, separators, long unbroken output).
3. Observe the bottom loader line occasionally jump to the top of the screen.

Not reproducible on Linux terminals (deferred wrap), which is why it looks intermittent and Windows-only.

## Related issues

- #8484 — same root cause, reported as "editor scrolls to top / cursor lost below fold"
- #8485 — proposed the same fix, closed by the contribution gate before review
- #6561 / #6562 — earlier instance of the same class ("TUI double rendering on lines matching terminal width"), also fixed by disabling auto-wrap

## Proposed fix

Paint every main-screen render path (full redraw, deleted-line cleanup, incremental diff) with autowrap disabled (`CSI ?7l` / `CSI ?7h`), matching the guard `TuiAltScreen` already uses. Renders already truncate lines to the terminal width (there is a crash guard for over-wide lines), so nothing legitimately wraps and cursor tracking stays exact on every terminal.

I have a fix ready on my fork with regression tests covering all three render paths:

https://github.com/c3qu/pi/tree/fix/main-screen-conpty-autowrap-drift

Full `packages/tui` node:test suite passes (967/970; the 3 `imageFallback` failures are pre-existing on main). Happy to open a PR if this approach is acceptable.

issues.title: Package resolution during startup/reload installs and refreshes packages with no host-level opt-out

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### Summary

`DefaultPackageManager` (wired through `DefaultResourceLoader`) performs package mutation as a side effect of plain resource resolution during session startup and `reload()`. An embedding host cannot separate "resolve configured resources" from "install or refresh packages", so a reload triggered by an unprivileged client can run `npm`/`git` installs — including package lifecycle scripts — against the shared installation.

### Observed behavior (current `main`, checked 2026-11-01)

In `packages/coding-agent/src/core/package-manager.ts`:

1. `installMissing()` (~line 1388) calls `this.installParsedSource(...)` for missing npm/git sources during ordinary resolution. This runs `npm install` (or a git clone with prepare scripts).
2. Unpinned temporary npm sources are refreshed to `@latest` on load (~line 1404-1415) even when a cached install exists.
3. Unpinned temporary git sources are refreshed on every load (~line 1447).

None of these paths is gated by a host-facing option. `DefaultResourceLoaderOptions` exposes no flag to deny package mutation, and the existing `onMissing` callback on `PackageManager` is not reachable through the resource loader's option surface. Offline mode is a global switch that also disables unrelated network behavior, so it is not a per-host authorization seam.

### Why this matters for embeddings

A host that serves the SDK over a control socket (reload requested by a web client, for example) inherits whatever the reload path does. Our host contract requires that ordinary startup/reload performs zero package installs; missing or mismatched sources should return a stable "management action required" state, and install/refresh should only run behind an explicit, separately authorized management action.

### Suggested change

Add an option such as `allowPackageMutation?: boolean` (defaulting to `true` to preserve current behavior) on `PackageManagerOptions` and `DefaultResourceLoaderOptions`:

- when `false`, `installMissing` throws a stable error (we use `PI_RESOURCE_PACKAGE_MANAGEMENT_REQUIRED`) instead of installing;
- when `false`, temporary npm/git refresh paths are skipped, while already-installed resources continue to reload normally.

We carry this as a small local patch on 1.3.0 (option pass-through in `package-manager` and `resource-loader`, plus the guard in `installMissing` and the refresh conditions); happy to turn it into a PR if the maintainers want the seam.

issues.title: pi update: git clean -fdx fails on Windows against npm staging dirs (use -ffdx)
issues.body:
### Environment

- pi 1.4.0 · Windows 11 · git 2.52.0.windows.1 · msys2/Git Bash
- git-type extension installed under `~/.pi/agent/git/`
- Reproduced on both update paths: `pi update --extensions` and `pi update --all`

### What happens

```
Updating https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>...
Error: git clean -fdx failed with code 1
```

pi's update runner resets each git-type extension checkout with `git clean -fdx` before re-fetching/re-installing. On Windows that call exits 1 whenever the working tree contains npm's *staging* directories, which look like:

```
node_modules/@ast-grep/.cli-win32-x64-msvc-<hash>/ast-grep.exe
node_modules/@ast-grep/.napi-win32-x64-msvc-<hash>/ast-grep-napi.win32-x64-msvc.node
```

These are the left-over extraction dirs npm uses when installing platform-specific optional packages. `git clean -f` reports `Invalid argument` against them and bails with exit 1; `git clean -ffd` (double force) removes them without complaint, which is why the same repo is trivially fixable by hand but not via `pi update`.

### Repro steps

1. Install an extension whose `prepare`/`postinstall` pulls `@ast-grep/cli` (e.g. `pi install git:https://github.com/apmantza/pi-lens`) on Windows.
2. Run `pi update --extensions` (or `--all`) more than once. Each cycle re-installs `@ast-grep/cli`, so a `.<name>-<hash>` staging dir is produced.
3. The clean step hits that dir and fails; the whole update aborts even though the fetch and the rest of the install would have worked.

### Suggested fix

A single flag in pi's update runner — `git clean -ffdx` (or `-ffd`) instead of `-fdx` — makes the reset robust against these artifacts. It is also what `git-clean` itself recommends on Windows where the file may be momentarily locked/rename-blocked.

issues.title: Terminal query response fragments leak into editor input box on Windows/WezTerm ("79" / OSC color values appear on startup & session resume)

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows + WezTerm, pi 1.1.0 intermittently injects **terminal query response fragments as user keystrokes into the editor input box** on startup (new session) and on session resume:

- New session → `79` appears in the input box (DA1 response: `79` is WezTerm's truecolor capability parameter)
- Session resume → `e2e 8080` appears (OSC 11 background color response: the user's grayscale theme reports `rgb:e2e2/e2e2/e2e2`)

Fragments appear instantly (not typed char-by-char by a human), with no clipboard involvement, no extensions involved.

## Root cause chain (source-verified against pi-tui 1.1.0 dist)

1. pi 1.1 sends terminal capability queries on startup **and** on session resume: DA1 (`\x1b[c`, `terminal.js` `DEVICE_ATTRIBUTES_QUERY`) plus ~18 OSC 10/11/4 color queries (theme auto-detection, `theme-controller.js`), with a DA1 sentinel.

2. WezTerm replies:
   - DA1: `\x1b[?64;1;2;3;6;9;15;18;21;22;79c`
   - OSC 11: `\x1b]11;rgb:e2e2/e2e2/e2e2\x07`

3. On Windows, the pty splits these responses into multiple `data` events (observed inter-frame gaps of 60–220ms; resume is heavier → longer gaps).

4. **Leak path A (DA1 → "79")**: first fragment (`\x1b[?64;...;22;`, still a valid CSI-? prefix) enters `keyboardProtocolNegotiationBuffer`. After `KEYBOARD_PROTOCOL_RESPONSE_FRAGMENT_TIMEOUT_MS = 150` ms, `flushKeyboardProtocolNegotiationBufferAsInput()` **forwards the half response as user input** (by design: never drop a possibly-real keypress). The late second fragment (`79c`) does not start with ESC → `StdinBuffer` emits it **char-by-char as ordinary keypresses** → `editor.js` `insertCharacter` inserts printable chars → `79` in the input box.

5. **Leak path B (OSC → "e2e 8080")**: half OSC response (`\x1b]11;rgb:e2e2/`) has no terminator yet; after `stdin-buffer.js` `timeoutMs` (50ms sequence timeout) it is flushed as one "sequence" and forwarded as input; the late remainder (`e2e2/e2e2\x07`) is emitted char-by-char → `e2e2/e2e2` (reported as "e2e 8080") in the input box.

3-level timeouts (50ms sequence / 150ms negotiation / 10ms ESC) all **flush-and-forward instead of drop** — the right tradeoff for slow real keystrokes, but wrong for fragments of **expected terminal responses**, which can never be legitimate user input (`\x1b[?…` / `\x1b]…` prefixes are not producible by a user typing; user paste goes through bracketed-paste mode and bypasses these paths).

There is a comment trail in `editor.js` (~line 1052) fixing a similar leak for one kitty sequence (`[106;5u`), suggesting this class of leak has been patched case-by-case but paths A/B remain.

## Repro (deterministic, uses real pi-tui StdinBuffer)

Feed `\x1b[?64;1;2;3;6;9;15;18;21;22;` then (after >150ms) `79c` through a real `StdinBuffer` + replayed negotiation state machine → `7`, `9`, `c` are emitted as ordinary input. Same with `\x1b]11;rgb:e2e2/` + `e2e2/e2e2\x07` at >50ms gap. Scripts available on request.

## Suggested fix (upstream)

When a query is outstanding, enter an "expecting-response" state. On timeout, **drop the partial response and re-send the query** (responses are re-queryable; user keypresses must not be dropped — but a fragment starting with `\x1b[?`/`\x1b]` in the expecting-response window is never a user keypress). Re-arm until a complete response or a retry cap.

## Local mitigation we applied (works, verified)

- `terminal.js`: `KEYBOARD_PROTOCOL_RESPONSE_FRAGMENT_TIMEOUT_MS` 150 → 600ms (covers observed pty inter-frame gaps; both fragments reassemble into a complete DA1 response → consumed, zero editor leak)
- `stdin-buffer.js` `flush()`: if buffer starts with `\x1b]` (OSC) or `\x1bP` (DCS), extend the wait up to 1000ms total for the terminator instead of flushing at 50ms; drop only after the extended window (color probe failure is harmless).

Verified with deterministic repro: both scenarios now reassemble into complete sequences consumed by the terminal layer; no characters reach the editor.

Environment: Windows 10 x64, WezTerm, pi 1.1.0 (@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent + bundled pi-tui 1.1.0).

issues.title: Delayed OSC 10/11/4 color-query replies leak into input over Windows SSH/ConPTY; trailing BEL is treated as Ctrl+G

labels.name: last-read
labels.description: A marker label for triaging

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### Summary

Over Windows OpenSSH, a delayed terminal color-query reply is treated as user input. Its trailing BEL (`0x07`) is dispatched as `Ctrl+G`, which opens the external editor; with the Windows default `notepad` the SSH session dies. Even after remapping the editor key, a fragment of the color reply is typed into the editor on the first keypress.

### Environment

- pi `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` **1.1.0** (npm global install, native Windows process)
- Windows 10 22H2 (build 19045.6466), Windows OpenSSH 9.5p1 (`sshd` service)
- `HKLM\SOFTWARE\OpenSSH\DefaultShell = C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe` (Git Bash)
- Clients: **Yakuake (Konsole)** and **Ghostty** on Arch Linux, via `ssh`

### Steps to reproduce

1. SSH from Yakuake/Ghostty into the Windows host.
2. Run `pi` (or `pi -c`) in an interactive session.
3. Do not type anything.

### Observed

- pi immediately prints `Launching external editor: notepad` and the SSH connection closes.
- After setting `externalEditor` to `vim` and remapping `app.editor.external`, on the **first keypress** a fragment of a terminal color reply is inserted into the editor:
  - Yakuake: `b:6868/6868/6868`
  - Ghostty: `;8;rgb:5555/5555/5555`

These fragments match the tails of BEL-terminated OSC color replies:
`\x1b]11;rgb:6868/6868/6868\x07` (default background) and `\x1b]4;8;rgb:5555/5555/5555\x07` (palette 8).

### Analysis

`pi-tui` sends the terminal color query at startup (`pi-tui/dist/tui.js`):

```js
const TERMINAL_COLOR_QUERY = `\x1b]10;?\x07\x1b]11;?\x07${...Array of `\x1b]4;N;?\x07`...}\x1b[c`;
```

All color replies are BEL-terminated. The trailing `\x1b[c` (DA1) request is a sentinel that marks the end of the replies. The terminals answer DA1 first, so when the actual color replies arrive, the query has already been removed from the queue and `consumeTerminalColorResponse()` returns `false`, forwarding the reply to the focused component (the message editor):

```js
consumeTerminalColorResponse(data) {
    const query = this.pendingTerminalColorQueries[0];
    if (!query) return false;          // <-- color reply is forwarded to input
    if (DEVICE_ATTRIBUTES_RESPONSE_PATTERN.test(data)) { ... shift() ... }
    const response = parseOscColorResponse(data);
    if (!response) return false;
    ...
}
```

On top of that, over Windows SSH/ConPTY the reply is delivered in pieces. `StdinBuffer` flushes an incomplete sequence after `timeoutMs` (default **50 ms**, hard-coded and not affected by `PI_TUI_ESC_TIMEOUT`, which only applies to a lone `ESC`):

```js
const timeoutMs = this.buffer === ESC ? this.escapeTimeoutMs : this.timeoutMs;
```

So a partial `ESC ] ... ` is emitted as one input event (typed into the editor as text), and the remaining BEL arrives as a separate event and is dispatched as `Ctrl+G`.

### Suggested fix

- In `consumeTerminalColorResponse()`, also consume recognized OSC 10 / 11 / 4 replies when `pendingTerminalColorQueries` is empty, instead of forwarding them to input.
- Never dispatch a stray BEL / OSC-color-reply fragment as a key press.
- Consider making the `StdinBuffer` partial-sequence timeout configurable (or clamping it upward), so split color replies can reassemble. `PI_TUI_ESC_TIMEOUT` currently does not cover this case.

### Local workarounds used

- `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` → `"externalEditor": "vim"`
- `~/.pi/agent/keybindings.json` → `{ "app.editor.external": "ctrl+alt+e" }`
- Hot-patched bundle `dist/bundle/chunks/chunk-OTL6MGLJ.js`:

```diff
- pendingTerminalColorQueries[0]; if(!query) return !1;
+ pendingTerminalColorQueries[0]; if(!query) return parseOscColorResponse(data)!==void 0;
```

```diff
- new StdinBuffer({escapeTimeout:resolveEscapeTimeoutMs()})
+ new StdinBuffer({escapeTimeout:resolveEscapeTimeoutMs(),timeout:250})
```

### Notes

- I could not reproduce this with a plain user-level `sshd` on the same machine (no real terminal answering the queries); it requires the real OpenSSH service plus a terminal that answers the color/DA1 queries over the ConPTY path.
- The color query has no configuration switch, so the workaround above patches the bundle locally (overwritten by `pi update`).

issues.title: read/write views don't syntax-highlight .dart files (extension→language map misses dart, nix, groovy)

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### Summary

`getLanguageFromPath()` in `src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts` maps file extensions to highlight.js language ids. Its `extToLang` table has no `dart` entry, so `read` output and `write` previews for `.dart` files render as plain single-color text — even though the Dart grammar is registered *and* eager-loaded. The same table also omits `nix` and `groovy`, which are in the eager list too.

### Repro

Against the installed `1.4.0`:

```bash
cd "$(npm root -g)/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent"
node --input-type=module -e '
import { getLanguageFromPath } from "./dist/modes/interactive/theme/theme.js";
import { supportsLanguage } from "./dist/utils/syntax-highlight.js";
console.log(getLanguageFromPath("lib/main.dart")); // undefined
console.log(getLanguageFromPath("lib/x.kt"));      // kotlin
console.log(supportsLanguage("dart"));             // true
'
```

In the TUI: `read` a `.dart` file, or `write` a new one — the body is uncolored, while `.kt` / `.swift` / `.go` / `.py` highlight normally.

### Root cause

- `src/utils/syntax-highlight.ts` → `eagerLanguages` contains `dart`, `nix`, `groovy`. `test/syntax-highlight.test.ts` even asserts these are the "twenty most common languages".
- `src/modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts` → `getLanguageFromPath()`'s `extToLang` (~line 958) has ~37 entries (ts, js, py, rb, rs, go, java, kt, swift, c, cpp, cs, php, sh, sql, html, css, json, yaml, xml, md, lua, perl, r, scala, clj, ex, erl, hs, ml, vim, graphql, proto, tf, hcl, …) but **not** `dart` (nor `nix`, `groovy`).
- Call sites: `src/core/tools/renderers/read.ts:124` and `src/core/tools/renderers/write.ts:45` fall back to `theme.fg("toolOutput", …)` / plain lines when the lookup returns `undefined`.

Dart *does* highlight in fenced code blocks tagged `dart`, because the markdown path passes the language through directly and never consults the extension table. That asymmetry is likely why this went unnoticed.

### Also affected: HTML export

`src/core/export-html/template.js` keeps a second, shorter copy of the same map (missing `dart`, `kt`, `swift`), and the bundled `src/core/export-html/vendor/highlight.min.js` ships 37 grammars — `kotlin`, `swift`, `objectivec` included, **`dart` not**.

### Suggested fix

1. Add `dart: "dart"` (and `nix: "nix"`, `groovy: "groovy"`) to `extToLang` in `theme.ts`.
2. Add a test tying the two tables together (e.g. every eager language is reachable by at least one extension), so they can't drift again.
3. For export: add `dart` to the export map and to the vendored grammar bundle.

### Versions

Verified on `1.4.0` (npm latest, 2026-10-21) and `main @ bb36171` (2026-10-31). The table has had no `dart` entry since it was introduced on 2025-12-18 — I checked ~40 revisions of `theme.ts` between 2025-12-18 and 2026-10-08 and none contain `dart`.

Not part of this report: `edit`/`write` *diff* bodies intentionally don't syntax-highlight content (see #4064, closed as not planned).

### What happened?

With `openai` authenticated through **Sign in with ChatGPT**, Pi 1.3.0 reports a 272K context window for `gpt-6.1-sol`, although the same account's live model catalog reports a 500K default. This gives Pi a smaller context/compaction budget than the server advertises.

```json
{"slug":"gpt-6.1-sol","context_window":500000,"max_context_window":872000}
```

This is an account-specific catalog check, not an inference test above 272K. [OpenAI's documentation](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/models-and-inference) directs this sign-in flow to use `/v1/models` for the account's current catalog.

Related: #10840 and commit 5712b134e corrected `openai-codex` to 500K, but left `openai` at 272K. The static short-context pricing cap also applies when `openai` uses subscription OAuth, not an API key.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in to `openai` through Sign in with ChatGPT.
2. Run `pi -ne --no-mcp --list-models gpt-6.1-sol`:

```text
provider  model        context  max-out  thinking  images
openai    gpt-6.1-sol  272K     128K     yes       yes
```

3. With the same OAuth access token, query `GET https://api.openai.com/v1/models` and inspect the entry whose `slug` is `gpt-6.1-sol`. The tested account returns `context_window: 500000`.

### Expected behavior

For ChatGPT subscription authentication, use the account's advertised default context window (500K here), rather than inheriting the API-key pricing cap. This report does not request a blanket change to API-key defaults or use of the separate 872K maximum.

### Version

issues.title: github-copilot: on 401 or 403 before expires, refresh the session token once and retry

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
**Package**: packages/ai, `auth/oauth/github-copilot` and `auth/resolve`
**Version seen**: @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 0.99.1, @earendil-works/pi-ai 0.99.1

## What happens

Pi's `github-copilot` provider keeps the Copilot session token in `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` as `access`, with `expires` set to the token's `expires_at` less five minutes. `resolveStoredOAuth` mints a new token from `refresh` only when `expires` is less than five minutes away. It never mints on an API refusal.

When GitHub revokes a session token before its `expires_at`, every model call answers:

```
github-copilot API error (403): 403 forbidden
```

The failure lasts until the stored `expires`, up to about 24 hours, or until someone edits `auth.json`. The stored `refresh` (the GitHub OAuth token) stays valid for the whole period.

## Reproduction (observed 2026-09-30)

- 30 Pi sessions ran on one GitHub Copilot Enterprise seat, each with its own `auth.json`.
- Between 10:45Z and 11:00Z GitHub revoked every session token minted before that time. 27 sessions held such a token. Each answered 403 `forbidden` on both `GET /models` and `POST /chat/completions` at `api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com`.
- A new mint from `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` with the same `refresh` answered 200, and that token answered 200 on both endpoints.
- The old and new tokens' claims differed only in `iat`, `exp`, `ip` and `sl` (`sl=0` on the revoked tokens, `sl=1` on the new ones). `sku` and the feature flags were the same.
- Workaround: set `github-copilot.expires` to 0 in `auth.json`. Pi read the file again and minted a new token at its next call, and every session worked.

## Request

When a request to the Copilot API answers 401 or 403 and the stored `expires` is still in the future:

1. Refresh the session token once from `refresh`, under the same credential-store lock `resolveStoredOAuth` uses, so that concurrent requests and processes mint once.
2. Retry the failed request once with the new token.
3. If the refresh fails, or the retry answers 401 or 403 again, report the error as now.

One refresh and one retry per request keep a real authorization failure (a removed seat, a policy block) visible and bounded.

## Impact

Every Pi session on a Copilot seat stops on each model call after a server-side revocation and cannot recover without a manual edit to `auth.json`. With the retry, the first failed call recovers the session.

issues.title: A failed OAuth refresh fails the request while the stored token is still valid

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

`resolveStoredOAuth` (packages/ai/src/auth/resolve.ts) refreshes an OAuth token once it has less than five minutes left. If that refresh fails (network blip, 5xx from the token endpoint), the error is thrown and the request fails, even though the stored access token is still valid for up to five more minutes.

The code already says the five-minute window "does not impose a provider contract", but a failed refresh inside that window is treated as fatal.

### Steps to reproduce

Script run with `node repro.ts` from a checkout of main (Node 24 strip-types), importing `packages/ai/src` directly:

```ts
import { resolveProviderAuth } from "./packages/ai/src/auth/resolve.ts";

let stored: any = { type: "oauth", access: "still-valid", refresh: "r", expires: Date.now() + 4 * 60_000 };
const credentials: any = {
  read: async () => stored,
  list: async () => [{ providerId: "p", type: "oauth" }],
  modify: async (_id: string, fn: any) => ((stored = (await fn(stored)) ?? stored), stored),
  delete: async () => {},
};
const oauth: any = {
  name: "test",
  refresh: async () => { throw new Error("fetch failed"); },
  toAuth: async (c: any) => ({ apiKey: c.access }),
};
await resolveProviderAuth({ id: "p", auth: { oauth } }, credentials,
  { env: async () => undefined, fileExists: async () => false })
  .then((r) => console.log("resolved", r), (e) => console.log("rejected:", e.message));
```

Output: `rejected: OAuth refresh failed for p: fetch failed`, with the stored token valid for another 240 s.

### Expected behavior

When the refresh fails and the token in the store (re-read after the failure, in case another process refreshed it) is still valid for a safe margin (e.g. 60 s), use it and let the next request retry the refresh. Throw only when no usable token remains, or when the caller passed `minOAuthValidityMs` and the stored token does not meet it.

I can send a small PR with a test if this direction is acceptable.

### Version

1.4.0 (main at 9b7a44c48)

---

AI disclosure: I found and reproduced this with an AI coding agent; I reviewed the code path and the text myself.

issues.title: [Windows] [sink-thread] How do you use Pi on windows? What issues are you seeing?
issues.body:
## Motivation

There are gazzilion developers on windows. Some use pi. Many could use pi. There are however too many ways pi can be run on windows and as such it is hard to know where to focus energy (fixing bugs, having best docs, having out of box) vs what ways can be delegated out of core to extensions. 

## Ways to run pi on WIndows:

- Pi runs on windows, uses git bash (default)
- Pi runs on windows, uses wsl bash (?semi-automatic fallback)
- Pi runs fully on windows with pwsh.exe/powershell.exe bash replacement (only plugins?)
- Pi runs fully in wsl2

## Issues seen:

All of these have some papercuts. Windows/wsl bash suffers from https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7064, Windows/*  suffers from https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7427, Windows/git-bash suffers from git bash being iffy and e.g. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/6817 (among some closed). Full wsl2 has least amount of problems but might not be feasible due to compliance + still pi uses wrong keybidnings for copy/paste images with WT/allactitty. Running fully natively on windows/powershell isn't easy even with plugins as bash tool cannot be easily replaced (just shadowed; ie same name) and not all shell invocations can be hooked (RPC, ...).

## Call to action:
As such, I'd like to ask: how do you use pi on windows? Why this particular way and not any of other of the abovementioned ones? If you use some plugins, why and which ones? What's missing? What's challenging? What UX gaps are you seeing? 

Feel free to also link your other more specific issues.

issues.body:
### Environment

- `@earendil-works/pi-durable` **1.4.0** (npm)
- Node 22.x, Alpine Linux container (production deployment)
- Host app: LLM agent harness over durable conversations — long-running sessions with tool calls (multi-minute generations)

### Summary

After a process restart (deployment), any conversation whose lifecycle crossed the restart boundary stops consuming new submissions. New inputs are persisted with status `placed` (or `unanswered` if their run was aborted by the restart) but **never executed** — the conversation dead-locks permanently. The only recovery we found is creating a new conversation. Reproduced in production (3 conversations) and locally.

### Reproduction

1. Create a conversation; submit an input that starts a long generation (multi-minute)
2. While the generation is in-flight, `kill -9` the process (simulating a deployment restart)
3. Restart the process; reopen the Harness over the same storage
4. Submit a new input to the **same conversation** via `ConversationHandle.submit()`

- **Expected**: the new submission is consumed and a run starts
- **Actual**: it stays `placed` forever; subsequent submissions dead-lock too. Conversations created **after** the restart work fine — only lifecycle-crossing conversations are affected

### Observations (SQLite storage)

- `tasks` table: all rows `terminal` (no stuck run to await)
- `submissions` table: the post-restart input stuck at `placed`; the interrupted input settled `unanswered`
- `Harness.inspect()` shows queued/placed submissions are visible to scheduler state but never consumed

### Analysis clue

`Harness.waitForIdle()` internally calls `tasks.resume()`. In our startup recovery path we call `inspect()` + `waitForIdle()` after restart — **this successfully drives the stuck `placed` submission and the interrupted task completes** (verified locally: an interrupted 900-row analysis task auto-completed after restart + resume). Suspect: after restart the scheduler is left un-resumed, so `placed` submissions are never consumed.

### Impact

Every process restart (routine deployment) permanently dead-locks conversations users are actively using. In our production LLM-agent use, each deployment interrupts user sessions permanently. We shipped an app-level startup recovery (inspect + waitForIdle) as a workaround, but placed-submission recovery after restart feels like a framework-level gap in the scheduler semantics.

### Questions

1. Is auto-resuming `placed` submissions after restart the intended behavior, or should hosts explicitly drive recovery?
2. If explicit recovery is intended: is there a **supported API** for it beyond relying on the `waitForIdle()` → `resume()` side effect? We'd prefer the documented path over our current workaround.

issues.title: bash tool reports "Command timed out after N seconds" for a command that already exited with a real exit code
issues.body:
**What happened?**

When a bash command has already exited with a real exit code, but a descendant keeps the inherited stdout/stderr pipe busy, the tool reports:

```
Command timed out after N seconds
```

The command did not time out. Example measured here: the shell exited with code 1 after ~1.06s, the tool returned at 12.75s with `timeout: 3`, and the model was told `Command timed out after 3 seconds`. The real exit code 1 never reached the model, so it treats a finished-and-failed command as a slow one.

Root cause: `dist/core/tools/bash.js:107` only tests the `timedOut` flag:

```js
if (timedOut) throw new Error(`timeout:${timeout}`);
```

`waitForChildProcess` had already resolved with the real exit code (the child exited long before the deadline), and `killProcessTree` at the deadline is a no-op on a pid that no longer exists (`taskkill` exits 128), so nothing about that call is actually a timeout.

Related: #6787 asked for the timeout deadline to be enforced when descendants keep stdio active (auto-closed by the new-contributor gate). This report is narrower — I am not asking to change the wait, only to stop reporting a false `timed out` when the child already exited. That is a one-condition fix and it also preserves the wait behavior added for #5303.

**Steps to reproduce**

Windows 11, Git Bash, `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.4.0:

```bash
bash(command: "bash -c 'while true; do echo tick; sleep 0.05; done' & sleep 1; echo boom >&2; exit 1", timeout: 3)
```

Result: returns after 12.75s (varies: 5.1s, 12.0s, 22.7s in repeated runs) with output ending `Command timed out after 3 seconds`.

Control cases on the same machine:

| command | timeout | shell exited | tool returned |
|---|---|---|---|
| above (chatty descendant) | 3s | 1059ms, code 1 | 22744ms → `timed out` |
| same but descendant stdio redirected | 3s | 1050ms, code 1 | 1050ms → `Command exited with code 1` |
| `sleep 1; echo boom; sleep 300` | 3s | 3310ms (killed) | 3310ms → `timed out` (correct) |

**Expected behavior**

If the shell had already exited before the deadline, report its real exit code (the same `Command exited with code N` path), not `timed out`. Keep `timed out` for commands whose process was still alive at the deadline.

Suggested condition: record the exit timestamp, and in the `timedOut` branch throw only when the child had not exited before `start + timeoutMs`; otherwise return `{ exitCode }`.

**Version**

pi-coding-agent 1.4.0 (also present on `main`), Windows 11 + Git for Windows bash. Reached through pi-web-ui 0.113.1, which passes `timeout` through unchanged — reproduced directly against the SDK, no extension loaded.

---
_Filed by the reporter's coding agent; the measurements above were produced and re-run locally, not generated._

## What

Session-JSONL write-syscall coalescing (source-level slice, zero compiler events).

- **SessionManager**: initial file creation + rewrites carry every buffered entry in ONE write (was one write per entry). Appends stay synchronously durable (the session-manager suite pins same-tick reload visibility).
- **JsonlSessionStorage**: new `AppendBatcher` seam — write() coalescing with marker-ACK crash ordering (a caller's promise resolves only after the write() carrying its bytes reached the OS; SIGKILL never loses a committed mutation/turn), append-failure state convergence to the durable log, post-write fork staging.

## Before/after write-syscalls + bytes (real PTY runs, scripted 2-turn session, inotify write accounting)

| metric | BEFORE | AFTER | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| write() syscalls | 10 | **5** | **−50 %** |
| creation burst | 6 | **1** | −83 % |
| steady-state appends | 2 | 2 | 0 (sync-durability contract) |
| transcript bytes / entries | 2 775 / 10 | 2 774 / 10 | identical |

SIGKILL at idle after a committed turn: committed turn on disk (user+assistant present, file parses, reopen works). Clean exit appends 2 shutdown-bookkeeping lines a killed process never emits; committed content identical.

New pins: `jsonl-append-batcher.test.ts` (7: kill-9 ACK contract, coalescing, failure, drain, byte-identity), `session-write-batcher.test.ts` (4: sync durability, marker durability, byte-identity, creation integrity). prs.title: fix(tui): keep late and header-less color replies out of the prompt
prs.body:
Fixes #10256. Also covers the duplicates #10362, #10742, #10717, #10970, and the replies-after-DA1 part of #10250 / #10679.

## Problem

pi queries OSC 10/11 and OSC 4 (0-15) at startup and uses the trailing DA1 reply as the end marker. On Windows, ConPTY breaks that:

1. ConPTY answers DA1 itself, immediately, so the query completes before any color reply arrives.
2. The color replies come back with their `ESC ] Ps` header stripped, or only as a tail.

Captured bytes after DA1:

| Report | Bytes | Result on main |
|---|---|---|
| mintty (#10256, #10362) | `;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000` BEL `;1;...` BEL | text in prompt, each BEL is Ctrl+G and opens the external editor |
| WezTerm 20240203 (#10717, #10970) | `a8` ST, or `ESC[6;21;10t` `55` ST in one read | `a8` / `55` in prompt |
| Windows SSH (#10742) | `;8;rgb:5555/5555/5555` BEL | text plus external editor |
| tmux 3.6 (#10250) | complete replies after DA1 | replies forwarded as input |

## Fix

In `TuiBase`, keep checking input for color replies during a window that lasts 1 s after the query starts, completes, or times out, and is extended by every consumed reply.

- Complete OSC 10/11/4 replies in the window are consumed even after DA1.
- Single characters from the reply payload alphabet (hex, `;`, `:`, `/`, `#`, `r`, `g`, `]`) are held. A following BEL or ST marks them as a header-less fragment and both are dropped. Any other input, or 300 ms without a terminator, delivers the held characters in order, so typing is delayed but never lost.
- A BEL or ST with nothing held is a real Ctrl+G / Alt+\ and is delivered.

The terminator is the discriminator because the header is gone: no keyboard sends ST, and BEL directly after a run of hex characters is not typical typing. `StdinBuffer` and key timing outside the window are unchanged. The window is bounded, so a terminal that never answers DA1 does not hold input indefinitely.

Trade-off, only inside the window: typed hex characters can be delayed up to 300 ms, and hex characters typed immediately before Ctrl+G within 300 ms are dropped with it.

## Not covered

- #10657 (split DA1 through the keyboard negotiation buffer) and #11172 (split mouse reports): different code paths.
- tmux 3.6 tails with no terminator: indistinguishable from typing; upstream tmux bug fixed in 3.7.
- Late replies are consumed but not delivered to `onLateReply`.

## Tests

`packages/tui/test/terminal-colors.test.ts` replays the captured mintty, WezTerm, and tmux bytes through `StdinBuffer` and checks ordered delivery of typed text. The new tests fail on main and pass with the fix. Not verified on a real mintty/WezTerm terminal.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): keep updating git packages when git clean fails
prs.body:
Closes #11597

## Problem

On Windows, `pi update` stopped with `git clean -fdx failed with code 1` for git extensions such as pi-lens.

1. Another pi session has the extension loaded, so a native module (`@ast-grep/napi` `.node`) or `ast-grep.exe` is open in that process.
2. npm renames the in-use package dir to `node_modules/@ast-grep/.napi-win32-x64-msvc-<hash>`. Windows allows the rename, but npm cannot delete the dir afterwards.
3. The next `pi update` runs `git reset --hard`, then `git clean -fdx`. git prints `warning: failed to remove ...: Invalid argument` and exits 1.
4. pi threw, leaving the checkout at the new commit with the old dependencies.

The suggested `-ffdx` does not help. Reproduced locally (git 2.52, Windows): with a running `.exe`, or a `.node` loaded by another node process and its dir renamed, both `-fdx` and `-ffdx` fail with `Invalid argument`. Once the process exits, `-fdx` succeeds.

## Fix

In `cleanAndInstallGitDependencies`, a failed `git clean` no longer aborts the update. pi:

- prints a warning that files may be in use by another pi session
- still runs `npm install`, so dependencies match the new commit
- keeps the `.pi-update-incomplete` marker, so the next update retries the clean

## Tests

- `test/git-update.test.ts`: new regression test. A failing clean still updates and installs dependencies, warns, and keeps the marker. The next update cleans and removes the marker.
- `test/package-manager.test.ts`: updated the test that expected the throw.

`npm run check` reports `install-lock is out of date`, and `package-manager.test.ts > should expand ~ in exclusion and exact patterns` fails on Windows. Both also happen on `main` without this change.

prs.body:
Adds a troubleshooting section to the tmux guide (`packages/coding-agent/docs/tmux.md`, published at https://pi.dev/docs/latest/tmux) for the color-code text that tmux 3.6 types into the editor at startup.

tmux 3.6 forwards Pi's palette queries to the outer terminal. When a reply reaches tmux split across reads, tmux treats its bytes as key presses and sends them to Pi as typed text. tmux 3.7 fixes this ([tmux#4749](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/issues/4749), [tmux#4793](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/issues/4793)). Pi cannot filter the text because it arrives exactly like typing.

The section also notes that switching to a fixed theme does not help: `applyFromSettings()` queries terminal colors regardless of the theme, which reporters confirmed in #10679 (`--use-theme dark`) and #10256 (`"theme": "dark"`).

Related: #10250, #10679, #10256.

  - Built-in: crash when switching fullscreen -> regular or using `Ctrl+G` from fullscreen (#9186, microsoft/terminal#17515).
  - Built-in behind another terminal (mintty, OpenSSH): query replies leak into the prompt, BEL opens the external editor (#10256, #10362, #10742).
  - Old bundled (WezTerm 20240203): reply fragments in the prompt (#10717, #10970).
  - Built-in, classic console: reported regular-mode redraw issue (#6300).
- Notes that the fixes exist upstream and reach the built-in conhost with a future Windows update, timing unknown.

Sources: VS Code defaults `terminal.integrated.windowsUseConptyDll` to `true` (bundled conpty v1.25). Alacritty loads `conpty.dll` only if present (`alacritty_terminal/src/tty/windows/conpty.rs`) and its installer ships only `alacritty.exe`.

The crash was verified locally in the classic console window on conhost 10.0.26100.9807: fullscreen -> regular crashed 3/3 runs and `Ctrl+G` from fullscreen crashed 2/2 runs (`0xC0000005`).

prs.title: fix(ai): declare tools at the top level for a custom openai baseUrl
prs.body:
## What

Fixes #11637.

A `models.json` override of `providers.openai.baseUrl` changes only the URL, so the generated catalog's `supportsAdditionalTools` / `supportsToolSearch` assumptions survive it. With `toolSupport === "changes"`, every tool is then sent as an `additional_tools` input item while the top-level `tools` array stays empty. A proxy that accepts the request but drops those items answers 200, and the model sees no tools at all: it reports them as unavailable instead of calling them. Nothing fails, so Pi's error handling never surfaces it.

This makes the `openai` provider trust those OpenAI extensions only on the official endpoint. A proxy that does pass the items through opts back in with `compat.supportsAdditionalToolsOnCustomEndpoint: true`.

## Changed

- `packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses.ts`: `getCompat()` gates `supportsAdditionalTools` and `supportsToolSearch` on the endpoint being `https://api.openai.com/v1` for the `openai` provider. Other providers (`meta`, `xai`, `cloudflare-ai-gateway`, `opencode`, `github-copilot`, `openai-codex`) are unaffected because the check is scoped to `provider === "openai"`.
- `packages/ai/src/providers/compat-schema.ts`: new optional `supportsAdditionalToolsOnCustomEndpoint` (default `false`).
- `packages/ai/test/openai-responses-compat.test.ts`: two cases — a custom `openai` baseUrl declares `ping` at the top level; the same model with the new flag keeps `additional_tools`.
- `packages/ai/CHANGELOG.md`: entry under Fixed.

## Verification

- `npx vitest --run test/openai-responses-compat.test.ts` → 41 passed
- `npx vitest --run test/openai-responses-compat.test.ts -t "custom openai baseUrl"` → 2 passed
- Measured against the affected gateway before the change: top-level `tools` → `function_call: list_dir`; `additional_tools` → HTTP 200 and "tool is not available"
- Request capture confirmed the shape: `topLevelTools: 0`, `additionalTools: [28 tools]`, `removalNotices: 0`, `activeTools === requestedTools`

## Trade-off

Proxies that do pass `additional_tools` through now need the explicit flag; the new default is the declaration shape that works everywhere. `supportsMidConvoSystemMessages` is left unchanged because the affected gateway accepts developer-role messages — the dropped items are the failure.

issues.title: Desktop AppImage: image paste fails because bundled WebKitGTK needs 9 libraries that are not in the image

labels.name: status/need-information
labels.description: More information is needed to resolve this issue.

labels.name: priority/P2
labels.description: Medium - Moderately impactful, noticeable problem

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/platform
labels.description: Platform compatibility

labels.name: scope/linux
labels.description: Linux specific issues

labels.name: scope/packaging
labels.description: Package distribution

issues.body:
### What happened?

The Linux AppImage is the only artifact for non-Debian systems. It does launch
on rpm distros, but image paste into the app is broken until I worked around a
library hole the artifact never closes.

Measured against `Qwen-Code-Desktop_0.26.4_amd64.AppImage` (release
`desktop-v0.26.4`, 162,482,680 bytes), extracted with:

```console
$ chmod +x Qwen-Code-Desktop_0.26.4_amd64.AppImage   # the published asset is not +x
$ APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1 ./Qwen-Code-Desktop_0.26.4_amd64.AppImage --appimage-extract
```

1. `usr/bin/qwen-code-desktop` — 15 `DT_NEEDED`, 11 present in the bundle, and
   the 4 that are not are `libc.so.6`, `libm.so.6`, `libgcc_s.so.1`,
   `ld-linux-x86-64.so.2`. `RUNPATH` is `$ORIGIN/../lib`. The binary itself is
   fine.
2. The bundled `usr/lib/libwebkit2gtk-4.1.so.0` — 58 `DT_NEEDED`, 45 present in
   the bundle, 13 unresolved. Four are the C/C++ runtime family. The other nine
   are absent from the image, and installing the same sonames as system packages
   did not make the AppImage work:

   ```
   libfreetype.so.6  libfontconfig.so.1  libexpat.so.1   libharfbuzz.so.0
   libz.so.1         libX11.so.6         libgbm.so.1     libdrm.so.2
   libstdc++.so.6
   ```

3. The bundled baseline is Ubuntu 22.04-era (ICU 70, PCRE 3, libgcrypt 20). On
   Fedora 44 there is no provider for `libpcre.so.3` at all, `libicu` is 77.1
   with a 76.1 compat package, and `harfbuzz` is 12.3.2, so the artifact carries
   a dependency generation two releases older than any current rpm host.
4. GStreamer: 10 `usr/lib/libgst*-1.0.so.0` runtime libraries are bundled, zero
   plugin modules are, and there is no `gstreamer-1.0` plugin directory at all —
   consistent with `bundleMediaFramework: false` in
   `packages/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`. The only apprun hook present is
   `apprun-hooks/linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh`.
5. Practical result on a Fedora host: the window opens and the app is usable,
   but pasting an image does not work.
6. The `.deb` beside it declares `Depends: libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0, libgtk-3-0`, so
   deb users get exactly this closure resolved and installed by their package
   manager. The AppImage path resolves nothing.

### What did you expect to happen?

An AppImage is supposed to be self-contained, and these nine libraries are not
the user's to supply. I expect a complete bundle: every library the bundled
WebKitGTK declares in `DT_NEEDED`, present inside the AppImage.

### Client information

<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

```console
$ qwen --version
0.26.1

# Desktop shell: Qwen Code Desktop 0.26.4 (release desktop-v0.26.4), AppImage
# Platform: Fedora family, x86_64, rpm-based
# Paste the full `/about` output here before filing.
```

</details>

### Login information

Not relevant — this is an artifact/packaging defect and reproduces before any
login or model call.

### Anything else we need to know?

1. I searched before filing. Title searches for `rpm`, `shared object` and
   `libgbm OR webkit2gtk` return no matches. The five AppImage-titled issues
   are #11718 with fixes #11763/#11789 (bundled `PYTHONHOME`/`PYTHONPATH`
   leaking into spawned MCP servers), #12806 (aarch64 release matrix) and #13695
   (preserve bundled runtime integrity in AppImage). None covers the library
   closure, and 0.26.4 postdates #13695 while still shipping the same hole.
2. Reproduction in one loop:

   ```console
   $ cd squashfs-root
   $ for s in $(readelf -d usr/lib/libwebkit2gtk-4.1.so.0 \
       | sed -n 's/.*NEEDED.*\[\(.*\)\]/\1/p'); do
       find . -name "$s" -type f | grep -q . || echo "HOST-REQUIRED $s"; done
   ```

3. The paste symptom has been reported before from other angles, all against
   Linux: #1525 (2026-01-18, clipboard image paste request), #2885 (2026-04-04,
   image paste broken on Linux/Wayland), #3829 (2026-05-04, cannot paste images
   on Wayland), #12488 with fix #12489 (2026-09-22, silent failure when the
   Wayland paste helper is missing, follow-ups #12503 and #12505 still open) and
   #603 (2025-09-14, open, Wayland UI bugs). None of them identifies the
   packaging cause, which is what this report measures.

issues.title: feat(web-shell): add a waiting minigame above the composer

labels.name: priority/P3
labels.description: Low - Minor, cosmetic, nice-to-fix issues

labels.name: type/feature-request
labels.description: New feature or enhancement request

labels.name: category/ui
labels.description: User interface and display

issues.body:
## Summary

Add a small, dismissible waiting minigame above the main Web Shell composer.
While a prompt is running, a `Juust Relax` strip appears; clicking it opens a
horizontal Tetris board in the composer footer. The game closes when the turn
ends. It is local-only: no daemon, transcript, telemetry, or model changes.

## Motivation

Long turns currently show only a spinner, elapsed time, token count, and a
rotating phrase. A tiny self-contained game gives users something to do while
they wait without leaving the conversation. The interaction is optional and
never steals keyboard input from the composer.

## Scope

- Main App composer only (single session).
- Desktop / fine-pointer devices; hidden on coarse-pointer devices.
- `↑`/`↓` move, `→` speed up, `←` rotate, Space pause/resume, Escape collapse.
- 44×7 board; a full column clears and scores 50; speed rises with cleared
  columns.
- Best score and sound preference persist in `localStorage`.
- Game closes when the prompt stops streaming.

## Non-goals

- No welcome-page game, leaderboard, multiplayer, or cross-device scores.
- No split-pane, side-task, or mobile touch controls in this change.
- No backend or daemon API changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- The strip appears only while a prompt is active and after a short delay.
- It opens and collapses without breaking composer input; editor keystrokes are
  never hijacked by the game.
- The game closes when streaming ends.
- Split panes, side-task panes, and coarse-pointer devices do not render it.
- Engine and component tests cover spawn, movement, rotation, locking, column
  clears, scoring, pause, arm delay, open/collapse, and close-on-end.

A PR with implementation, tests, design notes, and page screenshots will be
linked here.

labels.name: priority/P2

labels.description: Waiting for user/maintainer feedback

labels.name: type/feature-request
labels.description: New feature or enhancement request

labels.name: category/platform
labels.description: Platform compatibility

labels.name: scope/linux
labels.description: Linux specific issues

labels.name: scope/packaging
labels.description: Package distribution

labels.name: scope/ci-cd
labels.description: Continuous integration/deployment

labels.name: roadmap/platform-distribution
labels.description: Roadmap: Platform and distribution

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

rpm artifacts in the Desktop release set, for Fedora and RHEL, published to the
same public asset bucket the installers already come from.

Patch inline below in a fenced diff (the issue form cannot take attachments).
Verified with `git apply --check` against the release tag `desktop-v0.26.4`
(`715a550cfca0`) and against current `main` (`06c1f989715f`); 3 files, 117
insertions, 19 deletions.

1. Two `build` matrix legs (`Linux x64 (rpm, Fedora 44)`,
   `Linux x64 (rpm, RHEL 10)`), driven by a `container` key so the next root is
   one added entry, not one added workflow. `tauri_args` passes
   `--bundles rpm`; Tauri's bundler already implements the target.
2. `Install rpm build-root dependencies`, since those legs run in containers as
   root with `dnf`; the existing dependency step gains a `matrix.container == ''`
   guard so the two are mutually exclusive. EPEL is enabled before WebKitGTK on
   the RHEL leg.
3. `command -v patchelf || true` in `Build desktop installers`. Today that line
   runs under `set -euo pipefail` and `patchelf` does not exist in any RHEL 10
   repo, so the leg would die before bundling. Only AppImage's linuxdeploy
   invokes patchelf, so the rpm path does not need it.
4. rpm in the artifact extension allowlist and in the collecting `find` — the
   current case statement drops anything that is not dmg/AppImage/deb/exe/zip.
5. An rpm branch in `scripts/smoke-linux-installers.js` (extract with
   `rpm2cpio | cpio`, then the same bundled-runtime checks), reached via a new
   `--require rpm` argument so the existing deb/AppImage strictness is
   untouched on today's legs.
6. One presence assertion in the OSS mirror step, gated to fresh builds so
   mirroring an older release keeps working.

Suggested commit message: `feat(desktop): build and publish rpm installers`.

### Why is this needed?

Because rpm users currently get the AppImage, and the AppImage does not run on
their distro without manual surgery — the companion bug issue #16030 has the
measurements (nine host-required sonames from the bundled WebKitGTK, declared by
nothing).

Repository facts, from the published metadata of each root today:

1. Fedora 44: `webkit2gtk4.1` 2.52.1 provides `libwebkit2gtk-4.1.so.0`;
   `javascriptcoregtk4.1` 2.52.1; `gtk3` 3.24.52; `mesa-libgbm` 26.0.3;
   `harfbuzz` 12.3.2; `patchelf` 0.18.0; `rpm-build` 6.0.1; `rust` 1.94.1.
   The rpm leg builds cleanly from the base tree.
2. RHEL 10 / CentOS Stream 10: no WebKitGTK in AppStream or CRB, and
   `patchelf` in neither. EPEL 10 carries `webkit2gtk4.1` 2.48.3 with
   `libwebkit2gtk-4.1.so.0` and `-devel`, so the leg works with EPEL enabled.
3. RHEL 9 / CentOS Stream 9: `webkit2gtk3` 2.54.1 provides only
   `libwebkit2gtk-4.0.so.37`, the legacy API, and EPEL 9 has no WebKitGTK 4.1
   either — so RHEL 9 is deliberately **not** in this patch. Pretending
   otherwise would ship an rpm that cannot install.
4. Per-root builds are mandatory, for the reason already documented in
   `desktop-release.yml` for the deb legs: glibc floors. Fedora 44 ships glibc
   2.43, RHEL 10 ships 2.39, RHEL 9 ships 2.34. One rpm cannot cover the family,
   so the matrix needs the root dimension rather than a new target triple.
5. No rpm distribution packages `fpm` — Fedora 44, CentOS Stream 9/10 and
   EPEL 9/10 all come back empty for `fpm` and `rubygem-fpm` — hence
   `gem install fpm` in the leg. Measured while building this: Fedora 44 ships
   Ruby 4.0.7, where `json` is no longer a default gem, so a bare
   `gem install fpm` produces an fpm that dies at load with
   `cannot load such file -- json (LoadError)`; the step installs
   `gem install json fpm`.

Publishing needs no workflow change: the mirror step already uploads every file
found by `find dist/desktop -maxdepth 1 -type f` and verifies against
`SHA256SUMS.txt`. The current published manifest for 0.26.4 lists 16 assets and
zero rpm, so the only missing thing is the artifact.

### Additional context

1. Deliberate non-goals, to keep this reviewable:
   
   1. No updater-feed entry. `create-desktop-update-manifest.mjs` maps one
      artifact per platform key and upstream reuses the AppImage as the Linux
      updater payload, so rpm updates come from the package manager. No
      `.rpm.sig` is required.
   2. `tauri.conf.json` `bundle.targets` stays as is, so a contributor's plain
      `npm run build` does not suddenly require `fpm`; rpm is requested via
      `--bundles` from CI only.
   3. No GPG repo signing and no Copr in this patch. An unsigned-but-repo-
     manageable follow-up is a separate decision.
2. Verification already performed locally, before asking for this to be
   merged: on `fedora:44` with this patch's package set and Node 22.20.0, the

   prerequisite work; say so and that becomes a second patch.
