## What this PR does

This PR implements the nine deferred non-blocking review suggestions from PR #12945 to improve trigger coverage, CI diagnostics, and regression tests for the Hosted latency gate. Specifically, it adds the SDK daemon SSE dependency to the Java workflow triggers, pins the latency CI contract steps and artifact uploads, adds independent literal assertions for all five comparison deltas and the no-tool null branch, introduces discriminating negative cases for validator invariants (like tool-wait arithmetic), preserves model assertion details by wrapping the fake server, propagates proxy failures at interaction points, retains raw failed measurements and their cause for CI diagnostics, and prints the delayed-worker shim on boot failure evidence.

## Why it's needed

These improvements enhance the reliability and diagnostics of the Hosted latency gate without widening the gate or changing its actual validation logic. By adding stricter contract tests and better failure artifacts, CI can catch regressions faster and provide developers with the exact evidence needed to debug Boot or latency failures without re-running jobs locally.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Reviewers can run the updated unit and contract tests locally to confirm the new assertions and negative cases pass correctly.
1. Run the CI contract test: `npx vitest run scripts/tests/sdk-java-workflow.test.js`
2. Run the latency baseline test: `npx vitest run integration-tests/cli/hosted-latency-baseline.test.ts`
Reviewers should also verify the `.github/workflows/sdk-java.yml` path additions and artifact upload paths match the expected CI wiring.

### Evidence (Before & After)

## Risk & Scope

- Not validated / out of scope: R1-1 (historical capture hashes) and R1-11 (CI classification machinery) are decisions/constraints, not edits in this PR. Real-provider latency and history-growth benchmarks remain separate work.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None.

prs.title: feat(acp): connect durable team reports and session approvals [13902 B/3]
prs.body:
Stack: **[#15657](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15657) → [#15658](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15658) → [#15659](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15659)**. This is **B**, based on A (`split/13902-agent-identity`, `3294001f39040a668fcbad20045b64e03dc1b6e6`); base branch: `split/13902-agent-identity`. C (`split/13902-teammate-activity`) depends on B. Split from #13902 at source commit `6ed7884c381dfe1c59bd975d6cf61dbb41ef441c`; candidate B: `435e4f949eca7232c2b48d3a259f5083cb788b8a`. Review B against A to isolate the coordination change.

## What this PR does

Connects an ACP-hosted leader to Team reports, roster membership and teammate approvals. Reports and join/exit notices enter the existing peer notification path with canonical teammate identity, survive recording and replay, and receive teammate attribution in the Web Shell. Pending reports participate in work holds, reversible close, queue overflow and shutdown flushing.

Teammate approvals reach the host independently of the leader's permission queue. Session scope, request UUIDs, binding epochs, ownership checks and retirement on manager replacement or teammate exit keep approval lifetime tied to the owning session. B includes producer, persistence, bridge, SDK/UI consumers and their tests. It consumes A's shared identity contract without depending on subagent runtime behavior. Tool activity and inter-agent message display arrive in C.

## Why it's needed

Without a leader sink, ACP-hosted teammate reports remain unread and teammate approval events have no consumer. The leader and its client need a delivery path that carries attribution, preserves undrained reports and exposes teammate approval requests.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. At candidate `435e4f949eca7232c2b48d3a259f5083cb788b8a`, run `npm run build` from the repository root, then run the package-local commands below serially. Each Vitest command runs from the stated package directory.
2. Deliver a teammate report and roster join/exit, then reload the transcript. Confirm canonical attribution, peer semantics and turn-marker correlation. Exercise reversible close, pending-report holds, overflow, repeat flush and shutdown with undrained reports.
3. Leave a teammate approval unanswered while the leader requests its own tool approval. Confirm the leader request remains visible. Exercise host answer/failure, standalone policy, session ownership, manager rebinding, teammate exit and cancellation; evaluate the inherited feedback below separately.

```sh
# cwd: packages/acp-bridge
../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/bridge-workflow-ancestor-trust.test.ts src/bridgeClient.test.ts src/transcript-replay.test.ts
# cwd: packages/cli
../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/acp-integration/acpAgent.test.ts src/acp-integration/session/Session.test.ts src/acp-integration/session/team-sink.test.ts
# cwd: packages/core
../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/agents/team/test-utils/coordination-harness.test.ts src/services/api-user-prompt.test.ts
# cwd: packages/sdk-typescript
../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/agent-identity.test.ts
# cwd: packages/web-shell
../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run client/adapters/transcriptToMessages.test.ts client/components/messages/SystemMessage.test.tsx
```

### Evidence (Before & After)

On candidate `435e4f949eca7232c2b48d3a259f5083cb788b8a`, `npm run build` exited 0. The focused package-local Vitest runs passed **3058 tests in 11 test files**: ACP bridge 356, CLI 2246, core 130, SDK 13 and Web Shell 313. These counts come from this split candidate, not the original PR.

Runtime, UI E2E and standalone typecheck were not run. Matched before/after protocol, persistence and UI evidence is not available. The build and focused tests do not establish that all verification obligations are complete; this PR remains a draft and the unresolved feedback below remains open.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ Build and focused tests; runtime/UI E2E and standalone typecheck not run |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not tested |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ Not tested |

### Environment (optional)

Local isolated worktree; repository-root build followed by serial package-local Vitest runs.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: notification durability and session-scoped approval lifetime cross queue, recording, bridge and shutdown boundaries. Roster transitions are event-based; there is no current-state snapshot for late attach or reconnect.
- Not validated / out of scope: exact-SHA runtime/UI and cross-platform validation are pending. Observational activity belongs to C. The source's unresolved feedback is retained.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: optional identity/attribution fields and session-scoped teammate permission metadata are added; no transcript migration is introduced.

Inherited unresolved feedback is not fixed by splitting:

- [R8-3: blanket XML escaping changes report/notice envelope fidelity across hosts](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13902#discussion_r4372372660).
- [R9-2: team teardown can queue a leader wake for each roster exit](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13902#discussion_r4372372667).
- [R9-5: the inserted permission interface changes BridgeClient JSDoc attachment](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13902#discussion_r4372372676).
- [R9-7: the abort fake does not reproduce reject-on-abort behavior](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13902#discussion_r4372372682).
- [R9-8: detach coverage does not establish that exit handling stays silent](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13902#discussion_r4372372686).
- [R9-9: an unoffered permission option can be reported as host failure](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13902#discussion_r4372372690).

A's unresolved replay feedback is inherited through the stack; its ownership remains with A.

Design: [English](docs/design/2026-10-11-agent-team-identity-projection.md) · [中文](docs/design/2026-10-11-agent-team-identity-projection.zh-CN.md). Both documents expand A with coordination decisions, constraints, acceptance criteria and the C follow-up boundary.

## Linked Issues

Related: #13785. Split source: #13902. This PR remains a draft. No automatic issue or PR closure is requested.

Stack links:

- A: [#15657](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15657) — prerequisite.
- B: [#15658](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15658) — this PR.
- C: [#15659](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15659) — depends on B.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

堆叠顺序：**[#15657](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15657) → [#15658](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15658) → [#15659](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15659)**。本 PR 是 **B**，基于 A（`split/13902-agent-identity`，`3294001f39040a668fcbad20045b64e03dc1b6e6`）；以 `split/13902-agent-identity` 为 base。C（`split/13902-teammate-activity`）依赖 B。拆分来源 #13902，固定源提交 `6ed7884c381dfe1c59bd975d6cf61dbb41ef441c`；B 候选为 `435e4f949eca7232c2b48d3a259f5083cb788b8a`。请相对 A 评审 B，以隔离协调层改动。

### 本 PR 做什么

将 ACP-hosted leader 接入 Team 报告、成员变更和队友审批。报告及加入/退出通知携带规范队友身份，进入现有 peer 通知路径，通过录制和重放保留，并在 Web Shell 中标注队友。待处理报告参与 work hold、可逆关闭、队列溢出和关机 flush。

队友审批独立于 leader 权限队列到达 host。会话范围、请求 UUID、binding epoch、所有权检查及 manager 替换或队友退出时的撤回，将审批生命周期绑定到所属会话。B 包含生产者、持久化、bridge、SDK/UI 消费方及配套测试。它消费 A 的共享身份契约，不依赖 subagent 运行时行为。工具活动与 agent 间消息展示由 C 交付。

### 为什么需要

缺少 leader sink 时，ACP-hosted 队友报告保持未读，队友审批事件没有消费方。leader 和客户端需要能传递归因、保存未排空报告并展示队友审批请求的投递路径。

### 评审测试计划

1. 在候选 `435e4f949eca7232c2b48d3a259f5083cb788b8a` 上从仓库根目录运行 `npm run build`，再串行执行英文部分列出的各包命令。每条 Vitest 命令均从标明的包目录执行。
2. 投递队友报告及成员加入/退出，再重载 transcript。确认规范归因、peer 语义和轮次标记关联。覆盖可逆关闭、待处理报告 hold、溢出、重复 flush 及含未排空报告的关机。
3. 保持队友审批未答复，同时让 leader 请求自己的工具审批，确认 leader 请求仍可见。覆盖 host 答复/失败、standalone 策略、会话所有权、manager 重绑定、队友退出及取消；下述继承反馈需另行验证。

**前后证据：**候选 `435e4f949eca7232c2b48d3a259f5083cb788b8a` 的 `npm run build` 退出码为 0。各包目录内的聚焦 Vitest 共通过 **11 个测试文件、3058 项测试**：ACP bridge 356、CLI 2246、core 130、SDK 13、Web Shell 313。这些数字来自本次拆分候选，不是原 PR 的历史结果。

未运行 runtime、UI E2E 或独立 typecheck，也没有匹配的协议、持久化和 UI 前后证据。构建与聚焦测试不代表所有验证义务均已完成；本 PR 保持 draft，下述未解决反馈仍然开放。

**测试平台：**macOS 已执行构建及聚焦测试，未运行 runtime/UI E2E 或独立 typecheck；Windows、Linux 未测试。

**环境：**本地隔离 worktree；从仓库根目录构建，再串行运行各包目录内的 Vitest。

### 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：通知持久性及会话级审批生命周期横跨队列、录制、bridge 和关机边界。成员变更基于事件，晚挂接或重连没有当前状态快照。
- 未验证或范围外：精确 SHA 的运行时/UI 及跨平台验证待完成。观察性活动属于 C。源提交的未解决反馈继续保留。
- 兼容性与迁移：新增可选身份/归因字段及会话级队友审批元数据；没有引入 transcript 迁移。

以下继承的未解决反馈未因拆分而修复：

- [R8-3：完整 XML 转义改变报告/通知 envelope 保真性及跨 host 行为](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13902#discussion_r4372372660)。

prs.title: fix(board): report canonical board names in JSON snapshots
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Uses the lowercase board storage name in CLI JSON snapshots, including when `--board` is supplied with mixed or uppercase spelling. Actor, owner, and ask-recipient labels retain their original spelling. Human board headings use the same canonical spelling. Adds focused JSON and plain-text heading regression coverage and documents both naming behaviors.

Codex assisted with implementation, regression coverage, and validation.

## Why it's needed

`show --board CaseJson --json` previously returned `"board":"CaseJson"` while its records lived under `boards/casejson/`. External consumers using the JSON field to construct a storage path received a name that did not match the directory spelling. The CLI now reports `"board":"casejson"` consistently.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Create a task on a mixed-case board and an ask on the uppercase spelling, then inspect that board using mixed, upper, and lowercase input. Confirm that all JSON snapshots and the plain-text `board:` heading identify the board by its lowercase storage name and expose the same records. Also confirm lowercase output for an empty board, unchanged mixed-case actor/owner/recipient labels, owner filtering, and rejection of invalid or missing board/actor names.

The original Windows verifier used real file storage and the final `node dist/cli.js` bundle with an isolated `QWEN_HOME`: seven successful commands and six expected input rejections passed. A separate real-command harness passed the same checks. The focused CLI suite passed 23/23 tests; full build, bundle, full workspace/integration typecheck, focused lint, and formatting checks passed. Against the original product behavior, the final regression suite produced four expected failures and 19 passes; the fixed product was restored afterward.

### Review revision (October 29)

Addressed R1-1 and R1-2 in `9c77d83a883c1b9df64ee7317fb2a44c7710bc81`. The documentation now explicitly covers the plain-text heading as well as JSON. Four additional non-JSON command cases assert the exact first output line for mixed, uppercase, lowercase and punctuation-containing board names; the original JSON cases remain intact.

The focused CLI suite passed **27/27** using its original Vitest configuration, global setup and setup files on Windows / Node 24.22.1. An independent rerun also passed 27/27. An in-memory mutation that changes only the plain-text heading back to the supplied spelling leaves the original 23 tests and the new lowercase control green, while exactly the three other new heading assertions fail (**24 passed, 3 failed**). Focused ESLint, Prettier and whitespace checks passed. No product logic changed.

These are command-parser/output tests with mocked board storage, using the same lockfile and reused dependencies/workspace artifacts. The normal full-build attempt stopped in Corepack with a cache-write EPERM before compilation; the CLI no-emit typecheck stopped with TS6305 for missing referenced workspace declaration outputs. Neither a new full build/bundle nor a full typecheck pass is claimed. This revision has no new Linux/macOS local execution; its upstream CI results are separate from the historical evidence below.

### Additional Linux verification (October 24)

Earlier head `6c3f3208abbc69ff824ef9a03961aa2f6b695444` also passed a [Linux fork verification run](https://github.com/Jun516/qwen-code/actions/runs/40064746728), including frozen dependency installation, a full workspace build, bundle, and real CLI checks on a filesystem first proven case-sensitive. Ten successful commands and six expected input rejections passed; JSON-derived task/ask paths contained the exact expected records, and actor/owner/recipient casing remained intact. The verifier commit is a direct child of this head and adds only two verification files, leaving the product tree unchanged. The [detailed report and artifact pointer](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15349#issuecomment-6380287580) record stdout, stderr and exit status.

That run records Linux execution of `6c3f3208`, before the later synchronization and review commits. It is historical evidence for that tree, not a full validation of the latest head, a Linux before/after baseline comparison, or a claim about a particular ext4 implementation. The latest head needs its own upstream checks.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before, JSON board names for inputs `CaseJson`, `CASEJSON`, and `casejson` were respectively `CaseJson`, `CASEJSON`, and `casejson`, while the only directory entry was `casejson`. After, actual built CLI commands return `casejson` for all three, with the same task/ask IDs and unchanged directory spelling. Empty `EmptyMixed` now returns `emptymixed`. The baseline canonical-name assertion failed; both final verification modes pass.

The global `qwen` binary was unavailable, so baseline reproduction used the built board command module and real storage rather than full CLI startup. Final verification did exercise the full built CLI. A separate E2E report contains commands, output, and the preserved baseline evidence.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ✅ tested |
| 🐧 Linux | ✅ earlier tree verified; latest-head CI pending |

### Environment (optional)

Windows and Linux, Node v22.18.0, built CLI bundle, isolated `QWEN_HOME`, real board storage, no model/API calls. The separate Linux result is linked above; no real user settings or credentials were required.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: callers observing board names in CLI output now receive the canonical lowercase spelling.
- Not validated / out of scope: a Linux before/after baseline comparison, a specific ext4 implementation, macOS, old uppercase-directory migration, claim/owner semantics, and the other follow-ups in #11755.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: no storage migration; the existing lowercase on-disk format is unchanged.

## Linked Issues

Addresses #11755 item 4 only. The issue's other follow-ups remain open.

### 补充 Linux 验证（10 月 24 日）

较早提交 `6c3f3208abbc69ff824ef9a03961aa2f6b695444` 曾通过 [Linux fork 验证](https://github.com/Jun516/qwen-code/actions/runs/40064746728)：冻结依赖安装、完整 workspace build、bundle，以及真实 CLI 检查全部成功。验证先证明临时文件系统大小写敏感，再检查 10 条成功命令和 6 条预期输入拒绝；由 JSON 拼接的 task/ask 路径含有准确记录，actor/owner/recipient 大小写保持原样。验证提交是本 PR head 的直接子提交，只增加两份验证文件，产品树相同。[详细报告](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15349#issuecomment-6380287580) 提供逐命令 stdout、stderr、退出码及 artifact 入口。

prs.title: feat(hooks): add FileChanged notifications for local sessions
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds `FileChanged` hooks for local, non-managed sessions. Hooks can observe literal filenames in the working directory or register absolute files and recursive directories through successful synchronous `SessionStart` and `FileChanged` output. Notifications carry the listening session, configured absolute path and `add`, `change` or `unlink`, including changes made by external processes.

Registrations follow session ownership, working-directory changes and hook reloads. Initially missing paths and deleted/recreated roots can recover. Explicit symbolic-link files and directory roots observe their targets while preserving the configured alias in notifications; recursive discovery keeps implicit symbolic links, `.git` and `node_modules` subtrees excluded unless explicitly registered.

CI compatibility repairs retain the complete gates while using fresh verification directories and runner-local Java dependency caches. Hosted workflow fault checks distinguish live consumption from a delivery-classification snapshot, and the digest-tamper probe updates its exact resource row by primary key. Attestation-loss injection covers both attempts of the existing bounded read-only EOF retry while preserving recovery-blocking assertions. RocketMQ downloads have bounded connection/transfer/retry windows. The hard-pinned 5.5.1 release first uses a public Apache mirror and falls back to the two official Apache sources; its independent SHA-512 check remains mandatory before extraction. Other versions retain the official-source checksum chain. Cold-resume TUI verification waits for the original assistant reply, then checks the typed user text in the same frame within the existing deadline. The branch also contains the upstream CI history and hosted macOS Intel startup-budget fixes. The self-hosted browser gate prepares missing DejaVu font data in the runner user's font directory, then rechecks that user. Preparation uses private APT lists and package extraction at the runner's existing privilege level; it never elevates or executes the PR-provided host installer.

Commit `be264d0c9f9f9662702f7c7a1a7c4d2a84311441` fixes a CI test that assumed an ordering Git does not guarantee. The preceding Linux run recorded 117,400 passes, one order-only failure and 152 skips: both expected worktree-prune entries were present, but reversed in all three attempts. The assertion now requires exactly the same two complete records without ordering. Production behavior, the 20-second deadline and test selection are unchanged. The original file passes 48/48; a controlled reversal of real Git announcement lines also passes the original case, and ten missing/extra/duplicate/wrong-object controls are rejected.

Commit `1a8b2591` integrates upstream main `4dd7ac7` and resolves the overlapping prune-test repair using the upstream order-normalized, exact two-record assertion. Commit `16a439b6` corrects cache-repair eligibility: only default `_tool` cache candidates invoke the unchanged canonical-path and symlink safeguards. Other configured cache roots retain their provisioned permissions and continue through the original Java installation and tests. No new privileges, test selectors, coverage guards or deadlines were introduced. Commit `16ef4bb269` qualifies the Managed database template in two unit-test fixtures. This preserves their original binding on the branch and selects the same named private template after newer main is integrated; SQL, transaction fields, assertions and test selection are unchanged.

## Why it's needed

Memory and other integrations need notifications from editors, shells and external writers, including files outside the working directory. This supplies a general filesystem event while leaving initial reconciliation and durable synchronization to the integration.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Register initially missing literal filenames, then create, atomically replace and delete them. Expect file notifications while unrelated siblings stay silent.
- Register an external directory, add nested files, delete and recreate the root, then write again. Notifications should continue; replacing or clearing dynamic registrations should retain static registrations.
- Register a symbolic-link file or directory, modify its target through the real path, and confirm the hook receives the configured alias. Multiple aliases should each notify. Refresh registration after retargeting a link; implicit child links should remain silent.
- Change the working directory or rotate the session and reload hooks. Only the current owning session should notify; temporary ACP/MCP configurations and managed, remote or sandbox sessions should remain disarmed.
- On a runner with font drift, expect DejaVu font data to be prepared under that runner's XDG/HOME directory, followed by the unchanged font check. Package or remaining-font failures must stop the gate; healthy runners make no preparation requests and PR-provided scripts never gain new privileges.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before the explicit-link repair, real CLI probes on the earlier source received zero notifications for static file links, dynamic file links and dynamic directory links, while the regular-file control notified. The d38 bundle passed all three configured aliases plus the control, preserving exact paths and session identity. Directory recreation produced `change → unlink → add → change`; both probes exited naturally with code 0 and empty stderr. These are historical source-scoped probes. The later main integration changes production Java, schema, SQL and other upstream inputs, so earlier SDK results are not current-tree runtime-equivalence evidence.

The resolved main-integration tree passed a complete build and typecheck, 1,714 core regressions, 912 ACP regressions, 50 Web Shell regressions and the complete 48-case prune file, all without test skips. Twelve strict assertion controls accept both valid report orders and reject missing, duplicate, extra or misattributed records. The subsequent two-file cache fix leaves the entire application package tree, dependency lock and manifests unchanged. Its workflow-contract checks pass 121/121, original cache-safety checks 8/8 and routing checks 92/92. The test engineer also verified 45 cache contexts and nine controlled flows without executing Java or modifying shared directories. Both source audits were clean; normal commit hooks preserved the verified trees.

Local workflow-reader runs retain their failures: the integration run recorded 1,235 passes, 23 failures and 25 conditional skips; the cache-fix reader run recorded 645 passes, 22 failures and 15 conditional skips. The 22 repeated failures reproduce with identical diagnostics on untouched main4dd under macOS Bash 3.2. The other original 90-second autofix timeout has no proven cause; isolated main/candidate controls passed without extending the deadline. The actual [1a8b Linux test job](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40664712936/job/122736421859) passed 117,940 test executions with zero failures and 152 existing skips, including the complete 150-case failure-reporter file, 339-case autofix file and original timed-out case. Initial local coverage-directory and linter-PATH failures remain recorded; serialization and the correct tool paths subsequently passed. Workflow-size validation also passed with the actual script under isolated Linux Bash 5, and the CI budget check passed.

### Current verification

Verification snapshot: 2026-10-29 09:16 Asia/Shanghai.

Current head is `16ef4bb269b146069d844d6df86cd6bd1cc45957`. The [Managed Agent fast gate](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40677250613), TUI, Landlock and reference-distribution workflows have succeeded. [Main CI](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40677250502) has also succeeded: required Lint & Static passed all 731 helper checks, Linux passed 117,940 test executions with 152 existing skips, no-AK integration passed 369/369, and browser smoke passed 403/403 plus six transcript cases. Its actual font probe selected DejaVu Sans on the healthy path; this run did not exercise cold font preparation. Serve A/B attempt1 hit the original 60-minute limit during official Node22.23.4 acquisition after a socket hang-up and stalled retry; both product builds/captures and the diff were unexecuted. Its complete failure logs remain preserved. The one same-source job rerun has now succeeded in all 16 workflow steps, including both original build/capture arms, the diff and artifact upload, with unchanged tests and deadlines. It used cached Node22.23.2-x64 under the original22.x setting; this cache-hit result does not verify the failed cold22.23.4-arm64 transfer. Visuals has also succeeded: head/base checks passed85/81, the render outcome and uploaded render-status both report success, and all118 screenshot pairs have zero pixel differences. Zero composed changes therefore produced no published PNG previews. Two raw videos were uploaded; optional GIF conversion was skipped because the host lacked ffmpeg. All eight product workflows have now succeeded. The new Live Host run actually checked out b616 on macOS26.6.2 ARM64 with Node22.23.3:374/374 tests passed without skips, followed by a successful build, ARM64 package, explicit ad-hoc signing and strict verification. These checks do not represent identity signing or notarization. The new-head automatic CR has now completed successfully and published a partial COMMENT review; formal approval remains separate from these completed product checks.

The preceding [Managed fast gate](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40669147407) recorded two SQL type errors after newer main made the Managed JDBC template private: two unit fixtures selected the unqualified host template. Commit `16ef4bb269` changes only those two field qualifiers and imports. The new fast job actually checked out `b61688f5` (main `11ef1988` + `16ef4bb2`) and recorded 5,834 Managed tests: 5,815 passed, 19 existing skips, and zero failures/errors. The two changed fixture classes executed all 57 integration and nine creation-skills cases with zero skips/errors, preserving the original SQL and transaction assertions. SDK tests recorded 421 total with nine existing skips; Java 11 daemon checks passed 4/4. Actual SDK, Managed and Broker Checkstyle goals reported zero violations. Fast runs test/package rather than verify, so it does not itself certify SpotBugs. Successful fast runs do not upload Surefire XML/TXT under the existing failure-only upload policy; the acceptance evidence is the complete raw console and exact-source class roster.

The [complete SDK run](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40669464577) has succeeded in all13 original lanes at immutable source `16a439b6`; all13 terminal consoles confirm that checkout. MariaDB10.11.18 and MySQL8.4.6 each completed all1,192 integration cases with zero skips/failures/errors, matching each66-class source roster and all four reclamation cuts and two reuse-concurrency methods. Hosted recorded165 total:161 passed and four conditional skips; fault45/45, admission2/2 and O4 recovery59/59 passed without skips. Both original PROVISIONER/SERVICE fault contexts and their blocking, lease and relaunch assertions remain intact. The single-broker7, multi-node10 and all20 CLI/database failover commands also passed. macOS recorded SDK412 passes/9 skips and Runtime Broker1,245 passes/13 skips, including the ownership-revision case.

Commit16ef changes only two unit-fixture injection fields/imports; production, dependencies, schemas, integration-profile tests and workflow inputs remain identical to16a. The13-lane result supplies qualified evidence for those unchanged inputs; it did not execute16ef's changed fixtures, whose acceptance is separately established by the newer b616 fast run. It also does not certify the whole later b616 integration, which contains144 additional paths, including74 Managed Java production paths. The approval-triggered full gate remains the maintainer acceptance stage for that integration. Test trees, Git stamps and compiled outputs are not claimed byte-identical.

The four current Hosted skips remain explicit: three public-workspace cases require macOS, and one method containing12 media scenarios needs the manual bundle-ready property. The SDK macOS lane does not execute that separate Hosted profile. Successful SQL and fault/admission XML are not uploaded by the existing policies; source-scoped proof uses complete console summaries, exact class/selector checks and the Hosted/O4 XML artifacts that were actually uploaded. Original failed/cancelled attempts and acquisition failures remain preserved.

Real HZ jobs now skip only optional permission repair, complete Java installation and execute verification; HK jobs still execute the unchanged local-cache safeguards. The preceding [1a8b SDK run](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40664899184) failed four jobs before Java setup because a configured shared cache was mistaken for a repairable local cache. Once the corrected 13-lane replacement was accepted, its remaining obsolete work was stopped; completed results and all four failure logs remain preserved. Stopped or unexecuted work is not counted as passing. Upstream now runs installed npm acceptance on schedule or manual dispatch, so the PR's skipped installation jobs are not new 9/9 or 96/96 results.

The [round-17 review](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13969#pullrequestreview-5688241194) reviewed the current16ef head, rechecked historical blockers and published no new inline blocker. It explicitly disclosed partial-review gaps and was COMMENTED, not APPROVED;14 nonblocking Suggestions are recorded as deferred in the review body. The [automatic CR workflow](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40677250268) succeeded. A separate check of the artifact-only, low-confidence R17-9 reproduced the missing-helper exit127 on an older source tree, but found no existing sdk-java tags or Java SDK release runs on October29; no currently blocked resumed release was established. This conditional old-ref compatibility risk remains recorded for follow-up. Current checks have no failures or pending jobs. The branch has no merge conflict; the two required formal approvals remain outstanding.

### Historical evidence and boundaries

The [be264 main CI](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40579375100) and its other seven product workflows succeeded, including 117,401 Linux passes with 152 existing skips, 372 browser plus six transcript cases, TUI installation 96/96 and Live Host 374/374. Those results belong to be264 or their recorded integration checkout37daa, not the latest head. The [d38 full SDK recovery](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/40526188684/attempts/3) succeeded in all 13 lanes. It retains four pre-existing Hosted conditional skips: one method containing 12 provider-media scenarios needs the manual bundle-ready property, and three public-workspace checks require macOS; admission checks do not replace those scenarios. New Java/schema inputs invalidate reuse of that old run as full acceptance of the merged tree.

The R15 font repair retains all 20 regressions, four independent controls and two real Ubuntu UID1000 cold-font controls, with unchanged system fonts/configuration and no Chromium-metric claim for those containers. The actual font-repair shell remains unchanged through both new commits. Earlier local application and metadata failures remain recorded separately, including core 2,493/one failure, CLI 3,651/two failures and the 269-pass/43-failure Node metadata baseline. No local control erases those wider failures. Java, Maven and SQL verification stays in CI because the original shared local budget is exhausted.

## Risk & Scope

- Filesystem notifications are best effort; integrations remain responsible for initial scans, reconciliation and self-trigger loops. Retargeted links require a registration refresh.
- Managed/remote filesystem producers, memory enable/disable events and durable synchronization remain outside this change.
- Design and user contracts are synchronized in [English](https://github.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/blob/codex/file-changed-hook/docs/design/file-changed-hooks.md) and [Chinese](https://github.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/blob/codex/file-changed-hook/docs/design/file-changed-hooks.zh-CN.md).

prs.title: feat(serve): auto-remove completed sub-sessions after a configurable TTL
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds TTL-based auto-removal of completed sub-sessions in `qwen serve` (daemon mode). A new `serve.subSessionCompletionTtlHours` setting (integer, hours; default `0` — keep completed sub-sessions forever, i.e. today's behavior) controls how long a finished sub-session stays in the workspace session roster before the daemon removes it; auto-removal is opt-in via a positive value.

After a sub-session's turn ends with a clean `end_turn` (an errored or cancelled turn never becomes eligible; the observer stop reasons `timeout`, `incomplete`, `shutdown` are ignored), the sub-session launcher starts a per-session completion clock. A 5-minute sweep (unref'd, serialized, so it never keeps the process alive or re-enters) then removes expired sub-sessions the same way the existing launch-rollback cleanup does: `closeSession` (tolerating entries the bridge reaper already closed) plus `SessionService.removeSession` for the persisted transcript, so an expired sub-session is no longer continuable — consistent with how closed sessions are treated elsewhere (#7420). A revived sub-session (a new prompt after completion) restarts the clock from its latest activity instead of being removed — the sweep confirms it against the persisted transcript's freshness even when the live entry is already gone — and running sub-sessions (an active prompt, running background tasks, or an active work state) are never removed. After a daemon restart, the first sweep rediscovers previously completed sub-sessions from the persisted session catalog (rows with a parent session only — never top-level sessions). Non-integer values and values below a setting's minimum produce a warning and fall back to the built-in default, mirroring the existing `serve.maxConcurrentSubSessions*` handling.

## Why it's needed

Finished sub-sessions (`create_sub_session`, daemon/serve only) currently accumulate in the session roster for the lifetime of the daemon. The bridge reaper closes the live entry of an idle completed sub-session, but the persisted transcript keeps the thread listed in the Web Shell sidebar until the daemon is restarted or the parent session is closed. On long-running daemons this turns into dozens of dead threads under a single parent session with no way to prune them except a restart. This is the request from #14289: auto-removal of completed sub-sessions, terminal-state only, with revival resetting the timer.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Unit level: `cd packages/cli && pnpm vitest run src/serve/create-sub-session.test.ts src/serve/run-qwen-serve.test.ts src/config/settingsSchema.test.ts` — the `sub-session completion TTL` block (21 fake-timer + real-fs lifecycle tests: removal at exactly the TTL moment, terminal state across repeated sweeps, persisted discovery after a restart, revival from persisted-transcript freshness, `0` keeps forever, the live guards — active prompt / background tasks / active work state, reaper arming for unobserved turns, errored and cancelled turns never removed, close-failure recovery, remove-false, transient summary error, in-flight sweep serialization, FIFO-evicted id survival, `stop()` clears the sweeper) plus `subSessionCompletionTtlMsFromSettings` (4 config-reader tests) and the schema pin test (default === runtime default, minimum 0).

Live: run `qwen serve` from this branch with `"serve": { "subSessionCompletionTtlHours": 1 }` in user settings, create a session and let its model spawn one trivial sub-session (`create_sub_session`, `completion: "sent"`). After the sub-session's turn finishes, wait ~65 minutes: the daemon logs `qwen serve: removed completed sub-session <id> from the roster (completion TTL 60min expired)`, the transcript `.jsonl` is gone from `~/.qwen/projects/<slug>/chats/`, and `GET /workspace/<id>/sessions` no longer lists the thread.

prs.title: ci(release): only file issues on failure and reconcile stale ones
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Both fan-out release notifiers treated a cancelled run as a failure and filed an issue, and neither workflow had any path to close that issue once a later attempt shipped. Each notifier now reacts only to an actual failure of its build or publish job, and each workflow gains a success-gated sibling job that closes the bot-authored issue an earlier attempt filed. The shared release step behind that reconciliation now takes the issue-title prefix and the release version, so the CLI release and both fan-out workflows reuse one implementation instead of growing separate copies.

## Why it's needed

A shipped release could sit under an open failure report: release v0.26.3's VSCode companion run passed on attempt 2 while its failure issue stayed open until it was closed by hand. Cancellation also filed issues for runs that shipped nothing. Stale failure issues are picked up by the scheduled autofix agent and turned into PRs against releases that already landed, so the false report has a cost beyond noise.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

From the repository root, run `npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts scripts/tests/release-fanout-workflows.test.js scripts/tests/release-workflow.test.js`. The five new cases pin that neither notifier mentions `cancelled`, that each reconcile job is success-gated, checks out the workflow's own commit, calls the shared step with its own title prefix, and cannot turn a shipped release red. One case drives the script with a fake `gh` and two bot-authored issues whose titles differ only by workflow prefix, and asserts that only the matching issue is closed. The existing release.yml reconciliation cases keep passing unchanged.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before, a cancelled build or publish filed `VSCode IDE Companion Release Failed for …` / `Chrome extension release failed for …`, and a passing re-run left it open. After, cancellation files nothing and a passing re-run closes the workflow-owned issue with a comment. This is CI-only behaviour, so there is no UI before/after.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

The script is bash and both jobs run on `ubuntu-latest`; Windows is not a supported target. Linux was verified inside a `node:22-bookworm` container with `jq` installed.

### Environment (optional)

Unit and workflow-contract tests only; no release run was triggered.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: each successful release now runs one short reconciliation job, which comments on and closes only a `github-actions[bot]` issue whose title matches `<prefix><version> on ` exactly. A human filing the same title is never touched, and the step is `continue-on-error` so it cannot fail a shipped release.
- Not validated / out of scope: the notifier still has no dry-run guard and does not react to a `prepare` failure in the companion workflow; both predate this change and were left untouched.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The workflows grow by about 1.5 KB each, within the size-ratchet allowance, so no baseline update is needed.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15840

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

两个发布下游通知器此前把「取消」也当成失败并创建 issue，而且两个 workflow 都没有在后续重跑成功后关闭该 issue 的路径。现在通知器只在 build 或 publish 真正失败时创建 issue，每个 workflow 新增一个成功才触发的兄弟作业，用于关闭上一次尝试创建的、由机器人提交的 issue。负责关闭的共用发布脚本现在接收 issue 标题前缀与发布版本，CLI 发布和两个下游 workflow 复用同一份实现，而不是各自再复制一份。

## 为什么需要

已发布的版本可能一直挂着一个未关闭的失败报告：v0.26.3 的 VSCode companion 运行在第 2 次尝试成功，但它此前创建的失败 issue 一直开着，直到被手动关闭。取消的运行也会创建 issue，尽管它什么都没发布。残留的失败 issue 会被定时 autofix 机器人捡走，针对已经发布的版本开出 PR，因此误报的代价不只是噪音。

## 评审验证方式

在仓库根目录运行 `npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts scripts/tests/release-fanout-workflows.test.js scripts/tests/release-workflow.test.js`。新增的 5 个用例固定住：两个通知器不再包含 `cancelled`；reconcile 作业为成功门控、checkout 使用 workflow 自身提交、用各自标题前缀调用共用脚本、且不会让已发布版本变红。其中一个用例用假 `gh` 和两条仅前缀不同的机器人 issue 驱动脚本，断言只关闭匹配的那条。`release.yml` 原有的 reconcile 用例保持不变并通过。

## 改动前后

改动前，build 或 publish 被取消也会创建 `VSCode IDE Companion Release Failed for …` / `Chrome extension release failed for …`，并且重跑成功后该 issue 仍然开着。改动后，取消不再创建 issue，重跑成功会带评论关闭该 workflow 创建的 issue。这是纯 CI 行为，没有界面前后对比。

## 测试环境

脚本是 bash，两个作业都在 `ubuntu-latest` 上运行，Windows 不是支持目标。macOS 通过；Linux 在 `node:22-bookworm` 容器内（安装 `jq`）通过。

## 风险与范围

每个成功发布多跑一个很短的 reconcile 作业，它只会评论并关闭作者为 `github-actions[bot]`、标题精确匹配 `<前缀><版本> on ` 的 issue；真人提交的同名 issue 不会被碰，该步骤设置 `continue-on-error`，不会把已发布版本变红。通知器仍没有 dry-run 门控、也不响应 companion 的 `prepare` 失败，这两点都是既有行为，本次未改。两个 workflow 各增长约 1.5 KB，仍在 size ratchet 允许范围内，无需更新 baseline。

## 关联 issue

Fixes #15840

</details>

prs.title: feat(web-shell): add a Scheduled tasks tab to the sidebar session-source switch
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a "Scheduled tasks" option to the Web Shell sidebar's Session source switch (and the archived switch). Selecting it lists exactly the bound controller sessions of persistent scheduled tasks — the conversations a task's prompts are injected into — which today have no place in the session list. The default "Tasks" tab is unchanged: bound controller sessions stay outside the default catalog, as the session-source-filter design documents. On the new tab the bound session renders with the existing clock marker and groups under its task, mirroring how per-run `scheduled_task_run:` sessions are grouped in the Tasks tab. The daemon needed no change: the public `sourceType` query parameter already accepts arbitrary source types and matches them exactly, and `scheduled_task` was never part of the hidden-catalog exclusion list.

## Why it's needed

Issue #12576: bound controller sessions of scheduled tasks are invisible in the sidebar. The root cause was confirmed by @doudouOUC — the default catalog's `sourceType=default` filter only admits `undefined`/`default`/`qwen-live`, and the sidebar offered no way to switch to the `scheduled_task` catalog. The alternative path (Scheduled tasks panel → task card → View conversation) still exists and is untouched; this adds a direct discoverability affordance. The earlier attempt (#11635, closed unmerged) took a broader approach; its deferred review findings live in #11738 and are not touched by this PR (the archive/delete guards there key on the live task binding, which is unchanged here).

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Create a persistent scheduled task (e.g. via the Scheduled tasks panel with "Dedicated task conversation"), run it once so the bound controller session exists. In the Web Shell sidebar, open the Session source switch: "Tasks" does not list the bound conversation (unchanged); "Scheduled tasks" lists it, clock marker included, grouped under the task. Archived variant: archive the bound conversation and check the archived switch. Non-UI evidence below (unit tests).

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (unit-level; sidebar tab is a two-option segmented control gaining a third option).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |

prs.title: feat(channels): deliver injected messages into the running turn
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a fourth channel `dispatchMode`, `inject`: a message that arrives while the agent is already working in a channel session is handed to the running turn's mid-turn queue and read by the agent at its next tool-batch boundary, instead of being buffered until the turn ends (`collect`) or queued as a new turn (`followup`).

The queue lives in the bridge (`AcpBridge`), is bounded at 20 messages / 20,000 characters, and is drained in batches the ACP child can actually consume (10 per response; the remainder stays queued for the next drain). A message is reported as injected only when the bridge accepted it. Everything the running turn cannot represent falls back to the existing collect buffer and is replayed as its own turn, in arrival order: a rejected or over-bound message, another chat's/thread's message under a collapsed session scope, an unauthorized member in a shared session, a recognized slash command, an image message (refused visibly — mid-turn injection is text-only), and any message on a bridge without the capability. When a turn ends before the agent drained, its unread messages are taken back at the turn boundary and replayed as a new turn instead of leaking into the next one; `/cancel`, `/clear` and session teardown drop them with the same buffer-drop notification the collect path uses.

The round-1 review's 10 Critical and 9 Suggestion findings are addressed in the same commits: drain batching against the consumer cap, turn-scoped settlement, a collect-replay marker (not `alreadyPrefixed`), the shared-session authorization gate, the per-message `onPromptInjected` hook, arrival-order sequencing once the fallback is open, the aggregate/depth char bound, text-only media handling, the email dispatch-mode guard, and the daemon-bridge fallback diagnostic.

## Why it's needed

Closes #15630. Today a user who sees the bot going the wrong way mid-task has only bad options: `steer` cancels the turn, `collect` makes them wait for it to finish, `followup` queues a new turn that may answer a stale question. `inject` lets the correction reach the work in progress, which is what a mid-task correction is for.

The guarantees above are part of the feature, not polish: the failure mode of a wrong delivery receipt is silently lost user input, and a message accepted for someone else's turn executes work under permissions approved for that turn's owner.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Unit/integration level with mocked bridge and child; no live channel platform is needed. From the repo root:

```bash
cd packages/channels/base && npx vitest run
cd packages/channels/wecom && npx vitest run
cd packages/channels/email && npx vitest run
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp-integration/session/Session.test.ts src/serve/channel-settings-store.test.ts
npx tsc --build packages/channels/base packages/cli
```

Behaviour to confirm, all named cases in `ChannelBase.test.ts`'s "mid-turn message injection (inject dispatch mode)" block unless noted:

- accepted injection calls `queueMidTurnMessage` only, logs delivered, fires `onPromptInjected` and does not buffer;
- a bridge rejection parks the message in the bounded fallback and every later message of that turn follows it in arrival order;
- both fallback bounds (20 messages / 20,000 chars) refuse visibly and tell the sender rather than dropping;
- a collect-buffer replay is never re-injected (`collectReplay`), so a parked message always becomes its own turn;
- undrained injections are replayed at the turn boundary (`ChannelBase.test.ts` "replays injections the running turn never drained as a new turn"; `AcpBridge.test.ts` "settles undrained mid-turn messages at the turn boundary instead of leaking them");
- a shared-session member who is not an operator is denied and buffered; another chat's message under `sessionScope: 'single'` is not injected;
- an image message is refused in-thread (text-only), a file attachment is buffered so its `saved to:` path reaches a turn (`WeComAdapter.test.ts` too);
- a recognized slash command is buffered, and the group-history backfill is composed into the injected text;
- `AcpBridge.test.ts` "caps one drain response at the ACP consumer batch and keeps the remainder queued" (queue 11 → drain 10 → drain the 11th);
- `/cancel` and `/clear` drop queued injections with a drop notification (`AcpBridge.test.ts` and `ChannelBase.test.ts`);
- the email adapter rejects `inject` (`packages/channels/email/src/config.test.ts`), and a bridge without the capability logs one diagnostic and buffers.

### Evidence (Before & After)

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unauthorized member injects into an operator's shared session | text reaches the running turn and executes under the turn owner's permissions | denied, falls through to collect buffering as its own turn |
| Turn ends with 15 queued messages the agent never drained | text stays queued and is injected into whatever turn runs next | taken back at the turn boundary and replayed as a new turn |
| 11 messages queued, one drain | one response carries 11, child keeps 10, the 11th is lost while the channel logged it delivered | first 10 delivered, the 11th delivered by the next drain |
| Collect-buffer replay while another turn registers | replay re-enters the inject arm and folds into someone else's turn | marked `collectReplay`, becomes its own turn |
| Image sent under `inject` | `[Alice] (image)` injected; the picture is invisible to the model | visible in-thread refusal (text-only path) |
| Chat-B message under `sessionScope: 'single'` | injected into chat A's running turn; the answer goes to A | buffered and replayed as its own turn in B |
| Email channel with `dispatchMode: 'inject'` | accepted by config, silently behaved as collect | rejected at config with the durable-claim reason |
| Bounded fallback full | message discarded with one stderr line | sender is told, stderr records the refusal |

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit and integration tests with a mocked bridge/child (Node 22).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: `inject` widens what a mid-turn message can do. The injected text enters a turn whose tool approvals belong to that turn's owner, so the arm now requires `isAuthorizedForSharedSession` (non-operators buffer instead) and never crosses a chat/thread boundary the running turn does not own. The degradation contract is deliberate: anything the turn cannot represent becomes a normal buffered turn rather than lost input.
- Semantics: nothing is reported delivered unless the bridge accepted it; the queue is settled at the turn boundary; ordering between injected and parked messages follows arrival order; the fallback is bounded (20 messages / 20,000 chars) and refuses visibly.
- Behaviour changes: the adapter-facing `dispatchMode` contract gains `inject` (email now whitelists `followup`/`steer` and rejects the rest), and `inject` on a daemon-managed (`qwen serve`) channel falls back to collect with a one-time operator diagnostic because `DaemonChannelBridge` cannot hand messages to a running turn — promoting them needs a channel-visible promotion contract and is out of scope here.
- Not validated / out of scope: no end-to-end run against a live agent child for drain timing (the tests drive a mocked child and bridge); the daemon promotion path is deliberately not implemented; queue capacity is the operator-facing global 20/20,000 bound, not a per-sender quota; images are refused rather than described to the model.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none for existing modes — `collect` stays the default and the new mode is opt-in per channel; no config format change.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15630.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

新增第四个 channel `dispatchMode`：`inject`。当 agent 已在某个 channel 会话中工作时到达的消息，不再等回合结束（`collect`）或排成新回合（`followup`），而是交给正在运行回合的 mid-turn 队列，由 agent 在下一个工具批次边界读到。

队列位于桥接层（`AcpBridge`），上限 20 条 / 20,000 字符，并按 ACP 子进程真正能消费的批量出队（每次响应 10 条，剩余留在队列中等待下一次 drain）。只有桥接层真正接受的消息才记为已注入；运行中回合无法表示的消息一律回退到既有 collect 缓冲，并按到达顺序作为自己的新回合重放：被拒绝或超出上限的消息、session scope 折叠后来自其它 chat/thread 的消息、共享会话中无权限的成员消息、可识别的 slash 命令、图片消息（明确拒绝——mid-turn 注入只支持文本），以及桥接层没有该能力的消息。回合结束时 agent 尚未读取的消息会在回合边界收回并作为新回合重放，不会泄漏到下一个回合；`/cancel`、`/clear` 和会话销毁会丢弃它们，并走与 collect 相同的 buffer-drop 通知。

第一轮 review 的 10 个 Critical + 9 个 Suggestion 在同一批提交中修复：按消费端上限分批 drain、队列与回合绑定并在回合边界结算、collect 重放标记（不用 `alreadyPrefixed`）、共享会话权限门禁、逐条 `onPromptInjected` 生命周期 hook、fallback 打开后的到达顺序、聚合/深度字符上限、纯文本媒体处理、email 的 dispatchMode 守卫、daemon bridge 的一次性诊断。

## 为什么需要

关闭 #15630。现在用户看到 bot 中途走偏时只有坏选择：`steer` 取消整个回合，`collect` 让他们等回合结束，`followup` 排一个新回合、可能回答的是过期问题。`inject` 让纠正能进入正在进行的工作——这正是「中途纠正」的用途。

上面那些保证属于功能本身而非润色：回执不实的失败模式是用户输入被静默丢失；而替别人回合接受消息，会让工作在「该回合所有者」的权限下执行。

## Reviewer 验证计划

### 如何验证

单元/集成层面，桥与子进程都是 mock，不需要真实 channel 平台。在仓库根目录执行：

```bash
cd packages/channels/base && npx vitest run
cd packages/channels/wecom && npx vitest run
cd packages/channels/email && npx vitest run
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp-integration/session/Session.test.ts src/serve/channel-settings-store.test.ts
npx tsc --build packages/channels/base packages/cli
```

需要确认的行为（除注明外均为 `ChannelBase.test.ts` 的 "mid-turn message injection (inject dispatch mode)" 块中的具名用例）：

- 注入被接受时只调用 `queueMidTurnMessage`、记录 delivered、触发 `onPromptInjected`，不进入缓冲；
- 桥接层拒绝后，本条消息停入有界 fallback，本回合后续消息按到达顺序跟随其后；
- fallback 的两个上限（20 条 / 20,000 字符）都会明确拒绝并告知发送者，而不是丢弃；
- collect 缓冲重放不会被再次注入（`collectReplay`），被 park 的消息一定成为自己的回合；
- 回合结束时未被 drain 的注入会在回合边界被重放（`ChannelBase.test.ts` "replays injections the running turn never drained as a new turn"；`AcpBridge.test.ts` "settles undrained mid-turn messages at the turn boundary instead of leaking them"）；
- 共享会话中非 operator 成员被拒绝并进入缓冲；`sessionScope: 'single'` 下来自另一个 chat 的消息不会被注入；
- 图片消息在会话中明确拒绝（仅文本），文件附件则被缓冲，使其 `saved to:` 路径能在自己的回合被读到（`WeComAdapter.test.ts` 同上）；
- 可识别的 slash 命令进入缓冲；group-history 补全会拼入注入文本；
- `AcpBridge.test.ts` "caps one drain response at the ACP consumer batch and keeps the remainder queued"（队列 11 条 → 第一次 drain 10 条 → 第二次 drain 第 11 条）；
- `/cancel` 与 `/clear` 会丢弃排队中的注入并发出 drop 通知（`AcpBridge.test.ts` 与 `ChannelBase.test.ts`）；
- email 适配器拒绝 `inject`（`packages/channels/email/src/config.test.ts`），没有该能力的桥只记录一次诊断并进入缓冲。

### 证据（修改前 / 修改后）

| 场景 | 修改前 | 修改后 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 无权限成员向 operator 的共享会话注入 | 文本进入运行中回合，按回合所有者权限执行 | 被拒绝，回退为 collect 缓冲并成为自己的回合 |
| 回合结束时队列里还有 15 条未被读取 | 文本留在队列，被注入到之后任意回合 | 回合边界收回，作为新回合重放 |
| 队列 11 条、执行一次 drain | 一次响应带出 11 条，子进程只保留 10 条，第 11 条丢失且日志记为已投递 | 前 10 条投递，第 11 条由下一次 drain 投递 |
| collect 缓冲重放期间又有回合注册 | 重放重新进入 inject 分支，被折进别人的回合 | 标记 `collectReplay`，成为自己的回合 |
| 在 `inject` 模式下发图片 | 注入 `[Alice] (image)`，模型看不到图 | 会话内明确拒绝（仅文本） |
| `sessionScope: 'single'` 下 chat-B 的消息 | 被注入 chat A 的运行中回合，回答也发到 A | 进入缓冲，作为 B 的新回合重放 |
| email 频道配置 `dispatchMode: 'inject'` | 配置接受，实际静默按 collect 处理 | 配置阶段拒绝，并给出 durable-claim 原因 |
| 有界 fallback 已满 | 消息被丢弃，只写一行 stderr | 告知发送者，stderr 记录拒绝 |

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

### 环境（可选）

N/A —— 使用 mock 的桥/子进程的单元与集成测试（Node 22）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/权衡：`inject` 扩大了中途消息能做的事。注入的文本会进入「工具审批属于该回合所有者」的回合，因此该分支现在要求 `isAuthorizedForSharedSession`（非 operator 一律进入缓冲），且绝不跨越运行中回合不拥有的 chat/thread 边界。降级契约是有意为之：回合无法表示的消息变成普通缓冲回合，而不是丢失。
- 语义：只有桥接层接受才记为 delivered；队列在回合边界结算；注入与 park 消息之间保持到达顺序；fallback 有界（20 条 / 20,000 字符）并明确拒绝。
- 行为变更：适配器侧的 `dispatchMode` 契约新增 `inject`（email 现在白名单 `followup`/`steer`，其余拒绝）；daemon 管理的（`qwen serve`）频道下 `inject` 会回退到 collect 并记录一次性诊断，因为 `DaemonChannelBridge` 无法把消息交给运行中回合——要做 promotion 需要 channel 可见的契约，不在本 PR 范围。
- 未验证/超出范围：没有对真实 agent 子进程做端到端 drain 时序验证（测试用 mock 子进程与桥）；daemon promotion 路径本 PR 未实现；队列容量是操作者可见的全局 20/20,000 上限，不是按发送者的配额；图片是明确拒绝而不是转述给模型。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：对既有模式无破坏——`collect` 仍是默认，新模式按频道显式开启；配置格式无变化。

Fixes #15630。

auto_merge.commit_title: feat(channels): deliver injected messages into the running turn (#15634)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* feat(channels): deliver injected messages into the running turn

Add an `inject` dispatch mode: when a prompt is already running for a
session, the channel hands the new text to the bridge's mid-turn queue
instead of cancelling the turn or buffering until it ends. The ACP child
pulls it at its next tool-batch drain boundary (`craft/drainMidTurnQueue`),
so the agent sees the message inside the current turn.

The queue is per session, bounded by message count and characters (dropped
rather than truncated, with an operator-visible log), and cleared on session
discard, process exit and stop. The drain was previously a stub that always
answered empty; it now returns and consumes that session's queued text.

Bridges that do not implement `queueMidTurnMessage` keep the `collect`
fallback so a message is never lost.

* test(channels): cover mid-turn injection and queue draining

Pin the inject routing (delivered to the running turn, no cancel, no
buffering), the collect fallback for bridges without the capability, and
the unchanged collect/steer/followup modes. On the bridge side, pin
per-session drain-once semantics, unknown-session drops, the message-count
bound, and teardown clearing on discard and stop.

* feat(cli): accept inject as a channel dispatch mode

* fix(channels): report mid-turn queue rejections instead of claiming delivery

The inject dispatch path logged "delivered mid-turn message" for every
call, but the bridge can refuse to queue the text — a stale session, the
20-message cap or the 20,000-character cap — and the refusal was only
visible on stderr. The collect fallback was reached only when the bridge
lacked the method, so a full queue silently lost the message while the
log claimed it had been delivered.

The bridge now returns a receipt (`accepted`, or `accepted: false` with
`blank` / `unknown-session` / `capacity`), and the channel logs
"delivered" only for an accepted message. A rejected injection falls back
to the existing collect buffer with the notification the collect branch
already sends, bounded to the same 20 messages / 20,000 characters so the
fallback cannot pin unbounded text; when that fallback is full the
message is refused with an explicit log instead of a false receipt.
Bridges without the method keep the previous collect behaviour.

* fix(channels): bind mid-turn injections to the running turn

- Batch the mid-turn drain at the ACP consumer's cap (10) and keep the
  remainder queued, so a response can no longer hand over messages the
  child drops while the channel logged them delivered.
- Settle undrained injections at the turn boundary: prompt() snapshots
  what it never drained, and the channel takes them back and replays them
  as their own turn instead of leaking them into the next turn.
- Mark a collect-buffer replay with collectReplay and keep it out of the
  inject arm, so a parked message always becomes its own turn.
- Gate injection on isAuthorizedForSharedSession, and keep it out of
  turns it cannot represent: another chat's/thread's message under a
  collapsed session scope, a recognized slash command, an image message
  (refused visibly, text-only), a file attachment (buffered so its saved
  path reaches a turn), and messages arriving after an earlier one was
  parked in the fallback (arrival order is kept).
- Add the per-message onPromptInjected lifecycle hook and the fallback's
  shared bounds; an over-bound refusal is now told to the sender instead
  of being silently discarded.
- Drop queued injections with the collect buffer on cancel/clear/session
  death, and notify through onPromptBufferDropped.
- Share the queue bounds and drain batch through ChannelAgentBridge; the
  fallback char bound is a depth bound, so a single oversize message is
  buffered rather than refused.

* fix(email): reject dispatch modes the email adapter cannot honour

The email adapter's guard only rejected the literal 'collect', so the new
'inject' mode slipped through to a mode it cannot deliver. Whitelist the
TLS-only modes (followup/steer) and reject everything else with the
durable-claim reason.

* test(wecom): keep a mid-turn attachment until its replay turn

Pin the adapter-side invariant behind the inject fallback: a file message
that cannot be injected is buffered with its on-disk directory intact
until its own turn runs, so the saved path is still readable then.

Also derive the child's mid-turn drain cap from the shared batch
constant instead of a second literal.

* fix(channels): replay undrained mid-turn injections in arrival order

* fix(channels): report only undrained mid-turn messages as dropped on cancel

* fix(channels): keep mid-turn arrival order when a message is parked for the turn

* fix(channels): refuse mid-turn media only when it would be injected

* test(channels): pin mid-turn settlement, teardown and fallback invariants

* docs(channels): correct the inject replay-bound and email deliverable rationale

* test(channels): pin the mid-turn media-refusal placement

* docs(channels): describe the bounded fallback and oversize parking accurately

* fix(channels): refuse mid-turn media that a replay cannot carry, before parking

Inline image bytes cannot survive a collect replay: the replay envelope strips attachments and imageBase64, so parking such a message silently destroyed the picture with no notice to the sender. Refuse it visibly before the bridge-capability arm and every other parking gate. Media saved to a local path still parks, because its `saved to:` line is plain text that survives the replay.

* fix(channels): compose group-history context once for a rejected injection

A rejected injection parked the already-wrapped text, and the collect replay then wrapped it again: two context markers and two current-message markers with stale context between them. Peek the pending history to compose the injected text, drain it only after the bridge accepts the injection, and park the unwrapped prompt so the replay composes a single fresh wrapper.

* test(channels): pin cancel-path resets, failure settlement and bridge teardown

Cover the remaining mid-turn invariants: the rewritten media tests keep the recoverable-path park covered, a rejected injection composes one fresh group-history wrapper, the cancel drop releases the admission ledger and turn-scoped gates, a failed turn settles its queue in the finally, stop() and dropMidTurnMessages clear the settled slot, and the character bound rejects an oversize message on an empty queue.

* fix(email): treat null dispatchMode as unset and name the refused value

An explicit `dispatchMode: null` reached the whitelist as an unsupported value and failed startup, although the adapter treats it as unset and falls back to followup. Accept null alongside undefined, and name the offending value in the refusal so an operator can fix the config.

* docs(channels): correct the inject replay and media-parking contract

State that email accepts only steer and followup, that buffered inject messages are coalesced into one follow-up replay prompt, and that a cancelled, cleared or rotated turn discards its queued injections. Inline images are refused while inject mode has a running turn because a parked replay cannot carry them; attachments saved to a path are buffered with their path.

* fix(channels): compose one group-history wrapper when an undrained injection is replayed

An accepted injection recorded the wrapped text, so a turn that ended
before the bridge drained it replayed that text as its own turn and the
replay nested a second wrapper — stale backfill was presented as the
message to answer. Record the raw prompt text, matching the parked path;
the running turn still receives the wrapped text.

Also pin the round-5 reviewed contracts: peek/drain parity, the /clear and
session-death inject purges, the accepted-only lifecycle signal, the
settled-ledger and not-supported-notice resets, and email's effective
followup fallback. Document that inject needs operators on shared scopes,
and correct onPromptInjected's contract comment: injected messages are
text-only, and an undrained one replays with the replay envelope's IDs.

* fix(channels): keep refused mid-turn message text out of process logs

The bridge's capacity rejection appended sanitizeLogText(text, 256) to
stderr; that helper only strips controls and truncates, so private chat
text (and anything secret in it) landed in process logs while the caller
already owns a fallible collect fallback. Log metadata only — queue depth,
chars, and the rejected length — and do the same for the caller's
fallback-full refusal diagnostic, which had the sibling leak.

Both logs stay diagnosable from metadata; unit tests assert the refusal is
still logged and that a canary in the rejected text never appears.

---------

Co-authored-by: Shaojin Wen <shaojin.wensj@alibaba-inc.com>

prs.title: feat(web-shell): add conversation activity view
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a ChatGPT-inspired activity mode to the Web Shell sidebar for trusted workspace conversations on the selected daemon. It brings approval/input/error states, observed unread completions, running work, optional pinned/scheduled conversations and recent date groups into a stable attention queue. Rows, hover details, actions, section headers and spacing reuse the ordinary sidebar; display preferences, mark-all-read and confirmed bulk archive/undo are available from the first category's menu.

The detailed behavior was investigated by decompiling and inspecting ChatGPT desktop's bundled code and checking supplied screenshots. This is an independently adapted implementation using Qwen's existing catalog, live-state, transcript and archive infrastructure; no decompiled source is included. Reference screenshots are in the Issue, and implementation screenshots are below.

## Why it's needed

Users running conversations across several workspaces need to see what requires attention without opening every project. A snapshot keeps rows stable while work completes or gets read. Closes #16020.

### Why retain frontend read state?

| Approach | Benefits | Costs / limitations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Existing frontend memory | Same blue-dot semantics in both sidebar modes; works with existing daemons; marking read is immediate with no receipt requests, migrations or write failures | Reload/remount loses markers; completions not observed while offline cannot be reconstructed; tabs/devices do not synchronize |
| New backend read fields | Can retain acknowledgements across restarts and expose them to multiple clients | Requires storage/API/capability changes, user-vs-daemon ownership, historical migration, completion/turn identity and concurrency rules; retries and late writes create new failure paths; a generic session update timestamp is not proof of an unread completed turn |

This PR chooses memory-only state to keep activity a focused navigation feature and preserve the existing completion-dot contract. Reading previews never acknowledges a conversation; mark-all-read updates the same set as ordinary rows. The persistence work tracked in #11451 remains separate and open. PR #12672 independently proposes browser-local persistence, not backend receipts; overlapping sidebar changes need reconciliation if it lands first. The optional live turn-error field is unrelated to read state and supports old-daemon fallback.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Run several workspace conversations, including one waiting for input/approval and one that completes while another is open. Toggle the bell or Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+U. Priority should show actionable work first; already-visible rows stay stable as state changes.
2. Toggle Pinned and Scheduled in the first header's menu, collapse/expand Priority and Pinned, and reset with the icon beside Display. Pins, row actions, hover workspace details and spacing should match ordinary mode; reset leaves the menu open.
3. Open an unread conversation or mark all priority items read. Blue dots should agree between modes. Reopening activity rebuilds its snapshot; refreshing clears memory-only unread markers. There should be no read-receipt writes.
4. Confirm bulk archive, exercise partial failures, and undo successful items. Running-work confirmation is explicit; failed archives remain, and undo does not restart work. Switching conversations while an archive is pending must not redirect the new conversation.
5. Check both themes and short/tall windows. Recent dates, incremental row budgets, unavailable-source and preview-retry states should remain understandable. Row width and right inset must match even when only one mode needs a scrollbar.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: ordinary workspace/pinned navigation has no attention-oriented activity mode. After: the same rows and controls are grouped into a stable activity queue. Screenshots below use synthetic daemon fixtures, not personal conversations.

| Ordinary sidebar | Activity view |
| --- | --- |
| ![Ordinary sidebar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/a3542ffa310fc1becb2168a5823bcf47e5e9413e/docs/design/images/activity-view/normal.png) | ![Activity view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/a3542ffa310fc1becb2168a5823bcf47e5e9413e/docs/design/images/activity-view/activity.png) |

<details>
<summary>Display menu and dark theme</summary>

![Display menu and reset](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/a3542ffa310fc1becb2168a5823bcf47e5e9413e/docs/design/images/activity-view/options.png)

![Dark theme activity view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/a3542ffa310fc1becb2168a5823bcf47e5e9413e/docs/design/images/activity-view/dark.png)

</details>

On the submission base, 378 targeted unit tests passed (141 Web Shell, 212 workspace routes, 25 SDK), and the full activity Chromium suite passed 15/15 in 2.2 minutes. Dependency-install prepare built and bundled the repository successfully; committed files passed formatting and ESLint. Review follow-up: all 699 sidebar tests and the 15-case activity browser suite pass; archive pending/result/undo survives closing the view, and ordinary sidebar attention/freshness behavior is preserved. Full build/typecheck/bundle passed. Full preflight completed with two local SDK environment failures (proxy validation and a packed provider executable), so it is not claimed green. Current-head remote CI remains pending.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--: | :--: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ local unit/build checks and Chromium fixtures |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested locally |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ not tested locally |

### Environment

macOS arm64, Node 24, pinned pnpm 11.24.0. Browser coverage uses the complete Web Shell frontend with mocked daemon HTTP/SSE and transcripts; it is not a live model end-to-end run.

## Risk & Scope

- Main tradeoff: intentionally ephemeral unread state. Older daemons without the optional turn-error overlay provide best-effort error visibility. Trust, selected-host and workspace boundaries remain in force.
- Out of scope: standalone/no-workspace, Managed Agent, live voice, cross-host activity aggregation, offline unread recovery and cross-client acknowledgements.
- Breaking changes / migration: none; no backend read fields, receipt endpoints, read capability or migration. Display preferences alone persist locally.
- This is one vertical feature: the view/model/controller, shared sidebar integration, live-error overlay and their tests need to work together. Most added lines are regression coverage and bilingual documentation; splitting those from the feature would leave the delivered behavior unverified.

Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/a3542ffa310fc1becb2168a5823bcf47e5e9413e/docs/design/activity-view.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/a3542ffa310fc1becb2168a5823bcf47e5e9413e/docs/design/activity-view.zh-CN.md), synchronized.

## Linked Issues

Closes #16020. Related: #14901, #15421, #11451 and #12672. Draft for maintainer feedback on the new feature scope.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

为 Web Shell 侧栏增加参考 ChatGPT 的活动模式，聚合当前选中 daemon 下可信工作区的会话。审批/输入/错误、已观察到的未读完成、运行中任务、可选的置顶/定时会话和最近日期分组组成稳定的关注队列。会话行、悬浮详情、操作、分类标题与间距复用普通侧栏；显示选项、全部标为已读和需确认的批量归档/撤销集中于第一个分类菜单。

详细逻辑来自对 ChatGPT 桌面端打包代码的反编译分析及用户截图核对。实现按 Qwen 架构独立适配，复用已有目录、实时状态、转录和归档设施，不包含反编译源码。参考截图见 Issue，本次实现截图见上方。

## 为什么需要

多个工作区同时运行会话时，用户需要直接发现待关注事项，而不必逐个打开项目。快照让会话完成或已读时列表仍然稳定。解决 #16020。

### 为什么保留前端已读状态？

| 方案 | 优点 | 代价 / 限制 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 既有前端内存 | 两种侧栏共享蓝点语义；兼容现有 daemon；已读立即生效，无回执请求、迁移或写入失败 | 刷新/重新挂载丢失标记；无法恢复离线期间未观察到的完成；标签页/设备间不同步 |
| 新增后端已读字段 | 可跨重启保存回执并供多个客户端读取 | 需要存储/API/能力变更、用户或 daemon 所有权、历史迁移、完成/轮次身份与并发规则；重试和延迟写入增加失败路径；普通会话更新时间不等于存在未读完成轮次 |

本次选择纯内存，保持活动视图作为聚焦的导航功能，延续已有完成蓝点契约。预览读取不改变已读；全部标为已读修改普通行使用的同一个集合。本 PR 不解决 #11451。PR #12672 独立提出浏览器本地持久化，并非后端回执；若其先合入，需协调重叠的侧栏改动。可选的实时轮次错误字段与已读无关，兼容旧 daemon 回退。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 在多个工作区运行会话，包括待输入/审批以及在另一会话打开期间完成的任务。点击铃铛或 Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+U；优先处理先显示待操作事项，已出现的行随状态改变保持稳定。
2. 在首个分类菜单切换置顶/定时任务，折叠展开优先处理与置顶，再通过“显示”旁图标恢复默认。置顶、行操作、悬浮工作区详情和间距应与普通模式一致；重置后菜单仍打开。
3. 打开未读会话或全部标为已读；两模式蓝点保持一致。重新打开活动重建快照，刷新清除内存未读标记，不应出现已读回执写请求。
4. 确认批量归档，验证部分失败并撤销成功项目。运行中任务有明确确认，失败项保留，撤销不重启任务。归档等待期间切换会话，不应把新会话导航走。
5. 检查浅深色和高低窗口。最近日期、增量行预算、来源不可用和预览重试状态清晰；即便只有一种模式需要滚动条，行宽与右侧留白也一致。

### 证据（前后对比）

之前：普通工作区/置顶导航没有关注事项活动模式。之后：复用相同行和控件组成稳定活动队列。上方截图使用模拟 daemon 数据，不含个人会话。

提交基线上，378 项定向单测通过（Web Shell 141、工作区路由 212、SDK 25），完整活动视图 Chromium 套件 15/15 通过，耗时 2.2 分钟。依赖安装的 prepare 阶段已成功完成仓库构建与打包，提交文件格式和 ESLint 通过。评审修复后，完整侧栏699项与活动浏览器15项通过；归档pending/result/undo可跨关闭保留，普通侧栏提醒/新鲜度行为保持。全仓构建/类型检查/打包通过。完整preflight结束时有两项本地SDK环境失败（代理校验、打包provider可执行文件），因此不宣称全绿；当前提交远端CI仍待完成。

### 测试平台

| OS | 状态 |
| :--: | :--: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ 本地单测/构建及 Chromium 模拟场景 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未本地验证 |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 未本地验证 |

### 环境

macOS arm64、Node 24、固定 pnpm 11.24.0。浏览器覆盖完整 Web Shell 前端，使用模拟 daemon HTTP/SSE 和转录，不是真实模型端到端运行。

## 风险与范围

- 主要取舍：未读状态有意保持内存态。旧 daemon 缺少可选轮次错误覆盖时，错误显示尽力回退。信任、当前主机及工作区边界保留。
- 不在范围内：无工作区会话、Managed Agent、实时语音、跨主机活动聚合、离线未读恢复和多端回执。
- 破坏性变更/迁移：无；不增加后端已读字段、回执接口、读取能力或迁移，仅显示偏好在本地持久化。
- 这是一个完整纵向功能：视图/模型/控制器、共享侧栏集成、实时错误覆盖及测试需要配合工作。新增行大部分为回归覆盖和双语文档；将其与功能拆开会让交付行为缺少验证。

设计：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/a3542ffa310fc1becb2168a5823bcf47e5e9413e/docs/design/activity-view.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/a3542ffa310fc1becb2168a5823bcf47e5e9413e/docs/design/activity-view.zh-CN.md)，内容已同步。

## 关联 Issue

解决 #16020。相关：#14901、#15421、#11451 和 #12672。以 Draft 征求维护者对新功能范围的反馈。

</details>

prs.title: fix(sandbox): install fonts-dejavu-core so capture cards render legibly
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds one font package (`fonts-dejavu-core`) to the runtime stage of the sandbox image, so the monospace family the capture-card renderer asks for actually resolves inside the sandbox.

## Why it's needed

`scripts/verify-capture.mjs` renders its cards with `font-family="DejaVu Sans Mono,Menlo,Consolas,monospace"`, but the runtime stage installed no fonts at all: the `apt-get install` list holds 17 packages and none of them is a font (`grep -ic font Dockerfile` = 0). Anything rendered inside the sandbox therefore falls back to whatever the base image happens to have, and the card is not the monospace layout the renderer asks for. This is the deferred review finding `ic:5747631789` from PR #11963 (issue #12325); the other three findings in that batch are out of scope here.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. `grep -n fonts-dejavu-core Dockerfile` — the package is in the runtime stage's `apt-get install` list, and no previously installed package was removed.
2. `git diff main -- Dockerfile` — the change is the single install-list line (one insertion, zero deletions).
3. Build the runtime stage and check the font file is present: `/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono.ttf`.
4. `scripts/verify-capture.mjs` is untouched, so the SVG still requests `DejaVu Sans Mono` and now has a provider for it.

### Evidence (Before & After)

- Before (live main `06c1f989715fa812fc26258525ef97627c15b855`): the runtime install list has no font package; `grep -ic font Dockerfile` → `0` (exit 1).
- After (this branch): `fonts-dejavu-core` is in the same list; diff is `1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)`.

Stated plainly, not hidden: the image-level check (item 3 above) was **not executed** in this pass — the local sandbox-image build did not complete within this round's budget, so the evidence above is file-level only. Item 3 is the check a reviewer should run; I am not claiming it passed.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   N/A  |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅ (file-level evidence only; image build not run) |

### Environment (optional)

N/A — Dockerfile-only change, no runtime code and no unit tests.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the sandbox image grows by the `fonts-dejavu-core` package and its dependencies (roughly a few MB). No other package is removed, and no other image layer changes.
- Not validated / out of scope: an image build was not run in this pass, so the installed font file was not observed in a built image. The other three deferred findings from PR #11963 are untouched.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; existing images keep working, the change only adds a font family the renderer already requests.

## Linked Issues

Refs #12325

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

给沙箱镜像的 runtime 阶段加一个字体包 `fonts-dejavu-core`，让截图卡片渲染器请求的等宽字体在沙箱里真能解析到。

`scripts/verify-capture.mjs` 用 `font-family="DejaVu Sans Mono,Menlo,Consolas,monospace"` 画卡片，但 runtime 阶段装了 17 个包、一个字体包都没有（`grep -ic font Dockerfile` = 0），沙箱里渲染只能用基础镜像碰巧带的字体，卡片不是渲染器要的等宽版式。这是 PR #11963 遗留的评审发现 `ic:5747631789`（issue #12325），同批另外三条 finding 不在本 PR 范围。

验证方式：① `grep -n fonts-dejavu-core Dockerfile` 命中且没有删掉原有包；② diff 只有这一行（+1/-0）；③ 构建 runtime 阶段后确认 `/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSansMono.ttf` 存在；④ `scripts/verify-capture.mjs` 未改动。

明确说明：第 ③ 条镜像级核对这一轮**没有执行**——本地沙箱镜像构建没在预算内跑完，上面的证据只到文件级。这一条留给 reviewer，我没有声称它通过。

风险：镜像体积增加该字体包及其依赖（数 MB 量级），不删除任何原有包；无破坏性变更。

</details>
