## Breaking Changes

No known breaking changes.

## Complete Change List

### Features

- Adds bounded SQL history queries for Managed local H2 and Hosted MySQL, enabling paged recent messages, journal transactions, and exact operation or command lookups. ([#15839](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15839)) by @doudouOUC
- Enables Generated UI by default and lets users continue chatting with interactive card values attached as removable context above the composer. ([#15856](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15856)) by @qqqys
- feat(web-shell): keyboard shortcuts for Session Overview and Split View ([#14179](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14179)) by @4ekuct25
- Adds a Russian locale for the Web Shell Goal card and Goals dialog, with English fallback for untranslated strings. ([#13685](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13685)) by @4ekuct25
- Extends Web Shell one-click daemon updates to pnpm, yarn, bun, and sudo-prefixed npm installs, and shows manual steps when automatic update is unavailable. ([#15849](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15849)) by @wenshao
- Web Shell and Qwen Code Desktop now show active background agent counts in the status-bar task pill while agents are running. ([#14002](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14002)) by @4ekuct25
- Managed WebShell now reads the latest 100 live items directly and pages upward for older messages, while live updates continue. ([#15865](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15865)) by @doudouOUC
- The /verify-pr local flow now reuses the current working tree only when it is a clean checkout of the PR head and records round details. ([#15913](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15913)) by @wenshao
- Archived conversations in Settings now show Export conversation and Restore inline beside More, making archive management faster. ([#15872](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15872)) by @deggs7
- PR watch now merges a stale base before attempting fixes when CI failures may be caused by the branch being behind. ([#15922](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15922)) by @wenshao
- Adds an experimental one-command Helm deployment for Managed Agent with Hosted Harness, MySQL, local execution, and an authenticated gateway. ([#15492](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15492)) by @doudouOUC
- Adds --in-place mode to the PR-watch skill to co-drive in your checkout, push the branch, and reply on the PR. ([#15929](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15929)) by @wenshao
- Keeps skill slash-command argument hints visible while typing and shrinks them to missing arguments. ([#15930](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15930)) by @wenshao
- Makes context memory files in the Context Usage panel clickable to open read-only previews such as AGENTS.md. ([#15932](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15932)) by @wenshao
- Makes autofix-pr post a pull-request comment when a round is blocked, stating what was attempted, what blocks it, and what human action is needed. ([#15978](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15978)) by @wenshao
- Adds a retry budget to /autofix-pr so a check left failing after three fix pushes is handed to a human and shown in /autofix-pr status. ([#15985](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15985)) by @wenshao
- Adds a Workflow switch in Web Shell, split panes, and VS Code chat to update saved session Workflow preferences for the next turn without interrupting responses. ([#15779](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15779)) by @qqqys
- Enables channel adapters to expose tools to agent sessions and adds QQ moderation tools, including recall, mute, kick, and join approval, controlled by moderationTools. ([#14348](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14348)) by @Eric-GoodBoy-Tech
- Adds a batch request and SDK method to fetch live-session snapshots for up to 20 selected workspaces in one call. ([#12513](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/12513)) by @XIQIXIQIXIQI
- feat(cli): support exact-version updates without npm discovery ([#11486](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/11486)) by @XIQIXIQIXIQI
- Improves the bundled code-review skill by re-anchoring after head drift, running actionlint checks, accounting for blockers, and refusing retries. ([#16001](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16001)) by @wenshao

### Bug Fixes

- Hardens the managed-agent upgrade command's check, backup, install, start, and verify phases, including cleanup after interrupted installs. ([#15853](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15853)) by @wenshao
- TUI CI now runs impact-selected checks and reserves full source TUI acceptance for nightly runs, manual dispatch, and high-risk changes. ([#15864](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15864)) by @yiliang114
- Main pushes now run one macOS E2E shard instead of two, while schedules, manual dispatch, and feat/e2e branches keep the two-shard matrix. ([#15873](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15873)) by @yiliang114
- The Web Shell floating approval card for tool approvals now uses a single scroll region, avoiding nested scrollbars in long diffs. ([#14621](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14621)) by @4ekuct25
- Release builds and eligible downstream jobs now use labelled runners on existing ECS hosts to reduce hosted-runner queue delays. ([#15832](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15832)) by @yiliang114
- CUA input, window selection, and session cleanup align with 0.27.0 across CUA SDK, Browser SDK, and Node REPL for more reliable sessions. ([#15784](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15784)) by @LaZzyMan
- Review command tests now pin ghApiAllNested pagination and response merging behavior to prevent regressions in GitHub API requests. ([#12560](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/12560)) by @indexGin
- The No-workspace sessions header now matches Pinned, Workspaces, and Recent with consistent height, muted text, spacing, chevron, and hover/focus behavior. ([#15897](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15897)) by @deggs7
- E2E builds now use the same pool-first runner routing and disk gate as other jobs, reducing hosted queue delays for post-merge test signals. ([#15885](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15885)) by @yiliang114
- Web Shell browser smoke tests now run on isolated ubuntu-latest runners to avoid shared-runner network failures. ([#15886](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15886)) by @yiliang114
- Web Shell now hides the No-workspace sessions sidebar section when it loads empty, matching Pinned behavior. ([#15916](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15916)) by @deggs7
- fix(web-shell): keep "+ Add session" clickable when the catalog is empty ([#15835](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15835)) by @2SinceJuly
- fix(ci): weight PR owner assignment by open issue load ([#15194](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15194)) by @DragonnZhang
- fix(cli): separate instruction files from auto memory in context usage ([#15863](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15863)) by @callmeYe
- fix(core): skip memory imports of files already loaded as context files ([#15687](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15687)) by @tneemo
- fix(core): retry bodyless 400 responses instead of treating them as fail-fast ([#15821](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15821)) by @Andrea-Bruno
- fix(cli): share hosted harness deadlines and bail after CI retries ([#14752](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14752)) by @zonemeen
- fix(web-shell): prune split panes whose session left the active catalog ([#14577](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14577)) by @4ekuct25
- fix(core): stop the session LSP client on Config shutdown ([#14778](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14778)) by @he-yufeng
- Session messaging guidance now explains safe-mode suppression or missing peer addresses without implying recipients do not exist. ([#13948](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13948)) by @haomint
- Memory writes now report omitted index entries and scan-cap omissions separately, with sample names and preserved warnings. ([#14937](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14937)) by @jabrailkhalil
- Web Shell tool-card diffs now wrap long lines so diffs with long comments or paths scroll vertically instead of showing per-line horizontal scrollbars. ([#13272](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13272)) by @ifan855
- /context now displays token counts of one million or more as millions in terminal, plain text, and OpenTUI views. ([#13237](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13237)) by @Shizoqua
- Fixed a CLI test-suite build failure by completing the settle-budget rename in hosted harness tests. ([#15935](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15935)) by @wenshao
- The sandboxed /verify-pr publisher now runs the artifact check itself and marks the round inconclusive if the check fails or cannot run. ([#15938](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15938)) by @wenshao
- Startup probe now separates broker write failures from wrong topic type, giving clearer fail-fast guidance and mqadmin remedy. ([#15941](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15941)) by @wenshao
- Fixes /verify-pr publishing to use the newest round and updates skill text to match CI harness-fault behavior. ([#15966](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15966)) by @wenshao
- Queues peer-controller registry writes from the same process before taking the cross-process file lock to reduce lock contention and make concurrent updates more reliable. ([#15971](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15971)) by @wenshao
- fix(managed-agent): stop a drained pool owner's not-found from retiring automations ([#15990](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15990)) by @wenshao
- Routes helper-test temporary files to the runner data-disk temp directory to prevent CI failures caused by a small host /tmp tmpfs. ([#15979](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15979)) by @yiliang114
- Exempts non-TUI package trees from the parity and no-flicker gates so PRs touching only them skip those lanes. ([#15937](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15937)) by @yiliang114
- Fixes session-commit registration when an absolute cd or pushd resolves to the same repository or a subdirectory, keeping commits tracked. ([#15953](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15953)) by @yiliang114
- isAoneHostFamily now uses the shared host normalizer so review remote matching and write routing judge Aone hosts consistently. ([#15934](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15934)) by @yiliang114
- fix(vscode): gate the companion vitest worker cap on the shared pool ([#15940](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15940)) by @yiliang114
- Peer-controller registry writers now wait up to 8s for a contended lock and can take over a crashed holder's lock without losing writes. ([#15992](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15992)) by @wenshao
- The CLI now requests consent for native extension commands before direct installation in OpenTUI; replacement or unmount cancels pending requests. ([#15947](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15947)) by @chiga0
- Fixes managed-agent cancellation, Maven embedding, Hosted fault testing, and SDK stream-idle recovery so verification flows behave reliably. ([#15927](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15927)) by @doudouOUC
- Makes each /verify round publish and update only its own status comment instead of overwriting other verification comments. ([#15988](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15988)) by @wenshao
- Fixes deep-verification reports so the verdict line stays a plain paragraph and the published comment is verified against the intended body. ([#16002](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16002)) by @wenshao
- Adds the missing development proxy for autofix-pr routes so the PR watches page reaches the daemon. ([#16004](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16004)) by @wenshao
- Updates MCP client and core to 2.4.0 to drop pre-bundled fast-uri 3.1.0 and improve dependency auditability. ([#15925](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15925)) by @yiliang114
- Uses the automatic GitHub job token for release publish checkout, reducing authentication failures while keeping PAT for branch push and release creation. ([#15730](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15730)) by @qwen-code-dev-bot
- Adds isolation so /verify-pr mutation matrix runs in its own tree and never on live measured cells. ([#15999](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15999)) by @wenshao
- Fixes /verify-pr PR badge binding when a flag is glued directly to the PR number, such as 15979--publish. ([#15989](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15989)) by @wenshao
- Extends built-in reasoning effort to DeepSeek-V4 and new Qwen prefixes while keeping explicit overrides. ([#15987](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15987)) by @wenshao
- Reports a registry that keeps changing during a write as PeerControllerError with code registry-changed and a retry message. ([#16007](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16007)) by @wenshao

### Performance

- Release builds now reuse verified native audio prebuilds from matching successful main releases to skip redundant native builds. ([#15854](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15854)) by @yiliang114

### Documentation

- Managed agent upgrade docs now state that SIGKILL skips cleanup and leaves a temporary upgrade directory that operators should remove. ([#15878](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15878)) by @wenshao
- Updated CI documentation to match the actual qwen-autofix job timeout and worst-case budget values. ([#15914](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15914)) by @yiliang114
- Adds a bilingual Managed Agent server configuration reference generated from server metadata to keep it current. ([#15939](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15939)) by @wenshao
- Adds a bilingual Managed Agent design document with a structure review and staged refactor proposal. ([#15942](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15942)) by @wenshao
- Reorganizes the bilingual Managed Agent deployment guide into three tiers for first-time deployments. ([#15944](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15944)) by @wenshao
- Adds documentation proposing scheduled /autofix-pr --in-place rounds that report findings and require explicit approval before editing. ([#15960](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15960)) by @wenshao
- Updates Managed Agent server docs to link setting tables to the generated configuration reference instead of duplicating settings. ([#15965](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15965)) by @wenshao
- Clarifies artifacts.read-timeout documentation to qualify storage stall behavior and retain the per-row lease note. ([#15980](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15980)) by @wenshao
- Managed-agent docs now note that private CSI sessions record no committed tool receipts and correct lease wording for artifacts.enabled. ([#16000](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16000)) by @wenshao
- Updates managed-agent documentation to describe extracted collaborators and reconciliation prerequisites without changing behavior. ([#16012](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16012)) by @wenshao
- Documents the ManagedAgentStore setter investigation and its Spring injection findings. ([#16014](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16014)) by @wenshao

### Internal Changes

- Updates Web Shell smoke tests to use the renamed Add workspace dialog and Workspaces sidebar label. ([#15860](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15860)) by @wenshao
- Adds a regression gate for managed-agent failover that verifies recovery when a replacement host loses its first takeover-load reply. ([#15857](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15857)) by @wenshao
- Managed public items, transcripts, recent history, and export now use bounded current-message paging instead of persisted snapshots. ([#15870](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15870)) by @doudouOUC
- Hosted fault tests now use Managed JDBC stores so identity handling matches production and avoids false test failures. ([#15882](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15882)) by @yiliang114
- Web shell test setup now selects the retained radio via keyboard focus and Space, making Generated UI retention checks more stable. ([#15896](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15896)) by @yiliang114
- Hosted recovery and transcript fixtures now follow current cancellation, cleanup, and transcript-event contracts for more reliable managed recovery tests. ([#15899](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15899)) by @yiliang114
- Web shell recovery tests now include transcript coverage and temporary storage routing so recovered sessions show confirmed answers and latest requests. ([#15883](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15883)) by @yiliang114
- Improved managed-agent test reliability by retrying expected 503 projection-pending reads during coordinator restart checks. ([#15910](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15910)) by @yiliang114
- Managed tests now count cancellation takeovers only after successful HTTP acceptance while recording all load attempts. ([#15912](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15912)) by @yiliang114
- Managed Agent Server is now organized into Maven modules while remaining a single executable service. ([#15871](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15871)) by @doudouOUC
- Managed crash-recovery validation now treats targeted cleanup loads as non-resuming recovery while still requiring cancellation takeover. ([#15926](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15926)) by @yiliang114
- Adds a failover test verifying Managed Agent recovery when a generation crashes before committing assistant output. ([#15881](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15881)) by @wenshao
- Managed Agent session creation now uses a single SessionCreationCommand and fails closed when workspace creation is unsupported. ([#15955](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15955)) by @wenshao
- Adds an E2E fault test ensuring Managed Agent recovers correctly when Harness crashes between sibling approvals. ([#15945](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15945)) by @wenshao
- Restores classifier-driven web-shell smoke routing to self-hosted ARM64 for admitted runs, with ubuntu-latest fallback for fork PRs. ([#15961](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15961)) by @yiliang114
- Adds test evidence and documentation pins for the A3 original-plan count and corrects related prose without changing production behavior. ([#15977](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15977)) by @wenshao
- Splits AgentStateStore into six role interfaces so managed-agent components can depend on narrower session-state contracts without behavior changes. ([#15962](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15962)) by @wenshao
- Tightens CI checks so the Runtime Broker fault gate only relies on Hosted process setup steps that cannot be skipped or ignored after failure. ([#15964](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15964)) by @wenshao
- Adds a CI fault scenario that crashes the managed-agent harness after earlier tool rounds to verify recovery of round, cost, and token state. ([#15981](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15981)) by @wenshao
- Adds tests confirming Aliyun OSS tool-publication object open operations retry transient service errors and client timeouts before succeeding. ([#15983](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15983)) by @wenshao
- Refactors Runtime Broker by extracting the UNKNOWN-execution lookup cooldown into a dedicated component without changing behavior. ([#15986](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15986)) by @wenshao
- Routes the Lint & Static lane to self-hosted ECS runners for all pull requests, including forks, while preserving timeout and override controls. ([#15974](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15974)) by @yiliang114
- Fixes Hosted attachment and harness-client lookups for decorated HarnessConnector beans by resolving the underlying connector state. ([#15984](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15984)) by @wenshao
- qwen review drive now builds its not-started unavailable report from one factory, keeping zero values and notes unchanged. ([#15943](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15943)) by @yiliang114
- Managed-agent recovery tests now verify B2 replacement attempt and stream identities, blanked retracted prefixes, and the live SSE view. ([#15993](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15993)) by @wenshao
- The review-salvage replay test now derives the supersede kill-dir prefix from the workflow text, preventing the stub glob from drifting. ([#15963](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15963)) by @yiliang114
- Refactors managed-agent runtime hold inventory handling without changing user-visible behavior. ([#15997](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15997)) by @wenshao
- Adds tests pinning private CSI receipt guards and applies a follow-up managed-agent design correction. ([#16011](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16011)) by @wenshao
- Adds tests covering managed-agent lapsed-lease ledger writes and result-store wiring, with no direct user-facing change. ([#16018](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16018)) by @wenshao

issues.title: [BUG] Custom openai-compatible provider: output budget clamped to the hosted-catalog ceiling (32K for qwen3.8-27b) even though the server accepts 262K — reasoning models return empty terminal stops

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [ ] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What happened? 发生了什么？

## What happened?
When a provider is configured as `kind = "openai-compatible"` in front of an
**operator-owned vLLM server** (e.g. a lab proxy), the output budget sent to the
server is clamped to the **hosted** catalog row's `limit.output` — **32768 tokens
for `qwen3.8-27b`** — even though the server itself accepts far more.

Verified against the real server (vLLM 0.32.0): `max_tokens = 131072`, `262144`
and `262000` are all accepted (HTTP 200, `finish_reason=stop`). The runtime still
emits `max_tokens=32768`.

With a reasoning model at `reasoning_effort: high` or `xhigh`, the model spends
the entire 32K allowance on hidden reasoning and never produces visible text. The
server returns a terminal `stop` with no answer, and the turn fails after two
retries:

> Model returned terminal stop reason `stop` with no answer or tool call
> (after 2 retries)

This makes long sub-agent tasks (reviews, planning, verification) fail reliably
end-to-end.

## Root cause (traced in the code)

1. The embedded model catalog (`crates/config/assets/models_dev.bundled.json`)
   declares for `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`:
   ```json
   "limit": { "context": 262144, "output": 32768 }
   ```
2. `route_budget.rs::effective_max_output_tokens_for_route` intersects the
   requested cap with the compatibility cap. For a Custom provider, the
   catalog-derived `max_output` (32768) is applied, so every request goes out
   with `max_tokens=32768`.
3. The same failure shape — reasoning consuming the entire output allowance,
   zero visible text — is already documented in `route_budget.rs` for another
   route class (#6285).

Custom providers are operator-owned endpoints, like the Ollama / SGLang / VLLM
routes that already have an operator-owned allowlist in
`route_declares_unknown_output_ceiling` — but **Custom itself is not in that
allowlist**, so a catalogued model name is still clamped by the hosted row.

## Expected behavior

For custom `openai-compatible` endpoints in front of operator-owned engines, use
the operator's real serving ceiling instead of the hosted-catalog `limit.output`:

- Add `ProviderKind::Custom` to the operator-owned allowlist in
  `route_declares_unknown_output_ceiling` (alongside Ollama / SGLang / VLLM).
- Honor the catalog's `generation_default` when present, otherwise the generic
  automatic cap.
- Keep the window-relative `ContextBudget` clamp as the hard cap (never raise
  any cap, only stop under-clamping).
- Unify the "custom" label with the existing `Unverified`/`RouteDeclaredUnknown`
  provenance so receipts stay truthful.
- Run `cargo test route_budget` (and add a regression test for the Custom route
  with a catalogued model name).

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

1. Configure a provider:
   ```toml
   [providers.myqwen]
   kind = "openai-compatible"
   base_url = "https://your-vllm-host/api"
   model = "qwen3.8-27b"
   ```
2. Run any task at `reasoning_effort = "high"` or `"xhigh"` (e.g. a review or
   planning sub-agent).
3. Observe the repeated empty terminal stop and the failed turn.
4. Compare the emitted request (`max_tokens=32768`) with the server's accepted
   values (`262144` works).

## Environment

- **Codewhale version**: 0.10.2 (main @ 44007bf)
- **Where**: TUI + sub-agents
- **OS**: FreeBSD
- **Channel**: built from source
- **Provider / model**: custom openai-compatible → `qwen3.8-27b` (vLLM 0.32.0)

### Codewhale version 版本

Codewhale  0.10.2

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

TUI (terminal interface)

### Operating system 操作系统

Other

### How did you get Codewhale? 获取方式

Cargo (crates.io)

### Provider and model 提供商和模型

_No response_

### Terminal and shell 终端

_No response_

### codewhale doctor (optional)

```text

```

### Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

## Extra notes

- Same failure class as #6285; related budget work: #5518, #5820, #6540, #5461.
- Workaround today: set `CODEWHALE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=262144` (env) or lower
  `reasoning_effort`.
- Optional separate change: correct the catalog `limit.output` for
  `qwen/qwen3.8-27b` (32768 → 262144) with fresh server evidence.
- I searched existing issues: no open issue or PR covers this case (searched:
  qwen, qwen3.8, 27b, empty stop, output cap, vllm ceiling, custom endpoint).

issues.title: tui: one send answered twice — the same user message is persisted bare and again with <turn_meta>, so every save re-branches
issues.body:
## Summary

One user send can run two engine turns and produce two different assistant replies. The journal shows why: the same user text is persisted twice, in two different shapes — once as bare text, once with a `<turn_meta>` tail — as sibling entries under the same parent. Because the save path compares the persisted branch with the live transcript by strict `Message` equality, a bare copy and a `<turn_meta>` copy of the same text never match, and each save re-branches the journal instead of appending to it.

This is deterministic. It needs no token threshold, no wall clock and no resume, which is what distinguishes it from the re-root trigger left unestablished in #7142.

## Impact

- **One send is answered twice.** The two replies are not a re-render: their texts differ (measured similarity 0.154; 1103 and 234 characters).
- **The persisted active path drops earlier assistant turns.** In one session document, 1231 journal entries backed an active path of only 53 entries, and every historical assistant reply was off-path; the only on-path assistant entries were the tool steps of the turn in flight.
- **Resuming such a session replays user turns without their answers.** The record still contains everything — the leaf simply does not reach it.

## Evidence

Sanitized from one session document on Windows 11 with a 0.10.x build. No third-party tooling is involved and no session content is reproduced here.

Timeline for a single send, offsets from the first write of that message:

```
t0        user       bare text of the message
t0+0.06   user       (injected server instructions)
t0+0.11   user       (injected server configuration)
t0+7.7    assistant  reply A, 1103 chars
t0+7.7    user       the same message text again, bare, appended after reply A
t0+9.8    user       the same message text with a <turn_meta> tail
t0+14.5   assistant  reply B, 234 chars, parented to the <turn_meta> copy
```

Census over the whole document:

- 83 groups of byte-identical entries: 21 `user`, 62 `assistant`.
- 10 pairs of sibling entries whose only difference is the presence of a `<turn_meta>` tail — same parent, written 1.2–2.1 s apart.
- One message appears 4 times, two of those writes 0.5 µs apart and chained as parent/child, so a single append loop wrote both.

## Mechanism

Both sides persist the same user text, but not the same `Message`:

1. `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/dispatch.rs` — `prepare_user_dispatch` pushes the bare text into `app.api_messages` and immediately saves a checkpoint built from it.
2. `crates/tui/src/core/engine/turn_loop/preparation.rs` — the engine pushes `user_text_message_with_turn_metadata(...)`, so its copy of the same text carries the `<turn_meta>` tail.
3. `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs` — `apply_engine_session_projection` mirrors the engine copy back through `app.set_api_messages(...)`.
4. `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/frame.rs` — `build_session_snapshot` re-branches the journal onto `app.api_messages`.
5. `crates/runtime/src/session_tree.rs` — `rebranch_active_messages_stamped` computes

   ```rust
   let shared_prefix = active_path
       .iter()
       .zip(messages)
       .take_while(|(entry, message)| entry.kind.projects_to(message))
       .count();
   ```

   and for a `Message` entry `projects_to` is exact equality:

   ```rust
   Self::Message { message: own } => own == message,
   ```

A bare copy and a `<turn_meta>` copy of one text are therefore never equal. The shared prefix stops at the first entry whose shape flipped, `leaf_id` moves back to that entry's parent, and the remainder of the transcript is appended as a sibling branch. The previous copy stays behind as evidence, so the same message is now persisted twice and the leaf sits on the newer one.

The result is visible downstream: `set_api_messages` already detects this discontinuity with

```rust
if unchanged == 0 && !self.api_messages.is_empty() && !messages.is_empty() {
    self.window_reroot_cause = Some("engine_projection");
}
```

but only after the fact. Nothing prevents the second turn, and nothing reconciles the two shapes.

## Relationship to existing reports

- **#7142** describes the same visible degradation — a live window re-rooted mid-session, earlier turns unreachable, no seam summary, no lifecycle event — and explicitly leaves the trigger unestablished. This report supplies a deterministic trigger plus a second, independent symptom: one send answered twice.
- **#6367** (closed) is the same save path discarding branch structure.
- **#6842** concerns the same machinery from the memory-growth side, not model visibility.
- **#7095** is a different fault: there the last save does not flush, so the record itself is missing.

## Suggested fix

Two candidate shapes, in order of preference:

1. **One shape from the start.** Do not let `app.api_messages` carry a user message the engine will rewrite. Either the TUI composes the same `Message` the engine will store, or the engine stops adding a tail to the copy it persists and instead adds `<turn_meta>` only at request construction — the copy on disk should not differ from the copy on screen.
2. **Shape-insensitive comparison, narrowly scoped.** Keep both writes but make the re-branch comparison treat a message and the same message with its `<turn_meta>` tail as one entry. This is the smaller compile surface but leaves two shapes on disk for every later reader to reconcile.

Independently of either: a user send must not start a second turn when the transcript already contains that text at the leaf.

## What I have not established

- Whether the double turn bills a provider request twice. The replies differ, so a model call did happen twice; the cost detail is not measured.
- Whether every shape flip re-branches the whole history or only the tail. Entry counts suggest tail-only in most saves and whole-path in some; I have not isolated which condition selects each.
- Whether the flip alone accounts for every observed re-root, or only some of them. It is sufficient to produce one, not proved to be the only cause.
- No fix is claimed or proposed as tested here.

Reproduction and evidence are kept locally. I am happy to provide a sanitised session document or run any probe a maintainer asks for.

## Rules (applied to every sub-EPIC)

1. Behavior-preserving — extraction only, no command/UX behavior changes.
2. Trait-first — define the boundary interface before moving code (pattern: EPIC-006 `CommandContext`).
3. Compiles at every step — bottom-up extraction, workspace stays green at each commit.
4. CI gate — extracted crate must never depend on `codewhale-tui` (e.g. `cargo check -p codewhale-commands` pulls no TUI).
5. Deliver one independently verified PR per completed FEAT against current upstream main; keep parent EPICs open until their remaining work and acceptance criteria are complete.
6. Sequencing — EPIC-006 first, then 007/008, then 009, then 010.

## Developer fast loop

The whole point of this decomposition: once a sub-EPIC's crate exists (EPIC-006 Feature 3 and later), day-to-day development happens **entirely outside the TUI monolith** (\~700k lines). The TUI is only compiled when you explicitly need it — TUI integration tests, `cargo test --workspace`, or the final pre-PR validation.

```bash
cargo check -p codewhale-commands          # production change check — seconds, not minutes
cargo test -p codewhale-commands           # test loop — compiles only the commands crate + thin test binaries, never the TUI
cargo watch -x "check -p codewhale-commands"  # continuous check while editing (cargo-watch)
cargo nextest run -p codewhale-commands    # optional: parallel test runner, faster startup
```

Why this stays fast:

* `cargo build` / `cargo check` never compiles `#[cfg(test)]` code, so production iteration is bounded to the small crate.
* `cargo test` compiles each `tests/` file as its **own small binary crate** depending only on the public API — a production change recompiles/relinks only those thin binaries, in parallel.
* The Gherkin acceptance harnesses live in separate test binaries (or a dedicated acceptance crate), so thousands of acceptance-test lines are **never part of the production crate compile**.
* Small white-box unit tests that need private access stay inline — they are cheap and cannot live outside the crate.

**Acceptance criterion for every extracted crate:** `cargo test -p <crate>` must compile only that crate and its test binaries — if it pulls in `codewhale-tui`, the boundary was cut wrong.

The numbers and impact motivating this are documented in [#4991](<https://github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/4991>) (Discussion: Compilation times and the TUI crate monolith): 476k lines / 82% of the workspace in one crate, 8–16 min release builds, 30+ min test suite, 2–3 iterations per hour.

issues.title: conformance: prompt fixtures fail on any host that has the optional tools
issues.body:
### Summary

The prompt conformance family (`crates/tui/tests/fixtures/conformance/prompt/`) cannot pass on a host that has the optional host-probed tools installed. The pin file the check compares against — `host_probed_tools.golden.json` — has never existed in this repository, and nothing records it.

The `events` family does not have this problem, because it pins the recorded host's tool set before running. The `prompt` family does not pin, so its result depends on what the runner happens to have installed.

### The two families are not symmetric

`crates/tui/src/conformance/events.rs:300` pins the recorded host before the turn runs:

```rust
let _host_tools = codewhale_dependencies::pin_recorded_host_tools(recorded_host_tools(case));
```

`recorded_host_tools` reads `recorded_platform.host_tools` from the case file, and `pin_recorded_host_tools` (`crates/dependencies/src/lib.rs:396-412`) makes `host_tool_available` (`:375-388`) answer from that set for the thread. So every events case reproduces the recording host regardless of what the runner has — the events goldens do contain `image_ocr` and `pandoc_convert` even though the machines running them need not have tesseract or pandoc.

The prompt family has no equivalent:

```
$ git grep -n 'pin_recorded_host_tools\|recorded_platform' -- crates/tui/src/conformance/prompt.rs
(no output)
```

`capture_prefix` therefore records whatever the current host produced, because the catalog consults the live probe at `crates/tui/src/core/engine/tool_catalog.rs:308`, `:350` and `crates/tui/src/tools/registry.rs:1126`, `:1141`.

### What that produces

`crates/tui/src/conformance/prompt.rs:223-245` compares every host-probed definition this host produced against the pin:

```rust
let probed_path = dir.join("host_probed_tools.golden.json");
let mut pinned: BTreeMap<String, Value> = std::fs::read_to_string(&probed_path)
    .ok()
    .and_then(|text| serde_json::from_str(&text).ok())
    .unwrap_or_default();
let mut drift = Vec::new();
for (tool, definition) in &probed_seen {
    if pinned.get(tool) != Some(definition) {
        drift.push(tool.clone());
        pinned.insert(tool.clone(), definition.clone());
    }
}
if !drift.is_empty() {
    let merged = Value::Object(pinned.into_iter().collect());
    failures.record(
        "host_probed_tools",
        golden::check_golden(&probed_path, &golden::pretty(&merged))...
    );
}
```

The file has never existed at any commit on any ref:

```
$ git log --all --diff-filter=ADR --name-status -- '*host_probed_tools*'
(no output)
```

And none of the three prompt goldens contain any of the four tool names, so the fixtures were recorded on a host that offered none of them:

```
agent_suggest.tools.golden.json                 code_execution=no image_ocr=no js_execution=no pandoc_convert=no
plan_mode.tools.golden.json                     code_execution=no image_ocr=no js_execution=no pandoc_convert=no
trusted_project_instructions.tools.golden.json  code_execution=no image_ocr=no js_execution=no pandoc_convert=no
```

On a host with none of the four, the loop is empty, `drift` stays empty, the check is skipped (it prints `host cannot offer [...]; their pinned definitions were not checked`), and the family passes. On a host with any of them, `drift` is non-empty on the first run and `check_golden` (`crates/tui/src/conformance/golden.rs:66-91`) returns `missing golden ...` outside update mode. The family fails.

Re-recording does not resolve it durably. `CODEWHALE_CONFORMANCE_UPDATE=1` would write the *local* tool definitions into the pin, and those are version-dependent — a pandoc 2.x description and a pandoc 3.x description are different bytes — so the next contributor's machine drifts again, and the goldens become a function of whoever recorded last.

### The case files describe a host that did not do the recording

All nine case files carrying a `recorded_platform` block (six under `events/`, three under `prompt/`) declare the identical block:

```json
"recorded_platform": {
  "recorded_on": "macOS",
  "os": "macos",
  "shell": "/bin/bash",
  "sandbox_enforcement": "local_os",
  "no_new_privs_active": null,
  "host_tools": ["code_execution", "image_ocr", "js_execution", "pandoc_convert"]
}
```

For the events family this is live data and it does its job. For the prompt family it is inert — `prompt.rs` never reads it — and it contradicts the recordings, which plainly happened without those tools. So the field is misleading precisely where it is unused.

### Why this has not surfaced

No workflow runs this suite. The only `conformance` hit under `.github/workflows` is `pet.yml`, which is `workflow_dispatch`-only and exercises the Kotlin/Swift port under `pet/`. `CODEWHALE_CONFORMANCE_UPDATE` appears nowhere under `.github`, and `.gitignore` does not exclude the missing fixture. So the failure is only reachable by a contributor who runs the suite locally on a machine with those tools installed.

### Reproducing

On a machine with `pandoc`, `tesseract`, `node` and `python` on `PATH`:

```
$ cargo test -p codewhale-tui model_visible_prefix_bytes_match_goldens
```

The prompt cases fail on `host_probed_tools` with `missing golden .../host_probed_tools.golden.json`. On a machine with none of the four, the same command passes.

```
$ git log --all --diff-filter=ADR --name-status -- '*host_probed_tools*'
$ git grep -n 'pin_recorded_host_tools\|recorded_platform' -- crates/tui/src/conformance/prompt.rs
```

### Notes

- I am not proposing a fix. The two obvious directions — pin the prompt family the way events does, or drop the host-probed comparison from the prompt family — change different things about what the prompt goldens are supposed to guarantee, and that is a maintainer decision rather than a patch.
- Unrelated to #7153, which is about streaming during compaction.

issues.title: 0.10.3: stop re-sending the whole goal snapshot on every continuation pass, and give the model the honest context figure

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
Reporter's build: `codewhale 0.10.2 (dev)`; code read at `main` `ecd256c90`.

## Problem

Every automatic goal-continuation pass appends a new user message carrying the **entire**
`GoalSnapshot` as pretty-printed JSON. In a long operate-mode goal those blocks are never
superseded, never deduplicated, and grow as the goal accumulates notes. In one measured
session they became the largest single occupant of the model's live history.

Measured on a 10.8-hour operate-mode session (833 messages in the saved history, compacted
once — the history carries one "Earlier turns of this session were condensed" checkpoint):

- 13 continuation blocks, 135,916 characters of block text in total (mean 10,455).
- That is **45.5% of all message text** in the live history; the per-message `<turn_meta>`
  accounts for a further 16.4%, leaving 38.1% for the actual conversation.
- The last eight blocks were the same size — 11,852 characters each, including that
  message's 812-character `<turn_meta>` — and all eight arrived within the final 65
  messages, so the model re-read the same goal state at the moment its context was
  tightest.
- One block decomposes as: 8,972 characters of JSON (1,571 `objective`, identical every
  pass; 6,883 `advisories`; ~518 for every other field), 2,056 characters of fixed
  instruction text (the `GOAL_CONTINUATION_PROMPT` preamble plus the closing "Continuation
  pass #N" paragraph), 812 of `<turn_meta>`, and ~12 of Markdown/JSON framing.

### The second half of the defect: the only token number the model sees is a lifetime bill

`tokens_used` inside those blocks ran 391,812,347 → 480,189,075 and never resets, because
it is a durable lifetime counter — `crates/tui/src/runtime_threads/manager.rs:5276` adds
`input_tokens + output_tokens` for every turn (`:5283`), and compaction rewrites history
without touching the goal record. It is a billing volume, not a context measurement.

With automatic compaction enabled the model receives **no** context-fill number at all:
`crates/tui/src/core/engine/compaction.rs:207` returns `None` from `context_pressure_line`
whenever `compaction.enabled`. So the only token figure in front of the model is that
lifetime sum, sitting next to `token_budget: null`. In the same session the model then
concluded, in its own words, that its context was exhausted:

> "In each Goal Continuation message the runtime sends me a goal-state block, and it has a
> `tokens_used` field — currently ~480M. That is accumulated token spend for the session,
> not context-window occupancy. I read it as 'the context is finished' — and that was my
> inference, not a fact." (translated from the session's original Russian)

That is the failure this issue is about, in both halves: the block spends 45% of the live
history re-stating one goal, and the one number it does supply is a bill that reads like a
budget. Trimming the block alone would delete the misleading field without giving the model
anything true to replace it.

Where the block comes from:

- `crates/tui/src/tools/goal.rs:820` — `render_continuation_prompt` serializes the whole
  snapshot with `serde_json::to_string_pretty`, then prints "Continuation pass #N" after it.
- `crates/tui/src/tools/goal.rs:651` — `GoalSnapshot`; `tokens_used` at `:656`.
- `crates/tui/src/tools/goal.rs:449` — `MAX_ADVISORY_NOTES: usize = 16` (a function-local
  const inside `record_advisory` at `:445`); advisories are the model's own past
  `update_goal status: "advisory"` notes. `update_goal` returns the snapshot — advisories
  included — as its tool result (`json_result(&snapshot)` at `:1306`), so the model already
  receives them when it writes one.
- `crates/tui/src/core/engine.rs:5463` and
  `crates/tui/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs:5880` — the two dispatch sites that turn the
  rendered string into the next user message.

## What Codewhale should do

1. **Render the continuation block as a delta, not a snapshot.** Send `objective` on the
   first pass (or when it changed); on later passes send a compact state line instead.

   *Implementation note (this is the part that needs a decision):*
   `render_continuation_prompt(&GoalSnapshot, u32)` has no access to history today — it
   cannot tell whether a previous continuation block is still in the transcript. Two
   workable shapes:
   - use `continuation_index` (objective only when `<= 1`) — zero new state, but loses the
     objective if compaction folded the first block away; or
   - add one caller-supplied flag (e.g. `objective_in_history: bool`), which the two
     dispatch sites set from the live session — the engine already knows whether history
     was replaced by a compaction checkpoint.

2. **Drop model-useless telemetry.** `tokens_used`, `time_used_seconds`, `elapsed_seconds`
   and `continuation_count` are not inputs to any decision the model makes. The pass number
   is already printed in the sentence after the JSON ("Continuation pass #N"). If a spend
   figure must stay for the model, name it for what it is — `billed_tokens_lifetime` — and
   never leave it as the only token number beside `token_budget`.

3. **Stop re-serializing `advisories`.** They are the model's own words: `update_goal`
   already returns the snapshot, advisories included, at the moment it writes one, and the
   note stays in the transcript. At 16 entries they were 6,883 of the block's 8,972 JSON
   characters in the measurement above.

4. **Give the model the honest context figure, in the same `<turn_meta>` block it already
   reads.** One passive line, for example:

   ```
   Context: 82400 / 131072 tokens (62.9%); auto-compaction at 90%
   ```

   - Numbers come from machinery that already exists: `route_context_budget_with_window`
     and `crates/tui/src/context_report.rs` (the same canonical pressure estimate the
     context meter, the compaction gate and `/context` read). No new estimator.
   - Informational only. It must **not** say "run /compact" or ask the model to take over
     compaction — that was the legitimate objection in #5620 and the reason
     `context_pressure_line` was gated off. The engine stays the only force path.
   - Emitted whether or not automatic compaction is enabled; while it is enabled the line is
     the model's only view of its own window.
   - `<turn_meta>` is per-message append-only content, not the session-pinned prefix, so a
     number that changes every turn costs no cache hit (`docs/CACHE.md`).

   **This is the explicit ask to revisit #6425.** That issue was closed `NOT_PLANNED` on
   2026-10-25 with: "no model-facing context notice while auto-compaction is enabled …
   revisit if users report surprise compactions." The measured session above is such a
   report, and so are the open #7133 and #6721. What #6425 asked for is what this asks for;
   the difference is that the evidence now includes a model that diagnosed its own context
   as exhausted from a billing counter.

5. **Keep everything that steers:** `status`, `blocker`, `evidence`, `progress`, gap state
   (`last_gap_fingerprint`, `repeated_gap_count`) and the completion/verification
   instructions.

Expected effect on the measured session: the last block shrinks from 11,040 to roughly
2,600 characters (11,040 − 8,454 for `objective` and `advisories`), and across 13 passes
the saving is **up to** ~110k characters — ~27k tokens at the four-characters-per-token
heuristic. It is an upper bound: advisories are FIFO-capped at 16, so earlier blocks were
smaller than the 11,852-character ones measured at the end. The context line adds ~55
characters per user message.

**Scope boundary.** Trimming changes the model-facing rendering only. The durable
`thread_goals` record, the TUI status/progress surfaces and `update_goal`'s own tool output
keep `tokens_used` and `advisories`; nothing is deleted from storage.

## Where (surface)

TUI / engine — the goal loop's continuation prompt and `<turn_meta>`
(`TUI (terminal interface)`, and `Providers and models` for the budget fields).
`codewhale exec` and the Runtime API reach the same renderer through
`render_continuation_prompt`.

## Workarounds or other tools

Today the only workaround is to keep goals short, or to clear and recreate the goal so
`tokens_used` and `advisories` start over. Neither is discoverable, neither addresses the
repeated objective, and neither tells the model how full its window is.

## Evidence and reproduction

Any long goal session reproduces it; the saved session JSON is the record. To measure a
session of your own:

```python
import json, sys
d = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
text = ["".join(b.get("text", "") for b in m.get("content", [])) for m in d["messages"]]
blocks = [t for t in text if "## Active Goal State" in t]
print("messages:", len(text))
print("continuation blocks:", len(blocks))
print("block chars:", sum(map(len, blocks)), "of", sum(map(len, text)))
print("largest block:", max(map(len, blocks), default=0))
```

No session identifiers, host paths, or credentials are included. The measurement is from
the reporter's own saved session.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A continuation block no longer carries the whole snapshot: for an active goal whose
      earlier block is still in history, `render_continuation_prompt` output is < 4 KiB
      (unit test on the existing fixture).
- [ ] The block no longer contains `tokens_used`, `time_used_seconds`, `elapsed_seconds` or
      `continuation_count`, or a renamed field states its scope (`billed_`/`session_`); a
      test pins whichever shape is chosen.
- [ ] `advisories` are absent from the block, or bounded by a byte budget covered by a test.
- [ ] An active goal that reaches continuation pass 3 sends the objective at most once
      (test), and still sends it once after a compaction checkpoint replaces history.
- [ ] With automatic compaction enabled, a turn's `<turn_meta>` carries one line naming used
      tokens, the window total and the percentage, and that line contains no "/compact"
      instruction (test).
- [ ] `cargo test -p codewhale-tui goal` passes. The existing pins are updated in the same
      change: `crates/tui/src/tools/goal.rs:1599`
      (`assert!(prompt.contains("\"blocker\": null"))`) and `:2235`–`:2238`
      (which assert `"Goal Continuation"`, `"finish issue 2199"` — the objective — and
      `"Continuation pass #2"`). `shared_prompt_text_names_only_callable_tools` in
      `crates/tui/src/tools/canonical_action_tests.rs:106` stays green.

## Related

- #6425 — soft model-facing context notice under auto-compaction (closed `NOT_PLANNED`,
  2026-10-25, "revisit if users report surprise compactions"). **Point 4 above is the
  revisit**, requested on the trigger that decision named; the measured session is the
  report, together with the open #7133 and #6721.
- #6490 — spend and context visible to the model plus a pre-compaction notice (closed
  `NOT_PLANNED`; point 4 covers the context half only, not the spend/cost half).
- #6217 — model-facing `context_status` tool (closed `NOT_PLANNED`; a passive turn-meta line
  is the cheap version of the same number, without a new tool).
- #7133, #6721 — open reports of compaction trouble.
- #6011 — TUI usage/token accounting diagnostics (open, human-facing surface).

## Contributing

No pull request is attached. Happy to test a patch, or to review one.

## Open questions for maintainers

- Should `objective` be re-sent once after a compaction checkpoint, on the theory that the
  summary may have folded it? (I lean yes; a one-shot repeat costs ~1.5 KB per compaction.)
- Is `tokens_used` in the model-facing block useful to anyone today? If not, dropping it
  entirely is simpler than renaming it.
- Should the context line name the auto-compaction threshold as well, or only used/total?
- Should advisory notes be readable on demand through a `goal_status` tool instead of being
  pushed on every pass?

## 0.10.3 status — 2026-10-25

Runtime extraction continues under #5316. Verified recent moves include browser helpers ([cd6203e1d2](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/cd6203e1d2)) and credentials ([0c2ab7d577](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/0c2ab7d577)); current runtime size is 9,526 strict production lines / 15,121 file-level lines. <!-- /cw-0103-status-20261025 -->

---

Part of the runtime/TUI crate split. Read first: `docs/design/TUI_DECONSTRUCTION.md` and the mover `scripts/split/move-modules.py` (it `git mv`s a top-level module, edits the `mod` lines, adds the name to the TUI's single path-alias block in `crates/tui/src/lib.rs:143-152`, and sweeps stale path strings). A lowercase reading of this task is "move small files"; the point is that these are **runtime-side subsystems with already-clean boundaries** — process supervision, shell dispatch, credentials exchange, runtime policy/logging, feature registry — that belong in the headless crate and will grow there.

Run slices one at a time — do not stack two `RS-n` slices in one working tree.

## Goal

Move ten modules from `crates/tui/src/` into `crates/runtime/src/`. Each one has **zero upward references** today (verified by `scripts/split/module_graph.py --report`), so no ratchet entry changes; their only dependencies are modules already resident in `crates/runtime` (or each other):

- `child_env` (1,423 lines) — no deps
- `logging` (134) — no deps
- `external_credentials` (938) — no deps
- `dsh_credentials` (148) — depends on `external_credentials` (moves in this batch)
- `shell_dispatcher` (994) — depends on `host_terminal` (already in runtime)
- `runtime_policy` (167) — no deps
- `process_tree` (935) — no deps
- `features` (375) — no deps
- `runtime_log` (588) — no deps
- `working_set` (2,505) — depends on `workspace_discovery` (already in runtime)

## Plan

1. Dry-run first: `python3 scripts/split/move-modules.py --dry-run child_env logging external_credentials dsh_credentials shell_dispatcher runtime_policy process_tree features runtime_log working_set` — read the printed path sweep. `--dry-run` writes nothing.
2. Run it for real, one module list in one change.
3. `crates/tui/tests/feature_registry.rs:10` carries `#[path = "../src/features.rs"] mod features;`. Update the include to the new location (`../../runtime/src/features.rs`) or switch the test to the runtime export if `features` is made `pub` there. Keep `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` green — it is the `docs/features.toml` drift guard and must keep failing on flag drift.
4. `grep -rn 'crates/tui/src/\(child_env\|logging\|external_credentials\|dsh_credentials\|shell_dispatcher\|runtime_policy\|process_tree\|features\|runtime_log\|working_set\)' --include='*.rs'` must be empty (the sweep leaves CHANGELOG history alone; that is intended).
5. `python3 scripts/split/module_graph.py --check` — totals must be unchanged (these modules never counted). If a count moved, a real reference appeared; fix it, do not raise the baseline.
6. `scripts/split/widen.py` only if the compiler reports privacy errors from the move.

## Done when

- [ ] The ten modules live under `crates/runtime/src/` with `pub mod` lines in `crates/runtime/src/lib.rs`; the TUI's `mod` lines are gone and the alias block names all ten
- [ ] `crates/tui/src` no longer contains these files; no stale path strings outside CHANGELOG
- [ ] `cargo check` for both crates is clean and `feature_registry` passes
- [ ] Ratchet `--check` passes with **no** baseline edit

## Verification

```sh
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-runtime --all-targets --locked
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --locked
scripts/dev-test.sh runtime
scripts/dev-test.sh tui features
cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry --locked
python3 scripts/split/module_graph.py --check
```

Quote the real `test result: N passed; M failed` lines and the ratchet `PASS` line in the PR.

## Out of scope

- `conformance` — it is `#[cfg(test)]`-gated and its user (`extension_host/protocol/tests.rs:471`) is also in the runtime closure; a cross-crate `cfg(test)` module is invisible to the other crate's test build, so it moves together with its user in RS-14
- `test_support` — carries `#[cfg(test)]` and UI fixtures; that split is RS-11
- `computer_meter` — it is `pub mod` today, i.e. a published-surface decision; handle it in RS-14's public-surface inventory
- Behaviour changes anywhere; new re-exports; new tests or comments (repo rule)

---

**Series:** RS-8 #6935 · RS-9 #6936 · RS-10 #6937 · RS-11 #6938 · RS-12 #6939 · RS-13 #6940 · RS-14 #6941 (keystone; blocked by the rest). Umbrella: #5316.

Engine main commit `896e781fbb` is pushed. Grouped activity, tool status and file receipts use the 15-locale catalog and the group cache tracks locale changes. On frozen `9fc5c898c7` plus the inventoried shared dirty tree, TUI lib and feature registry compiled and 197 focused existing cases passed; localization lib had 54 passes on unchanged localization inputs, and all 15 packs have 2,732 keys. The earlier broader mixed-tree run had 2,118 passes and one separate compaction failure. Rendered non-English journeys, native-speaker review, Windows, installed artifacts and final CI remain unverified; issue stays In Progress. Raw tool names in grouped summaries remain visible as names and deserve broader localization review.

## Incoming Engine takeover — 2026-10-29

Codex owns the existing localization/activity batch and the paths in the implementation claim below on canonical Engine main. The previous Claude session has stopped; its later source and verification receipts are being reviewed before landing. Latest recorded focused TUI run: 2,118 passed, one compaction failure; this is not release acceptance. The source has additional inherited provider, session, fixture and documentation changes that require separate review. No final CI, live-provider or release qualification is claimed.

## Current implementation claim — 2026-10-29

Coordinator owns the remaining ordinary-session activity and patch chrome on canonical Engine main bd7c7bba47b908df0ddff46de294bed1c6e608c2. Earlier question/approval/handoff/waiting/color, contributor /diff codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7101 and @Aboysky's merged /undo codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7121 remain landed; the undo fallback retains SyncSession. Do not reapply those contributions.

Finish the existing tool-run and file-activity counts, cached summary locale, typed file-mutation outcomes, patch/status headers and their current consumers. Reuse the existing ToolFamily MessageId mapping and locale catalog; migrate final consumers instead of adding another translation store or renderer-local language switches. Preserve raw tool output, filenames, diffs, receipt authority, timing, collapsed/expanded behavior and user text. Rebuild projection and rendered rows when the UI locale changes.

Exact paths: crates/localization/src/lib.rs and all 15 existing locale packs; TUI [history.rs](<http://history.rs>), history/tool_run.rs, history/file_mutation.rs, history/agent_activity.rs, history/checklist.rs and history/plan.rs; widgets/mod.rs, widgets/transcript_legacy.rs and widgets/tool_card.rs; [app.rs](<http://app.rs>); work_surface/model.rs, work_surface/views.rs, shell_job_routing.rs (explicit English diagnostic-format compatibility), tool_routing.rs, ui/activity_detail.rs and directly affected existing history/ui/render tests; key_shortcuts.rs only if the existing mutation detail hint requires the same locale plumbing; both changelog copies and documentation copy in docs/design/TUI_DECONSTRUCTION.md. No new test functions or code comments. One frozen native batch/build owner after edits, focused existing checks only.

Current preceding source proof: bundled controls and MCP status are complete with scoped receipts under artifacts/codex-0103-resume-20261029. No native build or source lease from those packets remains. No real provider/device, native-speaker review, full/hosted CI or release acceptance is established.

## Original report — observed on 0.10.2

**Version:** 0.10.2 (`ff466b2ed0bf`, npm build), Linux, `locale = "zh-Hans"` in `settings.toml`.
**Target:** 0.10.3

With the UI in Simplified Chinese, the main flow is translated: the composer placeholder 输入消息…, approval options 仅允许本次 / 不允许, the pet status 思考 / 回复 / 完成, the plan-handoff question 你想如何继续？, and the footer. But several messages you see in an ordinary session stay in English. None of these strings are in `crates/localization/locales/*.json`; they're hardcoded at the call site:

| What you see | Source |
| -- | -- |
| `/undo` note: `Undid your request "…". 1 file is back as it was before it: … The request and its reply were removed from the conversation.` | `crates/commands/src/debug/undo.rs:323` (`format!("Undid {request}. {count} before it:…")`) |
| `/diff` pager title `Changes since session start` | `crates/commands/src/debug/undo.rs:174` |
| `/color` note `Composer color for this chat: red` / `…reset to the theme default` | `crates/tui/src/commands/groups/session/color.rs:73-74` |
| Tool card status `… · waiting for approval` | `crates/tui/src/tui/history.rs:1411` |
| Plan handoff / question chrome: `Action required`, `Question 1 of 1`, `Other`, `Type a custom response`, `1-4 quick pick ↑/↓ move Enter confirm ←/h back Esc cancel` | `crates/tui/src/tui/user_input.rs` (e.g. `:459`) |
| Approval card `Save:   always ask first` | `crates/tui/src/tui/widgets/mod.rs`, `crates/tui/src/tui/approval/ask_rules.rs` |
| Grouped activity `Explored 3 files: explore +3 ›`, `patch done · Updated tides.py · +1 -1` | `crates/tui/src/tui/history/tool_run.rs`, `crates/tui/src/tui/widgets/mod.rs` |

## Repro

1. Put `locale = "zh-Hans"` in `$CODEWHALE_HOME/settings.toml`, or choose 简体中文 in `/settings`.
2. In a Git repo, ask for a fix that runs a shell command and edits a file, approve the card, then run `/diff`, `/undo` and `/color`.

## Expected

These go through `tr(locale, MessageId::…)` like their neighbours, and appear in `en.json` and every locale pack. `scripts/check-tui-locale-parity.py` only checks keys that exist, so it can't catch strings that never became keys.

## Notes

* The CHANGELOG for 0.10.2 also says the pet's activity words and the update note follow the UI language, and both do. These strings are the visible gap next to them.
* Fix direction: move each string to a `MessageId`, add the en/zh-Hans/zh-Hant/ja values (the other locales can fall back), and consider a small lint that flags new user-facing `format!`/string literals in `crates/tui/src/tui/` and `crates/commands/src/` outside the localization crate.

Found while recording a Chinese-language 0.10.2 demo.

issues.body:
## Read-only doctor fix landed — 2026-10-29

Engine `14a5723b75` is pushed. Configured routes now short-circuit Ollama adoption before credential inspection; an unconfigured diagnostic uses the non-migrating resolver, while exec retains its normal resolver. Against explicitly built CLI binary digest `35de7b5ec4e7a3f3191fd5770384c2a09fee357aec59ab30bc8f7bb07ca40ad3`, the existing diagnostic case passed configured loopback and unconfigured legacy-key scenarios, retaining the legacy bytes and creating no primary store. Nine local Ollama cases and one route diagnostic case also passed on the frozen mixed tree. No real Ollama or release acceptance is claimed; this issue remains In Progress.

## Evidence correction — 2026-10-29

The TUI integration harness launches `target/debug/codewhale`; it does not rebuild that executable when only the Engine test target is selected. The first recorded local failing diagnostic ran an existing binary whose exact source was not established, so it is not clean-`57e957f186` executable proof. A later failing rerun also used the pre-fix CLI binary. The corrected source was built explicitly as `codewhale-cli --bin codewhale`, and the exact-binary rerun passed as recorded above. The stale-binary failures remain evidence, not verification of the proposed fix.

## Read-only doctor regression claim — 2026-10-29

Codex owns `crates/tui/src/local_ollama.rs` and its two call sites in `crates/tui/src/lib.rs` for the Ollama-adoption credential-presence check. The existing loopback `doctor_text_probe_uses_a_legacy_key_without_migrating_it` case failed against a preexisting CLI executable because the diagnostic created the primary secret store; that executable's exact source was not established. Preserve route-adoption behavior while ensuring diagnostic credential inspection does not migrate a legacy store; verify the existing diagnostic and local-adoption checks. This is separate from real Ollama acceptance.

## What a new user hits

With no cloud key and Ollama running, the TUI adopts Ollama on first launch (`Provider switched: deepseek → ollama`), but the headless and diagnostic paths still insist on DeepSeek:

```
$ codewhale exec "Reply with exactly: QA-OK"
error: DeepSeek API key not found.
...
zsh: ~/.zshrc is interactive only; use ~/.zshenv.
...
Failed to configure provider route deepseek / deepseek-flash.

$ codewhale doctor
Not ready: the deepseek route has no verified key → save one with /provider ...
```

`config.toml` written on first launch keeps `default_text_model = "deepseek-flash"`, so the adoption is re-done (and re-announced) on every TUI launch and never reaches `exec`/`doctor`.

Also: the bare line `zsh: ~/.zshrc is interactive only; use ~/.zshenv.` in the key-missing error reads like a shell error.

## Repro

Fresh `HOME`/`CODEWHALE_HOME`, Ollama with one chat model, main `715bb2ed02` release build: run `codewhale` (TUI adopts Ollama), quit, then `codewhale exec "hi"` and `codewhale doctor`.

Expected: one answer to "which model am I using" across TUI, exec and doctor — either persist the adoption, or have exec/doctor apply the same keyless-local rule and say so.

Evidence: `CW/artifacts/qa-20261027/j-cli-1.txt`, `j-cli-2.txt`.

2026-10-28: Engine `8c4b29c2b9` changes the zsh startup hint into Codewhale prose so it is not mistaken for a shell-generated error. A source-extracted diagnostic compiled and rendered; rustfmt and diff checks passed. The existing F3 Auto-default draft in the same file was not staged. This is a wording fix only; the TUI versus exec/doctor Ollama route mismatch remains open and is under source review.

On frozen Engine `1014538dde`, an assertion added temporarily to the existing `tui::app::tests::reasoning_effort_scenario` failed: Low on a loopback vLLM `Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` route normalized to High. The temporary assertion was removed after recording the result. Draft PR codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7125 maps High to xhigh in its shaper, but the combined PR route has not been run; preserve Low/Medium through actual turn planning before considering it ready.

## Draft review: upstream effort normalization — 2026-10-29

Read-only review of draft Engine PR codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7125 at `e8490b81b87d9411eb7f15b7bce7df7d038f7b1c`: its adapter shapes the effort it receives, but does not change `ReasoningEffort::normalize_for_route_identity` or the turn planner. When no catalog effort ladder is available, that existing normalizer maps Low and Medium to High before Chat shaping. For a Qwen3.8 vLLM route, the draft then maps High to xhigh, so an explicit low/medium choice may be lost before the draft's shaper sees it. The draft's production-route test directly invokes Chat shaping with High and does not exercise this earlier normalization. Confirm against an actual planned route and preserve requested tiers end-to-end before accepting the draft. No patch, merge or contributor contact has been performed.

The vLLM Chat adapter assumes every template accepts low/medium/high. The pinned Qwen3.8-27B and Flash-Next templates instead accept low/medium/xhigh and raise on high. Other reviewed templates either only read a thinking toggle or use low/high/max.

Add narrowly matched, revision-sourced template facts and apply them after generic vLLM reasoning shaping. Qwen3.8 high/max sends xhigh, boolean templates omit effort, and GLM-5.3-Flash / DeepSeek-V4-Vision use their supported ladders. Unknown models and all non-vLLM routes retain their behavior. Credentials, routing, tools/history, streaming and token budgets are unchanged.

Acceptance: exercise the actual Chat route, validate every registry tier/alias, keep unknown and cloud routes untouched, and preserve unrelated request fields. This does not diagnose or claim to fix unrelated service errors on those models.

prs.title: feat: source navigation echoes and guarded fork-prefix inheritance
prs.body:
Index-free source-navigation echoes, bounded source reads and guarded fork-prefix inheritance on the existing Engine. Original contributor commits and credit are preserved; there is no replacement turn loop or indexing daemon.

**Current head:** [`70174cfd3`](https://github.com/AdityaVG13/CodeWhale/commit/70174cfd32c306f6c438812edd8cd723f691a778), following the history-preserving integration at [`40836d9e6`](https://github.com/AdityaVG13/CodeWhale/commit/40836d9e6f902ba7599132c8b21e1e3c9a7a953b) of upstream main [`96498ce2a`](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/96498ce2a7d12689275cea8a8feb5e0569b4431f). Website registries are regenerated from the merged source, not resolved by discarding either side's feature declarations or docs.

## Implemented slice

- Revision-qualified Rust function/method references carry a path, source window and revision, with stale-reference refusal rather than silently using old offsets. Guarded continuation/paging requires forward progress and retains the snapshot identity.
- Focused Rust grep results can supply bounded enclosing-function references and small complete bodies before a separate read. Declaration-line matches take priority across candidate files. Broad/truncated searches keep their ordinary output; this is syntax evidence, not macro expansion or name/type resolution.
- Native `grep_files` is eager beside file-name search, with explicit search argument schemas and aligned child/scout/workflow fixtures. Source whitespace survives tool-result projection.
- Bounded host observations remain separate from program-writable handles, current access authority and evidence delivered to a model. Program-internal reads do not count as delivery; only references surviving outbound projection enter the recipient's ledger.
- Source echoes remain in append-only tool/history evidence, not volatile additions to the pinned system/tool prefix. Making grep eager does grow the catalog; its actual contract is measured and budgeted in this change. Native read containment, deny rules and blocking-worker fences remain in place.
- Children retain the complete policy-allowed tool vector while preserving the current eager/deferred discovery and cache contracts. Fork-prefix inheritance stays gated by matching route/model/opaque receipt and supported dialect; unsupported or changed identities take the cold path.
- The skill index keeps eligible names enumerable without exposing mutable native skill paths. Workflow events retain task/workspace ownership.

## Current source-level verification

**224 selected `codewhale-tui` library tests passed: 0 failed, 0 ignored**, rerun on Linux from the existing RCH-built test executable. All 1,599 recorded source inputs match, and remote inputs were unchanged around execution. The selection covers search/navigation/read contracts, source-result projection and eager-tool/catalog behavior.

Four provider-free runtime metric tests passed separately. `scripts/check-runtime-contract-budget.py --receipt …` passes all 55 metrics exactly at the updated ceilings. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, touched-file `git diff --check`, web facts/cloud-facts/docs checks, and generated parity for all 90 feature rows and 25 documentation topics pass.

The native replay of the recorded search preserves its 11 raw hits and supplies the actual 564-byte definition, with exact guarded reading and same-size-edit refusal verified. This is diagnostic-client execution, not a model choosing or following the reference. Engine tests with injected model clients likewise establish host execution and projected request contents, not live-provider acceptance or completed-task improvement.

No full workspace suite, full web build, native macOS/Windows acceptance or packaged-release qualification is claimed. Historical receipts are not substituted for verification of the current source.

## Still draft: empirical qualification remains

This stays draft in accordance with [the contributor's scope decision](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6393#issuecomment-6207193232). The earlier baseline, including its failed completion and incomplete pilot, remains in [the maintained progress record](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6393#issuecomment-6185897898).

The six-attempt full/output-off/navigation-off comparison is complete but did not qualify an overall performance gain. The grouped-grep experiment was removed after smaller replay output did not translate into better fresh exploration. The latest smarter-exploration comparison stopped when its first control failed the frozen correctness rubric, without running a treatment or relaxing the rubric. See [the current findings and verification update](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6393#issuecomment-6524708140).

Remaining qualification is correctness-first completed tasks with a valid frozen control and contemporaneous ablations. No current-PR speedup, cost reduction, quality improvement, live-provider cache saving or independent quality review is claimed. Wider composition/impact-navigation work and release acceptance are not implied.

Refs #6393, CW-6439
