fix(session): keep history matched when turn metadata differs

## Summary

A single chat message can be persisted in two shapes — bare user text, and the
same text followed by a trailing `<turn_meta>` block — while the session journal
compared the two with strict structural equality. One shape mismatch zeroed the
shared prefix, so the journal treated the entire history as new: it cleared the
leaf, re-rooted the tree, and appended the rest of the transcript as a sibling
branch. Nothing was deleted, but everything before the mismatch stopped being
the active path.

The visible symptom, from #7178: one message produced two replies that differed
in length (1103 vs 234 characters), and a session whose document held 1231
journal entries had an active path of 53 — every earlier assistant reply
stranded on a branch that was still stored and never shown again.

This makes the comparison aware of the engine-owned envelope, and makes the
journal converge on the live transcript instead of forking over a payload it can
replace in place.

## Changes

- **Mask only the engine envelope, never the payload**: `normalized_blocks` in
  `crates/runtime/src/session_tree.rs` strips a leading `<turn_meta>…</turn_meta>`
  out of a text block instead of dropping whole blocks. A fused single block
  (`<turn_meta>…</turn_meta>\nhi`) normalizes to `Text("hi")` and matches the bare
  `"hi"`; a block that merely starts and ends with the tags keeps its trailing
  text, so a message whose real content looks like metadata is never masked away.
  The view borrows the existing blocks — nothing is cloned, nothing is allocated.
- **Refresh a metadata-only prefix instead of forking**:
  `rebranch_active_messages_stamped` rewrites a stored payload that differs only
  by the envelope to the live one, keeping the entry id, `created_at` and parent
  link (ordering comes from the parent chain), then appends only what is past the
  prefix. Journal and `session.messages` therefore converge instead of drifting.
- **Keep the strict comparison for synthesized kinds**: the relaxed match is
  limited to `SessionEntryKind::Message`, the only kind that stores an
  engine-stamped payload. `Compaction`, `BranchSummary`, `User`, `Assistant` and
  `System` still require byte equality with their projection, because a kind that
  could only match relaxed would be selected for a rewrite it cannot receive.
  This is also why `codewhale_models::turn_classify` is not reused here: its test
  is `starts_with("<turn_meta>") && ends_with("</turn_meta>")`, which accepts
  `<turn_meta>x</turn_meta>REAL CONTENT</turn_meta>`, and its
  `message.content.len() < 2` guard cannot see the fused single-block shape at
  all. Reusing it would restore both defects.
- **Converge the two other write paths**: `crates/engine/src/session_manager.rs` applies
  the same predicate to `journal_branch_to` and `update_session`, so a
  metadata-only difference falls through to the rebranch instead of being skipped
  and left divergent. Both append-only fast paths stay strict on purpose; they
  are safe now because a failing strict test no longer means "do nothing".
- **Unrelated Windows build fix, kept in its own commit**: `runtime_log.rs`
  imports `windows::Win32::System::Console` under `cfg(windows)`, but the
  `windows` dependency never enabled that feature, so `codewhale-runtime` does
  not build on Windows. CI is Linux-only, which is why it never surfaced. One
  line in `crates/runtime/Cargo.toml`; happy to split it into its own PR if you
  prefer.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] Tests

## Testing

- `cargo test -p codewhale-runtime --lib -- session_tree` → `test result: ok. 25
  passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 886 filtered out`
- `cargo check -p codewhale-runtime -p codewhale-engine --lib` → `Finished dev profile` (13m07s, no errors)
- Both gates were re-run after merging `upstream/main` (`4b85ac2cc`), which moved
  `crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs` to `crates/engine/src/session_manager.rs`; the merge
  carried these edits onto the new paths unchanged.
- Workspace-level clippy and tests are left to CI.

Three tests cover the new behaviour. Two are regression pins that fail on the
parent commit — `rebranch_refreshes_a_metadata_only_prefix_in_place` and
`a_metadata_shaped_payload_never_matches_a_shorter_turn` — and one guards against
over-eager masking (`rebranch_forks_when_the_content_actually_changed`), plus a
guard test asserting every non-`Message` kind still compares strictly. A
history-rewriting defect in the session tree had no pin at all, so the pins are
part of the fix rather than a separate test change.

prs.title: fix(markdown): keep a keycap in one span through the inline parser
prs.body:
## Summary

A markdown table cell that holds the `*` keycap (U+002A U+FE0F U+20E3) rendered with its row out of place: the row's `|` separators sat in different columns than the box above and below it, and the trailing `|` landed outside the table. A keycap with a digit base (`1` + U+FE0F + U+20E3) rendered correctly, so only the `*` form was affected.

`parse_inline_spans` cut a span in the middle of that grapheme cluster. The plain-text arm advances to the next inline marker, and `*` is a marker but does not open emphasis here because no closing `*` follows, so it stopped right after the `*` and left the two zero-width marks in a span of their own. The terminal then drew the cluster two columns wide while the spans reported one, moving everything after the cell.

## Scope

This fixes the parser defect only. I originally opened this against a broader report where keycaps misaligned in a real Windows Terminal, and that part turned out to be a separate, upstream bug that this patch cannot fix:

- Windows font fallback ignores `U+FE0F` and hands `U+20E3` to Segoe UI Symbol, so a keycap is drawn as split pieces rather than as one emoji (microsoft/terminal#9708). The fix there is microsoft/terminal#20790, still open.
- Reproducible with `Write-Host` alone, without Codewhale involved, so it is not a rendering bug in this repository.
- The remaining misalignment is frame-dependent and lower priority for that reason; there is no user-side workaround (`font.fallback` is not a real Windows Terminal setting).

The tui-kit grid is correct for these clusters: the renderer emits one 2-cell grapheme and the buffer records it that way. What this PR keeps is that the cluster never gets split into separate spans in the first place, which is wrong regardless of which terminal draws it.

## Changes

- **Plain text arm**: advance to the end of the grapheme that contains the marker offset instead of stopping at the raw offset, so a marker character that is the base of a cluster carries its marks with it.
- **Backslash arm**: carry the whole cluster, so an escaped keycap (`\*️⃣`) no longer emits a bare `*` and splits the marks off.
- **Emphasis arms**: require `*` and `_` to be a lone first grapheme before treating them as delimiters, so a keycap `*` cannot open emphasis and eat the marks.
- **Test**: render the table into a ratatui buffer and check both the column of every `|` and that the cell's symbol still contains U+20E3. The column check alone is not enough — the split and joined forms advance the buffer by the same number of columns because the zero-width marks are dropped either way, so a column-only assertion passes before and after the fix. Reverting the plain-text change turns the symbol assertion red with `the cell holds ["|", "*", "|", ...]`, which is the state the reported bug shipped in.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] Tests

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui-kit` — 216 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (3 added). Rebased onto `main` at `297b06d`.
- `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.
- Each fix was reverted individually to confirm its test goes red without it.
- CI on this branch is green, including `Test (windows-latest)` and `Test (ubuntu-latest)`.

Not verified locally: a full-workspace `cargo build`/`cargo test`. `rustc` aborts with `STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN` (0xC0000409) while codegen'ing `codewhale-tui` on my machine, before any test runs and independently of this change; the crate's own `cargo check` is clean. CI covers those gates.

## Checklist

- [x] Updated docs or comments as needed
- [x] Added or updated tests where relevant

prs.title: fix(goal): route a needed user answer to yield, not blocked
prs.body:
## Relationship to #7175 (already merged)

This is a follow-up, not a duplicate. #7175 and #7177 patch two different
surfaces that the model reads at two different moments.

**#7175 changed prompt text only** — two places, both engine-injected:

- `GOAL_CONTINUATION_PROMPT` in `crates/tui/src/prompts/text.rs` (+7/-4)
- the closing sentence of `render_continuation_prompt` in `goal.rs` (+1/-1)

Both strings are only present in a continuation pass, i.e. after a turn ends
with the goal still `Active` and the engine re-dispatches. A model that is
about to call `update_goal` for the first time has not seen either string.

**#7177 changes the tool schema instead** — two places, both always in the tool
catalog:

- `UpdateGoalTool::description()` (`goal.rs:1106`)
- the `status` parameter description (`goal.rs:1116`)

The schema is in the model's tool list on every turn — including the first
turn, and any turn where no continuation was scheduled. It is the document the
model reads when it decides whether the current situation is `blocked`.

The overlap is semantic (both say "a needed user answer is a yield"), and the
wording is deliberately aligned. The coverage is not: #7175 fixed the message
the engine writes, #7177 fixes the document the model reads. Neither alone
covers both moments, and the two do not contradict each other when both are
present.

## What and why

`update_goal` could only express "waiting for the user" as `blocked`, and
`blocked` is what the continuation loop treats as a stall. A goal that
legitimately needs an answer before the next pass can do anything useful
therefore reported a block, which is a different thing and ends the turn on the
wrong note.

This routes that case to `yield`: the goal stays unfinished, the turn ends, and
the user's next message resumes it. Three commits:

- `fix(goal): route a needed user answer to yield, not blocked` — the runtime
  change: `yield` described as the status for a needed user answer, `blocked`
  narrowed to "meaningful progress cannot continue", and the turn-loop guard
  that used to convert yield-on-question into blocked.
- `test(conformance): re-record the goal tool fixtures for the yield wording` —
  the prompt fixtures that record the tool description.
- `test(conformance): align the event fixture schema with the yield wording` —
  the event fixtures, which embed a byte-truncated (2048) copy of that same
  schema.

## Issue

No-Issue: tool-description and turn-loop change plus its conformance fixtures;
the separate fixture host-sensitivity problem is #7174

## How I tested it

Fixture regeneration was checked against the recorder rather than eyeballed:

- The event fixtures store `input_schema_json` truncated at 2048 **bytes** and
  decoded lossily. Replaying that exact procedure on the new schema reproduces
  the previous fixture value byte for byte (2046 characters, 2048 bytes), so
  the regenerator and the recorder agree.
- `tools_bytes` moves from 16349 to 16605, and the delta is fully accounted
  for: top-level description +134, `status` parameter description +122, +256
  total.
- Across the six event fixtures the old sentence `meaningful progress cannot
  continue` now occurs 0 times and the new wording 15 times;
  `active_tool_catalog_sha256`, `payload_json_bytes` and `tool_count` are
  unchanged.
- `cargo check` completed clean earlier on this branch;
  `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes, and no Rust source changed in the two
  fixture commits.
- The conformance suite is `#[cfg(unix)]`, so it is skipped on Windows. The
  Linux check is what exercises it.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and the fixtures covering the changed behavior
      are re-recorded
- [ ] No `docs/features.toml` row applies: no new command, flag, provider or
      feature, only the semantics of an existing internal goal status

prs.title: feat(tui): let the model read the transcript compaction replaced
prs.body:
## What and why

Compaction replaces the transcript with a summary, and everything the summary left out became unreachable. This gives the model two read-only tools back into the text it lost:

- `context_archive_search` finds a literal fragment in the archived transcript and returns a short snippet with the archive id of the message it came from.
- `context_archive_get` reads one message, or a range of messages, by those ids.

Both tools are bounded and refuse to run when there is no archive:

- ids are 12 hex characters derived from the message's position and content, so they stay meaningful across a restart;
- reads default to 4,000 characters and cap at 12,000; searches default to 5 results and cap at 20;
- the archive is capped at 64 MiB, and older bytes are dropped instead of growing without limit;
- matching is literal and ASCII case-insensitive: no regex, no wildcards, and punctuation inside a phrase must match the source.

The archive only holds what compaction actually replaced, so this does not add a second copy of the live transcript.

## Issue

No-Issue: no tracking issue was filed; this started from a direct request to give the model a way back into the pre-compaction transcript.

## How I tested it

- `cargo build --release --locked -p codewhale-cli -p codewhale-tui` — clean release build.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib compaction` — 56 passed.
- `python scripts/check-runtime-contract-budget.py` — all 55 metrics exactly at budget.
- Re-recorded the three prompt conformance goldens; the recorder test passed (`1 passed; 0 failed`).
- Ran the release binary with `exec --auto` and asked the model to name only the tools whose name begins with `context_archive`. It answered `context_archive_get` and `context_archive_search`, so both reach the model-visible catalog rather than only the registry.
- A live session against the release binary exercised compaction followed by an archive search and a read by id; the returned text matched the original.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [x] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it)

Opper is an EU-hosted, OpenAI-compatible gateway with 700+ models from 50+ providers behind one key. `/provider` uses `OPPER_API_KEY`, `https://api.opper.ai/v3/compat` and `claude-sonnet-4-6` as the bootstrap model. Bare pool names let Opper pick the route per request; `provider/model` ids such as `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` pin one route. prs.title: fix(goal): name the ask-the-user exit in continuation prompts
prs.body:
## What and why

The goal loop could not pause for a question.

When a continuation pass needed an answer from the user, the model asked in
prose and kept the goal `Active`. Nothing in the prompt named that exit, so the
next pass started with the question still unanswered — the model supplied its
own answer and carried on. The user saw the question scroll past and the agent
already several tool calls into an assumed answer.

Both continuation surfaces now name it:

- `GOAL_CONTINUATION_PROMPT` (`crates/tui/src/prompts/text.rs`) — the `yield`
  trigger widens from "finished a stage" to also cover "you need the user's
  answer before the next pass can do anything useful", plus one sentence
  stating that asking in prose without calling `update_goal` does not pause the
  goal, so the next pass must not invent an answer to keep the loop moving. It
  also says to load `update_goal` with `tool_search` when the tool is missing,
  because a continuation run without it would otherwise fall back to exactly
  the ask-in-prose path this change closes.
- `render_continuation_prompt` (`crates/tui/src/tools/goal.rs`) — the exit list
  already enumerated complete / not_achieved / blocked and ended with
  "Otherwise continue making progress toward the objective". The yield exit is
  now explicit there too: "If the next pass cannot make useful progress without
  an answer or decision only the user can give ... do not invent the answer and
  continue." The condition is deliberately the same width as the header's, so
  the sentence that comes later in the same message cannot silently widen the
  trigger.

No state machine change. `GoalPauseReason::Yielded` already exists and their
reply already resumes the goal; the gap was that nothing told the model to use
it for a question.

Known limitation, stated rather than implied: this is prompt steering, not
enforcement. A model that ignores the instruction still keeps the goal active —
`update_goal` is the only pause authority and the engine does not infer a pause
from the assistant asking a question. Making it mechanical would mean the
engine detecting a terminal question, which is not reliably decidable.

## Issue

No-Issue: prompt-text fix for a goal-loop behaviour gap; no issue tracks it, and it is two strings plus their existing assertions.

## How I tested it

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean, both before and after the follow-up
  wording pass.
- Existing assertions checked by reading, not by weakening them: the strings
  `Goal Continuation`, `Continuation pass #2`, `N equivalent gap sets in a row`
  and `"blocker": null` are all preserved verbatim; only the closing sentence
  of each surface changed.
- `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --lib --tests` and
  `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib goal` were started locally on Windows;
  the `codewhale-tui` lib-test binary aborts during codegen/link
  (`STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN`, `error: could not compile codewhale-tui (lib test)`)
  after ~31 min on this host, so the local suite verdict is left to CI. Please
  treat the Linux suite as the first real signal for this PR.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes; no test changed — the change is prompt text whose
      existing assertions still hold, and the repository's standing rule for this
      area is not to add tests
- [ ] No user-facing feature flag or `docs/features.toml` row applies: no new
      command, flag, provider or feature, only the wording of an existing
      internal continuation prompt

## Signature

prs.title: fix(runtime): keep private state on a filesystem that cannot express ownership
prs.body:
## Why

A GUI start on HarmonyOS hmdfs (the 2in1 user directory, `/storage/Users/currentUser`) failed one feature at a time:

```
Engine exited before becoming ready: error: workspace drive lease check failed for
/storage/Users/currentUser/magic/CodeWhale-VSCode: Codewhale credentials directory
must be owned by the current user
```

then `error: failed to build daemon state`, then `Codewhale credentials directory must be owned by the current user` again. Each fix revealed the next, because one mechanism — admit a directory by proving it is current-user-owned and closed to group and other — sits under the workspace lease, the owner control socket, the OAuth credential directory, plugin state, tool report files, pet-watch state and delivery files.

That mount cannot satisfy the proof. Measured on a HarmonyOS PC (`HPR-W72`, API 26):

| operation | result |
|---|---|
| `touch ~/.codewhale/x` | `mode=0640`, `uid=20001006` |
| `chmod 600 ~/.codewhale/x` | `Permission denied` (EPERM) |
| `mkdir -m 700 ~/.codewhale/d` | `mode=2771`, `uid=20001006` |
| `chmod 777 ~/.codewhale/d` | `Permission denied` (EPERM) |

Every object is reported as belonging to the logged-in user whatever uid created it, so the calling process (uid `20020225` for CodeArts, `20020084` for HiShell) is never the reported owner — and `chmod` on someone else's file is refused for that reason, not because the mount lacks mode support.

## What this does

The mechanism names the condition once. `private_footing` creates one `0o700` directory under the target, reads back what the mount made of it, and — when that is not the private owner and mode it asked for — asks the mount to narrow it and looks again. Only a mount that refuses, or keeps its own values after being asked, is *synthesising*. A filesystem that applies an unexpected mode at creation but honours the correction stores modes and keeps the full guard, so a default ACL or a setgid parent cannot silently relax a check. The probe runs only after a strict check has already failed, and its answer with its one warning is cached per directory, so a write path never probes a healthy filesystem.

Where the mount is synthesising, the private object is admitted with the ownership guard recorded as unverifiable. The no-follow component walk, the single-link check, atomic publication and the retained handle still apply.

**Two capabilities are kept apart**, because conflating them is what made the original failure look like a missing feature:

- Exclusivity is the kernel lock, not the ownership proof. The workspace lease is still taken and a second driver is still refused with the holder's pid, client, store and age. Only a filesystem that refuses advisory locks themselves (`EPERM`, `EACCES`, `ENOTSUP`, `EINVAL`, `ENOSYS` — never `EWOULDBLOCK`) is reported as unable to provide exclusivity, once per admitted workspace scope.
- The owner control socket has no other discovery path, so it degrades to HTTP only and logs what was lost. A daemon-only run and ACP publication still require it and name the reason.

Narrowing after a write goes through one helper that attempts the `chmod`, keeps the error where the filesystem stores modes, and excuses only a mount that cannot apply them — applied to the handle that was opened where one exists, so a substituted path cannot be the object narrowed. Checks that re-proved ownership on an object already admitted (the retained-directory identity comparison, an owner receipt's mode, a published socket's owner) now follow the guard it was admitted with.

A directory this process may not enter keeps its original error everywhere, so a filesystem that stores mode bits never takes the wider path.

## Scope

Two commits: the secret store's own mode/lock gate (self-contained, `crates/secrets` + `crates/memory`), then the runtime mechanism and its consumers. Three device/probe scripts are included; documentation and the cross-build `PATH` fix belong to #7151 and are not duplicated here. No CHANGELOG entry, per the maintainer's request.

`crates/tui/src/workspace_lease.rs` and `runtime_log.rs` moved to `crates/runtime` upstream (#7149, #7151-era refactors); the changes are replayed there rather than in `tui`. Because the module is now public API, `LeaseAttempt` is widened to `pub` to match `WorkspaceDriveLease::try_acquire`.

## Verification

Branch is rebased on `main` at `acfd66000` (0 behind).

- `check --workspace --all-targets --locked` clean; `fmt --all --check` clean.
- Clippy clean with CI's flags (`-A clippy::uninlined_format_args -A clippy::too_many_arguments -A clippy::unnecessary_map_or`) on config, secrets, memory, util, app-server, plugins, runtime **and tui**.
- Suites: config 813, secrets 55, util 51, plugins 201, app-server 177 + 15 integration, memory 4, runtime 928, cli 378.
- tui lib, full parallel run: **15 failed / 13403 passed**, then **17 failed / 13401 passed** on a re-run — the set varies run to run.

### The tui failures are pre-existing, not from this change

Measured against a clean `origin/main` (`acfd66000`) worktree, same suite, same machine:

| tree | failures |
|---|---|
| `origin/main` | 13 |
| this branch, run 1 | 15 |
| this branch, run 2 | 17 |

Every name that differs between the sets passes **individually** on its own tree:

- `core::engine::tests::recursive_rlm_round_waits_on_the_code_execution_gate` — passes alone here; also fails the `core::engine::tests::` group on clean `origin/main` (8 failures there, same 8 names).
- `runtime_threads::tests::preturn_control_status_does_not_make_empty_turn_succeed` — passes alone here; also fails the `runtime_threads::tests::` group on clean `origin/main`.
- `tools::subagent::tests::worker_compacts_past_its_context_window_and_keeps_working`, `runtime_api::tests::reload_config_with_malformed_file_returns_error`, `runtime_threads::tests::profile_constitution_...` — appear in one run and not the other, on both trees.
- `tools::subagent::tests::late_launch_permit_still_gets_the_full_work_budget` fails on **clean `origin/main`** and passes here.

## Not covered

- Windows: `bind_captured_owner` gained an `Option` return and the non-unix `tighten_mode*` stubs are by inspection only — no Windows toolchain on this machine; CI covers it.
- The synthesising-mount and no-advisory-lock branches cannot be produced on a portable filesystem. They are exercised on a real device by `scripts/ohos-secrets-store-smoke.sh` and predicted by `scripts/ohos-lease-footing-probe.sh`; `scripts/ohos-sign-binary.sh` cross-builds, strips, self-signs and verifies the Engine, which starts on the device above.

Refs #7151

prs.title: fix(tui): render code and links inside emphasis
prs.body:
## What and why

Bold, italic and strikethrough spans push their inner text as one plain run, so markup inside them reaches the screen as written. `**`--force`**` shows its backticks, and `**[the guide](https://example.com/guide)**` shows the brackets and the URL, with no hyperlink. This reply, at 100 columns:

```
Pass **`--force`** to overwrite the file.

Read **[the guide](https://example.com/guide)** first.

Then edit *`config.toml`* and run ~~`make old`~~ `make`.

**Note:** plain bold still works.
```

Before:

```
● Pass `--force` to overwrite the file.
▏
▏ Read [the guide](https://example.com/guide) first.
▏
▏ Then edit `config.toml` and run `make old` make.
▏
▏ Note: plain bold still works.
```

After, with `the guide` now a hyperlink to https://example.com/guide:

```
● Pass --force to overwrite the file.
▏
▏ Read the guide first.
▏
▏ Then edit config.toml and run make old make.
▏
▏ Note: plain bold still works.
```

Each emphasis arm now parses its inner text with the emphasis style as the base, so code, links, bare URLs, escapes and other emphasis inside it render as they do outside. A second reply covered the rest: `**bold with *italic* inside**` and `~~**old**~~` showed their inner asterisks before, `**a\*b**` showed the backslash, and a bare URL inside `*…*` had no hyperlink. `**a_b_c**`, `**3 * 4 * 5**`, `__init__` and `` `**not bold**` `` render the same as before.

An arm's inner text ends at the first closing delimiter of its own kind, so a delimiter can't nest inside itself and the recursion stays a few levels deep.

### Notes

`escape_note_backslashes` doubles a note's backslashes before it is rendered, and skipped any line with `*` or `~~` because emphasis printed its text as written. With escapes read inside emphasis, a note line like `**C:\Users\asus\.codewhale** is the home` would print `C:\Users\asus.codewhale`, so besides fenced blocks the escaper now skips only lines with inline code and table rows. That also fixes two note lines that were already wrong on `main`:

```
__C:\Users\asus\.codewhale__             before: C:\\Users\\asus\\.codewhale
**Saved** to C:\Users\asus\.codewhale    before: Saved to C:\Users\asus.codewhale
```

Both now print the path as written. `**…**`, `~~…~~` and `*…*` around the path, inline code and plain lines print it as written before and after. The comments on the escaper and its existing test, and the Unreleased changelog line that said emphasis lines are passed through, now say what the code does.

## Issue

No-Issue: markup inside bold, italic or strikethrough text is shown as written; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of the renderer change and one of `main` at c4f1e726d, the parent it was written on (`markdown_render.rs` hasn't changed on `main` since), in a pseudo-terminal at 100x30 with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the text above, and recorded the OSC 8 targets in the output; the rows above come from those runs. A second reply checked the cases in the paragraph above.
- Rendered the note lines above as a `HistoryCell::System` through `lines_with_copy_metadata` on `main`, on the renderer change alone, and on this commit. With the renderer change alone, `**…**`, `~~…~~` and `*…*` around the path lost the backslash before the dot; with this commit all seven lines print the path as written.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 13633 of 13633 passed, with the 341 tests whose names match `markdown`, `inline`, `emphasis`, `bold`, `italic`, `link`, `note` or `backslash` among them, and the four tests that came with the note escaper.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` with CI's flags (also on 1.99), `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets`, `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` and `scripts/sync-changelog.sh --check`: clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on 785f7d0d4; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior — `cargo fmt` passes; no new test, per AGENTS.md, so the runs above stand in for one

prs.title: fix(tui): keep balanced parentheses in a markdown link's target
prs.body:
## What and why

A `[text](url)` link ends at the first `)`, so a destination with parentheses of its own loses its last `)`. The hyperlink then points at a page that doesn't exist, and the `)` shows after the label. Wikipedia articles with a qualifier and old Microsoft Learn pages ending in `(v=vs.85)` are common examples. This reply, at 100 columns:

```
See [Rust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)) for the history.

The [function article](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Function_(mathematics)) says the same as https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Function_(mathematics).

The old [API page](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/desktop/legacy/ms123401(v=vs.85)) is archived.
```

Before:

```
● See Rust) for the history.
▏
▏ The function article) says the same as https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Function_(mathematics).
▏
▏ The old API page) is archived.
```

with these hyperlink targets:

```
Rust             -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language
function article -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Function_(mathematics
API page         -> https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/desktop/legacy/ms123401(v=vs.85
```

After:

```
● See Rust for the history.
▏
▏ The function article says the same as https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Function_(mathematics).
▏
▏ The old API page is archived.
```

```
Rust             -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)
function article -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Function_(mathematics)
API page         -> https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/desktop/legacy/ms123401(v=vs.85)
```

The bare URL on the second line was already right: bare URLs keep balanced parentheses (`bare_http_links_preserve_balanced_parentheses_in_target`). A named link now ends at the first `)` without a matching `(`, using the same `has_unmatched_closing_delimiter` check the bare URL path trims with. So `[y](https://example.com/f((x)))` keeps both, and `(see [docs](https://example.com/docs))` and `[z](https://example.com/z) (aside)` link as before. A destination whose parentheses don't balance, like `[x](https://example.com/a(b)`, is no longer a named link, as in CommonMark; it shows as written, with the bare URL inside it linked.

## Issue

No-Issue: a markdown link whose URL has parentheses loses its last `)`; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at c4f1e726d in a pseudo-terminal at 100x30 with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the text above, and recorded the OSC 8 targets in the output (OSC 8 is on by default outside Windows); the rows and targets above come from those runs. prs.title: fix(tui): drop the engine's status reply to a stream timeout change
prs.body:
## What and why

`/config stream_chunk_timeout_secs <n>` answers in the transcript with the new value and whether it was saved, then sends `Op::SetStreamChunkTimeout`. The engine answered that op with a status, "Stream chunk timeout set to <n>s", which arrives after the note and stays in the footer. After `/config stream_chunk_timeout_secs 120` at 100 columns, before:

```
Note stream_chunk_timeout_secs = 120 (session only; affects subsequent turns in this session)
…
 ● ask  Shift+Tab to change   work (Tab)   Work bar (Ctrl+])       Stream chunk timeout set to 120s
```

It was still there 7 seconds later. After:

```
Note stream_chunk_timeout_secs = 120 (session only; affects subsequent turns in this session)
…
 ● ask  Shift+Tab to change   work (Tab)   Work bar (Ctrl+])
```

At 80 columns it also pushes the Shift+Tab hint off the row, before:

```
Note stream_chunk_timeout_secs = 120 (session only; affects subsequent turns
▏    in this session)
…
 ● ask   work (Tab)   Work bar (Ctrl+])        Stream chunk timeout set to 120s
```

After:

```
Note stream_chunk_timeout_secs = 120 (session only; affects subsequent turns
▏    in this session)
…
 ● ask  Shift+Tab to change   work (Tab)   Work bar (Ctrl+])
```

The engine now stores the timeout without sending a status, the same as #7152 did for `SetFleetRoster` and 04de8eb67 for `SetCompaction`. Nothing reads that message. The other sender of the op, a runtime thread's config reload, already skips status events that arrive before a turn starts.

## Issue

prs.title: fix(setup): keep the setup checkpoint when a second instance is running
prs.body:
## Summary

`/config pet_mode --save` answered "宠物模式未能保存：无法删除要被替换的文件。(os error 1175)", and
the same refusal hit every other settings toggle — "无法保存确认。脱敏仍然开启。". A separate
report showed a setup checkpoint failing to persist to a path printed with a
backslash missing, and `doctor` reporting a half-applied setup that did not
exist.

The settings half is not transient contention, so the first attempt at it
(retrying the code) did not fix it. Measured on the affected machine, same file
and same ACLs, only the parent directory varies:

```
D:\CodeWhaleData            ReplaceFileW 1175, MoveFileExW 32, rename fails
D:\                         same
D:\CodeWhaleData\<any sub>  OK
C:\Users\asus\Documents     OK
```

`DeleteFileW` succeeds in the refused directories and rewriting the file in
place succeeds, so the bytes can be delivered without a rename. That is what
this branch now does as a last resort.

## Changes

- **A settings write lands even where renames are refused.**
  `atomically_replace_settings_file` keeps the `ReplaceFileW` retry, then calls
  `rewrite_settings_in_place`. `atomic_write` does the same for
  `setup_state.json` via `rewrite_in_place`. The in-place write truncates and
  rewrites, so it is not atomic — an interruption can leave a partial file.
  `Settings::load_persisted` already tolerates a corrupt document by falling
  back to defaults with `load_error` set, which bounds the damage.

- **The fallback is narrow on purpose.** Only the contention codes fall back —
  5 `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`, 32 `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION`, 33
  `ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION`, 1175 `ERROR_UNABLE_TO_REMOVE_REPLACED` — so a full
  disk or a real permission bit still reports its own error rather than being
  retried into an in-place attempt that would fail the same way.
  `ReplaceFileW`'s 1176 and 1177 stay out of the list: they can leave the
  replacement consumed or altered, which a retry cannot undo.

- **Both writers retry briefly first** — six attempts, `n * 50ms`, 750ms in
  total — because ordinary contention (another instance reading the file, a
  scanner) does clear.

- **The message stops eating its own cause.** It used `{err}`, which prints only
  the outermost `context` and drops the source chain, so the path was the only
  thing left to look at. It now uses `{err:#}`.

- **`doctor` stops flagging a user's own temp-named logs.** The
  `stale_setup_temp_files` check matched any file whose name starts with
  `.tmp`, so scratch files such as `.tmp-build-release.log` made a clean home
  report as half-applied. It now matches what a staged write leaves behind when
  it never lands: `.tmpXXXXXX` with no extension.

- **A note keeps the backslashes in a path.** The wrong path in the first report
  came from here: the note is correct, the renderer is correct, and the note was
  the one that did not escape. A transcript note is machine-generated and names
  paths, but it goes through the markdown renderer, which honours CommonMark
  §2.4 — a backslash before ASCII punctuation is an escape, so `\.` yields `.`.
  `escape_note_backslashes` now doubles a bare backslash in note prose, at the
  one place every note passes through.

  Three regions are passed through exactly as written, because the renderer
  already copies them verbatim and doubling a backslash inside one would
  *print* the extra backslash: a fenced block (closed only by a run at least as
  long as its opener), a line carrying a delimiter the renderer treats as a
  passthrough (backtick, `*`, `~~`), and a table row.

  `_`-delimited emphasis is deliberately not a passthrough trigger: `_` is
  everywhere in identifiers (`setup_state.json`), and a false positive would
  leave the paths this pass exists to protect untouched.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing

Run locally on Windows:

- **The reported failure, before and after**, against the affected directory:
  - before: `config set pet_mode false` → exit 1, `settings.toml` mtime
    unchanged, value still `true`.
  - after: `config set pet_mode false` → `set pet_mode in
    C:\Users\asus\.codewhale\settings.toml`, mtime advanced, `pet_mode = false`
    written. Repeated with another key and the value restored each time.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-config --lib -- persistence` → **30 passed; 0
  failed**, including the new `an_in_place_rewrite_replaces_a_longer_document`,
  which rewrites a longer document with a shorter one and asserts the old tail is
  gone.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-runtime --lib -- only_a_held_destination` → **1
  passed**: the allow-list retries 5/32/33/1175 and refuses 2/3/112/87.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-config --lib -- only_a_contended` → **1 passed**.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib -- a_system_note` → **3 passed**;
  `a_fence_of_four_backticks_is_not_closed_by_three` → **1 passed**.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib -- doctor_setup_consistency` → **4 passed**,
  the two existing cases included, so the narrower match did not stop the check
  from firing on a real orphan.
- `codewhale doctor` on the authoring machine no longer prints the
  `half-applied setup detected (stale_setup_temp_files_in_codewhale_home)` line
  it printed before this change.

**What I could not determine:** *why* those directories refuse renames. Restart
Manager reports no holder; no process has them as its CWD (checked with junction
resolution); a handle opened with `FILE_SHARE_DELETE` plus a mapped view does not
reproduce it; the ACL merge flags do not change the result. The fix therefore
targets the observable behaviour (delete works, rename does not) rather than the
cause. If a maintainer can name the mechanism, a narrower fix may be possible.

Not run locally: `cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked` and
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked`. CI is the
first full run; treat this section as what was actually observed, not a claim
about the whole gate.

      slice regenerated with `scripts/sync-changelog.sh`)

prs.title: Native HarmonyOS: fix the documented build, and ship a signed arm64 release
prs.body:
## What and why

Two commits that make native HarmonyOS a target maintainers can document and a release can serve.

**1. `docs(ohos)`: the guide's commands now work, and the page says what the device actually does.**

Following `docs/HarmonyOS.md` from a clean checkout failed before producing a binary. Two independent causes, both reproduced on the base commit:

- The documented `cargo check --target aarch64-unknown-linux-ohos -p codewhale-cli` dies inside `aws-lc-sys`' build script with `Required build dependency is missing. Halting build.` — the message names neither cmake nor HarmonyOS. `scripts/ohos-env.sh` now puts the SDK's own `build-tools/cmake/bin` on `PATH` and exports `CMAKE`.
- With that fixed, the check then fails on the workspace's `warnings = "deny"`: `function sha256_hex is never used`. `crates/cli/src/lib.rs` compiled `hashing` unconditionally, but its only caller is `mod update`, which is already `#[cfg(not(target_env = "ohos"))]`. The module now carries the same gate.

The page also gained what it was missing, verified on hardware (HPR-W72, HarmonyOS 7.0.0.111, API 26, 2in1): only signed code runs at all (`chmod +x` is irrelevant); `hdc shell` cannot execute a binary under `/data/local/tmp` because of its security label, so a correctly signed binary still reports `Permission denied` there and must be run from HiShell; an emulator is more permissive than a retail device. Signing with the SDK's own `binary-sign-tool` is now part of the instructions, along with the two things a self-signature does *not* grant (permissions, JIT), and the credential-storage behaviour of the 2in1 user directory.

The capability table separates what was observed from what the target's `cfg` gates make unreachable, and states plainly that the interactive TUI has not been drawn on a device yet. I did not write claims I had not verified.

Chinese mirror updated in the same style; both pages have the same 13 sections.

**2. `feat(release)`: releases build, sign and publish a native HarmonyOS binary.**

Until now a release could not serve a native device at all, and `npm i -g codewhale` there installed the static Linux build, which a device refuses to start.

`aarch64-unknown-linux-ohos` becomes an eighth artifact target producing `codewhale-ohos-arm64`, `codew-ohos-arm64` and `codewhale-ohos-arm64.tar.gz`. The leg installs the published OpenHarmony 6.1 SDK (`native;toolchains`, `cache: false`), cross-compiles, signs with the SDK's `binary-sign-tool -selfSign 1`, and **fails unless `display-sign` reads back `code signature is self-sign`** — an unsigned ELF is refused at `execve`, so shipping one would be a dead download. It also asserts the file is an aarch64 ELF with the musl interpreter.

npm's `openharmony` platform now resolves to that native asset; `PLATFORM_ALIASES` was removed with it, and the OpenHarmony x64 branch of `assertCnbMirrorSupportedPlatform` now says it is x64-only rather than claiming to include OpenHarmony. Inventory stays exact and enforced (38 files / 8 targets), with the workflow, bundler, release-notes generator, runbook, checklist and `docs/features.toml` updated together.

## Issue

No-Issue: HarmonyOS support gaps found and fixed while building the native target; no tracking issue exists.

## How I tested it

Everything below was run on this branch after rebasing onto `origin/main` (`6dd9af54c`).

**The two documented failures, reproduced on base then fixed:**

```
# base 6dd9af54c, documented command, clean env
error: failed to run custom build command for `aws-lc-sys v0.46.0`   # "Missing dependency: cmake"

# base + only the ohos-env.sh change — proves the two bugs are independent
error: function `sha256_hex` is never used  -> crates/cli/src/hashing.rs:2
error: function `hex_bytes` is never used

# this branch, same command, bare PATH with no system cmake, no -A suppression
Finished `dev` profile [optimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 4m 58s
```

**Guards, all green:**

```
release-workflows.test.js            PASS   (8-target/38-asset contract)
assemble-release-assets.test.js      PASS
ensure-release-assets-absent.test.js PASS
verify-release-inventory.test.js     PASS
install-safety.test.js               PASS
compiled-host-delivery.test.js       PASS
npm-wrapper-smoke.test.js            PASS
npm codewhale suite                  PASS   (101/101)
generate-release-body.test.sh        PASS
prepare-release.test.sh              PASS
check-ohos-deps.sh                   PASS   (no-SDK dependency graph guard)
check-feature-release-notes.sh       PASS
feature_registry (cargo test)        PASS   (2/2 — covers the new row)
dev-test.sh secrets                  PASS   (46 passed)
dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-cli  PASS   (host profile)
```

**The release leg's own commands, replayed by hand against the real SDK and a real 120 MB binary**, which is how I caught a bug in my own step logic: `llvm-readelf | grep -q` cannot be used under `pipefail` — grep exits at the first match, readelf takes SIGPIPE and reports exit 74, so a *good* binary read as a failed verification. The step now captures and matches with `case`. Replayed:

```
OK signature     code signature is self-sign
OK arch          ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, ARM aarch64 … interpreter /lib/ld-musl-aarch64.so.1
OK interpreter
```

**Not verified:** the GitHub Actions run itself. The reuse of `components: 'native;toolchains'` and the assumption that `toolchains` lands beside `native` come from the local DevEco layout; if that is wrong the leg fails at `test -f "${signer}"`, which is a clear failure rather than a bad artifact. No device test of the *published* asset is possible until a release carrying it exists.

I also added a guard in `release-workflows.test.js` that every `- name:` in the three release workflows starts its own line: a `run:` block that loses its trailing newline glues the next step header onto the script text, which YAML accepts and which silently drops the step. I hit that while editing.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change per commit, started from current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and the changed behaviour is covered (feature registry test, npm suite, release invariants)
- [x] User-facing docs updated, and the new row added to `docs/features.toml`
- [x] No `CHANGELOG.md` hunks (per CONTRIBUTING.md: entries are written on `main` at merge time)

prs.title: fix(tui): keep asterisks that don't open emphasis
prs.body:
## What and why

`*` and `**` open emphasis wherever a matching run comes later on the line, so prose with spaced asterisks loses them, and the text between turns italic or bold. At 80 columns, before:

```
● Pass the rest through with args and *kwargs, like the base class does.
▏
▏ The timeout is 5  60  60 seconds, so 18000.
▏
▏ It runs on the schedule 0 9   1-5.
▏
▏ The formatter picks up .rs and .toml files.
▏
▏ Squares: x  2 + y  2.
▏
▏ Still styled: the real fix and this one.
```

The model wrote `*args and **kwargs`, `5 * 60 * 60`, the cron schedule `0 9 * * 1-5`, `*.rs and *.toml` and `x ** 2 + y ** 2`. After:

```
● Pass the rest through with *args and **kwargs, like the base class does.
▏
▏ The timeout is 5 * 60 * 60 seconds, so 18000.
▏
▏ It runs on the schedule 0 9 * * 1-5.
▏
▏ The formatter picks up *.rs and *.toml files.
▏
▏ Squares: x ** 2 + y ** 2.
▏
▏ Still styled: the real fix and this one.
```

An emphasis run now needs text right inside both delimiters, so it can't start or end with whitespace. That is the whitespace half of CommonMark's flanking rule. The `_` arm already checks it on the opening side (#6042); the asterisk arms didn't check it at all. The last line (`*real*`, `**this**`) renders as before, and a run with a space just inside a delimiter, like `** note **`, now shows its asterisks, as GitHub does. Punctuation next to a delimiter still doesn't matter, so `**注意：**后面` stays bold.

## Issue

No-Issue: spaced asterisks in prose open emphasis and disappear; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at 36f058c56 in a pseudo-terminal at 80x30 with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the six lines above; the rows above come from those runs. A second reply in Chinese checked that `**注意：**后面`, `这是*重点*` and `**关键**` still render as emphasis on both builds, and that `3 * 4 * 5` keeps its asterisks only with this change.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 13623 of 13625 passed, with the 139 tests whose names match `markdown`, `inline`, `emphasis`, `bold` or `italic` among them. The 2 failures (`status_report_localizes_the_complete_japanese_surface`, `test_update_model_compaction_budget`) also fail on `main` at 36f058c56 without this change.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` with CI's flags (also on 1.99), `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit`: clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on 36f058c56; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior — `cargo fmt` passes; no new test, per AGENTS.md, so the runs above stand in for one
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: fix(tui): render ~~~ fences as code blocks
prs.body:
## What and why

The markdown renderer only knows backtick fences, so a code block opened with `~~~` renders as prose, although the rest of the codebase already treats `~~~` as a fence (memory import, the agent roster, the plan handoff title). `~~~` is a common way to wrap text that has backtick fences of its own, such as a README section. In prose, a `# comment` line becomes a heading with a rule under it, indentation is dropped, and `*all*` turns italic. At 80 columns, before:

```
● Here is the script:
▏
▏ ~~~python
▏ Count the lines in each file
▏ ────────────────────────────────────────
▏ import sys
▏
▏ for path in sys.argv[1:]:
▏ with open(path) as f:
▏ print(path, sum(1 for _ in f))  # all lines
▏ ~~~
▏
▏ And the README section, which has a fence of its own:
▏
▏ ~~~markdown
▏ Usage
▏
    python count.py *.txt
▏ ~~~
▏
▏ Done.
```

After:

````
● Here is the script:
▏
    # Count the lines in each file
    import sys

    for path in sys.argv[1:]:
        with open(path) as f:
            print(path, sum(1 for _ in f))  # *all* lines
▏
▏ And the README section, which has a fence of its own:
▏
    ## Usage

    ```bash
    python count.py *.txt
    ```
▏
▏ Done.
````

The parser's fence carry now records the fence character along with its length. A fence closes only on the same character and at least the opener's length, so a backtick fence inside a `~~~` block is code, and the other way round. Backtick fences parse as before. `streaming_preview_tail_source` in the thinking preview mirrors the parser's fence rule to pick a cut that isn't inside a code block (a review note on #6249 pointed out the two would drift if the parser learned tilde fences), so it gets the same change; without it, a cut could land inside a `~~~` block and the preview would render the rest of that block as prose.

This touches the same lines as #7146 (the parser's carry and `push_parsed_line`'s signature). If that one lands first, I'll merge `main` in and resolve it here.

## Issue

No-Issue: code blocks fenced with `~~~` render as prose in the transcript; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at 36f058c56 in a pseudo-terminal at 80x50 with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the message above; the rows above come from those runs. A second reply checked the edges: `~~~bash` and backtick `bash` blocks holding `echo "$HOME and $USER"` both render as code with the `$` left alone, a four-backtick block keeps a `~~~` line inside it as code, a `~~~~` block is not closed by `~~~`, and `~~struck~~` text still renders struck through. On `main` the `~~~bash` line shows as text and the `~~~~` block's `- inside` lines render as list items.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 13623 of 13625 passed, with the 266 tests whose names match `markdown`, `fence` or `thinking` among them. The 2 failures (`status_report_localizes_the_complete_japanese_surface`, `test_update_model_compaction_budget`) also fail on `main` at 36f058c56 without this change.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` with CI's flags (also on 1.99), `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets`, `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` and `cargo doc -p codewhale-tui-kit --no-deps` with `-D warnings`: clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on 36f058c56; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior — `cargo fmt` passes; no new test, per AGENTS.md, so the runs above stand in for one
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: fix(tui): fork a conversation by the history it carries, not the shape it stores
prs.body:
No-Issue: found while diagnosing a user report of `/undo` refusing with "Cannot identify an exact saved-history boundary" and "full history exceeds byte transport bound"; the report is reproduced and explained in this description.

## What this fixes

Two independent reasons `/undo` (and retry, and fork-at-turn) refused to cut a
conversation that was otherwise perfectly usable. Both were reported from the
VS Code client; the TUI hits the same code.

### 1. The fork was measured by its stored shape, not by its history

A saved session repeats its own conversation while it carries a journal:
`messages` and the journal's active branch hold the same turns, so the file on
disk is up to twice the history it holds. The reader that opens such a document
already knows this — `SessionManager::load_session_snapshot_with_limit` judges
an oversized file by `SavedSession::transport_form` — but the fork writer
measured the stored shape against the same 8 MiB canonical bound.

Concretely, on a 9.75 MiB conversation whose carried form was 5.2 MiB, the
runtime kept opening it, saving it and running new turns, while `patch-undo`
answered `400 full history exceeds byte transport bound; source retained`
before it touched a file. `/undo` is a fork, so the turn stayed in the
transcript.

`saved_document_digest` already measured `transport_form()`. Both now go
through one `ensure_history_transport_fits`, so the writer's rule and the
reader's cannot drift apart again.

### 2. The saved-history boundary counted engine traffic as user prompts

The boundary walk reads a saved transcript as "the prompts a person typed", so
it can align the transcript against the turn records. Two kinds of engine
message were counted as prompts, and neither is ever recorded on a turn:

- runtime-owned control messages — the MCP-server notice, shell-completion
  handoffs, the deferred-toolbox snapshot
- the `<image path=…>` / `</image>` tags that bracket an attachment

A conversation that had received any of them could not be cut at all: `/undo`
answered `Cannot identify an exact saved-history boundary`. Both are now
skipped. The runtime-owned check is the same recognition the session views
already use (`turn_classify::is_runtime_owned_user_message`) and keys off the
runtime provenance line in the `<turn_meta>` envelope — which a person's own
prompt does not carry, so a real turn is never swallowed.

## Tests

Two new tests, both in `crates/tui/src/runtime_threads/tests.rs`:

- `a_fork_measures_the_history_it_carries_not_the_shape_it_stores` builds a
  conversation whose file passes the bound while its carried form does not,
  asserts the fixture really is in that regime, then forks it. Reverting the
  production change makes it fail with the exact reported error.
- `runtime_traffic_and_attachment_tags_are_not_kept_prompts` builds the three
  shapes (MCP notice, screenshot prompt, toolbox snapshot) and asserts both
  walks a fork runs land where the records say.

Verified locally on `origin/main` (6a08f0312):

```
cargo fmt --check -p codewhale-tui                          clean
cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets (CI lint set)    clean
dev-test.sh ... recovery::                                  27 passed
```

prs.title: fix(tui): keep the indent of a paragraph nested in a list
prs.body:
## What and why

A paragraph indented under a list item renders flush left: the word wrapper drops spaces at the start of a row, so the indent never reaches the screen. Models write these often, as a bullet's second paragraph or a note after a numbered step's code block. At 60 columns, before:

```
● Setup:
▏
▏ 1. Install the dependencies:
▏
       npm install --save-dev typescript
▏
▏ This also writes a lockfile, which you should commit
▏ together with the change.
▏
▏ 2. Build:
       npm run build
▏ 3. Check the config:
▏
       {
         "strict": true
       }
▏
▏ - A bullet with a second paragraph.
▏
▏ The second paragraph of that bullet, indented two spaces
▏ and long enough to wrap.
▏ - Last bullet
```

The code under step 1 keeps its indent but the note after it doesn't, so step 1 looks finished and the note reads as top-level text. After:

```
● Setup:
▏
▏ 1. Install the dependencies:
▏
       npm install --save-dev typescript
▏
▏    This also writes a lockfile, which you should commit
▏    together with the change.
▏
▏ 2. Build:
       npm run build
▏ 3. Check the config:
▏
       {
         "strict": true
       }
▏
▏ - A bullet with a second paragraph.
▏
▏   The second paragraph of that bullet, indented two
▏   spaces and long enough to wrap.
▏ - Last bullet
```

The parser now carries whether a list is open, next to its code-fence state: a list item opens it, blank lines, code and indented paragraphs keep it open, and anything else closes it. While a list is open, a paragraph keeps its leading spaces, and `render_paragraph_tagged` wraps the text in the remaining width and draws the indent on every row, capped at half the width like a list item's indent (#7030); links shift with it. The decision is made when the line is parsed rather than in the renderer, because streaming renders the text between code blocks separately and a look-back there would not match the final render. Copy follows list items: the first row copies with its indent, as written, and wrapped rows strip it.

Command notes go through the same renderer, and some have indented rows that aren't under a list item, such as `/status`'s key/value rows and part of `/cost`. Those render as before: I ran `/status`, `/cost`, `/context`, `/hooks`, `/mcp`, `/skills`, `/tools`, `/memory`, `/doctor`, `/version`, `/usage`, `/agents`, `/workspace`, `/permissions`, `/sandbox`, `/todo`, `/goal`, `/diff`, `/stats` and `/profile` in one session on both builds, and the screens match once the session id is masked. A first version that kept every indent did shift `/status` and `/cost`, which is why the decision follows the list.

## Issue

No-Issue: a paragraph indented under a list item renders flush left; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at 588426ddd in a pseudo-terminal at 60 columns with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the steps and bullets above; the rows above come from those runs.
- Selection copy: with a throwaway test (not part of this PR) that selects `1. Install` followed by an indented paragraph, and `- item` followed by an indented line, at 24 columns and calls `selection_to_text`, this change copies both as written (`"1. Install\n\n   alpha beta … kappa"`); `main` copies them without the indent (`"1. Install\n\nalpha beta … kappa"`).
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 13880 of 13886 passed, with the 427 tests whose names match `markdown`, `paragraph`, `selection` or `transcript` among them. The 6 failures (`status_public_output_and_read_only_state_match_baseline`, `golden_turn_events_match`, `model_visible_prefix_bytes_match_goldens`, `interrupted_session_deletion_keeps_recovery_incomplete_and_can_finish`, `worker_compacts_past_its_context_window_and_keeps_working`, `reasoning_effort_uses_one_strict_alias_table_and_legacy_fallback`) also fail on `main` at 588426ddd without this change.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` with CI's flags (also on 1.99), `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit`: clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on 588426ddd; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior — `cargo fmt` passes; no new test, per AGENTS.md, so the runs above stand in for one
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: fix(tui): end a bare URL at full-width punctuation
prs.body:
## What and why

A bare URL runs to the next whitespace, and Chinese and Japanese text doesn't put a space after one. So the link takes in the punctuation and the words that follow, both on screen and in the OSC 8 target, which then points at a page that doesn't exist. This reply, at 80 columns:

```
● 项目地址：https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale。克隆后运行 cargo build
▏ 即可。
▏
▏ 文档在这里（https://docs.rs/ratatui/latest/ratatui/），先看 Buffer。
▏
▏ 维基条目 https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/北京，另外 https://example.com/a,
▏ then more.
▏
▏ 日本語：https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ジョン・レノン。続き。
▏
▏ 官网是“https://example.com/q”，另见‘https://example.com/s’。
```

left these hyperlink targets in the terminal once the reply finished, before:

```
https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale。克隆后运行
https://docs.rs/ratatui/latest/ratatui/），先看
https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/北京，另外
https://example.com/a
https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ジョン・レノン。続き。
https://example.com/q”，另见‘https://example.com/s’。
```

After:

```
https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale
https://docs.rs/ratatui/latest/ratatui/
https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/北京
https://example.com/a
https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ジョン・レノン
https://example.com/q
https://example.com/s
```

The text drawn in the link style covers exactly the target in both runs, so before this `。克隆后运行` and `），先看` were styled as part of the link too, and the last line was one link that swallowed the second URL.

A bare URL now also ends at full-width sentence and clause punctuation and brackets (`。，、；：！？（）「」『』【】《》〈〉`) and at curly quotes (`“”‘’`). It doesn't stop at every CJK character: ideographs and kana can be part of a URL, so `北京` and `ジョン・レノン` stay in the link. Trailing ASCII punctuation is trimmed as before, and `[text](url)` links are unaffected. A URL followed by an ideograph with nothing in between (`https://example.com然后`) still runs on, since that can't be told apart from an ideograph in the path.

## Issue

No-Issue: a bare URL in Chinese or Japanese text takes in the punctuation and words after it; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at 36f058c56 in a pseudo-terminal at 80x30 with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the text above, and recorded the OSC 8 targets in the output next to the screen (OSC 8 is on by default outside Windows); the rows and targets above come from those runs.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 13623 of 13625 passed, with the 411 tests whose names match `markdown`, `url`, `link` or `osc8` among them. The 2 failures (`status_report_localizes_the_complete_japanese_surface`, `test_update_model_compaction_budget`) also fail on `main` at 36f058c56 without this change.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` with CI's flags (also on 1.99), `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit`: clean.

## Checklist

prs.title: fix(tui): drop the engine's status reply to a fleet roster refresh
prs.body:
## What and why

Every fleet change ends in `Op::SetFleetRoster`, and the engine answered each one with a status: "Fleet roster refreshed for subsequent turns". The change itself already has a receipt (the `/fleet add|remove` note in the transcript, the route editors' toasts, the "Team … profile saved" status), so the engine's line only arrives after it and takes over the footer, where in English it also pushes the Shift+Tab hint off the row. After `/fleet add openai mock`, before:

```
Note Added openai/mock to the team My fleet (new personal team, now selected)
…
 ● ask   work (Tab)   Work bar (Ctrl+])                 Fleet roster refreshed for subsequent turns
```

It was still there 7 seconds later, and with `LANG=zh_CN.UTF-8` it is the one English sentence on the screen:

```
Note 已将 openai/mock 添加到 Fleet My fleet （新的个人 Fleet，已选中）
…
 ● ask  Shift+Tab 切换   work (Tab)   Work bar (Ctrl+]) Fleet roster refreshed for subsequent turns
```

After:

```
Note Added openai/mock to the team My fleet (new personal team, now selected)
…
 ● ask  Shift+Tab to change   work (Tab)   Work bar (Ctrl+])
```

```
Note 已将 openai/mock 添加到 Fleet My fleet （新的个人 Fleet，已选中）
…
 ● ask  Shift+Tab 切换   work (Tab)   Work bar (Ctrl+])
```

The engine now stores the roster without sending a status. Nothing reads that message, and the TUI is the only sender of the op. 04de8eb67 fixed the same kind of ack replacing a host receipt for `SetCompaction`.

## Issue

No-Issue: the engine's ack to a fleet roster refresh replaces the fleet receipts in the footer; I searched and found no issue for it

issues.title: [Feature]: Generate short multi-speaker dialogue with the bundled ElevenLabs plugin

labels.name: P3

issues.body:
### Summary

Add an optional tool to the existing ElevenLabs plugin that turns an ordered script with two selected voices into one generated dialogue MP3.

### Problem to solve

A scripted interview or podcast scene needs a relationship between each line and its speaker, together with the surrounding exchange. The [podcast_generator project](https://github.com/sjfischr/podcast_generator/blob/d1a7ca31814995bd3748b771ab348789df441783/README.md) implements this task using batches of speaker turns. Its author explains why synthesizing each turn separately and assembling the recordings does not provide the same conversational context. That is an external implementation and reported motivation; I have not independently evaluated its audio quality.

There is also an OpenClaw-specific consumer surface: [pixcli's registry README](https://hub.openclaw.ai/shellbot/plugins/openclaw-pixcli) advertises optional dialogue and podcast tools. It is an existing alternative, not a request from its author to migrate.

The bundled ElevenLabs integration currently accepts one text and one voice per synthesis request. A speaker name written into that text does not become a second voice assignment. The requested output is a short jointly generated exchange using the operator's ElevenLabs voices, rather than an ordinary spoken assistant reply. Applicability to operators of the bundled plugin is an inference from these public workflows, not a reported OpenClaw outage.

### Proposed solution

Keep this capability inside `extensions/elevenlabs`, behind an explicitly enabled plugin tool; `elevenlabs_dialogue` is a suggested name. Use the existing optional-tool registration and manifest contracts. Do not expand the core `tts` tool or the shared speech interface.

The initial tool would accept an ordered array of nonempty `{text, voiceId}` turns, with exactly two distinct voice IDs. Generate a single bounded scene using Eleven v3 and return one MP3 artifact. Preserve turn order and inline audio tags. Reject scripts above a total of 2,000 text characters before making a request; this intentionally excludes automatic long-form episode production.

Reuse the plugin's configured authentication, runtime-resolved secrets, trusted base URL and guarded HTTP helpers for `POST /v1/text-to-dialogue`. Use `mp3_44100_128`. Do not accept credentials, arbitrary endpoints or publication destinations in tool arguments. Keep normal tool admission, cancellation and current invocation authority. A provider error must not silently substitute another provider or turn the script into single-voice narration. Do not automatically regenerate or replay a request whose paid outcome is unknown.

Return the audio through existing media storage and tool-result/reply contracts. Artifact creation and delivery must be distinguished; do not claim delivery from a local path alone.

### Alternatives considered

- Repeated TTS calls followed by audio assembly preserve voice assignments, but each synthesis lacks the complete exchange. They remain useful when independently editable stems are the goal.
- The external Python project or a direct ElevenLabs SDK integration can already perform the vendor request; a custom OpenClaw tool can wrap that existing contract. An equivalent multi-voice operation in the current hosted ElevenLabs MCP was not established. These are valid alternatives; this proposal adds a narrowly scoped operation to an existing bundled owner, rather than claiming that OpenClaw cannot run such a workflow at all.
- pixcli already supplies dialogue tooling through its separately configured Meterkey service. Its README permits private output; it does not force public publishing. Keeping the existing ElevenLabs account and voice catalog is the distinction here, not an invented ban on other plugins.
- Other speech providers can offer dialogue, but their voices are not the selected ElevenLabs voice IDs.

### Impact

- Affected users/systems/channels: operators generating two-voice scripted scenes with the bundled ElevenLabs integration. The public projects establish the task, not the size of this population.
- Severity/urgency: an additional authoring capability; existing single-voice speech remains available. No production incident or urgency has been established.
- Frequency: unknown. Each qualifying scene needs one bounded dialogue request.
- Practical consequences: the bundled integration cannot currently express both speaker assignments in a joint synthesis. Operators use a separate integration or assemble independently generated turns. No measured time savings or quality improvement is claimed.

### Evidence/examples

- [External batch producer](https://github.com/sjfischr/podcast_generator/blob/d1a7ca31814995bd3748b771ab348789df441783/generate_podcast.py): `build_batches` and `generate_dialogue_batch` preserve speaker turns. Its older batch-size assumptions should not be copied.
- [ElevenLabs API contract](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-dialogue/convert): ordered text/voice pairs produce audio. This proposal uses a smaller two-voice subset and the current short-request guidance.
- [Current bundled request builder](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8b8c33ef334b3754f42afe2a2e212418abfa80f4/extensions/elevenlabs/speech-provider-factory.ts) and [plugin entry](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8b8c33ef334b3754f42afe2a2e212418abfa80f4/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts): scalar synthesis and no dialogue tool.
- [Existing optional-tool contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8b8c33ef334b3754f42afe2a2e212418abfa80f4/docs/plugins/building-plugins.md#registering-tools).
- Related [issue #165655](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/165655) / [PR #165656](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165656) concern dialogue-model transport for a single speaking voice and phone-call socket reuse. The inspected open PR sends one text/voice pair; this proposal concerns a structured multi-voice script and an audio file.

This is static source and public-contract research. No vendor request, installed-plugin execution or listening test was performed.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Suggested implementation: register an optional version 2 tool in the existing plugin and declare its manifest ownership; factor reusable plugin-local credential/config and request helpers rather than copying their policy. The public factory context already supplies runtime config, provider-key resolution and `assertInvocationCurrent`; recheck current authority after awaited preparation and before the request and artifact admission. Reuse focused media-store and bounded binary-response helpers. For a finished direct reply, the existing `canDeliverSourceReply` / `details.sourceReply` contract can deliver the artifact; nested Code Mode execution remains program data under that contract.

Non-goals: real-time calls, WebSocket pooling, new v4 model support, voice cloning, speaker identification, transcription, pronunciation-dictionary management, long-script chunking, audio editing, podcast hosting, public uploads, new persistent jobs, and a generic dialogue SDK. Existing TTS defaults, personas and fallback behavior remain outside this tool's operation.

Acceptance criteria:

- With the tool explicitly enabled and usable ElevenLabs credentials, submit a short A/B/A script with two accessible voice IDs. One dialogue request preserves the three turns and both IDs, and returns a playable MP3. Confirm the supplied voice assignments with a listening test as well as the request trace; do not promise subjective quality.
- The returned artifact is usable through the actual tool/result path. A direct source reply reaches only the admitted source conversation; a nested program call returns data without an unsolicited send.
- Empty text, malformed voice ID syntax, a missing second voice, and a script over the character budget fail before the vendor request. A syntactically valid voice ID may still be unavailable to the account; surface that provider access/validation failure honestly rather than claiming local validation proves access. The disabled tool is absent from discovery. Cancellation, a retired invocation, and credential/plugin disablement do not admit a new request or publish a success artifact.
- Authentication, validation, timeout, malformed audio and size-limit failures produce an actionable error, without silent voice/provider substitution or automatic paid regeneration. Existing single-voice TTS still works with its previous defaults.

Implementer unknown. Live synthesis, real tool delivery, failure/cancellation proof and focused plugin/contract checks remain work for the eventual implementation. Maintainers should decide whether this existing-owner enhancement is worth maintaining relative to the external alternatives.
