issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

An established owner's direct Telegram conversation is held by `providerReview` after an apparent identity-alias false positive, with findings available but no provider continuation or supported local owner-resolution action.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

The owner previously used this same Telegram conversation successfully. After a review stop, the owner needs a documented investigation/resolution path that preserves the review and history. We are not requesting an automatic retry or an override of a provider restriction. Installed documentation says a conversation without supported continuation remains stopped; this report asks maintainers to investigate the apparent false positive and the resulting owner-recovery gap.

### Actual behavior

The provider findings question whether the Telegram sender was authorised because the Telegram display-name alias differs from the workspace owner's name. The authenticated gateway owner confirms the account is theirs; the triggering input has `senderIsOwner=true`, existing workspace memory records the alias, and the gateway reports `sharingRole=owner`.

Repeated read-only observations show:

```json
{
  "status": "failed",
  "hasActiveRun": false,
  "sharingRole": "owner",
  "providerReview": {
    "explanation": "[present; private content omitted]",
    "canContinue": false
  }
}
```

The stored review has `errorType=other`, no continuation object, and valid native thread/turn identifiers. The UI presents findings but no Continue action. No fresh inference or blocked-workflow retry was used to test this.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.9 (bcfc888)

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2

### Install method

Global Node package installation; native Codex plugin installed through OpenClaw's npm-managed plugin installation.

### Model

openai/gpt-6-astra

### Provider / routing chain

Telegram -> OpenClaw -> native Codex app-server harness -> OpenAI

### Additional provider/model setup details

Codex plugin 2026.9.9; installed @openai/codex dependency 0.160.0. The affected review records runtimeId=codex and api=openai-responses. No credentials or private account identifiers are included.

### Logs

The bounded operational log records an incomplete error turn at 2026-10-20 18:31:34 +10:00. It does not retain the original provider error payload. The evidence therefore cannot distinguish a missing/null provider steer from one rejected by validation.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- Installed `docs/web/control-ui/chat.md`, Conversations stopped for review: without supported continuation, the conversation remains stopped.

issues.body:
### Summary

The Active Memory timeout circuit breaker (#74054) should pause recall after `circuitBreakerMaxTimeouts` consecutive timeouts (default 3) for `circuitBreakerCooldownMs` (default 60 000). It never opens when timed-out turns arrive more than `circuitBreakerCooldownMs` apart, which is the normal case in a chat:

- A recall has already used its whole budget by the time its timeout is recorded. Two back-to-back timeouts in one conversation are therefore at least `timeoutMs + setupGraceTimeoutMs` apart, plus however long the user takes to reply.
- Since PR #105316, `recordCircuitBreakerTimeout()` drops a key whose last timeout is older than the cooldown before incrementing it. With a budget of 60 s or more, every timeout restarts the count at 1. With the default 15 s budget, the breaker opens only if each timed-out turn lands within 60 s of the previous one.

So when the recall model can't finish inside its budget, every turn waits the full budget, then runs without memory context, and the in-flight model stream is aborted. Recall is never paused.

### Where (main @ cf2558f5639e)

- `extensions/active-memory/recall-state.ts:62-77`: `recordCircuitBreakerTimeout()` deletes every entry with `now - lastTimeoutAt >= cooldownMs`, including the key being recorded (loop at 64-68). It then sets `consecutiveTimeouts: (entry?.consecutiveTimeouts ?? 0) + 1`. `recall-state.test.ts:51` ("restarts an expired key before adding a new timeout") pins this behavior.
- `extensions/active-memory/recall-state.ts:45-60`: once the breaker is open, the first check after the cooldown deletes the record ("reset and allow one attempt through"). A probe that times out starts again from 1 instead of re-opening. PR #100176 proposed a half-open fix but was closed for inactivity without review.
- `extensions/active-memory/recall.ts:216-238`: the breaker check. `recall.ts:366` and `:382` already reset the key after any non-timeout result, so expiring the count is not what keeps it from going stale.
- `extensions/active-memory/types.ts:28-29`: defaults 3 / 60 000 ms. The schema allows a cooldown up to 600 000 ms, but a longer cooldown also widens the window that counts as "consecutive".

### Steps to reproduce

Unit level, with the same fake-timer setup as `recall-state.test.ts`:

```ts
const key = buildCircuitBreakerKey("main", "local", "slow-model");
for (let turn = 0; turn < 5; turn++) {
  vi.advanceTimersByTime(150_000); // each timed-out turn spends its full budget first
  recordCircuitBreakerTimeout(key, 60_000);
}
expect(isCircuitBreakerOpen(key, 3, 60_000)).toBe(true); // fails on main: the count is back to 1
```

End to end:
1. Enable Active Memory for direct chats with `logging: true` and the breaker defaults. Point recall at a model that can't answer within `timeoutMs`, such as a local reasoning model with `thinking` raised, or an endpoint that stalls.
2. In one chat, send five messages, each after the previous reply arrives.
3. Every turn logs `done status=timeout elapsedMs≈<budget>` and starts its reply only after the full budget. The breaker's skip line never appears (`skipped (recall paused after consecutive timeouts)` on main, `skipped (circuit breaker open after consecutive timeouts)` in 2026.10.6).

### Observed (one host, 2026.10.5 and 2026.10.6, 2026-10-16 to 2026-10-22)

Active Memory config: `mode: always`, `queryMode: full`, `promptStyle: recall-heavy`, `thinking: xhigh`, `timeoutMs: 120000`, `setupGraceTimeoutMs: 30000` (both at the schema maximum), `logging: true`, breaker defaults. Recall runs on the agent's own model, a local reasoning model served through oMLX (OpenAI-compatible, one inference slot). Counts come from the gateway log's `active-memory: … start` and `done status=…` lines:

| Outcome | Recalls | Elapsed |
|---|---:|---|
| completed | 211 | p50 63 s, p75 90 s, p90 113 s, max 148.5 s |
| timed out | 106 (30%) | 150.0–150.2 s, `summaryChars=0` every time |
| failed (unrelated errors, first three days only) | 41 | — |

- Timeouts came in runs of up to 13 with no completed recall in between. Run lengths: 1 (×36), 2 (×8), 3 (×5), 4, 6, 8 (×2), 13.
- Back-to-back timeouts were a median 643 s apart. 6 of the 52 back-to-back pairs were under 60 s apart, and 4 of those came from one burst of five concurrent recalls that timed out together.
- The breaker's skip line was logged 0 times in seven days (`skipped (circuit breaker open after consecutive timeouts)` in 2026.10.6; main logs `skipped (recall paused after consecutive timeouts)`).
- Raising `circuitBreakerCooldownMs` does not work around this. Replaying these 358 recalls through the 2026.10.6 breaker logic (outcomes as logged, state cleared at each gateway restart) with the maximum cooldown of 600 000 ms would have paused 3 recalls with `circuitBreakerMaxTimeouts: 3` and 8 with `2`. With the default 60 000 ms the replay pauses none, matching the log.
- The 106 timeouts held replies for about 4.4 h in total and returned nothing. Each one also aborted the in-flight stream. The provider logged a cancelled request, and the single inference slot spent 150 s on work that was discarded.

### Expected

- Count consecutive timeouts by outcome: a new timeout should not expire its own key. Pruning other stale keys and the 1000-key cap from PR #105316 already keep the map bounded, and a completed recall already resets the key.
- Keep the tripped state across the cooldown (half-open), as PR #100176 proposed. Let one probe through, re-open at once if it times out, and clear on success.
- Make the pause outlast the gap between turns, for example by skipping the next N recalls or by deriving the default cooldown from the recall budget. A 60 s pause expires before a human sends the next message, even with the default 15 s budget.

### Data for #86065

#86065 (raise the 120 000 ms `timeoutMs` ceiling) was closed as not planned because longer waits make the reply feel hung. The decision asked for live local-model measurements, and the table above is one, taken at the current ceiling:

- 17 of the 211 completed recalls finished between 120 s and 150 s, inside `setupGraceTimeoutMs`.
- 30% of recalls still reached the ceiling, so the user waited the full 150 s and got nothing back.

This issue doesn't ask to change the ceiling. A breaker that actually opens is what bounds that cost for slow deployments today, and any longer opt-in budget would depend on it.

### Related

#74054 and PR #74158 (breaker added), PR #105316 (expiry when a timeout is recorded), PR #100176 (half-open fix, closed as stale), #86065 and PR #87606 (ceiling), #90082 (the opposite failure mode, before these changes), #72015.

### Version

OpenClaw 2026.10.6 (fe06181), Linux arm64, npm global install. The breaker code is the same on main @ cf2558f5639e (2026-10-22).

issues.body:
## User story

As an operator, I want `openclaw gateway suspend status <suspensionId>` so I can poll an existing cooperative-suspension lease (running / draining / ready, blockers, expiry, optional lifecycle) without hand-writing `gateway call` JSON — especially while a host freeze, drain, or shutdown is in progress and I need a first-class terminal check before `resume`.

## Problem

Cooperative host suspension already has a supported Gateway contract:

- `gateway.suspend.prepare` (`operator.admin`) — create a short suspension lease (busy / draining / ready)
- `gateway.suspend.status` (`operator.read`) — poll that lease: `running` | `draining` | `ready`, plus blockers / `retryAfterMs` / `expiresAtMs` / optional lifecycle
- `gateway.suspend.resume` (`operator.admin`) — release the lease after thaw or abandonment

Docs already describe these RPCs ([external apps / cooperative host suspension](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/external-apps#cooperative-host-suspension), [gateway protocol](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/protocol/rpc-system-and-channels), [CLI query](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/gateway/query#gateway-suspend)). The native CLI already exposes prepare and resume:

```bash
openclaw gateway suspend [--request-id ...] [--wait ...] [--json]
openclaw gateway resume <suspensionId> [--json]
```

There is **no** native `openclaw gateway suspend status`. Operators who need a one-shot poll (drain progress after prepare with `drain: true`, shutdown progress after handoff commit, or "is this lease still held?") must compose:

```bash
openclaw gateway call gateway.suspend.status --params '{"suspensionId":"…","includeLifecycle":true}' --json
```

`gateway suspend --wait` only polls via repeated **prepare** with one stable `requestId`; it does not replace status polling for an already-issued `suspensionId` (including drain/shutdown phases where prepare is the wrong verb).

## Proposal

Add a native CLI verb that forwards the existing Gateway method only (Alix / #148903 / #181280 pattern — complete the terminal adapter; no new query engine, schema, permissions, or suspension behavior):

```bash
openclaw gateway suspend status <suspensionId> [--include-lifecycle] [--json] [--url ...] [--token ...] [--timeout ...] [--port ...]
```

Behavior:

- Call `gateway.suspend.status` with `{ suspensionId, includeLifecycle? }` matching the existing Gateway validators (`operator.read`).
- Print the Gateway JSON payload (`--json`) or a short human summary of `status` / blockers / expiry (consistent with sibling `gateway suspend` / `gateway resume`).
- Exit non-zero on RPC/auth failure; do not invent local lease state.
- Docs: add under `docs/cli/gateway/query.md` next to suspend / resume; TOC link from `docs/cli/gateway.md`; point to the existing protocol / external-apps pages.

## Acceptance criteria

1. On a running Gateway, after a successful `openclaw gateway suspend` (ready lease), `openclaw gateway suspend status <suspensionId>` exits 0 and returns `status: "ready"` (and `expiresAtMs` / optional lifecycle when requested).
2. When no matching lease is held, the command exits 0 with `status: "running"` (same RPC semantics as today — not an error).
3. While draining / after shutdown commit (where RPC still answers), the command returns the existing `draining` / lifecycle fields from `gateway.suspend.status` without calling prepare or resume.
4. Without Gateway / without read scope, the command fails with the same class of error as other Gateway RPC CLI verbs (no local fake status).
5. Packaged/registered CLI proof: before → missing `status` under `gateway suspend`; after → RPC observed with method `gateway.suspend.status` and successful JSON.
6. Colocated CLI registration / unit tests cover forwarding + option plumbing; no production LOC beyond the thin CLI adapter and docs.
7. Explicit non-goals: does not change suspension lease semantics, does not add persistent maintenance pause (#180736), does not replace `gateway suspend --wait` prepare polling, does not add new Gateway methods.

## CLI proof sketch

```bash
# With a local Gateway already running and credentials available to the CLI:
READY=$(openclaw gateway suspend --json)
ID=$(printf '%s' "$READY" | jq -r .suspensionId)

openclaw gateway suspend status "$ID" --json
# expect: { "status": "ready", "expiresAtMs": … }

openclaw gateway suspend status "$ID" --include-lifecycle --json
# expect: same + optional lifecycle / writeCustody fields when the Gateway provides them

openclaw gateway resume "$ID" --json
openclaw gateway suspend status "$ID" --json
# expect: { "status": "running" }

# Wire/parity check (existing escape hatch must keep working):
openclaw gateway call gateway.suspend.status --params "{\"suspensionId\":\"$ID\"}" --json
```

Independent reread: Command registration + Gateway client request only; canonical lease ownership stays in existing `gateway.suspend.status` handlers (`getGatewaySuspendStatus` / protocol validators).

## Scope / non-goals / related

- **Not** #180736 (persistent maintenance pause / queue-across-restart product). This only exposes the already-shipped `gateway.suspend.status` RPC as CLI.
- **Not** #127602 (operation-scoped restored-admission status) — different surface.
- Does not change `gateway.suspend.prepare` / `resume` / handoff behavior or scopes (`status` remains `operator.read`).
- Closely analogous to #148903 (`automations runs --all` exposing existing `cron.runs`) and #181280 (`sessions storage status|run` exposing existing `sessions.storage.*`).
- Note: #181352 was an accidental duplicate opened under a different GitHub identity; treat this issue as the canonical Feature request.

Prepared against current `main`. Runtime proof and review will be linked from the implementation PR; no maintainer sponsorship is claimed.

issues.body:
## Summary

`openclaw config set ... --provider-env` and `openclaw mcp add --env/--header` accept `KEY=VALUE` entries and build them into a plain object with `entries[key] = value`. When the key is `__proto__`, that assignment hits `Object.prototype`'s legacy setter instead of creating an own property, so the entry is **silently dropped** — the command still exits 0 and writes the config, just without the requested key. No warning, no error, nothing in the written file.

## Impact

- An operator who passes `--provider-env __proto__=…` (or `mcp add --env/--header __proto__=…`) gets a silently incomplete config instead of an error.
- The same failure mode is already guarded at the MCP server-name boundary (`src/config/zod-schema.root-support.ts`); the two CLI `KEY=VALUE` boundaries (`src/cli/config-cli-input.ts` `parseProviderEnvEntries`, `src/cli/mcp-cli.ts` `parseKeyValueEntries`) lack the guard.

## Environment

OpenClaw CLI, any platform.

## Suggested fix

Reject a `__proto__` key at the CLI `KEY=VALUE` parse boundaries with an actionable message naming the flag and key, matching the existing server-name precedent. Only `__proto__` is affected (the key silently dropped); `constructor`/`prototype` are ordinary own properties and not part of this bug.

> A fix is in progress in PR #172325.

## Summary

`createCodexPluginsTool` resolved the workspace for native-plugin discovery with `binding?.cwd?.trim() || options.context.workspaceDir?.trim() || ...` (`native-plugin-tool.ts`). The bound cwd is stored untrimmed (`app-server/thread-lifecycle-io.ts` persists `cwd: params.cwd` verbatim at session start), so this leaf trim rewrote the session's literal workspace identity before building the `plugin/list` request. The Codex app-server then scanned the trimmed impostor directory for marketplace plugins instead of the real one — **discovery silently returns nothing** for a workspace whose name carries edge whitespace.

## Impact

- Marketplace plugin discovery scans the wrong directory for a workspace whose name ends in whitespace.
- The stored binding record already keeps the raw cwd; only this discovery leaf trims it.

## Environment

Codex extension, paired node sessions / catalog continue path, Linux.

## Suggested fix

Use `readNonBlankString` on each fallback level in `createCodexPluginsTool`: nonblank values flow verbatim into the discovery `cwds` request parameter; blank/whitespace-only values still fall through to the next source. This matches the whitespace-preserving convention already used for the app-server binding `workspaceDir` in `conversation-binding-data.ts`.

> A fix is in progress in PR #188122.

issues.body:
## Summary

`openclaw config set` records the new value **in the clear** in the local config-audit record (`<state>/state/openclaw.sqlite`, `diagnostic_events`, scope `config-audit`, latest 50000 rows) when a value-taking option such as `--expect-current-json` appears **before** the config path and value — even when that path is secret-bearing.

The documented conditional write with the option first — `openclaw config set --expect-current-json <json> <secret-path> <secret>` — stores the secret unredacted. The same command with the option after the positionals redacts correctly.

## Why

`findConfigPositionals` decides which `config set` arguments are the path and the value, so it must skip the value of every value-taking option (`CONFIG_SET_VALUE_OPTIONS`). `--expect-current-json` is registered on `config set` (`src/cli/config-cli.ts:375-378`) but was **missing from the set**, so its JSON payload was counted as the path (`src/config/io.audit.ts:71-79`); the sensitive-path check then evaluated the payload instead of the real path and skipped the value (`src/config/io.audit.ts:114-123`).

## Impact

- A secret (e.g. `models.providers.openai.apiKey`) passed with the option-first order persists unredacted in the local audit DB.
- Any operator or tooling with read access to the state DB can recover it.

## Environment

OpenClaw CLI, any platform.

## Suggested fix

Add the missing value option to `CONFIG_SET_VALUE_OPTIONS` so positional discovery is order-independent (it is the only `config set` value option absent from the list). No config format, CLI surface, default behavior, or migration change.

> A fix is in progress in PR #172255.

issues.body:
## Summary

Slack outbound route discovery keeps issuing authenticated Slack API requests after the transport authority that authorized the send has been invalidated. The Slack `resolveOutboundSessionRoute` implementation (`extensions/slack/src/channel.ts`) drops the `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` callback that `src/sessions/confirmed-visible-message.ts:235` forwards into it, so none of its three remote lookups revalidate current authority before touching the network:

- Enterprise owner-heartbeat DM workspace discovery — `users.info` + `auth.teams.list` (`extensions/slack/src/enterprise-user-route.ts`)
- D-prefix conversation classification — `conversations.info` (`extensions/slack/src/channel-type.ts`)
- G-prefix conversation classification — `conversations.info` (same owner)

When a Gateway restart or delivery supersession invalidates the worker admission between message acceptance and route discovery, Slack still receives authenticated destination-metadata requests. The request cost lands on the operator's credentials.

## Why

The SDK contract already documents the parameter's purpose (`src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts:619-620`): "Revalidates transport authority before new route-discovery network requests." Slack already forwards the callback on the action path, send path, and conversation-metadata path — the **route path** (`resolveOutboundSessionRoute`) is the only remaining gap. This is the Slack analogue of merged #185972 (googlechat).

## Impact

- A workspace-controlled D/G conversation id or a revoked token keeps being probed after local authority expired.
- Route discovery requests land on the operator's credentials without current admission coverage.

## Environment

Slack channel, Gateway restart or delivery supersession between message acceptance and route discovery.

## Suggested fix

Forward the already-supplied `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` callback into the three route-discovery network owners, reusing the existing `fenceSlackReadFetch` / `createSlackLookupClient` mechanism. Zero new validators/options/config.

> A fix is in progress in PR #186346.

## Summary

The **mxc** sandbox fs bridge trimmed the tool-supplied `filePath` before mapping it onto its mounts (`extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts` `MxcFsBridge.resolveTarget`), so a literal file name like `" x.txt"` silently addressed its trimmed sibling `x.txt`. A sandboxed agent reading or writing `" x.txt"` touched the decoy file instead of the one the model chose.

## Impact

- Wrong-file reads and wrong-file writes in mxc-sandbox-backed agents for whitespace-bearing file names.
- The mount-containment guard is unchanged and operates on the literal-resolved path after the fix.

## Environment

MXC sandbox backend (Windows host), any file name with leading/trailing whitespace.

## Suggested fix

Resolve the caller's literal `filePath` in `MxcFsBridge.resolveTarget`, keeping only the optional invocation base (`cwd`) on its `trim()` blank-check — matching the shape accepted in the merged #187554.

> A fix is in progress in PR #187766.

issues.body:
## Summary

Two path-selected inputs still get trimmed before use, so a configured value whose name ends in whitespace silently addresses a **different** file or SSH key:

1. **Remote-shell sandbox file bridge** (`sandbox.backend: "ssh"` / remote shell): `resolveTarget` ran `params.filePath.trim()`, so requesting `" note.txt"` read/wrote the sibling `note.txt`. A read returned the wrong file; a write overwrote it.
2. **Configured SSH identity** (`gateway.remote.sshIdentity`): the identity was trimmed before reaching `ssh -i`, so a configured identity file whose path ends in whitespace loaded a different key. Three Gateway owners did this: `gatewayStatusCommand` (`sanitizeSshTarget` on the configured value), `resolveGatewayDeviceAuthRoute` (`normalizeOptionalString`), and `resolveSshConfig` (`opts.identity.trim()`).

## Impact

- Wrong-file reads and destructive wrong-file writes in SSH/remote-shell sandboxes for whitespace-bearing paths.
- SSH authentication with the wrong key when `gateway.remote.sshIdentity` ends in whitespace — the configured identity silently fails to authenticate or loads an unintended key.

## Environment

OpenClaw, Linux (isolated test box). Real reproduction on the compiled production `dist/` against a real `sshd` on `127.0.0.1:2222`; a real agent turn and real ssh client are used.

## Suggested fix

Keep the selected path literal at every owner that holds the configured value; the trimming resolver still owns only CLI-typed invocation strings and the SSH host target. The mount-containment guard is unchanged. A fix is in progress in PR #188906 (and independently in sibling PR #187825, which addresses the same remote-shell `resolveTarget` site).

issues.body:
### Summary

The exec auto-reviewer's pre-model guard `textLooksLikeReviewerDirective()` (`src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.ts`) denies ordinary shell commands as "reviewer-directed text" when a hyphenated CLI flag or subcommand contains `ignore` and a later path or argument contains `policy`, `system`, `prompt`, `instruction` or `developer`. Punctuation is normalized to spaces before matching, so `check-ignore`, `--ignore-case`, `--no-ignore` and `--ignore=` all become the bare word `ignore`, and the first regex then matches a filename like `channel-policy.md`.

For exec requests the result is `decision: "deny", risk: "high"` (widgets get `ask`). The agent is then told not to try a workaround, so a harmless read-only check fails with no way to recover.

### Evidence

Observed in production on 2026.10.x with an agent in `exec.mode: "auto"`:

```
command: git check-ignore media/outbound/<name>-channel-policy-2026-10-20.md
result:  Exec denied by auto-review (risk=high): exec reviewer denied the command because it contains reviewer-directed text
```

We ran the same function, copied verbatim from `main` @ `b1b0a8890` (2026-11-01), on a few commands:

| command | flagged |
|---|---|
| `git check-ignore media/outbound/channel-policy-2026-10-20.md` | true |
| `git check-ignore media/outbound/channel-notes-2026-10-20.md` | false |
| `git check-ignore -v docs/security-policy.md` | true |
| `grep --ignore-case system /var/log/install.log` | true |
| `rg --no-ignore 'prompt' src/` | true |
| `pytest --ignore=tests/integration tests/system` | true |
| `cat docs/review/reviewer-decision-log.md` | true |
| `git status --ignored docs/policy.md` | false |

The only difference between the first two rows is the word `policy` in the filename.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an agent with `tools.exec.mode: "auto"` (auto-review enabled).
2. Have the agent run `git check-ignore docs/security-policy.md` in any git repo.
3. The exec is denied before the reviewer model is called, with "contains reviewer-directed text".

### Expected / Actual

- Expected: common flags and file paths are not treated as prompt-injection directives. At most, borderline matches are deferred to the reviewer model or to `ask`, which is how widget requests are already handled.
- Actual: the exec is hard-denied with `risk=high` because the regex matches tokens produced by normalizing `-`, `=` and `/` to spaces.

Possible directions (any of these would fix our case):
- Match the directive patterns against whitespace-separated tokens before punctuation stripping, so `check-ignore` and `--ignore-case` do not yield a standalone `ignore`.
- Apply the directive heuristic to free-text fields only, or require multi-word phrasing such as `ignore (all|previous|the) ... instructions`.
- For exec, return `ask`/defer instead of `deny` when only this heuristic fires.

### Workaround

None that we want to recommend: the denial text forbids "workaround, indirect execution". Renaming files so they do not contain `policy` avoids it in practice.

### Version / OS / install

- OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (8b18b55); the same code is on `main` @ b1b0a8890
- macOS 26 (arm64), npm global install, Node 22.22

issues.body:
## User story

As an operator, I want `openclaw hooks test <name>` so I can verify that a hook **actually loads** (module export + handler import) and summarize which events it would handle — without enabling it in production or waiting for a live Gateway event.

## Problem

Today:

- `openclaw hooks check` reports eligibility / missing requirements only. Docs already say: **"This still does not test actual loading."**
- `openclaw hooks info` shows metadata and config checks, but does not import/execute the handler module.
- `openclaw hooks enable` can turn a hook on even when the module would fail to load at event time; operators discover breakage only in Gateway logs after reload.

There is no first-class dry load / smoke test for workspace or managed hooks.

Related but different: `hooks check` (eligibility), `hooks info` (metadata), plugin/hook pack install `--dry-run`, Gateway hybrid reload behavior.

## Proposal

Add:

```bash
openclaw hooks test <name> [--agent <id>] [--json] [--event <eventName>]
```

Preferred v1 (local, no live side effects):

- Resolve the hook like `info` / `enable` (name or unique `hookKey`).
- Attempt the same handler/module load path the Gateway loader uses (import the handler file; validate expected export shape).
- Report: `loadOk`, `eligible`, `events` (declared), optional `unknownEvents` warnings already tracked by discovery, and `error` when load fails.
- Optional `--event <eventName>`: report whether that event is in the hook's declared set (does **not** invoke the handler against a live session / does not enqueue Gateway work).
- Do not enable the hook; do not write config; do not call outbound webhooks.

## Acceptance criteria

1. For a known bundled/workspace hook with a valid handler, `hooks test <name> --json` reports `loadOk=true` and lists declared events.
2. For a hook whose handler file is missing or has a bad export, `hooks test` exits non-zero and reports a clear load error (eligibility alone may still look fine).
3. `hooks test` does not flip `hooks.internal.entries.*.enabled` and does not require a running Gateway for the local load path.
4. Optional `--event` reports matched/unmatched without invoking side-effecting handler code.
5. Colocated test covers loadOk true/false with a temp hook fixture.
6. Docs: `docs/cli/hooks.md` documents `hooks test` and contrasts it with `hooks check`.

## CLI proof sketch

```bash
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
# use a known bundled hook name from `openclaw hooks list` on a stock install
node openclaw.mjs hooks test session-memory --json
# expect loadOk=true (or the current bundled name), exit 0
# break handler path / use a fixture with invalid export → expect loadOk=false, exit != 0
```

## Scope / non-goals

- Not a full integration harness that fires real agent turns.
- Not replacing `hooks check` eligibility gating.
- Not invoking plugin-managed hooks' remote side effects; plugin hooks may report `unsupported` with guidance to test via the owning plugin.

issues.body:
## Summary

A bound Codex CLI **node session** whose true working directory carries significant whitespace (e.g. `/workspace/project `, alongside `/workspace/project`) is discovered, persisted, read back, and resumed as the **trimmed sibling** — so `codex exec resume` spawns in the wrong directory, which usually does not exist.

Four sites in the codex extension trim the cwd instead of preserving it:

- **Discovery** — `node-cli-sessions.ts` `readSessionFileSummary` trims the `session_meta` `payload.cwd` (`normalizeOptionalString`).
- **Write** — `conversation-binding-data.ts` `createCodexCliNodeConversationBindingData` persists `params.cwd?.trim()` into the binding record.
- **Read** — `conversation-binding-data.ts` `readCodexConversationBindingDataRecord` re-trims the stored cwd on restore (`normalizeOptionalString`).
- **Resume** — `node-cli-sessions.ts` `resumeLocalCodexCliSession` trims again right before spawning (`params.cwd.trim()`).

## Impact

- Session discovery lists the trimmed directory instead of the real one.
- The binding record stores the wrong cwd identity.
- `codex exec resume` is launched in the trimmed impostor directory — the session's files, tools, and repo context are wrong (or the directory is missing entirely).

## Environment

- Codex CLI node sessions (paired node host, `codex.cli.session.resume`).
- Any filesystem where a path may legitimately end in whitespace (shell quoting, tab-completion artifacts, user error).

## Suggested fix

Use `readNonBlankString` (the existing plugin-SDK helper, already used by the app-server branch for `workspaceDir`) at all four boundaries — discovery, write, read, resume — so nonblank literal filesystem identities survive unchanged. Blank or whitespace-only values still omit the field / fall back exactly as before (`readNonBlankString` keeps the trim-based blank check).

Same defect class as the merged literal-path fixes #187739, #187554, and #187777.

> A fix is in progress in PR #188121.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a Linux host without a systemd user session, `pnpm openclaw` (`scripts/run-node.mts`) refuses to run any command whenever runtime artifacts need rebuilding, i.e. on the first run and after any edit under `src/`. No Gateway was ever installed or started.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Linux host or container with no systemd user session (no `/run/systemd/system`, no `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`): Docker dev containers, Codespaces, WSL without systemd.
2. Fresh clone of `main` (7b29a23), `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, Node 24.22.2.
3. `pnpm openclaw --version` → refused (first run, artifacts not built yet).
4. After `pnpm build`, `pnpm openclaw --version` works. Edit any file under `src/` (e.g. add a comment) and run it again → refused.

### Expected behavior

When there is no service manager, there can't be a managed Gateway service, so the runner should fall through to the checks it already does next (active Gateway lock, port in use) instead of refusing. `openclaw gateway status` already treats "service-manager-unavailable" as a normal, diagnostic-only state.

### Actual behavior

Every command is refused with `UpdatePreMutationError` (full output under Logs). The suggested `openclaw gateway status --deep` / `openclaw gateway stop` go through the same runner, so they are refused too.

Where: `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-publication.ts` (`withGatewayRuntimeArtifactPublication`): `readGatewayServiceState` throws `ServiceInspectionError("service-manager-unavailable")`, which `inspectionFailed` turns into `refuse()`. The `absent` check needs `runtime.missingUnit === true`, which can't be observed without a manager. Called from `scripts/run-node.mts` (`withRunNodeRuntimePublication`).

### OpenClaw version

Source checkout of main at 7b29a23 (this code path is unchanged on current main, 0a92a693d1)

### Operating system

Linux (Docker dev container with no systemd user session)

### Install method

Source checkout: pnpm 12.15.0, `pnpm openclaw` (scripts/run-node.mts)

### Model

N/A (fails before any command runs; no model involved)

### Provider / routing chain

N/A (no provider involved)

### Logs

```shell
UpdatePreMutationError: Runtime artifacts changed, but the affected Gateway is running or its offline state could not be verified. Run `openclaw gateway status --deep`, stop the affected Gateway with `openclaw gateway stop`, and retry the original command.
  [cause]: ServiceInspectionError: busctl --user machine Manager.Version: exit 1; Failed to connect to bus: No such file or directory
  No supported service manager detected. Manage the Gateway through the supervisor or terminal that started it.
```

### Impact and severity

Affected: contributors running a source checkout on container / WSL / Codespaces setups without a systemd user session.
Severity: blocks workflow; `pnpm openclaw` / `pnpm dev` can't be used after any edit.
Frequency: always, on the first run and after every edit under `src/`.
Consequence: the only workaround is a full `pnpm build` (~9-11 min) plus `node openclaw.mjs`.

### Additional information

Related:
- #169426 (open) fixes the same root cause for the test-preparation fence (`scripts/lib/live-gateway-dist-fence.mts`), not this path.
- #150494 relaxed the same verdict for `openclaw update` preflight when service inspection is unavailable.
- #160392 deliberately kept source-CLI rebuild publication strict, so the question is whether service-manager-unavailable can count as "no managed Gateway" here, with the lock and port checks still enforced.

Happy to send a PR if a maintainer agrees on the approach.

issues.body:
## User story

As an operator, I want `openclaw config explain <path>` so I can see **why** a config value is what it is (authored vs runtime default, which `$include` owns it, env/SecretRef state) without dumping the whole tree or guessing from `config get` alone.

## Problem

Today:

- `openclaw config get <path>` prints the **redacted runtime value** only.
- `openclaw config diff` (#178016) lists authored-vs-effective differences across many paths.
- `openclaw config export --safe` (#178014) dumps the full redacted tree.

None of these answer a single-path support question: "Did this come from my file, an include, an env SecretRef, or a runtime default?" Operators dig through include files and `${ENV}` by hand, and sometimes mistake a default for an authored secret/plaintext value.

Related but different: #178016 (bulk diff), #178014 (full export), #103606 (externally managed hot-reload).

## Proposal

Add:

```bash
openclaw config explain <path> [--json]
```

Behavior (v1):

- Load the same config snapshot as other read-only config commands.
- For `<path>`, report structured provenance, for example:
  - `path`
  - `runtimeValue` (redacted via existing `redactConfigObject` / UI hints — same as `config get`)
  - `authoredPresent` (bool: present on `sourceConfig` after include/env)
  - `source` enum: `authored` | `default` | `unset` (and optionally `include` when include ownership applies)
  - `include` (when `includeProvenance` owns the path): include file path + ownership fields already tracked on the snapshot
  - `secretRef` summary when resolution facts / SecretRef metadata exist for the path: `{ source, provider, id, state }` **without** resolving or printing the secret value
- Missing/invalid config fails clearly (same policy as `config get` / `config validate`).
- Unknown schema paths fail like `config get`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. For an unset schema path that has a runtime default, `config explain` reports `source=default` (or equivalent) and a redacted runtime value when one exists.
2. After `config set <path> <value>`, explain reports `authoredPresent=true` / `source=authored` for that path.
3. When the path is owned by a `$include` file, explain names that include path (from snapshot `includeProvenance`).
4. When the path is backed by a SecretRef / env ref, explain shows ref identity fields and does **not** print the resolved secret; plaintext secrets still redact like `config get`.
5. `--json` emits a stable machine-readable object; human mode is readable without requiring jq.
6. Colocated unit/integration test covers at least authored vs default for one path; docs update `docs/cli/config.md`.

## CLI proof sketch

```bash
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/openclaw.json"
printf '%s\n' '{}' > "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH"
node openclaw.mjs config explain agents.defaults.heartbeat.every --json
# expect source=default (or unset+default filled), no crash
node openclaw.mjs config set agents.defaults.heartbeat.every '"30m"'
node openclaw.mjs config explain agents.defaults.heartbeat.every --json
# expect authoredPresent=true / source=authored, runtimeValue visible as 30m
```

## Scope / non-goals

- Not a bulk authored-vs-runtime listing (that is #178016 `config diff`).
- Not a full redacted export (#178014).
- Does not resolve/print secret material; SecretRef identity only.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add a separate, genuinely byte-resumable transport for Git-source updates using immutable Git object artifacts.

### Problem to solve

Operators updating source checkouts over unstable networks can lose a partially downloaded Git pack. Fetch retries reuse objects already imported by Git, but do not establish an offset from which the interrupted pack can continue. This is separate from the retry/progress work in #184452 and the weak-network report #184442.

### Proposed solution

Start with pinned incremental Git bundles for official stable/beta releases. Retain partial files outside disposable inspection repositories; bind them to repository, target, asset identity, length and SHA-256; request the remaining bytes with HTTP Range; validate response ranges and the complete digest; then hydrate the existing private inspection repository and retain current candidate admission and rollback.

The producer, supported baselines, artifact immutability, retention and fallback policy need explicit design review. Missing prerequisites, older releases, custom remotes and development targets keep the existing Git transport. No production updater behavior is changed by the initial proposal.

### Alternatives considered

More fetch retries improve recovery probability but do not provide byte resume. A moving archive URL lacks a pinned representation and does not preserve the Git object/history contract. A full-history bundle needs measured size and publication cost; GitHub release assets must be smaller than 2 GiB.

### Impact

Affected: Git-source installations on intermittent or bandwidth-limited connections.
Severity: interrupted updates cause delays, repeated transfer and operator intervention.
Frequency: depends on network conditions; no population-wide frequency or speedup is claimed.
Consequence: downloaded bytes from an unfinished pack can be transferred again.

### Evidence/examples

A local executable experiment creates a real incremental Git bundle, interrupts HTTP after 65,536 written bytes, and verifies a fresh process requests exactly that retained offset. A separate SIGKILL/restart scenario also resumes at 65,536. The reconstructed bundle passes SHA-256, exact target/payload checks and git fsck --strict. It also covers ignored/malformed/unsatisfiable ranges, changed bytes, encoded responses, complete-file recovery and missing Git prerequisites.

This is a synthetic protocol proof, not proof of an installed OpenClaw upgrade or live GitHub artifact delivery. An architecture proposal PR with the runnable experiment will follow.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself, starting with a separate architecture proposal and executable protocol proof for maintainer feedback.

Version: 2026.10.7 (157d8c2), Slack channel, Linux.

**What happens.** Outbound Slack deliveries that end up `unknown_after_send` are retried by gateway/delivery-recovery (3 reconcile passes over ~2 min each, then they stop). The log lines carry only the entry id and the reconcile error, e.g. `channel_not_found` or `Slack history contains no exact durable delivery marker`. Audit then shows a terminal `outcome=unknown failureStage=queue` row (metadata only).

**Gaps (no supported way to answer "did the user get it?"):**
1. No documented CLI/RPC to list, inspect (target + payload), or settle outbound queue entries. `openclaw health --json` gives only `deliveryQueues.failed[{queueName,count,oldestFailedAt}]`; external sqlite3 is (rightly) blocked under the state dir. `openclaw channels dead-letters` covers inbound only.
2. The recovery log never names channel/target or a payload digest, so an operator cannot tell which conversation lost a message.
3. For `channel_not_found` the entry was retried 3x although that error is permanent for the target (isPermanentDeliveryError has no Slack `channel_not_found`/`is_archived` pattern), and I could find no terminal audit row for it (other two entries each have one).
4. "no exact durable marker" leaves the outcome `unknown` forever; there is no operator action to mark delivered/undelivered or to resend once a human has checked Slack.

**Ask.** `openclaw message queue list|show <id>` (redacted payload preview + target) and `... settle <id> --delivered|--undelivered`, plus Slack permanent-error patterns and a target in the delivery-recovery log line.

Prior art searched (gh search, openclaw/openclaw): "unknown_after_send", "Slack history contains no exact durable delivery marker", "delivery queue list inspect operator". Related but different channel/cause: #125764, #126246, #115328, #100979 (no reconcileUnknownSend for Telegram/iMessage/Discord). Nothing covers Slack reconciliation or operator inspect/settle.

issues.body:
# Feature request: Resize oversized JPEG camera photos in Control UI before upload

## User-visible problem
An Android Chrome user cannot attach an ordinary camera photo in the Control UI webchat: the UI reports the image is too large. The original photo has not reached the agent, so its exact size, dimensions and MIME type remain unconfirmed.

## Environment
Installed OpenClaw version reported by setup inspection: 2026.10.7. Client: Chrome on Android; exact Android/Chrome versions unknown.

## Installed-code evidence
The installed chat attachment policy caps maxImageBytes at MAX_IMAGE_BYTES = 6291456 bytes, independently of agents.defaults.mediaMaxMb. The Control UI admission path permits an oversize image for resizing only when file.type === image/png. The image worker path validates a static PNG header with a 25-megapixel budget. Thus oversized JPEG camera photos are rejected before resize in the inspected build. This is code inspection, not a controlled reproduction with the user photo.

## Expected behavior / request
Extend browser-side preprocessing to oversized static JPEG photos: preserve visual orientation, use bounded pixel dimensions and memory, resize/re-encode a transmission copy to the advertised byte and batch budgets, leave the original unchanged, and show clear progress/error feedback. Do not silently flatten animations. Consider other supported static formats after format and browser checks. No need to raise the model-side image cap.

## Suggested validation
Test Android Chrome camera/gallery JPEG upload above 6 MiB, portrait EXIF orientation, high-resolution photos with bounded memory, ordinary images below the limit, static transparent PNG, animated formats, cancellation and multi-attachment byte budgets.

## Related work
Release 2026.9.7 documents static-PNG resizing (PR #159960). Issue #30300 describes a different historical large-image call-stack failure; this request concerns admission/format coverage rather than that error.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let `image_generate` submit a caller-prepared alpha PNG as the mask for an explicitly selected, direct OpenAI Images API edit.

### Problem to solve

An editor can already have a source photograph, an optional logo reference, and a same-size alpha mask identifying the intended edit region. A [developer's concrete logo-placement workflow](https://community.openai.com/t/how-to-overlay-a-logo-onto-a-specific-area-using-base-image-logo-mask-api-limitations/1289633) uses these inputs. OpenClaw's ecosystem also has an [authored editing helper](https://github.com/LeoYeAI/openclaw-master-skills/blob/e5199b56ae1ff72e141586c17695563486c46702/skills/media-generation/scripts/edit_image.py) that sends a separate multipart mask through its own HTTP client.

The bundled OpenAI path accepts ordinary reference images, but cannot assign one the API's distinct mask role. Adding a mask to `images` sends another ordinary reference; an unknown OpenAI option does not supply the missing mapping. Users who need that structured input must use another client or provider.

The forum author is an external API user, not an established OpenClaw user. Their complaint also concerns model precision, which mask transport cannot resolve. This request adds submission of an existing region-selection artifact through this particular bundled route, with the model's existing guidance semantics.

### Proposed solution

Add an optional mask selection to the existing OpenAI image tool options. Reuse authorized reference loading and the existing provider request, background task, and output delivery. Submit the selected PNG as the separate multipart `mask`, exclude it from ordinary references, and keep the first source image and other references in order.

Limit the first implementation to explicit `openai/<model>` selection on the supported public Images API-key route. Validate a source and one alpha PNG mask against the current vendor format, byte, and dimension requirements before upload (the multipart API reference currently specifies a PNG mask under 4 MB with matching source dimensions), within existing OpenClaw resource limits. Preserve geometry and alpha. Check the actual selected transport and authentication mode before provider upload: an `openai/<model>` name alone does not ensure an API-key route. Reject unsupported routes or malformed input instead of discarding the mask, running an unmasked fallback, or changing credential classes.

A provider-specific index or tag over existing references is sufficient; a new generic SDK contract is unnecessary. Exact option naming belongs to the owner.

### Alternatives considered

- Describe the region or send a visual mask as another reference. These useful strategies do not assign the API mask role.
- Use the external helper or a custom provider. These valid alternatives maintain a separate client workflow instead of using the bundled provider.
- Use the [Bedrock image plugin](https://github.com/cheeseandcereal/openclaw-bedrock-images/blob/2e405cb867bbcff8b4d1b90d3563b15f3668fdd4/README.md), which documents source/mask reference positions, or ComfyUI/local editing. OpenClaw already supports such third-party mask workflows. They use different backends and do not demonstrate a generic SDK deficiency.

### Impact

- Affected: Editors who prepare masks and use the bundled OpenAI direct-API path. Their number is unknown; the external caller is not a verified native consumer.
- Severity/urgency: Distinct mask submission is unavailable through this route. Ordinary editing and external alternatives remain available; broader urgency is unknown.
- Frequency: The limitation applies whenever a separate API mask is needed. Actual usage frequency is unknown.
- Consequence: Users must maintain or switch clients/providers to submit that artifact. No measured time savings or generated-image quality improvement is claimed.

### Evidence/examples

- [OpenAI multipart edit reference](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/python/resources/images/methods/edit) for the separate mask field and upload constraints.
- [Current OpenAI mask documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/image-generation#edit-an-image-using-a-mask): a separate alpha mask applies to the first image. It provides soft guidance, without guaranteed exact boundaries.
- [Tool option normalization](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f20e7dbea8fc33024ca4cacc9c103188bf6e17bc/src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.ts#L254) and [direct multipart construction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f20e7dbea8fc33024ca4cacc9c103188bf6e17bc/extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts#L853): no distinct mask mapping at the inspected main revision.
- [PR #71379](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/71379) explicitly limits itself to edit geometry and leaves native mask upload as a separate follow-up. [PR #143068](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143068) explicitly excludes masks.

Verification was static against pinned main and public originals. No live request, model-quality experiment, or latest-stable audit was performed.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

The existing OpenAI provider owns this vendor mapping. Existing `inputImages` and extensible `providerOptions` can carry a selected mask; the tool adapter must retain it. An illustrative new option could select the final element of `[source, logo, mask]`; this is proposed behavior, not supported syntax.

The loader optimizes some images. Preserve source/mask alignment and alpha using the existing raw-image option under the same file, sandbox, network, byte, and dimension limits. Do not independently resize the pair. Keep the total-input bound explicit and the mask selection in the existing request identity.

Non-goals: mask creation, a painting UI, outpaint layout generation, hard pixel preservation, model-quality fixes, new providers, a new batch/queue owner, persistent state, CLI flag parity, or guarantees for OAuth/subscription, Azure, or custom endpoints. No implementer has committed.

Acceptance criteria:

- A real tool invocation with authorized source/mask files on an explicit direct OpenAI route sends mask bytes in the multipart mask field, keeps other references ordered, and delivers through the existing task flow.
- The mask is never silently treated as an ordinary reference, resized out of alignment, omitted on fallback, or used to trigger an authentication switch.
- Missing sources, invalid selections, invalid alpha PNGs, dimension mismatches, and unsupported routes fail before provider upload. Calls without a mask retain their behavior.
- Boundary tests inspect the actual tool-to-provider HTTP request with synthetic files, including a larger source/mask pair and existing limits. An isolated authenticated smoke can verify delivery when an implementer has authorization; fidelity remains model-dependent.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When an agent reads a finished background exec with `process` `action: "log"`, the queued notify-on-exit completion event is never acknowledged. A later exec-event heartbeat then relays that completion to the user as a reply with no context, minutes after the agent already read and used the result. Only `action: "poll"` acknowledges the completion today.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In a channel conversation (seen on Telegram, Codex app-server runtime via `gateway_exec` / `gateway_process`), have the agent run a short command with `exec` that gets backgrounded (for example a small `yieldMs`), with the default `notifyOnExit`.
2. The command exits while the turn is still running. The completion event is queued and its exec-event wake is skipped with `reason=requests-in-flight` while the turn runs.
3. In the same turn, the agent reads the result with `process` `{ "action": "log", "sessionId": "<id>" }` and carries on.
4. The turn ends.

Source-level repro on `main` (13d5ba30de6): start a notify-on-exit background exec, let it finish, call `process` `log` on it, and acknowledge the tool result (`acknowledgeInternalToolResult`). The completion is still in `peekSystemEventEntries(sessionKey)`. The same sequence with `poll` removes it.

### Expected behavior

Reading the finished process with `log` counts as collecting its result, like a terminal `poll`. The completion event is retired once the result is delivered, and the queued exec-event wake is skipped as stale (the existing check in `src/infra/heartbeat-runner-prompt.ts`).

### Actual behavior

The completion stays queued. As soon as the turn ends, the exec-event heartbeat runs, and the model relays the stale "command finished" result to the user as a fresh message.

Also, `log` on a finished process does not say how it ended (no `Process exited with code N.`) unless it was stopped by request, although the tool description promises `poll/log: status, output, ... completion`.

### OpenClaw version

Observed live on 2026.9.2. Reproduced at source level on `main` 13d5ba30de6.

### Operating system

Source repro on macOS 26 (the bug is platform-independent).

### Install method

Source checkout

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (model-independent; the bug is in the process tool's acknowledgement)

### Provider / routing chain

Codex app-server (`gateway_process` is the Codex alias of the `process` tool)

### Additional provider/model setup details

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs

```
completed: source=exec-event intent=event status=skipped reason=requests-in-flight   (repeated about once a second while the turn ran, ~9 min)
... turn reads the result with process log, sends its last reply ...
session turn created ... trigger=heartbeat
completed: source=exec-event intent=event status=ran reason=ran
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

`src/agents/bash-tools.process.ts`: `finishedPollResult` attaches `acknowledgeNotifyOnExit(finished)` to the terminal poll result; the `log` case returns a plain `textResult` with no acknowledgement. `src/auto-reply/reply/bash-command.ts` already acknowledges after showing a finished session's output and exit label.

### Impact and severity

Affected: any channel user whose agent reads background exec results with `log`. Severity: low to medium. A confusing out-of-context message reaches the user, and a heartbeat model turn is spent. Frequency: whenever a backgrounded command finishes during the turn and the agent reads it with `log` instead of `poll`.

### Additional information

Fix PR to follow: on an ended process, `log` appends the same terminal line `poll` uses (`finishedSessionText`) and acknowledges the completion when the result is delivered.

issues.body:
## Summary

Docs already prescribe `channels.stop` / `channels.start` for **non-destructive per-account recovery** (keep pairing/credentials; crash-loop safe-mode manual override). Operators today must hand-craft:

```bash
openclaw gateway call channels.stop --params '{"channel":"…","accountId":"…"}'
openclaw gateway call channels.start --params '{"channel":"…","accountId":"…"}'
```

The `channels` CLI already has list/status/login/logout/dead-letters but **no** first-class `start` / `stop` / `reconnect`.

## Proposal

Add under the existing `channels` tree (no new top-level namespace):

- `openclaw channels stop --channel <id> [--account <id>] --json`
- `openclaw channels start --channel <id> [--account <id>] --json`
- `openclaw channels reconnect …` (stop then start)

Thin Alix-style adapters over existing Gateway RPCs (`operator.admin`). Blank `--account` rejected. Prefer these over `gateway call` in docs and crash-loop recovery hints.

## Why this is not invent-diagnostics

Restart recovery, CLI channels docs, and troubleshooting already name these RPCs as the supported recovery path. This only exposes them on the same command tree operators already use for channel ops.

## Acceptance

- Packaged CLI stop → `{ stopped }` / start → `{ started, outcome }`
- `channels status --probe` after recovery
- Unknown channel fails closed (nonzero)
- Blank `--account ""` rejected before Gateway call

issues.body:
[Bug]: Failover classifier defaults a 400 with a redaction-destroyed body to `format`, forcing a model-swap recovery instead of overflow recovery

## Summary

When a provider returns a **400** whose body the diagnostic redactor destroys (replaces with `[Malformed diagnostic JSON redacted]` / `[Oversized diagnostic JSON redacted]` / `[Unserializable]`), the failover classifier **defaults it to `reason=format`**. `format` is a *terminal format failure* in `failover-policy.ts` (`isTerminalFormatFailure`), which hides the real error and drives a **model-swap recovery** (next configured fallback model) instead of the **token-budget overflow recovery** (auto-compaction) that fits a context/request-size 400.

This is the 400-path analog of #179962 (P1, 429 path, "the long-window check reads the redacted text"), fixed by #179967 for the 429 path only. The same root cause — **the classifier makes its decision from redaction-destroyed text** — also applies to 400/422, where the consequence is worse: a silent, terminal model-swap.

## Root cause (code)

1. `packages/ai/src/utils/provider-error.ts` — `buildProjection()` runs `stringifyField()` → `redactDiagnosticText()` on the 400 body **before** the `errorMessage` is assembled. The comment says it plainly: *"Redact complete structured data before clipping its message/body projections."* So the classifier never sees the raw body.
2. `packages/ai/src/utils/credential-redaction.ts` — `projectDiagnosticText()` replaces the **entire** body with a placeholder when it is oversized (`> 16 KiB` → `[Oversized diagnostic JSON redacted]`) or when a balanced JSON fragment fails `JSON.parse` (`[Malformed diagnostic JSON redacted]`).
3. `src/agents/failover/classification-rules.ts` — the `400/422` branch: if the (redacted) message doesn't classify and it's not the no-body wrapper, it does `return toReasonClassification("format")`. A placeholder body is neither, so it falls through to `format`.
4. `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-policy.ts` — `isTerminalFormatFailure()` treats `reason=format` as terminal: `shouldFallback = failoverFailure && !isTerminalFormatFailure(...)`. The run surfaces the error / swaps to the next model instead of running `recoverEmbeddedRunOverflow()`, which has a **token-count** path (`isContextOverflow(assistant, contextTokenBudget)`) that does not depend on the error text at all.

## Reproduction (no network) — verified against the real compiled code

Running the **actual shipped** redactor + classifier (`packages/ai/dist/provider-error-*.mjs`, `dist/classify-*.mjs`):

```
// A context/request-size 400 body that is large enough to be redacted
// (vLLM overflow 400 bodies embed the offending prompt verbatim):
raw body (112 KB, valid overflow wording)
  -> classify(raw)            = context_overflow   (CORRECT)
  -> redactDiagnosticText()   = [Oversized diagnostic JSON redacted]
  -> projectProviderError()   .errorMessage = "400: [Oversized diagnostic JSON redacted]"
  -> classify(projected)      = format             (WRONG — drives model-swap)
```

And the exact placeholder strings:

```
classify("400: [Malformed diagnostic JSON redacted]")  -> format   (should be null)
classify("400: [Oversized diagnostic JSON redacted]")  -> format   (should be null)
classify("400: [Unserializable]")                       -> format   (should be null)
classify("400 status code (no body)")                   -> null     (already correct — the precedent)
```

The no-body case already returns `null` with an explicit comment that defaulting to `format` *"triggers a compaction loop that cannot recover."* The redaction-destroyed case is the same situation (no classifiable signal survives) but is **not** covered, so it mis-defaults to `format`.

## Real-world incident (2026-10-24, Kebabman's gateway)

- Primary `gpufarm/qwen3.8-27b` (vLLM, `--max-model-len 1010000`) returned a **400 in ~212ms** (a fast request-validation rejection, pre-tokenization) on a ~196k-token prompt.
- The 400 body was redacted to `[Malformed diagnostic JSON redacted]`; the failover decision logged `reason=format` and swapped to the fallback `qwen3.8-27b-uncensored-r9700`.
- The fallback (262144 window) then genuinely overflowed (`prompt(196609) + max_tokens(65536) = 262145 > 262144`), triggering auto-compaction, after which the fallback model produced a 65k-token content loop.
- The primary's 400 was **not** a model-unavailable or size-overflow condition — the primary's window is 1M. The `format` misclassification is what sent the run down the fallback path at all.

## Expected behavior

A 400/422 whose body was destroyed by the diagnostic redactor carries **no classifiable signal**. It should be classified `null` (like the no-body case), letting the caller choose recovery — including the token-budget overflow recovery — rather than being forced into a terminal `format` model-swap.

## Suggested fix

In `src/agents/failover/classification-rules.ts`, in the `400/422` branch, detect a redaction-placeholder body and return `null` before the `format` default (mirroring `isUnclassifiedNoBodyHttpSignal`). See linked PR.

## Impact

- Wrong recovery path (model-swap instead of compaction) for any 400/422 whose body is oversized or malformed-JSON — common for context/request-size rejections, which embed the prompt.
- The real error is hidden from the user and from telemetry (only the placeholder is logged), making diagnosis hard.
- A healthy primary can be abandoned for a smaller-window fallback, which then fails for a different reason and can cascade (as in the incident above).

issues.body:
### Summary

Let the bundled ElevenLabs speech provider apply existing pronunciation dictionaries, selected by dictionary ID and version ID, to ordinary TTS audio.

### Problem to solve

Pronunciation corrections can be reusable assets. A [sports-announcer developer](https://www.reddit.com/r/ElevenLabs/comments/1vjasax/pronunciation_correction_layer_for_elevenlabs/) describes saving, auditioning, and reusing name-specific alias rules in ElevenLabs dictionaries.

The proposed OpenClaw workflow is to configure an existing dictionary version once and use normally spelled text through auto-TTS, `/tts audio`, or the `tts` tool. At [main fe6f5c2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fe6f5c2119ae57123906973f77f447bcb55a60ac/extensions/elevenlabs/speech-provider-factory.ts), the bundled provider's config normalizer, request resolver, and HTTP builder omit dictionary locators. Arbitrary provider-config keys do not reach the request.

This is a request to reuse existing rule inputs, not a pronunciation-quality guarantee. The external developer is not an established OpenClaw user; applicability to OpenClaw is an inference from the existing synthesis workflow and code.

### Proposed solution

Add an optional operator-configured list under `tts.providers.elevenlabs`. A proposed shape, subject to maintainer naming decisions:

```json5
pronunciationDictionaryLocators: [
  { pronunciationDictionaryId: "dictionary_id", versionId: "version_id" },
]
```

Validate and normalize it in the ElevenLabs plugin, carry it through the existing request resolver, and serialize it as `pronunciation_dictionary_locators` without rewriting the synthesis text. Preserve order and the vendor limit of three locators. Require explicit nonempty IDs and versions; reject malformed or oversized lists before a paid request. Omission or an empty list preserves today's request behavior.

Reuse existing global/scoped provider configuration and persona binding. No new core tool, shared manager, or model-emitted directive is requested.

### Alternatives considered

- [Hidden TTS text](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fe6f5c2119ae57123906973f77f447bcb55a60ac/docs/tools/tts/commands.md) already separates visible text from spoken respelling or markup. It can solve individual corrections, but does not select an existing server-side dictionary version.
- The [elevenlabs-voices skill](https://github.com/robbyczgw-cla/elevenlabs-voices/blob/184ecf35b76f40640ea077bea965f5b1bc29522a/scripts/tts.py) applies local substitutions and calls ElevenLabs separately. Custom scripts or speech providers, including a local CLI adapter, can implement the API call too. These are viable alternatives requiring a separate synthesis implementation or rule representation.
- Voice/model selection, personas, language hints, seed, and normalization do not make the current bundled HTTP builder send dictionary locators. The existing ElevenLabs plugin is the narrow owner for this optional input.

### Impact

- Affected: users reusing curated ElevenLabs rules for names or domain terms in ordinary spoken output; their number is unknown.
- Severity/urgency: an optional provider capability gap; no outage or urgent regression is established.
- Frequency: saved corrections recur in the external announcement workflow; actual OpenClaw frequency is unknown.
- Consequence: users must prepare spoken replacements or maintain a separate API/skill path. No measured time savings are claimed.

### Evidence/examples

- [ElevenLabs synthesis API](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-speech/convert) supports ordered dictionary/version locators, at most three per request.
- The [dictionary guide](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/text-to-speech/pronunciation-dictionaries) distinguishes aliases from model-dependent phoneme support. Current non-English IPA guidance requires v4; forwarding a locator does not guarantee universal phoneme support or consistent acoustics.
- [Current provider implementation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/fe6f5c2119ae57123906973f77f447bcb55a60ac/extensions/elevenlabs/speech-provider-factory.ts) shows the missing input chain.
- [OpenClaw #44108](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/44108) mentions a custom ElevenLabs lexicon file. It requests file editing, and does not prove native TTS consumes that file or that its author requested dictionary locators.
- Verification is static at the pinned main revision. No live synthesis, pronunciation-quality test, or latest-stable audit was performed.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Implementation belongs in `extensions/elevenlabs/speech-provider-factory.ts`: plugin-local normalization, request resolution, and the shared buffered/streaming HTTP builder. Existing provider-config maps accept structured values; no generic SDK expansion is needed. Request assertions already exist in `extensions/elevenlabs/speech-provider.test.ts`.

Acceptance criteria:

1. With an existing dictionary ID/version configured, `/tts audio` and ordinary auto-TTS send the exact ordered locators alongside unchanged synthesis text, preserving current visible text and audio delivery.
2. Existing scoped config and provider-bound persona precedence apply. A scoped empty list clears inherited locators.
3. Omitted/empty lists add no request field; malformed entries or more than three fail before network synthesis.
4. Buffered and streaming request paths preserve the input; unrelated providers receive no ElevenLabs fields. Existing credential, timeout, SSRF, and fallback behavior remains applicable.
5. Add transport request assertions and an opt-in live smoke using an existing alias dictionary and supported model. Verify input reuse and the expected correction without claiming deterministic acoustics.

Non-goals: dictionary creation/upload/editing, PLS parsing, roster UI, crowdsourcing, automatic version updates, model-quality fixes, native Talk UI, and realtime WebSocket support.

Dictionary IDs must be accessible to the existing credential; this adds no permissions or management calls. An inaccessible dictionary can fail that provider attempt, and existing fallback may speak without equivalent rules. Document this limitation. No implementer has committed.

issues.body:
# [Bug] `decision_evaluate` rejects a manifest-conformant call pre-dispatch (`unavailable / unsupported-input`) on 2026.10.7 — OpenRouter Jev route

**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (794d650), deployed via the repository's Docker Compose
(`scripts/docker/setup.sh`, image `openclaw:local`).
**Provider:** `openrouter`, authenticated with a single api-key profile (store-backed SecretRef).
**Decision model:** `openrouter/~typesafe/jev-latest` (also reproduced with the pinned
`openrouter/typesafe/jev-1.13`).
**Surface:** the built-in `decision_evaluate` agent tool, invoked through `POST /tools/invoke`.

## Summary

`decision_evaluate` returns `{"status":"unavailable","reason":"unsupported-input"}` **before any
dispatch** for input that satisfies the selected row's own declared rubric, while every
manifest-derived surface for that same row resolves correctly (projection, tool capabilities,
provider readiness). No request reaches the provider. The rejection reproduces for two spellings of
the model — the declared `~latest` alias and the exact pinned id.

The same condition surfaces to the operator as the tool description carrying the literal string
`Provider limits are undeclared; use concise evidence and explicit true/false descriptions.`

## Expected vs actual

**Expected:** a conformant `contractVersion: 2` call with a `text` state and one `boolean` question
dispatches to the provider and returns a decision.

**Actual:** pre-flight rejection, no network call:

```json
{
  "status": "unavailable",
  "reason": "unsupported-input",
  "guidance": "Shorten the state or rubric, reduce question counts, and check the selected model's declared limits. Host bounds are 256 questions for legacy input or 400 with contractVersion 2, 1 MiB of JSON, 20000 JSON nodes, and depth 32. No evidence was truncated or sent on a host-bound rejection. The selected provider supports boolean, choice, score, box questions. Supported input modalities: text, image. Limits: images up to 4194304 decoded bytes in image/png, image/jpeg, at least 2 Choice alternatives, at most 255 Choice alternatives, at least 2 Score levels, at most 10 Score levels, at most 262144 tokens per state-plus-question. Optional confidence is a provider-specific distribution metric, not correctness probability."
}
```

Gateway log at the same moment:

```
[decisions] Decision input was rejected; the caller retains its fallback policy.
```

Note the `guidance` text is populated **from the row's declared capabilities** — including `box`,
which only `jev-1.14` / `~typesafe/jev-latest` declare — so capability resolution succeeded even
though the runtime then rejected the call.

## Repro

```bash
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18789/tools/invoke \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN" \
  -d '{
        "tool": "decision_evaluate",
        "args": {
          "contractVersion": 2,
          "state": { "type": "text", "text": "The gateway runs in Docker on a VPS." },
          "questions": {
            "q1": { "type": "boolean", "instructions": "Is the gateway running in Docker?" }
          }
        }
      }'
```

This deployment reaches the gateway through a host-level Tailscale Serve route, so the request also
carries `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Forwarded-Proto` / `X-Forwarded-Host` to satisfy its
`gateway.trustedProxies` configuration; that is orthogonal to the failure (without them the request
is refused earlier with `proxy_attribution_required`, which is expected for this setup).

## Evidence that the row and provider are fine

1. `models.list` → `decisionModels` lists all three declared OpenRouter decision rows:

   ```
   openrouter / typesafe/jev-1.13      | plugin: openrouter
   openrouter / typesafe/jev-1.14      | plugin: openrouter
   openrouter / ~typesafe/jev-latest   | plugin: openrouter
   ```

2. `models.list` → `providerOutcomes` reports the provider as ready:

   ```json
   [{ "provider": "openrouter", "profileId": "openrouter:<profile>", "status": "ready" }]
   ```

3. The configured model resolves in the ordinary model list (`~typesafe/jev-latest`, `provider:
   openrouter`, `contextWindow: 262144`).

4. Direct completions to the same model over OpenRouter succeed (HTTP 200; a yes/no answer with
   probability 0.99, ≈$0.000013 per call) — so credentials, routing and the model are not at fault.

5. The bundled plugin manifest declares exactly those three rows with `inference.decision`
   (`extensions/openrouter/openclaw.plugin.json`), and the adapter accepts exactly those ids
   (`extensions/openrouter/decision-provider.ts:26-32`).

6. Reproduced identically with the exact pinned id `openrouter/typesafe/jev-1.13`, and (per the
   operator) with an agent-driven call as well as this HTTP one.

## Suspected code path

`src/agents/decision-inference.ts` — the pre-flight gates that return this exact pair:

- `:160-171` — the canonical provider/registration match (`pluginId` / `source` equality against the
  prepared plugin registry);
- `:172-177` — the prepared-catalog row lookup
  (`prepared.modelCatalog.entries.find(entry => entry.provider === canonical.provider.id && entry.id === modelId)`);
- `:221-223` — `supportsInput(...)`, which cannot be the cause here: the modality (`text`), the
  question type (`boolean`), the reasoning mode (omitted) and the limits (a few hundred bytes) are
  all within what the row declares.

Since the projection, the tool capability description and the guidance text all read the **manifest**
catalog and resolve correctly, while the runtime reads `prepared.modelCatalog.entries`, a divergence
between the manifest catalog and the prepared catalog (or a registration `pluginId`/`source`
mismatch) looks like the most likely cause. Which of the two would need either instrumentation or a
maintainer's read of the intended wiring.

## Impact

`decision_evaluate` is unusable on this route: the caller falls back (per the log line) and no
decision call ever dispatches. Nothing is corrupted or leaked — "no evidence was sent".

## Workarounds

None found. The surface can be disabled by setting `agents.defaults.decisionModel` to an empty
string.

## Not a duplicate of #164991

That issue concerns the external `@openclaw/typesafe` provider's V1 `credentialReady` path for
provider id `typesafe`. This report is the bundled **OpenRouter** route (provider id `openrouter`),
which per the docs requires no separate TypeSafe login; V2 providers omit `credentialReady`
entirely.
