prs.title: fix(slack): stop replies after their parent is deleted
prs.body:
Related: #96692; complements #119737. Compared with merged backport #180878, this draft retains observed-deletion lifecycle and per-physical-write/retry coverage; neither check and publication are atomic.

## What Problem This Solves

A threaded reply can outlive its parent. An observed parent deletion currently becomes only an informational event, so queued output, native buffered output, and files can continue publishing to a destination that no longer exists.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retire the exact active publishing address after an authorized deletion, without cancelling the underlying agent work. Carry that publication-only signal through deferred replies, previews, native streaming, and ordinary delivery. At the ordinary sender boundary, verify the live parent before each physical text/card send and file completion, including known-safe transport retries. Native retries and preview/final edit retries honor observed parent retirement too. Managed writers and deletion signals reach partial updates, both finalization paths, explicit rate-limit retries, and invalid-block replacement; ambiguous final-edit readback keeps the original reader. Keep earlier accepted parts and do not turn a later failure into permission to replay them.

This complements the confirmed-placement receipt work in #119737. It does not replace that PR or claim to repair every existing receipt/reconciliation inference. A parent read and Slack write are not atomic. Native streams without an observed deletion remain a separate limitation.

## User Impact

After OpenClaw observes deletion of an active reply parent, it stops publishing further output to that parent, including buffered native output. Child deletions and another workspace's matching timestamp leave unrelated publishers intact; explicit top-level sends remain supported. Ordinary threaded sends now require a readable live parent, adding bounded read requests and failing without publication when that evidence is unavailable. Workspace/listener and direct-handoff authority stay scoped to the existing delivery owner.

## Evidence

- Independent review found a native HTTP429 replay gap, and hosted review found a preview/final edit replay gap. Both are corrected in this candidate. A fresh frozen review of the complete staged candidate reported no actionable P0–P2 findings. Its confidence is limited by unavailable surrounding source and unrun tests, types, lint and formatting; live behavior remains unverified.
- Candidate base: `7dcc40f7addb9e45ce3e36768c505ff9cb005209`.
- Regression cases cover deletion before pending final text/file output, deferred delivery, native buffered append/stop, workspace/child isolation, queued sender release, multipart acceptance, upload completion, and identity/transport retry boundaries.
- All 23 original changed TypeScript files and the seven follow-up files passed Node syntax parsing, and `git diff --check` passed. These do not establish type or runtime correctness.
- Local dependency setup is blocked: Corepack's fetch of the repository-pinned pnpm version received HTTP 403 from the managed package registry before installation. No alternate registry, package-manager version, or credentials were used.
- The focused repository test wrapper exits before collection because `node_modules` is unavailable. Tests, typecheck, lint, formatting and CI are pending; syntax-only checks and source review are not substitutes.
- No live Slack test messages, service changes, deployment or release performed. The incident's original raw Slack response is unavailable, so this is boundary repair rather than proof of the provider's exact fallback behavior.

Draft: validation and independent review must be resolved before readiness.

Production growth is needed to propagate exact-parent retirement across existing ordinary, preview, deferred and native publishing owners and to verify queued writes at the transport boundary. No configuration, schema, dependency or persistent-state changes.

Known readiness blocker from the #180878 comparison: the published head can drop the configured account reader when a monitor supplies its writer, and Enterprise parent reads can inherit the listener lookup policy. A six-file correction with credential-isolation and transport-deadline regressions is staged locally. Syntax and whitespace checks pass; fresh frozen review of the complete staged candidate reported no actionable P0–P2 findings, with unavailable unchanged source context and unrun checks as limits. The configured signing agent refused the normal commit signature, so the correction is not yet committed or pushed. No signing configuration or security hooks were bypassed. Runtime/type/lint/format validation remains pending.

One `onFailure` handler in `fetchChatMetadata` covers both calls and always posts the models notice. Closes #183031 ## User Impact Users look for a model or provider fault that does not exist. prs.title: fix(whatsapp): quote every line of multi-line blockquotes
prs.body:
## Summary
A multi-line Markdown blockquote in an outbound WhatsApp message keeps its quote only on the first line. WhatsApp quote syntax is per line (`> ` at the start of each quoted line), but `markdownToWhatsAppChunks` turns `> a\n> b\n> c` into `> a\nb\nc`, so every line after the first arrives as ordinary text and the quote visibly ends after one line. The same happens when a quote is split across chunks: a quote line carried into the next message loses its `> ` marker. Every WhatsApp text path goes through this function (agent auto-replies via `auto-reply/deliver-reply.ts` and the outbound adapter / `message` sends via `send.ts`).

## Root cause
`extensions/whatsapp/src/targets-runtime.ts` parses with `blockquotePrefix: "> "`, but the shared Markdown IR emits that prefix once at `blockquote_open`, before the first line only. The WhatsApp renderer then renders each chunk without re-quoting the remaining lines:

```ts
// before
const render = (chunk: MarkdownIR) =>
  renderMarkdownWithMarkers(
    chunk,
    {
      styleMarkers: WHATSAPP_STYLE_MARKERS,
```

`WHATSAPP_STYLE_MARKERS` has no blockquote marker (WhatsApp has no paired quote delimiter), so the `blockquote` style span covering lines two and later renders as plain text.

## Fix
A local `quoteWhatsAppBlockquoteLines` pass inserts `> ` at every line start inside a blockquote span (skipping blank separator lines and lines inside fenced code blocks, and quoting a chunk that begins inside a quote), remapping all IR ranges through the shared `applyMarkdownTextEdits`. It runs on each chunk before rendering:

```ts
// after
const render = (chunk: MarkdownIR) =>
  renderMarkdownWithMarkers(
    quoteWhatsAppBlockquoteLines(chunk),
    {
      styleMarkers: WHATSAPP_STYLE_MARKERS,
```

## Why this is the right boundary
Per-line quote syntax is a property of WhatsApp's wire format, not of the shared Markdown IR, which other channels render with native quote constructs or no prefix at all. Applying it inside the WhatsApp chunk renderer means both callers of `markdownToWhatsAppChunks` (auto-reply delivery and direct sends) are fixed through one function, and because it runs per chunk, quote lines carried into a later chunk are re-quoted. This mirrors the Slack fix for the same IR behavior in #190020. Output without blockquotes is unchanged (the pass returns the IR untouched), and code blocks inside quotes are not prefixed so their content stays verbatim. Signal also sets `blockquotePrefix: "> "`, but Signal has no quote construct and that prefix is a plain-text fallback, so it is left as is here.

## Verification
- `extensions/whatsapp/src/text-runtime.test.ts`: added "quotes every line of a multi-line blockquote" (`> **First** line\n> second line\n>\n> - item\n\nafter` renders as `> *First* line\n> second line\n\n> • item\n\nafter`) and "keeps the quote on blockquote lines carried into later chunks" (limit 20 yields `["> alpha beta gamma\n", "> delta epsilon"]`). Both fail on pristine main and pass with the patch; the whole file (34 cases) passes with the patch.
- `oxfmt --check` clean on both changed files.
- Local tsgo and oxlint were not run per the contributor workflow for this batch; GitHub Actions covers them.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: An outbound WhatsApp reply containing a multi-line blockquote reached Baileys with `> ` only on the first quoted line (and on no line of a quote carried into a second chunk), so WhatsApp showed lines two onward as plain text.
Real environment tested: A tsx driver ran from source the real WhatsApp outbound adapter `whatsappChannelOutbound.sendText` with a real `createPluginRuntime()` plugin runtime and real channel runtime-context registry, a real `channels.whatsapp` config (isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`), and the real `createWebSendApi` listener; the real `sendMessageWhatsApp` path resolved the account, chunk limit and table mode and ran `markdownToWhatsAppChunks`. Only the Baileys socket was replaced, by an object whose `sendMessage(jid, content)` prints the exact payload it receives. Pristine main 88f2b3062c2 first, then this patch, identical inputs.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$D WA_AUTH_DIR=$D/auth WA_LIMIT=<limit> node --import tsx wa-proof-driver.ts "<reply text>"` with limit 4000 for the three-line quote and limit 20 (`channels.whatsapp.textChunkLimit`) for the chunked quote.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 88f2b3062c2)
agent reply text="> Quoted from the spec:\n> line two of the quote\n> line three of the quote\n\nMy reply."
baileys sock.sendMessage #1 to=15555550123@s.whatsapp.net text="> Quoted from the spec:\nline two of the quote\nline three of the quote\n\nMy reply."
delivered messageId=MSG1
agent reply text="> alpha beta gamma\n> delta epsilon"
baileys sock.sendMessage #1 to=15555550123@s.whatsapp.net text="> alpha beta gamma\n"
baileys sock.sendMessage #2 to=15555550123@s.whatsapp.net text="delta epsilon"
delivered messageId=MSG1

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
agent reply text="> Quoted from the spec:\n> line two of the quote\n> line three of the quote\n\nMy reply."
baileys sock.sendMessage #1 to=15555550123@s.whatsapp.net text="> Quoted from the spec:\n> line two of the quote\n> line three of the quote\n\nMy reply."
delivered messageId=MSG1
agent reply text="> alpha beta gamma\n> delta epsilon"
baileys sock.sendMessage #1 to=15555550123@s.whatsapp.net text="> alpha beta gamma\n"
baileys sock.sendMessage #2 to=15555550123@s.whatsapp.net text="> delta epsilon"
delivered messageId=MSG1
```
Observed result after fix: On main the payload handed to the Baileys socket drops the `> ` marker from quote lines two and three and from the quote line carried into the second message; with the patch every quoted line, including the carried one, starts with `> `, and the unquoted `My reply.` paragraph is unchanged.
What was not tested: No live WhatsApp account or phone, so rendering in the WhatsApp client was not observed (the quote rendering relies on WhatsApp's documented per-line `> ` syntax); the gateway auto-reply path was not booted, though it calls the same `markdownToWhatsAppChunks`; full build not run.

prs.title: fix(markdown): preserve Slack and WhatsApp quote continuations
prs.body:
## Summary

- Preserve Slack and WhatsApp blockquote prefixes on continuation lines and later message chunks.
- Emit prefixes from the shared marker renderer using parser-owned quote containers, retaining nested quote depth through fallback projection and slicing. Rendered-size chunking counts the prefixes without rewriting IR text or span offsets.
- Opt in only these two renderers. Discord and other renderer output is unchanged; fenced code bodies remain literal.

Includes yetval’s original commits from #190020 and #190028. The final implementation removes their duplicated IR-rewriting/offset-remapping helpers and keeps one rendering owner. Existing regression fixtures cover nested multiline quotes and quoted formatting across chunk boundaries without additional test lines or files.

## Validation

Native outbound proof and nested-depth repair receipts: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190066#issuecomment-6553348115

- Built artifacts in secretless Node 24.22.1 Docker, frozen main `72cab24990b3746574ac83e3d73c79530b8cc198` versus candidate. Actual built runtime send entry points, not formatter-only calls.
- Both channels twice per ref: multiline quote, rendered-limit chunk split, nested quote, nested split, nested heading/link/task/emphasis, fenced code, single-line quote and unchanged non-quote controls.
- Slack: actual WebClient HTTP writes to a local Slack Web API fixture, with stored conversations.history readback.
- WhatsApp: built sendMessageWhatsApp through the built listener send API; local Baileys socket fixture uses real generateWAMessage and WebMessageInfo protobuf encode/decode. This proves native outbound payloads, not live delivery, login or client rendering. No real credentials.
- The first reviewed implementation lost nested depth because style spans merge overlapping quote ranges. The repair uses the existing container depth metadata and preserves it through projections. Retained built-output counterexamples cover the reviewed implementation on both channels, twice.
- Repaired Slack suite: **45 passed**; shared parser, renderer/chunker and fallback suites: **103 passed**. Local WhatsApp Vitest stalled before case collection; no local unit pass claimed. Built WhatsApp outbound proof completed; hosted exact-head CI owns the remaining suite/typecheck gates.
- Changed-file Oxlint/Oxfmt; no test growth. The initial docs lint failure was owned and repaired by spelling the quote marker’s following space outside its inline code span.

Production +71/-5 (net +66), tests +4/-4 (net 0), docs +5 against frozen main. No new named SDK exports, dependencies or config options.

## Merge risk

Two-way door: revert restores prior formatting; no persisted-data, config or protocol migration. Blast radius is Slack/WhatsApp blockquote text and rendered chunk budgets. Other renderer output is unchanged because the new line-prefix option is opt-in. Parser-owned block metadata remains non-serialized.

prs.title: perf: delete redundant workspace Git commands
prs.body:
> **Not landed: A fails the declared owner performance gate.** All 12 owner arms and all 12 real-Gateway arms passed byte identity and cleanup. Gateway latency/loop criteria pass, but warm owner staging elapsed median rose 569.234→585.716 ms beyond the 10.246 ms A/A spread, and first-owner staging loop-maximum p95 rose 55.443→79.167 ms beyond the 7.373 ms spread. No samples were discarded or rerun. Exact-head CI [41272625010](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41272625010) is green at `9fe356eb8bba633b38cbfac29601acb1c9736f43`; no merge intent was submitted.

## What Problem This Solves

Workspace patch preparation rereads tree IDs that fast-import already knows, imports an identical empty tree, and diffs it against itself. Result staging discovers repository identity twice.

## User Impact

Changed patch preparation uses five Git commands instead of seven; empty-entry patches use three instead of seven; warm staging uses two instead of three. Workspace bytes and native import launch behavior remain intact. This is the command-deletion portion of #189989, isolated for independent measurement before landing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fast-import returns its root tree directly. Empty-entry preparation reuses the original base tree and pack. Staging retains common-directory identity and the captured environment in its owning function and passes them to the existing shared ref queue. Cold initialization still discovers the newly initialized repository through that owner. The single-use ensure helper disappears; file descriptors use scoped disposal, and the final synchronous authority check still immediately precedes native import. An earlier duplicate check before opening the private input is removed.

No broker routing changes, configuration, schema, dependency changes or caches. Production delta is +45/-45, net zero across five Gateway files. No process/broker production files change.

## Evidence

The new production-path regression preserves binary/NUL/CRLF/Unicode/deletion bytes and counts actual Git command admissions. It fails on exact parent `9518ced8ac3ae72d37bcb75297e9c13e2d1d47db` with seven commands where five are expected; candidate passes, including empty and warm-staging counts. Native imports remain two for a changed patch, one for an empty patch and one for staging. Focused test execution was 957 ms (57.40 s including first compiled-test preparation).

Codex autoreview is clean P0–P2. The focused regression and six recovery, checkpoint, ref-serialization and staged-read sibling suites pass (84 tests total). `pnpm check:changed --staged` completed: its initial type/lint setup failures came from a shared dependency projection and a missing lint-package projection; private physical dependency copies now replace those projections, and the compiler boundary, core/test/script typechecks and scripts lint pass. Targeted owner lint passes after renaming a shadowed callback parameter; fresh Codex review of the final bytes is scoped-clean P0–P2. An accidentally unscoped manual core-lint retry additionally reported existing line caps outside this change; it is not the changed-file lint verdict. Five additional Talk type-export reports disappeared with the private dependency setup: the pinned production export scan now passes on unchanged source. No shared dependencies or tracked dependency files changed. The unrelated `observePublication` dead-export regression in #187994 was previously reproduced on this exact parent and introduced by `3c67c5c3e491ba135cff9b17ca205257b8c74b6c`; it is left unchanged.

### Acceptance rule fixed before measurement

Baseline is `9518ced8ac3ae72d37bcb75297e9c13e2d1d47db`. Use committed `scripts/perf/workspace-reconcile-gateway-measure.ts` and its preload, a fresh real Linux Gateway per arm, 8 GiB touched ballast, 4,096 synthetic inventory files, minimal QA database, exact binary results and joined cleanup. Run 12 arms serially: baseline control 1; AB; BA; baseline control 2; AB; BA; AB. No discarded valid samples or timing-driven reruns. Record host load and source/build/workload hashes.

For each of dispatch, first changed turn, warm changed turn and unchanged turn, record elapsed time and loop p95, p99 and maximum separately. For each metric, define the allowed absolute spread as the absolute difference between its two baseline-control observations. Both the five-sample candidate median and nearest-rank p95 must be no greater than the matching baseline statistic plus that spread. P95 is the observed maximum at n=5. This includes the p95 of per-run maximum loop delay that regressed in the combined PR. Controls estimate observed drift, not a confidence interval. Keep all CPU, RSS, signed heap-delta and launch-count observations visible; heap delta is not allocation.

Also run the committed `scripts/perf/workspace-reconcile-spawn-measure.ts` owner workload with 62,000 files / 1,142,784,000 bytes, 620 changed files and 8 GiB ballast. Use the same interleaved control/comparison order; separate first-owner from two warm iterations. Apply the analogous absolute-control-spread rule to elapsed, loop p99 and maximum at median/p95, retaining all CPU/allocation and exact tree/pack/commit fingerprints. The existing owner workload does not record loop p95, so no such owner claim is made.

The real-Gateway companion and owner-scale fixture cover different boundaries. Neither claims btrfs or a 35 GiB session database. All measured launch costs are synchronous initiation of asynchronous ChildProcess.spawn calls; full Gateway capture excludes synchronous exec APIs and broker CPU. Final measurements and exact-head CI must meet the rule before landing.

## Completed A measurements

All Gateway elapsed medians rose within the measured A/A spreads. Passing those cells is not a causal speedup claim; the slow baseline pair remains included. Dispatch main-thread CPU median rose 26.2%, warm changed-turn retained heap delta rose 130%, and owner warm patch/staging allocation increased 72.6%/61.4%. These adverse observations are retained below.

<details>
<summary>Full fixed campaign: controls, raw failures, counts, timings, CPU, allocation/heap and limits</summary>

# Lane 2081A fixed performance campaign

Candidate `9fe356eb8bba633b38cbfac29601acb1c9736f43` vs exact parent `9518ced8ac3ae72d37bcb75297e9c13e2d1d47db`; PR #190084. Production 45 additions / 45 deletions (net 0), command deletion only; native descriptor launches remain.

**Acceptance: FAIL.** Owner: 2 failed of 36 cells. Gateway: 0 failed of 32 cells. No adverse sample was dropped, rerun, pooled across phases, or waived.

## Method and limits

The rule was recorded in acceptance.json before measurement and published in the PR. Both campaigns ran the same fixed 12-arm sequence: control A1, AB, BA, control A2, AB, BA, AB. The five comparison baseline processes and five candidate processes exclude the two controls. For each phase and metric, each candidate median and nearest-rank across-run p95 must be no more than the corresponding baseline statistic plus the absolute A/A control difference. For owner warm operations, the control statistic uses each control process’s two warm iterations. With five first-owner/Gateway or ten owner-warm samples, p95 is the observed maximum. Two controls measure observed spread, not a confidence interval. Percentages and resource metrics remain disclosed independently of this rule.

Owner workload: real createWorkspacePatch and result staging owners, 62,000 synthetic files × 18,432 bytes = 1,142,784,000 bytes; 620 changed files; one first-owner iteration and two warm iterations in each fresh process. Gateway workload: actual isolated Gateway, paired node, and local mock model provider through sessions.create/dispatch and chat.send/agent.wait; 4,096 inventory files, then changed binary output, warm changed binary output, and an unchanged turn. All accepted output bytes, patch/tree/pack/commit fingerprints matched. Each process retains 8 GiB touched ballast. Gateway minimum RSS is validated by the workload.

Local Linux arm64 Docker/OrbStack, overlayfs, Node 26.12.1, Git 2.39.5; eight CPUs, 24 GiB container limit, nonroot UID 1000. Native fs-safe 0.27.0 and proc-safe 0.4.2 use the pinned Linux companions. All data is synthetic; no production data or credentials were copied. The owner fixture covers workspace scale; the Gateway fixture uses a minimal QA database. This does not reproduce the 35 GiB agent database, btrfs, or full production concurrency.

Native spawn metrics capture ChildProcess.prototype.spawn: native asynchronous Gateway/parent launches only. Synchronous spawn APIs are excluded; the metric is synchronous initiation time of asynchronous launches, not child command runtime. Gateway main-thread CPU and process CPU exclude broker process CPU. Gateway heapUsedDelta is retained heap change, not allocation. Owner allocatedBytes is cumulative main-isolate allocation; external allocations and worker isolates are outside that counter. Owner totalCpuMs includes broker and reaped child CPU at Linux 100 Hz tick resolution.

prs.title: fix(clickclack): discussion rooms fail with PostgreSQL agents
prs.body:
Related: #188643, #175199

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: opening a ClickClack discussion room from Panels → Discussion fails when the Gateway's agent database family uses PostgreSQL.

## User Impact

Discussion rooms can be created and reopened with PostgreSQL-backed agents. SQLite behavior, session resets during channel creation, current-account checks, and binding commit authority are preserved. No configuration, schema, retention, or public SDK change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The opening path still performed a synchronous session read at its effect boundaries. PostgreSQL correctly refuses that read on the Gateway thread. This uses the plugin's existing prepared-session authority helper for each effect and final binding commit, releasing each preparation in a finally block. It deliberately reacquires current session authority after HTTP instead of freezing one incarnation for the entire open. Existing FIFO, quarantine/recovery, and binding CAS owners remain unchanged.

This is separate from #188643, which fixed NUL-containing revocation keys when shared state uses PostgreSQL.

## Evidence

**Baseline:** built source `9c22cf86f68b34269e49a25a95827c1c23b52ce0`, isolated PostgreSQL 17.11, synthetic state/token, and a loopback ClickClack HTTP fixture. Actual CLI/Gateway `sessions.create` succeeded; `session.discussion.open` returned `UNAVAILABLE: PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker…` before any remote channel POST. The committed real-storage regression also fails on unchanged production source at `service-open.ts:274 → assertEngineStoreExecutionAllowed`.

Initial published head: `25e6c72731ff6134258e171a8cc59c64dc7539ce`. Its Git tree `b51a601c9703edd63bea0891dcf7c493cb8ffd11` exactly matches the reviewed, built implementation commit below; the managed publisher added its commit attribution/receipt without changing source bytes. Both commits have the exact @etzelm coauthor trailer.

**Built product at the reviewed implementation commit:** `f54f44abfa07d4a474aa27639b0109a6bcd72107`. Both official build stamps report that head and clean inputs. The executing runtime was the repository's pinned Bun fork, version 1.4.4. No Gateway handler, session reader, authority owner, or database boundary was mocked.

| Actual built Gateway case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| PostgreSQL agents: create → discussion open → independent discussion info | Open; exactly one remote channel; persisted binding matches the PostgreSQL session row |
| PostgreSQL agents: public `sessions.reset` while the channel-create HTTP response is held | Open; lifecycle revision changes, session ID is preserved by the public reset contract, and the persisted binding remains current |
| SQLite parity through the same CLI/Gateway flow | Open; exactly one remote channel; independently read persisted binding matches the current session |

All three product cases passed and completed fixture cleanup. The three Gateway PIDs and PostgreSQL PID file were verified absent afterward. Independent SQL checks compared the binding with `session_nodes.current_session_id`; results were not inferred only from an RPC acknowledgment. The PostgreSQL product cases took 26.0s and 26.8s of test time; SQLite took 24.2s. These are behavior receipts, not performance claims.

**Focused validation:**

- New service regression uses real SQLite/PostgreSQL session and plugin-state owners; only external HTTP transport is replaced. It covers ordinary opening, a changed session ID during HTTP, and archive/removal/credential/destination changes before creation. It is red on the base and green on the repair.
- SQLite service, persistence, CAS/refusal/recovery, shutdown, and new authority tests: **69 passed in 3 files**, 75.21s wall time including preparation.
- Supported PostgreSQL conformance runner: **2 passed in 2 files**, including the new agent-storage regression and existing PostgreSQL shared-state revocation case, 36.98s wall time. The new regression itself took 1.8s. PostgreSQL catalog/trigger preflight passed.
- Conformance-planner tests: **6 passed**. Targeted production and test typechecks, scoped lint, formatting, whitespace, and the test-line budget passed. The dedicated **234-line allocation** covers the final 233-line real-storage regression and one line of phase-based reset-fixture growth; the shared ceiling is unchanged. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Fresh independent **Auto Review**, full six-file candidate against `9c22cf86…`, P0–P2: **scoped-clean**, no findings. The author simplification pass retained the existing authority owner and only the lifetime handling needed for these effects.

**CI follow-up:** the first hosted run exposed an ordinal-based reset fixture in `service.test.ts` (`session read 2`), reproduced locally as 38 passed / 1 failed. The new authority preparation intentionally adds a read and refuses a stale selected incarnation. The fixture now triggers its existing initial-read and after-create-read reset scenarios by service phase instead of read count; its binding and presentation assertions are unchanged. All **108 tests in the four affected service files** pass (63.2s command wall time), including both reset cases. Production code is unchanged from the built product proof. Follow-up targeted typecheck/lint/format, the exact 197-line test budget, author simplification, and fresh independent Auto Review of the two-file follow-up passed. No failed assertion or authority guard was relaxed. Fixture-follow-up source tree was `6aaf0b18460ad9e5d47a8eba831c3287703b6ae8` (local reviewed `cb3ccc3bcd08afeb621046ae3fa6882e1141304c`; managed published `ea0008ae395997ed69823495f54190e7d47febc0`). That prior review exposed the authority-recovery issue repaired below; latest-head CI and re-review remain separate gates.

### Authority-recovery finding repaired

ClawSweeper correctly found that an authority refusal was entering transport reconciliation. The follow-up separates preparation/adoption bookkeeping from attempted HTTP, permits ambiguous-outcome recovery only after a dispatched mutation, and re-prepares live authority before every recovery/name-conflict relist. No catch identifies errors by message, and no guard is relaxed.

The real-storage regression now counts channel GETs as well as creates. It was red on the reviewed head (4 GETs observed versus 3 expected), then green on SQLite and PostgreSQL. It proves successful ambiguous-create recovery still relists and adopts, while archive/removal/credential/destination refusal produces no follow-up GET; retirement during a failed POST produces neither relist nor binding. PostgreSQL conformance: 2/2 passed, new regression 1.945s; SQLite strengthened regression 1.759s. The exact grant is now **234 lines** (233-line real-storage regression plus one phase-fixture line), with the shared ceiling unchanged.

At clean local commit `46586bfbd0b227746dbf9545b5433f261278827c`, official built Gateway/PostgreSQL product proof was rerun: allowed open/reset-during-HTTP/info passed; public `sessions.patch {archived:true}` during the held create response refused attachment and an independent persisted-state query found no binding. Sanitized channel traces through the real HTTP client:

```text
allowed/reset: GET /api/workspaces/:workspace/channels -> POST /api/workspaces/:workspace/channels -> open/info; binding matches current PG session
archive during POST response: GET /api/workspaces/:workspace/channels -> POST /api/workspaces/:workspace/channels -> UNAVAILABLE inactive; binding absent; no follow-up channel request
```

Archive product test: 23.5s, runner exit 0; allowed reset: 26.4s, runner exit 0. An earlier archive attempt passed assertions but had a worker graceful-shutdown error; the verbose diagnostic run above completed cleanly, which does not establish a fix to that harness event. A separate attempted product credential-reload fixture was **not accepted as proof**: waiting for config.patch application while holding the plugin HTTP response caused a reload drain timeout; observing persistence alone was not equivalent to applied authority. Credential/destination retirement is therefore proven by the real-client/real-storage service boundary, not claimed as completed built-Gateway reload proof. No live account or provider was used.

Both final build stamps report local commit `46586bf…` with clean inputs. Managed published head is `a0fd38358dc454a223dc872e17177e6f26ba3719`; local source tree is `ed73f23dce42000afce2233d6accb8b203ae5959`. Production/test types, scoped lint/format, ratchet, author simplification and fresh independent Auto Review P0–P2 passed; existing CAS/refusal/recovery siblings remain green (108 tests across four files before the additional request controls). All owned Gateways and PostgreSQL were stopped.

**Known local failure, not hidden:** `test/scripts/extension-test-plan.test.ts` has three filesystem-inventory failures: owner-boundary balancing, candidate-checkout inventory, and Workboard directory/glob selection. All three reproduce after restoring both changed routing inputs to their base bytes. The ClickClack repair and test do not participate in those discovery cases. No assertions, guards, or baselines were weakened; hosted CI remains separate evidence.

**Limits:** the ClickClack network endpoint is synthetic, not a live external account. No model inference, paid provider calls, live Team data/service operations, actual migration, or deployment was performed. This changes storage/control behavior, not visual rendering.

## Contributor credit

Co-authored with Mitchell Etzel (@etzelm).

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @etzelm](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/65edb98b-73fa-47e9-8242-be1ae73fb4b9)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/1ce36f09-e234-44a0-85ed-3e2b7c4acf8b)

## Worked on by

- @etzelm

prs.title: fix: session cleanup times out before the Gateway finishes
prs.body:
Related: #170474

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw sessions cleanup` reports a timeout when Gateway maintenance takes longer than ten seconds, even though the cleanup may still complete.

## User Impact

Delegated session cleanup can wait up to two minutes for its result, including cleanup across multiple agent stores. No configuration or migration is required. This does not make maintenance itself faster; a stalled request can now take longer to report a timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Give the delegated `sessions.cleanup` call a bounded 120-second deadline, leaving headroom above the roughly 27 seconds reported in the issue. The shared Gateway request default, explicit-store cleanup and local dry runs retain their existing behavior. The regression exercises the command through the real Gateway client and WebSocket protocol, using a controlled clock to return a valid aggregate result after eleven seconds.

## Evidence

- On base `e61083f8f116b50e742a64e219c6a26342e67fcd`, the actual CLI command `pnpm openclaw sessions cleanup --all-agents --json` exited 1 with `gateway timeout after 10000ms`. The isolated protocol peer completed after 11,002 ms with the connection already closed.
- On final commit `4ec9243d374df177139132c8fad22186d2ce642f`, the same shipped CLI exited 0 with the aggregate result after 11,005 ms; the connection remained open until the response arrived. `pnpm build:runtime` passed (4m 27s), with the build stamp matching this commit and clean inputs.
- Focused regression: 1 passed; test body 364 ms. The original real-time wire regression failed on the base with a dispatched-request timeout and passed with the fix.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, targeted oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent review of the final change: no P0-P2 findings; issue timeline and open PRs checked for duplicates.
- The combined run of the new regression and unchanged existing cleanup test file produced 11 passes / 3 failures, due to Windows/POSIX absolute-path expectations and a dry-run table expectation. That run is not a full-suite pass.

The delayed peer is a synthetic, isolated Gateway protocol fixture; it proves the shipped CLI waiting contract, not the throughput or mutations of a large real session database. No external model calls or user data were used.


<details>
<summary>Captured shipped CLI output and protocol trace (redacted)</summary>

Both runs used `pnpm openclaw sessions cleanup --all-agents --json`, the repository's supported shipped CLI entry point, against the same isolated protocol peer. The peer completes exactly one cleanup request after an eleven-second delay. Addresses, local paths, request IDs and connection IDs are omitted. Tokens were never recorded in these logs.

Base: `e61083f8f116b50e742a64e219c6a26342e67fcd`, exit code **1**.

```text
  }
}
OpenClaw took too long to respond.
Your request may have completed. Check its result before trying again.
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```

```json

{"time":"2026-10-13T03:15:41.557Z","event":"closed","code":1005}
```

Final head: `4ec9243d374df177139132c8fad22186d2ce642f`, exit code **0**.

prs.title: fix(sessions): anchor catalog import identity to source coordinates
prs.body:
Closes #127378

## What Problem This Solves

Adopting a Pi, OpenCode, or Claude CLI session whose history rows carry no native IDs could wedge permanently after a crash: the adoption retry re-imported the bounded recent window under window-position identity, so after the source grew, one window position named a different message and the transcript store rejected the conflicting idempotency key. This change anchors imported rows to immutable source coordinates, so a recovery retry recognizes the overlap and only appends the new rows.

- Problem: `importSessionCatalogHistory` minted durable keys from the retained-window index (`item.id ?? index`); window growth between import attempts remapped one index to different content, and the conflicting-key rejection blocked adoption recovery permanently.
- Solution: the importers require stable identity up front and fail closed before any write; the built-in readers synthesize coordinate-derived ids (`pi-row-<line>`, `oc-row-<exportPos>:<part>`, `claude-row-<byteOffset>`) when native ids are absent, exposed through the existing optional `id`/`uuid` field.
- What changed: identity validation in both importers (generic + Claude), coordinate synthesis in the Pi, OpenCode, and Claude readers, regression tests for the readers and the recover-after-growth path.
- What did NOT change: the gateway protocol schema (`id` stays optional), the preservation path's existing identity scheme, and provider behavior when native ids are present.

## Why This Change Was Made

A retained-window position is not durable identity; source coordinates are stable under the append-only growth that retries observe.
- Best fix: follows the issue's suggested repair — require stable identity at the importer boundary and have built-in readers supply it from immutable source coordinates.
- Alternative rejected: content-hash identity — identical prompts legitimately repeat, and an occurrence ordinal shifts when an earlier duplicate leaves the window.
- Risk / non-goals: coordinates assume append-only sources (Pi in-place rewrites, OpenCode undo, and Claude rewrites can still remap them); providers unable to supply identity now fail recovery-safe adoption explicitly instead of minting colliding keys — a paired node running an older payload surfaces a clear adoption error rather than silent corruption; sessions left pending under the old index keys recover with duplicated overlap rows instead of staying wedged.

## User Impact

Adopted external sessions that crash during history import now recover on retry instead of failing forever with "Transcript idempotency key … conflicts with the admitted message". Identical repeated prompts in imported history are preserved — each repeat keeps its own coordinate identity.

## Evidence

Recovery before/after from the real runtime chain (real Pi JSONL file → real Pi reader → `importSessionCatalogHistory` → real transcript store; 200 ID-less rows, one appended before the retry — the issue's frozen repro):

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First import (200 ID-less rows) | 200 rows, keys `pi-catalog:pi-session:0..199` (window position) | 200 rows, keys `pi-catalog:pi-session:pi-row-2..pi-row-201` (JSONL line number, blank line counted) |
| Source grows by one, recovery re-import | `RECOVERY-FAILED: Transcript idempotency key "pi-catalog:pi-session:0" conflicts with the admitted message.` — adoption permanently blocked | 201 rows, 201 unique keys, last row `message-200`; overlap deduped, only the new row appended |

```
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs zz-proof-127378.mts
AFTER-IMPORT: rows=200 uniqueKeys=200
AFTER-IMPORT: firstKey=pi-catalog:pi-session:pi-row-2 lastKey=pi-catalog:pi-session:pi-row-201
AFTER-RECOVERY: rows=201 uniqueKeys=201
AFTER-RECOVERY: lastMessage=message-200
PROOF-RESULT: recovery succeeded
```

Before the fix, the same harness printed `RECOVERY-FAILED: Transcript idempotency key "pi-catalog:pi-session:0" conflicts with the admitted message.` — the error reported in the issue. Coordinate stability under append-only growth is additionally covered by parser tests for all three readers, and the full adopt → grow → recover path by `pi-session-catalog-continuation.test.ts`.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `git grep`/`git diff` and targeted vitest runs to analyze issue #127378, locate the window-index identity fallback in `session-catalog-history-import.ts`, and implement coordinate-based import identity across the three built-in readers. The implementer understands the code: an idempotency key must name the same source row across recovery re-imports, so identity comes from append-stable source coordinates. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.body:
Supersedes #169159, thanks @JasonBuildAI.

Related: #169157.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes SQLite snapshot reads and Doctor migration detection failing when Windows EFS-encrypted cache directories reject same-directory renames with `EXDEV`.

## User Impact

Affected Windows users can inspect SQLite state without relocating their cache or disabling encryption. Other rename errors still fail visibly; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Copy directly into the existing partial snapshot instead of promoting an intermediate `first` file. At final publication, fall back only on `EXDEV` to the existing guarded, exclusive file-copy primitive, flush the destination, and remove the staged file. The family stays private until preparation returns, so publication does not require an atomic rename. Existing cleanup owns failed copies.

Production delta: +21/−8, net +13. Removed the intermediate file, its redundant rename, and its cleanup branch. The remaining growth is the required durable fallback; no new module, wrapper registration, or policy owner. Legacy `first` artifacts remain recognized for abandoned-snapshot cleanup after upgrades. Test delta: +44, with a dedicated allocation for the three preparation paths and the distinct non-EXDEV failure control.

## Evidence

- Candidate: `9af7ded4487eb38dce6401b46d89b2e4f491d2f9`.
- Base: `c32d920dab6bcb2eb55251bc71665816bb04f809`, current main at investigation. Both unhandled runtime renames were still present. #190069 (`c9569e415c92416497f25d2352dac69282a852b2`) only normalizes repository-check paths and does not repair runtime snapshot publication.
- Red on unchanged main production code: all three simulated `EXDEV` cases fail (synchronous copy, asynchronous copy, online backup); the `EPERM` control passes. Tests exercise real SQLite reads, source preservation, private file permissions, and cleanup.
- Green: primary snapshot suite, 30 passed (10.56 seconds wrapper wall time, 8.84 seconds Vitest duration). Copy and cleanup suites also pass (39 existing tests plus the four regressions before their move to the primary suite; 36.86 seconds wrapper wall time including compilation).

prs.title: fix: SQLite snapshot reads fail on Windows EFS-encrypted profile directories
prs.body:
Related: #169157

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: read-only SQLite snapshot publication fails with `EXDEV: cross-device link not permitted` when the private staging directory inherits the EFS Encrypted attribute (for example `%LOCALAPPDATA%\openclaw` under a corporate encryption policy), which makes `openclaw doctor` stop at state-migration detection and block every later migration step.

## User Impact

User impact: on affected Windows machines, read-only state inspection and `openclaw doctor` now complete instead of refusing to continue with "check filesystem health and write permissions or set XDG_CACHE_HOME to a writable filesystem". No user action or data migration is required, and behavior on unencrypted filesystems is unchanged (the rename fast path is still used).

## Why This Change Was Made

Node's Windows rename path reports same-directory moves as a cross-device error on EFS-encrypted directories even though both paths are on one volume. That made the two publication renames inside the private staging directory (`first` -> `database.sqlite.partial`, and the `database.sqlite.partial*` -> `database.sqlite*` loop) abort every snapshot. The publication helper now falls back to copying the already-verified staged bytes (descriptor copy + fsync) and removing the staged file only when the rename is rejected with EXDEV; other rename failures still fail closed. The staged files are closed private copies in a single-process staging directory, so the rename's atomicity is not load-bearing here. The helper lives in a small sibling module because `sqlite-readonly-location.ts` is at the repo's 700-line cap.

## Evidence

Before the fix (2026.9.9, commit 3258dd876, Windows 11 build 26200, EFS-encrypted `%LOCALAPPDATA%`), minimal reproduction calling the snapshot API on a plain SQLite source:

```
FAILED: Error: SQLite read-only worker failed while creating its private snapshot: EXDEV: cross-device link not permitted, rename 'C:\Users\Jason\AppData\Local\openclaw\openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-43361feb-...\openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-7d621f7e-...\first' -> 'C:\Users\Jason\AppData\Local\openclaw\openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-43361feb-...\openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-7d621f7e-...\database.sqlite.partial'; snapshot staging root ...: check filesystem health and write permissions or set XDG_CACHE_HOME to a writable filesystem (code=EXDEV)
```

`openclaw doctor` with a fresh state home stopped at migration detection:

```
Doctor stopped because a state migration refused to continue. Resolve the reported migration failure before retrying. Later repairs were not run.
Failing check migration-detection (step-refused): Failed detecting Codex native pending assignments: Error: SQLite read-only worker failed while creating its private snapshot: EXDEV: cross-device link not permitted, rename [redacted-path]
Failing check device-auth (blocked-by-prior-refusal): Migration step "device-auth" was not run because prior step "migration-detection" refused execution.
Failing check device-identity (blocked-by-prior-refusal): ...
Failing check meeting-transcripts (blocked-by-prior-refusal): ...
Failing check managed-worktrees (blocked-by-prior-refusal): ...
```

After the fix, the same reproduction and the same doctor command on the same machine:

```
prepared: C:\Users\Jason\AppData\Local\openclaw\openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-...\database.sqlite
cleanup: ok
```

```
—  Doctor complete.
```

with no `step-refused` or `blocked-by-prior-refusal` failures in the output.

Trigger characterization on the affected machine: `cipher /c C:\Users\Jason\AppData\Local` reports "New files added to this directory will be encrypted" and `dir /a` shows `E` on `AppData\Local\openclaw`; `fs.renameSync` within one directory fails with EXDEV under `%LOCALAPPDATA%` and `%APPDATA%` (file and directory renames), while `cmd` `move`, PowerShell `Rename-Item`, and `[System.IO.File]::Move` succeed in the same directory, and the same Node rename succeeds under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp`, the profile root, and `D:\Temp`.

Checks run locally:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.test.ts -t "EXDEV"` -> 2 passed. Without the fix, the new EXDEV test fails at `src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.ts:370` with `EXDEV: cross-device link not permitted`, so the regression test demonstrably detects the defect.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` -> exit 0.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on the changed files -> clean.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mts --base upstream/main` -> OK. `check-assertion-safety-ratchet.mts --base upstream/main` -> OK.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/run-lint.mts --base upstream/main` -> Control UI Lit ratchet OK; the plugin-sdk boundary dts generation step then timed out after 300 s on this machine (load/network-bound, unrelated to this change).

Known gaps: the regression test simulates the EXDEV rejection so it runs deterministically on every OS; the EFS reproduction itself is Windows-only. Repo-wide `pnpm check` fails on this base commit before this change as well (line-cap, database-worker, assertion-safety, and changelog-attribution ratchet failures reproduce with a pristine checkout); the two ratchets that this change can affect now pass. The background reclamation claim rename in `src/infra/sqlite-snapshot-staging.ts` shares the same failure mode but only degrades cleanup logging, so it is intentionally out of scope for this minimal fix (noted in the issue).

AI disclosure: this change was drafted with AI assistance at my request, under my direction and review.

prs.title: feat(plugins): let plugins post transcript-only chat notices
prs.body:
## Problem

Skill Workshop is moving from core into the bundled `skill-workshop` plugin. Its "Learned" chat row uses a core-only transcript marker, `skill-workshop-change`. A plugin cannot write that marker: the plugin SDK mirror writer accepts only `channel-final` markers. Adding another Workshop-only kind would grow core for one feature.

## Fix

- **One generic marker kind, `plugin-notice`:** `{ kind: "plugin-notice", pluginId, type, data }`, with `data` as JSON.
  - It joins the transcript-only allowlist, so a notice row is never replayed to the model, including rows whose provider and model fields were stripped (#99470).
  - Turn replay treats it as an operational notice, like the model-fallback notice: it never completes a foreground user turn.
- **SDK:** `appendAssistantMirrorMessageByIdentity` (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/session-transcript-runtime`) now accepts a plugin notice as `deliveryMirror` and stores only its four known fields. No new SDK exports.
  - A plugin notice is identified by its data, not its text: an unkeyed notice never folds into an earlier row with the same text. Use `idempotencyKey` to make retries safe.
- **Workshop moves onto it:** the review notice is now `pluginId: "skill-workshop"`, `type: "skills-changed"`, with the same `agentId`, `runId` and `skills` data. The Control UI Learned row reads the data through `readPluginNoticeData`. The `skill-workshop-change` kind is removed.
- **Docs:** the SDK entry-point page describes how to post a plugin notice.

## Impact

- **No visible change:** new Learned rows render the same in the Control UI, and channels get the same text and Undo button.
- **Older rows:** only 2026.10.10 betas wrote `skill-workshop-change`; no stable release did. Those beta rows stay out of model replay through their `openclaw`/`delivery-mirror` provider and model fields, and the Control UI shows their text as a plain notice instead of the Learned row.
- **Restart notice** and other mirror rows are unchanged.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New SDK test: two unkeyed notices with the same text (after an ordinary answer with that text) are stored as two rows with their own data; fails without the fix | pass |
| Stored-row compatibility: a literal 2026.10.10-beta `skill-workshop-change` row stays out of model replay (SDK test) and renders as a text notice in the Control UI (`chat-system-notice` test) | pass |
| New SDK test: a plugin notice is stored with only its known fields, read back by plugin and type, and still excluded from replay with provider and model stripped | pass |
| `review-outcome`, turn replay, Control UI notice and Learned-row unit tests (5 files, 123 tests) | pass |
| Workshop contract e2e: gateway notice history, gateway review, Control UI app, Learned notice browser test | pass |
| `check:changed`: typecheck, lint, boundaries | pass, except the Plugin SDK surface budget (3855 > 3854), which fails the same way on clean `origin/main`; this PR adds no SDK exports |
| `git diff --check` | pass |

### Upgrade from the latest stable release (v2026.10.9)

1. The published `openclaw@2026.10.9` package seeded a session in an isolated state directory through its own SDK: a user turn, a model answer and a `channel-final` delivery-mirror row (agent database schema 25).
2. This PR's build ran `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` on that state. It backed up both databases and migrated them (exit 0).
3. This PR's SDK read all three stored rows unchanged, then appended two unkeyed plugin notices with the same text (`runId` `review-1` and `review-2`).
4. A new process reloaded the transcript and passed it through the replay filter (`normalizeAssistantReplayContent`):

```json
{"rows":["user:Deploy the site.","assistant:Deployed.","assistant:Deployed.","assistant:Review complete","assistant:Review complete"],
 "notices":[{"runId":"review-1"},{"runId":"review-2"}],
 "replay":["user:Deploy the site.","assistant:Deployed."]}
```

Existing sessions survive the upgrade. Both new notices keep their own data after a reload. The model sees neither the notices nor the old delivery-mirror row.

prs.title: fix(worker-environments): isolate a corrupt profile snapshot from the environment list
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
listRows decoded every worker-environment profile snapshot with an unguarded JSON.parse. A stored "null", "{}", or truncated snapshot threw inside the row map, so one bad environment made the whole list unreadable. null and {} also passed the shape check and later crashed on profileSnapshot.project or handed undefined settings to requireWorkerProfile.

## User Impact
Gateway placement and environment reads keep returning the healthy environments when one stored snapshot is corrupt. A direct read of the bad environment fails with an error that names it.

## Why
Snapshots are written as { install, settings } before a project exists, so the decoder requires a JSON object with a settings object. It does not require project or executionMode, which are added later. List reads skip the bad row and warn. A lookup of that one id still throws.

## Evidence
src/gateway/worker-environments/store-row-codec.test.ts covers null, {}, truncated JSON, a snapshot stored before project preparation, and a list that keeps the healthy row.

Closes #180197

prs.title: fix(test): preserve fixture cleanup custody and runtime ownership
prs.body:
Test fixtures could lose nested cleanup evidence or resolve an ambient runtime after isolating HOME. The lifecycle test also duplicated process-death policy and could consume an unsafe PID receipt.

Use the canonical reject-on-abort wait and validate PID >1 before group operations. The shared fixture owner recursively classifies cleanup custody after joining registered commands and preserves the containing error/cause identity. Crabbox fixtures resolve pinned pnpm before HOME isolation, then colocate a physical Node executable with its pnpm adapter under the existing suite-owned dependency root. This matters because the real receiver supplies NODE_BIN=dirname(process.execPath), which the selected installer prepends to PATH; a PATH-only adapter or Node symlink falls back to hosted Corepack. All five dependency scenarios now assert the actual private Node path emitted by that installer.

The repeated-pnpm cancellation case uses the existing receipt owner instead of a timing assumption. It preserves real implementation exit130, durable exit receipts and retained-shell launcher143 behavior. Release failures still force/join owned PIDs; receipt-channel close is awaited after fixture custody settles.

Validation:
- Final complete Crabbox Node owner: 284 pass, 1 existing skip.
- All five dependency scenarios pass under Node and Bun with a real ambient Node executable and a pnpm sentinel. Actual installer receipts select the private runtime, never the ambient sentinel.
- The previous PR head fails the same graph scenario by invoking ambient pnpm. Replacing the private Node copy with a symlink fails under Node and Bun for the same reason.
- Persistent nested aggregate/cause regressions use a real joined command and preserve strict cause identity. The original shallow owner fails both under Node and Bun.
- Three resistant-child fault modes pass under Node and Bun: injected PID1, cleanup error, and ordered body-plus-cleanup errors. Weakened PID/retention controls fail.
- Whole Crabbox Bun previously passed 284 tests with 1 existing skip before the final awaited-close/private-Node shape. Final changed dependency scenarios and repeated-pnpm case pass under Bun. No whole final Bun or native Windows claim.
- Actual receiver-adapter and release-hold mutations fail without overriding genuine child exit behavior. The malformed-receipt negative catches the original aggregate/cause, confirms all six owned PIDs dead after cleanup joins, then rethrows.
- Both relevant test-type lanes, type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Independent source review reports no actionable P0-P2 findings.

Production/tooling LOC: 0. Test/support LOC: +139. Removed the local wait implementation and shallow cleanup predicate. Existing timeouts, real dependency installs, graph assertions and production receiver/installer/cancellation policy are preserved. No billed-minute saving is inferred.

prs.title: fix(models): saving provider credentials shows that provider's models
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Adding a provider did not make it usable when a model allowlist (`modelPolicy.allow`) existed. On the Team server, saving a Particle API key in **Settings → Models → Connect provider** succeeded, but no Particle model appeared in the model picker: the allowlist hid them all. Sign-in flows (CLI, chat `/login`, Telegram, Control UI wizard) asked **Show all <Provider> models / Keep current restrictions** with Keep as the default. The API-key save path skipped even that, and #189917 only added a text warning that told the user to edit config by hand.

## Fix

Saving credentials for a provider is now the request to use its models. When the allowlist that governs the agent hides **every** model of that provider, the save adds `<provider>/*` to that allowlist, through the existing model-policy owner (`src/commands/models/auth-model-policy.ts`):

- per-agent `agents.entries.<id>.modelPolicy.allow` when the agent sets its own policy, otherwise `agents.defaults.modelPolicy.allow`;
- an unmigrated legacy `agents.defaults.models` allowlist gets the wildcard key, so none of its models is dropped.

Nothing changes when there is no allowlist, or when the allowlist already names some of the provider's models (an exact ref such as `openai/gpt-x`, or a narrower wildcard such as `clawrouter/anthropic/*`). The policy owner decides that: the check reads providers from `createModelVisibilityPolicy(...).allowedKeys`, which resolves exact refs, aliases and bare legacy refs (inferring their provider from configured provider rows) the same way the picker does. A deliberate exact list is never widened.

Paths:

- API key / token save (`models.authSetApiKey`, `openclaw models auth paste-api-key`, `paste-token`): the wildcard is added in the same config write as the credential's auth profile.
- Sign-in (`openclaw models auth login`, Control UI wizard, chat `/login`, Telegram `/login`): after the credential is saved, one write adds the wildcard. The login result carries `modelAccess: { message, applied }`; chat and Telegram append "Added `<provider>/*` to allowed models." to the completion message; the Control UI wizard reports an unconfirmed apply as before.

Removed: the post-save select prompt, the deferred `onModelAccessRequested` request, `offerProviderLoginModelAccess` / `answerProviderLoginModelAccess`, the `/login access` and `/login choice` model-access commands, `createLoginChoicePrompt`, `ProviderModelPolicyChangedError`, and the #189917 Control UI warning. `provider-auth-login-flow-runtime` is a private-local SDK subpath (docs/plugins/sdk-subpaths.md), so its only consumers are bundled (core chat `/login`, Telegram), migrated here.

Authority: every `models.authSetApiKey` save now checks live requester authority (`readGatewayRequestMutationAuthority`, the guard `config.patch` uses) before its credential and config writes. Before, browser saves without `expectedOwnerId` passed no guard; the save now also widens the allowlist, so a requester whose connection or scopes end mid-save cannot commit it. Owner-bound CLI saves keep their owner check and add the same requester check.

Plugin setup defaults still cannot change restrictions (`withoutProviderModelPolicy` is unchanged); only the credential save does.

This reverses the ask-first default from #144468 by maintainer decision.

No undo button: the `models.authSetApiKey` result has no field for the change, and adding one is a protocol change; the change is a single visible `provider/*` allowlist entry.

## User Impact

Add a provider key or sign in → its models show in the model picker, even under an existing allowlist that did not mention the provider. Operators who listed specific models of that provider keep exactly their list.

## Evidence

Real Gateway, real config write (`src/gateway/server-methods/models-auth-api-key.integration.test.ts`): config `agents.defaults.modelPolicy.allow: ["other/*"]`, `models.authSetApiKey` for `fixture` → saved config `["other/*", "fixture/*"]`. Negative control: with the new line disabled, the test fails `expected [ 'other/*' ] to deeply equal [ 'other/*', 'fixture/*' ]`.

Policy owner (`src/commands/models/auth-model-policy.test.ts`, real config file):

- per-agent policy widened, defaults untouched;
- no allowlist / provider already allowed → config bytes unchanged;
- allowlist with exact `sample/one`, `sample/two` → unchanged; with `sample/family/*` → unchanged (both fail when the check is reverted to "literal `sample/*` missing");
- deferred legacy map keeps `existing-model` and gains `sample/*`;
- migrated model map is not treated as an allowlist;
- authority revoked during the writer's preflight → no write.

Sign-in end to end against a real plugin and config (`src/commands/models.auth.provider-resolution.test.ts`): `access`, `access-legacy`, `access-legacy-set-default` cases save the credential, add `authstore-proof/*` with no prompt, and log the notice.

Real key writer under revocation (`src/commands/models/auth-api-key.test.ts`, real auth store and config file): with an allowlist present, authority revoked inside the config write leaves the config bytes unchanged (no auth binding, no `sample/*`); unrevoked, the same write saves the binding and `["other/*", "sample/*"]`.

Bare legacy ref (`auth-model-policy.test.ts`): legacy map `{ tiny: {} }` with a configured `sample` provider that has `tiny` → saving a `sample` credential leaves config unchanged (fails against the earlier `DEFAULT_PROVIDER` parse).

Requester authority (`src/gateway/server-methods/models-auth-status.set-api-key.test-support.ts`): authority ends during the save → the RPC fails with "Gateway requester authority changed" and the writer's `assertCurrent` throws before commit. Negative control: with the handler's default guard replaced by a no-op, the test fails.

Surface tests: chat `/login` and Telegram completion messages include the notice; Control UI wizard reports unconfirmed apply; mocked-Gateway Control UI E2E (`model-provider-login.e2e.test.ts`) passes.

Control UI, mocked Gateway, policy `allow: ["openai/*"]`, save a Particle key:

Before (main, #189917): the dialog stays open with a config-editing instruction.

![Before: dialog tells the user to edit modelPolicy.allow](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/793cafbe-5e2d-4be0-b111-a95265d6db8a)

After: the Gateway widens the policy during the save; the dialog closes like any successful save.

![After: dialog closes after save](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/480dced1-3ec3-4fed-b092-c2b6842ba31b)

Commands:

- `pnpm test src/commands/models/auth-model-policy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 7 passed.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/models-auth-api-key.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 1 passed (~12.5 s, real Gateway, existing test extended; no new boot).
- `pnpm test src/commands/models/auth.test.ts src/commands/models.auth.provider-resolution.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 80 passed.
- Chat/Gateway/Telegram/UI suites: passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1 pnpm check:changed`.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

Merge danger: one-way for configs: a credential save can now write `<provider>/*` into a model allowlist. A revert stops new writes but does not remove entries already added. Blast radius: operators who rely on an allowlist that does not mention a provider to keep that provider hidden after someone adds its credentials. Only admins can save credentials.

prs.title: fix(discord): button fallback feedback fails after plugin acknowledgement
prs.body:
Related: #169147

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes invalid Discord fallback acknowledgements when a matched plugin declines a button after the interaction has already been acknowledged.

## User Impact

Fallback feedback stays private and leaves the original decision panel intact. Accepted actions are not retried or dispatched again. There are no configuration, dependency, approval, or data migrations.

## Why This Change Was Made

A component's native acknowledgement sends callback type 6 (`DeferredMessageUpdate`). The existing silent feedback helper then calls `reply`, which edits the source message in that state. Sending `content` to a Components V2 source is invalid; an ephemeral reply flag does not turn that source edit into a private message.

The shared `replySilently` owner now uses an explicitly private follow-up only for `deferred-update`. Initial replies, privately deferred replies, and replies after an initial response keep native routing. The nonfatal feedback-error callback is unchanged. Generic native `reply` and intentional component editing are not modified.

The declined-plugin monitor regression runs `onMatched` against an actual native `ButtonInteraction`, then asserts one type-6 callback, one private follow-up, zero source PATCHes, and one downstream dispatch. Six focused native serialization cases also cover both V2 and legacy sources and the other response states. A single pinned upstream merge needed to unblock CI preserves upstream's reduced monitor cases and retains this native regression, which upstream had removed in its test reductions.

## Evidence

**Behavior or issue addressed:** private fallback acknowledgement after a matched plugin pre-acknowledges and declines; no original-panel mutation or duplicate dispatch.

**Real environment tested:** Linux x64, Node 24.21.0; current-source native interactions with offline mocked external boundaries, plus a real user click through the equivalent exact-byte repair in the installed Discord 2026.9.9 plugin. These are separate proof lanes, not a claim that current main was deployed.

**Exact steps or command run after the patch:** canonical `pnpm test` commands for native interactions/helper and monitor tests, the exact-path changed-check planner/formatter/scoped diff, plus `node combined-main-proof.mjs`. Commands, results, and failed attempts are recorded below.

**Evidence after fix:** the real-click screenshot and sanitized native readbacks below, copied offline before/after output, and committed native/monitor regressions. Root independently reran the combined proof. Fresh independent source review and shared `autoreview --mode local --engine codex --max-priority P2` both found no actionable issues; the latter exited 0 with `scoped-clean` on the initial frozen three-file diff.

**Observed result after fix:** the real user saw a private checkmark; the original V2 panel remained intact with `edited_timestamp: null`; native transcript readback contained one callback, one terminal assistant response in one run, and no tool calls. The combined offline proof additionally records one type-6 acknowledgement, one private follow-up, zero source PATCHes, and exactly one downstream dispatch at mocked REST boundaries.

**What was not tested:** current-main live deployment, external retry deduplication, full suite/build, and successful full local extension type gates. A focused project using the canonical extension-test compiler settings passed for both changed fixtures; full hosted CI is tracked below. No authenticated Discord REST wire trace was captured during the real click; type-6/decline attribution is derived from the enabled plugin's registered namespace and exact handler source, not fabricated wire logs.

### Real Post-Fix Discord Click (2026-10-11)

![Real post-fix Discord click: preserved Components V2 panel and private acknowledgement](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f4446017-5736-433d-bf62-d1e46d0946f9)

The operator sent one harmless native Gateway `message.action` presentation: a Components V2 panel titled **Discord acknowledgement verification - PR #169162**, with a single **Verify acknowledgement** button. Its inert value began `cardops:proof-169162:` and requested only a fixed final marker, with no tools, card/listing/offer changes, or financial actions. The owner clicked once, confirmed **"Clicked; private checkmark appeared"**, and supplied the screenshot attached below. No synthetic interaction or callback replay was sent.

Canonical Gateway `plugins.list` readback reports both Discord `2026.9.9` and `cardops-intake-handoff` `1.0.1` installed, enabled, and runtime `active`, with no plugin diagnostics. The latter plugin registers Discord namespace `cardops`. Its actual handler starts with:

```js
if (!String(ctx?.interaction?.data || "").startsWith("cardops:hold-price:")) {
  return { handled: false };
}
```

Thus this deliberately non-action value selects the matched namespace and declines without running the CardOps hold command. Native dispatcher source awaits `onMatched` acknowledgement before invoking that handler. This is source-derived attribution; the private screenshot and the readback facts below are directly observed. The installed silent-feedback compiled helper has the independently verified patched SHA-256 recorded in the deployment section.

Sanitized actual observations (all times UTC; private identifiers, endpoints and tokens omitted):

```text
2026-10-11 14:54:44.870  native Gateway send receipt: verification panel created
2026-10-11 14:54:55.398  native transcript: one user button callback
2026-10-11 14:55:15.625  native transcript: one terminal assistant response; same single run
2026-10-11 14:55:17.433  Discord readback: one final channel message
                         content: PROOF-169162 dispatch completed.

source panel GET: flags=32768; content=""; edited_timestamp=null
source panel: original title, harmless text, button label and component layout present
transcript: user callbacks=1; terminal assistant replies=1; runs=1; tool calls=0
transcript: hasMore=false; active runs=0; terminal status=done
channel messages after panel containing the proof marker: 1
user screenshot: private checkmark plus "Only you can see this"; source panel intact
```

This proves a genuine post-fix click, private visible feedback, source-panel preservation, and one completed downstream dispatch on the shipped-version installation. `edited_timestamp: null` is the native Discord preservation observation, not a claimed before/after byte hash. The screenshot contains no IPs, API keys, phone numbers, interaction tokens, or non-public endpoints. No card, marketplace, or financial action was executed.

### Local Passing Proof

- Six new native interaction tests passed on Node 24.21.0 / Vitest 5.0.0 in 1.31 seconds with a small isolated offline config. This is not the repository's canonical/full suite or a frozen main dependency install.
- A combined offline harness ran the actual current native interaction, component fallback handler, plugin-interactive helper, and silent acknowledgement owner. Only external REST, registry, authorization, namespace dispatch, and final agent delivery boundaries were mocked. The matched namespace hook explicitly invoked the real `onMatched` acknowledgement before declining.
- Formatting completed for all three changed files; `git diff --check` passed.

```text
[ok] baseline: real type6 pre-ack + declined namespace + source content PATCH rejected; dispatch=1
[ok] patched: real type6 pre-ack + declined namespace + private follow-up=1; source PATCH=0; dispatch=1
[ok] current native interaction and actual plugin/fallback source; external REST/registry/auth/agent boundaries mocked; network=0; replay=0
```

The baseline rejection above comes from an explicitly synthetic offline V2 contract validator. The original production logs retained `DiscordError: Invalid Form Body`, but not Discord's structured response body. This PR does not claim to have recovered a historical `errors.content` response or to explain every acknowledgement error.

### Required Gates And Limits

These canonical commands were attempted but stopped before running their checks because the isolated sparse checkout lacked wrapper prerequisites. A bounded 90-second supported source expansion also timed out. These are **unrun/blocked gates, not passing tests**:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/monitor/monitor.test.ts extensions/discord/src/internal/interactions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  blocked before collection: test/helpers/temp-dir.ts missing
pnpm tsgo:extensions
  blocked: package-manager bootstrap failed before checking types
pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
  blocked: sparse checkout missing run-tsgo.mts / preinstall prerequisites
node scripts/check-changed.mjs --dry-run --files extensions/discord/src/monitor/agent-components-reply.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/agent-components-reply.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/monitor.test.ts
  blocked before planning: scripts/changed-lanes.mts missing
```

Subsequently a physically complete checkout of PR head `edc8137ed60d6f66e1ee52fa0139d67d2de1b0e4` completed a frozen dependency install. The canonical changed-path planner, exact-three-file formatter, and scoped diff check passed. Both canonical extension type commands reached the compiler but hit their built-in 120-second watchdog without source diagnostics; these are not passing type checks. A first test attempt hit a 60-second cold-worker silence deadline before collection; a bounded retry prepared the native worker in 76 seconds and ran the tests.

That canonical retry passed the native interaction/helper suites (36 tests) and 30 monitor tests. The strengthened monitor case exposed an incomplete test fixture: its final channel-message REST POST returned no message receipt. A conservative test-only correction now supplies a typed minimal channel receipt and asserts that final delivery occurs, without suppressing downstream delivery or altering production code. The subsequent canonical warm monitor run passed **31/31**, including the strengthened real native pre-ack/decline case. Focused canonical coverage is **67/67 across sequential commands**, not one green all-three run or the full suite. The original failed attempt is retained as failed, not relabeled a pass.

Prior published head: `123bd59d539ead2dee0f5b26ea5c8ae52c871dad`. Its tested `monitor.test.ts` SHA-256 was `eabbdcb9143ce5df8f7b5b85833260d8f4b1e25d0ce63c8aabc5482358e11cbb`; production/helper source bytes remain unchanged from the initial reviewed head. Root reviewed that fixture diff and shared AutoReview exited 0, `scoped-clean` at P0-P2, before commit/push.

### CI Fixture Correction

Typed correction head: `062b8eb8eec8dc841ce2240b6c2a6aaba05b4ad9`. The previous head's CI failed `check-test-types` with TS2352 in the two native raw-interaction fixtures. Both now supply the required Discord API fields and use `satisfies ConstructorParameters<...>[1]` instead of unsafe whole-payload assertions. The existing test-only Discord runtime adapter also exports `Locale`; the first corrected runtime attempt caught that missing export and is retained as a failed attempt. Production code and REST behavior assertions are unchanged.

After the adapter correction, one canonical `pnpm test` invocation passed both sequential shards: **67/67**, 36 native/helper tests and 31 monitor tests, exit 0 in 85.46 seconds. A focused type project extending the canonical extension-test config passed for both changed fixtures, with no loosened compiler settings or diagnostic suppressions. The full local extension-test typecheck reached its 300-second watchdog without diagnostics; it is not a passing full type gate. Formatter and whitespace checks passed for all four PR paths. Current published head: `64f528a969ede9e4f299527bf733374fefd74eb0`. GitHub could not start ordinary pull-request CI on the typed correction because of a merge conflict. One merge of the already-fetched frozen `345f4002261812d1da7b44ad68d000c4d6795171` snapshot resolves that blocker; no further moving-base updates are planned. The only manual conflict resolution retains the PR's native declined-plugin test while preserving all upstream reductions. Formatter, scoped whitespace checks and independent full four-file AutoReview passed after resolution. The 67 local tests above belong to the pre-merge typed correction, not an assertion that the merged head has the same test count.

**Exact-head hosted CI is green:** [CI run 38152456767](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38152456767) completed successfully on `64f528a969ede9e4f299527bf733374fefd74eb0`. `check-test-types`, all five core test-type shards, production types, lint and the selected regression jobs passed. The exact commit's aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency-review and security-sensitive-review statuses are all `success`. Skipped, unselected lanes are not counted as passing tests. ClawSweeper's fresh exact-head review completed at 15:58 UTC on October 11: **Before merge: None; Findings: None**. Validated source SHA-256 values:


Actual canonical commands on the physically complete frozen-install checkout (Linux x64, Node 24.21.0, pnpm 12.9.0, Vitest 5.0.1):
