prs.title: fix(agents): compact long tool turns and refresh context totals
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long embedded tool loops could fill a 1M context window before auto-compaction, while `sessions.list` continued showing the previous turn's token count. The threshold was 980,000 tokens, fresh usage stayed in memory until the whole run settled, and the mid-turn admission check was disabled by default.

## User Impact

Built-in client maintenance now starts by 75% of the active window. Provider-owned compaction and native runtime policies retain ownership. Every prepared embedded request is checked against the hard window, including the first request. Context totals refresh during tool loops from the request owner's measured context plus pending content, and final settlement supersedes its own intermediate observations.

Older prompt-only snapshots become unknown until refreshed. No configuration option, SQLite schema change, or new cache is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider boundary makes and publishes one pressure decision through the existing keyed writer. Downstream transcript rescans and mixed-counter repairs are removed. Ordinary tool text no longer receives a blanket two-characters-per-token penalty; encoded data, numeric groups, and JSON delimiters retain content-sensitive sizing. Hard admission and context-engine assembly use nominal occupancy, while compaction planning retains its safety margin. Summary fitting and request admission share the same lexical estimator, so fitted summaries retain metadata without exceeding the final request budget.

This repairs the false positives behind the reverted default guard: the existing 32k prompt-cache fixture remains unchanged. Synthetic host budgets too small to reach their intended tool boundary now match their existing model windows, with behavioral assertions preserved. The cold native-auth fixture also awaits its existing preparation owner; its setup failure reproduces on the exact parent and was introduced by #169580.

Related: #189810, #189891, #189888, #164551. Thanks @amittell for the ordered final-context snapshot precedent and @vincentkoc for the realistic lifecycle fixture budget. This change covers the accounting overlap with #164551 together with admission and threshold ownership.

## Evidence

- The production-path 1M HTTP regression fails on the exact parent and passes with the fix: persisted growth during a long tool turn, one compaction before 80%, no over-window request, and a successful next turn. Boundary/guard checks pass 33/33; threshold/consumer checks 116/116; provider-compaction ownership checks 23/23.
- The final local replay passes all 49 affected cases across the 12 files representing the eight reverted CI jobs, plus five nested reload scenarios. All four 32k prompt-cache cases pass unchanged. The first PR head's ten failed node jobs were treated as PR-caused: nominal-unit assembly and context labels were completed, prompt-only expectations and conflicting fixture mocks corrected, and the affected local replays pass (107 accounting cases, 174 additional consumers, and eight selected repair cases).
- Shared-fixture replays pass 245/245 across four suites and 319/319 across the cron harness consumers and real fallback suite. All six selected native ownership cases pass. Codex review of the complete change and final repair completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Live OpenAI production transport completed a tool continuation. Independent counts cover prose, code, dense hex, CJK, short-key JSON, and the complete prompt-cache request. JSON exposed an undercount (26,806 actual versus 16,389 projected); the regression now projects 30,605 and blocks a 20k window. The full prompt-cache control counts 13,974 versus 28,620 projected. This is bounded calibration, not a universal tokenizer guarantee or a live 1M compaction test. Anthropic validation was unavailable because the test account had insufficient credits.
- Five alternating pressure-owner benchmark pairs on 720 history messages plus 65k pending text: prose CPU 1.544→1.017 ms/op and sampled allocation 970,218→2,953 B/op; JSON CPU 1.214→0.978 ms/op and allocation 964,401→687,222 B/op. A/A median CPU drift was −0.54% (range −1.83% to +0.54%). These compare the existing estimator; enabling default admission adds approximately 1 ms of estimator CPU per request on this fixture. On a clean synthetic 40.286 GiB database with 5,000 session rows and 62,000 workspace files, publication performs exactly one keyed patch per request: median p50 1.983 ms, main-thread CPU 1.078 ms, sampled main-thread allocation 358,624 B/write. Session count and activity are preserved. Worker allocation was not measured; APFS does not prove btrfs behavior. The fixture has 227,312 events across 1,311 populated transcripts.
- The next CI head exposed four stale request-budget prices and two compaction failures caused by the summary fitter still using prose-only pricing. The shared-owner repair adds no production lines, preserves fixture windows, and passes all 49 affected cases across request budgets, small-context compaction, prepared prompts, and prompt-cache behavior. Core/normalization/safeguard tests pass 65/65; the 33 boundary checks pass again. Codex review, targeted lint, and types are green. Full changed-file checks pass for this repair. Exact-head PR CI remains the broad landing gate.

Runtime delta: +38 lines (349 added, 311 removed); regression/test-support delta: +412; reusable benchmark tooling: +412. Runtime growth supplies durable request-boundary publication and ordered settlement after deleting downstream repair machinery. All benchmark data is synthetic.

CI on the merged-main context also exposed an inherited browser import regression from #189973 (`31866655fd60`): `media-facts.ts` imports the Node-only transcript clone used by browser attachment/history views. All three UI-job signatures reproduce on exact CI main parent `c2a39e4c5a8166d1f5ea6703d1dfaa7d7c45de79`, including the nested mock error. This is a main regression requiring follow-up, not a passing check. The six failed UI E2E shards reproduce the same handled Navigation/app-start failure on that exact parent, including routes without console errors; modal details name `node:util/types.isProxy`. The final node-consumer repairs pass 41 gateway/announcement tests and all eleven message-buffer scenarios. The latter fixture now declares 32k after its request owner projected 22,180 against 16k, preserving output budget and behavioral assertions. Announcement fixtures also use their own temporary database instead of shared `/tmp` state; no shared database was modified. Final-head CI accounting remains in progress, and any inherited-only landing will retain the failed-check evidence.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep MCP App confirm previews surrogate-safe
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI MCP App confirm strip truncates `decision.text` with a raw UTF-16 `slice(0, 200)`. When an emoji straddles unit 200, the preview keeps a lone high surrogate and Chromium renders a replacement character next to the ellipsis.

Path: `ui/src/components/mcp-app-confirm-solid.tsx` (message and file confirms from App Bridge `sendMessage` / open-file).

Prior attempt: #167108 (closed without merge for missing Control UI evidence).

## User Impact

An MCP App that sends a long user message whose text has an emoji just past the 200-unit cap no longer shows a broken glyph in the “Send this message to the assistant?” preview.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route the display cap through the shared surrogate-safe helper `truncateUtf16Safe`, matching the existing Control UI pattern (`usage/view-details`, `session-run-terminal`, `draft-title`, …). The 200-unit contract and ellipsis stay the same; only the cut becomes code-point aligned.

## Evidence

### Reachability

`dispatchMcpAppMessage` builds the confirm preview from the full App message content (join of text/title blocks). The only wire bound is an 8 MiB JSON cap — no 200-unit pre-trim. A production App `sendMessage` with `199 × "a" + "🚀" + tail` therefore reaches this strip.

### Real Solid component before/after (same mounted `McpAppConfirmation`)

Input: `a×199 + 🚀 + b×40` (UTF-16 241, code points 240).

| | wellFormed | lone surrogate | utf16 length | tail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base `slice(0,200)` | false | true | 201 | `a a U+D83D U+2026` |
| fix `truncateUtf16Safe` | true | false | 200 | `a a a U+2026` |

Unit test (committed) is red on base / green with this fix: `keeps a boundary emoji whole in the truncated message preview`.

### Chromium before/after (product confirm CSS, same truncate contract)

Base:

![base](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/mcp-confirm-surrogate/evidence/mcp-confirm-surrogate/confirm-preview-base.png)

Fix:

![fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/mcp-confirm-surrogate/evidence/mcp-confirm-surrogate/confirm-preview-fix.png)

prs.title: fix(agents): accept whitespace-only oldText in edit tool calls
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
The edit parameter guard treats non-empty whitespace-only `oldText` as missing because it checks trimmed length. A unique existing whitespace span is rejected before the edit engine can perform a valid replacement.

## User Impact
An agent can collapse a unique run of blank lines or replace an exact whitespace span that the engine already supports. Empty oldText remains invalid, and ambiguous matches remain invalid.

## Why This Change Was Made
Check raw string length rather than trimmed length in the existing shared edit replacement guard. Keep structural argument validation at the guard and content matching/uniqueness with the existing edit engine.

**The tool JSON schema and description are unchanged.** No prompt, tool-name, path policy, permission or engine matching changes. The model-visible edit declaration captured from the actual provider requests is identical on both refs.

Fold the committed regression into the existing payload-preservation/path-cleaning case. It preserves whitespace oldText, raw newText and canonical path handling without adding a case or test seam. Remove the duplicate standalone case: production delta 0 and test delta 0, two files. Contributor commits are preserved.

## Evidence
Exact head `5be7d6cc8d528de991229a999df231b514daa1c1`; pinned main `c2a39e4c5a8166d1f5ea6703d1dfaa7d7c45de79`.

[Built Linux Gateway, scripted provider and real-file evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190039#issuecomment-6553377781).

A real built Gateway turn receives one scripted model `edit` call and returns its actual tool feedback to the provider. The host-workspace edit tool, guard, engine, filesystem and session persistence are real. Two independent files per case, per ref:

| Case | Main | Candidate |
|---|---|---|
| Unique non-empty whitespace span | Missing-edits error; unchanged file | Applied; exact requested bytes |
| Empty oldText | Refused; unchanged file | Refused; unchanged file |
| Ambiguous whitespace span | Refused; unchanged file | Uniqueness error; unchanged file |
| Normal unique text | Applied | Applied identically |

All 16 turns complete; outcome is established by the actual tool result and file bytes, not turn exit status. The complete advertised edit declaration has identical schema and description, SHA-256 `b1aae1ab4b8a1620170d3bed8ebf5ae737cd0c370d591102e50c1daf9484c41d`.

Candidate owner suite: 16 tests pass. The same consolidated regression on pinned main fails with the intended missing-edits error. Core build, targeted lint, formatting and whitespace pass.

Proof limits: Linux host-workspace tool, not a live sandbox run. Only provider responses are scripted; no real-provider/model-reasoning or UI claim.

## Merge Danger
Two-way door: reverting restores the whitespace-only refusal with no state migration. Blast radius is wrapped edit calls with non-empty whitespace-only oldText. Empty values, exact matching, uniqueness, overlap, fuzzy-boundary checks, path authorization and published tool contracts retain their existing owners and behavior.

prs.title: fix: reduce catalog and database read memory overhead
prs.body:
> **Do not merge — performance acceptance fails.** Head `a30b415ce3ac443a53c2156993bd57e998c214ae` passes CI and functional checks, but the five-pair comparison shows **sessions.list p99 +32.35%** and event-loop delay tail telemetry **+20.04%**. Both cross the unchanged 20% stop threshold. No merge is requested.

## What Problem This Solves

Catalog lookup loads standalone configuration schemas and system-event execution machinery when it only needs prepared inventory. Database reads also repeatedly scan SELECT bodies for mutation keywords, creating temporary allocations and falsely treating ignored SQL tails as writes.

## User Impact

Across five compiled baseline/candidate pairs, retained catalog-worker heap falls **96.205 → 79.593 MiB (−17.27%)**. Under eight-agent Gateway load, median peak process RSS falls only **3796.992 → 3702.832 MiB (−2.48%)**, while process CPU falls **2.68%**. The remaining approximately **3.62 GiB** peak is still substantial.

This branch is **not accepted for landing**: session-list p99 rises **105.351 → 139.432 ms (+32.35%)**, history median rises **14.86%**, and several other latency metrics worsen. These measurements compare the **whole branch** with the frozen baseline; they do not isolate the incremental RSS effect of the SELECT change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepared catalogs consume captured facts through shared AuthStorage/ModelRegistry implementations; standalone facades retain public identity and acquire config/source/environment readers before yielding. Narrow schema and runtime-snapshot imports avoid broad validation graphs. Model suppression reuses captured plugin metadata.

The plugin loader supplies its lazy system getter through a synchronous factory using the existing native resolver and captured cache owner. A stable compiled system entry preserves source/packaged loading and host-facade identity.

Native-prepared SELECT statements now skip mutation and transaction-control scans. Native execution observation stays in place, so callback writes still invalidate receipts. Batches, CTEs, PRAGMAs and writes retain their existing classification. This follows the [SQLite first-statement prepare contract](https://www.sqlite.org/c3ref/prepare.html), without a result cache or parser replacement.

Production/build net **+208 lines**, tests/support **+229**, metadata **0**, against the frozen baseline. The SELECT increment is **+3 production / +12 test lines**: it enforces the prepared-statement boundary while removing repeated scanning. Earlier growth establishes prepared/standalone and synchronous runtime ownership boundaries. No new cache, configuration/environment option, schema, protocol, or feature removal. Test-line allocations total **195 LF lines**; the additional 12 cover receipts, ignored SQL tails, callback writes and batch mutation.

## Evidence

### Current compiled comparison

[Completed five-pair run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_6980540522120a5d74e4d94c889687ff), direct AWS m7i.xlarge, observed 4 CPUs / 15.33 GiB RAM, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0. Both arms were independently built and run serially in B1,C1,…,B5,C5 order.

- Candidate carrier: `7ff30cd57a93ffb8423f0abc3585c4657fd5a22c`.
- Candidate tree: `ec8a6f7a7d09f6726057000dabe0ffae95b37ff3`, exactly matching published head `a30b415ce3a`.
- All 20 catalog/team processes completed 100 requests each. Ordered response hashes and counts match: catalog/configured/runtime rows **501/1/501**, or **2001/1/2001** for four providers.
- All ten Gateways launched, completed and verified **24 turns** each. Per run: **256 history, 100 updates, 64 each readiness/UI/session-list/load-subscription probes, 128 cron calls, four initial subscriptions and one fresh connection**. No failed requests, budget violations, early exits or unclean exits. Plugin metadata scans during load: **zero**.
- All **640 readiness responses were HTTP 200 but reported eventLoop.degraded=true**. Successful transport is not healthy event-loop qualification.
- Compiled catalog static closure: **1340 files / 15,168,434 bytes → 1055 / 11,310,978**. Checked broad config/protocol/system-execution boundaries are absent from the candidate closure.
- Catalog heap is measured after forced GC outside request timing. Whole-harness RSS includes the source controller. Gateway RSS covers all isolates and instrumentation. Main-heap endpoints vary with GC phase and are **not retained-memory savings**.
- This is isolated synthetic Linux proof, not deployment, ARM or constrained-device qualification.

An independent archive audit reproduced the numbers and functional counts. Session-list p99 equals the maximum of each run's 64 raw samples:

- [Current CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41271483871) is **fully green** at `a30b415ce3a`.

- Restoring the old classifier produces exactly **one failure / one pass / 46 skipped** in the selected regression. The ignored-tail SELECT increments the write receipt to 2 instead of preserving 1 at `src/infra/sqlite-schema-facts.test.ts:78`. Candidate bytes were restored and the source diff verified clean before measurement.
- Independent P0–P2 review of the SELECT increment found no actionable defect. A separate dependency/sibling audit confirms callback observation and unchanged batch/CTE/PRAGMA/control paths. This is source/contract review, not performance acceptance.
- [Corrected packaged/owner proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_af754c16e5c170e26ab71af1adc78a50): build, runtime-registry suite, core types and source/dist/missing-entry smoke pass. Scoped commands/event ordering, host identity and overrides survive broad materialization. Restoring the eager system import fails the intended boundary guard; source restored.
- [Corrected opaque-handle proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_bb2900a9334629bd5fd77ba0853873dd): four session-event tests pass; a module-local WeakMap makes cross-runtime redemption fail with the expected ownership error.

The earlier benchmark's focused-proof shell masked a stale call-count failure and invalid smoke/negative-control assertions. That aggregate-success claim is **retracted**; corrected runs above replace it. The earlier five-pair numerical observations were separate valid measurements, not correctness proof for this head.

### Allocation diagnosis

The separate completed CPU/heap captures in the packaged-owner run motivated the SELECT repair. Sampling includes collected objects: these are **allocations, not retained heap or a leak measurement**.

Three classifier stacks across transcript-worker profiles account for approximately **165 + 155 + 175 MiB**: unquoted-character scanning, whitespace normalization and mutation-keyword scanning under prepared snapshot reads. SQLite workers repeat that work. The SELECT fast path removes those scans at their owner. Its incremental allocation/RSS saving has not been isolated in a separate profile.

A few short-lived worker captures are incomplete, and main-thread heap polling misses some nested isolates. Worker heap sums are partial; process RSS is the aggregate measure. Traced timings do not replace untraced acceptance samples.

### Unchanged acceptance rule

Same isolated host/runtime, separately built arms, five serial alternating pairs, fresh state, recorded host load, cold/warm observations separated; report median, p95 and spread.

1. Compiled catalog: committed `scripts/perf/catalog-worker-retention-measure.ts`, `--built-worker`, five workspaces, 5000 remote rows, runtime plugin, 20 rounds; separate four-provider team case. Compare post-GC heap, first-request and warm latency.
2. Real isolated Gateway: committed `scripts/bench-gateway-concurrency.ts`, mock provider over real transport, 250 sessions, eight concurrent agents, three turns each, 20 history messages of 1024 characters, 64 probe rounds, 100 updates, two update clients, two history clients, four subscribers and control-plane probes; fresh process, zero warmups.
3. Profile separately, never substitute traced timings.

Acceptance requires measurable retained catalog-heap reduction and stable/improved user-facing metrics. Every worsening metric requires explicit owner acceptance; **a 20% move is a stop, never “within spread.”** Current session-list p99 and event-loop tail results fail that rule.

### Review follow-through and named follow-ups

The old ClawSweeper config-capture finding is repaired: standalone facades acquire their reader before the first await. That old review does not cover this head. Request one exact-head re-review once the performance hold is resolved; no prepare/merge request has been submitted.

- Catalog loader imports still reach the install-record writer/install barrel instead of the existing reader. Source-only counterfactual removes 44 modules with zero production LOC growth; unimplemented and unmeasured.
- Resident-worker limits are mostly per-pool and CPU-based. Transcript lanes can total 12 slots on four CPUs and nine on one/two CPUs; demand creation and idle retirement exist. No lifecycle leak or safe pool merger was established. Preserve writer/FIFO and native-settlement boundaries.
- History workers reach shared-state writer code through cron-store selection. A read-only selection kernel removes 19 modules in source-only analysis; unimplemented, no RSS claim.
- Non-SELECT prepared statements retain conservative full-input mutation classification. Evaluate their native compiled-statement boundary separately; this patch does not broaden their behavior.

Eager-system provenance: [runtime split](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/132716), followed by [session-event handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180079), both authored/merged by @steipete. Source edges are verified; historical RSS impact is not quantified.

prs.title: fix(doctor): 2026.10.10 update refuses when an imported audit archive lost its sanitized companion (backport #186998)
prs.body:
Related: #186974
Backport of #186998 (`4a0ab0928cc`) to `release/2026.10.10`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on 2026.10.10 betas, `openclaw doctor --fix`, and so an update, refuses at the `audit-logs` migration and blocks every later repair when an already-imported legacy config-audit archive is re-detected and its sanitized companion is gone.

## User Impact

User impact: a 2026.10.10 update on a host in that state finishes instead of refusing and rolling back. Real unimported records still refuse with the backup-restoration guidance, as on main.

## Why This Change Was Made

#186998 fixed this on main on 10-28, after `release/2026.10.10` was cut. It is not in beta.4, beta.5 or the branch tip `1cdcfc00d84`, by ancestry and by subject. The production change and docs here have the same patch-id as main's (`051fd155b6deec28`), and the release branch's two audit source files are identical to beta.4's, so they apply as is.

main refactored both audit test files after the cut. This keeps the release branch's `state-migrations.audit-logs.test.ts` and adds main's two missing-companion cases to `state-migrations.audit-skips.test.ts`. It also adds a case for the shape I hit (same bytes, size and mtime under a new file identity), and a Doctor-runner case for the other half of the rule: an unimported record with the companion gone still refuses.

## Evidence

- **Hit on a real 2026.10.10-beta.4 update on one of my macOS gateways (2026-10-31 04:07Z).** Doctor ran 434 s and exited 1:
  ```
  Failing check audit-logs (step-refused): Skipped config audit log recovery because its sanitized archive is missing or truncated
  Failing check managed-outgoing-images (blocked-by-prior-refusal): Migration step "managed-outgoing-images" was not run because prior step "audit-logs" refused execution.
  ```
  `apns-registrations`, `exec-approvals` and `mcp-oauth` were blocked the same way, and the update rolled back.
- **Cause, read-only on that host's state.** The raw-archive checkpoint (`migration.legacy-audit-raw`) records `dev 16777231, ino 19235396, size 478022, recordCount 0`. The file now reads `dev 16777230` with the same inode, size and mtime, and `config-audit.jsonl.migrated.sanitized` does not exist. Only the device number moved, so detection stopped matching and the step refused although nothing remained to import.
- The same production change on the same data: with #186998 carried onto beta.4 (same patch-id as this PR), doctor on that host logged `Skipped config audit log recovery because its sanitized companion is missing and no records remain to import; left ~/.openclaw/logs/config-audit.jsonl.migrated.raw in place.`, ran every later step, and the update finished with rc 0 at 07:30Z.
- Installed-package upgrade, latest stable (npm `openclaw@2026.10.9`, `8b18b55`) to this branch's build at `23e85739821`. Run with an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `--profile upgradeproof` and port 29789, and `doctor --fix --non-interactive` each time. No launchd label or LaunchAgent was added on the host.
  1. 2026.10.9 on a seeded legacy `logs/config-audit.jsonl` of 3 `config.write` records: exit 0, `Migrated config audit log -> shared SQLite state (3 new row(s))`. Afterwards the raw archive's sha256 is `f6cc44861440c55a…`, the checkpoint reads `ino 185071743, size 423, recordCount 0`, the `config-audit` history holds 5 rows (the 3 legacy rows hash to `ab40ca823113eea8…`), and `openclaw.json` hashes to `2ccd48ad6b26cc54…`.
  2. The raw archive is copied beside itself and renamed over (ino `185071743` -> `185071842`, same size and mtime_ns), and the sanitized companion is removed.
  3. 2026.10.9 again: exit 1. `audit-logs (step-refused): Skipped config audit log recovery because its sanitized archive is missing or truncated`, and `managed-outgoing-images`, `apns-registrations`, `exec-approvals` and `mcp-oauth` are blocked by the prior refusal.
  4. This branch on the same state: exit 0, `Skipped config audit log recovery because its sanitized companion is missing and no records remain to import; left <state>/logs/config-audit.jsonl.migrated.raw in place.`, and `Doctor complete.` A second run: exit 0, the same skip.
  5. After steps 3, 4 and 5, every value from step 1 is unchanged: the raw sha256, the checkpoint row, the 5 history rows with the same legacy hash, and the `openclaw.json` hash.
  6. This branch's `doctor --lint` over that state ran 39 checks. Its 3 findings are environment warnings (browser cookie import, a Codex route for the default model, no gateway auth token); none concern state or migrations.
- Tests on this branch at `23e85739821` (Node 26.12.1):
  - `pnpm test src/infra/state-migrations.audit-skips.test.ts src/infra/state-migrations.audit-logs.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 52 passed, 0 failed.
  - Control: with `state-migrations.audit-logs.ts` and `state-migrations.audit-sanitized.ts` reverted to the branch tip, 4 failed and 10 passed in `audit-skips`. The three skip cases get `outcome: "refused"` with `Skipped config audit log recovery because its sanitized archive is missing or truncated`, the message from the real host. prs.title: fix(ui): keep boot cache writes on schedule without Canvas
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189738

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes delayed warm-reload cache writes when a Gateway connects without a Canvas surface.

## User Impact

The sidebar boot cache keeps its original write deadline when no Canvas surface is advertised.

## Why This Change Was Made

An empty Canvas lease startup asynchronously republishes an unchanged Gateway snapshot, which restarts the pending boot-cache write. Skip that initial runtime load while retaining the existing path for removing an already loaded or loading lease. Regenerate the boot manifest from browser captures.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the existing deadline regression from [scheduled main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41269343462/job/124738772736): the cache was absent at 500 ms after an unrelated publication at 400 ms.
- The unchanged regression and focused boot, Canvas renewal, Gateway auth, observer, and plugin-capability suites pass: 121 tests on Node and 121 on pinned Bun.
- Cold and warm production-build browser captures pass for New Session and Chat, including warm reload. Comparing the same frozen base and candidate removes exactly one Canvas runtime chunk per route. Eight other regenerated module entries were already present in the base capture.
- UI typecheck, type-aware lint with compiler diagnostics, formatting, and the grouped UI build with boot-size budgets pass.

- Fresh local ClawSweeper review of the committed range: no findings; security cleared.

prs.title: fix(cli): show the reason for invalid numeric flag values
prs.body:
Fixes #189962

## What Problem This Solves

Invalid values for numeric CLI flags (`logs --limit/--max-bytes/--interval`, `devices list --timeout`, `channels status --timeout`, `models status --probe-timeout`) fail with only the generic "The CLI command failed." The real reason is visible only with `OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1`.

## User Impact

Users who mistype a number now see which flag was wrong and what value is expected, e.g. `--limit must be a positive integer.`, matching how `tui --history-limit` already behaves. Exit code stays 1.

## Why

The shared parsers threw plain `Error`s, which the root failure renderer hides. They now throw `ExpectedCliError` (via `throwExpectedCliError`), which the renderer prints. Changed: `parseOptionalPositiveInteger` (`src/cli/parse-positive-integer.ts`), `invalidTimeout` (`src/cli/parse-timeout.ts`), and the models `--probe-timeout` parser, kept private inside `src/commands/models/list.status-command.ts`. Messages are unchanged.

Credit to @obviyus for e67ba461ee5 / 0e5bbe7e678: `ExpectedCliError` now lives in the lightweight `src/cli/expected-cli-error.ts` so parsers don't import the heavy `failure-output.ts` (keeps `check-cli-bootstrap-imports` happy), the probe parser was inlined, and the tests were folded into the existing suites. 208dbb90535 updates `register.status-health-sessions.test.ts`, whose old expectation (runtime.error + exit) predates the error now propagating to the root renderer; that was the red `checks-node-changed-compact-large-7` shard.

## Evidence

@obviyus's built-CLI comparison above (secretless Linux arm64 Docker, Node 24.22.1, 24 runs): main printed the generic error every time, the candidate printed the flag reason.

Independent capture: built CLI via `node openclaw.mjs`, isolated HOME, Linux x64, Node v24.22.1.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): keep cached Details progress until live facts differ
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload with cached Details can turn the saved progress activity label into a disconnected warning, then turn it back after reconnect, even though the progress facts have not changed. The saved plan remains present throughout this unnecessary presentation swap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record the progress display inputs and their card revision/update time in the existing scoped browser snapshot. Keep matching cached presentation until the live progress read and the own-parent/hydrated-child read settle, including settled optional-child failure. Reuse one loaded-subagent predicate in Progress and Background. The desktop composition keeps its existing lazy boundary.

## User Impact

Previously loaded desktop Progress keeps its runtime presentation through reconnect and updates in place when fresh facts differ. Actions retain live authority. Cold loading keeps its existing loading presentation. This change adds no product configuration, store, server schema, or Gateway protocol.

## Evidence

**Final-head validation in progress:** current PR head is `563e0ea492748d313912259b93517c46022605f8`, rebased onto `042ad2da5f2e5a83ab03a748fd9ac607bc7fd491`. The previous head exposed a type-only import cycle; the existing snapshot patch alias now lives in its schema owner, with every consumer migrated. The discarded preload also left a stale generated boot-manifest hunk after rebase; it has been removed by preserving the exact canonical base artifact. The current 15-file diff has no boot-manifest or route-level preload change. Fresh performance and final-head validation are running. Measurements below remain explicitly historical at `119beb720cdf` / `c11a330ba232`; the interrupted 67-file full-UI checkpoint does not count as a completed suite.

Candidate `119beb720cdffe92afc377fc69818aadf84e894d`, main baseline `c11a330ba2321370909d90fef752e294584c7337`. All interleaved comparisons below ran on one AWS `c7a.4xlarge`, lease `cbx_45885e08ff59`, with repository Chromium. Native A/B and A/A host samples were 92.46% and 93.25% idle. Native and Team fixtures are distinct; their samples are not pooled. Each route has 11 A/B pairs and 11 A/A pairs. Timings from held transport or CPU/layer diagnostics are excluded.

### Cached Progress behavioral result

Eleven interleaved chat pairs hold only the owning synthetic admission proxy's authenticated viewer upgrade until cached Progress is visible. Before/after screenshot receipts retain null hello and an unreleased hold. Each screenshot has new-loader/FCP/compositor evidence and differs from the old-page surface. The original Gateway connection then resumes unchanged. All 44 original Progress crops were byte-compared with four inspected complete-content representatives; the full plan and all three steps are visible before hello and at final.

The strict whole-card DOM-text witness improves from **0/11 stable baseline reloads to 10/11 candidate reloads**. Runtime label/plan/step presentation stays unchanged in **11/11 candidate reloads**; baseline runtime changes in all 11. Candidate pair 1 changes only the closed refresh tooltip from “Updated 1m ago” to “Updated 2m ago”; that change remains counted. prs.title: fix(codex): project native child hook diagnostics
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: synchronous Codex hook notifications emitted for an owned native child are dropped because the foreground projector only accepts its own thread and the native child monitor does not admit hook notification methods.

## User Impact

Operators and trajectory consumers can observe SubagentStart and SubagentStop hook runs for an already-owned native child under the child canonical native run identity, including while a follow-up native turn is pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native child monitor now admits hook/started and hook/completed, routes only notifications whose thread is an already-registered child, and sends them through the existing hook payload projector. Pending turns no longer hide the current child from hook observation, while turn completion handling remains unchanged. Hook observations remain diagnostic events; they do not create ownership, change child lifecycle, or participate in completion delivery. The projector now accepts the narrowed hook-method union directly, satisfying the assertion-safety ratchet.

## Evidence

- corepack pnpm exec vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-notification.test.ts --config vitest.config.ts - 41 tests passed, including a registered-monitor pending-turn routing regression.

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.

prs.title: fix(litellm): allow single-image Gemini edits
prs.body:
Supersedes #169129, thanks @LiuwqGit. Thanks also @obviyus for the edit-only scope and earlier boundary evidence.
Related: #169120.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes single-image Gemini edits through LiteLLM failing with HTTP 400 `UnsupportedParamsError` because OpenClaw always sends `n=1`.

## User Impact

Default and explicit count=1 image edits omit `n`; callers requesting multiple outputs retain their count and normal backend errors. Generation behavior is unchanged. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing LiteLLM multipart edit builder now sends `n` only for counts greater than one. LiteLLM's [Gemini edit adapter](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/60fc121ce8ab995cb2997e0bbd0a980ee93c627d/litellm/llms/vertex_ai/image_edit/vertex_gemini_transformation.py#L51) supports `size` but excludes `n`; its [parameter validator](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/60fc121ce8ab995cb2997e0bbd0a980ee93c627d/litellm/images/utils.py#L37) rejects unsupported supplied parameters. There is no global parameter dropping or model-name special case.

Production delta: **+4/-4, net 0**. The existing multipart explanation is consolidated into one comment covering the upload and Gemini constraints. There is no new helper or state owner. Test growth is **11 lines**, with a scoped allocation for the distinct default/explicit edit-count regressions and unchanged generation-count control; existing upload assertions and scaffolding are reused.

## Evidence

- Main `042ad2da5f2e5a83ab03a748fd9ac607bc7fd491` unconditionally sends multipart `n`. Landed #190058 (`a460b0c1ead257e25296b586b3ad6d46bf47ab81`) changes OpenAI geometry, and #189830 (`c43e20b17d563b059a620c2d25ff3713897537b2`) changes returned image reporting; neither repairs LiteLLM edit counts.
- Before production edits, the expanded provider suite failed **3 cases**, with **18 passing**: omitted count with one/two references and explicit count=1 all received `"1"` where the expected multipart field was absent. Explicit count=2 and generation controls already passed. Command wall time: 41.70 s, dominated by first-run worker compilation.
- After repair, `timeout 90 nice -n 10 pnpm test extensions/litellm/image-generation-provider.test.ts extensions/litellm/image-generation-provider.url.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed **30 tests across two files** in **12.50 s command wall time** (10.60 s Vitest). This covers the production provider's request assembly, reference uploads, URL output handling, credentials, and deadlines. The successful CI shard reports 0.095 s of provider case time and 1.176 s of URL-suite case time; those are summed test-case times, not standalone command wall times.
- Narrow TypeScript check for the changed files and their import closure, changed-file lint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. The temporary typecheck config includes the repository's ambient declarations.
- AutoReview: Codex, P0–P2, complete local candidate against the main commit above, **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. Supplied unchanged context includes the shared image-provider owner and LiteLLM URL suite. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; its hosted review was automatically queued for this head. AutoReview supplies the completed independent review.
- Contributor source was read only with `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff`; it was **never checked out or executed**. This implementation and its tests were written on the task branch from main. Both human commit authors are credited in the commit.
- Proof limits: request-boundary tests and current upstream source inspection establish the parameter contract. No paid Gemini API call, real LiteLLM proxy run, live Gateway operation, or Team deployment was performed. Earlier contributor fixture evidence is not presented as a live Gemini result. LiteLLM's own contributor instructions do not govern changes in this repository.

Exact-head [CI run 41272434425](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41272434425) succeeded in 452 s elapsed, and [Security Review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41272434672) passed. Merged as `bf87b5cedbea6e684f564386111a69dfda42034c`; both human co-author trailers were verified on the landed commit.

prs.title: fix(ci): check hidden sources in database worker ratchet
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The database-worker CI ratchet skips hidden current-source files, inherits developer ripgrep settings, and can repeat a full historical analysis even when the compared source tree is unchanged.

## User Impact

CI checks hidden credential writers and database boundaries consistently. Current sources retain nonignored untracked files; staged and historical reads stay Git-backed. Runtime configuration and product behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The source-discovery owner now explicitly disables ripgrep configuration, includes hidden files, uses portable slash-separated keys, and preserves producer source traversal order. Strict snapshot equality and fresh current-tree validation remain unchanged.

On the frozen repository, default ripgrep missed three tracked xai boundary declarations: 22,271 current files versus 22,274 historical files. That mismatch defeated identical-snapshot reuse. This repairs discovery rather than weakening equality or adding another cache. It does not make ripgrep and Git identical for tracked-but-ignored files, symlinks, or global ignore rules.

Removed paths: ambient-config-dependent enumeration and platform-dependent path keys. Net production delta against frozen base: +5 lines; tests: +73 lines. The production growth expresses the source-membership and portable-key contract.

## Evidence

Current candidate: 2e04a4506358d13573a0ada8a30cb82421f8cc29. The revised candidate bytes passed 226 focused tests, targeted production/test oxlint and pinned formatting. Independent owner-boundary and v3-registration reviews are clean. Exact-head CI is green on the new revision ([CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40478008697)); this does not clear the failed performance qualification. The separately registered v3 workload stopped after its first block on warm wall time; timing qualification failed. No completed-distribution claim is made.

The previous 2d740836 candidate also sorted source-map insertion order, which affects compiler project traversal. This revision removes that unneeded ordering expansion from current, staged and historical discovery; existing final inventory-row ordering remains. Snapshot reuse already compares complete membership and text independently of insertion order. A reversed-insertion regression proves equal rows and historical reuse while fresh invalid current sources still fail. Removing this confound is not a proven explanation or fix for the measured v2 CPU regression. Its stopped outcome remains below, unmodified.

With the new regression tests against the old discovery implementation, exactly three selected tests failed as expected: hostile ripgrep settings produced an invalid source path; hidden membership forced an extra historical analysis; and a hidden invalid current credential writer escaped validation despite a warm baseline. The fixture was restored after this reproduction.

Tests cover matching current/staged/historical path/text membership, hidden and ordinary untracked files, ignored generated files, hidden and ordinary content/add/delete/rename changes, cache invalidation, and fresh current/staged credential diagnostics.

The previous alias/type-query optimization was fully reverted from this final diff. Its first matched block breached the preregistered stop rule: warm candidate 65.699s versus baseline 44.190s (+48.7%). Four completed samples do not establish a distribution or a speedup. This PR makes no compiler-query optimization claim.

### V2 performance acceptance registered before the stopped discovery benchmark

- Real committed workload: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-database-worker-ratchet.mts --base 2d740836b9caabb01d751c0c592d6dc768571fb3 --no-merge-base`, on one clean checkout and frozen installed compiler.
- A proof-only Node load hook selects frozen-base or candidate discovery implementation without changing disk source bytes. Record and verify loaded digests. The three hidden-file membership differences are intentional repaired inputs and must be reported explicitly.
- Five counterbalanced serial blocks per variant, with cold and warm conditions separate. Cold starts with empty isolated artifact cache/output; warm uses the immediately preceding variant's direct baseline cache. Node compile cache disabled; fixed Node 4 GiB / Go 8 GiB limits and four Go CPUs. Record host load, elapsed time, process-tree CPU and sampled peak RSS.
- Require identical complete inventory row hashes and verdicts; candidate current/historical source maps must match exactly. Cold unchanged-tree analysis count should fall from two to one; every warm run must still analyze current sources. Changed-source and negative-writer fixtures must retain their diagnostics.
- Report median, empirical p95, range and all failures. Profile separately from latency samples. Any measured 20% regression stops performance qualification; no timing gain will be claimed from an interrupted sample set.

The first discovery benchmark was stopped after six successful old-head runs and one interrupted baseline run to apply that CI fix. Those old-head samples are excluded from the final-head results below.


### Previous head 2d740836: v2 stopped, timing not qualified

Four complete counterbalanced blocks produced 16 valid runs. The controller stopped before block five because block four warm user CPU rose from 71.021728s to 92.265093s (+29.91%), above the registered 20% limit. The threshold was not changed and the unchanged experiment was not rerun.

| Block four warm metric | Baseline | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Wall seconds | 80.323454 | 85.190104 | +6.06% |
| User CPU seconds | 71.021728 | 92.265093 | +29.91% — stop |
| System CPU seconds | 25.386205 | 15.716195 | -38.09% |
| Sampled process-tree peak RSS bytes | 10969628672 | 10799742976 | -1.55% |
| Largest-child peak RSS bytes | 6463127552 | 6387171328 | -1.18% |

Candidate one-minute host load rose 8.99 to 15.15; the matching baseline started at 13.65 and ended at 15.19. These observations do not establish whether the measured CPU regression is caused by host contention or the candidate. The registered qualification failed. No numeric CI-minute, cash-saving, memory-leak or completed timing-distribution claim follows from these samples.

All 16 runs exited successfully with identical complete inventory row SHA-256 `634074da18367f013d611d1bbc17ea1c1269ef7abfbfb4b1013a005458695eca` and unchanged verdict (168 T1; 15 deprecated-only compatibility calls). Candidate current and historical source paths and bytes matched exactly. The old current-source enumeration omitted the three tracked hidden declarations. Every cold baseline performed two inventories; every cold candidate performed one. Every warm variant still performed one fresh current inventory and reused only the direct baseline cache. Loaded implementation digests, common source bytes, cold/warm cache contracts and sampled RSS were asserted. The exact native checkout remained tracked-clean at the reviewed head.

<details>
<summary>Individual completed observations; four paired blocks, incomplete experiment</summary>

No distribution summary is reported: the registered five samples per variant/condition were not completed. Each cell lists the individual observed wall seconds / user CPU seconds / system CPU seconds / sampled process-tree peak RSS bytes. All 16 completed runs are included.

</details>

### V3 acceptance registered before execution

This is a new source revision and separately registered experiment. It uses the same actual ratchet workload, frozen-base implementation, installed compiler, five counterbalanced serial blocks (20 runs), isolated cold/warm caches, runtime limits, process-tree sampling and unchanged 20% guards on paired wall time, user CPU, system CPU and sampled peak RSS. The exact committed candidate HEAD and loaded implementation digests must match before execution; the controller rejects the stopped 2d740836 head. Candidate current/historical canonical path/text hashes and membership must agree; actual insertion order is recorded diagnostically without requiring equality. Complete inventory row hashes/verdicts, current validation and cache call-count contracts remain hard assertions. V2 and v3 samples are not pooled. No distribution summary is reported before all five observations per variant/condition complete. Any guard breach stops qualification without changing limits or rerunning the unchanged candidate. No timing or cash-saving claim follows from a stopped qualification.


### Current head 2e04a450: v3 stopped, timing not qualified

The controller stopped after the first complete block (four of 20 registered runs). Warm wall time exceeded the unchanged 20% guard. Warm system CPU also exceeded its guard; execution stopped at the first checked breach. The unchanged candidate was not rerun, and no thresholds were changed. One observation per variant/condition does not establish a distribution.

These observations do not establish the cause of either regression or clear the failed qualification. Preserving producer traversal order removed the prior code confound, but did not establish acceptable warm performance. This CI-cost proposal is deferred and remains on hold. Hidden-source parity and independence from ambient ripgrep settings remain a named correctness follow-up on this PR. The cold two-to-one reduction applies only when complete snapshots are equal; source-changing comparisons still need two analyses. No further profiling, speculative cache/sort patch, or unchanged rerun is scheduled.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw plugins inspect` and its `info` alias report not-found for manifest legacy IDs and case variants already accepted by other plugin commands. For bundled FishAudio, `fish-audio` and `Fish-Audio-Speech` fail even though the canonical `fish-audio-speech` exists.

## User Impact

Diagnostic inspection can now find that plugin through its legacy or case-canonical identity. Exact ID remains first priority, followed by exact display name; normalization is only the final lookup fallback. Unknown IDs still fail.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the already-loaded metadata normalizer and existing plugin-ID normalizer at the existing inspection selector. No second alias table, runtime activation, install/config write, new flag or policy. @yetval's contributor commit is preserved unchanged in production.

Consolidated regression into the existing runtime-inspect fixture, retaining exact ID/name precedence and dependency-repair assertions while adding case and legacy selectors. Whole-change delta: production+4/-1, tests+11/-12(net-1), docs+2; no test allocation increase.

## Evidence

Independent built Linux Node24.22.1 CLI in secretless Docker, real bundled FishAudio manifest, isolated explicit profiles/config/state/workspaces. Twice each on main, inspect/info legacy and case queries exit1/not-found; twice each on candidate they exit0 and return canonical fish-audio-speech from the built bundled source.

Exact ID and display-name controls succeed on both refs; unknown ID still errors. Real local manifest collision controls confirm exact legacy-looking IDs and case-looking display names retain priority over canonical fallback. Main regression:1failure/12passes; candidate13passed. Targeted lint/format pass. [Independent captured CLI evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190022#issuecomment-6553299185).

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores missing diagnostic lookups; no migration or state writes. Blast radius is target selection for plugins inspect/info only. Exact ID/name ordering, runtime acquisition, activation/config policy and unknown-ID refusal remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix(litellm): image edits fail for Gemini models because n is always sent
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #169120

## What Problem This Solves

Single-image edits through the bundled LiteLLM provider always send multipart `n=1`. LiteLLM's Gemini edit backend rejects that explicit unsupported parameter with HTTP 400 `UnsupportedParamsError`, even though omitting `n` already means one output image.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the LiteLLM **edit** request builder changes: include `n` when `count > 1`, otherwise use the endpoint's existing single-image default. Multi-image edits retain their requested count and normal error handling. No global `drop_params`, new retry, model-name special case, or transport change.

The contributor's commit is preserved. A follow-up narrowing commit restores the original generation builder and its default-count assertion. **Image generation is unchanged**, including JSON `n: 1` for a single generated image. The issue reports that generation already works; changing that behavior is unnecessary.

## User Impact

Single-image Gemini edits no longer fail solely because OpenClaw supplies redundant `n=1`. Explicit multi-image requests still send their count rather than silently dropping an unsupported parameter. Other providers and generation requests retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

Current integrated head `401c2aad24c67e9c53aa098d47821341dadba1b2` merges current main `a7fe06b17a966`. The reported conflict was only in the provider test file: upstream’s consolidated layout is retained, with default-edit omission, explicit multi-image count, and generation count=1/count=2 assertions preserved. The production provider is byte-identical to proven `d91502a7840fb0c8a3767a281de3af3ffc74bae0`, so the linked Gateway A/B evidence carries; this integration does not add a real-provider claim. Fresh isolated frozen install, changed-file format check, and provider suite pass **20/20**. Current delta: production **+5/-1**, tests **+13/-5**.

[Built-Gateway A/B multipart captures and output receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169129#issuecomment-6432278843), comparing pinned main `ce503a58dad3b06cfba1cc357bab3e5a0435f024` with narrowed candidate `d91502a7840fb0c8a3767a281de3af3ffc74bae0`:

- Fresh isolated Linux `node:24.22.1` containers installed frozen dependencies and passed supported `pnpm build:runtime`. The runtime artifact contains the final production change; the final amendment only consolidated tests.
- The shipped agent command dispatches to the built Gateway, whose real `image_generate` tool runs the LiteLLM provider against a local LiteLLM-compatible HTTP fixture. It receives a real PNG file part. The fixture models the reported Gemini contract: reject explicit edit `n` with HTTP 400 `UnsupportedParamsError`; accept omission and return a known valid PNG.
- **Main twice:** default count and explicit count=1 each send multipart `n=1`, receive HTTP 400, and persist no output PNG.
- **Candidate twice:** the same default/explicit-one operations omit `n`, receive HTTP 200, and persist one PNG each. Shipped image metadata decoding reads both as 1×1 PNGs, 68 bytes each.
- **Controls on both refs:** shipped `infer image edit` with non-Gemini `gpt-image-2`, count=2 sends `n=2` and writes two PNGs. `infer image generate` with the Gemini route, count=1 still sends JSON `n: 1` and writes one PNG. Generation behavior is unchanged.
- Gateway image work is asynchronous: the first agent turn acknowledges task admission. The recorded failure/success is the actual provider operation and persisted artifact, not a claim that this initial acknowledgement failed.
- Before integration, candidate provider tests passed **10/10** and changed-file format checks pass. The strengthened existing default-edit multipart regression fails on main exactly at `form.has("n")` (true versus expected false) and passes with the fix. Default omission is consolidated into the existing multipart test; explicit multi-image count remains a distinct regression.
- Simplification retains one request builder and adds no helper/state owner. That pre-integration delta was production **+5/-1**, tests **+20/-0**; current integrated totals are listed above.

Earlier contributor evidence exercised the public CLI and a real LiteLLM 1.105.0 proxy with stubbed Vertex AI. That remains earlier-head evidence, not a real Gemini API run. This new run proves the narrowed production path through a built Gateway but also uses local model/provider fixtures.

**Outstanding proof prerequisite:** the [previous review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169129#issuecomment-6109716373) explicitly requests an actual Gemini image returned through LiteLLM because the dependency's AGENTS.md requires real provider APIs. No Gemini credentials are available to this proof lane. The known PNG above is fixture output, not real Gemini output, and does not satisfy that requirement if it remains applicable.

## Not fixed here

Generation is intentionally unchanged. This does not enable Gemini multi-image counts, globally discard unsupported parameters, prove semantic image-edit quality, or establish real Gemini deployment behavior. Unsupported explicit multi-image parameters still surface their normal errors.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting restores explicit `n=1` on single-image LiteLLM edits; no schema/config migration or durable-state change. Blast radius is LiteLLM multipart image edits. Generation and other providers are untouched.

prs.title: fix: keep unfinished CI gate statuses pending
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Security Review can publish a durable failed `openclaw/ci-gate` status when GitHub reports the parent CI run as completed but its unique gate job is still in a recognized unfinished state.

## User Impact

Maintainers now see that inconsistent snapshot remain pending until the existing reconciliation path observes the gate's real terminal result. Merging remains blocked while the job is unfinished. Completed failures, skipped or cancelled jobs, contradictory conclusions, malformed or unknown states, missing or duplicate gates, and API or identity failures continue to block.

## Why This Change Was Made

The publisher already refreshes and revalidates the exact CI run, head, repository, branch, and attempt after reading its jobs. Its final classifier, however, treated every unique gate other than `completed/success` as failure. This change shares the existing recognized unfinished-status vocabulary between run and job classification, maps only a unique unfinished gate with a null conclusion to pending, and leaves success restricted to a unique completed-success gate. The existing scheduled reconciler already re-evaluates pending results, so no workflow, polling, permission, or dependency change is needed.

## Evidence

The existing CLI-level fixture reproduced the defect on the base revision: a completed parent with one `in_progress`/null gate produced `pending → failure` instead of `pending → pending`. On the corrected exact tree:

- changed-file formatting and lint passed;
- the selected scripts and test-root-scripts type graphs passed; and
- the complete Security Review owner suite passed 188/188, including all five recognized unfinished states, completed success, and the nearest contradictory, malformed, missing, duplicate, failed, skipped, and cancelled controls.

The original historical attempt-jobs response was not retained, so this proves the source-deterministic classification defect and its correction rather than reconstructing that payload byte for byte. Hosted CI and required exact-head reviews remain pending at initial publication.

prs.title: fix(ai): validate local tool input against the canonical schema
prs.body:
Closes #185534

## What Problem This Solves

On Gemini-routed sessions, Code Mode / Tool Search rejected a valid `read({ path, optional: true })` call with `optional: must be equal to "true"`, even though `optional` is declared as boolean `true`. The documented call now succeeds and returns the structured `not_found` result.

- Problem: the Gemini wire projection stringifies `enum`/`const` values (`const: true` → `enum: ["true"]`) while keeping `type: "boolean"`. Catalog dispatch validated local arguments against that model-facing projection, so the schema became unsatisfiable: `true` violates the string enum and `"true"` violates the boolean type.
- Solution: retain the provider-neutral schema that produced each projection and bind it as the tool's execution schema. Catalog dispatch already resolves execution schemas, so local validation now uses the canonical contract while the model still receives the Gemini-compatible projection.
- What changed: `packages/ai/.../agent-tools-parameter-schema.ts` retains the canonical schema; `agent-tools.finalize.ts` binds it as the execution schema; `agent-tool-availability.ts` fills only missing execution schemas.
- What did NOT change: the model-facing schema, Gemini's stringified enums, and owner-declared execution schemas (exec/bash) are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The projection is a wire-format workaround (#104567), not the tool's input contract; validating local arguments against it was the regression.

- Best fix: separate the canonical execution contract from the provider projection at finalization, so every affected literal is covered instead of widening `read.optional` alone.
- Alternative: dropping the enum for non-string types (changes the Gemini projection and #104567's behavior) or retyping the schema to string (breaks the tool handler that expects a boolean).
- Risk / non-goals: only routes with a lossy projection bind an execution schema, and an execution schema declared by the tool owner always wins.

## User Impact

Gemini + Code Mode / Tool Search users can call `read` with `optional: true` and get `kind: "not_found"` for missing paths instead of an input-contract error. No config or API changes.

## Evidence

Observed result at head `7f7436c6d`, using the real `read` tool, the real finalization pass with `modelProvider: "google"`, and the real catalog dispatcher against a temp workspace:

```text
model-facing read.optional: {"type":"boolean","enum":["true"],"description":"Missing paths return structured not_found instead of failing."}
execution read.optional:   {"type":"boolean","const":true,"description":"Missing paths return structured not_found instead of failing."}
read(missing, optional=true): OK details={"kind":"not_found","status":"not_found","path":"does-not-exist.txt","optional":true}
read(present.txt): OK details={"kind":"text","content":"hello from openclaw\n"}
read(optional=true, no path): ERROR Invalid arguments for tool "openclaw:core:read": path: must have required property 'path'; received undefined (undefined). Expected input: { path: string; ...; optional?: true }.
```

Before, with the three source files reverted to upstream main (`15c2e6838`) on the same head:

```text
execution read.optional:   {"type":"boolean","enum":["true"],...}
read(missing, optional=true): ERROR Invalid arguments for tool "openclaw:core:read": optional: must be equal to one of the allowed values (allowed: "true"); received true (boolean). Expected input: { ...; optional?: "true" }.
```

The last after-fix line is the control: real validation is still active, and calls that genuinely violate the contract are rejected.

Focused tests:

- `packages/ai/src/providers/agent-tools-parameter-schema.test.ts` — 38 passed (canonical retained behind Gemini and stripped-keyword projections; absent for lossless providers).
- `src/agents/agent-tools.finalize.test.ts` — canonical bound for Google routes; owner-declared execution schema still wins.
- `src/agents/tool-search-runtime.test.ts` — new regression: a Gemini-routed catalog accepts `read({ path, optional: true })` through the canonical contract.
- Red check: with the production files reverted, both new regression tests fail; they pass on this head.

Not tested: a live Gemini API request (no provider credentials in this environment). The Gemini projection itself is unchanged and remains covered by the existing `cleanSchemaForGemini` tests.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep, git diff, and `node --import tsx` to analyze issue #185534, locate the projection/validation split in `agent-tools.finalize.ts`, and implement the fix. The implementer understands the code: provider projections stay model-facing, while local dispatch validates the canonical schema retained at finalization. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix: existing device folders stay disabled for models on the default runtime
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: New Session disables "Existing folder" on a paired device when the selected model runs on the default OpenClaw runtime but has no runtime set in config (for example `particle/particle-ai/particle-1`, xAI, OpenRouter or GitHub Copilot models).

## User Impact

User impact: models that run on the built-in OpenClaw runtime can start sessions in an existing folder on a paired device, whether or not their runtime is set in config. Starting a chat from provider setup, and switching New Session back from a hosted environment, no longer save the Gateway's default runtime as a session-level runtime choice.

## Why This Change Was Made

`models.list` left out `agentRuntime` on a row when the Gateway resolved it to the implicit OpenClaw runtime. Each client had to know that a missing field meant OpenClaw. New Session read the missing field as "unknown runtime" and disabled existing device folders. The Gateway then accepted the same request, because dispatch resolves the runtime itself.

Every row now states its resolved runtime. For the default case this is `{ id: "openclaw", source: "implicit" }`, with its placement facts. The `implicit` source already exists in the protocol schema, so the wire contract does not change. Only the value is filled in more often.

Two UI paths used "the row has a runtime" to mean "send this runtime to `sessions.create`": Start Chat after provider sign-in, and New Session's "back to host" choice. Both now skip a runtime whose source is `implicit`, through one helper (`selectableRuntimeId`), so they keep sending nothing for the Gateway's own routing.

<details>
<summary>Consumer audit</summary>

I checked every reader of a row's `agentRuntime` in the Control UI, CLI, TUI, iOS/macOS (`OpenClawKit`) and Android.

- **Fixed:** the existing device folder gate; `resolveModelRuntimeEntry` for sessions on `openclaw`; fast-mode and access-program lookups; picker highlighting of the base row for sessions on `openclaw`.
- **Unchanged:** picker labels and Android runtime names are gated on `source` `model`/`provider`. A click on the base picker row still sends no runtime.
- **Changed and intended:**
  - Thinking-profile matching in the web UI, `ChatSessions.swift` and `ChatController.kt` no longer lets a session on another runtime (for example `codex`) borrow the OpenClaw row's thinking levels. This matches the existing "must not supply another runtime's profile" rule.
  - A model's base row with `runtimeChoices` now shows its "OpenClaw" runtime label.

</details>

## Evidence

- New regression tests. Each fails on `main` and passes on this branch:
  - `models-list-result.service-tiers.test.ts`: a model without a configured runtime states `openclaw` / `implicit` / `worker-turn`. On `main` the field is missing.
  - `model-providers-page.login-start-chat.test.ts`: Start Chat for a row with an implicit runtime creates the session without `agentRuntime`.
  - `hosted-environment.test.ts`: going back to host with an implicit base runtime leaves no runtime choice, and still resolves to `openclaw`.
- I updated the existing `models.list` row expectations to include the stated runtime, reusing the shared `EXPECTED_IMPLICIT_OPENCLAW_RUNTIME` fixture.
- Focused local runs: Gateway `models*` suites, `ui/src/pages/new-session`, `ui/src/pages/model-providers`, `ui/src/pages/model-setup`, `ui/src/pages/chat` and `ui/src/lib` all pass.
- Production trace: on a live Gateway, `models.list` returned no `agentRuntime` for all `particle` rows. The `openclaw` runtime advertised `cloudPlacementExecutionMode: "worker-turn"`. New Session showed "Existing device folders require a worker-turn runtime" for Particle-1 on a paired device.
- Live Gateway: a user-authorized Gateway ran this commit (`5084ccfe`, supported source updater, downtime 262 s). `models.list` returned `agentRuntime` on all 97 model rows, and Particle-1 reported `openclaw` / `implicit` / `worker-turn`.

Before (stock main, Particle-1 on paired device `mbp-m5`): "Existing folder" is disabled with "Existing device folders require a worker-turn runtime".

![Before: Existing folder disabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f9d624c3-8ec1-4bd9-a023-e788af251ba0)

After (this branch, same device and model): "Existing folder on device" is enabled, and "Browse folders on mbp-m5" appears.

![After: Existing folder enabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/08d20f63-9a9a-462f-b198-5d28ecbeb6f3)

**Merge danger:** two-way door. A revert fully undoes it: no state, config or schema writes. Blast radius: every `models.list` client gets a filled `agentRuntime` on rows that used to leave it out. A client that treated "has `agentRuntime`" as "explicitly pinned" would change behavior. The audit found two such clients (both fixed here) and none in the native apps.
