prs.title: fix(daemon): use monotonic clock for scheduled task settlement deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, stopping or updating the Gateway can hang or bail out early when the system clock is adjusted: the scheduled-task settlement probe computes its deadline and remaining budget from `Date.now()` (wall clock) while the PowerShell probe's `spawnSync` timeout and the poll `sleep` are monotonic timers. A clock jump forward shrinks the probe timeout (a 280s budget collapsed to 50s, or 1ms past a 330s roll), killing PowerShell before settlement can be observed; a clock jump backward keeps the wall-clock deadline from ever elapsing, so the loop never exits. The fix uses a monotonic clock (`performance.now()`) for the deadline and remaining budget, matching the sibling `isScheduledTaskDefinitionAbsent` in the same file.

- Problem: `prepareScheduledTaskSettlement` seeds its deadline and reads the remaining budget from the wall clock (`Date.now()`), while the consuming `spawnSync` timeout and `sleep` poll are monotonic timers — a cross-clock-domain budget.
- Solution: compute `deadline`, `remaining`, and the exit comparisons with `performance.now()` so the budget lives entirely on the monotonic clock.
- What changed: all six `Date.now()` usages inside `prepareScheduledTaskSettlement` in `src/daemon/schtasks-state-probe.ts` became `performance.now()`, plus a new regression test and an update to the existing settlement test's clock mock.
- What did NOT change: the caller contract (`stopScheduledTask` / `restartScheduledTask`), the settlement result shape, and the default timeout constants all remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`prepareScheduledTaskSettlement` is the only cross-clock-domain spot left in this file: its sibling `isScheduledTaskDefinitionAbsent` already computes `remainingTimeout()` and `expired()` from `performance.now()`, and the file's other deadline helpers use `performance.now()` too. The settlement deadline is a purely process-internal closure variable — never serialized, persisted, or compared across processes — so a full switch to the monotonic clock is safe and keeps the budget aligned with the monotonic timers that consume it. No new parser, policy branch, or configuration surface is introduced. The existing `schtasks.settlement.test.ts` clock mock was moved from `Date.now()` to `performance.now()` while preserving the test's intent (settlement exhausts the full stop budget without a false restart).

## User Impact

Windows Gateway stop/update no longer stalls or fails spuriously when the system clock is adjusted (NTP resync, manual set, DST), because the settlement deadline is no longer skewed by wall-clock jumps. The settlement still waits the full configured stop budget before declaring the task unavailable, and still refuses a restart only when settlement genuinely cannot be confirmed.

## Evidence

**Real shipped command, real runner (before/after)**: a `windows-latest` runner installs a real Scheduled-Task Gateway (`openclaw gateway install`), then runs the actual shipped `openclaw gateway stop --force` while a preload steps the wall clock (`Date.now()`; `performance.now()` stays monotonic) between the settlement deadline seed and budget read — exactly the NTP/manual-set/DST incident. Both builds drive the real `schtasks.exe`/PowerShell subprocess; the only difference is the clock source of the settlement deadline (`Date.now()` pre-fix vs `performance.now()` post-fix):

| wall-clock jump | pre-fix (Date.now deadline) | post-fix (performance.now deadline) |
|---|---|---|
| +280s (forward, in-roll) | `openclaw gateway stop` ok (50s budget) | ok (full 60s budget) |
| +380s (forward, past roll) | **stop FAILS** (1ms budget → settlement unavailable → unverified) | ok (full 60s budget, inert) |
| -280s (backward) | ok (inflated budget, over-waits) | ok (inert) |

Proof artifact + workflow: `SunnyShu0925/oc-winproof` [run #40486854535](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-winproof/actions/runs/40486854535).

**Raw CLI output (inline, current head `e804ccc7dcd`)** — verbatim, redacted to service/port only (no IPs, keys, endpoints):

```console
$ # post-fix (performance.now deadline): clock +280s between deadline seed and budget read
$ openclaw gateway stop --force --json
stop exit=0 elapsed=6.4801074s
{ "action": "stop", "ok": true, "result": "stopped",
  "service": { "label": "Scheduled Task", "loaded": true, "loadedText": "registered" } }
[proof-inject] settlement Date.now reads stepped: 5   # wall clock jumped, deadline monotonic -> inert
VERDICT[post-fix-forward]: STOPPED bounded completion in 6.4801074s

$ # pre-fix (Date.now deadline): same command, clock +380s (past the 330s roll) collapses remaining to 1ms
$ openclaw gateway stop --force --json
stop exit=1 elapsed=4.443505s
{ "action": "stop", "ok": false,
  "error": "Gateway stop failed: Error: Task settlement unavailable; stop unverified.",
  "hints": ["Run openclaw gateway status --deep to inspect the service, then retry."] }
VERDICT[pre-fix-forward-380]: STOP_REFUSED exit=1
```

Under the same wall-clock jump the pre-fix build fails the very `openclaw gateway stop` that succeeds on the post-fix build: the collapsed 1ms budget times out the real PowerShell probe, settlement reports `unavailable`, and `terminate()` refuses to confirm the stop. The backward jump is equally inert post-fix (`stop exit=0 elapsed=5.41s`).

**Unit regression (forward wall-clock skew)**, pre-fix RED / post-fix GREEN:

```console
$ vitest run src/daemon/schtasks-state-probe.test.ts   # pre-fix (reverted to Date.now)
AssertionError: expected 50000 to be 60000   (280000 ms)
AssertionError: expected 1 to be 60000        (380000 ms)
$ vitest run src/daemon/schtasks-state-probe.test.ts   # post-fix (monotonic)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  18 passed (18)
$ vitest run src/daemon/schtasks.settlement.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  37 passed (37)
```

Full daemon shard: 118 files / 1943 tests passed.

**What was not tested**: the settlement state machine/JSON parsing beyond the clock budget are covered by the existing 37-test settlement suite (unchanged apart from its clock-mock alignment).

**Open PR collision check**: no open PR touches `schtasks-state-probe.ts` / `schtasks.settlement.test.ts` (searched open PR topics `settlement`/`schtasks`/`monotonic clock` and changed-file lists).

Per review: added a real-Windows proof (forward + backward clock steps, before/after table) and fixed the new regression test's floating-promise lint by returning the `withMockedPlatform` promise from the test callback (CI `check-lint-core-2`).

## Current repair status — 2026-10-27

Published head: 15b871c07d089b0458d717ececc61772befa68f3. [Exact-head CI completed successfully](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40542097208): 66 jobs passed, 26 intentionally skipped, including a passing baseline-ratchets job and CI gate. Raw red/green/control captures retain their original 1ada0531 / 0e613fe5 identities. Independent captured-artifact review now passes A/B/C, explicitly receipt-scoped; no new live/provider-perception claim.
- 204 affected tests passed on integrated 5832409c, including all four spawn-workspace consumers, specialist policy/routing, Computer atomic/observation/gateway/schema, cancellation/no-replay and budget paths. Typed lint and supported core/agent-test types passed. Later canonical movement was assessed: 9 receipt-owner guards and core types passed on 4679a2cb; final chat-diagram/Pele movement does not alter these owners. Final CI owns the updated UI/build/lock graph.
- Real secretless AWS build, compiled SDK bridge, and package creation passed on exact prior 982dda9f. These are NOT final-head package receipts. Hosted Package Acceptance refused that fork SHA before build because canonical source admission was not met; no guard was weakened.
- The stable-to-source Docker transition failed BEFORE activation at candidate config admission: baseline 2026.10.8 versus source package 2026.10.7, with retired heartbeat config. This is not a passing upgrade. The newer-config guard explains why automatic projection can refuse; original metadata was retained only as a digest, so causality is source-supported rather than independently captured. No version/config rewrite, downgrade override or retry was used. Raw diagnostics retained; owned AWS lease released.
- Completed direct OAuth, ClawRouter capability/image/tool, and Sol/Terra desktop form proofs remain preserved at their original heads without replay. Linux window-capture limitation remains; no macOS/Windows certification, production change, deployment or merge is claimed.
<!-- interaction-owner-repair-status:end -->

## What Problem This Solves

Computer and browser interaction currently have to use the chat model even when an operator wants different models for those workflows.

## User Impact

Users can select separate Computer and Browser models globally or per agent without changing chat, utility, or subagent model choices. Unset agent selections inherit defaults; an empty string keeps the chat model in control. Existing unconfigured behavior is unchanged.

When configured, the corresponding tool accepts a complete task instead of individual actions. Task text and observations, including screenshots, may be sent to the selected provider. Existing permissions, connections, approvals, cancellation, and model/tool policies remain in force. Failures do not replay partially executed tasks on another model.

## Why This Change Was Made

The specialist runs through the original authorized tool and returns its result to the parent. Interaction tasks use the source run’s normal deadline and tool-call budget—there are no extra specialist-only time, response-count, or action-count caps. This adds four config paths: Computer/Browser defaults and their per-agent overrides; the generated config surface baseline is updated accordingly.

## Evidence

- 44 focused runtime/finalizer/prompt-prefix tests pass, including cancellation, policy denial, source authority retirement, task ordering, and no replay.
- Red/green provider-boundary regressions prove completion beyond the former response-count and tool-call caps (25 observation responses and 66 tool calls).
- 49 focused UI tests and bundled settings persistence/reload E2E passed. Core/UI typechecks, changed-source lint/format, config docs and i18n checks passed.
- Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable defects; the cap-removal follow-up was independently reviewed.
- Live-provider smoke passed both specialist tool names: the model read a verification code from screenshots, filled/clicked a fresh Chromium fixture, and reported the verified result. The parent received no images. This used constrained test action adapters, not the native OS driver or a full Gateway deployment. The subsequent cap-removal-only follow-up is covered by the red/green runtime regressions.
- Broad changed-file validation timed out; the earlier full-tree scan flagged an unchanged onboarding test-helper export. Feature-owned findings were repaired and affected checks rerun. Production Gateway state was not changed.

### Before

![Default chat-model control for Computer and Browser](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02cd0d03-f372-4409-af24-9b9625ec2a71)

### After

![Independent Computer and Browser specialist selections](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/040e9df1-2223-4cef-9b3c-c0d068752998)

<!-- interaction-crabbox-validation -->
## Crabbox validation — repaired and exercised

Exact head: 19a11278ce05ebe37fd7ff2b42c4c57e31f0f2c7. Retained failing head: 2ff6d205409c72712d95028c10d0867c9e660674.

Two producer/consumer defects were repaired:
- The ClawRouter catalog adapter now reads supported versioned input metadata for the selected endpoint, preserving explicit flat overrides and rejecting unrelated/unsupported/malformed facts. No model-name whitelist or capability-check bypass was added.
- Models settings and Agent overview explicitly request/read the detailed catalog projection needed by capability-filtered interaction selectors, including cache subscriptions and login reconciliation. Compact chat/bootstrap projections remain unchanged.

Validation:
- Terra passed the same synthetic image-and-tool probe through direct Codex ChatGPT OAuth and the real ClawRouter Responses API. No OAuth credentials were copied to a remote box.
- Real AWS Linux Gateway: Sol parent with Terra Computer/Browser, normal UI selection and reload persistence, chat/utility settings preserved. Both image-code fixtures were filled/submitted/verified through stock tools. Server state recorded exactly one correct submission each; invalid-code probes were rejected.
- Passive unchanged-payload HTTP witness observed actual Sol and Terra response model IDs; screenshot image blocks went to Terra, not the parent. No mocked inference or synthetic action adapter counted as end-to-end proof.
- Independent source-blind artifact validation passed after adding persisted-settings and invalid-code rejection receipts; this was evidence validation, not a second live deployment.
- Exact-head remote build, 353 regressions (44 runtime/finalizer/prefix + 290 affected UI/cache/route + 19 catalog/native-routing), and package/UI typechecks passed. Scoped lint/format and independent P0–P2 reviews passed.

**Platform caveat:** a read-only Linux window-specific capture failed before mutation. That recording and failure are retained. The successful Computer fixture used the advertised desktop-screenshot/pixel-input path; this PR does not claim to fix that driver API family or certify macOS/Windows.

### Raw failure capture

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da88078a-be70-40e2-a905-abc30674fbb6

### Raw successful desktop/browser capture

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55036587-2786-4f35-a141-3482c2f81f60

### Real settings before / after reload

![Real settings before specialist selection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a0936392-415e-42d0-bca3-3c14be04aae5)

![Real settings after persisted Sol/Terra selection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9739b71d-3125-413f-b78c-dbba2aaab623)

Owned lease cleanup completed; temporary provider handoff files removed. Production configuration and browser profiles were untouched.

<!-- interaction-review-followup -->
## Follow-up: delegated policy and failure handling

The earlier ClawSweeper review identified two real runtime defects. Both are repaired in authored commit `c5262abf9570aea857c97197e260b49400ba34bd`, retained without rewriting this task branch. That follow-up was published at `81f469f43c5b75fd16ebdd155d7a4c124441f4b2` (see the later CI follow-through below).

- **Task versus action policy:** only the outer complete-task envelope is classified through the existing host-owned dispatcher mechanism. Task hooks remain enabled; the original narrowed action executor still checks the actual, post-hook action at final I/O. Screenshot-only Computer and Browser policies now work; a hook-rewritten click is rejected. Denied tools do not become task tools.
- **Actionable failure:** specialist failures use canonical user-facing provider-error copy and warn the parent to inspect current UI state before repeating potentially performed actions. Provider cancellation is distinguished, and the existing protected-network-error and terminal fallback-stop owners preserve the no-replay identity, including network-origin Browser tools. No fallback model or extra specialist cap was introduced.
- **CI fixture typing:** the new detailed-catalog fixture now implements its actual async request signature.

### Additional verification

- 145 targeted regressions passed on integrated head `7d55986b4a1def39565dd7ca53bc20d3b1dde724`: affected runtime/finalizer/prefix/network-error contracts, production authority handoff, Responses terminal-error/stream handling, and Models catalog publication. Production core, agent-test, and UI-page-test typechecks passed; scoped lint/format and two isolated independent P0–P2 code reviews passed.
- The final canonical range contained only private legacy-Doctor helper exports and Jiti/Babel stack-format scoping. It did not change the authored interaction fix or its policy/error/config owners. It was integrated to satisfy the fresh-base gate; the two Jiti regressions also passed on the final head. Prior results are retained with their actual tested refs, not relabeled as fresh runs.
- A supplemental **real stock Browser** probe used a fresh isolated headless Chrome profile and production task/finalizer/operator/source-budget owners. It began against the reviewed working tree whose authored content is recorded by `c5262abf`, rather than asserting a clean pinned HEAD. Its first setup attempt failed because Browser state was not initialized; that failure is retained. After normal production state-store initialization the authority clauses passed. The optional screenshot-description fixture returned no text; image capture succeeded. No parent-image-privacy claim is based on this standalone probe.
- Actual latest-stable `2026.10.7` CLI persisted and validated a credential-free configured-provider fixture. Candidate production config readers retained the authored chat/fallback, utility, subagent model/thinking, thinking default, and Fast values. Missing specialist selectors preserved original atomic tools; defaults and explicit blank agent overrides behaved as documented. Candidate reads did not change the persisted bytes. This is genuine stored-config compatibility, not a packaged Gateway/channel/database upgrade certification.
- Independent source-blind assessment passed for the supplied Browser and stable-config artifacts only. It was not an independent live retest or provenance attestation.

### Existing proof and remaining scope

The real OAuth/ClawRouter Terra capability comparisons and Sol-parent → Terra Computer/Browser form videos above remain evidence of their recorded `19a11278` head; completed form tasks were not replayed. Their model capabilities/catalog facts were not changed by this follow-up.

The separate Linux window-specific capture limitation remains. The supplemental Browser probe is not a full Gateway operator-enrollment/approval or all-platform certification. Full CI on the new head and a fresh hosted review are not claimed complete.

The previous-head subagent-progress and Reload Config CI failures were independently reproduced on unmodified canonical `5962ce779a8a425d1ffc9e1279b6242154c467e9`; they are recorded as inherited failures, not masked or silently fixed here. The PR-caused catalog test type errors were fixed.

No merge, release, production configuration change, credential change, or deployment was performed.

<!-- interaction-typed-lint-followup -->

Latest published head: `584c7c6f2d3ad8b548ac202da34dbdf4752f4ae7`. The test-only authored correction is `9099b93535b7f311c3e2f176c5f8ba1b01e8a7aa`.

- Type-aware Oxlint on all four interaction runtime/test files: **0 warnings, 0 errors** with 293 rules.
- All 26 interaction runtime/policy tests and 11 ClawRouter catalog tests passed on `584c7c6f`; agent-root test types and generated config-baseline check passed.
- Canonical movement was integrated without rewriting the task branch. The new Liquid AI plugin changed the generated config hash; the checksum conflict was resolved by the canonical generator, not hand-editing generated output.

Other CI evidence remains explicit:
- The known four subagent-progress failures and Reload Config E2E failure were reproduced on the untouched canonical baseline; they were not masked here. The subagent failures still occurred in the intermediate integration run.
- CI also reported a chat-markdown collapsed-preview failure. That file is unchanged by this PR, and its 26 focused tests passed both on the untouched baseline and on the PR. The shared/full-suite CI failure is **not reproduced or claimed fixed**.
- The lint job also emitted existing max-line warnings for three unrelated, unchanged agent files. These warnings are separate from the repaired PR-owned typed errors.

### Terminal CI result on `584c7c6f`

prs.title: fix(ui): stop the pull request list from re-announcing on every CI poll
prs.body:
Fixes #185717.

## What Problem This Solves

The pull request list announces the entire rendered list — every reference, branch and state, including the row links — on each CI status poll, instead of announcing only what changed.

## User Impact

A screen reader now hears only the row count, and only when it changes, plus one CI entry per pull request when that pull request's CI state actually moves. Rows render and behave exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`aria-live="polite"` sat on the `.chat-prs` container, which wraps the whole row list. CI status refreshes re-rendered that container, so each poll re-announced the whole card.

The list now stays out of the live region. Two `sr-only` status regions carry the announcements, following the existing `AttachmentReadStatus` pattern in `chat-attachments.tsx`:

- **Count** — `2 pull requests`, updates only when the count changes.
- **CI snapshot** — one entry per pull request, in stable URL order:

  ```
  2 pull requests with CI: openclaw/openclaw#103469: Failed (3 passed, 1 failed, 0 running, 0 skipped); openclaw/openclaw#103471: Passed (6 passed, 0 failed, 0 running, 0 skipped)
  ```

Keying the announcement to each pull request's identity, state and four exposed counters preserves changes that aggregate totals hide: two pull requests exchanging failing/passing states leave the totals identical, and check progress inside a still-pending pull request never moves a total at all. Identical snapshots and reordered rows produce the same string, so they produce no DOM change and no announcement — the silence comes from the value not changing, not from suppressing anything.

Production change is `+50/−1` across the component and one locale module; the rest of the diff is the route e2e.

## Evidence

### Every real CI transition reaches the live region

Measured on head `542bc2e`, and on the previous head `d444521` with the same harness, same fixtures, same Chromium and the same dependency install — only the component under test differs. Each count is `MutationObserver` records inside the two polite live regions, one mutation per genuine text update.

| Step | `d444521` | `542bc2e` |
|---|---|---|
| Identical poll ×5 | `[0,0]` | `[0,0]` |
| Check progress while still pending | `[0,0]` — lost | `[0,1]` |
| running → failing | `[0,1]` | `[0,1]` |
| **Two PRs exchange failing/passing** | **`[0,0]` — lost** | **`[0,1]`** |
| Remaining failure → passed | `[0,1]` | `[0,1]` |
| Row count 2 → 1 | `[1,1]` | `[1,1]` |

On `d444521` the exchange step left the text at `2 pull requests with CI: 1 failing, 1 passed` while both row badges had visibly changed — the transition `@obviyus` reproduced through the built Control UI. On `542bc2e` the same step rewrites the region to name each pull request's new state, and identical polls still move nothing.

The same run also shows the regions are rewritten, never rebuilt (element identity kept across every step), and hold no links or buttons at any point.

### The broken base

On `origin/main` the surface has a single live region that contains the row links, and its announced payload is the row markup rather than a summary:

```
1 live region, 2 <a> descendants
text: openclaw/openclaw#101 feature/pr-101 +4 −3 CI openclaw/openclaw#102 …
```

That is the defect in #185717. It is red on `main` by construction, not by a failing assertion.

### Run

- Route e2e: `ui/src/e2e/chat-pull-requests-live-region.e2e.test.ts` drives the real chat route through the mock Gateway and covers identical polls, pending progress, running → failing, the balanced exchange, and a count change.
- Behavioural proof above: mounted `ChatPullRequestsContent` in Playwright Chromium with reactive signal updates, one `MutationObserver` per polite region.
- Format: `format --check` clean on all three changed files. Typecheck, lint and the built-route e2e are left to `checks-*`.

### Gaps

- **Not a screen-reader recording.** This is live-region mutation, element-identity and accessibility-tree evidence. None of it proves what a given screen reader speaks.
- **The route e2e's assertions are not discriminating on their own.** Mounting `ChatPullRequestsContent` with the same scenario the route e2e drives, and replaying its steps, the assertions hold on `origin/main`, on `d444521` and on `542bc2e`: on `main` the whole-list region mutates on every step, and once the two regions exist the CI region mutates on any real transition. The step-by-step table above is what separates this head from the previous one; the route e2e covers the shipped path, not that separation.
- **Local environment skew.** This checkout installs `@solidjs/compiler` 2.0.0-rc.16 while `ui/package.json` requires rc.18. Browser-mode testing and the control-UI bundler ran here, but the skew means local results are not byte-identical to CI; `checks-ui-e2e` remains the authoritative run for the built route.
- **Not run locally:** the built Control UI through an isolated Gateway. That upstream lane (`@obviyus`) is the strongest remaining check.

---

Companion change: async question cards had a related live region problem and are fixed separately in #185565.

prs.title: fix(cli): message read loads every plugin when the channel plugin is external
prs.body:
Closes #185280

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw message read --channel discord` loads the full plugin registry locally (about 0.5 GB and 20+ s of CPU per call) when Discord is installed as an external npm plugin. The Gateway already owns the action.

## User Impact

User impact: Gateway-owned `message` actions on external channel plugins now go straight to the Gateway without loading the plugin locally. A `message read` against npm-installed Discord drops from about 27 s wall / 31 s CPU / 526 MB to about 11 s wall / 12 s CPU / 430 MB on our host. The remaining time is CLI startup; plugin loading is gone (see Evidence).

**Risk: this adds a public manifest field**, `channelConfigs.<id>.gatewayMessageActions` (documented in `docs/plugins/manifest/surfaces.md`).
- It is optional. It is used only when the channel plugin is neither bundled nor loaded in the CLI process. A bundled or loaded plugin's `actions.resolveExecutionMode` still decides.
- An external plugin's manifest is untrusted data. Here it only chooses the Gateway route. The Gateway still runs its own account, target, and read-authority checks with its loaded plugin.
- Existing external Discord installs benefit after the next `@openclaw/discord` release that ships this manifest. Older plugin packages keep today's behavior.
- An undeclared action to an external channel now runs one extra validate-only config pass and one metadata snapshot read (~0.2 s) before the existing local preload.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fixing `isGatewayOwnedMessageAction` alone does not help. With the predicate forced to `true` on `main`, `runMessageAction` → `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin({ allowBootstrap: true })` still bootstraps the plugin, measured at 14.4 s / 596 MB. The message route needs a channel plugin object, even for actions it only forwards to `message.action`.

So the decision moves into manifest metadata, and the route gets a plugin object that needs no runtime:

- The manifest mirrors the actions the runtime adapter sends to the Gateway. A Discord test keeps the list equal to the discovered actions whose `resolveExecutionMode` is `"gateway"`, so the runtime adapter stays the single owner.
- When the scoped channel plugin is not available locally, the message CLI asks the existing runtime-free manifest channel adapter (`src/channels/plugins/read-only.ts`). For a declared action, it returns that adapter with Gateway-only `actions` and `outbound.deliveryMode: "gateway"`. The CLI passes it to the normal `runMessageAction` through the scoped plugin registry, so routing, target, account, and policy code is shared, not duplicated.
- Dry-runs, broadcasts, and undeclared actions keep the current local preparation path.

Production +190/−21 (including the 38-line Discord manifest entry and one line in `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`, because the manifest normalizer now imports `src/channels/plugins/message-action-names.ts`), tests +100, docs +15/−9.

The delegated adapter reads the normalized, typed `record.channelConfigs` with an own-property check, so it adds no type assertions.

## Evidence

**Before/after measurement** (taken on the first revision; the review repairs do not touch the runtime path). Release-shaped packages built with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` from `main` (`ed141d0198`) and from this branch, so Discord is not bundled. Both runs use:
- the same `@openclaw/discord` package, built from this branch with `scripts/plugin-npm-publish.sh --pack` (the old core ignores the new field)
- a separate isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` per variant
- a loopback test Gateway on port 28789

Command: `openclaw message read --channel discord --target channel:123456789012345678 --limit 1 --json`, 3 runs each, measured with `/usr/bin/time`.

Every run reaches the test Gateway's `message.action`, which the Discord plugin rejects with "read target channel is not allowed" (dummy token, allowlist policy). So all six runs exercise the same CLI → Gateway path. The host was busy (load average ~8), so absolute times are inflated for both variants.

| Run | Before wall | Before CPU (user+sys) | Before max RSS | After wall | After CPU (user+sys) | After max RSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 31.0 s | 35.0 s | 525 MB | 13.4 s | 10.3 s | 431 MB |
| 2 | 25.5 s | 29.7 s | 524 MB | 10.5 s | 13.4 s | 429 MB |
| 3 | 24.3 s | 29.0 s | 528 MB | 9.0 s | 10.8 s | 429 MB |
| **Mean** | **27.0 s** | **31.2 s** | **526 MB** | **11.0 s** | **11.5 s** | **430 MB** |

CPU profiles of one run each:
- Before: `loadPluginRegistryHandle` 24.6 s inclusive, of which `createPluginGenerationArtifact` is 17.4 s.
- After: `loadPluginRegistryHandle` and `bootstrapOutboundChannelPlugin` 0 ms, `resolveGatewayDelegatedChannelPlugin` 0.2 s, `resolvePluginMetadataSnapshot` 1.2 s. The rest is CLI module loading.

**Tests.** Each of these was red before the fix.
- `src/cli/program/message/helpers.test.ts`: a read on an external channel whose manifest delegates it skips `loadPluginRegistryHandle`, runs config-ready in validate-only mode, and runs `messageCommand` against the delegated adapter. Undeclared actions still finish full config-ready and preload. 53 passed.
- `src/channels/plugins/read-only.test.ts`: a delegated read through the real `runMessageAction` reaches `message.action` with no runtime or setup load (fixture markers). This caught the outbound bootstrap during development. The same test checks that undeclared actions and disabled plugins are not delegated. 30 passed (the three delegation cases are folded into one regression; it goes red when `outbound.deliveryMode: "gateway"` is removed).
- `extensions/discord/src/channel-actions.test.ts`: the manifest list equals Discord's discovered Gateway-mode actions. 12 passed.
- Also run after the rebase: `src/plugins/manifest-registry.test.ts` (65), `src/cli/program/register.message.test.ts` (10), `src/cli/program/message/register.read-edit-delete.test.ts` (5 + 1 skipped), `src/cli/program/message/register.thread.test.ts` (6), all passed.

**Review repairs** (now rebased onto `a4e20a8b244`):
- The wrapper inventory now lists `src/channels/plugins/message-action-names.ts`. `test/scripts/pr-worktree-provision.test.ts` (16 + 2 skipped), `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` (35) and `test/scripts/pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts` (3) pass; they failed in CI on `e81e39d81d`.
- The Gateway request mock in `read-only.test.ts` is an untyped `vi.fn()`. A `vi.fn<NonNullable<OutboundMessageGatewayOptionsInput["request"]>>()` still fails `tsgo` (TS2322): Vitest's `Mock<T>` takes `ReturnType<T>`, which turns the generic `Promise<T>` into `Promise<unknown>`. Untyped `vi.fn()` has no cast and is the pattern in `src/infra/approval-gateway-resolver.test.ts`.
- `pnpm check:assertion-safety` and `pnpm check:max-lines-ratchet` pass against `3c64f85073`.
- `src/plugins/bundled-plugin-categories.test.ts` failed on `e81e39d81d` because the old merge base `ed141d0198` shipped `extensions/knowledge/openclaw.plugin.json` without `categories`; `main` fixed that in 0957af2568, and the test passes after the rebase.
- Test-line growth is +100 (down from +135) after folding the new cases into existing suites without dropping any assertion. `check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base <main> --no-merge-base` passes against `a4e20a8b244` (6,246,128 of 6,320,000).

**Checks.** `tsgo` passes for `tsconfig.core.json`, `tsconfig.extensions.json`, `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.plugin-sdk.json` and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json`. `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` pass on the changed files. `scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mts --files-json <changed files>` passes for the core and extensions shards.

**Target names and mentions (`d051165`).** Review found that the runtime-free delegated adapter has no target grammar: a mention such as `<@123456789012345678>` was rejected in the CLI (`Unknown target …`), and a channel name such as `#name` reached Discord's Gateway `read` handler unresolved and was refused (`Discord read target channel is not allowed.`, seen live on `aa10b3b`; 2026.10.9 reads the same name). Now:
- CLI: when the delegated adapter has neither `messaging` nor `directory`, an operator call (`conversationReadOrigin: "direct-operator"`) defers target lookup to the Gateway (`message-action-routing.ts`).
- Gateway: `message.action` resolves a direct-operator target with its loaded plugin through the existing `resolveMessageTarget` before dispatch, when the plugin has a target resolver or directory. A target that is already canonical resolves to itself, and agent-runtime callers (which resolve before sending) are not rewritten. The send-default target lookup that already lived in `send.ts` moves with it into `message-action-target.ts`, so `send.ts` shrinks (line-cap ratchet).
- Tests, red before and green after: `read-only.test.ts` (a mention now reaches `message.action` unresolved instead of failing in the CLI) and `message-action-target.test.ts` (an operator's `#general` resolves to the plugin's `channel:C42`; a delegated caller's target is left as sent). `send.test.ts` (79), `read-only.test.ts` (30), `send.scheduled-reads.integration.test.ts`, `message-action-runner.plugin-dispatch.test.ts` and `cli/program/message/helpers.test.ts` pass; `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, oxfmt and `pnpm check:import-cycles` are clean.
- The branch now includes current `main` (merged at `b829a7f`, no conflicts), so it is on a 2026.10.9 base.

**Real bot and upgrade from 2026.10.9 (2026-10-30, head `d051165`).** Release-shaped package of this head (`scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs`, Discord not bundled) and `@openclaw/discord` packed from this head. Isolated prefix and `OPENCLAW_HOME`, loopback Gateway, a real Discord bot as `channels.discord.accounts.main`, an allowlisted private test channel.
1. Install `openclaw@2026.10.9` and `npm:@openclaw/discord@2026.10.9`; both `--target channel:<id>` and `--target '#<channel name>'` read the latest message.
2. Stop the Gateway and run `openclaw update --tag <this head's tgz> --no-restart --yes` from that install:
   ```
   Update mode: npm / Update target: 2026.10.9
   Admission checks: config: ok, database-schema: ok, node-runtime: ok, plugin-availability: ok.
   Plugins updated; Gateway restart skipped (--no-restart).
   openclaw --version: OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (d051165)
   ```
   `channels` is unchanged (same `accounts.main`, guild and channel allowlist); the only config changes are Doctor's `agents.entries.main` and the `wizard` record. The published Discord plugin stays installed.
   (The first attempt failed in the candidate Doctor because the test's home directory was group-writable: `… writable without sticky protection; … chmod go-w …`. That is current `main`'s state-directory check on my test directory, not this change; after `chmod go-w` on the test directories the same update passes.)
3. With the published 2026.10.9 Discord plugin (no `gatewayMessageActions`), reads take the existing full-load path and both targets work: `channel:<id>` wall 35.5 s / max RSS 486 MB, `#name` 31.4 s / 589 MB.
4. With the Discord plugin packed from this head (`openclaw plugins install <tgz>`), reads take the delegated path and both targets work, two runs each: `channel:<id>` 5.8 s and 5.5 s / 372 MB, `#name` 5.7 s and 4.9 s / 371 MB. Each returns the same latest message as step 1.

The timings come from a busy host; read them only as a check of the measured table above.

prs.title: fix(update-repair): use monotonic clock for deadline budget
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the update repair agent runs an embedded agent turn, the per-turn deadline is derived from `Date.now()` (wall clock) but the remaining budget is consumed by a monotonic timer (undici `headersTimeout`/`bodyTimeout`). A wall-clock forward jump (e.g. NTP sync) collapses the remaining budget toward 1ms — `Math.max(1, deadline - Date.now())` — and prematurely aborts healthy repair turns. A rewind inflates the remaining budget and lets stalled HTTP calls run far past the configured timeout.

`src/infra/update-repair-agent.runtime.ts` seeds the deadline with `Date.now()` and hands `Math.max(1, deadline - Date.now())` to `runEmbeddedAgent`, which eventually reaches `ensureGlobalUndiciDispatcherStreamTimeouts`. Fix: seed and remaining-budget read both now use `performance.now()` so the deadline stays in the same clock domain as the downstream monotonic timer.

- **Problem**: deadline computed with `Date.now()` (wall clock) is consumed by a monotonic undici stream timeout, so system time adjustments distort the repair turn timeout.
- **Solution**: use the monotonic clock (`performance.now()`) for both the deadline seed and the remaining-budget handed to the embedded agent.
- **What changed**: `src/infra/update-repair-agent.runtime.ts` (two clock-domain alignments) and one regression test in the existing suite.
- **What did NOT change**: the outer `setTimeout(() => controller.abort(...), params.timeoutMs)` — it uses a fixed constant, not a remaining budget, and Node `setTimeout` is already monotonic.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runScopedUpdateRepairTurn` is the canonical owner of its per-turn deadline: it seeds `deadline` at the top of the function and derives `timeoutMs` from it before passing it to `runEmbeddedAgent` → `runEmbeddedAgentEntry` → `attempt-setup.ts` → `ensureGlobalUndiciDispatcherStreamTimeouts` (undici, monotonic). Mixing a wall-clock seed with monotonic consumption is the defect; aligning both operations to `performance.now()` keeps the deadline entirely monotonic. The deadline is process-local (a closure variable, never serialized or compared across processes), so the monotonic clock is the only correct choice.

- **Best fix**: yes — two equivalent one-line changes put the whole deadline pipeline in the monotonic domain; no new structure or configuration surface.
- **Risk**: none identified. `timeoutMs` is an in-process argument to the embedded agent runner; the outer abort timer is a fixed constant and unchanged.

## User Impact

Repair turns complete within their configured timeout regardless of wall-clock adjustments. Under a clock rewind, a stalled HTTP call no longer hangs beyond the turn budget; under a forward jump, healthy repair turns are no longer prematurely aborted with a 1ms timeout.

## Evidence

**Shipped CLI entry point proof (`openclaw triage --run` + real provider, head `4db0649`).** The shipped `openclaw triage --run` command triggers embedded repair via `runUpdateRepairLoop` → `runLocalUpdateRepairTurn` → `runScopedUpdateRepairTurn` — the exact function where the deadline seed (line 339) and remaining-budget read (line 431) were changed from `Date.now()` to `performance.now()`. A `--import` preload injects an NTP-style +310s forward jump into `Date.now()` at the budget-read site (stack-line matched), leaving `performance.now()` monotonic. The same preload, config, provider (Qwen3-235B), and budget apply in both builds.

**Shipped `openclaw triage --run`, clock jumps +310s between deadline seed and remaining-budget read:**

| build | clock domain | shipped entry behavior | repair turn outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| pre-fix (`Date.now`) | wall → wall (+310s) | port 1 starts; `[PROBE] Date.now seed seen` → `[PROBE] Date.now budget read seen, injecting +310s`; `remaining = max(1, 300000 − 310000) = 1ms` | turn aborts ~43s after start (1ms budget starves the HTTP call) |
| post-fix (`performance.now`) | monotonic → monotonic | port 1 starts; `Date.now` injection never fires (line-matched calls use `performance.now`); full budget consumed | turn completes normally — 6 real model requests issued |

```
PRE-FIX : [PROBE] Date.now seed seen / budget read seen → injecting +310s
           Starting repair turn 1 with zte/Qwen3-235B-A22B → embedded repair aborted (~43s)
POST-FIX: [PROBE] (no Date.now interception — monotonic clock unaffected by the jump)
           Starting repair turn 1 with zte/Qwen3-235B-A22B → 6 model requests; turn completes full budget
```

**In-process proof (round 1, still valid):** A line-matched `Date.now` shim in the in-process proof (budget 50s, real Qwen3-235B) collapses `timeoutMs` to 1ms on pre-fix, while post-fix delivers ~28–32s and returns `status: ok`.

**Regression test (bidirectional, mocked transport):**

| build | clock domain | `timeoutMs` | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| pre-fix (`Date.now`) | wall → wall (+60s) | **1 ms** | FAIL `expected 1 to be greater than 5000` |
| post-fix (`performance.now`) | monotonic → monotonic | **~9999 ms** | ✓ pass (9/9) |

All 9 suite tests pass on post-fix head; 8 existing tests unchanged. Net diff: +34 −2 across 2 files. Rebased to `origin/main` (113 commits, no conflicts).

prs.title: perf: broker workspace Git imports and remove redundant commands
prs.body:
> Split follow-up: command deletions are isolated in #190084, with no broker-routing changes and an independent interleaved measurement gate. This PR remains held for broker regression diagnosis. No merge intent has been submitted. Broker routing will land only if it beats Part A on both elapsed time and p95 loop delay with A/A controls; otherwise this PR will close with the profiling findings. The original adverse results below are retained.

## What Problem This Solves

Workspace reconciliation and result staging can stall a large Linux Gateway while Git forks directly from its main process.

**Merge held for performance acceptance.** The full Gateway campaign removes three native imports per changed turn (~197–198 ms median initiation) and improves warm maximum-loop-delay median 70.19→22.95 ms, but dispatch/cold/warm elapsed medians regress 27.6%/20.9%/21.2%. Warm maximum-loop-delay p95 worsens 73.53→291.50 ms. These are retained adverse results, not a broad latency win; owner acceptance is required before landing.

## User Impact

Linux Gateway rollback snapshots and prepared workspace result imports use the existing small spawn broker. Workspace bytes, ref serialization, live launch authority, timeout, and cleanup contracts remain intact. No configuration or schema change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Numeric stdin descriptors forced the native transport. Prepared private input files now remain broker-owned through Execa's existing file input, and result staging uses the existing prepare/launch handshake to recheck its live owner at final initiation. The command owner preserves caller context and settles refused launches without retaining nonexistent process custody.

Fast-import returns the tree it just created, deleting the follow-up rev-parse. Directory-only or fully conflicted patch preparation reuses its empty base tree. Unchanged snapshots already skip staging; mutable branch/head and common-directory checks retain their existing correctness boundaries.

Received history packs retain their checked O_NOFOLLOW file descriptors; converting those to paths would lose the checked file binding. Their separate index-pack launch remains native. Workspace inventory is owned by #189904 and is untouched. The Gateway intentionally selects native transport on non-Linux platforms; that existing platform boundary remains unchanged.

Related: #189277, #189904. Rebased onto the latter’s merge; its existing command and file-output owners are retained.

## Evidence

CI on `3091340bb549` found an overbroad no-PID error settlement and two tests tied to the retired descriptor/attempt details. Repair `60a946082aee7ff5603994d7ddb841094da5c3ec` restores uncertainty for unconfirmed errors and updates the tests to observe prepared file bytes and actual child launches. All 19 selected regressions/authority cases pass, as do targeted lint, core/gateway/process-test typechecks, and fresh Codex review. Final exact-head CI run [41268640138](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41268640138) is green at `f28d7398f1df70b849afcf380ff9b20917867c7b`. The final commit adds reviewed proof scripts; production code remains at `60a946082aee7ff5603994d7ddb841094da5c3ec`.

Acceptance fixed before measurement: identical patch/tree/pack/staged-commit results; zero native Gateway launches in raw snapshots and ordinary staging; reduced spawn blocking and loop delay. Measure CPU/allocation and preserve adverse cells; ≥20% regressions stop landing pending owner acceptance.

Final baseline is `9518ced8ac3ae72d37bcb75297e9c13e2d1d47db` (includes #189904). Five interleaved AB/BA pairs and separate A/A controls; one first-owner and two warm iterations per arm. Synthetic Linux ARM64/overlayfs fixture: 62,000 files / 1,142,784,000 bytes, 620-file changed delta. Touched 8 GiB ballast; observed RSS 8,530,272–8,536,832 KiB. Node 26.12.1, Git 2.39.5, pinned fs-safe 0.27.0 native addon. No production data.

**Owner acceptance required before landing:** warm staging parent-process CPU p95 **2,237.523 → 2,837.861 ms (+26.83%)**; total CPU p95 +16.28%, despite main-thread CPU p95 falling 310.820 → 136.634 ms. Extra CPU is in other parent threads; its cause is unproven. Warm patch median elapsed time also increased 13.91%. No broad tail-latency improvement is claimed; A/A spread does not waive these cells.

| Warm operation | Native launches | Total Git launches | Spawn ms median | Main CPU ms median |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Changed patch | 2 → 0 | 7 → 5 | 144.936 → 0 | 165.755 → 39.016 |
| Empty patch | 2 → 0 | 7 → 3 | 173.953 → 0 | 136.921 → 5.915 |
| Result staging | 1 → 0 | 3 → 2 | 76.516 → 0 | 71.327 → 23.708 |

All output fingerprints match. Separate profiles: native-spawn self time **1,252.460 → 0 ms**, including 929.156 ms under raw-tree ancestry. No cgroup throttling or OOM. The original-parent campaign also had adverse first-owner patch total-CPU p95 (+26.5%) and empty-patch elapsed/CPU p95 (+31.6%/+25.3%); those remain prior-head evidence. An intermediate integration run was stopped before completion for a file-cap repair and has no performance verdict.

Exact-original-parent regression preserves binary/NUL/CRLF/Unicode/deletion bytes, then fails with three native Gateway launches; candidate passes. Earlier workspace proof passed 71 tests plus 21 prepared-fact tests. Final integrated Node proof passed **83 tests**, including inventory/file-output siblings and launch-refusal/custody/context contracts; three Linux-only tests skipped on macOS. Codex autoreview is clean. `pnpm check:changed --staged` completed. Its worker-cap failure was fixed by moving unchanged failed-child cleanup into the existing cleanup owner; the ratchet rerun passes. Script/full-tree dead-export scans fail on unrelated `scripts/lib/release-publication-watch.mts: observePublication`: the narrow scan reproduces on clean exact parent `9518ced8ac3ae72d37bcb75297e9c13e2d1d47db`. Commit `3c67c5c3e491ba135cff9b17ca205257b8c74b6c` / #187994 introduced the unused export; its module is byte-identical at that commit and this parent, with no external consumer. This is a newly appearing main regression, not a passing check or noise. Production dead-export scan passes. All other planned checks passed; the corrected line-cap check also passes against the committed candidate. The successful-path owner measurements belong to `3091340bb549107b39c521ece97a357825554f13`; the later repair only narrows terminal-error settlement and test observations. Measured diff SHA256 `7ddf36e8246bf378305f2aaf4125b90a889e1394d062d754d965f4769c0e171e`.

The actual Linux Gateway companion campaign is fixed before its measured runs: two serial baseline A/A controls, then five alternating A/B pairs, each a fresh built Gateway with 8 GiB touched ballast and 4,096 synthetic inventory files. Record dispatch, first changed turn, warm changed turn and unchanged turn separately. Qualification is excluded. Accept only byte-identical binary results and zero native asynchronous Gateway fast-import launches for raw snapshots/ordinary staging; record launch counts and initiation ms, loop delay, CPU, elapsed time and heap-used delta with median/p95/ranges. Preserve every adverse cell; ≥20% stops landing pending owner acceptance. Heap delta is not allocation. The capture wraps ChildProcess.prototype.spawn and excludes spawnSync/execFileSync and broker CPU. Source/build/driver hashes accompany every result. This complements the production-scale owner fixture rather than replacing it.

A real isolated Gateway/paired worker/scripted provider test passed exact bytes, permissions/legacy dispatch, 12 concurrent finalizations, control responsiveness and restart/audit (104.379 s product execution). That run was unballasted because the launcher strips inherited NODE_OPTIONS. The actual Linux Gateway A/A and five interleaved A/B pairs also completed: all 12 runs / 48 scopes pass exact bytes and cleanup. Its 4,096-file/minimal-DB companion complements the 62k/1.1GB owner campaign; neither claims btrfs or 35GiB database qualification. Full results and fixture limits appear below.

Reproduce with committed `scripts/perf/workspace-reconcile-spawn-measure.ts`: `--prepare <proof> --base-ref 9518ced8ac3ae72d37bcb75297e9c13e2d1d47db --native-package <pinned-target-addon>`, generate `--fixture <workspace>`, then `--compare <proof> --fixture <workspace>`; separately add `--control` for A/A. Defaults match the workload. `--sample <proof>/<arm> --fixture <workspace> --cpu-profile <path>` profiles a separate sample.

Production delta **+164/-87, net +77 lines**. Growth supplies guarded Execa launch/custody handling; command deletions do not fully offset it. No new runtime owner, cache, configuration, schema, dependency, or protocol version.

<details>
<summary>All adverse cells and complete A/B and A/A tables</summary>

Parent CPU includes worker threads; total CPU adds broker/reaped children in 10 ms ticks. Allocation is cumulative main-isolate allocation, excluding other isolates/external buffers. First-owner uses a fresh process with warm filesystem caches. P95 is the observed maximum at these sample sizes.

prs.title: fix(update): preserve repair budgets across clock changes
prs.body:
Supersedes #185384, with thanks to @SunnyShu0925.

## What Problem This Solves

Installation-repair agent turns can receive a 1 ms timeout or an inflated timeout when the system clock changes during preparation.

## User Impact

Repair turns keep their configured elapsed-time budget across forward and backward wall-clock corrections. The invoking repair runtime must contain the fix; an older updater does not gain it from a candidate it has not started.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `monotonicDeadlineAfter` and `remainingMonotonicMs` helpers for the process-local per-turn deadline. The existing fixed abort timer, expiry clamp, authority checks, and cleanup retain their current behavior.

Smallest scope: +3/-2 production lines, 25 regression lines, and a separate 25-line test allocation for this regression. No new clock owner, configuration, storage, or migration.

## Evidence

- Regression through `runUpdateRepairTurn` with isolated state and a mocked embedded transport: after 250 ms of preparation, a 10,000 ms budget must pass 9,750 ms even when wall time jumps ±60,000 ms. Red on main `b1615fd4432c5646684fd57d77e16702e35e4a0c`: forward = 1 ms; backward = 69,750 ms. Green with the fix.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #168935 and fixes #168945.

On Windows, repository checks pass native backslash paths into classifiers that use canonical Git paths. The SQLite worker ratchet consequently reports growth from 705 to 1,855 on an unchanged checkout. The changelog checker rejects allowed human credits in docs mirrors and misses nested frozen records.

## Why This Change Was Made

Normalize paths where filesystem discovery produces them. Ripgrep emits canonical paths for the SQLite inventory; recursive changelog discovery and relative file paths use the release-artifact owner's existing format. Classification, attribution policy, CI configuration, dependencies, and runtime storage remain unchanged.

Production delta: +4/-4, net zero. Test delta: +40/-2. The existing genuine-growth controls remain intact.

## User Impact

Windows contributors can run these checks without false failures. Frozen contribution records receive the same attribution checks as on other platforms; docs mirrors retain their existing human-credit exception.

## Evidence

Head: `7309c697f1174e56cf9b618626cac31791b0d5d3`.
Base: `c579e1afd1a90198a7b9b5a8fc01d37a02adce76`.
Host: Windows, Node 26.2.0, pnpm 12.9.0, ripgrep 15.2.0.

- **Red:** the unchanged base reports SQLite T1 growth of 705 → 1,855. The inventory equality regression fails because working-tree paths/classifications differ from the identical Git snapshot.
- **Red:** actual changelog CLI fixtures reject an allowed docs-mirror credit (exit 1, expected 0) and omit a forbidden frozen-record credit (exit 0, expected 1). Initial-note and bot-credit cases also expose noncanonical diagnostic paths.
- **Green:** 10 focused tests passed across both checker suites. They cover unchanged inventories, real mutation growth, shrinking/split inventories, operation exceptions, allowed mirror credits, forbidden frozen credits, initial notes, and bot credits.
- **Actual repository checks:** `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-database-worker-ratchet.mts --base c579e1afd1a90198a7b9b5a8fc01d37a02adce76` and `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-changelog-attributions.mts` passed on the committed head.
- **Inventory proof:** the complete working-tree inventory equals the pinned Git snapshot: 693 rows, T1=705, T2=384, T3=244, W=1101.
- Formatting, focused script/test lint, `git diff --check`, script typechecking, all four root-test typecheck partitions, graph boundaries, coercion guards, Docker E2E boundaries, and the raw HTTP/2 guard passed. The full changed-file gate passed every check through typechecking and coercion, then stopped at the host-blocked dead-export scan. No checks were bypassed.

Limitations: the two existing Bash integration cases were not counted as passing. A clean-base replay fails because the host's `bash` launcher cannot find `/bin/bash`; the candidate's attempted Bash case also hit a transient cleanup permission error. The new regressions execute the actual Node CLI with isolated filesystem fixtures. No operator Gateway or real user data is used.
The dead-export scan could not load `oxc-resolver` 11.24.2 because Windows Application Control blocked its native binding. A clean-base replay at `c579e1afd1a90198a7b9b5a8fc01d37a02adce76` reproduced the same policy block. The tail lint checks were run separately and passed; this is not a claim that the full gate passed.

ClawSweeper reviewed head `7309c697f1174e56cf9b618626cac31791b0d5d3`, accepted the recorded Windows behavior proof, and found no code issues. Its remaining request was to mark the PR ready after validation. Hosted full CI will run after the draft transition.

prs.title: fix(slack): hand transport authority to route-discovery lookups
prs.body:
Fixes #190078

Related: #185972

## What Problem This Solves

Slack outbound route discovery keeps issuing authenticated Slack API requests after the transport authority that authorized the send has been invalidated. The Slack `resolveOutboundSessionRoute` implementation (`extensions/slack/src/channel.ts`) drops the `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` callback that `src/sessions/confirmed-visible-message.ts:235` forwards into it, so none of its three remote lookups revalidate current authority before touching the network:

- Enterprise owner-heartbeat DM workspace discovery — `users.info` + `auth.teams.list` (`extensions/slack/src/enterprise-user-route.ts`)
- D-prefix conversation classification — `conversations.info` (`extensions/slack/src/channel-type.ts`)
- G-prefix conversation classification — `conversations.info` (same owner)

When a Gateway restart or delivery supersession invalidates the worker admission between message acceptance and route discovery, Slack still receives authenticated destination-metadata requests. Remote consequence: a workspace-controlled D/G conversation id or a revoked token keeps being probed after local authority expired; the request cost lands on the operator's credentials.

**Precedent: #185972** — `fix(googlechat): stop metadata lookups after sender authority expires` (merged 2026-10-27). Its body states verbatim:

> "Separate follow-up: audit Slack's analogous route-discovery callback handoff."

This PR is that follow-up. Same shape, same mechanism: forward the **existing** `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` callback into the route-discovery network owner; zero new validators/options/config.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SDK contract already documents the parameter's purpose (`src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts:619-620`):

```ts
/** Revalidates transport authority before new route-discovery network requests. */
assertDirectAdapterHandoff?: () => void;
```

Slack already implements the guard everywhere except the route path:

| Path | State before this PR |
| --- | --- |
| Action path (`action-runtime.ts:276-282`, `312-319`, `actions.ts:229`) | already forwards the callback into `createSlackLookupClient` / write clients |
| Send path (`client-delivery.ts:390`) | already fences delivery via `beforeRequest` |
| Conversation metadata (`channel-type.ts:60-67` → `client-options.ts:176-190`) | `resolveSlackConversationInfo` already accepts the callback and `fenceSlackReadFetch` asserts it before every fetch |
| **Route path (`channel.ts` `resolveOutboundSessionRoute`)** | **dropped it — the only remaining gap** |

This change forwards the already-supplied callback at the three route call sites, widens `resolveSlackChannelType`'s parameter type to pass it through, and hands it to `createSlackLookupClient` in `resolveSlackEnterpriseUserTeamId` (that factory already accepts and fences it). The fence implementation itself is untouched; action and send paths are untouched; no other channel is touched.

Production LOC: +15/−13 (net +2 across three files: `channel.ts` +12/−12 — the two identical conversation-lookup argument objects consolidate into one shared lookup scope, which both forwards the callback and keeps this over-cap file from growing, as the line-cap ratchet requires; `channel-type.ts` +1; `enterprise-user-route.ts` +2/−1). Test LOC: +154/−5 (net +149).

Classification: `behavior-completing` — completes #185972's transport-authority handoff coverage for Slack's analogous route-discovery path.

## User Impact

An accepted message keeps its successful receipt and local history. With **current** authority, route discovery is byte-for-byte unchanged: the same requests go out and the same routes resolve (proven live below). With **invalid** authority, Slack no longer receives new route-discovery metadata requests; the route resolution fails with the authority error instead of silently completing a lookup the operator's admission no longer covers. Callers without handoff context (`src/gateway/conversation-list.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`, `src/infra/outbound/targets.ts`, cron delivery targets) pass no callback and behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

### Heads

- Base (RED): `d45ff6de6c486eb7d68931492e84af4842e02e44` (`docs: point logo work to the brand-kit README (#186198)`, current `main` at pickup)

prs.title: fix(mxc): resolve literal sandbox file paths without trimming
prs.body:
Fixes #190077

## What Problem This Solves

The mxc sandbox fs bridge trimmed the tool-supplied `filePath` before mapping it onto its mounts, so a literal file name like `" x.txt"` silently addressed its trimmed sibling `x.txt`. A sandboxed agent reading or writing `" x.txt"` touched the decoy file instead of the one the model chose.

Precedent: #187554 ("The configured directory's whitespace belongs to its filesystem identity"). Sibling: #172869.

## Why This Change Was Made

`MxcFsBridge.resolveTarget` in `extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts` now resolves the caller's literal `filePath`; only the optional invocation base (`cwd`) keeps its blank-check via `trim()`, matching the shape accepted in #187554. The mount-containment guard is unchanged and still operates on the literal-resolved path.

Classification: `behavior-completing` (extends the literal-path contract to the mxc bridge owner).

## User Impact

Agents working in the mxc sandbox backend now read and write the exact file the model named, including names with leading/trailing whitespace. Ordinary paths, absolute paths, and outside-root rejections behave identically.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `ed26a563f` (branch `fix/mxc-literal-file-path`)
- Current-main RED baseline: `c77cfc122d2883848edde882e75446b761dd2711`
- Production entry: real dispatch via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/mxc/test/fs-bridge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (Node 24.18, Linux x64, secretless Docker)
- Canonical owner exercised: `MxcFsBridge.resolveTarget` in `extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts:178`, through the public `readFile` with real filesystem files
- Decision surface: the `filePath` parameter of sandboxed agent file tools (`Type.String` schema, no pattern constraint; no upstream trim in the tool chain)
- Recorder/readback boundary: the file bytes returned by `readFile`, asserted byte-for-byte against distinct literal/decoy contents
- Acceptance RED: on current main, the new assertion failed — `readFile(" x.txt")` returned the decoy's contents (`"decoy-data"` instead of `"literal-data"`); the two pre-existing test variants passed (1 failed / 2 passed)
- Acceptance GREEN: on exact head, all 3 tests pass, with both `" x.txt"` → literal and `"x.txt"` → decoy observed through the real bridge over real files
- Legal controls: the trimmed sibling still resolves to itself; the pre-existing native-tool-paths matrix (workspaceOnly true/false) and its mutation denials are unchanged and green
- Cleanup: isolated temp workspaces only; no mxc runtime, Gateway, or production config touched (the bridge owner is host path math plus real fs access checks)

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/mxc/test/fs-bridge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 3/3 (RED run on main: 1 failed / 2 passed at the new assertion)
- `oxfmt --check` on both changed files — clean
- Not tested: live mxc container end-to-end (the changed owner is pure host-side path resolution + fs, exercised with real files here); Windows container-path normalization

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+4/-1`
- Test LOC: `+29/-0` (existing test file only)
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the existing mount-containment guard (`isPathInside`) and mount table; no new validator or export
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none
- Two-way door: reverting restores trimmed-path resolution

## Maintainer edits

<details>
<summary>land-ready notes</summary>

- Maintainer edits are allowed on this branch (small, single-owner change).
- Alternative considered: normalizing only in the containment check — rejected: the resolved host path itself must stay literal or the fs target is wrong.
- Scope declaration: this PR changes the mirror/local mapping only; the mxc spawn launcher and readiness owners are untouched.

</details>


## Shipped-run proof (2026-10-30)

Reviewer demand: terminal evidence of **shipped file tools selecting ` x.txt` rather than `x.txt`**, with the Windows-flow boundary disclosed (no shipped Windows MXC flow was captured).

**Entry point: compiled shipped module + real fs** — no vitest, no tsx, no mocks.

- Class: `MxcFsBridge` compiled from this PR's sources by the repo's own extension build (same tsdown build that emits `dist/extensions/mxc/index.js`).
- The mxc Linux registration path is intentionally dormant (`registerMxcPlugin` warns and returns early off-Windows before registering any backend), so the class was imported through a **scratch-only re-export entry** (`extensions/mxc/proof-entry.ts`, worktree-local, never committed) that the same build emitted as `dist/extensions/mxc/proof-entry.js`. It was instantiated with the **exact shipped construction expression** from `mxc-backend.ts`: `new MxcFsBridge(sandbox)` — the same call the backend's `createFsBridge` performs for agent file tools. The compiled class is the shipped build output.
- The mxc read/write path under test is pure Node path-mapping over the mount table plus a real fs-safe root: no MXC binary and no Windows host is required for the code this PR changes.

**Boundary disclosure:** no Windows host is available for this run. The changed owner (`MxcFsBridge.resolveTarget`) is OS-agnostic Node path-mapping; Windows-specific container-path normalization (drive-letter/case semantics) is out of scope for this change and untested. This run is the strongest Linux shipped evidence for the mxc bridge.

Exact commands (scratch worktree at `b17f25996` + this PR's disjoint `extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts`; local-only, nothing pushed from it):

```
export PATH=/tmp/node24/node-v24.22.1-linux-x64/bin:$PATH
cd <scratch-worktree>
pnpm openclaw --version            # full build; emits dist/extensions/mxc/proof-entry.js
node proof/mxc-driver.mjs          # head run -> GREEN below
# red pairing: restore base bridge, rebuild, rerun
git show c77cfc122d2883848edde882e75446b761dd2711:extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts > extensions/mxc/src/fs-bridge.ts
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-external-plugin-local-dist.mts
node proof/mxc-driver.mjs          # base run -> RED below

```

Seeds: ` x.txt` = `PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-content`, `x.txt` = `PROOF_DECOY_4B7A1C-content` (0o644) under the rw agent-workspace mount.

Base `c77cfc122d2883848edde882e75446b761dd2711` (pre-fix `.trim()`) — exit 1:

```
read ' x.txt' (cwd=/sandbox) -> "PROOF_DECOY_4B7A1C-content"          <-- trimmed to the decoy
writeFile ' x.txt' (cwd=/sandbox) -> ok
  on-disk ' x.txt' -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-content"                   <-- literal untouched
  on-disk 'x.txt'   -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-WRITTEN-BY-SHIPPED-BRIDGE" <-- decoy received the write
FAIL  read selects literal (relative+cwd)
FAIL  relative write landed on literal file
FAIL  relative write left decoy untouched
OVERALL: RED
```

Head `ed26a563fd3c370651150800d588fa5273ee1737` (this PR) — exit 0, full output:

```
read '/sandbox/ x.txt' -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-content"
read '/sandbox/x.txt'   -> "PROOF_DECOY_4B7A1C-content"
read ' x.txt' (cwd=/sandbox) -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-content"          <-- literal selected
read '/sandbox/plain.txt' (control) -> "PROOF_PLAIN_77AA00-roundtrip"
writeFile ' x.txt' (cwd=/sandbox) -> ok
  on-disk ' x.txt' -> "PROOF_LITERAL_9F3E2D-WRITTEN-BY-SHIPPED-BRIDGE"   <-- literal updated
  on-disk 'x.txt'   -> "PROOF_DECOY_4B7A1C-content"                       <-- decoy untouched
resolvePath '/sandbox/ x.txt' -> hostPath=.../agent-workspace/ x.txt     <-- literal identity kept
resolvePath '/sandbox/x.txt'   -> hostPath=.../agent-workspace/x.txt
PASS  read selects literal (absolute)
PASS  read selects decoy for unpadded sibling
PASS  read selects literal (relative+cwd)
PASS  relative write landed on literal file
PASS  relative write left decoy untouched
PASS  resolvePath keeps literal identity
PASS  resolvePath keeps decoy identity

```

Controls: absolute-path read/write with only an interior space (`/sandbox/ x.txt`) is not affected by the trim bug and behaves identically on base and head; plain unpadded `plain.txt` round-trips on both. The defect scope is exactly a tool-supplied **relative** name with leading whitespace — the scenario the added regression test pins.

Cleanup: proof temp workspaces under `/tmp` removed; the scratch worktree (including the local-only `proof-entry.ts` re-export and its package.json build-config tweak) was never pushed; the PR branch itself is unchanged — head stays `ed26a563fd3c370651150800d588fa5273ee1737`, no commit/push was needed.

prs.title: fix(codex): use the literal bound workspace cwd for plugin discovery
prs.body:
Fixes #190076

## What Problem This Solves

`createCodexPluginsTool` resolved the workspace for native-plugin discovery with `binding?.cwd?.trim() || options.context.workspaceDir?.trim() || ...` (`native-plugin-tool.ts`). The bound cwd is stored untrimmed (`app-server/thread-lifecycle-io.ts` persists `cwd: params.cwd` verbatim at session start), so this leaf trim rewrote the session's literal workspace identity before building the `plugin/list` request. The Codex app-server then scanned the trimmed impostor directory for marketplace plugins instead of the real one — discovery silently returns nothing for a workspace whose name carries edge whitespace.

## Solution

Use `readNonBlankString` on each fallback level. Blank or whitespace-only values still fall through to the next source (`context.workspaceDir`, then the configured default workspace), but non-blank values flow verbatim into the discovery `cwds` request parameter. This matches the whitespace-preserving convention already used for the app-server binding `workspaceDir` in `conversation-binding-data.ts`.

## Impact

- Marketplace plugin discovery scans the literal bound workspace directory.
- Fallback semantics for blank/whitespace-only values are unchanged.
- No other consumer of the binding store is affected: the stored record itself already kept the raw cwd.

## Evidence

Red-green on a pristine `origin/main` worktree (remote runner, vitest):

- **Before:** 1 failure — `expected cwds ["/bound/company"] to equal [" /bound/company "]` in the `plugin/list` request.
- **After:** `native-plugin-tool.test.ts` 9/9 passed; consumer regression `plugin-marketplace-discovery.test.ts` 5/5 passed.

Real behavior proof (2026-10-30): the shipped tool, driven against the pinned `codex-cli 0.164.0` app-server (`plugin/list` over stdio, no mocked catalog), returns `literal-ws-bundle@literal-ws` for a session bound to `/tmp/pr188122-proof/ws/company `, while the `.trim()` selection returns the sibling's `trimmed-sibling-bundle@trimmed-sibling`. Full transcript: [#issuecomment-6524133566](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188122#issuecomment-6524133566).

## Precedent

Same defect class as merged #187554 (configured directory identity) and #187739 (session cwd identity). Sibling sweep PRs: #187751, #187766, #187777, #187816, #187825.

prs.title: fix(config): keep config set secrets redacted when a value option precedes the positionals
prs.body:
Fixes #190075

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw config set` records the new value in the clear in the local config-audit record when a value-taking option such as `--expect-current-json` appears before the config path and value, even when that path is secret-bearing.

## User Impact

User impact: an operator who runs the documented conditional write with the option first — `openclaw config set --expect-current-json <json> <secret-path> <secret>` — no longer gets that secret stored unredacted in `<state>/state/openclaw.sqlite` (`diagnostic_events`, scope `config-audit`, latest 50000 rows). The same command with the option after the positionals already redacted correctly; both orders do now. No config format, CLI surface, or default behavior changes, and no migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

`findConfigPositionals` decides which `config set` arguments are the path and the value, so it must skip the value of every value-taking option; `CONFIG_SET_VALUE_OPTIONS` is that hand-maintained contract. `--expect-current-json` is registered on `config set` (`src/cli/config-cli.ts:375-378`) but was missing from the set, so its JSON payload was counted as the path · `src/config/io.audit.ts:71-79`. The sensitive-path check then evaluated the payload instead of the real path and skipped the value · `src/config/io.audit.ts:114-123`. Adding the missing entry restores the order-independent positional discovery the list exists to provide; it is the only `config set` value option absent from the list. Repair classification: behavior-completing.

## Evidence

Rebased head: base `fa0bc65a7d` (current `main`) → candidate `2cae560f02`. The live CLI before/after proof below was captured on the original pair `482631a7d880f41588fc33540ecd8b188033d2b3` → `32f7ef384bb722af723514268824a5ed8fbe1b06`; both built with `OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts`, each run using its own isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, read back with a read-only `node:sqlite` query against the state DB.

BEFORE (base) — the record keeps the value:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE node openclaw.mjs config set models.providers.openai.apiKey SEED_VALUE_AAA
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$STATE node openclaw.mjs config set --expect-current-json '"SEED_VALUE_AAA"' \
    models.providers.openai.apiKey PROOF_SECRET_9F3E2D

argv: [".../node",".../openclaw.mjs","config","set","--expect-current-json","\"SEED_VALUE_AAA\"","models.providers.openai.apiKey","PROOF_SECRET_9F3E2D"]
needlePresent: true
```

AFTER (candidate) — same command, same persisted config value, record redacted:

```text
argv: [".../node",".../openclaw.mjs","config","set","--expect-current-json","\"SEED_VALUE_AAA\"","models.providers.openai.apiKey","***"]
needlePresent: false
```

Controls:

| Control | Result |
|---|---|
| Documented order (option after the positionals, `channels.slack.token`) | redacted `***` before and after |
| Non-sensitive path (`--expect-current-json 19001 gateway.port 19002`) | `19002` still recorded in the clear after the fix (no over-redaction) |

Focused test at the rebased head — `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config vitest.config.ts src/config/io.audit.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`:

| Head | Result | Wall time |
|---|---|---|
| `fa0bc65a7d` with the unpatched `io.audit.ts` | 1 failed \| 18 passed — the new option-before case persists `secret-value` where `***` is expected | ~11s |
| candidate `2cae560f02` | 19 passed | 11.3s |

Added cases follow the existing `redacts %j in persisted audit process info` table: the option-before regression and an option-after order control. `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean on both changed files.

Not tested: no live Gateway process was started; the audit record is written by the `openclaw` CLI process itself, which is the writer under test. Broad suites are left to CI.

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- **Land-ready why:** one-line production change inside the existing owner, plus a table case; the invariant is already documented by the sibling entries.
- **Alternatives considered:** deriving the set from Commander's option metadata (larger change, new coupling) and clearing the record's argv entirely (drops the diagnostic value this list exists to preserve while redacting).
- **Scope:** `config set` positional discovery and its audit redaction only; no other command, schema, or output path is touched.
- **Precedent:** the sibling entries (`--batch-json`, `--ref-*`, `--provider-*`) already encode order-independent positional discovery; the same rule was recently applied to option-order handling in `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-export-common.ts`.
- Allow edits from maintainers is enabled.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Impact surface</summary>

| File:line | Risk |
|---|---|
| `src/config/io.audit.ts:28` | Adds one member to the value-option set; only affects argv scanning for `config set` audit records. |
| `src/config/io.audit.test.ts:189` | Two new table rows; no shared harness change. |

</details>
