prs.title: fix(cli): reject reserved __proto__ keys in provider-env and mcp env/header
prs.body:
Fixes #190074

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw config set ... --provider-env` and `openclaw mcp add --env/--header` accept `KEY=VALUE` entries and build them into a plain object with `entries[key] = value`. When the key is `__proto__`, that assignment hits `Object.prototype`'s legacy setter instead of creating an own property, so the entry is silently dropped — the command still exits 0 and writes the config, just without the requested key. No warning, no error, nothing in the written file.

This is the same failure mode the repository already guards against at the MCP server-name boundary (`src/config/zod-schema.root-support.ts`):

```ts
// Plain assignment treats "__proto__" as a setter, so one unhardened map builder
// can silently drop the server. Reject the name at the config boundary instead.
```

This change applies that same principle to the two CLI `KEY=VALUE` boundaries: instead of dropping a reserved key silently, reject it with a message that names the flag and the key.

## User Impact

- An operator who passes `--provider-env __proto__=…` (or `mcp add --env/--header __proto__=…`) now gets an actionable error instead of a silently incomplete config.
- No change for any other key: normal entries are parsed and written exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The silent drop happens at the point the CLI parses each entry, so the guard is added there — that is also where the message can name the offending flag (`--provider-env`, `--env`, `--header`), which a schema-level error cannot.

- `src/cli/config-cli-input.ts` — `parseProviderEnvEntries` rejects a `__proto__` key.
- `src/cli/mcp-cli.ts` — `parseKeyValueEntries` (used by both `--env` and `--header`) rejects a `__proto__` key.

Scope follows the existing precedent exactly: only `__proto__` is rejected (the key that is silently dropped). `constructor`/`prototype` are not touched — plain assignment to those keys creates ordinary own properties, so they are not affected by this bug.

## Evidence

### Control-red: same commands, base vs this change

Run through the real CLI entry (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts …`) with an isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`.

| Scenario | Base (`main`) | This change |
|---|---|---|
| `config set secrets.providers.runner --provider-source exec --provider-command <cmd> --provider-env __proto__=injected --provider-env NORMAL_KEY=control` | exit `0`, no error, written `env` keys = `["NORMAL_KEY"]` (`__proto__` dropped) | exit `1`, `--provider-env key "__proto__" is reserved; use a different key name.`, nothing written |
| `mcp add probe --command <cmd> --no-probe --env __proto__=injected --env NORMAL_KEY=control` | exit `0`, no error, written `env` keys = `["NORMAL_KEY"]` (`__proto__` dropped) | exit `1`, `--env key "__proto__" is reserved; use a different key name.`, nothing written |
| `mcp add probe --url https://mcp.example.test/mcp --no-probe --header __proto__=injected --header X-Normal=control` | exit `0`, no error, written `headers` keys = `["X-Normal"]` (`__proto__` dropped) | exit `1`, `--header key "__proto__" is reserved; use a different key name.`, nothing written |

Raw JSON from the proof (base):

```json
{
  "providerEnv": { "exitCode": 0, "stderrHasError": false, "writtenEnvKeys": ["NORMAL_KEY"] },
  "mcpEnv":     { "exitCode": 0, "stderrHasError": false, "writtenMsKeys": ["NORMAL_KEY"] },
  "mcpHeader":  { "exitCode": 0, "stderrHasError": false, "writtenHeaderKeys": ["X-Normal"] }
}
```

Raw JSON after the change:

```json
{
  "providerEnv": { "exitCode": 1, "stderrFirstLine": "--provider-env key \"__proto__\" is reserved; use a different key name.", "writtenEnvKeys": [] },
  "mcpEnv":     { "exitCode": 1, "stderrFirstLine": "--env key \"__proto__\" is reserved; use a different key name.", "writtenMsKeys": [] },
  "mcpHeader":  { "exitCode": 1, "stderrFirstLine": "--header key \"__proto__\" is reserved; use a different key name.", "writtenHeaderKeys": [] }
}
```

### Regression tests

Added cases assert the rejection and that no config is written, for both boundaries:

- `src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` — `rejects a reserved __proto__ provider env key before writing`
- `src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts` — `rejects a reserved __proto__ key in --env and --header before writing`

```
$ node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  72 passed (72)
```

```
$ node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.mcpcheck.config.ts
 Tests  33 passed | 1 failed (34)
```

(`src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts` is excluded from the default CLI project and needs the host-owned SQLite broker, so it was run through an isolated scoped config.)

The single failure is a pre-existing environment failure on this host — `requires initialize to finish within the configured probe timeout before saving` — which spawns a probe child process; it fails identically on the unmodified base and is unrelated to this change (the new test passes in isolation).

### Lint

```
$ oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json src/cli/config-cli-input.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
```

### Types

Scoped `tsgo` over the changed files reports no errors in `src/cli/config-cli-input.ts` or `src/cli/mcp-cli.ts`. The remaining errors in the run are pre-existing dependency gaps in unrelated files (`pg`, `@resvg/resvg-js`, `@openclaw/proc-safe`) and are identical on the base.

### Sibling check

`gh search prs` for `__proto__ env`, `reserved prototype`, and `parseKeyValueEntries` returns no open or closed PR touching these two sites. This is distinct from #171770, which preserves `__proto__` keys in plain runtime maps (`cron` command env / process-env merge); the sites here flow into config that is validated through `z.record`, where the key is dropped regardless, so rejection — not preservation — is the correct fix and matches the existing boundary precedent.

prs.title: fix(scripts): preserve unrelated anchors and cached artifacts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unrelated anchors and cache entries being removed or overwritten by PR tooling and Bun staging.

## User Impact

PR tooling preserves unrelated anchors and cache entries. Each invocation retires only its own state.

Unrelated retained state may use additional disk space. Bun archives are downloaded into invocation scratch on each run instead of being kept in the shared archive cache.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove cross-entry anchor and dependency-cache sweeps from PR tooling while preserving operation-owned retirement. Keep Bun download, extraction, and cleanup inside the invocation's scratch directory.

Production LOC: +8/-130 (net -122). Tests: +352/-114. Documentation: +16/-14.

## Evidence

- Regression coverage includes owned-anchor retirement, preservation of unrelated anchors and dependency caches, and invocation-local Bun staging.
- Added the `scripts/pr wrappers` case `supervisor startup preserves unrelated anchors while retiring its own` in `test/scripts/pr-wrappers.test.ts`.
- Repaired-source static checks and before/after source comparisons passed during qualification. Prior focused test results retain their original source binding.
- Normal commit hooks passed and the signed commit was cryptographically verified. The committed eight-file patch matches the reviewed patch; the worktree and index are clean.
- Final-head hosted CI, including execution of the named supervisor-startup case, is pending. This draft is not merge-ready.

prs.title: perf: reduce model picker work while searching
prs.body:
## Problem and change

Opening and searching a large model catalog repeatedly scans every model to select its few mounted rows. Reuse the prepared catalog index and virtualizer keys for large contiguous lead/More lists; small lists keep their existing filter. An equality-bearing keys memo prevents geometry-only updates from repeating selection. The 1,000-model mobile fixture keeps the same catalog order, keyed focus, shortcuts and visible choices. No domain owner, native row-measurement policy, lazy boundary, dependency or new cache changes.

Source-mapped counts: membership checks fall **5,973→54 first-open/search** and **4,964→36 warm**. Added mounted-key lookups are 81/60 and key-projection items 302/261. Row creation, uncached geometry reads and size corrections remain 45/34; window publications remain 65/51. Small-list helper calls rise 9→16 / 6→10; timings include that cost.

## Performance proof

Times are milliseconds, median / nearest-rank p95. Each triplet is counterbalanced base/head/base on one host; all observations and A/A controls are retained. Chromium is mobile 390×844/touch with 128 MiB V8 old-space, thread-CPU task metrics and whole-renderer CPU. This is not physical Android OS memory-pressure proof. WebKit reports application/wall elapsed time, never CPU.

| Flow / metric | Base median / p95 | Head median / p95 | Median change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Chromium 6× first-open/search task · 40 triplets | 635.48 / 764.08 | 599.21 / 743.90 | -5.71% |
| Chromium 6× warm open/search task · 20 triplets | 549.64 / 729.29 | 528.54 / 678.99 | -3.84% |
| Chromium 1× first-open/search · 20 triplets | 79.71 / 82.88 | 74.57 / 79.12 | -6.45% |
| Chromium 1× warm open/search · 20 triplets | 61.06 / 63.91 | 57.67 / 59.68 | -5.56% |
| Chromium 4× first-open/search · 20 triplets | 371.38 / 439.18 | 336.83 / 392.35 | -9.30% |
| Chromium 4× warm open/search · 20 triplets | 281.64 / 302.80 | 242.04 / 264.71 | -14.06% |
| WebKit application first-open/search · 20 triplets | 153.00 / 158.00 | 146.00 / 159.00 | -4.58% |
| WebKit application warm open/search · 20 triplets | 107.00 / 114.00 | 103.50 / 115.00 | -3.27% |

The refreshed 6× source cohort is `ebf13610e1b8b29462c68eb71e18450effe6fdc7` → `536f23ac8b4f628fa688734da4ce559dbcc98a01`: 180/180 observations pass. The fresh 1×/4×/WebKit cohort is `72cab24990b3746574ac83e3d73c79530b8cc198` → `c97c988aa23605a902d7f003a57fee39d84f3c38`: 360/360 pass. The transition between these cohorts changes the terminal dependency and a release script, not UI source or the measured picker path. The final merge includes the landed drawer/image/Systems work and #190033; timings retain their exact source identities rather than being relabelled as final-head timings. The range patch and its three files are byte-identical throughout.

First-open/search clears the ≥5% 6× task threshold (−5.71%) with script −14.63% and renderer CPU median −4.56%. Warm's refreshed 6× gain is 3.84%, not separately claimed as ≥5%. First-open ready time improves 290.55/350.3→284.75/342.5 ms in the pooled 6× cohort. The 300 ms target remains unmet; no unavoidable floor is claimed.

### Accepted tradeoffs and measurement limits

This is an aggregate flow win, not an all-metrics improvement. In the refreshed 6× cohort, first-open renderer CPU p95 +0.46% and wall p95 +0.47% are below the campaign's 1% noise threshold; the initial CPU-tail concern (+15.06%) was tested with 20 additional triplets rather than omitted. Layout median/p95 +3.13%/+4.83% and style median +3.16% remain disclosed (style p95 −6.17%).

At fresh 1×, all task/CPU/wall medians and p95s improve. First-ready median rises 70.2→74.4 ms (+5.98%) while its control is 75.2 ms; p95 rises 0.1 ms, and paired median is −0.69%. Warm style/layout p95 rises 0.281/0.273 ms. Warm heap-after p95 rises 1,263,908 B (+3.88%).

At fresh 4×, task/CPU/wall and first-ready medians/p95s improve. First layout p95 rises 3.128 ms (+6.55%; paired p95 +15.96%, A/A +12.33%). Warm net-heap delta median rises 998,236 B (+106.74%); this remains an adverse raw result. The observations have low/negative and ~1.9 MB net-change clusters (10/20 low or negative controls versus 5/20 candidate), so signed paired percentages cannot establish allocation savings. No GC trace proves its cause. Warm heap-after median/p95 changes +1.69%/−0.49%; RSS −0.17%/+0.28%. These bounded endpoint costs are accepted with the measured aggregate win; no all-memory-green or leak-free claim.

At WebKit, application p95 rises 1 ms in each flow (+0.63%/+0.88%); first wall p95 rises 0.35 ms (+0.15%), all below the sub-1% band. First assertion-tail median/p95 rises 7/10→8.5/11 ms (+21.43%/+10%). Its boundary is the last MutationObserver/native-value commit to scenario end, including visibility assertions and a browser evaluation round trip; it is neither CPU nor paint latency. Full first-native-input→scenario-end improves 159/168→155.5/167 ms, and last-input→last-mutation improves 2→1 ms (p95 stays 2). Last-input→scenario-end is 9→10 ms with 12 ms p95 unchanged. Warm last-input→last-mutation p95 is 3→4 ms (the control is also 4 ms), while final-input completion p95 remains 11 ms. WebKit first-open readiness improves 90/92→88/91 ms. An earlier commit mechanically lengthens the measured tail, but its full cause is not proved; this is not described as a harness-only interval or an all-final-key-latency win.

A separate final-head WebKit diagnostic (one base/head/base triplet per first/warm flow, 6/6 pass, trace overhead included) confirms a mixed rendering/protocol tail. First-open head has one post-mutation style pass and three short layout records, matching controls; tail ScriptProfiler elapsed union is 0.715 ms versus 1.143/0.692 ms, not CPU. Its sampled paint is later (+7.24 ms versus +4.76/+5.81 ms from the final native input). First-phase recording adds its own calls, so diagnostic timings are not pooled with or used to replace untraced results. The small final-key/paint uncertainty is accepted with improving whole-action metrics; no pure-harness or universal-latency claim.

The independent evidence review verifies source maps, all captured asset hashes, result hashes and arithmetic. No failed/slow observations are excluded.

## Validation and size

The existing focused checks pass on the identical range implementation: 8 unit tests, 18 Chromium browser tests and 18 WebKit browser tests. Full exact-head PR CI is required after this update. The previous profile-page failure was not attributed inherited: #190033 fixed the unconfigured-channel runtime load, and its exact-head full CI passed before merging.

Final byte/static checks: `pnpm tsgo:ui` and production `pnpm deadcode:knip` pass. Both exact source builds and strict checks pass on base `c2a39e4c5a8166d1f5ea6703d1dfaa7d7c45de79` and head `a5611941f0379b5d96b18ba25a64ead45c5dad72`: startup JS **89,596→89,607 B gzip** (+11 B, within the 64 B build-variance allowance); startup CSS **34,184→34,184 B, one request**; Chat JS **1,273,453→1,273,290 B**; New JS **782,206→781,793 B**. No budget exception or new ignore.

Production LOC **807→830**; browser test **457→465**; full own diff **+33/−2**. The extra code reuses the existing index and preserves small-list behavior. Solid refactor census: `createMemo` 21→22; other imperative API counts unchanged. Independent P0–P2 code review is scoped-clean; the final range patch hash is `b958cbf87cbfb3c51bdddea06d3bf64f7d224781da1af8360a744834910a0cce`.

Reproduce with `scripts/bench-control-ui-interactions.ts --steps model-picker-first-open-search,model-picker-open-search --viewport mobile --pairs 20 --counterbalance --cpu-throttle 6 --low-memory --thread-cpu-time --renderer-process-metrics`, frozen base/head/base bundles; repeat at rates 1 and 4. WebKit uses `scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts --engines webkit --network-profiles localhost --viewport mobile --pairs 20` with the same steps/bundles. Counts are separate `--function-counts` runs.

## Visual proof

Inspected synthetic captures are pixel-identical. Host tags, classes and selectors are unchanged.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Model picker before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c2e57cbf-0ade-445b-94ab-ca719e5c6421) | ![Model picker after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66a7583e-8642-4a12-847c-5b2140e88a45) |

Release-note context: less repeated work when opening and searching a large model catalog on slower devices.

prs.title: fix(memory-lancedb): auto-capture stores OpenClaw's own [System] retry turns as user memories
prs.body:
Closes #189955

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: memory-lancedb auto-capture stores OpenClaw's own `[System]` turns as user memories when a stranded-reply retry, or a `sessions_send` restart note, quotes text that contains a capture trigger.

## User Impact

User impact: with `autoCapture` on, only what the user said is stored. `[System]` rows already in a store stop coming back from recall and are no longer used for duplicate matching. They stay on disk and still show in `openclaw ltm list`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core prefixes every turn it writes itself with `[System]` (`formatSystemTurnPrompt` in `src/sessions/system-turn-prompt.ts`) and sends it as a user-role message, so `extractUserTextContent` hands it to capture like any user text. Capture now goes through `capturableUserText`, which checks the raw turn for that marker before sanitizing, because sanitizing can remove the marker line along with a quoted context block. It then applies `shouldCapture`, which also rejects the marker. `isRecallableMemoryText`, which gates both recall and duplicate matching, skips such rows too. The marker is matched in the plugin because plugins cannot import the core helper, and a leading timestamp envelope is allowed before it.

Deleting rows already stored is left out. That is a retention change, and recall no longer surfaces them. One tradeoff: a user message that itself starts with `[System]` is no longer captured.

## Evidence

- New qa scenario `memory-lancedb-system-turn-capture` (in this PR): real gateway, qa-channel, mock-openai, `messages.visibleReplies: message_tool`, memory-lancedb `autoCapture: true`.
  - The first prompt is not capturable, so the `[System]` retry is the first capturable text. A later turn in the same conversation, `QA-MEMORY-BARRIER 記住 ...`, must be stored before the store is read; captures for one session run in order, so the retry's capture has settled by then.
  - It fails if any stored row contains the retry's `send it now with message(action=send)` instruction, so it catches the retry whether or not its `[System]` line survived.
  - With main's memory-lancedb at `eef407423d4`: fails after the barrier settles, with `[System] Your previous reply was not delivered because you did not call message(action=send). Your reply text was: "QA-STRANDED-85714：...". If the user should see a reply, send it now with message(action=send). If no reply is needed, answer exactly NO_REPLY.` stored. The gateway logs two `auto-captured 1 memories`: the retry turn and the barrier.
  - This branch at `f517e265d7f`: passes with `barrier rows=1; retry rows=0`.
  - Command: `node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario memory-lancedb-system-turn-capture --concurrency 1 --fast`, after `pnpm build`.
- `pnpm test extensions/memory-lancedb/memory-policy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 4 passed.

prs.title: fix(update): PostgreSQL rollback retries fail after a recoverable refusal
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: PostgreSQL update rollback fails with `EEXIST` on every retry after a recoverable refusal before database publication.

## User Impact

User impact: after correcting the reported obstruction, operators can retry the same native `update restore --backup-root` request. Earlier recovery preparations, original PostgreSQL namespaces, current update history, and existing publication/authority checks remain intact. No schema, configuration, durability, or retention-policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each attempt needs a fresh anchor destination. Add an attempt UUID to the existing recovery artifact name rather than overwriting or trusting an earlier preparation. The existing backup/recovery owner still owns those artifacts; no new lifecycle manager or cleanup policy is introduced.

## Evidence

- **Real baseline RED before the production edit:** built source `9c22cf86f68b34269e49a25a95827c1c23b52ce0`, isolated PostgreSQL 18.6, actual Gateway readiness, Workboard CLI creation, and persisted native migration receipt. A task-owned `.migrated-<runId>` obstruction caused the intended prepublication refusal. Removing only that obstruction and retrying the same receipt failed at `COPYFILE_EXCL` with `EEXIST`. Original anchor/store and namespace remained intact. Full run: 54.17 seconds. This initial product reproduction used Node 24.20.0; final proof below uses the supported runtime.
- **Real fixed product flow:** reviewed working-tree build on Node **26.12.1**, PostgreSQL **18.6**; no mocked transport or storage. Same request: obstruction refused, obstruction removed, retry returned `status: restored`. The retained Workboard card and store UUID matched; the new anchor pointed at a verified fresh namespace; original namespace survived; SQLite audit AUTOINCREMENT high-watermark **5000** and exact current update-history rows were preserved. Real `workboard list --json` returned the card, and the restored Gateway reached `/readyz` ready. All task-owned children joined. **89.36 seconds**. Workboard has no PostgreSQL identity sequence; the explicit allocation oracle is the SQLite companion store, not an invented PG sequence.
- **Committed regression path:** the extended existing PostgreSQL backup integration case is RED on unchanged production base at the intended `EEXIST`, then GREEN with the fix. It retains binary/large-integer canonical data and exact-state restore checks. New test growth: **12 lines**, separately allocated; no additional fixture/boot. Base wrapper 65.49 seconds; fixed backup case 19.44 seconds.
- **Affected siblings:** **36 tests passed in 3 files**, including SQLite generation/refusal, interrupted-publication retention, current-history preservation, live authority, local credential, and native update retry/config recovery controls. Full fixed wrapper **284.36 seconds**, including worker preparation. Targeted production-core and infra-test typechecks, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, line-budget ratchet, docs inventory, and whitespace checks passed.
- **Build:** supported `pnpm build:runtime` completed, **97.48 seconds**. This ran on the reviewed prepublication working-tree snapshot, not a subsequently created Git commit. The tested production owner SHA-256 is `7e92a49f9e88e1b9621fc37a1af868b73fc5a9ccdca157b5f8b9f749ee66f96a`; both build stamps bind the selected base plus their recorded input signatures. Current main `02b28c9d0b5ae329b07a1e758c9cfca8f1798bca` has byte-identical restore-owner source to the selected base. The published production owner at `ef4f16f4c253f84d951d79bc26d3904bd034bb49` was independently fetched and matches the tested SHA-256 above.
- **Fresh independent Auto Review:** complete local candidate against `9c22cf86f68b34269e49a25a95827c1c23b52ce0`, P0–P2, source context for restore/backup/native CLI and SQLite controls: **scoped-clean, zero findings**. Source assessment; reviewer did not rerun tests.
- **New mature published-data compatibility proof (not latest stable):** normal npm installation of exact `openclaw@2026.10.7` passed the unchanged seven-day age policy; the installed binary reports `2026.10.7 (157d8c2)`, matching first-party tag commit `157d8c2bc3ea2fa183afdc11088e69690bf8e64e`. Its real Gateway created a durable session, persisted an injected transcript without inference (`runStarted:false`), and wrote `USER.md` through its RPC. Published SQLite schemas **state 20 / agent 25** upgraded through the candidate native protocol to **37 / 39**; the candidate Gateway loaded the same transcript and retained timezone, workspace, auth selection and exact user-file bytes. Native rollback restored **20 / 25**; the actual published Gateway restarted and read the retained transcript and settings. After re-upgrade, a real SQLite Workboard card was ported to PostgreSQL, the synthetic obstruction refused publication, and the same receipt successfully retried after removing only that obstruction. Final candidate Gateway history, Workboard rows/store UUID, original PostgreSQL namespace and settings remained intact. **148.95 seconds; all children joined; no mocked storage/transport, no model calls.** The released Gateway briefly advertised `agent-database-inspection-pending`; the harness followed that specific retryable readiness response before checking history. The first harness attempt stopped at that readiness response and is not counted as a passing run.
- **Latest-stable published-data compatibility — PASS:** exact published **2026.10.9 (8b18b55)**, installed from npm in a disposable prefix, then the already-built candidate at the unchanged production SHA-256 above. Node **26.12.1**, PostgreSQL **18.6**, **178.49 seconds**. The actual released Gateway created a persistent session/transcript without inference (`runStarted:false`) and wrote `USER.md`. Native candidate `update migrate --backup-root` upgraded published SQLite schemas **state 20 / agent 25 → 37 / 39**. The candidate Gateway read the transcript. Native `update restore --backup-root` restored **20 / 25**, and the actual published 2026.10.9 Gateway restarted and read the original transcript. Timezone, workspace setting, auth selection and exact user-file bytes survived each boundary. Re-upgrade and native `update finish` succeeded. Then actual `database port --family workboard --to postgres` ported a SQLite card; a task-owned publication obstruction refused recovery; removing only that obstruction let the **same persisted receipt** retry successfully. Final candidate Gateway history, PG card/store UUID, original namespace and settings matched. All children joined. The released history endpoint briefly returned its advertised retryable `agent-database-inspection-pending`; the harness waited only for that specific response. This exercises installed-release/native-upgrade/native-rollback/released-Gateway compatibility, not a managed package-swap installer.
- **Narrow, human-authorized installation exception:** the ordinary seven-day age guard initially refused the Oct. 29 release. The requester subsequently authorized test-only exceptions for **only `openclaw@2026.10.9` and `@openclaw/ai@2026.10.9`**. Before installation, registry ownership, expected SHA-512 integrity, official release tag/build identity and registry SLSA provenance were checked. Both provenance subjects bind first-party publication tooling commit `ee860ffb31039c05bacacd3387c05649c0ea7033` (merged official [#187565](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187565)); Git ancestry to current official main was verified. The product build separately binds release commit `8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41` and official release [#187583](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187583); that maintenance-release commit was not falsely treated as a main ancestor. Exact top-level manifest pins and every matching lock entry/integrity were checked **before executing the released binary**. `npm audit signatures` passed: **493 verified registry signatures, 150 verified attestations**. All other dependencies retained the seven-day guard; existing install-script approvals were unchanged (unapproved scripts were not run). No global/workspace config or persistent exception file was changed. Disposable installation removed after proof; selected lock/build metadata and sanitized results retained locally. The earlier accidentally reconciled prefix stayed quarantined and supplied no proof.

<details>
<summary>Latest-stable proof commands and sanitized terminal result</summary>

Task-owned Node 26.12.1 and npm cache were used. Only the two literal additional package names were exempted, with exact version pins; existing Codex exclusions were preserved:

```sh
npm install --prefix .openclaw/tmp/pg-rollback-proof/stable-2026.10.9-authorized-exact \
  --save-exact --omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund --min-release-age=7 \
  --min-release-age-exclude='@openai/codex' --min-release-age-exclude='@openai/codex-*' \
  --min-release-age-exclude='openclaw' --min-release-age-exclude='@openclaw/ai' \
  openclaw@2026.10.9 @openclaw/ai@2026.10.9
npm audit signatures --prefix .openclaw/tmp/pg-rollback-proof/stable-2026.10.9-authorized-exact
.openclaw/tmp/pg-rollback-proof/tools/node-v26.12.1-linux-x64/bin/node \
  .openclaw/tmp/pg-rollback-proof/published-latest-proof.mjs latest-upgrade-1
```

The local harness invoked the installed public CLI directly for the released baseline and `pnpm openclaw` for the built candidate; it asserted produced state, not CLI exit codes alone:

```text
EXACT_RELEASE_PIN_VERIFIED version=2026.10.9 commit=8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41
published Gateway ready; session.runStarted=false; injected transcript and user file persisted
published schemas: state=20 agent=25
candidate-upgrade: exit=0; candidate Gateway ready; schemas: state=37 agent=39
candidate-rollback: exit=0; published Gateway ready; original transcript/settings read back
PUBLISHED_BASELINE_UPGRADE_ROLLBACK_DATA_SETTINGS_PASS
candidate-reupgrade: exit=0; candidate-accept: exit=0
port-workboard: exit=0; capture-pg-update: exit=0
pg-restore-obstructed: exit=1 (expected publication refusal); original anchor unchanged
pg-restore-retry: exit=0 (same receipt, only owned obstruction removed)

ALL_PROOF_CHILDREN_JOINED
```

No model calls, live Team state, cloud resources or credentials were used. Production source/head and maturity policy remained unchanged by this proof.

</details>

- **Exact-head CI:** `ef4f16f4c253f84d951d79bc26d3904bd034bb49` passed all three PostgreSQL conformance shards and the [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41263453372/job/124726369419). No code or head change was made for this new proof. Current main `72cab24990b3746574ac83e3d73c79530b8cc198` retains byte-identical pre-fix restore-owner source.

Simplification: production **+2 net lines**, regression **+12**; one allocation decision stays with its existing owner. Existing conservative retention of earlier recovery preparations is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(agents): apply_patch reports earlier hunks it already applied whe…
prs.body:
# fix(agents): apply_patch reports earlier hunks it already applied when a later hunk fails

Related: #127496 (follow-up to #160409)

## What Problem This Solves

#160409 made `apply_patch` check every update hunk before writing, so a missing update target or a context mismatch now rejects the patch with no file changes. Failures that only appear while writing still leave earlier hunks applied, and the error names only the hunk that failed:

- `Add File` onto a path that already exists
- `Delete File` of a missing path
- `Move to` onto an existing file, or a move whose source removal fails after the destination was written
- I/O errors, or cancellation between hunks

The model gets a single error and has no way to tell that earlier files were created, changed, or deleted. It then resends the whole patch from an outdated view of the files.

## User Impact

When a patch fails partway through, the tool error now lists the changes that already landed, using the same `A`/`M`/`D` markers as the success summary, and tells the model to re-read those files before retrying:

```
Cannot create existing.txt: the file already exists. Use "*** Update File: existing.txt" to change it, or delete it earlier in the same patch.
The patch stopped partway; these earlier changes were applied and not rolled back:
A created.txt
M notes.txt
Re-read these files before retrying, and do not resend the hunks already applied.
```

A failure on the first write leaves the error text unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

#127496 offers two options: compensate (roll back with an undo journal) or keep the earlier changes and report them. This PR takes the reporting option:

- It adds no new state, journal, or backend preconditions. #122933 stalled while trying to model those preconditions across the host and sandbox backends.
- It follows the repo guidance to prefer cheap mechanisms, such as best-effort recording with a warning, and to accept rare, visible, recoverable edge cases.
- Rollback can still be built on top of this later if maintainers decide on it. Even then, a rollback that fails would need this same partial-effect report.

Details:

- The error object is kept and only its message is extended. `AbortError`, `ToolInputError`, and the host-root-escape markers survive, so cancellation handling and the containment hint behave as before.
- If a move writes the destination but fails to remove the source, the destination is reported as `A` (a new copy), not `M` (a finished move).
- The summary type and formatting moved to `src/agents/apply-patch-summary.ts`, because `apply-patch.ts` would otherwise go over the 700-line `max-lines` cap. Its one external type import moved with it.

Not changed: there is still no rollback, and earlier hunks stay on disk. If maintainers decide rollback is required, that is a separate follow-up.

## Evidence

New `src/agents/apply-patch.partial-commit.test.ts`, run through the public tool boundary:

| Case | Upstream main | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Add + update succeed, then an add onto an existing file fails (real host fs) | only the failing hunk's error | error also lists `A created.txt`, `M notes.txt` |
| Cancellation after the first write (sandbox bridge) | `AbortError`, no applied paths | still `AbortError`, lists `M a.txt` |
| Move: destination written, source removal fails | no applied paths | lists `A new.txt` |
| Failure on the first hunk | unchanged message | unchanged message |

- `pnpm test src/agents/apply-patch.partial-commit.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 4 passed, about 45 s on a cold shard (mostly worker preparation); the tests themselves take under 40 ms. Without the source change, 3 of the 4 fail.
- `pnpm test src/agents/apply-patch*.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (all 9 apply_patch test files): 158 passed, 2 skipped.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` on the touched files: clean.

prs.title: fix(sessions): keep binding-scoped DM rows in cleanup --fix-dm-scope
prs.body:
## Summary
`openclaw sessions cleanup --fix-dm-scope` retires live DM sessions that routing still uses. When the global `session.dmScope` is `main` (the default) but a route binding overrides it, for example `{ agentId: "main", match: { channel: "telegram" }, session: { dmScope: "per-channel-peer" } }`, every inbound Telegram DM is routed to a peer-keyed session such as `agent:main:telegram:direct:123456789`. The cleanup flag treats that row as a stale leftover from an earlier dmScope setting and plans `retire-dm-scope` for it; applying the flag removes the row from SQLite and moves its transcript to a deleted archive, so the next DM from that peer starts a fresh conversation.

## Root cause
`src/config/sessions/cleanup-service.ts` decides staleness from the key shape and the global `session.dmScope` only:

```ts
// before
if ((params.cfg.session?.dmScope ?? "main") !== "main") {
  return false;
}
...
return (
  (parts.length === 2 && parts[0] === "direct" && Boolean(parts[1])) ||
  (parts.length === 3 && Boolean(parts[0]) && parts[1] === "direct" && Boolean(parts[2])) ||
  (parts.length === 4 && Boolean(parts[0]) && Boolean(parts[1]) && parts[2] === "direct" && Boolean(parts[3]))
);
```

Routing (`resolveAgentRoute` in `src/routing/resolve-route.ts`) applies `binding.session.dmScope` for the matched binding (`choose(matched.binding.agentId, matchedBy, matched.binding.session)`), so a binding-level `per-peer`, `per-channel-peer` or `per-account-channel-peer` scope keeps producing exactly these key shapes even though the global scope is `main`. The cleanup check never looks at bindings.

## Fix
The key shape already names the scope that produced it. The check maps the shape to that scope and keeps the row when a route binding for the same agent sets that scope, matching the channel for channel-scoped keys and the account (or `*`) for account-scoped keys, using the same lowercase channel comparison routing uses:

```ts
// after
const dmScope =
  parts.length === 2 && parts[0] === "direct" && parts[1]
    ? "per-peer"
    : parts.length === 3 && parts[0] && parts[1] === "direct" && parts[2]
      ? "per-channel-peer"
      : parts.length === 4 && parts[0] && parts[1] && parts[2] === "direct" && parts[3]
        ? "per-account-channel-peer"
        : undefined;
if (!dmScope) {
  return false;
}
return !listRouteBindings(params.cfg).some(
  (binding) =>
    binding.session?.dmScope === dmScope &&
    normalizeAgentId(binding.agentId) === normalizeAgentId(params.targetAgentId) &&
    (dmScope === "per-peer" ||
      normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(binding.match.channel) === parts[0]) &&
    (dmScope !== "per-account-channel-peer" ||
      binding.match.accountId?.trim() === "*" ||
      normalizeAccountId(binding.match.accountId) === parts[1]),
);
```

## Why this is the right boundary
`isMainScopeStaleDirectSessionKey` is the single predicate behind both the dry-run preview and the applied retirement (local and Gateway-delegated cleanup), so fixing it covers every path that reaches `--fix-dm-scope`. Bindings are read with the existing `listRouteBindings` owner. Rows with no binding override, rows on other channels or accounts, and rows whose binding belongs to a different agent are still retired exactly as before. When a more specific binding without an override would win routing for some peers, the row is kept rather than retired; keeping a row is recoverable, retiring a live one is not. The concepts doc paragraph for `--fix-dm-scope` now states that binding-scoped rows are kept.

## Verification
- New `src/config/sessions/cleanup-service.fix-dm-scope.test.ts` seeds five direct rows in a real SQLite store and runs `runSessionsCleanup` with `dryRun` and `fixDmScope`. It asserts that rows produced by a channel binding (`per-channel-peer`, mixed-case `Telegram`), an account binding (`per-account-channel-peer`, `slack`/`work`) and a `per-peer` binding are kept, while a row whose binding belongs to another agent and a row on an unbound account are retired. It fails on main (all five retired) and passes with the patch; I ran it both ways with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- `oxfmt --check` is clean on the changed files.
- Local tsgo and oxlint were not run per the contributor workflow for this batch; GitHub Actions covers them.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: `openclaw sessions cleanup --fix-dm-scope` planned to retire `agent:main:telegram:direct:123456789`, the session a `per-channel-peer` route binding routes every Telegram DM from that peer to, because the global `session.dmScope` is `main`.
Real environment tested: Real Gateway started from source (`node --import tsx src/entry.ts gateway run`, token auth, loopback, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `HOME`), config with no `session.dmScope` and one route binding `{ "agentId": "main", "match": { "channel": "telegram" }, "session": { "dmScope": "per-channel-peer" } }`. The session row was created through the real `sessions.create` Gateway method and given history with `chat.inject`; cleanup ran through the real `openclaw sessions cleanup` CLI, which delegates to the running Gateway. Pristine main 0e24b7e5953 first, then this patch on a fresh state dir with the same config and calls. The production `resolveAgentRoute` was called with the same config to show which key a Telegram DM routes to. Nothing was stubbed.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `openclaw gateway call sessions.create --params '{"key":"agent:main:telegram:direct:123456789"}'`, `openclaw gateway call chat.inject --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:telegram:direct:123456789","message":"..."}'`, then `openclaw sessions cleanup --dry-run --fix-dm-scope`; after the patch also `sessions.create` for an unbound `agent:main:discord:direct:42` and the same cleanup command.
Evidence after fix:
```
# Routing for the same config (production resolveAgentRoute)
inbound telegram DM 123456789 routes to: agent:main:telegram:direct:123456789 (matchedBy=binding.account, dmScope=per-channel-peer)

# BEFORE (pristine main 0e24b7e5953)
$ openclaw sessions cleanup --dry-run --fix-dm-scope
Maintenance mode: enforce
Entries: 1 -> 0 (remove 1)
Would retire stale direct DM sessions: 1
Planned session actions:
| retire-dm-scope | agent:main:teleg...456789 | just now | gpt-6-astra | visibility:shared owner:gateway-owner id:15f42609-... |
Total: 0 kept, 1 pruned

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
$ openclaw sessions cleanup --dry-run --fix-dm-scope
Maintenance mode: enforce
Entries: 1 -> 1 (remove 0)
Would retire stale direct DM sessions: 0
Planned session actions:
| keep | agent:main:teleg...456789 | just now | gpt-6-astra | visibility:shared owner:gateway-owner id:267f3c08-... |
Total: 1 kept, 0 pruned

# AFTER, plus an unbound leftover row agent:main:discord:direct:42
$ openclaw sessions cleanup --dry-run --fix-dm-scope
| retire-dm-scope | agent:main:disco...ect:42 | just now | gpt-6-astra | ... |
| keep            | agent:main:teleg...456789 | 1m ago   | gpt-6-astra | ... |
Total: 1 kept, 1 pruned
```

prs.title: fix(memory): rebuild remote workspace indexes through the Gateway
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes remote workspace memory maintenance that cannot rebuild the Gateway index through the standalone memory CLI. That CLI process does not own the running Gateway's registered remote file access, so it can inspect local files instead of the Harness workspace.

## User Impact

Operators can run `openclaw gateway call memory.index --params '{"agentId":"main"}' --timeout 180000` to rebuild with the current Gateway configuration and remote workspace binding. Workspace files stay on the Harness; the derived index stays on the Gateway. The method requires `operator.admin` and may call the configured embedding provider.

## Why This Change Was Made

The memory-core plugin already owns indexing and remote file discovery. This adds an administrative Gateway entry point that reuses those owners. It carries the caller's live authority through asynchronous preparation, embedding dispatch/retry boundaries, and the existing database publication guard. Disconnection, revocation, or configuration replacement prevents later host-issued embedding calls and index publication. The result uses the native asynchronous status helper, so built-in database reads run in their worker and PostgreSQL returns aggregate counts. Status and repair guidance direct remote workspace maintenance to the Gateway.

This is a general split-storage maintenance gap exposed by the OCE + Strands Box integration. It is not a Box syscall defect and does not require a Box-specific memory implementation. No schema, storage format, embedding default, or network policy changes are included.

The existing manager and publication worker still own indexing, writes, and cleanup. The admitted request/connection cancellation signal is composed with the inline embedding operation's existing timeout signal. An existing retry backoff may finish before authority is rejected, but no later host dispatch is admitted. Already accepted provider work cannot be retracted; provider-owned asynchronous batches retain their existing API, which does not expose a cancellation signal.

## Evidence

The PostgreSQL path now discards a cancelled or revoked operation's private TEMP stage even when another borrower keeps the same database connection alive. Only `database.stage.discard` bypasses the expired request-maintenance assertion. The live database, captured Agent owner, caller guard and worker connection still authorize cleanup; publication remains refused.

- Real PostgreSQL regression: both disconnect and revocation leave a TEMP table on the original implementation, and both pass with this change. The test retains a co-borrower, verifies the same backend PID, unchanged published source rows, zero remaining TEMP stages, caller-owner rejection and preservation of the original failure. The baseline leak run preceded an additional caller-refusal assertion; these are not byte-identical test snapshots.
- All 95 directly changed cases pass: 63 embedding-policy, 2 PostgreSQL cleanup, 15 workspace-file, 3 paused-deadline and 12 Gateway SDK cases. An additional 33 conformance-runner / native-worker registry cases and the concrete shared-fixture cold-status consumer pass (129 distinct cases total). Native formatting, scoped typed lint and the memory-core production, extension-test and tooling typecheck lanes pass with the locked dependency graph. No hooks or package checks were disabled.
- Fresh independent source review traced the cleanup permission to the connection-owned stage map and found no remaining actionable authority issue. This was a separate read-only subagent review; the previously unavailable local autoreview helper did not produce a validated machine report.
- Test setup now initializes only its owned database before plugin registration; the workspace-file suite initializes its own per-case state. The shared cold-state fixture remains cold for other consumers. The initial broader fixture proposal was rejected after its status-only consumer failed, and the final narrower change passed that regression. This is test initialization, not a production database-admission change. All 41 consumers of the shared fixture were enumerated, but only the directly affected suites and the identified cold-status risk were rerun.
- The installed OCE qualification uses the existing approved older OpenClaw runtime plus its compatibility backports; those results do not substitute for current-main PostgreSQL proof. No OpenClaw version pin is changed here.

Draft only. The independent-helper merge hold remains; no merge or readiness promotion is requested. Fresh installed OCE + Strands Box acceptance is in progress on a new image and will be reported separately.

prs.title: fix(macos): chat accent updates after Control UI changes
prs.body:
Related: #128922

## What Problem This Solves

The Mac chat window does not refresh the Gateway-wide saved accent (`ui.prefs.accent`) when only chat is open. The existing per-profile accent path already updates separately; Gateway-wide changes can leave chat on its old color.

## Why This Change Was Made

The long-lived Mac control connection reads Gateway config on connection and `config.changed`, resolving the saved Gateway preference before `ui.seamColor`. The Talk Mode config reader uses the same precedence so it cannot overwrite the chat color. Profile appearance retains separate inherit, theme, and color states, so an explicit theme choice cannot fall through to a Gateway color. The shared hex decoder used by iOS remains available with its prior result. Superseded reads and replaced Gateway leases remain fenced.

## User Impact

Chat can pick up a Gateway-wide saved accent without opening Mac Settings or Talk Mode, while a personal profile accent continues to win. Normal shared-token Control UI connections receive an owner profile and save Appearance changes through `users.prefs.set`; this PR does not claim that those edits exercise the Gateway-wide path.

prs.title: fix: preserve literal Windows task environment values
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: generated Windows Gateway task scripts change environment values containing carets, exclamation marks, or quotes before the Gateway process receives them.

## User Impact

User impact: newly generated Windows task launchers preserve literal environment settings, including quoted values and surrounding whitespace. Existing installed scripts keep their legacy recovery behavior and remain recognizable during managed repair, including their previous command/cwd bang escaping; normal service reinstallation regenerates the launcher. No configuration or scheduler-policy changes are introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The task script now owns its delayed-expansion setting and uses SET-specific escaping rather than inserting carets inside quoted values. Readback recognizes that same literal format, while retaining legacy installed-script parsing. The existing CLI-shim caller uses the same serialization owner.

## Evidence

- Real native Windows / Node 24.22.1: the production renderer and encoder write a temporary CMD script which launches Node through the system CMD. Exact child environment, cwd, and argv match with inherited delayed expansion both off and on; a synthetic quote/metacharacter payload cannot create its marker file. Includes percent variables/batch parameters, carets, bangs, embedded quotes, shell operators, brackets, whitespace, an empty NODE_OPTIONS clear, and representable Unicode.
- The same native regression fails on the exact base (child exit 255); the repaired version exits 0 and passes both recovery and effective readback.
- Parser contracts: 13 passing cases, including legacy recovery and rejection of ambiguous/nonliteral assignments.
- Legacy upgrade audit regressions cover ordinary previously generated scripts and static old `^!`-escaped argv/cwd (including caret-bangs), plus custom-script negative controls. Two independent P2 review findings were reproduced and repaired rather than waived.
- Final focused proof: **25 passed** (13 parser contracts, 11 task-audit scenarios, one real-CMD matrix exercising both inherited expansion settings). Production core and services-test typechecks pass. Type-aware lint (293 rules) and formatting pass on all ten changed files.
- Independent manual and canonical full-context P0–P3 final-byte reviews are clean after both reproduced P2 compatibility findings were repaired; validated canonical status `scoped-clean`, exit 0, all ten source/test hashes unchanged. CI will validate the published head separately.
- Local broad consumer runs were not all green: 26 Windows-host platform/path-case failures matched exact-base replay. A further unchanged Darwin dangling-file-symlink fixture fails `EPERM`; a standalone Node control without repository imports reproduces that host limitation. No assertions were weakened or tests skipped to conceal these results. Native Windows CLI-shim and CMD/CIM redirection suites passed.
- Scope limitation: no real task registration, daemon installation, or live Gateway changes were performed. Launcher encoding/code-page support and existing empty-value/PATH policy are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(terminal): opening a terminal from an agent conversation fails with "no explicit owner" in multi-agent fleets
prs.body:
Related: #142789

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: opening the operator terminal from an agent's conversation fails with "Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner" in multi-agent fleets (`agents.ownership: "explicit"`) when the request identifies the conversation but not the agent.

## User Impact

User impact: in multi-agent fleets, a terminal opened from an agent conversation now starts in that agent's workspace instead of failing.

The owner is only inferred when the session key names its agent (`agent:<id>:…`). These requests are still rejected before a shell starts, with the same guidance as before:

- a session key without an agent prefix, even when `agents.defaults.systemAgent` is configured;
- a request with no owner at all, e.g. an agentless dashboard view;
- mismatched agent/session pairs, unknown agents and sandboxed agents.

Opening a terminal from a fully agentless view is out of scope here, so that part of the linked issue still fails closed. That is why this PR is `Related` rather than closing the issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

`terminal.open` ran launch policy with only `agentId` before it looked at `sessionKey`. With no implicit default owner, a session-scoped request was rejected before its owner was resolved. The Control UI panel sends `sessionKey` and sends `agentId` only when the host has one (`ui/src/components/terminal/terminal-panel-session-boot.ts`).

For agent-qualified session keys, the handler now resolves the owner with the existing shared resolver (`resolveRequestedSessionAgentId`) and then applies the unchanged launch policy. The existing post-await revalidation stays in place.

Unqualified keys keep the existing launch default. The shared resolver would map them to a compatibility owner (the system agent in explicit fleets), and #123429 deliberately kept terminals from defaulting to the system agent, because workspace and sandbox policy belong to the selected agent.

## Evidence

Current head: `75158c8cf5756658a4dad5ecf0f050dc46e51262`, synchronized with main `27e7e5ee87ccbc1cfa11b7e0b79d78bbf503280f`.

The October 25 conflict was confined to `terminal.test.ts`: main consolidated test helpers and timer cleanup in #183159, including cases already moved into this PR's ownership suite. The resolution keeps main's retained cases and assertions, keeps ownership coverage in `terminal.session-owner.test.ts`, and drops the now-unused `openOwnedTerminal` helper. The production handler, ownership suite, and shared fixture are unchanged from the previously passing head `ac41ebfac4`. Gateway-local terminal restrictions, monotonic deadlines, and post-await authorization checks remain intact.

**Local validation on the merged source:**

- 136 tests pass across five files: terminal RPC (29), session ownership (12), launch policy, final node-dispatch authority, and terminal session management.
- Core production types and the `core-test-gateway-methods` test type graph pass.
- Targeted lint, formatting for all five PR files, and the PR diff check against main pass.
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` succeeds with Node 24.22.1 and repository-pinned pnpm 12.15.0, both managed by mise.
- Independent read-only source review found no actionable issues and confirmed that the retained upstream tests and assertions are preserved. This is a mechanical conflict repair; no successful CLI autoreview is claimed (the earlier CLI attempts were unavailable).

Per-file timing for `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`:

| Test file | Local wall time | Current-head CI seconds |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `terminal.test.ts` (29 cases) | 104.03 s | Pending |
| `terminal.session-owner.test.ts` (12 cases) | 15.07 s | Pending |

The first command includes staging the pinned Bun runtime and rebuilding worker artifacts (69.82 s for the compiler phase). These are whole-command wall times, not test-case time. The remaining three files pass 95 cases in one focused command (18.21 s reported by the wrapper).

**Hosted CI.** [Run 40191768368](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40191768368) is running for `75158c8cf57`. The last passing run is [39710959431](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39710959431), at `ac41ebfac4cfd5ab7c70c884f2c0db0788b877cc`; that is prior-head evidence.

The real Gateway proof below is retained from `ac41ebfac4`, not rerun on this head.

**Isolated real Gateway at the prior head `ac41ebfac4`, before/after.** Setup:

- explicit fleet with `main` and `research`, each with its own workspace, and `agents.defaults.systemAgent` set to `research`;
- `gateway.terminal.enabled`, token auth on loopback;

prs.title: fix(feishu): accept the documented markdown table mode
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes gateway startup rejecting Feishu's documented `markdown.tables` option and applies the selected table mode across sends, replies, presentations, and previews.

## User Impact

Channel and account table settings are accepted, including the delivering/default account. Ordinary `off` table messages settle as authored rich-text posts. In `off`, presentations keep controls and show literal rows in card text and live previews. When idle close reuses a posted answer, missing reasoning follows it without duplicating it.

Accepted-prefix failures keep their receipts and do not replay accepted content. The unchanged post renderer still draws authored Markdown tables as grids.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu's strict schema gains the shared table option and keeps the legacy `markdown.mode` and `markdown.tableMode`. Formatting-aware delivery converts whole logical tables before chunking. Core's formatted text send in `deliver-channel.ts` now calls a channel's `beforeSendAttempt` hook before it records the send as started, so if the process stops during Feishu's first runtime load, recovery sends the reply once instead of losing it. Presentations and reasoning degrade undrawable block-mode tables to readable lists. For `off`, display-only delimiter escaping leaves authored fallback and deduplication text alone. The PR also declares `block` as Feishu's table default (see Table default).

The generated channel baseline gains two entries, `channels.feishu.markdown.tables` and `channels.feishu.accounts.*.markdown.tables`. Core and plugin counts stay unchanged. [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f659a3576b1/AGENTS.md#L96) permits narrow source-verified exceptions with a reason. This exception is not maintainer approval.

## Evidence

### Upgrade proof

Published stable `2026.10.2` (`b8952d477f0c`) seeded channel `markdown.mode: native` and `markdown.tableMode: ascii`, an account's `mode: escape` and `tableMode: simple`, and two accounts without Markdown settings. The proof head (`effbf8c7a8ab`) used that state, main (`29fc232d40be`) a copy. Both used fresh detached worktrees and separately packed Feishu plugins.

| Check | Stable | Proof head | Upstream main |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Legacy config validates, keys and overrides read back unchanged | Yes | Yes, before and after migration | Yes, before and after migration |
| Feishu config object on disk | Seed | Byte-identical | Byte-identical |
| Stored session loads with the same key and ID, and a label update survives restart | Created and patched here | Yes | Yes |
| Documented `markdown.tables` at channel and account scope | Rejected, exit 1 | Accepted, all four values | Rejected, exit 1 |
| Account override wins, unset accounts inherit the channel value | Key rejected | Yes | Key rejected |

Both builds refuse the schema 24 agent database (Gateway exit 78) until `openclaw doctor --fix` migrates it to 26. Repair and shutdown then exit 1 with `ERR_SPAWN_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE`. The cause is undiagnosed and both databases stay readable. This is compatibility evidence, not a clean upgrade. Replacement was manual, not the published updater. Credentials were synthetic and Feishu accounts and transports disabled. Only the Feishu config object is byte-identical. Maintenance changed other config. The diff has no `src/state` change or database migration.

### Table default

Upgrade proof resolves `code` on stable and main and `block` on the proof head for unconfigured or legacy-only accounts. Legacy keys do not select the mode. In `auto`, stable and main route ordinary pipe-bordered tables to raw cards (`markdown.ts:25-27`, `outbound.ts:253-262`, `reply-dispatcher.ts:1289-1293` at main `29fc232d40be`, same logic at stable). Before captures show native grids. `block` retains them. Other modes convert before routing (`outbound-text-plan.ts:48-49`). Head lines use `948b2088919`.

Against main, standalone pipe-less and one-sided-pipe tables now get cards on `auto` sends and non-streamed replies. In chat text, blockquoted and list-opened tables take posts, but forced-card sends bypass that guard. Main sent these shapes to cards in streams or beside a fence or pipe table. Table messages needing multiple static cards also take posts. These posts use `code` unless fences cannot survive the cut. The five-table limit excludes streams. Direct post sends and edits still resolve `code`. Comments now convert raw rows to `code`. Explicit modes and size/fence safeguards apply.

A `code` default would fence those grids in cards (the `code` row at `outbound.markdown-tables.test.ts:640`, line 662 at `948b2088919`). `block` also drops "Avoid Markdown tables." from Feishu group prompts, even with account `code` or `bullets`, because `src/auto-reply/reply/groups.ts:126-131` reads the plugin default. Telegram and Matrix already declare `block`. Maintainers decide the default.

### Current repair verification

CI tested `cf49e1d3c83` merged with main `0858cc64613`. On that head 88 checks passed, none failed, 49 were skipped and CodeQL was neutral. In `checks-node-changed-1`, `telegram-ingress-coalescing.e2e.test.ts` passed 20 tests, and the shard's seven other targets, six contract tests and a gateway e2e test, passed 115. Locally at `cf49e1d3c83`, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test`, four ratchets and five generated-file check scripts passed, and `extension-feishu` passed 1256 tests.

### Fresh Lark before/after rendering

[Comparison and limits](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-6093982920) cover four byte-identical synthetic fixture pairs through the production send, reply and streaming components with the real SDK. Captures compare plugin source `e7f29073f4dc` with rendering files published at `34f132a1bb49`, not whole deployments, and were not retaken at `effbf8c7a8ab`. Merges after `34f132a1bb49` left `presentation-card.ts`, `card-table-shapes.ts`, `markdown.ts` and `outbound.ts` unchanged, kept the off-mode projection in `streaming-update.ts`, and moved the reasoning formatter and close route into `reasoning-structure.ts` and `table-routing.ts` intact, so the three off-mode rows render through the same code. The idle row's settlement bookkeeping took upstream's latest-settlement shape, so that row rests on the proof head's regression tests, not the captures.

| State | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Off-mode presentation | ![Native table despite off mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff00b807-a9e6-465b-9f63-5829ea331710) | ![Literal rows and retained button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/96bf5ced-1f4e-4375-985f-cf0a9ab4132f) |
| Off-mode answer preview | ![Native answer-preview table](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e54aec3f-9a7c-41a7-886d-145522b8feed) | ![Literal answer-preview rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02c9e642-b5dd-4203-a3cf-87be4de7f7aa) |
| Off-mode reasoning preview | ![Reasoning-table rows missing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/325f6680-67b2-4de6-99f7-a93a0eb9afb1) | ![Reasoning-table rows visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c07ea2c4-df53-4628-9793-8e1946bbf661) |
| Idle reuse of accepted answer | ![Reasoning disappears after idle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4087a562-8abe-4253-8517-ac947981a16c) | ![One answer and separate reasoning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/430c18ca-2774-45cc-9055-44da9e169007) |

Both runs exited 0. Idle settlement adds exactly one reasoning-only post and keeps two actual receipts without replaying the accepted answer. All three dispatcher cases keep byte-identical authored final-post payloads. The button is retained, not clicked. All eight images were verified in the saved comment. The captures used no Gateway, model or mainland Feishu client. Lark still joins adjacent quoted paragraphs in the reasoning preview, not addressed here.

### Historical evidence

Pinned to the commits named, not current-head proof.

- CLI at `dbb422c85a5` (before) and `08c0c469de4` (after). Before, `config validate` rejected `tables` at channel and account scope (exit 1) and `gateway run` refused to start (exit 78). After, validation passed, the Gateway reached ready and shut down with child exit 0, and `doctor --fix --non-interactive` removed no `markdown` key.
- Gateway send RPC at `314ddb95`, HTTPS Feishu stub, real SDK, `renderMode` unset. Accounts resolved `code`, `bullets` and `off` as configured across full, reply and default-account sends, all exit 0.
- Authority proof at `c311d8a5d53` ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-5707888042)), registered sender, production components, real SDK. Allowed sent four of four with every receipt. Revoked after one of four was accepted, kept its receipt and exact content in the partial-delivery envelope, and the claim guard refused the pending terminal rather than replay it.
- Lark client round at `9d52663f11b` and `d0f6e3a3ba0` ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-5689525610)), real SDK, 62 captures. Blockquote and list-opened tables became readable fenced posts, and a mixed message kept both tables.
- Regression tests for schema acceptance, account selection, off-mode finals, comment delivery, block posts, preview dedupe and presentation cards each failed before the fix and passed after.

prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185220

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: People rows, personal groups, owner artwork, warnings, and agent previews lose their last-known presentation when the Gateway disconnects or a saved sidebar reloads.

## User Impact

The sidebar keeps useful context in place while reconnecting, without treating cached activity as a live run or granting cached rows permission to modify sessions. No configuration change or migration is required. Native catalog cold-offline restoration remains outside this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing scoped, bounded display snapshot rather than introducing another state owner. Preserve only admitted display facts, exclude incognito contributions before deriving roster cards, and keep all personal-group preference replacements tied to the complete current navigation owner—not filtered cached membership.

## Evidence

- Real-Gateway Chromium proof in Crabbox: all three scenarios fail on pinned base 3e0c6103 and pass on the final candidate. Covers disconnect grace, offline/cached reload, recovery, a new Gateway PID, People/Person grouping, roster previews/rings, and cached group removal preserving newer preferences.
- Model inference used a synthetic loopback Responses stream; the Gateway, browser, persistence, and reconnection path were real. This is not a production outage or live paid-provider claim.
- Focused snapshot/owner and consumer suites, PR-presentation tests, UI typecheck, scoped lint/format, and whitespace checks passed. Two cached-group menu regressions fail before the preference-owner repair and pass after it.
- Independent structured review and targeted follow-up review completed through P2; the actionable preference-loss finding was repaired and rechecked.
- Hosted CI exposed two test-only type-contract errors. The corrected fixtures pass both owning core test-type graphs and both component-menu regressions; assertions and production code are unchanged. The following hosted run passed those type and UI checks; final-head CI is now running.
- CI ownership now registers the browser suite with the canonical real-Gateway and private-server inventories; 332 planner/workflow tests pass. The normal cold entrypoint prepares private-QA before workers. The inference fixture preserves external proxy routing while exempting only its owned loopback hosts.
- ClawSweeper's cached-group P2 is repaired: accepted removal/reorder now refreshes the existing sanitized display snapshot, while complete navigation preferences remain write input. Both menu regressions fail on the previous head and pass with the repair; the rebuilt real-Gateway suite passes all three scenarios and checks actual DOM removal.
- The independent expected serial inventory now includes the newly registered suite. All three hosted ownership failures reproduce before this one-line consumer update and pass after it; the complete 14-test ownership suite, type-aware lint, and format pass.
- A legacy snapshot-shape regression confirms pre-expansion rows/cards load when the new display fields are absent. The storage version and Gateway config/state contracts are unchanged; no full stable-to-candidate upgrade is claimed.
- Follow-up review found that a second offline reload could resurrect accepted group edits. The existing capture owner now persists its already-admitted cached display model. Two persistence regressions fail before and pass after; 48 focused tests, UI typecheck, both affected test-type graphs, scoped lint/format, and all three rebuilt real-Gateway scenarios pass.
- Current-head hosted CI is running. The prior head had one independently reproduced baseline failure in the startup-resolution-count test; that failed result is retained, not claimed as green or as current-head coverage.
- Inspected before/after captures are embedded below and were delivered in the work session.

Coverage limit: native catalog sections retain placeholders rather than their own cold-offline row projection. This is a separate pre-existing source finding, not covered or repaired by these three live scenarios. Attention payloads, live presence, and operational authority remain intentionally excluded from the saved display.

prs.title: perf(ui): window agent selector rows and identity reads
prs.body:
The first agent-menu opening rendered all 300 options and their avatars. Visiting Agents also requested identities for the entire roster, even with the menu closed. Reuse the shared picker window so only the visible rows, overscan, and active keyboard target mount; identity reads now follow that mounted window and the selected agent.

Search still filters the complete roster. Home/End and arrow navigation materialize their target before updating `aria-activedescendant`; the listbox retains focus. Agent tags, classes, selection callbacks, lazy route boundaries, and fixed avatar geometry remain. The shared picker's default row and trigger markup moved intact to a presentation file; its small-menu selected-row reveal now receives the same geometric correction as the former agent menu.

Settings keeps its existing identity effect, and New Session/palette keep their existing plain-owner notifications. No new effect, cache, timer, controller, or copied identity list was added. The Agents detail owner only ensures its selected agent. A direct selected-agent lookup also removes the outgoing draft's repeated full-roster filter allocation. Generic deferred teardown was not justified by the source-mapped evidence and is unchanged.

## Proof

Qualification uses 300 synthetic agents, six first-visit routes (Agents, Advanced, Plugin Settings, Model Providers, Channels, About), standalone first menu open, and navigation through first menu open. The prescribed matrix is 20 serial base/head/base triplets per cell, Chromium 1×/4× and WebKit, desktop/mobile. Same-byte A/A controls identify host noise. Traces are separate; no WebKit CPU claim. Timing acceptance is ≤5% median regression with p95 holding, or further samples resolving a flagged cell. Targets are ≤50 ms / ≤200 ms route tasks at 1×/4×.

**Qualification is still running; auto-merge is not armed.** The current 4× desktop first-open cell cuts CPU median/p95 from 467/505 to 226/242 ms and input-to-commit from 417/443 to 185/198 ms. Mounted rows and avatars fall from 300 to 15; no head sample has a ≥50 ms opening task. Combined-flow median/p95 falls from 1,185/1,317 to 846/867 ms. Eight desktop 4× cells and the first three mobile cells are complete; remaining mobile, 1× and WebKit cells are in progress. The four flagged desktop routes also have ten additional triplets: Advanced/About headline tails do not repeat, Plugin Settings CPU/readiness hold, and Model Providers' small tail increase is below the identical-base control's increase. Full final numbers will replace this interim paragraph before landing.

The remaining observed route maximum is 289 ms on desktop Agents. A separate source-mapped trace reports a 252 ms task: 96 ms initial incoming mount plus a 156 ms microtask checkpoint. Cleanup ancestry accounts for 49 ms of the checkpoint, alongside incoming Agents bindings; these overlapping stack buckets must not be summed. File grammar/parser setup accounts for roughly 18 ms of the initial mount. Earlier full AgentFiles deferral increased first-Files readiness substantially and was rejected. Generic teardown deferral would change subscription/write lifetimes without removing the dominant incoming work. This is an attributed target gap, not a claim of an irreducible browser floor.

prs.title: fix(agents): clarify pending child yield guidance
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `sessions_yield` tells a turn to end normally when an earlier child is already pending, even if the current turn still has independent unfinished work.

## User Impact

Agents retain clear guidance to continue their active work after an `already_pending` response, while pending child completions still resume the session as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The response does not create a new yield claim, but that fact does not prove the current turn is finished. The guidance now distinguishes the child wait from the current turn and keeps the existing claim and lifecycle behavior unchanged. The public tool reference now carries the same qualification.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(pairing): pairing list and approve print only "The CLI command failed." instead of the reason
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw pairing list` and `openclaw pairing approve` print only "The CLI command failed. For help, run `openclaw doctor`." for every input problem, so users never see why, for example when no chat DM pairing channel is configured or a pairing code doesn't match.

## User Impact

User impact: pairing commands now print the actual reason and the next step, such as "use openclaw devices approve instead" or "No pending pairing request found for code …. Run openclaw pairing list --channel telegram". Exit codes and `--json` output are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pairing command threw plain `Error` for its input checks. The root failure handler treats plain errors as unexpected and replaces them with the generic line, while `--json` showed the real message. The checks now use the existing `throwExpectedCliError` helper, like logs, devices and exec-approvals, so the message is printed as-is. No wording or behavior changes beyond that.

Related: #182614 (pairing approve "fails silently" in Docker). #177999 adds `pairing dismiss` in the same file with the same helper.

## Evidence

Before/after output captured on a build of `main` at 7b29a23 on Linux, Node 24.22.2, fresh state directory with no channels configured. Tests were rerun on the new base c1efa8bc31 (no changes to the pairing files between the two).

Before:
```
$ openclaw pairing list
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
$ openclaw pairing approve ABC123
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
$ openclaw pairing approve telegram ABC123
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
$ openclaw pairing list --json   # the reason was only visible here
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "No chat DM pairing channels are configured. To approve a TUI or device request, use openclaw devices approve instead." } }
```

After (same build plus this change):
```
$ openclaw pairing list
No chat DM pairing channels are configured. To approve a TUI or device request, use openclaw devices approve instead.
$ openclaw pairing approve ABC123
Usage: openclaw pairing approve <channel> <code> (or: openclaw pairing approve --channel <channel> <code>)
$ openclaw pairing approve telegram ABC123
No pending pairing request found for code "ABC123". Run openclaw pairing list --channel telegram to list pending requests.
$ openclaw pairing list --channel telegram --account ' '
--account must not be blank
```
All exit 1, as before.

Tests:
- `pnpm test src/cli/pairing-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 13 passed.
- New test "shows the devices redirect in human failure output, not a generic failure" runs the real `formatCliFailureLines` path. It fails on `main` (`expected '[openclaw] The CLI command failed.…' to contain 'No chat DM pairing channels are configured.'`) and passes with the fix. The existing tests only checked the thrown message, which is why they passed while users saw the generic line.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on both files: clean.

Local review: autoreview / local ClawSweeper not run (not available in this environment). Self-reviewed the diff: only the error type changes; messages, control flow and exit codes are the same.
