prs.title: fix(tui): keep multiline local /btw questions off the main turn
prs.body:
## Summary
In local TUI mode (`openclaw chat`, `openclaw terminal`, `openclaw tui --local`), a `/btw` or `/side` question that spans more than one line (typed with Shift+Enter or Ctrl+J) is not run as a side question. It runs as a full main agent turn instead, and the literal `/btw ...` text is written into the session transcript as a user message, so the question the user asked "without changing future session context" becomes permanent session context. Single-line `/btw` works, and the Gateway-backed TUI handles the multiline form correctly.

## Root cause
`src/tui/embedded-backend.ts` detects the side question with its own single-line regex:

```ts
// before
const sideCommand = /^\/(?:btw|side)(?::|\s)+(.*)$/i.exec(opts.message.trim());
const question = !explicitFollowup ? sideCommand?.[1]?.trim() || undefined : undefined;
```

`.` does not match `\n` and `$` is anchored to the end of the whole input, so any question containing a newline fails to match, `question` is `undefined`, and `sendChat` falls through to the normal `agentCommandFromIngress` turn. The TUI client side (`isTuiBtwCommand` in `src/tui/commands.ts`) does recognize the message as `/btw`, so the two halves of local mode disagree. On the Gateway path the shared command registry already preserves multiline `/btw` arguments (`btw` is in `ARGUMENT_PRESERVING_COMMAND_KEYS`, from #176293).

## Fix
Use the text command that `sendChat` already resolves a few lines earlier with the shared `resolveTextCommand` (the same resolver it uses for `/followup` and `/queue`):

```ts
// after
const question = command?.command.key === "btw" ? command.args : undefined;
```

`resolveTextCommand` maps the `/side` alias to `btw`, accepts the `/btw:` colon form, and keeps every line of the argument. `/followup /btw ...` still resolves to `followup`, so it stays a queued followup exactly as before, and a bare `/btw` still yields no question.

## Why this is the right boundary
The embedded backend is the local-mode owner of side-question routing; the bug is a second, divergent parser there. Replacing it with the registry resolver that the Gateway path and the rest of `sendChat` already use leaves one parser for `/btw` and `/side` across both TUI backends. The TUI client classification, the Gateway `chat.send` path, and the side-question runner (`runBtwSideQuestion`) are unchanged.

## Verification
- `src/tui/embedded-backend.test.ts`: the existing "emits side results for local /$command" cases now take the question per row; the `/btw` row uses a multiline question with an indented second line and asserts `runBtwSideQuestion` receives it verbatim, `agentCommandFromIngress` is not called, and `chat.side_result` carries the full question. The `/btw` row fails on pristine main and passes with the patch; the full file passes with the patch (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/tui/embedded-backend.test.ts`).
- `oxfmt --check` clean on both changed files.
- Local tsgo and oxlint were not run per the contributor workflow for this batch; GitHub Actions covers them.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: In local TUI mode a multiline `/btw` side question ran as a full main agent turn and was persisted into the session transcript instead of being answered as a side result.
Real environment tested: The production local TUI backend `EmbeddedTuiBackend` from source under `node --import tsx`, inside the real CLI command lifecycle (`withCliProcessScope` + `withCliCommandCleanup`, as `openclaw chat` runs), isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, real session store and transcript, real agent runner and real `runBtwSideQuestion`. The only external piece is a loopback OpenAI-compatible HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 configured as provider `loop/mock` that streams a fixed reply. Run on pristine main 72cab24990b and on this patch with identical inputs.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `HOME=$H OPENCLAW_HOME=$H OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$H/.openclaw node --import tsx drive.mts`, where the driver calls `backend.sendChat({ sessionKey: "agent:main:main", message: "Remember: the sky is blue." })`, waits for the final event, then `backend.sendChat({ sessionKey: "agent:main:main", message: "/btw what color is the sky?\nanswer in one word" })`, waits for the final event, and reads `chat.side_result` events plus `backend.loadHistory(...)` user turns.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 72cab24990b)
input: "/btw what color is the sky?\nanswer in one word"
chat.side_result emitted: no
session transcript user turns (2): ["Remember: the sky is blue.","/btw what color is the sky?\nanswer in one word"]

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
input: "/btw what color is the sky?\nanswer in one word"
chat.side_result emitted: yes
side_result.question: "what color is the sky?\nanswer in one word"
session transcript user turns (1): ["Remember: the sky is blue."]
```
Observed result after fix: The multiline `/btw` question is now answered as a side result carrying both lines, and the session transcript keeps only the real conversation turn instead of gaining the side question as a main user message.
What was not tested: The interactive terminal rendering of `openclaw chat` was not driven through a PTY; the backend was driven directly with the same lifecycle the CLI uses. No real hosted model provider was called. The Gateway-backed TUI path is unchanged and was not re-run.

prs.title: fix(ui): reserve transcript media geometry through decode
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Remote transcript images without dimensions shrank their already-admitted preview boxes when decoding completed. That admitted another tall row while its virtual position still used the 120 px estimate, producing an extra **273 px painted correction**. The representative 96-message media scenario reproduces it on the merge base; the census traced its introduction to #186512.

## User Impact

Remote image loading keeps surrounding transcript messages in place. Unknown dimensions use the existing 3:2 preview box, with the full image fitted inside it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reserve the image presentation's box once, using known dimensions or the existing 3:2 fallback, and keep it through decode and display-fact writes. Decoded dimensions remain available for the next admission. Eager cached first paint, decoded-image custody, local paste sizing, and read authorization remain intact. Unknown remote images fit fully inside their reserved frame; they no longer resize surrounding messages on decode.

This is deliberately confined to the media presentation owner. **#183800 overlaps `chat-message-images-solid.tsx`; preserve its windowing changes and this frame-size lifetime when integrating.** No virtualizer, observer scheduling, route, import boundary, or dependency changes.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Production media scenario, Chromium/local, missing dimensions, 10 interleaved base/head pairs plus 20 candidate A/A captures | Extra 273 px correction: **10/10 → 0/30** |
| Reset-bounded maximum layout-shift window, median | **0.13499 → 0.00029** (reference census: approximately 0.082) |
| Cached-image regression | Fails on base because the frame changes from 3:2 to 2:1 after decode; passes with fix, while dimensions and cached pixels remain recorded |
| Focused tests | 2 cached-image tests; all 29 browser geometry cases covered (25 passed first run, 4 updated responsive expectations passed afterward) |
| Focused E2E repair | `chat-image-loading.e2e.test.ts`: known and missing dimensions both pass; stable decode, learned remount size, sibling gap retained |
| Local static checks | UI typecheck, targeted lint/format, production Knip, and diff check pass |
| Production builds and strict performance checks | Startup **89,588 → 89,598 B gzip** (+10 B, within 64 B build variance); CSS **1 request / 34,184 B** unchanged; chat boot **1,272,759 → 1,272,829 B (+70 B)** |
| Independent review | Codex autoreview, P0–P2, full image lifecycle and test context: no actionable findings; followed by equivalent alias/name cleanup for the existing line limit |

All 30 candidate captures passed with no 273 px correction. Candidate A/A median/max shift window: 0.00025 / 0.00066. A fresh build and reproduction of committed head `4609c4d7279` after equivalent lint cleanup also passed without the correction. Final startup growth is within build variance; the 70 B chat growth is below its existing cap and accompanies the measured layout-stability win. CI uses `ci:full` for all UI units, Control UI E2E, browser-extension, and real-Gateway shards. Local browser runs were headless, synthetic-only. The media scenario uses a production build and its synthetic native-HTTP Gateway fixture; no live-provider claim. Geometry capture forces layout reads, so its timing/CPU values are diagnostics, not a latency claim.

Production module: **748 → 751 lines** (+3); tests: +7 net lines with a scoped allocation; docs: +5. Solid counts unchanged: 0 effects, 1 cleanup, 2 owned listeners, 0 DOM queries/owner APIs. One presentation-size value prevents repeated layout changes; no additional observer/cache machinery.

![Before: unknown-size images shrink after decoding and the transcript corrects by 273 px](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/611652de-edd5-4e4f-85da-78ba6ff5e5fd)

![After: remote images stay in their reserved frame and surrounding messages remain stable](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20f4e443-af73-4c98-9a97-ee69cb450e91)
CI follow-up: the first full run passed the other selected code checks but failed the image-loading test’s former shrink-on-decode expectation. The test-only follow-up now checks stable decode and correctly sized remounts; its focused local E2E passes (2 cases, 15.55 s including setup). Independent P0–P2 review of the repaired assertions is clean. The earlier required-heading context failure was corrected. The production implementation and measured bundle inputs are unchanged by this follow-up.

Replacement CI follow-up: the image-loading cases pass. A cross-tab sidebar test observed 3 snapshot writes instead of at most 1; its exact case passes on the latest completed scheduled main run (41265289027), the retained merge-base build, and the retained candidate build, so no inherited-failure exception is claimed. Its counter includes delayed whole-projection captures after the first saved receipt; only one tab has a virtual clock. One targeted rerun of the failed job passed after this timing-flake diagnosis. Full CI run [41268839384, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41268839384/attempts/2) is now successful on exact head `f1ed1585c70a6518bf93a4b66738c0b2cd23b30b`, including the CI gate. prs.title: fix(macos): Mac tab reloads forever when its page keeps crashing
prs.body:
Related: #183928
Depends on: #185432 (this branch is stacked on it; the diff shows both until that PR merges)

Depends on the Mac tab load-failure change for #183927 (branch `mac/5a-tab-load-error`); this branch is stacked on it and reuses its failure view and Reload retry.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Mac tab reloads in an endless loop when its page's web content process keeps quitting.

## User Impact

User impact: a page whose web content quits is still reloaded automatically, up to twice. If it quits again before the user navigates or reloads, the tab stops reloading and shows "This page stopped repeatedly" with Reload. Reload, a toolbar navigation, Back/Forward (Browser panel buttons, or Navigate > Back/Forward and their Command-[ / Command-] shortcuts), or a pointer click on a link starts a fresh budget. Each tab counts on its own.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every WebContent termination of a reading tab ran `webView.reload()` with no limit (`apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardWindowController.swift:1493-1494` on `70c70646d86`), so a page that crashes on load keeps reloading, using CPU and network, and never becomes usable.

The tab now owns a small budget (`DashboardBrowserTab.automaticReloadLimit = 2`). `DashboardNativeBrowserHost.webContentProcessDidTerminate(_:)` spends one automatic reload per termination; once spent, it shows the shared failure state from #183927 instead of reloading. The budget is not restored when a load finishes, because in the reported loop each termination follows a reload that finished successfully. It is restored only by user intent: Reload, toolbar navigation, Back/Forward, and main-frame link activations with a physical pointer button (which page script cannot synthesize). Back/Forward from the Browser panel (`perform(.back/.forward)`) and from the Navigate menu and its shortcuts (`DashboardWindowController.navigateBack()`/`navigateForward()`) go through the same `DashboardNativeBrowserHost.goBack(in:)`/`goForward(in:)`, so every Back/Forward command the app provides resets the budget. There is no new setting and no time window: two unrelated exits over a long session (for example under memory pressure) also spend the budget, and the cost of that is one Reload click, which restores it. The dashboard's own web view keeps its existing failure page from #183280.

## Real behavior proof

The PR build, packaged and launched through its normal entry point, with a page whose content process keeps quitting.

- Run: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/41208243695 (`proof 5b`, success; artifact `mac-proof-5b`).
- Environment: GitHub-hosted `macos-26` runner, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Xcode 26.6. The app is packaged from this PR's head `c1160a13e196` (`identity.txt`: `source_sha = expected_sha = c1160a13e196e65f204d3bb15515abc1ae8aba73`) with `scripts/package-mac-app.sh` (debug, ad-hoc signed, `ai.openclaw.mac.debug` 2026.10.9). It talks to a job-owned loopback Gateway and a loopback HTTP fixture that logs every page load (`logs/fixture-hits.jsonl`).
- Harness: `scripts/mac-proof/5b.sh` on `etzelm/openclaw` branch `mac/proof-5b-raise` (`ec76014ea5f`). Crashes are induced by SIGKILL of the tab's WebContent process. Only processes whose kernel responsibility record names the PR build are killed. The native failure view is read from the window with Vision OCR (`logs/settled-view-*.txt`), because WebKit keeps AppKit subviews of a `WKWebView` out of the accessibility tree. Navigate > Back/Forward are clicked in the menu bar.
- Scenario and result (`scenario.log`; the counts are fixture loads of that path):
  1. A new tab opens `/page/crash`. After three terminations the loads go 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 3: two automatic reloads, then no third. OCR: "This page stopped repeatedly / Choose Reload to try loading it again." with Reload.
  2. Toolbar Reload: load 4, the failure view is gone. The next termination reloads automatically (load 5).
  3. Link to `/page/b`. Its terminations take its loads 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 3, settling on the failure view. Navigate > Back loads `/page/crash` (load 6), and its next termination reloads automatically (load 7).
  4. Navigate > Forward loads `/page/b` (load 4). Two further terminations both reload (loads 5, 6) with no failure view.

```
14:29:25 termination 1: loads of /page/crash = 2
14:29:30 termination 2: loads of /page/crash = 3
14:29:38 termination 3: loads of /page/crash = 3
14:30:01 termination after Reload: loads of /page/crash = 5
14:30:29 page b termination 3: loads of /page/b = 3
clicked Navigate > Back
14:30:41 termination after Back: loads of /page/crash = 7
clicked Navigate > Forward
14:30:51 termination 1 after Forward: loads of /page/b = 5
14:30:56 termination 2 after Forward: loads of /page/b = 6
14:30:58 PASS 5b: bounded reloads, settled view, Reload and menu Back/Forward reset
```

The dialog over the chat pane in every shot is the runner's own local network prompt, for its `hosted-compute-` agent, not for the app. It does not cover the Browser panel.

![11-settled-failure-view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/053e715b926a22d3f18cadea10ffc6d2d369d4d3/mac-item-5-tab-failures/proof-run-41208243695/11-settled-failure-view.png)
(After three terminations, the tab stops on "This page stopped repeatedly" with Reload and keeps the address `/page/crash`.)

![12-reload-recovered](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/053e715b926a22d3f18cadea10ffc6d2d369d4d3/mac-item-5-tab-failures/proof-run-41208243695/12-reload-recovered.png)
(Reload loads the page again; the next termination reloads automatically.)

![20-page-b-settled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/053e715b926a22d3f18cadea10ffc6d2d369d4d3/mac-item-5-tab-failures/proof-run-41208243695/20-page-b-settled.png)
(`/page/b` has spent its own budget. The next step is Navigate > Back, after which `/page/crash` reloads automatically after a termination.)

![31-forward-budget-restored](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/053e715b926a22d3f18cadea10ffc6d2d369d4d3/mac-item-5-tab-failures/proof-run-41208243695/31-forward-budget-restored.png)
(After Navigate > Forward, two terminations reloaded `/page/b` and no failure view is shown.)

Recording (app window only, 132 s): [recording.mov](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/053e715b926a22d3f18cadea10ffc6d2d369d4d3/mac-item-5-tab-failures/proof-run-41208243695/recording.mov)

## Evidence

Offscreen renders from the real controller in the regression harness; the grey band is a test harness readout of the published tab state and the fixture's page-load count, not app UI.

![b-before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/8741e3612b3ea2b8c0cfb96990e57865054ebdae/mac-item-5-tab-failures/b-before.png)
(Before, on main: after three content-process exits the page has been reloaded three times, 4 loads in total, and it keeps reloading on every further exit.)

![b-after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/8741e3612b3ea2b8c0cfb96990e57865054ebdae/mac-item-5-tab-failures/b-after.png)
(After: the first two exits reload, the third leaves the tab on the native failure view with Reload: 3 loads in total.)

Focused real-WKWebView regression in `DashboardNativeBrowserFailureTests` that SIGKILLs only the WebContent process WebKit reports for a task-owned tab (`_webProcessIdentifier`), against a loopback `DashboardHTTPFixture` that counts page loads:

- the first two terminations reload; the third shows the failure, is not loading, and keeps the tab URL;
- a second tab on another host still reloads after its own termination;
- Reload loads the page, clears the failure, and the next termination reloads automatically again.
- after a load that is not a user action (`WKWebView.load` called directly, so no reset) moves the tab to a second page, Navigate > Back (`DashboardWindowController.navigateBack()`, the command behind Command-[) and then Forward each restore the full budget: on each history entry two terminations reload and no failure view appears.

Results on macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Swift 6.4 (Command Line Tools), on top of `mac/5a-tab-load-error` before it gained `e164e6e589e`. The suites were not re-run after merging #185432's current head and main into this branch (`c1160a13e19`, both merges clean except the appended test suite); the running-app proof above is on that merged head.

Earlier results:

- `swift test --filter DashboardNativeBrowserFailureTests` on this branch: 4 tests passed (the 3 from #183927 plus this one).
- The extended test with only the Navigate menu change reverted (sources at `1853bd4e7da`): fails at `browser.failureView == nil` with "exit 2 at /crashing after menu history"; menu Back left the budget spent, so the second termination showed the failure view.
- The budget test before the Navigate menu leg was added, with all of this branch's sources reverted (A sources; test loop bound written as `2` because `automaticReloadLimit` does not exist there): fails at `browser.failureView != nil` and `!crashing.isLoading`; the third exit reloads again.
- Siblings `DashboardNativeBrowser|DashboardHTTPFixtureTests|DashboardBrowserDownloadTests|DashboardBrowserCookieBoundaryTests|DashboardCloseShortcutTests`: 39 tests in 8 suites passed.
- `swift build --build-tests`, `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` (0 files need formatting), `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` (only the existing `DashboardManager.swift` file_length violation, also on base), `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, `git diff --check`: clean.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base <current main>` on this branch (the stack head, so it also covers #183927's files): every guard passed except `lint apps` (the existing `DashboardManager.swift` file_length violation) and `macOS app CI tests` (1 failed, 607 passed), whose one failure is the tooling test `test/scripts/generate-gateway-protocol-plugin.test.ts`, which builds a fixture Swift package and fails on this machine because the shim it probes forwards to the test runner's own Node (v26.3.0 here, below the required >=26.12.1), so the protocol plugin rejects every candidate; it does not touch the files in this change. The lint result is identical on base and head (`scripts/lint-swift.sh macos`: 1 violation, the same `DashboardManager.swift` file_length).

## Related work

- #152668 (open, prepare integrated tab logins before opening links) touches `DashboardNativeBrowserHost.swift`, `DashboardWindowController.swift` and `apps/.i18n/native-source.json`. No shared lines: its host change removes `self.onOpen?()` in `open` (line 160 on `70c70646d86`), a few lines above this stack's `navigate`/`perform` changes; its controller hunks are in lines 99-559, ours at 1331-1496. It already conflicts with current main on its own. Whichever lands second regenerates the i18n inventory with `pnpm native:i18n:baseline` (the inventory records source line sites).
- No open PR covers #183927 or #183928 (searched by symptom and by the owner file names).

## Gaps

- The reporter's loop was induced by killing the content process; a page that naturally crashes on every load was not available, so the regression induces terminations the same way (SIGKILL of only the test tab's own WebContent process).
- The two images under Evidence are offscreen renders from the regression harness; the running app is shown under Real behavior proof.
- Budget reset by toolbar navigation and physical link clicks is covered by code review only; the regression test calls the Navigate commands directly, and the running-app proof clicks Navigate > Back/Forward in the menu bar (not their key shortcuts). Browser panel Back/Forward shares the same `goBack(in:)`/`goForward(in:)` helpers but is not exercised by the test.
- WebKit's default right-click menu in a reading tab (Back, Forward, Reload) calls WebKit directly and does not reset the budget, as before this change; filtering or rerouting those items is left for a follow-up.
- The `macos-swift` CI job is skipped for this PR, so the Swift suites last ran locally with the Command Line Tools (same local stand-ins as #183927) before the merges that produced `c1160a13e19`.
- There is no running-app "before" run. The behavior on main (unbounded reloads) is shown by the offscreen renders under Evidence and by the regression test with this branch's sources reverted.

prs.title: fix(openai): avoid unsupported sizes for legacy image models
prs.body:
Related: #168665

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes image generation and edits failing with unsupported dimensions when users select a legacy GPT Image model and request a wide or tall aspect ratio through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

## User Impact

Users selecting `gpt-image-1.5`, `gpt-image-1`, or `gpt-image-1-mini` receive the closest supported standard dimensions for aspect-ratio hints, including through custom proxies. No configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenAI plugin now shares its legacy-model list between per-model geometry capabilities and native request limits. This prevents core normalization from selecting flexible-model dimensions for legacy models while retaining flexible sizes and custom deployment behavior.

This addresses the confirmed geometry defect. The issue's separate report of missing background-task error delivery is not established by this change.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the new 13-case regression file produced 11 unsupported-size failures and 2 passing controls. After the fix, `pnpm test extensions/openai/image-generation-geometry.test.ts extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.test.ts src/image-generation/runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 71 tests across three files.
- Tests use the real image-generation runtime and OpenAI plugin to inspect generation JSON and edit multipart payloads for custom endpoints; native OpenAI and Azure clamping, flexible sizes, authentication, and streamed image handling are also covered.
- Local environment: macOS arm64, Node 24.19.0. Final cold routed run: 1114.94 s; OpenAI lane: 512.84 s. These include compilation and initialization costs; CI seconds are unavailable before publication.
- The final run used a separate, identical source/dependency copy and isolated filesystem module cache after the original local directory repeatedly triggered compiled-worker source-metadata checks on unchanged files.
- Contract reference: [OpenAI Images API](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/images/methods/generate).
- After-fix live validation ran through the shipped CLI with a real custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint using gpt-image-1.5. Generation with a 16:9 hint and reference-image editing with a 9:16 hint both exited 0 and returned ok: true. The edit visibly added the requested red boat. Endpoint and credentials are redacted. The endpoint returned 1536x1024 for both images, so the edit output is not evidence of portrait dimensions; exact outbound dimensions were not captured during these live calls. Payload normalization remains covered by the focused regression tests.
- The reporter supplied the pre-fix live HTTP 400 and successful supported-size control in the linked issue. The shipped CLI build completed locally; the full repository test suite was not run.
- CLI AutoReview was attempted but the reviewer connection reset before producing a report. A supplemental independent read-only review found no actionable P0–P2 findings; this does not mark the CLI AutoReview gate as passed.
- Production extension typecheck, scoped strict test typecheck, formatting, and changed-file guards passed. Database legacy-store, media-download, runtime-sidecar, import-cycle, coercion, and deprecated-API guards also passed.
- Remote CI subsequently passed production types, test types, lint, and changed-file checks. One gateway test shard failed during suite loading with ERR_INVALID_URL_SCHEME at cli-process-tree.test-support.ts:4; the failing test and helper are unchanged in this PR and identical to current main, but the complete baseline shard has not been reproduced. The aggregate CI gate remains failed.
- Follow-up: removed the duplicate gpt-image-1 native-dimension case requested by review. The two OpenAI files now pass 61 tests (12 new regressions plus 49 existing cases).

### Live generation evidence

```text
Shipped CLI live verification; custom endpoint redacted.
Generation used pnpm openclaw (build-and-run wrapper); editing used node openclaw.mjs (built shipped launcher).
node openclaw.mjs infer image generate --model openai/gpt-image-1.5 --prompt "A simple lighthouse on a rocky island, daylight" --aspect-ratio 16:9 --quality low --count 1 --timeout-ms 180000 --output [OUTPUT]/generated.png --json
Exit code: 0
{
  "ok": true,
  "capability": "image.generate",
  "transport": "local",
  "provider": "openai",
  "model": "gpt-image-1.5",
  "attempts": [],
  "outputs": [
    {
      "path": "[OUTPUT]/generated.png",
      "mimeType": "image/png",
      "size": 2662277,
      "width": 1536,
      "height": 1024
    }
  ],
  "ignoredOverrides": []
}
```

### Live reference-image edit evidence

```text
Shipped CLI live verification; custom endpoint redacted.
Generation used pnpm openclaw (build-and-run wrapper); editing used node openclaw.mjs (built shipped launcher).
node openclaw.mjs infer image edit --model openai/gpt-image-1.5 --prompt "Keep the lighthouse and add a small red boat" --aspect-ratio 9:16 --quality low --count 1 --timeout-ms 180000 --output [OUTPUT]/edited.png --json --file [OUTPUT]/generated.png
Exit code: 0
{
  "ok": true,
  "capability": "image.edit",
  "transport": "local",
  "provider": "openai",
  "model": "gpt-image-1.5",
  "attempts": [],
  "outputs": [
    {
      "path": "[OUTPUT]/edited.png",
      "mimeType": "image/png",
      "size": 2536033,
      "width": 1536,
      "height": 1024
    }
  ],
  "ignoredOverrides": []
}
```

prs.title: fix(codex): keep literal node-binding cwd values without trimming
prs.body:
Fixes #190067

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex CLI node-conversation binding record persisted the session cwd after `.trim()` (`conversation-binding-data.ts`), the record reader re-trimmed it on restore (`normalizeOptionalString`), the session-file discovery summary trimmed it too (`node-cli-sessions.ts` `readSessionFileSummary`), and the resume path trimmed it again right before spawning (`node-cli-sessions.ts`: `cwd: ... params.cwd.trim()`). A session whose true cwd is a literal whitespace-padded directory (e.g. `/workspace/project `) was therefore discovered, written, read, and resumed as the WRONG directory: the spawned `codex exec resume` runs in the trimmed impostor, which usually does not exist. Same defect class as the merged literal-path fixes #187739, #187554, and #187777.

## Solution

Use `readNonBlankString` (the same helper the app-server branch of this file already uses for `workspaceDir`) at every site that handles the binding cwd: **discovery** (`readSessionFileSummary` keeps the session_meta `payload.cwd` verbatim), **write** (persist the raw cwd into the binding record), **read** (restore the raw cwd), and **resume spawn** (pass the literal cwd to `runCodexExecResume`). Blank or whitespace-only cwd values still omit the field / fall back exactly as before: `readNonBlankString` keeps the trim-based blank check and only preserves the value, so the old `""`-is-falsy behavior at both write and read is unchanged.

## Impact

- Session discovery and binding records preserve the session's literal cwd identity end to end.
- `codex exec resume` spawns in the directory where the session actually lived, even when its name carries edge whitespace.
- Identity-comparison sites elsewhere trim both operands and are unaffected by verbatim storage.

## Test growth

No net test lines: the regression coverage rides on existing tests instead of adding new ones. The diff is `6 insertions / 6 deletions` across three existing test files, with no new test cases; the earlier 71 added test lines are gone, and `check:test-lines-ratchet` passes.

- Discovery keeps the literal `session_meta.cwd`: `node-cli-sessions.test.ts` "keeps history usable with hydrated cwd" now uses a whitespace-padded rollout cwd (existing assertion).
- Resume passes the binding cwd to the spawn: the same file's "anchors relative CODEX_HOME for legacy/catalog-user commands" now resumes in a `project `-style directory (existing spawn-cwd assertion).
- Binding write: `commands.test.ts` "binds only a listed Codex CLI node session" now asserts the stored record carries the discovered literal cwd.
- Binding restore: `conversation-binding-node.test.ts` "revalidates a queued node binding that is …" now restores a literal cwd (existing resume-argument assertion).

## Evidence

### Shipped runtime proof: discovery and resume through the real CLI, Gateway, and node host

Entry points are shipped product surfaces: a real `openclaw nodes invoke --node … --command codex.cli.sessions.list` / `codex.cli.session.resume` (CLI → Gateway `node.invoke` → paired node host). The Gateway and node host ran the production `dist` built from the reviewed head with `scripts/build-all.mts`; the node host is `openclaw node run` and advertised `codex.cli.sessions.list` + `codex.cli.session.resume`.

Fixture: a genuine session created by the real Codex CLI running inside `…/work/codexproj ` (trailing space), so the rollout's `session_meta` is Codex's own output. A sibling directory `…/work/codexproj` carries `identity.txt=TRIMMED-DIR`, the literal directory carries `identity.txt=LITERAL-DIR`; a `/proc` watcher records the real spawned Codex process tree's cwd and the marker it sees.

| Observation (same fixture, same CLI, same node host) | head `ee4d6c3e5` | base `3cd0dd638` |
|---|---|---|
| `codex.cli.sessions.list` session `cwd` | `…/work/codexproj ` (literal, trailing space) | `…/work/codexproj` (trimmed) |
| `codex.cli.session.resume` with binding `cwd` = `…/work/codexproj ` → Codex banner `workdir:` | `workdir: …/work/codexproj ` | `workdir: …/work/codexproj` |
| `/proc/<pid>/cwd` of spawned `codex exec resume` (node wrapper and native binary) | `[…/work/codexproj ]`, marker `LITERAL-DIR` | `[…/work/codexproj]`, marker `TRIMMED-DIR` |

Head transcript (abridged; the base leg runs the identical commands from the base `dist`):

```
$ openclaw nodes invoke --node <node> --command codex.cli.sessions.list --params '{"limit":5}'
{ "ok": true, "payload": { "sessions": [ { "sessionId": "01a18f8e-…", "cwd": "/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj " } ] } }

$ openclaw nodes invoke --node <node> --command codex.cli.session.resume \
    --params '{"sessionId":"01a18f8e-…","cwd":"/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj ","prompt":"…"}'
OpenAI Codex v0.146.0
workdir: /tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj 
model: gpt-5.6-sol
provider: openai
session id: 01a18f8e-917a-7212-9421-5265296f29d7
user
continue in the literal directory
# the provider hop then fails: 403 "Country, region, or territory not supported"

# /proc watcher, spawned process tree
pid=211617 cwd=[/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj ] identity=[LITERAL-DIR] cmd=node …/codex exec resume --skip-git-repo-check … - 
pid=211637 cwd=[/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj ] identity=[LITERAL-DIR] cmd=…/vendor/…/codex exec resume --skip-git-repo-check … -
```

Base transcript (same commands, base `dist`):

```
$ openclaw nodes invoke --node <node> --command codex.cli.sessions.list --params '{"limit":5}'
{ "ok": true, "payload": { "sessions": [ { "sessionId": "01a18f8e-…", "cwd": "/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj" } ] } }

$ openclaw nodes invoke --node <node> --command codex.cli.session.resume \
    --params '{"sessionId":"01a18f8e-…","cwd":"/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj ","prompt":"…"}'
OpenAI Codex v0.146.0
workdir: /tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj
session id: 01a18f8e-917a-7212-9421-5265296f29d7

pid=583566 cwd=[/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj] identity=[TRIMMED-DIR] cmd=node …/codex exec resume … -
pid=583589 cwd=[/tmp/p188121gw/work/codexproj] identity=[TRIMMED-DIR] cmd=…/vendor/…/codex exec resume … -
```

What the capture proves and what it does not: Codex's own `workdir:` banner and the kernel-observed `/proc/<pid>/cwd` show the CLI was launched in the literal directory on this head and in the trimmed sibling on the base commit — exactly the user-visible difference. The model turn is not part of the claim; this machine's region blocks `api.openai.com` (403 "Country, region, or territory not supported"), so the run stops at the provider hop after loading the genuine session in the recorded directory. Setup facts, disclosed because they are not product behavior: the isolated Gateway used the operator opt-in `gateway.nodes.commands.allow: ["codex.cli.session.resume"]` (the documented dangerous-node-command allow, needed for a direct `nodes invoke`), and the one-time node pairing was approved with `openclaw nodes approve`. Binding serialization and restoration to that same resume argument are covered by the existing tests above and by the Control UI persistence capture below.

### Binding persisted and restored through the shipped Control UI

Entry point: the shipped Control UI (`openclaw dashboard` issues the owner handoff URL), a real Gateway built from the reviewed `dist`, a paired node host (`openclaw node run`), and a genuine Codex 0.164.0 session created inside `…/work/codexproj ` (trailing space). The only UI action was: open the node's Codex catalog row, type a message, press send. The Control UI calls the shipped `sessions.catalog.continue` RPC, which installs the Codex plugin's session binding.

The Gateway persisted the binding in its SQLite store (`state/openclaw.sqlite`, table `current_conversation_bindings`); the row is inspectable:

```
binding_id:        generic:webchat<US>default<US><US>agent:main:harness:codex:node-session:ea0f1088de7be187158b1b7ea154048bb85bcf2e30e6d7862400df57b3ae5793
target_session_key: agent:main:harness:codex:node-session:ea0f1088…5793
metadata.data:     {"kind":"codex-cli-node-session","version":1,
                    "nodeId":"ff118971…7008a",
                    "sessionId":"01a19233-7502-7512-b65b-fd1fa5f782c7",
                    "agentId":"main",
                    "cwd":"/tmp/p188121proof/work/codexproj"}
```

Then the Gateway was restarted (the binding existed only on disk), the same adopted session was reopened in the Control UI, and a message was sent. The plugin restored the binding and continuation spawned Codex in the stored cwd — the kernel-observed process tree:

```
pid=1539699 cwd=[/tmp/p188121proof/work/codexproj] identity=[TRIMMED-DIR] cmd=node …/codex exec resume --skip-git-repo-check --output-last-message …/last-message.txt 01a19233-…-fd1fa5f782c7 -
pid=1539725 cwd=[/tmp/p188121proof/work/codexproj] identity=[TRIMMED-DIR] cmd=…/vendor/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex exec resume --skip-git-repo-check --output-last-message …/last-message.txt 01a19233-…-fd1fa5f782c7 -
```

The turn then stops at the same region-blocked provider hop described above (403), after the session was loaded in the bound directory.

Compatibility with existing state:

- The same store was opened by the pre-fix build `3cd0dd638` (the released 2026.10.9 line): the pre-fix reader restored the same row and spawned `codex exec resume … 01a19233-…` in the same cwd, so the store written by the fix build is readable by existing code without migration (no schema change, `kind`/`version` unchanged).
- For this session the stored `cwd` is exactly the value the pre-fix writer produces: Codex's own app-server catalog already normalizes the thread cwd, so the fix's writer stores `/tmp/p188121proof/work/codexproj` unchanged. Existing rows written by the pre-fix build therefore take the same read path.
- Latest published stable `openclaw@2026.10.9` does not bundle the Codex extension (67 bundled extensions, no `codex`), so there is no released producer of this data model; `3cd0dd638` is the pre-fix behavior for it.

Known capture gap: the two asks above needing a messaging channel are environment-blocked here. The literal-cwd *binding write* path runs through the `/codex resume … --bind here` command, which requires a channel that implements `bindings.resolveCommandConversation` (Discord/Telegram/Matrix/LINE/Feishu/iMessage). This host has no leased Telegram/Discord QA credentials (the shared Convex credential broker is unavailable), and the webchat surface is not a binding channel by design, so the shipped-Control-UI capture necessarily goes through the Codex catalog path, which receives an already-normalized cwd from Codex's app-server. Literal cwd at the writer/reader boundaries is covered by the existing tests, and literal cwd at the node resume boundary by the direct node capture; a channel-credentialed or maintainer-run `/codex resume --bind here` capture is required to show the literal value stored through the binding itself.

Scope note: the Codex app-server catalog normalizes `cwd`, so the catalog-continue binding path stores an already-normalized value; literal whitespace preservation is what the direct node `codex.cli.sessions.list`/`codex.cli.session.resume` capture above shows, and what the writer/reader tests assert.

### Red-green for the consolidated tests

Remote Linux runner, `vitest run <file> --maxWorkers=1`. With only these test edits applied and the two production files reset to `3cd0dd638`, the coverage fails; on the reviewed head it passes.

Base (`3cd0dd638` production files):

- `node-cli-sessions.test.ts` — 3 failed: both "anchors relative CODEX_HOME for legacy/catalog-user commands" cases (spawn cwd expected `…/project `, got `…/project`) and "keeps history usable with hydrated cwd" (listed cwd trimmed).
- `commands.test.ts` — 1 failed: "binds only a listed Codex CLI node session (listed: true)" (stored record cwd trimmed).
- `conversation-binding-node.test.ts` — 4 failed: every "revalidates a queued node binding that is …" case (restored binding reached resume with a trimmed cwd).

Head `ee4d6c3e5`:

- `node-cli-sessions.test.ts` → 1 file passed (23.7s).
- `conversation-binding-node.test.ts` → 4/4 passed (15.1s).
- `commands.test.ts` → 1 file passed (525s wall for that file; the touched case is one of its fast unit tests).

### Checks

- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base 3cd0dd6380a1a1586c6db4574b6fc231eb3367df --no-merge-base` → `Test lines OK: 6287170; ceiling: 6330844`.
- `git diff --check` clean.

## Precedent

Same defect class as merged #187739, #187554, and #187777. Sibling sweep PRs: #187751, #187766, #187816, #187825.

prs.title: refactor(comfy): use virtual time for music deadline test
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/188252

## What Problem This Solves

The Comfy music polling-timeout regression uses a real one-second deadline despite mocked external I/O.

## User Impact

No product behavior change. The distinct local music timeout regression and its original request, fixture and exact error assertion remain.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing workflow deadline suite’s timer pattern to advance polling and performance.now together. Attach the rejection assertion before advancing1000ms, then restore real timers in the existing cleanup. No production code, helper, mock decision seam or expected result changes.

## Evidence

- Production delta0; net4 test lines added, with an exact4-line allocation. The existing test file grows from133 to137 LF.
- Formatter, syntax, whitespace, normal signed hooks and the exact-base staged test-line ratchet passed.
- pr-simplify/test-audit completed.
- Fresh full-range local ClawSweeper review of c9405cd28d98d909548e383f101636e497e42e1c..9626d023fb9a23732904c4c3342c83ad89a97c0b covered both files and found no actionable defects.
- Qualified native execution passed both focused suites: 14 cases across the music provider and workflow deadline owners. External wall time was 97.700s; Vitest reported 90.38s. Case-time sums were 2.070s for music and 1.476s for deadline coverage; individual file wall times were not emitted. The music-timeout case reported 256ms on the candidate only.
- The owning extension-test typecheck passed in 33.814s. Typed lint of the changed test passed in 234.050s, including its automatic SDK boundary declaration preparation. Each official check ran once against the unchanged reviewed head; passing tests were reused when completing types and lint.
- The separate comparable base/head study of the same committed timeout case remains pending before landing. Candidate timings and head CI do not establish that comparison. Normal native preparation and exact-head CI also remain pending; CI seconds are not yet available. No speed, product-latency or CI-time improvement is claimed. Production, runtime imports and packaging are unchanged; no additional full-package build gate is introduced.

## Predeclared comparable test-cost protocol

This is a new protocol recorded before the first sample; the comparison has not run. Its reserved slot follows G37's accepted handback and prior V25/S34 commitments. The 14 functional cases, types and typed lint already passed once and will not be rerun as setup.

1. **Workload and variants:** run only the committed `honors req.timeoutMs for the music workflow poll deadline` case. Preserve its original music request, `timeoutMs: 1000` and exact `Comfy workflow did not finish within 1s` rejection. A uses the original test blob at `c9405cd28d98d909548e383f101636e497e42e1c`; B uses `9626d023fb9a23732904c4c3342c83ad89a97c0b`. Only this test and its allocation differ in the committed range; production remains unchanged.
2. **Samples:** five serial pairs, `A1 B1 A2 B2 A3 B3 A4 B4 A5 B5`. No warmups, replacement samples or parallel campaign check. Reuse the qualified private checkout and frozen Node 26.13.0/Vitest 5.0.5 inputs. Record the actual worker executable, version and PID.
3. **Cache and capacity:** each invocation gets a fresh private `OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH` and private `NODE_V8_COVERAGE` destination. This is fresh-process/module-cache measurement, not a claim of a cold OS cache. Keep the already qualified `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` selection, `GOMAXPROCS=1`, `GOMEMLIMIT=3GiB` and one worker. Record CPU/load, memory/swap and custody before/after every sample; back off on real pressure. Unrelated isolated tests are a resource input, not an automatic veto.
4. **Custody and coverage:** keep HEAD/binding fixed, overlay only the committed test variant, and restore candidate bytes plus all 20 frozen input hashes after every invocation, including failures. Retain owning test/deadline coverage and actual worker/source/output bindings. Missing coverage remains a gap; do not infer native work or require identical polling counts across real and fake clocks. No main refresh, install, qualification replay, benchmark or extra package-build gate.
5. **Measurements:** preserve every raw result and JSON report. Record actual assertion duration, reported file duration, Vitest total and externally measured selected-file invocation wall/user/sys/max RSS. Invocation wall includes wrapper/import/setup; JSON assertion windows are not file-import wall. Report all samples, median, nearest-rank p95 and min/max. The earlier candidate-only 256ms is not comparative evidence.
6. **Acceptance and stop:** both variants must pass the same exact rejection with one selected case and retain deadline coverage. Candidate case median/p95 must improve; other observed cost cells must hold or improve unless a real regression receives explicit public maintainer acceptance. Restore sources, then stop before the next sample if any comparable candidate cost cell regresses by 20% or more. Preserve failures, partial pairs and every measured point; no discarded samples or extra runs. A setup, invariant, binding or restoration failure also stops the study. No product latency, CPU, RSS or physical-allocation gain is claimed.

Use the same committed runner for every sample:

```sh
GOMAXPROCS=1 GOMEMLIMIT=3GiB OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node /usr/bin/time -l node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/comfy/music-generation-provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 \
  -t 'honors req\.timeoutMs for the music workflow poll deadline' \
  --reporter=verbose --reporter=json \
  --outputFile .local/g35-focused-proof/timing-report.json
```

The exact title and one passing selected case must be present in the report. Native preparation and exact-head CI remain required after an accepted comparison; only a verified remote merge counts as landed.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): restore the cached sidebar sooner on warm reloads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Warm reloads spend unnecessary work restoring large grouped sidebars, and native host reparenting or a slow expanded-child roster can discard already displayed cached rows. The campaign's dashboard-deep-link reload evidence recorded 14 visual states; this supporting change targets the sidebar restoration work within that flow.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the sidebar owner attached across same-turn host reparenting, matching the bridge view's existing lifetime. Transient menus and person cards still dismiss immediately at native detach. Remove the three-second forced partial handoff so the cached sidebar remains until the root and expanded-child reads settle. Preserve the DOM identity of a newly selected offscreen row while its scheduled geometry update is pending. The offscreen-row suppression and its scrolling-test adaptation are now upstream in #189821; their superseded L259 changes were removed.

The settings-correct Team-shape fixture and probes remain reusable by the warm-reload rig: involving-me/category/created, 97 groups, five collapsed sections, empty-groups policy, previews off, pins, archived dashboard-qualified chat targets and expanded children. The existing reconnect and delayed-child regression cases are retained.

## User Impact

Cached rows remain displayed through same-turn reparenting and slow roster handoff; newly selected rows remain mounted while geometry catches up. No configuration, Gateway protocol or server schema changes.

**This does not fix the chat-route initial blank or the deletion invalidation storm.** The storm is handled separately in #189729. The initial chat owner/model and scheduled-geometry gap is assigned to a follow-up that builds on this branch. Both limitations remain observable and are not described as fixed here.

## Evidence

Revalidation is in progress for rebased head `0728461eb388d980af4fc7c7203a1eeba92c898e` on main `6794f68478b6fc4163ebbe97cafe3252e543c1f2`. #189729 and #189821 landed while the prior head was being validated. Current runtime changes total **+4 LOC** across three files. Independent review is clean through P2; all reviewed source/context bytes were verified unchanged by the last unrelated-main rebase.

### Historical combined comparison

The measurements below cover the earlier combined L259 prototype, including offscreen-row suppression now landed in #189821. They are retained for campaign provenance and the requested per-pair counts; they are **not an isolated speedup claim for the remaining rebased diff**.

Accepted supporting measurements: 11 interleaved pairs per route on one quiet AWS `c7a.4xlarge` (`cbx_962e59f9fa51`), repository Chromium, synthetic Team-scale data, real loopback Gateway, 80 ms network profile, unprofiled. Measurement candidate `1674aedfc2de`, base `84133d32283a`; the original combined candidate also precedes the immediate transient-menu/person-card dismissal repair at native detach. The remaining rebased diff is validated separately below. All 556 captured PNGs across 44 warm runs were inspected. The ordinary rig pauses peer JavaScript, so it does not prove storm behavior. Timings are not from the shared Mac.

| Metric | Main median | Candidate median | Better pairs |

| First populated sidebar pixels, chat | 942.54 ms | 783.61 ms | **10/11** |

### Final-head validation

Head `0728461eb388d980af4fc7c7203a1eeba92c898e`, pristine main control `6794f68478b6fc4163ebbe97cafe3252e543c1f2`, AWS `c7a.4xlarge` lease `cbx_8ffb8be1f7c0` ([run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_398dc90f25706f061c423056a489c262)). prs.title: feat: retain completed Git update download batches
prs.body:
Related: #185253

## What Problem This Solves

An interrupted Git-source update should keep completed downloads when its temporary inspection checkout is removed or the updater process exits.

## User Impact

Official public `openclaw/openclaw` source checkouts can retry using already completed Git batches. Only missing objects are requested again; the interrupted batch can restart.

This is object-batch recovery, not byte-offset continuation inside a pack. A metadata pack can also restart. Multiple requests and separate blob packs can increase first-transfer bytes and latency compared with ordinary Git. Private repositories, forks, other Git services and npm updates retain their existing transport.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing remote, ref and candidate selection owners. Fetch commit/tree metadata first, then hydrate missing history and candidate-tree objects in native compressed Git batches of at most 128 object IDs. Keep Git's object store and negotiation tips in stationary artifact storage under the existing file lock; retain it on failure and remove it after success.

Hydration follows Git's native promisor-fetch contract, including disabled negotiation for missing objects. This also covers a cached pinned commit whose promised blobs are absent. Download work stays within cancellation and the original deadline, before candidate metadata reads, validation and mutation admission. There are no publisher artifacts, release-workflow changes, public options or database migrations.

## Evidence

- 156 related tests passed: existing Git admission/activation/rollback suites, transport restart recovery, named promisor remotes, cached pinned commits, historical rename/deletion and fallback contents, partial clones, cancellation/deadlines, and candidate rejection followed by successful retry.
- The restart regression transfers a real 128-object batch, interrupts the next batch, destroys the inspection repository, then proves a new instance never requests the completed batch's object IDs.
- Core and services-test typechecks, targeted production/test lint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Independent `autoreview` completed with no P0–P2 findings after fixing its cached-pinned-target finding.
- Live GitHub: fixed target `f623a2ccbd6ee80cb5ad1127c5cecfdf6e79d6db`, real `blob:none` metadata fetch, completed first object batch, sustained TLS disconnect during the next batch, then a new Git process requested only the remaining objects. Strict fsck and all twelve historical/fallback trees matched ordinary Git.
- Real isolated CLI update completed with exit 0/status `ok`, including retained-runtime preparation, candidate build, Doctor, config/plugins/recovery checks, Gateway startup, admitted-pack import and activation. A new CLI process requested zero of the 654 blobs completed by earlier invocations. Installed source/build/runtime commits agreed afterward, the same isolated state loaded successfully, and the completed download cache was removed. Refused-network and SIGINT runs had previously left the old installation usable.
- The final promised-root-tree repair has a CI-safe red→green `tree:0` regression. It was also compiled and booted separately; full CLI versus final-helper source scopes are stated below. The native published-latest-stable driver qualification also passed; its same-version/different-build source scope and captured result are below.
- Actual production helper, separate Node processes: first process was SIGKILLed after 128 blobs were imported. A new Node reclaimed the dead owner's cache lock and fetched the remaining 135 objects, with zero overlap against the completed batch. Metadata was not retransferred; strict fsck, historical/fallback content, final tree and the unchanged installed checkout all passed.

<details>
<summary>Measured costs and proof boundaries</summary>

The live three-blob fixture deliberately used one object per batch to exercise interruption between batches. Including its interrupted request, the run used 83,322 server-to-client TLS bytes and 10 HTTP requests; ordinary Git for the same delta used 10,449 bytes and 2 requests. A separate all-three-object batch plus metadata used 68,865 TLS bytes and 4 requests. These are actual proxy-observed wire bytes, not local pack sizes. They demonstrate recovery and its overhead, not a general traffic or speed improvement.

Production uses up to 128 objects per batch. This bounds object count, not compressed bytes. Git object compression is retained; ordinary fetch may choose better cross-version delta bases.

New transport tests took about 2.3 seconds of test execution. The full rejection/retry/activation regression took 8.1 seconds on this host and covers two complete updater runs; helper-only tests would miss that lifecycle boundary. The six-suite run took 123.79 seconds including cold compiler preparation. The final head `5955935c` passed [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40449467396/job/122015287743): 70 successful checks, 60 skipped and one neutral, with no failures. Skipped checks are not counted as passed qualification.

The implementation has one internal download owner and uses native Git objects/refs instead of a new manifest, database or publishing protocol. Existing step factories moved to their command owner to keep the updater within its file-size gate. No version is published and no merge is requested.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Captured runtime output and exact scope</summary>

Executed through the supported CLI in a task-owned checkout, HOME/state directory and loopback listeners:

```text
pnpm openclaw update --channel dev --no-restart --yes --json --timeout 1200
```

Selected fields from the captured CLI result and controller:

```json
{
  "exit": 0,
  "seconds": 1074.48,
  "status": "ok",
  "mode": "git",
  "before": "199d263a74fdd30e8225750a38f155beed689423",
  "after": "33b8144615ac38a58b2be2099e1bb02d175dabe5",
  "builtCommit": "33b8144615ac38a58b2be2099e1bb02d175dabe5",
  "sourceRuntimePrepared": true,
  "downloadCacheRemoved": true
}
```

Selected fields extracted from the actual client-side Git packet trace of the new CLI process:

```json
{
  "previously_completed_blobs": 654,
  "unique_wanted_oids": 91,
  "previously_completed_blobs_requested_again": []
}
```

The branch moved while the interrupted update was being prepared. These are 91 newly requested object IDs, with no intersection against the 654 already completed blobs.

Captured production-helper SIGKILL/new-Node result:

```json
{
  "firstNodeReturncode": -9,
  "firstCompletedBatch": 128,
  "resumedBatchSizes": [
    128,
    7
  ],
  "repeatedCompletedObjects": 0,
  "metadataPackRetransferred": false,
  "staleLockReclaimedAndReleased": true,
  "strictFsck": "passed",
  "historicalFallback": "matched",
  "installedFilesUnchanged": 31
}
```

Captured real live-holder contention result. The second Node reached the actual lock timeout, performed no shared-cache initialization, and used the existing Git fallback. After the holder released normally, a fresh Node reused its completed pack:

```json
{
  "liveHolderFirstBatch": 128,
  "contenderObservedLockTimeout": true,
  "contenderCacheInitializations": 0,
  "sharedPackHashesUnchangedDuringContention": true,
  "holderReleasedNormally": true,
  "resumedBatchSizes": [
    128,
    7
  ],
  "repeatedCompletedObjects": 0,
  "strictFsck": "passed",
  "productionSourceSha256ObservedAfterRun": "5bb67fad2d02cfba7eda8bc0a4e02c8733ecaad290e33ed96145bbdf7d62b992"
}
```

Captured Gateway readiness after the completed upgrade, and again after compiling the final helper repair:

```json
{"ready":true,"coreReady":true,"failing":[],"eventLoop":{"degraded":true,"reasons":["cpu"]}}
```

The host was running parallel builds during those probes; this is readiness evidence, not a performance qualification.

Source attribution: the full CLI run used the four production files from `10c73200`, rebased by the ordinary dev-update flow onto official target `63a05a41365026646b71df6ec7b0e390c506695a`; its local installed result was `33b81446`. The only later production repair in `5955935c` changes how an absent promised root tree is inventoried. That repair has an observed red→green regression, and its exact helper SHA-256 `5bb67fad2d02cfba7eda8bc0a4e02c8733ecaad290e33ed96145bbdf7d62b992` matches the live contention proof and a separately compiled/booted isolated build `f926e640`. The long normal upgrade is not being represented as a byte-identical run of that later repair.

Existing isolated state was reused: agent `main` remained present; operator settings remained gateway mode `local`, auth mode `token`, update channel `dev`; public schema declarations remained state 34/agent 37. Real Doctor/recovery/Gateway processes consumed those databases. No database schema or storage format changes are introduced here. Existing unknown-writer recovery advisories were retained; this does not claim database bytes stayed unchanged or automatic database restoration was universally available.

Default adoption and its measured transfer-cost tradeoff remain for the update owner to decide; this PR is not a merge or release request.
</details>


<details>
<summary>Published stable driver qualification: captured result</summary>

The native `scripts/e2e/published-driver-update-docker.sh` cell from `5955935c` passed locally. It installed the stock npm `openclaw@2026.10.7` tarball, then used that published updater to install the locally built candidate tarball through `openclaw update --tag /tmp/openclaw-current.tgz --yes --json`. All native assertions ran, including durable update status, managed Gateway replacement, readiness, running build identity, persisted session content, retained state fixture bytes and incognito cleanup.

Selected fields from the captured result:

Candidate source is the post-upgrade moving-main build `f926e640` described above, carrying the exact final-helper SHA-256 from `5955935c`; it is not being represented as a package built from the exact PR-head tree. Canonical packaging and integrity checks passed without altering producer receipts or stamps. The container, managed service and disposable volume were settled after the test. prs.title: fix(zalo): honor markdown.tables on outbound sends
prs.body:
## Summary
`channels.zalo.markdown.tables` (and its per-account override under `channels.zalo.accounts.<id>.markdown.tables`) is ignored for every Zalo send that goes through the channel outbound adapter: the message tool, `openclaw message send`, cron and heartbeat delivery. A Markdown table in those sends reaches the Zalo Bot API as raw `| a | b |` pipe text no matter which mode is configured, while inbound replies in the same chat already render the table with the configured mode (`code` by default). So the same agent output looks different depending on whether it was a reply or a proactive send, and an operator who sets `tables: "bullets"` for a Zalo account still gets pipe tables on scheduled or tool-initiated messages.

## Root cause
`extensions/zalo/src/send.ts` `sendMessageZalo` is the single transport for the Zalo outbound adapter (`zaloPlugin.outbound.sendText`/`sendMedia` and the message adapter both route to it through `sendZaloDelivery`). It posts the text it receives unchanged:

```ts
// before
const response = photoUrl
  ? await sendPhoto(token, { chat_id: normalizedChatId, photo: photoUrl, caption: text || undefined }, ...)
  : await sendMessage(token, { chat_id: normalizedChatId, text: truncateUtf16Safe(text, 2000) }, ...);
```

The only table conversion for Zalo lives in the inbound reply pipeline (`extensions/zalo/src/monitor.ts`, `preparePayload` calling `convertMarkdownTables(payload.text, tableMode)`), and core outbound delivery does not convert tables on behalf of channels. Every send that does not start as an inbound reply therefore skips the configured mode.

## Fix
`sendMessageZalo` resolves the table mode for the resolved account and converts the text once before choosing the text or photo-caption transport:

```ts
// after
const text = convertMarkdownTables(
  rawText,
  resolveMarkdownTableMode({ cfg: options.cfg, channel: "zalo", accountId: account.accountId }),
);
```

This is the same shape Nextcloud Talk (`sendMessageNextcloudTalk`), IRC (`sendIrcMessages`) and Nostr already use in their send owners.

## Why this is the right boundary
`sendMessageZalo` is the one function every Zalo outbound adapter send passes through, so converting there covers plain text and photo captions, the message tool, CLI sends, cron and heartbeat in one place instead of patching each caller. `resolveMarkdownTableMode` already handles the account override and the channel default, so the account resolved for the send picks the mode. Inbound final text replies that are durably delivered through this adapter were already converted by the monitor's `preparePayload`; `convertMarkdownTables` is idempotent on its own output for `code`, `bullets` and `off` (verified on the same table input), so those replies are unchanged. The monitor's direct media reply path is untouched. Zalo's chunk limit and the 2000-character truncation are unchanged; the conversion runs per adapter send after core chunking, which matches the Nextcloud Talk and Nostr senders.

## Verification
- Added `renders text tables with the account markdown.tables mode` and `renders caption tables with the account markdown.tables mode` to `extensions/zalo/src/send.test.ts`. With the base channel set to `tables: "off"` and the `work` account set to `tables: "bullets"`, a table sent through `sendMessageZalo` with `accountId: "work"` must reach the Bot API `text` field (and the photo `caption` field) as the bulleted rendering. Both fail on main (raw pipe table) and pass with the patch; the existing cases in the file still pass.
- `oxfmt --check` clean on both changed files.
- Local tsgo and oxlint were not run per the contributor workflow for this batch; GitHub Actions covers them.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: Zalo outbound adapter sends ignored `channels.zalo.markdown.tables` and the per-account override, posting raw Markdown pipe tables to the Zalo Bot API.
Real environment tested: The real `zaloPlugin` from `extensions/zalo/src/channel.ts`, registered in the active plugin registry the way the gateway registers channel plugins, driven through `zaloPlugin.outbound.sendText` with a real config file (default account `markdown.tables: "code"`, account `shop` with `markdown.tables: "bullets"`). Account resolution, table-mode resolution, `sendMessageZalo` and the real Zalo API client (`callZaloApi`, JSON POST over HTTP) all ran unmodified; only the Zalo Bot API host was replaced by a local loopback HTTP server via the existing `ZALO_API_URL` override, which records each request path and body. Run on pristine main 7735f0b1069 and on this patch with identical inputs. The CLI `message send` path could not be used locally because the bundled channel loader fails on an unrelated `unicorn-magic` package export error under `node --import tsx` on this machine.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<tmp> OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<tmp>/openclaw.json ZALO_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:28417 node --import tsx drive.mts <default|shop>` where `drive.mts` registers `zaloPlugin` and calls `zaloPlugin.outbound.sendText({ cfg, to: "zalo:9876543210", text, accountId })` with the text `| Plan | Price |\n| --- | --- |\n| Basic | $5 |\n| Pro | $12 |`.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 7735f0b1069)
zaloPlugin.outbound.sendText accountId=default -> messageId zmsg-1
zaloPlugin.outbound.sendText accountId=shop -> messageId zmsg-2
--- loopback Zalo Bot API received:
POST /bot12345:default-token/sendMessage
{"chat_id":"9876543210","text":"| Plan | Price |\n| --- | --- |\n| Basic | $5 |\n| Pro | $12 |"}
POST /bot67890:shop-token/sendMessage
{"chat_id":"9876543210","text":"| Plan | Price |\n| --- | --- |\n| Basic | $5 |\n| Pro | $12 |"}

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
zaloPlugin.outbound.sendText accountId=default -> messageId zmsg-3
zaloPlugin.outbound.sendText accountId=shop -> messageId zmsg-4
--- loopback Zalo Bot API received:
POST /bot12345:default-token/sendMessage
{"chat_id":"9876543210","text":"```\n| Plan  | Price |\n| ----- | ----- |\n| Basic | $5    |\n| Pro   | $12   |\n```"}
POST /bot67890:shop-token/sendMessage
{"chat_id":"9876543210","text":"**Basic**\n• Price: $5\n\n**Pro**\n• Price: $12"}
```
Observed result after fix: On main both accounts post the raw pipe table regardless of configuration; with the patch the default account posts the configured `code` rendering and the `shop` account posts its own `bullets` rendering, each through its own bot token.
What was not tested: No real Zalo bot or device rendering; the photo caption path was exercised only by the colocated regression case because the live photo send needs public DNS for the photo host; the CLI and gateway `message send` entry points were not run locally (plugin loader environment issue noted above); full build not run.

## Evidence

- Canonical autoreview on base `31866655fd60e1ba7848daefb3a1234bb0c89084` through head `487d297b7e3424040c2c0f982266a0996ad080b4`, with the four source/guide files supplied intact and findings through P2: `scoped-clean`, no findings.

- Simplify pass: retained one LAN mode table and a short wide-area explanation; no runtime machinery or tests added. Production/test LOC delta: 0/0; docs: +16/-11 (net +5).

prs.title: fix(cli): match infer web --provider ids case-insensitively
prs.body:
## Summary
`openclaw infer web search --provider <id>` and `openclaw infer web fetch --provider <id>` reject a valid provider id when its casing differs from the plugin id. `--provider Brave` fails with `Unknown web_search provider "Brave".` and `--provider Firecrawl` fails with `web.fetch provider "Firecrawl" is not available`, even though the same command already treats the value case-insensitively everywhere else: its own secret scoping lowercases the flag, the web search plugin loader lowercases it to pick which plugin to load, and `tools.web.search.provider` / `tools.web.fetch.provider` in config are matched case-insensitively (config validation was aligned with that in #177836). A script or a user typing the provider name the way the docs and UI label it gets a hard failure instead of a provider call.

## Root cause
`src/cli/capability-cli/web.ts` passes the raw flag value through to the runtimes:

```ts
// before
const provider = opts.provider as string | undefined;
...
return runWebSearch({ config: cfg, providerId: provider, args: { query, count: limit, limit } });
...
const resolved = resolveWebFetchDefinition({ config: cfg, providerId: provider });
```

`runWebSearch` loads the plugin using `normalizeOptionalLowercaseString(providerId)` (`src/web-search/runtime.ts`), so the Brave plugin is loaded, but the explicit-selection guard then compares the raw value against the loaded ids (`providers.some((entry) => entry.id === explicitProviderId)`) and throws. `resolveWebFetchDefinition` looks the raw value up with `providers.find((entry) => entry.id === providerId)` and returns null. Every bundled web search and fetch provider id is lowercase (`brave`, `firecrawl`, `duckduckgo`, `tavily`, `exa`, `perplexity`, `searxng`, ...), so any other casing can never match.

## Fix
Normalize the flag once where the CLI reads it, for both subcommands:

```ts
// after
const provider =
  opts.provider === undefined ? undefined : normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(opts.provider);
```

The lowercased id then flows into secret scoping, `runWebSearch`, and `resolveWebFetchDefinition`, so all three steps of the command agree on one provider id.

## Why this is the right boundary
The `--provider` flag is the only caller that hands an explicit, user-typed provider id to these runtimes: the agent `web_search` and `web_fetch` tools select providers from config or runtime metadata (already lowercased), and the Gateway search test RPC passes ids it got from the provider status list. Normalizing untrusted CLI input once at the trust boundary matches the sibling `infer tts convert --provider`, which runs the flag through `normalizeSpeechProviderId` before calling its runtime. Behavior for lowercase ids is unchanged, an omitted flag still means automatic selection, and an unknown provider still fails with the same error (now naming the lowercased id).

## Verification
- New `src/cli/capability-cli.web-provider.test.ts` drives `infer web search --provider Brave` and `infer web fetch --provider Firecrawl` through the real command registration and asserts the runtimes receive `brave` and `firecrawl`. Both cases fail on pristine main (the raw `Brave` / `Firecrawl` reaches the runtime) and pass with the patch (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/capability-cli.web-provider.test.ts`).
- The existing `src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts` suite (102 cases, including the web search/fetch provider SecretRef and dispatch cases) passes with the patch.
- `oxfmt --check` is clean on the changed files.
- Local tsgo and oxlint were not run per the contributor workflow for this batch; GitHub Actions covers them.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: `openclaw infer web search --provider Brave` and `openclaw infer web fetch --provider Firecrawl` failed with an unknown or unavailable provider error because the flag was compared case-sensitively against lowercase plugin ids.
Real environment tested: The real CLI run from source with `node --import tsx src/entry.ts`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `HOME` (fresh empty state, default config), `BRAVE_API_KEY` and `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` unset, on pristine main 52e113b095d and on this patch with identical inputs. The real bundled Brave and Firecrawl plugins were loaded; nothing was stubbed. The Brave call stops at its own missing-key check before any network request; the Firecrawl fetch makes one real request for https://example.com.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<fresh> HOME=<fresh> node --import tsx src/entry.ts infer web search --provider Brave --query openclaw --json` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<fresh> HOME=<fresh> node --import tsx src/entry.ts infer web fetch --provider Firecrawl --url https://example.com --json`
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 52e113b095d)
$ openclaw infer web search --provider Brave --query openclaw --json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Unknown web_search provider \"Brave\"."
  }
}
exit=1
$ openclaw infer web fetch --provider Firecrawl --url https://example.com --json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "web.fetch provider \"Firecrawl\" is not available; check it with `openclaw infer web providers`."
  }
}
exit=1

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
$ openclaw infer web search --provider Brave --query openclaw --json
{
  "ok": false,
  "capability": "web.search",
  "transport": "local",
  "provider": "brave",
  "attempts": [],
  "outputs": [
    {
      "result": {
        "error": "missing_brave_api_key",
        "message": "web_search (brave) needs a Brave Search API key. Run `openclaw configure --section web` to store it, or set BRAVE_API_KEY in the Gateway environment. ...",
        "docs": "https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/web"
      }
    }
  ],
  "error": "missing_brave_api_key"
}
exit=1
$ openclaw infer web fetch --provider Firecrawl --url https://example.com --json
{
  "ok": true,
  "capability": "web.fetch",
  "transport": "local",
  "provider": "firecrawl",
  "attempts": [],
  "outputs": [
    {
      "result": {
        "url": "https://example.com",
        "finalUrl": "https://example.com",
        "status": 200,
        "extractor": "firecrawl",
        ...
```
Observed result after fix: The mixed-case `--provider` now reaches the selected provider: search is dispatched to `brave` (which then reports its own missing API key, the same result the lowercase `--provider brave` gives on main) and fetch is served by `firecrawl` with HTTP 200, instead of both commands failing before any provider runs.
What was not tested: No Brave API key was configured, so a successful Brave search response was not exercised; other web providers were not run individually; full build not run.
