prs.title: fix(gateway): paired-node Claude continuations retain Gateway context
prs.body:
Closes #145636

## What Problem This Solves

A Claude CLI continuation on a healthy paired node can fail with a Gateway-runtime or capability error after its originating request ends. Detached work retains a live Gateway resolver but deliberately does not retain the direct request context.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two paired-node readers now use the existing resolver-first `getInProcessGatewayRequestContext` in the current request-scope owner. This integrates with main's `PluginRuntimeExecutionFrame` storage instead of reintroducing the former AsyncLocalStorage owner or a second accessor. A resolver returning `undefined` remains authoritative: stale direct context cannot revive a retired owner.

The command policy, expected connection and pairing generation, dispatch-time authority, and skill/run/placement lifecycle checks remain intact. There are no configuration, protocol, database-schema, or public SDK changes.

## User Impact

A detached Claude continuation can use its still-live Gateway and connected paired node. A retired owner fails before any node lookup, policy check, or dispatch.

## Evidence

- Conflict refresh onto main `f76e79be6a8fc934afd0faf1315f0261cfc4bafe`; current head `eb7a861ea7c06c277806dd2c6d0dba6b0f9c0443` also checks the captured Gateway remains current at dispatch and skill authority use. [Remote focused tests](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/actions/runs/40626335729) passed 18 tests across both affected Gateway suites on a temporary child of this head. Full CI and refreshed real-node proof remain pending; earlier evidence below refers to the revisions identified there.

Reconciled against main `cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984`; candidate `2220ac4be308a06c58c1c1fc774bf8a83115414d`. The production diff is two reader substitutions, plus focused regression coverage.

### Actual Gateway and signed-node boundary

The same temporary source-runtime fixture starts the actual Gateway with an isolated home, config and state, loads a startup plugin through the normal loader, and captures its real context in an authenticated RPC. A separately signed WebSocket node completes normal local device pairing and command approval, verified in the persisted pairing records. After the capture RPC finishes, the fixture invokes the production `invokeNodeClaudeCliRun` in a resolver-only scope and repeats with a retired resolver plus deliberately stale direct context.

Main before the fix, observed with clean shutdown:

```json
{"resolverOnly":{"directContext":false,"dispatched":0,"ok":false,"error":"Gateway node runtime unavailable"},"retiredOwner":{"staleDirectContextPresent":true,"additionalDispatches":1,"ok":true}}
```

Exact candidate after the fix:

```json
{"head":"2220ac4be308a06c58c1c1fc774bf8a83115414d","expectedFixed":true,"actualGateway":true,"signedNode":true,"devicePaired":true,"commandApproved":true,"resolverOnly":{"directContext":false,"dispatched":1,"result":{"ok":true,"payload":{"exitCode":0,"stderrTail":"","truncated":false},"payloadJSON":null,"error":null}},"retiredOwner":{"staleDirectContextPresent":true,"additionalDispatches":0,"result":{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"Gateway node runtime unavailable"}}}}
```

The fixture exited 0, and the Gateway reported a clean shutdown.

This exercises real Gateway startup, plugin loading, authenticated RPC, signed WebSocket transport, persisted device/command pairing, NodeRegistry and the changed production invocation owner. The node returns a synthetic successful Claude-command payload. It does not establish live Claude model inference or a full terminal-close/Web-composer UI walkthrough.

The fixture uses synthetic data only. Update checks, telemetry and hosted catalog refresh are disabled with the documented config/environment opt-outs. Proof code and generated logs are temporary and are not committed.

### Regression coverage and checks

- Before the two reader substitutions: 13 failures / 3 passes across the invocation and paired-node skill suites. Detached dispatch failed unavailable; stale-context retirement incorrectly dispatched; skill preparation failed its Gateway/capability boundary.
- After, on the identical candidate tree: 27/27 tests across node invocation (5), paired-node skills (11), request-scope owner (7), and native Bash execution policy (4). Existing coverage for command denial, pairing-await authority retirement, capability requirements, skill delivery/authoring and publication retirement remains active under the resolver-only scope.
- Combined focused command: `pnpm test src/gateway/node-agent-cli-runtime.test.ts src/gateway/node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/gateway-request-scope.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin-native-bash.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 85.02s wall time including the first compiled-subprocess generation.

prs.title: fix(ui): prune the live cli-assistant segment when its row persists mid-run
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #180927. In a Control UI webchat session on a CLI backend with block streaming off, the assistant reply appeared twice: the live stream bubble kept the partial text while the durable row, persisted mid-run, was admitted beside it. The reporter measured the corresponding gateway failure 360 times in one day.

The pane already clears the live stream when a persisted row owns the active run — but that ownership check requires an explicit envelope run id (`event.runId` / row metadata), and the mid-run transcript publish can omit it. CLI assistant rows are self-proving: the Gateway stamps the run id into the persisted idempotency key (`cli-assistant:<runId>`), which the projection layer already canonicalizes into the row's run id.

## What Changed

`ui/src/pages/chat/session-message-apply.ts` only:

- A persisted CLI assistant row (`role: assistant`, `api: "cli"`) whose canonical idempotency-key run id is present now qualifies as producer-owned for the matching active run, even when the envelope omits the run id.
- That ownership feeds the existing persistence path, which clears the live stream so the durable row replaces the bubble instead of duplicating it.

The first revision of this PR keyed a different stream owner (`chatStreamSegments`) that the CLI assistant flow does not write; that path is gone. No other surface changes: rows without CLI provenance keep the terminal-stream behavior, and no delivery path gains or loses a send.

## Evidence

**Red/green regression** (`session-message-apply.test.ts`, real pane event path: live `chatStream` filled, then the persisted `session.message` row):

```
fix applied (9caa2aab):  ✓ 10 passed (10)
  - clears the live stream when a cli assistant row persists mid-run (without an envelope run id)
  - clears the live stream when a cli assistant row persists mid-run (with a matching envelope run id)
  - keeps the live stream for mid-run persisted rows without cli provenance

fix reverted, same tests:  × clears the live stream ... (without an envelope run id)
  Tests  1 failed | 9 passed (10)
```

**Adjacent suites after the change:**

```
session-message-apply + chat-pane-{session,snapshot}-hydration + tool-stream-fallback: 57 passed (57)

prs.title: fix(discord): false "couldn't finish" notice when a queued message is answered in its thread
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Discord shows "⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this request" after the agent answered a message in a thread it created from that message, when the message arrived while the session was still busy with an earlier turn.

## User Impact

User impact: in Discord channels, a message that waits in the queue behind a running turn can be answered in its own thread (thread-create from the message, then thread-reply, ending with `NO_REPLY`) without a false failure notice in the channel. Messages handled right away were already fine.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord registers an active thread route for each inbound message so that a thread created from that message counts as replying to it (thread replies are tagged `sourceReplyRoute: "current-source"`). The route was released when the message's dispatch returned. A message queued behind an active turn returns from dispatch right after it is enqueued, so its queued run started later with no route. Its thread was never adopted, the thread replies did not count as the source reply, and the required-reply check reported an empty response.

The queued run now holds the same route from `onQueuedFollowupAdmitted` until `onQueuedFollowupSettled`. Route registration counts its holders, so a queued run admitted before its dispatch returns keeps the route after the dispatch releases its own hold. Those two hooks are now always set on Discord dispatches (before this change they were set only when a draft stream existed); the draft handling inside them is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Live observation on a 2026.10.7 Gateway (Discord guild channel, `claude-cli` backend, automatic visible replies). Two turns in the same session did the same thing: thread-create from the source message, several thread-replies, then `NO_REPLY`. The turn that started right away completed silently. The next message had arrived during that turn (`injection_unavailable`, `disposition: followup-policy`) and ran about 2.5 minutes later as a queued follow-up. It logged `cli empty response diagnostics: backend=claude-cli reason=exit exitCode=0 … useResume=true` and posted the failure notice. The route lifecycle in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts` is the same on `main`.
- New regression tests in `message-handler.process.draft-final.test.ts`:
  - `keeps the source-message thread route for a queued turn until it settles`: the queued run is admitted after its dispatch returned.
  - `keeps the route for a queued turn admitted before its dispatch returns`: covers the holder count.
  - Both fail on `main` (`expected false to be true` when the thread reply is checked) and pass with this change.
- `pnpm test:extension discord`: 259 files, 2,637 tests passed. Focused `pnpm test` on the touched process and action tests: 91 passed.
- `pnpm format:check` and type-aware oxlint on the changed files are clean. `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` pass.
- Gap: I did not run the Discord e2e skill against an isolated Gateway because I don't have Discord test bot credentials. The live evidence above is from the reporting Gateway before the fix.

## What Problem This Solves

Opening or closing mobile navigation rebuilds the full shell view and republishes unrelated sidebar properties. Delayed label measurements also rewrite the class of an already-stopped marquee.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

The reported compound sidebar regression crossed the intentional 441 ms sheet-spring change in #188162. The benchmark waits for closing motion before delivering its second input. History and traces ruled out the later desktop geometry changes as its cause; Chromium had zero layout passes through the measured cycle.

The existing shell owner now publishes drawer changes separately. Its existing view supplies reactive drawer bindings and the commit acknowledgement; a simultaneous full-shell invalidation still takes the full path. Stopped marquees use a forced class toggle, which leaves the class attribute untouched when the scrolling token is already absent. The benchmark gains independent mobile open/close cases alongside the retained compound cycle.

The reduction in the DOM span removes late no-op mutations; it is not a claim that the visible spring paints faster.

prs.title: refactor(models): use one wildcard grammar for agent and role model policies
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** `modelPolicy.allow` had two grammars under one name. Operator roles accepted a model-name prefix such as `openai/gpt-*`; agent policies rejected it. Role matching used a separate glob matcher, and five other callers detected wildcards by hand (`endsWith("/*")`, `slice(0, -2)`, `startsWith`). The copies agreed today but could drift, for example on padded refs like `"openai / *"`.
- **Fix:** `src/config/model-policy-ref.ts` now owns one parser (`parseModelPolicyWildcardRef`: `provider/*`, `provider/namespace/*`, `provider/family-*`) and one matcher (`modelPolicyWildcardMatches`). Role policy matching, config validation, `isModelKeyAllowedBySet`, configured model entries, alias candidates, `models status` and the legacy Codex wildcard migration use them. The role-only parser, the role glob matcher and the role-only validation branch are deleted.
- **User impact:** agent policies now also accept model-name prefixes such as `openai/gpt-*`. Existing agent and role configs keep their meaning; no config is invalidated.

## Evidence

- New regression in `model-visibility-policy.test.ts` (agent policy `openai/gpt-5.6-*` allows `gpt-5.6-sol`, not `gpt-5.5`) fails on `origin/main` and passes here.
- Validation table adds `openai/gpt-*` (valid for agents) and rejects `openai/gpt *` and `*`.
- Focused suites pass: model visibility, config model-ref validation, operator model policy, role mutation authority, `models status`, legacy Codex model migration, configured model entries, model selection.
- Role compatibility: `modelPolicyWildcardMatches` is a plain prefix test, the same set the old role glob (`^prefix.*$`) accepted, because the parser forbids any other `*`. A new operator-policy regression (`allow: ["vendor/*"]`, `deny: ["vendor/restricted-v1*"]` must deny `vendor/restricted-v1` itself) fails on the first head of this PR and passes now. Stored role snapshots keep the same canonical wildcard keys, so restored policies match as before.
- `pnpm check:changed` (dead-code step skipped) passes; config docs baseline regenerated.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: no stored state or migration; a revert restores the narrower agent grammar. Blast radius: model policy matching for agents and operator roles. Role semantics are unchanged (same prefix rule, same normalized `provider/model` key).

Pash/Sarah check: Sarah's commits on these files (#161609, #162335, #161048, #161004, #159363, #158307, #158703, #151176, #123875) touch Agents API, Codex and Slack config help/validation entries. This PR edits only model-policy wildcard parsing, matching and help text, so their behavior is unchanged.

prs.title: refactor(decisions): streamline OpenAI distribution decoding
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/188252

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI and ClawRouter distribution decoding repeats each item’s record check and copies every distribution before checking whether any probability is positive.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Result values, wire/rubric ordering, malformed-response rejection, refusals and usage retain their existing semantics.

## Why This Change Was Made

Narrow each distribution item once and retain the positive-probability fact during the existing loop. Keep the Map, membership and duplicate checks unchanged; reject cardinality before all-zero distributions.

Extend the existing provider-wire table for primitive entries, unknown/missing labels and all-zero choice/score responses. The score case also protects resetting the positive flag between questions. A literal key-order expectation protects wire insertion order. These26 additional test lines require the matching allocation.

## Evidence

Node syntax, native formatting, whitespace, normal signed commit hooks and the LF ratchet passed. Fresh full-range local review found no actionable defects.

Production size is unchanged. Source-level targets are2N→N record checks and1→0 temporary distribution copies; these are not measured runtime gains.

Qualified provider/runtime/compatibility/ClawRouter tests, types, lint, exact-head CI and matched actual-caller counters/profiles remain pending.

The committed comparison workloads are the ordinary mixed request (a Boolean question, a two-label choice and a three-level score), and the separate 255-label choice capacity case. The ordinary case checks complete literal results, wire order and usage; the maximum case checks successful dispatch and answer count, not the complete returned probability map. This is not an isolated two-label benchmark.

Compare identical final committed test fixtures on baseline/head production variants using five interleaved pairs per workload, fresh qualified workers/caches and source/output bindings. Preserve ordinary mixed-request cost acceptance and the 20% stop policy; no replacement samples. Source-bound counters must distinguish per-item guards and eliminated distribution-copy sites from unrelated work. Counts remain unmeasured. No latency, CPU, RSS or physical-allocation improvement is claimed.

Fresh local-model setup should prefer an available Llama.app model without replacing an existing installation or configured default.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): retain bounded full replies during reload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A warm reload loses the full assistant reply already displayed by live recovery: the browser snapshot contains the 8,000-character history preview, so the first restored row is truncated and later expands by about 280 px.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain the accepted full display response at the transcript recovery owner in existing scoped row-display facts. The renderer can show it while offline or reconnecting; changed source previews reject stale facts, and normal live revalidation remains. Server replay and pairing QR data are removed before retention. The single facts write owner admits a recovered object only when its serialized UTF-8 size is at most **64 KiB**, including its exact source. Larger replies retain today's preview then automatic live recovery behavior.

Projection **13 → 14** drops old disposable cache records: expect **one cold reload after deployment**, then complete cached rows on subsequent reloads. Existing row pruning, 12 MiB record, 24 MiB total, and 20-session limits remain. No server schema, protocol, runtime configuration, or history-request changes.

## User Impact

Loaded replies within the bound return with their complete text/media and final row height. Release-note context: preserve previously displayed complete assistant replies during warm reloads.

## Accepted Paint Tradeoff

The accepted product tradeoff permits paired FCP and first-painted-row increases up to **+90 ms on chat / +60 ms on dashboard** when the first restored row is complete, rather than painting a shorter preview that then expands. Chromium retains the old compositor surface until the new paint. Complete text 11/11, zero expansion, final geometry earlier 11/11, existing cache bounds, and no LoAF/CLS regression beyond A/A remain required.

The final unprofiled run below passes those gates. Its negative paint medians have mixed pair signs and are not presented as a paint-speed improvement. The consistent win is complete cached content and final-row geometry about 0.42–0.51 s earlier, without the 280 px expansion.

## Bounded Attribution

Assessment: **class (a), normal complete-row Markdown/DOM rendering and paint scheduling; no actionable class (b) hotspot found**. This is a bounded assessment from exactly one profiled A/B warm pair per route, not an exact causal allocation of every millisecond in the prior unprofiled FCP rise. No further optimization or trace run is proposed.

Head `596deb526d8e104d1f8f1846f7abb6300ad1f504`, base `04d6904c734a`, AWS `cbx_534db4f28027`, c7a.4xlarge. Same real-Gateway long-Markdown fixture and signed-in admission. Four warm profiles/timelines total. Profiled reports are marked and excluded from timing comparisons; profiler startup, module-cache generation and scheduling materially perturb the wall timings.

To isolate initial cache rendering, source-mapped V8 samples were clipped to the common interval before either arm's first full-message response (about 880 ms chat, 945 ms dashboard under instrumentation). Candidate cached text is already complete in this interval. Inclusive function times overlap; the grouped snapshot/Markdown figures below use exclusive samples.

| Initial interval observation | Chat base → candidate | Dashboard base → candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Snapshot/schema/cache exclusive samples | 4.36 → 6.23 ms | 5.57 → 4.80 ms |
| Facts `read` inclusive samples | 0.39 → 2.13 ms | 1.10 → 1.07 ms |
| Markdown exclusive samples | 32.35 → 27.18 ms | 19.66 → 31.66 ms |
| Layout timeline duration | 81.25 → 78.60 ms | 73.18 → 79.54 ms |
| Style timeline duration | 39.18 → 36.63 ms | 42.66 → 36.66 ms |

The dashboard pair shows about 12 ms extra ordinary Markdown samples and 6 ms extra layout; the chat pair does not reproduce an additional Markdown/layout CPU cost under instrumentation. The measured cache paths are far too small to explain the earlier +85/+54 ms unprofiled wall rise. Source inspection confirms `json.unknown` is an identity reader (`ui/src/lib/snapshot-json.ts:29`), facts reads are synchronous, and `extractTextCached` is memoized. There is no sampled extraction hotspot. These observations support normal render/paint scheduling rather than a new heavyweight cache validation or admission wait. Single-pair sample differences are not performance gains or regression estimates.

Both candidates record exactly one text/height state: complete 7,439-character rendered text at 3,718.5 px. Both baselines record a 6,728-character preview at 3,438.546875 px and then the complete state. No visible cached-preview-to-full replacement appears in either candidate. Source-mapped stacks and raw traces are preserved for independent inspection; no claim is made that a MutationObserver proves absence of every invisible intermediate DOM operation.

The final unprofiled comparison below validates the bound and accepted limits. Profiled timings remain attribution-only.

## Evidence

Performance head: `9dbc39e9cd91770fbe6c6a0f96f523b2b1210f7b`. AWS Crabbox `cbx_3d6c787e45fb`, c7a.4xlarge, 16 CPUs / 30 GiB. One fixed instance for 11 interleaved pairs plus A/A, both routes, both harnesses. Real-Gateway RTT shaping: 80 ms; native Team-scale: live-fast, untraced. A/B quiet-host CPU idle: 92.43%.

The real rig uses production HTTP/WebSocket and synthetic long Markdown. The native Team-scale bench cross-checks the UI with synthetic WebSocket fixtures. Measurements exclude builds/tests; no local-Mac timings are performance evidence.

| chat | 0/11 → 11/11 | 279.95 px → 0.00 px | 95,149 → 113,432 | +18,283 (+19.22%) |

Snapshot growth exceeds the 5% preference. The additional full display and exact source cost about 18 KiB per measured snapshot, below 0.08% of the existing 24 MiB total budget. This removes the visible missing final list items/links and row-height settlement. Canonical history stays unchanged; the existing row pruning, 12 MiB per-record, 24 MiB total and 20-session bounds remain. JSON bytes exclude Blob payloads.

prs.title: fix(release): keep diagnostic FRV blocks pending
prs.body:
## Summary

- Treat a validated `blocked_diagnostics_running` release decision as an active pending handoff instead of a failed release.
- Print the exact parent run and `pnpm frv watch --run <id>` continuation command.
- Preserve fatal behavior for terminal blockers, orchestration errors, and failed workflow conclusions.

## Why

FRV can intentionally stop foreground polling once a release is blocked while diagnostic jobs continue draining. The release is still active in that state, but the CLI currently throws, prints `FAILED`, and exits 1. That misclassifies a recoverable pending release as a failed one.

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run test/scripts/full-release-validation-at-sha.test.ts --config vitest.config.ts -t "observes a validated blocker promptly"`
- `pnpm exec vitest run test/scripts/full-release-validation-at-sha.test.ts --config vitest.config.ts -t "does not use wrong name metadata"`

prs.title: fix(cron): missing-account refusal suggests doctor --fix for jobs Doctor skips
prs.body:
Closes #189908

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a scheduled automation has no recorded inference account and would use a stored auth profile, every run is refused, and the refusal suggests `openclaw doctor --fix` even for jobs Doctor always skips, such as a heartbeat migrated to an automation on an explicitly set Codex runtime, so operators who follow it are refused again on the next run.

## User Impact

User impact: the refusal now leads with the `openclaw automations edit <jobId> --model <provider/model>@<profileId>` command it already printed, and says when `openclaw doctor --fix` does not apply instead of offering it unconditionally.

- The new sentence, shown for every runtime: `openclaw doctor --fix may record it instead, but never for a job that targets the main session, whose primary model uses a CLI runtime, whose runtime is explicitly set to something other than openclaw or auto (by a compatible session runtime override or agentRuntime config), or whose session is model-locked.`
- Operators in those four cases, including a migrated heartbeat on an explicitly set Codex runtime, are pointed at the edit command instead of a repair that leaves the job unchanged. Other operators still see `doctor --fix`, now in this longer conditional sentence.
- The edit command also sets the job's primary model to the one in the command, which Doctor's adoption does not. The troubleshooting entry for this message now leads with the edit command and lists the same four cases.
- Unchanged: which runs are refused, which account Doctor adopts, how credentials are used, and the message's opening sentence, its runtime and account sentence, and its edit command. All four call sites share the message function, so all of them show the new text. Stored jobs are not changed; a job refused today shows the new text on its next refusal.

## Why This Change Was Made

#185070 (`f31b33f`) unified this refusal for every runtime, with `or with openclaw doctor --fix` as the second path. Doctor's account pass (#172792, `d277de7`; its description: "native-owned cases are not silently assigned another account") always skips a job that targets the main session, whose primary model uses a CLI runtime, whose runtime is explicitly set to something other than `openclaw` or `auto` by a compatible session runtime override or `agentRuntime` config, or whose session is model-locked. This PR keeps Doctor and the refusal as they are and changes only the hint.

The sentence states those four cases the way Doctor evaluates them, and the comment on the message function points to Doctor's account pass as their source. Deciding at run time whether Doctor would adopt the job would mean recomputing Doctor's decision from the job's primary selection and session entry at all four call sites, which raise this refusal for the candidate being run, possibly a fallback model. Doctor can also leave a job unchanged for other reasons, such as a personal account, no available stored account, an explicitly selected profile that cannot be used, or several eligible accounts when none is the one a run would use; "may" makes no claim about those.

Not changed: Doctor and its output, the refusal condition, the message function's signature and its four call sites, and Gateway startup diagnostics (they read only the configured runtime policy and print their own hint).

<details>
<summary>Doctor's skip conditions and the matching clauses (source at d67aa608643f)</summary>

| Doctor's account pass skips the job when | Source (`inference-binding-migration.ts`) | Doctor prints | Clause in the new sentence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| it targets the main session (`sessionTarget: "main"`) | [L95](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d67aa608643f6583a6c6102c522043794aafe064/src/commands/doctor/cron/inference-binding-migration.ts#L95) | nothing | "a job that targets the main session" |
| the job's primary model selection uses a CLI runtime | [L135-L160](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d67aa608643f6583a6c6102c522043794aafe064/src/commands/doctor/cron/inference-binding-migration.ts#L135-L160) | nothing | "whose primary model uses a CLI runtime" |
| a compatible session runtime override, or else the configured runtime policy for the primary selection, is set and is neither `openclaw` nor `auto` | [L161-L178](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d67aa608643f6583a6c6102c522043794aafe064/src/commands/doctor/cron/inference-binding-migration.ts#L161-L178) | `runtime <id> inference ownership was left unchanged; no host account was adopted. …` | "whose runtime is explicitly set to something other than openclaw or auto (by a compatible session runtime override or agentRuntime config)" |
| the session entry has `modelSelectionLocked` | [L129-L134](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d67aa608643f6583a6c6102c522043794aafe064/src/commands/doctor/cron/inference-binding-migration.ts#L129-L134) | `its session is owned by a native runtime; no host inference account was adopted. …` | "whose session is model-locked" |

- "Model-locked" names the flag Doctor checks. The flag also protects ordinary UI sessions ([`agent-harness-session-key.ts` L230-L232](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d67aa608643f6583a6c6102c522043794aafe064/src/sessions/agent-harness-session-key.ts#L230-L232)), so the sentence does not call these sessions native-owned.
- Implicit Codex routing (no session override, policy unset or `auto`) does not trigger the explicit-runtime skip; Doctor may still decline adoption for its other documented reasons.
- The `Runtime …` sentence names the candidate being run, which can be a fallback model; the exceptions refer to the job's primary model, as Doctor does.
- A main-session `agentTurn` job runs as a scheduled turn inside the main session ([`execution-context.ts` L325-L327](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d67aa608643f6583a6c6102c522043794aafe064/src/cron/execution-context.ts#L325-L327)), so it can reach this refusal.

</details>

## Evidence

**Live run: the latest stable writes the state, then the base build and this change run on that same state** (2026-10-31 UTC; Linux x86_64, Node 24.22.1). Stable is `OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (8b18b55)`, npm `latest` at the time. The base build is `d67aa608643f` and reports `OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (d67aa60)`. This change is a build of that same commit with this PR's production change applied in the working tree, so it reports the same `OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (d67aa60)`; its built output has the new sentence and not the old one (`OLD` / `NEW` in the excerpts). One isolated `HOME`; the Gateway listened on loopback with token auth; one real OpenAI OAuth sign-in (device code), the only stored auth profile (`openai:<profile>`); the default model `openai/gpt-6-astra` with `agentRuntime: { id: "codex" }` in model config. The Gateways of the base build and this change used the bundled Codex plugin (`Codex app-server: using bundled 0.164.0`); the global `@openclaw/codex@2026.10.9` plugin from the stable install was overridden by the bundled one as a duplicate plugin id. For the test, heartbeat used `target: "none"`, `every: "24h"` and a fixed prompt asking only for the reply `FU14-HEARTBEAT-OK`, and runs were started with `openclaw automations run <jobId>`. Redacted excerpts are in the collapsed block below.

- **Stable writes the state.** `openclaw@2026.10.9` from npm, in an isolated prefix, stored a heartbeat automation `heartbeat-main` (`payload.kind: "heartbeat"`, `sessionTarget: "main"`) that had not run.
- **Before (base build).** `openclaw doctor --fix --yes` migrated it to an `agentTurn` job, still `heartbeat-main` (`sessionTarget: "session:<session-key>"`, `delivery.mode: "none"`), and printed `Automation heartbeat-main (<job-id>): runtime codex inference ownership was left unchanged; no host account was adopted. Use that runtime's account/recovery flow if this job needs adoption.` The next run was refused (run status `error`) with `Automation has no recorded inference account. Runtime codex would run openai/gpt-6-astra with stored account openai:<profile>. Record the account with openclaw automations edit <jobId> --model openai/gpt-6-astra@openai:<profile>, or with openclaw doctor --fix.` After a second `doctor --fix --yes`, which printed the same line, the next run was refused again with the same sentence.
- **After (this change, same state).** `doctor --fix --yes` printed the same line and left the job unchanged. The next run was refused with `Automation has no recorded inference account. Runtime codex would run openai/gpt-6-astra with stored account openai:<profile>. Record the account with openclaw automations edit <jobId> --model openai/gpt-6-astra@openai:<profile>. openclaw doctor --fix may record it instead, but never for a job that targets the main session, whose primary model uses a CLI runtime, whose runtime is explicitly set to something other than openclaw or auto (by a compatible session runtime override or agentRuntime config), or whose session is model-locked.`
- **Following the message.** `openclaw automations edit <jobId> --model openai/gpt-6-astra@openai:<profile>` succeeded, and the job list then showed `payload.model` as `openai/gpt-6-astra@openai:<profile>`. The job list does not output the inference binding; that the `model@profile` capture this command uses records one with `runtime: "codex"` is shown by the focused-test reproduction below. The next run was not refused and completed a turn on the real Codex harness (this state has only one stored account): status `ok`, summary `FU14-HEARTBEAT-OK`. For that run, the refusal text appears 0 times in the run record, the console log and the file log, and the run window has exactly one Codex app-server session file, with one turn started (`task_started`) and one completed (`task_complete`).

<details>
<summary>Redacted excerpts</summary>

```text

NPM_LATEST 2026.10.9

│  Automation heartbeat-main (<job-id>):      │

SOURCE=doctor --fix --yes, 3rd run (this change)

=== RUN 1 (base build) ===

STATUS=error
ERROR=Session event execution failed
Automation has no recorded inference account. Runtime codex would run openai/gpt-6-astra with stored account openai:<profile>. Record the account with openclaw automations edit <jobId> --model openai/gpt-6-astra@openai:<profile>, or with openclaw doctor --fix.

Record the account with openclaw automations edit <jobId> --model openai/gpt-6-astra@openai:<profile>. openclaw doctor --fix may record it instead, but never for a job that targets the main session, whose primary model uses a CLI runtime, whose runtime is explicitly set to something other than openclaw or auto (by a compatible session runtime override or agentRuntime config), or whose session is model-locked.

Notes: `<profile>`, `<job-id>`, `<uuid>` and `<session-key>` are redaction markers; `<jobId>` in the refusal text is OpenClaw's own placeholder. Commit hashes are shortened. Under each run, the refusal line is taken from the Gateway console log (the run record's error field holds only the generic `Session event execution failed`), and lines the excerpt had split are rejoined as in that log. Doctor prints its ownership line inside a box; only the first line of that message is shown, and the full line is quoted above. Section headers and `SOURCE` labels were added by the extraction script and relabeled here; they are not OpenClaw output.

</details>

**Regression test** on `d67aa608643f` (Linux x86_64, Node 24.22.1), `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`. Red: the base with only the test change applied. Green: with the production change as well.

- `src/cron/isolated-agent.auth-continuity.integration.test.ts`, case `enforces unadopted stored account before provider HTTP through the real runner` (real isolated runner; it also asserts that no provider HTTP request is made): the expected message is now the full new text.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): resolve literal remote-shell and ssh identity paths without trimming
prs.body:
Fixes #190056

## What Problem This Solves

Two path-selected inputs still trimmed their value before use, and the SSH identity kept being trimmed again by the Gateway callers that feed the tunnel.

- The remote-shell sandbox file bridge (`sandbox.backend: "ssh"` / remote shell) resolved `" note.txt"` to the sibling `note.txt`. A read returned the wrong file; a write overwrote it.
- The SSH tunnel (`openclaw gateway status`, client `gateway.remote.sshIdentity`) passed `gateway.remote.sshIdentity.trim()` to `ssh -i`, so a configured identity file whose name ends in whitespace loaded a different key.
- After fixing the tunnel, three Gateway owners still trimmed the configured identity before it reached the tunnel: `gatewayStatusCommand` (`sanitizeSshTarget` on the configured value), `resolveGatewayDeviceAuthRoute` (`normalizeOptionalString`), and `resolveSshConfig` (`opts.identity.trim()`). A user configuring `gateway.remote.sshIdentity: "/keys/id test "` never got the trailing space to `ssh -i`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the selected path literal at every owner that holds the configured value; the trimming resolver still owns only CLI-typed invocation strings and the SSH host target. The mount-containment guard is unchanged.

- `startSshPortForward`/`resolveSshConfig` load the exact identity file they are given (`-i`).
- `gatewayStatusCommand` preserves the configured `gateway.remote.sshIdentity` verbatim; CLI `--ssh-identity` still normalizes.
- `resolveGatewayDeviceAuthRoute` preserves the configured identity verbatim.
- The remote-shell bridge keeps the caller's `filePath` literal; only the invocation base goes through the trimming resolver.

Precedent: #187777 (OpenShell mirror-mode renderer), #187554 (linked hook discovery paths). Original fix by @wangmiao0668000666.

## Evidence

All legs are proven against the **compiled production `dist/`** (no vitest, no test doubles), running a real agent turn / real ssh client against a real `sshd` on `127.0.0.1:2222`, on an isolated Linux box. The fixture drives the real entry points: Leg A and Leg C use the shipped `ssh-tunnel-*.mjs` / `gateway-status-*.mjs` bundles, and Leg B runs the shipped `dist/entry.js agent --local` with a mock OpenAI-compatible model that asks the `read` tool for `" note.txt"`.

Harness: `proof-188906.mjs` / `proof-matrix.mjs` (Leg A/B: dynamically imports the compiled `ssh-tunnel-*.mjs`, runs the real `startSshPortForward` against a disposable loopback `sshd`, and runs the real agent turn). Leg C invokes the compiled `gatewayStatusCommand` bundle with the configured trailing-space identity. Ref under test swaps `dist/`; everything else is identical.

### Leg A — ssh tunnel identity (gateway.remote.sshIdentity)

`startSshPortForward({ target: "root@127.0.0.1:2222", identity: "/proof/keys/key.pending " })`. The configured identity path ends in a trailing space. Two contradictory keys are installed: the LITERAL path `/proof/keys/key.pending ` (RSA `SHA256:XI06ezVZAi99pMBJo/uw62G4ZNXWsgbS5L9U+6uMuok`) and the trimmed sibling `/proof/keys/key.trim` (RSA `SHA256:o2b1l7QQtnCpRbbsioGAeDlZOVhxdUopbtHzfiqcEdQ`). The server logs exactly which public key was accepted during kex; the tunnelled HTTP request proves the tunnel carries the process.

| ref | identity | result | server sees |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| head `3e023096ccb` | `/proof/keys/key.pending ` | `tunnel started`, HTTP `200 OPENCLAW_PROOF_HTTP_OK` | `Accepted publickey ... RSA SHA256:XI06ezVZAi99pMBJo/uw62G4ZNXWsgbS5L9U+6uMuok` (the LITERAL key) |
| base `8034bb1fafb` | `/proof/keys/key.pending ` | `tunnel rejected` (ssh exit 255) | ssh stderr: `Warning: Identity file /proof/keys/key.pending not accessible: No such file or directory.` — the trailing space was trimmed, so ssh loaded the nonexistent `key.pending` path |

### Leg B — remote-shell sandbox file bridge

The ssh sandbox runtime (`sandbox.backend: "ssh"`, `ssh.workspaceRoot: /proof/mirror`) mirrors the agent's local workspace to `<workspaceRoot>/<runtimeId>/workspace`. The local workspace holds BOTH the literal `" note.txt"` (`PROOF_REMOTE_LITERAL_4C1D`) and the decoy `note.txt` (`PROOF_REMOTE_DECOY_9A2B`). The mock model asks `read(" note.txt")`; the shipped agent resolves the path through the real `resolveTarget`.

| ref | model observed | agent result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| head `3e023096ccb` | `READ RESULT literal=true decoy=false: PROOF_REMOTE_LITERAL_4C1D` | `PROOF_LITERAL` — read the literal `" note.txt"` |
| base `8034bb1fafb` | `READ RESULT literal=false decoy=true: PROOF_REMOTE_DECOY_9A2B` | `PROOF_DECOY` — trimmed `" note.txt"` → read the sibling `note.txt` |

### Leg C — configured gateway-status entry point (P2 caller fix)

The compiled `gateway-status-*.mjs` bundle (`gatewayStatusCommand`) is invoked with a real config whose `gateway.remote.sshIdentity` ends in a trailing space, against a real `sshd` on `127.0.0.1:2222`. Two contradictory identity files are installed: the LITERAL path `/proof-c/keys/key.pending ` (RSA `SHA256:XI06ezVZAi99pMBJo/uw62G4ZNXWsgbS5L9U+6uMuok`) and the trimmed sibling `/proof-c/keys/key.trim` (RSA `SHA256:o2b1l7QQtnCpRbbsioGAeDlZOVhxdUopbtHzfiqcEdQ`). The command runs the real chain `gatewayStatusCommand → resolveSshConfig → startSshPortForward → ssh -i`, and the server logs which key was accepted.

| ref | sshd sees | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| head `79c4156a3e2` (P2 fix) | `Accepted publickey ... RSA SHA256:XI06ezVZAi99pMBJo/uw62G4ZNXWsgbS5L9U+6uMuok` (the LITERAL key, twice) | the configured trailing-space identity reaches real `ssh -i` unchanged |
| base `8034bb1fafb` | `Connection closed by 127.0.0.1 ... [preauth]` | the identity was trimmed to `/proof-c/keys/key.pending`, no usable key → sshd rejects before authentication |

## Focused tests

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Node 24.22.1, Linux:

- `src/infra/ssh-tunnel.test.ts`: 26 passed (whole file; new case `passes the configured identity to ssh without trimming its whitespace`). On base the new case fails with `expected [ '-i', '/keys/id test' ] to deeply equal [ '-i', '/keys/id test ' ]`.
- `src/agents/sandbox/remote-fs-bridge.test.ts`: 24 passed (whole file; new case `addresses literal whitespace-padded paths instead of their trimmed siblings`). On base it fails because `" note.txt"` returns the trimmed sibling's bytes.
- `src/infra/ssh-config.test.ts`: 7 passed (new assertion keeps `-i "/keys/id test "` literal instead of trimming).
- `src/gateway/client-bootstrap.test.ts`: 24 passed (new case `preserves trailing whitespace in the configured ssh identity path` asserts `resolveGatewayDeviceAuthRoute` returns `identity: "/keys/id test "`).
- `src/commands/gateway-status.test.ts`: 31 passed (new case `passes a configured ssh identity to the tunnel without trimming its whitespace` asserts `startSshPortForward` receives `identity: "/keys/id test "` for `gateway.remote.sshIdentity: "/keys/id test "`).

Existing directory, mount-root, symlink-escape and read-only protections keep their assertions.

Not tested: real SSH host, Windows, macOS, mounted gateway flows, live gateway, real remote gateway server (Leg C's remote probe fails after the tunnel is up; the key-acceptance evidence is the sshd auth log).

## Merge danger

Two-way door: revert restores the trimming. No stored format, migration or protocol change. Users who (unintentionally) relied on trailing whitespace being ignored in `gateway.remote.sshIdentity` or in remote-shell relative paths now address the literal value they supplied; that matches every file tool and the documented behavior of #187777.

prs.title: fix(codex): stop background exec completions from replaying full history into a fresh thread
prs.body:
Related: #183286, #179363, #172026, #178982

## What Problem This Solves

When a background `exec` finishes in a Codex-backed WebChat session, the completion wake does not continue the session's bound native thread. It starts a fresh transient thread, replays the full session history into it uncached, and does it again for the follow-up turn. On a long session every completion wake costs a full uncached history read. In one observed session, four completion wakes each sent about 190k uncached input tokens.

This finishes, for event wakes, what #183286 started: tool declarations belong to the session, not to the turn. #183286 kept seven native Codex thread, plugin, and supervision declarations stable across owner and completion turns. A completion wake still differed from the user turn in three other ways, and each one alone forces a new thread:

1. **Tool-policy scope.** The default session-event source policy caps every follow-up at the producer's tool list. A wake with a cap runs as a turn-scoped restricted turn, which the Codex harness serves on a transient thread with native code mode off (48 eager dynamic tools instead of 10).
2. **`skill_workshop` schema.** The personal-library schema is published only on human turns that carry an authoring grant. A wake publishes a narrower schema, the dynamic tool catalog fingerprint changes, and the bound thread rotates. The Claude CLI runner already fixed this in #172026 (`resolveStableCliSkillAuthoring`); the embedded/harness path never used it.
3. **Conversation context.** An internal (WebChat) session stores no delivery route, so `buildSessionEventContext` never matched the wake's own WebChat route and dropped the session chat type. The wake's developer instructions then lacked the "You are in a WebChat direct conversation" line, the live thread config fingerprint changed, and Codex had to cold-resume the thread.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each layer is fixed where the difference starts, without widening authority:

- **Scope (A).** A cap from a conversation-scoped producer turn is the session's own policy, and the follow-up re-derives that policy itself. `createCodingToolsGatewayCaller` marks the caller identity session-scoped when the policy scope is `conversation` and no caller-supplied source policy exists, and `session-event-target` skips it only when the follow-up's destination is the same session. The mark is not set when group, per-DM, or sender policy narrowed the producer (`groupPolicy`/`senderPolicy`). Those come from the inbound request, the wake cannot rebuild them, and the cap keeps carrying them. The caller-inheritance merge keeps the mark only for an inherited owner of the same agent and session that has no narrower cap of its own. Cross-session follow-ups, sender-narrowed producers, and turn-scoped producers keep the cap exactly as before.
- **Policy lifetime stays host-owned.** No public SDK option is added. The host already computes the attempt's policy lifetime for Codex (`pluginHarnessToolPolicyScope`, `resolvePluginHarnessToolPolicies`). Host policy preparation now records that value in the attempt's host capability, and the host's tool construction (`createToolSurfaceAsync`, which is how Codex builds every dynamic tool) passes it to the internal tool options. A plugin cannot set it through tool options: a plugin-supplied `toolPolicyScope` is overwritten by the host value, and when the host has none the cap stays in place (fail-closed).
- **`skill_workshop` (B).** The #172026 helper moves from `cli-runner/` to `src/agents/stable-skill-authoring.ts` as a per-runtime factory and is also applied at the embedded attempt dispatch. Internal turns publish the session's last human shape with an expired grant: the declaration matches, personal-library calls fail with `AUTHORITY_EXPIRED`, and workspace calls keep the ordinary no-grant rule (unsandboxed runs only). Grants that are already expired (transcript follow-ups, stranded-reply recovery) now carry `expired: true` and no longer replace the remembered human shape.
- **Context (C).** For a session that stores no delivery route, an event on that session's own WebChat route (`channel: "webchat"`, `to: <sessionKey>`, the shape `chat.send` and subagent announce already use) keeps the session chat type. Events routed to any other session still get none.

Out of scope, noted for follow-up: when a thread's config does change (for example a model switch), Codex can take longer than OpenClaw's 2-second unload budget to close a code-mode thread after `thread/unsubscribe` (measured 0.7 s, 2.9 s, and 10.6 s in this harness). The cold resume then fails with "Codex did not confirm unloading its previous configuration". With this change, completion wakes no longer take that path.

AI-assisted: written with Claude Code. Every claim below was checked by running it.

## User Impact

- Background `exec` completion wakes in Codex-backed sessions continue the bound thread with native code mode on. The wake reads the session prefix from cache instead of replaying the full history uncached, and the next user turn stays on the same thread.
- No tool, personal-library, or workspace access is widened. Sessions narrowed by group, per-DM, or sender policy keep today's behavior, including the fresh-thread wake.
- On internal turns with a remembered personal default target, `skill_workshop` calls that rely on that default now return `AUTHORITY_EXPIRED` instead of running against the workspace. Explicit `target=workspace` calls keep the no-grant rule.

## Evidence

### November 1 upkeep (current head)

Rebased onto main `72cab24990b`; `git range-diff` confirms all four existing commits are patch-identical. Added only `config/test-lines-allocations/codex-exec-event-thread.txt` (282 lines): the authority final-effect matrix, host-owned policy scope, expired skill-authoring grant, and wake-context regressions protect distinct contracts. The shared test-line scalar is unchanged.

- Test-line ratchet passes: 6,366,399 lines / 6,385,147 effective ceiling. `git diff --check` passes.
- Local focused run is **not green**: wake-context 3/3 passed; permission suite 27 passed / 4 failed. The local install has `@openclaw/fs-safe` 0.26.13 while current main requires 0.27.0; the installed `advanced` module lacks `overwriteFileHandleWithAuthority`, breaking actual writes (including the same-session regression). Other selected agent suites did not yield valid results in this wrapper run. Total wrapper time: 116.17 seconds. Fresh CI is required; the older passing evidence below is historical, not a claim about this head.
- Previous-head CI lint failed on an untouched `sessions-send-tool.admission.test.ts` curly-brace violation. The old test-line budget failure is addressed by the rebase and dedicated allocation. No claim that new-head CI is green yet.
- Maintainer security-sensitive approval remains required; contributor changes cannot satisfy that gate.

Regression tests, each shown failing without its fix and passing with it:

| Test | Without fix | With fix |
|---|---|---|
| `host-capability.tool-policy-scope.test.ts` (new): host-prepared scope reaches tool construction; a plugin-supplied `toolPolicyScope: "conversation"` does not | 2 failed, 1 passed (host value not injected) | 3 passed |
| `session-event-permissions.test.ts` "bounds a same-session background completion's final effects: same-session" | fails: `writeOffered: false`, expected `true` (the producer cap is kept) | passes |
| `agent-tools.session-event-cap.test.ts` "a sender narrowed by toolsBySender" (real `createOpenClawCodingTools`, real caller identity, no mock) | fails: `expected true to be undefined` when the sender check is removed | 3 passed |
| `stable-skill-authoring.test.ts` "keeps the human shape when a follow-up passes an expired grant" | 1 failed, 3 passed | 4 passed |
| `session-event-context.test.ts` "keeps the session chat type only for $route" | 1 failed, 2 passed | 3 passed |
| `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` "offers the human turn's skill_workshop definition on an internal turn" | asserts the surfaces differ without the helper | equal with it |

### Authority controls around the same-session exemption

`session-event-permissions.test.ts` "bounds a same-session background completion's final effects" runs the production path: a real `captureSessionEventTargetForHost` under a caller identity, the real `enqueueSessionEventForHost` admission, the real harness host capabilities and managed tool surface, and a real file write. Each row captures a producer whose ceiling lists only `read`:

| Row | Producer identity | Follow-up tool surface | File after the follow-up |
|---|---|---|---|
| `same-session` | same session, marked session-scoped | `write` offered | written |
| `restricted-sender` | same session, not marked (the caller leaves the mark off when `senderPolicy` or `groupPolicy` narrowed the turn; see the caller test above) | no `write` | unchanged |
| `cross-session` | other session, marked | no `write` | unchanged |
| `revoked-before-write` | same session, marked; the session permission mode is set to `read-only` after the tool surface is built | `write` offered, call refused (authority/permission error) | unchanged |

Result: 4 passed. With `session-event-target.ts` restored to its base version, the `same-session` row fails (`writeOffered: false`).

Expired personal-library calls: `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` builds the real coding tools for an internal turn and shows `skill_workshop` with `target: "personal"` rejected with "fresh message" (`AUTHORITY_EXPIRED`). `stable-skill-authoring.test.ts` shows an expired grant refuses personal-library calls and never replaces the remembered human shape; the sandboxed-run refusal for workspace calls is unchanged code from #172026 and is not re-tested here.

What this does not show: the embedded dispatch wiring (`resolveStableEmbeddedSkillAuthoring` at `run-attempt-dispatch.ts`) is a single call covered by the two tests above through the same factory, not by a dispatch-level test.

Touched suites: the files above plus `gateway-caller-context.test.ts` and `agent-tools.delegated-authority.test.ts` pass. The new production-boundary rows pass 4 of 4. `tsgo` core and the `src` test shards: clean. `oxfmt` on the repository: clean. `check:test-mock-exports` and `check:max-lines-ratchet` against the base commit: OK (the PR adds no mock factory and no line to `agent-tools.ts` or `cli-runner/prepare.ts`).

### Required test lanes that fail on this PR's CI

Three required lanes failed on the earlier heads. Each was checked against `main`:

- `src/gateway/mcp-http.exec-completion.test.ts` "an empty CLI final": fails the same way with every file this PR touches restored to `origin/main` (`1e89f5b3fe8`), and fails in CI on unrelated PRs (for example https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40290743775 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40292785214). It is inherited.
- `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.requester-wake.e2e.test.ts` "drains a restored interrupted predecessor before later cohorts": fails the same way with the PR's files restored to `origin/main`, and fails in CI on an unrelated PR (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40292474849). It is inherited.
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.operator-continuation.test.ts`: all 20 tests pass locally on this branch merged with `origin/main`. I could not reproduce the CI failure. By construction this PR cannot reach that path: the new session-scoped marking requires `toolPolicyScope: "conversation"`, which that test never sets, so its follow-up ceiling is unchanged. I did not find this failure on another PR, so I cannot call it inherited.

Live run against a real Codex app-server (codex 0.162.1, the version pinned on `main`), an isolated gateway, and `chat.send`. Script: user turn, a turn that starts `exec` with `background=true`, the completion wake, then a user turn. Wire capture of the app-server JSON-RPC, base `4fa442e3327`:

```
# stock (4fa442e3327)
in thread/start None dynTools=10
-> thread thread-A
# user turn
in turn/start thread-A
usage thread-A in= 20064 cached= 0
out turn/completed thread-A completed
# user turn that starts the background exec
in turn/start thread-A
usage thread-A in= 20204 cached= 20061
usage thread-A in= 21343 cached= 20201
usage thread-A in= 21589 cached= 21340
out turn/completed thread-A completed
in thread/start None dynTools=48
-> thread thread-B
# completion wake (turn 1 of 2)
in turn/start thread-B
usage thread-B in= 29269 cached= 0
out turn/completed thread-B completed
in thread/start None dynTools=48
-> thread thread-C
# completion wake (turn 2 of 2)
in turn/start thread-C
usage thread-C in= 29183 cached= 0
out turn/completed thread-C completed
```

```
# this branch
in thread/start None dynTools=10
-> thread thread-A
# user turn
in turn/start thread-A
usage thread-A in= 20064 cached= 0
out turn/completed thread-A completed
# user turn that starts the background exec
in turn/start thread-A
usage thread-A in= 20204 cached= 20061
usage thread-A in= 21336 cached= 20201
usage thread-A in= 21632 cached= 21333
out turn/completed thread-A completed
# completion wake (turn 1 of 2)
in turn/start thread-A
usage thread-A in= 21761 cached= 21629
out turn/completed thread-A completed
# completion wake (turn 2 of 2)
in turn/start thread-A
usage thread-A in= 21830 cached= 21758
out turn/completed thread-A completed
# next user turn
in turn/start thread-A
usage thread-A in= 22124 cached= 21827
out turn/completed thread-A completed
```

The live run used commit 591bd2b60aa on base `4fa442e3327`. The branch was then rebased onto `d4ae3a73118` without conflicts. Typecheck and the regression and affected suites were rerun after the rebase. Commit `80b8c1192d9` came later: it moves the marking decision into `createCodingToolsGatewayCaller` and adds the tests above, with no change to the runtime behavior traced here; the live trace was not repeated.

Stock: each wake turn starts a fresh thread with 48 dynamic tools and 0 cached tokens. Patched: one thread with 10 dynamic tools for the whole session. The wake turns are plain `turn/start` calls on the bound thread, reading 99% of their input from cache, with no `thread/resume` or `thread/unsubscribe` in the wire log. The next user turn stays on the same thread. (The stock run's next user turn did not reach the app-server before the harness stopped, so it is not shown.)

What this evidence does not show: the harness covers a WebChat direct session with no group, per-DM, or sender policy. Sessions with those policies are covered by the unit tests above, not by a live run.

prs.title: fix(packaging): exclude source-build ledgers from npm packages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Build-only source-module ledgers are published in the main and bundled AI packages and count toward the installed-tree limits enforced by shipped updaters.

## User Impact

Installed packages omit unused build metadata while retaining runtime exports and package integrity inventories. Source builds retain the ledgers needed to construct standalone artifacts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Exclude `.source-module-urls` directories at both owning package manifests. Tests exercise real npm and pnpm publication, bundled AI, similarly named runtime directories, and filename/content inventories. Production delta: two manifest rules; no runtime, migration, or budget changes.

The frozen comparison base includes the previously merged Brotli omission from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188097.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186506

## Evidence

- Source head: `87a2e9c5be351fc0c8115da2acf8788495772f88`.
- Eight focused test files passed on Linux with Bun and Node: 201 tests per runtime, covering real publication, inventories, build ledgers, standalone source/sidecar consumers, and command cleanup.
- Targeted format/lint and file-size/test-line checks passed.
- Independent exact-head source review completed with no findings.
- Canonical build, AI/root packing and tarball integrity checks passed. The installed Linux npm 12 package passed CLI version, AI import and selected Doctor (`core/doctor/node-runtime`) checks.
- Installed-tree budget: **46,400 / 47,500 entries** and **572.5 / 900 MiB**. No budget changes or exceptions.
- [Exact-source Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41267905504): all 17 command phases passed. Native completion and outer supervision both exited 0 and settled without forced cleanup.
- Candidate SHA-256: `c0aed1bce14cc1c777c66de9850615ac103264a35e1082e48661e9a94e4bf9ca`. Built from tree `5fed0094950d51b5aa0bcc640d5c8f507c88bce2` through native carrier `b495c43777719a44c6e102318c69f98d71bd524c`.

Follow-up: consolidate cancellation ownership between the package-build launcher and its implementation; this remains separate from the publication rules reviewed here.

Current hosted CI on `87a2e9c5` completed **failed**: [run 41268824876, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41268824876), [`check-lint-extensions-2` job 124737751607](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41268824876/job/124737751607), reports `typescript/consistent-return` at `extensions/workboard/src/gateway.ts:350`; the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` also failed. The gateway source, lint rule and runner are identical on frozen base `d6d76cd1`, this head and captured main `28476eeec2d`; baseline CI was not rerun. **Landing remains held; no waiver or inherited-CI exception has been applied.**

prs.title: fix: avoid loading unconfigured channel runtimes for profiles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening a personal profile asks for Discord account-link status even when Discord is not configured. The handler falls through to the bundled channel resolver, which synchronously loads the full Discord runtime. The profile real-Gateway CI test stalled in this RPC for 15 seconds and then 38 seconds in run 41265660907, before the initial profile name rendered.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve loaded and request-scoped channel adapters first, and allow bundled fallback only when the channel has an explicit configuration record. Use the same resolver when rechecking the adapter's identity during OAuth completion. Configured adapters remain usable before a channel runtime starts; stored identities remain visible as unavailable and can still be disconnected after configuration is removed.

This adds no cache or lifecycle state. A disabled but explicitly configured channel may still load its adapter; its existing adapter eligibility rules remain authoritative.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Regression on unchanged handler | Cold unconfigured status fails as expected; other 8 tests pass |
| Focused handler suite on fix | 9/9 pass; 53.79 s including compilation, about 5 s test work |
| Work count | Unconfigured status/disconnect load the bundled channel zero times |
| Core typecheck / targeted lint / format | Pass |
| Full build | Pass; 3m30s |
| Independent review | Autoreview P0–P2, complete source context, no actionable findings |
| Profile real-Gateway test | PR CI will exercise the prebuilt runtime; no inherited-failure claim |

The added cases cover empty status, saved-link status/disconnect without configuration, and configured fallback linking. Existing real Discord adapter and live-authority revocation tests remain intact. Production LOC: 214→221; test LOC: 329→377 (48 allocated regression lines). No UI markup, screenshot, or layout change.

Related diagnosis: #189949. This fix is separate from that model-picker performance change.

Release-note context: avoid loading an unconfigured channel runtime while opening a personal profile.

prs.title: perf(sessions): avoid recopying admitted transcript payloads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Preparing replay or media envelopes for transcript storage can copy immutable message payloads that were already admitted.

## User Impact

Fewer duplicate payload walks and allocations during message appends. Stored transcript bytes, replay sanitization, media normalization, and mutable-envelope behavior are preserved; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

`canonicalizeSessionEntry` owns the SessionManager ingress, using `normalizeTranscriptJsonValue` to establish immutable payload ownership. Unchanged messages already reuse that fact. Replacement envelopes in replay/image sanitization and persisted-media canonicalization lost it, so worker preparation walked the unchanged children again.

Reuse the existing `cloneTranscriptEnvelope` operation introduced by #183772 at those replacements. Raw ingress and newly created branches still pass through normalization; the prepared append continues carrying canonical JSON to the writer. Remove the sanitizer's extra copy of its already-new image envelope. Runtime delta: **−1 line**; no new cache, state, schema, or public API.

This is intentionally bounded ownership propagation. It does not remove the normalizer from direct append ingress or claim that unchanged descendants inside every changed array are reused.

## Evidence

Two storage-preparation regressions fail on the parent because unchanged payload identities are copied despite equal bytes, then pass with ownership propagation. Independent expected JSON covers replay removal, canonical media, non-finite values, omitted array values, Unicode and a lone surrogate. Existing normalization/admission, sanitizer, persisted-media, prefix-stability and provider replay proof passes: **87 distinct focused tests**. The final changed file takes 16.26 seconds including compilation/startup; its two added cases are milliseconds.

The production Control UI build passes (22.68 seconds). `pnpm check:changed --staged --base 079889d5a09102246b34b363ff340591729d5a80` passes on the final change. Production and full-tree unused-file scans pass. Test-line growth is allocated only for the two distinct regression cases.

Codex autoreview completed at P2 over the local change against `079889d5a09102246b34b363ff340591729d5a80`. Its sole finding predicted that the new helper import would break browser bundling. Rejected after checking the actual supported UI build: it succeeds, and no emitted source map contains `transcript-json.ts`; the unused normalizer is tree-shaken. The reviewer did not run that build. No accepted actionable finding remains; this is a reviewed disagreement, not a claim that the reviewer returned scoped-clean.

The final head is `975a82f153559a24a6d0cefc042457efac11fe98`. [CI run 41266846931](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41266846931) passes, including `security-fast` and `openclaw/ci-gate`; hosted Codex review completed on that head with no findings. No inherited-failure exception is used. The benchmark's macOS clone-copy correction also passes independent Codex review and `pnpm check:changed --base HEAD` before its commit.

The predeclared acceptance rule was five A/A pairs and five counterbalanced A/B pairs for each of untraced append timing, sampled allocation, and separately instrumented normalization-owner timing. Every arm performs 1,000 real awaited appends after 12 warmups. Require equal persisted-message hashes, fewer normalization visits/allocations, and no established material (>20%) aggregate append CPU/latency regression. No completed sample was excluded or repeated. CI started while measurements finished; merge remained gated on the same rule.

Workload: one closed **35.129 GiB synthetic SQLite database**, **10,000 sessions / 1,000,000 events**, and a **62,000-file / 1.116 GB** synthetic workspace. Each arm clones the seed; the seeded legacy inline rows provide background occupancy, while measured appends use the current real `SessionManager.appendMessageAsync` path. Four equally weighted message shapes cover plain tool results, replay replacement, signature replacement, and legacy media, with 16 KiB text and nested tool details. macOS/APFS, Node 26.12.1; no production data. This does not establish Linux/btrfs I/O or whole-Gateway performance.

Normalization boundary calls remain 2,000 per 1,000 appends; recursive admission and normalization visits each fall **117,000→85,750 (−26.71%)**. The plain-message control remains 114 visits per append in both versions. The initial 100-append diagnostic and the scale pair agree.

All following CPU, wall and allocation totals are per **1,000 appends**; latency rows summarize each arm's per-append percentiles. Each side has five samples, so nearest-rank across-arm p95 equals the maximum shown. Owner timing is separately instrumented; whole-append timing is untraced. Allocation is main-isolate V8 sampled allocation (32 KiB interval, including collected objects), not retained heap or RSS.

### AB results

| Metric | Parent / A: median [min, p95=max] | Fixed / B: median [min, p95=max] | Mean paired delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Normalization CPU, ms | 104.191 [93.751, 108.512] | 79.050 [76.903, 108.046] | -16.81% |
| Normalization wall, ms | 93.024 [83.227, 98.011] | 68.299 [66.054, 104.258] | -17.52% |
| Normalization allocation, MiB | 85.507 [83.864, 87.220] | 62.381 [60.460, 62.889] | -27.51% |
| Total main-isolate allocation, MiB | 812.606 [807.627, 823.820] | 788.973 [785.931, 798.555] | -2.67% |
| Append process CPU, s | 18.744 [18.251, 24.270] | 20.595 [20.097, 21.781] | +5.17% |
| Append main-thread CPU, s | 2.080 [2.066, 3.017] | 2.257 [2.236, 2.344] | +0.63% |
| Append wall, s | 24.350 [17.259, 41.144] | 21.609 [19.880, 27.747] | +0.62% |
| Per-append median latency, ms | 4.033 [3.740, 12.213] | 4.421 [3.850, 4.509] | -3.66% |
| Per-append p95 latency, ms | 72.515 [68.682, 179.825] | 86.095 [72.078, 112.173] | +8.31% |

### AA results

| Metric | Parent / A: median [min, p95=max] | Parent / B: median [min, p95=max] | Mean paired delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Normalization CPU, ms | 104.539 [100.735, 105.272] | 105.099 [95.990, 126.606] | +5.77% |
| Normalization wall, ms | 91.750 [88.597, 95.613] | 92.544 [85.103, 117.768] | +6.97% |
| Normalization allocation, MiB | 86.566 [83.066, 88.494] | 85.785 [82.924, 86.961] | -0.73% |
| Total main-isolate allocation, MiB | 812.000 [801.917, 815.959] | 816.228 [810.144, 833.101] | +0.88% |
| Append process CPU, s | 20.237 [19.619, 23.017] | 20.104 [18.289, 26.857] | +0.48% |
| Append main-thread CPU, s | 2.299 [2.201, 2.712] | 2.306 [2.030, 3.396] | +2.11% |
| Append wall, s | 22.593 [21.102, 28.292] | 22.519 [19.697, 40.836] | +4.75% |
| Per-append median latency, ms | 4.526 [4.310, 5.423] | 4.537 [3.828, 8.883] | +11.21% |
| Per-append p95 latency, ms | 78.047 [75.526, 118.257] | 82.256 [71.992, 174.098] | +8.37% |

Host one-minute load range across all arms: 11.41–58.90. All 60 persisted-message hashes match: `9b7838e3e8199a0fe4cf456267d245665483d47563feb09bac8158bf939fae59`.

The owner improvement is measurable: median normalization CPU −24.13% (paired mean −16.81%) and allocation −27.05% (paired mean −27.51%); total main-isolate allocation median −2.91%. **Do not interpret this as an overall append speedup:** process-CPU median rises 9.87%, main-thread CPU 8.51%, and median per-arm p95 latency 18.73%, while wall median falls 11.26%. The paired deltas and A/A controls are shown above; none of the untraced aggregate median/p95 changes crosses the predeclared 20% threshold. The high-load first owner-mode candidate is retained, not dropped.

Separate 100 µs CPU profiles of 1,000 real appends preserve the same byte hash. Inclusive normalization samples fall 611→493 (91.84→74.03 sampled wall-ms); `normalizePlainJson` samples fall 458→356. The added ownership propagation helper has nine samples (1.36 sampled wall-ms), so the profile does not show a comparable replacement hotspot. GC samples fall 1,234→1,001. These single profile arms provide attribution only; the quantitative CPU claim comes from the five-pair owner pass above.

Reproduce an arm with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/transcript-append-normalization-measure.ts --scratch <isolated-volume-dir> --output <result.json> --mode timing --operations 1000 --seed-database <closed-synthetic-db> --workspace <synthetic-workspace>`. Run allocation, owner timing and profiles separately with `--mode allocation`, `--mode owner`, and `--mode profile`. Baseline adds `--owners-dir <directory-containing-parent-versions-at-repo-relative-paths>` for the two changed runtime modules; unchanged dependencies and worker kernels are shared. The harness records/holds owner source hashes. Use `scripts/perf/session-read-transactions-fixture.mjs --root <seed-root> --sessions 10000 --events 1000000 --target-events 100000 --body-bytes 40000 --target-body-bytes 1024` to recreate the scale fixture.

<details>
<summary>Ingress/caller audit against parent 079889d5a091</summary>

| prepareTranscriptMessageAppendForWorker caller | Ingress evidence |

| session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-message-append.ts:101 | prepareTranscriptMessageAppend wrapper admits raw non-user messages; reports at session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-reports.ts:338,402 are raw, synchronous manager at session-manager-append.ts:245 is canonical. Normalization retained. |
