prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body: ## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Persistent OpenClaw agents today are externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation delegate store** (TaskFlow-backed) persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts. The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **TaskFlow backing**: durable delegate queue via the platform's managed-task infrastructure - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → TaskFlow record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, TaskFlow delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. Spans emitted (all in `openclaw.*` or `continuation.delegate.dispatch` namespace — no platform/OTel-semconv emissions): | Span | Emitted when | |---|---| | `openclaw.run` | Each agent turn (root + every continuation/delegate-spawned child run) | | `continuation.delegate.dispatch` | Each `continue_delegate` consumption from TaskFlow (one per delegate hop) | | `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.context.assembled`, `openclaw.model.call`, `openclaw.model.usage`, `openclaw.tool.execution` | Existing per-turn observability surfaces, parented under their `openclaw.run` | --- ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Sessions can elect future work with `continue_work`, dispatch bounded background work with `continue_delegate`, and request guarded compaction with `request_compaction`. The runtime preserves budgets, restart recovery, finalization ownership, and trace lineage across those boundaries. **Presented candidate:** `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` (tree `d5e701bcce20bb3c972ddf1451b02d88cc04808e`) — the exact upstream-visible head of `codeagent/85651-upstream-1ba243c8-gates`. The branch was advanced to this head by fast-forward from the previously presented `e76395810becd0ad0f2997cae8b4f777e6439d81`, which remains an ancestor (`git merge-base --is-ancestor e7639581 3821eaef` holds). No presented history was rewritten. **Presented and current candidate are now the same commit.** There is no undisclosed descendant: `3821eaef72` is content-frozen and every receipt below is bound to it. **Current candidate validation:** Mode-B run [`35364768803`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/35364768803) (`openclaw-local-ci`, `workflow_dispatch`) is bound to product `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and routing/workflow head `fcf0478fd1c8cbec0489d022a7e4eac6188de153`. It ran 2026-09-18T15:49:35Z to 2026-09-18T17:47:43Z and finished **68 jobs succeeded, 3 failed, 3 cancelled, 3 skipped**. The run is terminally **non-green and release-ineligible**, and every residual is classified: - `agentic-gateway-methods` (job `105667082763`) was **cancelled at the workflow's exact 90-minute job limit** on the `ronan` seat while still heartbeating and emitting new log lines. The same shard completes on the `elliott` and `emeric` seats. This is seat throughput against a 5,231-test shard, not a product verdict — and that same cancelled log carries **111 `sessions.send-followup-status` lines, all 111 passing**, against the real stale `/tmp/openclaw-agent.sqlite` on the host that originally produced the `uses schema version 17` failure. - `hosted(agentic-agents-tools,auto-reply-reply-dispatch,…)` (job `105667083998`) received `The runner has received a shutdown signal` and exited 143. 778 passing test lines were captured and **no test failure precedes the signal**. Two further hosted jobs (`105667084144`, `105667084159`) are the same reclamation class. - `hosted(core-runtime-media-ui-3,core-runtime-infra-repo-tooling,…)` (job `105667084127`) is red only because `subagent-announce.live-tree-chain-proof` hit `sessions_spawn model "openai/gpt-6-astra" is not usable: The selected account ... unavailable`. That is an account provisioning gap, observed identically in six prior runs. - `aggregate + status` (job `105701732269`) is the expected fail-closed policy consequence of the residuals above, not an additional product-test failure. **No product-owned test failure and no routing failure occurred in this run.** Newly green on this exact head: the four re-laned toolchain shards `core-tooling-5`, `core-tooling-7`, `core-tooling-12` and `core-tooling-14` all succeeded on hosted runners after per-seat tooling failures, and `agentic-commands-doctor-config-state` succeeded on two different seats. The Mode-B planner identity digest `sha256:42dffd23ec447c6e4b726d0e6345f1dc2417801048aee49b96f3332233ef1f34` is preserved across those lane moves, so no shard identity changed. These residuals are runner, seat-throughput, and account-provisioning properties of the execution environment. They are not addressable inside this branch and are recorded here rather than presented as green. **Real environment tested:** An OpenClaw instance exercised live Discord ingress/egress and OTel/Tempo with content capture disabled. The full evidence chain, execution identity, ancestry, and materiality record are contained in the linked corpus rather than repeated here. **Observed behavior:** - A real retained ambient Discord event aged to 1,069,503 ms and was suppressed as `stale-ambient-backlog`; attempts remained zero. - A fresh addressed request completed with attempts zero and produced a visible response after 45.565 seconds. - Typed `continue_work` and bracket `CONTINUE_WORK` each armed and fired one five-second wake with granted provenance and completed Tempo model-call spans. - Cost-cap rejection passed an exact-source disposable fixture. - Max-chain matrix, scheduler, durable recovery, typed tool, and product delegate regression surfaces passed; the row remains partial because a docs-owned generated wrapper is stale. ### Evidence The canonical matrix contains 38 rows: **31 pass, three partial, one fail, and three missing** (`PROOFS/INDEX.json` -> corpus `7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567`). `R-CD-2` is the single fail. The partial rows are `R-CD-COLLECTION-ON-COLLAPSE`, `R-CD-TOKEN` and `R-RC-2`. The three missing rows are `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY`, `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2`. This is not acceptance-complete. The two return rows and `R-OBS-2` are missing for different reasons, and all three are producer gaps rather than absent behavior: - `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY` records zero of its 24 observations (12 authority cases against both the typed-tool and bracket-token surfaces). Its pending receipt requires allowed delivery to show exact effects, revoked and reassigned recipients to show zero prompt, wake and channel effect, schema v18/v19, restart replay, a signed authority, and full cleanup. The row's own `manifest` and harness `supporting_docs` pointers are currently **dangling on the docs default branch**: the harness exists but was never merged there. - `R-CD-RETURN-OVERLAP` and `R-OBS-2` each have a present manifest and failed only because the current-corpus input they read (overlap evidence file, exported trace tree) is absent. **Limits:** Historical live and Mode-B evidence for earlier heads is ancestry/materiality evidence, not exact-target execution. Run `35364768803` above *is* exact-target for `3821eaef72`. All seven non-pass rows remain gated on producer execution against this frozen head; no acceptance receipt from an older deployment composite is reused as final evidence. ## Proof links and ClawSweeper🦞 guidance Proof artifacts live in `karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs` on `main`. `PROOFS/INDEX.json` points at the corpus for the SHA this PR presents, `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`. Reviewed docs checkpoint: `c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c`. - [Corpus directory](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393) - [README — identity, what is proven, honest limits](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/README.md) - [RESOLVED-SHA.md — SHA identity and gate verdicts](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/RESOLVED-SHA.md) - [METHOD.md — reproducer commands](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) - [TRANSPOSED-FROM.md — why nothing was transposed](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/TRANSPOSED-FROM.md) - [Manifest](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/proofs-manifest.json) - [INDEX.json](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/INDEX.json) - [Prior published board (not superseded)](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567) ### What this corpus claims, and what it does not **Status: `STATIC_GATES_ONLY_NO_LIVE_ROWS_AT_THIS_SHA`.** Rollup `38 total / 0 pass / 0 partial / 0 fail / 38 not_fired_at_this_sha`. Proven at `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`, receipts being the real stdout of the real runs committed under `gates/` and `mergeability/`: | gate | verdict | |---|---| | `pnpm tsgo:core` | **pass** rc=0 | | `pnpm lint` — oxlint core, extensions, scripts | **pass** rc=0 | | Gate 2.7 vs the absorbed base `715077a3be` | **pass** — 839 files, 466 GENUINE, 373 SAFE-NEW, **0 FROZEN-STALE**, **0 MIXED-CLOBBER** | | `vitest` rollback-custody regressions | **pass** 10/10 | | `vitest` delivery-queue + session-delivery | **pass** 124/124 | | `vitest` gateway maintenance + close + delegate-artifacts | **pass** 123/123 | | `vitest` production-boundary + spawn-cleanup | 28/30 — two tracked reds | **Diff size has not grown across four absorbs.** From the absorbed base — which is what this PR shows — the change is 839 files, +140,919 / −4,301, against 841 / +140,951 / −4,277 before this cycle. (`git diff upstream/main HEAD` reports 2,358 files, but that is the symmetric difference including upstream commits newer than the merge base, and is not what a PR shows.) The worktree was clean at publication: zero untracked files, no stray additions. **Two known reds, neither hidden nor softened.** `karmaterminal/openclaw#1356` is an order-dependent failure of the `operator-revoked` queued-collector cleanup: it **passes in isolation** with all four `cleanupComplete` operands true and the child session genuinely deleted, and fails only when the `operator-completed` arm has run first. Upstream's own test and test-support files for it are byte-identical to ours, so the divergence is product-side. `karmaterminal/openclaw#1350` is the streamed-text offset/fencing contract, pre-existing. **No live behavioral row was fired at this SHA, and none is presented as though it were.** The fleet that runs these behaviors serves composite `1baff536afa549fea75660403c453bbd265352c0`, a *divergent sibling* of the presented SHA rather than an ancestor of it — their merge-base is `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` and neither is an ancestor of the other. A live fire on that runtime would be evidence about the composite, so every row is marked `not_fired_at_this_sha` instead of being carried over as a pass. The prior corpus at `3821eaef72` remains linked per row as the baseline to re-fire against. Live rows are unblocked by a redeploy onto a runtime that has this SHA as a git ancestor. That redeploy is itself a migration boundary: this head carries the agent schema bump **21 → 22** via `migrateTranscriptFtsRowSchema`, and the fleet serves 21, so it wants migration-success and rollback-compatibility receipts of its own. Both are maintainer-side, not gated on this PR. ### PROOFS METHOD The corpus uses a Grafana k6 proof harness for live rows; [`METHOD.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) carries the exact reproducer commands for every static gate above, including both Gate 2.7 invocations and the `git merge-tree --write-tree` mergeability check. `MAX_WORKERS=1` is mandatory for the vitest reproducers — OpenClaw's fixtures are not safe under concurrent access — and two of those commands deliberately take no `--config`, because passing the wrong one silently reports "No test files found" and exits 0. `TRANSPOSED-FROM.md` records source-to-target ancestry and materiality; for this cycle it records a deliberate refusal to transpose across 520 commits and four absorbs. ## Future actions and #130741 composition Maintainer PR #130741 addresses the complementary fresh-sweep race: it captures the current `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before the first await and uses those values as cleanup CAS facts. The return covenant addresses a different time axis: whether historically accepted child work may return to a logical recipient after benign successor creation. The current candidate and #130741 head `e1afc703f49a07687c0876ba6350cafa87a3638a` merge cleanly in a synthetic composition. If #130741 lands, the composed result should preserve both guarantees: - keep #130741's fresh sweep-time exact-run/session lifecycle fence; - keep the covenant's durable logical-recipient generation for historical return admission and delivery; - do not overload broad `lifecycleRevision` as historical return authority; - do not terminate or orphan accepted descendants merely because `/new` or ordinary `/reset` creates a successor session. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially TaskFlow plus host Cron / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A TaskFlow tool adapter is also not a lifecycle host. It can call the core-owned `api.runtime.tasks.managedFlows` API to create, link, pause, resume, finish, cancel, and inspect durable flow records. Marking a waiting record as running does not reacquire a session lane or invoke the model; recording a `childSessionKey` created by a separate spawn surface does not spawn the child or deliver its return. There is no equivalent host continuation capability for this PR to wrap. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It preserves that PR's review lineage and the earlier continuation work descended from #79925, but it does not reuse either closed PR or ask reviewers to infer the current result from them. The replacement carries a current, independently reviewable branch and a complete proof subtree bound to its presented SHA. #85651 was not abandoned because the feature failed or because we accepted its classification as a skill. It was closed after automated labeling put the change in the wrong submission category. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.

prs.title: improve(postgres): read each chat history page from one database snapshot
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Loading one page of chat history on PostgreSQL opens a new read-only transaction for every step of the page read, so a single page costs several blocking `BEGIN ... READ ONLY` / `ROLLBACK` round trips over the database bridge instead of one: two to three on a ported production store, seven in a sparse Claude CLI session after a provider switch.

## User Impact

User impact: each `chat.history` page on PostgreSQL is now read from one database snapshot, with one transaction round trip instead of several. Returned messages and pagination are unchanged, and SQLite is unchanged. No end-to-end latency change was measured on the test host (see Evidence).

## Why This Change Was Made

The history worker runs one task at a time, and no read snapshot outlives a task. The `chat.history` page task now holds one PostgreSQL `REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY` snapshot from its first read until the page is assembled. That covers the Claude CLI import check (revision read and, after a provider switch, its tail read) and every page and tail-scan read. Every read still goes through the read scope's admission (`acquire`), so validation and path checks run per read as before. A failed read rolls the held snapshot back and the next read opens a fresh one. A failed rollback retires the connection, as `runPostgresTransactionSync` does, and the snapshot uses the same `BEGIN` and read-snapshot scope.

Scope: this changes the page task only. The pending-input read that the handler issues before the page is its own worker request with its own snapshot, and the history reader cap (#169110) is untouched. This composes with #188952 (deferred read-only `BEGIN`), which works at the connection's execute level and touches different files.

## Evidence

Evidence files: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/tree/assets/pg-r2-l3c-history-snapshot-evidence (paths below are relative to it).

- **Regression test** (new, live PostgreSQL), red on base and green with the change (`tests/red-v3.log`, `tests/green-v3.log`). Read-only `BEGIN`s for one page, base vs fix: sparse page 3 vs 1, Claude CLI session after a provider switch 7 vs 1. A second test checks that a failed statement inside the held snapshot is rolled back and the next read works. Without that rollback it fails with `25P02` (`tests/mutant-unit.log`).
- **Live PostgreSQL conformance** (`tests/conformance-fix.log`, `tests/conformance-base.log`, counts in `tests/SUMMARY.txt`): with the change, 12 files and 75 tests pass. On base, 11 files and 72 tests pass (the same set without the new file). With #188952 also applied, the new test, two bridge suites and `connection.test.ts` pass (`tests/with-188952-*.log`). Consumer unit tests for the changed modules pass (`tests/unit-fix.log`). In `pnpm check:changed`, typecheck, lint and guards pass. Knip reports two unused exports in files this change does not touch, and they are also present on base (`tests/check-changed.log`).
- **Running Gateway statement trace**, six sequential `chat.history` calls on a ported production store (`traces/`). Read-only transactions per call go from 3.0 to 2.0 and statements per call from 14.17 to 12.17, with reads per call unchanged (8.17). The page task now takes one snapshot. The other one belongs to the separate pending-input request.
- **Closed-loop `chat.history`-only bench**, same store, 3 interleaved runs per arm, medians (`bench/medians.tsv`; per-run values with load average in `bench/table.tsv`; raw `pg_stat_statements` and Prometheus scrapes in `bench/runs/`):

| arm | read-only transactions per call | statements per call | p50 / p95 / p99 ms | sessionTranscript queue wait per request |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| concurrency 1, base | 2.76 | 11.27 | 2.61 / 6.14 / 10.16 | 0.0 ms |
| concurrency 1, fix | 2.11 | 9.93 | 2.59 / 5.88 / 9.39 | 0.0 ms |
| concurrency 8, base | 2.74 | 11.14 | 10.34 / 19.21 / 26.46 | 1.95 ms |
| concurrency 8, fix | 2.09 | 9.83 | 10.27 / 19.34 / 29.14 | 1.93 ms |

The host's 1-minute load average was 4.9 to 9.0 on 32 threads during these runs. Worker requests per call were unchanged (2.36 at concurrency 8).

### Gaps

- The Gateway bench and trace ran on `ac2c420`, the build that wrote the ported store, with this patch applied (only an import line conflicted). Current `main` would not admit a `pg_restore` of that store, so on `main` the change is covered by the tests and conformance above rather than by a Gateway bench. `main` also shares idle bridge transports across stores (#188614), and `ac2c420` predates that.
- Latency: p50 and p95 are flat, and p99 moved within run-to-run spread. At concurrency 8 the queue wait for the two history workers is unchanged. That queueing is the reader-pool limit tracked in #188956, which this change does not address.
- `set_config`: none per call on the bench build. The bridge already skips schema setup when the schema is unchanged, so there was no redundant per-call `set_config` to drop. On `main`, a switch can still occur when a shared idle transport last served another store; not measured.
- After a provider switch, the Claude CLI import check still reads the tail twice (now inside one snapshot). This is a possible follow-up, as is sharing a snapshot with the pending-input request.
- Not benchmarked together with #188952 (tests only).

prs.title: fix(telegram): flood-limited replies keep retrying for 20+ minutes when Telegram answers slowly
prs.body:
Related: #141959

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Telegram final reply, delete or reaction that keeps getting flood-control (429) answers can keep retrying for over 20 minutes, instead of giving up at the five-minute delivery budget, when each attempt is slow to come back.

## User Impact

User impact: a reply that Telegram keeps rate-limiting now gives up once another flood wait would take it past five minutes from its first attempt, and reports the 429 to the caller's existing failure handling, instead of the chat staying silent for 20 to 35 minutes while later sends queue behind it. The gate stops allowing further flood waits once they would exceed the five-minute elapsed-time budget. An attempt already queued or awaiting Telegram's response is not interrupted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The account flood gate promises a five-minute budget for non-replaceable calls, but it only added up the flood-pause sleeps (`waitedMs += waitMs`). Time spent in the per-chat queue and waiting on Telegram's response between 429s was never counted. In the 2026.10.4 trace on the issue, each cycle was an 8-second pause plus about 28 seconds inside the request path, so the 300-second budget allowed about 37 cycles, roughly 22 minutes per request.

The gate now measures wall-clock time from the call's start: before sleeping it checks `Date.now() - startedAtMs + waitMs` against the same five-minute budget. Nothing else changes: `retry_after` is still honored, replaceable calls (previews, typing) still yield at once, and `getUpdates` stays with the ingress worker. The Telegram retry docs now state the five-minute limit.

Not in this PR, so this does not close the issue: the other asks on the issue (escalating backoff after repeated 429s, cron run status while delivery is blocked, the inbound control lane waiting on outbound flood waits, and replay of `unknown_after_send` entries) are separate changes.

## Evidence

Regression test in the existing account limiter suite (`account-throttler.test.ts`, `stops retrying a final reply five minutes after it started, counting slow 429 responses`): the real grammY `Api` with the account transformer, where every `sendMessage` answers 429 `retry_after: 8` after 28 seconds (the issue's cycle shape), under fake timers.

```
# main + test only
× stops retrying a final reply five minutes after it started, counting slow 429 responses
  → expected undefined to match object { error_code: 429 }      (still retrying after 10 minutes)
Tests  1 failed | 23 passed (24)

# with the fix: 9 attempts, the last one before 5 minutes, then the 429 is reported
extensions/telegram/src: account-throttler, bot-message-dispatch.progress-lifecycle.telegram-http,
  send.telegram-http, outbound-adapter.telegram-http, send.transport-close-proof, draft-stream,
  polling-session, sendchataction-401-backoff, channel.gateway, bot/delivery.resolve-media-local
                                              all passed
```

`pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files pass; docs lint passes (pre-commit).

### Live run

A real Gateway (`openclaw gateway run`, built from `main` at `749df769909` with and without this PR's limiter change: `account-throttler.ts` as in `6b863b746dd`, unchanged since; the Telegram sources are identical between `749df769909` and this branch's base) with the Telegram channel's `apiRoot` pointed at a scripted Bot API on loopback. Every `sendMessage` answers HTTP 429 `retry_after: 8` after 28 seconds (the cycle shape in the 2026.10.4 trace). One `openclaw message send --channel telegram -t <chat> -m "final answer"`; the CLI stops waiting at its 60-second gateway timeout, the Gateway keeps the send, and the scripted API logs every attempt.

| Build | Attempts | First to last attempt | Gave up (first attempt to the reported 429) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 38 | 0 s to 1332 s | after 1360 s (22.7 min) |
| this PR | 9 | 0 s to 288 s | after 316 s (5.3 min; the ninth attempt was in flight at 5 minutes) |

```
# this PR, scripted Bot API log (seconds since it started) and Gateway log
273.5s sendMessage START {"chat_id":"<chat>","text":"final answer",...}
301.5s sendMessage -> 429 retry_after=8
309.5s sendMessage START ...
337.5s sendMessage -> 429 retry_after=8
[telegram] sendMessage failed: Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (429: Too Many Requests: retry after 8)

# main: same setup
1353.8s sendMessage START ...
1381.8s sendMessage -> 429 retry_after=8
[telegram] sendMessage failed: Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (429: Too Many Requests: retry after 8)
```

Test lines are net +21 against `main`, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/telegram-flood-budget-elapsed.txt`: one case in the existing limiter suite; no existing case drives slow repeated 429s, and the neighboring flood cases each assert a different pause rule.

Proof artifice: the Telegram Bot API is a local script that answers every send with a slow 429 and is reached through the channel's `apiRoot`; the bot token is fake; the regression test uses fake timers.

Restart and crash window: the change only bounds how long one in-memory call keeps retrying; it writes no state and does not touch the delivery queue, spool or recovery, so a restart mid-retry ends the call exactly as before.

Not tested: a live Telegram bot under real flood control (real Telegram flood control was not exercised; the scripted API provides repeatable timing without rate-limiting a real bot), and which operation produced the extra ~28 seconds per cycle in the reporter's trace. The fix bounds the total time either way.

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): keep a synthesis page status when refreshing it
prs.body:
## Summary
Refreshing an existing synthesis page with `openclaw wiki apply synthesis` (or the `wiki_apply` agent tool with `op: "synthesis"`) without passing a status silently rewrites the page's `status` frontmatter to `active`. A status set earlier through `wiki apply metadata --status review` (or `wiki_apply` `op: "metadata"`) is lost on the next summary refresh, while the same refresh keeps the page's `confidence`, `questions`, `contradictions` and `claims`. Agents refresh syntheses routinely, so a curated `review`/`stale`/`draft` marker does not survive the next summary update.

## Root cause
`applyCreateSynthesisMutation` in `extensions/memory-wiki/src/apply.ts` spreads the existing frontmatter and then overrides `status` with the mutation value or a hard-coded default:

```ts
// before
      status: params.mutation.status?.trim() || "active",
```

Every other optional metadata field in the same object is only written when the mutation supplies it, so the existing value survives the `...parsed.frontmatter` spread. `status` is the one field that falls through to `"active"` instead of to the value already on the page. The sibling `update_metadata` path (`buildUpdatedFrontmatter`) already leaves `status` untouched when none is supplied, so the two paths disagree.

## Fix
Fall back to the page's existing status before the `active` default:

```ts
// after
      status:
        params.mutation.status?.trim() ||
        (typeof parsed.frontmatter.status === "string" && parsed.frontmatter.status.trim()) ||
        "active",
```

A new synthesis still starts as `active`, an explicit `--status` / `status` still wins on refresh, and a refresh without one keeps what is already on the page.

## Why this is the right boundary
`applyCreateSynthesisMutation` is the single writer for synthesis pages; the CLI (`wiki apply synthesis`), the `wiki_apply` tool and the gateway method all route through `applyMemoryWikiMutation`, so one change covers every caller. It reuses the existing-frontmatter value the function already parsed (the same pattern it uses for `id`), and matches how `update_metadata` and the dashboard writer in `compile.ts` already preserve a non-empty `status`. No schema, option, or output format changes.

## Verification
- Added `keeps a curated status when a synthesis is refreshed without one` in `extensions/memory-wiki/src/apply.test.ts`: creates a synthesis, sets `status: review` via a metadata mutation, refreshes the synthesis body without a status and asserts `review` is kept, then refreshes with `status: "stale"` and asserts the explicit value wins. It fails on main (`expected 'active' to be 'review'`) and passes with the patch; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/apply.test.ts` reports 6 passed.
- `oxfmt --check` clean on both changed files.
- Local tsgo and oxlint were not run per the contributor workflow for this batch; GitHub Actions covers them.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: `wiki apply synthesis` refreshing an existing page without `--status` reset a curated `status: review` back to `active`, while `confidence` on the same page was kept.
Real environment tested: The production `registerWikiCli` command tree from `extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli.ts`, wired the way `extensions/memory-wiki/index.ts` wires it (real plugin-state keyed store and blob store for the compiled cache, source-sync and import-run state), loaded with the real config loader from an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_HOME` and run under tsx on Node 26.9. Real vault on disk, real ingest, apply and compile. Pristine main b9b71084613 first, then this patch, identical commands on a freshly deleted vault each time. Nothing was stubbed.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `openclaw wiki init`, `openclaw wiki ingest ./alpha.md`, `openclaw wiki apply synthesis "Alpha Budget" --body "Alpha budget is 40k." --source-id source.alpha`, `openclaw wiki apply metadata synthesis.alpha-budget --status review --confidence 0.4`, `openclaw wiki apply synthesis "Alpha Budget" --body "Alpha budget is now 45k." --source-id source.alpha`, reading the page frontmatter after the metadata update and after the refresh.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main b9b71084613)
$ openclaw wiki ingest ./alpha.md
Ingested alpha.md into sources/alpha.md. Refreshed 16 index files.
$ openclaw wiki apply synthesis "Alpha Budget" --body "Alpha budget is 40k." --source-id source.alpha
Updated syntheses/alpha-budget.md via create_synthesis. Refreshed 4 index files.
$ openclaw wiki apply metadata synthesis.alpha-budget --status review --confidence 0.4
Updated syntheses/alpha-budget.md via update_metadata. Refreshed 1 index file.
$ grep -E "^(status|confidence):" vault/syntheses/alpha-budget.md
status: review
confidence: 0.4
$ openclaw wiki apply synthesis "Alpha Budget" --body "Alpha budget is now 45k." --source-id source.alpha
Updated syntheses/alpha-budget.md via create_synthesis. Indexes unchanged.
$ grep -E "^(status|confidence):" vault/syntheses/alpha-budget.md
status: active
confidence: 0.4

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
$ openclaw wiki ingest ./alpha.md
Ingested alpha.md into sources/alpha.md. Refreshed 16 index files.
$ openclaw wiki apply synthesis "Alpha Budget" --body "Alpha budget is 40k." --source-id source.alpha
Updated syntheses/alpha-budget.md via create_synthesis. Refreshed 4 index files.
$ openclaw wiki apply metadata synthesis.alpha-budget --status review --confidence 0.4
Updated syntheses/alpha-budget.md via update_metadata. Refreshed 1 index file.
$ grep -E "^(status|confidence):" vault/syntheses/alpha-budget.md
status: review
confidence: 0.4
$ openclaw wiki apply synthesis "Alpha Budget" --body "Alpha budget is now 45k." --source-id source.alpha
Updated syntheses/alpha-budget.md via create_synthesis. Indexes unchanged.
$ grep -E "^(status|confidence):" vault/syntheses/alpha-budget.md
status: review
confidence: 0.4
```
Observed result after fix: On main the summary refresh flips `status: review` to `status: active` while `confidence: 0.4` survives; with the patch the same refresh keeps `status: review`, and only the summary body and `updatedAt` change.
What was not tested: The `wiki_apply` agent tool and the gateway `wiki.apply` method were not driven live (they call the same `applyMemoryWikiMutation`); the CLI ran through the production command registration under tsx rather than a packaged build, because loading bundled plugins from source on this machine fails on an unrelated ESM-only dependency; full build not run.

prs.title: fix(gateway): node reconnects repeat the same withheld-command warning
prs.body:
Closes #168742

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway warn logs fill with the same `node command surface withheld` line every time a node reconnects with an unchanged withheld command set, so a new or changed withholding decision is buried among repeats.

## User Impact

User impact: operators see each node's withheld command set once at warn per Gateway run, and again whenever that set changes; identical repeats are still available at debug. Which commands are withheld is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The warn line is useful the first time and whenever the decision changes, but nothing remembered what had already been logged. Node connect reconciliation now keeps a bounded record of the last withheld set logged per node (256 nodes, pruned with the existing `pruneMapToMaxSize`), tied to the existing `close-and-restart` global singleton lifecycle, and compares sets with the existing `sameNodeApprovalSurfaceSet`, so ordering and duplicates do not count as a change.

- First set for a node after Gateway start, or a different set: `warn` (unchanged message).
- Same set as last logged: `debug` (same message).
- A connect with nothing withheld clears the node's record, so renewed withholding warns again.
- The record is cleared on Gateway close and on in-process restart (unmanaged/container Gateways and `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN` keep the process), so every Gateway start records each node's current outcome once at warn. Evicting a node from the bounded record only costs one extra warn on its next reconnect.

This follows the approach proposed in the issue and the ClawSweeper review on it.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway + signed node reconnects.** I used a throwaway harness modeled on `src/gateway/server.node-version-mismatch.test.ts` (not committed): it pairs a macOS node device, starts a real in-process Gateway with `startServer`, and reconnects the same signed node 3 times over WebSocket while it declares `ollama.chat` and `ollama.models` (not admitted by policy). Captured console output, device id redacted:

Before (current `main`), console level `info`:

```text
console.warn: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
console.warn: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
console.warn: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
```

After, console level `info`:

```text
console.warn: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
```

After, console level `debug` (repeats still visible):

```text
console.warn: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
console.log: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
console.log: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
```

**In-process Gateway restart** (follow-up to review): the same harness connects the node twice, closes the Gateway with `restartExpectedMs` (restart path), starts a new Gateway in the same process, and reconnects. Console level `debug`:

Previous PR head `8593b97` (module-level map survived the restart):

```text
console.warn: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
console.log: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
----- in-process Gateway restart -----
console.log: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
```

Current head:

```text
console.warn: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
console.log: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
----- in-process Gateway restart -----
console.warn: [node-connect] node command surface withheld node=<device-id> commands=ollama.chat,ollama.models
```

**Focused regression tests** in `src/gateway/node-connect-reconcile.test.ts` cover repeated and reordered sets, a policy change (`gateway.nodes.commands.allow`) that changes the set, a cleared-then-returning set, separate nodes, and the first identical reconnect after `drainGlobalSingletonLifecycleState("close")` and `("restart")`. The repeat/policy/separate-node cases fail on `main`, the two lifecycle cases fail on the previous PR head, and all pass with this change (the cleared-then-returning case guards existing behavior).

**Local checks** (Node 24.21.0, pnpm 12.9.0):

- `pnpm test src/gateway/node-connect-reconcile.test.ts`: 19 passed
- `pnpm test src/infra/device-pairing-node-desktop-migration.test.ts src/node-host/linux-node-plugin.integration.test.ts src/gateway/server/ws-connection`: passed
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` (first head); `pnpm tsgo:core` and the `core.test.gateway-root` shard after the follow-up: passed
- `oxfmt --check` and `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the changed files: clean
- `pnpm check`: the line-cap, max-lines (env var budget), and assertion SAFETY ratchets fail on files this PR does not touch; the same failures reproduce on current `main`. All other checks pass.

Not covered: config hot reload of `gateway.nodes.commands` in a running Gateway (the unit test covers a changed set through config), and a restart through the CLI run loop or a process respawn (the harness covers the in-process `server.close` restart path).

## AI Disclosure

I used an AI coding agent (Cursor) to help find the issue, write the change and tests, and run the validation above. I reviewed the diff and the before/after output myself.

prs.title: fix(gateway): stop repeated node reconnect warnings
prs.body:
Supersedes #168825, thanks @scs0209.
Related: #168742

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway logs repeat the same withheld-command warning whenever a node reconnects with an unchanged command policy outcome.

## User Impact

Operators see a warning for each node's distinct withheld command set, while identical reconnect outcomes remain available at debug. Command admission and pairing behavior are unchanged. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared node-connect reconciler owns this warning for WebSocket and watch HTTP nodes. Reuse `rememberBoundedKey` and the existing close/restart lifecycle set instead of introducing a separate cache implementation. Keys include the node identity and sorted unique withheld commands, so another node or a previously unseen policy outcome still warns.

The bounded history retains 1,024 distinct node/set keys per Gateway run. Returning to a previously warned set stays at debug; eviction can produce another warning. Gateway close and in-process restart clear the history.

Production delta is +11 lines; test delta is +57 lines. The necessary growth is the shared dedupe/lifecycle wiring and warning key; no safe dead code in this owner was identified to offset it. A separate 57-line test allocation covers reconnect, changed-policy/node, and lifecycle regressions without changing the shared baseline. The simplify pass retained one warning owner and no custom cache machinery.

## Evidence

- On current main `52e113b095d9414278358ef643a7947104e49b57`, the regression fails at warning counts: identical reconnects each warn (3 failing regression cases, 9 existing tests pass; 2.47 seconds wall).
- With the fix: `pnpm test src/gateway/node-connect-reconcile.test.ts src/infra/device-pairing-node-desktop-migration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 22 passed. The final reconciliation-only rerun passes all 12 tests in 2.80 seconds wall (699 ms Vitest duration).
- Negative control: changing `gateway.nodes.commands.allow` changes the withheld set and emits a new warning. Separate nodes, reordered/duplicate commands, and close/restart reset are covered through the real reconciliation/policy owner.
- Focused oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check`, mock-export and test-line guards: pass. Initial PR CI passed the typecheck, lint, and test jobs, then exposed two test-guard defects, corrected here by preserving logger exports and using an integer-only allocation. Final [CI run 41268886286](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41268886286) passed all selected jobs on `ec3f9d5bf7bdd68fec9490083db4c33b2fc3cb71` (8m 28s elapsed).
- Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2): initial review scoped-clean. The correction review identified two index-only copies of those test-guard defects; both were corrected before committing. It found no other P0–P2 defects.
- Contributor source was read using `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff` and was never checked out, installed, built, or run. This is an independent reimplementation on trusted main. Tests exercise the shared connect owner; no real signed-node WebSocket/Gateway boot is claimed.

prs.title: fix(macos): first dashboard open is slow in remote mode
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the macOS app never preloads the dashboard in remote connection mode, so the first open after launch waits for a cold web load.

## User Impact

User impact: in remote mode the dashboard loads hidden once the Gateway connection is authenticated, so the first open can show an already-loaded dashboard, as in local mode. Remote identity dashboards still resolve their sign-in address after hello and never receive pre-hello native credentials. At most one extra hidden load per app launch.

## Why This Change Was Made

The launch preload from #106997 uses the synchronous `immediateWindowConfiguration()`, which #137933 deliberately limited to local mode (`DashboardManager.swift:436-437` on main: "Remote dashboards must resolve the server's sign-in route before any document receives native credentials, including the synchronous fast path."). That guard stays. Remote mode now arms a one-shot preload at launch and starts it when the control channel reports connected, resolving the route through the same `windowConfiguration(for: .primary)` path a visible open uses, then presenting hidden.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and change details</summary>

Root cause on main 939750da217:
- `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/MenuBar.swift:464-468`: one `preloadIfConfigured()` call 2 s after launch.
- `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardManager.swift:460-464`: preload requires `immediateWindowConfiguration()`.
- `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardManager+Routes.swift:131-136`: `guard mode == .local`, added in 0d2bc80eee0 (#137933).

Change:
- `preloadIfConfigured()`: when the immediate config is unavailable in remote mode, arm the remote preload; start it at once if the control channel is already connected. It returns the started task (`@discardableResult`) so callers can join it. Its only caller is the launch hook in `MenuBar.swift` on `DashboardManager.shared`, which always observes gateway changes, so the former `observesGatewayChanges` term in the arming expression was redundant.
- `handleControlChannelStateChange(.connected)`: after reconciling existing documents, start the armed preload.
- `DashboardRemotePreloadDecision` (new, pure logic): `start` only when armed, remote, primary target, no main controller, no presentation or main-window open in flight, and connected; `wait` while not connected; otherwise `discard`. It is spent when it starts; reconnects never re-arm it, and a failed lookup is not retried until the next launch.
- `openWindow(for:reuseExisting:)` counts main-window opens while they await their lookup (`mainOpensInFlight`). The preload checks that count when it starts and again after its own lookup, together with the live channel state and the window lifetime, so an explicit open on either side of the lookup keeps the first document. Signed-out or credential-less configurations are skipped.
- It presents through `presentDashboard(..., source: nil, present: false)`, which records the presented endpoint. A newly created main controller now honors `present`; the default stays `true`, and only this call passes `false`.
- The hidden controller is retained before its document loads: `DashboardWindowController.retainHidden()` marks the never-shown window experience-hidden, the same lifetime `hideForExperience()` uses. So `hasRetainedWindow` is true, `documentHost.isNativeAuthAvailable()` answers native sign-in challenges, and `dashboardControllers()` includes it, so `handleEndpointState` reconciles reconnects and route changes before the first open. `show()` and `windowWillClose` clear the flag as before, so closed-window and stale-credential rejection is unchanged.
- The window also records that it was never shown (`DashboardWindow.isUnshownPreload`, cleared by `show()`). `openWindowCount(for:)`, which the Gateways menu card displays, skips it, so a hidden preload does not read as "1 window". The flag lives on the window, so it survives an endpoint change that replaces the controller.
- Reuse on the first visible open: `showResolvedPrimaryDashboard` resolves again and keeps the document unless `requiresIsolatedDashboardDocument` (`DashboardManager+Construction.swift:299-312`) sees a TLS, auth, browser-session or route change. Native-device auth compares URL, token, password and the legacy credential map. The token comes from the live hello snapshot or config (`GatewayConnection.swift:1300-1310`) and the legacy map holds only a token or password from the same binding (`GatewayConnection+ControlUIAuth.swift:24-27`), so the two lookups match while the same hello snapshot is live. After a reconnect that reissues a device token or bumps the route revision, the first open replaces the document, which is no worse than main. `openOrFocusDashboard(.primary)` sees the experience-hidden preload, resolves the route again for the user gesture and presents through the same reuse check, so the document is kept when nothing changed. `DashboardRemotePreloadTests` cover the reuse through `show()` and both open orderings (see Evidence).
- Test seam, DEBUG only: `testControlChannelConnected` overrides the live control channel state the preload reads (`ControlChannel.shared.state` is socket-driven). Tests arm the preload through `preloadIfConfigured()` itself, with remote mode and onboarding set as at launch.
- The hidden load runs `update(url:auth:)` like the existing local preload, including its guarded browser-profile import offer check (`DashboardWindowController.swift:497-502` on main), so remote mode gains no new UI path.

</details>

## Evidence

Built and tested locally on macOS 27.0.1 with Command Line Tools only (no Xcode.app), using host-side workarounds that change nothing in the repository; CI `macos-swift` remains the authority.

<details>
<summary>Build host workarounds and test isolation</summary>

A copy of the CLT PackageDescription/PackagePlugin modules without their stale `.private.swiftinterface` (`SWIFTPM_CUSTOM_LIBS_DIR`), stand-in `SwiftUIMacros`/`PreviewsMacros` compiler plugins (`-load-plugin-executable`; CLT ships neither), `-F`/`-rpath` to the CLT Testing framework, `node scripts/prepare-apple-mermaid.mjs`, and the two XCTest-only test files (`MacNodeLocationServiceTests`, `SimpleTaskSupportTests`) left out of the build because CLT has no XCTest. Tests ran with `--skip-build` under `sandbox-exec` with a private `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `TMPDIR`, a named test profile, and no access to the operator's `~/.openclaw`, Keychains or non-loopback network.

</details>

- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --product OpenClaw`: `Build of product 'OpenClaw' complete!`, no warnings from the changed files.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests`: `Build complete!`.
- Native sign-in on the hidden preload (head `c05592db154`, test-only follow-up): new `DashboardRemotePreloadTests` case `hidden remote preload answers native challenges only while its document is current` sends a real `OpenClawNativeGatewayAuth` WK challenge from the hidden preloaded document through the production `ControlUINativeGatewayAuthMessageHandler` (only the native provider is a gated stub, as in `DashboardNativeGatewayAuthBridgeTests`). Cases: `current` gets the reply; `socket` (the provider's response is no longer current), `document` (the WebView commits a new document) and `browser-identity-pending` (the document switches to a browser identity while the challenge waits) get an error and no credentials; `browser-identity` (a browser identity document) is rejected without the provider being called. The preload stays hidden in every case.
  - `swift test --filter DashboardRemotePreloadTests`: `Test run with 5 tests in 1 suite passed` (the four earlier tests plus the new one, which runs 5 cases).
  - Red, retention: without `controller.retainHidden()` in `presentDashboard`, `current`, `socket`, `document` and `browser-identity-pending` time out waiting for a challenge the handler never forwards (the hidden document is not native-auth available), plus the earlier retention assertions: `Test run with 5 tests in 1 suite failed ... with 8 issues`.
  - Red, reply guard: without the post-provider `canUseNativeGatewayAuth` / revision / `isCurrent()` guard in `ControlUINativeGatewayAuthMessageHandler`, `socket`, `document` and `browser-identity-pending` receive the credential reply: `... failed ... with 6 issues`.
  - `DashboardRemotePreloadDecisionTests` (it mirrored the decision enum's guards) is removed; the manager suite covers the observable preload, reuse, ordering and reconciliation behavior.
  - Dashboard suites plus `DashboardNativeGatewayAuthBridgeTests`: `Test run with 69 tests in 10 suites failed with 6 issues`, the same 6 environment issues listed below; the bridge suite passes. `scripts/format-swift.sh macos`: `0/417` and `0/33 files require formatting.`; lint with CI semantics exits 0.
- Earlier head `62766ffc00a`: `swift test --filter DashboardRemotePreload`: `Test run with 9 tests in 2 suites passed` (including the since-removed decision tests).
  - `DashboardRemotePreloadTests` (real `DashboardManager` with a loopback HTTP fixture and gated endpoint lookups; every test arms through `preloadIfConfigured()` with remote mode and onboarding set): `first open reuses the hidden remote preload document` (the preloaded controller is hidden, has a retained window, answers native sign-in and is not counted by `openWindowCount(for: .primary)`; after `show()` it is the same instance, now visible and counted once); `open in flight before authentication owns the first document`; `open that starts during the preload lookup owns the first document` (the preload resumes and finishes first and installs nothing; the open's window is the one shown); `hidden remote preload follows an endpoint change before the first open` (after `handleEndpointState(.ready(...))` with a new URL and token, the same hidden window carries the new token, stays retained and is still not counted).
  - `open in flight before authentication owns the first document` alone: `Test run with 1 test in 1 suite passed`.
  - Red check, retention: without the `retainHidden()` call, `Test run with 9 tests in 2 suites failed ... with 4 issues` (`preloaded.hasRetainedWindow`, `preloaded.documentHost.isNativeAuthAvailable()`, `reconciled.auth.token == "rotated-primary-token"`, `reconciled.hasRetainedWindow`).
  - Red check, launch arming: without the `remotePreloadPending` assignment in `preloadIfConfigured()`, `Test run with 9 tests in 2 suites failed ... with 3 issues` (the reuse, preload-lookup and endpoint-change tests find no preload).
  - Red check, window count: without the unshown-preload filter in `openWindowCount(for:)`, `Test run with 9 tests in 2 suites failed ... with 2 issues` (`manager.openWindowCount(for: .primary) == 0` in the reuse and endpoint-change tests).
  - Earlier round: with `mainOpensInFlight` removed from the preload decision, both ordering tests fail.
- Existing dashboard suites, `swift test --filter "DashboardReconnectTests|DashboardWindowOwnershipTests|DashboardTokenlessRouteTests|DashboardGatewaySelectionTests|DashboardGatewaysTests"`: `Test run with 67 tests in 9 suites failed with 6 issues`, and the same filter on unmodified main 939750da217 fails with the identical 6 issues (same tests, cases and assertions). Four are `Caught error: .keychain(-61)` because the sandbox denies Keychain writes. The other two are `configured presentation uses its owned health probe` (mode .local, `controller.currentURL`) and `superseded primary presentation preserves the selected profile` (initial-command, `showConfiguredWindowIfPossible()`). This change adds no failures.
- `scripts/format-swift.sh macos`: `0/33 files require formatting.`
- `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` with the pinned tools from `scripts/install-swift-tools.sh`: one violation, `file_length` on `DashboardManager.swift` (1561 > 1500). Unmodified main already fails the same rule at 1505. With CI semantics (`GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`, limit rules advisory per `scripts/lib/check-limits.mts:11-13`) it exits 0.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 939750da217`: 11 lanes ok (including `format changed files` and `native state schema version guard`). Two failed, neither from this diff:
  - `lint apps`: the local strict run of the same `file_length` rule above (base already over the limit).
  - `macOS app CI tests` (Vitest for macOS tooling scripts): `Tests 1 failed | 607 passed (608)`. The failure is `test/scripts/generate-gateway-protocol-plugin.test.ts > resolves supported Node shims and reports failed probe reasons`, which shells out to `swift build` and hits this host's Command Line Tools manifest link error (`Undefined symbols ... PackageDescription.Package.__allocating_init`). This change touches neither that script nor its test.
- Gaps:
  - The full native suite and the XCTest-based files did not run here; CI's `macos-swift` job is the authority (`docs/platforms/mac/dev-setup.md`).
  - The packaged-app run below is on a GitHub-hosted runner with a job-owned loopback Gateway, not a real remote host; the base comparison stops before the first open (see Real behavior proof).
  - The live run shows the hidden document's native challenge being answered; the refusal cases (browser identity, socket or document retirement while a challenge waits) are shown on the hidden preload by the test above, not in the packaged app.

## Real behavior proof

Packaged app (ad-hoc signed debug build, `ai.openclaw.mac.debug`, app 2026.10.7) built from this PR head `c05592db15442a5dda82477da1ff64f7bbe2fb49`, on a GitHub-hosted macOS 26.6.2 arm64 runner. Run: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/41188038343 (job `proof 4a-head`, artifact `mac-proof-4a-head`, `identity.txt`: `source_sha=c05592db15442a5dda82477da1ff64f7bbe2fb49`). The same scenario also passed on the previous head `62766ffc00a` (identical app sources; run https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/41182007510).

Setup: a job-owned `openclaw gateway` on loopback with token auth and a placeholder default model (no model is called). The app runs in remote mode (`gateway.mode=remote`, direct transport) against a loopback logging proxy in front of that Gateway, so every HTTP request and WebSocket upgrade from the app and its dashboard WebView is timestamped (query values are not logged). The dashboard document is the request with `Sec-Fetch-Dest: document`. The app is launched normally (no `--dashboard`), then opened once with `openclaw://dashboard`, the same action as the menu item. The full CoreGraphics window list (on and off screen) is read before and after the open.

Result (`summary.md`):

| moment | dashboard document requests | dashboard window |
|---|---|---|
| launch to first open | 1 | on screen: none, off screen: 39 |
| first open to settled shot (~47 s: 16-frame burst, ~26 s on the runner, then 20 s settle) | 0 | on screen: 39 (same window as before open: yes) |

```
09:53:25 app launched: OpenClaw.app args:
09:53:36 document requests before any open: 1 (first seen 11.0 s after launch)
09:53:49 local network alert: pressed Allow in UserNotificationCenter
09:53:49 windows before-open: 0 on screen, 6 off screen
09:53:49 dashboard window before open: on screen=[] off screen=[39]
09:54:15 first-open frame burst done (16 frames, 250 ms apart)
09:54:36 windows after-open: 1 on screen, 5 off screen
09:54:36 dashboard documents: before open=1, open..+20s=0; window on screen after open=[39] same as preloaded=yes; page socket none s after open
09:54:36 PASS 4a: hidden remote preload loaded the dashboard document off screen; the first open showed that window without a new document load
```

The proxy log shows the hidden page's document at 09:53:34.993 and its Gateway WebSocket (the only upgrade with an `Origin` header) at 09:53:47.169, both before the open; nothing new after it. The Gateway log shows that page socket authenticating (the app's native control channel, no `Origin`, connected separately at 09:53:30):
```
09:53:47.330 [ws] client connected conn=3f7fcc67-... client=openclaw-macos mode=ui role=operator auth=token build=2026.10.7-c05592db1544-...
09:53:47.344 [ws] res ✓ connect 53ms
09:53:47.356 [ws] → hello-ok
```
That connect is the native challenge path: the page takes its `client` from the app's `nativeConnectAuth` reply only (`ui/src/api/gateway-connect-plan.ts:135-152`), and the app signs it as `client.id = "openclaw-macos"`, `mode = "ui"` (`apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardNativeGatewayAuth.swift:50`); a page without native auth connects as `openclaw-control-ui`. The connect carries the page's own build id (the app's native channel reports `build=legacy`). So the hidden preloaded document asked for and received a native challenge reply before the first open.

The review's other two boundary cases (a browser identity document gets no native credentials; a retired socket or document gets no pending reply) are shown on the hidden preload by the new test in Evidence, through the production message handler. A browser identity route needs a Gateway that advertises an https sign-in origin (trusted-proxy or Tailscale Serve, `src/gateway/control-ui-identity.ts:17-28`), which this loopback job does not have.

Once its document has loaded, the hidden page may open its own Gateway socket before any open (as here; in an earlier run, 40542122063, it waited until shown), so a remote launch can hold that one page connection; it is the connection the first open shows.

Before the open, nothing on screen; the 1240x860 dashboard window 39 exists off screen:

![before open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/2f74c6ff4dc42389639b99c2a3a125d0983a5b44/mac-item-4a-preload-r5/10-screen-before-open.png)

The first frame right after the open shows the already-loaded dashboard shell while the chat pane repaints; the next captured frame (the 16-frame burst took ~26 s on this runner, so ~1.6 s later) is fully rendered, still with no new document request or socket:

![first open frame 00](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/2f74c6ff4dc42389639b99c2a3a125d0983a5b44/mac-item-4a-preload-r5/20-first-open-frame-00.png)
![first open frame 01](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/2f74c6ff4dc42389639b99c2a3a125d0983a5b44/mac-item-4a-preload-r5/20-first-open-frame-01.png)

Before (current PR base `3d064947c6b`; the root-cause line numbers above are from main `939750da217`, where this branch started; previous harness revision `3b74ff0466f` with the same launch-to-open checks, run https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/41178439473, job `proof 4a-base`, `identity.txt` `source_sha=3d064947c6bb6d6c1bda930c67ec8672f56dbbc0`): no hidden load at all.
```
07:22:42 document requests before any open: 0
07:22:54 windows before-open: 0 on screen, 4 off screen   (four 1024x30 windows, no dashboard window)
```
That base job then stopped on a harness bug (fixed in the runs above) before the first open, so it shows only the launch-to-open half: no dashboard document in 109 s after launch and no dashboard window at 121 s.

Harness: `scripts/mac-proof/4a.sh` on fork branch `mac/proof-4` (`64506d45e0a`). Logs contain no tokens, keys or non-loopback addresses.
