prs.title: fix(sessions): cold PostgreSQL conversations fail after idle readers close
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes cold transcript writes and restoration-dependent operations failing on PostgreSQL after the Gateway's cached native reader retires.

## User Impact

Cold conversations no longer depend on a boot-admitted main-thread database connection. SQLite, native maintenance, source checks, writer ordering, cancellation and commit settlement retain their existing contracts. No configuration, schema, durability, retention or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the agent database's existing worker execution generation for cold restoration. Preserve the ordinary committed display notification as well as the separate facts-only receipt publication; reopening historical archives must still refresh readers.

The author simplification pass kept one owner and no new connection, fallback, cache or API. Production is net −1 line. The new real-engine regression and adjusted native-publication fixture add exactly 142 test lines, with matching scoped allocation; the shared baseline is unchanged.

## Evidence

Qualified locally on **Node 26.12.1 and real PostgreSQL 17.11** with SQLite controls; all state, services and model traffic were disposable and local.

- **Base red, fixed green:** a Gateway-role main process with no host compatibility reader restores a real cold archive, preserves the original rows and rewrite generation, publishes one ordinary display notification, then appends and reads subsequent messages. The base throws “PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker”.
- **Built Gateway RPC:** the warm baseline initially succeeds because startup retains a reader. A fixture explicitly invokes that production reader owner's idle cleanup—not a shortened production timeout or a natural 30-minute wait. After observing native readers **1→0**, base chat.inject refuses with the same guard and makes zero provider requests. The final build succeeds, retains original history, completes a real agent turn through a deterministic loopback HTTP model, survives a new-process restart, and completes a later turn: **two actual model HTTP requests**. No Team data or paid provider was used. An initial fixture signal collided with the Gateway restart signal; the corrected non-restart stimulus was rerun on both base and final source.
- **86 focused tests passed across six files**, covering both engines, publication, cancellation, stale source/owner checks, missing/corrupt archives, reopen and parent-fork consumers. Final command wall time: **119.6 seconds**, including compilation/wrappers. The two-case conformance file runs in about 5–6 seconds of test time; hosted CI time is not yet available.
- Production and affected infra/session test typechecks, scoped lint/format, whitespace, exact test-line allocation and database worker ratchet passed. The inventory remains **168→168 T1** calls; this is not a whole-Gateway SQL or performance claim.
- Fresh independent **Auto Review, complete local candidate against 9c22cf86, P0–P2: scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The reviewer assessed the supplied diff/source context, not an independent test execution.

**CI follow-up:** [Initial exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41266454178/job/124730545714) caught an obsolete incomplete-mock exemption for the fixture removed here. The same failure reproduced locally. Removing precisely that one exemption makes the mock-factory ratchet pass; no exemption was added or broadened. Fresh independent P0–P2 review of this one-line follow-up is scoped-clean. Runtime/test source and the built-product proof are unchanged; the updated head requires its own CI.

### Inspectable shipped-runtime capture

Re-ran the same local shipped-Gateway flow with actual whitelisted RPC, reader-owner and received HTTP-request observations recorded below. This is **metadata/evidence only**: the full tracked index equals published head `e9d21854d4e9bb894bc2191e2300a462165385db` (`git diff --cached --exit-code e9d21854d4e9bb894bc2191e2300a462165385db` exited 0), and `git diff --exit-code` exited 0.

The maintained `createOpenClawTestInstance` starts `dist/index.js`; that working-tree runtime was built with `pnpm build:runtime`. The native publisher preserves the guest Git HEAD, so the retained build stamp correctly says base `9c22cf86`, `inputsClean:false`, **not** the published commit. The production inputs equal the published tree; the subsequent commit only removes the stale mock exemption. The complete regular-file dist manifest was identical before/after this run. Hashes below identify captured bytes, not independent attestation.

Exact run (Node 26.12.1 selected on PATH, `TEST_PG_URL` points only to the task-local PostgreSQL 17.11 service; no paid provider):

~~~sh
cp .openclaw/tmp/pg-cold-proof/pg-cold-restoration-proof.e2e.test.ts test/pg-cold-restoration-proof.e2e.test.ts
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 \
  node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres \
  --connection "$TEST_PG_URL" -- test/pg-cold-restoration-proof.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# Temporary harness returned to ignored scratch afterward.
~~~

The fixture invokes the actual reader owner's `closeIfIdle()` using a task-only SIGURG preload, rather than waiting 30 minutes or changing production policy. History flags are computed from **actual public RPC payloads** against synthetic markers (full payload SHA retained); request counts increment on **actual received HTTP POSTs**. Agent status is the actual RPC result; PID inequality verifies a new process. The task-only instrumentation contains no connection admission bypass. The final Gateway, model fixture and owned schemas were cleaned up; the disposable PostgreSQL server was stopped after capture.

prs.title: fix(exec): macOS app node exec with timeoutSeconds 0 ends after 20 seconds
prs.body:
Related: #185429 #139706 #163978 #162789 #135272 #166652 #142874

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `exec` on a macOS app node with `timeoutSeconds: 0` ("0 disables" the process lifetime) ends after about
20 seconds with `TIMEOUT: macOS app exec host response timed out; execution outcome is unknown`, and the result is
lost.

## User Impact

User impact: no-expiry commands on a macOS app node return their result instead of an unknown outcome after 20 s.
The node host ships inside OpenClaw.app, so users get this with the next macOS app build. Runs stay bounded by the
Gateway invoke deadline (default 1805 s for `timeoutSeconds: 0`), which cancels the node invocation, the same bound an
explicit `0` already has.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway forwards an exec timeout of `0` to the node as `timeoutMs: null`, documented as "no expiry". The macOS app
runs a null timeout without a timer. The node host's socket client exempted only `0` from its response deadline, so
`null` got the 20 s default. #172117 fixed every finite timeout; this is the one input it left out. The change treats
`null` like `0`.

Reach: the node host collapses an absent nested timeout into `null` before calling the app, so every `system.run`
without a nested timeout loses the node-side 20 s deadline, not only `timeoutSeconds: 0`. Those calls stay bounded
by their Gateway invoke deadline plus `node.invoke.cancel`. Example: the remote-skills bin probe uses a shorter Gateway
deadline, so nothing changes for it in practice. One accepted edge case: if the Gateway link drops mid-run, the node
host waits as long as the companion runs, as it already does for `0`.

Overlap: draft #163978 (last updated 2026-10-15) reworked the same deadline before #172117 landed and targets the
code from before it. This is the minimal residual on current main. The 20 s default for direct callers that omit
`timeoutMs`, pinned in `src/infra/jsonl-socket.test.ts`, is unchanged.

<details><summary>Root cause path (origin/main 2bf23407639)</summary>

- `src/agents/exec-tool-timeout.ts:24-27`: `timeoutSeconds: 0` gives `runTimeoutMs: 0`, sent as nested `timeoutMs`.
- `src/gateway/node-registry.system-run.ts:71-81`: `timeoutMs <= 0` becomes `null` ("preserving null for no expiry").
- `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.ts:328`, `:747`: the exec host request carries `timeoutMs: null`.
- `src/infra/exec-host.ts:59-65`: only `=== 0` disables the deadline; `addTimerTimeoutGraceMs(null)` is `undefined`, so the `?? 20_000` fallback applies.
- `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/ExecHostExecutor.swift:139`, `ShellExecutor.swift:212-219`: a nil timeout runs with no timer.

The test imports the Gateway normalizer on purpose, so the wire value in the test is the one the Gateway really
sends.

</details>

## Evidence

Focused test `src/infra/exec-host.socket.test.ts` "waits past the 20 s fallback for a Gateway no-expiry run". It runs a
real Unix-domain-socket peer with fake timers: it derives `timeoutMs` from `normalizeSystemRunInvokeParams`, advances a
fake day, then replies.

- Base (`src/infra/exec-host.ts` from origin/main), `pnpm test src/infra/exec-host.socket.test.ts` (excerpt, lines in log order):
  ```text
  FAIL   infra  src/infra/exec-host.socket.test.ts > exec host real UDS boundary > waits past the 20 s fallback for a Gateway no-expiry run
  AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times
          "code": "TIMEOUT",
          "message": "TIMEOUT: macOS app exec host response timed out; execution outcome is unknown",
  Tests  1 failed | 8 passed (9)
  ```
- Branch, `pnpm test src/infra/exec-host.socket.test.ts src/infra/exec-host.test.ts src/infra/jsonl-socket.test.ts src/node-host/invoke-system-run.socket.test.ts`:
  ```text
  Test Files  4 passed (4)
       Tests  26 passed (26)
  ```
- Neighboring node-host suites on the head, `pnpm test src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts src/node-host/invoke-system-run.environment.test.ts`: `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 59 passed (59)`.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base origin/main`: 33 phases ok, including format, lint, typecheck core and core tests, and import cycles. The dead export scan fails on `extensions/browser/src/browser/client.types.ts: BrowserGraphicsDevice`, a file this diff does not touch (not re-run at base).

### Real behavior proof (macOS app node)

After (app built from this head, `81b290c95b4`):
- Run: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/40554854403 (mac/proof-3, macos-26-intel, Xcode 26.6)
- App: OpenClaw.app 2026.10.7 debug (adhoc); bundled private runtime build `2026.10.7-81b290c95b4b-2026-10-27T17-58-06.000Z`
- Node: `clientId openclaw-macos`, packaged app, node `8f10b9bf3873…`
- Request: `node.invoke system.run`, `sh -c 'sleep 45; echo done'`, `timeoutMs: 0`
- Result: `ok: true`, `exitCode: 0`, `timedOut: false`, `stdout: "done\n"`; gateway logged `node.invoke 55802 ms`; scenario `PASS 3 head: done after 59s`

Before (same command on a real installed app node, pre-patch):
- App 2026.10.6, commit `41c5d94f722c`, built `2026-10-22T19:35:02Z`; bundled runtime `Contents/Resources/runtime` contains `request.timeoutMs === 0 ? 0 : …` only.
- Gateway `exec` tool, `host=node`, `timeoutSeconds: 0` → `TIMEOUT: macOS app exec host response timed out; execution outcome is unknown` after ~20 s; no stdout.

Gaps: the after case ran through `node.invoke system.run` (the same Gateway → node host → exec-host route, including the patched `exec-host.ts`), not the agent `exec` tool, because the hosted runner exposes no `exec` tool on `/tools/invoke`. The `exec` tool on a patched app node was not run. The test peer proves the TypeScript transport, not Swift policy or native execution. The Swift side needs no change because it already runs a nil timeout without a timer, but its behavior on the cancel path (whether the child dies when the socket closes) was not observed natively.

prs.body:
Related: #182568. Depends on #182590.

## What Problem This Solves

Browser users cannot see their paired companion apps from Updates; the existing Apps panel is visible only inside a native app.

## User Impact

Updates → Apps lists paired native installations with their reported app version and connected/offline state. Remote entries say **Update on device** and offer no remote update action or release-available indicator. The current native app retains its existing local controls, even while the inventory request is pending or fails.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the read-only initial inventory slice discussed in #182568, not a fleet updater. It reads existing `node.list` facts, excludes unapproved and non-native clients, preserves separate installations, and deduplicates the local app only by exact node ID. Gateway remains the default tab. Native lifecycle, release discovery and the Mac automatic-installation policy (#160530) are unchanged.

**Stack:** this branch includes the unmerged presentation-only parent #182590. Review the [inventory-only diff](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/compare/e54dc02de6abe36d3ed37e7d8ab9fb55dba8dfc9...75823680136e5417f3bf0c9174fbff755e5e1e48): 12 files, +425/-130 (including the five-file test-only CI repair). Do not merge independently of the parent; its presentation decision remains with maintainers. No backend, protocol, native-app, dependency or CSS changes are added by this slice.

## Evidence

**Current CI caveat (2026-10-25):** [checks-ui-e2e (6/9)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40137666909/job/121002814403) is red in the unchanged compact agent-picker test: after selecting Writer, its checkmark has no bounding box at 390px. Both viewport cases pass unchanged locally. The matching main job failed a different test, so its coarse pre-existing classification does not establish this failure as inherited. Cause remains unclassified; the passing replay is not a repair or evidence of green CI.

- 60 focused UI tests,42 confirmation-runtime tests and all5 native-device browser scenarios pass. A deferred-read regression fails before the repair and passes afterward: local Check now stays usable while `node.list` remains pending; choosing a remote app removes the local action. Tests also cover filtering, exact-ID deduplication, unknown version, read failure and stale-connection retirement.
- Production UI typecheck, focused lint/format, keyless i18n, Solid guards and UI build pass. Build reports the same inherited CSS budget warnings as the parent (296.5 vs296.3 KiB gzip); no CSS or budget changes are included. Independent source review found the pending-read issue; it was fixed and re-reviewed.
- **Real Gateway proof:** shipped browser Updates → Apps → actual WebSocket `node.list` (no RPC interception), with synthetic paired offline iOS/Android/node-host identities created through the production pairing APIs in separate secretless state. Both native apps rendered; node-host was excluded. Desktop/narrow views had no overflow or browser errors; all 106 fetched assets matched the tested UI build. Temporary Gateway stopped and its port verified free.
- **Fixture proof:** separate connected/offline scenarios cover both widths; settled card opacity verified as1. These are not physical-device or native-updater demonstrations.
- Provenance: tested UI source was the final inventory tree atop `e421d3ed`; the published stack moves it onto the parent's test-only `e54dc02` cleanup. Production bytes are unchanged (Apps source SHA256 `e6fe69a5250ea5ceb104ed9f433c5d203cfe9a2dfe8d88a2f1b5cb33c4fc24ae`). Real backend remained `e421d3ed`, served through the supported custom UI root. This is not a same-build compatibility test.
- No update/install control or `node.invoke` was used. Entering Updates automatically reads `update.status`; the isolated Dev lookup returned unavailable without preventing Apps inventory. No physical connected-device, update execution or public report submission is claimed. The first hosted run exposed three stale test-consumer/fixture assumptions. All were reproduced and repaired without production changes; current-head hosted checks/re-review follow the test-only repair.

<details>
<summary>Before — browser Updates has no Apps inventory</summary>

![Before browser Updates](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/735ebfb48fa75af20732f202176475ad4fc31e3f/after.png)

</details>

![After — real Gateway, synthetic paired iOS app](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb5c203c-3873-40bd-87ad-f9a265034c9b)

![After — narrow viewport, synthetic paired Android app](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/792b9de5-97d9-4781-a559-3b15a57a562a)

### Hosted review repair

The native action test now opens the lazily mounted Apps tab; the lifecycle mock returns a valid `node.list` response; the browser test awaits the produced Apps heading. The mock Gateway also supplies an empty inventory by default. Existing acknowledgement, retry and route-retirement assertions remain unchanged. Production/source assets and earlier screenshots are unchanged.

### Hosted CI consumer follow-through (25 October)

Current head: `075dbd7afc908175bc920170e9674a59b0bea8e6`. A stale forced-colors E2E scenario still queried Beta/Stable radio buttons after the Updates channel control became a dropdown. It reproduced before repair (missing Beta radio); the existing scenario now exercises the actual Appearance segmented control in both light and dark forced-color modes. prs.title: fix(ui): dashboard widget links do nothing in the macOS app
prs.body:
Related: #142606

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: clicking an `https` `target="_blank"` link inside a dashboard HTML widget does nothing in the macOS app.

## User Impact

User impact: in the macOS app, a deliberate click on a widget link opens the destination in the default browser, the same place other external Dashboard links already go. Every click opens, including two clicks in quick succession. Browsers keep their current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI opens widget links with `window.open` from the `host.open` MessagePort task. WebKit's popup blocker does not carry the click's gesture across a MessagePort, so the dashboard web view drops the open before the app's existing new-window handoff runs.

`host.open` now offers the URL to the app's existing `openclawLink` owner first (`postNativeExternalLink`) and keeps `openExternalUrlSafe` for browsers, the pattern the browser-tab card and browser panel already use. The native receiver accepts `openclawLink` only from the Control UI main frame and calls the same `ControlUIDocumentHost.openExternal`. The native route stays per caller rather than inside `openExternalUrlSafe`, because moving it there would change the destination for every caller and would hand `blob:` URLs to a native handler that cannot open them.

The native route skips the popup blocker, so it applies that blocker's rules itself: the gesture must be in this widget, and each open spends it. An open goes native only when all of these hold (`ui/src/lib/board/widget-bridge.ts` `openNativeLink`):

1. **The dashboard has live activation** (`navigator.userActivation.isActive`).
2. **The gesture was in this widget.** The board host asks the widget's own sandbox proxy frame for its `navigator.userActivation.isActive` (`ui/notifications/sandbox-activation-query` with a random id, `ui/src/lib/board/widget-sandbox-host.ts`). The answer counts only from `frame.contentWindow` at `sandboxOrigin`. No answer within 250 ms means refuse. The proxy answers in `src/agents/sandbox-host.ts` and never relays `sandbox-` notifications from its inner frame, so the widget cannot forge the answer. Activation reaches the proxy frame only from input inside its own widget (WebKit probe below). The proxy is served fresh by the Gateway, so this also covers stored widgets that keep their approved wrapper bytes.
3. **The request is still current after that await.** Widget retirement, a Gateway disconnect or reconnect, and a document reset bump the request generation, so `isCurrent()` returns false. In that case `host.open` throws `widget link request is no longer current` before both the native opener and the `window.open` fallback. The same lifecycle paths settle every pending activation query as inactive and drop its id (`cancelActivationQueries`), so a late proxy answer finds nothing to resolve. The native receiver gets no widget lifecycle identity, so the bridge enforces retirement before it posts.
4. **Each open spends the gesture.** Before posting, the bridge consumes the page's transient activation the way an opened popup does: `document.createElement("input").showPicker()` runs WebKit's consume-user-activation (`HTMLInputElement::showPicker` calls `LocalDOMWindow::consumeTransientActivation`, which clears activation in every frame of the page). A detached text input has nothing to show. The bridge then checks that `isActive` really went false, and refuses otherwise (fail closed). One real click or key in a widget yields at most one open. The next open needs new input, and a new click opens at once. There is no rate limit or time budget.

Browsers without `openclawLink` (`hasNativeExternalLink()` is false) skip all of this and keep the old path.

New wrappers also read bridge and prompt port messages through a `MessageEvent.prototype.data` getter captured before widget code runs (`src/canvas/wrap.ts`), the same approach the shortcut bridge uses. That closes the port theft itself for new documents. The proxy binding and per-open consumption cover stored widgets.

Widget-side gates are unchanged: trusted click, adopted view ticket, `http(s)` only, private port. No popup permission, sandbox attribute, or Swift change.

**Why not `document.activeElement`:** a WKWebView probe with real HID input and the dashboard's 3-level nesting showed that a cross-origin widget with no activation of its own can focus itself (`input.focus()`, `link.focus()`, `window.focus()`). The parent's `activeElement` then becomes that widget's frame while activation from a click elsewhere is still live, so it does not prove a gesture in that widget.

<details>
<summary>Root cause trace (main 5291a06cc263)</summary>

| Hop | Code | Result in WebKit |
|---|---|---|
| Trusted widget click to `host.open` | `src/canvas/wrap.ts:147-154` | reaches the host |
| Proxy port hand-off and request dispatch | `src/agents/sandbox-host.ts:393-404`, `ui/src/lib/board/widget-sandbox-host.ts:178-191, 260` | synchronous into `BoardWidgetBridgeOwner.handle` |
| `host.open` | `ui/src/lib/board/widget-bridge.ts:129-137` | calls the opener |
| Opener | `ui/src/lib/open-external-url.ts:73` | `window.open` returns `null` |
| WebKit popup gate (`ControlUIDocumentHost.swift:56`) | | blocked: no `decidePolicyFor`, no `createWebViewWith` |
| Native handoff | `DashboardWindowController.swift:312-340`, `ControlUIDocumentHost+NavigationPolicy.swift:375-378`, `AppActivation.swift:62-65` | never reached |

A `null` result from `window.open` is not the failure signal: with `noopener` WebKit returns `null` even for opens it performs.
</details>

### Risk

- In the macOS app, widget links go to the default browser through `openclawLink` (`target: "external"`). That is the destination the app's new-window delegate already uses for Dashboard `window.open` requests.
- The popup blocker no longer runs on the native route. Its rules are applied by the four checks above. A widget gets at most one open per real gesture inside it, the same as a popup.
- A native open spends the page's activation, as an opened popup does. Another activation-gated action on the same gesture afterwards needs new input.
- A slow proxy answer (over 250 ms) refuses the open. The user can click again.
- Any other host that installs `openclawLink` gets the same route. Only the macOS dashboard does today.

## Security boundary

The native route skips WebKit's popup gate, so the remaining guards are pinned by tests, WebKit probes, and the app runs below:

- **Port theft.** Widget code can redefine `MessageEvent.prototype.data` and read the wrapper's private port and ticket when host-init arrives. On 98f66694ae2 a stored widget with old wrapper bytes that steals its port opens nothing after a click outside it, and one click inside it opens exactly once while it keeps sending through the stolen port (app run below). New wrappers no longer leak the port (captured getter). The `wrap.test.ts` case runs the real wrapper with a `data` override and goes red without the getter.
- **Retirement during the activation query.** `host.open` rechecks `isCurrent` after the query and rejects before either opener. Pending queries are settled as inactive on retirement, disconnect, reconnect and reset. Tests: `widget-bridge.test.ts` (retired during a pending query, for both a positive and a negative answer) and `widget-sandbox-host.test.ts` (retired, reconnected, disconnected while the query is pending: no `openclawLink`, no `window.open`, activation untouched, query timer released at once). App run below: with the query held, killing the Gateway opens nothing on 98f66694ae2 and opened the link on 2031987bfa4.
- **Native receiver.** `openclawLink` is accepted only from the dashboard web view's main frame (`DashboardWindowController.swift:546-556`) and receives no widget lifecycle identity. Retirement is therefore enforced in the bridge before posting (above).
- **Proxy activation answer.** Only the widget's own proxy window at the sandbox origin, with the query's random id, can answer. Answers from another frame, another origin, a wrong id, or no answer within 250 ms refuse (`widget-sandbox-host.test.ts`). The proxy answers from its own activation and never relays a widget-sent `sandbox-activation` (`mcp-app-sandbox-http.test.ts`).
- **Gesture spent per open.** One gesture opens one link even when requests race the query (`widget-bridge.test.ts`). An engine whose `showPicker()` leaves activation live, or throws, gets no native open.
- **Wrapper** (`src/canvas/wrap.ts:147-154`): forwards only `isTrusted` primary `target=_blank` clicks or middle clicks. On the real wrapper, scripted `click()` and synthetic `click`/`auxclick` on https, `javascript:` and `data:` anchors post no `host.open`.
- **Host and owner:** `host.open` from the window channel, another frame, another origin, a second port offer, or a forged or retired ticket never reaches `openclawLink`. The forged-port test now waits on the host closing the forged port, not on a sleep. 11 non-HTTP(S) URLs reach neither `openclawLink` nor `window.open`. The host-realm `^https?://` check is the binding scheme gate.

## Real behavior proof

Shipped macOS app built from the exact source, real HID pointer clicks, before and after, plus stolen-port and retire-during-query legs on the new head and on the previous head.

- Environment: MacBook Pro, Apple silicon (arm64), macOS 27.2 (26B123), Xcode 27.1, default browser Google Chrome 156.0.8078.74. App built with `scripts/package-mac-app.sh` (debug, ad-hoc signed, `ai.openclaw.mac.debug`, app version 2026.10.7) from 98f66694ae2. Each run's `identity.txt` records `source_sha` = `expected_sha` (98f66694ae2, 2031987bfa4 or 5291a06cc263).
- Harness: fork `etzelm/openclaw` branch `mac/proof-6b` commit `4cedbb52eba` (`scripts/mac-proof/6.sh`, `6s.sh`, `6r.sh`, driver and instrumentation in `scripts/mac-proof/local-185433-r8/`) on lib `mac/proof-5` `f354d51cefd`. It runs locally (`PP_LOCAL=1`, isolated state dir and app profile) with a loopback Gateway on 28789, the MCP App sandbox on 28790, and a fixture on 127.0.0.1:38790 that records each hit with its User-Agent. A fixture hit from Chrome is the final effect, whichever opener caused it.
- Targeted tests on the same build tree: `widget-bridge` + `widget-sandbox-host` 63/63.

### After, head `98f66694ae2dde1a19db163a2688db9b6c96beb4`: PASS, and two quick clicks both open

```
14:44:11 HID click 1 posted at the link's AX center
14:44:12 allowed open via: HID pointer click 1
14:44:16 double click: mouse-ups at 1793483055815 and 1793483056323 ms, 508 ms apart (app re-activated between them)
14:44:17 after-double: probe v1 moves:6 down:trusted-b0 click:trusted-d1-act-yes dbl:2
14:44:17 double click hits /double = 2 at 21:44:15.885Z 21:44:16.392Z
14:45:56 final-effect hits /synthetic = 0
14:45:56 final-effect hits /forged-open = 0
14:45:56 final-effect hits /forged-request = 0
14:45:56 allowed hit opener: {"at":"2026-10-31T21:44:11.451Z","port":38790,"path":"/widget","ua":"... Chrome/156.0.0.0 Safari/537.36"}
14:45:56 PASS 6 (HID pointer click 1): the click opened the default browser; two clicks under a second apart opened twice; ...
```

One real click opened `/widget` in Chrome. Then two real clicks on a second link, 508 ms apart, opened it twice (fixture hits 507 ms apart). The widget recorded both trusted clicks (`dbl:2`). Chrome takes the front after the first open and covers the app here, so the harness brings the app back between the clicks, as a user would. A first attempt without that step sent click 2 into Chrome and opened once. The previous head's shared 1 s budget refused any second open inside a second (its own unit test pinned that), so this step would lose the second open there.

- Widget in the dashboard panel before the click: 

  ![after-12-before-click.jpg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/86f36bad11592d926802838a23c431c36a0e6e3d/mac-item-6-widget-links/proof-r8/after-12-before-click.jpg)
- Default browser after the two clicks (tab strip, bookmarks, icons and banner blacked out):

- Recording (app window only): [after-recording.mp4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/86f36bad11592d926802838a23c431c36a0e6e3d/mac-item-6-widget-links/proof-r8/after-recording.mp4)

### Before, base `5291a06cc263f0815fa087fd02bbdb29c3839089`: FAIL

```
14:47:07 HID click 1 posted at the link's AX center
14:47:28 after-hid-1: probe v1 moves:2 down:trusted-b0 click:trusted-d1-act-yes dbl:0

The widget's probe shows the trusted click with user activation, and the fixture logged no request:

### Stolen port: outside click opens nothing, one inside click opens once

The `6s` widget overrides `MessageEvent.prototype.data`, keeps the wrapper's port and ticket, and sends `host.open` for `/stolen` through it every 300 ms for the whole run. The harness stores it with a Gateway on 7bdf01c0b32 (old wrapper bytes that leak the port) and serves it from the source under test. It clicks chat text outside the widget, sends a keystroke, and then clicks plain text (not a link) inside the widget once.

New head 98f66694ae2:

```

The one inside click opened once. Between the two probe reads the widget sent 40 more requests through the stolen port (`sent:57` to `sent:97`), and only that one was accepted (`oks:1`). Previous head 2031987bfa4, same harness: outside click 0 opens, and the one inside click gave **3** opens (`21:53:37.850Z 21:53:39.911Z 21:53:41.892Z`), the reusable window the budget allowed.

The production query window is a few milliseconds (immediate proxy answer, 250 ms timeout), too short to retire the widget inside it from outside the app. For this leg only, the driver applies timing instrumentation to the served build and restores it afterwards (`local-185433-r8/instrument.mjs`). The proxy sends its usual answer, read at answer time, 2500 ms late. The dashboard waits up to 10 s for it instead of 250 ms. No check in the path changes.

`6r.sh` first clicks a control link with the Gateway up. The held answer must still open it, which shows the instrumented path works. Then it clicks the retire link and kills the Gateway (`kill -9`) right after the click, inside the hold. The Gateway disconnect is the retirement the review describes: the frame stays rendered, the host goes inactive and `connected: false`, and the proxy is still alive to answer.

New head 98f66694ae2:

```

15:01:08 control: click helper ran 1793484064709..1793484065527; hits /control = 1; browser hit 2489 ms after the click returned
15:01:14 retire: click helper ran 1793484073904..1793484074273; Gateway pid 79050 killed at 1793484074290 (17 ms after the click returned; the proxy answers ~2500 ms after the click)

```

```

14:58:16 retire: click helper ran 1793483895968..1793483896346; Gateway pid 76799 killed at 1793483896364 (18 ms after the click returned; the proxy answers ~2500 ms after the click)
14:58:17 after-retire: probe r1 moves:7 down:trusted-b0 control:trusted-act-yes retire:trusted-act-yes
14:58:26 final-effect hits /retire = 1 (any opener: native link owner or window.open fallback)
14:58:26 RESULT 6r: OPENED: the widget link pending when the Gateway dropped reached the default browser (1 hit)
```

The leg is armed. On the previous head the same trusted click with activation opened `/retire` in Chrome at 21:58:18.832Z, 2.5 s after the Gateway was killed. On the new head nothing reached the browser. The fixture count covers any opener. WebKit would also block a `window.open` from this task, so the unit tests pin separately that the fallback is never called (`window.open` spy, `widget-sandbox-host.test.ts`).

  ![retire-new-51-after-retire.jpg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/86f36bad11592d926802838a23c431c36a0e6e3d/mac-item-6-widget-links/proof-r8/retire-new-51-after-retire.jpg)

The app's session list is blacked out in every shot and recording. No tokens appear (the Gateway token lives only in the temp state dir).

## Evidence

- **WebKit consumption probe** (MacBook, macOS 27.2, WKWebView, real HID clicks, dashboard-like parent, proxy-like frame and opaque-origin widget, two widgets). The parent uses this PR's sequence: own activation, proxy activation, then `document.createElement("input").showPicker()`. Results: after one open, the parent, both proxies and both widget frames report `isActive=false`. Two real link clicks about 625 ms apart both opened. A burst from one trusted click (+300 ms, +900 ms, no new gesture) opened once. After an outside click the reuse was still refused because the proxy reported false. A link click in A and then in B about 480 ms later both opened.
- **WebKit focus/activation probe** (round 7): the proxy frame's activation is set only by a click or key inside its own widget. It stays false after parent clicks and keys, after clicks in a sibling widget, and after focus theft.
- **Red/green** (Studio): the new tests against 2031987bfa4 production code: 10 fail. Single-check mutations of this patch: no `isCurrent` recheck 4 fail, no query cancellation 3 fail, no consumption 4 fail, no consumption check 1 fail. Full patch: `widget-bridge` + `widget-sandbox-host` 63/63. Wider UI (`lib/board`, `native-link-routing`, `components/board`, `canvas-widget-view-owner`) 272/272.
- `tsgo:ui` exit 0. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 2031987bfa4`: every check ok (format, lint, UI and core-test typecheck, guards) except the dead export scan (`BrowserGraphicsDevice`, `resolveGatewayRecoverySchemaPaths`), which flags files this PR does not touch and fails the same way on 2031987bfa4 and on main.
- Gaps: middle click (`auxclick`) is unproven in the app, because the harness produced no `auxclick` in the widget (both click kinds share `host.open`). Chromium behavior is from the live proof in #128125 and was not re-run for this head. One browser-mode test file could not start on the test host (Playwright Chromium not installed). The retire app leg uses the timing instrumentation above, and the unit tests cover the retire paths at production timing. Widget link routing to the reading tab or the Gateway browser preference is out of scope: the destination stays the default browser, as for Dashboard `window.open` today.

prs.title: Request speakerphone output for Android Talk
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Android, `RealtimeCommunicationAudio` sets `AudioManager.mode =
MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION` to start a Talk session but never requests the
loudspeaker as the output device. Android's default routing for
`MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION` is the earpiece unless a Bluetooth/wired headset is
attached, so continuous Talk plays back quietly through the earpiece
instead of the main loudspeaker - unexpected for a hands-free,
phone-away-from-the-ear conversation.

iOS already has an explicit speakerphone setting for Talk (see the Talk
settings page in the iOS app / dashboard). Android has no equivalent
request anywhere in the realtime audio path - this looks like a parity gap
rather than an intentional platform difference.

Any custom realtime voice provider plugin (via `registerRealtimeVoiceProvider`)
used through Android's Talk feature is affected equally to the built-in
OpenAI/xAI providers, since the audio routing logic is shared and
provider-agnostic.

## Evidence

Confirmed from the current Android source
(`apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/RealtimeCommunicationAudio.kt`)
that `start()` sets `audioManager.mode = AudioManager.MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION`
and requests audio focus, but never calls `setCommunicationDevice(...)` or
`isSpeakerphoneOn = true` anywhere - there is no output-device request in
this file or in the related `RealtimePlayout.kt` / `AndroidAudioInputSession.kt`
/ `TalkModeManager.kt` files (checked via direct source review, not
assumption). This matches standard documented Android behavior: apps using
`MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION` get earpiece-by-default routing unless they
explicitly request another device.

This PR requests the speaker explicitly when a Talk communication-audio
session starts, and releases it cleanly when it ends - using
`AudioManager.setCommunicationDevice()` on Android 12+ (the documented
replacement for the deprecated speakerphone API), falling back to
`isSpeakerphoneOn` on older versions. Existing Bluetooth/wired routing in
`AndroidAudioInputSession` still takes priority when an external device is
actually connected, since device selection there is handled separately by
the OS once a route is active - this change only affects the otherwise-
silent default when no other device is connected.

Not yet verified on-device or via a local build - no Android SDK/Gradle
toolchain was available in the environment this patch was written in. The
change is a minimal, targeted addition using documented public
`AudioManager` APIs, confirmed against the current Android platform API
surface and against this repo's actual current source, but it has not been
compiled or run. Flagging this explicitly rather than claiming it's been
tested - would appreciate a maintainer or anyone able to build the Android
app confirming it compiles and actually fixes the earpiece-default
behavior on a real device before merging.

prs.title: fix(macos): Mac tab shows a blank or stale page when a load fails
prs.body:
Related: #183927

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Mac tab shows a blank white page (new tab) or silently keeps the previous page (loaded tab) when a page fails to load, and Reload does nothing for a failed first load.

## User Impact

User impact: when a link is broken or the Mac is offline, the tab now keeps the address that was tried, says why it could not be opened, and offers Reload, which retries that address. Stopping a load, navigating somewhere else, and download or default-browser handoffs still keep the current page without an error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main-frame failures reached `DashboardNativeBrowserHost.navigationDidFail(for:)` without the error, so the tab only retired its link alias and published unchanged state (`apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardWindowController.swift:1467-1470`, `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardNativeBrowserHost.swift:269-272` on `70c70646d86`). Reload called `webView.reload()` (`DashboardNativeBrowserHost.swift:174`), which replays the last committed item; a failed first load never commits one, so nothing happens.

The tab owner now receives the error. Deliberate interruptions (`NSURLErrorCancelled`, and WebKit's policy interruption 102 used for response-policy cancels such as downloads and default-browser handoff) are ignored as before. Any other failure shows a native failure view over the tab's web view: a title, the system error description (no page content and no URL), and a Reload button. The tab keeps the failing URL; the published tab URL prefers it, and Reload (the button or the toolbar) loads it again. The next navigation that starts clears the failure.

The failure view is AppKit, added as a subview of the reading tab's `WKWebView`, so it follows the existing presentation frames and hiding and the untrusted page cannot script or restyle it. It is layer-backed and sets its background in `updateLayer()`: the first revision was a plain opaque view filled in `draw(_:)`, and in the running app it painted over the whole dashboard window (see the running-app proof below). No bridge, Control UI, or privileged dashboard failure-page code is involved. Favicon and alias handling from #184839 is unchanged: a failed navigation never commits, so the shown page keeps its icon.

## Evidence

### Running-app proof

The packaged app built from this branch (debug, ad hoc signed, `ai.openclaw.mac.debug` 2026.10.7) ran on macOS 27.2 arm64 with Xcode 27.1, launched with `--dashboard` against a task-owned loopback Gateway and HTTP fixture. Accessibility drove it by process id, and the native failure view, which WebKit keeps out of the accessibility tree, was read and clicked from the window via Vision text recognition. Window screenshots and a recording of only the app's windows.

1. A new tab opens an address nothing listens on. The failure view shows "This page couldn't be opened / Could not connect to the server.", the address bar keeps `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/first-load`, the fixture starts, and the failure view's Reload loads the page (fixture: one request for `/first-load`).
2. The loaded page follows a link to another unserved address. The failure view shows, the address bar keeps `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/broken`, the fixture starts, and the toolbar Reload loads it (one request for `/broken`). The failure view is gone after each recovery.

The first revision (`9ad45a61910`) passed the same flow, but while the failure view showed, its background covered the whole dashboard window: chat, tab strip, address bar and toolbar. `e164e6e589e` makes the view layer-backed, and it now stays inside the tab.

The Browser panel of `e164e6e589e` at full resolution, cropped from the window screenshots (the failure view's text is small grey on dark in the full-window shots below):

Failed first load, then after the failure view's Reload:

![panel-failed-first-load](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/panel-fixed-10-new-tab-failed.png) ![panel-recovered-native-reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/panel-fixed-11-new-tab-recovered-native-reload.png)

Failed navigation from the loaded page, then after the toolbar Reload:

![panel-failed-navigation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/panel-fixed-21-loaded-tab-failed.png) ![panel-recovered-toolbar-reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/panel-fixed-22-loaded-tab-recovered-toolbar-reload.png)

The same crop from frames of the `e164e6e589e` recording at 9 s (first load failed), 21 s (recovered), 25 s (navigation failed) and the last frame (recovered), so the sequence can be checked without playing the video:

![frame-09s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/frame-fixed-t09s.png) ![frame-21s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/frame-fixed-t21s.png) ![frame-25s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/frame-fixed-t25s.png) ![frame-end](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/frame-fixed-end.png)

Text recognized in each crop and frame: [text.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/9532ed1427030c5d12a40b79885af6a70b2ce82a/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/panel/text.txt).

Failed navigation, `9ad45a61910` (whole window covered) and `e164e6e589e` (failure view inside the tab; the address bar shows the attempted URL):

![before-loaded-tab-failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/before-21-loaded-tab-failed.png)
![after-loaded-tab-failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/fixed-21-loaded-tab-failed.png)

![after-native-reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/fixed-11-new-tab-recovered-native-reload.png)
![after-toolbar-reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/fixed-22-loaded-tab-recovered-toolbar-reload.png)

Recordings: [`9ad45a61910`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/before-recording.mp4), [`e164e6e589e`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/fixed-recording.mp4). Build identity, scenario logs and fixture request logs are next to them ([fixed identity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/fixed-identity.txt), [fixed scenario log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/87eb46377ce58ce1c3ab101f1be1102037d04546/mac-item-5-tab-failures/running-app/fixed-scenario.log)). The bottom-left avatar is masked.

With `e164e6e589e`, on the same Mac: `swift test --filter DashboardNativeBrowserTests` (Xcode 27.1): 27 tests in 4 suites passed. SwiftFormat and SwiftLint `--strict` on the changed file: clean. `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos`: only the existing `DashboardManager.swift` file_length violation.

### Offscreen renders and regressions

Each image is an offscreen render of the reading tab's web view from the real `DashboardWindowController` in the regression harness. The grey band at the bottom is a test harness readout, not app UI: it prints the tab state `DashboardNativeBrowserHost` publishes to the dashboard (loopback port masked). The tab strip and address bar are Control UI web chrome and are not part of these renders.

New tab whose first load fails, before (blank white page) and after (native failure view with Reload; the tab state already reported the attempted URL on base):

![a-before-new-tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/8741e3612b3ea2b8c0cfb96990e57865054ebdae/mac-item-5-tab-failures/a-before-new-tab.png)
![a-after-new-tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/8741e3612b3ea2b8c0cfb96990e57865054ebdae/mac-item-5-tab-failures/a-after-new-tab.png)

Loaded tab whose navigation to `/next` fails, before (old page stays and tab state still reports `/article`) and after (failure view; tab state reports the attempted `/next`):

![a-before-loaded-tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/8741e3612b3ea2b8c0cfb96990e57865054ebdae/mac-item-5-tab-failures/a-before-loaded-tab.png)
![a-after-loaded-tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/8741e3612b3ea2b8c0cfb96990e57865054ebdae/mac-item-5-tab-failures/a-after-loaded-tab.png)

Focused real-WKWebView regressions in `apps/macos/Tests/OpenClawIPCTests/DashboardNativeBrowserTests.swift` (`DashboardNativeBrowserFailureTests`), driving `DashboardWindowController` and its navigation delegate against task-owned loopback `DashboardHTTPFixture` endpoints:

- a new tab opened on a released loopback port shows the failure, keeps the attempted URL in tab state, and after the endpoint comes back the failure view's Reload button loads it;
- the same from an already loaded page: the page and its favicon stay, tab state shows the attempted URL, toolbar Reload loads it, and Back stays available after the retry;
- stop, replacement navigation, and a non-displayable response (download policy cancel) show no failure.

Results on macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Swift 6.4 (Command Line Tools), base `70c70646d86`:

- `swift test --filter DashboardNativeBrowserFailureTests` on this branch: 3 tests (5 cases) passed.
- The same flows on base (tests rewritten to base APIs, failure-view assertions dropped): the failed first load never retries (`Time limit was exceeded`, still waiting for the retried load), and after a failed navigation from a loaded page the tab state still shows the old page's URL (`failed.url == attempted.absoluteString` is false).
- Siblings `DashboardNativeBrowser|DashboardHTTPFixtureTests|DashboardBrowserDownloadTests|DashboardBrowserCookieBoundaryTests`: 34 tests in 7 suites passed.
- `swift build --build-tests`, `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` (0 files need formatting), `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` (only the existing `DashboardManager.swift` file_length violation, also on base), `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, `git diff --check`: clean.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base <current main>` on the stacked follow-up for #183928, whose diff against main includes every file of this branch (not run separately on this branch): every guard passed except `lint apps` (the existing `DashboardManager.swift` file_length violation) and `macOS app CI tests` (1 failed, 607 passed), whose one failure is the tooling test `test/scripts/generate-gateway-protocol-plugin.test.ts`, which builds the Swift package itself and fails on this machine with the Command Line Tools manifest link error (`Package.__allocating_init` undefined); it does not touch the files in this change.

## Related work

- #152668 (open, prepare integrated tab logins before opening links) touches `DashboardNativeBrowserHost.swift`, `DashboardWindowController.swift` and `apps/.i18n/native-source.json`. No shared lines: its host change removes `self.onOpen?()` in `open` (line 160 on `70c70646d86`), a few lines above this stack's `navigate`/`perform` changes; its controller hunks are in lines 99-559, ours at 1331-1496. It already conflicts with current main on its own. Whichever lands second regenerates the i18n inventory with `pnpm native:i18n:baseline` (the inventory records source line sites).
- No open PR covers #183927 or #183928 (searched by symptom and by the owner file names).

## Gaps

- The offscreen renders under "Offscreen renders and regressions" come from the real `DashboardWindowController` on a host without a logged-in GUI session; the running-app proof above is the window evidence.
- The offscreen renders and the test results under them were built with the Command Line Tools (Swift 6.4) only, no Xcode; the running-app proof and its test run used Xcode 27.1. Xcode-only SwiftUI macro plugins (`@State`, `@Entry`, `#Preview`) were replaced locally by equivalent desugaring plugins, and two unrelated XCTest-based test files were left out locally because the CLT ships no XCTest. Nothing in this change uses SwiftUI. The `macos-swift` CI job is the authoritative native run.

- Known edges, unchanged in scope: the failure view sits over the tab's web view, so a snapshot of a failed loaded tab (for example Annotate) still captures the previous page underneath; a same-document navigation by that previous page (`pushState`, hash change) does not start a provisional load and so leaves the failure shown; Reload retries a failed POST as a plain GET of the same URL.

prs.title: fix: honor explicit npm commands on Windows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Windows command execution silently running the host’s bundled npm instead of the npm/npx executable or wrapper explicitly selected by a caller.

## User Impact

Plugin command-runner callers can use an explicit npm/npx path or native executable without losing the selected installation, version, or wrapper behavior. Missing explicit paths fail normally rather than falling back to another npm installation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the bundled-CLI shortcut for generic npm/npx aliases, but send explicit paths and native executables through the existing Windows executable resolver and trusted batch wrapper. Existing unsupported-command and unsafe batch-argument checks remain intact. No dependency, configuration, or public API changes.

## Evidence

- Native Windows / Node 24.22.1: the real command-runner API previously substituted host npm for runnable task-local `npm.exe`, `npx.exe`, and an explicitly selected npm batch wrapper. After the fix, four direct-process/runner comparisons have matching output and normal exit code 0, with unchanged timeouts.
- Exact-base regression: **4 failed / 23 passed**; fixed owner suite: **27/27 passed**, including native batch argv checks, four existing real PTY cases, and unsafe-argument rejection. Affected Windows execution suite: **18/18 passed**.
- Targeted production and test typechecks, type-aware lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent source review and canonical exact-source P0–P3 review completed with no introduced findings. Canonical helper status: `scoped-clean`, exit 0, complete validated report; full caller and native execution evidence supplied.
- Cost: changed test file’s Vitest duration **99.76s**, predominantly transformation (93%); approximately 6s executing tests, mostly the existing PTY cases. Repository wrapper wall time **109.23s**. Final-head broad CI, Linux changed-test shards, production/test types, lint, security review and required gates passed at `e52f4f0b63f6719d1cfe84bcf8d4d78bb69ca3bb`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40448872171.

Closes #189635
Closes #189636

## What Problem This Solves

Windows Parallels upgrade smoke can exhaust its harness deadline before the installed CLI receives its full update timeout, while packed installs can leave the CLI unavailable in a fresh shell.

## User Impact

Operators can qualify the actual Windows update result and persisted CLI handoff. This repairs the E2E harness; it does not change the shipped updater or add a system-wide pnpm prerequisite.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Windows helper and its enclosing phase now reserve setup, launch, reporting, and cleanup time around the command budget. Launch refuses when setup has already consumed the available command budget. Post-update diagnostics run in the existing verification phase. Packed fixtures preserve the existing User PATH and add the verified npm global prefix only when absent; verification uses a new PowerShell process with persisted Machine/User PATH.

## Evidence

- 173 affected tooling tests passed (94.59 seconds in Vitest; 102.56 seconds including the wrapper). Targeted scripts/tooling typechecks, matching lint, formatting, whitespace, and test-line budget checks passed.
- The new admission regression fails against base `418bb925ca475c3aafdd06757174cf5779e557fe` and passes with the repair. The 80 net added regression lines exercise this boundary and native package-install exit/PATH behavior.
- Native Windows 11 ARM64 PowerShell: the base fixture fails with `incorrect persistent CLI PATH handoff`; both repaired success cases pass, including case-insensitive prefix deduplication; npm exit 23 still fails with the actual exit code. These use the same generated script and shared fixture as the Windows tests.
- Local autoreview covered the full staged snapshot committed as `cdf6f1ac53b749d4a71550dce3c2068978cc787e`, based on `418bb925ca475c3aafdd06757174cf5779e557fe`: scoped clean through P2, no remaining findings. The [hosted review of this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189975#issuecomment-6552450367) also found no code defects; its missing live evidence is now supplied below.
- **Uninterrupted native Windows 11 ARM64 upgrade passed.** The installed CLI returned exit 0, report status `ok`, with a 3600-second overall CLI budget; reported execution took 2987.319 seconds. All 15 native phases passed. The slowest phase was `upgrade.update-dev` at 3128.865 seconds inside its separate 3870-second harness envelope. No manual source recovery, install, or build completed the update.

prs.title: build(release): stop releases shipping a Codex plugin floor that admits broken plugins
prs.body:
Refs #181619

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a release can ship with a Codex plugin floor (`minimumCompatibleVersion` in `src/plugins/official-runtime-plugins.ts`, #168930) that still admits plugin releases the new core breaks. Nothing checks the floor against the release, so it falls behind silently. #181619 is the result: 2026.10.6 made the Codex execution deadline require `startedAtMonotonicMs`, the floor stayed at `2026.9.7`, and a left-behind `@openclaw/codex` 2026.10.5 loads and fails every turn after 1 ms instead of being refused with the repair command. 2026.10.7 ships the same floor.

## User Impact

User impact: none at runtime. Release tooling only. `release-check` now fails when a version-bound runtime's floor no longer type-checks against the release being cut, and names the fix (raise the floor). Users then get the existing refusal with `openclaw update repair` / `openclaw plugins update codex` guidance instead of silently failing turns.

## Why This Change Was Made

The floor is the existing owner for this (#168930): a hand-kept literal, bumped "when a Plugin SDK subpath used by this runtime is removed". Two kinds of change slipped past it:

- a newly required argument: `startedAtMonotonicMs` (#155801, included in 2026.10.6);
- removed exports: `sanitizeToolArgs` (#169063) and `HEARTBEAT_RESPONSE_TOOL_NAME` (#180106) on main.

The Codex runtime imports these private-local SDK pieces lazily and declares an open-ended `pluginApi`, so a stale floor only shows up as failing turns after an update.

`scripts/check-official-runtime-floor.mts` checks the floor itself: for each version-bound runtime it takes that runtime's source at its floor release tag and type-checks it inside the checkout being released (root `tsconfig.json`, so the core's SDK is read from source). A type error in the old runtime means the floor admits a runtime this release breaks. It catches both removed exports and changed arguments. It reuses the release checkout's install for third-party dependencies.

- `release-check` calls it before packing. It reads the floors from the release checkout (`process.cwd()`), not from the trusted tooling checkout the npm preflight runs from, so each release line is checked against its own floor.
- A floor that is not a released tag is skipped (no published runtime can be older than it).
- A floor above the release version fails, because it would refuse the runtime published with that release.
- Release checkouts are shallow and tagless, so the check fetches only the floor tag.

Also: the floor comment now covers exports and required arguments, and points to the check; `docs/help/testing-updates-plugins.md` describes the step next to `release:check`.

Not changed: the floor values themselves. The stable line needs `2026.10.6` (published plugins 2026.10.6 and 2026.10.7 pass `startedAtMonotonicMs`). Main needs its own value: on packaged builds of main `a3a5add7136` with real model turns, the published plugins I tried fail there: 2026.10.5 and 2026.10.6 import `sanitizeToolArgs` (removed by #169063), and 2026.10.10-beta.3 imports `HEARTBEAT_RESPONSE_TOOL_NAME` (removed by #180106). So main's floor has to be the first `@openclaw/codex` release built after #180106, set when that release is cut; this check will report it then (the main run below shows the same removals).

## Evidence

Unit tests (`test/scripts/check-official-runtime-floor.test.ts`, 9): released floor is checked; unreleased floor is skipped; floor above the release fails; non-version-bound/no-floor/no-source runtimes are ignored; runtime errors are separated from setup errors; a compiler run that fails without diagnostics is a broken check, not a pass; the floors are read from the checked checkout, and a checkout without floors reports none.

End-to-end on real release checkouts (proof bench, Linux), `checkOfficialRuntimeFloors` against each core, 15 to 65 s per run:

| Core checkout | Floor | Result |
|---|---|---|
| v2026.10.7 | 2026.9.7 (as released) | fails: `run-attempt-turn-state.ts(173,65): Property 'startedAtMonotonicMs' is missing` |
| v2026.10.7 | 2026.10.6 | passes |
| v2026.10.10-beta.3 | 2026.9.7 | fails: `startedAtMonotonicMs` missing; no exported member `sanitizeToolArgs` |
| v2026.10.10-beta.3 | 2026.10.10-beta.1 | passes |
| main with this change | 2026.9.7 (as on main) | fails: no exported member `HEARTBEAT_RESPONSE_TOOL_NAME`, `normalizeHeartbeatToolResponse`, `isSilentReplyPayloadText`; heartbeat tool options gone |

### Live run: the check on real release checkouts

Proof bench (Linux, Node 26), output as captured. The v2026.10.7 runs use the npm preflight's shape: this branch's script run directly from a separate tooling checkout (`TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=<tooling>/tsconfig.json node --import <tooling>/scripts/tsx.mjs <tooling>/scripts/check-official-runtime-floor.mts`) with the release checkout as the working directory. The main run is `pnpm check:official-runtime-floor` on this branch.

v2026.10.7 with its released floor (`2026.9.7`), then with the floor raised to `2026.10.6`:

```text
official-runtime-floor:
codex 2026.9.7 no longer type-checks against OpenClaw 2026.10.7; raise its minimumCompatibleVersion in src/plugins/official-runtime-plugins.ts to the first release that does:
  .artifacts/official-runtime-floor/codex/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-turn-state.ts(173,65): error TS2741: Property 'startedAtMonotonicMs' is missing in type '{ startedAtMs: number; timeoutMs: number; settlementTimeoutMs: number; ...
exit=1

official-runtime-floor: codex 2026.10.6 type-checks against OpenClaw 2026.10.7.
exit=0
```

v2026.10.10-beta.3 with floor `2026.9.7`, then `2026.10.10-beta.1`:

```text
official-runtime-floor:
codex 2026.9.7 no longer type-checks against OpenClaw 2026.10.10-beta.3; raise its minimumCompatibleVersion in src/plugins/official-runtime-plugins.ts to the first release that does:
  .artifacts/official-runtime-floor/codex/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-turn-state.ts(173,65): error TS2741: Property 'startedAtMonotonicMs' is missing in type ...
  .artifacts/official-runtime-floor/codex/extensions/codex/src/app-server/tool-progress-normalization.ts(2,3): error TS2724: '"openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime"' has no exported member named 'sanitizeToolArgs'. Did you mean 'sanitizeToolResult'?

official-runtime-floor: codex 2026.10.10-beta.1 type-checks against OpenClaw 2026.10.10-beta.3.
```

main with this change (floor `2026.9.7`), first lines:

```text
codex 2026.9.7 no longer type-checks against OpenClaw 2026.10.7; raise its minimumCompatibleVersion ...:
  .../src/app-server/event-projector-assistant.ts(3,10): error TS2305: Module '"openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-chunking"' has no exported member 'isSilentReplyPayloadText'.
  .../src/app-server/heartbeat-tool-fallback.ts(3,3): error TS2305: Module '"openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime"' has no exported member 'HEARTBEAT_RESPONSE_TOOL_NAME'.
```

Without this change, `release-check` has no such step, so the same checkouts pass it with the stale floor; that is how 2026.10.6 and 2026.10.7 shipped.

Release-workflow shape (trusted tooling from main, working directory = the v2026.10.7 checkout): with the release's floor at 2026.9.7 it fails on `startedAtMonotonicMs`; with the release's floor set to 2026.10.6 and the tooling's floor left at 2026.9.7 it passes, so the floors are read from the release.

Earlier prototype of the same method (old plugin source type-checked against a newer core): plugin 2026.10.5 on 2026.10.6 and 2026.10.7 and plugin 2026.9.6 on 2026.9.7 (#168748's removed `agent-harness-task-runtime`) are flagged; plugin 2026.10.6 on 2026.10.7, 2026.10.4 and 2026.10.3 on 2026.10.5, and matched pairs show no errors.

Live, released npm packages, real model (#181619 comments): core 2026.10.6 + plugin 2026.10.5 fails both turns; `openclaw doctor --fix` refreshes the plugin to 2026.10.6 and both turns answer. The reporter confirmed the same on 2026.10.7: a plain npm upgrade left the plugin at 2026.10.5 with no warning, and `openclaw plugins update codex` fixed it.

Pre-PR lanes on the proof bench, run in parallel: `tsgo:core`, `tsconfig.scripts.json`, type-aware oxlint (4 configs) on the changed files, format check, `lint:docs`, and `test/scripts/check-official-runtime-floor.test.ts`, `test/scripts/release-check.test.ts`, `test/release-check.test.ts`, `test/package-scripts.test.ts`. `pnpm check:changed` itself stalled on its SQLite ratchet step in the bench container (unrelated to this change), so those lanes were run individually.

CI on this head runs every lane because `package.json` changed. The red jobs are outside this change and reproduce on main's code on the bench: `src/gateway/server-methods/session-catalog.test.ts` (1 failed), `extensions/codex/media-understanding-provider.test.ts` (2 failed) and `test/cli-json-stdout.hooks.e2e.test.ts` (1 failed, same "gateway remote mode misconfigured" assertion) fail there too; the Control UI controller guard flags `extensions/workboard/browser/pages/workboard/view-selection.tsx:393` (`querySelector`), from #182020 merged today; `extensions/anthropic/cli-process.test.ts` passes on the bench (24/24) and failed once in CI on an `EPIPE` timing assertion.

Limits: it checks the floor release only, assuming newer plugin releases are at least as compatible; behaviour changes that keep the same types are not caught; it needs network access to fetch the floor tag.

prs.title: fix(openai): let fast voice answers skip acknowledgments
prs.body:
Related: #175603.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway-controlled OpenAI Talk acknowledges every delegated request immediately, even when the answer is ready fast enough to speak directly. Repeated acknowledgments make short conversations feel repetitive and add unnecessary speech before the result.

## User Impact

Work starts immediately. An answer or failure arriving within 1.5 seconds skips filler. Slower requests receive at most one short acknowledgment using the existing caller-language, naturally varied wording from #175603. Wording variation remains model-directed, not guaranteed.

Spoken updates, follow-ups, controls, and call shutdown cancel an unsent acknowledgment. Status, cancellation, final results, and failure delivery retain their existing ownership. No new configuration or client changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Race the existing consult against a short acknowledgment timer in its existing controller. This avoids a separate predictive model call or delaying the actual work. The timer is canceled when the consult settles or its presentation becomes obsolete, and uses the original socket's delivery checks.

The 1.5-second window is an initial UX choice, not a measured latency improvement. An answer arriving just after that window can still follow an acknowledgment already submitted to the provider.

## Evidence

- Baseline regression: 12 failures / 20 passes against the unmodified controller, including the new fast-answer, slow-answer, and cancellation cases failing on its immediate append.
- All 89 focused tests pass across delegation (32), public delegation (8), Gateway bridge and browser session (36 combined), and agent-tool prompt stability (13). Two old consumer expectations of immediate filler were updated and their 40-test subset rerun successfully.
- Changed delegation/public-delegation suites: 25.43 seconds including compilation; 28.19 seconds including runner cleanup. Earlier four-suite voice run: 6.52 seconds with cached compilation. Hosted CI timing pending.
- OpenAI package typecheck, type-aware lint of all four touched TypeScript files, formatting, and whitespace checks pass.
- Independent autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings in the diff. Review was limited to supplied changes; focused execution provides the runtime proof above.
- Graphify AST-only refresh completed for the OpenAI package. Generated graph files are not part of this PR.

No live provider/audio or physical-device acceptance test was run. The running Gateway and native app were not changed.

The simplification pass retains one timer in the existing controller and no new policy owner, queue, config surface, or predictive classifier. Production delta: +30/-2 lines; tests: +113/-17; docs: +5/-2.

prs.title: improve: clarify update settings and recovery actions
prs.body:
Related: #182558

## What Problem This Solves

Update settings mix everyday controls with build details, while failed-update dialogs hide useful recovery actions on a separate page.

## User Impact

A compact status/version/action card is followed by Preferences and a concise latest-attempt summary. View result opens existing progress and recovery; terminal details stay optional. Refresh status, Try again, Report failure and Diagnose stay visible, with Diagnose primary.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the presentation-only slice of #182558. Existing update, retry, diagnostic and report owners retain confirmation, live permissions and attempt identity. Report and Diagnose leave the dialog for their working surface; closing does not cancel the update.

Refresh status does not promise fresh package discovery (#182567). Companion inventory/release indicators (#182568) and separate Mac installation policy (#160530) remain outside this PR. The Apps tab exposes only existing bridge capabilities and accurately labels combined automatic checking/downloading.

The initial screenshots and layout were rejected and have been replaced by the corrected card/detail hierarchy below.

## Evidence

**Current CI caveat (2026-10-25):** [checks-ui (2/3)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40137637341/job/121002713033) is red in the unchanged navigation-rail test: an upstream tooltip-clear precondition fails before Escape is sent. Focused replays of the exact CI merge revision and a local Bun replay of shard 2/3 do not reproduce that failure. The shard has three other local assertion failures, all reproduced on its unmodified main parent. The original hosted failure remains unclassified; a passing replay is not a repair or evidence of green CI.

[Capture setup and limitations](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/735ebfb48fa75af20732f202176475ad4fc31e3f/README.md). Source: `56cce017b066ed3751fab038c68917919ba96264`.

- Final-base production UI typecheck and performance pass; chat startup gzip decreases 77 B, CSS grows 62 B raw / 15 B gzip, with no budget changes.
- Ten affected browser scenarios pass after updating upstream test consumers (nine initial passes plus the corrected dismissal scenario rerun). The frozen pre-rebase candidate also passed 78 focused unit tests and 11 shipped-bundle report/diagnosis browser scenarios.

- Corrected live Gateway captures use credential-free isolated state and show a genuine check error/retained refusal, not a successful installation. Fixture captures do not prove native installation or model-backed diagnosis. Captures precede the nonvisual sidebar simplification and test-only rebase resolution.
- Whole-candidate autoreview helper was interrupted after producing a disproportionate 58-pass plan; no completed helper verdict is claimed. Completed independent source/visual reviews provide separate coverage. Hosted review at `e421d3ed` completed with no actionable code findings; product acceptance remains with the area owner.

- Previously reviewed head `e421d3ed2da336829ace239535d8c3530698965c` integrates upstream’s consolidated settings tests without changing the reviewed production patch. All 35 affected settings tests pass after conflict resolution; the 14 confirmation browser scenarios pass on the unchanged retry code. Production UI typecheck, focused lint/format, assertion-safety and independent native Codex review pass. Earlier visual evidence remains applicable. Hosted checks at `e421d3ed` have no failing or pending checks; later test-only cleanup requires its own current-head reconciliation.

### Real recovery handoff on the reviewed runtime

Shipped Settings → Updates → View result was exercised against an isolated real Gateway. UI assets, backend metadata and the actual WebSocket handshake all identify `e421d3ed2da336829ace239535d8c3530698965c`. The subsequent commit only removes a forwarding-helper echo test; production code is unchanged.

- This uses a synthetic durable failure record, not an actual failed installation. No public failure report was submitted. The isolated Dev-channel status lookup reports unavailable; this is not successful release-discovery or installation proof. Existing CSS budget warnings remain, with the previously measured production delta unchanged.
- Two mounted-page target-retirement tests remain and pass; lint, formatting and diff checks pass. A redundant forwarding-helper echo assertion was removed under the author simplification pass.

### Hosted CI consumer follow-through (25 October)

Current head: `29f0442448f24d4bba0a7bbb2ebe4a9f10e04167`. A stale forced-colors E2E scenario still queried Beta/Stable radio buttons after the Updates channel control became a dropdown. It reproduced before repair (missing Beta radio); the existing scenario now exercises the actual Appearance segmented control in both light and dark forced-color modes. Existing real-Gateway and recovery proof remains applicable; no install, merge or deployment performed.

prs.title: feat: discover Llama.app local models
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Users need Llama.app chat without replacing their managed llama.cpp provider, credentials, or local embeddings.

## User Impact

Adds the independent `llama-app` catalog and inference namespace at port 9931, with optional app-scoped credentials. Existing endpoints, managed processes and defaults remain untouched. Interactive setup, fresh-install preference, branding and desktop qualification are separate drafts. **This remains a partial draft, not qualified end-to-end support.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the shared external-server owner introduced by [the identity refactor](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190000). This existing draft has been narrowed and rebased onto that dependency rather than duplicated. Catalog discovery is passive and scoped; discovered models are not new saved configuration. Registration-order fixtures now select their intended provider by ID.

## Evidence

- Six focused suites: 33 passed, 19 failed, 46.962 seconds wall. The failures include guarded HTTP/SSE fixture access and managed direct-loopback admission. Two representative existing discovery/media failures reproduced on the parent commit without this slice (47.468 seconds wall); no proxy/NO_PROXY or egress override was used. New guarded Llama HTTP tests are **not passing evidence** on this host.
- Plugin production/test closure typecheck, 11-file targeted lint, formatting, generated plugin inventory and whitespace checks passed. Fresh independent P0–P2 autoreview of the complete slice was scoped clean.
- Separate raw upstream HTTP qualification used official `llama serve` b11941 (`19ff817fb25e9a1b838b1d7f9f4325f7bf9779c4`), the runtime pinned by released Llama-macOS 0.46.1, with a small Qwen model. Passive listing, streaming, schema enforcement, a tool replay and disconnect cancellation worked. This is Linux upstream-wire evidence, **not OpenClaw agent or native-app proof**.
- The guarded OpenClaw transport attempt failed before inference with `UND_ERR_SOCKET`; end-to-end setup/chat, incompatible-profile and replaced-endpoint credential rejection traces, stable upgrade preservation, and native Mac/Windows proof remain open. The prior review's security/compatibility qualification requests are not claimed resolved.
- CI seconds unmeasured; broad CI and platform gates remain pending. No readiness, merge, release or protocol/dependency change.

- Exact, separate **261-line** regression allocation is tracked; shared test scalar is unchanged and the allocation check passed. The correction changed no production/test bytes, so prior source reviews and focused proofs remain applicable; prior-head CI is not relabeled as current-head CI.

<details>
<summary>Required per-file wall costs (integrated draft candidate)</summary>

Commands used `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`. CI seconds remain unavailable. These measurements describe the integrated candidate; original per-slice proof is listed above. Wall time includes compiler preparation. Red results remain failures and are not waived or hidden.

| Test file | Wall | Observed result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `extensions/llama-cpp/llama-app.test.ts` | 39.878 s | 4 failed | 2 passed (6) |
| `extensions/llama-cpp/src/media-setup.test.ts` | 9.506 s | 8 failed | 6 passed (14) |
| `extensions/llama-cpp/src/setup.non-interactive.test.ts` | 9.150 s | 10 passed (10) |
| `extensions/llama-cpp/src/external-server/discovery.test.ts` | 36.582 s | 7 failed (7) |

</details>
