prs.title: fix(diagnostics): tool error spans don't say whether a tool failed, was cancelled or timed out
prs.body:
Closes #182541

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an exported tool error span can't tell a failed tool from a cancelled or timed-out one, and a failed Codex command loses its exit code.

## User Impact

User impact: operators reading traces see why a tool call ended (`openclaw.tool.terminal_reason`: `failed`, `cancelled`, `timed_out`, or `other`) and, for a Codex command, its exit code (`openclaw.tool.exit_code`) on the `openclaw.tool.execution` error span. Metric labels are unchanged and no tool output is exported.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `tool.execution.error` event already carries `terminalReason`, and the Codex `commandExecution` item carries `exitCode`, but neither reached the span. The Codex native tool projector now forwards a command item's exit code on the error event (new optional `exitCode` field), and diagnostics-otel copies both values onto the error span only. Plugins can emit this event too, so an unrecognized reason becomes `other` and a non-integer exit code is dropped.

`src/infra/diagnostic-events.ts` is over its line cap, so the tool error event fields move unchanged to a type-only sibling (`diagnostic-tool-error-types.ts`), following the existing `diagnostic-run-types.ts` pattern; `DiagnosticToolTerminalReason` is re-exported from the same place as before.

## Evidence

Two focused regression tests, red on `main` (0a9d5cc49d9) and green with this change:

- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.native-audit.test.ts` › reports a failed command's exit code and terminal reason without its output: a failed `commandExecution` item (exit code 2, with output) yields `tool.execution.error` with `terminalReason: "failed"`, `exitCode: 2`, and no output text.
- `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.tool-error.test.ts` (new, real OTel SDK harness): the finished error span has `openclaw.tool.terminal_reason` and `openclaw.tool.exit_code`; the duration metric's labels do not; an untrusted event with an unknown reason and a non-integer exit code exports `other` and no exit code.

Without the change (tests kept, source reverted): `service.tool-error.test.ts` 2 failed of 2 (`expected undefined to be 'other'`, missing span attributes); `event-projector.native-audit.test.ts` 1 failed, 35 passed. With the change: 2/2 and 36/36 passed, and the existing `service.test.ts` passes 70/70.

- `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main`: typecheck (core, core tests, extensions, extension tests), core lint, formatting, line-cap and the other guards passed. Extension lint timed out preparing boundary artifacts on a loaded machine; rerun directly (`run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json` on the four changed extension files), it passed. The dead-export scan failed on 95 existing unused exports, none in files this PR touches.
- Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`): the new tests take 77 ms, 5 ms and 29 ms. File wall times were dominated by cold transforms on a loaded machine (`service.tool-error.test.ts` 108 s, 94% transform).
- Plugin SDK surface: diagnostic event types reach public SDK exports, so `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:diff` lists this change: `tool.execution.error` gains an optional `exitCode`, and `DiagnosticToolTerminalReason` keeps its definition, now re-exported from the sibling. This may need the API-diff acknowledgement.
- Not checked: a live Codex run exporting to a real collector. The projector and exporter are each proven at their own boundary with synthetic inputs.

prs.title: improve(ui): reset sidebar width from the divider
prs.body:
Closes #172170

## What Problem This Solves

After resizing the desktop sidebar, users must guess its original width; reloads preserve the custom size. Double-click the divider, or focus it and press Enter, to restore and save the canonical default width.

The reset uses the existing navigation preference owner. Dragging, arrow keys, Home/End, collapsed navigation, and mobile drawers retain their behavior. Upstream's tooltip removal is preserved: the separator keeps `Resize sidebar` as its accessible name, with reset guidance in `aria-description`.

## Evidence

Integrated upstream `fc719e9e65af579d08213dc5161b34a02be4608e` in `f6db245799ec4b75ab8547e8631197a03f9f3d0a` with a normal merge, preserving both prior contribution commits. Documentation and browser-test conflicts retain both sides, including upstream scrollbar coverage.

- All 9 sidebar browser scenarios pass, including double-click after viewport resizing, Enter, persisted reloads, resize-state cleanup, LTR/RTL scrollbar isolation, and desktop/mobile navigation. The focused reset scenario took 2.49 s; the browser test phase took 44.43 s.
- All 26 shell/divider owner tests pass. UI and sidebar E2E typechecks, targeted lint/format, i18n verification, controller guard against the integrated base, and diff checks pass. Fresh Codex review through P2 found no actionable defects.
- Release-build comparison passes with Node 24.22.1, Vite 8.3.5, and Pako 3.0.2 on the same host/toolchain. Chat boot gzip: base 1,272,374 B, candidate 1,272,563 B (+189 B), existing cap 1,276,669 B. Both use 20 chat boot JS requests. Startup gzip increases by 29 B; CSS is unchanged. No budget, compressor, measurement, or unrelated production code was changed.
- The previous head's 243 B gate excess is resolved by current upstream integration. The new candidate is also below the former 1,275,713 B cap. No speculative optimization was needed.
- New inspected 1280×800 mock-Gateway screenshots below show 452 px returning to 310 px through double-click; browser tests independently verify keyboard reset and reload persistence. These use synthetic data, not a live Gateway or physical device.

`hk check` is unavailable in this upstream repository (no `hk.pkl`); its supported checks above were run directly. An initial controller check compared against the old merge base and reported upstream debt; the explicit integrated-base comparison passes.

Maintainer product approval for the reset gestures remains required. ClawSweeper's previous review found no actionable correctness issues; neither that review nor this repair constitutes maintainer approval. This PR remains open and is not merged.

## Current screenshots

![Before reset: sidebar widened to 452 px](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/199eb6ae-d212-4102-ae2b-3d6b4359f150)

![After double-click: sidebar restored to 310 px](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/86b5e011-37eb-4df1-baed-6cd59ca927d0)

## Earlier evidence

**Before — resized sidebar at maximum width:**

![Before: the sidebar has a custom 452 pixel width](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8e536781-643b-45f8-ad99-ff78ad998561)

**After — double-click restores the default:**

![After: the sidebar returns to its 310 pixel default](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0211c7e-da53-4bc1-860d-09eff3d2a98b)

The earlier captioned mouse/keyboard comparison recording remains available:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5c51003e-b24b-45b7-8685-87fc15f8a912

prs.title: fix(channels): match canonically equivalent Unicode in directory queries
prs.body:
<details>
<summary>maintainer-edits</summary>

Maintainers may push to this branch to finish or adjust the change; "Allow edits by maintainers" stays enabled. The touched pair is one production file plus its existing test file, so a maintainer can re-point or narrow it without rebasing anything else.

</details>

<details>
<summary>maintainer-options</summary>

- **Land-ready**: comparison-only fix inside the single owner of config-driven directory query matching; shipped-CLI base/head receipt covering both canonical directions plus controls; `+3/-2` production in one file, `+31` in the existing test file, zero new files, zero config/schema/auth/storage surface.
- **Alternatives considered**: (a) patch each channel lister instead — rejected, nine config-driven listers funnel through this one helper and would re-derive the same predicate; (b) rewrite stored config keys to NFC — rejected, that mutates user data and no sibling PR did it; (c) do nothing — rejected, the sibling directory filters already landed this predicate, so the shared helper is the remaining inconsistency.
- **Scope**: `src/channels/plugins/directory-config-helpers.ts` + `src/channels/plugins/directory-config-helpers.test.ts`. No `plugin-sdk` export-list change (`scripts/lib/plugin-sdk-shipped-surface.json` untouched), no lockfile change.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw directory groups list --channel irc --query "<NFD #café>" --json` returns `[]` even though `channels.irc.groups["#café"]` is configured. The config-driven directory filter lowercases both operands and never normalizes Unicode, so a decomposed (NFD) query misses a composed (NFC) key — and the reverse misses too. The same predicate covers every config-driven directory listing: `irc`, `line`, `reef`, `signal`, `telegram`, `zalo`, `zalouser`, plus the config halves of `feishu`, `matrix`, `discord`, `slack` and `msteams`.

Precedent: #187148 (merged, same shape in the feishu/slack/telegram local filters), #188003, #187199, #187611, #189131, #189360. This PR only swaps the point — those siblings never reached the shared helper.

## Why This Change Was Made

`applyDirectoryQueryAndLimit` is the single owner of config-driven directory query matching. It now normalizes both operands to NFC after lowercasing, so composed and decomposed spellings compare equal. Stored ids, returned entries and spelling, `limit`, empty-query behavior and non-matching queries are unchanged. No validator, option, config key, schema, dependency or persistence change; the `plugin-sdk` export list is untouched.

Production LOC is `+3/-2` (one file).

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

An operator who types or pastes `#café` in either Unicode form now gets their configured group back from `directory groups list` instead of an empty list. Same-form queries and non-matching queries behave exactly as before, and accent folding is **not** introduced (`#cafe` still misses `#café`).

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `a9086c35ec2cef06c279155869d157b390b702ef`
- Current-main RED baseline: `87396e72d2474de52693866212c305c0a0ef9f13`
- Production entry: real source CLI `openclaw directory groups list --channel irc --query <text> --json` (argv/command tree identical to the packaged CLI), Node 24.22.1 in a `lexiflow-all` container
- Canonical owner exercised: `applyDirectoryQueryAndLimit` in `src/channels/plugins/directory-config-helpers.ts:20-25`
- Decision surface: `--query` on `directory groups|peers list` for config-driven channels; fixture is a generated `channels.irc.groups` keyed by channel name
- Recorder/readback boundary: JSON envelope (`[]` vs `[{kind,id,name}]`) plus process exit code; fixture strings printed as code points
- Acceptance RED: unchanged baseline returns `[]` for both cross-form directions while both same-form controls return the entry
- Acceptance GREEN: exact head returns the original entry for both cross-form directions; controls byte-identical to base
- Legal controls: composed×composed and UPPERCASE×composed return the entry on both revisions; the unit suite additionally proves no accent folding
- Cleanup: each run used a fresh isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` / `OPENCLAW_HOME` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` under a disposable container `HOME`, deleted after the run. No production Gateway, session, channel, token or user config was touched.

### BEFORE / AFTER

Fixture bytes (verified on both revisions, `distinct: true`): composed `23 63 61 66 e9` · decomposed `23 63 61 66 65 301`.

| Direction | Base `87396e72d24` | Head `a9086c35ec2` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| composed key × decomposed query | `[]` (exit 0) | `[{ "kind":"group", "id":"#café", "name":"#café" }]` (exit 0) |
| decomposed key × composed query | `[]` (exit 0) | same entry (exit 0) |
| composed key × composed query (control) | same entry | same entry |
| composed key × UPPERCASE query (control) | same entry | same entry |

The failure shape is a silently empty result, not a non-zero exit: the CLI succeeds and reports zero matches.

```text
RED  base 87396e72d24 — composed key × decomposed query
$ openclaw directory groups list --channel irc --query '#cafe<e + U+0301>' --json
[]
exit=0
RED  base — decomposed key × composed query
$ openclaw directory groups list --channel irc --query '#café' --json
[]
exit=0
RED  base — control, composed key × composed query
$ openclaw directory groups list --channel irc --query '#café' --json
[ { "kind": "group", "id": "#café", "name": "#café" } ]
exit=0
```

```text
GREEN head a9086c35ec2 — composed key × decomposed query
[ { "kind": "group", "id": "#café", "name": "#café" } ]   exit=0
GREEN head — decomposed key × composed query
[ { "kind": "group", "id": "#café", "name": "#café" } ]   exit=0
GREEN head — controls (composed x composed, UPPERCASE x composed)
[ { "kind": "group", "id": "#café", "name": "#café" } ]   exit=0   (both, byte-identical to base)
```

No empty-argv token is involved in this change.

Unit receipt on the same two trees (Node 24.22.1, `--maxWorkers=1`):

```text
RED  Tests  2 failed | 7 passed (9)   exit 1
     AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [{ kind: 'group', id: '#café' }]
     src/channels/plugins/directory-config-helpers.test.ts:79
GREEN Tests  9 passed (9)             exit 0
```

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/channels/plugins/directory-config-helpers.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — RED `2 failed | 7 passed` (exit 1); GREEN `9 passed` (exit 0)
- sibling `src/channels/plugins/directory-adapters.test.ts` — `4 passed`; sibling `extensions/feishu/src/directory.test.ts` — `29 passed`
- `oxfmt --check <the two files>` — "All matched files use the correct format" (exit 0)
- `oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json <the two files>` — `0 warnings, 0 errors`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` — 8 errors on the **pristine baseline and on head, sorted lists byte-identical (`diff` empty)**: all 8 are tree-local dependency drift (`@openclaw/fs-safe@0.26.13` installed vs `0.27.0` required by `pnpm-lock.yaml` at base, plus missing `@noble/hashes`). Zero errors in either touched file.
- `check:test-lines-ratchet` (same algorithm) — total `6,361,886` vs ceiling `6,382,193` (baseline `6,319,970` + allocations `62,223`) → slack `20,307`; `+17` test lines, no new allocation needed.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- Not tested: full repository suites (only the touched file plus its two directory siblings ran); per-channel live network directory lookups for slack/discord/mattermost/telegram (they inherit this predicate but were not re-proven against their servers); macOS/Windows hosts; a fully installed `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` typecheck — blocked by the tree-local drift above, so the baseline-diff method is used instead.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+3/-2` · Test LOC: `+31/-0` · Files: 2 · New files: 0
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/string-coerce` plus `String.prototype.normalize`; no new helper, validator, option, dependency or export.
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: **none** — comparison-time only, no stored value rewritten, no lockfile change.

### Compatibility note (`merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility`)

Written for the review label; the API surface and its contract are untouched:

- `applyDirectoryQueryAndLimit` ships through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/directory-runtime`, and this changes **matching behavior only**: signatures, export list, ordering, `limit`, and returned identifier bytes are unchanged. The shipped-surface gate (`plugin-sdk:surface-report --check`) fails only on removals/budgets and the export list is identical; `check-source-contracts` is green on this head.
- On composed (NFC) stored keys — the common case — the change is **pure widening**: every query that matched on base still matches (enumerated over all raw substrings of six composed keys: 0 losses), and canonically equivalent queries in the other form now hit; same-form controls return byte-identical entries.
- Accepted edge case: a raw fragment that stops before a combining mark (e.g. `cafe` typed against a key stored decomposed) previously matched **only because that key happened to be NFD**; it now behaves exactly like a composed key always did. Verified for every raw-substring fragment of decomposed keys: `base(NFC form of the key, q) ≡ head(NFD key, q)`, 0 exceptions. Any form of the full name matches on both key forms.
- Precedent: the identical two-sided `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(...).normalize("NFC")` idiom already merged in `extensions/feishu/src/directory.ts:45`, `extensions/whatsapp/src/directory-config.ts:92`, `extensions/slack/src/directory-live.ts:82`, `extensions/matrix/src/directory-live.ts:146`, and `src/cron/service/ops-read.ts:208`.

### Impact surface

| File:line | Change | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/channels/plugins/directory-config-helpers.ts:21` | query operand normalized to NFC | comparison-only; widens to canonical equivalents only, never to different text |
| `src/channels/plugins/directory-config-helpers.ts:25` | id operand normalized to NFC | same; returned id bytes unchanged |
| `src/channels/plugins/directory-config-helpers.test.ts:64-93` | 2 direction cases + 3 controls | test-only |

Consumer fan-out: `listDirectoryEntriesFromSources` → the config listers of `irc`/`line`/`reef`/`signal`/`telegram`/`zalo`/`zalouser` and the config halves of `feishu`/`matrix`/`discord`/`slack`/`msteams`; also re-exported as `openclaw/plugin-sdk/directory-runtime`.

Proof recorded 2026-11-01 (UTC).

prs.title: perf(control-ui): overlap Sessions and Cron route readiness
prs.body:
First visits to Sessions and Cron serialize route JavaScript behind stylesheet loading. Cron also waits for the page module before starting its inventory read. At 100 ms RTT, these waits delay usable content.

This change adds Sessions and Cron to the existing parallel stylesheet-preload policy, shares their document CSS without pulling page chrome into style-only consumers, and groups Cron modules that already load together. Default Cron navigation starts the existing scoped inventory read while the lazy page module loads; the page joins that read and retains visible loading, errors, and retries. Shared defaults and query construction keep both callers on the same query. Filtered/deep-linked visits and Gateways without inventory support retain their page-owned read.

Route imports remain lazy. The measured static startup and Chat/New boot asset sets exclude Cron domain/page chunks; later interactions can still load them. Agents retains the optional Cron page/pagination boundary. There is no new scheduler, cache, or state owner.

## Measured result

Accepted as a scoped net win after two same-head cohorts: **360 captures, twenty observations per base/control/head in each of six cells**, using both B/C/H and B/H/C orders. Base/control: `edc86dd18f36a84126ced2ea35d3f9be61ec1615`; candidate: `752741cbee5cf4f77b6c516065676deabb9769e6`. The synthetic production-renderer workload covers cold Chat, New Session, and warm reload/switch/stream/typing on localhost and at 100 ms RTT. It does not measure real Gateway/provider latency.

Both cohorts passed native correctness and transcript-witness validation. Independent recomputation checked 624,096 numeric/null fields without mismatch. No historical-head observations were pooled. Values below are median / nearest-rank p95 milliseconds; paired H/C is the median of within-triplet percentage changes, not a ratio of marginal medians.

| Route/workload | Base | A/A control | Head | Paired H/C | H/C arm-p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Cold Sessions, 100 ms RTT | 803.70 / 814.60 | 805.10 / 813.40 | 687.50 / 695.70 | −14.26% | −14.47% |
| Cold Cron, 100 ms RTT | 796.45 / 804.60 | 793.70 / 806.00 | 618.20 / 628.90 | −22.19% | −21.97% |
| Warm Sessions, 100 ms RTT | 805.55 / 810.00 | 803.50 / 810.60 | 688.25 / 695.50 | −14.24% | −14.20% |
| Cold Cron, localhost | 106.65 / 122.50 | 102.75 / 121.40 | 93.55 / 104.40 | −11.95% | −14.00% |

Remote Sessions H/C is −14.43% / −14.17% across cohorts A/B, Cron −22.14% / −22.70%, and warm Sessions −14.06% / −14.41%. The primary gains survive both orderings. Captured interval requests fall 37→36 for Sessions, 30→27 for Cron, and 45→44 for Settings; encoded bytes fall 88,141→87,872 B, 92,147→90,692 B, and 186,623→186,316 B. These are interval counts, distinct from boot assets below. Application RPC counts/response bytes are unchanged on this exact pair.

## Acceptance limits

This is **not an all-metrics-clean result**. One-minute host load ranged 5.63–25.93, so acceptance uses the predeclared twenty-pair CPU/work fallback alongside A/A and both orderings. Every complete task/thread paired median stays within +5%; the strong route gains and reduced requests support the scoped result. No confirmed >20% affected CPU regression or added workload was found.

| Adverse observation retained | Result and context |
| --- | --- |
| Warm-local Sessions script CPU | H/C +5.37% paired, p95 +8.11%; H/B +2.77%, A/A −1.64%. B/C/H median/p95: 68.921/79.552, 68.712/74.840, 72.160/80.908 ms. Positive direction occurs in both batches and both orders; it is not dismissed as one outlier. |
| Same interval, total work | Task H/C +3.87%, p95 +3.28%; thread +3.87%, p95 +3.15%. TaskOther +7.68%, p95 +10.67%, is already part of that total. The approximately 856 ms CPU window includes about 750 ms after readiness, so it does not isolate pre-ready work. |
| Cold-local Settings | Script H/C +3.19% paired, p95 +15.30%; task +2.31%, p95 +2.56%. Boot/New task tails also increase. |
| Warm-local typing | Per-run input-delay p95 H/C +22.90%, arm-p95 +17.09%; H/B +1.11%, A/A −11.41%. Input-to-next-frame median H/C +10.84%, H/B +5.59%. |
| Warm-remote typing | Per-run input-delay p95 H/C +6.96%, H/B +2.38%, A/A −11.86%; forward/reverse H/C +17.09%/−16.93%. |
| Cold-local / New-local composer tails | Enabled-composer arm-p95 H/C +50.44%/+54.28%. All first exposures and later observations remain included. |

Whole-stream task H/C is −0.09%/+0.24% locally/remotely and script +0.28%/+1.16%. The listed wall/typing tails remain inconclusive on this host; CPU stability is not a claim that every keystroke tail improved. The source changes fetch ordering and shared CSS placement, not Sessions application logic; precise attribution of its small script increase is unresolved.

The harness gives base/control the same server-root cache and head a different root; clearing the browser cache does not clear that server cache. This limits cold first-exposure comparisons, without quantifying the delay or justifying sample removal. Warm arms prime every role, so this explanation is not applied to warm typing. All batch/order and first/later strata were retained.

All 120 warm runs deliver 645 ordered deltas and writes, one pane render, zero rail observations, matching final normalized HTML, growing extent, and a pinned tail. Local runs retain all 43 typed characters; remote runs retain their actual 43/44 characters without per-key normalization. Warm-local saved native paint is null in all sixty runs, not zero milliseconds. Remote saved/live paint exists in all sixty runs and has 0% paired H/C median movement. Local live paint H/C is +1.25% paired, p95 +1.22%. Warm-remote CLS remains about 0.190 in all arms; this change does not fix that shift.

## Proof

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| UI typecheck | Passed |
| Directly changed inventory, chunking, Vite tests, once each, one worker | 71 passed (19 + 9 + 43) |
| Formatting and exact-base test-lines guard | Passed |
| Production Knip | Passed |

prs.title: fix(exec-policy): keep tools.exec.mode auto when set leaves its policy unchanged
prs.body:
## Summary
`openclaw exec-policy set` silently turns `tools.exec.mode: "auto"` into `"ask"` whenever it touches `--security` or `--ask`, even when the requested values are exactly what `auto` already resolves to (`allowlist` / `on-miss`). `openclaw exec-policy set --ask on-miss`, `openclaw exec-policy set --security allowlist`, and `openclaw exec-policy preset cautious` all do it. The command prints "Synchronized local exec policy." and nothing mentions the mode change, but the native auto-reviewer is now off: every allowlist miss needs a human approval, headless hosts with `askFallback: deny` start denying commands the reviewer would have allowed, and Codex app-server sessions lose the Guardian `auto_review` mapping.

## Root cause
`src/cli/exec-policy-cli.ts`, `applyConfigExecPolicy`:

```ts
// before
const currentPolicy = resolveExecModePolicy({ mode: normalizeExecMode(root.tools.exec.mode), ... });
const security = policy.security ?? currentPolicy.security;
const ask = policy.ask ?? currentPolicy.ask;
const mode = resolveExactExecModeFromPolicy({ security, ask });
```

`resolveExecPolicyForMode("auto")` is `{ security: "allowlist", ask: "on-miss", autoReview: true }`. The write keeps only `security` and `ask`, then projects them back through `resolveExactExecModeFromPolicy`, which maps `allowlist` / `on-miss` to `"ask"` and can never return `"auto"`. So `autoReview` is dropped on every security/ask write from an `auto` config.

## Fix
```ts
// after
const mode =
  currentPolicy.autoReview && security === currentPolicy.security && ask === currentPolicy.ask
    ? currentPolicy.mode
    : resolveExactExecModeFromPolicy({ security, ask });
```

When the current mode carries the auto-reviewer and the resulting pair is unchanged, the current mode is kept. Any real change still goes through the existing projection (for example `auto` + `--ask off` becomes `allowlist`, `auto` + `--ask always` becomes explicit `security`/`ask`).

## Why this is the right boundary
`applyConfigExecPolicy` is the single writer of `tools.exec` for both `exec-policy set` and `exec-policy preset`; both go through it, so one change covers both. The exec-approvals defaults written alongside (`applyApprovalsDefaults`) store only security/ask/askFallback and are unchanged. Doctor's migration (`legacy-config-migrations.runtime.tier-eval.ts`) only projects legacy `security`/`ask` pairs that never had a mode, so it has no `auto` to preserve. The existing "retains untouched policy" contract in `exec-policy-cli.test.ts` is extended rather than changed, and `docs/cli/approvals.md` now states the behavior.

## Verification
- Added two cases to the existing `retains untouched policy when setting ask=$ask` table in `src/cli/exec-policy-cli.test.ts`: `auto` + `--ask on-miss` stays `{ mode: "auto" }` (fails on main with `{ mode: "ask" }`), and `auto` + `--ask off` becomes `{ mode: "allowlist" }`.
- Local gates left to GitHub Actions.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: `openclaw exec-policy set --ask on-miss` on a config with `tools.exec.mode: "auto"` rewrote the mode to `ask`, silently disabling the auto-reviewer.
Real environment tested: upgrade from the published stable release to this patch on macOS, Node 26.9.0. Stable `openclaw@2026.9.9` (bcfc888, installed with `npm i -g openclaw@2026.9.9 --prefix <scratch>`) created the state; the candidate is the real `openclaw` CLI built from this branch (head c52094f3e7e, `node scripts/run-node.mjs` full dist build, then `node openclaw.mjs`). The contrast run uses the same build with `src/cli/exec-policy-cli.ts` reverted to pristine main 168651f715b. HOME, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR and OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH point at a scratch directory (fake values only), no Gateway is running, so every command uses its real local owner path, the real `openclaw.json`, and the real SQLite approvals store. Nothing was stubbed.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: with v2026.9.9: `openclaw config set tools.exec.mode auto`, `openclaw config set logging.level debug`, `openclaw config set gateway.port 28791`, `openclaw approvals allowlist add --agent main "/usr/bin/git"`, `openclaw approvals allowlist add --agent "*" "/usr/bin/uname"`; then with the candidate on the same state: `openclaw exec-policy set --ask on-miss`, followed by `openclaw config get tools.exec`, `config get logging.level`, `config get gateway.port`, and `openclaw approvals get --json` (filtered with jq to the stored defaults, allowlist patterns and effective mode).
Evidence after fix:
```
# Upgrade, candidate = this patch (c52094f3e7e)
$ openclaw config get tools.exec   # v2026.9.9, before upgrade
{
  "mode": "auto"
}
$ openclaw config get logging.level
debug
$ openclaw config get gateway.port
28791
$ openclaw approvals get --json | jq '{defaults: .file.defaults, allowlist: (.file.agents | map_values([.allowlist[].pattern])), mode: .effectivePolicy.scopes[0].mode}'
{"defaults":{},"allowlist":{"main":["/usr/bin/git"],"*":["/usr/bin/uname"]},"mode":{"requested":"auto","requestedSource":"tools.exec.mode","effective":"auto","note":"requested mode applies"}}

$ openclaw exec-policy set --ask on-miss   # candidate c52094f
Synchronized local exec policy.

$ openclaw config get tools.exec   # candidate c52094f, after edit
{
  "mode": "auto"
}
$ openclaw config get logging.level
debug
$ openclaw config get gateway.port
28791
$ openclaw approvals get --json | jq '{defaults: .file.defaults, allowlist: (.file.agents | map_values([.allowlist[].pattern])), mode: .effectivePolicy.scopes[0].mode}'
{"defaults":{"ask":"on-miss"},"allowlist":{"main":["/usr/bin/git"],"*":["/usr/bin/uname"]},"mode":{"requested":"auto","requestedSource":"tools.exec.mode","effective":"auto","note":"requested mode applies"}}

# Same upgrade, candidate = pristine main 168651f715b exec-policy-cli.ts (v2026.9.9 state seeded identically, read back as above)
$ openclaw exec-policy set --ask on-miss   # pristine main candidate
Synchronized local exec policy.

$ openclaw config get tools.exec   # pristine main candidate, after edit
{
  "mode": "ask"
}
$ openclaw config get logging.level
debug
$ openclaw config get gateway.port
28791
$ openclaw approvals get --json | jq '{defaults: .file.defaults, allowlist: (.file.agents | map_values([.allowlist[].pattern])), mode: .effectivePolicy.scopes[0].mode}'
{"defaults":{"ask":"on-miss"},"allowlist":{"main":["/usr/bin/git"],"*":["/usr/bin/uname"]},"mode":{"requested":"ask","requestedSource":"tools.exec.mode","effective":"ask","note":"requested mode applies"}}
```
Observed result after fix: after upgrading v2026.9.9 state to this patch, the unchanged-policy edit keeps `tools.exec.mode` at `auto` (effective mode `auto`), and the unrelated settings (`logging.level`, `gateway.port`) and both stored allowlist entries are intact; on pristine main the same upgrade path flips the mode to `ask`.
What was not tested: no live exec run through the auto-reviewer with a model provider; no Gateway-owned path (exec-policy refuses a foreign owner and writes through the local owner); rolling back to v2026.9.9 afterwards is refused by main's existing state database schema 20 migration, independent of this change; `preset cautious` was covered by reading the shared writer rather than a separate run.

### Fresh-state runs (real CLI, seeded `{ "tools": { "exec": { "mode": "auto" } } }`)
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 168651f715b)
$ cat openclaw.json
{
  "tools": { "exec": { "mode": "auto" } }
}
$ openclaw exec-policy set --ask on-miss
Synchronized local exec policy.
$ openclaw config get tools.exec
{
  "mode": "ask"
}

# AFTER (this branch, identical inputs)
$ cat openclaw.json
{
  "tools": { "exec": { "mode": "auto" } }
}
$ openclaw exec-policy set --ask on-miss
Synchronized local exec policy.
$ openclaw config get tools.exec
{
  "mode": "auto"
}
```

Additional runs on this branch, fresh `auto` config each:
```
$ openclaw exec-policy set --security allowlist
Synchronized local exec policy.
$ openclaw config get tools.exec
{
  "mode": "auto"
}

$ openclaw exec-policy set --ask always
Synchronized local exec policy.
$ openclaw config get tools.exec
{
  "security": "allowlist",
  "ask": "always"
}
```
A real policy change (`--ask always`) still leaves `auto` as before.

prs.title: fix(exec-policy): preserve auto mode for unchanged policy
prs.body:
Supersedes #168178, thanks @yetval.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes automatic command review being silently disabled when `exec-policy set` reapplies the current security or ask value.

## User Impact

Users who selected `tools.exec.mode=auto` retain it when the resulting security/ask policy is unchanged, including the shared cautious preset path. No new options or migration are required.

Security: this preserves existing operator intent only. A real security/ask policy change uses exactly the previous conversion, including deny and always-ask behavior; it does not broaden exec permissions or bypass ownership, approvals, or config-write guards.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing local writer reconstructs a mode from security/ask, which cannot distinguish automatic review from ask-on-miss. Preserve auto only when both resulting values match the current policy.

Production LOC is net zero (+8/-8): removed the redundant missing-file fallback and version reassignment because the approvals snapshot owner always supplies a version-1 file, including missing or malformed storage. Tests add 15 lines; the separate 15-line allocation covers this regression table without changing the shared baseline.

## Evidence

- Base: current main `e7fdb9b177010a71531ed0c09e782fa311f32574`; later main changes do not touch this writer. With only the new tests applied, `pnpm test src/cli/exec-policy-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` fails four cases: ask-only, security-only, both unchanged values, and cautious preset all save `ask` instead of `auto`. The four real-change controls pass on the base.
- Fixed head `1848e6c45be477621e6d22160d41c07ab122991d`: all 35 focused CLI tests pass (35.73s command wall time, 33.78s Vitest including cold worker compilation; test bodies under 1s). Controls cover ask-off, always-ask, deny, and full policy changes.
- Isolated process proof through the repository local-state-owner CLI fixture, real configuration writer and SQLite approvals store: `exec-policy set --ask on-miss --json` persists/reports `ask` on main and `auto` after the fix. Following with `--ask always` removes auto and persists `{security:"allowlist",ask:"always"}`. An unrelated logging setting survives.
- Focused typecheck (the two changed TypeScript files plus repository ambient declarations), targeted lint, changed-file format check, and `git diff --check` pass. All planned [PR CI jobs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41268274249) passed on that exact head (515s total workflow wall time), and [Security Review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41268869491) passed. Broad proof ran in PR CI.
- Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) reviewed the complete local diff against `e7fdb9b177010a71531ed0c09e782fa311f32574`: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. It assessed the supplied diff/contracts; unchanged-source inspection and execution were performed separately by the implementing lane.

Contributor code was read with `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff` only and was never checked out or run. This is an independent replacement credited with `Co-authored-by: yetval <yetvald@gmail.com>`.

Limitations: the full development CLI refused before command execution because its runtime-publication preflight could not inspect the production service environment; that safeguard was left intact. Persistence proof therefore uses the repository CLI process fixture. No live model execution, stable-version upgrade, or Team Gateway changes were performed.

prs.title: fix: worker transfer accepts untrusted TLS certificates when the gateway fingerprint is blank
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a TLS authentication mismatch in the shared node-worker transfer HTTP helper. When `tlsFingerprint` is whitespace-only, the existing code treats the raw string as truthy and sets `rejectUnauthorized: false`, but the pin verifier skips the empty value after trimming. This leaves the transfer helper without CA validation or an enforced pin.

This PR hardens the **shared HTTP helper**. It does **not** establish that the usual shipped CLI/worker connection path allows a whitespace fingerprint through its upstream validation, or that a production interception has been demonstrated. The reachability question remains tracked in #167094.

## User Impact and Scope

For a caller that reaches this helper with a blank or whitespace-only fingerprint, the patch restores ordinary TLS certificate-chain validation instead of silently skipping peer authentication. Valid pins continue to use exact fingerprint verification; malformed non-blank pins fail before a request socket is created.

**Security scope:** This is defense-in-depth for a confirmed helper-level defect. The original report's end-to-end production exposure is not yet proven. No user action is required for the helper fix itself.

## Why This Change Was Made

`withNodeWorkerTransferHttpRequest` previously enabled pin mode on raw fingerprint truthiness, while `waitForTlsPin` returned without verification on trimmed blank input.

The helper now normalizes once with the shared `normalizeTlsFingerprint`:
- A valid normalized fingerprint is required before disabling CA validation for explicit pin mode.
- Empty/whitespace inputs use ordinary CA validation.
- Non-blank invalid fingerprints fail fast with `invalid-tls-fingerprint` before opening a socket.

`waitForTlsPin` retains its own normalization and receives the normalized value.

Related: #167094.

## Evidence Already Available

The new `src/node-host/node-worker-transfer-http.test.ts` exercises the helper against a real self-signed HTTPS endpoint in-process:
- Valid certificate fingerprint → HTTP 200, with the pin verified.
- Whitespace-only fingerprint → certificate-trust rejection. With the implementation reverted, this test reportedly reproduces the bug (the untrusted request succeeds).
- Non-blank malformed fingerprint → `invalid-tls-fingerprint` without connecting.

Contributor-reported local checks:
- `pnpm test src/node-host/node-worker-transfer-http.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 3 passed.
- Neighboring node-worker transfer suites: 22 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pnpm tsgo:prod`, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, oxlint and oxfmt: clean.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: only the existing `OPENCLAW_*` environment-variable budget failure (456 vs. 455), reportedly reproduced on pristine main.

**Evidence limit:** These tests exercise the shared HTTP owner under Vitest, not a shipped node-worker transfer entry point. They do not yet demonstrate final effects on bearer credentials or transfer-body bytes at the authenticated production HTTP boundary.

## Before Merge — Security Boundary Evidence Needed

- [ ] Run a shipped node-worker transfer entry point with a known-valid fingerprint against an accepted TLS peer; provide **redacted** terminal output showing successful transfer.
- [ ] Exercise an untrusted or wrong-pin TLS peer at the transfer HTTP boundary and show that the peer receives **neither bearer authorization credentials nor transfer-body bytes**.
- [ ] Exercise a blank/whitespace fingerprint through the production owner boundary and capture CA rejection (or document precisely which upstream shipped validator makes that input unreachable).
- [ ] Record the test setup and relevant latest stable-release behavior, and attach sanitized evidence here. Redact tokens, hostnames, IPs, keys, phone numbers, and non-public endpoints.

No shipped-entry-point results or final-effect proof are claimed in this description. ClawSweeper review requested the above before merge; a new review should only be requested after the evidence is attached.

prs.body:
Supersedes #168533, thanks @avelev99.
Related: #167094.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes worker workspace transfers accepting an untrusted HTTPS peer when the gateway certificate fingerprint contains only whitespace.

## User Impact

Blank fingerprints now use standard CA verification; explicit correct pins still accept self-signed peers, and wrong pins reject them before sending credentials or workspace bytes. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Normalize with the existing shared fingerprint helper before choosing TLS pin mode. Move malformed-pin rejection to request creation and remove duplicate normalization from the socket verifier. Production delta: -2 lines; regression tests: +19 lines, with an exact separate test-line allocation for download/upload TLS admission coverage.

Security review: the previous raw-string truthiness check disabled CA validation for whitespace while the verifier skipped trimmed blanks. Only a normalized SHA-256 pin now disables CA validation, and that pin is verified before HTTP transmission. HTTP behavior, pooled-socket pin verification, and proxy routing are preserved. Upstream CLI/WebSocket and worker-endpoint validators also reject malformed pins; this is hardening of the shared transfer owner, not a claim of a demonstrated CLI interception.

## Evidence

- Baseline `d1b6e3010097ca5130bd630beba99ed9d7fc5e75`: focused regression run failed exactly the whitespace download and upload cases because both transfers completed against a self-signed HTTPS peer; the other eight admission cases passed.
- Fixed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/node-host/node-worker-transfer-client.test.ts src/node-host/node-worker-bundle-installer.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 67 passed, 1 platform skip; 35.56 seconds wall time including a cold worker compilation, about 1 second executing tests. - The real `runNodeWorkerWorkspaceTransfer` download/upload paths reject undefined, empty, whitespace, wrong, and malformed pins with zero decrypted HTTP bytes and zero HTTP requests received by the rejected peer. Existing correct-pin tests complete downloads and uploads, including pooled and replacement sockets and managed proxies. The shared self-signed certificate is expired, so CA-mode assertions accept either self-signed or expiration rejection.
- Targeted typecheck of the changed source/test import closure, targeted Oxlint, formatting, test-line allocation check, and `git diff --check` passed.

prs.title: fix(discord): render edited message content like sends
prs.body:
## Summary
The Discord `edit` message action (the agent message tool's `action: "edit"` and `openclaw message edit --channel discord`) sends the new text to Discord verbatim, while a `send` of the same text goes through the Discord outbound renderer. So an edited message renders differently from the message it replaces:

- Markdown tables stay raw pipe text instead of the configured `markdown.tables` mode (Discord default: fenced `code` block), because Discord does not render Markdown tables.
- CommonMark `__bold__` reaches Discord unchanged, where `__x__` means underline. Sends normalize it to `**x**`.
- `channels.discord.mentionAliases` handles (`@alice`) stay plain text instead of becoming `<@id>` mentions.

An agent that sends a status table and later edits it with updated values ends up with a broken raw table in the channel.

## Root cause
`extensions/discord/src/actions/runtime.messaging.messages.ts` reads the agent text and hands it straight to `editMessageDiscord`, which PATCHes it as `content`:

```ts
// before
const content = snapshot
  ? (buildDiscordTextChunks(/* retained progress compositor text */)[0] ?? "")
  : readStringParam(ctx.params, "content", {
      required: true,
      allowEmpty: true,
      trim: false,
    });
```

Both send transports (`sendMessageDiscord` in `send.outbound.ts` and `sendWebhookMessageDiscord` in `send.webhook.ts`) run text through `prepareDiscordOutboundText`, which applies `renderDiscordMarkdown` (table mode plus CommonMark bold normalization) and `rewriteDiscordKnownMentions`. The edit branch never called it.

## Fix
The agent-authored edit branch now uses the same renderer, with the same account resolution the send path uses:

```ts
// after
: prepareDiscordOutboundText(
    readStringParam(ctx.params, "content", {
      required: true,
      allowEmpty: true,
      trim: false,
    }),
    {
      cfg: ctx.cfg,
      account: resolveDiscordAccount({ cfg: ctx.cfg, accountId: ctx.accountId }),
    },
  ).textWithMentions;
```

## Why this is the right boundary
`prepareDiscordOutboundText` is already the single owner of "agent Markdown to Discord wire text" for both send transports, so the edit action reuses it instead of growing a second renderer. The fix sits in the agent-authored edit branch rather than inside `editMessageDiscord` because the other branch of the same action (retained progress edits from `progressSnapshot`) already carries Discord-ready compositor text that was chunked to the account limit and is sent with `allowed_mentions: { parse: [] }`; rendering it again could change its length and turn inert handles into mention chips. That branch is untouched. Plain text without tables, `__` spans, or known `@` handles is returned unchanged, so existing edits such as `"  Changed caption\n"` and `""` keep their exact bodies (covered by the existing body-preservation cases).

Slack (`normalizeSlackOutboundText` in its edit path) and Telegram (`renderTelegramHtmlText` in `send-edit.ts`) already render edits the same way they render sends; Discord was the outlier.

prs.title: fix: GitHub identity setup failures report no cause in Gateway logs
prs.body:
Closes #181165

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: GitHub identity setup recordings contain no cause in the Gateway log when `tools.github.configure` fails; the operator sees only a generic `GitHub identity setup failed` error.

## User Impact

Operators can read the actual failure cause from the Gateway log (for example a missing `gh` CLI, an expired one-use setup handoff, or a store error) instead of reproducing the failure and guessing across the several fallible setup steps covered by the single try block.

## Why This Change Was Made

The handler's catch block discarded the caught error completely, so nothing about the failure reached anywhere. This change binds the error and logs it using the established gateway logging convention (`logWarn` + `formatErrorMessage`, matching the sibling `mcp-app.ts` catch paths) before responding with the unchanged generic error. There is no behavior change: same error code, same message, same response shape.

## Evidence

- Before (observed in production logs): 10 failed `tools.github.configure` calls on 2026.10.5 (Gateway journal, 2026-10-22 01:44–02:00 UTC), each logging only the `res ✗ … errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage="GitHub identity setup failed"` response envelope, with no cause-bearing log line anywhere near them. Method and context: #181165 (full journal slices inspected, not just grep hits).
- Regression test (per the review's next-step ask), run locally on this change: `src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.test.ts` — *"logs the unavailable-handoff cause while retaining the generic response"* — handoff consumption throws; the test asserts `logWarn` carries the thrown cause (`tools-github: GitHub identity setup failed: setup handoff expired before use`) while `respond` keeps the byte-identical generic UNAVAILABLE error shape. **Red on the base** (fix stashed): `1 failed | 12 passed` — only the new test fails, at the `logWarn` expectation. **Green with the fix**: 13/13 (`pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/tools-github.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, vitest 5.0.3 on Node v24.22.1).
- Runtime note, stated plainly: local runs used Node v24.22.1 (sha256-verified from `nodejs.org/dist/v24.22.1/SHASUMS256.txt`); this host does not have the pinned OpenClaw Bun fork, so vitest fell back to Node (printed by the harness). PR CI runs the standard lane.
- Scope check: 2 files changed, 32 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-) — production: `catch (error)` binding, one `logWarn` line, two convention imports (+4/−1 vs base); the rest is the regression test and its spy setup.
- Known upstream-main statuses observed while running the local check graph (all empty-diff, none from this change): the max-lines suppression ratchet reports three `ui/` files (`ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts`, `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts`) that are identical to base `d5ce64b7` — inherited `main` state, zero hunks from this patch.

prs.title: fix(telegram): drop native commands from DM senders dmPolicy does not admit
prs.body:
Closes #181955

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: with `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`, a stranger's ordinary DM is dropped silently, but their builtin native command (`/think`, `/login`, ...) gets the reply `You are not authorized to use this command.` — confirming to an unknown sender that a bot is listening. Scoped direct-chat allowlists could still reach an earlier refusal even after the first repair.

## User Impact
Unadmitted DM senders, including senders excluded by a scoped direct-chat allowlist, are now ignored for native commands exactly as they are for ordinary messages. Senders admitted by dmPolicy but denied by `commands.allowFrom` keep the deliberate refusal; explicit command grants, owners, and group-command behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made
Native dispatch has more than one visible authorization-refusal boundary. A scoped direct `allowFrom` rejection happens during base-access evaluation, before final command authorization, so a final-only silence check left that path visible. The shared refusal path now applies the same DM-admission decision at every visible boundary. The final gate uses the latest owner result, while earlier boundaries preserve their existing explicit-grant and scoped-restriction semantics.

## Evidence
- Registered Bot pipeline with an owned loopback Bot API fixture: on the previous head, scoped-direct `/think` still produced the refusal (base-red). After the repair, account-level and scoped excluded senders produce no outbound reply and start no turn. An admitted command-denied sender still receives the refusal, an explicitly authorized sender retains the `/think` argument menu, and the existing group refusal regression stays green.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` against `bot-native-command-dispatch.routing.test.ts`, `.delivery.test.ts`, and `.concurrency.test.ts`: 38/38 passed. `bot-native-commands.registry.test.ts`: 8/8 passed, including `requireAuth:false` plugin commands. Node 24.22.1.
- Both extension production and extension-test tsgo lanes passed. Targeted extension lint completed with 0 warnings/errors across 292 rules, oxfmt passed, the SQLite worker ratchet passed against the PR merge base, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Broader local coverage is not claimed green: `pnpm test:extension telegram` timed out after 30 minutes with the first 11 files passing and no observed test failure; it did not finish. The full changed-check also reports existing dead-export findings outside this diff.
- Live Telegram Test Server proof was not run: the standalone doctor found no authenticated Convex launcher or broker environment pair, so no live trace or live cleanup is claimed. Independent `autoreview` produced no verdict because Codex returned HTTP 403.

prs.title: fix(telegram): ignore native commands from senders the DM policy rejects
prs.body:
Closes #181955

## What Problem This Solves

With `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`, a normal message from a sender who is not on the list is dropped. The same sender's native command (`/status` and the rest of the menu) got the reply "You are not authorized to use this command." That tells a stranger a bot is listening.

## User Impact

Senders the DM policy does not admit get no reply to native commands, the same as for ordinary messages. A sender who is admitted but is not allowed to run the command still gets the refusal. Pairing still replies, so a first contact can finish the challenge. `commands.allowFrom` denials are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

#131408 made the refusal text deliberate for a channel-admitted sender who lacks command permission. This path was also used when `dmPolicy` itself rejected the sender. The command authorization result now carries that distinction, and the native-command dispatch returns without sending when the denial is `dm_policy_not_allowlisted` or `dm_policy_disabled`.

## Evidence

Regression in `src/channels/message-access/telegram-native-owner.test.ts`: a native command as sender 300 with `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` and `allowFrom: ["999999"]` must not call the handler and must not send a message. The existing owner-admission cases still expect the refusal text.

I could not run the OpenClaw suite on this machine. CI is the run that counts.

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): honor system agent for CLI defaults
prs.body:
Fixes #188953

## What Problem This Solves

On an explicit-ownership multi-agent install with `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` set, `openclaw wiki` without `--agent` asks for an agent that is already configured. The CLI still resolves its default through the deprecated `resolveDefaultAgentId`, which only accepts legacy raw markers or a sole agent; the configured system agent is ignored.

In plain terms: the user already told OpenClaw which agent is the default work owner, but the wiki command does not read that setting. This change uses the same owner-aware resolver as other CLI operations.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveAgentOperationAgentId` is the existing core resolver for CLI operation owners: it consults the explicit ownership system agent before falling back. It was not reachable from the memory plugin, so this adds it through the existing private-local-only `memory-core-host-runtime-core` facade instead of expanding the public plugin SDK surface.

The CLI preAction, gateway request context, and active-memory query fallback now use the same owner-aware helper. `config.ts` keeps its lightweight legacy fallback because Doctor imports it and must not cold-load the memory runtime/Kysely graph; the CLI resolves the system agent first and passes the explicit agent ID into config resolution.

## User Impact

`openclaw wiki search`, `get`, `status`, and `doctor` work without `--agent` when `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` is configured, matching other CLI operation surfaces. The misleading "add an agent" hint is no longer shown when an owner is already configured. `--agent` remains authoritative.

## Evidence

Focused memory-wiki CLI/config/gateway/query suite:

```text
$ node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-memory.config.ts \
    extensions/memory-wiki/src/cli.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/config.test.ts \
    extensions/memory-wiki/src/gateway.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
Test Files  4 passed (4)
Tests       99 passed (99)
```

The new regression uses `agents.ownership: "explicit"`, two entries, and `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId: "main"`, then runs the real `registerWikiCli` preAction without `--agent` and asserts the doctor resolves the `main` agent-scoped vault.

Base red check (production changes reverted, regression kept):

```text
FAIL  ... > resolves agents.defaults.systemAgent for the default CLI agent
Error: No default memory-wiki agent is configured. Pass --agent <id>, or add an agent with `openclaw agents add`.
```

Shipped CLI, built from commit `22ecfe63017` (code-identical to the current head; the only later commit is an empty review-refresh commit) in a clean checkout and run against an isolated Gateway with fresh state:

```console
$ node dist/index.js wiki status
Wiki vault mode: isolated
Vault scope: agent (main)
Vault: ready (.../state/wiki/main)
...
EXIT 0

$ node dist/index.js wiki status --agent ops
Wiki vault mode: isolated
Vault scope: agent (ops)
Vault: ready (.../state/wiki/ops)
...
EXIT 0
```

The config has `agents.ownership: "explicit"`, `main` + `ops`, `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId: "main"`, and `plugins.entries.memory-wiki.config.vault.scope: "agent"`.

Latest-stable upgrade on the same state (v2026.10.9 release `8b18b55`):

```console
# release build 2026.10.9 (8b18b55): create the main vault and one source page
$ node dist/index.js wiki init --agent main
Initialized wiki vault at .../upgrade-state/wiki/main (9 dirs, 5 files).
$ node dist/index.js wiki ingest upgrade-source.md --agent main
Ingested upgrade-source.md into sources/upgrade-source.md. Refreshed 16 index files.

# this build 2026.10.9 (22ecfe6): migrate the release state, then read with no --agent
$ node dist/index.js doctor --fix
Doctor complete.
$ node dist/index.js wiki status
Vault scope: agent (main)
Vault: ready (.../upgrade-state/wiki/main)
Pages: 1 sources, 0 entities, 0 concepts, 0 syntheses, 9 reports
EXIT 0

$ node dist/index.js wiki status --agent ops
Vault scope: agent (ops)
Vault: ready (.../upgrade-state/wiki/ops)
EXIT 0
```

The source page created by the release build is still present and counted after the upgrade; the configured vault path and settings are unchanged. This is also the data-model compatibility check for the stored vault.

The config module intentionally keeps the lightweight legacy resolver so Doctor enumeration does not cold-load the memory/Kysely graph.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used source inspection and the existing memory-wiki CLI test harness to trace the owner-resolution gap through the four call sites and add the explicit-ownership regression. The implementer understands the code: the private facade exposes the core operation-owner resolver, and memory-wiki now consumes it instead of the deprecated legacy-only default.

prs.title: fix(ui): show website identity in dashboard gallery (#178467)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Dashboards whose primary content is a session:website widget appear as empty boards in the Dashboards gallery with the message 'A clear board, ready for work'. This occurs because session:website is registered with previewSafe: false to prevent passive code execution, causing board-document.tsx to filter out the widget and leaving BoardView with zero active rectangles (view().empty === true).

## Solution
Rather than changing previewSafe: true (which would allow unisolated iframes in gallery thumbnails), this change computes a safe websiteIdentity from authorized snapshot metadata during passive rendering. When BoardView detects an empty layout rectangle set, it inspects websiteIdentity and renders a recognizable website preview card featuring the built-in globe icon, saved title, and localized Website badge.

## Invariants & Security
- previewSafe: false is strictly retained in CORE_BOARD_WIDGET_ELEMENTS.
- Exactly 0 iframes or executable website widgets are mounted in passive mode.
- 0 network requests are initiated.
- Truly empty boards continue to display the standard empty-board prompt.
- Other unsafe widgets (agent:node-browser, mcp-app) remain isolated and do not display a website card.
- Mixed boards with preview-safe widgets (HTML) continue to render normal widget previews.

## Evidence
- Focused unit & integration regression tests: 27/27 pass.
  - ui/src/components/board/board-document.test.ts (14/14 pass).
  - ui/src/pages/dashboards/dashboards-page.test.tsx (6/6 pass).
  - ui/src/lib/board/widgets/website.test.ts (5/5 pass).
  - ui/src/lib/board/widgets/index.test.ts (2/2 pass).
- TypeScript check: pnpm tsgo:ui (0 errors).
- Linter checks: pnpm lint:ui:styles and pnpm lint:ui:no-raw-window-open (0 errors, 0 warnings across 6091 files).
- Build check: pnpm --dir ui build (clean build of 6325 modules in 1m 19s).
- Visual evidence: Playwright browser verification with system Chrome confirming recognizable card rendering with globe icon and widget title, and 0 iframes mounted.

Fixes #178467

prs.title: fix(voice): Discord controls and phone consults fail with PostgreSQL agent stores
prs.body:
Related: #189036

Contributor credit: Mitchell Etzel (@etzelm) requested and guided this repair.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @etzelm](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/65edb98b-73fa-47e9-8242-be1ae73fb4b9)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/91bf5c8e-90b2-4f50-a7b4-fd877499b08b)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Discord voice active-run controls and realtime phone-call agent consultations fail when agent storage uses PostgreSQL.

## User Impact

The two bundled voice surfaces can use PostgreSQL-backed agent stores while retaining model-selection locks, current speaker/call authority, and the existing synchronous SDK contracts. No configuration, schema, migration, or permission-policy change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both consumers still reached synchronous session-entry reads on the Gateway thread, which PostgreSQL intentionally refuses.

- Expose the existing worker-backed model-lock check as an additive async SDK helper, reuse its existing candidate selection/predicate, and await it in voice-call before fast-context lookup and before returning its result. Recheck the live call after each wait.
- Allow asynchronous caller-policy preparation in the existing run controller and migrate Discord to it. Preparation repeats for each injection admission; a separate live caller assertion remains at enqueue and cancellation effects, including the legacy key-selected path.
- Preserve the synchronous helper/callback and released dependency-adapter contracts; no synchronous fallback is selected after a worker failure.

This is distinct from @ceckert's #189036: that PR owns the four Gateway Talk surfaces and explicitly excludes these bundled SDK consumers. This PR leaves those Gateway callers untouched and does not import that branch. Both touch the shared run controller; whichever lands second must reconcile that common owner without duplicating its implementation or dropping either set of live guards.

The private async lock check is consolidated rather than adding another lock owner. Production changes are +58/-22 lines; no new manager, cache, or storage owner is introduced. The 242 net test lines cover the distinct consumer lifetime, worker-failure, model-lock, fingerprint and final-cancellation boundaries and are recorded in their own test-line allocation.

## Evidence

### Actual product and storage boundary

Built the clean baseline `9c22cf86f68b34269e49a25a95827c1c23b52ce0` and the candidate with the canonical `pnpm build`, on Node 24.20.0. All six changed production blobs remain unchanged since the candidate product proof; later adjustments only prepare runtime config in the cancellation-test fixture and migrate the root Discord integration assertion.

The disposable Gateway used real PostgreSQL 17.11 agent storage (`database.engine: sqlite`, `database.families.agent.engine: postgres`). A signed synthetic Twilio webhook issued the one-use stream URL; a carrier WebSocket sent documented start/media frames through the real voice-call server and bundled OpenAI Realtime bridge. Local Realtime WebSocket and model SSE protocol fixtures supplied synthetic transcript/tool output and a deterministic model response. The actual OpenClaw agent turn, session controller, storage, public history RPC and shutdown ran normally. No paid provider traffic or live Team state was used.

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Clean baseline, PostgreSQL | Final tool result contains `PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker`; zero agent-model requests. |
| Candidate, PostgreSQL | One agent-model request; final tool result contains `VOICE_PRODUCT_ANSWER`; authenticated `chat.history` returns that assistant answer. |
| Independent PostgreSQL read after clean Gateway shutdown | `assistant_rows=1`, `marker_answers=1`. |
| Candidate, SQLite control | Same signed-carrier flow returns `VOICE_PRODUCT_ANSWER` with one model request; clean shutdown. |

A separate source-bound probe runs the real registered voice-call consult handler and the actual Discord voice consumer/public controller against real PostgreSQL session reads. Both baseline consumers refuse at their synchronous session reader; both migrated consumers pass on PostgreSQL and SQLite. The Discord backend is a synthetic guarded run attached through the real controller, not a real Discord transport. A separate Gateway-role probe confirms the deprecated synchronous PostgreSQL read still throws the original main-thread guard.

Limits: the carrier is a simulator, and Realtime/model responses are protocol fixtures. This does not claim real Twilio/Discord server operation, microphone capture, speech recognition/synthesis quality, or commercial model inference.

### Regressions and checks

- With the original six production files temporarily restored, the three new run-control regressions fail for the intended behavior: allowed async-policy steering does not reach the backend, and cancellation proceeds instead of honoring the revoked caller. The candidate was restored byte-for-byte; the complete stop/control suite passes 12 tests.
- New consumer cases deny use after speaker revocation, session/call replacement or closure, worker failure, and a model lock applied during fast-context preparation. Existing synchronous callback/dependency-adapter cases remain covered. The synchronous model-lock helper and dependency-adapter type are byte-identical to the baseline.
- Shared Talk/control suites: 52 tests passed. Discord voice runtime e2e: 27 tests passed in both configured runs. Prompt-prefix stability: 14 tests passed. Voice-call runtime: 26 tests passed. The exact six-file Discord shard replay printed 169 tests passed.
- Core/extension production types, owning core/extension test-type graphs, targeted typed lint, formatting, SDK export/declaration generation, mock-export, line-cap and test-line checks pass. Full canonical build passed with bounded native thread pools after an initial local process-limit failure.
- Exact-head CI caught one missed root Discord integration assertion of the old callback shape. Reproduced locally (2 failures), migrated its expected async callback/live guard, and reran the complete file: 8 passed, exit 0 (13.19 s including preparation). A repository-wide callback search found no other unmigrated Discord expectations; legacy Gateway/synchronous SDK tests remain unchanged.
- Native Auto Review: complete local candidate against `9c22cf86`, through P2, **scoped-clean**, no findings. It reviewed code/context, not execution.

One larger run observed `realtime-turns.test.ts > treats a bare wake name as an activation for the next realtime transcript` fail before agent dispatch. An unchanged-code exact-shard replay printed all 169 Discord and 26 voice-call tests passed, but exec finalization failed during a transient stopped-container incident. No fix or clean terminal exit is claimed for that replay, and baseline attribution of the original wake-name failure remains unconfirmed. The separate control/prefix run subsequently completed with exit 0 after the sandbox recovered.

New-case files reuse existing suites rather than adding a cold suite/job: individual new cases take 1–2 ms in the consumer output; the voice-call file completed in 7.52 s wall, and the control/prefix command in 62.55 s including compilation/preparation. Exact-head CI for `d783c53ce3d87fdf4fb69130909dd9b7f3fae5da` passed [the aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41267798066/job/124735928893): no failed or timed-out jobs, all selected prerequisites succeeded, and `ALLOW_KNOWN_MAIN_RED=false`. The formerly failing root integration shard is green.

## Worked on by

- @etzelm

prs.title: fix(cron): keep automation pause notice names surrogate-safe
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Automation parent-pause notices truncate the job display name with raw UTF-16 `slice(0, 120)`. A user-configured name at that boundary can end mid-emoji, so the notice shows a lone high surrogate (replacement character) instead of the whole emoji.

## User Impact

The pause notice `Automation "…"` name no longer garbles when a configured automation name is long enough for an astral character to straddle the 120-unit display cap. Existing short names and the repair instructions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron job `name` is `NonEmptyString` (`minLength: 1`, no `maxLength`), and create/patch only trims — a user can store a name longer than 120 UTF-16 units. Inferred names already go through surrogate-safe `truncateWithMarker` (`inferCronJobName`), and sibling cron surfaces (`failure-alerts`, run diagnostics) already use `truncateUtf16Safe`. Only the pause-notice display cap still used a raw slice.

This routes the existing 120-unit cap through `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` (dependency-free). No length policy, schema, or notice wording change.

## Evidence

Red on base / green with fix, same input `name = "x".repeat(119) + "🚀"` (121 UTF-16 units):

| | shown length | lone surrogate | last code unit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base `slice(0, 120)` | 120 | yes | `d83d` (high half of 🚀) |
| fix `truncateUtf16Safe` | 119 | no | `0078` (`x`) |

Imported the real `buildScheduledParentPauseNotice` via tsx on base and candidate. Short name `"Nightly ingest"` still renders fully with the existing repair line `openclaw automations enable job-1`.

Regression test added beside the existing notice case: boundary emoji name must extract with no lone surrogate and length ≤ 120. Reachability: `packages/gateway-protocol` `NonEmptyString` has no `maxLength`; normalize only trims user-provided names.

## Merge Danger

- Display-only truncation of an already user-visible notice field; no scheduler, admission, or delivery behavior change.
- Two files: the notice builder + its existing unit test file. No shared roster/baseline edits.
- Same helper already used across cron; no new abstraction.

prs.title: fix(cli): stop reusing a removed local device token
prs.body:
Related: #189206 (reported by @AdoShan).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated device-token-mismatch warnings after this installation's own device is successfully removed from its default local Gateway.

## User Impact

`devices remove` and `devices clear --yes` now forget the removed local operator credential, so later CLI commands recover through their configured authentication. Other roles and remote Gateway credentials are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read-only RPC clients intentionally do not mutate credential storage. The explicit removal command now captures the existing local operator token before dispatch and conditionally clears it only after the Gateway confirms removal. A concurrently replaced token survives. Credential-store failures are reported without hiding the completed Gateway operation. The existing RPC setup and option type move to a sibling module to satisfy the command runtime’s line-cap ratchet.

This is the default-local operator recovery path; it does not change rotation/revocation, read-only diagnostics, cross-device token delivery, protocol versions, or schemas.

## Evidence

- Private Linux Gateway, normal pairing/native credential persistence, public token rotation, and independent bare CLI processes: before the fix, removal succeeded but the next two commands still retried the rejected cached token. After the fix, removal cleared the cache; both subsequent commands returned JSON without token-mismatch messages or matching Gateway log events. Read-only diagnostics before removal produced no observed credential-file changes; cross-device rotation still withheld the bearer.
- Six command/native-store regressions: before, the two removal assertions failed while four controls passed; after, all six passed. The controls cover another device, an explicit Gateway URL, failed removal, and concurrent credential replacement. All 64 tests across the touched CLI suite and related CLI/store suites passed.
- Core and targeted test types, production/test typed lint, formatting, test-line and max-line ratchets passed. P0–P2 independent review found no actionable defects; subsequent lint-only edits were separately checked for unchanged behavior.
- The required allocation records exactly 86 net new test lines, preserving the base's existing slack. The selected six-case Vitest run took 37.42s before and 42.06s after, including transform/setup; the new test bodies totaled about 12 seconds on this host.

Proof used a trusted source checkout and synthetic isolated state, not an operator Gateway or paid provider. The before/after CLI proof covers Linux's local primary operator flow; macOS and other origins were not exercised. The current main's relevant owner/caller inputs were checked against the pinned validation base.

Validation head: `f2b700f23d80eca804292dd07d3a8c62d28cc769`, based on official `91695eeb9b73d41834eb6b439af98a5959fc1169`. Before publication, the five relevant CLI/RPC/credential-store inputs on main `c633ec6376e1ce6cdf6268f98d1c86eb9395b074` were byte-identical to that validation base, and a merge-tree check found no conflicts. These checks reuse the completed proof above; they do not claim a new full-main or macOS run.


<!-- author-runtime-proof-189884-f2b700 -->
### Recorded CLI behavior at the committed head

The earlier paragraph reported assertion summaries. The following is a new capture of the actual child-process streams, rather than a reconstruction of that earlier run. A normal private Gateway paired and persisted the CLI credential; a public token rotation invalidated it and still withheld cross-device bearer delivery. The same private configuration, identity and persisted credential database were reused by independent CLI processes. The driver took 59.49s; the preceding normal cold CLI build took 205.02s and is separate.

New capture of actual child-process stdout/stderr at PR head f2b700f23d80eca804292dd07d3a8c62d28cc769; Node24.22.1/pnpm12.15.0.
Source tree was clean. Driver ran 2026-11-01 00:34:46–00:35:46 UTC in private PID/network/HOME/state namespaces.
Only ANSI color, the generated device ID, local addresses and private paths/secrets are redacted. JSON content below is captured output, not reconstructed.

$ pnpm openclaw nodes list --json
stdout:

stderr:

The fixture confirmed Gateway process-group termination and an actual close receipt (`SIGTERM`); the host operator Gateway and state were not used.

### Regression output and persisted-data compatibility

The initial six-case regression used the production command/credential owner with real SQLite state and a mocked RPC transport. Its recorded before-fix output was:

```text
 ×  infra  src/cli/devices-cli.gateway.test.ts > remove forgets the removed primary CLI operator token without touching other credentials 2639ms
 ×  infra  src/cli/devices-cli.gateway.test.ts > clear forgets the removed primary CLI operator token without touching other credentials 2864ms
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed | 4 passed | 11 skipped (17)
   Duration  37.42s (transform 57%, tests 32%, import 8%, setup 2%)
```

The corresponding after-fix run recorded:

```text

```

The `11 skipped` entries above are the unrelated cases excluded by the six-case name filter; the complete three-file run previously reported **64 passing tests**. No new skip or timeout exception was added.

A fresh exact-head check additionally ran:

```text
pnpm test src/cli/devices-cli.gateway.test.ts src/infra/device-auth-store.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --testNamePattern 'forgets the removed primary|preserves local operator credentials|local device token cache'

```

This fresh run took 148.44s including native worker preparation; its 11 filtered-out command cases are unrelated to the selected credential contracts. It verifies existing canonical SQLite rows, rather than changing their format:

- Both removal commands delete the matching pre-existing local operator credential while retaining the same device's node-role credential and the separately keyed foreign-origin credential.
- Other devices, an explicit Gateway URL, rejected removal and a concurrently replaced token retain their credentials.
- The existing native-store tests verify device/role/origin isolation, expected-token protection for local and origin tokens, malformed scope metadata behavior, worker-thread ownership and cancellation.

No schema, serialized format, migration, version, or credential-store implementation is changed by this PR. Cleanup uses the existing conditional-delete owner ([operation contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f2b700f23d80eca804292dd07d3a8c62d28cc769/src/infra/client-credential-operations.ts#L310)); the [native-store tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f2b700f23d80eca804292dd07d3a8c62d28cc769/src/infra/device-auth-store.test.ts#L12) and [command controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f2b700f23d80eca804292dd07d3a8c62d28cc769/src/cli/devices-cli.gateway.test.ts#L366) are inspectable at the same head.

The row tests above cover current-format data; the released-state upgrade and selective removal are recorded below. Rollback and macOS remain outside the proof claim.



<!-- author-released-upgrade-proof-189884-f2b700 -->
### Released v2026.10.9 upgrade and selective removal (Linux)

The released-state upgrade is now exercised at the unchanged PR head `f2b700f23d80eca804292dd07d3a8c62d28cc769`, using Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.15.0. The starting package is official [v2026.10.9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.9), release commit `8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41`. The downloaded registry tarball's SHA-512 matched both npm metadata and the release's published package evidence. Normal isolated npm installation retained its default lifecycle policy; the real released Gateway and CLI ran successfully under Node.

The released Gateway factory held its actual state-owner lease; its public SDK handshake created the primary identity/operator cache. A public cross-device rotation withheld the replacement bearer, and two separate released CLI processes reproduced the cached-token mismatch. Node-role and foreign-origin preservation rows were created through the released native credential owner; these are synthetic preservation markers, not claims of live node/origin authentication. No SQLite schema, rows or migration receipts were hand-seeded.

After the old Gateway, clients and child process groups closed, the entire isolated profile was copied for upgrade; the original released profile was retained. The released shared SQLite store was schema 20, with one primary identity, two local role rows and one origin row, and no independent client store. The normal head Doctor command below completed in 13.11s. Its actual scoped pre-migration backup remains present; shared state is now schema 36, client credentials are schema 1, and the canonical migration receipt is `complete`. These are existing migrations, not schema changes authored by this PR.

Before starting the new Gateway or pairing again, the head's native readers loaded the same device ID, complete public/private key material, rejected operator token, node marker and origin marker; the configuration file remained byte-identical. Two ordinary head CLI processes still reproduced the mismatch before removal. Self-removal then cleared only the operator row; both subsequent independent bare CLI processes returned JSON with no mismatch warnings or new matching Gateway events.
