prs.title: fix(media-understanding): honor rawKeyPrefix and agent-stripped keyPrefix in media scope rules
prs.body:
## Summary
`tools.media.<image|audio|video>.scope` accepts the same allow/deny rule schema as `session.sendPolicy` (`channel`, `chatType`, `keyPrefix`, `rawKeyPrefix`), but media understanding reads the session-key fields differently:

- `match.rawKeyPrefix` is accepted by config validation and then ignored. A rule whose only condition is `rawKeyPrefix` therefore has no condition at all and matches every session. `{ action: "deny", match: { rawKeyPrefix: "agent:main:discord:" } }` turns off voice-note transcription (and image/video description) for Telegram, Slack and every other channel, not just Discord.
- `match.keyPrefix` is compared only against the raw `agent:<id>:...` session key, so the normalized form that `sendPolicy` accepts (`keyPrefix: "slack:"`) never matches and the rule is silently skipped.

Link understanding reuses the same resolver, so `tools.links.scope` has the same two defects.

## Root cause
`src/media-understanding/resolve.ts`, `resolveScopeDecision`:

```ts
// before
const sessionKey = normalizeOptionalLowercaseString(params.ctx.SessionKey) ?? "";
...
const matchPrefix = normalizeOptionalLowercaseString(match.keyPrefix);
...
if (matchPrefix && !sessionKey.startsWith(matchPrefix)) {
  continue;
}
return rule.action;
```

The rule schema comes from the shared `createAllowDenyChannelRulesSchema()` in `src/config/zod-schema.allowdeny.ts`, which includes `rawKeyPrefix`. The resolver never reads that field, so a rule with only `rawKeyPrefix` matches everything. It also never strips the `agent:<id>:` prefix before matching `keyPrefix`. The other consumer of the schema, `resolveSendPolicy` in `src/sessions/send-policy.ts`, handles both fields.

## Fix
`resolveScopeDecision` now handles the two fields the same way `resolveSendPolicy` does. It matches `rawKeyPrefix` against the raw session key. It matches `keyPrefix` against either the raw key or the agent-stripped request key, which comes from the existing `toAgentRequestSessionKey` helper:

```ts
// after
const sessionKey = normalizeOptionalLowercaseString(params.ctx.SessionKey) ?? "";
const requestSessionKey =
  normalizeOptionalLowercaseString(toAgentRequestSessionKey(params.ctx.SessionKey)) ?? "";
...
if (matchRawPrefix && !sessionKey.startsWith(matchRawPrefix)) {
  continue;
}
if (
  matchPrefix &&
  !sessionKey.startsWith(matchPrefix) &&
  !requestSessionKey.startsWith(matchPrefix)
) {
  continue;
}
```

## Why this is the right boundary
`resolveScopeDecision` is the only place that evaluates media and link scope rules: the media runner and `src/link-understanding/apply.ts` both call it. Fixing it there covers image, audio, video and link understanding together. Raw-key `keyPrefix` rules that work today, such as `keyPrefix: "agent:main:telegram:"`, still match, because `keyPrefix` keeps accepting the raw key. Matching stays first-match-wins, and the `channel`, `chatType` and `default` handling is unchanged. The new code reuses `toAgentRequestSessionKey` from `src/routing/session-key.ts` instead of adding another way to strip the agent prefix.

## Verification
- Extended `src/media-understanding/resolve.test.ts` with two cases. The first checks that a `rawKeyPrefix: "agent:main:discord:"` deny rule allows `agent:main:telegram:direct:123` and denies `agent:main:discord:direct:456`. The second checks that a `keyPrefix: "slack:"` deny rule denies `agent:main:slack:direct:u789` and allows `agent:main:telegram:direct:123`. With `resolve.ts` reverted to main, both cases fail (2 failed, 6 passed). With this patch, all 8 tests in the file pass.
- `oxfmt --check` is clean on both changed files.
- Local tsgo and oxlint were not run per the contributor workflow for this batch; GitHub Actions covers them.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: a media scope rule with `rawKeyPrefix` matched every session and denied voice-note transcription on all channels, and a `keyPrefix` written without the `agent:<id>:` prefix never matched.
Real environment tested: I called the production `applyMediaUnderstanding` from `src/media-understanding/apply.ts`, the entry the inbound reply pipeline uses, from source with `node --import tsx`. It ran with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` on pristine main b9b710846130 and on this patch, with identical inputs. The config had a real CLI audio model entry (`type: "cli"`, `command: "/bin/echo"`). Each run passed one voice-note attachment stored under the state dir's `media/inbound`, plus real `agent:main:<channel>:direct:<peer>` session keys. Attachment selection, local-root checks, scope evaluation, CLI execution and transcript application were all real. Nothing was stubbed, and no network was involved.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1 OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<tmp> node --import tsx drive.mts <tmp>/media/inbound/voice-note.ogg`. The script calls `applyMediaUnderstanding({ ctx, cfg, agentId: "main" })` with `tools.media.audio.scope = { default: "allow", rules: [<rule>] }` for each session key shown, then prints the audio decision outcome and `ctx.Transcript`.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main b9b710846130)
scope rules: [{"action":"deny","match":{"rawKeyPrefix":"agent:main:discord:"}}] default=allow
  agent:main:telegram:direct:123 -> audio outcome=scope-deny transcript=null
  agent:main:discord:direct:456 -> audio outcome=scope-deny transcript=null
scope rules: [{"action":"deny","match":{"keyPrefix":"slack:"}}] default=allow
  agent:main:telegram:direct:123 -> audio outcome=success transcript="transcript: what is the weather"
  agent:main:slack:direct:u789 -> audio outcome=success transcript="transcript: what is the weather"
# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
scope rules: [{"action":"deny","match":{"rawKeyPrefix":"agent:main:discord:"}}] default=allow
  agent:main:telegram:direct:123 -> audio outcome=success transcript="transcript: what is the weather"
  agent:main:discord:direct:456 -> audio outcome=scope-deny transcript=null
scope rules: [{"action":"deny","match":{"keyPrefix":"slack:"}}] default=allow
  agent:main:telegram:direct:123 -> audio outcome=success transcript="transcript: what is the weather"
  agent:main:slack:direct:u789 -> audio outcome=scope-deny transcript=null
```
Observed result after fix: the Discord-only `rawKeyPrefix` deny rule no longer blocks the Telegram voice note, which is now transcribed. The `keyPrefix: "slack:"` deny rule now blocks the Slack voice note instead of being skipped. Sessions the rules do not target behave the same as before.
What was not tested: this was not driven through a live channel or gateway turn, which would reach the same function through the reply pipeline. Image, video and `tools.links.scope` were not exercised live; they share the changed resolver. Full build not run.

prs.title: fix: avoid repeated GitHub requests when discovering fork PRs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated GitHub requests while discovering a session's pull request when multiple candidate fork repositories belong to the same owner.

## User Impact

Session PR discovery avoids an unnecessary network round trip while preserving which fork repository is accepted. With normal GitHub ETags, the eliminated request is usually a bodyless 304; without validators, it also avoids transferring and parsing the duplicate list. No configuration or data migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fork candidates are distinct by owner/repository, but the list query selects owner:branch against the same base repository. Reuse each parsed list within that one discovery, then apply the existing repository-specific filter to every candidate. Subsequent discoveries still revalidate remotely. The candidate list is already bounded to three; production code grows by two net lines, without a persistent cache or a new TTL.

The accompanying scripts make the request-volume investigation reproducible through the real owner and a local Gateway, a recording loopback GitHub server, and the actual Control UI PR subscription store. Fixture responses and credentials are synthetic; external fetches are blocked. The fixture generator now includes the explicit agent ownership required for multi-agent startup.

## Evidence

The strengthened renamed-fork regression fails on the parent with two list requests where one is expected, and passes with the fix. The owner, publication, and staleness suites passed 39 tests; the final owner suite passed all 26 tests after simplification. All six fixture-generator tests passed. `pnpm check:changed --staged` and the production/full-tree unused-file scans passed. Independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

A final-source local Gateway qualification delivered PR 17 to all four UI viewers: four successful subscription calls and four nonempty ready snapshots. The recording server saw 11 requests (seven 200s and four 304s), 75,428 response bytes, and no unmodeled routes. This short run qualifies the harness; its timings are excluded from performance claims.


<details>
<summary>Owner measurements: five A/B pairs, A/A controls, separate allocation passes</summary>

The committed `scripts/perf/github-fork-discovery-measure.ts` runs the real owner with prepared repository contexts and a recording loopback server. Each arm performs 1,000 discoveries; all 48,000 measured assertions across four campaigns passed. The mock and client share a process, so these CPU/allocation figures include both. These are per-discovery measurements, not Gateway rates. `full` means responses without validators; `etag` means warm conditional responses. Allocation uses 32 KiB V8 sampling with collected objects included and sums tree `selfSize`.

| Mode | Metric per discovery | Baseline | Candidate | Change |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| full | HTTP requests | 2.000 | 1.000 | -50.0% |
| full | Response bytes | 46,842.000 | 23,421.000 | -50.0% |
| full | CPU µs | 652.664 | 390.526 | -40.2% |
| full | Mean arm p50 ms | 0.408 | 0.226 | -44.6% |
| full | Mean arm p95 ms | 0.970 | 0.600 | -38.1% |

| etag | HTTP requests | 2.000 | 1.000 | -50.0% |
| etag | Response bytes | 0.000 | 0.000 | both zero |
| etag | CPU µs | 391.551 | 246.982 | -36.9% |
| etag | Mean arm p50 ms | 0.294 | 0.175 | -40.7% |

| etag | Named-reader allocation B | 0.000 | 0.000 | both zero |

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| full | 1 | 701.408 → 339.031 (-51.7%) | 0.390 → 0.272 (-30.0%) | 1.025 → 0.688 (-32.9%) |

The one >=20% adverse candidate cell across all captured metrics is allocation-pass full pair 3 p95: 2.390 → 3.735 (+56.3%). Its total/named-reader allocations improved; its profiler-distorted latency is not used for timing acceptance. A/A adverse cells >=20%: unprofiled full p95 +43.9%, unprofiled ETag CPU +22.7%, profiled ETag CPU +59.7% / p50 +43.4% / p95 +158.3%. Controls and concurrent load preclude a precise latency magnitude claim. No allocation cell regressed.

Reproduce against the parent:

```sh
git show 079889d5a09102246b34b363ff340591729d5a80:src/gateway/control-ui-session-prs.ts > src/gateway/control-ui-session-prs.lane2080-base.ts

# Separate passes: --etag, --allocations, and --etag --allocations.
```

The shared host was busy and synthetic fixture generation ran concurrently. Counts and allocation reductions were consistent; timing magnitudes are not production forecasts. No production allocator attribution is claimed.

</details>

Acceptance for the full campaign: identical visible PR facts; one list request per distinct head query per discovery; no unexplained user-facing regression. Compare five interleaved baseline/candidate arms plus A/A controls, keeping cold setup separate from three-minute natural-poll windows and using the existing five-second foreground list cadence. Allocation sampling runs separately, using the actual sampling duration. Report ETag and absent-validator outcomes separately.

The full synthetic Gateway campaign is pending. It covers 10,800 retained sessions, four viewers of one active PR, a production-sized agent database (final physical size pending), and 62,000 tracked workspace files totaling about 1.1 GB. It does not exercise 100 simultaneously active Activity rows or prove behavior on btrfs. Landing waits for the completed measurements and exact-head CI.

prs.title: docs(ios): require Xcode 27.1 to build the iOS app
prs.body:
Related: #187045

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the iOS README says Xcode 26.x is enough, but the iOS app on `main` no longer compiles with Xcode 26.x.

## User Impact

User impact: developers building the iOS app know before they start that they need Xcode 27.1 or newer. There is no change to the app or to the iOS versions it runs on.

## Why This Change Was Made

#187045 added code that uses `toolbarVerticalEdge`, which is not in the iOS 26.5 SDK. The `@available` and `#available` guards let the app run on older iOS, but the compiler must still know the symbol. CI already uses Xcode 27, so this PR updates the two README prerequisites to match. If maintainers prefer to keep Xcode 26.x builds working, a compile-time guard would be the alternative and this PR can close.

## Evidence

- Xcode 26.6 (17F113) with the iOS 26.5 SDK fails on `xcodebuild build-for-testing`, on a tree where this file is unchanged from `main`:

  ```text
  apps/ios/Sources/Design/ChatProTab.swift:735:18: error: cannot infer key path type from context; consider explicitly specifying a root type
  ```

- The `@available` at `ChatProTab.swift:733` and the `#available` checks at `ChatProTab.swift:80`, `ChatProTab.swift:220` and `OpenClawProComponents.swift:199` all say `iOS 27.1`, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml:113` pins `IOS_SCREENSHOT_XCODE_VERSION: "Xcode 27.1 Build version 27A9275"`.
- Xcode 27.1 builds it: the `ios-screenshots` job on #187045's own head `2ee308df3f` [passed on CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40949460063/job/123714380788). That job builds the iOS app and checks that the selected Xcode is exactly `Xcode 27.1 Build version 27A9275` before it captures.
- Gap: I did not build with Xcode 27.1 locally, and I did not test whether an Xcode 27.0 SDK has the symbol. This PR only changes the README, so no tests were run.

prs.title: feat(release): add bound gate approval helper
prs.body:
## Summary

- add `pnpm release:approve` for one explicitly bound GitHub environment approval
- require exact repository, active run ID, SHA, workflow file, head ref, release title, and environment before the write
- accept the canonical `v<version>` workflow title while keeping title and tooling-ref identity checks independent
- require GitHub's `current_user_can_approve` capability before the POST
- resolve the effective GitHub approver and confirm the pending gate disappeared afterward
- treat an unavailable POST response or confirmation read as an uncertain write, with explicit read-only pending-gate and approval-history reconciliation commands before any retry
- support a read-only `--dry-run` preview

## Why

Repeated hand-written `gh api` snippets successfully approved release gates and then printed jq errors while parsing the POST response. That made a completed production effect look failed and invited unsafe blind retries.

## Validation

- 10 focused approval-helper tests passed
- canonical `v2026...` titles succeed from a version-free protected tooling ref
- mismatched release titles, SHA, workflow, ref, and unauthorized approvers fail before any approval call
- unavailable POST responses, failed confirmation reads, and still-pending gates emit read-only reconciliation guidance and prohibit blind retry
- `pnpm check:coercion-helpers`
- `pnpm check:script-erasability`
- `pnpm tsgo:scripts`
- tooling-test TypeScript check
- focused `oxlint` and formatting checks
- `git diff --check`
- independent P0–P2 review of the complete PR plus repair found one title/ref coupling issue; fixed before publication, with no other P0–P2 findings

No live protected-environment approval was exercised. GitHub remains the final approval authority; the helper now refuses a pending deployment unless GitHub reports `current_user_can_approve: true`.

Related retrospective item: RRI-83.

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): trace warm syntax readiness [do not merge]
prs.body:
## Outcome: failed performance gate; do not merge

Head `f060e76ad6156a05e8ef3d4e1cf2c36cf3cc6e37`; pinned main control `177fe32dfdd77152780442a4c13a806d26d088fc`. The bounded experiment is stopped. All 11 candidate reloads recolored on both routes, as did all 11 baseline reloads. Required zero-recolor result was at least 9/11 per route. No ready PR or landing is requested.

## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload of a dashboard or chat deep link can show cached code as plain text before syntax colors arrive. This experiment tested whether a fence-only early import and a maximum 100 ms route-loader join could remove that visible stage within the existing boot budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing highlighter-ready signal works. Temporary instrumentation on the previous early-import candidate showed that the module resolves late, rather than mounted rows waiting for a live-history revision. Both diagnostic arms used the same candidate; the labels below identify repeated captures, not an A/B comparison. Times are document-relative milliseconds.

| Capture | Import start | Module evaluated | Resolved | First plain DOM commit | First connected code | First app frame | Ready-triggered prepare | Colored DOM commit |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| base-chat | 324.7 | 1255.2 | 1255.3 | 387.2 | 415.2 | 535.4 | 1255.3 | 1290.5 |
| candidate-chat | 271.5 | 943.1 | 943.2 | 318.6 | 341.2 | 808.1 | 943.2 | 970.9 |
| base-dashboard | 279.1 | 1248.5 | 1248.6 | 364.2 | 411.1 | 220.2 | 1248.6 | 1281.8 |
| candidate-dashboard | 259.4 | 1108.6 | 1108.6 | 335.8 | 379.6 | 478.5 | 1108.7 | 1147.5 |

Ready triggered markdown preparation within 0.1 ms in all four captures; highlighted DOM committed 27.7–38.9 ms after readiness. The triggering cause was highlighter-ready notification, not a later history revision. DOM commit is recorded separately from connection/mount and captured paint. This attribution does not establish that every possible boot arrangement is inherently unable to beat mount.

The final candidate starts the existing single-flight highlighter import when the existing scoped snapshot prewarm first reads fenced text. Fence-free snapshots do not import it. The route loader joins that promise for at most 100 ms, then preserves the existing plaintext/lazy behavior. Readiness has one owner; HTML escaping and markup construction remain in the original renderer. Long fences retain the worker path. No new store, persisted fields, config option, protocol, or boot-budget allowance.

## User Impact

The natural warm-reload artifact remains. The code-heavy viewport has three collapsed 28-line fences (TypeScript, Python, Bash), each showing seven lines. These residual recolors are short synchronous-highlighter fences, not long-fence worker cases. The preloaded-runtime native regression passes, but that conditional result does not prove that a natural reload preloads the runtime in time.

## Evidence

AWS Crabbox `cbx_b41a84ec7015`, fixed `c7a.4xlarge`, repo headless Chromium. [Run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_65be89135f076496cc601afb71333c64). One box for the entire comparison; 11 interleaved A/A pairs and 11 interleaved baseline/candidate pairs per route. Unprofiled, 1720×1180, 80 ms RTT, 3,000 synthetic sessions with archived pinned targets and operator-shaped category/owner/sort/collapse preferences. CPU idle preflight: A/A 92.42%, A/B 92.94%. No Mac performance timings.

Pixels were audited from the first app candidate frame through settle, using each visible code region, not only the final frame or DOM classes. Every one of the 88 warm captures has three valid regions, nonzero settled syntax-color pixels, and an observed colored sample for every region. Every capture contains a plain-to-colored transition in all three fences. Full synthetic candidate plain/colored screenshots for each route were inspected; they show actual text recoloring. Frame times are capture samples, not exact transition instants.

| Comparison / route | Baseline zero recolor | Candidate zero recolor | Candidate better pairs | Baseline first plain → all colored, median ms | Candidate first plain → all colored, median ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| AA / chat | 0/11 | 0/11 | 0/11 | 688.1 → 1113.6 | 678.3 → 1130.5 |
| AA / dashboard | 0/11 | 0/11 | 0/11 | 627.7 → 1034.1 | 625.0 → 1056.4 |

### Code size and validation

UI runtime delta: **+86/−52 = +34 LOC**, across the existing renderer/readiness and snapshot/route owners (six files). Requested filtered production-stat command reports **14 files, +200/−64 = +136**, including benchmark/proof code and generated/configuration metadata. The experiment does not justify accepting this growth because it fails the primary gate. Tests are excluded from those counts.

Final-head boot asset budget passed unchanged: Chat 1,272,654 → 1,273,078 gzip bytes (+424), 20 → 20 requests; New 781,305 → 782,082 (+777), 15 → 15 requests; entry 89,599 → 89,594 (−5), 3 → 3 requests. No budget baseline raised.

Final-head focused proof on `cbx_b41a84ec7015`: 58 tests pass: native code-fences 6, markdown-highlight 13, browser highlighter 1, snapshot prewarm 14, warm-boot routing 8, snapshot routing 16. Authored native case fails on pinned main because no early grammar request is issued, and passes on candidate when runtime is explicitly preloaded. Native file command `pnpm test ui/src/e2e/chat-code-block-fences.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 32.10 s wall; main red control 37.89 s. UI types, controller types, candidate/baseline UI builds and asset check pass. Independent local review is clean through P2 for the full candidate and final loading/markup boundary repair.

Full UI e2e and check-changed were not run after the failed primary gate; draft CI is not broad green proof. The experiment stays unmergeable and is closed. No unrelated inherited failures were chased. All task leases are released: diagnostic `cbx_cf714cc1ef36`, discarded budget-preflight `cbx_de84d718c80f`, final comparison `cbx_b41a84ec7015`. No task Gateway remains running.

## Disposition

Park this lane under the lead’s escape hatch. This round establishes late module readiness and failure of the bounded 100 ms join; it does not prove that a larger boot change is inherently necessary. prs.title: feature(gateway): add suspend status CLI for existing Gateway RPC
prs.body:
Implements #181354

## What Problem This Solves

Cooperative host suspension already exposes `gateway.suspend.status` (`operator.read`) for polling an issued lease (`running` / `draining` / `ready`, blockers, expiry, optional lifecycle), but the native CLI only wraps prepare (`openclaw gateway suspend`) and resume (`openclaw gateway resume`). Operators who need a one-shot poll of an existing `suspensionId` (drain progress, shutdown observation, or “is this lease still held?”) must hand-write `gateway call` JSON. `gateway suspend --wait` only retries **prepare** and does not replace status polling.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw gateway suspend status <suspensionId>` exposes the existing `gateway.suspend.status` RPC as a first-class CLI verb with the same auth/error class as sibling Gateway-backed commands. Operators get lease status JSON (and optional lifecycle fields via `--include-lifecycle`) without composing RPC params.

## Why This Change Was Made

Thin Alix-style CLI adapter only: register `gateway suspend status`, forward `{ suspensionId, includeLifecycle? }` to the existing Gateway method, print the Gateway payload, and document next to suspend / resume. No new Gateway methods, schema, permissions, or suspension behavior. Nested `--json`/`--port` inherit from the parent `suspend` command (same pattern as other Gateway option inheritance).

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/cli/gateway-cli/suspend-cli.ts`, `src/cli/gateway-cli/register.ts`, `src/cli/gateway-cli/gateway-action.ts`, `src/cli/command-catalog.ts`, colocated tests, `docs/cli/gateway/query.md`, `docs/cli/gateway.md`
- Unit/registration: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/gateway-cli/suspend-cli.test.ts src/cli/gateway-cli/register.option-collisions.test.ts` — **38 passed**
- Packaged CLI proof below (Node 24.22.1, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, local Gateway with token auth)

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Operators need native `openclaw gateway suspend status <suspensionId>` that calls existing `gateway.suspend.status` and returns `running` / `ready` / `draining` JSON; missing Gateway must fail like sibling RPC verbs.

### Canonical reachability path

Packaged `openclaw gateway suspend status` → `runGatewaySuspendStatus` → `callGatewayFromCliWithTransport("gateway.suspend.status", …, { suspensionId, includeLifecycle? })` → existing Gateway handler (`getGatewaySuspendStatus`).

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Reuses `callGatewayFromCliWithTransport` and existing `gateway.suspend.status` owner. No new query engine, schema, permissions, or suspension lease semantics. Explicitly not #180736 (persistent maintenance pause).

### Real environment tested

Packaged CLI (`node openclaw.mjs`) after `qaRuntime` build on Node 24.22.1; temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` + `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`; local `openclaw gateway run` with token auth.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
export PATH="/home/box/.local/node-v24.22.1-linux-x64/bin:$PATH"
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/openclaw.json"
# config: gateway.mode=local, auth.token, bind=loopback
node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port 18794 --token "$TOKEN" &
READY=$(node openclaw.mjs gateway suspend --url ws://127.0.0.1:18794 --token "$TOKEN" --json)
ID=$(printf '%s' "$READY" | jq -r .suspensionId)
node openclaw.mjs gateway suspend status "$ID" --url ws://127.0.0.1:18794 --token "$TOKEN" --json
node openclaw.mjs gateway suspend status "$ID" --include-lifecycle --url ws://127.0.0.1:18794 --token "$TOKEN" --json
node openclaw.mjs gateway resume "$ID" --url ws://127.0.0.1:18794 --token "$TOKEN" --json
node openclaw.mjs gateway suspend status "$ID" --url ws://127.0.0.1:18794 --token "$TOKEN" --json
# parity: openclaw gateway call gateway.suspend.status --params "{\"suspensionId\":\"$ID\"}" --json
# negative: openclaw gateway suspend status "$ID" --url ws://127.0.0.1:1 --token "$TOKEN" --timeout 2000 --json  → exit 1
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
# openclaw gateway suspend --help
Commands:
  status                 Poll an existing cooperative Gateway suspension lease

# openclaw gateway suspend --json  (exit 0)
{
  "status": "ready",
  "suspensionId": "b565f0e4-2f49-44eb-b5d3-10b0115f08b3",
  "expiresAtMs": 1792732682159,
  "activeCount": 0,
  "blockers": [],
  "writeCustody": [],
  "requestId": "cli-06883a74"
}

# openclaw gateway suspend status <id> --json  (exit 0)
{
  "status": "ready",
  "expiresAtMs": 1792732682159,
  "writeCustody": []
}

# openclaw gateway suspend status <id> --include-lifecycle --json  (exit 0)
{
  "status": "ready",
  "ownerId": "cli-06883a74",
  "expiresAtMs": 1792732682159,
  "writeCustody": []
}

# after resume → status
{ "status": "running" }

# parity gateway call
{ "status": "running" }

# unreachable Gateway (exit 1)
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "gateway_transport_error",
    "kind": "closed",
    "message": "Gateway not reachable at ws://127.0.0.1:1 (ECONNREFUSED).",
    "reason": "connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:1"
  },
  "gateway": {
    "url": "ws://127.0.0.1:1",
    "urlSource": "cli --url"
  }
}
```

### Evidence before fix (base RED)

```text
# on upstream/main packaged CLI before this commit:
# openclaw gateway suspend --help
Usage: openclaw gateway suspend [options]
# (no Commands / status subcommand)

# openclaw gateway suspend status anything --json
Too many arguments for this command.
Try: openclaw gateway suspend --help
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Too many arguments for this command.\nTry: openclaw gateway suspend --help"
  }
}
```

### What was not tested

Live drain/shutdown phase (`status: "draining"`) under committed handoff; auth scope matrix beyond token operator success / unreachable Gateway failure; Control UI suspension indicator path.

prs.title: fix(hooks): resolve mapping header templates case-insensitively
prs.body:
## Summary
Hook mapping templates that reference a request header with its canonical capitalization render empty. A mapping such as `textTemplate: "GitHub event={{headers.X-GitHub-Event}}"` receives a request that carries `X-GitHub-Event: push`, yet the rendered wake text is `GitHub event=`. HTTP header names are case-insensitive and senders document them in mixed case (`X-GitHub-Event`, `X-Gitlab-Event`, `Stripe-Signature`), so copying the name from the sender's docs silently drops the value. When the header is the only template content, the request is rejected with `400 hook mapping requires text`, and a `sessionKey` templated only from a header is rejected as rendering empty.

## Root cause
`normalizeHookHeaders` in `src/gateway/hooks.ts` lowercases every header name before the mapping context is built, but `resolveTemplateExpr` in `src/gateway/hooks-mapping.ts` looks the header up with the name exactly as written in the template:

```ts
// before
if (expr.startsWith("headers.")) {
  return getByPath(ctx.headers, expr.slice("headers.".length));
}
```

Only an all-lowercase template name (`{{headers.x-github-event}}`) can match the lowercased map; any other spelling resolves to `undefined` and renders as an empty string.

## Fix
Normalize the template's header name with the same helper the request handler uses for the header map:

```ts
// after
if (expr.startsWith("headers.")) {
  return getByPath(ctx.headers, normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(expr.slice("headers.".length)));
}
```

## Why this is the right boundary
The header map is produced lowercase by `normalizeHookHeaders`, and `resolveTemplateExpr` is the single place where mapping templates read headers (text, message, name, sessionKey, to, model and thinking all render through it), so normalizing the lookup key there makes every templated field agree with the producer. Lowercase templates, which the docs show (`{{headers.x-event-type}}`), resolve exactly as before. `payload.*` and `query.*` lookups stay case-sensitive because JSON keys and query parameters are case-sensitive. Transforms are unaffected: they already receive the same lowercased `headers` object.

## Verification
- `src/gateway/hooks-mapping.test.ts`: new case "resolves header templates case-insensitively" maps `{{headers.X-GitHub-Event}} {{headers.x-github-delivery}}` against a lowercased header map and asserts the wake text is `push d-1`. It fails on pristine main (the event value renders empty) and passes with the patch; the full file passes (24 cases).
- `oxfmt --check` clean on both changed files.
- Local tsgo and oxlint were not run per the contributor workflow for this batch; GitHub Actions covers them.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: A hook mapping template that names a request header in mixed case (`{{headers.X-GitHub-Event}}`) rendered empty even though the request carried that header.
Real environment tested: Real gateway started from source with `node --import tsx src/entry.ts gateway run` (loopback, token auth, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`), with `hooks.enabled: true` and one mapping `{ id: "github", match: { path: "github" }, action: "wake", wakeMode: "now", textTemplate: "GitHub event={{headers.X-GitHub-Event}} delivery={{headers.X-GitHub-Delivery}}" }`, driven with curl over HTTP. The rendered wake text was read back from the real agent SQLite store the gateway wrote. Pristine main 74d1342d3ac first, then this patch with identical config and request. Nothing was stubbed; no model provider credentials were configured, so the queued wake turn itself fails at provider sign-in after the text is recorded.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19583/hooks/github -H 'Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'X-GitHub-Event: push' -H 'X-GitHub-Delivery: 7f3c-42' -d '{"ref":"refs/heads/main"}'`, then stop the gateway and run `sqlite3 $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite "select session_key, json_extract(message_json, '$.content') from session_pending_inputs"`.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 74d1342d3ac)
$ curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19583/hooks/github -H 'Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'X-GitHub-Event: push' -H 'X-GitHub-Delivery: 7f3c-42' -d '{"ref":"refs/heads/main"}'
{"ok":true,"mode":"now","eventOutcome":"queued"}
HTTP 200
$ sqlite3 $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite "select session_key, json_extract(message_json, '$.content') from session_pending_inputs"
agent:main:main|GitHub event= delivery=

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
$ curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19583/hooks/github -H 'Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'X-GitHub-Event: push' -H 'X-GitHub-Delivery: 7f3c-42' -d '{"ref":"refs/heads/main"}'
{"ok":true,"mode":"now","eventOutcome":"queued"}
HTTP 200
$ sqlite3 $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite "select session_key, json_extract(message_json, '$.content') from session_pending_inputs"
agent:main:main|GitHub event=push delivery=7f3c-42
```
Observed result after fix: The wake text the gateway recorded for the main session changes from `GitHub event= delivery=` on main to `GitHub event=push delivery=7f3c-42` with the patch; the header values from the request now reach the mapped template.
What was not tested: No live model provider turn (no credentials configured); agent-action mappings with header-templated `sessionKey`, `to` or `model` were not booted live, though they render through the same function; full build not run. Some bundled plugins failed to load in the from-source gateway because of a local dependency resolution issue unrelated to hooks, which does not touch the hooks HTTP path.

The Decision picker reads installed manifest rows only, so task capabilities adopted into a prepared catalog generation cannot appear there.

## User Impact

Pass captured entries to the existing selector projection. Prefer prepared Decision facts where available; preserve installed manifest advertisements when prepared inventory omits or clears those facts. prs.title: perf(memory): classify embedding retries once per failure
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/188252

## What Problem This Solves

Memory embedding retries classify the same provider failure separately for retry eligibility, cooldown and delay.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Existing attempt limits, cooldowns, query wait limits, cancellation and terminal-error behavior remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry one attempt-local budget through the scheduler's synchronous callbacks, refreshing it for every failure. Keep the caller-abort check first and preserve the shared scheduler, batch splitting and persistence behavior.

The existing mixed-error case now rethrows the same Error after changing its message and status from 429 to 502. Its result, attempt-count and delay-range assertions remain unchanged. Production grows one line; test support grows five lines, covered by the separate allocation of five. The shared baseline is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Source-only formatting, Node syntax, whitespace and normal signed commit hooks passed.
- Fresh independent review covered all three files in the complete committed range, found no actionable correctness or security issues and assessed the patch correct with confidence 0.94.
- Source inspection confirms the scheduler consumes the budget before awaiting and that each invocation retains separate state. The retry policy and test owners remain unchanged at the pinned current owner outside the granted hunks.
- Runtime tests, focused typecheck/lint, the native test-line ratchet and exact-head CI remain pending. The personal checkout is code-only because native dependency qualification refused a broken or escaping workspace link.
- Matched work and cost proof remains pending: five serial interleaved baseline/candidate pairs with identical final fixtures and fresh qualified workers/caches. The mixed-failure workload is expected to reduce classifications from six to two while preserving three attempts and two waits; this is unmeasured. The 20% stop policy applies. No latency, CPU, RSS or physical-allocation improvement is claimed.

prs.title: fix: stop closed macOS dashboards reconnecting after native auth refusal
prs.body:
Related: #168743

## What Problem This Solves

Closing or replacing a natively authenticated macOS Dashboard can leave its committed page reconnecting after that window can no longer obtain native authorization, producing repeated pre-connect warnings.

## User Impact

Closing or replacing a native Dashboard now retires and unloads its document. A retained window reopens its trusted route using the same WebView storage; hiding or minimizing preserves its live document. Exact repeated native-refusal warnings retain the first diagnostic and periodic suppressed counts rather than one warning per attempt.

Real-WKWebView and Gateway evidence is now available, with the revision and host limits below. The reporter's installed-app trigger and cessation of its reconnect loop remain unconfirmed. No full native-suite green or exact-new-commit native rerun is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stopping WebKit navigation does not unload a committed page. The existing controller now retires that document and its identity at actual native close/replacement, retains its trusted reopen route, and keeps the inert retirement page non-deliverable. Browser identity, origin/account storage boundaries and transient native recovery remain intact; there is no refusal cap or retry-policy change.

The Gateway extends its existing bounded authentication-log limiter only for pre-connect code 4008 and the exact raw reason native authorization unavailable. Code 1006, near-matches and credential-mismatch warnings keep their previous behavior.

The supplied native run also exposed an obsolete notification-test oracle: after closing, it expected the outgoing page to remain at /. The follow-up test repair now requires about:blank while closed, explicitly reopens, then waits for the retained / route instead of the stale notification's completion route. Window identity, closed state and non-close navigation checks are preserved.

## Evidence

- The notification replay test is repaired without removing ownership checks. Supplied stock-host focused runs pass **9/9 only with that dirty test patch**; they are not executions of the new commit.
- Real WKWebView evidence denies stale credentials and permits a fresh document after close, replacement and immediate reopen. A selective base overlay actually fails the two immediate-reopen assertions.
- New supplied focused TypeScript proof is **65/65**, separate from the historical **67/5-file** run. The synthetic real-Gateway trace emits **2 native + 3 control** warnings versus **12 + 3** on the selective base overlay; it does not prove app reconnect cessation.
- **Lint is not green:** normal scope has one source-verified inherited file-length violation; a different explicit touched-test scope reports 60 serious diagnostics. Restricted sibling sweeps, crashes, timeouts and omissions are disclosed below—not counted passing.
- **Remaining validation:** exact-new-head native execution and reporter-side built-app close/reconnect correlation. Current-head ordinary CI passed; the hosted review is high-confidence ready for maintainer review with no Before-merge items, but rates overall readiness 3/6—not Platinum overall. No full native-suite green or current-main validation is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Audited receipts, sanitized excerpts, source equivalence and all negative results</summary>

### Revision, source equivalence and hosts

The [reporter's public evidence comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185963#issuecomment-6552265574) and independently audited supplied bundle concern head f56bd97a670203f386ff71e313f25e50d6562afc and admitted base 3a3246e7c1389c03e933e1f15805306945b1df1c. The audit inspected artifacts; it did not rerun supplied scripts or tests. All 70 declared bundle checksums matched; ZIP SHA-256: 3c684b5ed17f6304d842331974a271b140bfb86ee3a16b288d861b61d99b6bb2.

The [new repair commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4abd9e5395cd30293cf5ffc625b97a114c6a2ec4) changes only DashboardNotificationWindowTests.swift (+4/−1) from that recorded head. Its complete resulting file is byte-identical to the published f56 file plus the audited patch (patch SHA-256 3151270b79163551c9f5082ba0dc15a161bb855139191716f680dd6682235d64; resulting Git blob 7ab8659bf05356f99fddfef4e7a05b4db7236e31). All eleven earlier changed source files still match f56. This establishes tracked-source equivalence, not a new-commit test execution or complete generated/untracked/build-input attestation.

- Host A is reported as stock Xcode 27.1/Swift 6.4 on macOS 27.2 arm64 with a GUI. Library/platform/AppKit records partly corroborate that metadata; the bundle does not contain a complete pinned checkout/toolchain attestation.
- Host B directly records swift.org 6.3.3/SDK26.5 without GUI, substitute SwiftUI/Preview macro plugins, and two omitted XCTest files (SimpleTaskSupportTests.swift and MacNodeLocationServiceTests.swift). Its results are adapted, restricted coverage—not a stock/full native build. Supplied Studio scripts omit untracked files from dirty-state output.
- Head-plus-patch passes still record the old f56 HEAD and a modified test. Base-overlay runs retain the head checkout/tests and restore selected production files, not a clean full-base checkout. Exact overlaid bytes cannot be independently reconstructed from the bundle. No supplied scripts or macro stubs were executed during this audit/update.

### Real WKWebView outcomes — including the original red test

Unpatched f56 is not native-green: “older manager command replay does not cancel a newer notification click” fails refreshed-close and new-window-close, receiving an empty path where its old oracle expected /. The supplied base overlay and head-plus-patch each pass its four cases on both hosts. The source owner inspected the real retirement implementation and wait helper before applying the audited correction above.

| Supplied selection | Audited result and limit |
| --- | --- |
| A, recorded clean-state f56, focused 9 tests / 3 suites | 8 test functions pass; older-manager fails with 2 issues; EXIT=1. The WK ownership matrix (10 cases), forbidden frame/browser-identity cases (3), retained close/reopen (2), replacement unload, device-settings (9 cases) and 3 ControlUIDocument tests pass. |
| A, f56 plus dirty test patch, same selection | 9 tests / 3 suites pass in 31.181 seconds; EXIT=0. Separate older-manager rerun passes 4 cases. Not an exact-new-commit rerun. |
| B, adapted focused selections | Auth bridge 4 tests pass, including 3 + 10 + 2 parameter cases; device settings 1 test / 9 cases and isolated conversation factory pass. Socket-retirement and saved-profile selections crash with signal 5 on both head and base overlay; those are not passes. |
| B, adapted restricted sibling sweep | 252 test-pass records; 253 tests / 46 suites fail with 2 issues, EXIT=1. The completed sweep's failing test is older-manager. Other attempts abort or remain incomplete. No full-suite green. |

The important completed negative control uses the real WK reply boundary: A's selective native base overlay reaches immediate-reopen, delivers a grant to the retired document and fails two assertions. The recorded head denies that stale recipient and completes a fresh current recipient after close, replacement and immediate reopen. It also accepts current/current-password/current-device-only and rejects document/provider/socket/browser-identity stale replies.

Sanitized excerpts below are supplied-log evidence, not independent reruns. Anchors name bundle-relative files; they are not public download URLs. Credential payloads, local paths and endpoint/host values are omitted.

    EVIDENCE/laptop/laptop-base-native-WK_challenge_replies_are_owned_.log:20,23,41–48
      immediate-reopen: expected error != nil and result == nil; both fail
      transition=immediate-reopen result=true error=false
      ten cases failed with 2 issues; EXIT=1
    EVIDENCE/laptop/laptop-head-native-focused.log:26–32
      close and replacement: stale response denied; new current recipient completes
      transition=immediate-reopen result=false error=true
      current-recipient=new-document completed; ten cases passed
    EVIDENCE/laptop/laptop-patch-head-native-focused.log:45–49
      older-manager four cases passed
      Test run with 9 tests in 3 suites passed after 31.181 seconds. EXIT=0

Other negative results remain material: A's base unload/reopen and replacement attempts time out at planning with no test-start marker; these are noncompletion, not assertion-red. Its base forbidden-frame filter reports No matching test cases were run, not coverage. A's experience selection fails with Keychain -60006 (10 tests / 3 suites, EXIT=1). B sweep run2 aborts on an uncalled download completion handler (signal 6); run3 has a miniaturize wait failure and Keychain -61 failures without a completed summary. The saved sweep script has nine exclusion-regex alternatives; the completed log lacks exact argv and earlier filters evolved. Exclusions/crashes are not passes, and not every failure/exclusion is independently matched on base.

### Gateway and focused TypeScript proof

New supplied focused tests: 65/65 in 3 files pass, EXIT=0. The same head tests with selective base connection.ts and handshake-auth-log-limiter.ts yield 63 pass / 2 fail, EXIT=1; only the two native-refusal aggregation regressions fail. Both captures identify Vitest 5.0.5, test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts and:

    node scripts/test-projects.mts src/gateway/server/ws-connection.test.ts src/gateway/server/ws-connection/handshake-auth-helpers.test.ts src/gateway/server/ws-connection/handshake-auth-log-limiter.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

A real isolated loopback Gateway and synthetic WebSocket client receive connect.challenge and send 12 native-refusal closes (10, wait 31 s, then 2), plus 3 connect-failed controls. The selective base overlay emits 12 native +3 control lines; recorded head emits 2 native +3 control lines, with suppressed=9 on the second native warning. This proves transport logging suppression, not authentication success or app reconnect cessation. The final suppressed attempt has no later emitted summary; 2+9 must not be presented as accounting for all 12 attempts.

    EVIDENCE/head-ts-focused.log:127–135: 3 files passed; 65 tests passed; EXIT=0
    EVIDENCE/base-overlay-ts-focused.log:185–195: 63 passed; 2 failed; EXIT=1
    EVIDENCE/live-gateway-head.log:3–15: 12 native closes +3 controls; 5 warning lines
    EVIDENCE/live-gateway-base-overlay.log:3–14: same plan; 15 warning lines

These captures do not establish complete dependency/configuration/source-state parity or a combined app-to-Gateway run.

### Formatting and lint — scopes are not interchangeable

Supplied SwiftFormat lint reports 0/416 files requiring formatting (6 skipped), then0/33, with one combined EXIT=0. It is not compilation or a blanket touched-test lint pass.

Both normal SwiftLint captures report 1 serious violation / 419 files, EXIT=2: DashboardManager.swift file_length 1505 >1500. Source comparison now independently establishes that DashboardManager.swift is byte-identical at admitted base 3a, recorded f56 and this candidate (SHA-256 896a2f6f9c430ab7cacde9f0345e43b26c809e4ce012e0965f713d0d51d5ec64). The PR does not introduce this failure. Current main has a separate provider addition, not identical bytes; it is not claimed lint-clean.

The additional explicit touched-file capture reports 60 serious violations / 5 files, EXIT=2, in the test-file inputs; DashboardWindowController.swift has no diagnostic there. This negative result is retained, not called green or silently attributed to base. Exact touched-command flags/effective config/version are absent from the bundle, so its 60 findings cannot be equated to the standard invocation.

The pinned standard owner is scripts/lint-swift.sh macos → run-swiftlint.mts --strict --config config/swiftlint.yml, plus the swabble config. Those wrappers/configs are unchanged across admitted base, f56, candidate and inspected current main. The standard config includes Sources roots, not the explicit test-file list. Its 1500 file-length warning becomes serious under local strict mode; the existing wrapper treats limit rules as advisory only in genuine GitHub Actions. This is source-policy inspection, not an executed CI/lint pass; no flags, baselines, exclusions or rules were weakened. The standard format wrapper also checks declared Sources roots, not every test file.

### Historical proof kept separate

Historical local October 27 validation leading to f69148d4cbef51ff1586c74a87637071b9ede57d: 67 tests /5 files passed (40.39s), targeted TypeScript lint/typecheck/format/diff checks passed. An isolated Gateway run observed 3 refused closes → 2 warnings including suppressed=1, another signed client remained connected, and a later signed reconnect received hello. Native-auth UI recovery 29 passed; draft-commit persistence 1 passed. The new 65-test bundle neither contains that historical terminal run nor independently reproduces it. Neither number is a new-head rerun.

The preconnect consolidation preserved 28 named tests and 38 transferred assertions; original/replacement overlap 36 passed and deliberate producer omissions failed the retained old/new guard families. Counted TypeScript test delta remains −24 with no baseline/counting-policy exception; these inputs are unchanged by the notification-test correction. [Recorded f56 ordinary CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40537596408/job/122318487019), its test-line ratchet and [app/test-target compilation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40537596269/job/122307432139) passed. They are historical-head evidence, not current-head native execution.

### Current source review and remaining gates

Fresh Auto Review of the complete 12-file candidate against admitted base 3a: P0–P2 scoped-clean, no findings. Reviewed patch SHA-256 fb9a44316c87771416cdd5c746ba2c273e3f8d76b5bda6095f79a79be68e0452; expected tree 4d7f0fdfbe10ea8a93bdd46c0dd2ebba7a3a789d. This is independent static source review, not a hosted rating or native execution. Diff check passed. No configuration, protocol or persisted-data migration is introduced.

At this head, [ordinary CI and its required gate passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41266485953/job/124731698532) (60 jobs, no failures), including the [unchanged test-line ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41266485953/job/124730574678). [Current-head macOS Periphery app/test-target compilation passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41266485968/job/124730418174) (439.74s); this is not WKWebView test execution. The [durable hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185963#issuecomment-6444950457), reviewed November1 at02:54:58UTC for this exact head, reports high-confidence Ready for maintainer review, no findings and no Before-merge items. Its actual scores are overall3/6, proof3/6 and patch4/6. The optional rating improvement is a real built-app-to-Gateway close/reopen trace showing reconnect cessation; the requested overall Platinum threshold is not yet reached.

The supplied production extract is from unpatched OpenClaw 2026.10.9: 14 daily rows total 27,898 refusals (27,896 principal-group rows +2 timeout-bearing rows). October 31 has 746 inter-line gaps, 734 bucketed 12–16s. It supports occurrence/cadence, not a verified closed-window cause or a fixed-app result.

Still open: exact-new-head affected native execution and reporter-side window-state correlation/real built-app proof that this loop ceases after Dashboard close. Newer-main validation is not claimed. Ordinary PR CI still excludes macOS execution under inspected main ebf13610e1b8b29462c68eb71e18450effe6fdc7; the existing trusted-main macos-swift(tests) dispatch is the maintained route. No full native-suite green is claimed.

</details>

Contributor credit: @etzelm reported and investigated the per-document refusal behavior.

prs.title: fix: bound Codex catalog startup and client cleanup
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/152886

## What Problem This Solves

Codex catalog startup can load the agent runtime prematurely and retain client work after its owner closes, while competing health refreshes can consume catalog admission during Gateway startup.

## User Impact

Catalog and client work keeps its existing owner, cancellation and cleanup boundaries. A canonically bundled Codex plugin can use the host's state APIs without mislabeling a locally patched archive as an official npm installation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the catalog factory available when the harness loads while deferring heavyweight authentication code and actual client/catalog requests. Close owned transport work, fence native catalog walks, and align the bundled harness with native Codex 0.159.3.

This branch also includes its inherited Gateway health ownership, catalog admission, fleet metadata and serialized build fixes. It contains six commits and 39 changed files relative to the release branch's common ancestor; the final Codex commit changes 24 files. It preserves installed-plugin provenance and the existing local-archive trust refusal. Host bundling uses the canonical package composer.

## Evidence

- 45 focused tests passed on the final source in 27.37 seconds; native version and npm lock checks also passed.
- The canonical Core build completed successfully, with source/dependency and process-closure checks preserved.
- The canonical bundled archive installed into an isolated private prefix. Its content inventory, bundled metadata and native 0.159.3 producer matched the packaged inputs.
- A real installed-loader check passed all three storage cells in 19.91 seconds: honest local archive refused; host bundle opened synchronous and asynchronous keyed stores; host-bundle selection with an unchanged global archive record opened both stores.
- A real isolated installed-CLI model turn passed in 17.05 seconds. It observed the pinned native app-server process and exact response marker, then closed its unit and removed private runtime state. It used a maintenance account, so it does not certify service-account credentials or production review jobs.

The full Core test/check suites and upstream CI have not run for this head. Fresh isolated nine-agent startup qualification is pending. This draft does not claim production release or review-job acceptance.

prs.title: fix(codex): pass /v1/responses client functions to the Codex runtime
prs.body:
Closes #113318

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on the Codex runtime, caller functions sent as `tools` to `/v1/responses` or `/v1/chat/completions` are never shown to the model. With a pinned or `required` `tool_choice` the request then fails with HTTP 502 (`tool_choice required a <name> tool call, but the agent did not produce one`); with an optional `tool_choice` the model can only answer in prose.

## User Impact

User impact: callers can pass their own functions, including a pinned `tool_choice`, to an agent on the Codex runtime and get the call back, the same as on the built-in runtime: a `function_call` output item on `/v1/responses`, or `choices[].message.tool_calls` on `/v1/chat/completions`. OpenClaw does not run these functions; the caller does. When a pinned or `required` `tool_choice` is still not satisfied, the request fails with the same 502 as before; optional-tool requests may still return prose.

## Why This Change Was Made

The HTTP endpoint already hands caller functions to the run as `clientTools`, and the built-in runtime turns them into delegated tools. The Codex runtime builds its own tool list and left them out, so the model only saw OpenClaw's tools and answered in prose.

This adds a harness adapter, `createAgentHarnessClientTools`, next to the built-in runtime's `toClientToolDefinitions`. The built-in runtime keeps using `toClientToolDefinitions`. The new adapter reuses the same delegated-tool contract and its supporting helpers:
- the shared delegated pending result;
- the attempt's `toolsAllow` cap;
- the existing name-conflict error, which the endpoint maps to HTTP 400;
- the same eligibility: no client functions when tools are disabled, for memory runs, or for a model without tool support;
- source order for parallel calls: Codex reserves each call's slot when it arrives, before hooks run.

Codex adds these tools to the thread's dynamic tools. The existing bridge wraps them with the usual hooks, and their terminal result uses the existing terminal-tool release to stop the native turn, so Codex makes no second model request. The recorded calls go back as the attempt's `clientToolCalls`, which the shared runner already turns into each endpoint's tool-call output.

Accepted edge cases:
- A Codex-supervised thread keeps its saved native tool declarations and cannot add caller functions; with a pinned or `required` `tool_choice` such a request still fails with the existing 502.
- Like `sessions_yield`, the stop is a native interrupt, so Codex may record an interruption marker after the call. Changing the function set between requests on one session is a dynamic-tool change and is handled like any other.

The reporter's fork PR (hddms-matt-bot/openclaw#1) took a similar direction on older source; this change was written against current `main` and reuses the existing delegated-tool and terminal-release owners instead of a Codex-only delegation path.

Maintainer decision: this adds `createAgentHarnessClientTools` to the private harness SDK subpath `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-tool-runtime` (documented in the harness attempt-runtime page). If the owner prefers another surface, the Codex side only needs the tools, the reserve call and the recorded calls.

## Evidence

- New regression tests, red on `main` and green with the fix:
  - `run-attempt.dynamic-tools.test.ts`: a client function is declared to Codex, its call returns `clientToolCalls`, the turn is interrupted, and no OpenClaw tool runs. On `main`: fails ("expected [ 'managed_task' ] to include 'submit_probe_result'").
  - The same Codex file also checks that no client function is declared when tools are disabled or the model cannot call tools (a guard; it passes on `main` too).
  - `agent-tool-definition-adapter.test.ts`: the harness helper applies `toolsAllow`, keeps the model's order when a later call finishes first, and raises the shared conflict error. On `main`: fails (helper missing).
- Focused files pass with the fix (Codex dynamic tools 19, adapter 29, adapter fires-once, `openresponses-http.test.ts`).
- Core, core-test, extension and extension-test typechecks, lint and format pass on the changed files; `check:changed` and the baseline ratchets pass except checks that could not run offline on the test machine (listed below).
- Test lines are net +96 against `main`, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/codex-responses-client-tools.txt`: one Codex boundary test and one two-case eligibility table that reuses the existing run-attempt harness (`startTool`, `createStartedThreadHarness`) and one short helper test in the existing conflict-check block.

### Real Gateway proof with a real model

Tested revisions: base `6c298cb69d8` (`main`) and fix `066157068b1`. The PR head `5ec4cd4a5f5` differs from the tested fix only by the test-line allocation record.

An isolated Gateway built from the tree, the real Codex app-server (`@openai/codex` 0.164.0) and the real OpenAI model `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` on the Codex runtime. The request is the reporter's: `/v1/responses`, `tools: [submit_probe_result]`, pinned `tool_choice`, `stream: false`; a new session per request.

| Tree | Requests | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| base `6c298cb69d8` | 2 | 2 × HTTP 502 `tool_choice required a submit_probe_result tool call, but the agent did not produce one`, no output items |
| fix `066157068b1` | 3 | 3 × HTTP 200, one `function_call` `submit_probe_result` `{"greeting":"Hello"}`, status `completed` |

```
[6c298cb69d8] RUN1 status=502 runtime=codex model=gpt-5.6-luna output=[] tokens in/out 140686/363
[6c298cb69d8] RUN2 status=502 runtime=codex model=gpt-5.6-luna output=[] tokens in/out 161571/348
[066157068b1] RUN1 status=200 runtime=codex model=gpt-5.6-luna output=[function_call submit_probe_result {"greeting":"Hello"}] tokens in/out 30180/41
[066157068b1] RUN2 status=200 runtime=codex model=gpt-5.6-luna output=[function_call submit_probe_result {"greeting":"Hello"}] tokens in/out 30180/53
[066157068b1] RUN3 status=200 runtime=codex model=gpt-5.6-luna output=[function_call submit_probe_result {"greeting":"Hello"}] tokens in/out 30180/48
```

On `main` the model spent several steps (about 140k input tokens) looking for a function it could not see, then the Gateway failed closed. With the fix the turn ends at the call: one model step, and the function is returned to the caller instead of being run.

### Gateway proof with a scripted model (more cases)

The same Gateway and Codex app-server with a local fake model that calls a function only if Codex lists it (otherwise it answers "Hello" in prose):

| Run | HTTP | Output | Model saw the function |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v2026.7.1-1` (reporter's release) | 502, same error | none | n/a (that release's mock does not record tools) |
| base `6c298cb69d8` | 502, same error | none | no |
| fix `066157068b1` | 200 | `function_call submit_probe_result` | yes |
| fix, same session, different function | 200 | `function_call submit_other_result` | only the new one |
| fix, same session, no functions | 200 | message "Hello" | none left over |

With the fix, the fake model received one request per call and no `function_call_output`, so OpenClaw did not run the function.

Proof artifice: the second table uses a scripted local model endpoint; the first table uses a real OpenAI model.

Proof gap: the streaming (`stream: true`) path and `/v1/chat/completions` were not run live; they share the same attempt result. `check:changed` checks that need network on the test machine (Bun format/lint comparison, `knip`) and the SQLite worker ratchet (no `rg` in the container) could not run there; CI runs them.

prs.title: fix(agents): Claude CLI turns hit output limits on discarded stream frames
prs.body:
Related: #153545, #184352, #186085, #166127, #159930, #111382 This PR no longer adds environment overrides. The earlier revision restored output-limit tuning that #111382 removed; it is replaced here by an accounting repair inside the existing fixed limits, the direction the first review recommended. No limit, setting or environment variable changes. ## What Problem This Solves Claude stream frames the parser throws away (thinking signatures, empty thinking progress ticks, block and message stops, message deltas) are charged their full raw size against the 8 MiB output budget, and every one counts toward the 20,000-line limit. In long tool-heavy `claude-cli` turns that framing alone stops the turn with `CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters` and loses the final reply. This change charges those frames a fixed allowance. Other record types are charged as before. ## User Impact On the 1,980-step tool loop below, current `main` stops the turn after step 1,744 and returns no reply; with this change the same loop completes all 1,980 steps and replies `DONE`. Per tool round the charge drops from about 4,700 to 3,590 characters, so a `claude-cli` turn fits about 30 percent more tool calls before the unchanged limits apply. ## Why This Change Was Made `chargeClaudeStreamJsonLine` charges each Claude stream-json line its raw length unless a narrower rule applies: #153545 charges text, thinking and tool-input deltas their payload plus 32 characters (#186085 extended it to frames carrying `api_message_id`), and #184352 charges discarded child messages a fixed 64. Five `stream_event` kinds have no rule, although the parser reads at most one small field from them: | Frame | What the parser reads | Typical raw size | | --- | --- | --- | | `signature_delta` | nothing (`cli-output-events.ts:491`: "opaque continuation material") | about 2 KB, up to 21 KB | | `thinking_delta` with empty `thinking` (progress tick) | `estimated_tokens` (`cli-output-events.ts:483`) | 343 | | `content_block_stop` | `index` (`cli-output-events.ts:330`, `:467`) | 243 | | `message_stop` | the event type (`cli-output-stream.ts:524`) | 227 | | `message_delta` | nothing (`src/` has no reader of `message_delta`; `readCliUsage` reads top-level `usage`, not `event.usage`) | 740 | The charge only feeds the budget; it never changes what the parser reads or emits. `measureClaudeStreamControlFrame` (new, beside the partial-frame helper) charges a matching frame 32 characters, plus the `estimated_tokens` field for progress ticks and any wire whitespace around the JSON: - Progress ticks and stop frames have closed, bounded shapes, so like partial frames they no longer count toward the 20,000-line limit. Each costs at least 33 characters with its newline, so the 8 MiB budget still caps them at about 254,000 per turn. Progress ticks still reach `onThinkingProgress` once per frame. - Signature and message deltas carry discarded content of any size, so they keep counting as ordinary lines, and at most 8 KiB of each line goes uncharged; anything beyond that is charged. A turn may therefore parse up to 20,000 such lines of 8 KiB (about 156 MiB) where the budget used to stop near 8 MiB. That is acceptable because the content is discarded, not retained, and the line and single-line limits still bound the work; a test drives such lines until the line limit trips. - The envelope check that #186085 added for partial frames (allowed top-level keys, `api_message_id` at most 64 characters, `thinking_display` at most 32, valid block index) moves into `readBoundedStreamEvent` and is shared by both helpers instead of duplicated. `thinking_display` is accepted only on progress ticks. - An unknown key at any level, oversized or non-string metadata, a non-numeric estimate, thinking text, an empty signature or an invalid index keeps full accounting, as does any key a future Claude Code release adds until it is reviewed. `message_start` and `content_block_start` stay fully charged because they feed parser state. #166127 (tool results) and #159930 (Edit/Write file echoes) discount other record types and do not overlap. ## Evidence **Real behavior proof (shipped entry point).** One `openclaw agent exec` turn per build through the bundled `claude-cli` backend, built from `main` (67c3c3abfa6) and from this PR at 21fe91648a317548ac92b8b278f8a6986979264e (the follow-up commit changes only tests and the test-lines allocation, so the production code exercised is the code under review). macOS, Node 24, Claude Code 2.1.296, `claude-haiku-5-5`, `--thinking low`, each run with its own temporary `OPENCLAW_HOME` and this config: ```json { "agents": { "defaults": { "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5", "models": { "anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5": { "agentRuntime": { "id": "claude-cli" } } }, "timeoutSeconds": 7200 } } } ``` Prompt: run `echo step-K` with the `exec` tool for K = 1 to 1,980, one call per message, then reply `DONE`. Each round is one tiny tool call, so most of the stream is per-message framing (message start, block start and stop, message delta, message stop, snapshots and tool results), the shape of a long tool loop. | Build | Exit | Result | Tool calls | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `main` 67c3c3abfa6 | 1 | `CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters` after step 1,744, no reply (2,174 s) | 1,746 (incl. `ToolSearch` and the cancelled step 1,745) | | this PR 21fe91648a3 | 0 | `ok`, final `DONE` (2,882 s) | 1,982: 1,980 steps, `ToolSearch`, 1 rejected first guess | The `main` run stops after step 1,744: the parser refuses the stream mid-turn, the in-flight call is cancelled and no reply is returned. In the head run the model first called a bare `exec` (rejected: the tool was not loaded yet), loaded `mcp__openclaw__exec` with `ToolSearch`, then ran all 1,980 steps; that rejected first guess is the single tool failure and the two extra calls. The working directory holds only the prompt after both runs. A pass-through wrapper on `PATH` copied Claude Code's stdout to a file in both runs, because the gateway does not log the stream of a failed turn. Replaying each file through `chargeClaudeStreamJsonLine` from both builds, fed the way the live transport feeds the parser (it consumes control messages first): | Stream | `main` accounting | this PR accounting | | --- | --- | --- | | `main` run (25,659 lines) | 8,392,097 chars, trips at line 25,649 (the gateway stopped within 10 lines of it) | 6,442,638 (77%), 12,254 ordinary lines | | head run, completed (26,847 lines) | 9,312,559 (111%), would trip at line 24,101 | 7,103,109 (85%), 13,912 ordinary lines | On the completed stream that is about 4,700 characters per tool round on `main` and 3,590 with this change.
main 67c3c3abfa6: redacted output ``` $ openclaw agent exec --config openclaw.json --cwd work --message-file work/prompt.txt --thinking low --timeout 7200 --json { "ok": false, "status": "error", "final": "", "payloads": [], "model": null, "provider": null, "sessionId": "", "error": { "message": "CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters; refusing to parse output.", "kind": "exception" } } --- stderr (filtered) --- [agent/cli-backend] cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown [agent/cli-backend] cli live session start: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-5-5 activeSessions=1 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=cli:claude-cli:owner: durationMs=2166285 error="CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters; refusing to parse output." errorName=FailoverError [agent/cli-backend] cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-5-5 durationMs=2166902 runId= error=CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters; refusing to parse output. [model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5 candidate=anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5 reason=format next=none [state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: written; agent=main CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters; refusing to parse output. exit 1 (elapsed 2174s) --- Claude Code stdout (1980-step prompt) --- tool_use blocks: 1746; tool results: 1748; last echoed step: step-1744 ```
this PR 21fe91648a3: redacted output ``` $ openclaw agent exec --config openclaw.json --cwd work --message-file work/prompt.txt --thinking low --timeout 7200 --json { "ok": true, "status": "ok", "final": "DONE", "payloads": [ { "text": "DONE", "mediaUrl": null } ], "usage": { "input": 2, "output": 4, "cacheRead": 42888, "cacheWrite": 93, "cacheWrite1h": 93 }, "toolSummary": { "calls": 1982, "tools": [ "exec", "ToolSearch", "mcp__openclaw__exec" ], "failures": 1 }, "model": "claude-haiku-5-5", "provider": "anthropic", "sessionId": "" } --- stderr (filtered) --- [agent/cli-backend] cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown [agent/cli-backend] cli live session start: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-5-5 activeSessions=1 [state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: written; agent=main [agent/cli-backend] cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-5-5 durationMs=2873510 outBytes=4 outHash= [state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: written; agent=main exit 0 (elapsed 2882s) --- Claude Code stdout (1980-step prompt) --- tool_use blocks: 1982; tool results: 1984; last echoed step: step-1980 ```
Redaction replaced run and session ids, hashes and temporary paths, and dropped repeated skill-loading lines. This run shape exercises stop frames and message deltas; it has almost no thinking, so the signature and progress-tick savings show in the captured-stream breakdown below. **Charge breakdown on captured streams.** Each line fed through `chargeClaudeStreamJsonLine` from `main` (67c3c3abfa6) and from this PR, applying the real limits: | Capture | `main` | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | 41,071 real records, Claude Code 2.1.310 (694 completed gateway turns) | 12,316,948 chars, 12,697 lines | 9,639,274, 9,099 | | One complete real turn, Claude Code 2.1.296 (Haiku, thinking, 8 tools) | 469,353, 130 | 444,427, 88 | | Four failed production turns (41 to 73 minutes, 283 to 448 tool calls), rebuilt from their transcripts (estimates) | 5.09 to 5.43 MB (61 to 65%) | 4.14 to 4.37 MB (49 to 52%) | The four production turns failed on `main` before #186085 at 109 to 114 percent of the budget; #186085 brings them to 61 to 65 percent, and this change takes off another 0.95 to 1.06 MB each. **Tests and checks** (Studio, macOS, Node 24, at 11b83ab6550): - `src/agents/cli-output-control-frames.test.ts` (new): 45 passed. Covers the Claude Code 2.1.296 shape of each frame kind (exact charge and line accounting), wire padding, index-less and child-attributed frames, the 8 KiB allowance (at, just over, far over, with padding), every metadata cap at its limit, and full accounting for each rejected shape above. It also checks that progress ticks and tool starts still reach the parser callbacks, that 20,001 progress or stop frames complete, that signature and message deltas at the allowance stop on the 20,001st line, and that progress, block-stop and message-stop floods hit the 8 MiB budget at the computed frame. - RED: with only `cli-output-stream-limits.ts` reverted to `main`, 26 fail and 19 pass. 21 single-site mutations of the production file (zero charges, dropped or moved metadata caps, `thinking_display` anywhere, unknown event or delta keys, no padding, empty signatures, no index check, skipping the shared envelope check, no overflow charge, larger allowance, line-count flips, no estimate charge): 20 fail at least one test. The survivor removes the `thinking === ""` guard on progress ticks; it is equivalent today because the #186085 partial-frame rule charges any thinking delta with text first, and the guard stays so the control-frame rule never discounts thinking text on its own. - All 11 `src/agents/cli-output*.test.ts` files: 277 passed. `src/agents/cli-runner/` (83 files): 978 passed. - `cli-output-partial-messages.test.ts` drops its empty-thinking-progress and signature-delta rows, which expected full accounting for the frames this PR now discounts; the new suite covers both shapes with their new charges. The net test growth (264 lines) is recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/claude-stream-control-frames.txt`; `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base 67c3c3abfa6` and `git diff --check` pass. - `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and `oxfmt --check` on the touched files pass. - `pnpm check:changed --base 67c3c3abfa6` passes every step except the dead-export scan, which lists 4 exports in files this PR does not touch (`auth-controller.types.ts`, `repository-dispatch.ts`, `repository-integration.types.ts`); `pnpm deadcode:exports` on `main` (67c3c3abfa6) lists the same 4. - Docs: `docs/gateway/cli-backends.md` ("Inputs and outputs") gains one sentence on the control-frame allowance. `CHANGELOG.md` is left to release generation.

prs.title: fix: retain WebChat participants when reply admission is busy
prs.body:
Related: #185225

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing participant attribution when an authenticated WebChat input is persisted while another reply operation already owns the session admission slot.

## Why This Change Was Made

The busy admission completion path already has the resolved session target and prepared authenticated participant. It now records that participant through the existing owner, guarded by the transcript recorder's persisted-input state. Restart recovery remains outside this PR.

## Evidence

- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/pr185353-behavior-proof.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose`
- Result: **1 test passed**.
- The proof starts a real local Gateway with a temporary SQLite state directory and a loopback OpenAI Responses fixture.
- Alice and Bob use separate authenticated WebChat profiles. The test records Bob's `sessions.list` result before admission, while Alice holds the provider response, and after admission releases.
- Before and during busy admission, Bob's Involving me query excludes the shared session. After busy completion, the same query contains exactly one session and Bob's profile is present in `people`.
- Before releasing Alice's held provider response, Bob's `agent.wait` remains `pending` or `timeout`, provider request count remains exactly `1`, and Bob's session is absent from discovery. The proof logs this as `busyBeforeRelease` and `providerRequestsBeforeRelease`.
- Replaying Bob's exact idempotency key returns the same run id and does not increase provider request count.
- Base/head regression evidence: on base `e990b80e`, the focused busy-admission regression failed `1/1`; on the PR head before this Gateway proof, the same focused regression passed `1/1` and persisted the profile participant.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check test/pr185353-behavior-proof.e2e.test.ts`, `pnpm exec oxlint test/pr185353-behavior-proof.e2e.test.ts`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The current main test-lines budget and justification are preserved; no dependency or lockfile changes are included.

Redacted terminal trace from the Gateway proof:

```text
real local Gateway / authenticated WebChat
aliceProfileId: <redacted>
bobProfileId: <redacted>
beforeBusy: []
duringBusy: []
busyBeforeRelease: timeout
providerRequestsBeforeRelease: 1
afterBusy: ["agent:qa:pr185353-<redacted>"]
duplicateRunId: <same as busyRunId>
providerRequestsAfterBusy: <unchanged after duplicate>
persistedUserMessages: 2
```

The proof records the busy checkpoint before releasing Alice's held provider response; `timeout` is the bounded `agent.wait` result proving Bob's run had not completed yet.

The proof uses only local fixtures and loopback services. It does not require Android, a cloud account, an external endpoint, or an external model provider.
