prs.title: chore(deps): update libterminal to 0.3.11
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Adopt the reviewed [libterminal 0.3.11 release](https://github.com/openclaw/libterminal/releases/tag/v0.3.11) in the Control UI terminal.

## User Impact

The terminal receives the library’s startup cancellation and streaming performance fixes. No OpenClaw release or version bump is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

Update the exact dependency pin and pnpm-generated lockfile. The strict seven-day dependency maturity policy remains enabled; an exception names only the reviewed `@openclaw/libterminal@0.3.11` release and documents its removal date.

Simplification pass: no new runtime machinery, production code, or tests; production/test LOC delta is 0/0. The existing terminal integration, Ghostty patch, engine requirement, and optional peer metadata remain intact.

## Evidence

- Local ClawSweeper completed the full committed-range review: base `40955c1ae1e8509b6ea89542848f02104a591767` → head `692b960abbcc2707a29eb20cab20cd83667b6d04`. No actionable correctness/security findings; medium confidence. Its offline review could not inspect the published dependency contents.
- Independently verified the published 0.3.11 registry integrity, provenance, release commit, and packaged guides. The library release passed 168 unit and 10 real-WASM browser tests, including startup cancellation, Worker assets, streaming, and teardown.
- Pinned pnpm 12.15.0 generated only the intended dependency resolution changes; lockfile supply-chain verification passed. `git diff --check` and outgoing private-data checks passed.
- Fresh exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41265599297) passed the UI tests, production/test compiler jobs, production UI build/performance, and browser E2E. [The terminal runtime shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41265599297/job/124728032739) passed all four terminal-runtime cases among 138 files/569 tests: selection copying, keyboard handling, tab disposal isolation, and document listener cleanup. No local consumer test pass is claimed.
- CI remains failed by an inherited Workboard lint error: `extensions/workboard/src/gateway.ts:350:11`, `typescript(consistent-return)`, “Function expected no return value.” The identical diagnostic occurs in [newer scheduled-main job 124726940937](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41265289027/job/124726940937). The gateway, lint configuration, lint runner, and pinned Bun inputs are byte-identical between that main revision, the CI main parent, and actual tested merge `2be2a759ffe0f2c81e708112b3aa48c7c11204f2`. prs.title: fix(ios): Dashboard, Desktop and Terminal pages fail behind Cloudflare Access
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Dashboard pages, Desktop, Terminal and the per-session Dashboard in the iOS/iPadOS app do not load when the Gateway is behind Cloudflare Access. The Dashboard pages showed only "This Dashboard needs a browser session", and the other pages loaded with no Access cookie.

## User Impact

User impact: after native Cloudflare Access sign-in, Workboard, Activity, Skill Workshop, Instances, Dreaming, Usage, Automations, Desktop, Terminal and the session Dashboard load on iPhone and iPad. If the grant is missing or the edge refuses the browser session, the app shows a native fallback with **Try again** and **Open Gateway settings** instead of a blank page. Access apps with binding cookies will still show the fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native app already holds an Access session, but the embedded web view never received it. The web view's own non-persistent cookie store now gets a host-only, Secure, HttpOnly `CF_Authorization` cookie before the first load. One shared gate (`AccessGatedControlUI`) covers every Control UI host so none can skip it.

Safeguards: the cookie is built from a validated `Set-Cookie` header and fails closed; the token must match a strict JWT allow-list; WebKit content rules block every request to the Gateway host, on any explicit or implicit port, except the admitted authority (cookies are not port-scoped); a retirement generation closes the sign-out race; sign-out, expiry and account changes unload the page and delete the cookie.

## Evidence

- Physical iPad Pro (M4, iPadOS 27.2) and iPhone 18 Pro against a real Access-protected Gateway: Workboard, Activity, Skill Workshop, Instances, Dreaming, Desktop and Terminal work (tester-reported, no screenshots attached).
- Unit tests (`CloudflareAccessWebSessionTests`) and real-WebKit tests (`CloudflareAccessWebKitTests`): the content rules compile; a non-persistent store keeps the cookie host-only, Secure and HttpOnly; a table test covers allowed and blocked URLs for custom-port and default-port origins, including the implicit-port-443 case; and a live WebKit test with two loopback servers shows that without the rules an image and a fetch reach the other port, and with the rules neither does while the admitted page still loads. Related Access, Settings hub, proxy auth, Terminal hub and render-smoke suites pass on iPhone and iPad simulators (Xcode 27.2).
- Full `OpenClawTests` on the iPad Pro 13-inch simulator: 1241 tests, 1 failure in `WatchApprovalTransportSourceGuardTests` (a source-scan expecting a string not in the source; no Watch files changed here).
- `docs/platforms/ios.md` documents the embedded-page behavior behind Access. No stored settings, keychain items or schemas changed, so an upgrade keeps existing Gateway settings and Access grants.
- Strict SwiftFormat 0.63.1 and SwiftLint 0.65.1 are clean on the changed files. An existing `function_body_length` violation in `AppleReviewDemoChatTransport.swift` is unrelated.
- Device builds used a free personal team with push and HealthKit entitlements removed.

Gaps: no before/after screenshots yet (fallback copy is new UI); sign-out, expiry, binding cookies and multi-gateway isolation were not exercised on device; the implicit-port case is covered by the rule table test, not a live request; no network traces or before/after screenshots are attached yet.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep settled-turn finalization inside dispatched transcript custody
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A detached post-tool run can complete its tools but lose the recovered final answer when settled-turn finalization switches from the borrowed session manager to a direct store writer claim. The caller can be left without the final answer even though the tool work completed.

## Fix

Keep manager-owned finalization inside the dispatched transcript custody and retain the private run's session identity. Store-backed runs keep their existing committed writer-fence behavior. The merge from current `upstream/main` preserves main's incognito-reader / delivery-authority behavior.

The PR delta is only the finalizer implementation and its regression:

```text
A src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.run-embedded-agent.finalizer-writer-rebound.test.ts
M src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/settled-turn-finalization.ts
```

`packages/ai/src/providers/google-stream.ts` was restored byte-for-byte to `upstream/main` and is no longer in the PR delta.

## Evidence at current head

Current head: `77375feb322958ab6f8e3c0e1b7e48d342d33d50`.

- The source regression drives `runEmbeddedAgent`, the built-in OpenClaw harness, real `read` execution, real `runEmbeddedAttempt`, settled-turn finalization, borrowed transcript mutation, and actual admitted-run revocation. Only provider transport and nonessential plugin/runtime discovery are isolated with adjacent `mock-isolation` annotations.
- The shipped-entry proof below repeats the detached borrowed-manager finalizer path outside Vitest/mocks, with a local OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint reached through the production `openai-completions` provider transport. It uses isolated temp state/profile/workspace and synthetic nonhuman session ids.

## Shipped detached-review proof

Redacted command:

```sh
OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1 OPENCLAW_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 \
  node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs /tmp/pr167892-shipped-proof.mts
```

Isolation/outbound gate:

- State, agent dir, workspace, and provider endpoint were under `<temp-proof-root>`.
- No installed runtime, Gateway, human-facing session, production config, credential store, or provider routing was mutated.
- Redaction scan over the public evidence found no raw IPs, phone numbers, API keys, or non-public endpoint URLs.
- Provider transport was not in-process mocked: the run used the production `openai-completions` transport against a local OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint with zero-cost synthetic responses.

Redacted terminal/log excerpt:

```text
[agent/embedded] settled post-tool turn lacked a final answer: runId=detached-review-proof-run sessionId=internal-session-effects-review-run-proof provider=proof-local/proof-model — running isolated finalization
[proof] artifact=<temp-proof-root>/artifacts/proof.redacted.json
[proof] exitCode=0
[proof] recoveredAnswer="The review completed."
[proof] borrowedTranscriptMessageCount=6
[proof] borrowedLastMessage={"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The review completed."}],"api":"openai-completions","provider":"proof-local","model":"proof-model","stopReason":"stop","responseId":"chatcmpl-proof-3","__openclaw":{"runId":"detached-review-proof-run"}}
[proof] privateDurableTranscriptMessageCount=0
[proof] providerCalls=[{"call":1,"path":"/v1/chat/completions","hasTools":true,"toolNames":["read","tool_call","tool_describe","tool_search"],"messageRoles":["system","user","user"],"action":"tool-call-read"},{"call":2,"path":"/v1/chat/completions","hasTools":true,"toolNames":["read","tool_call","tool_describe","tool_search"],"messageRoles":["system","user","user","assistant","tool"],"action":"empty-post-tool-answer-and-advance-private-writer"},{"call":3,"path":"/v1/chat/completions","hasTools":false,"toolNames":[],"messageRoles":["user","user","assistant","tool","user"],"action":"settled-finalizer-recovered-answer"}]

prs.title: fix #188929: record conversation turn instructions in the Codex trajectory projection
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: The Codex harness records its compiled-context trajectory event with only the rendered developer instructions, omitting the entire conversation-instruction component (`buildCodexConversationTurnInstructions`) that the same turn registers through the inference relay, leaving the host trajectory incomplete for instruction-level diagnosis (#188929).
- Solution: Include the same conversation-instruction component in the recorded `systemPrompt` projection, using the identical builder and arguments as the relay registration.
- What changed: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-turn-request.ts` (one component added to the recorded join); regression case and faithful `joinPresentSections` stub in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-turn-request.provider-review.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: The instructions actually sent to the model (the relay registration is untouched); the trajectory event shape and recorder API; the native rollout path; no instructions were added or removed at runtime.

Fixes #188929

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `context.compiled.data.systemPrompt` in the retained trajectory carried persona/skills/memory markers but not the conversation heading, inbound-metadata marker, source-conversation guidance, or current tool-bindings heading that the inference relay registered for the same turn.
- **Real environment tested:** This branch's worktree on Linux x64, Node v24.20.0, pnpm 12.15.0, driving the real `run-attempt-turn-request` turn-start path with the provider-review harness and asserting the recorded `developerInstructions` against the real `buildCodexConversationTurnInstructions` output.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  pnpm install
  OPENCLAW_TEST_FILE_LOG=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/trajectory.test.ts \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-turn-request.provider-review.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  before (production file restored to unmodified main, same regression case):
    × AssertionError: expected 'developer instructions' to contain
      'Current OpenClaw conversation instruc…'  (the recorded projection lacked the component)
  after (this patch):
    ✓ recorded systemPrompt contains "Current OpenClaw conversation instructions"
      and "Current OpenClaw tool bindings"
    ✓ run-attempt-turn-request.provider-review.test.ts: 15 passed (15)
    ✓ trajectory.test.ts: see suite result (all pass)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The recorded `context.compiled` projection now carries the same conversation-instruction component the relay registers (conversation heading plus current tool bindings), so instruction-level diagnosis sees the complete system prompt; runtime instructions are unchanged.
- **What was not tested:** A live Discord parent session was not re-run; the turn-start path is exercised through the repo's provider-review harness against the real builders, with only RPC transport and agent execution mocked. This host's `/` is world-writable without the sticky bit, so tests resolving the default rolling log path use the repo-supported `OPENCLAW_TEST_FILE_LOG=1` route, which CI does not need. tsgo could not run locally (GLIBC too old for the native binary); CI type lanes remain the guardrail.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-turn-request.provider-review.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: a native acknowledged turn start records `context.compiled` whose `developerInstructions` contain the conversation-instructions heading and the tool-bindings heading produced by the real builder.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: it fails on unpatched main with the exact omission from the issue and pins parity between the relay-registered and trajectory-recorded instruction components without mocking the builder itself.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: the trajectory recording composed its `systemPrompt` from `buildRenderedCodexDeveloperInstructions()` (plus an optional MCP diagnostic notice) and never appended `buildCodexConversationTurnInstructions(...)`, while the inference-relay registration for the same turn composed a superset that includes it.
- Missing detection / guardrail: trajectory tests asserted the recorded prompt and event shape but never compared the recorded instruction components against the relay registration.

prs.title: fix(agents): detached tool runs lose their final reply
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Detached tool runs can finish their work but lose the recovered final reply; a cancelled finalizer can also append that reply to its borrowed transcript after admission closes.

Supersedes #167892, thanks @ethanhawkes-gif.

## User Impact

Detached runs return their recovered answer through the original transcript, and revoked runs cannot persist a late answer. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing harness admission for tool-free finalization, retain its native registration fingerprint, and carry the live run assertion into the borrowed manager's write admission. Current main already retains child writer context (#140399) and serializes session turns (#175837); these remaining finalizer boundaries still needed repair.

Production LOC is net zero (+43/-43): one finalizer parameter object replaces duplicate identity assembly, and redundant projection aliases are removed. The 210-line regression allocation covers the real runner/native-registration/tool/transcript composition that scripted backend tests miss.

## Evidence

- Unchanged two-case regression: **2 fail** on pinned main `7db5a3f79d186d617ae96fa48f64ebb2f8d49b91`, **2 pass** with this change. The affected production files also match newer main.
- Real `runEmbeddedAgent`, built-in harness, file write, native registration, private-session replacement, borrowed transcript and persistence. Only provider responses are scripted; no paid provider or production Gateway was used.
- Negative control: restoring harness admission without the manager assertion recovers the answer but persists it after real run admission is closed; the revocation case fails.
- Regression test time: under 2 seconds for both cases; cold wrapper wall time 38.3 seconds including compiler preparation. Broad CI passes: [run 41265778749](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41265778749).
- Seven affected harness, finalization, parent/child ownership, and prompt-prefix test files: **203 tests pass**.
- Reproduce with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/settled-turn-finalization.borrowed.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Focused typecheck (`core-test-agents-other`), changed-file lint/format and `git diff --check` pass.
- Codex autoreview: final local candidate against `7db5a3f79d18`, P0–P2, **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. No reviewer configuration was changed.
- Contributor code was read through GitHub and was never checked out or executed on this host.

Hosted ClawSweeper review of `d4bacc15eb75`: [no findings or before-merge work](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189984#issuecomment-6552454420).

prs.title: fix(oc-path): descend into JSONL line values when ** spans the line slot
prs.body:
Fixes #189957

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw path find 'oc://session.jsonl/**/event'` misses values nested inside a JSONL record, even though an explicit line selector followed by recursive descent finds them. Bare `**` also omits nested values.

## User Impact

Recursive JSONL searches now return the matching nested values with valid, reusable physical-line addresses. Existing non-recursive searches and JSON/YAML recursion are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing recursive walker consumes both the line address and JSON keys, but its slot packer groups them into a section such as `L2.nest.deep`. JSONL resolution requires the section to contain only the line address, so the final resolver drops the match.

Repair that producer: keep the line selector in the section and move consumed keys into the available value slots, preserving existing slot/depth limits and resolver validation. The format-local helper avoids copying on unchanged paths. No new syntax, setting, public API or fallback. Existing docs already define zero-or-more recursive `**` and JSONL descent inside each line.

@jerome-queck's commits, including the latest regression cleanup, are preserved. Regression coverage is consolidated into an existing table; its helper already round-trips every result. Whole-change delta: production+17/-1, tests+3/-3(net0), docs+2; no allocation increase.

## Evidence

Independent canonical runtime builds in secretless Linux Docker/Node24.22.1; real shipped CLI, enabled built plugin and isolated profile/config/state/workspaces. Twice on frozen main, nested `**/event` returns count0/exit1 and bare `**` returns only3 roots/line nodes. Twice on candidate, the nested match returns count1/exit0 and bare recursion returns all7 results. Every candidate address resolves through the real CLI. Non-recursive JSONL, JSON/YAML recursive controls and a size-bounded depth32 case pass; files remain unchanged.

Committed finder regression:2 intended failures/88passes on main; candidate finder/YAML suites130passed/2files, including expansion-budget and deep-path cases. Targeted lint/format pass. [Captured raw CLI output and exact source hashes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189960#issuecomment-6552483068).

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores missing recursive JSONL results; no persisted-state migration or write behavior change. Blast radius is JSONL recursive find output and its document-preorder enumeration. Newly valid results can appear earlier than previously discarded traversal routes. Non-recursive selection, physical-line identity, existing capacity checks and JSON/YAML behavior remain intact.

`redactSnapshot` was masking every `storage.encryption` string that looked sensitive, even when the value is ordinary encryption configuration rather than a credential. That hid useful diagnostics in config snapshots and made support harder.

This patch only redacts a candidate string when the value is concrete-sensitive **and** the key is either marked sensitive by a hint or sits on a sensitive path, so genuine credentials stay masked while harmless configuration remains readable. Ref #176229.

## Evidence

- Traced `redactValue()` through the config snapshot path: `storage.encryption` values without a sensitive hint or sensitive path now pass through unchanged, while hint-marked values still resolve to `[REDACTED]`.
- The existing config tests and lint/typecheck jobs pass on this revision; the change is limited to the redaction predicate.

prs.title: feat(cron): skip scheduled runs when a shell precheck finds no work
prs.body:
Supersedes #171738 and links the closed replay #112375. ## What Problem This Solves Scheduled jobs that poll for work still start a model turn when the inbox, queue, or watch target is empty. This supersedes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171738 and replaces the closed replay of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/112375. Those branches targeted the previous cron store and could not be applied to current main. This branch is based on current `openclaw/openclaw` main (`7559fb21a57059bd7483fb8c0a7117aff9794f92`). ## User Impact User impact: an operator can attach a host shell precheck to an `at`, `every`, or `cron` job. Exit code 0 continues into the trigger and payload. Exit code 2 records a skipped run with summary `precheck-no-work` and does not start the model turn. Denied, unapproved, timed out, or unexpected results fail closed and skip the payload. Agent turns cannot create or edit the command. Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/schedules#shell-precheck ## Why This Change Was Made Current cron jobs live in SQLite `job_json`, with validation in the cron service and execution in `executeJobCore`. The precheck is an optional field on that job, not a new config key or schema version. The probe runs through `createExecTool` with `nonInteractiveApproval` and no host-approval bypass, then the existing gateway allowlist and approval floors. `cron.triggers.enabled: false` disables it. Forced manual runs still run the probe; they do not skip it the way they skip a condition script. ## Evidence Local validation on `7712f5df3648054ff2bd2ecdd0c90d96b73d71c5`: - `pnpm test src/cron/job-precheck.test.ts src/cron/job-precheck-run.test.ts src/cron/service/timer-execution.precheck.test.ts src/cron/service/timer-execution.occurrence.test.ts src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-precheck.test.ts` — passed. Cron shard: 4 files, 86 tests. CLI shard: 1 file, 3 tests. The exec-policy file proves a marker file is not created when security is deny, ask is always, the job pin requires ask always, `toolsAllow` excludes exec, or run authority is rejected. An allowed `full`/`off` policy covers exit 2 (no work) and exit 0 (work). - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the changed TypeScript files — passed. - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check` on the 29 changed files — all matched files use the correct format. - `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed. - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test-services-cron.tsbuildinfo` — passed. ## Security review ### Threat model A precheck is an unattended host command. The realistic attackers are a model turn that tries to persist one, an operator who saved a command and later tightened exec policy, and a forced or restarted run that might otherwise skip the gate. The command can do anything the exec tool would allow, including reading or writing files on the gateway host. The feature must not add a second spawn path with weaker defaults. ### How approvals are enforced - The runner calls `createExecTool` with the resolved `tools.exec` host, mode, security, and ask, plus the live exec-approvals file that the tool already re-reads. It does not pass `bypassHostApprovalFloors`. - `nonInteractiveApproval: true` makes approval-requiring commands return `approval_required` before spawn. `ask: "always"`, an allowlist miss, and `security: "deny"` therefore do not run the command. - A stored `toolsAllowExecTarget` pin is applied with `pinExecToolTarget`, so a creator floor of `ask: "always"` still denies a headless run when global policy is `full`/`off`. - A defined `toolsAllow` that does not include `exec` denies the probe before the tool is built. - `assertRunCurrent` is awaited in `executeJobCore` and again inside the runner immediately before `tool.execute`. A rejected run does not spawn. - If the gateway does not wire `runJobPrecheck`, or `cron.triggers.enabled` is false, the job errors and the payload does not start. - Agent creates and patches that set a non-null `precheck` are rejected in the automations tool and again in `assertCronModelJobAllowed`. Clearing the field is allowed. `cron.run` of an existing job is not treated as authoring. - Invalid persisted prechecks quarantine the row instead of being dropped, so a bad write cannot fall open into an unguarded payload. - Each run re-reads current policy. A command saved under a looser policy is denied after the operator tightens it. ### Residual risks - Command payloads (`runCronCommandJob`) still spawn from their own runner and do not use this exec-tool gate. That path is unchanged. - Operators who can already persist command jobs can persist a precheck through the CLI or Gateway API. The protection is the run-time policy check, not a second save-time approval dialog. Reusing the stream approval dialog would describe the wrong effect. - `mode: "auto"` remains the existing exec auto-review path. With `nonInteractiveApproval`, a reviewer that approves can still allow a spawn. Tests pin `mode: "full"` so they do not depend on a reviewer. This change does not weaken or special-case auto-review. - When config omits security, the exec tool keeps its own non-sandbox default and the approvals file still applies its floors. That is the same default as other exec callers. - Exit codes are the only work signal. A command that prints a success banner and exits 2 is no-work. A command that exits 0 after doing nothing is work. Overlapping codes are rejected. - The probe runs on the exec host selected by `tools.exec` unless a gateway pin forces the gateway host. It cannot target a node or sandbox that the exec tool itself would refuse.
  
--- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > Introduces unattended host command execution on the gateway before scheduled agent turns, gated by exec policy but still a security-sensitive automation surface. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 7712f5df3648054ff2bd2ecdd0c90d96b73d71c5. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). Updated by merging current upstream main (merge commit `ce9c3641f4`); the precheck, occurrence and CLI cron tests (89 tests) and `pnpm tsgo:core` pass on the merged head.

prs.title: fix(codex): materialize native tool-output images from raw response items
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #153949.

Codex's native `ImageView` tool (and other native tools that hand back an
image) surfaces to OpenClaw as a raw `function_call_output` /
`custom_tool_call_output` response item whose `output` array contains a
nested `{"type":"input_image","image_url":"data:image/png;base64,..."}`
entry. `CodexGeneratedMediaProjection.recordRaw` (the Codex media owner)
only recognized raw `image_generation_call` items and returned immediately
for anything else, so this event shape was silently dropped.
`readCodexResponseOutput` deliberately omits non-text tool output from the
text transcript on the assumption that the media owner picks it up
(`extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-tool-output.ts:129`), so
the image bytes never reached the transcript or Control UI at all: the
assistant's reply referenced "the screenshot above" while no attachment
existed anywhere.

## What Changed

- `CodexGeneratedMediaProjection.recordRaw` now also inspects
  `function_call_output` / `custom_tool_call_output` raw items, scanning
  their `output` array for `input_image` entries.
- Each `image_url` is validated through the existing
  `sanitizeInlineImageDataUrl` guard (same validation already used for
  Codex history payload sanitization) and decoded via the existing
  `parseImageDataUrl` helper.
- Valid images are materialized through the exact same
  `recordImage`/`materializeImage` path already used for
  `image_generation_call` results, so they get the same size cap,
  concurrent-completion dedupe, and delivery/transcript wiring as
  generated images, and are marked as a side effect
  (`hadPotentialSideEffects`).
- Invalid or missing `image_url` values are skipped (fail closed): no
  placeholder, no partial write.

This is scoped to the raw-response-item media owner only; it does not
touch the `image_generation_call` path, billing/side-effect
classification for actual image generation, or the separate
dynamic-tool-image rendering path added in #120577 (which covers a
different event shape — dynamic tool results carried on typed thread
items, not this nested raw `input_image` payload).

## Evidence

New regression test, reverted against the pre-fix source
(`git checkout HEAD~1 -- extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-media.ts`)
to confirm it fails without the change:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts -t "saves a native tool-output input_image"
...
FAIL  |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts > CodexAppServerEventProjector media projection > saves a native tool-output input_image as reply media
AssertionError: Target cannot be null or undefined.
 ❯ extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts:394:34
    392|     const mediaUrl = result.toolMediaUrls?.[0];
    393|
    394|     expect(result.toolMediaUrls).toHaveLength(1);
```

Restored the fix and reran — passes:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts -t "saves a native tool-output input_image"
✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts > CodexAppServerEventProjector media projection > saves a native tool-output input_image as reply media 51ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)

Full relevant suites, all passing (89 tests):

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.replay-safety.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.final-media.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/tool-media-payloads.test.ts

prs.title: fix(agents): subagent results never reach the parent while a sibling waits for its reply
prs.body:
Closes #164334
Related: #164241, #158603, #161114

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a finished subagent's result never reaches its parent when another child in the same yielded batch has paused with `sessions_yield` `waitFor: "message"` and its pause notice was already delivered.

## User Impact

A parent that receives a child's "paused awaiting continuation" notice now still gets its other children's results as they finish, whether or not it has sent that continuation yet. The paused child's own result arrives separately after it resumes. Previously the parent stayed idle with zero wake attempts, even though `sessions_yield` had just told it the sibling's completion "will arrive as a later turn". In the reported case, that lasted about six hours until a human sent a message.

Plain `sessions_yield` pauses without a notice keep their existing one-combined-delivery behavior. There is no config, schema or migration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

A consumed pause notice hands the paused child's continuation to its requester. The child still sat in its frozen yield batch, and the batch waits for every member. The paused child was waiting for its requester, and the requester was waiting for the batch.

Consuming the notice now detaches that child into its own completion wave (`batchRunIds: [self]`), keeping its own completion custody. Frozen batch membership is mutual: wave selection, the wave's descendant scope and kernel outcome settlement skip a member whose own batch no longer lists the settling run.

Requester cron/operator authority follows the split. A yield authority still covers only its original cohort, requester session, operator and rearm generation, but each detached wave of that cohort can use it. It is narrowed as waves settle and released after the last one. Settled operator rows keep their binding, so a stray retry fails closed exactly as `discard()` already requires. The cohort rules and frozen-wave selection moved into small sibling modules to stay within the line caps.

Known limit, unchanged by this PR: the in-memory requester final attachment is keyed by the cohort's original run IDs and is never remapped. Resuming a paused child already created a new run ID, so a cohort containing a message-wait pause could not match it before this change either.

## Hardening and authority boundaries

- Each detached wave retains the original operator, requester incarnation and frozen cohort generation; no newer authority is borrowed.
- Admitted turns retain their own lifecycle while earlier waves settle. Custody releases only after both scoped work and admitted delivery acknowledgements finish; original-source revocation still cuts it off immediately.
- Exact admitted-wave retries may retrieve the Gateway's cached result, but cannot create new input/execution if the cached outcome is missing.
- Operators without Cron-management entitlement receive lifecycle-only acceptance tracking, never a Cron capability or new permission.
- No persisted schema, config option, orchestration registry or live Gateway change.

## Evidence

Raw red/green excerpts, reproducible commands, SHA-256 bindings, postcommit build metadata, and proof limitations: [proof behind the proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164366#issuecomment-5974580321).

Reviewable immutable source: [Gateway admission regressions](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/gateway/server.requester-pause-authority.test.ts), [receipt/lifecycle tests](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/agents/subagents/requester-cron-authority-cohort.test.ts), and [actual acceptance boundary](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-admission-phase.ts).

Exact candidate: `a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8`.

- **Real Gateway admission + SQLite proof:** `server.requester-pause-authority.test.ts` runs the public `agent` method through the actual Gateway handler, admission/actor identity and runtime stores. Original operator revocation, expired authority, requester reset, late retirement, cached retry, cache eviction and a retired delivery claim are exercised. The agent-command/provider bridge is synthetic; this is not a live model or ordinary outside-harness UI demonstration.
- **Non-Cron negative control:** an `operator.write` client with no admin override and no Cron entitlement originally reached execution/input staging twice after cache eviction. The repaired code replays without changing transcript/admission count, rejects cache-missing retry, and still delivers the next detached completion. Cron authority stays undefined.
- **Original-source liveness:** cached retries and their captured dispatch assertion reject independently revoked channel-owner grants and registry lifecycle rotation while the operator profile and requester session remain unchanged. The after-await case is owner-level assertion proof on a genuinely admitted/cached wave, not a raced public transport request.
- **Timing reproductions:** late-wave retirement, ambiguous sibling/final acknowledgements, and zero-scoped-turn unsettled receipts failed before their repairs. Immediate revocation remains covered. Prior fixture-reference errors are not counted as bug reproductions.
- **Coverage retained:** 18 Gateway cases and 37 authority/cohort cases pass; retirement tests were moved intact into a coherent sibling module to meet the line-cap ratchet. Existing registry/lifecycle/completion/outbox/codec cases remain.
- **Validation:** full `pnpm check:changed` passed including production/test types, lint, dead exports, runtime cycles and line caps. `git diff --check` and six-file format validation passed.
- **Independent review:** final full-delta autoreview through P2 is scoped-clean for this exact head. Earlier actionable findings were reproduced and repaired, not waived. The reviewer assessed supplied source/test evidence; its isolated sandbox did not independently execute the repository.
- **Build:** postcommit `pnpm build` passed in 378.64s; `dist/build-info.json.commit` matches this exact head. An earlier build was invalidated by removal of temporary review inputs during compilation; it was not credited, and the stable-namespace rerun passed.
- **CI/security:** current-head CI/ClawSweeper reconciliation and authorized upstream security approval remain pending. No merge/deployment has been performed.

prs.body:
Related: #64103

## What Problem This Solves

Agents reading session inventories lack an explanation of terminal-looking run statuses and can mistake them for permanent session or task completion.

## User Impact

The existing tool description and session guide now explain last-run outcomes and suggest considering a same-session follow-up before spawning replacement work, subject to current access and lifecycle admission checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

This follows the [narrow clarification proposed in the current issue review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/64103#issuecomment-4323766467). `done`, `failed`, `timeout`, and `killed` retain their existing meanings. A run outcome neither establishes overall task completion nor guarantees that another run will be accepted.

No wire values, output fields, schemas, runtime behavior, or admission checks change. In particular, this does not infer a `resumable` flag from status or promise that all terminal-looking sessions can continue. The reported duplicate-spawn cascade has not been deterministically reproduced on current main; this PR addresses the evidenced guidance gap and does not claim to fix that runtime behavior.

## Evidence

- Conflict refresh on main `f76e79be6a8`; current head `dabc114bb05dd2efaa529314c2cb111a7bef8d3b` retains the clarification and updates generated prompt snapshots using [remote generation](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/actions/runs/40625874783). [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40626164721) passed on this head. Earlier runtime evidence below refers to its stated earlier head.

- Running-Gateway proof on exact head `71f5e43e823366b069e440036711e82ffb2536a5` passed: an authenticated agent turn used the normal deferred-tool `tool_describe` control, and the next HTTP request to the loopback mock OpenAI Responses endpoint contained the complete updated `sessions_list` description. The captured description exactly matches the committed snapshot; `agent.wait` returned `ok`, shutdown was clean, and the process tree was joined. No task tool was executed.
- Inspected the canonically assembled model-facing tool description. The generated dynamic-tool JSON changes only `sessions_list.description`; input schemas and all other tools remain unchanged. The other three regenerated artifacts contain derived prompt counts and SHA-bound deltas.
- Existing description tests fail against the old text for both the default and Control UI-linked descriptions, then pass 10/10 with this clarification. Vitest duration: 0.681 s; total local wall time: 2.711 s. Per-test hosted CI time is not yet measured.
- Canonical prompt-snapshot regeneration and fresh check passed: all seven snapshot artifacts current.
- All `check:docs` constituent checks passed: docs formatting, docs/template lint, MDX, i18n glossary, internal links, config examples, and changelog mirrors. Internal-link audit: 14,930 links, zero broken; docs lint: 1,316 files, zero issues.
- Focused TypeScript lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings; the final seven-file diff also received a clean read-only scope and semantics review.

Validation used direct repository Node entrypoints with a read-only borrowed dependency installation whose manifest and lockfile match the candidate, plus isolated `markdownlint-cli2` 0.23.3. No dependency reconciliation or full installation was performed. Full build, full runtime suite, and full typecheck/`check:changed` aggregate were not run for this guidance-only change.

<details>
<summary>Focused commands and assembled guidance</summary>

```sh

Before spawning replacement work, consider a same-session follow-up; it still requires current access and lifecycle checks to admit new work.

</details>

The fixture used the production `startGatewayServer`, `GatewayClient`, `agent`/`agent.wait` RPCs, built-in OpenClaw runtime, normal Tool Search catalog, and OpenAI Responses transport. prs.title: fix(config): update config snapshot can tear the .pre-update rollback point
prs.body:
Addresses the "Pre-update config snapshot is non-atomic" item of #184894.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an update process interrupted mid-write of the `.pre-update` config snapshot can leave a torn rollback point at exactly the moment an update is in flight, losing the only copy of the pre-update config taken outside the rotating `.bak` ring.

## User Impact

User impact: the pre-update rollback point is published by a same-directory rename, avoiding a visible partial replacement during an ordinary interrupted write. This does not establish power-loss durability. An interrupted snapshot attempt cleans up after itself and keeps the prior rollback point usable.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createPreUpdateConfigSnapshot` wrote `${configPath}.pre-update` directly with `flag: "w"`, which truncates the existing file before the new content lands. The fix writes to a unique same-directory temp file (`flag: "wx"`, mode 0600) and renames it onto the snapshot path — the repo's standard temp + rename publication. A failed attempt removes its temp file, and the existing in-process coalescing marker still resets so a later attempt can retry.

## Evidence

- New regression test in `src/config/config.backup-rotation.test.ts` ("keeps the previous snapshot intact when a snapshot attempt fails mid-publication"): red on `origin/main` (the in-place write replaces the previous snapshot, so the older rollback content is lost) and green with the fix (previous snapshot intact, no temp leftovers, retry publishes the newer content).
- The existing suite passes unchanged, including "replaces a preexisting snapshot once per process" and the transient read/write retry test (#105431).
- `pnpm test src/cli/update-cli/` and the touched config suites pass; `pnpm check:changed` passes typecheck core, typecheck core tests, lint, and formatting. The only red lane is the pre-existing `deadcode` unused-export scan, which flags three exports in files this PR does not touch.

---

**Update (proof evolution):** the update-snapshot isolation proof (`runUpdateSnapshotIsolationProof`) asserted the snapshot mutates through a single in-place `writeFile` and blocked `rename` entirely. With atomic publication the proof keeps its containment intent but admits the rename path: `fsp.rename` is wrapped with fixture-root checks on both endpoints (instead of being blocked), `rm` stays blocked, the proof asserts exactly one temp write whose file no longer survives beside the rollback point, and the directory-tree delta assertion still requires that nothing but `.pre-update` is added. All four selection cases pass locally (`update-command-config-snapshot.test.ts`, pushed as c677d8552b4).

**Remaining proof:** No shipped update CLI interruption-and-retry run or latest-stable upgrade with existing state has been performed. The focused tests establish the snapshot owner behavior, not the full update journey.

prs.title: fix(config): preserve rollback snapshots when pre-update writes are interrupted
prs.body:
Supersedes #185021. Related: #184894.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an interrupted update snapshot write can destroy the previous `.pre-update` config rollback point and leave partial bytes visible to readers.

## User Impact

User impact: the previous config copy remains intact until its replacement is complete, and a failed snapshot attempt can retry. Malformed older copies remain refused by post-update recovery. This requires the updater taking the snapshot to contain the fix; it does not establish power-loss durability.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry kaguranananana's reviewed atomic-publication fix and updated isolation proof from c677d8552b4. The existing snapshot owner now creates a private exclusive temporary file beside the destination and renames it after writing. Failed writes or renames clean up and release the retry marker. No new snapshot format or recovery owner is needed: package rollback uses captured activation preimages, and the post-core reader already refuses malformed explicit snapshots instead of consuming them or falling through to a potentially stale `.bak`.

## Evidence

- Red on main 079889d5a091: a focused test writes a real partial file, then injects an I/O failure. The owner returns best effort, but a reader sees `{"gateway":{"mode":"` instead of the previous complete JSON. Exit 1 at the intended preservation assertion.
- Green owner suite: 14 tests, including partial-write and rename interruption, previous bytes visible during publication, cleanup, retry, permissions, and backup rotation. File wall time 8.40s, test time about 4s; new interruption cases 5–6ms each.
- Green post-core consumer suite: 8 tests, including a malformed `.pre-update` alongside a valid `.bak`, with no channels restored and no config replacement. File wall time 43.19s including import/transform; test time about 22s. Existing command lifecycle coverage is reused.
- All four fresh-process config selection isolation cases pass (54.65s file wall time). Separate processes are necessary to prove selection after importing under another home without touching operator state. All 26 focused tests plus three managed package/profile consumer tests pass; format and `git diff --check` pass.
- [Exact-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41262460016) passed completely (attempt 1, 1,404 seconds), including selected typechecking, lint, tests, PostgreSQL conformance, and CI/security/dependency gates. The bounded local lint attempt timed out during boundary preparation; a queued Crabbox allocation was stopped before its payload. No broad suite ran on the production host.
- Autoreview: Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, medium, P0–P2, complete local candidate against 079889d5a091; `scoped-clean`, no findings. Hosted ClawSweeper reviewed the same head with no code findings; its requested upgrade compatibility proof is now complete below.
- Simplification: one snapshot owner, no new durable state or rollback validator. Source delta +18, tests +56; the separate 56-line test allocation covers the interruption/retry regression, isolation migration, and torn-input recovery case.

Proof: filesystem fault injection and real post-core command composition establish interruption and refusal behavior; the installed-package upgrade establishes existing-state compatibility. The [single-scenario stable-upgrade proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41262665301) passed on its first attempt: published stable 2026.10.9 to exact candidate d6889e4660ab through the updater, with existing-state survival assertions, Doctor checks, isolated Gateway startup, health/readiness probes, and status checks. The scenario took 1,194 seconds, with cleanup joined and no failures. Packaging, integrity, and npm 12 installation acceptance also passed. Existing JSON/JSON5 bytes and filenames remain compatible; the repair neither changes schemas nor adds fsync to the previously non-durable snapshot path. # What Problem This Solves

A signed-in warm dashboard reload still replaces board skeletons with a late sandbox widget.

# Why This Change Was Made

This experiment tested early exact-proxy startup and bounded cached height, preserving the sandbox security contract.

# User Impact

**STOP: the experiment fails admission and is being closed. Do not merge.**

# Evidence

Head: `2750fa29222b082a7c4e205184140915ae4b6cdb`. Baseline: `183327d2319a5e86ad8a9b17e58320e172770305`. Experiment: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189777. No merge or ready PR.

The candidate fails the predeclared gate. Complete widget pixels improve by a paired median 236.778 ms (10/11 better), below the required 300 ms. Dashboard hello handling regresses by a paired median 62.376 ms in 9/11 pairs, above max(10 ms, 3%) = 15.404 ms. The A/A hello distribution has mixed signs (6/11 worse, paired median +15.173 ms). Earlier first-colored-pixel detection overstates the primary improvement because three candidate captures are clipped before their complete widget frame. No sandbox-security change is proposed.

## Scope and method

One quiet AWS c7a.4xlarge, 16 CPUs, repo Chromium 156.0.8078.4; CPU idle before A/A 93.31%, before A/B 91.95%. Eleven interleaved A/A pairs and eleven interleaved baseline/candidate pairs on each route. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: confirmed merges can leave a checkout pending cleanup without showing the native command that completes that cleanup.

## User Impact

Operators receive the scoped cleanup command and a receipt-safe finalization sequence after releasing the checkout. No background retry is implied.

prs.title: fix(tools): accept optional boolean in read tool input schema
prs.body:
Closes #189440

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `read` tool calls fail validation with `optional: must be equal to constant` when a model provides `"optional": false`.

## User Impact

User impact: Models that explicitly pass `"optional": false` to indicate a file is required (such as small models like `gpt-5.4-mini`) will no longer fail argument validation, avoiding unnecessary model round trips and aborted turns.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `readToolInputSchema` previously declared `optional` as `Type.Optional(Type.Literal(true))`, which strictly rejected `"optional": false`. Changing it to `Type.Optional(Type.Boolean())` allows boolean values while preserving the existing behavior: `read.ts` continues to treat `optional !== true` as non-optional (throwing on missing paths), and `optional: true` as optional (returning structured `not_found`).

Alongside the schema update:
- Updated Code Mode catalog expectation in `src/agents/code-mode.test.ts` to expect `optional?: boolean` instead of `optional?: true`.
- Added validator-to-reader regression test in `src/agents/sessions/tools/read.test.ts` verifying that `validateToolArguments` accepts `{ path: "...", optional: false }` for existing files and throws an error when the path does not exist.

## Evidence

- Unit tests in `src/agents/sessions/tools/read.test.ts`:
  - `accepts optional: false for existing files and throws for missing files through validation` passes.
- Code mode hint test in `src/agents/code-mode.test.ts`:
  - Passes with updated `optional?: boolean` type signature.
- Verification trace:
  - Input: `{"path": "present.txt", "optional": false}` -> `validateToolArguments` succeeds (`validated.optional === false`), reader returns file contents.
  - Missing file input: `{"path": "missing.txt", "optional": false}` -> `validateToolArguments` succeeds, reader throws file not found error.

prs.title: fix(cron): let Doctor recover migrated Codex automations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #189908.

Migrated `heartbeat-main` automations on an explicitly selected Codex runtime remained unbound after repeated `openclaw doctor --fix` runs, then failed the inference-account safety check.

## User Impact

Doctor can record the host-managed OpenAI account that the Codex run would use, together with its runtime, while preserving inherited models and fallbacks. The refusal leads with explicit account adoption and limits its Doctor hint to eligible host-managed accounts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The blanket runtime skip conflated Codex selection with native account ownership. Doctor now passes Codex facts to the existing auth planner for every probe and records a stored account only when the current plan selects one. Native/implicit authentication stays unbound; locked-session, account authorization, revocation, backup, and transaction safeguards remain in place.

Related: #189939. Thanks to @Satoshi-Kusumoto for the diagnosis and recovery-message guidance, reimplemented here with commit-author credit. This working repair supersedes that PR's blanket statement that Doctor never handles explicitly selected Codex runtimes.

## Evidence

- The committed owner regression is red against main `079889d5a09102246b34b363ff340591729d5a80`: repairing twice followed by scheduled auth throws the issue's original `Automation has no recorded inference account ... or with openclaw doctor --fix` refusal. Restoring the fix makes all three runtime-source cases pass (model, provider, session override).
- Focused validation: **40 tests passed** across Doctor account migration, real-runner account continuity/refusal, inference-binding execution, and prompt-prefix stability. Total 195.54s; the Doctor file took 58.45s including its existing full-Doctor tests. The three new owner cases took 3.832s / 2.108s / 2.679s.
- Full process regression: the exact persisted migrated `heartbeat-main` shape, explicit Codex runtime, Doctor CLI twice, separate isolated Gateway, and a completed forced cron run. The real Codex adapter sent the expected synthetic OAuth account before `turn/start`, and assistant history contained the result. **Passed: 72.07s total / 61.962s test time.** Uses the existing synthetic app-server fixture; no live provider or published-stable binary installation is claimed. A complete runtime build passed; test-only fixture iterations reused those identical production artifacts through the supported prebuilt-dist contract.
- Targeted lint, format, and `git diff --check` passed. Autoreview (Codex), P0–P2, reviewed the final substantive local candidate against `079889d5a091`; scoped-clean, no findings. A subsequent callback-variable rename fixed lint without changing behavior.

prs.title: fix(update): retain ledger diagnostics in failure reports
prs.body:
Related: #189921

## What Problem This Solves

Generated update-failure reports can say `Failed phase requested: exit unknown` when a matching restart sentinel has a null exit code even though the update ledger recorded a known exit and useful failure details. The optional top-level error was also omitted entirely.

## User Impact

Future reports retain recorded failure diagnostics and include recognized error facts. This improves reporting; it does not fix the update failure reported in #189921 or recover facts that were never recorded.

## Why This Change Was Made

Report preparation now fills missing sentinel step values from the same run's ledger, preserving the existing successful-retry precedence and mode/target fallback. Errors use the existing public diagnostic allowlist and a 200-byte budget; the 16,000-byte report limit is unchanged. No new raw logs, private fields, state, or update/recovery behavior are introduced. The reporting CLI or Gateway must contain the fix.

The two step-selection branches now share one merge. Net production growth is two lines. A dedicated 53-line test allocation covers the report-preview and error/redaction regressions.

## Evidence

- Red on main `6d5040f9f6e8390864fc4e2d834c709bb09bb851`: real sentinel builder + temporary ledger + `update.report` preview reproduced `exit unknown` despite recorded exit 23 and richer details; top-level error regressions failed because no error was rendered.
- Green: four focused files, 144 tests passed, using isolated state and timeouts (96.84 s wrapper wall time). Preparation: 75 tests / 41.40 s including cold compilation; Gateway report pair: 59 tests / 41.69 s; CLI failure reports: 10 tests / 8.94 s. After adding the fixture's required empty command field, the masking regression passed again (20.21 s wrapper).
- Targeted TypeScript, oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Shared autoreview, Codex engine, P0–P2, on the complete local candidate against the base above: `scoped-clean`, no findings. Included unchanged sentinel, report projection, step, and redaction owners as review context. The committed code is the reviewed candidate.
- Hosted ClawSweeper stopped before review at its input-safety gate and produced no verdict ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/41264642129)). The added token-like strings are intentional synthetic redaction fixtures; the complete outgoing patch was inspected. The independent autoreview above completed before this hosted attempt. No scanner policy was changed and no hosted clean review is claimed.
- Initial cold-ledger reconnect failures were traced to group-writable local scratch ancestry and reproduced with main code. Re-running in a private temporary directory passed all cases; no product code or assertions were weakened.
- Focused local tests only. No live Gateway, deployment state, or stable-upgrade test was run; the change only projects already-recorded report evidence.

- Exact-head [CI run 41263827043](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41263827043) passed (24 min 23 s elapsed, including PostgreSQL conformance). Required dependency/security review and aggregate CI statuses passed. Squash merged as `18fb74fb173eaeeebec02ce60cf4edc29ec57a29`, verified reachable from `origin/main`.

prs.title: fix(cli): preserve secret store results when cleanup fails
prs.body:
Closes #127544 (reported by @steipete).

## What Problem This Solves

Offline `secrets store` mutations can commit successfully and then exit `1` without a completion message when an independent expired-entry purge fails. A multi-name removal also stops before its remaining requested names.

## User Impact

Successful local `set`, `rm` and `import` commands keep their completion result and exit `0` when only retention cleanup fails. They emit one warning on stderr per command, including a multi-name removal. Primary mutation and ownership failures retain their failure behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR proposes **success with a cleanup warning** for the exit-contract choice in the issue, matching the existing Gateway's best-effort retention cleanup. It remains a proposal for maintainer review. The catch surrounds only the independent purge; it does not encompass the authoritative mutation, current-owner check, resource settlement or Gateway runtime refresh.

The existing command-output wrapper owns warning deduplication, and every mutation caller supplies that command's reporter. No storage implementation, transaction boundary, retention period, schema, version or public configuration is changed. The necessary production growth is 21 lines for outcome separation and command-scoped reporting; no new manager or exported test seam is introduced.

## Evidence

Validation base: `cdf14a50f59a5abe5ce3df008d3141e9e789f2cc`. The reviewed and validated file bytes were committed unchanged as `b928d1c4cfa979e8bed514c178c7039021f80f90`.

- **Real CLI/SQLite before:** a disposable expired tombstone was created with normal CLI writes under a fixture clock. An external Node preload rejected only the expiry kernel's native `DELETE ... deleted_at_ms < ...` preparation; the product schema was untouched. Actual `set` and two-entry `import` values were readable in independent CLI processes, yet both commands exited `1` with no success message. A two-name `rm` committed its first removal, then exited `1` before the second. This normal CLI reproduction took **73.82s**.
- **Real CLI/SQLite after:** with the same purge fault still observed at the native statement boundary, all three commands exit `0` with their normal completion and **one** cleanup warning. Both removal targets are absent, the set value is `debug`, and both imported values match. An independent primary-INSERT failure still exits `1`, emits no completion and leaves no value. All owned CLI process groups drained; **88.44s**. Private HOME/state/PID/network namespaces were used; no operator Gateway, external model or paid resource was used.
- **Committed regression:** the four selected cases were **3 intended failures / 1 primary-failure control pass** before the fix. The complete changed CLI suite is now **21 passed**; **112.96s wrapper wall / 102.10s Vitest**, mostly compiler/import preparation. The existing Gateway purge-failure/reload contract also passes (**1 selected case**, 11 unrelated cases filtered out); its handler still returns the committed result after purge failure.
- **Checks:** scoped production and test-consumer types, canonical typed lint, formatting, MDX, whitespace and line/max-line/test-line ratchets pass. The separate allocation is exactly **42 net new test lines**; the shared scalar is unchanged. Native test budget is **6,364,033 / 6,383,792**, leaving **19,759** lines.
- **Independent review:** canonical `autoreview`, Codex, P0–P2, **scoped-clean** for the source/test/docs. Its sensitive-filename filter omitted the public allocation text; that two-line metadata record was independently checked against its staged blob and actual +42 LF delta, with no findings. The filter was retained.

Recorded after-fix child-process stdout/stderr excerpts follow. Only ANSI color and private fixture paths/addresses are redacted; these are captured streams, not reconstructed command results. Values below are synthetic, non-secret env entries.

<details>
<summary>Actual CLI output with the purge fault active, plus the primary-failure control</summary>

```text
$ pnpm openclaw secrets store set LOG_LEVEL --kind env --value debug
stdout:
Stored LOG_LEVEL (env).

stderr:
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs secrets store set LOG_LEVEL --kind env --value debug
Secret store changes were saved, but expired-entry cleanup failed: synthetic purge-delete unavailable

exit=0
```

```text
$ pnpm openclaw secrets store rm REMOVE_ONE REMOVE_TWO --yes
stdout:
Removed 2 team store entries.

stderr:
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs secrets store rm REMOVE_ONE REMOVE_TWO --yes
Secret store changes were saved, but expired-entry cleanup failed: synthetic purge-delete unavailable

exit=0
```

```text
$ pnpm openclaw secrets store import --from <fixture.env> --yes
stdout:
Imported 2 team store entries.

stderr:
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs secrets store import --from <fixture.env> --yes
Secret store changes were saved, but expired-entry cleanup failed: synthetic purge-delete unavailable

exit=0
```

```text
$ pnpm openclaw secrets store set REJECTED_VALUE --kind env --value never
stdout:

stderr:
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs secrets store set REJECTED_VALUE --kind env --value never
synthetic primary-insert unavailable
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.

exit=1
```

</details>

Actual Node **24.22.1** / pnpm **12.15.0** satisfy this branch. The frozen installation's physical runtime lock matches the branch. Normal CLI build checks passed before and after; an initial offline build could not fetch lock-pinned native assets, so the trusted build populated its verified public package cache first. The CLI fault proof itself remained network-isolated.

This proves the Linux offline CLI reporting contract and real persisted mutations under a bounded injected cleanup failure. It is not a released-version upgrade/rollback, macOS/Windows or provider/model test. Gateway routing and its required runtime-refresh failure semantics are unchanged and remain distinct from retention cleanup.

prs.title: fix(ui): match palette session settings search against NFC queries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Command palette session settings filters machine and choice rows with `toLocaleLowerCase().includes` only. An NFD project displayName (or an NFD query) does not match its NFC form, so a user typing `münchen` can miss a project labeled `München` in NFD.

## User Impact

Searching workspace choices in New session → Settings by a name with combining marks can hide the project even when it is present.

## Why This Change Was Made

Comparison-side NFC is the established Control UI local-search pattern. Normalizing only the comparison copies keeps stored project names intact while making NFC and NFD forms interchangeable.

## Evidence

- Extended `ui/src/pages/new-session/palette-session-menus.test.tsx` opens palette session settings with an NFD project `displayName` (`München`) and asserts both NFC and NFD queries keep the `[data-project="muenchen"]` row.
- Red on base (HEAD production): NFC query returns no project row while NFD query still matches. Green with the fix: 6/6 suite pass including both NFC cases.
- Production change is comparison-side only in `ui/src/pages/new-session/palette-session-settings.ts` (`query` and the choice filter use `toLocaleLowerCase().normalize("NFC")`).

## Merge Danger

- Stacked on still-open NFC branches (login-search / model-providers / where-picker / session-sharing); GitHub may list those files until those PRs land. This change only touches `palette-session-settings.ts` and `palette-session-menus.test.tsx`.
- Does not change placement, preferences, or submission—only the client-side filter equality.

## What Problem This Solves

Automatic recovery cleanup tests spend avoidable CPU and memory deeply comparing complete file Buffers, including a real canonical SQLite recovery backup.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the real migration and fixtures, both different-content rows, Gateway-owner destination mutation, all physical-owner replacement phases, and every existence, row, retention, identity, hash, and ownership check. No hashes substitute for byte equality.

## Evidence

- Profiled before editing: about **1.49s** in Vitest equality under the remount case, on a **1,404,928-byte** real SQLite backup. One native comparison replaces per-byte JavaScript traversal and complete entry-array construction.
- **3 serial before + 3 serial after**, then **5 serial robustness runs**: all 18 cases passed in every valid run. Same Node 26.12.1, pnpm 12.15.0, Vitest 5.0.5, host, private dependency installation, temp root, and module cache.

prs.title: docs: clarify Codex pre-turn tool verification
prs.body:
Closes #167921

## What Problem This Solves

Operators could mistake a tool preview for proof of the final Codex tool surface before inference. The initial guidance also suggested `/diagnostics` for a routine pilot turn without explaining its upload consequence.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish provisional checks from evidence of an admitted turn, find a pilot thread in an ordinary harness session, inspect it using the correct native home, and see the upload consequence before approving `/diagnostics`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The docs explain the limits of pre-turn verification and identify saved policy, `tools.effective`, and `/codex status` as provisional checks. For a permitted pilot turn, they direct operators to `/codex threads [filter]`, qualify `/codex binding` for explicitly bound conversations, and explain how to inspect the native thread on the same host with the selected `CODEX_HOME`. They also explain that approving `/diagnostics` uploads Codex thread feedback and logs to OpenAI.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(cli): stop children after an early launcher disconnect
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174268 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174545

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a respawned CLI child staying alive when its launcher disconnects after parent binding but before startup installs the parent watcher.

## User Impact

An already-bound child enters normal shutdown even when its parent IPC channel has already closed. Detached update workers retain their independent lifetime; there are no configuration or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node clears `process.channel` before emitting `disconnect`, so the old missing-channel guard skipped the existing termination owner. Check the disconnected state after parent admission and before requiring a live channel. Reuse the existing idempotent shutdown and backstop.

This covers an already-recorded parent. Parent death before the environment marker is consumed remains a separate startup race.

## Evidence

- Real launcher-exit reproduction: four baseline failures on macOS Node 24.16.0/26.7.0 (preload and environment binding), then 16 passing repaired/admission/no-IPC/unref observations. These dependency-free probes require normal shutdown and output closure; cleanup kills and timeouts are not success.
- [Blacksmith Testbox proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41259288587), Linux Node 24.22.1: 38 tests passed across the respawn-process, maintenance-owner parent-lifetime, launcher-shutdown, and CLI-invocation suites. Tests took 30.18 seconds total; the changed process file took 0.782 seconds. Targeted lint, formatting, and the services test-typecheck passed. The delegated command exited 0 and its one-shot lease stopped successfully; the backing Actions step may appear cancelled during provider cleanup.
- Fresh independent review and local autoreview through P2 found no actionable defect. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its checkout had unrelated state; hosted review is requested through the documented fallback. The only post-proof changes clarify “Node” in a comment and test title, with final formatting/diff checks passing.
- Production delta: +6 lines for the existing parent/IPC lifecycle contract. Tests: +100 lines, with a separate allocation for the real-process ordering and admission regressions. No native compiled-runtime or live Gateway qualification is claimed.

Additional optional Scriptc interoperability proof: the [frozen native diagnostic](https://github.com/vincentkoc/scriptc/actions/runs/41264933842) passed 24 observations using [this PR's pinned helper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/17f92d91bdbe9164c6a9ca516542d30220de7ef5/cli-parent-lifetime.mjs) and Scriptc `8b9f7981e9198831474bbbe2eb47c48407daa380`: seven cases each under Node, native plain, and native ASan/UBSan; two compiled-parent-to-native-child parent-death cases; and one historical Node negative control reproducing the old late-watch bug. Cases cover disconnect, parent death, the existing 10-second escalation, unref, late watching, and wrong/absent markers. All 31 owned process groups drained without supervisor-forced cleanup; parent-death checks used adopted `waitpid` plus pipe EOF, with source/input readbacks and owned cleanup verified.

Native SIGTERM/work/exit paths were admitted to compiled IR; the helper and IPC transport remain in the Node island. ASan used `detect_leaks=0`, so this is not LeakSanitizer proof. This supplements the original Testbox proof; it does not qualify full Gateway, service, install/update, runtime adoption, or detached-worker behavior.

prs.title: fix: Control UI live replies stall after managed media directives
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Control UI replies stalling when a long response includes a managed `MEDIA:` line.

Fixes #185298

## Why This Change Was Made

The live projector filters completed managed media lines while preserving the canonical display transform for later text. It also keeps whitespace-only lines intact when prose continues after media.

## User Impact

Long Control UI replies with managed media keep streaming, with visible text matching the canonical display transform.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/live-chat-projector.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 8 tests passed, including canonical whitespace parity.
- `node src/gateway/proof-managed-media-stream.mjs`: runs the focused Gateway proof through the committed runner. The test feeds an assistant delta, a fixture tool result carrying the same relative media URL, then later assistant deltas with that URL marked managed. Production Gateway chat event handlers and the live projector emit the replacement before continued appends, remove the managed directive, preserve the blank line, and retain the absolute unmanaged control. The agent event source is stubbed at the existing Gateway test seam; this proof makes no external model request.

before: `MEDIA:chart.png` appears in the first Gateway delta before the fixture tool result.

after: the full replacement removes the managed directive before subsequent append frames, while canonical blank-line spacing remains.

negative-control: `MEDIA:/tmp/a.png` remains visible because it is an unmanaged absolute reference.

Tested head: `53b30bee1cc13cffc75b800e3114c1cdd9d230c6`.

```text
[gateway-stream-proof] assistantDirective=MEDIA:chart.png toolResultMediaUrl=chart.png toolResultBeforeActivation=true replacementBeforeContinuedDeltas=true frames=[{"state":"delta","deltaText":"Intro\nMEDIA:chart.png\nDone "},{"state":"delta","deltaText":"Intro\nDone again","replace":true},{"state":"delta","deltaText":"\n\nNext"},{"state":"delta","deltaText":"\nMEDIA:/tmp/a.png"}] visible=["Intro\nMEDIA:chart.png\nDone ","Intro\nDone again","Intro\nDone again\n\nNext","Intro\nDone again\n\nNext\nMEDIA:/tmp/a.png"]

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed | 17 skipped (18)
```

<details>
<summary>Gateway proof script</summary>

```javascript
#!/usr/bin/env node

import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";

const result = spawnSync(
  "pnpm",
  [
    "test",
    "src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat.test.ts",
    "--maxWorkers=1",
    "--testNamePattern=activates managed-media filtering after tool output before later Gateway deltas",
  ],
  {
    stdio: "inherit",
    env: { ...process.env, OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STREAM_PROOF: "1" },
  },
);

if (result.error) {
  throw result.error;
}

process.exitCode = result.status ?? 1;
```

</details>

The earlier live model run at `911eeb75f52a401b9ab1db7f66ec4c5db700be44` is not used as evidence for late managed-media activation; its built-in image read did not create the matching managed media reference.

The append-safe checkpoint follows the live-projection pattern in [#184543](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184543).
