prs.title: fix(agents): keep exec approval followup observation deadline on the monotonic clock
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an async `exec_approval_followup` run completes on the gateway, OpenClaw keeps observing it for a bounded 6-minute window before deciding whether to resume the originating session. That observation window is budgeted on the wall clock (`Date.now()`) but consumed by the monotonic timer that backs the gateway `agent.wait` RPC. When the system wall clock is adjusted (NTP step, VM clock sync, or a laptop waking from hibernation), the two clocks diverge and the observation window is distorted.

- **Problem**: `waitForAgentFollowupRun` seeds `observationDeadline = Date.now() + timeout` and reads `remainingMs = deadline - Date.now()`, passing that budget into a gateway wait consumed on the monotonic clock (`performance.now()` / `setTimeout`). Budget computed in one clock domain, spent in another.
- **Solution**: align the whole observation budget to the monotonic clock — seed `observationDeadline` and read `remainingMs` / `retryDelayMs` with `performance.now()`, matching the monotonic consumer.
- **What changed**: `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-followup.ts` (3 deadline reads `Date.now()`→`performance.now()`; per-wait budget rounded up with `Math.ceil` for the gateway `agent.wait` integer `timeoutMs` schema); the deadline regression test now controls the monotonic clock.
- **What did NOT change**: the transport retry/backoff policy and the observation lifecycle (reason `"deadline"`, `transportErrors` accounting) are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The observation deadline is a pure process-local closure (never serialized/persisted/cross-process), so a monotonic clock is the only correct source. The gateway consumer already computes its own monotonic `DispatchDeadline`; passing it a wall-clock-derived remaining budget is a cross-clock-domain mismatch. Switching the three reads keeps the seed and every remaining-budget read on the same (monotonic) domain, zero external contract change.

- **Best fix**: yes — one canonical owner, no new parser/policy branch.
- **Alternative**: keep `Date.now()` and rely on the per-wait `Math.min` cap; rejected because the cap only bounds a single wait, not the total observation window, nor the `retryDelayMs <= 0` exit from a forward wall jump.
- **Risk**: low — `Math.ceil` on the remaining budget never shrinks the observation window and always yields an integer accepted by the gateway validator.

## User Impact

Exec approval follow-ups for async commands now complete on a stable, clock-skew-proof observation window. Under NTP/hibernation clock steps, a healthy agent run is no longer prematurely declared complete (dropping slow terminal output), and a finished run is no longer observed far beyond its deadline.

## Evidence

**1. Shipped exec-host public-entry clock-skew proof, both directions.** Driven through the exec-host **public shipped entry** `sendExecApprovalFollowupResult` (`bash-tools.exec-host-shared.ts`) — the exact function `exec-host-node.ts` / `exec-host-gateway.ts` call after an approved async exec. It registers the handoff, then `sendExecApprovalFollowup` runs through the **production** `GatewayRecoveryRuntime` the Gateway registers at startup — **no** `registerGatewayRecoveryRuntime` override, **no** internal-function call. Both the `agent` dispatch (production `recovery.dispatchAgent` → real in-process `agent.run`, accepted against a synthetic-provider run that stays pending) and the wait (production `recovery.waitForAgent` → shipped wait transport) are unmodified shipped code. A 30 s wall step (−30 s / +30 s) is injected inside `waitForAgentFollowupRun` via a `Date.now` proxy; a pass-through probe on `recovery.waitForAgent` records the round-1 budget handed to the wait transport. (Observation budget shortened 6 m→20 s as a disclosed control; the per-wait cap cannot mask it.)

```console
# BACKWARD (−30s rewind)
[proof] production recovery runtime present = true (Gateway auto-registered)
[proof] recovery.waitForAgent budget timeoutMs=20000 -> shipped wait transport   # post-fix: BOUNDED
[proof] recovery.waitForAgent budget timeoutMs=49999 -> shipped wait transport   # pre-fix: INFLATED +30s
# FORWARD (+30s jump)
[proof] recovery.waitForAgent budget timeoutMs=20000 -> shipped wait transport   # post-fix: BOUNDED, observation proceeds
[proof] outcome=undefined elapsed=2652ms / NO agent.wait dispatched             # pre-fix: observation ENDED IMMEDIATELY (drops slow output)
```

| leg | skew | production-recovery budget (round 1) | window |
|---|---|---|---|
| post-fix | −30 s | 20000 | bounded |
| pre-fix | −30 s | 49999 | inflated +30 s |
| post-fix | +30 s | 20000 (proceeds) | bounded |
| pre-fix | +30 s | none (ends immediately) | drops slow output |

Keeping the budget on the monotonic clock makes the shipped wait budget immune to wall-clock steps in both directions. The accepted run stays the sole delivery owner (`direct_deliveries=0`; no competing direct delivery), and the integer `timeoutMs` passes the shipped `validateAgentWaitParams`.

**2. Integer-boundary proof (P2).** `performance.now()` is fractional; the `agent.wait` schema requires an integer `timeoutMs`. `sendExecApprovalFollowup` was driven through a recovery runtime whose `waitForAgent` re-runs the shipped validator on the exact params. Same fractional remaining budget (59999.75 ms), before vs after the one-line `Math.ceil`:

```console
before: [waitForAgent] timeoutMs=59999.75 -> shipped validator: REJECT
after : [waitForAgent] timeoutMs=60000   -> shipped validator: ACCEPT
```

`Math.ceil(59999.75) === 60000` never shrinks the budget; `Math.max(1, ...)` keeps the positive minimum.

**3. Regression.** Pre-fix the new test fails (`Number.isInteger(59999.75)` false); post-fix it passes, full suite green (18/18).

**What was not tested**: the divergence itself (NTP/hibernation) is injected by the proof; direct-delivery and session-resume paths are unchanged and covered by existing suites.

**Collision check**: `origin/main` still has the wall-clock reads (bug live); sibling PR #181942 touches the same three reads for the same defect; both open.

prs.title: fix(queue): stop exposing ignored timeout options
prs.body:
Closes #184737

## What Problem This Solves

Direct command-queue callers could pass execution-timeout options that the queue never consumes. The embedded-run controller owns execution deadlines after admission, while the command queue owns admission and scheduling.

## Change

The direct queue boundary now accepts `CommandQueueAdmissionOptions`, which excludes execution-timeout fields. Embedded-run callbacks retain the timeout-capable `CommandQueueEnqueueOptions` contract. This is a type-contract correction; deadline ownership and runtime behavior remain with the existing controller.

## Evidence

### Direct-call type regression

The same direct call was checked against the actual queue option declarations at base `main` (`60aaedd81245e7366998c4ea5c0956a503f7545b`) and PR head (`064d9132f9`):

```ts
enqueueCommandInLane("proof", async () => undefined, { taskTimeoutMs: 50 });
```

- Base: compiles successfully because the direct queue type includes `taskTimeoutMs`.
- PR head: rejected with `TS2353`: `taskTimeoutMs` does not exist in `CommandQueueAdmissionOptions`.
- The standalone strict `tsc` probe is the contract guard: it compiles on base and reports `TS2353` on the PR head for this exact literal.

### Gateway behavior

- Test: `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/gateway-timeout-recovery-subagent.e2e.test.ts`, “delivers a child completion once while parent timeout recovery is active”.

prs.title: fix(slack,feishu,zalouser): multi-line /btw and /loop arguments arrive on one line
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/185266

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in Slack, Feishu and Zalo Personal, a slash command with a multi-line argument (`/btw` with a pasted stack trace, a multi-line `/loop` prompt) reaches the command on one line, with its line breaks and indentation gone. In Zalo Personal this happens when the message mentions the bot.

## User Impact

User impact: Slack, Feishu and Zalo Personal users can paste traces, code and lists into `/btw`, `/side` and `/loop`, and the model receives them as typed, as it already does in channels whose mention stripping runs in core.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183606 made core `stripMentions` keep the whitespace of text that starts with `/`. These three channels build the command body in their own helpers (`stripSlackMentionsForCommandDetection`, `normalizeFeishuCommandProbeBody` and Zalo Personal's `stripOwnMentionsForCommandBody`), which strip mentions and then collapse every whitespace run to one space, so core never sees the line breaks. Each helper now applies the same rule as core: after mention stripping and trimming, text that starts with `/` keeps its whitespace; any other text is collapsed as before, so command detection for text like `Please /help` is unchanged.

Behavior note: a command followed by more lines (for example a mention, `/stop` and a second line) now reaches command matching with its line break, so these channels read it the way core already reads the same text since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183606.

Size: production +10/-10 lines in three helpers (the Zalo Personal one also drops an `if` around a `slice` that already returns an empty string past the end); tests +21/-2 lines (one new file beside the Slack helper, one case added to an existing Feishu inbound test, one test beside the existing Zalo Personal inbound normalization tests). No config, state or SDK surface changes.

## Evidence

Tested at `844005b38fa` (base `upstream/main` `e68d5552923`).

An isolated QA Gateway ran the real Slack plugin against a local fake Slack API with signed Events API deliveries; the model is the mock OpenAI provider, which records each request. The scenario sends a warmup DM (so the DM has a session), then this DM, and reads the `/btw` question from the recorded model request. Same scenario on both sides.

```text
/btw QA-BTW-MULTILINE why does this fail?
  at first (a.ts:1)
    at second (b.ts:2)
```

Before (base `e68d5552923`):

```text
Status: fail
model received the /btw question as "QA-BTW-MULTILINE why does this fail? at first (a.ts:1) at second (b.ts:2)"
```

After (this PR):

```text
Status: pass
receivedQuestion: "QA-BTW-MULTILINE why does this fail?\n  at first (a.ts:1)\n    at second (b.ts:2)\n"
```

Observed result: before, the model received the stack trace joined into one line; after, it receives the three lines with their indentation.

Regression tests, one per channel, each failing on the base and passing with the fix:

- Slack: the helper whose result becomes `CommandBody` (through `textForCommandDetection`) keeps the lines of a mention-prefixed multi-line `/btw`. `prepare.test.ts` already covers the collapse of non-command text (`Please /help continue`); it is over its line cap, so the new case sits beside the helper.
- Feishu: a mention-prefixed multi-line `/btw` added to the existing DM command test in `bot.test.ts`, which checks `CommandBody` and `BodyForCommands` in the inbound context.
- Zalo Personal: `normalizeZaloInboundMessage` keeps the lines in `commandContent` (the value `monitor.ts` passes as `CommandBody`) for a multi-line `/btw` that mentions the bot.

Checks: the touched tests (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, wall time per file at 844005b38fa in the table below), plus `extensions/feishu/src/sequential-key.test.ts`, `monitor.message-handler.ingress.test.ts`, `monitor.message-handler.debounce-policy.test.ts`, `extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/prepare.test.ts`, `message-handler.test.ts`, `message-handler.debounce-policy.test.ts`, and `extensions/zalouser/src/monitor.group-gating.test.ts`, `ingress.test.ts`, `zalo-js.listener.test.ts`; `pnpm check:test-mock-exports`, `oxfmt --check` and oxlint (type-aware) on the changed files, `git diff --check`; the broad suites run in this PR's CI.

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions/slack/src/monitor/commands.test.ts` | 2.3 s (1 test, Vitest 0.49 s) | 1 ms of test time (1 test) in `changed-extensions-config-3` (16 files, Vitest 91.84 s), CI run 40428675605 at 844005b38fa |
| `extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts` | 25.2 s (62 tests, Vitest 23.01 s) | 19.64 s of test time (62 tests) in `changed-extensions-config-5` (3 files, Vitest 26.51 s), CI run 40428675605 at 844005b38fa |
| `extensions/zalouser/src/zalo-quote-metadata.test.ts` | 10.0 s (12 tests, Vitest 7.87 s) | 1.97 s of test time (12 tests) in `changed-extensions-config-6` (6 files, Vitest 75.03 s), CI run 40428675605 at 844005b38fa |

`bot.test.ts` is an existing file of 62 tests; this PR adds one case to an existing DM command test.

Not covered, and why:
- No run in a real Slack workspace: the author has no Slack workspace for this, and the maintained Slack e2e lane leases its workspace credentials from the maintainers' pool, which the author cannot use. The Slack run above drives the real Slack plugin and Gateway, but the Slack API is a local fake and the model is the mock provider. The mock provider records the request the Gateway sends, so the after run shows the exact `/btw` text a real model would receive; no real model was called.
- No live Feishu or Zalo Personal run. The author has no Feishu tenant or Zalo account, and the QA harness has no local API for either. In each, the fix is the same rule in the helper that produces the command body, and its regression test checks the value passed on as `CommandBody` (for Zalo Personal, `commandContent`, which `monitor.ts` passes as `CommandBody`). For Feishu, that test goes through the inbound handler.

prs.title: fix(cron): owner-targeted automation failure alerts go to the last chat, not the owner
prs.body:
Closes #189947

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: failure alerts for automations with `delivery.target: "owner"`, such as heartbeats migrated by Doctor, go to the job session's last conversation or the channel's default recipient instead of the owner DM, or fail with `Delivering to Telegram requires target <chatId>` when neither exists.

## User Impact

User impact: for owner-targeted automations without an alert-specific route, failure alerts, including the auto-disable alert when it is sent on that route, now go to the same owner DM as the automation's own delivery.

- **No identifiable owner, or DMs blocked.** When no owner can be identified (for example DMs open with `allowFrom: ["*"]` and no `commands.ownerAllowFrom`), or `delivery.directPolicy: "block"` is set, the alert is now recorded as Not delivered and the existing in-app fallback notification is queued; the automation's own delivery does not send in these cases either. Previously such an alert could go directly to the job session's last conversation, such as another DM sender, or, when the session had no last conversation, to the channel's `defaultTo` recipient. To keep receiving these alerts directly, set `commands.ownerAllowFrom` (for an unidentified owner), or configure an explicit failure-alert recipient (`failureAlert.to`, `delivery.failureDestination.to`, or `cron.failureAlert.to`). The in-app fallback path is unchanged; where the fallback's follow-up turn sends its reply was not verified.
- **Alert-specific settings.** A `channel`, `to`, or `accountId` in the job's `failureAlert`, in `delivery.failureDestination`, or in global `cron.failureAlert` keeps its configured routing and does not inherit owner targeting.
- **Jobs that are not owner-targeted.** An alert that inherits the job's primary route now also honors its `delivery.directPolicy: "block"`: when the session's last conversation is a DM, the alert is blocked and recorded as Not delivered, as the job's own delivery to that DM is.
- **Upgrade.** When an alert newly inherits the owner target and the job already has an open failure incident with the same cause, the job may alert once more after the cooldown through the owner route. Repair-first handling and the auto-disable alert keep their existing timing. No config or schema change.

## Why This Change Was Made

With no alert-specific route, the failure-alert route comes from the job's primary announce target, the last tier of the documented route order ([`delivery.md` L163-L167](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md?plain=1#L163-L167)). Owner targeting (`target`, `directPolicy`) was added to the cron delivery plan in #179387; the alert-route projection carries channel, recipient, account, and thread only. Without `target`, the Gateway alert sender resolved the alert as an ordinary channel delivery (`channel: "last"` for the Doctor and setup shape) and did not reach the owner resolver that the automation's own delivery uses.

The alert route now carries `target` and `directPolicy` when it inherits the primary route and no alert-specific `channel`, `to`, or `accountId` is set in the job's `failureAlert`, `delivery.failureDestination`, or global `cron.failureAlert`. The dispatcher and the Gateway alert sender pass both fields to the existing `resolveDeliveryTarget`; owner resolution itself is unchanged. This follows the documented owner contract: owner delivery "does not follow the last group conversation or guess a recipient when owner identity is ambiguous" ([L118-L122](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md?plain=1#L118-L122)), and a missing owner route is recorded "without falling back to the last conversation" ([L124-L126](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md?plain=1#L124-L126)); see also [`troubleshooting.md` L60](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/docs/automation/cron-jobs/troubleshooting.md?plain=1#L60) and [`heartbeat.md` L171-L172](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/docs/gateway/heartbeat.md?plain=1#L171-L172). The route-order section of `delivery.md` now adds: "When this tier applies, failure alerts keep the primary target's owner targeting and `directPolicy`."

For owner-targeted jobs without an alert-specific route, the external alert send now resolves only a positively identified owner DM, or records Not delivered; it no longer resolves the session's last conversation or the channel's default recipient.

The route is computed per failure and not stored. The stored incident signature gains the target only when an alert inherits it, so a move from the session's last conversation to the owner counts as a changed destination ([L159](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540/docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md?plain=1#L159)). `directPolicy` is not part of the signature, and the signatures of all other jobs, including owner-targeted jobs with an alert-specific route, are byte-for-byte unchanged.

Unchanged: the owner resolver, alert-specific routes, repair-first escalation, the in-app fallback, the settlement of a blocked DM alert as Not delivered, and notices that do not use the alert route.

<details>
<summary>Which notifications use the failure-alert route</summary>

Every failure-alert intent takes its route from the same `resolveFailureAlert` result.

| Notification | Uses the failure-alert route | After this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Execution-failure alert (threshold and cooldown) | Yes | Inherits `target` and `directPolicy` with the primary route |
| Auto-disable alert for a recurring job, when an alert route is enabled | Yes | Same |
| Terminal one-shot failure alert, also used as the fallback of a repair request | Yes | Same |
| Required-delivery failure alert | Only through an alternate failure destination | Unchanged: explicit destination, no inheritance |
| Owner-conversation repair request | No: a turn in the owner conversation | Unchanged |
| Auto-disable notice when no alert route is enabled | No: in-app notice | Unchanged |
| In-app fallback after Not delivered | No | Unchanged |
| "Did not start" notice | No: session notice | Unchanged |
| Alert with no Gateway alert sender | No: goes straight to the in-app queue | Unchanged |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Alert destination before and after, by configuration</summary>

Owner-targeted job with no alert-specific route unless noted. Not delivered queues the in-app fallback notification in every row. "Alert-sender test" is the new Gateway test, "resolver test" the existing `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-target.owner.test.ts`, and "producer test" `src/cron/service/failure-alerts.account-routing.test.ts`.

| Owner identity and session state | Before | After | Checked by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Owner identified; last conversation is the owner DM | Owner DM | Owner DM | Source reading |
| Owner identified; last conversation is another DM | That DM | Owner DM | Alert-sender test |
| Owner identified; last conversation is a group | That group | Owner DM | Alert-sender test (session fixture) |
| Owner identified; no last conversation, no channel `defaultTo` | Missing-target error, Not delivered | Owner DM | Alert-sender test; live log (before) |
| Owner identified; no last conversation, channel `defaultTo` set | The `defaultTo` recipient | Owner DM | Source reading |
| Owner identified; `directPolicy: "block"` | The session's last route | Not delivered (`dm-blocked`) | Alert-sender test (rejection, nothing sent); producer test |
| No owner identified; last conversation is a DM | That DM | Not delivered (`no-route`) | Resolver test; issue reproduction (before) |
| No owner identified; last conversation is a group | That group | Not delivered (`no-route`) | Resolver test |
| No owner identified; no last conversation, no `defaultTo` | Missing-target error, Not delivered | Not delivered (`no-route`) | Resolver test; issue reproduction (before) |
| No owner identified; no last conversation, `defaultTo` set | The `defaultTo` recipient | Not delivered (`no-route`) | Source reading |
| Not owner-targeted; `channel: "last"`, `directPolicy: "block"`, last conversation is a DM | That DM | Not delivered (DM blocked) | Producer test; source reading |
| Any job with an alert-specific `channel`, `to`, or `accountId` | Configured route | Configured route | Producer test (`accountId` at each level, job-level `channel`); source reading for `to` |

</details>

## Evidence

Focused tests on `f47669efcec2` with this change (Linux x64, Node 24.22.1, Vitest on Node, `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`); the pushed commit `4697df95fb0c` has the same changes.

- `src/cron/service/failure-alerts.account-routing.test.ts` (extended), producer and dispatch: an owner-targeted primary route passes `target` and `directPolicy` to the alert route, including the channel-less delivery that Doctor and setup write and with an announce-only global alert config; the dispatcher forwards both fields to the Gateway alert sender. An `accountId` at each of the three alert-route levels, an explicit alert `channel`, and a webhook alert without a URL keep their own routing without the owner target. An open incident alerts again after the cooldown when its destination changes to the owner; an incident signature computed by the base code for a non-owner route still deduplicates; changing only `directPolicy` does not reopen an incident.
- `src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.owner-target.test.ts` (new): the alert route from the real `resolveFailureAlert` goes to the real Gateway alert sender (`sendGatewayCronFailureAlert`) and the real `resolveDeliveryTarget`, including its owner branch. An owner-targeted alert is sent to the owner DM (the final send's target is `111`) and settles as delivered when the session has no last conversation, has another DM, or has a group as its last conversation. With `directPolicy: "block"` and a DM last conversation, the alert is rejected with `Owner delivery unavailable (dm-blocked)` and nothing is sent. Mocked: session-store reads (the last conversation is a fixture), channel selection, and the final send (`sendCronAnnouncePayloadStrict`); the channel is a generic test plugin registered as `telegram`. Owner identity uses the test plugin's `user:` form; the linked issue's reproduction used a Telegram-style plugin with numeric IDs.
- No identifiable owner: the owner branch's outcome for a missing owner (and for a blocked owner DM) is covered by the existing resolver tests in `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-target.owner.test.ts`. By source reading, the alert sender throws on a failed resolution and the rejected send settles as Not delivered; rejected alert sends for other causes are covered in `src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.test.ts`.
- Before and after: without the production change, `failure-alerts.account-routing.test.ts` has 5 failed, 14 passed (19): the three inheritance cases (an owner target without a channel, with `directPolicy: "block"`, and with an announce-only global alert config), the dispatch case, and the post-cooldown owner alert; the explicit-selector (three `accountId` levels and a job-level alert `channel`), webhook, pre-change signature, and `directPolicy` signature cases pass on both. `server-cron-notifications.owner-target.test.ts` has 4 failed (4): on the base the alert failed with the test channel's missing-target error (`Telegram target is required`) when the session had no last conversation, went to the other DM (`999`) or the group (`-100777`), and with `directPolicy: "block"` was sent instead of being rejected. With the change: 19 and 4 passed.
- Partial reverts: reverting one part of the production change at a time fails the matching cases. Without the alert-specific selector check, the three explicit `accountId` cases and the explicit alert-channel case fail; without the job-level `accountId` in that check, its case; without the target in the incident signature, the post-cooldown owner alert; with the target appended even when absent, the pre-change signature case; with `directPolicy` in the signature, the pre-change signature and `directPolicy` cases; without the Gateway passing `directPolicy` to the resolver, the blocked-owner alert case.
- Test cost (Vitest Duration): `failure-alerts.account-routing.test.ts`, 19 tests, 34.05 s (transform 93%); the same file on the clean base, 7 tests, 34.36 s (transform 93%), so the time above 30 s is the file's existing module transform, not the added cases. `server-cron-notifications.owner-target.test.ts`, 4 tests, 8.89 s (transform 71%, import 22%). CI seconds: in this PR's CI, the 19 `failure-alerts.account-routing.test.ts` tests took 0.06 s in total (sum of per-test times) in their own Vitest shard ([`checks-node-changed-4`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41262655161/job/124719140732); Duration 39.88 s, transform 95%), and the 4 `server-cron-notifications.owner-target.test.ts` tests took 0.04 s in the `agentic-control-plane-runtime-cron` shard ([`checks-node-changed-compact-small-1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41262655161/job/124719140770); 10 files, 191 tests, Duration 72.41 s).
- Test lines: `config/test-lines-allocations/cron-failure-alert-owner-target.txt` records 303 net added test lines (140 in the producer test, 163 in the new Gateway file). prs.title: feat(voice-call): add optional Telnyx noise suppression for inbound realtime calls
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds an optional `telnyx.noiseSuppression` setting to Voice Call. When it is set, inbound realtime calls run Telnyx per-call noise suppression (`Denoiser`, `DeepFilterNet`, `Krisp`, or `AiCoustics`) on the caller's audio before it reaches the realtime model.

It is off by default. With the setting unset, calls without media streaming and outbound dials send exactly the same Telnyx requests as before.

## What Problem This Solves

Background speech from a TV or another person in the room reaches the realtime model as if the caller had said it. Telnyx can isolate the caller's voice per call, for example with Krisp's telephony voice isolation model.

Voice Call couldn't use that, because it starts streaming inside the `answer` command and Telnyx rejects `suppression_start` while streaming is active (422, code 90045).

## Change

When `telnyx.noiseSuppression` is set and the call streams media, `TelnyxProvider.answerCall` runs these steps in order:

1. `answer` without the stream fields.
2. `suppression_start` with the configured direction, engine and engine config. This step is capped at 5 seconds so the stream token stays valid. If it fails or times out, Voice Call logs a warning and streams without suppression.
3. `streaming_start` with the same stream settings the answer would have carried.

When the setting is unset, the single `answer` still carries the stream fields inline, unchanged from today.

The config is validated in both the manifest schema and `normalizeVoiceCallConfig`; `engineConfig` requires `engine`. The docs in `docs/plugins/voice-call/realtime-and-streaming.md` cover the direction semantics, the engine fields, and the Telnyx number setting below.

**Prerequisite:** set the number's own noise suppression to `disabled` in Telnyx. A number-level setting engages the default engine at answer, and a later `suppression_start` collides with it; Telnyx returns a 500 for that collision.

## Failure handling

| Step that fails | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `answer` (setting on) | Voice Call sends a best-effort hangup, then reports the answer failure. Telnyx may have answered before its HTTP response was lost; that answer carries no stream, so without the hangup the caller would sit on silence until duration cleanup. |
| `answer` (setting unset) | Unchanged. The answer carries the stream inline, so a lost response still connects media, and no hangup is sent. |
| `suppression_start` | Logs a warning and streams without suppression. The call continues. |
| `streaming_start` | Voice Call hangs up the answered call and reports the failure. |

Both hangups share one helper, and a failed hangup is only logged. This resolves the earlier silent-call window when the answer response is lost: the contributor-side cleanup option from the review is implemented in `2df6212`.

## Evidence

The live runs below are real inbound calls to a Telnyx local number through a source build of this branch, loaded as a bundled plugin. The setup used a Call Control app with number-level suppression `disabled`, a Tailscale funnel, OpenAI realtime, and `inboundPolicy: allowlist`.

Hostnames, call control IDs and the caller are redacted. Timestamps are local (UTC-5).

The current head, `d34caf48e06`, is `2df6212` rebased onto main `24015bf60cb`, plus test-only commits for the review's P3 findings; the two generated config baseline files were regenerated, and `docs/plugins/voice-call/configuration.md` was merged with main's new Twilio call recording section. Since `2df6212`'s base, the only main change to the Telnyx provider, the runtime, the webhook or the media stream is one line in `runtime.ts` from #189687 that passes Twilio's `record` setting to the Twilio provider, so the runs below on `2df6212` exercise the same Telnyx answer path as the current head.

### Upgrade from current stable v2026.10.8, on head `2df6212`

All runs used one profile, one state directory and one config file.

**A. Stock `v2026.10.8` (`dc2523e`), config without `noiseSuppression`.** Four inbound calls were answered and streamed. The first three ended with the model calling `openclaw_end_call` (`endReason=hangup-bot`). The gateway was stopped during the fourth call's setup; v2026.10.8 closed that record as `completed` on shutdown.

**B. Checkout of this branch (`2df6212`), same profile, config untouched.** `openclaw doctor --fix` ran the core state migration for the newer build. That migration belongs to v2026.10.8 to main, not to this plugin. After it, the gateway started and three inbound calls behaved exactly as before:

```
22:12:37.815 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:13:28.983 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=8fea48a4-... endReason=hangup-bot
22:13:34.990 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:13:55.616 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=05f267e5-... endReason=hangup-bot
22:14:01.298 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:14:37.845 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=0a54b7ad-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

**C. `noiseSuppression` added with `config set ... --strict-json`, no other change.** The config was Krisp with `krisp-viva-tel-lite-v1.kef`. The call was a normal conversation with no suppression warning and no answer failure:

```
22:15:40.991 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:15:42.112 [voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call 28ab70e0-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>, initialGreeting=queued)
22:16:14.703 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=28ab70e0-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

**D. Rejected `suppression_start` on the same head.** The model was set to a name Telnyx does not accept, and two calls were placed.

Both calls had `suppression_start` rejected. On the first, Telnyx's own `streaming_start` then failed to reach the media destination, and Voice Call hung the answered call up through the shared helper. The second call streamed without suppression and finished normally.

```
22:24:50.955 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:24:51.486 [telnyx] Noise suppression failed to start for call 70f2a343-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>); streaming without it: Telnyx API error: 422 {
  "errors": [ { "code": "10000", "title": "Invalid request",
    "source": { "pointer": "/noise_suppression_engine_config" },
    "detail": "The 'noise_suppression_engine_config' parameter model must be one of: krisp-viva-tel-v2.kef, krisp-viva-tel-lite-v1.kef, krisp-viva-pro-v1.kef, krisp-viva-ss-v1.kef." } ]
}
22:24:52.886 [voice-call/events] Failed to answer inbound call v3:<redacted>: call answered but Telnyx streaming_start failed; hanging up: Telnyx API error: 422 {
  "errors": [ { "code": "90046", "title": "Media Streaming failed", "detail": "Failed to connect to destination" } ]
}
22:24:53.750 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=70f2a343-... endReason=completed

22:24:57.684 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:24:58.077 [telnyx] Noise suppression failed to start for call 3e06844d-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>); streaming without it: Telnyx API error: 422 { ...same 10000 error... }
22:24:58.939 [voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call 3e06844d-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>, initialGreeting=queued)
22:25:17.777 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=3e06844d-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

Thirty seconds after the hung-up call, the existing realtime stream watchdog logged `Realtime stream WebSocket never connected within 30s` for `70f2a343`. That call was already finalized, and the warning had no effect on it or on the next call. The watchdog belongs to the stream token issued before the answer; this PR does not change it.

### Stored call history after the upgrade

These records were read back with `openclaw voicecall tail` on `2df6212` after legs B through D. They include the four calls that v2026.10.8 wrote before the upgrade:

| Call | Written by | Started | Answered | Ended | State | End reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 61706121 | v2026.10.8 | 17:46:45 | 17:46:46 | 17:47:32 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 368ae1dc | v2026.10.8 | 17:47:36 | 17:47:37 | 17:48:06 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| a7d22a6f | v2026.10.8 | 17:48:15 | 17:48:16 | 17:48:49 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 49b062ca | v2026.10.8 | 17:49:07 | 17:49:08 | 17:49:09 | completed | completed |
| 8fea48a4 | 2df6212 | 22:12:37 | 22:12:38 | 22:13:28 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 05f267e5 | 2df6212 | 22:13:34 | 22:13:35 | 22:13:55 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 0a54b7ad | 2df6212 | 22:14:01 | 22:14:02 | 22:14:37 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| c96579c8 | 2df6212 | 22:14:51 | 22:14:52 | 22:14:53 | completed | completed |
| 28ab70e0 | 2df6212 | 22:15:40 | 22:15:42 | 22:16:14 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 70f2a343 | 2df6212 | 22:24:50 | - | 22:24:53 | completed | completed |
| 3e06844d | 2df6212 | 22:24:57 | 22:24:58 | 22:25:17 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |

All 11 records in the store load on the new build with their original timestamps and end reasons, including the four written by v2026.10.8.

`49b062ca` and `c96579c8` are calls that were in setup when the gateway was stopped. Each build closed its record as `completed` on shutdown.

`70f2a343` is the streaming-failure call from leg D. It has no `answeredAt` because the hangup came before Telnyx's `call.answered` webhook was processed.

So on `2df6212`, all three live paths ran against real Telnyx: Krisp on, a rejected `suppression_start`, and a `streaming_start` failure cleaned up with a hangup.

The one path not exercised live is a lost `answer` response, which can't be arranged against Telnyx on demand. The unit tests cover it.

### Earlier runs (head `c1a26c2`, [comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183266#issuecomment-6458928065))

- Krisp in a room with a multi-voice video playing: the model stayed on the caller through English and Korean speech.
- The same rejected-suppression and streaming-failure paths as above.
- An upgrade from v2026.10.7.

### Tests

- `runtime.telnyx-answer.test.ts` starts the real runtime with Telnyx and realtime enabled and POSTs a `call.initiated` webhook to its listener. It mocks only the outbound HTTP edge and asserts the Telnyx commands for three paths: unset, Krisp, and rejected `suppression_start`. It replaces the constructor-forwarding test the review flagged.
- `providers/telnyx.test.ts` covers:
  - the request order and payloads,
  - engine field mapping,
  - the 5 second suppression bound,
  - fail-open on network errors,
  - hangup on a failed stream-less answer (and none on a failed inline-stream answer),
  - hangup on a failed `streaming_start`, even when that hangup fails,
  - unchanged outbound dials.

  The unset-answer case is folded into the existing streaming-answer test.
- `config.test.ts` covers the rejection cases.

## For the voice-call owner

This adds one optional block, with 10 config paths, under `telnyx`. It stays inside the existing Telnyx provider, and the defaults are unchanged. ClawSweeper recommends approving the optional capability. A maintainer decision on exposing it is the remaining item I can't close from the contributor side.

prs.title: fix: avoid Gateway stalls during workspace inventory and vector search
prs.body:
Related: #189277, #188913

## What Problem This Solves

Workspace inventory and cold vector searches still fork the large Linux Gateway directly, stalling its main thread. Inventory's parent-owned numeric file descriptors also prevent a simple substitution of the broker spawn function.

## User Impact

Workspace inventory, Git pack helpers, and vector workers use the existing small spawn broker. Inventory stdout is written to a broker-owned file; its bytes never travel through the Gateway heap. The Gateway receives completion and byte count. Gateway-internal helpers retain Gateway cgroup placement; agent execution intent is unchanged.

The output owner preserves exclusive `wx`/0600 creation, bounded writes, cancellation, launch authority, and cleanup. Unbounded stdout inherits a regular file descriptor; bounded stdout is checked and written within the broker. File completion joins child completion before releasing custody. Existing native fallback remains supported. Vector workers await pipe admission and retain their broker identity while reused.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Git owner must still select mutable tracked/untracked/ignored files. No upstream prepared inventory exists for this request; a commit or index alone cannot replace untracked/ignore selection. The fix moves process/file ownership instead of caching the scan. It removes Gateway stdout streaming, redundant file-output completion frames, empty pipe-prefix frames, and repeated option preparation.

Net production growth against `92b32cadcc30ddfd44a17c450d8ccfda9f75f6ee` is **321 lines**: inventory itself shrinks by one line, vector ownership adds 39, and the broker/file-output implementation adds 283. That growth supplies file ownership and completion/error/cleanup receipts that the broker previously lacked. Stateless command construction is extracted to keep the host within its existing line cap; admission and lifecycle state remain host-owned. Tests add 254 lines and the reproducible measurement script adds 423. No runtime configuration, cache, database schema, dependency, or protocol-version change.

## Evidence

The native-spawn regressions fail on the exact main parent: inventory reports the Gateway parent, and a real broker-context vector query produces a native host launch. The direct-file regression also fails on the earlier streaming PR head, where stdout is a pipe. Final Node proof passes **112 tests**, with five platform skips, covering inventory, file output, launch/close ordering, host settlement, handoff, execa, and vector queries. Earlier unaffected pack/sync and memory-owner sibling proof is retained. Bun fallback coverage passes. Codex P0–P2 autoreview is scoped-clean.

`pnpm check:changed` completed with inherited dead-export failures. Introduced lint/line-cap failures were repaired; affected core/script/test typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, wrapper inventory and line-cap checks pass. The inherited findings and exact-parent attribution are below. Exact-head [CI 41262700593](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41262700593) passed on `3cae33dc05750c1f63a836289bb8d9e70286c7a9`: 73 successful jobs, 26 skipped, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards. Build artifacts and Darwin PR tooling also passed; no reruns were needed.

### Final file-output measurements

Synthetic Linux ARM64/Node26.12.1/overlayfs fixture: **62,000 files, 1.143 GB**, parent about **2.2 GB RSS and 14,155 mappings**; small retained broker. Five interleaved before/after processes, first-owner and warm calls recorded separately, plus fresh baseline-only A/A. All output bytes are checked. No heap-sampling instrumentation runs during acceptance measurements.

| Warm median | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Inventory Gateway forks | 2 | 0 |
| Inventory synchronous spawn blocking | 60.878 ms | 0 ms |
| Inventory wall time | 82.354 ms | 25.462 ms |
| Inventory main-thread CPU | 37.578 ms | 2.110 ms |
| Inventory total CPU, including broker/Git | 81.331 ms | 22.908 ms |
| Inventory main-isolate allocation | 892,784 B | **619,816 B** |
| Pack wall time | 2808.604 ms | 2831.199 ms |
| Pack main-thread CPU | 31.178 ms | 5.774 ms |
| Pack total CPU | 2839.775 ms | 2854.649 ms |
| Pack main-isolate allocation | 4,964,760 B | 2,600,584 B |

A separate CPU profile records inventory-stack native spawn self time **167.208 → 0 ms**. All 30 measured candidate command launches avoid native Gateway spawning.

The candidate meets the predeclared **median** allocation ceiling of 993,800 B, with zero Gateway forks/blocking. Its five warm allocation samples are `[1138480, 624880, 610336, 619816, 607944]`; one exceeds the ceiling. Allocation p95 is 1,051,312 → 1,138,480 B (+8.29%). First-owner inventory allocation is 1,456,288 → 1,514,800 B (+4.02%), with wall time 81.402 → 31.023 ms. This is a median improvement, not a per-call allocation bound.

Final inventory wall p95 is 83.309 → 56.337 ms, ranges 75.610–83.309 → 23.413–56.337 ms. First-owner p95 is 91.253 → 32.621 ms. Pack warm p95 is 3121.285 → 3162.695 ms (+1.33%); first-owner pack p95 is 2830.338 → 3365.461 ms (+18.91%). With five samples, the reported p95 is the sample maximum; this does not establish production-tail safety.

Fresh A/A inventory wall medians are 76.310/71.239 ms and p95s 79.479/79.443 ms. Allocation medians are 1,085,632/978,784 B; ranges 786,104–1,210,784 and 846,056–1,107,664 B. A/A warm pack p95s are 2784.700/2829.774 ms; first-owner pack p95s 2844.307/2751.354 ms. The observed pack-tail increase is retained, not attributed away.

The rejected streaming version allocated 3.062 MB versus 0.994 MB. Its worse wall tails were: warm inventory p95 164.132 → 330.477 ms (+101.35%), first inventory 104.829 → 174.620 (+66.58%), warm pack 3450.688 → 4463.321 (+29.35%), first pack 3512.983 → 5703.050 (+62.34%). Its A/A first-inventory p95s were 283.243/233.237 ms and warm-pack p95s 4668.5/3609.2 ms; warm-inventory medians were 90.360/76.037 ms. Those tails were inconclusive under A/A. Broker-owned writing proved feasible, so the conditional acceptance of the extra 2 MB was **not used**. The first file-owned revision still measured 1,084,832 B; the final revision removes redundant broker work instead of selecting a favorable rerun.

Reproduce with `scripts/perf/workspace-inventory-spawn-measure.ts`: prepare frozen owners against the parent, create its synthetic fixture, then `--compare <proof> --fixture <workspace> --samples 5 --commands 1 --rss-mib 2048 --mappings 7000`; add `--control` for A/A. The script records bundle hashes. Filesystem caches are warm; first-owner is not cold disk. This is owner-level Linux proof, not full Gateway, x64, btrfs, or agent-database proof. This owner does not access an agent database; no production data was copied.

### Inherited main regressions

A clean detached exact parent `92b32cadcc30ddfd44a17c450d8ccfda9f75f6ee` reproduces the same six production/four full-tree dead-export findings (exit 1):

- `ChannelIdentityLinkAdapter` and `PersonalGitHubActionV2`: #188910 / `4674051ce50a1da3100962e4c2d29152d02a29fe` added an unused export and removed the last external consumer.
- Backup spool constants: `4fb684e294e27aed927548aaf64d2a7b8ba4696f` moved the consumer into its owner, leaving exports.
- Production-only `CHAT_SEARCH_HIGHLIGHT` and `syncChatSearchHighlight`: #170434 / `d5be7a6a42934658aacc09803c52d056b1fba29b`; external consumers are browser tests.

Later main #189894 / `cde4bfe4f10ce470ded7264c68d9a72ae03594cc` fixes the backup/chat findings. These are main regressions for follow-up, not passing checks or noise.

### Other direct-spawn audit

Inventory runs per workspace transfer/preflight/admission, not unconditionally every turn: two `git ls-files` calls, three with `.worktreeinclude`; the same helper also runs Git preflight and pack commands. Vector workers launch on cold database acquisition and are reused for 30 minutes, cap two; alternating more databases can churn.

Guarded remote-shell commands and persistent Docker START still launch natively per command to preserve final launch authority (#167571/#177942). Their execa path lacks the native broker's prepare/launch initiation guard; removing the overrides would weaken that boundary. Remote directory upload also overlaps open #162742. These need an owner-level guarded-execa follow-up. Other audited matches are retained tunnels/inference/watchers, startup/recovery, maintenance/CLI, platform-specific node-host work, or subprocess-side launchers. prs.title: feat(google): use the Interactions API for all Gemini text models
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#189395 made the Gemini Interactions API the default for Flash text models on the official AI Studio endpoint. Pro, `gemini-4-argon` and other Gemini text models still defaulted to GenerateContent, so the API-key `google` provider used two different Gemini transports depending on the model family.

## User Impact

User impact: every Gemini text model on the official AI Studio endpoint (Flash, Flash-Lite, Pro, the default `google/gemini-4-argon`, `-latest` aliases, and forward-compatible Gemini IDs) now uses the Interactions API by default.

Unchanged:
- Gemma models keep GenerateContent.
- Custom base URLs (proxies) without an explicit `api` keep GenerateContent.
- An explicit model- or provider-level `api` still wins. Set `api: "google-generative-ai"` on a model to keep explicit `cachedContent` handles, which the Interactions API does not support (it uses implicit caching).
- Vertex AI, Gemini CLI, image generation, speech, Live, embeddings, media understanding, web search and PDF processing keep their routes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Interactions transport reached parity with GenerateContent in #189395 (managed proxy/TLS, key rotation, OAuth bearer auth, tool choice, private video handling, upgrade replay). The default decision already lives in one place, `resolveGoogleModelApi`; this widens its rule from Flash to Gemini text models and lets live discovery admit Gemini rows that advertise only Interactions.

## Evidence

Live runs against AI Studio with this branch built locally (`agent --local --json`, isolated profile; endpoint from debug logs). All requests hit `/v1beta/interactions`.

| Case | Model | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tool call, then next-turn replay | `google/gemini-4-argon` | `exec` ran, `pro-tool-42`; next turn: `Tool output: pro-tool-42 \| Codeword: HERON-31` |
| Tool call, then next-turn replay | `google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview` | `exec` ran, `pro-tool-42`; next turn: `Tool output: pro-tool-42, Codeword: HERON-31.` |
| Thinking `off` / `low` / `high` | `google/gemini-4-argon` | correct answers at each level (`391`, `265`) |
| Long context, ~352k input tokens, needle at line 6123 of 9000 | `google/gemini-4-argon` | `MAGPIE-5150` |

Direct API probes with the same key: Pro, `gemini-4-argon` and `gemini-pro-latest` return 200 on both APIs. Gemma on Interactions returned its reasoning as answer text, so Gemma stays on GenerateContent.

Regression tests: AI Studio defaults for `gemini-4-argon` and `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` (Interactions) and Gemma (GenerateContent) fail on `main` and pass here; Pro, `-latest` and forward-compatible resolution expectations updated. Focused Google provider suites pass locally; CI runs the full suites.

<details>
<summary>Simplification</summary>

The Interactions default and native-video admission used two identical predicates (`isGoogleFlashTextModelId` after widening, and `isGoogleNativeVideoModelId`). Both are now one `isGoogleGeminiTextModelId`, used by the API resolver, discovery, native-video normalization and the GenerateContent video handoff. Production delta against `main`: +14/−17 lines; tests +28/−10.
</details>

prs.title: feat: let sandboxed plugin tabs invoke declared session actions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tabs need narrowly authorized session actions without receiving Gateway credentials or a general-purpose parent HTTP proxy. This replaces #80388 and builds on #107323.

## User Impact

Plugins can expose declared actions for the parent-selected session. Revoking device authority or session access while an action waits now prevents the action from running. Failed action-enabled pages show a sanitized explanation and Retry, which obtains a fresh grant before reloading.

Existing canonical session navigation and the direct iframe flow for tabs without actions are preserved. The unused `allowChatNavigation` schema field is removed; no second public navigation API is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bridge keeps authorization in the existing Gateway dispatcher, registered action scopes, trusted session context, persisted access checks, and payload/result schemas. Sandboxed pages receive neither bearer tokens nor mutation cookies.

This refresh addresses the [latest review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110102#issuecomment-5005741905): recheck both authorities synchronously immediately before invoking the plugin handler, provide recoverable page errors, remove the obsolete schema field, and repair the reported lint errors. Earlier navigation and causal MessagePort test fixes are retained; branch history is preserved.

## Evidence

Validated source: [`edbac97f93bc`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110102/commits/edbac97f93bc6fc633779cdee607b081abc0063c).

- **Gateway: 6 tests pass.** The real dispatcher, persisted session authority, and row-preparation boundary are exercised. Current authority permits one action effect; revoking the device or removing session membership while preparation is held returns `UNAVAILABLE` with **zero effects**.
- **Plugin UI: 51 tests pass** across document, page, and bridge suites. New cases cover an HTTP failure followed by Retry with a fresh grant, policy-error reporting, and redaction of a redirect error's private URL/token.
- **Regression sensitivity demonstrated:** keeping the new tests but restoring affected production files from `82f71f3` makes both authorization-revocation cases and all three new error/retry cases fail. The current-authority control still passes. Restoring the repaired files produces the passing results above.
- **Independent review:** no actionable high/medium-priority findings in the 11-file refresh.
- **Static checks pass:** changed-file formatting, type-aware oxlint, UI stylelint, UI i18n catalog validation, and `git diff --check`. The PR context/evidence policy also accepts this description locally.

**Remaining verification gaps (not waived):**

- **Browser/screenshots/end-to-end evidence is blocked.** Chromium crashes with `SIGTRAP` before loading the isolated fixture; a minimal launch without PR code reproduces the crash, including with `--no-sandbox`. The installed stock Firefox ESR also exits before Playwright can connect; no Playwright-patched Firefox is installed. No current-head browser assertions, network captures, or before/after screenshots were produced. Historical captures are not presented as current proof. Full Gateway startup, authenticated WebSocket flow, production cookies, plugin discovery, and deployment remain unverified. The retained navigation tests pass in the focused UI suite, but their separate base-fail replay has not been recorded.
- The broader changed-file check stops at the line-cap ratchet because this host's Git 2.34.1 does not support `git cat-file --batch -z`. Its preceding conflict-marker check passes; later gates and broader type checks are not claimed as passing.
- Replaying the two previously failing chat-test files yields 8 passing assertions but an unhandled Lit `ChildPart has no parentNode` exception in `chat-message.mcp-app.test.ts`. The run therefore fails. Those files are unchanged, but that alone does **not** establish that the failure is unrelated to this PR; causality remains unresolved.
- New-head hosted CI has not yet been validated. Maintainer review and the screenshot requirement remain outstanding.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands and local test cost</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/plugin-host-hooks.registry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/plugin/plugin-ui-document.test.ts ui/src/pages/plugin/plugin-page.test.tsx ui/src/pages/plugin/plugin-ui-bridge.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

On an isolated service capped at 50% CPU and 6 GiB RAM, final command wall times were 558.46 s and 64.49 s respectively (Vitest-reported durations: 492.82s and 45.86s). The persisted-authority scenarios exercise the real persistence/projection/dispatcher boundary with a causal preparation barrier, not sleeps or a mocked authority decision. CI seconds are not yet measured; these resource-capped local times are not CI estimates.

The old-source regression runs failed as expected in 866.35 s (authorization) and 51.30 s (page errors/retry). Production files were restored and their checksums verified afterward.

All verification used a separate checkout and private test state/config under resource limits. The live Gateway was not restarted, reconfigured, deployed to, or used as a test target.

</details>

## Remaining Maintainer Decision

The public `sessionActions` bridge still needs maintainer sponsorship and a long-term owner. This is an updated review candidate, not a merge request or a waiver of exact-head CI, screenshots, or owner review.

prs.title: fix(acp): tolerate owner-repair verdicts on discarding close with clearMeta (#151859)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Partially addresses openclaw/openclaw#151859 (task-maintenance discard teardown), resolving the P1 review blocker identified on openclaw/openclaw#152131 while complementing the task-maintenance cleanup deduplication in openclaw/openclaw#152613.

When an ACP session record has an unmigrated or unverifiable backend locator (raising `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired` with `SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED`), automated task maintenance cleanup (`loadTaskAcpSessionCloser` in `src/tasks/task-registry-acp-cleanup.ts`) fails closed every minute even though it explicitly requests to destroy both persistent state and stored metadata (`discardPersistentState: true`, `clearMeta: true`, and `allowBackendUnavailable: true`). Because teardown was blocked by the record's own provenance verdict, residue records survived and triggered repeated maintenance failures indefinitely.

*(Note: Gateway CLI deletion in `src/gateway/session-reset-acp.ts` returns earlier from cancellation and omits `clearMeta`; this PR focuses strictly on the maintenance closer path where `clearMeta: true` and `discardPersistentState: true` are supplied together).*

In #152131, an attempt was made to permit discard-close past owner-repair verdicts, but it inadvertently suppressed owner-repair errors even when `clearMeta` was false or omitted. That introduced a P1 state lifecycle violation (`[P1] Preserve ownership failures when the session metadata is retained`), because an unmigrated session metadata entry would be retained on disk after a reset without notifying the operator or prompting for offline migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

To satisfy the product owner's state lifecycle decisions (*Preventative Preservation & Action Observability*):
1. **Strictly gate owner-repair bypass on `clearMeta: true`**:
   - In `src/acp/control-plane/manager.close-session.ts`:
     - Recovery branch allows `ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED` with `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired(acpError)` **only** when `Boolean(input.discardPersistentState) && Boolean(input.clearMeta)` and `input.allowBackendUnavailable`.
     - In both the fast-reset branch and recovery branch, fresh-session preparation catches `isAcpOwnerRepairRequired(freshError)` **only** when `input.clearMeta` is `true`.
2. **Preserve fail-closed semantics for retained resets**:
   - When `clearMeta` is `false` or omitted (undefined), owner-repair errors are **always preserved and rethrown**, whether `discardPersistentState` is `false` or `true`. Stored metadata in the session store and SQLite database remains byte-for-byte intact.
3. **Comprehensive Regression Coverage**:
   - In `src/acp/control-plane/manager.owner.test.ts`:
     - Fast-reset path (`identityHasStableSessionId` false): verifies retained resets (`clearMeta: false` and `undefined`) across both `discardPersistentState` variants reject with `SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED` and leave metadata intact; verifies discarding reset with `clearMeta: true` deletes metadata and bypasses runtime close.
     - Recovery path (`identityHasStableSessionId` true): verifies retained resets reject and leave metadata intact; verifies non-discarding close rejects; verifies discarding close with `clearMeta: true` succeeds, records `runtimeNotice`, and deletes metadata without invoking `runtime.close`.

## User Impact

- Task registry maintenance cleanly purges residue ACP sessions whose backend locators are unverifiable or unmigrated, stopping perpetual maintenance log spam without manual intervention.
- Sessions undergoing non-destructive resets or retaining metadata are strictly protected from silent provenance mutation and continue to fail closed with directions to run Doctor repair.

## Evidence

### Real Runtime Verification: ACPX Backend Wiring & Production Task Closer

Executed against real SQLite session storage (`openclaw.sqlite`) wired to the actual ACPX locator check (`assertAcpxSessionOwnerLocator`) and production maintenance closer (`loadTaskAcpSessionCloser`):

```text
=== ACPX & TASK REGISTRY MAINTENANCE CLEANUP VERIFICATION ===
[Setup] Unmigrated ACPX session initialized in SQLite:
  • sessionKey: legacy-session-1
  • backend: acpx | mode: persistent
  • state database: openclaw.sqlite

[Backend] Verified authentic ACPX locator check:
  • Exception: AcpRuntimeError [ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED]
  • Detail code: SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED
  • Message excerpt: ACP session "legacy-session-1" has an unqualified or unverifiable backend locator. Stop the Gat...

[Test 1] Retained reset attempt (clearMeta: false)...
  -> Rejected as expected: fail-closed against unmigrated state
  -> Error detail: ACP_SESSION_INIT_FAILED [SESSION_OWNER_MIGRATION_REQUIRED]
  -> Stored metadata in SQLite preserved byte-for-byte: true

[Test 2] Invoking actual loadTaskAcpSessionCloser() from src/tasks/task-registry-acp-cleanup.ts...
  • Task closer loaded successfully from production task registry
  -> Production maintenance cleanup completed successfully!
  -> Metadata purged from openclaw.sqlite (readAcpSessionEntry?.acp): undefined (deleted)

=== ALL PRODUCTION & BACKEND VERIFICATION CHECKS PASSED ===
```

### Data-Model & Migration Compatibility Proof

- **SQLite Schema Version**: Unchanged (native state schema remains `v17`, verified by `pnpm check:native-state-schema-version`).
- **Data Migration / Backfill**: None required. No table schema, column, or type definitions are modified.
- **Backward & Forward Compatibility**:
  - Pre-existing session entries in `openclaw.sqlite` remain byte-for-byte intact and fully backward-compatible across upgrades.
  - Normal operations and retained resets (`clearMeta: false` or omitted) continue to fail closed and preserve stored metadata byte-for-byte in SQLite without modification.
  - Only explicit destructive cleanup (`clearMeta: true` and `discardPersistentState: true` with `allowBackendUnavailable: true`) removes the session record from SQLite.

### Automated Suites & Ratchets

- **Unit & Control-Plane Test Suites**:
  - `src/acp/control-plane/manager.owner.test.ts`: 10/10 tests pass across unit and acp projects.
  - Full `src/acp/control-plane/`: 42 files, 329/329 tests pass.
- **Ratchet & Quality Audits**:
  - `pnpm oxlint`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
  - `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`: 2 changed files; no growth/violations.
  - `pnpm check:assertion-safety`: OK, 0 new unannotated assertions.
  - `pnpm check:changed`: All 21 checks passed (typecheck core, typecheck core tests, format, ratchets, Knip deadcode, import cycles).

prs.title: feat(ui): add saved gateway account switching
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This repair closes the remaining Gateway-profile correctness and proof gaps:

- Active profile removal uses the returned survivor projection directly, so the deleted URL cannot be reintroduced by fallback loading.
- Query-aware migrated credentials are sent only to their owning exact endpoint at the outgoing WebSocket client boundary.
- Successful token-mode migration retires the old origin-scoped token; clearing an owned migrated profile retires both exact and legacy slots.
- Query-distinct profiles cannot recover a neighboring profile's credential.

Profiles remain local browser metadata. Credentials remain session-scoped; no server-side account or shared credential store was added.

## Evidence

- Pushed head: `9b7ed952e4a4d0fd5367c96074b62b93496f38cb`.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 exec vitest run ui/src/app/settings.node.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-store.auth.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-registry.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-store.test.ts --reporter=dot` — **117/117 passed** across 4 suites.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 exec oxfmt --check ui/src/app/settings.ts ui/src/app/settings.node.test.ts ui/src/app/gateway-store.auth.test.ts ui/src/pages/connection/connection-page.ts` — passed.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 tsgo:ui` — passed from an independently owned checkout install.
- `npx --yes pnpm@12.3.4 ui:build` — passed: **3,401 modules**, **840 finalized sidecars**, startup JS gzip **345,895 B** under the **352,235 B** limit; startup CSS **44,978 B** under the **51,200 B** ceiling.

## Fresh headed-browser proof

Run on 2026-09-11 against exact-head build `8023b23`/the pushed repair checkout, using disposable token Gateways and temporary state:

- `ws://127.0.0.1:19889` with a synthetic redacted token label `personal`.
- `ws://127.0.0.1:19890?account=team` with a synthetic redacted token label `team`.
- Real headed Chromium opened `http://127.0.0.1:19889/settings/connection`; the UI reached the actual WebSocket Gateway handshake and displayed token-authenticated connected state for both endpoints.
- Browser flow added and switched to the query-bearing Team profile, then confirmed removal of the active Team profile. The page reconnected to the surviving `19889` profile and the removed row stayed absent.
- The outgoing-boundary regression captured the actual client constructor options: migrated exact URL plus its owned token; after token-mode hello, the exact token key existed and the legacy origin key was gone.
- The clear regression seeded an owned origin-migrated token, cleared it, and verified both that profile and a query-distinct neighbor loaded with an empty token; the legacy key was absent.
- Browser storage and console diagnostics were redacted: no token values were retained. Browser console reported 2 development/runtime errors from the session; no zero-console-error claim is made.

## Limitation

After the browser's first successful token handshake, the Gateway issued a device grant. Clearing the visible Gateway secret and clicking Connect therefore remained connected through device authentication; this does not claim that clearing revokes an existing device grant. The no-token-reuse claim is proven at the outgoing client boundary and by the storage regression, while the live browser proof confirms the real handshake, profile switching, survivor removal, and endpoint identity.

The final post-push exact-head startup check launched runtime `9b7ed95` but detected that the runtime build stamp was still from `8023b23` while the rebuilt UI was `9b7ed952`, and correctly returned HTTP 503 rather than serving a mixed build. The interactive headed-browser receipt therefore comes from the immediately preceding compatible runtime; the final-head changes are covered by the 117-test suite, exact-head UI build, and the outgoing-boundary regression.

No new ClawSweeper review was requested.

prs.title: fix: queued follow-ups drop the implicit reply target
prs.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
-->

Closes #142268

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Queued follow-up answers on resolver-less channels (Telegram after restart, no live dispatcher) dropped the implicit reply target, so `reply_to_message_id` was missing.

This PR restores that injection for same-channel external/legacy turns. It does **not** claim ordinary overlapping-turn parity through a live Telegram Test Server run.

## Why This Change Was Made

Queued follow-up delivery already stores `messageId` / `originatingReplyToId` at admission. Payload resolution only applied reply tags and never ran the same implicit-injection helper the live path uses.

Queued payloads now go through `resolveReplyThreadingPayloads`. Implicit `currentMessageId` is injected only for resolver-less channels, with the same origin/provenance exclusions as `routeReply` (same-channel external or legacy user turns). Channels that own `resolveReplyTransport` keep correlation at `routeReply`, so empty/`replyToId` opt-outs survive. Restart-sentinel still keeps `originatingReplyToId`. Explicit `replyToId` still wins. `replyToMode` `off` / `first` / `all` stay authoritative.

## User Impact

On resolver-less transports, queued follow-up answers reply to the triggering same-channel message. Cross-channel and internal/inter-session IDs are not forwarded. Channels with a transport resolver still decide correlation at final routing.

## Evidence

Rebased onto current `main` as a single commit. Head SHA: `c6f38a93c8f7f9266efe7d3b39dbfd1aa799494b`. Marker: `PROOF_OK_c6f38a93`.

Focused Vitest after this revision (`test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts`): `followup-delivery.test.ts` + `followup-delivery.channel.test.ts` + `followup-delivery.implicit-reply.test.ts` + `followup-delivery-payloads.test.ts` + `followup-turn-admission.test.ts` — **137 passed**.

Coverage:

- same-channel queued `messageId` still injects `replyToId` on resolver-less channels
- Discord-origin / Slack-destination IDs are withheld at decision time
- inter-session child announcements stay unthreaded
- restart-sentinel keeps `originatingReplyToId`
- explicit `replyToId` survives excluded implicit IDs
- empty `replyToId` opt-out survives decision and delivery through the real channel resolver
- decision-to-delivery matrix matches those exclusions through the real channel resolver
- core tests use a fixture channel; they no longer import `extensions/qa-channel`

Sabotage: switching decision injection back to unguarded `resolveFollowupCurrentMessageId` turns the foreign-channel and inter-session tests red.

Runtime observation on `ba68eaeb` used the real Gateway + Telegram transport after restart and recorded the queued answer referencing message 11. That remains the dispatcher-less recovery proof. Telegram Test Server E2E for ordinary overlap was **not** rerun (no Convex QA broker credentials on this fork).

## Maintainer refresh — September 14, 2026

prs.title: fix: session assessments stop after five-second Codex discovery
prs.body:
Closes #189508

## What Problem This Solves

Cold Codex model discovery can finish just after five seconds even though the utility completion still has time available. OpenClaw's separate five-second `model/list` deadline can therefore abort a session assessment or Activity recap before inference starts.

## Change

Use the existing bounded-turn budget for discovery, retaining the enclosing deadline, caller cancellation and current-owner checks. Preserve Marvinthebored's production fix. Remove the test-line allocation file and share the real-WebSocket setup across cold discovery and both wall-clock correction cases. The tests now advance Date, performance and timers deterministically instead of waiting on the wall clock.

The whole PR changes production by +2 lines and tests by **−1 line**, with no allocation exception or new configuration.

## Evidence

The focused bounded-turn and clock suites pass **28/28** in Node 24.22.1 Docker. Against main's owner, the same consolidated clock file has **2 passes / 1 failure**: discovery returned after 5,008 ms is rejected with `model/list timed out`. Both wall-clock correction cases retain the total-deadline and caller-signal assertions. Changed-file lint and formatting pass.

Authoritative native timing: [`codex-rs/models-manager/src/manager.rs:419–425` at `ce0323f2f2`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ce0323f2f2d3b25e82806cd555237da3db4e1897/codex-rs/models-manager/src/manager.rs#L419-L425) bounds best-effort catalog refresh after an auth change at five seconds, including auth resolution and cache access. That native refresh boundary races the former OpenClaw cap.

Built Linux Gateway + real managed Codex 0.164.0 proof on exact head `26a59250a34d69a16b029cc20b5fd073db92a876`: delaying the fixture's cold catalog HTTP responses made main fail two Activity recaps with `model/list timed out`; candidate completed both in **17.164 s / 18.009 s**. Native model/list responses took **5,089 / 5,102 ms** on the candidate. Fast discovery remained successful on both refs. A 30-second catalog hold still triggered the existing **20-second outer recap deadline**, before any inference request. All requests used synthetic local endpoints and credentials; no paid key or OpenClaw timing injection was involved.

[Observed native Gateway evidence and control boundaries](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189512#issuecomment-6551996171).

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the shorter discovery deadline. There is no state, schema, dependency or public API migration. Blast radius is Codex-backed bounded utility completions. A slow discovery may use more of the already-authorized completion budget; the outer deadline and caller cancellation remain authoritative.
