prs.title: fix(macos): keep authored agent order when saving config
prs.body:
Closes #165055

## What Problem This Solves

An unrelated macOS config save alphabetizes the agent roster and can change which agent the Gateway treats as first.

The first PR revision also refused saves for valid configurations whose Gateway intentionally returns `raw: null` to protect secrets. The prior follow-up restored those saves through the existing `config.patch` contract. This follow-up fixes a separately reproduced Unicode scanner defect that rejected existing quoted keys beginning with a literal combining mark.

## User Impact

Existing configurations retain authored object-key order across local-file and Gateway saves. Valid redacted Gateway configurations remain editable, and quoted Unicode keys survive unrelated full-document saves. No config option, migration, or change to secret redaction is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Removing `.sortedKeys` alone is insufficient because Swift dictionaries do not retain JSON source order. Both full-document save paths use one source-aware writer. Local saves read the existing file under their existing lock; Gateway saves retain the source with the loaded document's route lease and revision hash.

When the Gateway intentionally withholds source text, the app instead sends only the differences from the loaded structured baseline through `config.patch`. Unchanged agent entries and redacted credentials are omitted, so the Gateway-owned source retains their order and values. Explicit `replacePaths` preserves full-array edit intent for reorder, shrink, and subtree deletion instead of invoking ID-keyed upserts. Revision, route, fallback, and local credential-preservation guards remain in place.

The writer scans Unicode scalars so a literal combining mark cannot absorb an opening quote into a Swift grapheme cluster. Foundation still owns JSON5 validation and key decoding.

The full-document writer retains existing keys, omits deleted keys, appends new keys deterministically, and accepts JSON5 comments, quoted/unquoted keys, escapes, and trailing commas. Retained array values keep their object order when moved or when neighbors are inserted/deleted. Arbitrarily moved-and-modified array objects without stable identity receive deterministic order; comments and whitespace are normalized as before.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `ae4cd9bbcab468fbde71ef994386d2a1aa81e0b6`. Unicode follow-up parent: `94f792074cadacd6eb6a27e88b7acbaaca0d2ff8`. Base: `c3b2b7d3fc1a053d2f6907e55e1629c16fc53706`. macOS arm64, Swift 6.4.

### Unicode compatibility control and repaired behavior

At the published parent `94f792074cadacd6eb6a27e88b7acbaaca0d2ff8`, Foundation accepts a strict JSON document whose quoted key and string value begin with literal U+0301 scalars. An unrelated browser edit fails in both production save owners:

```text
BEFORE local save refused; original fixture unchanged
BEFORE raw-present Gateway save throws DecodingError; no config.set request
AFTER three local saves succeeded; combining-mark key/value and authored order retained
AFTER three raw-present config.set saves succeeded; key/value/order and baseHash retained
```

The exact production `OpenClawConfigFile.saveDict`, `ConfigStore.load/save`, and `ConfigJSONWriter` sources were compiled with synthetic transport/peripheral adapters and run using `sandbox-exec -f proof.sb unicode-before-proof before` and `unicode-after-proof after`. The sandbox denies operator files, network, preferences/Keychain services, and child processes. Only disposable fixtures were used; this is not installed-app/live-Gateway E2E.

The new parameterized Swift regression fails before for both double-quoted JSON and single-quoted JSON5, then passes with scalar scanning. It creates literal combining marks through Swift scalar escapes rather than JSON escape tokens and checks preservation across repeated unrelated edits, including strings containing delimiter/comment text.

### Valid raw-null compatibility control and repaired behavior

The exact published first revision `21fa0613ea2f389d6d1eeb998d85ccd3c1c03a12` refuses a valid raw-null save with ConfigStore error 4. At prior head `94f792074cadacd6eb6a27e88b7acbaaca0d2ff8`, the repaired production `ConfigStore.load/save` owner succeeds against the same boundary.

A synthetic configuration deliberately gives its token the same value as an unrelated configuration field. The exact production `redactConfigSnapshot` owner therefore returns `raw: null` while retaining structured configuration. The proof then exercises five edits through the compiled production Swift save owner and applies the captured requests using the exact production `applyMergePatch` owner:

```text
browser off, browser on, browser off, provider-model reorder, provider-model shrink
5/5 saves succeeded through config.patch
Every request retained baseHash=synthetic-revision
Unchanged gateway/auth and agents were absent from every patch
Auth credential retained; agent roster remained zmain,alpha
Model reorder and shrink retained exact replacePaths and final array intent
```

The Swift owner ran in an OS sandbox against disposable fixtures. Gateway transport and peripheral app adapters were synthetic. This is direct save-owner plus production redaction/merge-contract proof, not an installed-app/live-Gateway end-to-end run. No operator configuration, installed app, or live Gateway was changed.

### Original ordering control

At the earlier first PR revision, compiled exact baseline and repaired local/Gateway serialization owners showed:

```text
Baseline: three unrelated local saves and three config.set encodings -> alpha,zmain
First PR revision: all six retained authored zmain,alpha
All three config.set requests retained baseHash
```

The full-document writer was unchanged by the prior raw-null compatibility follow-up; the scalar scanner correction above is new on this candidate. The earlier raw-null refusal is superseded by the repaired behavior above.

### Tests and checks

- Current exact-source pure serializer and merge-patch tests: **10 tests / 13 cases passed in 0.002s** in a separately linked, audited OS-sandboxed Swift Testing executable. This includes the failing-before literal Unicode regression, existing JSON5 comments/escaped keys/trailing commas, array movement/insertion/deletion, minimal patches, and array replacement/subtree deletion.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --product OpenClaw` passed in **20.72s**.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` passed in **21.36s**. This is test-bundle compilation, not native suite execution.
- Strict pinned SwiftLint on both follow-up files passed with zero violations. Full macOS SwiftFormat, native i18n verification, and `git diff --check` passed. Touched tests now use required failable UTF-8 conversions.
- Broad macOS lint / `check:changed` still report only the unchanged, previously documented `QuickChatFocusedTextCapture.swift:232` multiple-trailing-closure violation. All other changed-check lanes passed; no unrelated production fix is included.
- Current independent P2 AutoReview: **scoped-clean**, no accepted/actionable P0-P2 findings. Reviewed source bytes match this candidate. Scope is this two-file Unicode follow-up versus the published parent. The inherited Codex auth attempt failed with HTTP401 and is not counted as a clean review.
- Earlier raw-null repair retains its five production-owner saves, nine pure tests/eleven cases, and clean compatibility review at `94f792074cadacd6eb6a27e88b7acbaaca0d2ff8`. Those are explicitly earlier-head measurements; the compatibility owner was not changed by this follow-up.

### Remaining checks and limits

Current-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper reassessment are pending. Previous-head green CI is not current-head validation. Full native test execution requires disposable macOS CI/VM and was not run on the operator desktop. The separate generic JavaScript full-suite attempt was interrupted without an aggregate result and is not claimed as passed or as native proof.

prs.title: fix(ui): session New window/New tab always fails with "Allow pop-ups" in the macOS app
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #144582

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users of the native macOS app choosing "New window" or "New tab" from the Control UI session tab menu would always see the toast "Allow pop-ups for this site, then try again." There is no way to allow pop-ups for the embedded WKWebView, so both actions were dead ends (the same actions work in a regular browser).

- **Related:** #144582 (labels: clawsweeper:queueable-fix, clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear, clawsweeper:source-repro).

## Why This Change Was Made

The web side reserves an inert `about:blank` popup via `window.open` and later redirects it to the session route. The macOS shell's `createWebViewWith` delegate classifies the `about:blank` request as ignorable and returns nil, so `window.open` returns null and the UI reports a blocked popup. The fix hands the final session URL to the existing native `openclawLink` bridge (already used by the Browser panel's external open) whenever that bridge is present, and keeps the previous `window.open` reservation as the browser fallback.

- **Intended outcome:** inside the macOS app, New window / New tab from the session menu hand the final session URL to the native link bridge instead of failing; no popup-blocked toast. The receiving default browser opens the Control UI session route; it needs its own gateway sign-in, so a previously paired browser renders the session directly while a never-paired browser lands on the Control UI login gate (an explicit sign-in surface) rather than the session.
- **Out of scope:** creating a native dashboard window/tab for the session (the shell has no such API today; whether to add one is flagged as a maintainer decision below); browser popup semantics are unchanged.
- **Highest-risk area:** routing the action through the native bridge hands a credential-free URL to the default browser, which does not inherit the app's WebKit credentials — a browser that never signed in to this gateway will not see the session.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The native receiver already validates main-frame + trusted same-origin source before opening; the posted URL intentionally carries no credentials (Gateway credentials must not be exposed in URLs), and an unauthenticated receiving browser is stopped at the login gate, which the E2E now asserts explicitly. Without the bridge (regular browsers), or if the post throws, the previous flow including the blocked-popup toast is preserved and covered by tests.

## User Impact

macOS app users can open a session from the session menu's New window / New tab items again: the session route now opens through the native link handoff in the default browser instead of failing with an impossible "Allow pop-ups" instruction. The receiving browser must be signed in to the gateway itself: an unpaired browser reaches the Control UI login gate (explicit sign-in) rather than the session; a browser that has already paired renders the session directly. Regular browser behavior is unchanged.

- **Success criteria:** with the native link bridge present, both menu actions post the final same-origin session URL and never call `window.open`; without the bridge, the previous reservation + toast flow is kept. The posted URL grants nothing on its own: a never-paired receiving browser stops at the login gate without rendering the session.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `ui/src/lib/sessions/session-menu-navigation.ts` (bridge handoff placed before the popup reservation); regression fixtures in `session-menu-navigation.test.ts` ("hands … to the native shell link bridge instead of a blocked popup", "falls back to the browser popup when the native link bridge rejects the post"); the real-Gateway E2E in `ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` (real Gateway + served Control UI + a page-level `openclawLink` bridge stand-in, covering both actions, the posted destination loaded verbatim in a paired isolated browser context, and the never-paired context stopping at the login gate).

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Linux, Node 26, Playwright Chromium, a real Gateway child process built from this branch (`createOpenClawTestInstance`), and the Control UI served from this branch's source. The page-level `window.webkit.messageHandlers.openclawLink` bridge is installed through a browser init script before any page script runs — the same surface the macOS dashboard shell installs — and, like the native receiver, it does not open anything inside the source browser. The handoff destination is verified in isolated browser contexts that share no cookies, storage, or page state with the source page, modeling how an external default browser receives the `NSWorkspace.open` handoff: one context signs in to the gateway once through the Control UI's gateway confirmation surface (the analog of a previously paired default browser) and then navigates to the posted URL verbatim with no credential parameters appended; a second, never-paired context loads the same posted URL and must stop at the Control UI login gate. The macOS app itself is not runnable in this environment.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/lib/sessions/session-menu-navigation.test.ts ui/src/app/native-link-routing.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/vitest-ui-e2e-config.test.ts
  pnpm exec oxfmt --check ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  pnpm exec oxlint ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-e2e.json --builders 1
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:** real-Gateway E2E (`session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`, head `d626215`) output:
  ```text
  ✓ hands session New window and New tab to the native link bridge instead of a popup 28328ms
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  1 passed (1)
  ```
  Both "New window" and "New tab" from the session menu post to the bridge:
  ```json
  [
    { "type": "open-link", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/chat/main/native-bridge-proof", "target": "external" },
    { "type": "open-link", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/chat/main/native-bridge-proof", "target": "external" }
  ]
  ```
  with zero `window.open` reservations from the menu code and no "Allow pop-ups" toast. The destination is then verified the way an external default browser receives it, in isolated contexts that share no state with the source page: the paired context first signs in once through the Control UI's gateway confirmation surface, then navigates to the exact posted URL verbatim — no `gatewayUrl` or token parameters appended — and renders the session's transcript, so the loaded session comes from the handed-off URL plus the receiving browser's own independent sign-in state. The never-paired context loads the same posted URL and stops at the `openclaw-login-gate` sign-in surface without ever rendering the session: the handoff grants nothing by itself, and an unauthenticated browser reaches an explicit sign-in flow instead of the session.
- **Observed result after fix:** with the `openclawLink` bridge present, `open-new-window`/`open-new-tab` hand the final same-origin session URL to the bridge and never touch `window.open`; the blocked-popup toast no longer fires. A receiving browser already signed in to the gateway renders the intended session from the posted URL; a never-paired receiving browser is stopped at the login gate. Without the bridge (regular browser), the previous reservation + fallback flow is preserved (covered by unit tests).
- **Before evidence:** with `session-menu-navigation.ts` restored to its pre-patch state (same worktree, patched E2E), the E2E fails — `AssertionError: expected undefined to deeply equal { type: 'open-link', …(2) }`, `Test Files 1 failed (1)` — the bridge never receives anything because every attempt goes through the `about:blank` popup reservation, matching the report (so the destination steps are never reached on unpatched code). At unit level the regression tests fail on main with `AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called … Number of calls: 0`.
- **What was not tested:** live macOS app / WKWebView runtime and the native Swift receiver (no macOS hardware in this environment); the native receiver path is unchanged and covered by existing native tests.
- **Proof tier:** L2 (real Gateway, real served Control UI, real browser; the WKWebView host bridge surface is installed at page level as the shell does, not mocked at module level; the handoff destination is verified in isolated browser contexts — one paired through the real sign-in surface, one never-paired — rather than a state-sharing same-browser tab).
- **Proof limitations:** no macOS environment available; the WKWebView message-handler transport and the Swift-side `NSWorkspace.open` handoff would need a reporter/maintainer repro on macOS. The bridge contract asserted in the E2E matches the existing native `DashboardWindowController.receiveLinkMessage` validation (main frame, trusted same-origin source, http(s) URL). The posted URL is credential-free by design: it grants session access only in a browser that already signed in to the gateway, and an unpaired browser lands on the login gate (now asserted explicitly). Whether the macOS session actions should instead open an app-owned authenticated destination (a new app window/tab that retains the app's WebKit credentials, as the ClawSweeper review recommends considering) is an open maintainer decision — this PR keeps the external-browser handoff and makes its sign-in requirement explicit and tested rather than building new native windowing unilaterally.
- **Review state:** Follow-up on the ClawSweeper review of `8d40173`: reworked the E2E destination step that previously appended `gatewayUrl` and token parameters before loading the posted URL (which overstated what an unpaired default browser receives) — the destination now signs in explicitly first and loads the posted URL verbatim, and a never-paired negative case asserts the login gate; the destination-access claim in this body is corrected accordingly. Rebased onto latest main (`d626215`). CI lanes pending on the updated head. Note: `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway` previously failed on `quota-reset-status.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` ("expected 'Signed in' to be 'Ready'") — a main-level failure unrelated to this PR's files (the same test fails identically on other current PRs, e.g. #146400) and not chased here.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): mount only visible sidebar rows and prepare advertised methods once
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Campaign evidence for a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link recorded a 14-state UI timeline. This PR addresses render work within that reload: grouped Control UI sidebars mount overscan rows in every category below the viewport. Roughly 140 rows mount while only about 30 fit in the native viewport. Each row also repeatedly scans the full advertised-method catalog, consuming CPU between transcript DOM creation and first text paint.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing window owner and return an empty range when a category is wholly below the viewport (`beyond === 0`). Selected, focused, dragged and menu-owned rows retain their existing exceptions; headers, spacer height, pagination and scroll anchors retain their owners. Prepare advertised-method membership once per catalog array identity in a WeakMap. Hello/capability refreshes replace the array, so new connections and refreshed catalogs get distinct facts without cleanup bookkeeping. Live phase and scope admission remain unchanged.

Overlap: #189791 (`steipete/coldload-sidebar-reload-regression`) was open when this branch rebased. Its offscreen-category window fix overlaps this one; whichever lands second must rebase and retain only the remaining delta. This PR does not change L259's snapshot staging/handoff work.

## User Impact

Less main-thread rendering during warm reload, with the same visible sidebar layout and logical sessions. The lead accepted the recorded small-wins results: real-Gateway LoAF improves in all 11 pairs on both routes; dashboard text paint improves in all 11; chat text paint improves by a paired median 92 ms in 8/11. Native dashboard CLS rises by **0.000253** (A/A paired median **0**), explicitly accepted as negligible. This does not claim that the whole cached-page campaign exit criterion is complete.

## Evidence

All performance comparisons ran on the same quiet AWS **c7a.4xlarge**, lease `cbx_7a051eb464c4`, with repo Playwright headless Chromium. Each harness/route used 11 alternating baseline/candidate pairs and an independent 11-pair A/A control. No performance result came from the shared Mac. CPU idle before the final visual run was 93.3%. Real-Gateway comparisons used synthetic 3,000-session data, archived chat/dashboard targets, three acknowledged live viewers, tall Markdown, and 80 ms RTT. Native comparisons used the Team-scale cold-load bench, `live-fast`, warm reload, archived session, pane-chrome probes, LoAF and RPC probes. Timed comparisons were unprofiled and omitted screenshot capture.

Both fixtures used the operator settings: category grouping with 97 catalog groups / 102 section-order entries, created sort, five collapsed sections, involving-me, preview off and stored empty-groups mode `always`. In the current projection that stored mode means **always hide empty groups**; native settled headers therefore number 71, not 97. This is the existing semantics, not a product change.

The recorded comparison baseline runtime was `7b29a23da2a6e787eca43c757bbc489f83d5b682`; candidate was the two runtime edits originally committed as `d5380c837ffe97ea44a3733a93989550541be2dc`. Diagnostic tools came from fixture commit `5e2a2b5eaf5109b82e40ef384b4c4928389d8879`. Both arms used the same Gateway build. These are the previously recorded and lead-accepted runtime-patch results, not fresh measurements of the rebased head. The candidate runtime diff is unchanged after rebase.

Values below are **median [Q1, Q3]**, milliseconds except CLS and row counts. Paired delta is candidate minus baseline; medians of pairs need not equal differences of arm medians.

Real chat first text paint has overlapping IQRs and only 8/11 wins; the lead accepted this small win and replaced the original lane-specific threshold. Real chat hello-handled has a +16.4 ms paired median with 6/11 worse and overlapping IQRs; the A/A control is similarly noisy, so this is not a demonstrated regression under the campaign rule. Native dashboard CLS has separated IQRs and 10/11 positive deltas (one tie); the lead explicitly accepted this +0.000253 CLS movement as negligible; native dashboard A/A has paired median zero.

Connect was the first RPC in **100% of samples** across both harnesses, both arms and controls. Each measured real reload issued one document navigation. Real settled mounted transcript rows remained one in both routes (the tall final virtualized row); native counts remained four chat / three dashboard. Real sidebar mounts fell **142→10**; native **139→31**. These are mounted DOM counts, not deletion of logical sessions. Native settled header sequences matched in every pair. The native harness does not expose owner hello-handled or final-row DOM completion in this configuration; its received-hello milestone must not be substituted for those missing metrics.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/188252

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin completion accounting resolves configured and catalog prices even when an explicit billed cost already takes precedence.

## User Impact

No intended result or billing-policy change. Recorded costs, including billed zero, retain precedence; missing costs keep direct or aggregate estimation, and unavailable costs stay unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve prices only inside the existing estimation fallback. Keep the shared accounting owner, price arguments, usage callbacks and sparse diagnostic semantics unchanged. No cache, API, SDK or configuration change is introduced.

Production decreases by one line. The existing host-dispatch case also protects billed zero through returned usage and logging; two owning cases independently assert direct and aggregate configured-price fallback. Tests grow 40 lines with an exact separate allocation.

## Evidence

- Qualified execution passed 88 tests across four accounting, host-dispatch, pricing and usage suites in 87.915s wrapper time. Core types, owning plugin test types and targeted typed production/test lint passed.
- Native author formatting, syntax, whitespace, signed hooks and the source test-line ratchet passed. Fresh independent full-range review of `03f2b2d44c04ee6aa805fb998c458a97628e0c9e..3599e3e5c632487e6f9ce1bc41a2cad658ee4478` found no actionable findings (confidence 0.95).
- Current-owner intake confirmed the eager lookup remains present. Source, reviewed head, qualified dependency inputs and native binding were independently verified before and after measurement. Only the production file varied during comparison; final committed test inputs were identical.
- Native preparation passed at the unchanged reviewed head. The ordinary squash route merged it as `72943b04f5aba1337efd4e59a13e68103c9e72b4`; the observed final PR rollup had 60 successes, 153 skips and one neutral result, with no failures. Native completion is recorded. No production latency, CPU, RSS or physical-allocation gain is claimed.

## Matched work and cost

The acceptance rule was published before measurement: five serial interleaved baseline/candidate pairs, retain the first baseline and every point, unchanged outputs, fewer billed-path lookups, unchanged necessary fallback lookups. Any 20% adverse measured cell stops the sequence. No additional or replacement samples were run; the largest adverse paired cell was 15.812%.

Normal native compiler-output reuse is unchanged. The production file is restored after every command. Observed one-minute host load ranged from 8.030 to 14.248.

All ten runs passed the same four literal-output cases. Actual worker profiles contained both the pricing resolver and its lower implementation even at zero: billed host lookups fell **2→0**, while direct/aggregate configured fallback stayed **2→2**. Every run retained four accounting completions and two host dispatches. This exercises the real runtime accounting consumer with provider I/O isolated; it is not live-provider latency evidence.

prs.title: fix(browser): recover Chrome relay CDP connections
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Chrome automation failing to establish a CDP connection through the extension relay when tab attachment work is slow or spans multiple tabs.

## User Impact

Users can recover the relay connection and enumerate browser tabs after a timed-out handshake or disconnected owner socket. Limiting native tab attachments also avoids overwhelming Chrome during startup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Playwright CDP connection uses a custom transport whose handshake can remain pending beyond the configured five-second deadline. Target enumeration waits for tab attachments, while the relay previously started attachment work without a concurrency bound. A disconnected owner could also retain a rejected close request and prevent safe reacquisition.

This change enforces the handshake deadline and closes the transport on timeout, limits native tab attachments to two concurrent operations, cleans up failed attachment work, and treats an already disconnected owner as recoverable.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on upstream with a deterministic synthetic relay and Playwright's real CDP connection logic: the handshake remained pending past 5,001 ms instead of timing out.
- Regression coverage uses five synthetic tabs and verifies the five-second timeout, maximum attachment concurrency of two, cleanup after a failed/slow attachment, no queued attachment amplification after timeout, reconnect, and enumeration of all five pages.
- Owner integration coverage terminates the borrowed owner socket, reacquires the relay, and enumerates tabs successfully.
- Focused validation: 46 tests passed across the relay bridge, Playwright timeout/reconnect, and owner connection suites. File-scoped Oxlint and formatting checks passed.

Confirmed affected environment: OpenClaw 2026.9.9 with Chrome extension v2.3.0. The failure was also reproduced against upstream before this fix.

Verification limitations: the repository-wide extension typecheck reports unrelated dependency/type errors, including missing `@aws-sdk/client-s3`, `linkify-it`, and `tlds`, plus errors in other extension/core files. The repository lint wrapper did not complete package-boundary artifact preparation; file-scoped Oxlint passed. No live Chrome or production service was used.

prs.title: fix(ui): saving a provider key says when the model policy hides its models
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: saving an API key in **Settings → Models → Connect provider** succeeds silently when `agents.defaults.modelPolicy.allow` hides every model of that provider, so the provider never appears in the model picker and nothing says why.

## User Impact

User impact: after the key saves, the dialog stays open and says that the model policy hides the provider's models, with the `provider/*` entry to add: to `agents.entries.<agent>.modelPolicy.allow` when the selected agent sets its own policy (it replaces the default), otherwise to `agents.defaults.modelPolicy.allow`. Saves for providers the policy allows close the dialog as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already decides policy visibility: `models.list` with `view: "all"` marks each model `manualSelectionAllowed` from the agent's model policy. After a successful key save, the provider page reads that list for the saved provider and warns only when the Gateway marks every model hidden. The UI does not match allowlist patterns itself. `models.list` does not say which config level owns the policy, so the warning names both instead of adding a protocol field. The warning uses the existing post-save warning path, which already keeps the dialog open for discovery failures.

## Evidence

Mocked-Gateway Control UI run of the real dialog flow (policy `allow: ["openai/*"]`, save a Particle key; `models.list view=all provider=particle` returns `manualSelectionAllowed: false`):

Before (main): the dialog closes with no explanation.

![Before: dialog closes silently](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/88c4d47c-50c3-4980-ac0e-b26fa498773f)

After: the dialog stays open with the policy warning.

![After: dialog names the model policy](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed03db88-d142-479f-b8f9-5ad896604025)

- `pnpm test ui/src/pages/model-providers/model-providers-page.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 35 passed, 1.8 s wall. The new cases check the warning when every model is hidden and no warning when one model is allowed; both fail with the fix reverted.
- Gateway side is existing coverage: `src/gateway/server-methods/models.prepared.test.ts` publishes `modelPolicy.allow: ["test/first"]` and checks `view: "all"` marks other models `manualSelectionAllowed: false`.
- `pnpm check:changed` (dead-code skipped) and `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` pass.
- No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

Merge danger: two-way door. UI-only; a revert restores the silent close. Blast radius: the Models settings key dialogs (add and edit) gain one extra `models.list` read per successful save; a failure of that read shows as a warning, not a failed save.

prs.title: fix(cron): Gateway shutdown with running stream jobs no longer warns that stream owner stops failed
prs.body:
Related: #167752

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every Gateway stop or restart with a running stream automation ends with `[shutdown] completed ... with warnings: cron` and `cron-stream: owner stop failed`, because the shutdown retirement of the stream source and its final state write are refused after the Gateway already sealed the cron receipt authority.

## User Impact

User impact: operators no longer see a cron shutdown warning on every stop of a Gateway that runs stream jobs, so the warning again means something. The stopped stream job keeps a durable `stopped` state with a retired source identity instead of staying `running` after the process exited; a batch that the stop loses is counted durably as well. Sources still respawn on the next start; no other stop path changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The close prelude seals the receipt authority on purpose, before cron tears its watchers down, so that no new effect enters a stopping Gateway. The stream owner's shutdown stop then needs writes that settle an already-running source: retire its identity, persist its final state, and record a batch that the stop lost. All of them went through the ordinary mutation path and were refused. The owner now marks only its `shutdown` stop as a settlement write, the cron service carries that mark through to the receipt authority (which already admits settlement writes after the seal), and the service keeps its resident store for those writes instead of reloading a sealed store. Every other stop reason keeps the ordinary path and remains fenced.

Two review findings shaped the follow-up commit `ac11be9fffa` (the commit before it, `5c6d3bbc7a9`, only removed the forwarding-only bindings test; the production and test changes it describes are in `ac11be9fffa`). Loss counters written while the stop finalizes (`finishStop` records a buffered, pending or unsettled batch) carry the same settlement mark, so they are durable after the seal instead of failing with `cron-stream: failed to persist loss counters`. A stream child that does not exit within the bounded shutdown stop is persisted as state only (`streamStatus: "error"`, `streamRestartExhausted: true`); the failure path that also emits the run event and dispatches a failure alert is not used during shutdown, because the Gateway has already stopped its channels at that point. The stop error itself still reaches the shutdown warning. Outside shutdown a failed stop records the failure exactly as before.

## Evidence

Focused tests (Vitest, fresh install of this checkout):

- `src/cron/service.stream-worker.test.ts`: the case `retires and persists a running source on shutdown after the receipt authority sealed new effects` runs the real cron service through the same owner-to-service bindings the Gateway uses, seals the authority with `beginCronReceiptAuthorityClose()`, checks that an ordinary state write is still refused, leaves one output line inside its quiet window, then stops all watchers with reason `shutdown`. Against the unchanged base it fails with `Cron receipt authority is unavailable; wait for Gateway settlement or restart.` (the message from the report); with this change the stop settles, the durable row holds `streamStatus: "stopped"` with a retired identity and `streamDroppedBatches: 1`, and the authority drains cleanly. Against the first commit of this PR the counter expectation fails because the counter write still took the ordinary path. 7 of 7 pass.
- `src/gateway/cron-stream-watchers.stop-settlement.test.ts` (new, a sibling of the watcher test file, which is at its line cap): a stop-reason matrix over all eight reasons asserts that only `shutdown` carries the settlement mark on retirement, state and loss-counter writes, that `removed`, `trust-disabled` and `cron-disabled` still retire without it, and that the remaining reasons do not retire. It is kept because it pins the fencing contract of the seven non-shutdown reasons, which the service-level case does not cover. A second case stops a child that ignores its cancel: on `shutdown` the failure is persisted as state only with the settlement mark and no failure record is written; on `disabled` the failure record is written as before. Against the first commit of this PR the two `shutdown` cases fail. 10 of 10 pass; `cron-stream-watchers.test.ts` is unchanged against main and passes 44 of 44.

Test cost (`pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1` on one worker, this host): the two watcher files together 61.8 s wall time, `service.stream-worker.test.ts` 24.8 s.

Checks: `oxlint --type-aware` on the changed files, `tsgo` core graph, the services-cron and gateway-root test type graphs, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:max-lines-ratchet`, `check-no-conflict-markers`, and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files.

CI note: the first run of this PR failed one inherited test, `test/plugins/dreaming-cron-doctor.integration.test.ts` (`plugin service startup timed out after 5000ms (memory-core/memory-core-index)`). The file is not touched by this PR and is identical to the merge base; the same case fails the same way on the unchanged merge base on this host.

## Real behavior proof

Setup: the Gateway was started from the checkout's sources (`node --import tsx src/entry.ts gateway --port <port> --allow-unconfigured`) in a transient systemd user unit with a 3 GiB memory cap, with its own state directory, its own config (token auth, loopback bind, Control UI off, cron enabled), `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`, no channel and no model provider configured. A stream job was created through the CLI against that Gateway (`automations add --stream-command '["sleep","3600"]' --session isolated --message ...`), the child process was confirmed as a running child of the Gateway, and the Gateway was stopped with SIGTERM to its PID. The durable row was read from the isolated state database afterwards. The bundled build could not be produced on the proof host within that memory cap, so the sources ran through tsx; no production Gateway was involved.

Before (unchanged merge base `476ce032f4f`): the stop logged

```
[shutdown] cron: Cron receipt authority is unavailable; wait for Gateway settlement or restart.
[shutdown] completed in 2675ms with warnings: cron
```

and the durable row of the job kept `"streamStatus":"running"` with its original `streamSourceIdentity` after the process had exited.

After (tree of `ac11be9fffa`): the same scenario logged

```
[shutdown] completed cleanly in 354ms
```

with no cron warning; the durable row holds `"streamStatus":"stopped"` and a `streamSourceIdentity` that differs from the one the job was created with (retired). No `sleep 3600` process survived either stop.

Variant with output: the same scenario with `--stream-command '["sh","-c","sleep 10; echo buffered-line; sleep 3600"]'` and `--stream-batch-ms 30000`. The quiet window did not hold the line for 25 s, so the batch had already fired and its run was in flight when SIGTERM arrived (no model provider, so the run fails). Before: the Gateway drained that run for 60 s (`isolated agent setup timed out`), then logged the same `Cron receipt authority is unavailable` warning and `completed in 1175ms with warnings: cron`; the row stayed `running` with its original identity. After: `[shutdown] completed cleanly in 1400ms`, the row is `stopped` with a retired identity and `streamDroppedBatches: 1`. The dropped-batch counter was recorded before the seal in both runs because the run settled during the drain, so this variant does not isolate the sealed counter write; that path is shown by the service-level test above.

prs.title: fix(browser): recover after the Chrome relay owner disconnects
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes browser control staying broken after the authenticated Chrome relay owner websocket drops, until the Gateway restarts.

Supersedes #168189, thanks @jimmarkunas.

## User Impact

The next browser call can reconnect to the configured Chrome relay without restarting the Gateway. Recovery authenticates the same profile and port; it does not select another browser or replay the interrupted action.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing lazy lifecycle already checks owner liveness, but retiring a dead borrowed client requests a cleanup acknowledgement over its closed socket and retains that rejection. Let the connection owner discard a closed client, then reuse the existing authenticated acquisition path once on the next call. Native cleanup and attachment fencing remain daemon-owned, and live-socket shutdown still waits for acknowledgement. There are no background reconnect loops or new settings.

Production delta: **−2 lines**. Removed redundant retirement-acknowledgement state, since retirement already invalidates the client, and updated the obsolete lifecycle comment. The takeover deliberately leaves attachment scheduling and handshake deadlines outside this repair.

## Evidence

- Regression on main's browser code (`b7d77957a83a`; affected inputs identical at `101a6afdecdc`): **1 failed, 2 passed**. A real authenticated websocket is dropped after browser control enumerates a fixture tab; the next readiness call fails with `Relay owner connection unavailable` while closing the old owner.
- With the fix: **26 passed across 5 focused files**, 37.83 seconds wall time including compiler preparation. The changed owner integration file takes about 112 ms of test time. Recovery successfully enumerates the tab again and makes exactly two authentications to the configured profile and port.
- Negative controls pass: listener proofs for another profile, port, owner, or key are rejected. Existing native-detach acknowledgement, peer-loss cleanup, retirement, and lifecycle tests also pass.
- File-scoped Oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. The local package-boundary typecheck could not resolve absent generated Plugin SDK declarations; PR CI subsequently passed production and test type checks.
- Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) reviewed the complete local change against `b7d77957a83a`, with relay server/bridge/native cleanup context: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The test allocation was subsequently reduced to its exact 29-line growth.
- Simplification pass retained one owner and removed duplicate retirement bookkeeping. Test delta: **+29 lines**, allocated in `relay-owner-reconnect.txt` because the prior tests covered graceful retirement but not unacknowledged socket loss. Hosted [CI run 41262881240](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41262881240) is green on `4d19ac7c7417` (493 seconds wall time; the broader changed-node test job took 337 seconds). Security review also passed.

Proof uses production browser-control, Playwright, authentication, relay, and lifecycle code with a synthetic extension; no live Chrome, agent/model, or production Gateway was exercised. The contributor's code was read with GitHub view/diff only and was never checked out or executed. Human contributor credit is preserved in the commit trailer.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the missing work signal when a chat is waiting on subagents or still has task-owned background commands running.

## User Impact

The existing compact footer keeps its claw, elapsed time, and separate subagent/command counts visible, including in bubble mode. Counts open the existing Subagents and Processes panels. Detached services do not keep an idle conversation looking busy, and unavailable command observations are labeled rather than presented as zero.

## Why This Change Was Made

Implements the selected minimal-footer design without restoring the removed delegation tracker or per-worker narration. Command classification comes from the execution owner's retained request ownership, not command-name or output heuristics. The visible conversation shares the existing process observation with the panels.

Counts cover reconnectable background exec processes, not every foreground tool or OS process. Truncated inventories show a lower bound with "+". Older workers lacking ownership metadata remain inspectable in Processes but do not acquire an inferred busy signal. No execution, cancellation, retention, or permission behavior changes.

prs.title: feat(ui): show the recorded exec warning in the approval history
prs.body:
Closes #180242

## What Problem This Solves

When an exec approval is shown to a reviewer, the operation's `warningText` — the safety warning attached to a potentially dangerous command — is rendered prominently (live approval page `ui/src/pages/approval/approval-presentation.tsx`, and `**<warningText>**` in channel approval notifications via `src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.ts`). The Control UI **approval history** table never rendered it: `HistoryRow` shows `commandText` only, so an operator auditing past approvals cannot see why a command was flagged as dangerous at the moment it was approved.

The field is already in the data path end to end, so nothing but the renderer was missing:

- `ExecApprovalPresentationSchema.warningText` (`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/approvals.ts:134`)
- persisted in the full presentation (`src/gateway/operator-approval-store.rows.ts` `stringifyPresentation`)
- returned unchanged by `approval.history` (`src/gateway/server-methods/approval.ts` `buildApprovalSnapshot`)

## Why This Change Was Made

Implementing the conditional warning note recommended in #180242: reuse the existing presentation field and the existing warning styling, next to the historical command, with no storage, RPC, config, or decision change.

- `ui/src/app/approval-presentation.ts` — `execWarningText(presentation)` extracts the recorded warning for exec presentations and returns `null` for other kinds or when absent. This module already owns approval presentation summaries (`summarizeApprovalScopeLabel`), so both approval surfaces now read the same predicate.
- `ui/src/pages/approvals/approvals-page.tsx` — the local `Cell` helper gains an optional `warning` note that renders under the cell value, and the request cell passes `execWarningText(...)`. Rows without a recorded warning are unchanged, including `Cell`'s existing `mono` command styling.
- `ui/src/styles/components.css` — `.approval-history-warning`: a compact body-font, `--warn`-toned line under the command (the cell is monospace, so the note resets the family instead of looking like more command text).
- `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-approvals.ts` — `approvalHistory.warningLabel: "Warning"`.

**Behavior classification: behavior-preserving.** Additive rendering of an already-returned field; no approval, grant, or history read/write path changes. Solid escapes text nodes, so a recorded warning containing markup is displayed literally and never executed (covered by the regression test).

## User Impact

Operators auditing approval history can now see the recorded blast-radius warning on the row it belongs to, instead of losing it after the decision. Exec rows that carried no warning look exactly as before, as do the other six columns, the standing-grants table, pagination, and the retention footer.

## Evidence

Mock-Gateway Control UI harness (`installMockGateway` + Playwright, the repository's UI proof path) rendering `settings/approvals` at 1200×1000, dark theme, with one warned exec row and one unwarned exec row.

**Before** (base `64ab0917`): the warned row shows only the command.

![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0123bb4c-921b-4aed-9ae8-56b139f15333)

**After** (this head): the recorded warning is rendered under the command in the request cell.

![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0545f05a-3f88-4134-b328-0f0df5e3ec97)

Close-up, before → after:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![before table](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16f81eac-3771-4ef6-a951-f2ed97da528e) | ![after table](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5229ebf1-f812-42a5-80f6-8c989bb69693) |

The second row (`pnpm test ui/src/pages/approvals`, no recorded warning) is pixel-identical in both captures, which is the "no misfire" control for the conditional render.

### Red on base

`git checkout HEAD^ -- ui/src/pages/approvals/approvals-page.tsx` (source only, new test kept):

```text
 × |unit| src/pages/approvals/approvals-page.test.tsx > shows a recorded exec warning beside the command without executing its markup 24ms
   → expected  to have a length of 1 but got +0
⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ Failed Tests 1 ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯
AssertionError: expected  to have a length of 1 but got +0
      Tests  1 failed | 12 passed (13)
```

Failure is at the intended assertion (no `.approval-history-warning` node), and only the new test fails.

### Checks

```sh
# regression test (after)
cd ui && node ../scripts/run-node-package-bin.mts vitest run --config vitest.config.ts \
  src/pages/approvals/approvals-page.test.tsx
# Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  13 passed (13)   Duration 9.51s

pnpm exec oxlint ui/src/pages/approvals/approvals-page.tsx \
  ui/src/pages/approvals/approvals-page.test.tsx ui/src/app/approval-presentation.ts
# Found 0 warnings and 0 errors

pnpm exec stylelint ui/src/styles/components.css --config config/stylelint.config.mjs
node scripts/run-format.mts --check <changed files>
# All matched files use the correct format

node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/control-ui-i18n-verify.ts verify
# raw-copy baseline entries=71, source keys=11407, no drift
```

## Not tested

- `pnpm tsgo:core` does not run on this host (the pinned `tsrs` needs glibc ≥ 2.29; host is 2.17), so type checking for the new `CellProps`/`execWarningText` signatures is delegated to CI.
- No live production Gateway with a real 30-day approval ledger was exercised; the proof is the repository's mock-Gateway UI harness plus the DOM regression test. The history payload shape itself is unchanged and already covered by `approval.history` tests.
- Non-English locales: only the English catalog gained `approvalHistory.warningLabel`; foreign translations arrive through the post-merge locale pipeline, not by hand here.
- Stacked/mobile layout was not captured; the note is a block inside the existing responsive cell and adds no new column.

## References

- Implements the recommendation in #180242 (`Maintainer decision needed → Add an inline warning note`).
- Sibling requests in the same table, intentionally not included here: #180243 (approval severity in history) and #180244 (approval scope/blast radius in history). The `Cell` note slot introduced here is the natural place for them if maintainers want one combined history layout.
- Existing warning presentation this follows: `ui/src/pages/approval/approval-presentation.tsx` (`role="note"` + `approval-page__warning`), `src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.ts` (channel notification emphasis).

<details>
<summary>Maintainer edits</summary>

- `Cell` gained one optional prop (`warning`) plus a local `CellProps` type; both are file-local, no new exported API outside `execWarningText`.
- Diff: +70/−2 across 5 files (page, app helper, CSS, English catalog, regression test).
- No RPC, storage, config, documentation, or approval-decision behavior touched.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- **Land-ready as is:** additive render of a field the history RPC already returns, with regression coverage and inspected before/after captures.
- **Wanted instead a dedicated column:** deferred deliberately. A `Warning` column would be empty for most rows and would consume table width; the inline note keeps the seven existing columns and can be promoted to a column later without touching the data path.
- **Wanted all three history requests together:** this PR is the smallest of the family and the `Cell` note slot was built to accept the severity (#180243) and scope (#180244) renders. Happy to extend it in a follow-up rather than grow this diff.
- **Scope statement:** no visual change outside warned exec rows in the approval history table.

</details>
---

### ClawSweeper verdict

Diff: production +31/−2 (page +14/−2, `execWarningText` +6, CSS +10, en catalog +1) | tests +39/−0 → **+70/−2 across 5 files**.

| Dimension | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Overall readiness | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** — "unresolved product direction caps the overall assessment" |
| Proof confidence | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** ✨ media proof bonus — "Sufficient (screenshot): inspected before/after screenshots exercise the actual Control UI settings/approvals route in Chromium … proves the changed rendering boundary." |
| Patch quality | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** — "No actionable review findings were identified." |
| Recommendation | **"Approve the inline warning: accept this focused addition to the existing request cell without changing the seven-column layout."** |

[ClawSweeper review (2026-10-27)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185200#issuecomment-6430379600) — labels `proof: sufficient`, `rating: 🦐 gold shrimp`, `status: ⏳ waiting on maintainer`; CI `openclaw/ci-gate` pass.


---

## Decision requested (not an approval claim)

The ClawSweeper `Recommendation` quoted above is an **advisory design suggestion, not a contract approval** — it was written by the review bot, and no maintainer has recorded a decision on this direction. This PR renders an already-recorded field (`warningText`) in the existing approval-history request cell, and it is waiting on an owner decision before merge.

| Option | Effect | Cost if chosen |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Accept (this PR)** | Auditors see the recorded blast-radius warning under its historical command; unwarned rows are pixel-identical. | A warning-toned note under the command cell; the seven-column layout and all other columns are unchanged. |
| **Decline and close** | History keeps showing only the command; operators lose the warning after the decision. | The `Cell` note slot (built to also accept severity #180243 / scope #180244) is unused; nothing else changes. |
| **Wanted a dedicated column** | Deferred deliberately; the inline note can be promoted to a column later without touching the data path. | Table width would grow and most rows would carry an empty column. |

prs.title: fix(codex): settled-turn recovery rejects sessions containing a media-only user turn
prs.body:
Closes #185079

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex settled-turn finalization repeatedly fails with `invalid_content` when the session history contains a legitimate media-only user turn — a message persisted with empty text plus ordered `__openclaw.media` facts (for example, a JPEG-only Telegram message) and no upstream-text fallback. The projection validated every earlier message before trimming, so one such historical turn kept rejecting every later finalization context capture on that session.

## User Impact

User impact: a verified historical media-only message no longer invalidates settled-turn recovery. It projects as a bounded, deterministic marker naming the attachment types, and finalization context capture succeeds for sessions that contain one. Empty messages without any well-formed media fact are still rejected, upstream text keeps winning over the placeholder, and current-turn evidence and pairing checks are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`projectUserMessage` required non-empty text and threw `CodexHistoryRejection("invalid_content")` for a blank user turn. The persisted representation for media-only turns is exactly that shape (empty `content`, media metadata under `message.__openclaw.media` — the documented "media-bearing user turns use ordered `message.__openclaw.media` facts" convention). The payloads themselves are not replayable through the text-oriented recovery projection, so the fix projects a deterministic `[User media attachment unavailable in this context: <types>]` marker — the same approach the projector already uses for image tool results (`[Image tool result: <mime>]`) — capped at the first eight entries with a `+N more` suffix, always inside the existing byte budgets.

## Evidence

- New regression tests in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/settled-turn-projection.test.ts`: against unpatched `origin/main`, exactly the two placeholder-projecting cases fail (media-only turn rejected with `invalid_content`); with the fix all 26 cases pass, including the guards for empty turns without well-formed media facts (still `invalid_content`), upstream-text precedence, and the placeholder cap.
- `pnpm test:extension codex` passes except two `transport-startup.test.ts` cases that fail identically on unpatched `main` on this machine (macOS native process inspection returns a permission error in this environment); the projection suites themselves are fully green.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes typecheck extensions, typecheck extension tests, and lint extension changed files. The only red lane is the pre-existing `deadcode` unused-export scan flagging three exports in files this PR does not touch.


**Remaining proof:** No end-to-end Gateway/Codex recovery run with persisted media-only history has been performed. The regression tests cover the projection boundary; they do not establish the full recovery and finalization flow.

prs.title: fix: native Codex turns fail with "settlement is closed" when they finish after 6 minutes
prs.body:
Related: #185121

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a native Codex turn that finishes normally after running more than 6 minutes without OpenClaw-visible progress is stopped by the reply watchdog right after it completes. The run then fails with `session placement turn settlement is closed`, and its finished result is discarded.

## User Impact

User impact: long native Codex turns, such as research or scheduled agent runs (and more of them on slower hosts), keep their completed results instead of failing just after they finish. A run that stays stuck after its native turn ends is still stopped, one full stall window (6 minutes) after the release.

Tradeoff: a native runtime that drops liveness without finishing now gets up to one more stall window before the stall stop. Execution deadlines, terminal-cleanup deadlines and explicit Stop are unchanged. Other `runtime_owned` waits (the `agents_wait` collector and sessionless lane executions) keep today's behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

While a `runtime_owned` wait is live, the native runtime owns liveness and the watchdog only observes. Other wait owners publish semantic progress when their wait ends. The native turn's wait instead just stops being current, so on the next tick the watchdog measured the stall window from the last progress *before* the turn started, and stopped a run that had just finished.

The native turn's wait is now registered through `beginNativeRuntimeLivenessWait`, which opts in with `releaseStartsSemanticWindow: true`. While such a wait is live, the watchdog records the last time it observed it live, and measures the semantic window from the later of that time and the last semantic progress. Releasing the wait therefore starts a fresh window instead of expiring the protected interval after the fact. No progress event is invented and the stall policy is unchanged.

It is opt-in rather than applied to every `runtime_owned` wait, because `agents-wait-tool.test.ts` ("does not protect a collector after revoked authority / stalled reread") requires the `agents_wait` collector to lose protection immediately, and a blanket change would break that contract.

Tests: the existing `protects explicit live %s waits, not detached flags` case still covers plain `runtime_owned`. A new watchdog case covers the opted-in release. Two `runs.liveness.test.ts` cases encoded the old timing and are updated:

- `reports quiet runtime waits without scheduling abort` now expects the fresh window after release, then the same controller-owned `run_stalled` stop. It releases between diagnostic heartbeats, so the controller timer, not a heartbeat landing on the same instant, reaches the stall first. That tie exists on `main` for any stall deadline that lands on a heartbeat tick.
- `waits in bounded slices, then reclaims host-owned work without a millisecond spin` previously expected a waiting turn to reclaim the run 1 s after the native runtime released liveness. It now reclaims after the fresh window, still with `run_stalled`.

That second case is the main behavior change for review: a waiting turn now waits up to one stall window for a just-finished native turn to finalize, instead of reclaiming it at once. If you would rather keep a faster reclaim, a shorter finalization grace after release (for example the existing 60 s cleanup window) would also fix the reported failures. I kept the full window because that is what other wait owners get when they publish progress on release.

Possible follow-up, not in this diff: when the watchdog stops a run for a real stall, the lane's abort check reports the closed placement before the abort reason, so users see `session placement turn settlement is closed` instead of the watchdog's stop reason. #180212 works on preserving watchdog causes for automation failures.

## Evidence

**Red/green.** Focused tests on unpatched `main` source (new and updated tests kept) fail at the release tick:

```text
 ✓  protects explicit live runtime_owned waits, not detached flags
 ×  starts the semantic horizon when a native runtime-owned wait releases, never retroactively
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times
    342|     live = false; // The native turn completed and released liveness.
    343|     await operation.watchdog.tick();
    344|     expect(cancel).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 37 passed (38)
```

(The runner stops after the first failing shard, so the updated `runs.liveness` case was not run red.)

The same tests pass with the fix:

```text
session-controller.watchdog.test.ts
 ✓  protects explicit live runtime_owned waits, not detached flags
 ✓  starts the semantic horizon when a native runtime-owned wait releases, never retroactively
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  38 passed (38)
runs.liveness.test.ts
 ✓  reports quiet runtime waits without scheduling abort
 ✓  waits in bounded slices, then reclaims host-owned work without a millisecond spin
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```

**Related tests with the fix:** `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` with the fix: `session-controller.watchdog` 38/38, `runs.liveness` 8/8, `agents-wait-tool` 44/44 (including `does not protect a collector after revoked authority` and `... after stalled reread`), `question.recovery` 16/16. `oxlint` 0 warnings / 0 errors and `oxfmt --check` clean on the touched files. `pnpm tsgo:core` passes. Pre-commit checks, including the line-cap ratchet, pass; the native wait moved into a small exported helper so `runs.ts` shrinks instead of growing.

**Real-world occurrences before the fix.** One Linux host running the native Codex harness (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`), 2026-10-25/26 ET, two scheduled research jobs (A, B). Every failure happened well under the job's configured timeout (1260 s), and each lane ran under one Gateway process (no restarts):

| Error (ET) | Job | Lane time | Agent output written | Watchdog `blocked reason=cleanup_pending` logged |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10-25 21:04:27.7 | A | 511.6 s | 13.7 s before the error | 21:04:28 |
| 10-26 08:59:56.3 | A | 511.1 s | 4.3 s before | 08:59:57 |
| 10-26 10:41:35.8 | A | 572.4 s | 13.8 s before | 10:41:34 |
| 10-26 11:57:45.1 | B | 408.3 s | (job writes no separate file) | 11:57:44 |
| 10-26 12:22:09 | A | 621.0 s | 13.4 s before | 12:22:07 |
| 10-26 15:34:33.0 | A | 751.3 s | 7.0 s before | not logged |

The watchdog line lands within about 2.5 s of the error each time it is logged. None of these runs logged a `no_semantic_progress` warning first, because the policy only observes while the wait is live. Journal excerpt for the first run (session keys and run ids redacted):

```text
21:04:27.735 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main durationMs=511596 error="session placement turn settlement is closed" errorName=AbortError taskKind=turn
21:04:27.764 [model-fallback/decision] model fallback chain stopped: reason=caller_signal_aborted candidate=openai/gpt-6.1-sol errorName=AbortError
21:04:28.440 [diagnostic] reply watchdog: sessionKey=<redacted> action=blocked reason=cleanup_pending
```

**Mechanism (line numbers on `main` at d209419bb9):**

- A native Codex turn registers a deadline-free `runtime_owned` wait that stays current while the handle's `ownsLiveness()` is true (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts:963-976`). Codex's `ownsLiveness()` turns false once the turn completes (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-active-turn.ts:593-597`).
- While a wait is live, the watchdog policy returns `observe` with no warning or stop (`src/sessions/session-controller.watchdog-state.ts:80`). Lane/maintenance waits (`src/sessions/session-controller.operation.ts:190`) and human input (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-state.ts:282`) publish semantic progress when they end; the native wait does not.
- On the next 1 s tick (`src/sessions/session-controller.watchdog.ts:397`), the semantic deadline `progressOrigin + abortMs` (`:146`, 6 min from `:111`) is already in the past, so the watchdog returns `stop` / `semantic_stall`.
- The stop runs `expireOwner` (`src/sessions/session-controller.operation.ts:298`) and the execution cleanups (`src/sessions/session-controller.operation-recovery.ts:210-231`), which include the placement's forced-terminal settlement registered at `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/lane-controller.ts:457`.
- The lane's normal completion path then re-checks placement in `throwIfAborted` (`lane-controller.ts:291`), which throws `SESSION_PLACEMENT_TURN_SETTLEMENT_CLOSED` (`src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-admission.ts:549`), and the completed result is dropped.

**Live after-fix Gateway proof (2026-10-27 UTC): passed.** A real local Gateway and native Codex turn ran one synthetic native-shell workload for **390,001 ms**. At the exact native terminal receipt, the owning watchdog's last raw semantic progress was **422,336 ms earlier (7m02.336s)**. The turn completed, `agent.wait` returned `ok`, the connected client received the exact final marker, and the same assistant final was persisted in `chat.history`.

```text
last_raw_semantic_progress = 2026-10-27T00:19:58.354Z
native_terminal_receipt    = 2026-10-27T00:27:00.690Z
raw_semantic_quiet_gap_ms  = 422336 (> 360000)
native_status             = completed
native_wait_registered    = true
watchdog_closed/recovery  = false / false
agent.wait                = ok
local_chat_final/history  = exact marker received / exact marker persisted
result_marker             = WATCHDOG_SETTLED_6BA2C4DF45BE0718489A770C
```

The observation used temporary same-process Inspector logpoints that always returned false, bound to the exact synthetic session, run, and watchdog-attempt object. It read the **raw** semantic clock when the native terminal flag became true, rather than the fix's projected semantic horizon. No accepted semantic renewal occurred after that exact native registration. No clocks, policy, waits, or deadlines were changed, and no debugger pause occurred. The target observer disabled and disconnected after recording terminal. This exercised the real native registration, completion, settlement, WebSocket final-delivery, and canonical-history paths while scheduled work continued on the host.

**Build provenance:** reviewed PR head `5374b18239630999118aa5b7d8a9c849d9a67a5c`; installed build `e620ac5f5f927bd29c8ea6c528942893e33822dc`, based on upstream `3d7f8fbf399df62820f8982cab7f7c2de83648b0` plus the operator's existing local patch set and this PR. Both build stamps identified clean inputs at that installed head. All four files changed by this PR exactly matched its reviewed blobs. Seven additional watchdog/native-path files also matched. The notification controller's pre-existing difference only resets suppression telemetry after a confirmed steering input; this one-input run did not steer. The native terminal flag, liveness, and settlement path are identical. This is explicit evidence from the installed variant; the whole repository heads differ.

| Reviewed file | SHA-256 of the matching installed/PR bytes |
|---|---|
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts` | `992810824c8c016c706bb3997587399623df0ce393c96ea03cec63cda75cddef` |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.liveness.test.ts` | `6fe4754ac016762382b4976b0f96197091914c1ff25accfa709653f09f85990e` |
| `src/sessions/session-controller.watchdog.ts` | `cbc74f36bff24217be8cc7879e1b5a1817efc50be283c285f843f4855e8d394c` |
| `src/sessions/session-controller.watchdog.test.ts` | `b1b7c7783dfc44a8ce4bce0f059fd86fdfdaf385527cf1efc3842300196fe1f8` |

The existing watchdog and liveness tests continue to verify the `run_stalled` stop once the fresh semantic window expires. A new independent scoped review of the PR head found no actionable P0/P1 defect; the existing exact-head CI remains the broad test evidence.

**Maintainer decision still requested:** confirm acceptance of the full six-minute semantic window after native liveness ends, including unexplained liveness loss. The live proof establishes successful native completion and delivery; it does not substitute for the session-controller owner's product decision.

prs.title: docs: add Prized hosting guide
prs.body:
Closes #185116

## What Problem This Solves

Readers choosing where to run OpenClaw find no guide for Prized in the Hosting section or on the `/vps` provider picker.

## User Impact

User impact: readers can run the Gateway on a Prized box by following one guide, found from the Hosting nav, the Linux server provider picker and the Platforms page.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page follows the shape of the other hosting guides and uses OpenClaw's own install path: `install.sh --no-onboard`, then `openclaw onboard --install-daemon`, as in the DigitalOcean guide. (Prized's own walkthrough lets the installer start onboarding and runs `openclaw gateway install` afterwards; both end with the Gateway as a systemd user service.) The Gateway stays on loopback, and the Control UI is reached through an SSH tunnel. The page is linked from Hosting > App platforms in `docs.json`, the `/vps` card group and the Platforms list, each kept alphabetical, plus one glossary entry that keeps the product name untranslated. Docs only, with no code, config, schema or runtime changes.

Prized is my company. Prized rents cloud VMs and does not host or manage OpenClaw. I'll keep this page current. Prized's own walkthrough is at https://prized.dev/docs/openclaw.

## Evidence

I ran every command on the page, from `prized box resize` on, on a fresh Prized Micro box on 2026-10-25, with OpenClaw 2026.10.7.

- The box was running with auto-pause off after `prized box new --wait` (Ubuntu 24.04.5, 2 vCPU, 3.8 GB RAM, user lingering on).
- `install.sh --no-onboard` exited 0 and installed Node v24.22.1. `openclaw` was on `PATH` in a new login shell.
- `openclaw onboard --install-daemon` ran interactively with QuickStart and a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The live completion check passed, the systemd user service was installed, the Gateway was reachable, and onboarding ended in the terminal chat, which Ctrl+C twice leaves.
- `openclaw gateway status` showed it running, connectivity ok, listening on 127.0.0.1:18789. The Gateway used about 1.5 GB of memory (RSS).
- Through an `ssh -N -L` tunnel to 127.0.0.1:18789 on the box, the Control UI answered HTTP 200. Pasting the token from `openclaw gateway auth-token --show` connected a fresh browser, which paired without a manual approval. `--show` refuses to print outside an interactive terminal, so the page says to run it in the SSH session.
- Pause and resume: after `prized box resume --wait` the Gateway kept its PID, and an `openclaw agent` turn answered.
- Cold restarts (resize to Nano, then back to Micro): the user service came back at boot, and an agent turn answered.
- `pnpm check:docs` passes on this branch: format (1401 files), markdownlint (0 issues), MDX, i18n glossary, links (16009 checked, 0 broken), config examples and changelog. `pnpm docs:check-links:anchors` reports the same 7 broken anchors as main, none on these pages.

Gaps:

- The model was a local OpenAI-compatible stub, so no real provider or channel was connected.
- I didn't sign up a new Prized account to re-run the sign-up tour.
