prs.title: feat(memory): let workspaces exclude generated files from search
prs.body:
Related: #101422 Supersedes #177868 by @CheekyHobson: their reviewed head `a2008ab09`, ported onto current main with co-author credit on the commit, plus the proof ClawSweeper asked for. ## What Problem This Solves Generated dreaming reports under `memory/dreaming/` are indexed like curated notes and crowd them out of memory search, and there is no setting to exclude paths inside the default memory folders. ## User Impact User impact: operators can set `memory.search.excludePaths` (globally or per agent), for example `["memory/dreaming/**", "memory/.dreams/**"]`, to keep matching workspace files out of memory search and file watching. - Unset or empty changes nothing. The index scope hash is identical to the one 2026.10.9 writes, so this setting adds no rebuild on upgrade. - Setting or changing the list is a scope change, like changing `extraPaths`: `openclaw memory status` reports it, vector search pauses, and `openclaw memory index` rebuilds and drops the excluded rows. - Search only: excluded files are not deleted, `memory_get` can still read them, `memory forget` still scrubs them, and short-term recall/promotion eligibility is unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made One workspace-relative glob check, next to the existing `extraPaths` glob matcher in the memory host SDK, is applied where search scope is decided: file discovery (local and remote workspace providers), watcher eligibility, and the index scope hash. Shared watchers include the exclusions in their selection keys, so agents with different exclusions on one workspace rebaseline when one joins or leaves (the P2 ClawSweeper found on #177868). Changes compared with #177868 at `a2008ab09`: - Rebased onto main: the scope hash goes through the single `resolveConfiguredMemoryScopeHash()` owner, and the matcher is exported from `plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-engine-fs`, the subpath #181891 narrowed the file worker to, instead of `engine-storage`. Both are private local-only subpaths, so this adds no third-party SDK contract. - The matcher lives in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts` beside `matchesExtraMemoryPathEntry` instead of core `src/memory/root-memory-files.ts`. - Added the config field label, corrected the docs about the rebuild step, and linked the setting from the dreaming docs. - Tests: replaced the 13 s CLI e2e case with a manager test of about 4 s that mirrors two unforced `openclaw memory index` runs (the real CLI run is below). Dropped a test that indexed an excluded file through a private method, a `selectionKeys` shape test covered by the join/leave behavior test, a worker integration test that still passed with the P2 fix reverted, and (after ClawSweeper's review) a test that only checked the worker request shape. Size against main: production +67/-8 in 15 files; tests +148/-3; docs +15/-4; generated baselines +3/-3. (#177868 was +439/-18 in 33 files.) ### Maintainer decision needed #101422 asks for both search exclusion and recall/promotion eligibility control. This PR is the narrow first stage: search discovery, watching, and index scope only, with defaults and promotion safeguards unchanged. ClawSweeper's review of #177868 recommended approving that narrow search stage and leaving recall inclusion and diagnostics to follow-up work; the alternative is one combined search+recall include/exclude design. An operator on #101422 said the search-only step covers their need. Config surface: `pnpm config:docs:gen` raises the core count by 4 (2586 -> 2590 on main `87396e7`) for `memory.search.excludePaths` and `agents.entries.*.memory.search.excludePaths`, each with its `.*` item path. That is the new setting itself. ## Evidence Real runs on head `8eb4b7b` (on main `f980e01`). Synthetic workspace: 3 curated files (`MEMORY.md`, `memory/backups.md`, `memory/garden.md`) and 7 generated reports (5 light, 2 REM, one REM report containing only "No strong patterns surfaced."). Isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` under `env -i`, Node 26.12.1, and a local OpenAI-compatible embeddings stub on 127.0.0.1 (deterministic vectors, no provider calls). **Upgrade and CLI:** 2026.10.9 from npm builds the index; this branch keeps its scope hash with no `excludePaths` (the re-chunk comes from main's #168867), then drops the 7 reports after `excludePaths` plus `memory index`; the curated note stays first and an edit refreshes it.
Terminal output (paths redacted to $OPENCLAW_HOME) ```text $ openclaw --version # npm openclaw@2026.10.9 OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (8b18b55) $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.595 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.489 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.477 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.467 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.456 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.445 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 # stored index identity (2026.10.9): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":5} $ openclaw --version # this branch OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (8eb4b7b) $ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive # main's state migrations since 2026.10.9 Upgraded agent database schema in $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: v25 -> v38 $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/10 files · 11 chunks Dirty: yes Index identity: index chunking implementation changed (owner: openclaw, code: chunking_version) $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. # stored index identity (this branch, no excludePaths): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} $ openclaw config set memory.search.excludePaths '["memory/dreaming/**","memory/.dreams/**"]' --strict-json Updated memory.search.excludePaths. Restart the gateway to apply. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/3 files · 10 chunks Dirty: yes Index identity: index scope changed (owner: configuration, code: scope) Vector search: paused until memory is rebuilt $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 3/3 files · 3 chunks Dirty: no # indexed rows by path: {"path":"MEMORY.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/backups.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/garden.md","chunks":1} $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. # edit memory/backups.md: 02:30 -> 03:15 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 03:15 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. ```
**Gateway watcher:** a throwaway loopback Gateway with `excludePaths` set. One agent turn (a local chat-completions stub that calls `memory_search` once) opens the Gateway's default memory manager and its watcher. Then, with no further CLI calls, a new dreaming report is written and the curated note edited: the watcher refreshes the note within 1-2 s across runs and never indexes the report.
Terminal output ```text $ openclaw gateway run --bind loopback ... # throwaway Gateway [gateway] ready $ openclaw agent --agent main --message "When does the nightly backup run?" Done. # memory_search tool result (from the stub's log): path: memory/backups.md # indexed memory/ rows before edits: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # wrote memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-29.md and edited memory/backups.md (02:30 -> 04:45); no CLI calls from here # after the Gateway watcher sync (~1s), plus 5s more: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 04:45 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # dreaming rows: {"dreamingRows":0} ```
**Regressions fail without the fix:** - `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` "rebaselines shared exclusions when a differently scoped agent joins and leaves" fails with `excludePaths` removed from `selectionKeys` ("expected setScopes to be called once, but got 0 times"). - `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` "drops generated Dream reports once excluded and keeps curated edits fresh" fails when the config resolver drops `excludePaths` (the report is still found). **Changed test files** (`pnpm test --maxWorkers=1` on `685db0c`, same test code as `8eb4b7b`, where they pass again; CI seconds to follow): | File | Result | Wall | Vitest duration | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` | 29 passed | 48s | 41.65s | | `manager-reindex-state.test.ts` | 49 passed | 40s | 36.19s | | `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` | 11 passed | 71s | 64.91s | | `watch-policy.test.ts` | 6 passed | 47s | 41.51s | | `internal.test.ts` | 43 passed | 4s | 749ms | | `memory-search.test.ts` | 39 passed | 46s | 42.06s | Vitest time is mostly cold transform; the new manager case takes about 4 s and the other new cases take 1-24 ms. **Checks:** `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` on `83eb31b` (main `200afde`, same code) passes typecheck (core, core tests, extensions, extension tests), lint, format, config docs baseline, Plugin SDK package exports, plugin boundaries and the other changed-file guards. Three lanes fail outside this PR: wrapper shadowing (`buildSkillWorkshopPromptSection`) and the public Plugin SDK surface budget (`agent-harness-runtime`) fail identically on clean main `200afde`, and the dead-export scan lists only auto-reply, gateway and UI exports this PR does not touch. The `pnpm check:docs` content checks pass. Test lines grow by a net +145, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/memory-search-exclude-paths-188294.txt`: default scope-hash compatibility, the shared-watcher rebaseline, discovery and glob matching, and the exclusion rebuild. **PR CI:** earlier runs had failures inherited from main: `read-file.test.ts` after the fs-safe 0.26.14 bump (#188352) and `archive-restore.postgres.test.ts` from #155538, both fixed on main (#188531, `34a4e118dc1`), then `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` while main was over its test-line ceiling (main's own scheduled job logged the same overage with net delta 0). #188780 restored the headroom. The branch now merges main `87396e7` at `f8eea0d`: only the generated config baseline conflicted and was regenerated; the PR diff is unchanged. On `f8eea0d`, the test-line ratchet passes locally (slack 20,324, this PR +145 under its allocation), `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions` and `config:docs:check` pass, and the touched tests plus `memory-files-worker.test.ts` and `workspace-memory-client.test.ts` (files main also changed) pass. `checks-node-changed` on `a63b2b5` failed in `plugin-sdk-package-contract-guardrails.test.ts` after main's #188833 referenced an untyped SDK entrypoint in a guide; main fixed it in #188937, and that test passes locally on `f8eea0d`. On `5a03cd1`, `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-3` (and so `ci-gate`) failed in `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-publication-admission.test.ts` because main's #189247 changed seal-less agent-database opens while that memory-core test still expected the synchronous integrity check; it failed the same way on main `f8e492f` without this PR. Main fixed the test in #189449, and it passes locally on `f8eea0d`. **Local review:** autoreview, Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode against `upstream/main`, P0–P2: scoped-clean, "patch is correct" (0.87). It ran on `685db0c`, before the rebases onto `200afde` and `f980e01`, which changed only the base and the generated baseline files. Not covered: Windows paths (the matcher normalizes `path.sep`) and a live remote node workspace (the harness test checks that list and watch requests carry `excludePaths`).

prs.title: fix(chat): queued messages reappear after a delayed history refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes queued messages reappearing above the composer when an older saved-input page arrives after a newer update has consumed or cancelled the message.

## User Impact

Queued rows stay retired after delivery or cancellation, and server-accepted messages now say **Queued for a new turn** instead of silently losing their local Steer action. This does not add server-side re-steering or change requester authority, FIFO/steering policy, or model-runtime recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing pending-input owner now rejects navigation responses that crossed a meaningful custody transition, including receipt-only retirement and change-and-change-back updates. Equivalent deserialized refreshes still complete in one read. Receipt observations stay bounded to the current request and are discarded with it; no persistent history or new state owner is added.

Simplification retained the existing navigation and queue owners: production growth is 130 additions/4 deletions; regression coverage is 205 additions/3 deletions. The additional state protects reproduced stale-response cases rather than adding a second ordering policy.

## Evidence

- 69 focused pagination/custody/dismissal tests passed in 5.90 seconds wall time (Vitest 4.72 seconds). Regressions cover stale consumed/cancelled rows, receipt-only retirement, exact queried absence, equivalent fresh-object snapshots, and A→B→A custody transitions. Equivalent refreshes use one read; invalidated navigation uses two, with zero sends.
- Composer queue suite: 15 tests passed. UI typecheck, changed-owner type-aware lint, whitespace checks, UI build, controller check, and keyless i18n checks passed.
- Real Control UI with a synthetic Gateway: Show earlier messages → newer consumption update → delayed stale page; the retired row stays absent, with zero chat.send calls. This is isolated mock-Gateway boundary proof, not a live-provider test.
- Independent review of the exact candidate completed; three reproduced review findings were fixed and rechecked. Local commit: 365f033978ab4041c9e2da10e2bda46eab00eca7.
- Matching Before/After screenshots below use the real Control UI with synthetic data, the same dark theme, 1280×900 viewport and fixed timestamp. The crops show the accepted queue row and surrounding composer; Steer remains correctly unavailable after server acceptance. CI seconds are not available yet.

### Before

![Before: accepted queued row without an explanation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44679b6d-c0cd-4eb5-a762-f718f7717507)

### After

![After: accepted row says Queued for a new turn](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f0c014ec-7eb5-4f74-ac41-0d1c4cf2c959)

Human contributors: @VACInc, @vyctorbrzezowski, @shakkernerd, and @hannesrudolph.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4bb3b6e0-653c-489b-b976-1a2a8494a3d3)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b7d7adaa-3b5b-4ac0-b86a-6d5ebecb9f05)

**Human review hold:** do not merge or deploy before Vyctor reviews this fix.

prs.title: fix(telegram): Mini App unavailable when the Gateway is published via gateway.publicOrigin instead of Tailscale
prs.body:
Closes #167981 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: `/controlui` cannot open the Telegram Mini App when the Gateway is published through a reverse proxy or tunnel with `gateway.publicOrigin` instead of Tailscale Serve/Funnel. On mixed ingress (Tailscale Serve plus a public origin) the Mini App always got the tailnet URL, which fails on phones that are not on the tailnet (`net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED`). ## User Impact User impact: operators who already publish the Gateway over HTTPS and set `gateway.publicOrigin` can use the Telegram Control UI Mini App without Tailscale Funnel or Tailscale on the phone. - Tailscale-only installs: unchanged (`gateway.publicOrigin` is unset by default). - Mixed ingress with `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` unset: the public origin is used (core already admits `gateway.publicOrigin` into the Control UI origin policy in that case). - Mixed ingress with an explicit `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` that does not list the public origin (e.g. tailnet-only): the Tailscale URL is kept, so the upgrade does not break a working launch. - Public origin excluded by the allowlist and no Tailscale: `/controlui` replies with an error naming the origin to add to `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins`. ## Why This Change Was Made `resolveTelegramMiniAppUrls` checks `gateway.publicOrigin` first, using the shared `resolveGatewayPublicOrigin` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/config-contracts` (absolute origin, no path/query/hash). It is used only when it is `https:` (Telegram only opens HTTPS WebApp URLs) **and** the Control UI origin policy admits it; the page, Control UI and WebSocket (`wss:`) URLs then honor `gateway.controlUi.basePath`. Otherwise the unchanged Tailscale path runs. The origin-policy check mirrors core `resolveControlUiAllowedOrigins` + `checkBrowserOrigin` (`src/config/gateway-control-ui-origins.ts`, `src/gateway/origin-check.ts`): an unset list admits the public origin; an authored list (including an empty one) must contain the origin or `"*"`, compared after trim + lowercase with the same `normalizeOptionalLowercaseString` helper. `resolveControlUiAllowedOrigins` is not exported through the plugin SDK, so the ~8-line rule lives next to the resolver instead of widening the shipped SDK surface; happy to switch to an SDK export if maintainers prefer. `dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback` is deliberately not treated as admitting the origin (it depends on the proxy forwarding `Host`), so such installs keep the pre-change Tailscale URL. Expected publishing failures are thrown as `TelegramMiniAppUrlError`; `/controlui` and the Mini App auth route show its message (so the allowlist hint reaches the owner) and keep the generic `TELEGRAM_MINIAPP_URL_ERROR` for unexpected exceptions. `initData` verification, owner checks, launch tickets and the bootstrap handoff do not depend on the ingress and are untouched. Docs (`docs/channels/telegram/mini-app.md`, `docs/web/dashboard.md`) describe the URL source order, the mixed-ingress rule and the new error. ### Maintainer decision: publicOrigin vs Tailscale Proposed rule: the configured public origin wins only when the Control UI origin policy admits it; Tailscale-only installs are not affected (`gateway.publicOrigin` is unset by default), and mixed installs with a strict `allowedOrigins` keep their Tailscale address. Rationale: an operator who set `gateway.publicOrigin` has declared the canonical external URL, and a Mini App runs on a phone that is often not on the tailnet. ## Evidence - `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/ extensions/telegram/src/bot-native-command-dispatch.miniapp.test.ts`: 7 files, 59/59 passed (`url.test.ts` 13/13; `routes.test.ts` asserts the auth route returns the `TelegramMiniAppUrlError` message with 503). Mixed-ingress cases: allowlist unset → public origin (Tailscale CLI not called); allowlist `[tailnet]` or `[]` → Tailscale URL; allowlist with the public origin (case/whitespace-insensitive) or `"*"` → public origin; excluded public origin without Tailscale → error naming `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins`. Earlier cases (https origin with `tailscale.mode: off`, `basePath` + non-default port, `http:` / path / invalid origin falling back to Tailscale) still green. - `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: passed (exit 0). - `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed files; `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet` OK. Full `check:changed` was not run locally (its extension-test typecheck shard gets OOM-killed on the 15 GB dev host); relying on CI.
Runtime comparison: base (c75ff3cbf5) vs head, same script, stubbed tailscale status --json The script imports `resolveTelegramMiniAppUrls` (base file taken with `git show :extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/url.ts`), stubs `runCommand` to return `Self.DNSName = host.tailnet-example.ts.net.`, and runs it with `tsx`: ```text == base (i) publicOrigin, tailscale off: ERROR Mini App needs an HTTPS gateway URL. Set `gateway.tailscale.mode: serve` or `funnel`, then retry /controlui. (ii) mixed, allowedOrigins unset: pageUrl=https://host.tailnet-example.ts.net/__openclaw_tg_miniapp/ gatewayUrl=wss://host.tailnet-example.ts.net (iii) mixed, allowedOrigins=[tailnet only]: pageUrl=https://host.tailnet-example.ts.net/__openclaw_tg_miniapp/ gatewayUrl=wss://host.tailnet-example.ts.net (iv) tailscale serve only: pageUrl=https://host.tailnet-example.ts.net/__openclaw_tg_miniapp/ gatewayUrl=wss://host.tailnet-example.ts.net == head (i) publicOrigin, tailscale off: pageUrl=https://gateway.example.com/__openclaw_tg_miniapp/ gatewayUrl=wss://gateway.example.com (ii) mixed, allowedOrigins unset: pageUrl=https://gateway.example.com/__openclaw_tg_miniapp/ gatewayUrl=wss://gateway.example.com (iii) mixed, allowedOrigins=[tailnet only]: pageUrl=https://host.tailnet-example.ts.net/__openclaw_tg_miniapp/ gatewayUrl=wss://host.tailnet-example.ts.net (iv) tailscale serve only: pageUrl=https://host.tailnet-example.ts.net/__openclaw_tg_miniapp/ gatewayUrl=wss://host.tailnet-example.ts.net ``` Cases (iii) and (iv) are byte-identical between base and head.
Live trace: mixed ingress deployment (2026.9.7 with an equivalent local patch) ```text Deployment: OpenClaw 2026.9.7 + local patch with the same resolver semantics; Telegram channel; gateway.bind=loopback; gateway.tailscale.mode=serve (tailnet) AND gateway.publicOrigin=https:// (Cloudflare Tunnel connector on 127.0.0.1, gateway.trustedProxies=[127.0.0.1], gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins includes https://). Client: Telegram for Android 13.0.0. The phone is not on the tailnet: before the patch the Mini App opened https:///__openclaw_tg_miniapp/ and failed with net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED. Mixed ingress launch after the patch (UTC, gateway log, identifiers redacted): 2026-10-09T22:08:14.285Z Telegram DM Mini App command (/dashboard on 2026.9.x; /controlui on main) dispatched to the Telegram plugin 2026-10-09T22:08:15.452Z [telegram/send] telegram outbound send ok operation=sendRichMessage (Open dashboard web_app button) 2026-10-09T22:08:21.025Z [gateway/ws] webchat connected conn= remote=127.0.0.1 client=openclaw-control-ui webchat v2026.9.7 2026-10-09T22:10:33.211Z [gateway/ws] webchat disconnected code=1001 conn= durationMs=132411 (Mini App closed by the user) First launch on that device (Mini App auth route → bootstrap handoff → operator device): 2026-10-09T20:45:03.250Z [gateway] device pairing auto-approved device= role=operator 2026-10-09T20:45:38.401Z [gateway/ws] webchat connected conn= remote=127.0.0.1 client=openclaw-control-ui webchat v2026.9.7 remote=127.0.0.1 is the tunnel connector on loopback: the authenticated Control UI WebSocket came through the public origin, not through the managed Tailscale Serve listener, while Serve was active. ```
## Real behavior proof: test stand, stable → PR head (2026-10-10) Separate gateway instance (own profile, own Telegram bot, `gateway.bind: loopback`) published both ways, i.e. the mixed-ingress case from the review: - `gateway.tailscale.mode: serve` on a dedicated tailnet node (``); - `gateway.publicOrigin: https://` through a Cloudflare Tunnel, `gateway.trustedProxies: ["127.0.0.1"]`. The Telegram side is real: the owner account sends `/controlui` to the bot and opens the inline `web_app` button through `messages.requestWebView`, so the page gets Telegram-signed `initData` and the real launch ticket. Desktop runs open that URL in headless Chromium on a tailnet host. Phone runs use Telegram for Android 13.0.0 on a device that is **not** on the tailnet. | Run | Build | Config | Mini App URL | Result | |---|---|---|---|---| | R1 | 2026.9.9 from npm (`bcfc888`) | mixed ingress, `allowedOrigins` unset | tailnet host | tailnet client: page 200 → auth 200 → Control UI → WS 101, operator device paired. Phone: `net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED` | | upgrade | PR head `33bfb4a678` | same file | – | first start refused with "Sessions remain unavailable … run `openclaw doctor --fix`"; `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` migrated the agent DB (no gateway keys changed), then the same config started | | R2 | PR head | same mixed config | **public origin** | page 200 → auth 200 → Control UI → WS 101 in 1.15 s, operator device paired | | R3 | PR head | `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins: ["https://"]` (hot reload) | **tailnet host, retained** | page 200 → auth 200 → Control UI → WS 101 | | R3n | PR head | same as R3, Control UI opened on the public origin | – | rejected before auth (`origin-mismatch`, UI "Browser origin not allowed"): exactly the dead end the admission check avoids | | phone R5 | PR head + #167999 | mixed config | public origin | Control UI renders on the phone. Rendering in that Chromium 114 WebView needs #167999; with this PR alone the phone reaches the gateway, then the UI stops on `URL.parse` (documented in #167999) |

prs.title: fix: Markdown heading links open files without leaving the chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: clicking a Markdown file link with a heading fragment can leave the file reader and navigate to a nonexistent chat instead.

## User Impact

Users can follow document-relative links such as `multiplayer-agentic-workflows.md#additional-human-agent-development-records` and local `#section` links in Markdown previews without changing sessions. Existing session links, line links, and literal filename hashes remain supported. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Authored file destinations now keep path, line, and fragment separate, with percent decoding after fragment parsing. The existing reader supplies the document's path and carries heading requests through its retained-file navigation. Heading targets are document-scoped data attributes, not page-global IDs; the Markdown render cache also includes the document path.

## Evidence

### Follow-up assessment: retained-file refresh

The latest source-only timing finding is **not reproduced on the reviewed runtime at `83689dd0`**. A production-build browser scenario held the sixth `sessions.files.get` response, kept the same Markdown article mounted, then returned changed content with the requested heading placed 80 paragraphs below the old document end. The existing runtime scrolled to the new heading without changing the chat URL or resolving another session. Temporary tracing confirmed that the view-facing panel still held its previous fragment while the response was pending; its first callback for the new fragment saw the refreshed heading already rendered. The proposed early-consumption precondition was not observed.

The regression covering that delayed response and retained DOM is published at `cdcd432a`. The final Vitest report passes in **1.838 s** (**12.88 s** invocation, including a **9.23 s** production build); the UI-E2E-chat typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. No production code was changed. The independent authoring review could not complete due to a runner failure. This trivial, test-only update was published on explicit maintainer direction; no independent-review success is claimed.

- **Review findings repaired:** heading metadata is restricted to file readers with a document path, so the passive-document corpus is unchanged byte for byte; the sanitizer preserves level-five and level-six heading targets; relative resolution retains UNC roots and Windows separators.
- **Exact-head CI typing error repaired:** the browser test now checks the unknown RPC payload through runtime matchers rather than accessing an untyped property. The previously failing UI-E2E typecheck leaf passes locally.
- **277 tests pass across nine focused suites**, including the unchanged transcript corpus, file-link rendering, streaming, audio transcripts, hex colors, and workspace preview/reference/loading behavior. The review regressions reproduced **six failures before repair**, then all **66 tests in the two direct suites passed**.
- **Production-build browser regression passes:** sibling-document click, same-document keyboard navigation, and level-five/level-six heading clicks all reach their target in the existing reader, preserve the chat URL, and cause no new session resolution. The case takes **1.824 s**; invocation wall time is **29.84 s**, including a **24.93 s** production build.
- **Prior runtime-head validation (`83689dd0`):** UI typecheck, UI-E2E-chat test typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Independent Auto Review reported no P0–P2 findings for that runtime patch. The nine-suite invocation takes **7.60 s** (**9.36 s** wrapper wall time); the two direct suites take **1.79 s** (**3.47 s** wrapper wall time). Hosted CI timing is pending for the new head.
- **Conflict resolved against main at `3249150425a59cf49a9100685abb2b11e397e6ce`**, preserving upstream's inlined audio-transcript/hex-color handling. At that runtime head, the published source tree matched the locally tested/reviewed tree.
- **Original bug reproduction:** on base `518c1140`, clicking the guide link navigates from `/chat/main` to `/chat/multiplayer-agentic-workflows.md#…`; the reader fix prevents that navigation.
- **Screenshot access verified:** both existing public image URLs now return HTTP 200 with PNG bytes matching the inspected chat-delivered images. The earlier upload-access hold is resolved.

UNC and drive-path checks exercise the rendered-link boundary, not a live Windows filesystem. A previous broader browser-suite attempt stopped during bootstrap and is not relabeled passing. During the expanded proof, native scroll rounding placed a heading at 83.609375 px against an 84 px viewport edge; viewport assertions now compare at CSS-pixel precision. One setup attempt also failed with unpainted text before interaction; the browser flow now awaits font readiness. No product timeout or retry policy was relaxed.

### Before

Clicking the heading link exits the reader and navigates to a document-shaped chat route.

![Before: file reader lost after the heading link navigates away](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec48d196-315e-4b0a-b779-df0ba8e8481d)

### After

The sibling document opens at its heading in the existing session.

![After: target document and requested heading visible in the file reader](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d7abfdd-5070-44a3-8784-6d721ff1e093)

<details>
<summary>Scope and simplification</summary>

The fix reuses existing workspace preview, navigation, and Markdown-island owners; no replacement reader or route-level filename workaround. Net change against refreshed main: +154 production TypeScript/TSX lines, +280 test lines, +6 documentation lines. Added code carries document context and fragment intent and gives rendered headings local targets. The fixture recreates the reported guide/target names with synthetic content; no private guide content or logs are published.

</details>

## Worked on by

- @jjjhenriksen

prs.title: fix(telegram): open Mini App through the configured public origin
prs.body:
Supersedes #167985, thanks @aspalagin.
Related: #167981

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Telegram `/controlui` returns a Tailscale setup error or an inaccessible tailnet URL when the Gateway is already published through an HTTPS reverse proxy using `gateway.publicOrigin`.

## User Impact

Operators can open the Mini App through their configured HTTPS public origin. An explicit Control UI origin allowlist still controls whether that origin is selected; HTTP origins remain refused. Excluded or unusable public origins retain the existing Tailscale fallback. No migration or new setting is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Mini App URL owner now uses the shared `resolveGatewayPublicOrigin` helper, also used by other Control UI surfaces. It builds page, Control UI, and WebSocket URLs from one selected origin and preserves the Control UI base path. Public-origin precedence is explicitly authorized by the maintainer takeover task.

Simplification removed the redundant Tailscale published-host formatter call (no service name was supplied), a redundant base-path type check, and a separate derived Control UI URL variable. Production delta is +5 lines; the remaining growth admits HTTPS public origins against the configured allowlist. Test delta is +50 lines, with an exact allocation for URL admission/fallback regression coverage; the command and auth tests now exercise real URL resolution instead of supplying fixed URLs.

## Evidence

## What Problem This Solves

Provider access search in Control UI compares the query and card fields with `toLocaleLowerCase().includes` only. An NFD provider display name (or an NFD query) does not match its NFC form, so a user typing `münchen` can miss a provider labeled `München AI` in NFD.

## User Impact

Searching Providers by a name that uses combining marks can return no rows even when the provider is present, forcing users to guess another spelling or open the full list.

## Why This Change Was Made

Comparison-side NFC is the established Control UI pattern for local search (same as usage, dashboards, and the open session-sharing / where-picker fixes). Normalizing only the comparison copies keeps stored display names intact while making NFC and NFD forms interchangeable.

## Evidence

- New sibling test `ui/src/pages/model-providers/view.search-nfc.test.ts` mounts Provider access with an NFD `displayName` (`München AI`) and asserts both NFC and NFD `providerQuery` values match one `[data-provider-id]` row; it also retypes the query through the search input.
- Red on base: with the production change removed, the NFC query case fails (`expected 0, found 1` provider rows). Green with the fix: 2/2 pass.
- Production change is comparison-side only: `query()` and the card field check use `toLocaleLowerCase().normalize("NFC")` in `ui/src/pages/model-providers/view.tsx`.

## Merge Danger

- Stacked on the still-open session-sharing and where-picker NFC branches (`fix/session-sharing-nfc`, `fix/where-picker-nfc`); GitHub may list those files until those PRs land. This change only touches `ui/src/pages/model-providers/view.tsx` and its new sibling test.

prs.title: fix(release): unify plugin OIDC recovery preflight
prs.body:
## Problem

Merged #187991 added a safe trusted-publisher OIDC recovery preflight for regular plugin npm recovery, but extended-stable recovery still lacked that check. The shared workflow also did not independently require protected-tag preflight tooling to remain on trusted current-main ancestry, and regular recovery's selected-package rule existed only in operator guidance.

## Change

- Admit the existing read-only `trusted_publisher_preflight` job for extended-stable from protected `release-publish/*` tooling.
- Bind every trusted-publisher preflight tooling SHA to current `main` ancestry in addition to the protected tag's exact SHA binding.
- Preserve regular recovery as `publish_scope=selected` with an explicit package list.
- Preserve extended-stable as `publish_scope=all-publishable`, no explicit plugins, the exact canonical `extended-stable/YYYY.M.33` tip, and the existing final `PATCH >= 33` version rules.
- Keep artifact qualification and publication jobs unchanged.
- Replace the extended-stable caveat with the supported recovery command.

## Impact

Release operators can verify npm trusted-publisher authentication before either regular or extended-stable plugin recovery without packing or publishing. Invalid tooling, source, or selection combinations fail before the OIDC exchange.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/plugin-npm-extended-stable-workflow.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 58 passed
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json --incremental`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json test/scripts/plugin-npm-extended-stable-workflow.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check .github/workflows/plugin-npm-release.yml .agents/skills/release-openclaw-maintainer/references/publication-recovery.md test/scripts/plugin-npm-extended-stable-workflow.test.ts`
- Repository workflow guard scripts and `git diff --check`
- Independent P0–P2 re-review of the complete local diff: clean after fixing its regular-scope finding

The local `pnpm check:workflows` wrapper could not bootstrap pinned actionlint/zizmor because this host lacks Python venv/ensurepip support; PR CI remains the broad workflow-lint proof. No live npm OIDC exchange or publication was attempted.

## Simplification

One helper now owns current-main tooling ancestry checks across protected preflight and existing extended-stable admission paths. Tests share one executable policy fixture rather than duplicating workflow-policy setup. Production behavior growth is limited to the missing admission rules; artifact qualification and real publication remain on their existing paths.

prs.title: fix(mcp): unreachable remote MCP server no longer blocks Doctor-gated Gateway startup
prs.body:
Related: #162228, #144911, #143070

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: standalone Doctor lint rejects an otherwise usable installation when a configured remote HTTP/SSE MCP service is unavailable, including a server that initializes but never answers its tool-catalog request.

## User Impact

Recognized remote connection, authentication and deadline failures become actionable warnings tagged `mcp-service-unavailable`. An error-threshold Doctor gate can proceed while the affected remote tools remain unavailable.

**Scope narrowed in response to review:** local stdio startup failures remain errors, including ambiguous `mcp-remote` proxy failures. Numeric JSON-RPC errors, unknown failures, invalid catalogs, pagination-integrity failures and cleanup failures also remain errors. This is a partial fix, not a resolution of every case in #162228; it no longer asks maintainers to accept broken local children as warnings. No config or stored-data migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing MCP owners now retain a typed availability classification through catalog collection and startup backoff. The pagination owner supplies a typed deadline error; classification uses transport provenance and structured error fields, never server-message text. Doctor preserves the strongest finding when different inspection contexts report the same server, so an earlier warning or deferred-auth notice cannot hide an error.

The repair is reconstructed on newer main at `f91bca9546f5`, reusing the existing catalog-projection owner rather than expanding the oversized runtime module. Current updater probe deferral, OAuth inspection ownership, last-good catalogs and retry behavior are preserved. A local merge check against `1e48ec3a9e3` succeeds; its newer enterprise-MCP capability preparation is not overwritten.

## Evidence

### Actual compiled CLI behavior — October 21

Ten independent ordinary standalone invocations used credential-free synthetic private config/state, real loopback MCP transports and the compiled CLI:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --json \
  --only core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas --severity-min warning
# Repeat each scenario with --severity-min error.
```

| Synthetic failure | Finding at warning threshold | Exit: warning threshold | Exit: error threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Refused remote Streamable HTTP connection | warning; `mcp-service-unavailable` | 1 | 0 |
| Initialized remote server delays `tools/list` beyond the real 10-second deadline | warning; `mcp-service-unavailable` | 1 | 0 |
| Remote catalog repeats its pagination cursor | error; no availability code | 1 | 1 |
| Missing local executable | error; no availability code | 1 | 1 |
| Local stdio child exits during initialization | error; no availability code | 1 | 1 |

Every invocation reported `checksRun: 1`. At error threshold, remote-only warnings were filtered out (`findings: []`, exit0). Representative sanitized output projection:

```json
{"scenario":"refused-http","threshold":"warning","code":1,"checksRun":1,"severity":"warning","errorCode":"mcp-service-unavailable"}
{"scenario":"catalog-deadline","threshold":"error","code":0,"checksRun":1,"severity":"below-threshold","errorCode":null}
{"scenario":"closed-stdio","threshold":"error","code":1,"checksRun":1,"severity":"error","errorCode":null}
```

**Build provenance/limit:** this CLI proof ran on [assembled fork commit dda926bb935](https://github.com/Grynn/openclaw/commit/dda926bb93528517d02666179d4478579af6e4a9), which contains this exact repair plus separately reviewed immutable-launcher/runtime fixes and other local units. All 13 files in this PR are byte-identical there to `92b501e7e5af68ad01b829ff005739fe69ed45b1`. Its full `pnpm build` passed with the live-service safeguard enabled. This is real compiled CLI evidence, **not an exact standalone PR-head build, a production deployment or a full installed-release Doctor certification**. No serving credentials, user state or model calls were used. The older blocked CLI attempt remains historical evidence, not a success claim.

### Regression and cost evidence

- Production Doctor detector covers real refused HTTP, typed catalog deadline, remote auth and malformed/integrity controls. Same-server warning/error aggregation has genuine baseline failures and repaired passes. Stdio remains error without requesting a severity-policy exception.
- `pnpm test src/flows/doctor-mcp-availability.test.ts src/flows/doctor-core-checks.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **60/60 pass**, measured wall **51.65s**, peak RSS **5,591,232 KiB** (includes compiler/bootstrap work; not a steady-state latency benchmark).
- After final owner extraction: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-start-backoff.test.ts src/flows/doctor-mcp-availability.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-retirement-boundaries.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **32/32 pass**, measured wall **57.73s**, peak RSS **5,532,380 KiB**.
- Focused types, type-aware lint, formatting, scoped line-cap and diff checks pass. Final independent P0–P2 review of the full 13-file repair completed scoped-clean; its former compiled-CLI evidence gap is now addressed with the explicitly scoped proof above. Current-head PR CI remains separate from these local checks.
- Simplification: failure/retirement projection uses the existing catalog owner; the old duplicate retired-catalog literal is removed. Necessary growth is typed failure provenance and strongest-severity aggregation, plus distinct real transport/ordering regressions; no new manager, database schema or runtime policy option.

prs.title: docs(codex): RFC for recovering pending provider-review linkage
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/178923

Builds on merged prevention PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179054.

## What Problem This Solves

An earlier failed acknowledgment can leave an existing conversation bound to a replacement native thread while its pending provider review still identifies the original; the normal review UI then rejects continuation with `Provider review no longer matches the native thread`.

## User Impact

**RFC/design only, not a working recovery fix.** This draft does not restore affected conversations or change runtime behavior. It proposes verifying current authority, restoring the original link through canonical ownership, and then requiring a separate normal acknowledgment with all existing safety checks intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #179054 prevents new replacements but explicitly does not repair an already-mismatched binding. This draft records the recovery contract, a data-only native policy comparator, and an already-mismatched regression specification. It implements no recovery endpoint, authority issuer, binding/review mutation, or acknowledgment path.

The OpenClaw coordinator and native broker remain unimplemented. Confirmation of the provider's ownership/configuration guarantees remains a dependency: Codex 0.160.0 exposes useful policy fields, but matching those fields does not establish exclusive native ownership or a configuration generation valid through canonical commit. If existing native semantics cannot supply that guarantee, provider support is required. Unknown evidence must refuse recovery.

Consistency repair must preserve the pending review and cannot approve continuation, fabricate ownership, spoof a channel sender, bypass catalog/current-policy checks, or replay held input.

## Evidence

- **23 supporting offline checks passed** for the data comparator and scenario fixture (22 data-comparison checks and one fixture consistency check).
- **31 actual recovery acceptance scenarios are specified but unexecuted**, including recovery of an already-mismatched state, authorization failures, changed policy/catalog/review, concurrency, idempotence, partial/uncertain recovery, rollback/crash disposition, and separate normal acknowledgment.
- No successful recovery, live provider acceptance, full Gateway/native integration, repository Vitest/build/typecheck or CI result is claimed.
- Local proposal diff syntax and full-content privacy scans passed. Only generic fixture identities and public source references are included.

Before this can become a recovery fix, implement and validate the coordinator/native broker and catalog preparation, resolve the provider-guarantee dependency, and prove the already-mismatched regression fails on prevention-only #179054 and passes on the implementation. This RFC should not close an existing-mismatch recovery report.

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

Cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed recall require a Gateway-hosted owner and fail closed when that owner, route, incarnation, or policy is withdrawn. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain available.

## Implementation

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent.
- Recheck route, incarnation, aliases, physical owner, and policy at final disclosure.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory and direct Wiki consumers; filter final snippets, citations, and recall side effects synchronously.
- Preserve self-only reads, ordinary memory/wiki retrieval, and archived metadata-only inventory behavior.

prs.title: fix(oc-path): refuse JSON values on unsupported formats
prs.body:
Related: #189923

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw path set` accepts `--value-json` for Markdown and YAML but silently discards it. A command can report success while replacing a value with literal JSON text instead of the typed value the operator requested.

## User Impact

Unsupported uses now fail before editing with `not-writable`, explaining that `--value-json` only applies to JSON, JSONC and JSONL and directing the operator to a plain `<value>` without the flag. YAML and Markdown files remain unchanged. The CLI has a positional `<value>`, not a `--value` option.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the documented format-specific contract from #86060: Markdown strings and YAML scalar coercion are not new typed-JSON mutation formats. One guard in the shared edit owner rejects the flag before both replacement and insertion dispatch. No new flag, format, setting or type-conversion path. Existing JSON behavior and ordinary YAML writes are unchanged.

Reported by @jerome-queck in #189923. This addresses silent flag acceptance; typed YAML or Markdown values remain a separate feature request. It does not add YAML map/sequence replacement or alter null coercion.

## Evidence

Built canonical runtime artifacts in secretless Linux Docker, Node24.22.1, with real shipped CLI commands and isolated profile/config/state/workspaces. On frozen main `7faf32da36cdb`, two runs each write JSON text into YAML and Markdown frontmatter and report success. On the candidate, two runs each exit1, emit the clear refusal, and leave the complete files byte-identical. JSON typed-object writes and plain YAML scalar writes work identically on both refs.

Committed regression cases fail on main (2 intended failures/49passes) and pass on candidate. Focused CLI, universal and YAML suites:167passed/3files; final consolidated universal suite also passes. Targeted lint and formatting pass. Production+6/-0; tests+9/-9(net0); docs+4. Existing assertions remain; no test allocation increase. [Independent built CLI evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189941#issuecomment-6551864864).

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores silent flag acceptance; no migration or stored-state change. Blast radius is unsupported `--value-json` uses on Markdown/YAML through oc-path. These now refuse instead of writing misleading string values. Callers relying on the ignored flag must remove it; plain writes and supported JSON/JSONC/JSONL flag uses are unaffected.

prs.title: feat(pdf): add explicit OpenAI native document opt-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Platform users cannot explicitly choose native PDF document input through the PDF tool while preserving existing upload and model-selection behavior.

## User Impact

`agents.defaults.pdfNativeOpenai: true` opts an already-selected OpenAI vision model into complete-document input. **Unset or false preserves extraction and the existing provider order**, including saved configurations upgraded from the latest stable release. Selecting an OpenAI model alone does not authorize complete-document upload.

Page selection, passwords, unknown completeness, page/text/image truncation, size-limit violations, custom endpoints, Codex/ChatGPT transports and text-only models retain bounded extraction. Completeness checks still require the configured extractor. Existing Anthropic and Google paths are unchanged.

## Implementation

This replaces the earlier automatic-upload/provider-preference proposal with one default-off core boolean at the existing PDF configuration owner. The bundled OpenAI provider implements a narrow optional media-understanding hook using the official [PDF input contract](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/file-inputs): inline `input_file`, official Platform HTTPS `/v1/responses`, `store: false`, each PDF under 50 MB and combined PDF input at most 50 MB. There is no persistent Files upload, automatic provider preference or new dependency. The official configuration generator records the single additional core leaf; channel/plugin surfaces are unchanged.

Prepared credentials, headers and symbol-attached request/auth overrides use the existing scoped egress helpers. The native branch also reuses the host-owned `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` scope with `assertModelCurrent`, the **original model's** credential authority and the retained provider-resource assertion. The existing HTTP guard rechecks these synchronously immediately before dispatch after asynchronous preparation and on redirects. This closes the assert-only operator/credential retirement gap across lazy provider and DNS awaits without adding an authorization abstraction or changing shared HTTP behavior.

Capability adoption and the proposed setting placement remain normal maintainer product decisions. This branch provides a concrete default-preserving candidate for that decision.

prs.title: fix(skills): retain source context in review cancellation diagnostics
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A rejected Workshop experience review loses the source correlation and collapses every anchor mismatch into the same error. Operators cannot distinguish a rewritten completed turn from an unavailable anchor projection after the queued candidate is discarded.

Refs #156948, #164279. [Observed diagnostic limit and bounded scope](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/156948#issuecomment-6288213684).

## User Impact

Existing cancellation/failure logs identify the first failed anchor field (or `unavailable`) and a source fingerprint. No new raw identity, transcript value, conversation key, path or message content is recorded. Expected cancellations remain DEBUG; actual failures remain warnings.

The historical refusal cannot be reconstructed. This is diagnostic repair, not a claim that the historical refusal was incorrect or that the broader issues are resolved.

## Change

Reuse the existing comparison owner in SQLite and committed-actor readers. Every prior predicate, exact actor scope check, and physical database-path alias rule remains. The scheduler adds SHA256(JSON.stringify([agentId, sessionId, entryId])) to its existing log. `unavailable` means no usable anchor was returned; it does not assert deletion.

No schema, config, SQL query, retry, re-anchoring, acceptance policy or authority relaxation. Maintainer decision requested: accept the fixed field names and bounded source fingerprint in these existing diagnostics. No approval is assumed.

## Evidence

- Baseline `39fb90fb35d5ae628a0316fe40cd9b7b9bbbe055`: real SQLite validation lacks mismatch reasons; five scheduler cancellation/failure cases lack source correlation. The committed-actor diagnostic also failed before its change.
- After resolving the real GitHub conflict against official main `3213e3e542c5658f4095d08942f2636e6a40153e`, all **35 focused cases pass**. Main's actor-fixture simplification is retained, together with the generation diagnostic assertion. Existing lifecycle, permissions and SQL-statement controls remain.
- **Running compiled Gateway proof passes**, using standard source-QA plugin staging and loopback synthetic inference. Ten ordinary `chat.send` / `agent.wait` turns reach the unmodified review threshold. Public `sessions.compact` changes the transcript before the real idle timer runs the queued review. Its actual cancellation log has the expected bounded reason and independently calculated fingerprint at **DEBUG**. An eleventh ordinary turn succeeds. The owned Gateway exits. No scheduler callback or logger is mocked in this proof; no internal cancellation hook is injected.
- The reproducible opt-in scenario is `extensions/qa-lab/src/workshop-anchor-diagnostics.e2e.test.ts`. Its body takes **48.284s**, Vitest **78.10s** including compilation, wrapper **82.31s**. It retains the real 30-second product idle interval; the existing unit/SQLite suites own the cheaper predicate matrix. This opt-in E2E timing is local; hosted CI supplies the broader integration proof.
- Targeted proof types, lint, format, whitespace and outgoing-content gate pass. Fresh independent P0-P2 review is recorded separately; it does not execute the project.
- Prior head `bc5d003f689caafa456049d1e640d9029505dd8c` completed hosted production/test types, lint stripes, selected tests, security checks and aggregate CI successfully. Final head `5c99913874a641bc1091941508801aa0e98ec9c2` completed [hosted CI run 39413661817](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39413661817) with **SUCCESS**, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards and the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`. Production/test types, selected tests, lint, boundary, QA and security checks passed. Readback shows no failed or pending checks.

Captured terminal result from the isolated Gateway scenario (allowlisted fields only):

```json
{
  "candidateHead": "5c99913874a641bc1091941508801aa0e98ec9c2",
  "seconds": 82.31,
  "gatewayStopped": true,
  "foregroundTurnsCompleted": 11,
  "rewriteCompacted": true,
  "mismatch": "unavailable",
  "sourceFingerprint": "f294355d59610236b23c6f8e24d3298dd94d8a2446e70ceae7c8c17a4c88ccda",
  "sourceCorrelationMatches": true,
  "cancellationObserved": true,
  "severity": "DEBUG",
  "failureWarningAbsent": true,
  "ordinaryTurnAfterCancellation": "ok",
  "realGateway": true,
  "model": "loopback-synthetic",
  "delivery": false
}
```

The initial proof harness used the wrong log-accessor name; it was corrected. A packaged-plugin preparation attempt separately stopped in update-repair before readiness, while same-checkout static tooling held artifact ownership. Neither setup failure is used as a product verdict. The successful proof uses the supported source-staging route and runs serially after static checks, without bypassing a lock. This demonstrates the running diagnostic path, not package installation, stable-upgrade compatibility, live-provider behavior or official-release equivalence.

The integrated first head exposed a private test-helper import in the new proof fixture. Both failing boundary checks are addressed by using the existing public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/test-env` re-export of the exact same functions. The 20-case extension-boundary suite, corresponding static boundary check, lint, focused independent review, and the running Gateway proof all pass after this correction. No production employee runtime, downstream private patch/package, customer data, configuration or external delivery was changed.

prs.title: feat(agents): expose configured descriptions in agents_list
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent configuration accepts descriptions, but `agents_list` omits them. A requester choosing an allowed subagent cannot see the operator-authored capability summary. Fixes #7490.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose bounded, nonblank descriptions only in on-demand discovery. Preserve the complete authorized roster, ordering, resolved model/runtime metadata, and existing child-agent restrictions. Each description is limited to 512 UTF-16 units without splitting a surrogate pair, with a shared 4096 CJK-aware weighted-unit budget. Later description text may be shortened or omitted; agent rows remain.

## User Impact

Names, descriptions and existing model/runtime metadata remain available together. Documentation at the current per-agent-entry and subagent-discovery owners describes model visibility and excludes secrets or tenant-sensitive material. There is no new configuration, authorization, persistence, provider, or automatic prompt-roster mechanism.

Existing nonblank descriptions would become model-visible to already-authorized discoverers after upgrade without an operator editing configuration. That disclosure choice requires the maintainer decision below; the spawn allowlist alone does not establish prior operator expectations.

prs.title: fix(diagnostics): identify native main-thread stalls on Linux
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long Linux Gateway freezes can produce a stall profile with `samples=0` and no evidence of what the main thread was waiting for.

## User Impact

Operators get up to three live kernel snapshots in the existing bounded stall profile, without configuration changes. This adds diagnostic evidence; the underlying cause of a particular freeze still needs investigation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing JavaScript stall reporters run after the main thread resumes. A small Linux worker now observes a shared heartbeat and asynchronously reads the main thread's procfs state after a one-second gap. It records the wait channel, syscall number, permitted kernel-stack symbols, I/O and scheduler counters, process status counters, and system pressure. It never reads syscall arguments or memory addresses. Captures are bounded to three per stall and the full profile remains within 2 KiB.

Wait channels distinguish page/file waits, writeback, futexes, and compaction. Scheduler runtime and run-queue counters prevent treating every `R` state as scheduling starvation. Missing permissions and unsupported procfs facilities degrade independently. Existing profiler runtime/conflict policy is unchanged; related macOS policy work in #181551 remains separate.

## Evidence

- Real Linux/ARM64 Node 26.12.1 main-thread `Atomics.wait`: exact base lacks kernel evidence; candidate captures three `S` / `futex_wait` / syscall `98` snapshots. Unprivileged kernel-stack denial is tolerated; a privileged synthetic btrfs run also captures stack symbols.
- Node focused suites: 33 passed, one Linux-only test skipped on the macOS host; the same production entry point was exercised in Linux containers. Bun focused suites also passed. Combined kernel/JavaScript payload-cap regression included.
- Synthetic btrfs benchmark: 10,800 sessions with approximately 35 GiB SQLite blob payload, 62,000 files with 1.1 GiB workspace contents; baseline/candidate ABBA and idle A/A controls. No operator data. All 10 candidate stalls captured three snapshots; maximum profile size 993 bytes. Warm medians (8 windows/side): reporting 0.425→0.397 ms, total CPU per 3.6-second stall 9.295→11.520 ms, main-thread CPU 2.220→1.919 ms, main allocation 479,500→676,620 bytes, new worker allocation 1,267,532 bytes. Idle controls: total CPU 8.365→10.747 ms per 3.6 seconds, main CPU 2.055→3.149 ms, worker allocation 196,444 bytes; warm resident overhead approximately 7.7 MiB. Timing/allocation variability is substantial; no speedup claim. The explicit tradeoff is bounded off-thread diagnostic work and a lightweight always-on heartbeat.
- Codex local autoreview of the complete candidate against `cde4bfe4f10ce470ded7264c68d9a72ae03594cc`, P0–P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Only subsequent brace formatting, a Promise-executor lint fix in the benchmark, and the exact test-line allocation count changed. A second focused Codex review covers the subsequent mock-export CI repair.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all gates except the existing unused-export scan passed. Targeted lint and formatting pass. The base findings are `ChannelIdentityLinkAdapter` (introduced by #188910, `4674051ce50a`) and `PersonalGitHubActionV2` (last production consumer removed by #188910, `4674051ce50a`; the type itself originated in #168948). Both production and full-tree scans reproduce on the exact main parent `cde4bfe4f10ce470ded7264c68d9a72ae03594cc`. These are main regressions, not ignored noise.
- First CI attempt: the mock-completeness ratchet correctly rejected the new closed module mock. The correction preserves real exports with `importOriginal`; production code is unchanged. The guard passes; focused recorder tests pass on Node (18 passed, one platform skip) and Bun (17 passed, two native/platform skips). A second Codex P0–P2 delta review is scoped-clean.
- Production growth: +153 lines for the observer and recorder integration; tooling +79, tests +74 (explicit regression allocation). The new worker is necessary because no JavaScript detector currently runs during a blocked main thread. No database schema or cache changes.

Limitations: samples are non-atomic and best-effort; observer scheduling or filesystem delays can miss evidence. Zero V8 samples does not itself establish D-state blocking. The synthetic workload proves attribution and observer cost, not the cause or repair of any production freeze. PSI is unavailable in the local Docker kernel and is reported as empty arrays.

prs.title: fix(tests): bind read-worker tasks before starting sibling reads
prs.body:
## Problem

The sibling-close state-reader test assigns mocked worker tasks in submission order. Each cold read first awaits a filesystem probe, so two reads started together can consume those FIFO mocks in reverse order. The hourly CI failure rejected the closed read correctly but inspected the sibling's signal under the first task's label.

## Change

Wait until the first task is captured before starting the sibling read. Both task results remain pending when the first path closes, and every cancellation, sibling-survival, and pool-lifecycle assertion stays unchanged.

## Validation

- [Failing hourly CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41258366086/job/124706461537); source tracing identifies the task/path association inversion.
- The unchanged focused case passed locally, consistent with intermittent submission ordering; this is not a deterministic local red reproduction.
- All 20 tests in `src/state/openclaw-state-read-worker.test.ts` passed with the repository-pinned Bun runtime (11.8 seconds).
- Targeted formatting, type-aware lint, whitespace checks, and signed commit hooks passed.
- Fresh review of the exact committed diff found no correctness or security issues.

Local execution used an independent frozen installation with byte-identical determining state-reader modules and the exact edited test. This is boundary proof rather than a whole-head replay; current-head hosted CI supplies broader coverage.

Test-only change; no production behavior, dependencies, or public contracts change.

prs.title: fix(agents): Claude CLI per-call usage keeps the stream-start output count
prs.body:
Related: #148603

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Claude CLI per-call usage keeps the output count Claude Code reports when a model call starts (usually 1 to 5 tokens) instead of the call's real output, so `lastCallUsage`, and the live usage of single-call turns, undercount output.

## User Impact

User impact: for `claude-cli` turns, `lastCallUsage` now carries each call's real output count. Single-call turns (most plain replies) now show the right output tokens in `sessions.list`, `/status`, reply usage footers and cron run records, because their live usage is that call. Context sizing is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Claude Code's `assistant` snapshots repeat the usage from the start of their call. The final output count arrives only in that call's `stream_event` `message_delta`, which the stream parser never read (the gap listed under "Not in scope" in #148682 and in the 10-29 ClawSweeper summary on #148603). The parser now keeps each parent call's `message_start` usage and applies that call's `message_delta` output count to it. It merges into that call snapshot rather than the parser's latest usage, because a background agent's records (`task_progress` totals, subagent snapshots) can arrive in the middle of a parent call, and mixing them would under-size context. `message_delta` records with `parent_tool_use_id` (subagents) are ignored. Only the output count is taken from the delta, so a delta that reports only `output_tokens` still works.

This is the second remaining gap on #148603. The first one (live usage uses the latest call rather than the whole turn) is covered by the open #187118; the two changes touch different code and do not depend on each other. With both merged, `usage` is the whole turn and `lastCallUsage` is the latest call, with its real output.

## Evidence

- Tests in `src/agents/cli-output-jsonl.test.ts`, red on base `92b32cadcc3` and green with the fix:
  - The existing reparse test of the real Claude Code 2.1 capture `test/fixtures/cli/claude-2.1-thinking-progress.jsonl` pinned `usage.output` at 5 (the snapshot value). It now expects 534, the capture's `message_delta` and `result` value.
  - The real subagent capture `claude-2.1-subagent-forwarding.jsonl`: the last parent call's usage is now output 66 (its `message_delta`), not 4.
  - A new synthetic test: a `message_delta` with only `output_tokens` updates the call started by `message_start`, a background `task_progress` usage record in the middle of the call does not leak into it, and a subagent `message_delta` is ignored.
  - On base: 3 failed, 19 passed. With the fix: 22 passed. Cost: `pnpm test src/agents/cli-output-jsonl.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, about 1 s of test time.
- Consumers: every `src/agents/cli-output*`, `cli-runner*`, `cli-runner/*` and CLI transcript test, plus `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-cli-*.test.ts`: 109 files, 1,379 tests, all passing. `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, oxfmt, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:test-mock-exports`, `check:assertion-safety` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Runtime proof, built Gateway CLI in an isolated state dir (`openclaw agent --local --json` with the `claude-cli` runtime). A stand-in `claude` on `PATH` replays the real Claude Code 2.1 capture above over the live stdio transport. Same turn, base build vs this branch:

  | | base `92b32cadcc3` | this branch |
  | --- | ---: | ---: |
  | `agentMeta.usage.output` | 5 | 534 |
  | `agentMeta.lastCallUsage.output` | 5 | 534 |
  | `agentMeta.diagnosticUsage.output` (Claude's `result`) | 534 | 534 |
  | session row `outputTokens` (`openclaw sessions --json`) | 5 | 534 |
  | session row `totalTokens` (context) | 41,373 | 41,373 |

  The same turn with a background `task_progress` record (`usage.total_tokens: 9678`) inserted before the parent's `message_delta` gives the same values on this branch: output 534, context 41,373.

AI-assisted (Claude Code).

prs.title: fix: keep CLI subagent role instructions on follow-up
prs.body:
Related: #143017. Follow-up to #185887.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Claude CLI subagents lose their standing role instructions when a follow-up arrives without the original launch prompt. A persistent child also lost its persistent-mode instructions once its completed run record was swept, in both CLI and embedded preparation.

## User Impact

Child sessions retain their role and delegation-depth instructions on follow-up. Unchanged role inputs preserve the prepared system prompt and the native-session reuse decision. A persistent (`mode: "session"`) child keeps its persistent standing instructions and prompt fingerprint after the five-minute run-record sweep. Current depth policy and caller-provided additions still take effect. No configuration or migration is required. Children spawned before this change keep the previous fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

#185887 introduced a shared standing-instructions renderer and used it in embedded preparation. CLI preparation still consumed only the current request's extra prompt. This change uses that renderer at the CLI boundary and avoids repeating the role already supplied on launch. Main sessions, side questions, control operations and isolated completions keep their existing behavior.

The spawn mode used to come only from the retained run record. The registry sweeps completed session-mode records after `SUBAGENT_SESSION_RUN_TTL_MS` while the child session stays available. Follow-ups omit or force the cleanup flag, so a swept persistent child fell back to run mode. The spawn owner now records `spawnMode` on the child's session entry next to `spawnDepth`, `subagentRole` and `subagentControlScope`. Reset, rollover and lineage, capability facts and reserved plugin slot keys preserve it. A re-spawn on a reused key rewrites it. CLI and embedded preparation read the entry, or the stored row when the caller has no entry. They fall back to the run record and then the cleanup flag only for entries created before this change. `sessions.patch` cannot set the field.

## Evidence

Current head `297ddb9c845994a987f954efcb518a0a394e6c03`: patch commit `90c2702ea58bc20784c8e05c5312af313a7279d9` plus a merge of `main` at `8088fcd`. The merge conflict was in a test file only, and the diff against `main` is unchanged. The live proof and the before/after runs below used `90c2702` on base `9f3da25c107e88380e84f8a70f8f703422ba5995` (earlier qualified head `3360f06`). After the merge, the focused files, `tsgo:core`, the core test type shards, lint, format and the test-line ratchet were rerun.

- **Before:** the launch/follow-up regression fails at final system-prompt equality. The new swept-persistent regressions fail on the previous production code:
  - CLI preparation with no run record;
  - the embedded `persistent-swept` follow-up, which shows "Ephemeral";
  - spawn entry write and clear.
- **After:**
  - continuity, spawn-patch and embedded-prompt files: 57 pass;
  - capability-store, reconciliation, `sessions_send` authority, fast-path and policy consumers: 110 pass;
  - reset/rollover with `spawnMode` in the owned-child fixture: 7 pass.
  - These runs overlap with the earlier 102-test qualification, so the counts are not additive. That qualification covered the standing-instructions renderer, prefix stability and the synthetic Anthropic native-stdio boundary.
- **Static checks:** `tsgo:core`, the core test type shards, focused type-aware lint, formatting, test-line, max-lines, line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets pass (test-line allocation 173). A fresh independent review returned ready with no mandatory findings. Its one coverage note (rollover fixture) is applied.
- **CI:** the earlier red `checks-node-changed-compact-large-25` job was an inherited fixture failure in `subagent-spawn.production-boundary.test.ts` ("Gateway SDK resource host is not bound", #189317). #189329 fixed it on `main` after this PR's first CI run. The same failure appeared on unrelated PRs in that window. The later red `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)` on `90c2702` was a stale sidebar badge expectation in `boot-module-boundaries.e2e.test.ts`, fixed on `main` by #189641 (test-only). This PR changes no UI files.
- **Live proof (attached `claude-live-evidence-297ddb9.zip`, which supersedes `claude-live-evidence-90c2702.zip`):** both cases use the real Claude CLI native login. The persistent case was repeated on this exact head `297ddb9` with the same result (`live-proof.md` section 3).
  - **Run-mode child, `openclaw agent` on an isolated Gateway.** The child is followed up with `sessions_send`. The child's binding `extraSystemPromptHash` changes on base `9f3da25` (`a6f79a73…` → `84a5df93…`) and stays `a6f79a73…` on this head, with the same native Claude session resumed in both.
  - **Persistent thread-bound child, QA Matrix lane on a local homeserver.** After a 7-minute wait the child's run records go from 1 to 0, and the follow-up resumes the same native session. A pass-through observation of the `appendSystemPrompt` sent to Claude shows the difference. At `3360f06` the follow-up prompt contains "Ephemeral: termination after completion is normal." At this head it does not, and the entry carries `spawnMode: "session"`.
- **Upgrade from stable 2026.10.9 (`upgrade-proof.md`):** the published `openclaw@2026.10.9` ran a run-mode child that was then followed up. The same state was upgraded to this head with the documented `openclaw doctor --fix` (agent database schema 25 to 39).
  - **Stored data:** parent and child keep their OpenClaw sessions, and the model, runtime and `subagents.maxSpawnDepth` settings are preserved.
  - **Legacy child:** on 2026.10.9 its follow-up lacked `# Subagent Context`; after the upgrade it has it. Entries from before this change have no `spawnMode` and use the pre-existing fallback. On a `sessions_send` follow-up that fallback renders persistent wording, the same as at `3360f06` without any upgrade (control run).
  - **Legacy native session:** the changed prompt starts a fresh native Claude session once for such a legacy child. Its OpenClaw history remains.
  - **New child after the upgrade:** it records `spawnMode: "run"`, keeps its native session and code word, and gets run-mode instructions.

The tests use actual CLI admission, prompt preparation, binding hashes, native-session reuse resolution and the real session store with no run record. They are not a paid-provider cache or billing measurement. Restart and upgrade continuity is covered only by the single-process runs above. Broad platform coverage remains with PR CI.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction, scope and test cost</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.command-continuity.test.ts src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn-session-patch.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-system-prompt.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-models.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
```

To reproduce the failures, restore the production files to the previous head and keep the new tests. Verification used Windows, Node 24.22.1 and pinned pnpm 12.15.0 through the repository wrappers. The three-file run took about 5.5 minutes including worker preparation.

Scope: 21 files, +307/-19. Production is +127/-14: the CLI consumer plus the spawn-mode owner, preservation sites and store reader. Tests are 173 net lines with a matching allocation. The shared ceiling is unchanged. The existing renderer remains the single role owner, and no cache is introduced.

</details>
