prs.title: fix(codex): enable discovery for eligible restricted turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Restricted local Codex turns publish full dynamic-tool schemas even when the selected native model can discover deferred tools. This bypasses the existing searchable-loading setting and adds the complete schema surface to those turns.

## User Impact

Eligible restricted turns can use deferred schemas with the existing `codexDynamicToolsLoading` setting, whose default is `searchable`; explicit `direct` remains the opt-out. The model receives the complete qualified tool-name inventory and retrieves schemas through its native discovery mechanism. Tool execution still passes through the existing OpenClaw policy checks. Unlisted models, unavailable catalogs and the existing direct-loading exclusions keep direct declarations. Existing immutable thread catalogs and successor rules keep their current owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

The loading decision must use the selected model from `model/list` on the connection that will execute the turn. The patch acquires and retains that startup lease before preparing declarations, checks the native model identity, and preserves the existing ownership rules when acquisition fails or is cancelled.

A process replacement repeats connection-specific discovery but keeps the logical run's first context-engine assembly outcome, including an ordinary rejection. Reassembling there could substitute a different history after admission. Current-attempt authority and projection checks remain in their existing owners.

For these newly deferred restricted turns, the complete deferred-name inventory is admitted against the existing catalog-budget convention. Other searchable turns and retained native catalogs keep their existing admission. Overflow fails before native startup and tells the user to enable fewer tools, use a larger context window, or set `codexDynamicToolsLoading` to `"direct"`; count, size and limit stay in the diagnostic. It does not drop names or silently publish full schemas. Guidance follows the actual native calling surface, including Code Mode. There is no new configuration, SDK export, persistent cache or stored-data migration.

## Evidence

- Base: `9f3da25c107e88380e84f8a70f8f703422ba5995`. Current head: `d31deab6e9017a7d3190574ca1a300d0de037a46`, which is `9ab1559` plus a test-only commit. Earlier qualified head: `42ca0174d05b7545f0df08b73b4ce5d625eb6fa8`. Results below are for the earlier head unless marked as a review follow-up or an upgrade.
- **Upgrade from stable 2026.10.9 (attached `codex-discovery-evidence-d31deab.zip`, `upgrade-proof.md`):** a real isolated Gateway with the published `openclaw@2026.10.9` and `@openclaw/codex@2026.10.9`. The restricted agent (`tools.deny: ["group:runtime", "group:fs"]`) ran a `session_status` turn there. The same state was then switched to the upgrade target, with the documented `openclaw doctor --fix` (agent database schema 25 to 39).
  - **Stored data:** on every target, the existing session keeps its OpenClaw session and history and recalls the earlier tool result. `codexDynamicToolsLoading`, `tools.deny` and the model setting are unchanged.
  - **`searchable`:** the released 2026.10.9 already deferred 45 of 55 tools for this agent. After an upgrade to this head, the existing and new sessions defer 48 of 61 and call the tool. After an upgrade to base `9f3da25` they defer 0 of 61, because #175903 forces direct declarations when native discovery is unavailable.
  - **`direct`:** stays direct before and after an upgrade to this head.
  - This PR therefore keeps the released deferred behavior across the upgrade instead of switching restricted searchable agents to direct.
  - This PR adds no persisted field.
- **Review follow-up (`9ab1559fb125743ee3dc1143bf6798a7db73c81e`):** inventory admission now runs only for restricted turns whose model is listed on the executing connection, and the overflow `userMessage` names supported next actions. The overflow regression covers both paths at a 100-token window. The restricted turn fails before `thread/start`. The ordinary searchable turn starts and completes without a `model/list` probe; it fails with `TOOL_INVENTORY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` on the earlier head. `run-attempt.dynamic-tools` and `tool-inventory-budget` pass 24/24. Format, type-aware lint, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, max-lines, assertion-safety, test-mock-export, timeout-race and test-line ratchets pass. In `d31deab`, the redundant unrestricted catalog case is removed, as the review suggested. The overflow table's unrestricted row covers it. `run-attempt.dynamic-tools` passes 21/21, and the allocation is now 711. The self-referential catalog hash test and its fixture are removed. A fresh independent review returned ready with no blocking findings; the one wording note it raised is applied. The fixture-admission native acceptance below ran on the earlier head.
- **Shipped-entry live proof (`9ab1559`, attached `codex-discovery-evidence-9ab1559.zip`):** each run used a real isolated Gateway, two `openclaw agent` turns and a remote model through the Codex harness, on a turn restricted by `tools.deny: ["group:runtime", "group:fs"]`. With `searchable` configured, base `9f3da25` deferred 0 of 61 dynamic tools. This head deferred 48, and the model called the deferred `openclaw__session_status` after a native `ALL_TOOLS` search. Explicit `direct` at this head deferred 0. Each follow-up turn recalled the tool result without another call, in the same native thread. Limits: one model, tool and session per mode; prompts request discovery; no restart, upgrade, overflow or cache/billing claim.
- Baseline reproduction: the listed-model regression fails on the base after successful tool dispatch; the unlisted/direct control passes. With the patch, both pass.
- Focused candidate run: 301 passing tests in 16 files, six platform skips and one existing guarded-collector shell failure. The same unchanged `echo allowed` test fails on base production on Windows; its other two collector controls pass. No expected-failure exception was added. Coverage includes catalog fallback, exact native identity, inventory boundaries, client cleanup, startup-replacement recovery, and retained successful/rejected context assembly.
- Independent review found a borrowed-client abandonment defect in the initial port. The corrected fixture discriminates it: five borrowed-client regressions fail with the earlier helper while three owned-client controls pass; all 17 helper tests pass with the corrected helper. A separate fixture setup failure is retained in the evidence and is not counted as reproduction.
- Full `pnpm build` passes (15m56s), as do Codex packaged-entry types, the canonical extensions-test TypeScript graph, focused type-aware lint/format and line/environment ratchets. Node 24.22.1, pinned pnpm 12.15.0, Windows repository test wrapper with its supported Node fallback.
- Scope at the current head: 21 files, +1123/-64; production +363/-40, net test growth 711 lines with an exact allocation. No shared budget ceiling changes. The port keeps upstream prompt materialization and existing lifecycle owners instead of adding a parallel manager.
- Native acceptance on the earlier head passes with pinned Codex 0.164.0 in searchable and explicit-direct modes: two synthetic turns per mode, one actual tool execution, returned executor-only receipt, then same-thread recall without another call. Declaration exposure differs as expected. The probe uses production harness tool authority and real native/model I/O with isolated test admission/storage; it does not claim deployed-Gateway, durable-store or restart coverage. Prompts explicitly request discovery and forward the entire Code Mode result.

`model/list` membership is a conservative compatibility proxy, not a native capability flag. The supported source assumptions were inspected at Codex 0.164.0 (`6aaac694803004a63c6f393d153c96d22521a6b9`) and are recorded in the attached evidence; refreshed native metadata can drift. This patch does not repair Code Mode image projection or establish provider cache/billing savings.

prs.title: fix(auth): inline API-key failures break on PostgreSQL agent stores
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Gateway using PostgreSQL agent storage cannot record an authentication failure for a config-backed API key and instead reports “PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker.”

## User Impact

User impact: inline API-key failure bookkeeping completes on PostgreSQL without a spurious database-thread error. The caller keeps its normal provider sign-in error, and SQLite keeps its existing behavior. No schema, configuration, public API, or migration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The operation already captures the agent database execution before asynchronous preparation. Pass that execution to the existing worker store instead of acquiring a second, native database handle on the Gateway thread. Write ordering, live-owner checks, transaction/publication handling, and cleanup remain with their existing owners.

The simplification removes nine net production lines (mostly wrapper removal; the larger displayed diff is indentation). The regression reuses the existing Gateway-thread subprocess harness and production retry controller. Its 138 new test/support lines have a separate test-line allocation; the shared budget is unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Before:** on base `975e68cf820a536e068a3c04fdc511ac28005693`, the PostgreSQL 17.6 Gateway-role probe exits 1 at `withOpenClawAgentDatabaseRuntime` with the main-thread guard error. The same probe succeeds on SQLite.
- **After:** the PostgreSQL probe succeeds and both caller-visible and persisted failure counters equal 1. Unrelated main-thread PostgreSQL SQL still refuses before and after the operation.
- **Focused conformance:** 15/15 tests pass: the new PostgreSQL/SQLite subprocess regression (2 tests, 3.92 s file duration) plus the existing inline-auth worker suite (13 tests, 10.90 s). The complete focused invocation, including preparation, took 50.62 s. CI timings are not yet available.
- **Static checks:** core typecheck, state/logging test typecheck, lint and formatting on all four TypeScript files, staged whitespace check, and test-line ratchet pass.
- **Independent review:** bound Auto Review, OpenClaw engine / `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, local candidate against the exact base above, P0–P2 coverage: `scoped-clean` with no findings. The reviewer inspected source and supplied results; it did not independently rerun tests.

### Full built-Gateway before/after proof

Ran on 2026-11-01 at 01:28 UTC with real PostgreSQL 17.6 and isolated state. Both source snapshots were built through the supported `sourcePerformance` build profile: baseline `975e68cf820a536e068a3c04fdc511ac28005693` and this exact PR head `1c4c86387d86ed90417d22776034807461026cca`. The PR source tree was verified as `3c41427fbe1ce1c3318095f9dd3f0a7939c9356f`.

Each case launched its own **actual built Gateway process**, connected an authenticated normal test client, then executed `sessions.create → chat.send → agent.wait → chat.history`. A loopback OpenAI-compatible provider fixture received the real configured API-key request and returned HTTP 401 with `authentication_error / invalid_api_key`. Gateway execution, model routing, the retry controller, transcript persistence, and database writes were real—not mocked or called directly by the fixture.

| Built revision | Agent engine | Provider requests | Persisted inline errorCount | Forbidden native-open diagnostic | Public terminal/history |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| baseline `975e68c` | PostgreSQL | 1 | 0 | Present | Normal sign-in error; 2 history messages |
| PR `1c4c863` | PostgreSQL | 1 | 1 | Absent | Same sign-in error; 2 history messages |
| baseline `975e68c` | SQLite | 1 | 1 | Absent | Same sign-in error; 2 history messages |
| PR `1c4c863` | SQLite | 1 | 1 | Absent | Same sign-in error; 2 history messages |

Every request's Authorization header matched the synthetic config-backed key. The terminal status is intentionally `error` because the provider returns 401; the public error remains “Couldn't sign in to the AI service.” This fix repairs the missing durable bookkeeping and spurious internal database error, **not** the provider's authentication failure. Counters were read from the actual agent store after each Gateway stopped; no expected counter was seeded.

The live WebSocket hello reported the expected build identity in each case:

- Baseline: `2026.10.9-975e68cf820a-2026-11-01T01-07-49.804Z`
- PR: `2026.10.9-1c4c86387d86-2026-11-01T01-09-15.610Z`

The repository E2E runner completed all four arms successfully: one fixture test, **32.36 s** of test time, **80.25 s** file duration / **91.44 s** complete successful invocation including compiled-process preparation. Temporary fixture SHA-256: `f76e215c18c96949a8943597c5b9fd373a9c6abcce31e08e7bb18e4b22859151`; inspected result JSON SHA-256: `6474feafe5a94de5af25491bffe45b555818e2b2dd0b349b1db4d7cb66c6128e`. These identify local artifacts, not independent attestations.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized observed output and invocation</summary>

```text
base postgres requests=1 authorized=true terminal=error historyMessages=2 persistedErrorCount=0 forbiddenNativeOpen=true
head postgres requests=1 authorized=true terminal=error historyMessages=2 persistedErrorCount=1 forbiddenNativeOpen=false
base sqlite   requests=1 authorized=true terminal=error historyMessages=2 persistedErrorCount=1 forbiddenNativeOpen=false
head sqlite   requests=1 authorized=true terminal=error historyMessages=2 persistedErrorCount=1 forbiddenNativeOpen=false
Test Files 1 passed (1); Tests 1 passed (1); exit 0
```

The temporary fixture uses the repository's `withBuiltGateway` / managed-process owner and real public RPCs, with source snapshots made using `git archive`. It was run through `pnpm test test/pg-inline-gateway-proof.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, with workspace-local HOME/state/workspace/log/temp roots, the private local PostgreSQL connection, and bounded `GOMAXPROCS=2 RAYON_NUM_THREADS=2`. Initial setup attempts exposed and corrected only an exhausted local compiler thread budget and an obsolete fixture-only heartbeat key; neither was counted as behavior proof, and no runtime guard or declaration requirement was disabled.

</details>

**CI at this head:** [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41257881888/job/124710190907) and PostgreSQL conformance [1/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41257881888/job/124705178436), [2/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41257881888/job/124705178390), [3/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41257881888/job/124705178415) are successful.

Limits: the provider protocol response is a local deterministic fixture, not paid/live inference. This matrix keeps shared state on SQLite while selecting the tested agent engine. It is not the Team server's production migration or a qualification of every mixed-engine family combination. No live Team data or service was changed; every disposable Gateway and the test PostgreSQL server were stopped.


Contributor credit: Mitchell Etzel (@etzelm), for the migration investigation and request.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @etzelm](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/65edb98b-73fa-47e9-8242-be1ae73fb4b9)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bd8637e5-f2c4-4c31-90a8-2bac60980c3e)

prs.title: fix(ui): keep the PDF toolbar download's original filename
prs.body:
Closes #187543

## What Problem This Solves

Downloading an uploaded PDF from the Control UI's native PDF viewer toolbar suggests a name like `57384738-0f0c-4235-ae6f-d93b180ee80d.pdf` instead of the file's original name. The fix names the preview's blob URL after the attachment, so the toolbar download keeps the original filename.

- Problem: the preview hands the browser's native PDF viewer a bare `blob:` URL; the viewer's toolbar download derives its suggested filename from the URL, and a bare blob URL has only its UUID. The server's correct `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="r75-monthly-report.pdf"` never reaches that handoff.
- Solution: append `#<original filename>` to the blob URL passed to the viewer iframe — Chromium's PDF viewer uses the URL fragment as the suggested download name for blob URLs. The blob identity and its revocation are unchanged.
- What changed: the iframe source in `chat-pdf-preview.tsx` plus a Chromium browser test asserting the fragment. What did NOT change: the attachment card's download action (already correct), the worker asset, and any server route.

## Why This Change Was Made

The defect is purely in the viewer's blob handoff, and the URL fragment is the browser-native way to carry a suggested filename across it.
- Best fix: a one-line presentation-level change reusing the label the component already treats as the filename.
- Alternative rejected: adding an authenticated filename-bearing route or changing the media response — the server response already carries the right name, and a new route would widen the security surface for no gain.

## User Impact

Downloading from the PDF viewer toolbar saves `r75-monthly-report.pdf` instead of a UUID; document bytes and the card-level download are unchanged.

## Evidence

Real Chromium (vitest browser mode) rendering the shipped component with a real preview worker and a real blob handoff, asserting the viewer's URL carries the original name:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-pdf-preview.browser.test.tsx
✓ |chromium| src/pages/chat/components/chat-pdf-preview.browser.test.tsx (1 test) 53ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

The test asserts the rendered `iframe.sidebar-pdf-preview__frame` `src` is a `blob:` URL ending in `#r75-monthly-report.pdf`; with the fix reverted the same test fails on that assertion (bare blob URL). Chromium's PDF toolbar derives its suggested filename from that fragment.

What was not tested: clicking the native toolbar itself (browser chrome, not page DOM) and non-Chromium viewers.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `git grep` and a vitest browser-mode run to analyze issue #187543, locate the bare blob handoff in `chat-pdf-preview.tsx`, and implement the fragment-based filename. The implementer understands the code: the native viewer names toolbar downloads from the iframe URL fragment, so the preview must append the attachment's original name there. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(codex): normalize overlength Responses call_id in settled-turn projection
prs.body:
Fixes #130965

## What Problem This Solves

When a Codex-harness turn finishes its tool work without producing final text, OpenClaw runs *settled turn finalization*: it projects the transcript into raw OpenAI Responses items and injects them into the Codex thread via `thread/inject_items`.

On current `main`, `extensions/codex/src/app-server/settled-turn-projection.ts` never bounds the replayed `call_id` to the 64-character Responses contract:

- `requireCallId()` (`:51-57`) rejects only empty ids and ids longer than **256** characters — it never rewrites.
- The `function_call` emission (`:154-165`) and the `function_call_output` emission (`:181`/`:234`) embed that id verbatim.

So an 83-character historical `call_id` reaches OpenAI unchanged and the request is rejected:

```text
Invalid `input[3].call_id`: string too long. Expected a string with maximum length 64, but got a string with length 83 instead.
```

Finalization then fails closed, the channel surfaces a generic generation error, and the affected session has to be deleted to recover (`impact:session-state`, `impact:message-loss`).

**The upstream harness is not a viable fix site.** I checked `openai/codex` at tag `rust-v0.153.0` (`41e22fee981a63b3698df7ed36bad393cda24715`): `thread/inject_items` forwards `call_id` byte-identically.

- `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs:943-971` — `thread_inject_items_response_inner` deserializes each raw item into a `ResponseItem`, calls `validate_response_item_image_urls(&items)?` (its only validation), then `thread.inject_response_items(items)`. No `call_id` inspection.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs:34-60` — that validator rejects only remote HTTP(S) `input_image` URLs; `ResponseItem::FunctionCall { .. }` is in the pass-through arm.
- `codex-rs/core/src/codex_thread.rs:617-652` → `codex-rs/core/src/session/inject.rs:72-107` — `inject_client_response_items` maps items through `annotate_client_response_item`, which only attaches `CodexHarnessMetadata { client_authored }` for developer messages and otherwise stores the `ResponseItem` unchanged.
- `codex-rs/core/src/context_manager/normalize.rs:21-80` — the only history-level `call_id` logic (`ensure_call_outputs_present`) *pairs* missing outputs by cloning `call_id` verbatim; it never shortens or rewrites.
- No `call_id` length bound exists anywhere under `codex-rs/`.

Whatever the projection emits is what OpenAI receives, so the contract has to be enforced here.

## Why This Change Was Made

A per-projection deterministic resolver rewrites overlength ids into the `call_` ≤64 Responses shape, and **both** emission sites resolve through it, so a `function_call` and its `function_call_output` can never diverge.

- Resolution happens where the id is read (`resolveCallId(requireCallId(...))`), so the emitted items *and* the duplicate / ambiguity / completeness bookkeeping in `projectSettledCodexMessages` operate on one id space.
- The map is created inside `projectSettledCodexMessages` — per invocation, not module-level.
- The rewritten tail is derived from a `sha256` prefix of the **full original id**, so the mapping is stable across calls and processes, and two distinct overlength ids cannot collide.
- Ids already within 64 characters pass through **byte-identical** — no gratuitous rewriting, so prompt caching and every currently-working id are unaffected.
- Empty ids and ids over the existing 256-character sanity bound still throw exactly as before. Only the (64, 256] band changes behavior, from "silently forwarded and rejected by OpenAI" to "deterministically rewritten".

Production change is ~30 lines in one file. **No new configuration option. No new plugin-SDK export. No change outside `extensions/codex/src/app-server/`.**

### Local implementation vs. exporting core's resolver

Core already owns an equivalent transform — `createOpenAIResponsesToolCallIdResolver` / `normalizeOpenAIResponsesToolCallIds` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/openai.ts:95-190` — but it is **not exported through `plugin-sdk`** (`normalizeOpenAIResponses*` appears nowhere under `src/plugin-sdk/`), and extension production code may only cross into core via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` (root `AGENTS.md:94-95`).

I asked on the issue which shape you prefer and did not want to block on the answer, so this PR ships the **local** option and documents it in a comment at the resolver:

| | Local resolver (this PR) | Export core's resolver through plugin-sdk |
|---|---|---|
| Plugin-SDK surface | unchanged | widened (a new published API) |
| Duplication | one structurally similar resolver | none |
| Blast radius | `extensions/codex` only | every plugin-SDK consumer |
| Decision owner | contributor | maintainers |

If you would rather have the export, say so and I will swap the implementation — the tests are written against projected output, not the resolver, so they carry over unchanged.

Two deliberate differences from core's version, both narrowing scope rather than widening it:

- **Pass-through predicate is length-only** (`id.length <= 64`), where core additionally requires the `^call_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,59}$` shape. The reported failure is a length rejection, and a length-only predicate guarantees every id that works today keeps working byte-identically. A stricter predicate would rewrite currently-valid ids (including this file's own `"call-1"` fixtures) for no reported benefit.
- **No `callId|itemId` pairing split.** Core handles that because it also normalizes `function_call.id`; this projection emits only `call_id` and never an item `id`, so the pairing form does not arise here.

## User Impact

A Codex-harness turn that replays a historical tool call with an overlength `call_id` now finalizes normally instead of failing closed and stranding the session. Every id that already satisfied the Responses contract is untouched.

## Evidence

All of the following was actually run — no step is claimed from inspection alone.

**Pre-fix red (stash method), local, base `d2a616bdf373a5b3cac0add8e9b2f70cd0802f42`.** With the production file stashed and only the new tests present:

```text
× projectSettledCodexMessages > rewrites overlength call ids once per projection and keeps the pair deterministic
AssertionError: expected 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa…' to match /^call_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,59}$/
Tests  1 failed | 23 passed (24)
```

That is the defect case failing for the intended reason — the 83-character id arrives unrewritten. The other added cases (pair identity, collision-freedom, byte-identical short ids, and the duplicate / ambiguity / completeness guards under overlength ids) pass on base by construction: they are regression guards protecting behavior a careless fix would break, not additional proofs of the defect.

An earlier standalone reproduction against untouched `main` printed the projection directly and showed the failure end to end:

```text
"type": "function_call",       "call_id": "call_…MnQwE"   (83 chars)
"type": "function_call_output","call_id": "call_…MnQwE"   (83 chars)
call_id lengths: 83 83
```

**Post-fix green, local.** `settled-turn-projection.test.ts` → **30 passed (30)**, every pre-existing case included.

**Changed-file gate, local.** `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- extensions/codex/src/app-server/settled-turn-projection.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/settled-turn-projection.test.ts` → **exit 0**, all lanes green: conflict markers, max-lines ratchet, assertion SAFETY ratchet, changelog attributions, doctor deprecation registry, guarded extension wildcard re-exports, plugin-sdk wildcard re-exports, **extension test core imports**, duplicate scan coverage, dependency pin guard, format, doctor contract closure, **plugin boundaries**, package patch guard, **typecheck extensions**, **typecheck extension tests**, **coercion helper declaration guard**, deprecated API usage, **dead export scan (Knip: 0 entries, script/production/full-tree)**, lint, database-first legacy-store guard, media download helper guard, runtime sidecar loader guard, **runtime import cycles (0)**.

**Two-sided proof on an isolated Linux box** (Hetzner VPS, Docker `node:26`, fresh clone of base `d2a616bdf3`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`):

- **Side A** — base + *test file only*: `settled-turn-projection.test.ts` → `Test Files 1 failed (1)`, `side-a exit=1`, failing case `rewrites overlength call ids once per projection and keeps the pair deterministic`.
- **Side B** — base + *full patch*: same file → `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `side-b exit=0`.

So the change is what turns that case from red to green, reproduced on a second OS and a clean dependency tree — not just on my machine.

**Adjacent suite.** On the pre-reservation head, `npx vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/` was exit 0 with **3430 passed, 0 failed**. Re-running it locally on the current head reached **3460 passed with 0 test failures** and then aborted on a vitest worker crash under local disk pressure, so I am not presenting that re-run as a clean green — CI on this head is the authoritative adjacent signal.

`pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` is not applicable to this change and was not run: the fix adds no plugin-SDK export, and the boundary is instead covered by the `plugin boundaries` and `extension test core imports` lanes above, both green.

Core is untouched — the diff is exactly two files, both under `extensions/codex/src/app-server/`.

### ClawSweeper review round 1 — P1 collision, fixed in `64929bd861`

ClawSweeper blocked this with a P1 I had missed, and it was right. The rewrite puts generated ids in the same `call_` space raw ids occupy, and nothing kept them apart. Since `projectSettledCodexMessages` keys its duplicate / ambiguity / completeness bookkeeping by the *resolved* id, a transcript carrying both an overlength id **and** a legitimate raw call whose id equals that id's rewrite was rejected as `duplicate tool call` — the exact fail-closed finalization this PR exists to remove.

I reproduced it before changing anything. Projecting the overlength pair alone yields `call_aaaa…aaaa_8ddbdef916`; feeding a transcript that holds that id *and* the overlength one threw `Codex settled-turn projection found a duplicate tool call`.

Worth being explicit: three independent model reviews all saw this overlap and waved it through as "~2^-40, fail-closed, not a practical hole". They were wrong — the colliding value is *derivable*, not merely improbable, and a history that mixes normalized and original ids (exactly the provider-switch origin the issue describes) can contain both. The bot caught what the reviewers rationalized.

Fix: collect every id the transcript replays verbatim before resolving, and skip those when generating. A clash re-derives from a salted hash of the original instead of colliding, and generated ids are reserved as they are produced so two rewrites cannot converge either. Salting is deterministic, so the mapping stays a pure function of the transcript. The mixed-collision regression the review asked for is added, and it fails with the reservation disabled, reporting exactly `duplicate tool call`.

Production delta for this round is **+57/−9**. That growth is the reservation invariant itself — the passthrough scan, the salted rebuild, and the taken set. I could not absorb it into the existing resolver: it cannot know which raw ids a transcript will replay until it has seen them, so the pre-pass is load-bearing rather than defensive.

### ClawSweeper review round 2 — boundedness regression, fixed in `1c24988fab`

Round 2 confirmed the collision fix was addressed, and caught a second defect — one my *own* round-1 fix introduced. Reserving replayed ids needed the whole id set up front, and the shortest way to get it was `[...messages]`. That defeats the caller: `settled-turn-context.ts:136` passes `verifiedSettledMessages()`, a **generator** that pulls message payloads lazily, precisely so the projection can reject at its item and byte limits *before* the rest of the history is read. Draining it first forces every later SQLite payload to load even for a transcript the projection was about to refuse.

I checked the caller this time rather than assuming: `function* verifiedSettledMessages` at `settled-turn-context.ts:55`. The finding is correct.

Fix: stream again, and defer the rewrite. Bookkeeping keys on the **original** ids, exactly as it did before this PR, so duplicate / ambiguity / completeness still hold on unmodified values and no rewrite can invent a duplicate. Once the transcript is proven complete, rewrite the collected items — already bounded by `MAX_RESPONSE_ITEMS` and `MAX_PROJECTION_BYTES`. The resolver still reserves every verbatim-replayed id, so round 1's collision fix is preserved.

Added a laziness regression: a generator that throws if drained past the item limit. It fails with the materialization restored, reporting `history was drained past the projection limit`.

This round is **+49/−47** production, so close to net-neutral, and the deferred rewrite is simpler than the pre-scan it replaces. Cumulative production growth over the whole PR is now modest rather than the +57 round 1 carried.

### Injection-boundary proof — added in `c7ce0f4eee`

Round 3 was right that the assertions stopped one layer short: OpenAI rejects the *request*, and what reaches OpenAI is whatever `bounded-turn` hands to `thread/inject_items`. So I moved the assertion to that boundary.

`settled-turn-injection.test.ts` drives the **real** `runBoundedCodexAppServerTurn` against the repo's existing fake app-server client and asserts on the **recorded `thread/inject_items` params** — the outbound payload, not the projection's return value. Observed request sequence:

```text
model/list -> config/read -> configRequirements/read -> thread/start
  -> mcpServerStatus/list -> thread/inject_items -> turn/start
```

Two-sided at that boundary, from the same 83-character source id:

| | on-the-wire `call_id` lengths | result |
|---|---|---|
| base `d2a616bdf3` | `83, 83` | fails — `expected 83 to be less than or equal to 64` |
| this branch | `64, 64` | passes, both sides identical |

**What this is, precisely:** a harness-level boundary proof. The transport is faked and **no Responses call is billed**. It is not a live Codex session, and I am not presenting it as one.

**What was still missing at that point** — an after-fix trace from a real authenticated Codex app-server against the live Responses API — is now provided in the "Live proof" section below, run on my own subscription login rather than a maintainer budget.

**Independent pre-submission reviews.** Three independent models reviewed the diff read-only against the caller chain, core's equivalent transform, and the repo's extension-boundary and test-audit rules. All three returned **GO** with no CRITICAL or MAJOR production findings. Their MINOR/NOTE points are folded into this description rather than waved away:

Both of the review's test-coverage findings are now **fixed in `50f5ffb1e6`** (tests only, no production change):

- **The `<= 64` passthrough boundary was unpinned.** The gate is inclusive on purpose — the Responses `maxLength` is 64, so a 64-character id must stay byte-identical — but the suite only exercised lengths 83 and 6, so narrowing it to `< 64` would have silently begun rewriting ids that already replay correctly, with every test still passing. There is now a case asserting a 64-character id is projected unchanged on both sides while a 65-character id is rewritten into the `call_` ≤64 shape and stays identical across the pair. I confirmed it **fails under exactly that `< 64` mutation** (`Tests 1 failed | 27 passed`, the boundary case) and passes once restored — so it is pinning the bound, not just describing it.
- **The fail-closed table had lost its short-id coverage.** `missing result` / `duplicate call id` / `tool-name mismatch` had been retargeted from `"call-1"` onto the overlength id. Those three rows are now generated for *both* id shapes from a single helper rather than a duplicated table, so the pre-existing short-id paths stay covered alongside the overlength ones (`fails closed for 'duplicate call id (short id)'` and `… (overlength id)`, etc.).

- **The resolver comment overstated its fidelity to core.** It said it "keeps a local copy" of core's resolver, when the trigger is deliberately narrower (length-only vs core's shape regex and `call_id|fc_id` pairing split). Left as-is, someone could later swap in core's resolver assuming parity and silently change emitted ids for previously-passthrough transcripts. The comment now states the narrowing and why, in `1a65b3eee9` (comment only, no behavior change).

Suite after the deltas: **30 passed (30)**; `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` → **exit 0** on both changed files.

- The collision-freedom test passes on base, so it is a companion invariant guarding against a plausible bad fix (deriving the tail from the truncated prefix alone — the two fixtures share an 82-character prefix and differ only in the last character, leaving the hash as the sole discriminator). It is not itself a bug-regression test, and I am not citing it as one.
- The 256-character bound is no longer the API-conformance bound; it survives as an absurd-input ceiling that preserves base fail-closed behavior. Worth a comment line so a later reader does not mistake it for dead code.
- If OpenAI ever enforces the `call_` *shape* rather than only the length on injected history, this projection would still fail closed; exporting core's resolver is the durable answer, and at that point this local copy should be deleted rather than aliased (`AGENTS.md:111`, one canonical path).
- Three of the four fail-closed guard cases now use the overlength id instead of `"call-1"`. That is a net widening — the duplicate case now also fails if the rewrite ever becomes non-deterministic — but the pure short-id variants are gone; `"call-1"` byte-identical pass-through keeps its own dedicated case.

*Disclosure: this contribution is by Sho (human, @shojikumaru) working with AI assistance — implementation by an AI agent under my direction, with the verification above run and read by me, plus independent model reviews before submission. Maintainer edits are welcome: "Allow edits by maintainers" is enabled.*

### Live proof — real managed Codex app-server against the live Responses API

The remaining gate was an after-fix trace from a real authenticated Codex app-server, not a fake transport. That trace now exists, and it is two-sided. It was produced on my own ChatGPT-authenticated Codex login (no maintainer budget involved, no API key), so the earlier "I will not spend a maintainer's API budget uninvited" objection no longer applies.

**Setup.** A `*.real-binary.live.test.ts` harness in the same style as `thread-lifecycle.restricted-mcp.real-binary.live.test.ts`: it calls the **real** `runBoundedCodexAppServerTurn` with the finalizer's exact parameters (`taskLabel: "settled-turn finalization"`, `requireNoExternalCapabilities: true`, `allowEmptyText: true`, `historyItems` from `projectSettledCodexMessages`) and a `clientFactory` that wraps the real `createIsolatedCodexAppServerClient` (managed `@openai/codex` 0.153.0 binary, `homeScope: "user"`, native ChatGPT auth) with a `request` spy so the literal `thread/inject_items` params are recorded as they go to the app-server. Nothing is faked between the projection and OpenAI. The source transcript is the same 83-character `call_` id used by the unit tests. The base side runs the projection file checked out at `d2a616bdf3` (the merge base) through the identical path.

**Result.** Same request sequence on both sides:

```text
model/list -> config/read -> configRequirements/read -> thread/start
  -> mcpServerStatus/list -> thread/inject_items -> turn/start
```

| | on-the-wire `call_id` (from the recorded `thread/inject_items` params) | live Responses outcome |
|---|---|---|
| base `d2a616bdf3` | `83, 83` — the raw id forwarded verbatim | **rejected, HTTP 400**: `[StringParam] [input[3].call_id] [string_above_max_length] Invalid 'input[3].call_id': string too long. Expected a string with maximum length 64, but got a string with length 83 instead.` |
| this branch `c7ce0f4eee` | `64, 64` — `call_aaaa…aaaa_d7395395db`, identical on `function_call` and `function_call_output` | **accepted, turn completed**: final assistant text `Done—the update has been sent.` (usage: 2795 input / 11 output tokens) |

The base-side 400 is byte-for-byte the error class from #130965, produced by the live API from the unmodified projection, so the reproduction and the fix were measured against the same provider on the same day.

<details>
<summary>Recorded <code>thread/inject_items</code> payload on this branch (verbatim, synthetic content, nothing redacted)</summary>

```json
[
  { "type": "message", "role": "user",
    "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "Send the update." }] },
  { "type": "function_call",
    "call_id": "call_aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa_d7395395db",
    "name": "message", "arguments": "{\"action\":\"send\"}" },
  { "type": "function_call_output",
    "call_id": "call_aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa_d7395395db",
    "output": "Message sent." }
]
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Base-side live error, as thrown by <code>runBoundedCodexAppServerTurn</code></summary>

```json
{
  "type": "error",
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": null,
    "message": "[StringParam] [input[3].call_id] [string_above_max_length] Invalid 'input[3].call_id': string too long. Expected a string with maximum length 64, but got a string with length 83 instead.",
    "param": null
  },
  "status": 400
}
```

</details>

**Honest notes on the run.** (1) The first attempt failed on both sides with a `401 Missing bearer` because the repo's live-test harness stages `auth.json` under an isolated `HOME` while the user-scope home resolver consults the mocked `os.homedir()`; pinning `CODEX_HOME` to the staged home fixed the harness, and only the second run is reported above. (2) The model was the account's `live-default` selection; I have not hand-picked one. (3) The harness is not part of this PR's diff — it depends on a checked-out copy of the base projection and a harness-specific `CODEX_HOME` pin, neither of which belongs in the tree. I can commit an env-gated head-only version as a `*.live.test.ts` if maintainers want it in the suite; say the word.

### Rebase onto current `main` — head `7170120704`

Round 5 reported merge conflicts with main's newer typed history-rejection handling (#139933 replaced the projection's message-bearing `Error`s with `CodexHistoryRejection(reason)`). Rebased onto `aafe0878fd`. The production file merged cleanly — this PR adds no rejection sites, so no production line changed in the rebase. Only the test file conflicted: the fail-closed table and the laziness regression now assert on main's reason codes (`invalid_pairing` / `incomplete_pairing` / `item_limit`) instead of the retired message strings; assertions on the rewritten ids are unchanged. Mechanical, no behavior change, so no separate comment.

Proof on the rebased head: the five `settled-turn-*` suites **85 passed (85)**; `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` on the three changed files **exit 0**; swapping in main's projection file makes **4 tests fail** (the injection-boundary test plus three projection regressions) and restoring this branch's file makes all 31 pass, so the regression coverage still bites on current `main`. `mergeable: MERGEABLE`.

### Re-port onto the `HistoryProjection` design — head `2c172601d2` (2026-09-13)

`main` rewrote this file after the last rebase: #143081 replaced the generator-based projection with a `HistoryProjection` class (`"reject"` mode for current-turn evidence, `"omit"` mode for prior turns) and now assembles the final injected array in `SettledTurnPriorContext.prependTo(current)`. A mechanical rebase was not possible, so this head is a re-implementation of the same reviewed semantics on the new structure (a second, test-only commit `2c172601d2` tightens three assertions after review; previous history is kept at the old head `7170120704` for comparison; the branch was rewritten on top of `4675c2b4d6`).

What is unchanged: the trigger (`length > 64` only; a 64-character id is byte-identical), the deterministic `call_` + clipped tail + sha256 rewrite, salting on clash, reservation of every verbatim id before any rewrite, laziness (the projection still rejects at `item_limit` / `byte_limit` before the caller's generator is drained), bookkeeping keyed on original ids, and the local-resolver rationale.

What moved: the rewrite now runs **once, in `prependTo`**, on the concatenated notice / prior-groups / current array, with the shared `seenCallIds` set as the reservation namespace. That is the one place ids leave the projection, and it means an overlength id in an earlier turn group is normalized the same way as one in the current turn — the old head only covered the current turn because prior context did not exist yet. `projectSettledCodexMessages` itself still returns original ids; `settled-turn-evidence.ts` is untouched.

Tests: the five ported regressions and the fail-closed table for both id shapes are back, plus two new cases for the new design — an overlength id inside a prior turn group, and a current raw id that equals what a prior overlength id would rewrite to (proving the salted re-derive works across the prior/current boundary). The injection-boundary test now assembles `historyItems` through `prependTo`, the same path production uses.

Proof on this head (local, macOS):
- Base-red: new tests against `main`'s projection file → **6 failed / 27 passed**, failing for the intended reasons (unrewritten 83-char id, `invalid_pairing` on the raw-id collision case, 65-char id passed through, prior-group id unrewritten, injection payload carries 83-char ids). Restoring this head → all green.
- Focused suites (`settled-turn-projection`, `settled-turn-injection`, `settled-turn-context`, `settled-turn-prior-context`, `settled-turn-finalizer`): **101 passed (101)**.
- Adjacent suite `extensions/codex/src/app-server/` under `test/vitest/vitest.extension-codex.config.ts`: **2907 passed; 8 failures, all in files this PR does not touch (`auth-refresh-authority.integration` fixture-manifest owner, `attempt-startup`, `managed-binary` host-shim detection: host-environment conditions, identical on base by construction since neither the tests nor their subjects are in this diff), then a vitest worker crash ended the run. CI is the authoritative adjacent signal**.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` on the three files: **exit 0, all 29 lanes green (plugin boundaries, extension test core imports, typecheck extensions + extension tests, lint, format, import cycles 0)**.
- Mutation checks: moving the trigger to `> 63` is killed by the 64-character passthrough test; skipping the clash retry loop is killed by both collision tests. Both reverted.
- Independent review before this push: three read-only reviewers on the commit (GLM 5.3, Opus 5, Kimi K3, all GO; their three MINOR findings, all test-side, are the follow-up commit).

The live authenticated trace above was taken on the old head and was not rerun; the wire shape it proved (`inject_items` carrying 64-character ids) is what the boundary test pins on this head.

### On the `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr` label

I read that label as "does not recommend queueing a new **automated** fix PR", not as a moratorium on human contributions — and the ClawSweeper comment states plainly why the automation stopped: *"Reproducibility: no… the authoritative Codex behavior and a current finalization trace could not be inspected."* That is precisely the gap closed above: a reproduction on current `main`, and the authoritative Codex injection contract read at a pinned tag with file:line citations. If that reading is wrong, or if this belongs to someone already, close it and I will step aside without argument.

prs.title: fix(ui): stop chats jumping to older messages when revisited
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chats reopening on older messages after navigating among enough sessions to recreate a transcript.

## User Impact

Returning readers keep the same loaded message and viewport-relative position, including when the pane was resized while away. Latest/end-follow behavior is unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

This addresses session-return jumps only; it does not claim to fix spontaneous jumps while staying in the same session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scroll cache retained only an absolute pixel offset. Recreated variable-height rows start from estimates, so the same offset can identify a different message. Retain a visible bubble key and its relative top in the existing bounded cache, keep its row mounted during initial measurement, and restore from committed geometry. If the saved bubble has disappeared or is folded, retain the existing numeric fallback.

Reuse the existing message-anchor and restore owners; consolidate restore settlement and retry cancellation there rather than add another cache. This complements #183595's layout-specific footprint caching: its inspected head leaves the scroll cache, controller, and pixel restoration unchanged. No changes to that PR are included here.

## Evidence

- Chromium production-bundle regression: with 100 synthetic variable-height messages, visit ten other sessions and return. Base shows messages 90–92 instead of 99–100 despite restoring the same 13,557 px offset; the regression fails on message identity.
- Candidate restores messages 99–100; reader-anchor error is 0 px at the same width and less than 1 px after resizing while away. Both browser cases pass on the final candidate.
- 18 focused browser tests passed: new restoration cases, native composer scrolling/delayed-send scrolling, and older-history/prepend anchoring. The restoration cases were rerun after the final owner consolidation and fallback adjustment.
- Focused scroll, history, cache, controller, and prepend tests passed, including the absent-message fallback. UI production and chat/E2E test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Independent full-source autoreview completed through P2 with no actionable findings. An earlier incomplete context assessment was resolved by supplying the full lifecycle, capture, ref, and folded-renderer sources.
- Synthetic mock-Gateway UI evidence only; no production conversations, service state, or real model calls were used. Broad CI remains GitHub-owned.

### Test cost

- Unit entrypoint: `pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-scroll-cache.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed both cases. Measured shell wall time was **7.542 s**; the wrapper reported **7.02 s** and Vitest reported **3.78 s**. The new absent-message case took **48 ms**; the retained cache case took **591 ms**.
- Browser lane: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/chat-reader-restoration.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, with `OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1`, passed both cases. Vitest reported **37.50 s** wall duration, including a **19.77 s** production build; the two test bodies took **13.203 s**. This is the browser-lane measurement, not a separate measurement of the plain `pnpm test` spelling.
- **CI seconds:** no per-file hosted-CI cost or whole-job delta was measured. The estimated added test-body cost is approximately **13.3 runner-seconds** (13.203 s for the new browser file plus 0.048 s for the added unit case), using local observations with proof capture enabled. This estimate excludes shared build/worker setup and does not account for CI-host speed differences. Browser coverage is necessary because native row measurement, pane eviction, and viewport geometry expose the defect while pixel-only unit fixtures can pass on the broken base; the existing suite-level Gateway/build fixtures are reused.

Before returning to the chat (base restores the wrong messages):

![Before: revisiting the chat incorrectly shows synthetic messages 91 and 92](https://91b59577e757131d68d55a471fe32aca.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/openclaw-crabbox-artifacts/crabbox-artifacts/v2/org/b3BlbmNsYXc/owner/Z2l0aHViOjU4NDkz/publish/reader-proof-assets/20261026-215055-435852767/before.png?X-Amz-Expires=604800&X-Amz-Date=20261026T215055Z&X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=a677a1e59413a4e54bcc2da5fec6164a%2F20261026%2Fauto%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=67720e4aa2167cbd7dae1b932708d00c4a3c452f2a946ce80b04ba23d3ddbdd6)

After the same navigation (candidate restores the reader's messages):

![After: revisiting the chat preserves synthetic messages 99 and 100](https://91b59577e757131d68d55a471fe32aca.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/openclaw-crabbox-artifacts/crabbox-artifacts/v2/org/b3BlbmNsYXc/owner/Z2l0aHViOjU4NDkz/publish/reader-proof-assets/20261026-215055-435852767/after.png?X-Amz-Expires=604800&X-Amz-Date=20261026T215055Z&X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=a677a1e59413a4e54bcc2da5fec6164a%2F20261026%2Fauto%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=19f51fadff4ac2cb71f44a0dacc9d6b0ec24b40a968d6025e8bbaa111756870a)

The inspected images are hosted by the approved artifact store; these links expire on November 2, 2026.

<details>
<summary>Implementation scope</summary>

The existing pane/session cache remains the sole position store. No schema, persistence, permission, dependency, or public configuration changes. Existing numeric restoration remains available when no rendered message anchor exists. Runtime growth is 85 net lines; tests add 114 lines. No new reactive effects, listeners, or DOM-query ownership.

</details>

Reported by @GrahamMcBain.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @GrahamMcBain](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/275079e8-95f5-4641-b23f-6c3a526635c8)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/c30931f7-2cbc-4e74-b18d-5674cd25f706)

prs.title: feat(codex): explicitly discard unwanted generated image candidates
prs.body:
Related: #184967

## What Problem This Solves

During Codex image iteration, an unwanted earlier candidate can be automatically published after the agent sends its chosen image.

## User Impact

Agents can explicitly discard unwanted candidates before finishing. Intentional batches and other unsent images retain their current delivery behavior. Discard does not delete files, undo messages, or erase generation side-effect tracking. No configuration or migration is required.

**Maintainer decision needed:** this proposes the explicit per-asset discard contract discussed in the issue review; that review is not design approval. Existing native-owned catalogs are preserved, so a saved catalog without this tool needs a fresh thread.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Codex plugin exposes `generated_media` (`list` / `discard`) through normal plugin registration, tool policy, discovery, and Code Mode. Listing supplies current-turn IDs and file references; discard validates every ID before changing the existing projection's automatic-delivery set. Sending one candidate does not implicitly discard another.

An existing opaque tool binding connects the tool to that turn's projection and is cleared on disposal. No new core tool, SDK surface, configuration, dependency, global registry, or persistent state.

## Evidence

- **10 production-owner checks passed** on `158b633e` against the actual projection and tool: B-only exact bytes after discarding A; A's artifact and generation provenance retained; untouched batches, destination-scoped receipts, atomic unknown-ID rejection, duplicate events, and expired/closed bindings covered. This source-owner probe is **not** an app-server/model/channel E2E test.
- **Negative control:** restoring unconditional automatic-media seeding in the compiled probe fails the same B-only assertion with A+B. This isolates the delivery invariant, not a claim that the new command exists on the base commit.
- Canonical `autoreview` on `158b633e`: `scoped-clean` through P2. Independent audit caught the missing manifest declaration (fixed); the subsequent test-only relocation was independently reviewed with no P0–P2 findings.
- **CI passed on current head `abf58bbc`:** [completed CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40409199504). All selected test, lint, typecheck, docs, and guard jobs succeeded; nonselected lanes were skipped. This includes the normal `check-lint` lane after replacing the map spread CI caught on the initial head. Local scoped formatting, diff checks, and source typechecks also passed.
- Added projection/bridge, plugin-registration, and attempt/tool-lifecycle regressions. **No local Vitest pass claimed:** compiled-worker preparation and source/watch collection did not reach assertions under the host resource limits. Lint was also stopped during SDK declaration preparation. The selected CI test and static-check lanes subsequently passed on `abf58bbc`, as linked above.

prs.title: fix(runtime): merged Windows env blocks lose PATH entries from differently cased keys
prs.body:
Addresses the `withNodeRuntimePath` duplicate Windows PATH spelling item of #184894.

## What Problem This Solves

A direct call to `withNodeRuntimePath` with both `PATH` and `Path` retains directories only from the first spelling. This proposal concatenates both values before prepending the selected Node runtime.

## User Impact and Open Decision

If differently cased values reach this helper in a production Windows lifecycle, concatenation would retain both lists. That production scenario has not been demonstrated: review notes that the normal spawn caller normalizes duplicate aliases first, and that first-key precedence may be an intentional contract. This PR is a draft until a maintainer decides whether that behavior should change and a relevant Windows flow is demonstrated.

## Why This Change Was Made

The helper currently sorts PATH-keyed variables, reads the first value, and writes it to every spelling. The proposed change instead concatenates the values, retaining the first spelling's order and removing the duplicate runtime entry. Single-key behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- The added helper regression fails on the unpatched base for the dual-spelling input and passes with this change; single-key, duplicate-entry, and no-PATH cases remain unchanged.
- `pnpm test src/process/exec-spawn.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/update-command-node-runtime.test.ts src/infra/node-options.test.ts` passed. The lifecycle script test failed identically on the base because the pinned Bun fork could not be staged locally.
- The changed-file typecheck and lint lanes passed; the broader check reported pre-existing unused exports outside this diff.
- No shipped Windows update or recovery path was exercised. The macOS host cannot establish whether duplicate aliases reach this helper or whether combining them is the intended product behavior.

prs.title: feat: unify theme and Lobster Pack discovery in Appearance
prs.body:
Depends on #184960 and #160093. Registry counterparts: [ClawHub #4065](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/4065) and [ClawHub #3837](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/3837).

Companion ClawHub Appearance integration: [ClawHub #4070](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/4070).

## What Problem This Solves

Users need one place in Appearance to discover themes and Lobster Packs without confusing theme data with executable plugin packages.

## User Impact

Adds **Explore Appearance → Themes / Lobster Packs** beside the existing theme choices. Themes reuse browse, pinned install-and-apply, and personal-theme removal. Packs show their current installation state and link to existing plugin review/management controls and the LobsterDex. Browsing never records an encounter or installs a plugin; collection history remains browser-local.

**Draft dependency boundary:** this branch currently composes the theme foundation from #184960 and category acceptance from #160093 so the new UI can be built and tested. Its main-targeted diff therefore includes inherited theme changes, not just integration glue. It does not replace or close either original PR. Full custom-pack contribution/rendering support and production theme browsing still require the foundation PRs and the ClawHub Themes API deployment. This PR performs no deployment.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing theme owner, plugin discovery owner, Gateway connection lifecycle, management routes, and collection owner rather than introducing another installer, renderer, preference store, or permission model. Fixed-category discovery keeps pack searches scoped; changing a theme query retires the previous page and cursor before a failed search can reuse it.

Jacqueline Henriksen (@jjjhenriksen) requested and directed this integration. The linked foundation PRs retain their original authorship.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/20481d59-f95b-4760-8f8c-82f1e4d414b4)

## Evidence

- 137 focused tests passed: category/query identity, ClawHub validation and filtering, and Gateway profile/theme persistence and authority boundaries. The two added query regressions failed before the repair and passed afterward.
- Production-bundle browser flow passed for packs: on-demand browse, failed-read retry, category-preserving search, installed management links, empty state, catalog refresh after plugin-change events, mobile fit, no preview collection/install, and Dex navigation (2.6s test body).
- Production-bundle theme flow passed: search/retry, pinned install/apply, reload persistence, inherited-default reset, personal-theme re-selection, and removal (1.7s test body). Its fixture now persists only after observing actual writes and keeps deferred-request cursors bound to the same request predicate.
- Core/UI typechecks, targeted UI lint, stylesheet lint, formatting, English i18n verification, documentation listing, and whitespace checks passed.
- Final independent two-chunk review returned no actionable P0–P2 findings on the frozen candidate.

The browser scenarios use synthetic Gateway responses, not a deployed ClawHub service. No live registry installation or published-release compatibility is claimed. Hosted CI remains separate from these local results.

Before/after captures use the real Control UI, dark mode, a matched 1440×1200 viewport, and synthetic content. Both inspected captures are embedded below.

### Before

![Before: Appearance with built-in themes and import](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63934c26-a075-48de-b456-7d852f4a7010)

### After

![After: Explore Appearance with Themes and Lobster Packs](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ababbf8e-0ee9-4bf7-9475-3a0c1f008fb5)

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): load the code highlighter early on warm reloads [do not merge]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Stopped: the early-highlighter experiment fails its pixel gate. Do not merge.** A signed-in reload of a chat or dashboard deep link paints cached fences plain and colors them later. This is the separate style stage identified in the campaign reload timeline. The baseline fixture now reproduces it in 11/11 reloads on each route.

Measured head: `6c2973d382f537316409644ea6df7bc7289951e9`; pinned main baseline: `edd9cd176a246d0aa9ef35f81121ccc59f8dc1a5`. The cached-token fallback remains untouched at `a19a1e832a4fd07cec371de1eab21363ac048ce2` on `steipete/coldload-code-highlight-cached-paint`. This experiment branch is also preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing scoped snapshot prewarm starts the existing optional highlighter import without awaiting it. Shared readiness moves out of code-block chrome into a small owner; every existing consumer moves with it. Short fences use the existing synchronous renderer if ready, otherwise the existing lazy path. There is no new representation, store, observer, configuration or protocol. The plaintext-reset change was not carried over. Long-fence worker scheduling is unchanged.

The built runtime comprises a small 894-byte wrapper and a 72,537-byte shared grammar chunk (raw JavaScript). The grammar module registers the existing 14 languages. Warm hashed assets use the existing service-worker cache-first policy; this experiment does not establish a service-worker hit rate. Cached bytes still require per-document import/evaluation. HTTP response receipt before an app frame alone does not prove the renderer had a ready runtime at its earlier DOM commit.

## User Impact

The change is only +8 UI runtime lines, but does not reliably eliminate recoloring. Remaining measured failures are **short, collapsed 28-line fences** in TypeScript, Python and Bash (7 lines visible each), not long-fence worker cases. The worker threshold is above 300 lines. The conditional native test proves first-commit coloring when readiness is explicitly established; ordinary reloads fail the separate pixel gate. Further scheduling changes are outside this stopped experiment.

## Evidence

One quiet AWS **c7a.4xlarge** lease, `cbx_ae7f79863925`, repo headless Chromium 156.0.8078.4. Real-Gateway rig: 1720×1180 viewport, synthetic 3,000-session fixture, archived pinned targets, three visible short fences, 80 ms RTT, operator-shaped sidebar preferences (involving-me/category/created, 97 custom groups, 102 section-order entries, five collapsed groups, previews off). CPU idle before capture: A/A 93.21%, A/B 93.15%. No profiling and no route/runtime holds during measurement. Both arms use their committed generated manifests and production UI bundles, served by one Gateway build. No generated-only patch was applied.

**11 interleaved pairs plus 11 A/A pairs per route: 44 pairs / 88 warm reloads.** The Team-scale bench also completed 11 interleaved pairs plus A/A on both routes on the same instance (88 additional runs), using live-fast latency, Gateway HTTP, archived-session and pane-chrome probes.

Related: #146408.

## What Problem This Solves

Restores unknown-allowlist warnings when a silent availability probe runs before agent tools are assembled.

## User Impact

Operators receive the existing diagnostic once. Tool selection, deny filtering, filter callbacks and audit reporting keep their behavior. No configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only a reporting call consumes the existing warning key; silent callers omit the optional callback. MCP adapters preserve the supplied reporter. The existing policy pipeline and bounded cache remain the single owner.

This maintenance normally merges canonical main repair `e25c026eb75d34ecdeed1d64d68454fb919f3c19` for the exact failed mock-exports gate. It retains @steipete's original [#187120](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187120) commit, author and history. prs.title: fix(macos): WIP — Launch at Login reports success after launchctl fails
prs.body:
Related: #127613

**WIP — native regression tests are GREEN at the source revision cited below; visual/native-flow and final review gates remain. Not ready for maintainer review or merge.**

## What Problem This Solves

Launch at Login could appear successful after a required launchctl command failed, and the settings bridge returned before the operation completed.

## User Impact

Failed changes stop, reconcile the toggle, and display actionable recovery guidance in the existing Dashboard setting. Loaded-job refresh does not unload the running app; disabling future autostart still leaves it running. Persistence failures perform no launchctl operation and preserve the previous visible value when no state was observed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing serialized owner checks bootstrap/kickstart exit statuses, stops after the first failure, verifies the final loaded state, and restores the prior plist on activation failure. An absent job needs no bootout. Only the current intent publishes its outcome.

prs.title: fix(sessions): persist explicit toolOverrides.webSearch true
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.patch` silently drops `toolOverrides.webSearch: true` while normalizing the session overlay. A lone `{ "webSearch": true }` becomes an empty overlay and is deleted on write. `webSearch: false` already persists, and the sibling boolean maps (`skills`, `mcpServers`) already keep `true`.

Schema already allows either boolean (`SessionToolOverridesSchema.webSearch`). Callers that send an explicit enable, including a session patch of `{ "webSearch": true }`, get a successful patch whose stored entry omits `webSearch`.

Persisting that `true` also made a native composer display bug reachable: with `tools.web.search.enabled` false, a retained session `webSearch: true` showed the composer as On even though execution still disables search.

## Why This Change Was Made

`normalizeSessionToolOverrides` kept `webSearch` only for the strict check `raw.webSearch === false`. That owner is what `sessions.patch` uses before it stores or deletes the overlay. The normalizer now keeps `typeof raw.webSearch === "boolean"`, so an explicit `true` is stored the same way as an explicit `false`. Non-booleans are still dropped.

The native effective-state predicate now requires the global baseline before a session override, matching `resolveWebSearchToolOverrideState` in `ui/src/lib/sessions/tool-overrides.ts`. `composerWebSearchEnabled` stays false when web search is unavailable or `webSearchBaseEnabled` is false, including when the stored override is `true`.

This does not loosen other fail-closed tool gates. Runtime checks that treat `webSearch !== false` as "not session-disabled", and the global `tools.web.search.enabled` kill switch, are unchanged. `intersectSessionToolOverrides` still only retains a web-search deny. Persistence and the native display predicate are the contracts changed.

The earlier implementation candidate, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/121378, was closed unmerged.

## User Impact

`sessions.patch` with `toolOverrides.webSearch: true` now keeps that value on the stored session entry, including when it is the only override and when it sits beside other overlay fields such as `skills`. `webSearch: false` still persists. Replacing the overlay and `toolOverrides: null` still replace or clear it. The stored value survives a Gateway restart.

A persisted `true` does not re-enable web search while the global kill switch is off, and the native composer no longer shows that state as On.

## Evidence

Head `cdb6300983c780be6e1b7cc63a35bbc90f501f6d`, rebased onto current `upstream/main`.

Isolated loopback Gateway (throwaway state directory, not the operator Gateway). Redacted `sessions.patch` / `sessions.list` readback for `agent:main:websearch-proof`:

```text
patch {webSearch:true}        -> list {webSearch:true}
patch {webSearch:false}       -> list {webSearch:false}          # replacement
patch {skills:{docs:true}, webSearch:true}
                              -> list {skills:{docs:true}, webSearch:true}
patch toolOverrides:null      -> list toolOverrides absent       # clear
patch {webSearch:true}
stop Gateway, start again on the same state
                              -> list {webSearch:true}            # reopen
```

Focused regression on that head:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts -t "persists explicit toolOverrides|normalizes tool overrides"
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  2 passed | 125 skipped (127)
```

The existing native global-disable regression now loads a retained `webSearch: true` override and expects `composerWebSearchEnabled == false` before and after toggle, with no settings patch. This host has no Swift toolchain, so that test was not executed locally.

`git diff --check` was clean.

Fixes openclaw/openclaw#121377

prs.title: feat: retain repository disk authority through recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repository recovery needs to remember which exact retained disk owns accepted work, rather than treating an older Gateway mirror as the latest workspace after a restart.

Prerequisite #189019 is merged as `ff3ab23502010d1437c4afa5d7657a6d5e23111a`. GitHub subsequently retargeted this PR to `main`; the history-preserving integration retains the original 66-file authority/recovery child scope.

## User Impact

No disk-mode selector is enabled. Mirrored sessions keep their existing behavior. This is an inactive implementation prerequisite, not delivery of retained-disk workspaces.

Shared-state schema v38 adds nullable repository and pending-result authority fields after v37. Existing pending results remain mirrored, optional repository storage stays lazy, and older binaries refuse the upgraded schema. Rollback uses the existing exact predecessor backup.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The existing repository owner binds one immutable environment/resource receipt. The existing pending-result owner records that authority when accepting custody; retries never infer it from a replacement environment.
- Recovery settles only the original attached disk after cleanup. A missing/replaced disk, stale placement, failed cleanup, or transfer stays held: no stale-mirror restore, automatic replacement, input replay, or disk destruction.
- Until explicit disk I/O/export support follows, stored file fallback, new publication fallback, and Gateway materialization refuse disk authority. Previously pinned publication snapshots remain usable.
- SQLite, PostgreSQL, Doctor, predecessor restore, generated catalogs, and native schema-version metadata move together. No new manager, queue, cache, config switch, or public protocol field.

Simplification retained one repository owner and one pending-result owner, reused existing cleanup/settlement, shared migration registration, and one predecessor-schema transform chain for runtime admission and generated catalogs. Against the prerequisite: production/metadata +615/-131, tests +651/-18, generated catalogs +152/-110. Nullable fields and migration/recovery/consumer proofs account for the growth; activation, provider lifecycle, and explicit I/O/publication remain separate.

## Exact candidate and completed qualification

Signed head **`4484b72104c5a0440b265edded765e7863214c56`**, tree **`e0d308184606aca3f41d4cbfc3bc7e7199e7522c`**, has parents prior S5 `85fd5881e810bb35f9d36ea0389bb7cd9bcc1c50` and landed prerequisite/main `ff3ab23502010d1437c4afa5d7657a6d5e23111a`. The original native proof-publication receipt remains historical. Required R2 installed-v38 qualification is now complete on this unchanged candidate; correction review is READY for ordinary native qualification. This is not full feature activation or a merge claim.

- Native integration resolved 26 explicit conflict tuples, mostly replay of the squashed prerequisite. Independent child-only replay isolated one behavior overlap: retain the runtime disk-authority argument and the already-landed #188805 interrupted-drain recovery/refusal branch. All 66 child paths survive. Generated resolutions retain canonical output blobs; no hand-edited generated bytes or new production mechanism/test scaffold.
