prs.title: fix(control-ui): retire deleted sessions once without wiping cached sidebars
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated publications of an already-confirmed session deletion caused each mounted chat pane to invalidate the same snapshot again. In a real isolated Gateway with two browser tabs and 20 unrelated roster publications, the tabs broadcast **25 / 5 invalidations for one deleted session**. Each event also retired the entire cached sidebar, including unrelated conversations.

The repair produces **1 / 1 broadcasts**, preserves the sidebar through two virtual minutes of churn with **zero wipes**, removes the deleted row from cached reloads, and writes the sidebar only when its display model changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shell already retires each confirmed deletion. Remove the competing pane replay instead of adding another deletion-deduplication owner. A single canonical pruning helper removes the deleted session and its nested rows, navigation references, and boot-roster entry. Display, in-flight prewarm, IndexedDB, and the already-published boot roster consume that operation within their existing lifetimes; account/scope retirement still clears the whole projection.

History: [#125128](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/125128) made the pane's replayed cache deletions observable by the persistent snapshot owner. [#168206](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168206) extended one session's invalidation to the entire sidebar projection. This is amplification of those existing paths, not an identified post-r241 introducer.

Two associated owner fixes remain: malformed individual conversation/board/history records evict only that record instead of resetting the entire database; identical sidebar models skip duplicate cross-tab writes, and roster receipt `ts` does not count as a display change. These are plausible contributors to the live three-record chat cache and write churn, **not proof of their exact live causes**. Real two-tab probes observed zero whole-database resets; aggregate corruption, I/O recovery, account retirement and projection-version eviction remain separate paths.

## User Impact

Deleting one conversation removes it without emptying the rest of the cached sidebar. Unrelated conversations remain available on reconnect and reload, and a deleted conversation does not return from the cache. Unchanged roster publications and cached-to-live handoff do not keep rewriting the sidebar.

This PR does **not** fix the chat route's first-frame blank/skeleton or claim seamless complete first paint. That separate admission/paint-holding work belongs to the other reload lanes. No new configuration, Gateway protocol, server schema, or retention policy.

## Evidence

All browser fixtures and media are synthetic; no private capture content is included.

| Contract | Before | Repair |
|---|---|---|
| Real Gateway, two tabs, deletion plus 20 unrelated state publications | 25 / 5 sends, one unique deleted key | 1 / 1 sends |
| Native two-tab normal deletion, two virtual minutes of churn | Broad sidebar invalidation reproduced at the owner boundary | One send + one receive per tab; zero wipes; one shared write; survivor restored with connect held; deleted row absent |
| Native subagent deletion, same churn | Duplicate peer writes in intermediate repair | Same event/wipe/reload contract; two writes for two distinct models: row prune, then retained-parent child-load targets |
| Independent writers, two meaningful models | Four puts | Two puts; expired identical model still refreshes |
| Malformed individual conversation/board/history record | Unrelated valid chat lost in each of three regression cases | Unrelated chat retained |

The native write bound is 1 write / 2 virtual minutes for normal deletion and 2 / 2 for a subagent (0.5/min and 1/min), with no further writes during churn. The observed live baseline was 71 writes / 183 seconds (23.3/min). These are different workloads, so this is a deterministic work-count bound, not a paired wall-clock speed claim.

### Validation

Final head: `080142de4798fb81e869ab509110c8d8bd1420d1` (rebased base `1440bb1771372334bea23d7642bb52deb7db1845`). Independent Codex review is clean through P2; range-diff preserved all seven patches. [Exact-head CI is green](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41251775744).

AWS lease `cbx_27e1468e115e`, fixed `c7a.4xlarge` (16 vCPU / approximately 31 GiB), [final-head validation run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_facf63748bfedc2a7067b0c2d2b031ea):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Focused owner tests | 6 files / 130 tests passed; 13 s |
| Controller guard | Passed; 5 s |
| Base/candidate bundle budget | Passed; 63 s |
| Canonical UI build | Passed; 28 s |
| Native two-tab regression | Both normal and subagent cases passed; 38 s; writes `[1,0]` / `[2,0]` |
| `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` | 829 s; all checks passed except the full-tree unused-export scan described below |
| Full UI e2e | Completed on final head: 878 files passed, 6 failed, 3 skipped; 3,337 tests passed, 2 failed, 17 skipped; 4,941 s command wall |

Four of those six file failures were setup errors: my initial payload installed Chromium but omitted WebKit. After installing WebKit, all four files passed individually on the same final head: `logs-scroll` (3 tests), `tooltip-first-activation` (2), `chat-composer-picker-layout` (4), and `workboard-native-bundle` (4). This resolves 13 of the 17 skipped cases; the remaining four cases retain their existing opt-in proof, live-provider, or desktop-fixture requirements. This is a full run plus focused setup repairs, not a claim that the original full invocation was green.

[Follow-up proof and main controls](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_ffc0dd49594315831576262354c442ea), same AWS lease: both actual failing cases reproduce on freshly fetched main `17e2d54e2fbea1161bb8da5a3bbb6a9a35214d3a` with the same errors:

| File / failing case | Candidate and main control |
|---|---|
| `chat-outbox-migration.e2e.test.ts`: preserves qualified/global v3 Blobs through migration, reload and retries | Initial-roster readiness timeout on the standalone legacy seed page |
| `extensions/qa-lab/src/control-ui-automation-management.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`: configured owners/admin manage a Telegram-created job | Crabline fixture setup rejects a private mutation boundary writable by another POSIX principal |

The full-tree unused-export scan reports `DATABASE_SNAPSHOT_FREE_SPACE_RESERVE_BYTES` and `MAX_DATABASE_SNAPSHOT_EXTRACT_BYTES` from untouched `src/commands/backup-verify-spool.ts`. Current main's scan passes. The same two findings reproduce on recorded base `1440bb1771372334bea23d7642bb52deb7db1845` ([base control](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_bd074d8fdff55a373d96c44110db9d40)); they are inherited from the base and fixed since on current main. No scan bypass was used.

The final startup comparison is **89,492 B gzip versus base 89,313 B (+179 B)**, three requests in both arms, with the 89,930 B enforcement limit unchanged. Earlier CI found two attributable import-boundary failures: [static schema imports added 3,553 B](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41249610097/job/124680517144), then [stored dynamic module imports exceeded the manual-import ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41250633807/job/124683911805). Both are repaired: utility reads are destructured, schema loading happens on deletion before opening the IndexedDB transaction, and prewarm retains only its derived snapshot promise. No budget waiver, loader helper, new owner, or baseline allowance.

Earlier real-Gateway proof: AWS `cbx_0c8b568d76c3`, [baseline](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_3c20b5353bdf1e70af247b02de5d281e), [repair](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_7e87accf40ad436a045b9e80c6bae637).

Changed-test command costs (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, one file per command): `sidebar-snapshot.test.ts` 4.42 s; `chat-pane-session-presentation.test.ts` 5.85 s; `session-snapshot-store.test.ts` 2.83 s; `sidebar-snapshot-store.test.ts` 2.82 s. The final-head remote focused command covers these four plus the existing prewarm and invalidation suites: 6 files / 130 tests, 13 s. The native two-case command takes 38 s on the final-head AWS box. These are validation costs, not performance comparisons.

### Bounded simplification and LOC

The bounded compression pass retained the original +173 runtime lines. Required CI repairs to the import boundary bring the final change to **+177 runtime LOC** (**+179** under the requested diff-stat filter, which includes the two-line allocation file). It did not reach +130 without weakening a proven lifecycle/privacy behavior. Boot already re-reads the pruned prewarm model; IndexedDB, display, and prewarm already use the same pruning helper. Adding a coordinator merely to combine their lifetime adapters would create another owner.

| Runtime file | Net LOC | Required responsibility |
|---|---:|---|
| `sidebar-snapshot-data.ts` | +62 | One canonical prune across pins, pages, nested children, section counts, personal entries and boot roster; unchanged input preserves identity |
| `sidebar-snapshot.ts` | +24 | Prune displayed cache and accepted capture, fence pending stale work, preserve unchanged handoff serialization |
| `session-snapshot-database.ts` | +42 | Prune the persisted model in the existing transaction; preserve key-only prefix clearing so account retirement does not load transcript bodies |
| `session-boot-snapshot.ts` | +18 | Refresh the already-published cached roster from the pruned prewarm copy, without clearing unrelated rows |
| `session-snapshot-prewarm.ts` | +9 | Chain pruning onto in-flight reads so stale prewarm cannot restore the deleted row |
| `session-snapshot-invalidation-events.ts` | +9 | Distinguish session pruning from full sidebar/scope retirement |
| `session-sidebar-snapshot.ts` | +11 | Suppress identical peer writes atomically; preserve expiry refresh |
| `session-snapshot-store.ts` | +5 | Evict malformed records locally and cancel stale sidebar operations |
| `sidebar-snapshot-capture.ts` | +4 | Ignore receipt-only timestamps and omit confirmed-deleted navigation entries |
| `chat-pane-session-observation.ts` | -7 | Delete the competing retirement loop |

Test audit consolidated the parameterized native regression from **274 to 240 lines** by sharing native IDB instrumentation, row lookup and probe readout. Both session shapes and all storage-event, churn, privacy, write and reload assertions remain. Reaching 180 would trade away the real native instrumentation or compress the required auth/roster/bootstrap fixture into less readable code. No new production test seam or exported helper. Exact test-line allocation: **358**, reduced from 392; no slack. Five test files plus the offline/reconnect documentation accompany the ten runtime files.

### Synthetic before/after reload

Repaired live sidebar immediately before warm reload, then cached sidebar after reload with connect held. These prove survivor retention and deleted-row absence; they do not claim first-paint completeness.

![Synthetic live sidebar after deletion, before warm reload](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/572e3fcd-da26-4903-9fa7-45598d64dbed)

![Same sidebar restored from cache with connect held after warm reload](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/27a3ec57-e530-459c-9c0c-e713e4717b2e)

prs.title: feat(control-ui): show worker lifecycle and telemetry
prs.body:
Closes #163982

## What Problem This Solves

The Systems page hides worker lifecycle history, can leave a reclaimed worker shown as `Attached` until reload, and does not connect live dedicated workers to the CPU, memory, and disk telemetry their enrolled nodes already report.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish active workers from recent destroyed or failed workers, inspect lifecycle/provider/profile/lease/error details, see terminal state changes without reloading, and troubleshoot or right-size live dedicated workers from the same resource graphs used for base systems.

Workers without dedicated node telemetry show an explicit not-reported state. Shared-host workers do not expose whole-host statistics as if those measurements belonged to one worker.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Systems inventory now retains terminal worker records, groups active and historical workers separately, and refreshes canonical `environments.list` data when durable `sessions.changed` events or worker placement changes arrive.

For dedicated workers, the Gateway additionally projects the enrolled node identity. The Systems inventory joins that exact identity to `node.list`, reuses the existing host-stat history and graphs, and continues polling while the worker is selected. No provider shell probe, SSH command, or second telemetry poller is introduced.

## Evidence

### October27 identification repair

Short worker IDs now remain visible beside lifecycle status. [Exact-head regression results and before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163995#issuecomment-6456168501). This fixes the same-profile identification finding; history-policy acceptance and main integration remain pending.

### Earlier lifecycle and telemetry evidence

The following results document earlier tested revisions; they are not a new full-suite or live-runtime qualification of the October27 head.

Live Apple Container lifecycle, captured from the same Systems page without a reload:

**Before reclaim — worker is Attached**

![Systems sidebar showing an attached worker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff22cbbe-35d0-4d25-a08c-6799626eb040)

**After reclaim — worker moved to Recent worker history as Destroyed**

![Systems sidebar showing the reclaimed worker as destroyed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee681765-dd7b-4cad-adf6-0708837275eb)

- Live transition observed in about one second and repeated twice without reloading.
- Disposable live telemetry proof: an Apple Container worker reached `ready`, published a dedicated node identity, and reported Linux host stats with 5 CPUs, load averages, 4.26 GB memory capacity, and 541.13 GB disk capacity through `node.list`. The worker was reclaimed; provider and Apple Container inventories were empty afterward.
- Focused validation:
  - Gateway environment projection: 20/20 pass.
  - Gateway protocol schema: 22/22 pass.
  - Systems telemetry/UI: 36/36 pass, including distinct session and telemetry-node names.
  - Changed-file formatting and lint: pass.
  - Core and UI typechecks: pass.
  - Production Control UI build: pass.
- Earlier branch-wide validation:
  - `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base origin/main`: pass (335.15 s).
  - `pnpm test:changed`: 20,926 pass / 3 skip; one unrelated `shell-viewport.test.ts` RAF-coalescing assertion failed under the full parallel lane, then passed 3/3 isolated reruns (11/11 each).
  - Upstream `control-ui-performance`: pass. The local check showed a nondeterministic gzip edge 24–30 B over the 373,454 B startup limit while raw startup JS stayed exactly 1,208,683 B with and without the Systems reconciliation helper, confirming this patch does not change the startup asset set.
  - Repo autoreview helper was attempted but unavailable because its local Codex credential returned HTTP 401; no review verdict was produced.

The two older `Destroying` rows visible in the screenshots predate this worker and are a separate provider-history cleanup issue.

prs.title: perf(ui): reduce shared agent selector setup and focus work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large agent rosters still add avoidable work to route changes and first agent-menu opening after #189725. New Session rebuilt its welcome selector on ordinary publications, and custom menu rows allocated unused group/default render machinery and repeated focus work.

## User Impact

The selector keeps its lazy first-open behavior and real keyboard/focus contract while doing less setup and DOM mutation. New Session retains one welcome selector through publications and typing. Routes, host tags, classes, request counts, and lazy boundaries are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the welcome selector in its existing owner with `children()`. Construct menu group fallbacks and default row renderers only when used; sort merged controls once, avoid discarded initial-focus lists, and skip unchanged `tabIndex` writes. Compile the markdown scan regex only for the scanned grammar, preserving the current-main start boundary and authored-link grammar.

No automatic menu DOM warmup is added: it would restore closed-menu row/avatar work, and the current renderer cannot yield/cancel partway. The existing lazy-content and selected-avatar-until-open contracts were inspected. No idle scheduler, cache, deferred cleanup, dependency, or import-boundary change is introduced. Round one's slower standalone first opening was explicitly accepted because navigation through first open improved: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189725#issuecomment-6549652876.

The historical 56 ms (1×) / 327 ms (4×) maxima were **Agents first visits**, not Advanced, Plugin Settings, or first-menu-open measurements. The benchmark now filters observer entries from the actual action start; pre-action CDP/setup work is excluded identically from base and head. This measurement correction is not a product speedup.

## Evidence

Base `7232a8de67eff527b3f5764987312f2424beda94`; head `fff86475689625a9d0463a87594ae17338bbd416`. Same Apple M3 Ultra (32 CPUs, 512 GiB), headless production bundles with synthetic Gateway fixtures and 300 agents. Host load is recorded per observation. Each primary cell uses 20 serial base/head/base triplets with a byte-identical A/A control: six routes, standalone first open, and navigation through first open; desktop/mobile; Chromium 1×/4× and WebKit. All **2,880/2,880** primary observations passed. No WebKit CPU or long-task value is invented where unsupported.

Application time means first native input to last observed DOM commit; full-flow time retains automation/assertion time. Neither is INP or paint timing.

Acceptance: median regression ≤5%, p95 holding or explained by the same-byte control; investigate distinct tails with ten additional triplets. On this shared host, use renderer thread CPU and structural counts alongside A/A to distinguish work from scheduling noise. Trace timings diagnose ownership and are separate from untraced performance claims.

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| First open, Chromium 1×, desktop | Application median/p95 101.15/105.1 → 87.45/90.6 ms; CPU 105.47/107.45 → 104.06/106.01 ms |
| First open, Chromium 1×, mobile | Application 77.1/79.4 → 62.8/66.3 ms; CPU 98.05/105.07 → 96.75/100.69 ms |
| First open, Chromium 4×, desktop/mobile | CPU median −1.71%/−3.89%, p95 −1.22%/−2.18%; application and longest-task p95 improve |
| First open, WebKit desktop/mobile | Application 94/97 → 90.5/96 ms; 93/99 → 91/95 ms |
| Navigation through first open, WebKit desktop/mobile | Full-flow 504.5/524 → 471.5/506 ms; 989.5/1006 → 964.5/992 ms |
| All 12 WebKit route cells | Readiness median improves 0.95–9.68%, p95 improves 0.67–13.00%; full A/A values below |
| First-open work | 1,819 → 1,219 mutations; zero closed rows; 300 open rows/avatars; selected focus and requests preserved |
| Welcome selector regression | 8 → 1 constructions; typing retains it, catalog targets dispose it, return creates one new selector |
| Correctness | UI typecheck; 31 menu-navigation, 3 New Session, 44 current-main markdown-link tests; observer regression; tooling typecheck and scoped lint/format passed |
| Build/dead code | Base/head strict `pnpm ui:build` passed; production `pnpm deadcode:knip` passed |
| Bytes | Startup JS gzip 89,390 → 89,396 B (+6, within 64 B variance); raw 279,196 B unchanged; CSS gzip 34,125 B and one request unchanged; Chat boot 1,272,074 → 1,271,846 B; New boot 780,978 → 780,673 B |
| Review / CI | Fresh independent P0–P2 autoreview clean; `ci:full` run 41255750132 succeeded (44 executed jobs, no failed job) |

### Follow-up assessment

All 300 additional observations passed (180 at 4×; 120 at 1×). They remain separate from the primary 2,880 observations. The original desktop combined 4× longest-task flag did not repeat: median/p95 270/279 → 262/270 ms. Mobile combined 4× CPU, application time and full-flow medians/p95 improve; its longest p95 increase (308 → 331 ms) is smaller than same-byte A/A (308 → 334 ms). Mobile Advanced content-ready median/p95 improve by 9.4/3.1 ms. The 1× mobile combined full-flow p95 is flat, resolving the primary +15 ms flag; CPU and application medians/p95 improve.

Raw increases remain disclosed. Mobile Plugin Settings at 4× has an extra-run CPU p95 744.93 → 780.34 ms and content p95 626.3 → 662.2 ms. Seven of ten paired heads use less CPU; the median is +0.55%; the p95 is one maximum with one additional layout/style pass. The primary CPU tail tracked A/A (+3.26% vs +3.12%). This is an unresolved observed tail, not proof of harmless noise or a reproduced persistent regression. Mobile About at 1× has readiness p95 48.6 → 53 ms while CPU, script, layout, scenario and wall-time tails improve; its two-frame readiness probe can include scheduling delay, but that cause is not proven. Desktop combined at 1× has longest p95 64 → 65 ms while CPU is flat and application/full-flow timing improves. Desktop Advanced visit-ready p95 rises 32.8 ms in a run whose A/A p95 shifts −56.4 ms; content-ready and CPU improve. These observations do not support an all-metrics-win claim. No attributable repeated CPU regression is established, and no measured head timing median regression exceeds 20%.

### Attributed remaining work and target gap

The historical **56 ms at 1× / 327 ms at 4×** values were route-only **Agents first visits** (`accepted-qualification-1x/engines-vcPoWi` and `accepted-qualification-4x/engines-6wI8aD`, desktop pair 16 for 327 ms). They were not Advanced, Plugin Settings, or standalone menu opening. Those older observer windows included work before the actual action; the corrected observer is applied equally to the new base and head. It is not counted as a product improvement, and the old maximum is not directly comparable to the new one.

Final-head diagnostic captures comprise 28 passed observations, one base/head pair per viewport/step at 1×/4×, with Plugin Settings additionally at 4×. V8 samples are source-mapped, restricted to the mark-selected renderer PID/TID, and clipped to the action. These instrumented samples explain ownership; they do not replace the untraced distributions or recover the exact earlier outlier. Adjacent render tasks and microtask checkpoints are reported separately; a composite is not one uninterrupted task. Inclusive stack categories overlap and must not be added together.

| Final 4× head diagnostic | Attributed work |
| --- | --- |
| Agents, desktop | Render task 85.9 ms then 156.3 ms microtask checkpoint. In the render task, Agents JSX subtree 44.0 ms and file grammar 11.8 ms (base grammar 23.1 ms). In the checkpoint, cleanup stack overlap 43.2 ms, route 12.5 ms, bridge 19.0 ms; runtime/native/unattributed nearest-owner bucket 50.9 ms. |
| Agents, mobile | Render task 84.7 ms then 153.1 ms checkpoint. Agents subtree 41.2 ms; file grammar 11.9 ms (base 23.6 ms). Checkpoint cleanup overlap 45.5 ms, route 11.6 ms, bridge 14.5 ms; runtime/native/unattributed 51.5 ms. |
| Standalone first open, desktop/mobile | Longest intervals 225.1/206.5 ms. Native `showPopover()` owner at `overlay-lifecycle.ts:27` accounts for 95.0/93.8 ms; `OptionRow` at `agent-select.tsx:89` 24.8/22.6 ms. Avatar stack overlaps 34.7/37.7 ms. All 300 rows still mount on demand. |
| Combined visit/open, desktop/mobile | Largest intervals 215.0/231.1 ms: desktop is the route checkpoint; mobile is menu opening, including 101.3 ms in native popover display. The larger 314.9/269.9 ms adjacent composites include separate task/checkpoint intervals and are not single-task metrics. |
| Plugin Settings, desktop/mobile | Largest intervals 123.4/109.7 ms (base 116.7/115.1 ms), mixing outgoing New Session disposal and incoming settings mount. Cleanup overlaps 46.9/44.5 ms; native/runtime/unattributed bucket 43.5/47.9 ms. Closed selector rows remain zero. This one pair does not explain away the extra-run mobile CPU outlier. |

In a later first-open interval, the base focus routine (`menu-runtime.ts:111`) contributes 69.3 ms desktop / 65.8 ms mobile of sampled time across the action; that prominent bucket no longer appears among the head hotspots after skipping unchanged tabindex writes. It is separate from the larger native-popover interval, not an additive slice of it.

At 1×, final-head sampled longest intervals are 30.6/31.5 ms for Agents and 48.8/47.7 ms for standalone opening. Native popover display accounts for 22.5/22.6 ms of the latter.

The primary untraced head maxima remain **50 ms route-only / 50 ms standalone / 62 ms combined at 1×**, and **279 / 231 / 341 ms at 4×**. The requested strict <50 ms / <200 ms targets are not reached. The follow-up reaches 65 ms combined at 1× and 331 ms combined at 4×; distributions and A/A are disclosed separately. These are **not established browser floors**. The next scalable owner is AgentSelect's 300-row/thumbnail mount: windowing needs catalog-wide navigation plus a registration-driven real-focus handoff, and visible-range avatar leases. The existing searchable picker retains input focus and is not a drop-in replacement for this menu. Generic deferred teardown or idle warmup would move work without proving cleanup/focus correctness, so neither is introduced here.

Production UI LOC: **2,783 → 2,787 (+4)**. Nine-file diff: **+254/−136, net +118**, including tests and observer proof. Most menu diff is moving existing branches behind demand. Solid refactor census: effects 1→1, untrack 2→2, onSettled 11→11, memos 10→10, signals 3→3, dynamic imports 4→4, ordered subscriptions 4→4. Owner APIs, direct listeners, DOM queries, render effects, and component cleanup remain zero; owned `children()` sites 1→2.

prs.title: feat(google): use the Interactions API for Gemini Flash models
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gemini Flash models on the API-key `google` provider still used the GenerateContent API, even though OpenClaw already ships the Gemini Interactions transport (#149880). New Flash models found by live discovery or forward-compatible model resolution also inherited GenerateContent, and discovery dropped any Flash row that did not advertise `generateContent`.

## User Impact

User impact: `google/gemini-*-flash*` text models (including Flash-Lite, `gemini-flash-latest`, and future Flash IDs) now use the Interactions API by default when the effective base URL is the official Google AI Studio endpoint. Everything else keeps GenerateContent:
- Pro and other non-Flash models, including the default `google/gemini-4-argon`.
- Any custom `models.providers.google.baseUrl` (proxies) without an explicit `api`.
- An explicit model- or provider-level `api: "google-generative-ai"` always wins; a model-level `api: "google-interactions"` selects Interactions for any Gemini text model.

Behavior notes:
- Interactions uses implicit caching. A configured `cachedContent` handle is ignored on this route instead of failing the turn; explicit cache creation already only ran for GenerateContent.
- Native video keeps working on Flash: video becomes an Interactions `video` input after payload hooks run. Hooks see placeholders only, like on the GenerateContent route (#122074); only the untouched placeholder slots are materialized. Clip offsets/FPS map to `processing`.
- Media understanding, web search, PDF, image generation, speech, Live, embeddings, Vertex and Gemini CLI keep their current routes.
- Music (Lyria) and video (Veo) SDK clients, and the reusable `@openclaw/ai` Google client without a base URL, now pin `apiVersion: "v1beta"` instead of relying on the `@google/genai` default. A configured versioned base URL still wins.

## Why This Change Was Made

Interactions is Google's newer Gemini API, and Flash is the model family most people run on API keys. The Google provider's model normalization (`resolveGoogleModelApi`) is the single owner of the default: it reads the effective endpoint and only authored config counts as an explicit choice, so catalog metadata cannot override a proxy. Pinning the SDK API version keeps beta-only features stable across future SDK major upgrades.

## Evidence

Live proof against the Gemini API with an AI Studio key, isolated profile, this branch built locally (`agent --local --json`; endpoint taken from debug logs). A local GenerateContent-only fake proxy recorded request paths for the proxy rows.

| Case | Model | Endpoint hit | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default, official endpoint | `google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | `/v1beta/interactions` | `flash-pong` / `default-pong` |
| Tool call + next-turn replay | `google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | `/v1beta/interactions` | `exec` 2 calls, 0 failures, `tool-ok-42`; next turn recalled it |
| `cachedContent` configured on the model | `google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | `/v1beta/interactions` | `cache-pong` (previously threw) |
| Provider-level `api: "google-generative-ai"`, no base URL | `google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | `/v1beta/models/gemini-3.5-flash-lite:streamGenerateContent` | `override-pong` |
| Model-level `api: "google-interactions"` on Pro | `google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview` | `/v1beta/interactions` | routed correctly (account returned an error for Pro) |
| Non-Flash default | `google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview` | `/v1beta/models/gemini-3.1-pro-preview:streamGenerateContent` | routed correctly (429 for Pro on this account) |
| Proxy + `api: "google-generative-ai"` | fake proxy | `POST /v1beta/models/gemini-3.5-flash-lite:streamGenerateContent` | `proxy-pong` |
| Proxy + `api: "google-interactions"` | fake proxy | `POST /v1beta/interactions` | proxy 404 as expected |
| Interactions `video` shape emitted by this branch, sent directly | `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | `/v1beta/interactions` | 200, `Red` for a red test clip |

`gemini-3.8-flash` returned Google-side 503 "high demand" on both APIs during testing, so live proof used `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`.

Regression tests (base-red / head-green): payload hooks never receive video bytes and cannot inject or swap video parts; catalog Flash on a proxy without `api` resolves GenerateContent; explicit provider/model APIs win on both endpoints; forward-compatible Flash follows the configured endpoint. Focused suites for catalog, discovery, forward-compat routing, overrides, prompt-cache behavior, Interactions request conversion, the GenerateContent transport, and SDK `apiVersion` pins pass locally; full typecheck and suites run in CI.

Not covered live: native video through a channel attachment end to end (unit tests plus the direct shape probe above), music/video SDK calls (paid models), and the proxy default without `api` (a loopback proxy is classified as a custom non-Google endpoint on both `main` and this branch, so it cannot represent a remote Google-compatible proxy; covered by unit tests).

prs.title: improve: Doctor flags cron failure alerts that could not be delivered
prs.body:
Related: #186990

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Doctor gap behind #186990: when a scheduled automation fails and its failure alert cannot be delivered (for example on a gateway with no messaging channel configured), the delivery failure was recorded only in the job's state fields, and `openclaw doctor` never surfaced it.

## User Impact

User impact: operators running `openclaw doctor` now see which automations have an undeliverable failure alert, the recorded reason (such as "Channel is required (no configured channels detected)"), and what to do next: configure a messaging channel for the Gateway or set an explicit delivery target on the job. No behavior changes outside Doctor output, and the check is read-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor already reports chronic failures, auto-disabled jobs, and in-flight markers, but it did not read the settled alert-delivery result. This adds a finding next to those, driven by `lastFailureNotificationDeliveryStatus` and `lastFailureNotificationDeliveryError`.

Scope follows the agreement in the issue thread:
- Only `not-delivered` warns. `delivered`, `not-requested`, `unknown`, and absent fields stay silent, so an unsettled delivery is never reported as a failure.
- The recorded reason is sanitized before display (control characters stripped, whitespace collapsed, capped at 200 characters).
- Repair-brief wording and deduplication of repair requests are deliberately untouched. Current source already has a repair-per-streak marker and an owner-directed fallback, and the reporter is running the bounded repro to settle those separately. This PR uses `Related:` rather than `Closes` for that reason.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes</summary>

- Detection lives in `inspectCronJobHealth` and runs for enabled and disabled jobs, so it is placed before the early `continue` that only the auto-disabled path needs.
- Tests are in a new `index.failure-alert.test.ts` because `index.test.ts` is already at the repo's file-length cap.
- `docs/cli/doctor/checks.md` lists the new check beside the other cron reports.

</details>

## Evidence

- New tests (3 passed) cover: a channel-less failed alert produces the warning with job name, recorded reason, and fix hint; a delivered alert produces no warning; `not-requested`, `unknown`, and missing fields produce no warning. These match the verification criteria the maintainer set on the issue.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passes.
- Existing `index.test.ts`: 27 of 28 pass, and the one failure (`reports a moved partition, refuses --yes guessing...`) also fails on unmodified `upstream/main` on Windows. The message embeds the store path JSON-escaped, so the raw-path match fails. It is unrelated to this change.
- Docs file passes `oxfmt --check`.
- On my Windows machine the local pre-commit hook cannot launch `pnpm` (`spawn pnpm ENOENT`), so I ran the docs checks manually and relied on CI for the rest.

prs.title: fix(ui): prevent accidental archives after sidebar child removal
prs.body:
Closes #167415.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes accidental session archives when the last child disappears and a user clicks again at the sidebar disclosure's previous position.

## User Impact

In hover/fine-pointer layouts, Archive keeps its position as child membership changes. Childless rows reserve the missing disclosure space only while actions are surfaced, preserving full resting title width. Touch/mobile and team layouts retain their existing placement and always-visible action clearance.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing CSS owner keeps Archive outside the disclosure slot. The parent row supplies the missing inline space on hover/focus when there is no disclosure; no runtime state or new CSS variable is introduced. The rule applies only to rows with Archive, leaving pure catalog-menu rows to their owner.

This revision integrates official main `51420782b3810b4aa1230aa9621aec78f7dbbd3c`. Main deliberately moved status indicators back to the leading side in `f28de2e8e690e73a9be4c270c338a35d3a9d13bf`; that cutover remains intact. Retired trailing-status rules and the removed unread-hover test block are not restored. The presentation test matches main exactly. This follow-through applies the contributor-approved +243 test-line allocation after an actual merge-ref CI budget failure. No further main integration or runtime change is included.

## Evidence

Head `c0969c6c3583904688101ec534e441392cd817b9`; tree `1c97867c5a215e9431ea338c9a1be053612dac80`. Node 24.22.1 / pnpm 12.15.0 match the branch, with the qualified dependency definitions and lock unchanged. Proof uses the production UI bundle, native Chromium and an owned synthetic Gateway, not an operator Gateway or physical touch device. The behavior runs and screenshots below belong to `a07b994f`/tree `45ef6729`; the latest synchronization retains the Archive CSS block, regression and named owning renderers/fixtures. Compared with the previous qualified synchronization, only the package metadata changed among 20 named inputs; the Archive block, renderers, stylesheet and regression remain unchanged. The prior upstream People-list change remains outside this fix. These are qualified reused results, not a new browser execution.

- **Actual main before:** the saved-coordinate regression fails with the exact official-main stylesheet. At `(277, 99)`, hit-testing finds Archive, a trusted repeated click targets Archive, and the parent receives **1 archive RPC**. The same scenario first exercises ordinary Archive as a positive control. The wrapper took **121.87 s**; the test reaches the intended hit-target assertion.
- **Qualified a07 behavior:** **3 cases pass**: fine-pointer owner-title clearance, coarse-media owner-title clearance, and the original child-deletion point. The same saved point now hits/clicks a non-Archive element and produces **0 parent archive RPCs**. Hover/focus title clearance and resting width are checked independently.
- **Coarse-media regression:** review found that the first unpublished conflict candidate moved always-visible touch actions without matching resting clearance. Its actual wide, non-mobile coarse-pointer case failed with title end **141 px**, actions start **113 px** (**28 px overlap**). Restricting the new positioning to hover/fine media restores the original coarse placement; the final case has title end **141 px**, actions start **159 px**. This is Chromium media emulation, not hardware certification.
- **Retained failure:** the final two-file selection has **3 passed, 1 failed, 5 unselected** in **206.92 s**. The unchanged first-line/title sibling fails at initial roster readiness before layout assertions. Diagnostics show an open mock socket, connected Gateway phase, successful route and a `sessions.list` request, without a page error. An exact-main-CSS control in the same ChildToggle→Presentation file order passes that sibling and fails the expected original Archive-point case (**125.96 s** wrapper). The readiness cause remains **unclassified**; a passing replay is not a repair. Earlier readiness failures retain their own scope. No wait limit, assertion or readiness guard was weakened.
- **Checks:** Current integration consumer types, styles, formatting, line caps and whitespace pass again. The prior qualified type-aware lint retains its a07 scope. The current native budget gate passes at 6,301,879 against 6,302,243 (364 lines spare).
- **Independent review:** The complete two-file P0–P2 review identified the coarse-pointer clearance finding. After the real before/after regression above, a fresh corrective-delta review is scoped-clean; both records form the review chain. A separate one-line allocation review is also scoped-clean. Static review does not certify the failed readiness case or pending CI.

Before repeated click: main places Archive at the old disclosure coordinate. The screenshot precedes that repeated click; its archive toast belongs to the ordinary-Archive positive control.

![Before: Archive occupies the former disclosure coordinate](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/23c4481f-e3e6-4370-a88a-1edc2ed239a4)

After: Archive stays left of the empty disclosure slot, while main's leading-status design remains intact. The a07 behavior capture is byte-identical to the inspected uploaded frame; its execution provenance is retained through this qualified synchronization.

![After: the previous disclosure coordinate stays clear of Archive](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1f7ce915-bbde-47d5-8109-58f14c3be3b5)

prs.title: fix(daemon): Gateway repair stops the Gateway and fails when macOS denies the Trash
prs.body:
Related: #188563

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on macOS, Gateway repair from the app (and `openclaw gateway uninstall`) stops the Gateway and then fails with "LaunchAgent removal failed (EPERM)" when macOS refuses the move into `~/.Trash`, leaving the Gateway unloaded; the app's recovery repeats the same removal and fails again.

## User Impact

User impact: removing or repairing the app-managed Gateway no longer fails on the Trash. The stopped LaunchAgent's plist now goes into the Trash under a timestamped name (`ai.openclaw.gateway-<ms>.plist`), so it no longer collides with an earlier same-name item there, and a copy stays recoverable. If macOS still refuses the move with `EPERM`/`EACCES`, the plist is deleted from `~/Library/LaunchAgents` instead, so the reinstall (or the app's recovery of the previous Gateway) can continue.

## Why This Change Was Made

`uninstallLaunchAgent` boots the service out first, then moves its plist into `~/.Trash`. The issue reports, from the reporter's local diagnostics (raw TCC logs not attached), that macOS privacy protection (TCC) denied that access to the app's Bun helper (`SystemPolicyAllFiles`), while the user's own `LaunchAgents` directory stays writable, so the move failed after the service was already gone. The live run below reproduces that denial through the app when the Trash already holds a same-name `ai.openclaw.gateway.plist` that the app's helper did not put there itself (reproduced with one moved there by Finder and one moved there from a shell). Moving the plist into the Trash is allowed without Full Disk Access; replacing an existing Trash item that carries no access grant for the helper is not. A same-name file the app trashed earlier is replaced without error. The reporter has since confirmed that their Trash holds such a file; how it got there is not known.

The uninstall now moves the plist to `~/.Trash/<label>-<Date.now()>.plist`, the naming Doctor's legacy cleanup already uses. A timestamped destination avoids the fixed-name collision reproduced in our tests; it is not a guaranteed-unique name, and macOS can refuse moves for other reasons, so the fallback stays.

`removeBootedOutLaunchAgentPlist` (in `launchd-service-files.ts`, the plist owner) keeps the Trash move and, only on `EPERM`/`EACCES`, deletes the plist instead, the way the systemd uninstall already removes its unit file. Doctor's legacy LaunchAgent cleanup had the same Trash dependency and now uses the same helper; it still reports the Trash destination when the move succeeds. Other errors (and a plist that vanished concurrently) keep their existing handling.

Not in this PR, so this does not close the issue: the issue also asks that a removal failure after unload preserve or restore the previous working service. This change removes the Trash-permission failure; if deleting the plist also fails, the service still stays unloaded. That restoration is a separate change.

## Evidence

Runs on an AWS EC2 Mac (macOS 27.0, Node 24), this branch on main `82c8ad576b3`.

**Regression test** (`src/daemon/launchd.test.ts`, `removes the booted-out plist when Trash mkdir/rename is denied without Full Disk Access`): the real `uninstallLaunchAgent` with the launchd and file-system fixtures, where creating or renaming into `~/.Trash` fails with `EPERM`.

```
# main (test only)
× launchd uninstall > removes the booted-out plist when Trash mkdir is denied without Full Disk Access
  → promise rejected "Error: LaunchAgent removal failed (EPERM)…" instead of resolving
# with the fix
src/daemon/launchd.test.ts                 Tests 74 passed (74)
src/commands/doctor-gateway-legacy-services.test.ts + src/commands/doctor-gateway-services.test.ts
                                           Tests 65 passed (65), combined across both files
```

Doctor's legacy LaunchAgent cleanup is covered by a new row in its existing table (`doctor-gateway-legacy-services.test.ts`, `settles legacy macOS cleanup for Trash-denied plist`): the Trash move fails with `EPERM`, the plist is deleted, cleanup reports it removed, and the note names no Trash destination.

Format and lint pass on the changed files (pre-commit). `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass.

### Live run

We now reproduce the permission failure through the app. Applying the removal fix makes uninstall succeed while preserving the existing Trash file; restoring the release code makes the failure return. The hosting cycle below (uninstall under the denial, app takeover, reinstall, reconnect) passes with a branch-built CLI.

Setup on two AWS EC2 Macs: Apple M1 on macOS 27.0, and Apple M4 on macOS 26.5 (25F71), the closest AWS image to the reporter's 26.5.1. Each runs the notarized 2026.10.9 app (Developer ID: OpenClaw Foundation) from `/Applications`, set up "On this Mac", with OpenClaw listed in Full Disk Access and its switch off. Each run turns "Keep OpenClaw running when the app is closed" on (installs the LaunchAgent), then off, which runs the app's own `gateway uninstall` through its bundled Bun CLI. Before the failing runs, Finder moved a same-name `ai.openclaw.gateway.plist` into `~/.Trash`.

| Mac | CLI code | `~/.Trash` before uninstall | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1, macOS 27.0 | release | Finder-placed same-name plist | `LaunchAgent removal failed (EPERM)` (2 runs; each logged twice, uninstall then the app's recovery) |
| M1 | release | no same-name file | Removed; plist moved to Trash |
| M1 | this PR's removal logic | Finder-placed same-name plist | Removed; plist deleted, service gone, no error; Finder's Trash file unchanged (same SHA-256) |
| M1 | release, restored right after | Finder-placed same-name plist | `LaunchAgent removal failed (EPERM)` again |
| M4, macOS 26.5 | release | Finder-placed same-name plist | `LaunchAgent removal failed (EPERM)` (one uninstall attempt plus one recovery attempt) |
| M4 | this PR's removal logic | Finder-placed same-name plist | Removed; Finder's Trash file unchanged (same SHA-256) |
| M4 | release | no same-name file | Removed; plist moved to Trash |
| M4 | release | same-name plist created and moved into the Trash from a shell (no Finder) | `LaunchAgent removal failed (EPERM)` |
| M4 | release | same-name plist the app itself trashed in the previous run | Removed; the earlier Trash file is replaced |

Creating the existing Trash directory returned EEXIST; the subsequent rename failed with EPERM, matching a TCC denial for the app's Bun helper:

```
# release CLI, M1 (fs_usage, bun; errno 17 = EEXIST, 1 = EPERM)
13:21:23.510452 mkdir  [17] ~/.Trash
13:21:23.544012 rename [ 1] ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist
# TCC, same moment (one request)
13:21:23.510 AUTHREQ_CTX    msgID=164.128 service=kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAllFiles
13:21:23.510 AUTHREQ_ATTRIBUTION responsible=ai.openclaw.mac (/Applications/OpenClaw.app) accessing=bun (~/.openclaw/runtime/2026.10.9-release-…/bin/bun)
13:21:23.541 AUTHREQ_RESULT msgID=164.128 authValue=0
# app log
13:21:23.577 [gateway.launchd] Gateway daemon command failed (exit 1): Gateway uninstall failed: Error: LaunchAgent removal failed (EPERM). Check permissions and retry.
13:21:24.959 (same, the app's recovery attempt)

# removal fix, M1: rename denied, unlink succeeds, plist absent
13:32:17.381920 mkdir  [17] ~/.Trash
13:32:17.382024 rename [ 1] ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist
13:32:17.382157 unlink      ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist
13:32:17.382243 openat [ 2] ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist

# macOS 26.5, M4: the same sequence
13:52:57.534581 mkdir  [17] ~/.Trash
13:52:57.537 AUTHREQ_CTX msgID=137.80 service=kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAllFiles, responsible=ai.openclaw.mac, accessing=bun
13:52:57.570 AUTHREQ_RESULT msgID=137.80 authValue=0
13:52:57.570194 rename [ 1] ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist
# removal fix, M4
13:54:24.110721 rename [ 1] ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist
13:54:24.110798 unlink      ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist
```

**Final change, branch-built** (M4, macOS 26.5): the release tag `v2026.10.9` plus this PR's production changes (Trash fallback, `hasErrnoCode`, timestamped Trash name), built with `pnpm build` and placed as the app's runtime `dist`. `~/.Trash` held a same-name `ai.openclaw.gateway.plist` created and moved there from a shell, the case the release refuses.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| "Keep OpenClaw running" on | LaunchAgent installed from the branch-built runtime, `state = running`, Gateway HTTP 200 |
| off (uninstall) | `mkdir [17]` → `rename` succeeds into `~/.Trash/ai.openclaw.gateway-1793494086095.plist`; no `EPERM`, no TCC denial, no daemon-command failure; the delete fallback is not reached; the earlier Trash file unchanged (same SHA-256); the app takes over hosting, HTTP 200 |
| on again (reinstall) | LaunchAgent reinstalled and running, HTTP 200 |
| settings | `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` SHA-256 identical before and after the cycle |

The fallback path was exercised the same way earlier with the fixed name (M4, branch-built `v2026.10.9` + `d29a399f43a`): `mkdir [17]` → `rename [1]` → `unlink`, no daemon-command failure, plist removed, Gateway healthy after reinstall, settings unchanged.

| Build | Same-name item already in `~/.Trash` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Released app (fixed name, no fallback) | yes | `EPERM`, Gateway left unloaded |
| This PR before the timestamped name (fixed name + delete fallback) | yes | uninstall succeeds by deleting the plist; no Trash copy |
| This PR (timestamped name + delete fallback) | yes | uninstall succeeds; plist kept in the Trash under a new name |

The reporter confirmed on the issue: macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), OpenClaw listed in Full Disk Access with its switch off, and `ls ~/.Trash` denied in Terminal, the same permission state as these runs. They then confirmed in Finder that their Trash contains `ai.openclaw.gateway.plist`, the same-name file that triggers the denial here.

Proof artifice: the same-name Trash file was created by hand and moved into the Trash with Finder (AppleScript `delete`), and the Full Disk Access entry was added with its switch off by hand. The M1 fixed runs applied this PR's removal logic to the release bundle's CLI file. prs.title: fix(memory): resolve literal extra-memory root paths without trimming
prs.body:
Fixes openclaw/openclaw#189914

## What Problem This Solves

`normalizeConfiguredMemoryExtraPaths` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/config-utils.ts`) trimmed every configured extra-memory root with `.trim()`. Memory `extraPaths` are operator-authored filesystem identities: a literal directory whose name carries edge whitespace (e.g. `/srv/notes `) was rewritten to a different, typically nonexistent directory before `path.resolve`. The dedup key `` `${configuredPath}\0${pattern}` `` was also computed from the trimmed value, so two genuinely distinct literal roots such as `/srv/notes` and `/srv/notes ` silently collapsed into one entry, and the other directory was never indexed for memory search.

## Solution

Stop trimming the path. Keep the blank guard (`configuredPath.trim()` still decides whether an entry is kept) but store and key the raw value — the `readNonBlankString` convention used across the codebase (blank-check via trim, value preserved). Glob patterns are still trimmed; a pattern is not a filesystem identity. Updated the helper doc comment and every consumer expectation that encoded the old trimming behavior:

- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.test.ts` (shared normalizer consumer)
- `src/agents/memory-search.test.ts` (memory-search config consumer; previously expected `" docs "` → `"docs"`)
- `docs/reference/memory-config.md` documents the literal-path contract and how padded entries from earlier releases now resolve.

## Impact

- Memory search/index roots now point at the literal configured directory instead of a trimmed impostor.
- Distinct literal roots keep separate dedup keys; last-policy-wins for truly identical keys is unchanged.
- Blank or whitespace-only entries are still dropped exactly as before.
- Existing padded entries such as `" docs "` now select the literal `" docs "` directory; the docs note tells operators to correct entries that relied on the old trimming.

## Evidence

Unit tests (remote runner, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ... --maxWorkers=1`):

- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/config-utils.test.ts` + `internal.test.ts`: **68/68 passed** (wall 48s).
- `src/agents/memory-search.test.ts`: **39/39 passed** (wall 66s) — this is the consumer assertion that failed the prior head's `checks-node-changed-2` job at line 323.

Shipped CLI proof (built dist `2026.10.9-07bc3fe8c`, real `openclaw memory` CLI, FTS-only `provider: "none"`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`). Fixture: workspace with `notes/` (trimmed sibling), `notes /` (trailing-space literal root) and `archive/` (ordinary root), `memory.search.extraPaths = ["notes ", "archive"]`.

**Fresh configuration (head):**

```
$ openclaw memory index --agent main --force
Memory index updated (main): 2 files indexed.
$ openclaw memory status --agent main --index
Extra paths: …/workspace/notes , …/workspace/archive
Indexed: 2/2 files · 2 chunks
$ openclaw memory search beta-space --agent main
0.415 notes /NOTE.md:1-2
literal content: beta-space marker
$ openclaw memory search alpha-notes --agent main
No matches.
$ openclaw memory search delta-archive --agent main
0.471 archive/NOTE.md:1-2
ordinary content: delta-archive marker
```

**Upgrade from v2026.10.9 (same `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, data written by the published release):**

Published `openclaw@2026.10.9` (8b18b55) with the same config trims the entry and indexes the impostor:

```
Extra paths: …/workspace/notes, …/workspace/archive
$ openclaw memory search beta-space --agent main
No matches.
$ openclaw memory search alpha-notes --agent main
0.877 notes/NOTE.md:1-2
trimmed sibling content: alpha-notes marker
```

After `openclaw doctor --fix` (documented pending-schema upgrade step) and the head build on that same state dir, existing data loads (`Dirty: no`) and the literal root takes over:

```
Extra paths: …/workspace/notes , …/workspace/archive
Indexed: 2/2 files · 2 chunks
$ openclaw memory search beta-space --agent main
0.415 notes /NOTE.md:1-2
literal content: beta-space marker
$ openclaw memory search alpha-notes --agent main
No matches.
$ openclaw memory search delta-archive --agent main
0.471 archive/NOTE.md:1-2
ordinary content: delta-archive marker
```

Ordinary roots keep indexing and searching normally in both legs, and the literal root survives an in-place upgrade of the existing store.

## Precedent

Same defect class as merged #187554 (hooks `extraDirs` — "the configured directory's whitespace belongs to its filesystem identity") and #172869 (cron cwd CLI). Sibling PRs from the same sweep: #187751, #187766, #187777, #187816, #187825.


---

## Decision requested (not an approval claim)

This PR changes the interpretation of configured `memory.search.extraPaths` entries (stop trimming edge whitespace so a literal root keeps its filesystem identity). That is a **behavior change to an existing configuration contract**, so it needs an owner decision before merge — the `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility` label reflects that, not a code-quality issue.

| Option | Effect | Cost if chosen |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Accept (this PR)** | A configured `extraPaths` root with edge whitespace resolves to the literal directory instead of a trimmed impostor; distinct literal roots keep separate dedup keys. | Operators who relied on the old trimming must correct padded entries (documented in `docs/reference/memory-config.md`); blank entries are still dropped. |
| **Decline and close** | The trimmed-value behavior stays; a literal `notes ` root silently points at `notes` and the two directories collide. | No config-semantics change; the defect remains for operators with edge-whitespace roots. |

Same defect class as merged #187554 and #172869 (precedents in the body above).

prs.title: fix(cli): publish CoreDNS config atomically with preserved permissions
prs.body:
Closes #184888

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: `openclaw dns setup --apply` rewrites an existing CoreDNS `Corefile` (and its `.server` files) by truncating in place, so a crash or ENOSPC mid-write destroys the operator's DNS configuration with no backup and no recovery copy (the file lives outside OpenClaw's state dir).

## User Impact
A failed write no longer destroys the previous Corefile or `.server` contents. Existing file and parent-directory permissions are preserved (the previous code kept them by writing directly); newly created files keep `writeFileSync`'s umask-respecting permissions instead of the helper's restrictive defaults; CoreDNS setups that use a symlinked `Corefile` or a symlinked `conf.d` keep working and now also publish atomically.

## Why This Change Was Made
`writeFileSudoIfNeeded` called `fs.writeFileSync` on the final path (and `sudo tee` as fallback), which truncates before any content is written. It now uses `@openclaw/fs-safe`'s `replaceFileAtomicSync` (temp-file + rename): a failed publication leaves the previous bytes exactly as they were, verified by a regression that injects a `renameSync` failure. Options chosen deliberately: `preserveExistingMode: true` so existing rwx bits survive, `dirMode` pinned to the immediate parent's current mode so helper defaults cannot tighten existing directories, and `mode: 0o666 & ~process.umask()` for new files. Symlinked Corefiles publish to their real target (dangling links resolve the link target, normalizing its real parent when the target does not exist yet). The `sudo tee` fallback is unchanged.

## Evidence
Level A (real CLI entry `dns setup --apply` driven by the repo's test harness with synthetic paths and no operator files touched):
- Rename failure injected: the pre-existing Corefile is byte-identical afterward. Red on base (the truncate path left it partial), green with this change.
- Existing Corefile and parent directory modes preserved after a successful rewrite (0755/0644 fixtures); a newly created Corefile gets `0o666 & ~umask` rather than fs-safe's 0600.
- Real symlinked Corefile, a dangling link, and a symlinked `conf.d` directory all publish correctly and preserve the link itself; a nested dangling case whose target sits inside a symlinked directory also passes.
- All 12 cases in `src/cli/dns-cli.test.ts` pass (node 24.19, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --run`).
- Independent Codex review of the final diff found four findings, all addressed and re-verified (restrictive default modes, new-file umask mode, symlink handling, dangling-link parent normalization).
- Known boundary disclosed deliberately: fs-safe's `applyDirectoryMode` chmods the parent directory even when its mode already matches and does not restore it on failure; the privilege-escalation fallback (`sudo tee`) is unchanged and out of this fix's scope.
- Not run locally: tsgo/extension-boundary lanes and a live CoreDNS installation (CI covers the type lanes).

prs.title: fix(oc-path): avoid reading and editing a different Unicode key
prs.body:
Closes #189866

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw path resolve`, `find`, and `set` can silently select a different field when a decomposed Unicode key coexists with its composed spelling. Whole-address NFC conversion changes the identifier before the document resolver sees it.

## User Impact

Literal addresses now select the exact code points supplied. A write targeting U+0065 U+0301 changes that key, not its coexisting U+00E9 neighbor. File names and opaque session values retain their spelling. Markdown section/item slug rules are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove conversion at the existing shared address parser. Retain the raw4096-byte limit, BOM handling, syntax validation, control-character rejection and filesystem traversal checks. The redundant post-conversion cap disappears with the conversion. No new setting, API, dependency, schema or fallback.

@Malpin07's contributor commit is preserved. Current main was merged, retaining the landed YAML-alias and duplicate-key repairs. Regression coverage is consolidated into existing fixtures: exact Unicode writes, raw file/session round trips and byte-limit boundaries. Production+4/-15; tests+8/-8(net0); docs+5/-1; no test allocation increase.

## Evidence

Independent secretless Linux Docker / Node24.22.1 built CLI proof: two main runs read/find the composed neighbor and actually overwrite it; two candidate runs read/find and overwrite only the decomposed target. Every run independently checks disk values, ASCII reads/writes, untouched neighbor, comment and CRLF preservation, and the4096/4097-byte CLI boundary. Focused regressions fail on main for3intended reasons and pass on candidate:92tests/3files. Targeted lint and formatting pass. [Independent evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189868#issuecomment-6551468765).

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores whole-address NFC conversion; no migration or state rewrite. Blast radius is optional oc-path literal addressing across document adapters. Explicit `set` writes files, so review changes and keep normal backups. Canonically equivalent literal names intentionally remain distinct; callers must use the actual spelling returned by `find`. Markdown slugging and existing security refusals remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix(exec): keep POSIX backslash filenames off slash allowlist paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On macOS and Linux, exec allowlist matching rewrote every two-backslash sequence into a slash before comparing the path. A file whose name contains those two backslashes, such as `bin\\tool` directly under a directory, compared equal to an allowlist entry for `bin/tool`. The process that ran was that real file, not the allowlisted path.

In allowlist mode a miss is denied. In ask and auto modes a match runs with no prompt. `ask: always` still prompts. Windows matching already folds single backslashes and is unchanged.

Slash allowlist entries still match the same slash paths. Nothing stored in the allowlist file is rewritten.

## Evidence

Isolated state: `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-f094-proof/state` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/oc-f094-proof/openclaw.json` on worktree `/tmp/oc-f094` at `4b368290095c`.

`node scripts/run-node.mjs exec-policy set --security allowlist --ask off` stored `security=allowlist` and `ask=off`. `node scripts/run-node.mjs approvals allowlist add --agent main /private/tmp/oc-f094-proof/bins/bin/tool` saved that one grant. macOS resolves `/tmp` to `/private/tmp`, and the node host compares the executable realpath, so the saved grant is that realpath.

Two real executables:

- `/tmp/oc-f094-proof/bins/bin/tool` prints `SLASH_RAN`
- `/tmp/oc-f094-proof/bins/bin\\tool` (the filename contains two backslash characters) prints `BACKSLASH_RAN`

The proof calls production `handleSystemRunInvoke` with production `runCommand`, which is the node-host path that decides and then spawns.

```console
$ node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs /tmp/oc-f094-exec-proof.mts
{"label":"slash-allowlisted","command":["/tmp/oc-f094-proof/bins/bin/tool"],"events":["exec.finished"],"result":{"ok":true,"payloadJSON":"{\"exitCode\":0,\"timedOut\":false,\"success\":true,\"stdout\":\"SLASH_RAN\\n\",\"stderr\":\"\",\"error\":null}"}}

```

The allowlisted slash executable ran and printed `SLASH_RAN`. The backslash-named executable was denied with `allowlist miss` and did not print `BACKSLASH_RAN`. After `approvals allowlist remove` deleted the saved grant, the same slash executable was denied and did not run.

## Upgrade from v2026.10.7

Tag `v2026.10.7` (`157d8c2bc3ea`) wrote the saved grant with its own CLI:

`node scripts/run-node.mjs exec-policy set --security allowlist --ask off`

`node scripts/run-node.mjs approvals allowlist add --agent main /private/tmp/oc-f094-proof/bins/bin/tool`

The stored row is pattern `/private/tmp/oc-f094-proof/bins/bin/tool`, id `86f58380-42d6-4f45-a753-0b3a39d63811`.

On that stable build, production `handleSystemRunInvoke` plus `runCommand` ran both files:

```console

```

`openclaw doctor --fix --yes` on this head migrated that same state directory. The grant id and pattern string were still present. The same proof script, pointed at this head, then kept the slash executable and rejected the backslash filename:

```console
$ PROOF_ROOT=/tmp/oc-f094 node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs /tmp/oc-f094-upgrade-proof.mts
{"root":"/tmp/oc-f094","label":"slash-saved-grant","events":["exec.finished"],"result":{"ok":true,"payloadJSON":"{\"exitCode\":0,\"timedOut\":false,\"success\":true,\"stdout\":\"SLASH_RAN\\n\",\"stderr\":\"\",\"error\":null}"}}
{"root":"/tmp/oc-f094","label":"backslash-filename","events":["exec.denied"],"result":{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED","message":"SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: allowlist miss"}}}
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** POSIX exec allowlist comparison treated a filename containing two backslashes as a slash path, so a different executable could satisfy an allowlist grant and spawn.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS 27.0.1, Node v26.12.1, worktree `/tmp/oc-f094` at `4b368290095c`, isolated state under `/tmp/oc-f094-proof`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** From `/tmp/oc-f094`, with `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-f094-proof/state` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/oc-f094-proof/openclaw.json`, run `node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs /tmp/oc-f094-exec-proof.mts`. For the upgrade, v2026.10.7 wrote the grant, then this head ran `node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --fix --yes` and `PROOF_ROOT=/tmp/oc-f094 node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs /tmp/oc-f094-upgrade-proof.mts`. Both scripts call production `handleSystemRunInvoke` and production `runCommand`.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from that command:

```console
$ node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs /tmp/oc-f094-exec-proof.mts
{"label":"slash-allowlisted","command":["/tmp/oc-f094-proof/bins/bin/tool"],"events":["exec.finished"],"result":{"ok":true,"payloadJSON":"{\"exitCode\":0,\"timedOut\":false,\"success\":true,\"stdout\":\"SLASH_RAN\\n\",\"stderr\":\"\",\"error\":null}"}}
{"label":"backslash-filename","command":["/tmp/oc-f094-proof/bins/bin\\\\tool"],"events":["exec.denied"],"result":{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED","message":"SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: allowlist miss"}}}
{"label":"slash-after-grant-removed","command":["/tmp/oc-f094-proof/bins/bin/tool"],"events":["exec.denied"],"result":{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED","message":"SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: allowlist miss"}}}
```

Upgrade evidence, same saved grant id `86f58380-42d6-4f45-a753-0b3a39d63811`, after `doctor --fix` on this head:

```console
$ PROOF_ROOT=/tmp/oc-f094 node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs /tmp/oc-f094-upgrade-proof.mts
{"root":"/tmp/oc-f094","label":"slash-saved-grant","events":["exec.finished"],"result":{"ok":true,"payloadJSON":"{\"exitCode\":0,\"timedOut\":false,\"success\":true,\"stdout\":\"SLASH_RAN\\n\",\"stderr\":\"\",\"error\":null}"}}
{"root":"/tmp/oc-f094","label":"backslash-filename","events":["exec.denied"],"result":{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED","message":"SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: allowlist miss"}}}
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The saved slash grant spawned `/private/tmp/oc-f094-proof/bins/bin/tool` and its stdout was `SLASH_RAN`. The two-backslash filename was rejected with `SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: allowlist miss` before `runCommand` returned success. After the saved grant was removed, that same slash executable was rejected the same way and did not print `SLASH_RAN`. A grant written by v2026.10.7 (`157d8c2bc3ea`) still spawned that slash executable after `doctor --fix` on this head, and the backslash filename that stable had allowed was denied.
- **What was not tested:** A Windows host. The win32 separator fold was not changed. An npm package install of v2026.10.7 was not used; the upgrade used the `v2026.10.7` git tag, its CLI, and this head's `doctor --fix`.

## Summary

Existing slash allowlist entries keep matching those slash paths. A pattern that used `\\` as a separator now matches that literal name only, so a miss fails closed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An MCP callback belonging to an already-admitted agent turn can fail during Gateway drain with `cron.list unavailable during gateway suspension`. Its grant remains valid, but the fresh HTTP callback does not retain the original turn's root-work admission.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain the native root continuation in the existing MCP grant owner and enter it around callback dispatch. Release it when capture completes or the grant is revoked, and transfer it with the existing warm-process grant owner. Keep the existing request scope, caller validation, generation checks, and listener startup context intact. A fresh unrooted grant still cannot admit new root work during drain.

## Evidence

Validation: the original source fails the native-RPC regression during drain; the patched callback succeeds. Tests cover warm grant transfer/completion, admission closure, revoked grants, and unrooted admission denial. Existing question-authority and exec-egress controls pass (9 tests). Native formatting, diff checks, and focused typed lint pass with zero warnings/errors.

The first composite test command hit the native silent-worker timeout after its grant/archive cases had passed. The remaining sibling files were run separately to terminal success. Broader local type shards were not rerun; exact-head upstream CI remains pending. This contribution preserves the current native listener request-scope reset and does not create operator authority or widen caller permissions.


## Proof Scope

The native HTTP regression proves the callback/admission boundary using synthetic requests. Actual admitted-Claude execution issuing an MCP callback while Gateway suspension drains is still unobserved; this PR does not claim that provider-level proof. No production Gateway or provider credentials were changed for this contribution.

The earlier context/evidence failure was resolved by the authored sections above: the later `PR context and evidence` run at the same `b762f1ea6ad80a3d67f65bf1b381c84a59298783` head succeeded at 2026-10-09 08:51:44 UTC.

## Current-Main Closeout

Integrated main `bb7d32e55d48a85c6a08b374064e7a45d1e52b9c`; reviewed head `4fc504a105`. The only conflict was an upstream deletion of redundant mint/TTL test coverage adjacent to the two continuation regressions. Both regressions remain, and the upstream deletion is preserved. The three production owners have no upstream change since the original base, so the production contribution remains unchanged.

Fresh isolated Railway qualification: `pnpm test src/gateway/mcp-grant-store.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 22/22, 20.02 seconds runner time and 22.987 seconds wall time; native typed lint passed with zero warnings/errors in 22.5 seconds, and formatting/diff checks passed. Source SHA-256 for all four contribution files matches the committed source. A fresh independent merge-resolution review found no blockers. Previous-head CI remains previous-head evidence; current-head CI is pending. Actual admitted-Claude callback during suspension-drain remains unproven.

prs.title: fix(macos): selecting another gateway opens an extra chat window
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an extra window opening—or focus jumping to another window—when a user selects a different Gateway from the macOS native chat's bottom-left picker or uses the Cmd-1 through Cmd-9 Gateway shortcuts.

## User Impact

Ordinary picker selection, Gateways app-menu entries, and Cmd-1 through Cmd-9 switch the originating Gateway window, matching the embedded Dashboard's selection behavior. Each Gateway keeps its own chat, unsent draft, and attachments when switching back. Other windows and the app's primary Gateway remain unchanged. Option-Cmd-number and New Gateway Window explicitly open an independent window. The Dock retains open-or-focus behavior; menu selection also falls back to open-or-focus when no Gateway window is active.

**Draft: native build/focused-suite evidence below applies to prior head 9bc5eda2d19d. The shortcut follow-up at 63fafb7970bc has not been compiled or executed on macOS. Normal embedded-web picker/keyboard and credential-retirement proof, baseline reproduction, and inspected before/after captures remain outstanding.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The native picker and Gateway app-menu shortcuts previously called the generic Gateway open action, which correctly reuses a window belonging to the destination Gateway but cannot switch the originating window. Selection is now bound to the visible source shell and reuses its actual NSWindow; keyboard/menu selection uses the same native selection owner as the picker, or the existing Dashboard switch owner for a Dashboard window.

Inactive Gateway content stays owned by that window until it closes or the Gateway's ownership is retired. Retaining the existing composer owners avoids copying drafts or pending sends into another Gateway. This deliberately retains visited Gateway content in memory rather than discarding unsent work. The generic open/focus route is unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Shortcut follow-up — head 63fafb7970bc1a93cdb887032bf35e2aa87b8952:** added GatewaysMainMenuTests using real AppKit menu key-equivalent dispatch for Cmd-2/Cmd-1, same-window and per-Gateway draft restoration, an independent destination window, unchanged primary Gateway, and Option-Cmd-2 opening a separate window. The accessory test runner supplies the originating-window lookup explicitly because it has no stable global key window. The new suite has not been compiled/run in this Linux session; actual app dispatch with focus in the embedded web composer still needs macOS proof. Existing fork runs pinned to 9bc5eda2d19d do not validate this new shortcut path.
- **Reporter validation — October 26, 2026:** Jacqueline Henriksen reports successful real use with her local Gateway. Her [detailed validation follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184876#issuecomment-6425492775) separately records local builds and subsequent disposable-macOS fork validation; this is more detailed than the initial live-use report.
- **Native execution on prior head 9bc5eda2d19d:** the [fixed-source fork run](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/40393649250) at harness commit `94e463406579c83c33000efddeafe8c66e6a644c` has successful native test build/link (893 s) and focused-suite execution (80 s) steps. The follow-up identifies `WebChatGatewaySwitchTests`, `WebChatWindowLifetimeTests`, and `WebChatSwiftUISmokeTests`, and records unchanged production source relative to upstream PR head `9bc5eda2d19d224dbced54e4ae3d3b3520a30b50`. Step outcomes were checked live; log-level test counts and the full workflow result are not yet verified. At the earlier readback, the run was still building the Gateway/Control UI, before the embedded-conversation/capture step; that observation is not a current-head or full-workflow success claim.
- **Local build/formatting on prior source:** the same follow-up reports app build (177.456 s), native test compilation/linking (155.739 s), pinned formatting, and targeted lint success with a then-unpublished whitespace-only repair. Matching nearby install-argument/loop formatting adjustments are now included in WebChatManager, but pinned format/lint has not been re-executed on the shortcut head. The reported aggregate lint failure is an inherited DashboardManager file-length failure.
- Traced the original native picker through AppNavigationActions to WebChatManager's destination-window lookup; compared Dashboard's separate select/open-window handling and existing same-NSWindow assertions.
- Added production-action regression coverage for same-window selection with/without another destination window, independent drafts and restoration, observer visibility and retained-profile retirement, and cancellation after source closure/reselection. Existing native tests cover explicit independent windows.
- Passed: git diff --check against the managed base e923309c2978268898f7b57a11879fdfa174ca38.
- Independent Auto Review: the original candidate and the shortcut follow-up each received scoped-clean results at the default **P0-only** threshold. These are not compilation or runtime verdicts.

Existing forced-native tests/direct cleanup do not establish those boundaries. The linked [pre-fix run](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/40394508888) passed native compilation but was cancelled during Gateway/UI build, before behavioral reproduction; it is not baseline-red proof. No full-workflow, visual-success, or credential-retirement-success claim is made.

Complete PR delta against e923309c2978268898f7b57a11879fdfa174ca38: production +214/-33, tests +226/-1, docs +9/-0. Superseded by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189891. That rollback removed the unconditional provider-bound context checks introduced in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189810 and restored the canonical overflow recovery message.

Against the pre-rollback guard, the shared 4,096-token model caused lifecycle scenarios to fail before their assertions.
