prs.body:
## Status: ready

A is accepted for landing, including its negligible dashboard CLS tradeoff. Dashboard hello improves in 11/11 pairs, 570.42→468.20 ms, paired median −96.88 ms [−182.18, −60.44]. The former maximum-absolute-A/A clearance requirement is withdrawn for this consistent effect.

Dashboard CLS increases by a paired median +0.000287 (8/11 worse), approximately 0.0003 and below 0.001; this is an accepted tradeoff. A/A paired CLS range was [−0.002341, +0.000267]. Chat is untouched by this change; its measured variation is A/A-like noise. Final-head CI is green; standalone validation findings are classified below. This PR stops at ready review and will not be merged by this lane.

## What Problem This Solves

Literal dashboard deep links skip the early Gateway handoff and begin their connection after more application startup work. Chat links already overlap that handoff with startup. The campaign's original evidence counted 14 visible states during a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link; this change addresses its delayed handshake admission.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove only the chat-namespace restriction. Literal chat and dashboard routes use the existing credential owner, full session key, `chat.startup` history parameters, bounded event handoff, and adoption checks. Short/main references still wait for their resolver; confirmation-required endpoints, native startup and non-workspace documents keep their existing startup owner. No identity/signer preload or runtime configuration, protocol, cache or storage change.

History: the restriction was introduced with the chat-scoped optimization in #185683 (`4420648c4046`). Its comment protects short references, native handoffs, confirmation and route replacement; those independent guards are retained. No dashboard-specific authority or scope invariant was found. The existing handoff rechecks URL and credentials at adoption.

B stays dropped: live connection/route confirmation enables the favicon fetcher, changing settled message `linkFavicons` from false to true and adding actual favicon placeholders. That is a legitimate markup input change. Suppressing the preparation as redundant would be incorrect; this PR does not change it.

## User Impact

Dashboard reloads begin their Gateway handshake earlier while preserving cached views, authentication and route resolution. Chat continues through its existing early handoff and startup sequence; there is no change to chat rendering or requests. Cached page restoration keeps its existing ordering, including #185558's accepted earlier cached-row paint / later hello tradeoff. No application WebSocket request is sent before successful connect receipt.

## Evidence

The accepted comparison uses a synthetic signed-in 3,000-session fixture matching the campaign's archived targets/sidebar preferences; one quiet AWS c7a.4xlarge; the same built Gateway for both UI arms; an 80 ms CDP network profile (not calibrated per-RPC wire RTT); 11 interleaved warm pairs on chat and dashboard plus an 11-pair A/A control. Unprofiled results only. No absolute historical hello budget applies.

Performance proof was recorded before the mechanical rebase: UI baseline `828b81ad1f94`, candidate `02f405f70530`, AWS Crabbox `cbx_1d63caee9630`, actual c7a.4xlarge (16 CPUs), Chromium 156.0.8078.4. The production patch and owner files remain unchanged on the final validation head. Both UI arms used the same built Gateway. Quiet-host CPU idle was 92.41% for A/A and 93.48% for A/B. No CPU profiler ran during comparisons.

**Accepted performance result:** dashboard hello 570.42→468.20 ms, better in 11/11 pairs; paired median −96.88 ms [−182.18, −60.44]. The earlier maximum-absolute-A/A clearance rule is withdrawn for this consistent effect. A/A hello paired range was [−105.03, +87.56] ms, median +5.18 ms, IQR [−44.62, +51.47] ms. Candidate paired IQR is separated from the control paired IQR.

Chat is untouched by this change: it keeps its existing early handoff and startup sequence. Chat hello paired delta −4.81 ms (6 better / 5 worse) and other chat results are A/A-like noise, not a claimed chat improvement.

**Accepted CLS tradeoff:** dashboard CLS paired median increases by 0.00028717 (8/11 worse), approximately 0.0003 and below 0.001. A/A paired CLS range is [-0.00234068, 0.00026723], with median -0.00011550. The increase is retained and explicitly accepted as negligible.

Dashboard FCP paired median −17.12 ms (9/11 better), first ElementTiming row paint −16.07 ms (9/11 better), and LoAF −19.20 ms (6 better / 5 worse) accompany the handshake gain.

All values are milliseconds except CLS; brackets are [Q1,Q3]. Paired delta is candidate minus its paired baseline, which differs from subtracting the independent arm medians. Lower is better. prs.title: improve(canvas): keep large widget validation responsive
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large `show_widget` scripts block the Gateway thread during JavaScript syntax validation, and unchanged scripts are parsed again on every tool call.

## User Impact

Repeated widgets and markup-only updates reuse syntax validation. Large new scripts are validated in a worker so unrelated Gateway work can continue. The model receives the same syntax-error text, source location, and offending line before any widget is hosted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The full Acorn parse is useful model feedback and runs only on tool execution, not when a saved widget is viewed. Keep that parser, memoize its bounded diagnostic by exact UTF-16 content and classic/module grammar, and map errors back to each current HTML input. A 128-entry LRU retains digests and diagnostics, not source or ASTs; concurrent identical requests share work. Scripts at least 32 Ki UTF-16 units use the existing shared-compute `WorkerTaskPool` and normal packaged-worker registration. No configuration or database changes.

This adds 62 runtime lines plus one packaging-registration line. The growth supplies bounded reuse and asynchronous placement without a second widget-version cache or a competing worker lifecycle owner. Tests grow by 47 lines, including mechanical async assertions and regressions for reuse, grammar separation, and exact worker error feedback.

## Evidence

Synthetic canvas scripts, serial A1/B1/A2/B2 interleave: owner 7 rounds × 10 calls per arm; real `show_widget.execute` with a synthetic presenter 5 rounds × 5 calls per arm. Timing, allocation, and CPU profiles run separately. Source baseline: `92b32cadcc30ddfd44a17c450d8ccfda9f75f6ee`; Node 26.12.1, macOS arm64, shared host.

Real tool execution, median / p95 milliseconds:

| Distinct script | Main-thread CPU before → after | Largest timer interval before → after | Call latency before → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10 KiB | 2.259 / 2.457 → 2.274 / 2.660 | 2.828 / 3.800 → 2.946 / 3.925 | 1.830 / 3.656 → 1.951 / 3.728 |
| 100 KiB | 9.351 / 11.435 → 0.571 / 0.865 | 8.451 / 20.566 → 1.572 / 2.814 | 7.591 / 20.541 → 4.693 / 11.241 |
| 1 MiB | 57.197 / 59.716 → 2.144 / 2.275 | 51.552 / 71.145 → 1.437 / 1.856 | 50.523 / 70.859 → 51.181 / 71.648 |

Repeated 1 MiB tool calls: latency **49.60 → 1.27 ms**, main-thread CPU **53.24 → 1.30 ms**, total process CPU **85.25 → 3.64 ms**. Markup-only edits have the same reuse benefit. A/A distinct-script main CPU medians were 2.147/2.358 ms, 9.251/9.452 ms, and 56.886/57.250 ms respectively. Small unique calls are approximately neutral; timer intervals include scheduler noise.

The owner-only measurements agree: 1 MiB distinct main CPU **58.67 → 2.67 ms**, latency **54.42 → 53.76 ms**; repeated latency **53.33 → 1.27 ms**. Distinct 1 MiB total sampled V8 heap allocation grows **46.15 → 47.39 MB**, while main-thread allocation falls **46.15 → 1.17 MB**. Repeats fall **45.12 MB → 13.85 KB**. Sampling includes collected objects and worker isolates; native backing stores are excluded. Worker CPU profiles contain the large Acorn parse.

Cold-start tradeoff: the first 100 KiB source-runtime tool call takes **17.02 → 149.22 ms**, including the worker's TypeScript loader, while main CPU falls **17.07 → 5.50 ms**. This is explicitly separate from steady-state latency. Five fresh processes using the actual packaged worker measured a 100 KiB raw parse at **9.98 → 31.58 ms** wall and **10.21 → 3.29 ms** main CPU (synchronous prefix **9.98 → 2.08 ms**). This includes lazy pool construction and is a worker-boundary measurement, not a bundled full-tool measurement. The remaining first-worker latency cost is about 21.6 ms; reuse avoids it for unchanged scripts.

The regression fails against the original scanner because two identical script submissions call Acorn twice instead of once. All **105 focused tests** pass (`widget-script-syntax`, `widget-tool.presenter`, `widget-tool`; 62.64 s including worker compilation). `pnpm build` passes. Codex autoreview of the final local snapshot is scoped-clean through P2. `pnpm check:changed` completed: all typechecks, lint, formatting, and other guards pass; its unused-export scan fails in untouched channel identity, backup verification, GitHub OAuth, and chat-search files. The exact-parent owner scan at `92b32cadcc30ddfd44a17c450d8ccfda9f75f6ee` reproduces all six observed production findings and the same four full-tree findings (script scan: zero). These are main regressions; the attribution and subsequent partial repair are recorded below.

Reproduce with `scripts/perf/widget-script-syntax-measure.ts`; its header describes baseline/candidate modules, tool execution, allocation, and per-thread CPU profile modes. The parser has no database or workspace inputs: a large session database or workspace tree would add unrelated setup rather than exercise this owner. This proof covers the real execution owner and synthetic presentation, not live model latency or Gateway transport throughput.


| Inherited unused exports | Introducing regression |
| --- | --- |
| `ChannelIdentityLinkAdapter`, `PersonalGitHubActionV2` | #188910, `4674051ce50a`: adds the first export with only local use and removes the second type's last external consumer |
| `MAX_DATABASE_SNAPSHOT_EXTRACT_BYTES`, `DATABASE_SNAPSHOT_FREE_SPACE_RESERVE_BYTES` | `4fb684e294e2`: moves the budget consumer into the defining module but retains the exports |
| `CHAT_SEARCH_HIGHLIGHT`, `syncChatSearchHighlight` | #170434, `d5be7a6a4293`: exports used externally only by tests, so the production scan fails |

The baseline replay used unchanged prepared workspace dependencies. Its first attempt failed dependency resolution and is excluded. The qualified production replay also reported five baseline-only talk type exports; generated-artifact graph differences remain unqualified for those extra findings, so they are not attributed as new main regressions here. No unrelated source was changed. This baseline evidence is specifically for the branch parent; it does not claim a newer CI merge parent was tested.


Main advanced during validation: #189894 (`cde4bfe4f10c`) fixes the four backup/chat-search findings. The two identity findings from #188910 remain. The widget changes do not overlap that repair.


Exact-head CI [run 41258061355](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41258061355) passed at `193fff0e93687139eed84ddfdfd7fffea01b376e`, without reruns. Native ordinary landing merged that reviewed head as `51fd804b2fc76a43ac8a26a58e8177b5b8aa248e`; no admin exception was used.

prs.title: doctor: warn on undeliverable cron alerts (companion to #188946, proof)
prs.body:
Refs #186990

Builds on #188946 by @Nikhil-jaiswal007. Both commits are cherry-picked unchanged with authorship kept, rebased onto current main. This PR adds the Linux proof ClawSweeper asked for on #188946. Credit for the change goes to @Nikhil-jaiswal007. If #188946 lands instead, this can be closed.

## What Problem This Solves
When a scheduled automation fails and its failure alert cannot be delivered (for example, no messaging channel configured), the result is only stored in job state, and `openclaw doctor` never surfaces it.

## User Impact
User impact: `openclaw doctor` now warns when a scheduled automation's failure alert could not be delivered, with the reason and what to configure, instead of the failure staying hidden in job state.

## Why This Change Was Made
Doctor now reads `lastFailureNotificationDeliveryStatus` / `lastFailureNotificationDeliveryError` and warns only for `not-delivered`, with the reason and next steps. The ClawSweeper P2 on 9d744de (note mock dropped real exports) is fixed by the author's d08e625 (importOriginal spread).

## Evidence
Setup: Linux, built CLI, isolated HOME, cron store seeded with the PR's fixture shapes: one `not-delivered` job, one `delivered` job.

Before (main 88217c925; `src/commands/doctor/` is unchanged from there to base 43a3abe0595), `node openclaw.mjs doctor --non-interactive`:
```
(no Cron box and no failure-alert note anywhere in the Doctor output; exit 0)
```
After (this branch 0b72825e7f2, Doctor exit 0):
```
◇  Cron ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                                        │
│  1 automation has a failure alert that could not be delivered.         │
│  - Alert undeliverable (alert-undeliverable): Channel is required (no  │
│    configured channels detected)                                       │
│  - Configure a messaging channel for the gateway or set an explicit    │
│    delivery target on the job. Review with openclaw automations show   │
│    <id>.                                                               │
│                                                                        │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```
The delivered job is not listed.

### Tests
- check:test-mock-exports: 9d744de alone `exit 1`: "First-party mock factories must preserve real exports or explain isolation: src/commands/doctor/cron/index.failure-alert.test.ts:15: ../../../../packages/terminal-core/src/note.js"; branch `exit 0`: "Mock factory ratchet OK: 6438 grandfathered factories."
- Red (main doctor source + new test): `Tests  1 failed | 2 passed (3) (exit 1)`; the failing test is "warns when a failure alert could not be delivered, with the recorded reason"
- Green (branch): `Tests  3 passed (3) (exit 0)`
- oxlint exit 0, format check exit 0, git diff --check exit 0

### Upgrade from latest stable
Linux, Node 24.22.1, no Docker, so I did the `published-upgrade-survivor` steps by hand. Isolated npm prefix `$P` and fresh `HOME=$H`. No channels, accounts or secrets.

1. Stable: `npm view openclaw dist-tags --json` gives `"latest": "2026.10.9"`. Then `npm i -g --prefix $P openclaw@2026.10.9`, and `openclaw --version` prints `OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (8b18b55)`.
2. Settings and automation, with the stable CLI:
   - `openclaw config set gateway.mode local`, `config set gateway.port 19789 --strict-json` and `config set agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds 600 --strict-json`. Then `config validate` printed `Config valid: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`.
   - Started `openclaw gateway run --port 19789 --bind loopback` and ran `openclaw cron add --name "Morning brief" --cron "0 8 * * *" --tz UTC --system-event brief` (exit 0).
   - Stopped the gateway. Appended the PR's fixture jobs (one `not-delivered`, one `delivered`) to the same store with the v2026.10.9 source's `loadCronStore`/`saveCronStore`.
   - Stable `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` exited 0. The output has no Cron box and no failure-alert note.
   - `cron list --all --json` listed: heartbeat-main, Alert delivered, Alert undeliverable, Morning brief, Memory Dreaming Promotion.
3. Upgrade the same HOME to this branch (0b72825e7f2), using the built CLI `node openclaw.mjs`. `--version` prints `OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (0b72825)`.
   - `doctor --non-interactive` first stopped on the shared state-DB migration with exit 1: `Client credentials require backed-up migration custody; stop the app and run openclaw doctor --fix.` This is main's migration gate and is not touched by this PR.
   - `doctor --fix --non-interactive` exited 0. Then `doctor --non-interactive` exited 0 and printed:

prs.body:
Closes #187607

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the macOS status menu checks Off for Thinking and Verbose when a session inherits defaults or stores a value the menu does not represent.

## User Impact

Inherited and unrepresented preferences no longer look explicitly disabled. Explicit Off and represented non-Off selections retain their checkmarks and existing actions. No configuration, protocol, persistence, available-choice, or preview-lifecycle changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the display-only Off fallback in initial preference-menu construction and submenu reuse. Compare each existing item's value directly with the stored override, without resolving defaults in the client or adding another menu action.

This is the standalone two-file candidate, separate from #187603 / #188635 and #187602 / #188683. The combined #188635 overlay is not included.

## Evidence

@pollybot13 and @eisenhorn arranged and completed the native macOS validation, including the baseline and fixed test runs, 36 native captures, selection/request/readback checks, and delivery of the proof package. Mert Başar coordinated the handoff; Roboclaw reviewed the supplied artifacts, separately from that native execution: [proof run](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/actions/runs/41238730455).

- Product/proof base: `4591070b2f4b1b043b57c306fcd6d235e56b04a2`; workflow revision: `aa35bd8d87c6e743e5133b97050513987911100f`.
- Baseline builds; the new checkmark regression fails with 12 intended Off-versus-empty assertions while the 11 sibling test functions pass. The identical 12 tests pass with this fix in 9.710 seconds.
- Fixed build, Swift lint, source/test formatting and whitespace checks exit 0. Two existing file-length lint warnings remain in untouched DashboardManager.swift and GatewayConnection.swift; this is not a warning-free claim.
- Real AppKit submenu captures cover inheritance, retained-menu reuse, explicit Off/high/on controls and unrepresented values. Four generated mouse-selection cases per phase verify exact sessions.patch requests, fixture readback, other-preference preservation and a distinct unchanged control session over real loopback WebSockets.
- Proof boundary: synthetic sessions and generated WindowServer input, not a production Gateway, deployed app, physical human clicks or cross-process persistence. Each action/readback case uses a fresh seeded process; the capture/reuse matrix runs in one process per phase.
- Roboclaw verified the supplied hashes, logs, 36 native captures and selection/request/readback receipts. The complete candidate diff and changed-source hashes match the version executed by @pollybot13 and @eisenhorn exactly; no native tests were rerun during artifact review.
- Standalone candidate SHA-256: `c149a71c2924f9d793f6c11cdb0e8e85024b5260aa78c1e0833106d03bb82cb6`. The owner, loader and pre-change test fixture remained byte-identical upstream at `92b32cadcc30ddfd44a17c450d8ccfda9f75f6ee`. prs.title: fix(exec): dollar amounts in agent messages are corrupted when exec text uses $<digit> in double quotes
prs.body:
Closes #179890

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: dollar amounts in agent-sent messages are silently corrupted ("$900" becomes "00") when an `exec` command passes the text in double quotes.

## User Impact

User impact: exec commands that would deliver a corrupted dollar amount are refused before they run. The refusal shows the text as written next to what the shell would deliver, and how to fix it (single quotes, `\$`, or a quoted heredoc), so the agent retries correctly instead of sending the wrong amount to a customer. It can be disabled with `OPENCLAW_EXEC_DOLLAR_GUARD=off`.

**Open question for maintainers:** this is default-on and uses an environment switch. If you'd prefer it opt-in, or shipped as a plugin on the existing `before_tool_call` hook instead of in core, I'm happy to rework it that way. Tell me which shape you want.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runBeforeToolCallHook` checks `exec` command text for a `$<digit>` that the shell would expand, before any plugin or approval policy runs. Codex-native shell commands reach the same policy through the PreToolUse native hook relay. Relay planning now counts the guard as a before-tool-call policy and keeps `exec` in the PreToolUse matcher, so native commands are covered even with no other policy installed.

The scanner is deliberately conservative. It only flags an expansion it can show would be empty:
- It honours single quotes, `\$`, `$'...'`, quoted heredoc delimiters, `${...}`, `$((...))` and comments.
- It recurses into `$(...)`, including substitutions inside unquoted heredoc bodies, with their own quoting.
- It ignores `$0` (the shell or script name) unless it reads as money (`$0.50`).
- It stays out of commands that define functions or set positional parameters (`set --`, `shift`, `getopts`), where `$1.00` may be intended.
- It fails open on anything it cannot parse.

Code-mode `exec` (JavaScript) is excluded.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/shell-dollar-expansion-guard.test.ts` (35 tests): the hazard shapes, every safe quoting form, `$0`, populated positional parameters, heredoc command substitution, `bash -lc` unwrapping, fail-open, and the `runBeforeToolCallHook` veto, allow and disable cases. The `$0`, positional-parameter and heredoc-substitution cases fail on the previous revision and pass now.
- `src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.dollar-guard.test.ts` (6 tests): Codex `Bash` and `exec_command` are denied and single-quoted amounts pass. Relay planning enables PreToolUse for `exec` with no other policy and keeps it in a relay scoped to other tools; these planning cases fail without the relay change.
- The existing `agent-tools.before-tool-call*` and `native-hook-relay*` unit suites pass. `native-hook-relay.participants` and `native-hook-relay.remote-http` fail identically on `main` without this change in my environment.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- Replayed against 391 unique `$`-bearing exec commands from a production deployment: 18 were flagged, all genuine expansion bugs, with no false positives.
- Still to add: a gateway trace of a real agent refusing and retrying. I'll attach it before asking for re-review.

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): cached row text fidelity [do not merge]
prs.body:
**Experiment stopped: the final measured head fails the first-paint gate. Keep closed; do not merge.**

The text/height invariant passes 11/11 on both routes, but paired FCP is +85.41 ms on chat (9/11 worse) and +53.99 ms on dashboard (10/11 worse); first painted rows are +87.87 ms and +55.91 ms (9/11 worse on each). These exceed the predeclared threshold and the identical-code A/A control. The earlier prototype's passing secondaries do not override this final-head result after the required rebase.

## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in reload can paint a shorter cached assistant answer and then replace it with the complete live answer. The campaign's 14-state dashboard reload timeline includes this broader content-settlement problem; this experiment isolates the long-Markdown row identified by the independent native-frame audit.

The default history display projection caps text at 8,000 characters (`src/gateway/chat-display-projection.helpers.ts:24`; truncation at line 156). History inspection (`git log -p -S`) traces 12,000 → 8,000 to `4f00b769251d` (#67277, “Tighten context limits and bound memory excerpts”); `5f2273e81efc` moved it into the shared display projection, later split into the helper. This is a bounded history/display payload contract, rather than a snapshot byte cap. The live transcript automatically fetches the complete message, but that recovered display response was not retained in the browser snapshot. Reload therefore lost content the operator had already seen.

## Why This Change Was Made

At the transcript recovery owner, retain the accepted display message in the existing row-display snapshot, keyed by its capped source text. The same renderer can use it offline and while reconnect revalidates the message. Keeping the display message rather than just Markdown preserves inline media order and reference links. Server replay and pairing QR data are removed at that producer before retention; existing history serialization privacy rules stay unchanged.

This uses the existing disposable client cache, its row pruning, 12 MiB record cap, 24 MiB total cap, and 20-session retention. Projection version 14 drops old records for refill. There are no server schema, protocol, configuration, or history-request changes.

## User Impact

After a loaded answer has been cached, a warm reload can immediately show its complete text and media in place. A changed source preview rejects the older recovery, and reconnect still fetches live data. Release-note context: preserve complete previously displayed assistant answers in cached transcripts during reload.

## Evidence

Performance head: `84a55d719da3ca594cc0c388cd96e9db9a55f973`. AWS Crabbox `cbx_44fe690d0b66`, c7a.4xlarge, 16 CPUs / 30 GiB. One fixed instance for 11 interleaved pairs plus A/A, both routes, both harnesses. Real-Gateway RTT shaping: 80 ms; native Team-scale: live-fast, untraced. A/B quiet-host CPU idle: 93.13%.

Snapshot growth exceeds the 5% preference. The additional full display and exact source cost about 18 KiB per measured snapshot, below 0.08% of the existing 24 MiB total budget. prs.title: feat(skills): bundle Skill Workshop as a plugin that owns learned skill folders
prs.body:
## Problem

Skill Workshop is moving from core into a bundled plugin, one piece at a time. Skill loading, prompt path compaction and the security audit hard-coded Workshop's per-agent skill folder. The `skill-workshop` plugin id was still retired: releases since 2026.10.1 ignore any `skill-workshop` plugin policy and warn that the plugin was removed.

## Fix

- **New bundled plugin:** `extensions/skill-workshop`, enabled by default. It has no runtime registrations yet.
- **New manifest field `agentSkillsDir`:** one folder name under each agent's state folder. Skill discovery reads it from plugin metadata, without loading the plugin. The discovery worker gets it with the other plugin skill roots.
  - Learned skills keep the `workshop` tier and the `openclaw-workshop` source id. Stored snapshots and the UI "Learned" group depend on them.
- **Prompt path compaction:** keeps full paths for learned skills based on each skill's source, not a Workshop path lookup.
- **Security audit:** scans every plugin-declared learned folder, including folders of disabled plugins.
- **Plugin id restored:** `skill-workshop` is no longer a retired id. The "plugin removed" warning and the `plugins inspect` fallback are deleted.
- **Config migration**, with the new marker `meta.migrations.skillWorkshopPlugin` (approved by Ayaan; same pattern as `modelPolicyAllowlist`):
  - Unmarked configs: runtime config materialization and config validation both ignore an older `plugins.entries.skill-workshop` entry (including proposal-era settings such as `maxSkillBytes`) and its `plugins.deny` id. Validation warns that Doctor removes them, so old settings never block a config write or startup.
  - Doctor, which runs during `openclaw update`, removes that policy and stamps the marker. It never rewrites `plugins.allow` or `plugins.enabled`.
  - A config write records the marker only when nothing older needs repair. While older `skill-workshop` entries or deny ids are ignored, any write that touches `plugins`, including an equal value, a parent-path assignment or a list-index edit, is refused with "Run `openclaw doctor --fix`, then retry". The refusal lives in the shared write preparation (`prepareConfigWriteTopology`), which offline writes, Gateway `config.patch` writes and Doctor repair all use; Doctor passes because its candidate records the marker. `config set` checks the same rule before it reports "No change" or routes a patch to a running Gateway. No writer infers which part of a write is new.
  - Marked configs validate `skill-workshop` settings like any other plugin's.
- **Temporary second owner:** core Workshop code still writes learned skills until its writers move into the plugin. A test keeps the manifest folder equal to core's folder.

## Impact

- **Update behavior:** the installed updater runs first and is unchanged. Candidate-side runtime materialization and validation keep unmarked configs working. Candidate Doctor removes the old policy and records the marker.
- **Behavior change:** learned skills now load through the plugin, so an exclusive `plugins.allow` without `skill-workshop`, or `plugins.enabled: false`, stops loading them. Doctor does not rewrite those switches. Its existing "Skill Workshop tool policy" health check now warns when either switch keeps the plugin off while Workshop is on, and names the fix.
- **Config surface:** `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` rises (core +1 for the marker, plugin +21 for the new plugin's standard entry fields). Ayaan approved the raise.

## Upgrade proof

### Published driver × candidate cell

- **Setup:** published `openclaw@2026.10.9` installed in an isolated npm prefix. Isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, `OPENCLAW_HOME` and `HOME`.
- **Candidate:** built from this branch with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs`; the tarball integrity check passed.

1. **Seed with the published CLI.** It writes `plugins.deny: ["skill-workshop"]` and `plugins.entries.skill-workshop: { enabled: false, config: { maxSkillBytes: 20000 } }`, printing its own "plugin removed: skill-workshop … ignored" warning. A learned skill `cell-procedure` sits at `agents/main/agent/workshop-skills/`.
2. **Published `skills list`:** `cell-procedure`, source `openclaw-workshop`, eligible.
3. **Update with the published updater:** `openclaw update --tag <candidate.tgz> --yes --no-restart` exits 0. The candidate owns admission, and the installed package contains `dist/extensions/skill-workshop` with `agentSkillsDir`. The candidate Doctor step reports "Removed plugins.entries.skill-workshop" and "Removed skill-workshop from plugins.deny".
4. **Config after update:** the deny list is empty, the `skill-workshop` entry is gone, and `meta.migrations.skillWorkshopPlugin` is `true`.
5. **`skills list` after update:** `cell-procedure` is still listed and eligible, and its file is unchanged.
6. **New policy is honored:** `config set plugins.entries.skill-workshop.enabled false`, then `skills list`: the learned skill is gone.

### Pre-Doctor policy writes through the real writer (source CLI, fresh isolated state per case)

| Starting config (unmarked) | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026.10 entry `{enabled:false, config:{maxSkillBytes:20000}}` + deny | `config set plugins.entries.skill-workshop.enabled false` | refused: "must be migrated first. Run openclaw doctor --fix, then retry."; config unchanged |
| same, after `doctor --fix` | same command | entry `{enabled:false}`, marker `true`; the learned skill is hidden |
| `plugins.deny: ["skill-workshop", "diffs"]` | `config set 'plugins.deny[1]' telegram` | refused; config unchanged |
| `plugins.allow: ["diffs"]` (no Workshop policy) | `config set plugins.entries.diffs.enabled true` | written; the allowlist is never rewritten |

## Tests

- New tests for the migration, plugin enablement of learned folders, and the folder-equality guard.
- Changed fixtures:
  - Skill-loading fixtures that set `plugins.enabled: false` only to skip plugin loading now use `plugins.allow: ["skill-workshop"]`. This covers 2 Workshop contract fixtures and 7 other skill suites.
  - Three `plugin-skills` mocks now spread the real module, which shrinks the mock-export baseline by 3. The synthetic registry in `workspace-skill-loader.test.ts` gains the bundled `skill-workshop` record.
  - The retired-plugin validation row for `skill-workshop` is replaced. The new case uses the real bundled plugin: an unmarked config with proposal-era settings validates with a Doctor warning, and the same settings fail once the marker is recorded.
  - Migration tests cover the write refusal for older entries and deny ids, Doctor's exemption, and the unaffected allowlist case. Health check tests cover the plugin-off warning for an exclusive allowlist and for `plugins.enabled: false`. A shared write-preparation test covers refusing an equal-value write and accepting it once migrated.
  - The `plugins inspect skill-workshop` fallback test is removed with the fallback.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| All `src/skills` tests, all Workshop contract files, plugin manifest, root contributions, security audit, config meta and validation, inspect CLI, Doctor migration suites (174 files) | pass after the fixture updates above |
| New migration (4) and enablement (1) tests | pass |
| `check:changed`: typecheck all, boundaries, cycles, guards | pass |
| `check:changed`: lint | changed files pass oxlint; the full lint run reports `max-lines` in files this PR does not touch |

prs.title: fix(exec): keep Windows POSIX shell approvals one-shot
prs.body:
Supersedes #140127, thanks @PrisonBreakPB.
Related: #139917.

## What Problem This Solves

Windows operators can save reusable execution approvals for inline POSIX shell commands even though those shell carriers should remain one-shot.

## User Impact

Inline `sh -c` and `bash -c` commands on Windows, including package-manager and dispatch wrappers, no longer mint reusable rules. Repeated or changed payloads continue to require approval. Script-file and durable positional-carrier approvals retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The persistence collector unwrapped carriers and then analyzed POSIX shell payloads with the Windows cmd/PowerShell parser. Exclude POSIX shells from that fallback after the existing script and positional handling, matching the one-shot carrier policy on POSIX hosts.

Security review: this only narrows future approval generation. Current main already hashes argv and cwd, so this repair does not claim that approving one command grants arbitrary later payloads. It prevents deriving reusable rules with the wrong shell grammar. Direct commands and cmd/PowerShell approvals remain bound to their inner argv; changed arguments still prompt. Existing saved rules are not revoked or migrated; operators can review and remove previously saved carrier rules through the approvals controls. No schema or configuration changes.

## Evidence

- Reproduced against main `edc86dd18f36a84126ced2ea35d3f9be61ec1615` using the real shell evaluator and persistence decision owner: five Windows POSIX-shell cases failed because they returned an inner-executable rule; 51 other tests passed. No contributor code was checked out or run.
- After the fix: `pnpm test src/infra/exec-approvals-allow-always.test.ts src/infra/exec-allow-always-persistence.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 75 tests. Coverage includes direct/nested POSIX wrappers, Linux/macOS carrier policy, repeated/changed payload approval misses, and argv-bound cmd/PowerShell/direct-command controls.
- Changed-file suite: 1.87 seconds wall time on the passing run; two-file orchestration including cold worker preparation: 45.61 seconds. The [CI changed-node lane](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41246822393/job/124672159185) passed in 287 seconds total (228 seconds running its broader test shard).
- Focused TypeScript check, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Final autoreview: full collector/planner/wrapper context supplied; P0–P2 scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Reviewed the final local snapshot committed as `cac1b153266d753a53ee3259d31854556b866827` against the main commit above. Native Windows execution and a full Gateway/model approval round trip were not run; explicit Windows evaluator paths ran on Linux with synthetic executable fixtures.
- Simplification: production LOC +0 (6 added / 6 removed), including removal of the inaccurate inline-shell persistence example. Tests +41 lines; the dedicated test-line allocation covers the platform regression and native-wrapper controls without changing the shared baseline.
- The local repository-wide test-line ratchet reached its 60-second host limit without a result; the [hosted baseline ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41246822393/job/124672158481) subsequently passed.

Contributor credit: `Co-authored-by: PrisonBreakPB <2364197433@qq.com>` from the original PR's human commit author.

prs.title: fix: restore CLI message sends with agent tool policies
prs.body:
Related: #184964

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `openclaw message send` failing with `Cannot verify the installed tool authority for Template-managed agent "main"` when the selected agent has its own tool profile or allowlist. Even text-only sends and `--dry-run` fail for ordinary agents with no Template installation.

## User Impact

CLI message sends work again without changing agent policies or repairing a healthy state database. Explicit attachment read restrictions and genuine Template-consent failures remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The regression was introduced by [3c23d52c93b in #184964](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3c23d52c93b2479d8685564b7e5b4e3dcb47cc1e): the new `resolveEffectiveToolPolicy()` call in `src/media/read-capability.ts` reads Template consent during message preparation, including text-only sends.

The CLI config guard publishes its configuration synchronously, before that consent provenance has been initialized. Initialize the provenance and bind it to the effective command configuration before dispatch, using the same preparation owners as standalone agent commands. No media-policy checks are removed.

## Evidence

- Reproduced with the installed CLI: `openclaw message send --channel discord --target channel:123456789012345678 --message regression-probe --dry-run --json` exits 1 with the error above.
- New command-boundary regressions: **2 fail / 1 pass before**, **3 pass after**. They exercise real config, policy, and dispatch with isolated consent-row I/O. Both an agent-owned profile and a restrictive allowlist can send text; unreadable consent remains rejected.
- **35 focused tests passed** across the command, media workspace-access, and consent-preparation suites. Existing attachment-denial tests remain green. Command-suite wall time was 5.14 seconds for 14 tests; the three sequential test shards completed in 23.93 seconds.
- A separate Node process with no module mocks, isolated empty state, and a local channel adapter reproduced the same consent error before the fix. Afterward, dry-run succeeded without delivery, and a non-dry-run delivered the exact message to the local adapter once with `deliveryStatus: "sent"`. No external channel API was called.
- Changed-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The final isolated regression run also passed all 3 cases (33.16 seconds including cold worker compilation). The 76-line test allocation covers the missing CLI initialization boundary and fail-closed control.

### Shipped-CLI proof pinned to `a9bd00376c21`

Source builds of the CLI (`pnpm openclaw` → `scripts/run-node.mjs`) at head `a9bd00376c21` and PR parent `43af01b15c96`. Each case uses a fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, and `HOME`. Delivery cases use the bundled Mattermost channel pointed at a local `127.0.0.1` recording endpoint (`network.dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork: true`). The endpoint logs each request and whether the body contains the attachment bytes. The token is a placeholder; no external API was called.

| Case | Agent `tools` / consent state | Parent `43af01b` | Head `a9bd003` | Channel requests (head) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Text dry-run (Discord) | `allow:[message] deny:[read]` | ❌ `Cannot verify the installed tool authority…` | ✅ dry-run payload | — |
| Text send | `allow:[message] deny:[read]` | ❌ same error, 0 requests | ✅ `deliveryStatus: sent` | 1 (`POST /posts`) |
| Attachment send, read denied | `allow:[message] deny:[read]` | — | ❌ `path-not-allowed`, `sentBeforeError: false` | **0** |
| Attachment send, read allowed (control) | `profile:full allow:[read,message]` | — | ✅ sent | 2 (`/files` with bytes, `/posts`) |
| Template consent: current v2 row, matching digest | `profile:full allow:[read,message]` | — | ✅ sent | 2 |
| Agent config edited after consent (`allow += exec`), attachment and text-only | same row | — | ❌ `Cannot verify the installed tool authority…` | **0** |
| Row digest invalidated (config unchanged) | v2 row, wrong digest | — | ❌ `Cannot verify…` | **0** |
| Unsupported provenance schema | `…templateInstallRecord.v999` | — | ❌ `Cannot verify…` | **0** |
| Legacy v1 provenance | `…templateInstallRecord.v1` | — | ❌ `…uses a legacy dynamic tool policy…` | **0** |

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the backup and chat-search unused exports reported by `check-dependencies` in [scheduled full CI 41252475393](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41252475393).

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Backup limits and chat-search highlighting continue to use their existing owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove four unused export modifiers introduced by `4fb684e294e2` and `d5be7a6a4293` (#170434). The browser tests now exercise the existing production search watcher and state owner instead of importing private implementation details; their assertions remain intact.

## Evidence

- Fresh-main duplicate/owner check found no matching repair. Rebased cleanly onto `f121a7f70da4`; patch is identical to the accepted `bcd893b02508` candidate.
- Fresh-head focused proof: 8/8 real Chromium browser tests and 42/42 backup completeness cases pass.
- Fresh-head `pnpm deadcode:dependencies` clears all four targeted findings but exits 1 on two unrelated unused exported types already present on the new main base: `src/channels/plugins/types.plugin.ts: ChannelIdentityLinkAdapter` and `src/gateway/github-personal-oauth.ts: PersonalGitHubActionV2`. The former was introduced and the latter lost its external consumer in `4674051ce50a` (#188910); neither owner is changed here. The aggregate is not claimed green.
- Fresh-head `pnpm deadcode:exports` also exits 1 solely for those same two unrelated exported types; its script scan is clean. All four targeted exports are absent from both findings lists. Both scripts passed on the original accepted candidate; unchanged unused-file inventory proof was also clean.
- Parent validation: three scoped typechecks, lint, format, diff check, and the test-line ratchet pass. No allocations or baselines changed.
- Local Codex autoreview, P0–P2, `c633ec6376e1..bcd893b02508`: complete-context scoped-clean, no findings. Full watcher, state owner, and browser tests were supplied. Review did not execute tests; the rebase is patch-identical.

Simplify pass: no production machinery added, no new tests or test seams. Both production files retain their existing line counts; test setup grows by 14 lines to use the real search owner. No rendering change. Exact-head PR CI supplies broad proof.

Requested by @steipete

## Work sessions

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): seed cached sidebar rows after render reduction [do not merge]
prs.body:
## Result: failed gate; do not merge

Neither candidate passes the pre-declared LoAF gate on the common sidebar projection + bounded rendering base. Closing this experiment without promoting a ready PR or committing/pushing the rejected candidate overlay. The current PR head contains common dependency setup only.

| Variant | Chat empty-host median | Dashboard empty-host median | Chat LoAF paired delta | Dashboard LoAF paired delta | Own runtime LOC |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A: cache admission + early layout batch | 165.0 → 0 ms, 11/11 immediate | 155.6 → 0 ms, 11/11 immediate | +44.5 ms, worse 10/11 | +9.7 ms, mixed signs | +10 |
| B: cached window seed, recorded offset, normal rAF | 163.2 → 0 ms, 11/11 immediate | 154.2 → 0 ms, 11/11 immediate | +200.0 ms, worse 11/11 | +58.2 ms, worse 10/11 | +6 |
| A/A control | 181.1 / 193.9 ms | 166.9 / 181.6 ms | -3.7 ms, mixed signs | +20.7 ms, mixed signs | 0 |

The gate permits at most +15 ms paired LoAF and no adverse change beyond A/A. A also delays final rows (+159.0 ms chat, +34.2 ms dashboard; worse 10/11 and 9/11). Corrected B delays dashboard final rows (+38.3 ms, worse 9/11). Later hello medians in B have overlapping IQRs and mixed pair signs below the declared 9/11 threshold; they are reported, not used as an extra regression claim. Mixed-sign FCP/first-row/CLS changes are not treated as harm merely because a median rises.

## Problem and attribution

A signed-in warm reload of a dashboard-qualified chat deep link can have cached section hosts with no rows until the section-window owner's scheduled geometry publication. The earlier campaign reported this first-frame sidebar problem in 11/11 chat reloads. Both attempts repair that DOM boundary consistently, but move enough render/layout work earlier to exceed the blocking budget even after the bounded-row reduction.

A uses exact-link cached-roster admission and a cached microtask layout batch. B instead seeds initial estimated positions from the existing snapshot/row order/counts/collapse state and the scroll owner's recorded offset, then lets normal rAF own element geometry. B deletes the cache owner's superseded frame/100 ms paint delay. No new store, config, durable schema or Gateway protocol. The first B prototype still read DOM scrollTop; that was corrected and its failed results are retained separately below. Removing the getter did not recover the blocking cost.

## Proof and limits

One fixed quiet AWS c7a.4xlarge lease, `cbx_5516c52b531d`, run `run_c260e52e046983f8009f1b91bda1c4fc`; repo Playwright Chromium 156.0.8078.4; real isolated loopback Gateway; synthetic 3,000-session Team fixture; nondefault agent; archived dashboard-qualified targets; involving-me/category/created; 97 groups/102 order entries; five collapsed; empty groups always; previews off; two pins; eight expanded retained parents; 80 ms transport shaping; frozen peers. Eleven alternating-order pairs for each route/variant plus eleven A/A pairs per route. Common source `2b0e23a66664de6cdfd2debf24a22cf7adaf59e1` includes pinned main plus the projection and bounded-rendering runtime union. Quiet samples were 92.55–93.49% CPU idle. Timings come from the instrumented warm-reload proof, with no CPU tracing/profiling; no Mac performance timings are reported.

Native first-transcript-frame row assertion: common fails 3/3 at the intended assertion; A passes 3/3; corrected B passes 3/3. Native command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts ui/src/e2e/sidebar-complete-roster.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`; wall times common 46.55 s, A 46.75 s, corrected B 46.85 s. Focused warm-boot/route/controller units: 49 passed, pnpm wall 8.55 s. The changed roster browser-test context provider also passes its focused file: 4 tests, pnpm wall 8.09 s. Both candidates have independent clean review through P2.

All 1,490 delivered warm frames are indexed through 158 exact sidebar/header states, visually inspected with every original frame retained in provenance manifests. Each candidate has zero delivered empty/row-partial first sidebar surfaces on both routes and no populated-to-empty collapse. Each corresponding chat baseline has one blank first sidebar surface; A/A and the discarded prototype have none. All 176 warm runs are connect-first, one-document, and browser-error-free. Shared row top/height corrections at three sampled points are zero. Sparse compositor delivery misses most empty DOM intervals; pixels do not replace the primary DOM boundary or establish every display-vsync.

This does not establish complete whole-page warm parity. The synthetic captures also show inherited sidebar scroll reset on the first warm reload and later Details/dashboard-panel, avatar and artwork fill. Those remain outside this sidebar-row fix and are not repaired here.

Corrected B own diff: runtime +6, tests -47, common-arm probe instrumentation +20, docs net zero; whole own diff -21 lines. The required HEAD-only production stat currently describes common dependency setup (11 files, 281 added/50 deleted), not a committed candidate. No candidate was promoted; check-changed, full UI e2e and exact-ready-head CI were not run after the failed performance gate. Raw synthetic captures, source/build hashes and the reviewed overlay are retained locally. Lease release verified; no owned Gateway listeners remain. No merge.

prs.title: fix(codex): recover conversations after unused native threads disappear
prs.body:
Related: #158752

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Codex-backed conversations failing with `thread not loaded` when native cleanup removes an unused thread but its OpenClaw binding and managed client remain.

## User Impact

The next authorized request can reach the existing stale-thread recovery and start a replacement thread. Loaded threads with an unowned inference route, ambiguous failures, and revoked or aborted requests still fail closed. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inference preparation currently probes the recorded thread before the lifecycle owner's recovery boundary. An exact missing-thread response aborts that preparation even though the later lifecycle already knows how to recover it.

Reuse the existing typed `thread/read` missing-thread classifier, retaining caller admission and post-await revocation checks. Preparation does not mutate the binding or claim the absent thread; the lifecycle owner remains responsible for replacement.

This complements #158752's conversation-binding restart recovery: the separate gap here is the managed inference preflight, not its conversation attachment or RPC classifier changes.

## Evidence

- Personally checked native Codex 0.160.0 source at `a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc`, `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs` (`read_thread_view`): metadata-only reads return the exact invalid-request error when neither persisted nor live thread exists.
- Before the production fix, the real `startOrResumeThread` regression fails with `thread not loaded: old-thread`; the direct inference case also fails, while wrong-thread and wrong-code failures stay rejected.
- The lifecycle regression uses the real app-server client wire, owned inference routing, and persisted binding store; it asserts one replacement start and the new persisted binding. The shared synthetic server now emits the native missing-thread error for absent threads.
- An existing native-skill isolation test initially failed because it isolated `HOME` but inherited `CODEX_HOME`; that fixture now isolates both.
- Focused one-worker run passed 133/133 tests across inference routing, native configuration, and lifecycle binding suites (45.37 seconds wrapper wall time). Inference routing: 43 tests, 11.31 seconds shard wall time; the new lifecycle recovery case took 54 ms. The two lifecycle files together ran 90 tests in 30.84 seconds, including existing database/runtime fixture startup; no new process boots or sleeps were added.
- The four changed TypeScript files pass scoped `tsgo` and targeted Oxlint. Oxfmt, assertion-safety and line-cap ratchets, and `git diff --check` pass. Full-repository checks/build were not run for this narrow change.
- Upstream [CI run 37963384773](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37963384773) has a successful `openclaw/ci-gate`. The `checks-node-changed` job took 422 seconds (17:05:10–17:12:12 UTC); this is lane wall time, not isolated per-file test cost.
- Fresh independent source review found no actionable issue. The canonical autoreview helper was also attempted, but its isolated Codex reviewer could not authenticate (HTTP 401); it produced `reviewer_unavailable`, not a clean review verdict.
- No live Gateway changes or Android build changes in this PR. Native dependency source was inspected; an authenticated native-process end-to-end reproduction was not run for this submission.

prs.title: fix(codex): recover unused native threads without dropping history
prs.body:
Supersedes #167873, thanks @davelutztx.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Codex conversations repeatedly failing with `thread not loaded` after an unused native thread disappears while its managed client and conversation binding remain.

## User Impact

The next turn can create a fresh native thread and continue. Bindings with recorded conversation history remain intact when native state is missing, including after a client restart. Loaded threads without an owned inference route still fail closed. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the inference ownership check onto the existing lifecycle status read, where exact missing-thread errors already reach recovery and its logged warning. Warm reuse without its inference route takes that same cold path before writes. The existing `historyCoveredThrough` marker prevents recovery from replacing a conversation with acknowledged history.

This removes the duplicate preflight `thread/read`: production +18/-22, net **−4 lines**. Regression tests/support grow by 66 lines; a separate 63-line allocation covers the counted test growth. No new state, dependency, or public contract.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on main `edd9cd176a24`: the managed unused-thread regression rejects with the exact `thread/read` error; the recorded-history-after-restart regression incorrectly starts a replacement. Both pass with this repair. Same-client history and loaded-unowned controls remain protected.
- **168 focused tests passed** across inference routing, lifecycle bindings, native configuration, and native-process recovery (51.48s wrapper wall time). The changed native-configuration file has 21 passing cases; its assertions take about 3s within the shared 22.37s database-worker shard.
- Actual pinned Codex **0.164.0**, isolated client and SQLite binding store: native deletion, replacement binding, and subsequent completed turn passed (926ms test time). Model responses use synthetic loopback HTTP. The managed-route regression uses the real client wire against synthetic app-server responses; no live Gateway or external model call is claimed.
- Scoped typecheck, targeted typed lint, Oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed. Hosted [changed-node tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41257494305/job/124703955436) passed in 288s; [baseline ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41257494305/job/124703955050) passed in 305s. These are shared job wall times, not isolated test-file cost. The optional local ratchet run reached its 45s host limit; hosted proof completed it.
- Canonical autoreview: Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, medium reasoning, P0–P2, final local candidate against `edd9cd176a24`: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. `pr-simplify` completed.
- Personally inspected native `read_thread_view` at Codex `6851fae57cf7306e1d7a093d334b1116d33ce5ad`, `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs:2333–2388`: absent live and persisted state produces the exact missing-thread error.

Contributor source was read with `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff` and was never checked out or executed. Human commit credit is preserved as `Co-authored-by: Dave Lutz <dave@lutzfamily.net>`.

prs.title: improve(ui): use one shimmer across the Control UI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves Shimmers had drifted across the Control UI. Running labels used eight different sweeps and placeholders used seven speeds and seven highlight strengths, so two loading states on one screen moved differently. Reduced motion and forced colors behaved differently per surface, and several labels kept animating in forced colors. ## User Impact Every running label now sweeps the same way, and so does every loading placeholder. Reduced motion and forced colors show static text and static placeholders everywhere. Text never drops below the theme's muted color during a sweep. No copy, layout, or active conditions change, and no shimmer is added or removed. ## Why This Change Was Made `base.css` now owns two sweeps with tokens next to the duration scale, applied through one class each. They stay separate because they are different in kind: one paints real text, the other crosses an empty block. Duplicate keyframes are deleted, and the panel skeleton's copy of `.skeleton` goes too because every host renders in light DOM. | Family | Class | Keyframe | Duration | Easing | Highlight | Sweep width | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | Label | `.text-shimmer` | `text-shimmer` | 2.4s | ease-in-out | `--muted` to `--text`, 100% | 30% of a 200% gradient | | Placeholder | `.skeleton` | `shimmer` | 2s | ease-in-out | `--text` at 12% | 50% of the block | The reference for labels is the typing label: full cycle with a seamless wrap, band at a comfortable width, and already gated on both accessibility modes. The reference for placeholders is the lazy view skeleton's timing and geometry, with its highlight reduced from 18% to 12% because 18% reads heavy on large blocks in light themes. `--skeleton-base` stays overridable, since placeholders sit on different surfaces. Placeholders on raised surfaces use a new `--skeleton-base-raised` token, `--muted` at 15% over the surface. A fill that matches the surface shows only the sweep, so bars read as pieces moving sideways. A fill below the surface in a dark theme is no better: the highlight passes through the surface color and the bar opens a moving gap. The raised base sits past the surface in both modes, so the highlight only moves further from it. It applies to Settings rows, memory import, the activity feed and pulse card, the panel skeleton, the video attachment header, the mention menu, attachment checking, and the model trigger. The plugin catalog uses the same mix at 8%, keeping its lighter fill. Settings rows on the Carapace surface also drop their own background so they follow this base. The 12% highlight is unchanged. Lowest difference from the surface across these uses and the four themes, in 8-bit levels: 9 at rest and 29 at the highlight peak. Left on the default base: lazy view and usage, where the fill already sits past the surface. The chat image keeps its own fill because the placeholder is the whole frame. Values before this change, measured from the running app: | Label use | Keyframes | Duration, easing | Gradient | Reduced motion | Forced colors | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Typing | `text-shimmer` | 2.4s ease-in-out | muted to text, 30% of 200% | static | static | | Tool row | `text-shimmer` | 2.2s ease-in-out | text dipping to 42% text on bg | static | animated | | Recap | `text-shimmer` | 2.4s ease-in-out | text dipping to muted | static | animated | | Dictation | `text-shimmer` | 2s linear | muted to 55% strong text | static | animated | | Compaction | `compaction-shimmer` | 3.2s ease-in-out, holds | 105 deg, 260% | static | static | | Processes | `chat-processes-shimmer` | 2s linear | 100 deg, 50% of 200% | static | animated | | Subagents, Details and panel | `subagents-working-sweep` | 3.2s linear | 100 deg, 250%, no tiling | static | static | | Activity pill | `activity-pill-shimmer` | 2s linear | duplicated overlay over 65% or 80% text | static | animated | | Placeholder use | Keyframes | Duration, easing | Highlight | Reduced motion | Forced colors | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `.skeleton` default | `shimmer` | 1.5s ease-in-out | `--bg-hover` | off | animated | | Lazy view | `shimmer` | 2s ease-in-out | text 18% | off | animated | | Usage | `shimmer` | 1.35s ease-in-out | `--bg-hover` | off | animated | | Memory import | `shimmer` | 1.4s ease-in-out | `--bg-hover` | off | animated | | Model trigger, attachment check | `shimmer` | 1.45s ease-in-out | text 30% | off | animated | | Chat image | `shimmer` | 2.4s ease-in-out | `--bg-hover` 45% | off | animated | | Session title | `shimmer` | 1.5s ease-in-out | text 10% | off | animated | | Video attachment | `shimmer` | 1.5s ease-in-out | `--bg-hover` at 35% opacity | off | animated | | Panel skeleton | own `shimmer` copy | 1.5s ease-in-out | `--bg-hover` | off | animated | | Settings rows, Carapace | `oc-skeleton-sweep` | 1.2s linear | border color, 45% wide | off | animated | | Conversation | `chat-conversation-shimmer` | 2s linear | text 5%, 100 deg | static 3% overlay | animated | Left as they are on purpose, because they are not sweeps and converting them would add a shimmer: the opacity pulses on Sessions rows, Context, and link reader; the Details tally segment; the history boundary line; pet and memory artwork glows; the compaction fold, which now runs at its own 3.2s beside the label. Moves `text-shimmer` to `-webkit-text-fill-color` only, so nested syntax tokens and names paint through the gradient. `ui/src/styles/shimmer.node.test.ts` rejects new sweeps or text clipping outside `base.css`. ## Evidence Real app in Chromium against the mocked Gateway, with every state reached through Gateway data and events: nothing inserted into the DOM, no forced classes, nothing hidden. Frames are held at the same point of each animation's cycle so Before and After compare directly: 25, 50, and 75% for labels; 35, 50, and 65% for placeholders, whose band is offscreen for part of its cycle. Recordings run in real time. Each Before and After pair comes from one base commit: Settings rows, plugin catalog, panel, activity, and the five states below on `7232a8de67e`, the rest on `0022746e539`, the base before the last rebase. The settings rows lost their hairlines and 3 px of height between those two commits, from `main`, not from this PR. How the less common states are reached: several-people typing comes from `session.typing` events from eight people watching the session, because the line appears past five active people beyond the two preview rows. Attachment checking is a video in an assistant message with its metadata request still open, the path where the status card shows. Video loading is a sent video opened in the side panel with its bytes still pending. Memory import holds `migrations.memory.plan`, and the mention menu defers `users.mentionable`. Lowest text contrast against `--bg` at any sweep point, which is the muted color: Absolutely dark 6.22, Absolutely light 5.84, CRT 6.80, Beacon 12.30. Beacon's own floor is 7. The tool row previously dipped well below muted in dark themes. Element sizes match between Before and After in every captured use and theme (largest difference 0.00 px across 100 captures). Tests: new `shimmer.node.test.ts` and shimmer browser cases cover the reduced-motion and forced-colors gates, a surface resetting its own background, and compositor or paint-only animation. Focused unit tests pass (631) and the running tool, image loading, pending session, approval loading, and settings skeleton browser tests pass (44). Total CSS is 847 B smaller gzipped; `ui:check-performance:base` passes. ### Safari Safari 27.0.1 on macOS, window captures of the mock with data at the Gateway layer. Each strip is 8 successive frames in capture order, about 0.4 s apart, so the band shows in some frames and the placeholder rests in others. Bars hold their shape at rest and under the band in both modes, and tool row text stays painted while the band moves. | | Dark | Light | |---|---|---| | Running tool row | | | | Settings rows, Carapace | | | | Video attachment header | | | | Memory import | | | | Activity | | | | Panel skeleton | | | | Plugin catalog cards | | | | Compaction | | | | Activity pill, 15 agents | | | Activity is at `4b32deb1f26`, whose only style change is that card. The other placeholder strips and the tool row are at `d0eb72f902a`. Compaction and activity pill are from an earlier commit; their label styles have not changed since. The video state opens through an Accessibility press on the attachment's Open button in that window, with the video bytes left pending. In Safari the plugin catalog cards hold still at first while the chips above them sweep: no pixel changed across 8 frames at about 10 s after load, and the cards were moving at about 30 s, so the strips above are from then. The base commit shows the same freeze at 10 s. Removing `content-visibility: auto` from `.plugin-catalog-section` in a local test made the cards sweep at 10 s, so that rule is the cause, and this PR leaves it alone. ### Absolutely dark, labels prs.title: fix(codex): apply plugin input rewrites to native tools
prs.body:
Closes #189886

## What Problem This Solves

A plugin's `before_tool_call` rewrite currently denies a Codex-native tool call instead of applying the new input. Forwarding MCP rewrites without a guard can also round untouched numbers through `JSON.parse`.

## User Impact

Applies supported rewrites through `updatedInput`: Bash and `apply_patch` commands, and JSON-object arguments for `mcp__*` tools. Other rewrites still deny, including rewrites in the approval-time path. Codex's normal approval checks still apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

The relay checks and sends the same parsed JSON snapshot of the plugin result. It denies an MCP rewrite if that snapshot contains a value altered by parsing the original input, including moved values and overflow to null.

The guard is conservative: it treats `1.0` becoming `1` as a change and can block unrelated equal values. Whether to restrict it to actual numeric-value changes is the open question in #189886. Values a plugin derives from an altered number are outside this guard.

## Evidence

On `cab422622b4`:

- Targeted tests passed: 96 in `native-hook-relay.test.ts` and 16 in `native-hook-relay-cli.test.ts`, run serially.
- The runtime build and `git diff --check` passed.
- A real model through an isolated Gateway executed the rewritten shell command and sent the `1.0 → 2` MCP rewrite.
- Untouched and prepended `9007199254740993`, overflow to null, a non-enumerable array slot, and a hidden `toJSON` copy were denied before reaching MCP. A stateful `toJSON` check confirmed the checked snapshot was the one sent.

Not run: live approval enforcement, a live `apply_patch` rewrite, a live oversized-stdin fail-open check, or the full suite. The four `approval-bridge.test.ts` failures are reported to also fail upstream; that baseline was not independently rerun during this validation.

prs.title: fix(state): classify a superseded schema receipt as a re-admission
prs.body:
Fixes #188935

## What Problem This Solves

A long-running worker turn could still be lost when another writer republished the agent database schema while the turn held its handle: the turn ended with "OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply" instead of replaying the transcript commit.

- Problem: `adoptAgentValidationSchema` threw a plain `Error("Agent schema admission changed before handle adoption; retry the operation")` when a worker re-adopted an open handle with a superseded receipt. The shipped replay owner `isReplayableWorkerTranscriptCommitError` only recognises `AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError`, so `worker.transcript.commit` answered `retryable: false` and the commit was never replayed.
- Solution: throw the existing `AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError` from that site, keeping the current message (the class constructor now takes an optional message; its published default is unchanged).
- What changed: `src/state/openclaw-agent-db-validation-schema.ts` (throw site) and `src/state/agent-database-admission-error.ts` (optional message), plus the raced-publication regression in `src/state/openclaw-agent-db-validation-cache.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: admission/receipt rules, schema checks, retry policy, and every other producer of this class — the default message and all existing call sites are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The condition is exactly what the class documents ("a receipt lost its publication race; fresh admission can obtain current proof"), and two shipped consumers already branch on the type: `isReplayableWorkerTranscriptCommitError` (worker transcript reuse) and `openclaw-agent-execution-native.ts` (maps it to `open-refused` instead of tearing down the whole agent owner). A plain `Error` silently fell through both.

- Best fix: yes — the owner already defines the signal; only the throw site was out of contract.
- Alternative: teaching the classifiers to match on message text — rejected; that would spread string matching across owners and miss future call sites.
- Risk / non-goals: the thrown error is now retryable by design, so a repeating admission race would surface as repeated replay warnings rather than a silent turn failure; that is the documented behaviour of this class.

## User Impact

A reply is delivered instead of being dropped when a background schema republication lands inside a long turn; the Gateway logs `worker transcript commit interrupted; reconnecting` and the worker replays the commit against fresh admission.

## Evidence

Reproduced on the latest `main` at the real throw site, then green with the fix. The regression drives the real cache/receipt owner (SQLite), revokes the admitted schema cell, and re-adopts the handle — the assertion that the thrown error is `AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError` fails on the base and passes with the fix:

```console
$ node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/state/openclaw-agent-db-validation-cache.test.ts
# base (assertion added, fix absent)
AssertionError: expected error to be instance of SchemaAdmissionChangedError
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 50 passed (51)

# with the fix
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  51 passed (51)
```

Why that type decides the turn's fate — the shipped classifier and its caller:

```text
src/gateway/worker-environments/transcript-commit-failure.ts
  error instanceof AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError  -> replayable
src/gateway/worker-environments/transcript-commit.kernel.ts:48
  openOpenClawAgentDatabase(...)  ->  openclaw-agent-db.ts:224  ->  adoptOpenClawAgentDatabaseSchema(opened, true, true)
src/gateway/server/ws-connection/worker-connection.ts:503
  replayable  -> "worker transcript commit interrupted; reconnecting" (replay)
  otherwise   -> UNAVAILABLE / retryable: false (turn lost)
```

Classifier and worker-path coverage on the same head:

```console
$ node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/worker/worker.transcript-failure.test.ts \
    src/gateway/worker-environments/transcript-commit.lazy.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```

`oxlint` (0 warnings / 0 errors), `run-format --check`, and a targeted `tsc --noEmit` over the changed files pass.

What was not tested: the original 54-minute memory-core/Feishu incident was not replayed end to end (the window needs a live republication during a long turn); the proof is at the owner/classifier boundary that the incident reported, plus the existing worker transcript-failure tests.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used source tracing across the admission cache, the transcript-commit kernel, and the worker replay classifier, plus a red/green regression against the real SQLite receipt owner. The implementer understands the code: a superseded receipt is re-admission, so the throw site must carry the type the replay owner recognises. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(oc-path): use last duplicate JSON key to match runtime parsing
prs.body:
Fixes #189835

## What Problem This Solves

For named duplicate keys in JSON, JSONC, and JSONL, `path resolve` and `find` select the first occurrence even though runtime parsing uses the last. `path set` can report success after changing only that shadowed first occurrence, leaving the effective configuration unchanged.

## User Impact

Named-key reads, searches, predicates, and replacements now use the effective last occurrence. Real edits preserve earlier shadowed copies and unrelated source bytes. Insertion beneath a duplicated parent remains safely refused rather than editing the wrong copy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use last-key selection in the existing AST resolver/finder. Share a last-effective `jsonc-parser` node walk between JSONC and JSONL editors so edits target the correct source token, while retaining range formatting and source-preservation owners. No new grammar, dependency, public API, schema, authority, or configuration option.

Both commits by @jerome-queck are preserved. The live head fetched for takeover already included `a4a0460bdb29`, addressing the review's P3 recovery text. Its guidance was retained and verified through actual human CLI output and a successful retry after preserving the effective parent value—not replaced with a wording policy.

The follow-up consolidates the standalone regression file into existing JSONC resolve/edit, JSONL edit, and finder fixtures. All existing assertions remain; fixture data now discriminates first-versus-effective duplicate selection. Tests remain net zero lines. Current main was merged without rewriting contributor history, retaining the YAML alias fix from #189784 alongside last-wins JSON addressing. The merged finder retains its AST-access budget and stays within the existing lint ceiling.

## Evidence

[Independent built CLI and actual-write proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189855#issuecomment-6550984265): secretless Linux Docker, Node 24.22.1, real files, independently built base/candidate CLI artifacts. In all three formats, main reads/finds1 twice and reports successful edits while runtime parsing still sees2. Candidate reads/finds2 twice and real `set ... 5` makes runtime parsing see5, retaining the earlier1. JSONC comments/formatting, JSONL BOM/CRLF/literal tokens, nested duplicate parents, predicates, and winning scalar shapes are checked.

No-duplicate controls produce identical bytes on both refs. Candidate duplicate-parent insertion refusal leaves the file unchanged and prints actionable `--human` recovery text. Consolidating that parent while retaining its effective value, then retrying, succeeds.

After merging main `85ae35910a6e6f903fbe885eda88e7e343c3e09d`, fresh builds and an additional main/candidate pair reproduce the same JSON/JSONC/JSONL contrast. A combined workspace proof interleaves YAML alias reads, actual duplicate-JSON writes, and YAML alias/cycle reads again: both refs retain two alias matches, scalar aliases, finite cycle traversal, and identical unchanged YAML bytes; only the candidate updates the runtime-effective JSON key. Candidate:153 passed across5 focused files, including YAML-kind coverage. Targeted lint and formatting pass. This is shipped CLI proof, not helper-only or dry-run-only edit evidence.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores first-occurrence behavior; no migration. Explicit `set` writes workspace files, so preserve normal backups/review practices. Blast radius is named JSON/JSONC/JSONL object addressing and source-token replacement. Positional object selectors still count source entries, including shadowed copies; their semantics are not changed here. Safe insertion refusal and ordinary-file behavior remain intact.
