prs.title: feat(knowledge): share person-scoped project knowledge between agents
prs.body:
<!-- openclaw:attribution=off -->

Related: #186066 (parent #186050; prerequisite #186065). Complements #188494 without duplicating its USER.md/bootstrap changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Proposes person-scoped project Knowledge sharing between two explicitly authorized agents without granting a scoped specialist an ungranted personal space.

## User Impact

With the documented restricted embedded-runtime profile, A and B can publish/read the same project record revision and evidence. Personal record bodies, IDs, titles, record counts, evidence, standing indexes and automatic-recall candidates remain outside the specialist’s enabled retrieval paths. Revocation is persisted and rechecked for warmed leases/references and after restart.

**Permission/upgrade proposal:** verified direct requesters now need an explicit person/agent grant rather than falling back to agent-private or conversation knowledge. Existing records are not migrated or reclassified automatically. Unprofiled legacy audiences keep their legacy partitions and cannot traverse person-space directories. This is a reviewable proposal, not a claim of upstream architecture acceptance.

**Required boundary:** the qualified profile allows exactly eight Knowledge record/evidence tools, disables automatic workspace bootstrap/code mode/tool search, and excludes raw filesystem/execution/admin/cross-session history and globally numbered Knowledge History/Recent/revision APIs. Those history sequence identifiers are not represented as private activity counts. Workspace-file import is excluded; person-bound `knowledge_attach_file` also refuses host-workspace reads. Broader tools, bootstrap inputs, providers and native harnesses require separate qualification. There is no OS tenant-isolation or erasure claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse host-minted memory audiences and live authority. The authority owner separately attests requester provenance: unattributed system execution derived from a session owner/creator cannot become a person binding. Genuine roots and validated continuations retain the fact; the existing private recovery snapshot preserves it without turning older/unclassified execution state into a requester.
- Reuse named agent-store membership and the Knowledge registry/publication lane. An operator-only grant selects one store-local space per `(profileId, agent)` against the current binding. No union search or model-controlled store/scope selector.
- Resolve tools, provider search/get/health/candidates, evidence and standing indexes through the restrictive principal. Reuse the scope-key owner for storage/index/receipt/evidence paths and include the partition in standing-index cache identity.
- Check the original administrator inside the registry SQLite transaction, after lock admission and immediately before a permission write; grant changes are compare-and-set.

Knowledge remains the durable record/evidence/publication owner; LosslessClaw remains the conversational-history/compaction owner. No private LCM database reads, new memory owner, SQL table/migration, runtime config option or paid service. No new UI grant controls or USER.md owner/selection changes. The author simplification pass retained one storage/publication owner and replaced duplicate directory selection with the existing scope-key helper. Necessary growth covers grant state, requester provenance and owning-boundary regressions; the separate test-line allocation does not raise the shared baseline.

## Evidence

- Published head: `28600ce5c6f03558773c4daebe4a953ba7bbaeb5`; source base: `fbb9bc44e8c60c2e756ddcdd9f859e8d123d4065`. Final 41-file source artifact: 107,164 bytes, SHA-256 `fc37ea7735df87df46a81ca319e373c3c6ed3b4353c53a0e3591720089f134e5`. Follow-up to previously reviewed `c3044466`: eight files, 23,883 bytes, SHA-256 `a3d7a41b6feab2169abbcd7c6219ccb52243c1ef5b9d35cff781df9bd1379571`. No merge or deployment.
- Genuine red → green for two follow-up defects: (1) native space publication previously returned a published receipt with Git pending / “Unsafe Git content path.” Canonical `spaces/<64 lowercase hex>/` now reaches normal Git completion; exact record/evidence/descriptor bytes and replay are checked, while malformed partitions, traversal and unsupported scopes remain denied. (2) a real registry worker committed revocation, then lost its reply and exited; a warmed provider incorrectly returned the old record on the original client. Worker loss/uncertain permission settlement now invalidates the cached snapshot and reconciles durable authority before further access.
- Final Git/recovery/person-auth consumer run: **66 tests in six files passed**, two Vitest shards, **507.27s wrapper**, including source-runtime preparation. Five Knowledge suites: person-project, git-history, stores, conversation-grants and maintenance. Real isolated Gateway cases: shared-owner **25.050s**, verified-person **23.091s**. The verified-person flow uses synthetic trusted-proxy authentication through the actual host profile producer and obtains distinct canonical P/Q identities with `users.self`. Q has its own identically named space grant and direct session; successful empty list/null record/empty grep and denied evidence reads distinguish partition isolation from a generic authentication failure. Outgoing deterministic model requests are checked for absence of P’s private/project sentinels.
- Both Gateway cases verify the same project ID/revision/hash/evidence across agents, **committed Git receipts**, excluded-tool execution denial, read-only and missing-grant parity through WebSocket and both HTTP endpoints, revocation, and persisted denial after the Gateway PID changes. This qualifies the documented restricted profile with deterministic model I/O—not a live identity provider or live inference.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized terminal evidence from the final Git/recovery consumer run</summary>

```text
PASS shared-owner … preserves revocation after a new Gateway process (25050ms)
PASS verified-person … preserves revocation after a new Gateway process (23091ms)
PASS space publications commit exact records and evidence and replay without another commit (89ms)
PASS Git rejects malformed space partitions and unsafe or unsupported content paths before initialization (4ms)
PASS fences old person authority when a committed revocation loses its registry reply (742ms)
PASS rechecks the original administrator at registry publication and rejects stale grant revisions (371ms)
Gateway shard: 1 file / 2 tests passed
Knowledge shard: 5 files / 64 tests passed
[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 507.27s
```

The committed tests contain the exact negative assertions and use synthetic data only. These excerpts omit ANSI formatting and lifecycle/build noise; they are not a live-provider capture.

</details>

- The subsequent hosted-review P3 diagnostic repair adds an actionable administrator recovery path using the existing operator-only `person_grants` / `person_grant` operations and documented page. No access rule changed. After that diagnostic-only change and binding the test’s original Worker event method, all **five native person tests passed again (53.97s wrapper)**. The Gateway evidence above precedes only those narrow diagnostic/test-cleanup deltas; it is not relabeled as a fresh whole-flow rerun.
- Original requester-provenance/recovery regression coverage remains applicable: owner-derived system authority cannot mint a requester profile; marked and older/unclassified recovery state stay distinct. The six-file authority/principal/worker/recovery/admitted-context/audience run passed **138 tests**; the corrected HTTP dependency/provenance suite passed **27 tests**, and **14 prefix-stability tests** passed. These are retained prior-head proofs for unchanged owners, not current-head CI.
- Fresh static gates passed after all follow-up edits: targeted production and changed-test tsgo leaves extending repository configurations; type-aware lint for six changed TypeScript files; formatting for seven follow-up code/docs files; staged test-lines ratchet; `git diff --check`. Measured net test growth/allocation: **1,142 lines**. The final Gateway consumer run rebuilt the source runtime; the earlier full build’s inherited nonfatal UI CSS-budget warning is not claimed fixed. Unchanged documentation link set was previously audited: 16,196 links, zero broken.
- Independent narrative review inspected all **39 files at c3044466** and found the now-fixed uncertain-revocation P2. A separate final six-file follow-up review traced Git publication/replay, snapshot recovery and authenticated P/Q boundaries, verified all six resulting file hashes, and found no remaining P0–P2 findings in that delta. A diagnostic-only follow-up independently verified the existing operator operations, authority and documentation target, with no P0–P2 findings. The final test method-binding lint cleanup and measured allocation adjustment are mechanical follow-ups. These reviews did not independently rerun the reported tests. Native Auto Review failed internally without a report: **no native-helper-clean or whole-current-head clean verdict is claimed**.
- Compatibility lane: five separate OS processes exercised production registry seed → grant → cold read → revoke → cold revoked read, preserving existing membership/conversation/maintenance/schema/manifest/operational bytes except additive person-grant metadata. This is a **candidate-created legacy-shaped fixture**, not stable-created data. Public latest `openclaw@2026.10.9` contains no Knowledge implementation across 14,109 archive paths; `@openclaw/knowledge` returns 404. Therefore a supported stable binary could not seed an existing Knowledge fixture. Stable→candidate upgrade remains **unqualified**, not waived or passed.

**Remaining / not claimed:** full installed Knowledge–LosslessClaw save/compact/restart prerequisite qualification (#186065; owned separately); live-provider inference; latest-stable upgrade; broader tools/bootstrap/native harnesses; current-head broad CI/security and required maintainer/identity/grant approval. The reviewed permission change is still a draft proposal, not upstream architecture acceptance or merge readiness.

Co-authored-by: TheAngryPit <7040636+TheAngryPit@users.noreply.github.com>

prs.title: fix(sandbox): resolve bundled channel in sandbox explain (companion to #189343)
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/51245 (partial: this fixes the `sandbox explain` diagnostic only; the live Telegram elevated-execution denial steipete kept open in that issue is not addressed here, so the issue should stay open).

Builds on #189343 by @nikolas-sapa. Their commit is cherry-picked unchanged with authorship kept; this PR adds the test change and Linux proof that ClawSweeper asked for on #189343. Credit for the fix goes to @nikolas-sapa. If #189343 lands instead, this can be closed.

## What Problem This Solves
`openclaw sandbox explain --session telegram:slash:<id>` reports `channel: (unknown)` and `allowedByConfig: false` when the CLI's plugin registry has no channel plugins (the sandbox-backends scope is empty for stock docker/podman configs), even with `tools.elevated.allowFrom.telegram` configured.

## User Impact
User impact: `openclaw sandbox explain` shows the right channel and `allowedByConfig: true` for telegram sessions on stock docker/podman setups, so elevated-tool allow lists can be checked without confusing `(unknown)` output.

## Why This Change Was Made
- Original fix (@nikolas-sapa, 4e58d9b): fall back to the static bundled channel catalog after the runtime registry misses, for both the stored-delivery and the parsed-key paths.
- Added here: the stored-delivery regression test now uses a session key with no channel (`agent:builder:main`), so only the stored delivery context supplies telegram. It now fails if the stored-delivery fallback is removed (it previously passed because the key also resolved telegram).

## Evidence
Setup: Linux, built CLI, isolated HOME.

Config: `{"tools":{"elevated":{"enabled":true,"allowFrom":{"telegram":["123456"]}}}}`

Before (main 88217c925; `sandbox-explain.ts` and `channels/registry.ts` are unchanged from there to base 43a3abe0595):
```
Elevated:
  enabled: true
  channel: (unknown)
  allowedByConfig: false
```
After (this branch 46de5b0c90f):
```
Elevated:
  enabled: true
  channel: telegram
  allowedByConfig: true
```
`--json` before/after: before `"allowedByConfig": false` (no `channel` field); after `"channel": "telegram", "allowedByConfig": true`

### Tests
- Red (fix reverted): `Tests  2 failed | 18 skipped (20) (exit 1)`, both tests fail
- Red (stored-delivery fallback only reverted): `Tests  1 failed | 1 passed | 18 skipped (20) (exit 1)`, the stored-delivery test fails
- Green (branch): `Tests  2 passed | 18 skipped (20) (exit 0)`; whole file: `Tests  20 passed (20) (exit 0)`
- oxlint exit 0, format check exit 0, check:test-mock-exports exit 0, git diff --check exit 0

prs.title: feat(backup): preserve source artifacts for internal captures
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Internal filesystem captures need to read SQLite state without changing the source WAL index or recovering rollback journals in place.

## User Impact

No new CLI flags or changes to ordinary backups. This adds the internal `createBackupArchive({ preserveSourceArtifacts: true, ... })` mode for isolated migration/checkpoint capture processes. Default backup sanitization and compaction, archive format, and PostgreSQL `online: true` capture remain unchanged.

The internal mode preserves row IDs by skipping compaction, so free-page bytes can remain in its archive. It still applies the existing row-level sanitizers and is not a secure-deletion export.

## Why This Change Was Made

The backup owner applies the existing artifact-preserving read scope during planning as well as private SQLite acquisition. Legacy audit reconciliation is refused before it can take a source write lease. Acquisition uses verified private images and preserves row IDs. No companion profile, anchor inventory, CLI, or quiescence API is included.

The hosted review's P2 fixture finding is repaired at the shared backup scratch owner: drain fixture state, retire idle state readers and the retained native broker, then remove the case directory. Failed custody settlement retains the directory. The regression starts cold with a short fixture prefix so a long-socket-path fallback cannot mask the deleted-socket failure. Production behavior is unchanged by this repair.

Extracted and adapted from [galiniliev's source commit](https://github.com/galiniliev/openclaw/commit/be31051c80993015e53a8ec4fc98e5e6c62e846e), with contributor credit retained.

## Evidence

### Changed preserving mode through the production CLI consumer

This is additional evidence for the **changed mode**, distinct from the ordinary CLI compatibility run below. The existing stacked consumer in [PR #189685](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189685) executed its built CLI while a disposable Gateway and PostgreSQL 17.11 were running:

```text

```

The original native command and terminal receipt, successful build log, clean build stamps, capture output, witness implementation and retained archive were independently inspected—not inferred from PR6's rating. Runtime source was `399a3cfc1ab391ae5c17b85350aa2b7c1aabde6e`; both build stamps and build-info identify it. The [comparison to integrated consumer head `9bbf226cf8db03c4ed0b96effc4143d296620c2a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/399a3cfc1ab391ae5c17b85350aa2b7c1aabde6e...9bbf226cf8db03c4ed0b96effc4143d296620c2a) changes only three test/support/allocation files, so the tested production inputs remain identical.

The two archive modules as a whole are **not** claimed identical: PR6 adds profile/anchor inventory and its own destination policy.

The retained 953,531-byte archive has SHA-256 `7f149851302acccaeef09415c98c367b534135db960240dd81dcb7e3929f259c`. Its unique manifest reports `local-companion`, one PostgreSQL anchor and zero export capsules; it contains both the shared-anchor and fixed-local credential SQLite images. A separate read-only audit extracted private copies and matched whole-row hashes/counts against the original capture-time witness: **2 device identities, 2 device tokens and 1 native exec socket credential**, with the same anchor store/engine/namespace. No credential values are published. Retained final-effect receipts additionally show offline verify/restore, a successful allowed protected RPC after activation, and rejection before effect of a client revoked after capture.

This qualifies actual production-consumer selection/acquisition and a usable archive. PR6's credential-retention policy is not attributed to PR4, which retains its existing sanitizers. The exact-base WAL/DELETE fingerprint, row-ID and sanitization oracles below remain the detailed preservation proof; this retained consumer run is not mislabeled as a new before/after WAL measurement. No new public API or service rerun was introduced for this evidence audit.

With the shared cleanup repair, both unchanged preservation assertions pass.

This covers config capture, archive streaming/publication, audit migration/restore and bounded retries, credentials, ownership, privacy, mixed engines, ordinary backup commands, atomic publication, restore/verification and SQLite hardlinks. No test timeout, assertion, skip, or baseline exception was weakened.
- **Final-effect preservation:** Both WAL and rollback-journal cases compare source SHA-256, device/inode, size, mtime/ctime and sidecar presence, then extract the real archive and independently check committed values, row ID 71 and cleared destination leases. prs.title: fix(boards): publish widgets with PostgreSQL storage
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Board widget publication fails when agent storage uses PostgreSQL because the write path tries to open a database connection on the Gateway main thread.

## User Impact

HTML widgets and native session reports can be created, updated, and reopened with PostgreSQL-backed agent storage. SQLite and incognito behavior remain covered. No schema migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing worker-owned V2 publication capability instead of borrowing a host database handle. Preserve current target/source checks, admitted-write completion, committed and unknown-outcome invalidation, and cleanup handling.

Port of [Galin Iliev's original fix](https://github.com/galiniliev/openclaw/commit/8d13b462e866ba582753b540a32c4458b3ead632), adapted to current main's fixture split and read-admission changes. Co-authored with @galiniliev.

## Evidence

Current published head: `3206710d8f3d4902e26dc53be7b6011dcbc4416b`.

- **Baseline failure:** the production `SqliteBoardStore` class from `f1c93577085244aa96aa87b53a2df9b59d293bd7`, with only relative import URLs relocated into a task-local proof module, successfully read an empty snapshot from isolated PostgreSQL 17.11, then failed at `putWidget` with “PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker.” No database owner or admission boundary was mocked. This is a production-class reproduction, not a claim that the committed Vitest test ran red on the base.
- **Storage regression coverage:** the supported PostgreSQL conformance harness passed **57 tests in 5 files**, including real PostgreSQL HTML creation/update, report publication, document reads, and cold reopen. Existing suites cover FIFO, revoked authority, uncertain outcomes, committed invalidation, cleanup failures, SQLite persistence, and incognito isolation. This remains valid after the comment-only mock repair; executable code did not change.
- **Actual built Gateway request proof at the current head:** a disposable named-profile Gateway running `dist/index.js` completed authenticated WebSocket `sessions.create`, `board.widget.put` for HTML creation and update, `board.widget.put` for a native session report, and an independent `board.get`. Board revisions were **1 → 2 → 3**, and the read returned revision **3** with both widgets and the report props. An independent PostgreSQL query confirmed the two committed rows, HTML widget revision **2**, and the updated HTML bytes rather than the original text. **1 test passed; command exit 0; fixture cleanup completed.** No Gateway handler, database owner, or request authority was mocked.
- **Source/runtime binding:** the official `prepare-vitest-runtime.mjs --require-current-head --with-ai-package` preparation completed successfully. Both build stamps reported the current head and clean inputs. The live Gateway hello reported build `2026.10.9-3206710d8f3d-2026-10-31T18-52-15.775Z`; its actual executable was the pinned OpenClaw Bun fork. Entrypoint SHA-256: `155c2b503eb8745655a881eee2c7d120f8fbd2ba95be2968fc754f8679cc2cb2`.
- **Isolation and cleanup:** all database data was synthetic in task-owned PostgreSQL 17.11 containers. The Gateway used fresh HOME/state/config and a named profile, with unrelated plugins, UI, and schedulers disabled. Its PID was absent after cleanup; the final PostgreSQL container and its volume were also verified absent. No live user database, shared installation, or service was modified. This proves the Gateway storage flow, not a browser presentation or model-inference flow.
- Targeted TypeScript, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. After the mechanical repair, the strict mock-export ratchet, focused outcome-test lint, and test-line budget passed again.

## Review and CI Disposition

- **Independent local review:** autoreview (Codex), P0–P2, against base `f1c93577085244aa96aa87b53a2df9b59d293bd7` and the complete candidate committed unchanged as `e4c6bdb7eae5bf1c77dca506a2ebb01acbb5df84`: **scoped-clean**, no accepted/actionable findings; final source verification completed. The reviewer assessed code and owner contracts; runtime evidence was obtained separately. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable, so the documented hosted fallback is used.
- **Hosted P2 addressed:** [the review history](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189564#issuecomment-6546576255) records the prior head's Silver rating and changed closed mock finding. Commit `48ec70a24910456992cb98f642abc2b54d6b2bc5` documents its deliberate outcome/close-failure isolation immediately above the mock, prunes the obsolete fingerprint, and adds exactly one allocation line. No replacement baseline exception or executable test/production change was introduced. The existing independent code review and runtime tests are reused for this mechanical repair. The current-head [baseline-ratchet CI job passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41228603879/job/124618295892).
- **Failed CI retained, with qualified inherited-owner attribution:** [run 41228603879, attempt 1, checks-node-changed-4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41228603879/job/124618296234) fails the trajectory runtime-store-writer rollback/retry case with “Session reader validation does not match its current physical owner” (14 passed, 1 failed). Its actual merge `3317467359b31be71a2a4687b5f6a3bea5fc44c8` has ordered parents main `a8d7e641984c0dc9e53c616c64747b66c0dab9c5` and this PR head. Eleven relevant source/dependency input trees match between that baseline and tested merge. Six scoped base/merge controls passed but did not reproduce the original failure; those passes alone are not an exemption.
- **Causal baseline qualification:** a separate diagnostic on that exact tested main base warmed the real trajectory-read API, held its next read at the existing admission boundary, renewed validation through its real owner, then released admission. Original production code failed with the same physical-owner error (**exit 1**, one selected case). Moving only the existing validation capture into the admitted callback—the owner correction already proposed in [#188055](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188055)—made **all seven reader-pool cases pass, exit 0**, including existing revoked-admission/lifecycle cases. No worker, read result, guard, or authority decision was mocked. Both diagnostic changes were restored; no unrelated repair is included here.
- **Attribution limit and landing route:** the maintainer workflow accepted the same-API/same-boundary baseline mechanism, unchanged relevant inputs, and absence of Board-path involvement as scoped inherited-owner attribution. The exact historical CI interleaving and failed predicate remain unobserved: this is **not** the original rollback test failing naturally on main, an automatic matching-case classification, a repaired failure, or green CI. The published classifier remains **unknown**. Native exact-head review and `github_pending` preparation completed without pushing or changing source, retaining `tests.result: fail` and the exact failed attempt. Landing still requires protected verification of the inherited-failure evidence, live writer capability, required reviews, and security. No CI rerun or merge was performed for this preparation.
- **Completed exact-head hosted review:** [ClawSweeper revision 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189564#issuecomment-6546576255), completed at 19:32 UTC on October 31, rated **overall readiness, proof confidence, and patch quality Platinum Hermit (4/6)** at `3206710d8f3d4902e26dc53be7b6011dcbc4416b`, with **no actionable findings**. It accepted the shipped Gateway proof and explicitly retained the then-unresolved CI disposition. This is not a claim of all-green CI.

<details>
<summary>Commands, proof costs, and retained artifact identities</summary>

Storage run:

`node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection <isolated-local-dsn> -- src/infra/database-engine/board-publication.postgres.test.ts src/boards/sqlite-board-store.outcomes.test.ts src/boards/sqlite-board-store.worker.test.ts src/boards/board-store.test.ts src/boards/session-actor-board-store.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

The combined storage harness completed in 1653.60 seconds, including cold compilation and final artifact verification. Touched-file case totals: outcomes 10.453 seconds / 5 cases; worker 91.814 seconds / 22 cases; PostgreSQL 40.801 seconds / 1 case.

Gateway proof used a task-local selection of the canonical E2E config and the real `createOpenClawTestInstance` / `GatewayClient` owners:

`OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=600000 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config .openclaw/tmp/gateway-proof/vitest.config.ts --configLoader runner --maxWorkers=1`

The prebuilt contract was selected only after successful exact-head preparation. The bounded no-output watchdog was extended for observed active cold compilation; Gateway startup remained bounded at 120 seconds. Existing proxy settings were preserved with loopback exceptions for this owned fixture. Setup-only failures were corrected before the passing request run and are not counted as product passes.

The Gateway case took 11.146 seconds; the complete Vitest run took 187.27 seconds, including compilation/transformation. Its completed native worker generation had 18,194 inputs and 23,125 outputs, and final generation verification completed.

Retained proof SHA-256 values:

- Fixture: `15f29d4e355350af24bb956b4bab3a4507e05b5ca20f939e68ba81248d7c2504`
- Result receipt: `51b22a45a2337cf7bbcfe1f3a0653621c68e0136baef5aeb50fcbb2c77a5db7f`
- Passing log: `41a1ed1763e06b15181bdf2109505aadd232360742a6b10adc9329430991c4f6`
- Causal baseline red log: `2309c3ba751adcc31fb7c581571e7764c0498883d2c1cfe5798d7168d769852f`
- Counterfactual green log: `5ad1fb7b70d73a268dbc124fb465522a3a69316ea7a8d9cf5a3ae8d0d47879f8`
- Native inherited-failure evidence: `32812c8d22cac7006d8495e757eeea259423e5881826a880e851088c77f095f5`

Simplification removes the host-handle wrapper: production code is net -11 lines. The dedicated allocation is **94 test lines**: 93 regression-test lines plus the justified mock-isolation comment. The shared test-line baseline is unchanged; the mock fingerprint baseline shrinks from 6442 to 6441 entries.

</details>

prs.title: feat(database): capture externally quiesced SQLite migrations
prs.body:
## Problem

An external controller that has already suspended a local Gateway cannot produce an exact SQLite migration capsule until it stops that Gateway. An existing filesystem archive cannot establish that a live suspension covers both the archive and exact database images.

## User Impact

Controllers can capture an already-suspended local Gateway without stopping it or transferring suspension ownership. The mode creates its own filesystem archive and exact SQLite images; restore remains restricted to a new private staging tree. Capsules contain private credentials and retained operational state and must be protected accordingly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing local-state, source-preserving archive, snapshot, and restoration owners. The bounded suspension adapter authenticates to the selected local backend, verifies physical owner/process identity and zero write custody, renews only the original controller suspension, and joins pending renewal during cleanup. It never resumes or stops the controller. Offline behavior stays unchanged; this slice introduces no schema or retention change.

Source preservation means capture does not write source database or journal files. The running Gateway continues its durable ownership-lease heartbeat; captured lease rows never confer activation authority.

This quiesced slice builds on merged #189793, #189638 and #189685. Main reconciliation source **bbca6deaf7c42e6357a0d7088523cee1f8673e65** merges the verified prerequisite squash **0f9e7f726a3e2d72ec7c68cf6e9f03b16e443950** without rewriting published history. Its introduced binary diff against main is byte-for-byte identical to the validated eight-file `23b25e002..77ee2ca896` product delta; no prerequisite implementation is duplicated. The three squash-history conflicts retained the published blobs only after verifying that each incoming blob equaled its already-integrated parent. Optional `preparedBase`, logical-export/nonempty-PostgreSQL-anchor refusals, absent-local-credential handling, and physical/suspension authority guards are preserved.

## Evidence

### Source-qualified validation and main reconciliation

- **Main composition independently reviewed through P2: scoped-clean.** Resolved/committed tree `a40ce7a6e601a808a253d4551b7a8061c3e1ce23`; the complete eight-file binary delta matches the prior validated patch. Relevant capture/restore, credential, Gateway authority, snapshot, schema and dependency owners are unchanged between the former parent and landed main; the inspected configuration-validation delta is comments only. Unrelated incoming main changes are retained, not represented as executed runtime equivalence. Existing proof below keeps its actual source binding; new-head CI is separate.
- **9/9 focused tests passed on integration source `2335c6a6bed1d65d4c7f5a02b8aee6dc62927547`:** quiesced WAL/rollback source preservation and all six offline capsule cases, including verified PostgreSQL-companion refusal and absent local credentials. WAL/rollback cases: 2.924s/2.610s; Vitest 25.08s; repository wrapper 150.78s including 121.455s worker preparation. Targeted production/test types, scoped lint, formatting and diff whitespace checks passed. These unchanged owner/input checks are reused, not relabeled as a new execution after the mechanical main merge.
- **Prior independent integration review through P2: scoped-clean.** The earlier production adaptation incorporated the parent's typed anchor refusal; quiescence owner and CLI remained unchanged. Actual hosted review is [Diamond 5/6, no findings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189802#issuecomment-6549909922) on `ba4e37203a7d35e3b23caa5102102be2d9de62e4`. The later `77ee2ca8967d7bd7fcf37a8bfa29e464341b4338` head passed full CI, Darwin and all applicable statuses. These remain prior-head results; no duplicate hosted request solely for mechanical ancestry reconciliation.
- **Validated complete runtime build:** `pnpm build:runtime`, 5m39s. Both build stamps identify clean source `2335c6a6bed1d65d4c7f5a02b8aee6dc62927547`. That executed runtime has shared-state schema 37 and agent schema 39; it is not claimed to be rebuilt from the later main-reconciliation commit.
- **Real offline dependency compatibility and final authority:** published v2026.10.9 initialized absent databases and persisted a session through its real CLI/Gateway. The tested Doctor/Gateway upgraded that data to schema 37, including the resource-receipt column. Two distinct real device clients performed protected `agents.files.set` writes; one was revoked before capture. With the Gateway stopped, ordinary backup → normal offline exact capsule → fresh staging restore → explicit disposable-tree promotion succeeded. Transported local identities and cached tokens were read through their owners. The promoted Gateway loaded the retained session; the allowed device performed a protected file write. The captured revoked device, and then the allowed device newly revoked against the promoted authority, were rejected before authenticated dispatch with exact file bytes/inode/size/mtime/ctime unchanged. Config bytes, selected settings and user file were preserved. **79.932s test; 100.01s repository wrapper; cleanup joined.** This is actual schema-37 execution on the source identified above. Exact SQLite restores its authority snapshot; this does not claim that post-capture source revocations survive rollback.

### Quiesced production proof retained

- Real Node Gateway/CLI: existing non-drain suspension → quiesced capture → exact staging restore → promoted local-credential admission, with original controller ownership retained. A genuine replacement suspension caused stale-ID capture to refuse before output. Test 134.539s; complete wrapper 215.44s.
- Actual controller resume and reassignment **during native acquisition** each caused capture to fail before the next filesystem archive and capsule manifest, leaving the Gateway running or the replacement controller still holding its suspension. Accepted read-only native work joins; the next acquisition phase and publication are refused, rather than claiming instantaneous revocation of every in-flight byte. Test 31.434s; wrapper 68.69s.
- Published v2026.10.9 → upgrade → quiesced capture/restore/activation preserved session data, configuration, user file and authentication (94.841s test; 103.09s wrapper).
- These three quiesced runs used the retained feature build before the final absent-local-credential guard and later schema-37 integration. The tested present-local path is unchanged by that guard; quiescence/CLI sources remain unchanged. The native consumer tests and separately rebuilt offline schema-37 flow qualify the changed dependencies. No new quiesced live-run claim is made for the integration build or later mechanical main merge.
- **Precise source-write attribution:** the first unconditional shared-WAL byte assertion failed. Idle-suspended control and capture each changed exactly one `state_leases` row—the same gateway-owner/global owner's expiry, heartbeat and update timestamps, with unchanged owner/payload/creation identity and five-minute TTL. Independent page inspection found only lease data page 41 and expiry-index page 43 changed out of 776. All other rows/schema, client database-family bytes/metadata and config bytes stayed unchanged. No blanket table ignore or disabled authority heartbeat.

### Tests, review and retained failures

- Original focused lease/native/offline coverage: 27 tests pass (188.40s wrapper). Independent autoreview of the full introduced slice through P2 was scoped-clean; simplification retains one capture owner and one borrowed-suspension scope.
- The hosted mock-export finding was repaired by documenting each necessary fixture isolation boundary immediately above its mock. No executable test/assertion change or mock-baseline expansion. Mock-export and test-line ratchets passed; both touched suites passed 23/23 (102.017s wrapper). The exact 446-line allocation covers distinct lifetime/refusal/native-preservation contracts, including four isolation-comment lines.
- Earlier startup attempts under host I/O pressure exceeded the unchanged 60s readiness deadline and were not counted as product proof. After the reviewed source was integrated and rebuilt, host I/O full pressure fell to 0.43% before execution. An early stable fixture stop hit its three-second cleanup deadline; the fixture now reaches the existing bounded ready suspension before normal stops so accepted work settles first. All three stops and final cleanup joined in the successful run. No readiness, cleanup, RPC, lease or heartbeat timeout/guard was increased or disabled. Original failures remain recorded; no product-code cleanup fix is claimed.

Sanitized final-effect excerpts:

```text
REVOCATION_PROOF resume next_archive_absent_manifest_absent_controller_untouched=PASS
REVOCATION_PROOF replace next_archive_absent_manifest_absent_controller_untouched=PASS
OFFLINE_PROOF upgraded_real_state_schema37_resource_receipt_column=PASS
OFFLINE_PROOF promoted_gateway_ready=PASS
OFFLINE_PROOF promoted_transported_allowed_client_protected_file_write=PASS
OFFLINE_PROOF promoted_precapture_revoked_client rejected_before_authenticated_dispatch_file_bytes_metadata_unchanged=PASS
OFFLINE_PROOF promoted_newly_revoked_client rejected_before_authenticated_dispatch_file_bytes_metadata_unchanged=PASS
OFFLINE_PROOF joined_cleanup=PASS
```

Worked on by @galiniliev.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL installations need local restart checkpoints without exporting and later rolling back their live database rows.

## User Impact

`openclaw backup create --local-companion --verify` captures local files, fixed-local credentials, and PostgreSQL anchors. Verification and staging restore work while PostgreSQL is offline; activation reconnects to the same stores/namespaces and current rows. `restore --local-companion` also works through `--from` and refuses ordinary archives before extraction.

**This is not disaster recovery.** All portable families must select PostgreSQL. Local files roll back; PostgreSQL rows do not. Stop the Gateway before activation, keep the matching database available, and do not run original/restored installations concurrently with the same credentials. Legacy-audit migration inputs and saved PostgreSQL export directories are refused. Source-preserving capture keeps row IDs and may retain free-page bytes; it is not a secure-deletion export. Ordinary backups retain exports, online capture, sanitization, and fresh-namespace recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The manifest profile/anchor inventory lets the existing verifier reject store/namespace mismatches, sidecars, and undeclared exports offline. Existing credential owners preserve fixed-local credentials and rebind them to the matching anchor. Generic acquisition remains owned by #189638, now landed on main as `f33e48e6720fe0b7b8ba2801096f532275cd08a5`. This PR targets main and contains only PR6 changes; the squashed dependency is not duplicated in its diff.

Adapted from [Galin's source commit](https://github.com/galiniliev/openclaw/commit/be31051c80993015e53a8ec4fc98e5e6c62e846e), with contributor credit retained. No externally-quiesced capture API, PostgreSQL import/rollback path, new production manager, or competing state owner is added.

## Evidence

### Main integration after PR4 landing

Merged pinned main `f33e48e6720fe0b7b8ba2801096f532275cd08a5` into the existing publication lineage after the stacked PR automatically retargeted to main. Resolved only six duplicate preservation-option hunks in two files, retaining the reviewed companion behavior. The main-targeted diff is exactly the 19 PR6 files, with no PR4-only test/support/allocation delta. `backup-create.ts` is byte-identical to the Diamond-reviewed version; snapshot planning retains main’s existing weak-owner-map allocation helper instead of the equivalent local helper.

Inspected relevant main authority changes: pairing wait-observation labels, worker-identity detection (not the operator client path), and an early refusal to issue a token for a missing paired device. Token verification/revocation and the companion credential-restore owner are unchanged. The original actual Gateway/PostgreSQL and stable-upgrade evidence remains bound to its recorded source, not relabeled as a new-head execution.

Affected gates: **66 tests passed in 7 files / 2 shards** (capture and ordinary controls, archive completeness, credential promotion, source aliases, pairing worker, weak-map contract); wrapper 133.64s, native preparation 71.00s. Core and infra test typechecks passed; targeted type-aware lint had zero warnings/errors; formatting and diff checks passed. Fresh independent P0–P2 autoreview of committed `f0d71193a94d178b486623b929b9b2a63ae3f7f4` against pinned main completed source verification with the full PR6 delta and 18 frozen owner contracts: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. It did not independently rerun tests or live PostgreSQL. New exact-head PR CI is required. No product scope or test-budget expansion was added for this integration.

### Integrated production CLI / Gateway / PostgreSQL

Built through the supported owner at exact source `399a3cfc1ab391ae5c17b85350aa2b7c1aabde6e`; all build stamps/build-info matched. The subsequent merge `6818508e3090855e6478358b3897f62f323ac4e4` changes exactly two inherited test/support files and their allocation. At Diamond-reviewed head `9bbf226cf8db03c4ed0b96effc4143d296620c2a`, all production inputs were byte-identical to that tested runtime. The later main integration is qualified separately above; no fresh live PostgreSQL run on the new head is claimed. PostgreSQL 17.11 ran only in a disposable task-owned container/database; no live user state or Gateway was touched. No model inference is claimed for this authentication/RPC boundary.

1. Two distinct clients authenticated with native device tokens and exercised protected device-pairing RPCs. The built CLI captured `backup create --local-companion --verify` while the Gateway ran: one matching PostgreSQL anchor, zero export capsules.
2. **After capture**, the admitted administrator used `device.token.revoke` on the second client and changed a real PostgreSQL-backed label to `current-after-capture`.
3. Stopped/joined Gateway and PostgreSQL; confirmed PostgreSQL connection refusal. Built CLI offline verify and `restore --local-companion` returned `ok:true`. Promoted only the task-owned restored tree, with both services stopped. Read-only whole-row hashes/counts matched for two native identities, two tokens, and one native exec socket credential; the PostgreSQL anchor matched exactly.
4. Restarted the **same database** and a new Gateway on the restored tree. The captured allowed token authenticated and completed a protected rename. The captured token revoked after capture was rejected with `AUTH_DEVICE_TOKEN_MISMATCH` during connection authentication, **before its attempted protected rename**. An independently admitted read proved the forbidden label was never written. The post-capture label survived activation; the store anchor and every non-system namespace matched. No PostgreSQL import, new namespace, or rollback occurred during companion restore.
5. Stopped/joined all task services. The expected negative authentication message is evidence, not a failed test.

After the supported SQLite → PostgreSQL port, that same released credential authenticated against PostgreSQL and read the retained setting.

## What Problem This Solves

Reverts our regression in #189810 (`e44b8f449184`), which broke eight node jobs in [scheduled full CI 41252475393](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41252475393) by applying conservative context admission to previously working turns.

## User Impact

Restores the opt-in context-pressure checks and earlier overflow recovery behavior. This explicitly re-accepts the earlier risk that long tool turns can overflow with `midTurnPrecheck` disabled. That risk needs a fresh forward fix later.

## Why This Change Was Made

This urgent rollback is a clean inverse of our own change, restoring runtime behavior, consumer expectations, and configuration documentation together. No fixture budgets, assertions, retries, or baselines are weakened. Related #189888 adjusts fixtures while retaining the admission policy; this rollback deliberately withdraws that policy.

## Evidence

- Before the revert, real Gateway child-result cases fail 2/2 and the prompt-cache Responses case fails at first-turn completion. After the revert, all 49 named failure tests and 216 touched consumer tests pass; prompt-prefix stability also passes 14/14.
- Rebased onto fresh main `f121a7f70da4`; the patch is unchanged and all 18 reverted file blobs match the parent of `e44b8f449184`. Fresh-head focused rerun passes 279/279 across 21 files: all 49 named failure tests, 216 touched consumers, and 14 prompt-prefix stability cases (four Vitest shards, 887.08s including preparation).
- Parent validation: two scoped typechecks, scoped lint/format, generated configuration documentation, test-line ratchet, and diff checks pass.
- Local Codex autoreview, P0–P2, `c633ec6376e1..f365b8b5431a`: scoped-clean, no findings. It reviewed the complete inverse with unchanged-source context limitations and did not execute tests. The rebase is patch-identical; source inspection and boundary tests supply separate evidence.
- Four unrelated, pre-existing native-auth fixture failures occur before compaction in `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts`, in the cases preserving **explicit native OpenAI**, **default native OpenAI**, **default OpenAI with an unavailable selected profile**, and **API-key OpenAI** compaction ownership before the first attempt. All fail because shared auth store ownership is not prepared at `setRuntimeAuthProfileStoreSnapshot`. A representative failure reproduces before the revert with #189810 still present; relevant auth sources are unchanged. The two restored overflow-copy cases pass. This is an auth-fixture setup gap, not a claimed passing full E2E suite.

Simplify pass: one clean inverse, no new owner, wrapper, state, dependencies, or configuration. Broad proof comes from exact-head PR CI.

prs.title: improve: show gateway commit and build time on About
prs.body:
Original author: Chris Eckert (@ceckert). This is his #180353, rebased onto current `main` so it can land; that branch's managed workspace became unusable during its base refresh, so it could not be updated in place. The branch carries his `Co-authored-by` trailer, so the squash commit credits him.

## What Problem This Solves

Members can see the connected Gateway version but cannot identify its running commit or build time when diagnosing a possibly stale deployment.

## User Impact

Settings → About shows the Control UI and the connected Gateway as two separate sections, each listing version, commit (with copy) and UTC build time; the Control UI section also shows its branch. A member can tell whether the Gateway they are connected to includes a fix without assuming the browser bundle matches it. Missing provenance is omitted; a disconnected Gateway shows its version as unavailable. Host diagnostics and update operations remain restricted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing authenticated hello payload and About page rather than adding another version endpoint or screen. The Gateway reports `server.commit` and `server.builtAt` from the build provenance it captures once at startup, so a later checkout change does not relabel the running Gateway. No changes to `system.info` or `update.status` authorization.

The UI adds no new CSS. Both builds render with the existing Settings facts grid (`.settings-kv`) and the shared `CopyButton`, replacing About's bespoke copy state machine and its styles. `about.css` shrinks versus `main` (6,235 → 4,962 bytes), so the Control UI CSS budget check, which allows no growth while `main` is over its cap, passes.

Rebase notes (relative to #180353): `main` now owns build provenance in `readBuildProvenanceForModuleUrl`, so the Gateway build time is read from that record (`resolveRuntimeServiceBuiltAt`, normalized to ISO, unparseable values omitted) instead of a second build-info reader. About strings live in the deferred `en-about` catalog, and the hero keeps `main`'s Support link. The mocked Gateway carries commit and build time through `main`'s `control-ui-mock-scenario` module.

## Evidence

- Real Gateway handshake (in-process Gateway server, real WebSocket connect, device paired with member scopes `operator.sessions.read`/`operator.sessions.write`, production-shaped `build-info.json`): hello returned `server.commit` (short SHA) and `server.builtAt: "2026-10-30T21:00:00.000Z"`; `system.info` → `missing scope: operator.read`, `update.status` → `missing scope: operator.admin`. This closes the "isolated real Gateway/member handshake" gap listed on #180353.
- Unit: About view/page tests (both sections' facts, copy controls, localized UTC build time, omitted facts and unavailable Gateway), `connect-hello.update-scope` (member hello carries commit/builtAt, update details still omitted) and `version` tests pass.
- Browser (Playwright Chromium, production bundle, mocked Gateway, member scopes): `about.e2e` (both sections' facts, Gateway commit copy, zero `system.info`/`update.status` requests, no horizontal overflow at 375px) and `build-info-unicode.e2e` pass on the current head after merging `main`.
- Current head: UI typecheck, formatting and the line-cap ratchet pass.
- Local autoreview (Codex, `gpt-6.1-sol`, P1) on the earlier rail layout: scoped-clean, no findings. Not rerun on the reuse-only layout.

### Screenshots

Production-bundle captures of the reuse-only layout (desktop, 390px, dark) were inspected in the landing session: both sections render with the standard Settings card and facts grid, and the copy button takes the Settings 44px touch size on mobile. They are not embedded here because this publication route cannot upload images; the earlier rail screenshots from #180353 no longer match and were removed.

Contributor credit: Chris Eckert (@ceckert) authored this change: he identified the member-access gap and requested extending the existing About page. Design review: Vyctor Brzezowski (@vyctorbrzezowski).

prs.title: fix: keep encrypted reasoning replay stable after local session reloads
prs.body:
Fixes #167768

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a local Responses session changes the replayed bytes of an encrypted reasoning item when it is reopened after an in-turn tool continuation.

## User Impact

User impact: encrypted reasoning items use the same signature bytes during the first tool continuation and after session reconstruction. Visible thinking, ciphertext, IDs, status, live tool arguments, and previously approved history retain their existing behavior. No configuration change or migration is required.

Risk: fresh signatures carrying non-empty `encrypted_content` now take the stored form on the in-turn continuation, as node turns and reopened sessions already do. Their summaries and plaintext content are dropped from the replay signature. Items without a non-empty string in `encrypted_content` retain today's in-turn behavior, including plaintext content; storage still canonicalizes them on reload. Provider acceptance and cache statistics were not measured on a real provider. Better prefix reuse is an expected consequence for caches sensitive to replayed input, not a measured result.

## Why This Change Was Made

The local completion boundary now calls the existing transcript signature sanitizer before persistence for fresh signatures carrying non-empty `encrypted_content`. The sanitizer retains ownership of route eligibility, validation, and canonical bytes. Only blocks whose signatures change are copied.

This extends the byte-consistency approach in [#164287](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164287) to local sessions, with a narrower entry condition to avoid newly dropping plaintext-only reasoning during a turn. It does not change the sanitizer or rewrite stored history.

## Evidence

- Synthetic local-session tests cover one Responses route with distinct encrypted and plaintext-only (`encrypted_content: null`) cases. On main `f5e306d4fe0a1d2c2b844ea034c5341e7a97fb4e`, the encrypted case fails on raw versus canonical signature bytes; the plaintext-only case passes. The fix passes both cases and checks visible thinking, ciphertext, IDs, status, live tool arguments, unchanged history, and reconstructed-session replay.
- Focused command: `pnpm test src/agents/sessions/agent-session-reasoning-replay.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Baseline: 1 failed, 1 passed, 10.10 s wall. Fixed: 2 passed, 20.96 s wall, 0.371 s test time, including compiled-worker preparation. The plaintext-with-null case also fails with the prior presence-only guard and passes with the non-empty-string guard.
- Affected suites: 77 tests pass across 6 files, 57.95 s command wall time: reasoning replay (2), loop correctness (27), Responses EOF (27), code-mode source (16), transcript worker (3), and reasoning redaction (2).
- Touched-file formatting and typed lint, core types and all 27 core-test type graphs, docs MDX sanity, unused-export scans, and the remaining changed-file guards pass.
- No provider requests were made.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): show no preview instead of an error for local browser tabs
prs.body:
Closes #184828

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a local or private browser-tab URL fails its link preview with an invalid-request error instead of showing no preview.

## User Impact

Browser-tab cards for local and private addresses now show no preview instead of an RPC error. Public previews are unchanged, excluded addresses are never fetched, and other `controlUi.linkPreview` callers keep the existing `INVALID_REQUEST` response.

## Why This Change Was Made

The preview parser correctly rejects local/private targets from public fetching, but the handler mapped that rejection to a malformed-request error. The browser-tab card now opts into `allowUnavailable`, so those targets return an empty successful preview. The default RPC contract is unchanged: malformed input, credential-bearing URLs, and unavailable targets without the opt-in still return `INVALID_REQUEST`.

The opt-in is part of the shared preview cache identity, so a default hover cannot satisfy an opted-in browser card (or vice versa). The actual URL stays separate in the request.

This is the caller-scoped version of the issue's accepted "empty success" or "suppress in the browser-card client" outcomes. It avoids changing the response contract for every caller.

## Evidence

Running Gateway RPC on the current head, default config in an isolated state directory:

```
default local/private -> INVALID_REQUEST (unchanged)
allowUnavailable local -> {}
local listener hit count after allowed call = 0
allowUnavailable private IP -> {}
allowUnavailable public -> {"title":"Example Domain"}
allowUnavailable malformed -> INVALID_REQUEST
allowUnavailable: "yes" -> INVALID_REQUEST
```

The local listener counted its own requests: a direct self-test recorded 1 hit, and the allowed local preview recorded 0.

Control UI browser card, real Chromium against the built UI. The transcript is a fixture so the test reaches the card without an agent turn; the preview RPC is forwarded to an isolated real Gateway:

```
Browser card renders http://127.0.0.1:8080/ with no error.
Request captured from the built card:
{
  "request": {
    "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/",
    "allowUnavailable": true
  },
  "response": {}
}
```

prs.title: fix: local and private link previews fail instead of showing no preview
prs.body:
Closes #184828

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Control UI browser-tab card gets an `INVALID_REQUEST` error instead of a quiet "no preview" when the tab URL is a loopback, LAN, or otherwise unpublishable address.

## User Impact

User impact: local and private browser-tab cards render without preview metadata instead of surfacing a request error. Nothing new becomes fetchable, and malformed arguments are still errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The preview parser answered two different questions with the same `null`: "is this a well-formed anonymous http(s) URL?" and "is this destination allowed for a public preview?". The RPC handler could only read that as malformed input.

Input validity now lives in `parseControlUiLinkPreviewInput`, and destination eligibility in `isControlUiLinkPreviewEligible`. `parseControlUiLinkPreviewUrl` composes both, so every existing caller keeps the same behavior with no change in meaning: the per-hop redirect dispatcher and the declared social-image/icon selection still filter on eligibility instead of hoping the later fetch fails. The handler uses the input parser, then reports an ineligible target as empty metadata. Malformed params still fail with `INVALID_REQUEST`. No fetch, cache, or redirect policy changed.

This does revise one recorded response: a well-formed but unpublishable URL used to answer `INVALID_REQUEST` and now answers `{}`, which is the behavior the linked report asks for and the same empty-success path the handler already uses when previews are disabled. That response-contract change is the one item flagged as needing a preview-owner decision; ClawSweeper's own recommendation is to approve it.

## Evidence

Live Gateway from this head (isolated state dir, loopback port, token auth), with a logging HTTP server on `127.0.0.1:8099` that records any request it receives:

```
controlUi.linkPreview {"url":"http://127.0.0.1:8099/"}   -> {}
controlUi.linkPreview {"url":"http://192.168.1.10/"}      -> {}
controlUi.linkPreview {"url":"http://10.0.0.5/"}          -> {}
controlUi.linkPreview {"url":"https://example.com/"}      -> {"title":"Example Domain"}
controlUi.linkPreview {"url":"javascript:alert(1)"}       -> INVALID_REQUEST "invalid controlUi.linkPreview params"
controlUi.linkPreview {"url":"https://public.example",
                       "token":"not-forwarded"}           -> INVALID_REQUEST "invalid controlUi.linkPreview params"

requests recorded by the 127.0.0.1:8099 listener: 0
```

Tests:

```
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-projects.mts \
  src/gateway/control-ui-link-preview.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/control-ui.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  78 passed (78)
  Duration  30.29s
```

Red on base: reverting only the two source files to the merge base, five new handler cases fail; with the patch they pass. The existing parser coverage is unchanged: `http://[::1]`, `https://metadata.google.internal/`, and `https://8.8.8.8/` are still rejected by `parseControlUiLinkPreviewUrl`, which is the predicate the redirect and metadata-selection paths call.

Typecheck `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` (exit 0); lint and format clean on the changed files.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Outbound staging tests fabricated loaded media and saved files, then checked collaborator arguments instead of the resulting attachment. Their trusted-HTML success case also duplicated the real provenance suite.

## User Impact

No runtime or user-visible change. The tests now check real temporary files while retaining filename, MIME, byte-limit, provenance-failure cleanup, and publication-authority contracts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the three module mocks and their fabricated media fixtures. Keep trusted-HTML success, reload, and pruning coverage in the existing provenance worker suite; exercise the remaining staging contracts through the real loader and store. Remove only the two corresponding obsolete mock-factory baseline entries.

The preserved contracts originated in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90579 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158567. This is part of the maintainer-requested test audit, not a production repair.

## Evidence

- Frozen-base baseline: 55 tests passed across outbound staging, HTML provenance, media publication authority, and message-action media handling.
- Candidate: 54 tests passed across the same four files and shard order. The one removed case is the duplicated mocked HTML-success check.
- Temporary negative controls caught lost URL/buffer filenames, leaked staged HTML, and omitted publication guards in all four replacement cases. The unchanged provenance keeper also rejected reload after marker creation was disabled. Production source was restored byte-for-byte.
- The final lint correction adds an exact-once assertion for the injected provenance failure; that affected case passed again.
- Targeted lint, format, messaging test typecheck, mock-factory ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent preservation review and final correction review found no actionable P0-P2 issues.
- Test source: 104 to 97 lines; two obsolete baseline entries removed; no production changes.
- All required dead-code scans passed on the exact pushed head: dependencies, unused files, and exports, including their full-tree phases.

## CI Qualification

Run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40373977329, attempt 1, reports an inherited `check-test-types-core-2` failure: `reply-agent-turn-preparation.test.ts:646` passes a partial operation fixture to the typed `providedReplyOperation` option (TS2345). That case was added on main by `bd6807a336d65b22e65fb99643d7761d1ff9e3fc`, after this branch's frozen base.

The observed CI checkout is `d7440f719478c2fa8245fa1c5191a1f7b54dc275`, merging exact PR head `5670bcb6ca6c742aba4bdda3240b5dae7e4619e4` into baseline `e923309c2978268898f7b57a11879fdfa174ca38`. The failing fixture, production contract, typecheck configuration, workflow, and dependency inputs are unchanged between that baseline and tested merge. This PR's only changes are the two files described above; its frozen-source messaging typecheck passed.

The completed attempt has 29 successful jobs, 29 skipped jobs, and two failures: that typecheck and its aggregate CI gate. Independent `security-fast` passed. CI labels the error `new` against scheduled main run `40360902790`, which started at 16:37 UTC on October 26, before the failing case landed on main at 17:49 UTC. That older source has no `providedReplyOperation` test call. The attribution here instead uses the actual tested merge's newer main baseline and identical failure inputs; it does not claim matching-signature baseline evidence.

Agents can ask structured `ask_user` questions, but a multi-question or multi-select prompt could become a text list in Telegram, and the Control UI did not keep each answer visible in the conversation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The agent prompt, Telegram adapter, Control UI, and Gateway now carry the same structured question and draft-answer state. Telegram callbacks resolve by question index and session authority; Gateway revisions and terminal outcomes prevent replay from continuing the run twice. Existing approval controls remain separate.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto upstream `main` (base `974186dee30`); the branch has only nine question-related commits. No production deployment.
- Focused tests on Linux/Node 24.22.1: 147/147 passed across Gateway support, TUI, Control UI, and Telegram after the type fixes. prs.title: chore(plugins): cover unused URL expressions in plugin source capture
prs.body:
Related: #182125, #182194, #182403, #184340

## What Problem This Solves

The plugin source-capture rule that fixed a Gateway stall during model-change plugin reloads (#182194) no longer has any test. #182403 deleted its regression together with the bundled-reload module, and #184340 then removed this suite's only `visitPluginSourceReferences` assertion. The rule itself still guards external plugin source capture.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. A regression of the #182194 fix would again fail CI here instead of resurfacing as a Linux Bun teardown hang in `server.config-patch.test.ts`.

## Why This Change Was Made

#182125's only red job was a Bun no-output timeout in `openclaw.changes.list preserves an approved include-only operation without a duplicate write`, and its Testbox A/B classified the hang as pre-existing. I traced it to the cause, and the runtime fix was already on `main`:

- **What hangs:** `server.close()` waits in `restart.close.config-reloader`. `configReloader.stop()` joins an in-flight plugin reload. The test's in-process `set-default-model` write changes `agents.defaults.model` and `plugins.entries.openai`, which plans `reloadPlugins`. Before #182194, source capture treated the generated codec's unused `new URL(".", _scriptName).href` as an asset reference and recursively captured the host build. The reload made no progress until the prepared-model catalog watchdog fired (`Catalog preparation stalled after 180000 ms without progress`), which matches the 180 s hook timeout. Capture visits source references eagerly only under Bun, which is why this was Bun-only.
- **Why the A/B blamed `main`:** #182125's head and its A/B were based on `f04709b78a04`, about 2.5 hours before #182194 landed (`647d7d02d648`). Swapping only `config-reload.ts` kept the pre-fix capture code on both sides.
- **What this PR adds:** one unit test at the owner, `visitPluginSourceReferences`. It asserts that a used `new URL(...)` asset is reported, that discarded `new URL(...)` and `.href` calculations are not, and that a discarded URL's arguments are still traced. There is no production change.

A first attempt asserted through `inspectPluginSourceDependencies`. It passes even without the fix, because inspection does not turn `asset` references into captures. The visitor is the narrowest place where the rule is observable.

## Evidence

All Testbox runs used Blacksmith Linux x64 (nproc 4), the pinned Bun fork, and `CI=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.config-patch.test.ts -t "openclaw.changes.list preserves"`. Several runs were looped on one lease, because later runs on a lease hit the hang most often. Older commits were checked out inside the lease with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.

| Code under test | Bun runs | Result | Run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `f04709b78a04` (#182125 merge base) | 4 | 3 hung at `server.close` (`restart.close.config-reloader` pending) | [40282221072](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40282221072) |
| same, old code + current Bun pin | 4 | 3 hung (the fix is not in Bun) | [40283674588](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40283674588) |
| same, with restart tracing | 3 | 3 hung; log shows the catalog stall above | [40285482781](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40285482781) |
| `e29f83774f4a` (parent of #182194) | 4 | 3 hung | [40287902035](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40287902035) |
| `647d7d02d648` (#182194) | 4 | 4 passed | [40287686714](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40287686714) |
| `f04709b78a04` + only #182194's `plugin-source-references.ts` change | 4 | 4 passed | [40287880434](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40287880434) |
| `main` `7cadcedb8377` | 8 | 8 passed | [40279893784](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40279893784), [40280936082](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40280936082) |

A bisect over the 1,640 first-parent commits between `f04709b78a04` and `7cadcedb8377` narrowed the first good commit to #182194.

prs.title: fix(ai): send max_tokens on Model Studio compatible-mode endpoints
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Model Studio compatible-mode requests (`qwen`, `qwencloud`, `modelstudio`, `dashscope`, `qwen-token-plan`, and `bailian-token-plan`) send the output cap as `max_completion_tokens`. Alibaba's OpenAI-compatibility reference documents `max_tokens` for that surface and does not list `max_completion_tokens`, so the configured cap can be ignored or the request can be rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveOpenAICompletionsCompatDefaults` already treats this family as Model Studio for other flags, but `usesMaxTokens` omitted it and fell through to the OpenAI field. The fix adds that family only when the base URL is an Alibaba compatible-mode host (`*.dashscope*.aliyuncs.com` or `*.maas.aliyuncs.com` with a `/compatible-mode/` path).

Coding Plan hosts stay on `max_completion_tokens`. That surface shares the `modelstudio-native` endpoint class, and the cited reference does not cover it. Explicit `model.compat.maxTokensField` still wins. OpenAI and the other vendors that already select `max_tokens` or `max_completion_tokens` are unchanged. Unrelated `/compatible-mode/` proxy URLs are unchanged.

## User Impact

Compatible-mode Model Studio calls now send the configured output budget as `max_tokens`. A budget stored as `params.max_completion_tokens` is still honored; only the wire field changes. Coding Plan, OpenAI, and other providers keep their current field. No config migration is required.

## Evidence

On head `ecdd7b81ce7a9740b097340d0b336fb64134040c` (rebased onto current `upstream/main`):

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/ai/src/transports/openai-completions-params.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.compat.test.ts packages/ai/src/transports/openai-completions-transport.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests  81 passed (81)
```

Live transport proof did not call Model Studio, OpenAI, or Coding Plan. A local HTTP server on `127.0.0.1` received the raw POST body from `streamOpenAICompletionsRequest` in managed mode. Host classification came from `resolveProviderRequestCapabilities` (plugin metadata). The fetch hook refused every hostname except the three proof hosts and forwarded only the request body to that local server. No provider key was read or sent.

1. Model Studio compatible-mode (`qwen`, `https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1`, classified `modelstudio-native` / `modelstudio`) sent `max_tokens` and not `max_completion_tokens`.
2. OpenAI (`openai`, `https://api.openai.com/v1`, classified `openai-public` / `openai-family`) sent `max_completion_tokens`.
3. Coding Plan (`qwen`, `https://coding.dashscope.aliyuncs.com/v1`, classified `modelstudio-native` / `modelstudio`) sent `max_completion_tokens`.

Supersedes #168513, thanks @synthalorian.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes ignored or rejected output limits when Alibaba Model Studio is used through its OpenAI-compatible `/compatible-mode/v1` endpoint: OpenClaw sends the budget as the undocumented `max_completion_tokens` rather than the documented `max_tokens`.

## User Impact

Configured output budgets now use `max_tokens` on Alibaba compatible-mode endpoints. Coding Plan, OpenAI, unrelated proxies, and explicit `compat.maxTokensField` overrides retain their behavior. No configuration migration or operator action is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing shared `maxTokensField` compatibility flag, scoped to Model Studio's Alibaba hosts and compatible-mode path, following [Alibaba's API reference](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/compatibility-of-openai-with-dashscope). No transport or token-budget code path is added. The assertion-safety baseline is reduced from 2 to 1 for the removed redundant cast.

Production delta: +5/-4, net +1 line. Removing redundant validation/casting of already typed compatibility data offsets most of the host/path selection. The original host-normalized attribution behavior is preserved. Tests: +41 lines; the separate 41-line allocation covers the serialized-request regression and two existing budget expectations.

## Evidence

- Base `ac8d31250fed1d3745d968014598317c70592f60`: the new production-transport request capture fails for four Alibaba compatible-mode endpoints because `max_tokens` is absent; OpenAI, Coding Plan, and proxy controls pass (4 failed, 16 passed; wrapper 3.04s).
- Fixed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/ai/src/transports/openai-completions-transport.test.ts packages/ai/src/transports/openai-completions-params.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.compat.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: all 96 tests pass. AI files: 0.95s; prefix file: 63.91s including compilation; wrapper total: 67.41s.
- Focused typecheck (three touched TypeScript files using the repository's test-shard declarations), scoped oxlint, oxfmt, assertion-safety ratchet, and `git diff --check` pass. Broad proof is delegated to this PR's CI.
- Local autoreview of final committed range `ac8d31250fed..9e80a6909db1`: Codex, P0–P2, `scoped-clean`, no findings.
- Proof captures the final serialized production-transport request with synthetic credentials. It does not demonstrate vendor-side enforcement; no paid provider call was made. Contributor code was read only with `gh pr view/diff`, and was never checked out or executed on this host.

CI initially found the missing assertion-baseline shrink; that mechanical correction is now committed. The separate prompt-cache shard failure is inherited: all four cases in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.prompt-cache.test.ts` reproduce on unchanged main `ac8d31250fed`, failing at line 460 with `turn 1 completed: expected false to be true` (196.09s wrapper). [Current-head CI run 41254468972](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41254468972) has finished every job: the assertion ratchet, security-fast, and all other workloads passed or were skipped. The only root failure is the same four inherited prompt-cache cases ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41254468972/job/124694925279)); the aggregate CI gate is red because of that root. These remain failed evidence, qualified for the native inherited-failure landing exception.
