prs.title: fix(codex): preserve native continuation and yield acknowledgements
prs.body:
Related: #167410 (not a claim to close all reported timeouts).

## What Problem This Solves

Preserve a managed native parent's saved tool declarations while its last terminal child's completion is still awaiting delivery. This fixes a distinct gap after execution protection correctly ends: rebuilding the catalog for the completion turn could rotate the parent thread and make a follow-up to its original child fail lineage validation.

The PR also retains the original delayed-completion authority regression. Current main already owns that async-lifetime behavior; no stable-only lifetime patch is added to main.

## Reproduction and scope

A packaged Gateway + packaged native Codex test on the prior PR head completed two ordinary turns on one child, then genuinely yielded while the third result was pending. Automatic delivery resumed with a changed tool catalog, started a second native parent, and the original-child follow-up failed lineage checks. The provider was deterministic local scripted Responses, not a real model or OAuth acceptance test.

The new regression exercises the real harness lifecycle with a nonempty native tool catalog, holds terminal-child delivery after the execution pin releases, and admits the completion with no current executors. With only the catalog owner restored to the prior implementation, it fails with two native thread starts instead of one. With the repair, it preserves the original parent and rejects execution of the old tool.

## Follow-up: preserve terminal yield acknowledgements

A fresh live run on the separate stable candidate completed five original-child turns and automatically resumed all three delayed results, but two yield acknowledgements became `aborted by user`. It was not counted as a full acceptance pass.

The native dynamic-tool `item/completed` event precedes the handler's return. Interrupting at that point can replace the model-visible result with cancellation, even after OpenClaw has recorded terminal release. Waiting a JavaScript event-loop tick does not establish native output commitment.

The lifecycle owner now waits for matching `rawResponseItem/completed` function/custom output receipts in its existing model-response inventory. These prove recording in native model history before interruption. Nested Code Mode waits for the outer output; web/image calls are not incorrectly required to emit function outputs. No new protocol, timer, persisted state, or authority relaxation is introduced.

## Ownership and safety

- Read pending-delivery custody from the existing completion owner; no new custody registry or persistent state.
- Require the same physical native client, current assignment/history ownership, and the existing claimed delivery owner.
- Recheck catalog eligibility after reading native metadata.
- Keep execution pins released at terminal completion; never restore old executors.
- Release declaration eligibility when delivery settles, is abandoned, or loses custody.
- Share the existing child-execution predicate between its two monitor consumers; the oversized monitor file shrinks.

## Evidence — CI repair rebase, 2026-10-29

Source: `22540643f20c845ff5fea04408b89549d8448bbb`, rebased onto pinned main `02e19a39282d6af1cc93e01d7045681d0124b433`. All four PR commits are patch-identical to the previous series (`git range-diff` reports `=` for each); no continuation behavior or test assertion was changed in this refresh.

The previously failing `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` job reported 14 mock-export sites in two upstream Gateway tests. This base includes [upstream repair #187120](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187120) (`e25c026eb75`): justified whole-module isolation annotations for shutdown/startup tests and corresponding stale-baseline cleanup. The two red `openclaw/ci-gate` entries reflected that same underlying failure. All three PostgreSQL jobs on the previous head ultimately passed.

Current-head local validation in secretless Docker:

- Mock-export guard against pinned base: passed, 15.92 s.
- Focused continuation, native yield-output, same-child custody, Gateway shutdown/spawn-broker, and test-plan tests: 226 successful executions across 14 files, 413.22 s wrapper wall (the 54 configuration cases execute on both test runtimes).
- Production plugin types: passed, 25.40 s; scoped test types: passed, 16.18 s.
- Targeted type-aware lint with pinned runtime parity: passed, 216.57 s; formatting: passed, 0.47 s.
- Pinned-base line-cap and test-line budget: passed, 1.43 s and 4.65 s. No check or baseline was weakened by this PR.
- Independent native GPT-6-Sol source/rebase review of the full 15-file range `02e19a3..2254064`: no actionable P0–P2 findings. This is a source review, not CLI autoreview or live acceptance. Working tree and `git diff --check` are clean.

Hosted CI for this exact head passed on 2026-10-29: 132 check runs settled (68 successful, 62 skipped, 1 neutral CodeQL result, and 1 superseded/cancelled PR-context run), with zero failed or pending checks. The previously failing [baseline ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40962090873/job/123758008168) and the [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40965138477) both succeeded. The exact tested base is pinned above; subsequent main changes are not included in this local verdict. The live 10.7/10.8 backport acceptances and stock-versus-patched Docker comparison below remain evidence for their named artifacts, not a new package or live-model acceptance of this rebased upstream head.

## Historical source validation — 2026-10-28 upstream head

Source: `9c948da8a43477fb375ba8c7e5c08b14ef4b8ec2`, rebased onto pinned main `a919e5ecc4f6c579e16ab21499ccda3acaa1fb07` on 2026-10-28.

- At source-equivalent predecessor `d2b9766017ba75a56c419f8a316214201a145bdc`, 108 targeted cases across ten files passed in 215.03 seconds wrapper wall time, including delayed-completion authority, pending catalog custody, same-child follow-up, lifecycle/steering/output receipt tests and the real native-process yield test.
- Production plugin types, scoped extension-test types, targeted type-aware lint (including pinned Bun parity), formatting, pinned-base line-cap and test-line budget checks passed.
- Independent source review of this exact range found no actionable P0–P2. The original production/test patch is unchanged; the old test-budget-only increase was removed because upstream now owns a larger shared ceiling. Upstream shutdown, subagent cleanup, sidebar and annotated UI receipt fixes are preserved.
- The real native case uses pinned Codex 0.164.0 and synthetic inference. Historical controlled-failure evidence below still documents the patch mechanism; neither a new full packaged upstream acceptance nor hosted CI success is claimed for this rebased head.
- The initial lint attempt on the preceding base could not stage the pinned Bun parity runtime in an offline container. Canonical staging resolved the tooling prerequisite; no lint gate or parity check was bypassed.

### Full-suite registration correction and hosted CI

That pre-rebase head added only the missing `run-attempt-lifecycle-controller.output-receipt.test.ts` entry to the database-worker test plan. Hosted CI on the predecessor caught that direct test selection was insufficient to prove full-suite discovery. The exact final head passed 54 configuration cases on both test runtimes plus four receipt cases (112 executions, 215.31 seconds wrapper wall), and scoped lint/format. Production/test source is otherwise unchanged, so the preceding source checks remain applicable.

A separate hosted `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` failure lists 14 mock-export sites in `src/gateway/server-shutdown.runtime.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server.spawn-broker.test.ts`. Both files are byte-identical to pinned upstream main `a919e5e`; the same diagnostics reproduce locally. That pre-rebase check was **not green**; the later rebase described in current evidence below incorporates upstream’s repair. [Failing job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40791343185/job/123177622310). No gate or baseline was weakened.

## Historical source validation — pre-rebase head

Source: `7ac126cd15dc6f67d14944b4b4a97c1b8697313e`, based on pinned main `58bf6decb46a946365900bb6d2f93b96e9b52f69`.

- Controlled original-controller comparison: both new direct/nested receipt regressions fail on premature native interruption; candidate bytes restored afterward.
- 57 lifecycle/steering/receipt/native cases passed across four files (67.60 seconds total wrapper wall time). Existing fixtures now explicitly model recorded output; no assertions were weakened. Two native-sibling cases moved out of the oversized suite.
- 29 full-attempt dynamic-tool, parent-continuation and original-child follow-up cases passed across three files (59.52 seconds wrapper wall time).
- Real pinned native Codex process plus production run-attempt/bridge/lifecycle and a synthetic local Responses provider: recorded `yielded` output precedes `turn/interrupt`, no aborted acknowledgement, owned native process exits. The case took 6.464 seconds; it exercises an actual process/history boundary that the cheaper lifecycle tests cannot prove.
- The native test's host fixture supplies an eligible yield; it does not certify child-claim admission or automatic continuation. It uses isolated state and no operator credentials. The first setup attempts exposed test-lane/session-seeding omissions; those were corrected, not counted as product failures or successful proofs.
- Production plugin types, scoped test types, targeted lint/format, pinned-base line-cap ratchet and exact test-line budget passed. Fresh independent source review found no actionable P0–P2 findings in the production repair; native proof source was separately reviewed by the lead.
- Simplification: one receipt bit in the existing call inventory replaces the assumption that a flushed response is ready for interruption; no parallel lifecycle or registry. The production delta for this follow-up is 17 added / 3 removed lines.

## Historical packaged proof (prior head, not current-head certification)

`f8699fea349def102ef4377b5009a556819583ac` passed 52 targeted tests plus packaged continuation in a fresh isolated installation: one parent, one original child, five persisted child turns, three genuine yields and three once-only automatic consumptions (96.19 seconds). Archive SHA-256 `2bbc9dc04691464cd91545c296d64651bdced78f307751d3da1699262ad13839`; build ID `2026.10.7-pr184848-f8699fea349-20261027`; native Codex `0.164.0`.

That packaged proof used scripted local HTTPS Responses/WebSocket inference with no external network. It is historical after the acknowledgement repair, not a rebuilt-package or real-model/OAuth acceptance claim. The prior controlled catalog regression fails with two parent thread starts when only its owner repair is reverted.

## Evidence — live 2026.10.7 backport acceptance

On 2026-10-28, a fresh uninterrupted live native acceptance run passed against installed custom build `2026.10.7-custom-continuation-e7de3d6695e-20261028`, backport commit `e7de3d6695e0b4881b109291c666e60121989580`. The running Gateway reported `2026.10.7` and pointed to that installed package.

One native child completed two ordinary turns, then three delayed turns (25-second delay requested each). Each delayed completion automatically resumed the parent after an explicit `sessions_yield` acknowledgement of `status: yielded`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---:|
| Turns completed with the same native child | 5/5 |
| Confirmed yields on turns 3–5 | 3/3 |
| Automatic parent resumptions | 3/3 |
| Results consumed once | 5/5 |

No polling during delayed checks, manual wakeups, child replacements, or user interruptions. No `nothing_pending` or interrupted acknowledgements were counted. Mirrored notifications were deduplicated: this proves once-only consumption, not transport-level exactly-once delivery. An earlier interrupted run was inconclusive and is excluded from this table.

These live results apply to the **stable custom backport**, not the upstream PR head. [Live acceptance report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184848#issuecomment-6480604481).

## Evidence — live 2026.10.8 backport acceptance

On 2026-10-29, fresh live native acceptance passed on the installed custom 2026.10.8 backport. The reachable running Gateway reported `2026.10.8`; session status identified build `55e31f3`, matching the qualified custom source `55e31f3e44f82154a6ffdabe58e725bec094a09c` (`2026.10.8-custom-continuation-55e31f3e44f-20261028`). This was live model execution, not the earlier scripted-provider package proof.

One original native child completed two ordinary turns and three delayed follow-up turns (20-second delay requested per delayed turn). For each of turns 3–5, the parent called `sessions_yield`, received `status: yielded`, and was automatically resumed by that child's completion.

| Check | Result |
|---|---:|
| Turns completed with the same native child | 5/5 |
| Confirmed yields on turns 3–5 | 3/3 |
| Automatic parent resumptions | 3/3 |
| Results consumed once | 5/5 |

No polling during delayed checks, manual wakeups, replacement children, or user interruptions. No `nothing_pending` or interrupted yield acknowledgements were counted. Mirrored completion notices surfaced for turns 3–5 and were ignored after the first consumption, as in the 10.7 acceptance: once-only consumption is demonstrated, not transport-level exactly-once delivery.

This is additional **stable custom backport** evidence, not certification of the upstream PR head, unmodified 2026.10.8, or a new stock-versus-patched controlled comparison. No installation, restart, configuration change, or merge was performed for this acceptance. At that live acceptance, the upstream source head was `9c948da8a43477fb375ba8c7e5c08b14ef4b8ec2`; later rebases are separately qualified.

## Evidence — stock versus patched 2026.10.8 Docker control

On 2026-10-29, **stock failed and the custom stable backport passed the same continuation-focused probe**. These were real installed Gateway and native Codex processes with scripted local Responses inference, not live-model/OAuth acceptance or a rebuilt upstream-head test.

### Pinned inputs

- Stock: npm `openclaw@2026.10.8`, release commit `dc2523e5a5c7a309517fd7fa834add938231d526`; archive SHA-256 `7e36685a0b5fd9c8c3afcfa93ee33fad871f7c6c8b6e695cae6720d14a765f18`, also checked against registry SHA-512 integrity. Matching official `@openclaw/codex@2026.10.8` installed via the supported plugin CLI, with trusted-official registry ownership verified.
- Patched: custom stable source `55e31f3e44f82154a6ffdabe58e725bec094a09c`; archive SHA-256 `192509e3911ae9bba6437dc1f1f7dbac96525d612fc3f3ade82ceefef6b10f55`, using its bundled Codex plugin.
- Both: Node 24.22.1 and native Codex 0.160.0, identical native binary SHA-256 `12eb3e81114588aca3b7998f4f19e8997b056aca08e57a7ca7c8a3ec8c652aad`.
- Separate synthetic state; dependency staging online, execution with Docker networking disabled. No production credentials/state or Docker socket mounted. Installed packages owned Gateway/plugin execution; a read-only source client supplied only Gateway RPC transport.

| Check | Stock 2026.10.8 | Custom 2026.10.8 |
|---|---|---|
| Original-child completed turns | 3; stopped at first delayed continuation | 5/5 |
| Persisted confirmed yield outputs | 1 | 3/3 |
| Automatic completion wakeup | Observed after turn 3 | All 3 |
| Native parent identity retained | No | Yes |
| Current delayed-result payload supplied | No | Yes |
| Delayed results consumed once | 0 | 3/3 |
| Runtime phase, including setup/cleanup | 89.68 s; exit 1 | 54.31 s; exit 0 |

### Observed failure boundary

The stock child persisted three completed turns. Its original parent persisted `status: yielded` before the delayed third result was released. Automatic completion then arrived under a **different native parent ID**, carrying the inter-session wakeup placeholder without the current child-result payload. Both provider-visible instructions and input were inspected: the result marker occurred only in quoted earlier task/history text, not as the delivered completion. The current original-child event assertion failed before a fourth child turn could be requested. This was not merely failure to wake the parent or a timeout.

The patched control retained one parent and one original child, five distinct persisted completed child turns, three persisted `yielded` outputs, and three once-only delayed-result consumptions. No polling or manual wakeups drove delayed completion. A separate ordinary user turn requested the fifth child action only after the fourth result was consumed.

### Probe qualifications and limits

The old custom-package probe assumed bundled Codex; stock requires the official plugin installation above. Its first setup verification failure is excluded from behavior evidence. A separate strict assertion about inbound context residing in top-level provider instructions also failed before child execution: stock carries that context in input messages. That request-layout difference is **not counted as a continuation failure or missing-context proof**. A separately identified continuation-focused variant records the layout fact without blocking child execution; all payload, identity, yield and consumption assertions remain intact. Identical variant bytes were used for both compared packages, without modifying runtime implementations.

This comparison supports the continuing need for the **combined stable backport** in this scenario, not the independent necessity of every patch or certification of this PR's current upstream head. Registry-versus-bundled plugin packaging differs; this is not a single-change causal experiment. The narrower controlled regressions above remain the evidence for individual repair mechanisms. All eight task-created containers were removed by recorded creation IDs; production Gateway identity and availability were unchanged.

## Limits and operational impact

No live installation, restart, configuration change or merge is part of this PR-body update or the live acceptance run. The stable 2026.10.7 and 2026.10.8 backports remain separate from the upstream PR; both installed custom packages passed the respective live acceptance above. That does not certify a rebuilt package of the upstream PR head. The observed duplicate native notifications and intermediate visible-reply warnings are not claimed fixed by this acknowledgement patch. No claim of production restart recovery, provider/OAuth recovery, or all-plugin test-type coverage.

## Test-line budget

The upstream ceiling is preserved unchanged at 6,320,000. The old PR-specific budget increase is no longer part of the diff. The repository's exact test-line and pinned-base line-cap checks passed on the rebased head. Hosted CI seconds are not yet available for this head.

prs.title: fix(browser): isolate extension tab discovery from uninitialized page targets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With the extension in **All tabs**, a single tab whose **first navigation has not committed yet** makes Playwright's cold `connectOverCDP` fail, because Playwright awaits every Page initializer. Browser status succeeds, but listing or using unrelated healthy tabs fails with `browserType.connectOverCDP: Timeout 9000ms exceeded`.

A tab that is merely still waiting for its HTTP response is enough. The renderer does **not** need to be stalled or busy.

This revision separates native target inventory from individual Page initialization on lifecycle-registered extension relays. Healthy tabs remain usable. Selecting a not-yet-ready tab returns a bounded, target-specific readiness error; after it commits, the same native target recovers without restarting the Browser or losing healthy-tab snapshot references.

The relay's public auto-attach barrier, native debugger ownership, generation checks, access policy, quarantine rules, and transient inventory errors remain enforced. Only the private Playwright adapter defers its initial Page barrier. Failed initializers can publish dummy Pages with an empty main-frame URL, so selected-target recovery detaches and reattaches only that logical session through the existing relay.

## Upstream defect, product-level mitigation

The blocking behavior is reproducible **without any OpenClaw code**: plain `playwright-core` against plain Chrome, one healthy tab plus one background tab whose HTTP response is withheld, so its first navigation never commits.

| playwright-core | Pending tab open | After the response is released |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1.63.0 | Fails after 9,019 ms | Succeeds in 26 ms, 3 pages |
| 1.64.1 | Fails after 9,017 ms | Succeeds in 27 ms, 3 pages |

Upstream location: `_waitForAllPagesToBeInitialized` awaits `Promise.all` over every page, and each page waits for `_firstNonInitialNavigationCommittedPromise`. Upgrading Playwright does not help.

OpenClaw does not need initialized Page objects at connect time; it needs the target inventory. Deferring the initial Page barrier is therefore the correct product-side boundary, not a workaround for a renderer defect. An upstream report is still warranted and is not covered by this PR.

## Evidence

Isolated Proxmox Debian 13 amd64; Node 24.22.1; Chrome for Testing **156.0.8078.73** under Xvfb; `--no-sandbox` in the container fixture. Fresh synthetic Chrome profile and Gateway state. Canonical built Gateway daemon and browser CLI; **unmodified shipped extension 2.3.0**, paired through its normal Settings page in **All tabs** mode.

Fixture: one healthy HTTP page plus one **background** HTTP page whose response the test server withholds, so its first navigation never commits. No busy loop, no native API overrides, no injected Chrome errors, no inspector breakpoints.

Extension note: these runs used the **published Chrome Web Store package 2.3.0** (`kcdjddhmeafeomebliikmbpblkmkfoig`). It carries the same version string as the in-tree extension but differs in most module files, so earlier in-tree-only runs did not exercise the shipped artifact.

| Gateway revision | playwright-core | First `tabs` call | Result |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Published release 2026.10.8 (`dc2523e`) | 1.63.0 | 24,769 ms | **Fails** |
| Published release 2026.10.8, minimal fixture | 1.63.0 | 24,778 ms | **Fails** |
| Previous PR head `b3cee431` | 1.64.1 | 27,881 ms | **Fails** |
| Candidate `991200f72` | 1.64.1 | 2,757 ms | Succeeds with the pending tab still open |
| Published release 2026.10.8 plus `chrome://` and `devtools://` tabs | 1.63.0 | 3,436 ms | Succeeds |

CLI wall times include CLI startup; the Gateway recorded `browser.request` failing in 22,667 ms with `errorCode=UNAVAILABLE` and the 9,000 ms `connectOverCDP` timeout.

Two controls narrow the cause:

- During the blockage, `Page.getFrameTree` on the offending target answered in **1 ms** with an empty main-frame URL. The renderer was responsive; only the navigation was uncommitted.
- On the published release, releasing the withheld HTTP response made the next `tabs` call succeed in **2,124 ms** with no Browser or Gateway restart.
- Internal `chrome://` and `devtools://` tabs do **not** trigger the failure.

## Automated regression coverage and scope

`pw-session-pending-navigation.chromium.test.ts` now uses real Chromium and the pinned Playwright 1.64.1 with an HTTP response held before the first navigation commits. It exercises the production CDP adapter: cold connection returns, an unrelated healthy page remains usable, and releasing the response followed by a targeted reattach recovers the pending target without closing the healthy Page. The existing Chromium browser-extension CI step explicitly runs this test with `OPENCLAW_BROWSER_EXTENSION_E2E=1`.

Negative control: the same real-browser test with `deferInitialAutoAttach: false` fails at `connectOverCDP` with its 2500 ms timeout; enabling the adapter path passes. This tests the real Playwright barrier, not just mocked CDP replies. It does **not** automate the entire real extension/native-host relay, timed failed-initializer path, or stable snapshot-reference workflow; those broader paths remain covered by the manual evidence below and focused relay tests rather than claimed as full automated end-to-end proof.

Independent review found two related relay recovery defects: inventory could reannounce an already recovered root alias, and detaching that alias again did not suppress inventory before the next reattach. Both were reproduced by failing relay tests and fixed by checking physical root ownership and applying detach suppression to root aliases. The regression now includes repeated inventories, browser-session and second-client inventories, use of the recovered alias, repeated detach/reattach, and subsequent genuine `target_closed` recovery. The bounded follow-up source review passed.

Local evidence: 53 relay-bridge tests passed after both fixes; 9 transport tests and the new real Chromium test also passed together (63 tests total; the final repeated-detach fix and subsequent CI type-narrowing corrections were also verified by a fresh 63/63 run). One combined local run of the Chromium test exceeded its existing 15 s test budget; its cause is unestablished. Subsequent API-instrumented isolated and combined runs passed without increasing timeouts or enabling retries. This intermittent result is disclosed rather than claimed as a proven repair. The isolated local runner used installed SDK exports; canonical PR CI remains the full dependency/type/platform verification.

Test-line allocation is 710 rather than 562: the exact additional 148 lines cover the 110-line real Chromium test and net 38 relay regression lines. Against the PR frozen base, total and ceiling are both 6,308,182 (zero slack); the global baseline was not raised.

## Correction to the earlier revision of this description

Previous revisions of this description attributed the failure to a renderer that stops responding and proved it with a bounded 45-second JavaScript loop. That is a different state and **not** the reported trigger: an ordinary tab that is still loading is sufficient, and the offending renderer stays responsive.

The implementation is unchanged by this correction; the separation of inventory from per-Page initialization is what resolves the reproduced failure.

## Validation

- 104 focused owner/sibling tests passed across six browser suites.
- After the final lint-only test adjustment and refusal-classifier extraction, both changed suites passed again: 62 tests.
- Production and focused test typechecks, targeted Oxlint, formatting, commit hooks, and diff checks passed.
- Independent read-only review found no actionable issue in the new transport/readiness/recovery implementation.
- Tested head `991200f72` had an exact test-line recount of **6,312,189**, ceiling **6,312,189**, zero slack. The recovery follow-up adds 243 justified regression lines. Counting rules and assertions are unchanged. The refusal classifier moved to a coherent sibling module to respect the bridge's line-cap ratchet.
- Published head **`6d02a663132e911e3b94d0bf70094aa7a0315135`** merges current main `67a7001050ff57c67f73123713670e3e0af234ad` to resolve the new budget-only conflict. All browser source/tests are byte-identical to tested `991200f72` (`git diff 991200f72 HEAD -- extensions/browser` is empty). The merge retains main's existing **6,320,000** ceiling unchanged. The full native proof was not redundantly rerun for this mechanical merge.
- Broad checks are delegated to PR CI for this pushed head; older green CI is not claimed for this revision.
- The new uncommitted-navigation reproduction above is **manual isolated-environment evidence**. No automated regression test for it is added in this PR; see the section above.

## Proof boundaries

The reproduced mechanism is an **uninitialized page target**, not the original wrapped-refusal inventory race. The [independent NO-REPRO investigation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186674#issuecomment-6466831554) remains valid for that separate claim. The earlier wrapped permanent-refusal classifier is retained with its native-boundary and transient-error controls, but its complete-product before/after acceptance remains open. The bare Chrome refusal `Cannot access a chrome-extension:// URL of different extension` also appeared in **passing** runs, so it is not by itself evidence of the outage.

The mitigation is scoped to the extension-relay path, where `initialAutoAttach` is set. Direct-CDP connections (`cdpUrl`, hosted providers, `attachOnly`) still hit the upstream Playwright behavior; that is an accepted limit of this PR, not a claim of full coverage.

The operator's exact offending tab has not been identified. This proves the reproduced timeout mechanism and the fix, not that every reported timeout has that cause. No claim is made that this repairs the separate Windows native Chrome/PC crash; that remains unexplained. The operator's normal Chrome and production Gateway were not operated or modified for these tests.

Related: #156749, #156890, #162110.
CI follow-up: the first revision of these new tests exposed six TypeScript errors (unknown CDP response objects and potentially absent browser contexts). Commit `a045e86004` narrows these explicitly; the canonical `check-test-types` job on that commit has passed. The earlier revision also failed an unchanged UI effort-picker browser test. On current head `a045e8600477be718064531422bd90deb6ecb771`, that UI job, `check-test-types`, `build-artifacts` (including the new real Chromium test), and the complete canonical CI run [41250174340](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41250174340) passed. The earlier intermittent UI failure is not claimed as repaired by the browser changes. All three commit status gates subsequently reported success; GitHub reported mergeable=true and mergeable_state=clean.

prs.title: fix: hold queued messages through inline edits
prs.body: Closes #189845. ## What Problem This Solves Queued text can be sent while the operator is changing it in the inline editor. The browser checks the edit hold before preparing delivery, but preparation can wait for idle readiness. If the operator opens Edit during that wait, the original text can reach the Gateway before Save or Cancel. This was reproduced through ordinary Queue and Edit controls on an isolated real Gateway. A single real readiness response was delayed for 1.447 seconds and then forwarded unchanged; the original message was dispatched and accepted while the changed draft remained visibly open. ## User Impact An open queued-message edit continues to hold its source through delivery preparation. Saving can replace it through the existing queue, and canceling can resume the original input. The correction preserves queue order, current connection and source-version checks, attachment handling, and the existing distinction between Queue and Steer. There is no new configuration, state format, persistent flag, or public protocol. This change prevents a pending delivery continuation from sending text the operator is still editing; it does not withdraw work that the Gateway already accepted. ## Why This Change Was Made Final admission already decides whether the prepared queue item may be dispatched. It now checks the existing edit owner alongside the existing held-state check, after the preparation waits. This keeps the decision at the effect boundary without introducing another hold mechanism or changing the edit's source/draft ownership. The early drain check remains useful because it avoids preparation for an edit that was already open. Existing history and attachment checks retain their own boundaries. The new regression exercises the real outbox/edit/delivery owners with fixed external Gateway responses, including separate Save and Cancel continuations. ## Evidence - On unchanged production, both new delayed-readiness cases failed because the original text reached `chat.send` while the edit was open; the other 32 cases in that file passed. - On `1258f4cecd42956b49f78f77d606271b15eaa009`, all 73 tests in the four selected files passed: readiness, queued edits, creation handoff, and asynchronous send preparation. Both new cases retain the changed draft during the wait and then send the selected input exactly once after Save or Cancel. - Canonical AutoReview of `06a71d75..1258f4ce` completed with P0–P3 coverage and no actionable findings. It reviewed the committed change and supplied owner/caller context; it did not execute tests or substitute for independent engineering review. - Native changed-file format/lint, UI i18n, and the selected production/test type checks passed. The four-file test stage took 4.85 seconds; the combined invocation also included type checking. The new regression adds 88 test lines with an equal per-change allocation; the shared ceiling is unchanged. - Fixed-source browser proof passed on the same guest permissions and unchanged Gateway: one real readiness response held for 1.455 seconds, original queued input sent zero times while editing, Save delivered the edited text once, and Cancel on a distinct row delivered its original text once. Both useful replies completed; the unsaved Cancel draft was never sent, and the settled queue and editor were empty. - Independent engineering review found no actionable issue. Exact-head hosted CI passed, including all three UI shards, UI E2E, the Control UI performance check, and the selected lint/type/architecture/security families. The comparison uses distinct synthetic equipment and room-booking tasks to preserve previously accepted work. Both use the same viewport, theme, guest scopes, ordinary queue/edit controls, and delayed-readiness boundary. Content differs; the claim concerns delivery ownership, not pixel layout. The focused recording labels omitted waits and half-speed actions. The original baseline recording has a capture artifact and is excluded; its inspected still and protocol observations establish the before result. No natural failure frequency or broader platform coverage is claimed. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Original queued request answered while its changed draft remains open](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/990b1d7f-a9a0-4347-8440-b4a089a9e0b2) | ![Changed draft remains open with no original queued request delivered](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d583191e-7717-4baa-8cd1-1d95313096cc) | ### Queue, delayed\-readiness Edit, Save, Cancel and completed replies\. Omitted waits and half\-speed actions are labeled; final frame held for two seconds\. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/85852726-eff2-4b9c-b43e-652df9336550 ### Visual verification - Baseline: 06a71d75b01e3febb7949532b58cbde1a99e8127 - Exact head: `1258f4cecd42956b49f78f77d606271b15eaa009` - Scenario: Queue a follow\-up while a real reply is active, open Edit during one delayed idle\-readiness response, then Save\. Queue a distinct follow\-up, edit it, and Cancel\. Distinct synthetic workspaces avoid replaying accepted work; both cases use the same guest scopes, viewport, theme, queue controls and readiness boundary\. - Runtime/build: Candidate UI 1258f4ce; unchanged Gateway 2026\.10\.9\-06a71d75b01e\-2026\-10\-31T22\-10\-13\.199Z\. Served sources matched all four queue/edit owners\. - Readiness response delay: Before 1\.447 s; after 1\.455 s; each response forwarded unchanged once - Original input sent during edit: Before 1; after 0 - Save and Cancel continuation: Edited Save input 1; original Cancel input 1; unsaved Cancel draft 0; both replies completed - Settled queue and editor count: 0 and 0 - Ordinary Queue/Edit/Save/Cancel controls on an isolated real Gateway with a real model - Single guest connection; sessions read/write only; no admin scope - Exact candidate sources bound by served source maps - Original captures retained through assessment; private footer and recorder locator overlay excluded from published cut - Distinct synthetic equipment and room\-booking tasks preserve old accepted work; content differs, while the edit hold and dispatch boundary are equivalent

prs.title: fix(infra): keep the launchd recovery budget on elapsed time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The managed-service handoff recovery loop measured its budget on the wall clock:

```js
const deadline = Date.now() + params.recoveryTimeoutMs;
const run = (args) => runOwned("launchctl", args, undefined, deadline);
for (let inspection = enabled; enabled.code === 0 && Date.now() < deadline;) {
  ...
  await sleep(Math.min(500, Math.max(0, deadline - Date.now())));
}
```

Everything in that loop is local elapsed time, but it was seeded and consumed with `Date.now()`. A host clock correction during recovery (NTP step, VM pause/resume, manual change) either stretched the recovery wait past the configured timeout or expired it early, refusing a healthy `launchctl` restart during an update.

## Scope reduction (rebased onto current `main`)

This PR originally also converted the parent-exit path in `update-managed-service-handoff.ts`. Current `main` changed that contract: `params.parentExitDeadlineAt` is now created in the parent process (`parentExitDeadlineAt: Date.now() + owner.parentExitTimeoutMs`) and passed into the handoff script, so it is an epoch value that legitimately crosses a process boundary. Converting it to `performance.now()` would compare two unrelated clock domains, so that half is dropped — the remaining wall-clock dependency is the process-local recovery budget, fixed here.

Two deliberate boundaries in the reduced fix:

- **Spawn deadlines stay epoch-valued.** `runServiceCommand`'s `deadline` is shared with `params.parentExitDeadlineAt`, which comes from the parent process. Each local spawn therefore gets `Date.now() + remainingBudget()`; only the budget itself is monotonic.
- **Persisted timestamps keep `Date.now()`.** `serviceDowntimeMs` compares against the stored `serviceStoppedAtMs` epoch and is untouched.

This follows the owner established by #186484: `performance.now()` for process-local elapsed budgets, epoch for anything persisted or exchanged across processes. #186484 explicitly left managed-service handoff timing untouched, and this is that follow-up for the launchd recovery side.

## What Changed

```js
function createMonotonicBudget(timeoutMs) {
  const startedAt = performance.now();
  const remainingMs = () => Math.max(0, timeoutMs - (performance.now() - startedAt));
  return { remainingMs, commandDeadlineAt: () => Date.now() + remainingMs() };
}
```

## Evidence

`update-managed-service-handoff-command-source.test.ts` runs the embedded command source in a VM with injected `Date` and `performance`:

- Steps the wall clock **+1h** and then **−2h** mid-budget and asserts the remaining budget stays `180_000`ms while `commandDeadlineAt()` still tracks the live wall clock (`deadline − now === 180_000`).
- Asserts the recovery source drives its loop from that budget and no longer seeds it with `Date.now() + params.recoveryTimeoutMs`.

```
✓ src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-command-source.test.ts (12 tests)
```

`oxlint` clean on the three touched files.

### Known gap in this environment

`src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-command.test.ts` (the end-to-end handoff suite) cannot run in this checkout: it needs the sealed `dist` runtime and fails with `Managed handoff requires its sealed runtime; use the repository test runner or the dist-backed pnpm openclaw CLI`. That is an environment limitation here, not a result of this change — CI runs it with the built runtime.

prs.title: feat(provider): add Databricks Unity Gateway
prs.body:
Closes #155633

## What Problem This Solves

Organizations routing inference through Databricks Unity Gateway currently hand-author workspace routes, credentials, transport and model metadata. This adds provider-specific onboarding and model resolution through an externally distributed plugin.

## User Impact

Operators install `@openclaw/databricks-provider`, supply `DATABRICKS_HOST` and `DATABRICKS_TOKEN`, and run `openclaw onboard --auth-choice databricks-token`. Models use `databricks/<catalog>.<schema>.<model-service>`.

Same-workspace onboarding preserves existing routes, APIs, model entries, aliases and primary selections. Fresh setup uses `/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1` with `system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-5`. Non-interactive onboarding refuses reuse of a saved profile when `DATABRICKS_HOST` selects a different workspace, and rejects invalid explicit hosts before persistence. Trusted manual provider-config edits remain operator-controlled routing changes; this does not introduce immutable workspace identity in the credential format.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Databricks host validation, auth, onboarding and model resolution stay in `extensions/databricks`.
- Reuses the existing OpenAI-compatible streaming transport and credential store.
- Follows the in-repo-source / external npm and ClawHub package pattern used by official providers such as Cerebras and Radius; excluded from the core npm tarball.
- Adds `DATABRICKS_HOST` to untrusted workspace `.env` filtering, with a regression. Credential environment filtering comes from the manifest.
- No new external runtime dependencies, generic transport, credential owner, schema or migration. The lockfile adds only the workspace importer and existing `@openclaw/plugin-sdk` workspace devDependency.

## Current candidate

Merged with current main on October 25, 2026: head `ed3410f89b58993803b30e2cd91d240a3faeb12e`, a merge commit with parents `37b4873865e39e4d9eafd845ce2046df52a46bc7` (the October 21 candidate) and upstream main `e850f7c5419068f4eb598152fd8b0e164f995fcb`. This was a merge, so the branch history was not force pushed.

Merge conflicts were limited to generated docs and the zh-CN glossary. `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` and `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` were regenerated through their owning script, and both sides of the zh-CN glossary were kept. Databricks production and transport code are unchanged. The workspace dotenv regression uses main's refactored fixture helper and retains both Databricks host checks. Plugin version, API compatibility and build metadata remain aligned to `2026.10.4`; minimum host remains `>=2026.9.6`.

The installed-package/live/upgrade proof below applies to earlier candidates. It is retained as historical behavior evidence, not claimed as a fresh live run or current-head CI.

## Evidence

### October 25 merge proof

At exact head `ed3410f89b58993803b30e2cd91d240a3faeb12e`:

- `pnpm test extensions/databricks/index.test.ts extensions/databricks/gateway-transport.test.ts src/infra/dotenv-workspace-blocklist.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **28 passed** (9 infra + 19 provider/transport).
- The two failures diagnosed on October 21 (planner capacity 80/79 and the Feishu streaming bound) pass on the new main base.
- Package-boundary typecheck through `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs`, lint, `plugins:inventory:check` and `config:docs:check` passed.
- [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40256838088) on this head is still running. At the time of writing, three shards had failed in suites outside this diff: `test/cli-json-stdout.e2e.test.ts` (sandbox explain validation JSON), `test/cli-json-stdout.hooks.e2e.test.ts` (remote Gateway hooks error text) and `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/telegram-recovered-artifact.e2e.test.ts`. None of those files or their owners are touched here; their cause is not yet diagnosed and no baseline reproduction is claimed.
- `openclaw/ci-gate` and `openclaw/dependency-review` still require maintainer approval of this revision.

### October 21 rebase proof

At exact head `37b4873865e39e4d9eafd845ce2046df52a46bc7`, macOS arm64, Node 26.5.0, pinned pnpm 12.12.1:

- Normal root command `pnpm test extensions/databricks/index.test.ts extensions/databricks/gateway-transport.test.ts src/infra/dotenv-workspace-blocklist.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **28 passed** (9 infra + 19 provider/transport); two shards completed with exit 0 in 102.70 seconds.
- Plugin inventory, generated config docs, full `pnpm check:docs` (format, Markdown/MDX, glossary, links, config examples, changelog), changed-source formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Package-boundary typecheck (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/databricks/tsconfig.json --noEmit`) and targeted type-aware lint passed with exit 0.
- Fresh [hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39694286034) is running. The October 16 failures belong to the previous head and are not presented as current results. The separate dependency-review status still requires maintainer approval.


### Fresh CI diagnosis — October 21

[Current CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39694286034) is still running. Two failures observed so far:

- [Planner capacity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39694286034/job/119548250646): `keeps the hybrid hourly plan within the main-tier cap` reports 80 jobs versus cap 79. Reproduced the same planner API/options in separate exact-base `4397e7409d5` and candidate `37b4873865e` checkouts; both fail with the identical 80/79 result. This is a confirmed inherited failure; no capacity limit or assertion was relaxed.
- [Feishu stream bound](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39694286034/job/119548250454): `rejects oversized streaming tenant-token JSON before buffering the full body` fails at `streamState.canceled()`. The Feishu code and fixture are unchanged by this PR. Focused normal-root replay `pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on the exact candidate passed all 29 cases locally (57.51 seconds). This is not a proven repair or Linux baseline reproduction; hosted cause remains unresolved.

### October 16 rebase proof

- Normal test entrypoint: `pnpm test extensions/databricks/index.test.ts extensions/databricks/gateway-transport.test.ts src/infra/dotenv-workspace-blocklist.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **28/28 passed**, exit 0 on final head `26eea19eb89` (19 provider/transport + 9 workspace dotenv cases). Repeated after incorporating main’s provider-authentication changes. The cold run on preceding head `f22a48bfbb5` also passed (infra 76.99s, extensions 67.96s).
- On the patch-identical preceding rebase head `f22a48bfbb5`, `pnpm build:runtime` — passed (runtime compilation, CLI bootstrap guard, assets and UI build).
- On preceding head `f22a48bfbb5`, package-boundary production typecheck: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/databricks/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — passed.
- On preceding head `f22a48bfbb5`, targeted provider and dotenv type-aware lint, changed-source formatting, plugin inventory regeneration check, config baseline regeneration check, glossary check and internal link audit — passed (15,586 internal links, zero broken).
- Final-head config baseline check and `git diff --check` — passed. Independent mechanical-delta review — no actionable findings.

<details>
<summary>Cold-run focused terminal results (preceding patch-identical head f22a48bfbb5)</summary>

```text
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  9 passed (9)
  Duration  76.99s

[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.extensions.config.ts
✓ extensions/databricks/gateway-transport.test.ts > databricks gateway transport > onboards, streams a tool call, executes it, and sends the tool result back through Unity Gateway 427ms
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  19 passed (19)
  Duration  67.96s
```

These are isolated synthetic-credential tests, including real HTTP loopback streaming and tool execution; they are not a new authenticated Databricks live run.

</details>

### Live installed-package proof — October 13

Executed against a real Databricks workspace using the current candidate. The token existed only in the child process environment; onboarding used `--secret-input-mode ref`. Workspace and token are redacted.

| Boundary | Observed |
| --- | --- |
| Core runtime build | Completed successfully, 83.3 seconds |
| Release-pipeline plugin pack | `openclaw-databricks-provider-2026.10.2.tgz`, 8 files, 3 runtime JS modules, manifest, package metadata, README and 2 assets; no runtime dependencies |
| Managed install | `plugins install npm-pack:<tarball> --force --accept-capabilities`, exit 0 |
| Runtime identity | `plugins inspect databricks --runtime --json`: loaded, global origin, installed `node_modules/@openclaw/databricks-provider/dist/index.js`, provider `databricks`, no diagnostics |
| Source exclusion | Both bundled discovery and bundled source overlays disabled throughout install, onboarding and agent turns |
| Onboarding | Exit 0, primary `databricks/system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-5`, `openai-completions`, environment SecretRef; token absent from `openclaw.json` |
| Streaming and real tool round trip | `agent exec` exited 0; two HTTP 200 `text/event-stream` responses; exactly one successful `read` call; final reply exactly matched random file nonce `DBX-baf85764f87acf9d` |
| Non-catalog model | `databricks/system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-6` resolved dynamically; real streamed agent turn exited 0 and replied `DYNAMIC_OK` |
| Invalid explicit workspace | Browser URL containing `?o=1234` rejected with exit 1 before inference; active `openclaw.json` SHA-256 unchanged |

This proves local package installation and real inference through the installed runtime. It does not claim that the package is published or that catalog-linked official publisher trust has been established.

## Installed-runtime authority and stable-upgrade proof

Using the same packed plugin with bundled discovery and source overlays disabled:

- Started with published latest stable `openclaw@2026.10.2` (`b8952d4`), created an existing Databricks Serving route and saved synthetic workspace-A credential through its published SDK, then installed the candidate and ran candidate onboarding. Exit 0; deep comparisons confirmed provider route/API/model metadata, primary selection, aliases/model entries and saved credential including workspace metadata were unchanged.
- Positive control: saved workspace-A credential was reused successfully without a token environment variable.
- Workspace-B selection without a fresh token exited 1 before network access; active configuration hash was unchanged.
- Hostile cwd `.env` supplied an attacker workspace and token. A benign dotenv witness was loaded, proving the actual cwd loader ran, while `DATABRICKS_HOST` stayed absent. Onboarding exited 1 for missing trusted workspace; configuration hash was unchanged.
- A Node preload denied and recorded fetch, HTTP(S) and socket connection attempts. Both negative cases recorded `attempts: []`; it did not modify provider auth/config logic. Synthetic credentials were used for these boundary probes.
- The real-token live run above was separately scanned across 23 isolated state files: zero occurrences of the supplied token.

## October 13 validation (prior head)

- Focused provider, real-transport loopback and workspace `.env` suites: 28 tests passed across 3 files. Combined wall time 80.44 seconds on a heavily loaded macOS arm64 host, Node 26.5. Provider files: 19 tests, 28.32 seconds wall, individual transport scenario 416 ms. No new tests were added in the rebase.
- Extension package-boundary production typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, and changed-source formatting passed.
- Config baseline, plugin inventory and version-sync checks passed.
- Full docs checks passed: formatting, Markdown/MDX, glossary, links, config examples and changelog checks.
- `git diff --check` passed.

Fresh independent review was completed. Findings were checked against owning paths:

- The proposed interactive SecretRef failure did not reproduce through the registered auth method with source overlays disabled and an explicit plugin load path. The reviewer retracted it.
- The proposed dynamic API override failure is prevented by core's `applyConfiguredProviderOverrides`; the final resolution probe retained `anthropic-messages` and the configured route. No duplicate override was added to the plugin.
- The proposed immutable credential/workspace binding would change the trusted manual-config contract and credential semantics. The implemented guard covers onboarding workspace selection, not arbitrary operator edits; that scope is explicit above.

Prior-head [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38397087861) completed with 167 successful jobs, 22 skipped jobs and 6 failed jobs (5 shards plus the aggregate gate). The Databricks shard, production/test types, lint, package boundaries, docs, source contracts and npm-lock checks passed. The failing shards were OpenAI realtime auth fixtures (missing admitted database worker), Codex dynamic-tool host instructions, node-worker launch wire timeout, Telegram emoji gateway timeout, and QA POSIX SIGTERM lifecycle timeout. These are outside the Databricks diff; only the OpenAI failure was independently reproduced and repaired in separate #171064 (18 unchanged tests pass). Other failures are attributed by hosted logs and unchanged source scope, not claimed baseline reproductions. Dependency approval remains separate from the failed CI gate.

## Limits and maintainer decision

This is Unity Gateway support. Existing workspace Serving configuration is preserved, but broader Serving compatibility belongs to dependent #163202, which still requires its own repair, restack and validation. OAuth token minting/refresh, automatic live model discovery and per-workspace pricing are outside this change; unknown model services use fallback metadata.

The remaining product decision is whether Databricks receives official provider catalog sponsorship and in-repository maintenance. Maintainer edits are enabled. If accepted, the final head requires the existing maintainer dependency-change approval path; publishing/release is a separate action.

prs.title: fix(ui): explain blank pages in browsers without module scripts
prs.body:
Supersedes #167999, thanks @aspalagin.

Related: #167980

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: browsers without module-script support leave the Control UI nearly blank with no explanation or recovery guidance.

## User Impact

Affected users see **This browser is not supported** and instructions to update their browser or system WebView. Supported browsers retain their module startup behavior. No legacy bundle or polyfills are added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The document shell provides a standard `nomodule` notice, independent of modern recovery code that old engines cannot parse. A literal foreground color keeps the text readable without CSS variables. Two redundant existence guards around the same shell's always-present recovery buttons were removed: production LOC delta **0**. The regression adds 16 test lines with a scoped allocation; documentation adds two lines.

## Evidence

- Base: `c633ec6376e1ce6cdf6268f98d1c86eb9395b074`. The new regression fails on this main HTML because the unsupported-browser message is absent; the other 32 tests pass. After the fix, **33/33 pass** (`pnpm test ui/src/app/mount-fallback.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 2.16 s Vitest / 3.47 s runner). The hosted job timings are available in this PR's checks.
- Production UI build, UI typecheck, UI-app test typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed. [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41254922326) passed, including all seven UI E2E shards and the final CI gate.
- Chromium **60.0.3109.0**: exact base HTML stays nearly blank with a faint **Loading…** label and no recovery guidance; the production replacement HTML displays readable update guidance. Module support was absent in the actual browser. Both documents were served with the production CSP hash/header helpers. A modern Chromium browser skipped the notice and rendered a synthetic module application.
- Browser proof validates the document shell and CSP, using a task-owned loopback server and synthetic module response. It is not a full Gateway, authenticated session, Telegram, or real-device run. The contributor branch was read with `gh pr view/diff` and was never checked out or executed.
- Local autoreview of the complete production/test delta against the base: **scoped-clean**, P0–P2, no actionable findings. The final test differs only by formatting; the documentation/allocation records followed. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; the [hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189883#issuecomment-6550948377) also found no actionable issues on `5163e30ec4b913e810ff2148eaaab145cf88d2ec` and accepted the browser screenshots.

Before — current-main HTML in Chromium 60:

![Before: nearly blank page without recovery guidance](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3392f816-8d73-455c-9941-c141ac92822a)

After — built replacement HTML in Chromium 60:

![After: readable unsupported-browser notice and update instructions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8b54b922-4b24-4ce0-8bf8-60ae43253a2c)

prs.title: fix(macos): preserve the selected CLI when inspecting a managed install
prs.body:
Closes #140128

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS CLI selection changing when the app inspects a ready managed CLI while an external CLI is selected.

## User Impact

Inspecting installations no longer changes the selected CLI. A successful managed install or update still selects the verified managed CLI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Managed inspection returns status without persisting selection. Discovery retains its existing selection behavior, while installation and update record the managed CLI only after their success checks. No preference keys or formats changed, and no CLI is removed.

## Evidence

Current product head: `b3ee56297f4075c471fd624aa085b252fd126ac6`. The GitHub web merge on 31 October combined prior head `a2c6197e80d459f03b88b8de3030e8ca67e6ddda` with main `f1c93577085244aa96aa87b53a2df9b59d293bd7`. All earlier proof below remains pinned to its actual revision; it is not current-head execution.

- **Current PR CI:** [Run 41214035584](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41214035584) passed its selected preflight, security-fast, native-i18n, and CI-gate jobs. Its preflight log records synthetic merge checkout `cc79321ee`, merging product `b3ee562` into main `f1c9357`. The [combined CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41214232001) also reports success at `b3ee562`. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed. This is current PR composition evidence, not native runtime proof. Earlier [CI 40975271680](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40975271680) remains evidence for `a2c6197`, not this head.

- **Prior-head native-owner proof:** [Hosted macOS run 38597006067](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/38597006067) passed with QA/workflow `4cf95ff77fae422b8b380f4a2c49c4101a8f38b1` and clean initial/final product `76ee71b`. macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.0, Swift 6.4 arm64: 56 Swift Testing declarations across four suites, expanding to 64 executed cases (50 single-case declarations plus 14 cases from six parameterized declarations). Selection, managed-update success/failure, and older/missing/revoked canonical-verification controls passed. These are executable fixtures, not real npm installations or signed-app proof.
- **Prior-head canonical CI:** [Run 38599555604](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38599555604) passed at exact product `76ee71b`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Its macOS Swift and macOS Node jobs were skipped, not executed; native proof comes from the separate owner run above.
- **Prior applicability:** Source review of then-current main `794d6500f382311cab58f5d474a9ef248598e5f2` still finds the ready `managedStatus` selection write. This is source evidence, not a new live reproduction.
- **Prior-head review (29 October):** [ClawSweeper Revision 14](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) reviewed `a2c6197` on 29 October. It reports no findings, patch quality 4/6, and overall/proof 2/6. App-entry inspection and verified installation/update evidence, plus an existing-state upgrade from `v2026.10.9` preserving settings and data, remain required. The completed review does not establish a data-model defect.
- **Prior-head review:** [ClawSweeper's review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) at `76ee71b` identifies no code findings; app-entry and upgrade evidence remains outstanding. Revision 14 above supersedes that historical review.
- **Fixture follow-up:** [Commit `4298606`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4298606a9e38b4665dc014a71fd81bfb451d97af) changes exactly two positive Node fixture literals, preserving all assertions, old-runtime controls, and production source. Whitespace and exact source-delta checks passed. [Previous-head canonical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121014753) passed, including its CI gate, native i18n, and security-fast. The prior [combined CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121219433) also reports success at `4298606`. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed; no current-head native execution proof is claimed.

### Remaining qualification

- **App entry and update:** The owner tests and retained real-npm evidence cover the affected **unbundled** discovery/inspection path at their recorded revisions. Signed packaged-app proof is separate: it must establish the actual legacy-service inspection/update routing, selection preservation, and verified canonical selection. A fresh bundled no-op or forced override cannot stand in for the original bug. The 56 owner declarations do not directly cover `install(target:)` success/compatibility-failure selection paths. The discovery regression seeds the external tuple, so it proves preservation rather than independently proving first-discovery persistence.
- **Existing-state upgrade:** A disposable latest-stable-to-candidate app upgrade with existing settings/data retained remains unrun. No preference/schema format changed, and source review found no data-model incompatibility; the missing upgrade run is a proof gap, not an established migration defect.
- **Current composition:** The fixtures emit `v24.22.1`, which satisfies the current runtime requirement; the 24 October change addressed the higher minimum inspected at that time. This two-line fixture-only repair is published at `4298606`; native execution of the current composition remains unverified. This does not relabel the pinned original-head result or establish a production incompatibility.

### Retained real coexisting-installation proof

[Run 37386979616](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616) compared earlier product `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b` with baseline `3b16db73c0b5209aad2ee7c3fb5ddfb12fb208f9`, governed by corrected QA workflow `b166bce6b7ee4fc86631cb491fd7c17990be6362`. The candidate preserved external selection through ready managed inspection and left initially unset executable/version preferences unset: one native test passed in 74.660 seconds. The baseline failed exactly the five expected selection assertions; its verifier rejected other failures.

Both jobs used two distinct real `openclaw@2026.9.8` npm installations with verified published SHA-512 integrity on disposable hosted macOS runners. Cleanup, preference/environment restoration, and pristine-source checks passed. [Candidate receipts](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616/artifacts/11380755806) and [baseline receipts](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616/artifacts/11379004102) contain selection cells, installation identities, logs, and strict verification summaries. This covers inspection only at the earlier revision, not current signed-app install/update or upgrade behavior. Preceding failed QA attempts do not establish this result.

<details>
<summary>Historical CI and source qualification</summary>

[CI 37194001816](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001816), including native Swift, [macOS Periphery 37194001640](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001640), and [shared OpenClawKit Periphery 37194001665](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001665) passed at earlier head `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b`. Previously reported formatting, whitespace checks, and scoped Codex AutoReview remain historical proof, not a fresh review of the current head.

</details>

Maintainer review remains separate. The fixture-only follow-up changed no production source. The current head also includes the 31 October main merge. Swift owner tests, real installation, and app upgrade remain unverified for the current head; skipped CI lanes do not supply that proof.

prs.title: fix(ui): match dashboard gallery search against NFC queries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The dashboards gallery search hid matching cards when the query and session text used different Unicode canonical forms. A composed `münchen` query did not find a dashboard titled with decomposed text, and the reverse mismatch also failed for titles, authors, previews, and keys.

## User Impact

Users typing normal composed text in the dashboards search box can miss sessions whose display names, author labels, previews, or keys came from decomposed sources. ASCII queries were unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gallery filter lowercased both operands for case-insensitivity but left Unicode canonical forms unequal. Local comparison copies need NFC on the query and every matched row field, matching the Logs, activity, chat, skills, and Usage filters already fixed on main.

## Evidence

Red/green unit tests in `ui/src/pages/dashboards/view.test.tsx`:

- On base, the NFC-query case fails: NFC `münchen` against an NFD title yields no `[data-dashboard-session]`.
- With this fix, the full file is 7/7 green under `test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts`.
- Sibling `dashboards-page.test.tsx` stays 5/5 green.
- Production change is comparison-only in `visibleDashboardRows`. No Gateway, export, or persistence changes.

## Merge danger

**Two-way door:** a revert restores earlier lowercase-only matching. Blast radius is local dashboards gallery filtering. Faulty comparison could hide or show unexpected cards; it cannot alter stored sessions or Gateway writes.

prs.title: fix(ui): match config form search against NFC queries

## What Problem This Solves

The Settings config form search hid matching fields when the query and field text used different Unicode canonical forms. A composed `münchen` query did not match a field description stored with decomposed text, and `tag:` filters with diacritics failed the same way against NFD field tags.

## User Impact

Users typing normal composed text into config search could not find fields whose labels, help, enum text, or tags came from decomposed sources. Tag filters failed the same way against NFD field tags.

## Why This Change Was Made

The default text matcher and tag matcher lowercased operands for ASCII case-insensitivity but left Unicode canonical forms unequal. Local comparison copies need NFC on both sides so search behaves like the existing Logs, skills, activity, and chat filters.

## Evidence

Red/green node unit tests in `ui/src/components/config-form.search.node.test.ts`:

- On base, the two new cases fail: NFC query vs NFD description, and NFC/NFD `tag:` criteria vs NFD field tags.
- With this fix, the full file is 12/12 green under `test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts`.
- Production change is comparison-only: `defaultTextMatcher` and `matchesTags` NFC both operands after lowercase. No schema, hint, Gateway, or persistence changes.

## Merge danger

**Two-way door:** a revert restores earlier lowercase-only matching. Blast radius is local Settings config search visibility. Faulty comparison could hide or show unexpected fields in the form filter; it cannot change saved config values, authorization, or Gateway writes.

prs.title: fix(ui): normalize canonical Unicode in local search comparisons
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three Control UI searches can hide existing results when query and source text use canonically equivalent Unicode forms:

- Configuration field descriptions and authored `tag:` filters.
- Usage details' conversation filter.
- Dashboard gallery titles, authors, previews and keys.

## User Impact

A composed accented query now finds decomposed text, and a decomposed query finds composed text. Case-insensitive and ASCII matching keep working. Displayed text, configuration values, transcript content, tags and session keys are not rewritten.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each owning browser-local comparison lowercases its operands but previously left canonical forms unequal. Apply NFC after the existing lowercase operation on both query and candidate copies. Keep the existing predicates, tag conjunctions, role/tool filters, sort behavior and data ownership; no shared normalization policy or new helper API is introduced.

The dashboard change touches only query/candidate normalization. It does not change agent scoping or incorporate #188486. Logs normalization is already on main and is not duplicated here.

Includes @huwei-xydt's fixes from #189829, #189834 and #189853, cherry-picked with contributor authorship retained.

## Evidence

Built Gateway and matching built Control UI served in secretless `node:24.22.1` Docker, driven by real Chromium. On each of the three surfaces, two fresh browser contexts per revision exercised NFC-query/NFD-source and NFD-query/NFC-source, plus an ASCII control:

| Surface | Main, twice in each direction | Candidate, twice in each direction | ASCII control |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Configuration editor | No matching setting | Expected field and original value visible | Unchanged |
| Usage conversation | 0 matching messages | Expected original message visible | Unchanged |
| Dashboard gallery | 0 matching cards | Expected original card visible | Unchanged |

Configuration metadata came from a real disk-loaded fixture plugin. Dashboards were created through `sessions.create` and `board.widget.put`. Usage data came from real agent turns against the maintained deterministic local QA provider, with a decomposed assistant message appended through the supported `chat.inject` RPC. No browser Gateway mock or database edits were used. Persisted raw values were checked after filtering.

The three focused owner files pass **35/35** tests; focused lint and formatting pass. Bidirectional authored tags share the existing conjunction case, and Usage's retained stale-count fixture now also exercises canonical filtering. New duplicate fixture blocks were removed. Production +15/-7 (net +8), tests +10/-10 (net 0), docs +8; no SDK exports, schema, index or permission changes.

See the [paired screenshots and detailed receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189874#issuecomment-6550765240).

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous local matching behavior, with no persistent migration to undo. Blast radius is these three browser-local filters; an incorrect comparison could hide or overmatch visible results, but does not change server authorization or stored data.

prs.body:
Related: #167980 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: opening the Control UI in a browser without module-script support leaves a blank page because neither the app nor its modern recovery script can execute. ## User Impact User impact: affected browsers immediately show “This browser is not supported”, an instruction to update the browser/system WebView, and the troubleshooting link. Retry and wait controls are hidden. The established browser floor and supported-browser startup behavior stay unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made A separate ES5 inline script reuses the existing recovery panel before the module entry. The Gateway's existing CSP hashing authorizes it. A literal foreground color is assigned in this legacy branch so the notice remains readable without CSS variables, including after production minification. The change is limited to the static notice, its regression tests, and documentation. It contains no legacy API polyfills and makes no Chromium 114 or Telegram Mini App compatibility claim. ## Evidence Validated commit: `fb9fdf6c7d7751080c9e798ca3b893d1ebf70904`. - Notice regression suite: **16/16 passed** (`pnpm test ui/src/app/mount-fallback.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`; 6.00 s runner wall time, 3.60 s Vitest duration), including ES5 parsing and supported-browser behavior. - UI type checking, type-aware lint, formatting, i18n verification, and line-count ratchets passed. Production UI build passed. - Independent Codex autoreview found a foreground-color issue; the fix was verified against the final minified output and the browser proof below. - Hosted [control-ui-performance check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38405102432/job/115323686861) passed on this commit. The full [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38405102432) and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. [ClawSweeper's review of this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167999#issuecomment-6090490517) found no actionable issues, accepted the screenshots as sufficient proof, and marked the PR ready for maintainer review. ### Browser proof | Scenario | Result | | --- | --- | | Chromium 60.0.3112.0, before | Blank page | | Chromium 60.0.3112.0, after | Notice visible, retry/wait hidden | | Chromium 60, inline CSS-variable declarations removed | Notice remains readable; foreground `rgb(244, 244, 245)` | | Chrome 155.0.8059.39 | Connected synthetic chat and composer | | Chrome 155, overlay capability removed | Existing browser-floor rejection preserved | **Before — Chromium 60** **After — Chromium 60** **Supported browser — Chrome 155** Proof uses the production `serveControlUiIndexHtml` handler and security headers, a task-owned asset server, and a mocked Gateway WebSocket. All three candidate inline-script hashes were authorized by the served CSP. This is not a full Gateway or Telegram device run. The baseline uses exact base `43c68c34df7` HTML with candidate asset references; it is not a full base build. The CSS-variable case is a narrow simulation, not a pre-Chrome-49 browser run.
Local performance comparison discrepancy The separate local `pnpm ui:check-performance:base 43c68c34df71bed694fc4b1de0725f5e7495b8c1` run failed the absolute startup-JS budget (411,322 B versus 374,861 B). Its base comparison showed +38 B for chat boot, +44 B for new-session boot, and unchanged CSS. The hosted performance check linked above passed; the local discrepancy is recorded rather than claimed resolved.

prs.title: fix(bench): mobile log scrolling fails before anchor checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the mobile `data-logs-scroll` benchmark failing before it can verify reader anchoring: Playwright rejects wheel input on mobile WebKit, and the mobile Chromium census row times out at an unidentified scroll-boundary wait.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible product change. The mobile benchmark can now check that a live Logs tail preserves a reader's position and that the reader can return to the newest line.

## Why This Change Was Made

For mobile viewports, a native tap enters the existing Logs touch-input handler before a native scrollport jump to each edge. Desktop retains its existing hover/wheel path. The top-arrival, deferred-tail, first-retained-line, zero-offset, bottom-arrival, and newest-line assertions are unchanged.

This checks touch admission and scrollport navigation, not swipe physics, inertia, or wheel latency. The original failed census observations remain failure evidence; the exact cause of Chromium's original generic timeout is still unknown. No production UI, startup dependency, or budget changes.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm tsgo:scripts` | Passed once |
| Scoped oxlint for `scripts/lib/control-ui-data-log-scenarios.ts` | Passed once |
| Format check on both changed files; `git diff --check` | Passed |
| Independent local Codex autoreview, P0–P2, complete two-file patch against `ac8d31250fed1d3745d968014598317c70592f60` | Scoped-clean, no findings; reviewed before the browser proof |
| Native `data-logs-scroll`, mobile 390×844, Chromium 156.0.8078.4, CPU 1×, localhost, one pair | Passed; 2,000 retained lines; zero error events |
| Same native cell, WebKit 27.2 | Passed; 2,000 retained lines; zero error events |

The two browser cells used the same frozen production bundle (source `da5f3bbfcb49d488a7eb0f35ee38b3aa798b2f56`, index SHA-256 `8c1ded9c4a4c2f8622f8bdcd484795e0aaefbed30aa5529f4ab9bd7f5c7c3ee0`) and harness commit `b91de7dfa187d5fcd8f8e2b96d4a361e134f5d76`. This is correctness proof only: one pair without an A/A control does not establish a performance improvement. No new desktop run or UI build was needed for this harness-only change.

LOC: scenario 385 → 399; README 892 → 897; total diff +22/−3. The added branch is the smallest complete mobile input fix, with a README note making its measurement contract explicit.
