prs.title: feat(cron): let human owners manage and transfer automations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Automation owners cannot manage or hand over their schedules from the Automations page without administrator access.

## User Impact and Design

The editor gains an Owner selector beneath Agent. Administrators and the current human owner can edit or transfer an automation; other humans cannot modify it. Agent-created jobs retain separate conversation-scoped capability checks.

A transfer pauses the automation, cancels active occurrences, and retires captured execution authority. The recipient cannot silently use the previous owner's credentials. Trusted human-creator records supply the initial owner without rewriting audit provenance. Ordinary edits, force-run, or transferring back do not satisfy the requirement for fresh execution-authority capture.

The Gateway owns authorization and retirement; the UI reflects its decisions. Human ownership, immutable creator provenance, and agent/session capability stay separate. Host-command, session-routing, tool and approval restrictions are preserved. Requested by @VACInc.

## Review Repairs

Initial five findings repaired in `9b34a698` (original `3de16314`):
- Private `ownerTransferPending` distinguishes actual transfers from legacy app-only recovery.
- Pending transfers are blocked before isolated/main/named-session dispatch; only fresh private authority capture clears the guard.
- Profile-directory reads obey visibility, attachment and Gateway lifecycle admission.
- E2E inventory, direct run/remove commit-guard assertions and keyboard navigation are updated.

The active-execution finding on `156ed1d1` is repaired in **`49f55e04`**: the existing committed-mutation cancellation owner now cancels when human ownership changes, including force-runs of already-paused jobs. Explicit-disable cancellation remains intact, while display edits and unchanged ownership do not cancel. This adds two net production lines, not another revocation mechanism.

## Current Candidate and Proof

Published head **`be693bc6c568c5c5778925a324844710410173b1`** has exactly the tested `49f55e04` tree. Rebased onto `7232a8de67eff527b3f5764987312f2424beda94` as requested; the rebase tree matched an independent integration oracle. Upstream Memory/hovercard fixes were preserved, not replaced with obsolete assertions. Human credit and authored repairs were retained.

- **Final-head CI passed:** [run 41253288557](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41253288557). Pre-merge full check snapshot: **100 success, 66 skipped, 1 neutral, zero failed or pending**. Both real-Gateway E2E shards passed, including the active-transfer scenario.
- **Active transfer red/green:** on `156ed1d1`, both enabled/paused scheduler cases fail because cancellation never arrives, and the real Gateway/browser run incorrectly completes successfully after transfer. With `49f55e04`, scheduler **3/3 pass** and real-Gateway/browser **1/1 passes**.
- The browser proof first executes a real file-write tool through a local HTTP model with a synthetic credential. It then holds another model response during a force-run of a paused job, transfers ownership, and releases an attempted write. The run terminates with the transfer cancellation reason, the file does not exist, and no further provider request occurs. Former-owner denial, recipient edits, and isolated/shared recovery failures remain covered. No paid/external model or real credential is claimed.
- Local repair timings: scheduler 0.641 s test / 50.61 s wall including worker preparation; browser 6.827 s test / 55.42 s Vitest wall. The existing browser boot is reused. **41 net test lines** are allocated for the distinct in-flight boundary; no new suite or timeout increase.
- Targeted lint, formatting, canonical Cron and UI-E2E typechecks, and diff checks passed. Fresh independent P0–P2 autoreview of the repair is **scoped-clean**. Simplification retained the existing cancellation owner.
- **Latest-stable upgrade passed:** [run 41251264471](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41251264471), baseline **2026.10.8**, pinned package/workflow `156ed1d1`, both `base` and `cron-scheduled-authority` scenarios successful. Package integrity and npm install acceptance also passed. This is explicitly pre-repair-head evidence: the only later production change is post-commit active-run cancellation; schemas, migration, persisted fields, recovery and startup are unchanged. Current-head cancellation behavior is separately proven above. No image publication or deployment.

### Retained earlier proof and disclosed gaps

- Scheduler/session/fallback/store **44/44**, including legacy creator backfill, app-only recovery, transfer back, persistence and fresh-authority recovery. Four behavior regressions fail on original base `fd55221c` and pass with the fix; ownership UI likewise fails on the base.
- Gateway policy **21/21**, ownership UI **1/1**, E2E inventory **14/14**, production types/lint/build passed. Earlier lifecycle suite **33/34**: the cold lazy-render failure reproduced on untouched original base. A separate cold local rebased run timed out before Gateway readiness; the subsequently expanded red/green scenario reached the actual behavior, and final-head CI passed. Neither setup failure is counted as passing proof.
- Notice fixture repair preserves requester/foreign-job nondisclosure and write denial. Upstream Memory/hovercard expectations are retained; no production permission relaxation.
- An earlier local-review migration suggestion was declined because an unmerged, undeployed intermediate revision is not a shipped compatibility contract. Released stored-data compatibility is covered by the upgrade and legacy tests above.

## Visual Proof

Actual source UI, same synthetic fixture, Chromium 1440×1000, before original base and after `a58a740`; this UI is unchanged by the rebase and cancellation repair. Both sanitized captures were inspected, attached in the originating chat, and uploaded in [the proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189749#issuecomment-6549285963). Both images were also verified rendering at 1440×1000 in the actual GitHub PR page and those rendered screenshots inspected. Visual gate complete.

![Before: automation editor without human owner selector](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d7dd878-df73-421c-b7c4-5c5352c6f449)

![After: human Owner selector directly below Agent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01d3e8f5-c4b6-459c-9fd5-278f8ad72980)

**Final-head ClawSweeper review complete:** [review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189749#issuecomment-6549030790), reviewed `be693bc6` at 2026-11-01 00:06 UTC. No findings, no before-merge items, ready for maintainer review. No live Gateway, deployment, or user automation was modified.

## Worked on by

- @VACInc

prs.title: fix(daemon): avoid repeated Windows scheduler engine drift warnings
prs.body:
Supersedes #167827, thanks @xydigitLybnnnn.
Fixes #167778.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated Windows service drift warnings when Task Scheduler exports `UseUnifiedSchedulingEngine=true` for an otherwise healthy Gateway task.

## User Impact

Status and Doctor stop treating this known scheduler-populated value as an unexplained edit. Real launcher and account changes still appear, and replacement/publication checks continue protecting the engine value from silent loss. No migration or user action is required; native Windows execution was not independently repeated here.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing comparison owner accepts only the known `true` value during reporting, alongside its existing `false` default. It retains strict comparisons when a replacement command or prepared XML is supplied. Account aliases already use SID equivalence from #169481.

This independently reimplemented replacement adds five production lines, two documentation lines, and 28 regression-test lines. There is no equivalent dead or duplicate code in this owner to remove safely. The separate 28-line test allocation covers the reporting regression, a real launcher-drift control, and publication protection; the shared baseline scalar is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Base: current main `c633ec6376e1ce6cdf6268f98d1c86eb9395b074`. The new reporting regression fails with `unknown-edit` for `Settings.UseUnifiedSchedulingEngine`; the other 15 cases pass.
- Fixed: `pnpm test src/daemon/service-audit-schtasks.windows.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes all 16 cases, including launcher drift, mismatched/unresolvable account identities, omitted defaults, and engine-change rejection during publication. Local wall time: 41.03 seconds (Vitest: 38.45 seconds, mostly initial compilation; individual new cases: 23 ms and 21 ms). [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41254801185) passed in 475 seconds overall.
- Consumer proof: `pnpm test src/daemon/service-audit.definition-facts.test.ts src/daemon/service-definition-backup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes 105 tests in 30.12 seconds wall time.
- Targeted service test typecheck, changed-file Oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Broad CI and the combined security/CI gate passed before native landing.
- Autoreview: Codex, local candidate against `c633ec6376e1`, P0–P3, `scoped-clean`; no accepted findings. The subsequent test-allocation correction matches the measured 28-line growth.
- Task Scheduler I/O is synthetic in the focused tests; native Windows registration and a live Windows CLI run were not performed. The contributor's Windows observations remain separately documented in #167827. Contributor code was read with `gh pr view/diff` only and was never checked out or executed on this host.

prs.title: fix(daemon): stop flagging Task Scheduler-normalized Windows task fields
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, `openclaw update status --json` reports a permanent `serviceDefinition.drift` entry of kind `unknown-edit` for `Settings.UseUnifiedSchedulingEngine`. Task Scheduler can populate that element as `true` on registration even though the installer's XML never sets it, so a healthy task is misread as an unexplained operator edit:

- `update status` surfaces it as a permanent warning.
- `openclaw doctor` marks the service as custom/unexpected (`needsAggressive` in `doctor-gateway-services.ts`), so automatic service repair is refused behind `--force`.

Fixes #167778.

## Scope after merging `main`

The run-as account normalization (`Triggers.LogonTrigger.UserId` / `Principals.Principal.UserId`) this PR originally carried is now owned by upstream **#169481** ("recognize Scheduled Task account aliases", merged to `main` on 2026-10-12) with its own Windows test (`src/daemon/service-audit-schtasks.windows.test.ts`). After merging `main`, this PR keeps only the still-unique change:

- **Scheduler-owned setting (`nativeManaged`):** a non-default `true` is suppressed **only while reporting** a definition. When the caller supplies a prepared definition (transactional replacement via `expectedCommand`, or publication verification via `expectedXml`), it stays reported so a rewrite that cannot retain the value stays protected.
- **Native default (`nativeDefaults`):** `UseUnifiedSchedulingEngine: "false"` stays in the schema-default table, so an exported explicit `false` is never treated as an operator edit.

| installed value | reporting (`update status` / Doctor) | prepared definition (replacement / publication verification) |
|---|---|---|
| absent | no finding | no finding |
| `false` (native default) | no finding | no finding |
| `true` (non-default) | no finding (#167778) | `unknown-edit` (rewrite protected) |

Net diff vs `main`: 2 files, +44/−2.

## Evidence

### Windows end-to-end evidence (live Task Scheduler)

**Environment:** Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC `10.0.17763` (build 17763); openclaw `2026.9.9` / this head.

Registration **via `schtasks /Create /XML`** (repo `buildScheduledTaskXml`): stored definition has **no** `UseUnifiedSchedulingEngine`.
Registration **via the Task Scheduler service/COM path** (`Register-ScheduledTask`): stored definition has **`UseUnifiedSchedulingEngine=true`**, plus the canonicalized account (`Principal.UserId` = SID, `LogonTrigger.UserId` = `MACHINE\user`).

`schtasks /Create /XML` **rejects** the element, so the installer's only registration mechanism cannot submit or carry it:

```
schtasks /Create /TN <name> /XML <file> /F
ERROR: The task XML contains an unexpected node.
(37,7):UseUnifiedSchedulingEngine:
```

### Shipped CLI evidence (Windows)

Built this head (Node 24.21) and registered the Gateway task from the repo's own `buildScheduledTaskXml`, then set `UseUnifiedSchedulingEngine=true` through the Task Scheduler service (COM) API.

```
$ node openclaw.mjs update status --json
serviceDefinition.drift = []          # "UseUnifiedSchedulingEngine" occurrences: 0

$ node openclaw.mjs doctor
                                      # "UseUnifiedSchedulingEngine" occurrences: 0

# definition unchanged by inspection (exported XML content hash):
CONTENT_SHA256_BEFORE = 9f0849e0db305600fefa101f8f9014f5b701a2a28af867d83166fc2d077925cf
CONTENT_SHA256_AFTER  = 9f0849e0db305600fefa101f8f9014f5b701a2a28af867d83166fc2d077925cf
```

Control: when an earlier COM call also altered the run level, the only drift reported was `Principals.Principal.LogonType` — so the empty result is a real "no drift", not a skipped audit.

## On the "preserve the engine setting on replacement" finding

Because the XML import rejects `<UseUnifiedSchedulingEngine>`, the installer cannot express the field; `preserveServicePolicyXml` cannot target a node the OS refuses to accept. The field is only ever populated by the Task Scheduler service/COM path, i.e. it is scheduler-owned rather than installer-authored. This PR therefore suppresses a non-default value **only while reporting**, and keeps it reported during replacement/publication so an existing preference is never silently discarded by this change.

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/daemon/service-audit.definition-facts.test.ts
 ✓ tolerates the scheduler-forced UseUnifiedSchedulingEngine value
 ✓ keeps the scheduler engine setting protected during replacement
 ✓ tolerates the native default engine value during replacement
```

prs.title: feat: link Discord accounts from personal profiles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

People need to connect their own Discord account to their signed-in OpenClaw profile without asking an administrator to attest the link, and retain their existing session permissions when requesting work from Discord.

## User Impact

User impact: Settings → Profile gains Discord account linking, verified linked-ID status, and disconnect directly below Linked emails and above GitHub account. Linked members keep their actual allowed operator scopes in channel runs; linking does not grant administrator or command-owner privileges.

Deployment requires the selected Discord application's existing OAuth client configuration and the Gateway callback URL registered with Discord. Live Discord OAuth deployment qualification has not been performed; this PR does not change live configuration or credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

The flow reuses the personal-profile authorization boundary, provider-browser callback owner, and canonical channel-identity store. Discord proves the immutable user ID with the `identify` scope; short-lived one-use state and an initiating-browser cookie bind the callback. Conflicting links are rejected, and administrative attestation endpoints remain administrator-only.

prs.title: fix(acp): bind delayed ACP spawn dispatch to its child incarnation
prs.body:
Closes #133612

## What Problem This Solves

An in-flight ACP spawn could admit its original task into a child session that an operator reset or deleted and recreated before the first Gateway dispatch reached the admission owner. The delayed `agent` dispatch carried only the logical session key, so once the successor incarnation occupied that key the old spawn's work was admitted into it instead of being rejected as stale.
- `launchAcpChildThroughGateway` sent `sessionKey` but no committed child-session identity, and `spawnAcpDirect` did not forward the initialized child's identity.
- The launch request now carries `expectedExistingSessionId` and `expectedExistingSessionLifecycleRevision` (or `null` when absent). Both flow through the existing Gateway `agent` expected-session path (`agent-request-preflight.ts` → admission controller → `assertExpectedExistingSession`), which rejects the dispatch once that incarnation is retired. Reset preserves the session ID but bumps `lifecycleRevision`; delete/recreate changes both.
- What did NOT change: public `agent` RPC logical-session-key semantics, the admission controller, session-work admission handoff, successor-safe spawn cleanup, and normal accepted-child behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ACP spawn owns the child incarnation it provisioned, not whichever session later occupies that key. The existing admission owner already understands exact-session constraints, so the narrowest fix is to forward the two parameters it already supports — no new protocol, config, schema, or dependency. A session-ID-only constraint would have missed the same-ID reset schedule.

Alternative: the process-local session-work admission handoff mentioned in the issue. The expected-session constraint is strictly smaller and reuses the landed admission path; the handoff would duplicate authority the admission owner already provides.

## User Impact

An operator reset or delete/recreate of a child session while its first ACP dispatch is in flight no longer admits the old spawn's work into the successor. The stale dispatch is rejected before the successor starts work, and failure cleanup leaves the successor session intact. Ordinary spawns behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

Current head: `a7062b6e1bd` (rebased onto current main; mergeable/CLEAN with 60 checks passing). Command:

```text
pnpm test src/agents/subagents/spawn/acp-spawn.authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
...
✓ rejects a held ACP spawn dispatch after the child lifecycle owner applies reset 7823ms
✓ rejects a held ACP spawn dispatch after the child lifecycle owner applies delete and recreate 6779ms
✓ accepts the unchanged ACP child and executes its synthetic runtime turn 24366ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       13 passed (13)
```

The new cases drive the real `sessions_spawn` ACP tool through the real in-process façade/dispatch, with a synthetic ACP runtime backend and the real session lifecycle owner:
- **reset**: hold the first `agent` dispatch, apply `sessions.reset` to the child (same session ID, new `lifecycleRevision`), release. The dispatch rejects with "changed"; the synthetic runtime's `runTurn`, `ensureSession`, and `closeRuntime` are never called; the successor session entry and ACP runtime handle remain.
- **delete and recreate**: hold, delete the child row, reinitialize a successor ACP session, release. The stale dispatch rejects with "changed"; no successor backend execution; the successor entry and handle remain.
- **unchanged child**: no mutation; the spawn is accepted and the synthetic ACP `runTurn` actually executes for the provisioned child handle with the expected text.
- The gate also asserts the dispatched `expectedExistingSessionId`/`expectedExistingSessionLifecycleRevision` equal the committed child entry. With the production forwarding removed, those fields are absent and the cases fail — the regression is effective.

A synthetic ACP backend through the real spawn/Gateway/lifecycle owners is the confirmation path requested in the review; no dispatch or session-store mock is used for the final-effect cases.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. It traces the ACP spawn launch path (`acp-spawn.ts` → `acp-spawn-gateway.ts`) against the Gateway admission owner (`agent-request-preflight.ts`, admission controller, `assertExpectedExistingSession`) to find the delayed dispatch was unbound from the provisioned child incarnation. The fix forwards the initialized session ID and lifecycle revision through the existing constraint, covering both reset and recreate.

prs.title: fix(browser): omit unparsable gateway hint from extension pairing
prs.body:
Closes #186454

## What Problem This Solves

A browser node whose relay is local but whose Gateway is remote receives a pairing string the shipped Chrome extension always rejects, so setup ends at "Manual setup required (malformed_response)".
- Problem: for `gateway.mode: "remote"` over plaintext `ws://`, the pairing builder copied the remote Gateway URL into the optional `gateway` hint even though the extension accepts only `wss://` or loopback `ws://` hints. `parseGatewayHint` returned null, so `validatePairingFields` rejected a pairing whose relay URL and token were valid.
- Solution: publish the optional hint only when the extension can parse it. The relay URL, token, and relay validation are unchanged.
- What changed: one shared URL predicate in `extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-pairing.ts` now drives both relay-URL validation and hint emission; a regression test covers the plaintext remote case in `extension-pairing.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: the extension's URL policy, relay transport validation, `wss://` hint behavior, and `--gateway-url` validation errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The producer emitted optional metadata its only consumer is guaranteed to reject; fixing the producer keeps the plaintext-connection restriction intact.
- Best fix: omit unusable optional hints at the producer instead of relaxing the extension's URL policy (a plaintext non-loopback Gateway is still refused).
- Alternative: make the extension tolerate the hint — rejected because the hint carries no authority and widening that check increases risk for every pairing.
- Risk / non-goals: only the unusable-hint case changes; local loopback hints and `wss://` remote hints keep their current bytes.

## User Impact

`openclaw browser extension pair` and the native macOS bootstrap now hand the installed extension a pairing it accepts when the browser node uses a local relay in front of a plaintext remote Gateway, instead of requiring manual setup.

## Evidence

End-to-end on this branch: the shipped CLI produced the pairing string, the installed unpacked extension (Google Chrome 138, MV3 service worker) accepted it, and the extension authenticated to the real loopback relay daemon.

```text
$ openclaw browser extension pair --json          # this branch
{"pairingString":"ws://127.0.0.1:19199/extension#<token>","relayPort":19199,"remote":false}

Chrome 138 + unpacked extension, relay daemon on 127.0.0.1:19199:
[1] pre-fix CLI pairing (…?gateway=ws%3A%2F%2F192.168.1.20%3A8080…)
    extension parse : null
    pair message    : {"ok":false,"error":"Invalid pairing string."}
[2] fixed CLI pairing (…/extension#<token>)
    extension parse : {"relayUrl":"ws://127.0.0.1:19199/extension","token":"<token>"}
    pair message    : {"ok":true}
    relay daemon    : [browser/extension-relay] extension authenticated and connected to relay
    status          : {"paired":true,"state":"on","relayUrl":"ws://127.0.0.1:19199/extension"}
```

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| browser-node + plaintext `ws://192.168.1.20:8080` | hint emitted, parser returns null, extension rejects | hint omitted, extension pairs and connects |
| browser-node + `wss://gateway.example.com:9444` | parser accepts | parser accepts (unchanged) |
| direct-remote `wss://…:9443` | parser accepts | parser accepts (unchanged) |

The new regression test is red on `origin/main` and green with the fix; the relay integration test still passes:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-pairing.test.ts --run
 ✓ omits a plaintext non-loopback gateway hint that the extension cannot parse
 Test Files  1 passed (1) · Tests  5 passed (5)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-relay/gateway-relay-route.integration.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1) · Tests  9 passed (9)
```

What was not tested: native-host registration and the macOS app bootstrap were not exercised (no macOS host); the CLI entry point, the installed extension, and the standalone relay daemon covered that path instead.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used source reading plus `node --import tsx` and a headless Google Chrome run to trace the pairing builder into the shipped extension and the live relay. The implementer understands the code: the extension rejects any pairing whose `gateway` hint fails its own `isAllowedWebSocketUrl` check, so the producer must not emit a hint that check rejects. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/188252

## What Problem This Solves

Levanto registration eagerly loads Sage evaluation modules before an eligible decision request exists.

## User Impact

Registration and rejected calls avoid loading execution. Native results, prepared credentials, deadlines, cancellation, authority and resource settlement retain their existing owners. No startup or latency improvement is claimed.

prs.title: fix: another person's mid-turn group message is dropped instead of queued
prs.body:
Related: #157806

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in a group chat, a message from a second person is dropped while someone else's turn is running, and the sender gets an admin-facing refusal ("collaborative steering is disabled … resend as `/followup`").

## User Impact

User impact: with the default `messages.queue.allowCollaborativeSteering: false`, another person's mid-turn message is now queued as their own turn and runs after the current one, under their own identity and current permissions. They see the existing "Your message is queued for a new turn…" notice instead of a refusal. Nothing is dropped, and nobody needs to know about `/followup` or the config key. Operators who set `allowCollaborativeSteering: true` keep cross-person steering. Same-requester steering, queue caps, explicit `/followup` and access checks are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

#157806 correctly stopped one person's input from steering another person's execution with that execution's permissions. It enforced that by refusing the input. The same guarantee holds if the input instead becomes the sender's own followup turn, which the existing `requester-mismatch` followup path already supports. This change routes the disabled-collaboration case into that path on both the channel and `chat.send` entry points. It also removes the refusal helper, notice and its plumbing.

The session controller still rejects cross-requester injection into a live run. Only the reason changes, to the existing `requester_origin_mismatch`, so callers queue the followup instead of refusing.

## Evidence

**Targeted tests (exact head `0eef404`, rebased on current `main`):** 128 tests pass across steering fallback, native `/steer` → followup, `chat.send` direct followup and steering custody, message injection and the message-join controller. `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint, `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` are clean. With only the production changes reverse-applied, the new followup assertions fail (3 + 1 + 1 cases).

**Live Telegram Test Server userbot proof** ([details](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184846#issuecomment-6431055902)). One DM conversation; the first requester is the Gateway operator (`chat.send`), the second is the real Telegram user; the mock model is held so the first turn stays active.

| elapsed | Telegram |
| --- | --- |
| 30.4 s | Telegram user sends a message mid-turn |
| 31.4 s | SUT: "Your message is queued for a new turn after the current turn finishes…" |
| 50.9 s | SUT replies in the Telegram user's own turn after the first turn is released |

- The held operator turn's model request does **not** contain the Telegram user's text. Later requests are the user's separate turn.
- The Gateway logs `steering rejected; applying follow-up policy {"reason":"requester-mismatch", … "activeRunId":"proof-operator-turn-1"}`.
- No refusal, `/followup` hint or config key is shown.

**Authority (merge-risk item).** The cross-person message now enters the same followup admission that explicit `/followup` and `messages.queue.mode: "followup"` already use on `main`. This PR adds no new admission path and no new authority. At admission the queued turn:
- runs under the sender's own identity and requester key (asserted in `chat-send-direct-followup.test.ts`), never Alice's;
- re-prepares tool and permission policy from current config (`prepareReplyRunToolAuthority`, `followup-turn-execution.ts:380-386`);
- re-checks owner authority (`agent-runner-admission.ts:41-43`) and operator authority, and a revoked operator authority is consumed without execution (`followup-runner.test.ts:514`).

**Known pre-existing gap, not introduced here.** Channel **sender access** (`allowFrom`, group access) is decided once at ingress and is **not** re-evaluated when a queued followup drains. This is true for every queued followup on `main` today. `docs/concepts/session-controller.md` says "Authorization policy belongs at ingress", and Telegram's `channels.telegram.{dmPolicy,allowFrom,groupAllowFrom,groupPolicy}` reload as no-ops "captured at ingress/turn admission" (#146129).
- A live run confirmed it: removing the user from `allowFrom` through hot-reload `config.patch` while their message waited did not stop that queued turn.
- The narrow fix belongs in the channel message-access owner: a sender-access assertion composed into followup admission, like owner authority. It changes behavior for all queued channel input, so it will ship as a separate PR rather than widening this one.

**Data compatibility.** The removed `collaborative-steering-disabled` / `collaborative_steering_disabled` values lived only in in-memory admission state, transient injection outcomes and a diagnostics `reason` string.
- No database row, durable queue entry, receipt or schema stores or parses them.
- Refused input had no queue or recovery custody (old docs), so existing data cannot contain them.
- The config key and its persisted Doctor default (`false`) are unchanged. Omitted, `false` and `true` all keep loading; only the runtime behavior of `false` changes.

**Gap:** in the `chat.send` path the queued admission records `steering-unavailable` rather than `requester-mismatch`; the user-facing notice is identical.

prs.title: fix(skills): skill picker titles skills from embedded boilerplate headings
prs.body:
Closes #184724

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: skills that embed a shared boilerplate section in their SKILL.md body all render that section's heading as their title in the composer skill picker, so distinct skills can appear with identical labels.

## User Impact

User impact: a skill's picker title now comes from a heading that opens the skill's own body — the SKILL.md convention — instead of the first `#` heading found anywhere in the body. Skills that embed a shared reference section keep distinct labels. This changes title selection for skills whose first heading follows introductory prose; that policy requires maintainer review.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSkillDisplayName` matched the first ATX `#` heading anywhere in the body (`/m` flag) and used the frontmatter `name` only when the body had no heading at all. The Agent Skills spec treats frontmatter `name` as the skill identity, and a heading buried in the body is ordinary prose that often belongs to embedded shared content — in the reporter's install, the embedded spec's `# AI-First Note Rules` heading sits at the end of 47 of 49 skills and titles all of them.

The display title now requires the heading to open the body (after leading blank lines). Later headings fall back to the skill's identity: the frontmatter `name`, then the humanized directory name. Skills whose body starts with their own title — including every bundled and custodian skill and the pinned library flow, which asserts heading-derived display titles for such skills — keep the exact display they have today. Anchoring to the body opening preserves the deliberate heading-title design (the library flow's "keeps the heading separate from the selected command identity" behavior) while removing the boilerplate pollution the issue reports.

## Evidence

- New unit tests in `src/skills/loading/skill-materializer.test.ts`. Against unpatched `origin/main`, exactly the boilerplate case fails (title came out as "AI-First Note Rules" from the embedded section at the end of the body); with the fix all four cases pass: boilerplate heading ignored ("Obsidian Save" from the frontmatter name), body-opening heading kept ("Short Description"), title heading after leading blank lines kept, and the humanized fallback without any heading.
- Every existing assertion is unchanged: `skills.test.ts` heading-derived display, `library/service.test.ts` "keeps the heading separate from the selected command identity" (heading case still renders "Friendly Title"), and the bundled/custodian skills whose bodies open with their titles.
- `pnpm test` passes on all suites exercising the materializer and its consumers: `src/skills/loading/`, `src/skills/library/`, `src/skills/discovery/`, skills runtime resources, embedded agent runner skill-runtime suites, and the CLI live session registry. The one red file, `workspace-skill-sync.runtime.test.ts` ("preserving unchanged destinations"), fails identically on unpatched `origin/main` on this machine (macOS temp-dir ENOENT) and is untouched by this PR.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck core, typecheck core tests, lint, formatting, and the guard lanes pass. The only red lane is the pre-existing `deadcode` unused-export scan, which flags three exports in files this PR does not touch (`src/infra/sqlite-worker-operation-settlement.ts`, `src/boards/board-store.fixtures.test-support.ts`, `src/commands/cleanup-command.test-support.ts`); no path owned by this PR appears in its output.


**Follow-up:** Leading blank lines are now skipped without stripping indentation from the first content line, so an indented code block is not treated as a title. The new regression failed on the prior PR head and passed with this change. The materializer and library suites passed (28 tests); targeted lint, formatting and core typecheck passed. The full changed check was stopped before completion. The isolated autoreview completed on the full PR branch with an available account model and reported no actionable P0–P2 findings. Real Gateway picker proof and the title-precedence decision remain outstanding.

**AI-assisted**

## What Problem This Solves
The Gateway RPC `cron.list` already supports filtering by enabled state, schedule kind, last run status, trigger, and sorting by column/direction, but the `openclaw cron list` CLI only exposes `--all`, `--agent`, `--query`, and `--json`. ## User Impact
Operators can now run e.g. `openclaw cron list --enabled disabled --schedule-kind cron --sort-by name --sort-dir desc` to find disabled cron-schedule automations sorted by name, instead of inspecting the full list manually.


prs.title: fix(telegram): preserve reset-aware conversation naming lifecycle
prs.body:
Related: #183368 (one-shot refinement follow-up), #174317 (landed Dashboard refinement).

## What Problem This Solves

Reset and control-only turns can rename a Telegram DM topic (and its mirrored WebUI session title) from the command text itself: after `/reset` or a model switch, the "first turn after reset" path arms automatic naming from the service-command body, so a long-running topic like "YouGile" silently becomes a description of the model change before any substantive message arrives. The naming lifecycle also conflated one-shot in-conversation refinement with reset/new lifecycle transitions, and stale inference could overwrite an observed manual rename.

## User Impact

- `/reset`, `/model` and other service commands never arm or produce an automatic rename; the topic keeps its current name.
- After a reset, a substantive message re-checks the previous name: if the conversation continues the same task (e.g. YouGile/CRM), the old name is preserved; only a real topic change gets a new generated name.
- `/new` signals a new-topic intent but still requires substantive content before any naming.
- Manually set names (Telegram side or WebUI side) keep priority over automatic inference across reset/new transitions and both sync directions.
- A generated creation title keeps a skip-next marker only for new generated names; captionless media turns count with current media facts instead of hijacking the name.

## Implementation and Scope

- Telegram: non-command guard on the reset-aware first-turn path (`prepareTopicLabelTurn` with lifecycle revisions), refinement store keyed per lifecycle revision, topic-name cache hardening, captionless-media naming, and recovery from failed state-writes.
- Core: `session-title-refinement-state` (new, 123 lines) carries refinement lifecycle state; session rollover/preemption preserve the reset-aware presentation; session-entry projection/public-patch expose the preserved selection without new configurable thresholds.
- Config: `autoTopicLabel` refinement config (opt-in `refine`, defaults clamped), schema labels/help updates, regenerated baselines.
- UI: new-session create/draft params keep generated-title provenance consistent with the server-side skip-next marker.
- SDK surface: two helpers plus state type through the existing `reply-dispatch-runtime` subpath (`advanceConversationLabelRefinement`, `readConversationLabelRefinementSource`); no new subpath or RPC.

Remaining feature diff: 67 files, +4095/-262 (including regenerated config baselines and docs). Branch `reset-aware-topic-naming-20261026`, head `34b63f5cee6f0bd13bdf519ff6f730fbd3f0bde6`, rebased onto current `main` (`c824dc97`).

## Evidence

- 53 focused naming cases pass (topic-label refinement, topic-name cache, media naming, recovery, config precedence), plus infra and Telegram database/recovery shards (~120 tests total) under Node 24.22.1.
- Canonical full build completed (8m 42s) and a self-contained package tarball passed `check-openclaw-package-tarball` integrity, import-graph and declaration screening.
- The packaged runtime was deployed to an isolated test gateway (non-production, mock-LLM): health, control UI bootstrap, and build-info `2026.10.6-b7c0c041` verified live.
- One follow-up test (`retains a later refinement after foreground dispatch settles` in the media refinement suite) still fails: the deferred-dispatch fixture selects the "initial" lifecycle where "refine" is required; fix in progress in the fixture, not in product code.

## Live Proof Still Pending

No live Telegram refinement verdict or screenshot is claimed yet; mocked transport/model tests plus the isolated test-gateway deployment do not replace live evidence. No production deployment or merge is requested.

prs.title: fix: sandbox explain reports channel=(unknown) and allowedByConfig=false for telegram slash sessions
prs.body:
Closes #51245

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw sandbox explain --session telegram:slash:<id>` reports `channel: (unknown)` and `allowedByConfig: false` when the CLI process has no channel plugins registered, even though `tools.elevated.allowFrom.telegram` is configured — so the elevated-policy diagnostic misdirects operators configuring Telegram slash sessions.

## User Impact

Operators running `openclaw sandbox explain` for a Telegram (or any bundled-channel) slash session now see the real channel (`channel: telegram`) and the correct `allowedByConfig` verdict, so they can trust the elevated-allowlist diagnostic instead of chasing a phantom config problem.

## Why This Change Was Made

`sandbox explain` loads plugins with the `sandbox-backends` registry scope (`src/cli/command-catalog.ts`, `["sandbox"]` entry). For stock docker/podman configs `resolveSandboxBackendPluginIds` returns `[]` (core backends are filtered out), and an empty `onlyPluginIds` scope activates an **empty** plugin registry (`src/plugins/loader-runtime-core.ts`, empty-scope fast path). Channel inference in `sandbox-explain.ts` used `normalizeAnyChannelId`, which only consults that runtime registry — so bundled channels could never resolve in this CLI process, and the channel stayed `(unknown)`.

#182406 already normalized session-key aliases (`telegram:slash:123` → `agent:<agent>:telegram:slash:123`), but its tests registered a telegram channel plugin, masking the empty-registry reality of the CLI. The fix falls back to the static bundled-channel catalog (`normalizeChatChannelId`, `src/channels/ids.ts`) after the runtime registry lookup misses. Runtime registry stays first, so plugin-provided aliases keep winning. This matches the direction endorsed by the prior review on the closed attempts (#51584 wanted exactly this static fallback; #51286's raw-key scoping half has since merged as #182406). Diagnostic only — `sandbox explain` authorizes nothing; runtime elevated matching keeps consuming the ingress provider (`get-reply-directives.ts` → `resolveElevatedPermissions`), which is unchanged.

## Evidence

Red/green against `src/commands/sandbox-explain.test.ts`, run with `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/commands/sandbox-explain.test.ts`:

- **Red (pre-fix source + new tests):** two new tests set an empty plugin registry exactly like the real CLI (`createTestRegistry([])`) and assert the downstream fields:
  - "resolves the channel from a slash alias when the CLI registry has no channel plugins" — `telegram:slash:123456` with no stored entry (parsed-key path);
  - "resolves stored delivery channel when the CLI registry has no channel plugins" — stored delivery entry with `channel: "telegram"` (stored-delivery path).
  With `src/commands/sandbox-explain.ts` reverted to the pre-fix revision, both fail: `AssertionError: expected undefined to be 'telegram'` (2 failed | 18 passed).
- **Green (with fix):** same file: `Tests 20 passed (20)`.
- Formatter (`node scripts/run-format.mts --write` on both files) and `node_modules/.bin/oxlint` on both files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Typechecks: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` (prod) and `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs root` (test sources) — both pass.
- An independent fresh-context adversarial review (separate agent) of this diff returned one low-severity finding — missing empty-registry coverage for the stored-delivery path — which this branch addresses with the second test above; its other conclusion: the command remains diagnostic-only and grants no elevated access.

Not verified live against a real Telegram gateway (no Telegram access in this environment); the change is confined to the CLI diagnostic path, which the empty-registry tests reproduce faithfully.

## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, the MCP Events service test fixture can delete its temporary SQLite directory while worker-owned WAL/SHM handles are still closing, producing EBUSY cleanup failures.

prs.title: fix(completion): regenerate core-only caches when setup requests full…
prs.body:
fix(completion): regenerate core-only caches when setup requests full completion

Refs #127450

## What Problem This Solves

Setup asks for a **full** completion cache, meaning core commands plus plugin commands (`ensureCompletionCacheExists(CLI_NAME, { generationMode: "full" })` in `src/wizard/setup.completion.ts`). But `ensureCompletionCacheExists` returned `true` as soon as the cache path existed, whatever mode had built it.

`openclaw update` always rewrites every shell's cache in core-only mode (`tryWriteCompletionCache` sets `OPENCLAW_COMPLETION_SKIP_PLUGIN_COMMANDS=1`). So on a host that has updated before, setup:

1. requests a full cache,
2. finds the core-only file,
3. reports success and installs it unchanged.

Plugin commands then never complete, and setup gives no sign that anything is wrong.

## Change

- **Cached scripts record their mode.** `completion --write-state` adds a final `# openclaw-completion-cache: full` or `# openclaw-completion-cache: core-only` comment to each script. `#` starts a comment in bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell, and the line comes after the script body, so zsh's `#compdef` and the rest of the script are unchanged.
- **Mode is `full` only when plugin commands were actually registered.** A write with `OPENCLAW_COMPLETION_SKIP_PLUGIN_COMMANDS=1`, or one where plugin discovery was skipped because the config is invalid, is recorded as `core-only`.
- **`ensureCompletionCacheExists` checks the mode.** A `full` request reuses the cache only when it is marked `full`. A missing, unreadable, or older unmarked cache is regenerated. A `core-only` request still accepts any existing cache, so the update path behaves as before.
- **Docs:** `docs/cli/completion.md` documents the marker.

Production code grows by about 45 lines across `completion-runtime.ts`, `completion-cli.ts`, and `doctor-completion.ts`. There is no new state file or config key.

## Update behavior

Caches written before this change have no marker. A `core-only` request (`openclaw update`) still accepts them. A `full` request from setup regenerates them once, which is the fix. The next `openclaw update` writes marked core-only caches as usual.

## Deliberately not in scope

The issue's repair direction also suggests build/source identity, config and plugin-inventory identity, fencing for concurrent publication, and keeping the prior generation when a refresh fails. The issue is labeled `needs-product-decision` for those, and each adds ongoing machinery for staleness that is rare, visible, and easy to recover from:

- **Build and plugin changes** are already handled. `openclaw update` refreshes the cache after every upgrade, and `openclaw completion --write-state` rebuilds it on demand. The docs already tell users to run it to pick up plugin commands.
- **Concurrent core/full writers.** Each write is published atomically (`publishOutputFileAtomically`), so readers never see a torn file. If update and setup race, the last writer wins and its marker states truthfully what it contains. The next full request regenerates if needed.
- **Doctor/status health** (`checkShellCompletionStatus().cacheExists`) still checks only that the cache exists. Doctor generates core-only caches itself, so a core-only cache is not a problem for doctor.

## Evidence

- **Regression (`src/commands/doctor-completion.test.ts`):** five cases on a real filesystem, with the generator process mocked:

  | Requested mode | Existing cache | Regenerates? |
  |---|---|---|
  | `full` | `full` | no |
  | `full` | `core-only` | yes |
  | `full` | unmarked | yes |
  | `core-only` | `core-only` | no |
  | `core-only` | unmarked | no |

  With the old existence-only check restored, the `full` over `core-only` and `full` over unmarked cases fail (2 failed, 11 passed). With the fix, all 13 tests pass.
- **Writer (`src/cli/completion-cli.write-state.test.ts`):** a successful plugin registration writes `full`. An invalid config that skips plugins writes `core-only`. The existing byte-exact cache assertions now include the marker line.
- **Real CLI, isolated `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`:**
  - `pnpm openclaw completion --write-state --shell bash` ends with `# openclaw-completion-cache: full`.
  - With `OPENCLAW_COMPLETION_SKIP_PLUGIN_COMMANDS=1`, all four shell caches end with `# openclaw-completion-cache: core-only`.
  - The bash cache passes `bash -n`. zsh, fish, and pwsh are not installed on this host, so those shells' syntax was not checked.

## Tests

`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` (Node 24.22.2):

| File | Result | Wall time |
|---|---|---|
| `src/commands/doctor-completion.test.ts` | 13 passed | 43.3 s |
| `src/cli/completion-cli.write-state.test.ts` | 16 passed | 2.7 s |
| `src/wizard/setup.completion.test.ts` | 10 passed | 6.7 s |
| `src/cli/completion-runtime.test.ts` | 29 passed | 2.3 s |
| `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-post-update.test.ts` | 94 passed | 99.2 s |

Most of the wall time is compiler preparation on a loaded host. The new cases take a few ms each and use no timers, processes, or Gateway boots.

Also clean: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, type-aware `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check`.

prs.title: fix(ui): avoid forbidden requests from restricted operator roles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated forbidden diff requests when an operator requires sandboxing but views a host-workspace conversation, and optional branch/background requests without their required scopes.

## User Impact

Review explains the workspace restriction before making a request. Branch controls stay hidden without write scope, and Appearance skips background reads without read scope. A workspace change during a diff returns retryable `UNAVAILABLE`; genuine authorization denials remain `FORBIDDEN`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Conversation visibility does not imply access to its host files. The existing session-row projection now carries `workspaceReadDisabledReason`, using the same policy as file reads and the existing materialized workspace facts. Sandbox classification consumes the physical row owner already resolved by projection topology; request-facing resolvers retain their strict routing checks. The UI uses its selected-row owner and granted scopes. Server authorization remains authoritative. No new configuration, cache, database schema, or protocol version.

Canvas already binds widget reads to their session and handles pending widgets; cron already gates its view. Those owners are unchanged.

## Evidence

Restricted-operator browser regression: two forbidden diff calls per dashboard visit become zero, with an explanatory Review affordance. Session-only viewer: New Conversation branch calls 1→0; Appearance background calls 1→0; cron remains 0. The chat-header branch owner also goes 1→0.

Production UI against an isolated real Gateway: 5,000 synthetic sessions and 62,000 files / 1.14 GB; zero automatic diff requests and zero UI FORBIDDEN responses. A deliberate direct diff RPC still returns FORBIDDEN. This used APFS and a small synthetic database, not a 35 GiB database or btrfs; unrelated startup UNAVAILABLE responses occurred. No private data or live deployment was used.

Five interleaved owner benchmark pairs, with A/A controls:

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Denied RPCs / 5,000 diff activations | 5,000 | 0 |
| Client-owner elapsed median | 15.69 ms | 3.38 ms |
| Client-owner CPU median | 16.83 ms | 4.51 ms |
| Sampled allocation | 18.45 MB | 7.31 MB |
| Session projection CPU / read | 1.004 ms | 0.985 ms |
| Session projection allocation / read | 692.6 KB | 724.5 KB |

These are owner measurements, not end-to-end production latency. Client A/A CPU medians were 16.83/16.96 ms. Projection timing shows no meaningful speed claim on the loaded host; allocation rises 4.6%, and an unconditional 100-row response grows 15.7% to carry explanations. Existing shared-field transport can deduplicate repeated values.

Focused regression and affected-consumer proof covers projection invalidation, real RPC race classification, retained UI loaders, allowed diff behavior, and scope-gated browser navigation. The real Gateway test body took 21.3 s (63 s runner); focused test and final check details follow below.

Simplification: reused existing row materialization and selected-row lookup; shared file/presentation policy replaces duplicated admission text. Production delta +173 lines, generated validator +3, test delta +206, with a matching test-line allocation for the distinct regressions. Tooling adds reproducible owner measurements. Growth is needed to project a previously missing fact and distinguish permission from retryable workspace changes.

Focused results: 148 UI owner tests passed (7.21 s runner), 51 scope-owner tests passed, four diff-browser tests passed (21.60 s runner), the extended scope-browser scenario passed (16.37 s runner; other 13 cases passed separately), 12 projection/config tests passed, 64 file/race sibling tests passed, and three publication tests passed (43.72 s runner, 2.16 s test bodies). Publication snapshots were regenerated and verified to differ only by the additive nullable field.

Known main regression: production Knip reports `CHAT_SEARCH_HIGHLIGHT` and `syncChatSearchHighlight` as unused exports. The identical two failures reproduce on the exact main parent `d5be7a6a42934658aacc09803c52d056b1fba29b`, which introduced that module in #170434. This change does not touch that owner. It remains a main follow-up, not a passing check.

Pre-PR `pnpm check:changed`: all format, type, lint, schema, boundary, and lifecycle checks passed; exit 1 solely for the two exact-parent Knip failures documented above. Independent Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2.

![Before: restricted workspace sends forbidden diff requests](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9a33f0bf-1249-4106-8ea4-ff0f68572d39)

![After: Review explains sandbox requirement without a diff request](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3688a7b3-8526-479a-963e-7159aa667f2d)

![Before: Appearance reports missing read scope](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6cf17184-8e4a-4f89-8903-23e0a13e6e4f)

![After: Appearance skips the unavailable background request](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/91fc24c3-ab62-435d-913a-86e211cd4f7b)

CI repair: the first run exposed re-resolution of physical legacy row ownership in the new projection and older allowed-session fixtures missing the new fact. Both are fixed. Only the failed owners and affected sandbox policy were replayed: 46 backend/sandbox tests and 59 UI tests passed. Targeted type checks, lint, formatting, and a fresh Codex autoreview passed. Final exact-head CI provides the broad proof.


The subsequent CI run exposed an obsolete whole-module sandbox mock in environment-execution tests. Removing it lets those 18 tests use the real classifier; all passed locally, and focused Codex review was clean. This follow-up changes no production code and reduces test growth to +206 lines. All other test jobs in that run passed.

Final validation: [CI run 41253510831](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41253510831) passed on `13ed5bc6260f3c9123362103393e0c1341a1163d`, with all planned jobs complete and no failed jobs.

prs.title: fix(browser): avoid repeat DNS checks for unchanged action URLs
prs.body:
Related: #178058

## What Problem This Solves

Browser actions repeat a DNS policy check while preparing the response URL, even when that same address was admitted earlier in the request.

## User Impact

Unchanged-tab actions avoid one redundant lookup and return the same result and URL. This draft addresses the response-only duplicate; it does not claim to eliminate all per-action DNS checks or prove meeting audio recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The action route opts in to reuse its admitted address only for response URL projection, with an exact URL and complete navigation-policy match. Changed URLs, changed policies, missing admission and cancellation retain validation. Execution and navigation guards remain authoritative. There is no cross-request cache, new setting or protocol change.

## Evidence

Actual Browser Bridge HTTP actions against an isolated Chrome 155 tab on macOS arm64 / Node 26.4.0, with the default browser policy and real system DNS. Five serial baseline/candidate pairs used fresh processes; all 30 actions per revision returned identical page data and response URLs. All ten `about:blank` controls performed zero hostname lookups.

| Measurement | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DNS lookups per unchanged action | 4 | 3 |
| Warm action median (25 samples) | 270.30 ms | 270.70 ms |
| Warm action p95 | 289.54 ms | 287.59 ms |
| Cold completion median (5 samples) | 4770.63 ms | 4827.54 ms |
| Cold completion p95 | 5633.91 ms | 5371.78 ms |

The committed opt-in workload is rerunnable with:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs extensions/browser/scripts/bench-act-dns.ts --chromium <chromium-executable> --output <result.json>
```

Cold completion includes isolated browser/page/bridge startup and the observer positive control. Action timing excludes observer flushing. Host load and controller CPU/RSS are recorded; aggregate metrics did not regress by 20%. The workload's initial lint overlapped the first two pairs. No delayed DNS or simulated browser/provider results were used; slow-resolver stalls and meeting audio loss were not reproduced.

- New unchanged-URL regression fails on the base because it performs two policy validations rather than one; the other nine cases pass. All ten pass with the fix, including changed URL, in-place policy mutation, missing admission and cancellation controls.
- Three focused owner/action/navigation suites passed all 90 cases (7.07 seconds wrapper wall time). After the final test-only adjustment, the changed 10-case file passed again (19.94 seconds including cold compiler setup); CI case time is pending.
- Browser package production types, targeted test/workload types, typed lint, formatting and diff whitespace checks passed.
- One independent P0–P2 autoreview completed with no actionable findings.

Full PR CI is currently skipped because this PR is a draft; the local results above are not a full-CI claim.

Production delta: 25 insertions / 3 deletions in two files. The remaining additions are the focused regression coverage and opt-in measurement workload.

prs.title: improve(ui): show exec approval warning text in approval history
prs.body:
Closes #180242

**AI-assisted**

## What Problem This Solves
The approval history table shows the command text of past exec approvals but not the `warningText` that was presented to the reviewer at decision time. This warning (e.g. "Dangerous: redirects to /dev/null") is the auto-review rationale that justified the decision — it is persisted on the approval record and rendered in channel approvals (`approval-reaction-runtime.ts`), but the Control UI history view drops it. A reviewer looking back at history cannot see why a dangerous command was flagged.

## Why This Change Was Made
The data already exists in `ExecApprovalPresentation.warningText` and is rendered in every other surface (channel approvals bold it). This adds the same field to the history table as a dedicated Warning column, so the gap is a read-side render fix on already-persisted safety data. The change is minimal: one sibling component, one locale key, one CSS rule, and tests in the existing file.

## User Impact
Reviewers scanning past approvals in the Control UI can now see the warning text that accompanied each exec decision, making it possible to audit why high-risk commands were allowed or denied without cross-referencing channel logs.

## Evidence
```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/approvals/approvals-page.test.tsx
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
```
New test `renders the exec approval warning text in the history table` verifies:
- a row with `warningText: "Dangerous: redirects to /dev/null"` renders the text in a `.approval-history__warning-text` element
- a row with `warningText: null` renders no such element

prs.title: fix(update): preserve config edits during plugin finalization
prs.body:
Related: #189778

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plugin finalization aborting an update with “config changed since last load” when another writer edits config during package or plugin work, including same-version repairs.

## User Impact

Unrelated edits survive finalization. Already-applied changes succeed; owned-field conflicts or repeated concurrent writes produce a warning with `openclaw plugins doctor` / `openclaw doctor --fix` guidance instead of failing the core update or preventing Gateway recovery. Existing ownership, path, validation, and I/O refusals remain enforced. A plugin may remain unavailable until repaired.

This fix is **not yet released**. The separate Windows Gateway recovery repair is on main in #189647 (`ed79334f`), also not yet released. Leave #189778 open until release.

## Why This Change Was Made

Finalization previously replaced config against a hash captured before awaited plugin work. It now reapplies only its changed fields to fresh config using the existing config lock, five-attempt retry, and plugin publication/index rollback owner. The planning baseline is retained before in-memory channel restoration. Authority refusals propagate unchanged; warning settlement rechecks authority after rollback.

The original report does not identify the concurrent writer. Same-version convergence can run while the Gateway is online; the regressions exercise ordinary concurrent config edits without claiming to reproduce the reporter’s exact writer or Windows update.

## Evidence

- **Include/env retry invariant:** every attempt [reads a fresh snapshot and merges its write options](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/17bfaea3d1a2674dde4341bd1e33863ed723ee46/src/config/mutate.ts#L904-L955). The retry loop [reuses the prepared snapshot only for attempt zero](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/17bfaea3d1a2674dde4341bd1e33863ed723ee46/src/config/mutate.ts#L976-L1015). The snapshot owner [returns newly captured env restoration, include hashes/targets, and plugin metadata](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/17bfaea3d1a2674dde4341bd1e33863ed723ee46/src/config/io.snapshot.ts#L601-L610). The writer [selects the include boundary from that snapshot](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/17bfaea3d1a2674dde4341bd1e33863ed723ee46/src/config/mutate.ts#L324-L348) and [restores authored env references](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/17bfaea3d1a2674dde4341bd1e33863ed723ee46/src/config/io.write-values.ts#L35-L81).
- The [extended production-path persistence test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/17bfaea3d1a2674dde4341bd1e33863ed723ee46/src/cli/update-cli/update-command-plugins.persistence.test.ts#L302-L382) switches include destinations and changes the env value during the first commit. It proves the retry preserves the root `$include`, root and included env references, the old include byte-for-byte, concurrent values in the new include, and install-index rollback after exhaustion. No secrets are inlined and the include is not flattened or clobbered.
- The extended case fails with the original base finalization code (`603106d1a96a`: include conflict) and also fails when only the stale `envSnapshotForRestore` is retained (one commit attempt instead of the required successful second attempt). Both temporary controls were restored. The complete persistence suite passes: **17 tests**, 31.08 s Vitest / 32.98 s wrapper. Final formatted retry cases pass: **2 tests**, 39.99 s / 42.21 s including cold worker compilation.
- Targeted CLI-update test typecheck, focused oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Earlier unchanged-source proof covers 101 focused persistence, authority, finalizer, config-fence, and degradation cases; another 19 consumer/authority cases passed after the fixture correction.
- Fresh independent **Codex autoreview, P0–P2**, base `603106d1a96a` through the final local candidate: **scoped-clean**, no findings. The committed patch matches that candidate. Existing hosted ClawSweeper review found no code defects.
- Simplification retains the existing lock/retry/rollback owners. Production grows by 99 net lines; 177 net test/fixture lines cover distinct finalization contracts, including 50 additional lines extending the existing retry test. No test-only production seam, new schema, persisted format, public config/SDK contract, dependency, or config option is introduced. Persistence proof uses real config/include/index writes; a cheaper mocked layer cannot establish these guarantees.
- Exact-head [CI run 41252307222](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41252307222) is fully green on `17bfaea3d1a2674dde4341bd1e33863ed723ee46`, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards, the aggregate CI gate, and current dependency/security guards. Zero failures and zero pending checks. Prior-head CI remains historical evidence only.
- Installed latest-stable-to-candidate Windows upgrade and real Gateway/model proof were not run. External package/service/provider operations are stubbed in local finalizer composition. This limitation remains disclosed; no installed-upgrade or live Gateway claim is made.

## Work sessions

- https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/78580230-7d1b-4329-a7dd-72554eb66323

prs.title: fix(config): report write-safety refusals during dry runs
prs.body:
Related: #166718

## What Problem This Solves

`config patch --dry-run` can report success when a large provider-catalog reduction will be rejected by the real write's size-drop guard, misleading deployment preflights.

## User Impact

Structured config previews now fail early with a `write-safety` error and the same size-drop reason as the writer, plus its existing recovery guidance. The preview leaves config bytes unchanged and creates no backup or rejected-payload file. If persistence preparation refuses the change, JSON output retains the assignments, input modes, completed checks, and counters; plain-text output retains the original refusal. Existing write protection remains enabled; this does not add a public size-drop override or change value-mode's documented limited validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preview and commit share preparation of the authored, metadata-stamped payload and its canonical size baseline. Include-only mutations retain their existing write route instead of applying the root-file guard to an expanded config. The writer continues to own runtime activation, rejection artifacts, auditing, publication, and rollback.

The related roster-retention preview work in #153069 does not evaluate the serialized-byte guard. The public override requested in #166718 remains a separate product decision, so this PR does not close the entire issue.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the registered-CLI regression fails because the large-shrink preview succeeds; moderate-shrink and include-owned controls pass.
- Real CLI proof uses the normal `pnpm openclaw config patch --file <patch> --replace-path models.providers.bounty.models` entry point in isolated task-owned home/config/state, with 409 synthetic provider models and no provider calls or credentials. The original live failure was reproduced at `2b988ee83444` (the affected owner code is unchanged at this PR's base `80322af5c7e5`).
- Committed candidate `9982d96b8c1d` results: 409→32 root preview and actual write both reject with `size-drop`; the preview preserves original bytes and creates no artifact. 409→300 root and 409→32 include-owned changes pass preview and persist the exact requested model count. Include-owned writes preserve the root file. A real provider-builder shrink also rejects in both preview and commit; its preview has `checks.schema:false` and still returns `write-safety`, directly proving the review correction.
- `pnpm test src/cli/config-cli.integration.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 99 passed; 51.68 s runner wall time. The materially changed integration file has 34 tests and takes 29.83 s Vitest wall time; the cases reuse its existing real config-command fixture.
- Unchanged writer/reference coverage, run at `9982d96b8c1d`: `pnpm test src/config/io.write-config.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.reference-values.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 130 passed; 62.96 s total. Covers existing canonical-format/BOM sizing, references, include ownership, refusal, and rollback contracts.
- The supported CLI wrapper completed the production build for live proof. Core and core-test typechecks and changed-file lint passed. The aggregate changed check stopped at the unrelated existing `observePlacementAuthority` unused export in `src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-turn-authority.ts`; this file and its references are unchanged by the patch. The subsequent ready-for-review CI result and current follow-up are documented below.
- Follow-up `9b8e17b2b06`: parser-validated builder/batch inputs and thrown persistence refusals have registered-command regressions that failed before their corrections. For the empty-roster refusal, the old JSON path returned `operations:0`, empty `inputModes`, and false checks; its text-output control already passed. The corrected real CLI returns `operations:1`, `inputModes:["json"]`, all completed checks true, preserved counters, and the original schema refusal. It exits 1, leaves config bytes unchanged, and creates no backup/rejected file. The matching non-JSON regression preserves the exact original diagnostic.




### CI and conflict follow-up (2026-10-10)

Integrated main `0c94b6966078` to resolve the real `src/config/io.write.ts` import conflict. Both intents are retained: upstream `composeConfigWriteAssertions` and this PR's shared payload preparation. The PR delta against the new base remains the same nine files; no Doctor test, timeout, assertion, or CI workflow was changed.

The previous CI run [37805483456](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37805483456/job/113409493434) failed on `runs legacy state migrations in yes mode without prompting` at 30.228 s (30 s limit), causing the aggregate gate to fail. Diagnosis did not reproduce that failure:

- Exact old PR source `9b8e17b2b064`: original seven-file shard order, separate file processes, macOS arm64 / Node 26.4.0: all 87 tests passed; the named test took 10.582 s. A standalone diagnostic retained all assertions and the deadline, observed maintenance admission in 65 ms and overall completion in 12.939 s, and was removed afterward.
- Same old source in a credential-free Linux arm64 container, Node 24.19.0, 2 CPUs / 8 GiB: all five Doctor-file tests passed; the named test took 18.558 s. This matches the CI Node version and resource limits but not its Linux x64 hardware. The container was removed after diagnosis.
- Conflict-resolved candidate: original seven-file shard, all 87 tests passed; the named test took 12.338 s. Config CLI and writer suites passed 202 tests (34 integration, 65 CLI, 103 writer), 67.86 s combined runner wall time; integration file 27.12 s Vitest wall time.

The original CI timeout remains unattributed. These passing replays are not presented as a timeout fix; no retry logic, longer deadlines, weakened assertions, or speculative production changes were added. The subsequent CI run [38082056748](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38082056748) passed all 86 jobs on `64e6949e85a3`; this is prior-head evidence.

Final local validation on `64e6949e85a3`: types, targeted lint, formatting, and all remaining selected guards pass. The aggregate check stops at 17 Knip findings; the same canonical scan on a separately installed, clean `0c94b6966078` worktree reproduces the identical set (15 authentication/runtime exports, one Solid lint export, one UI test-helper export). They are inherited rather than introduced by this PR.



### Review guidance and async conflict follow-up

Commit `3687439fae0` reuses `createConfigWriteSafetyRejectionError` for actionable recovery guidance in both JSON and text previews, retaining the size-drop reason. The existing registered-command case failed before the message repair and now verifies both output formats and unchanged config/files. No new test fixture or production abstraction was added.

Integrated main `c6d71fae0ed` to resolve the writer conflict from #168481: topology preparation is now asynchronous, so the preview and writer await it and the shared payload type consumes its resolved value.

Validation: 202 tests passed across config CLI integration (34), CLI (65), and writer (103); 101.20 s runner wall time. Integration-file Vitest wall time: 46.38 s. No hosted CI timing for this new head yet.

Final local checks: production types, all core-test type groups, scoped lint, formatting, and the selected ratchets passed. The aggregate changed check stops at four Knip unused exports outside the PR diff: `stripClaudeCliGeneratedUserPrefixes`, `createChannelApprovalHandlerAsync`, `GitHubConnectionsContent`, and `reconnectGateway`. Their defining files match the integrated base; no clean-base Knip replay was run for this head. These findings remain recorded, not suppressed.



### Conflict refresh (2026-10-11)

Integrated main `0ff0202128f` for the new writer conflict. Preserved upstream's agent-deletion authority check before publication and awaited metadata recording. Applied upstream's payload cleanup in the extracted shared preparation function; audit metadata remains computed by the writer. No new behavior, tests, or dependencies were introduced by this conflict repair. The prior head `3687439fae09` had a successful [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38109291576); that remains prior-head evidence.

Conflict-resolved head `963d92c985b`: 137 tests passed (34 CLI integration, 103 config writer), 121.12 s runner wall time; CLI integration 61.12 s and writer 42.78 s Vitest wall time. Core types, scoped lint, formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed. New-head CI is pending.

prs.title: fix(cron): reject empty Code Mode fallback catalogs
prs.body:
Supersedes #167842, thanks @DasX.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes scheduled jobs reporting success without doing their work when a fallback model's Code Mode tool catalog is empty after filtering.

## User Impact

An explicit tool allowlist that resolves to no task tools now fails before model submission with the existing actionable allowlist/plugin diagnostic, recorded against the affected job's run. Permitted provider-hosted search and real shell tools remain usable. No configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Code Mode's `exec` and `wait` orchestrate task tools; an explicitly allowed shell `exec` must not make that bridge count as a task capability. The existing catalog admission owner now excludes marked controls and counts eligible hosted search through the existing route resolver. The prompt precheck and cron error-recording path remain the owners of rejection and reporting.

Production is +35/-31 lines (net +4). This removes the single-consumer client-presence helper and intermediate name array, and shares the existing search-route calculation rather than duplicating it. Tests grow by 60 lines, with a dedicated allocation for the empty-catalog regression and hosted-search/revocation controls.

## Evidence

- On main `43a3abe0595f0c77720f35472a42bced316bc3e9`, the regression using real Code Mode compaction failed all three empty-catalog cases (`exec`, `bash`, maintenance allowlist); 22 sibling cases passed. Wall time: 49.09 seconds including cold compilation.
- Fixed catalog: 25/25 passed. Search preparation/catalog integration: 23/23 passed, including inherited/global/session/runtime/execution denials, disabled/raw runs, and refresh revocation. Combined wall time: 56.23 seconds; individual test-file durations were 36.97 and 15.59 seconds, mostly compiler/import preparation.
- Autoreview completed on the local candidate against that main base: scoped-clean at P0–P2, with no actionable findings. The later explicit `clientTools: undefined` fixture field is a type-only correction.
- Final focused rerun: 73/73 passed in 54.22 seconds across search preparation/catalog integration, prompt-precheck rejection before submission, native-search routing, and prompt-prefix stability.
- Targeted typecheck of the four affected files and their imports, type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Exact-head [CI run 41252823747](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41252823747) passed in 504 seconds elapsed. The final Security Review publisher is a separate gate.

This is production-owner boundary proof. No live Gateway/model run or broad suite was run on the production Team host; PR CI supplies broad checks. The contributor's branch was read with `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff` and was never checked out or run. This replacement is independently implemented and credits Peik S. (`1935468+DasX@users.noreply.github.com`), the human author of all three source PR commits.

prs.title: improve(ui): show plugin approval severity in approval history
prs.body:
Closes #180243

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI approval history table (`ui/src/pages/approvals/approvals-page.tsx`) renders each row's `kind` as `Exec`, `Plugin`, or `System agent`, but never shows the plugin approval `severity` (`info` / `warning` / `critical`). That severity already drives the review flow — `src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-approval.ts` treats `critical` as forcing a human decision — yet an operator auditing past approvals could not tell a critical plugin approval from a routine `info` one without extra context.

## Why This Change Was Made

The history RPC already returns `presentation.severity` for plugin approvals, so this is a rendering-only gap. Surfacing severity directly in the history row lets operators scan for high-risk plugin approvals at a glance, matching the visual emphasis the gateway already gives `critical` severity at decision time. The chip sits next to the existing `kind` label rather than in a dedicated column, keeping the table clean for the non-plugin rows where severity does not apply.

## User Impact

Operators auditing plugin approvals in the Control UI now see a small colored severity chip (info = blue, warning = amber, critical = red) beside the `Plugin` kind label in each history row. Exec and system-agent rows are unchanged. The change is additive and cosmetic only — no data, config, migration, or RPC behavior changes.

## Evidence

- Added `ApprovalHistorySeverity` sibling component that reads `presentation.severity` when `presentation.kind === "plugin"` and renders a colored chip.
- Added `approvalHistory.severities.{info,warning,critical}` locale keys in `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-approvals.ts`.
- Added `.approval-history__severity` chip styles (info/warning/critical using existing `--info`/`--warn`/`--danger` tokens) in `ui/src/styles/components.css`.
- Added a test in the existing `ui/src/pages/approvals/approvals-page.test.tsx` verifying the chip text and per-severity class for critical/warning/info rows and the absence of a chip for an exec row.

Validation:
```
cd /home/code/github/openclaw-wt-180243 && node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/approvals/approvals-page.test.tsx
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
```

Typecheck (`tsc --noEmit` for `openclaw-ui`) and `oxlint` on the touched files reported no errors. The `check:line-cap-ratchet` pre-commit hook passed.
