prs.title: fix(cron): trigger-once watchers stay disabled instead of deleted when --delete-after-run is set
prs.body:
Closes #168334

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a recurring cron job created with `--trigger-once --delete-after-run` stays in the job store as a disabled row after its trigger fires, instead of being deleted.

## User Impact

User impact: recurring watcher jobs armed with `--trigger-once --delete-after-run` now remove themselves after their first successful fired run, so fired watchers no longer pile up as disabled jobs that need manual or scheduled cleanup.

Unchanged: recurring jobs without `--trigger-once` keep the per-run session and transcript cleanup meaning of `deleteAfterRun` (#84794) and are never deleted. A failed run, an unfired evaluation, or a trigger replaced while the run was in flight keeps the job. Jobs already stored are not touched: deletion only happens when a fired run completes, so existing disabled watchers stay until removed as before.

## Decision Requested

This changes the documented `once: true` outcome for one explicit flag combination, from "disabled" to "deleted" when the job also sets `deleteAfterRun`. ClawSweeper recommends approving deletion for that combination and documenting it; this PR does both (`docs/automation/cron-jobs/schedules.md`). Without `deleteAfterRun`, `once: true` still only disables the job.

## Why This Change Was Made

`--trigger-once` already ends a recurring job's life on its first successful fired run: the trigger disarms it and nothing reschedules it. The delete gate in `applyJobResult` only treated `at` and `on-exit` schedules as terminal, so the job was disabled but kept even when the operator asked for `--delete-after-run`.

`isTriggerOnceTerminalRun` marks that run as terminal when trigger ownership is current, the job has `trigger.once`, and the evaluation fired. Normal completion and startup recovery (`restoreFinalizedStartupRun`, which replays a run whose history was recorded before a crash interrupted the row commit) both use it, so the two paths cannot disagree. All other delete conditions are unchanged: current schedule ownership, `deleteAfterRun`, a succeeded completion, and the one-shot preserve path.

## Evidence

**Live behavior.** Captured on a 2026.9.9 gateway carrying the same normal-path change (commit shown by `--version`; the recovery wiring in this PR is unit-proven below). A throwaway command job, no model or channel involved:

```text
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.9.9 (157d653)

# stored jobs before (pre-existing watchers were stored by earlier builds)
jobs=44 trigger_once=12 trigger_once_disabled=12 proof_jobs=0

$ echo 'json({ fire: true })' | openclaw cron add --name proof-trigger-once-delete --agent main --every 1m --trigger-script - --trigger-once --delete-after-run --no-deliver --command 'echo proof-fired'
{
 "id": "2ea7fa1f-115b-4c93-98cb-13486ea46163",
 "schedule": {
  "kind": "every",
  "everyMs": 60000,
  "anchorMs": 1791620677356
 },
 "trigger": {
  "once": true
 },
 "deleteAfterRun": true,
 "delivery": "none",
 "enabled": true,
 "nextRunAtMs": 1791620737356
}

# after the first tick
$ openclaw cron runs --id 2ea7fa1f-115b-4c93-98cb-13486ea46163 --json   # fields shown
{"jobId":"2ea7fa1f-115b-4c93-98cb-13486ea46163","action":"finished","status":"ok","completionStatus":"succeeded","deliveryStatus":"not-requested","triggerFired":true,"summary":"proof-fired","runAt":"2026-10-10T08:25:37.399Z"}

$ openclaw cron list --all --json   # summarized
jobs=44 trigger_once=12 trigger_once_disabled=12 proof_jobs=0
```

The proof job ran once (`ok`, `succeeded`, trigger fired) and was deleted. The 12 trigger-once watchers already stored by earlier builds were loaded and left unchanged (44 jobs before and after), which is the upgrade-compatibility case: this PR adds no stored field or schema change.

**Tests**, run on this branch (tree `28538fc`) on top of `main` `27beb27` with Node 26 and the branch's own `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`:

- `src/cron/service/timer-outcomes.regression.test.ts`, eight new cases. Normal completion: fired success deletes; no `deleteAfterRun`, failed run, unfired evaluation, and a trigger replaced mid-run keep the job. Startup recovery: a current fired success deletes; no `deleteAfterRun` and a trigger retired before recovery keep it.
- **Fails without each fix:** reverting the `timer-outcomes.ts` change fails exactly the normal-path delete case; reverting only the `startup-run-repair.ts` wiring fails exactly the recovery delete case (1 failed, 25 passed). The keep cases pass either way.
- **Test cost:** `pnpm test src/cron/service/timer-outcomes.regression.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` runs the file (26 tests) in 18.8 s wall; the new cases take 1 to 11 ms each, plus module warm-up on the first case. Pure unit calls: no timers, sleeps, Gateway, or process boots.
- `pnpm test src/cron/service`: 585/585.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src`: clean. `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on all touched files: clean.

**CI on the previous head (`65932ac`)**: all checks passed except `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)`, which fails on two `ui/src/e2e/session-dashboard.e2e.test.ts` cases waiting for the Canvas "Pin to dashboard" button. This PR touches no UI code, and the same two cases fail identically on unrelated PRs from the same window (runs 38036941493 and 38036711499), so it is inherited.

Local gaps: the full `pnpm test` suite was not run locally (targeted lanes per `pnpm changed:lanes` were). Locally `pnpm check` hit the SQLite worker ratchet needing ripgrep (`spawnSync rg ENOENT`) and a stale max-lines baseline entry for an untouched file; CI's `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` passed.

prs.title: fix(cron): reject empty Code Mode fallback tool catalogs
prs.body:
Refs #166451

## What Problem This Solves

A scheduled fallback can report success with an empty task-tool catalog because Code Mode's JavaScript `exec` is mistaken for the shell `exec` named in the job's allowlist.

## User Impact

Empty Code Mode fallbacks fail before model submission, retaining normal cron error diagnostics. Valid provider-native-only search runs remain admitted even though hosted search is intentionally absent from the local catalog. This does not add tools or grant additional execution permissions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The callable-plan owner distinguishes marked Code Mode controls from real task tools. Tool preparation also carries policy-enabled native capability presence through the existing catalog owner, using the existing native-search route resolver, conversation policy and execution cap. The native tool is not registered as a local callable function.

The synthetic cron replay identified in review has been removed. Coverage now follows the real tool-preparation-to-catalog boundary in its existing owner test, including disabling search during a permission refresh.

## Evidence

- At the original PR head `0fe0a641a1f`, the native-presence owner regression fails (9 controls pass). The real preparation/catalog regression independently fails for native OpenAI search (12 controls pass).
- Previous-head regression run: 86 tests in 7 files passed in 177.43 s, covering the changed owners, allowlist guard, prompt phase, cron allowlist propagation, provider-runtime wrappers, and OpenAI Responses. An earlier 38-test pass also verified the old synthetic cron replay before removing it; that replay is not presented as runtime proof.
- Permission controls cover global denial, global search disablement, session disablement, runtime exclusion, execution exclusion, disabled tools, and a custom non-native endpoint. Existing shell `exec`, alias `bash`, maintenance allowlist, client-tool and catalog controls remain covered.
- Previous-head type-aware oxlint: 264 rules across all five changed TypeScript files, zero warnings/errors (43.3 s). Scoped `tsgo` passed for all three changed production roots with unchanged core compiler options, full transitive imports and existing ambient declarations (3.9 GiB memory peak, no swap). Both line-cap ratchets, conflict-marker check and oxfmt passed. This is not a claim that the full core or full test typecheck passed.
- Standalone regression command wall times during the red phase: callable-plan file 84.83 s (including a cold 59.54 s worker build), preparation/catalog file 26.93 s. New-head CI duration is not yet available.

## Real behavior proof

**Completed Gateway before/after proof for the empty-catalog fallback. The provider-native-only search control remains open.**

Run date: **2026-10-09**, 20:14-20:21 UTC. Tested head: **99c3d40a147dd554c56f9f2fc10aa4fac4aa40df**. Model: **google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite**, using the real Google endpoint and a runtime-only environment credential.

### Setup and provenance

- A real, isolated Gateway accepted the job through `cron.add` and `cron.run`; completion was read from `cron.runs`. Fresh temporary state and workspace, loopback only, no channels, no production state, delivery disabled.
- Reused this worktree's prepared test-worker build, started as `node --import tsx dist/entry.js gateway run`. TSX resolves workspace-package source imports; the Gateway core is compiled. All **14,729** recorded build inputs matched their SHA-256 manifest entries, with zero missing files or mismatches. This is not a claim of a fresh full distribution build.
- The configured primary was a deliberately unavailable test model, `google/c9-proof-primary`. A transport hook returned planned HTTP 503 responses for that model before outbound submission. The real fallback resolver selected `google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite`. Requests to the fallback's official Google endpoint were not simulated or translated.
- Code Mode was enabled and Tool Search disabled. Global tools were `["read", "exec"]`; the fallback-specific provider allowlist was `["web_search"]`; the scheduled job's `toolsAllow` was `["read", "exec"]`. Their intersection left zero task tools, while Code Mode still exposed its `exec` and `wait` controls.
- The before run used the same build and configuration with the pre-PR callable-presence expression restored by a checked, process-local module-load splice. Specifically, it removed the native-presence disjunct and the Code Mode control-name exclusion from that expression. No source files or compiled artifacts were edited. Google has no native route at this head, so the remaining native preparation code cannot affect this comparison. The after run used the unmodified PR expression.

### Observed results

| Run | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Before, old callable-presence expression | Empty catalog, real Gemini HTTP 200 responses, cron `status=ok`, despite the final answer saying it could not read the file. |
| After, PR head | Planned primary failure followed by the configured fallback; cron `status=error` with `No callable tools remain`. The fallback was rejected before a Google model request. |

Redacted terminal/runtime excerpts:

```text
BEFORE
PROOF_BASELINE old callable-presence expression restored
code-mode diagnostic {"boundary":"final-surface","catalogToolCount":0,"visibleToolNames":["exec","wait"]}
PROOF_REQUEST {"variant":"old","model":"gemini-3.1-flash-lite","declarations":["exec","wait"],"nativeSearch":false}
PROOF_RESPONSE {"model":"gemini-3.1-flash-lite","status":200}
PROOF_RESPONSE {"model":"gemini-3.1-flash-lite","status":200}
model fallback decision: decision=candidate_succeeded requested=google/c9-proof-primary candidate=google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite
PROOF_RESULT {"variant":"old","model":"gemini-3.1-flash-lite","status":"ok","summary":"I have no callable tools to read the local proof-note.txt.","durationMs":104810}

AFTER
PROOF_TRIGGER {"variant":"fixed","ok":true,"enqueued":true}
model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=google/c9-proof-primary candidate=google/c9-proof-primary reason=server_error next=google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite
[tools] No callable tools remain after resolving explicit tool allowlist (tools.allow: read, exec; tools.byProvider.allow: web_search; runtime toolsAllow: read, exec); no registered tools matched. Fix the allowlist or enable the plugin that registers the requested tool.
PROOF_RESULT {"variant":"fixed","model":"gemini-3.1-flash-lite","status":"error","error":"No callable tools remain after resolving explicit tool allowlist (tools.allow: read, exec; tools.byProvider.allow: web_search; runtime toolsAllow: read, exec); no registered tools matched. Fix the allowlist or enable the plugin that registers the requested tool.","durationMs":86877}
```

Both completed proof units exited **0**, with no OOM or timeout termination. They were serialized and limited to 3500 MiB memory plus 2 GiB swap, with at least 4500 MiB available before each start. Recorded peaks were 3.4 GiB memory and 1.1 GiB swap for the after run, and 3.4 GiB memory and 1.0 GiB swap for the before run. The Gateways were stopped and temporary state removed.

### Remaining proof gap: provider-native-only search

The earlier completed fallback run above was limited to a Gemini credential. At this head, `extensions/google/provider-policy-api.ts` does not expose `resolveNativeWebSearch`, so `src/agents/native-web-search.ts` selects the managed route for this Google model. Its managed search tool would not be a valid provider-native-only control. The existing OpenAI native route requires the OpenAI provider, Responses API and official endpoint; no OpenAI credential was used in that earlier run.

Therefore **no successful live provider-native-only control is claimed**, and this proof does not close the entire reviewer request. The already-recorded native preparation/catalog regressions remain test-based evidence: before the native-presence fix, the owner case failed with 9 controls passing and the real preparation/catalog case failed with 12 controls passing; after it, those files passed 10 and 13 tests respectively.

The earlier incomplete OOM attempt is superseded only for the empty-catalog fallback scenario. The original reporter's complete runtime trace remains unavailable, so this PR continues to reference the broader issue rather than claim that every zero-tool path has been diagnosed.


### OpenAI native-only follow-up: partial diagnostic, not a passed control

On **2026-10-09 UTC**, the same head was exercised with **openai/gpt-5.6-luna**, the **openai-chatgpt-responses** transport, SSE, and the embedded **openclaw** runtime. This is the ChatGPT-account Responses route, not the API-key Platform route. The model replaced GPT-5.4 Mini, which this head rejects as retired on the subscription route.

The job was submitted through the real Gateway's `cron.add` / `cron.run` APIs with the exact policy combination from the Codex P2 thread: global `tools.allow: ["web_search"]`, per-run `toolsAllow: ["web_search", "exec"]`, Code Mode enabled, and native search enabled. Provider selection was automatic. A fresh rootless container supplied private PID/network namespaces, read-only source mounts, and isolated writable state. Only a current access token and expiry were supplied, with no refresh token or production-auth mount.

Observed on the fixed head:

```text
code-mode final-surface: catalogToolCount=0, visibleToolNames=[exec,wait]
provider-tool-surface: [client:exec,client:wait,hosted:web_search]
OpenAI Responses HTTP 200: 7 requests
response.output_item.done: type=web_search_call, status=completed, action.type=search (6 occurrences)
response.completed: 0 observed
transport: stopReason=error, failureKind=provider-failure
cron.runs: status=error, durationMs=127477
error="cron: job execution timed out (last phase: model-call-started)"
```

The callable-presence check admitted the empty managed catalog and real provider-native searches completed. However, the transport repeatedly reported provider failures after the searches, automatic retries consumed the job's time budget, and the Cron run did **not** finish successfully. The final request was aborted at the deadline. This timeout is **not** counted as passed behavior proof. No old-code native-only run was added after this repeated failure; the required successful native-only before/after control remains open. This also does not establish successful native search on the API-key Platform route.

The earlier Gemini fallback proof remains unchanged. No product-source changes were made for this follow-up. The cached build inputs were rechecked: all 14,729 hashes still matched. The fixture uses the repository's `scripts/tsx.mjs` ESM loader; the initial generic TSX loader could not load the OpenAI provider's import-only dependencies and those preliminary local failures are not counted as provider runs.

The test containers and temporary state were removed. The shared OAuth credential payload checksum and its update timestamp were unchanged, and the non-probing model-status command still reported the OpenAI profile as `ok`.

### OpenAI native-only second attempt with gpt-6-luna: same provider error, not a passed control

On **2026-10-09**, 22:41-22:43 UTC, the same head (**99c3d40a147dd554c56f9f2fc10aa4fac4aa40df**) was exercised again with **openai/gpt-6-luna**. Apart from the model, the only fixture change was the job timeout (300 s instead of 120 s). Route (`openai-chatgpt-responses`, SSE), embedded `openclaw` runtime, prompt, Code Mode, native search and the Codex P2 policy combination (global `tools.allow: ["web_search"]`, per-run `toolsAllow: ["web_search", "exec"]`) were unchanged, as were the rootless container isolation and the access-token-only credential handling. The request observer now decodes the zstd-compressed request body, so the tool list below was read from the actual outgoing request.

Observed on the fixed head (redacted and shortened):

```text
code-mode diagnostic {"boundary":"final-surface","fallbackActive":false,"catalogToolCount":0,"visibleToolNames":["exec","wait"]}
code-mode diagnostic {"boundary":"provider-tool-surface","provider":"openai","model":"gpt-6-luna","afterToolIdentities":["client:exec","client:wait","hosted:web_search"]}
PROOF_NATIVE {"event":"request","model":"gpt-6-luna","toolTypes":["function","function","web_search"],"functionNames":["exec","wait"],"toolChoice":"auto","reasoningEffort":"low"}
PROOF_NATIVE {"event":"http","status":200}
PROOF_NATIVE {"event":"response.output_item.done","itemType":"web_search_call","status":"completed","actionType":"search"}
PROOF_NATIVE {"event":"provider-failure","kind":"stream-server_error","code":"server_error","message":"An error occurred while processing your request. ..."}
PROOF_NATIVE {"event":"provider-failure","kind":"response-failed-server_error","code":"server_error"}
embedded_run_agent_end {"isError":true,"failoverReason":"server_error","model":"gpt-6-luna","provider":"openai","rawErrorPreview":"Codex error: An error occurred while processing your request. ..."}
transient same-model retry 1/8 for openai/gpt-6-luna reason=server_error: delayMs=1143
```

The PR's callable-presence check admitted the empty managed catalog again, and OpenAI accepted the request and completed the hosted search. The provider then failed that same response with `server_error`, matching the gpt-5.6-luna attempt above. For this attempt the agreed stop rule allowed exactly one built-in retry before stopping. The harness stopped the isolated container earlier, right after the first failed response, because it counted that response's `error` and `response.failed` events as two failures. The scheduled retry was therefore never sent. In total **one** OpenAI request was made, `cron.runs` recorded no completion, and there is no `status=ok`. This is **not** counted as passed behavior proof, and no old-code run was performed.

This PR does not change the request sent to OpenAI; it only changes the callable-presence start check (`hasCallableTools`) and the native-presence input to it. The failure occurred after the provider had accepted the request and finished the native search. Every response with a completed native search observed on this route so far ended in `server_error` (six with gpt-5.6-luna, one with gpt-6-luna). Because both models fail the same way, the failure does not look model-specific; whether it comes from the ChatGPT-account route itself or from the combination of hosted search with Code Mode client tools was not isolated. The successful native-only before/after control therefore remains open, and the API-key Platform route remains untested.

The shared OAuth credential payload checksum and its update timestamp were unchanged before and after this attempt, the non-probing model-status command still reported the OpenAI profile as `ok`, and the test container and temporary state were removed.

## Conflict repair (2026-10-20)

Merged `main` at `79ffb0507edfa83117abd1b32eab3af8909d3c5a` into this branch to resolve actual conflicts, preserving the existing history. The published head is `b209afb04b3a0413c135f96335a5e1e703c2f64d`. Main consolidated tool planning into `attempt-tool-catalog.ts`; the guard now lives in that existing owner, without restoring the deleted run-plan module. Native search keeps the newly introduced prepared requester policy, including inherited denials.

Validation on this conflict resolution:

- Negative control against the merged main production files: 3 expected failures and 21 passes in the catalog suite. All three failures show that an empty Code Mode bridge was counted as a task tool. The router stopped after that failing suite; the preparation suite was not run in this negative-control invocation.
- Fixed catalog: 24/24 tests passed (67.80 s wall time, including cold compiler preparation). Preparation plus catalog integration: 20/20 passed (28.87 s). This covers eligible native search, inherited/config/session/runtime/execution denials, custom endpoints, and refresh revocation.
- Affected siblings: 43/43 passed across prompt-prefix stability, native-search routing, and bundle preparation (23.15 s + 45.02 s across their two selected test configurations).
- Core typecheck passed. Targeted type-aware lint: 0 warnings, 0 errors across four files. Independent review: no actionable P0-P2 findings.
- Published-head CI completed successfully; see the current-head CI result below.

The production delta against the merged main is +33/-10 lines, with tests +79/-6. The added eligibility fact is consumed by the existing catalog owner; no new policy or tool owner is introduced.

**Remaining evidence gap:** the earlier live native-search controls still ended in a provider error after completing search, not a successful run. This maintenance update does not claim a successful native-provider control and does not change the provider request. The new passing tests are preparation/catalog boundary proof, not live-provider success.

## CI note

The additional local `check:max-lines-ratchet` fails identically on the candidate and its checked main/base snapshot because of max-lines suppressions in three unchanged UI files:

- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`
- `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts`

These files are not part of this PR. The committed-tree `check:line-cap-ratchet` and the focused validation listed above pass. This note does not claim that remote current-head CI has passed.

### Current-head CI (2026-10-20)

GitHub reports 57 passing checks/status contexts and 56 skipped checks, with no failed or pending checks. `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. These counts include status contexts as well as check runs. The local max-lines note above remains a record of the pre-publication baseline comparison, not a claim of a current remote CI failure.

prs.title: improve(cli): show workspace binding in sessions text output
prs.body:
Closes #181155

AI-assisted: This change was authored with assistance from DeepSeek Harness.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw sessions --json` already emits `spawnedWorkspaceDir`/`spawnedCwd` for each session, but the default text table does not surface the workspace binding. When several worktrees run concurrently, a user scanning the plain `openclaw sessions` output cannot tell which session belongs to which workspace directory, so session ownership across concurrent worktrees is effectively undiscoverable in the default (non-JSON) view.

## Why This Change Was Made

The workspace binding was already computed and available on the session display row (`toSessionDisplayRow` exposes `spawnedWorkspaceDir`), and the JSON path already projected it. The text-rendering path simply never wired it into a column. Adding the column at the text-rendering boundary is the minimal, owner-respecting fix: it consumes an existing field through the same cell-formatter pattern already used for `Key`, `Age`, `Model`, and `Flags`, without introducing a new owner or duplicating state.

The column shows the workspace directory **basename** (via `path.basename`) to keep rows narrow and readable across multiple concurrent worktrees; sessions with no bound workspace render `-`.

## User Impact

Users running `openclaw sessions` (default text output) now see a `Workspace` column next to `Tokens (ctx %)` and before `Flags`, showing the basename of each session's spawned workspace. This lets operators immediately attribute a session to its worktree when multiple worktrees are active, without switching to `--json` and parsing machine output. Sessions without a spawned workspace display `-`, preserving a stable, scannable layout. JSON output is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Gap confirmed on `origin/main` (`src/commands/sessions-table.ts:21` exposes `spawnedWorkspaceDir`; the text table in `src/commands/sessions.ts` had no `Workspace` column).
- New cell formatter `formatSessionWorkspaceCell` added next to the existing `formatSessionModelCell`, following the same `sanitizeTerminalText` + `theme.muted`/`theme.info` rich/plain pattern.
- New column wired into the text table render in `src/commands/sessions.ts`, placed before the flex `Flags` column so existing column indices (e.g. `Tokens`) are unaffected.
- Test added in the existing `src/commands/sessions.test.ts` (`shows the spawned workspace basename in the text table`): asserts the `Workspace` header is present and that rows render the correct basename (`openclaw-wt-181155`, `openclaw-main`) and `-` for an untethered session.
- The existing `sanitizes persisted identifiers only for terminal output` test was made robust to the narrower `Flags` column by pinning a 240-column terminal (same pattern already used by the `aligns ... columns` test), preserving its sanitization intent.
- Validation: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/sessions.test.ts` → 27/27 passed; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/sessions-cleanup.test.ts` → 13/13 passed (shares `sessions-table.ts` formatters).

prs.title: feat(agents): let the system agent read usage cost
prs.body:
Closes #181148

AI-assisted: implemented by DeepSeek Harness.

## What Problem This Solves

The system agent's `openclaw` tool exposed read actions for status, health, overview, models, agents, channels, plugins, config, and audit, but had no action to report usage and cost. When a user asked the system agent "how much have I spent?" or "what is my token usage?", the agent could not answer from its own tool surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical usage/cost infrastructure already exists: `loadCostUsageSummary` in `src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts` and the `usage.cost` Gateway RPC (`src/gateway/server-methods/usage.ts`). The system agent tool simply had no action wired to it. This adds a `usage` action that follows the same read-only precedent as the recently merged `health` (#171971) and `overview` (#177273) actions, and the `plugin_list` action (#133122): register the action and operation kind, parse it, and execute it through the existing operation executor with no side effects.

The action is read-only: it scopes to the verified inference owner agent (`requesterAgentId`, falling back to the overview's default agent id) and formats the existing `CostUsageSummary` totals (tokens, cost breakdown, missing-cost lower-bound note) into text the agent can return.

## User Impact

Users can now ask the system agent about their usage and cost (for example "show my usage cost" or just "usage") and get a formatted summary of the last N days of token and cost totals for the active agent. No state changes; nothing is written. The action appears in the tool's `Read now:` description and action enum, so the model discovers it as a free read alongside `health` and `overview`.

## Evidence

- New `usage` operation kind added to the `SystemAgentOperation` union (`src/system-agent/operation-types.ts`) and the parse grammar (`src/system-agent/operations-parse.ts`), mirroring `health`/`overview`.
- `usage` executor case in `src/system-agent/operations-execute.ts` calls the new `loadUsageForOperation` helper (`src/system-agent/operations-execution-helpers.ts`), which delegates to `loadCostUsageSummary` or an injected loader, then formats `CostUsageSummary.totals`. `applied: false` — read-only, no audit write.
- `usage` registered in `SYSTEM_AGENT_TOOL_ACTIONS`, `SIMPLE_ACTIONS`, and the `Read now:` description in `src/agents/tools/system-agent-tool.ts`, with a `loadUsage` dep injected from the tool.
- Tests added in existing files (no new test files):
  - `src/agents/tools/system-agent-tool.test.ts`: `usage` is in the action enum, advertised in the description, and routes `{ kind: "usage" }` through the executor as a read (`approved: false`).
  - `src/system-agent/operations.test.ts`: the `usage` executor formats token/cost totals from the injected loader, uses `requesterAgentId` to scope the agent, and surfaces the missing-cost lower-bound note.
- Validation ran via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`:
  - `src/agents/tools/system-agent-tool.test.ts` — 22 passed (22).
  - `src/system-agent/operations.test.ts` — 21 passed (21).
  - `src/system-agent/operations-parse.test.ts` — 90 passed (90).
- `pnpm tsgo:core` could not run in this environment: the native `tsrs` binary requires GLIBC 2.29+ (host has older glibc) and the worktree shares the main install's `node_modules` via symlink, which tsgo rejects as escaping the checkout. Both are environmental, not code, issues; the Vitest runs exercise the real TypeScript through tsx and pass. No `as unknown as` casts; American English; `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `CHANGELOG.md` untouched.

prs.title: fix(oc-path): follow YAML aliases in path resolve, find and set
prs.body:
Fixes #189774

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw path resolve`, `path find`, and alias-slot `path set` treat YAML aliases as missing instead of following their anchored value. Files that share YAML values through anchors cannot be read or searched consistently through ordinary oc:// addresses.

## User Impact

Scalar/intermediate aliases resolve, wildcard and predicate searches include alias-backed values, and replacing an alias slot leaves its anchor intact. Writes through aliases remain refused. Recursive searches stop at cyclic alias edges without dropping distinct noncyclic logical paths. Reported line numbers refer to the anchor; merge keys (`<<`) remain outside this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse YAML's existing `Alias.resolve(doc)` at the shared resolver/finder owner. Preserve the logical edit slot and existing write restrictions. Keep the synchronous find document context bounded by `try/finally`, and use branch-scoped node/remaining-pattern memoization for recursive alias cycles.

All three commits by @jerome-queck are preserved; production is unchanged from the reviewed cyclic-alias repair. The follow-up documents behavior and keeps compact committed regressions within the explicit zero-growth ceiling: existing numeric/malformed-input test setup is simplified without removing assertions, existing tables gain alias read/replacement rows, and one cyclic-search case is retained. Final diff: production +49/-34; docs +6/-0; tests +15/-15 (net zero). Existing assertion-safety allowances mechanically shrink 9→3 and 2→1; no baseline expansion or test allocation.

Simplification review kept the bounded synchronous document owner rather than adding a factory or context API. Concrete result resolution receives its document explicitly after traversal. No new grammar, SDK, schema, or authority behavior.

## Evidence

[Independent built CLI proof on Linux Node 24.22.1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189784#issuecomment-6550391764): main misses scalar/intermediate aliases and wildcard results twice; candidate resolves them twice through real YAML files and its own compiled oc-path plugin. Alias-backed predicates and distinct alias paths are exercised. Dry-run replacement preserves anchor bytes, writes through an alias remain refused, and cyclic find completes with two finite paths. Ordinary direct reads are unchanged; all source files remain byte-identical after dry-run/refused writes.

132 tests pass across YAML-kind, shared find, and resolve suites; formatting passes. The compact alias read, alias-slot replacement, and cyclic-search regressions fail on frozen main for the intended reasons (3 failures, 37 existing cases pass) and all pass on the repaired head. The test file remains 148 lines. No mocked filesystem or direct helper substituted for the shipped CLI proof. Current main's cyclic search is already finite because it ignores aliases; this does not claim an infinite main hang. Existing contributor source/helper proof remains supporting evidence.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores alias misses; no configuration, file migration, or schema change. Reads/searches do not mutate YAML, and dry runs do not write. Blast radius is YAML alias traversal and shared recursive-search cycle bookkeeping; an incorrect memo could miss logical paths, covered by distinct-alias and existing non-YAML traversal controls. Alias-slot replacement is a normal explicit file edit; writes through an alias stay refused.

prs.title: fix: model catalog scan starves the gateway event loop on large catalogs
prs.body:
Closes #145675
Related: #138139

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with a large configured model catalog (hundreds of provider entries) would experience the Gateway becoming fully unresponsive to all concurrent traffic -- dashboard, chat channels, RPC -- for the duration of a catalog evaluation pass. Concurrent requests, including a plain HTTP request to `/healthz`, get no response at all until the scan finishes; from the outside this looks like the Gateway went offline.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createModelsListEntryEvaluator` scheduled every catalog entry as an independent `Promise.resolve().then(...)`, so a large catalog ran as one uninterrupted microtask batch with no point where control returned to the event loop between entries. The fix chains entries through a single tail promise and yields back to the event loop (via `setImmediate`) roughly every 8ms of wall-clock time spent evaluating, instead of letting every entry run in the same batch. No evaluation result, cache key, or ordering guarantee changes -- only *when* each result becomes available.

Separately, this also adds a smaller, always-correct improvement to `providerConfigMatchesRuntimeSnapshot` (called from within each entry's evaluation): a deep-equal shortcut before the two `hashRuntimeConfigValue` calls, for the common case of structurally-identical-but-not-reference-identical provider configs. This is related to #138139 but does not fully close it -- that issue's suggested identity-keyed memoization breaks an existing test that models in-place runtime-config mutation (`keeps distinct configurations current after runtime mutation and replacement`); details in [my comment on that issue](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/138139#issuecomment-5644065185). This PR takes the safe subset (a fresh-every-call shortcut, never stale) rather than the full memoization. (Note: #138351 has since merged a separate, narrower shared-object shortcut for that same function; this PR's `isDeepStrictEqual` addition targets the different, still-uncovered case of distinct-but-equal objects.)

## User Impact

The Gateway keeps answering concurrent requests while a large model-catalog scan runs, instead of appearing to hang or go offline until the scan completes.

## Evidence

### Real production reproduction (2026.9.4, before the fix existed)

This defect was found by diagnosing a live incident, not by reading the source in the abstract. On the affected install, while a catalog scan was in flight:

```text
$ top -bn1 -H -p <gateway-pid>
  PID USER  PR  NI  VIRT   RES   SHR S  %CPU %MEM  TIME+  COMMAND
 <pid> ...  20   0  27.6g  1.0g  ...  R  93.9  1.6  7:42.90 MainThread

$ curl -s -m 5 -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code} in %{time_total}s\n" http://127.0.0.1:18789/healthz
HTTP 000 in 5.002484s

$ openclaw gateway health
gateway timeout after 10000ms
```

After applying this fix and restarting:

```text
$ openclaw gateway health
Gateway Health
OK (79ms)
Telegram: configured

$ openclaw gateway call health
{ "ok": true, "eventLoop": { "degraded": false, "reasons": [] }, ... }
```

### Controlled before/after measurement (isolated repro, this checkout)

To get a clean, repeatable A/B measurement (not just the live incident above), I wrote a small standalone script (not part of this diff) that:
- builds the same `createModelCatalogDecisions` owner used by the real Gateway, with a synthetic 500-entry catalog across two providers,
- starts a real local HTTP server sharing the process's event loop (the closest same-process analog to the Gateway's own `/healthz` handler),
- fires real concurrent HTTP requests against it every 5ms while `Promise.all(entries.map(owner.evaluateEntry))` runs,
- measures actual request latency, success/timeout counts, total scan time, and process RSS.

Ran 3 times each on `main` (unpatched) and on this branch (patched), Node v24.19.0:

| | Unpatched (`main`) | Patched (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Concurrent requests attempted per run | ~18 | ~18 |
| Concurrent requests that **succeeded** | **1** (all 3 runs) | **17-18** (all 3 runs) |
| Concurrent requests that timed out | 0 (rest just never got a chance to run before the scan ended) | 0 |
| Median successful-request latency | 1653-1772ms (i.e. the one request that got through waited almost the entire scan) | 10ms |
| Scan wall time (500 entries) | 1627-1742ms | 1747-2519ms* |
| Process RSS delta during scan | +10MB | +10-21MB |

\* Slightly higher on the patched side -- expected, since the scan now periodically yields to the event loop instead of running flat-out; this is the traded-off cost of staying responsive, not a regression in per-entry work.

Raw output, patched run 1:
```json
{"entries":500,"scanElapsedMs":2519,"concurrentRequestsDuringScan":17,"concurrentRequestsSucceeded":17,"concurrentRequestsTimedOut":0,"maxRequestLatencyMs":2210,"medianRequestLatencyMs":10,"rssBeforeMb":627,"rssAfterMb":648}
```
Raw output, unpatched run 1:
```json
{"entries":500,"scanElapsedMs":1627,"concurrentRequestsDuringScan":1,"concurrentRequestsSucceeded":1,"concurrentRequestsTimedOut":0,"maxRequestLatencyMs":1653,"medianRequestLatencyMs":1653,"rssBeforeMb":630,"rssAfterMb":640}
```

Honest caveat: in every patched run, the very first concurrent request (only) landed before the first yield point and took longer than the steady-state 10ms median (up to ~2.2s) -- consistent with it racing the initial synchronous batch of promise-chain construction before any yield has occurred yet. Every subsequent request in every patched run was fast and none timed out; in the unpatched baseline, only that first request *ever* got serviced at all, and only once the whole scan had nearly finished.

### Test coverage

- Added a regression test (`yields to the event loop instead of monopolizing it across a large catalog scan`) that mocks `performance.now()` to force the yield threshold and asserts `setImmediate` is invoked. prs.title: feat(database): capture exact SQLite migration capsules
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary portable backups intentionally sanitize delivery/recovery state. They cannot serve as exact original-state capsules when moving a stopped SQLite installation to a disposable host for database migration.

## User Impact

Adds `openclaw database migration-capture capabilities|create|restore`. Operators retain exact native SQLite/configuration images with a verified filesystem base and restore only into new private staging. This does not import PostgreSQL, start services, resume database ports, or change ordinary backup sanitization.

Creation requires stopped writers, state-relative databases, valid pinned configuration, and an output outside live state/configuration roots. Unsupported PostgreSQL sources and external roots fail explicitly. The manifest digest is a producer receipt, not a substitute for operator custody of this sensitive capsule. The operator must bind a fresh base archive to the same stopped source generation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the offline state owner, existing recovery-store discovery, verified SQLite publication, archive admission, and matched shared/local credential owner. Restore admits every artifact before creating staging, overlays only private regular staged files, removes explicitly missing database families, and cleans failed staging. The manifest-pair guard permits installations that have shared state but no local credential database.

This is the smallest coherent offline create/verify/restore slice of [Galin's capture change](https://github.com/galiniliev/openclaw/commit/2c4173934ae1074ecca1b1f48eb13410c143d603). [Source-preserving archive acquisition #189638](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189638) and [PostgreSQL companion profiles #189685](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189685) are merged. [Externally quiesced capture #189802](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189802) remains a separate, dependent PR. The new capsule orchestration is necessary to combine existing owners; no new database/state manager or alternate recovery implementation is introduced.

## Evidence

### Combined companion admission

Integrated landed main `4fb684e294e27aed927548aaf64d2a7b8ba4696f`, retaining both ordinary companion selection and this PR's internal SQLite-only restore option. The combined guard checks typed PostgreSQL anchors as well as export candidates at **both** capture-base admission and SQLite-only restore admission, before output/target creation. Ordinary companion restoration and a zero-anchor SQLite-only companion remain accepted.

Both regressions were reproduced through genuinely verified archives on the combined unguarded code: creation and restore incorrectly returned `ok` rather than rejecting. No malformed-fixture failure was credited. After the two-condition repair, **50 tests across three affected files pass**, including the positive sibling cases, exact state/credential promotion, alias/tamper handling, archive completeness, and both physical-source refusal paths. Vitest 273.93s; complete wrapper 436.36s including 140.054s worker preparation and joined cleanup. The new capture-base and restore checks executed in 162ms and 33ms; the zero-anchor profile control took 90ms.

Core production, commands-test and infra-test typechecks pass. Source-backed type-aware lint passes all four touched files; formatting and diff checks pass. The exact **354-line** allocation gate passes (previous 292 plus 62 justified net lines for these independent admission paths and their positive control). No shared scalar, timeout, assertion, schema, authority or durability policy was weakened.

Fresh independent autoreview against pinned landed main completed final source verification with **no actionable P0–P2 findings**. It reviewed the selected source/patch and complete supplied admission owners; it did not execute project code or independently validate omitted dependency implementations. The prior complete credential-owner review remains separately recorded below.

The main integration carries the already-landed state-schema-37 migration. Earlier CLI evidence remains bound to its original source, not relabeled as new-head execution. The requested latest-stable and promoted-authority proof is now complete as detailed below; current-head CI and hosted reassessment remain pending.

### Latest-stable offline round trip and final protected authority — passed

Executed a complete new runtime built at clean integrated source `2335c6a6bed1d65d4c7f5a02b8aee6dc62927547` in [dependent PR #189802](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189802), which contains this PR's exact published dependency `23b25e002c40e7c88e3b53a230a4a7e0abe4a8b1`. This is explicitly **offline exact-SQLite proof**, not PostgreSQL companion proof or externally quiesced capture: the real command supplied `--base-archive`, no suspension IDs or `--externally-quiesced`, and the capture receipt contained no quiescence record.

1. Published npm **OpenClaw 2026.10.9**, independently resolved as latest stable, initialized absent databases and created/read a session through its real Gateway and CLI. Candidate Doctor upgraded that actual stored state. The candidate loaded the retained session, settings, shared authentication, and user file; schema **37** and `worker_environments.resource_receipt_json` were asserted.
2. Two distinct real Ed25519 clients received tokens through Gateway handshakes and native token-cache owners. **Both first performed protected `agents.files.set` writes**, proving the forbidden-client test was not a client that had never been authorized.
3. A real controller revoked one device before capture. Its device-token-only protected request was rejected with `device_token_mismatch`, **zero authenticated-handshake callbacks**, and an independent file witness unchanged: bytes/SHA-256, inode, size, nanosecond mtime and ctime.
4. After accepted work settled through the existing ready/non-drain suspension and the disposable Gateway stopped, the built CLI ran **backup create/verify → offline migration-capture create → migration-capture restore** into fresh staging. The capsule included the native local credential database. Exact configuration and user-file bytes matched; explicit disposable-tree promotion retained the old source separately.
5. Both transported identities and both cached bearer values loaded through the real local credential owners. A real Gateway then started on the **promoted restored SQLite authority** and loaded the stable-created session. The allowed client successfully performed the protected file write. The client revoked before capture was refused before authenticated dispatch, with the independent file witness unchanged.
6. The controller then revoked the remaining allowed client **against the promoted authority**. Its cached device-token-only write was also refused before authenticated dispatch with the same unchanged-file oracle. This proves final protected effects and denial, not just credential-row admission.
7. All three owned Gateway stops and final worker/fixture cleanup joined. **1/1 passed: 79.932s test, 86.48s Vitest, 100.01s complete repository wrapper; exit 0.** No live user installation, database, or non-public endpoint was used.

**Exact snapshot semantics:** restoring SQLite restores captured authority. This proof does not claim that a source revocation occurring after capture survives rollback. It proves a revocation present at capture and a new revocation against the activated restored owner.

**Source applicability:** parent `23b25e0` and executed `2335c6a` have identical backup/restore, credential rebinding, device identity/token, protected file-handler, and schema-upgrade owners. The capture module differs by PR5's reviewed suspension adapter; this execution selects the normal offline branch over the same owners, with both export/nonempty-anchor guards preserved. Parent inspection checked the actual introduced diff and proof fixture, not only the result summary. No claim is made that the full PR3 and PR5 trees are identical.

**Reproducibility/binding:** complete `pnpm build:runtime` stamps bind clean head `2335c6a`; build input signature `f9ec5de26145decf70e67f6e00d9c5122fd54a1575e986d2a6be5fbc71c0da17`, runtime-postbuild signature `48d845aa6a45b8d7a63a961277550192d17986378d75db0155589df7bda2cbd6`, executed entrypoint SHA-256 `9b04b8104f537ec5b85f62a0d67cc34d348dcc347116c908b08639c0066f83e2`, proof fixture SHA-256 `09afc4c3c93a7e07ad35524be795fa15ac8b8afe6c5dd3527b81da871b0a0980`. The retained disposable fixture uses `createOpenClawTestInstance`, the actual CLI and Gateway, and independent filesystem observations; no mocked auth or private credentials are included here.

**Earlier attempts retained:** two schema-36 attempts exhausted the unchanged 60-second Gateway startup deadline under heavy I/O and were not credited as final proof. The first schema-37 attempt hit the fixture's unchanged 3-second child-cleanup deadline. The passing fixture settles accepted work with the existing bounded suspension before each normal stop; all stop receipts passed. No Gateway readiness, cleanup, RPC timeout, lease heartbeat, authority check, or product code was weakened. Later success is not claimed as a product fix for those setup/timing failures.

### Earlier source-bound proof

- **Real alias regression:** the owner captured a canonical state root while restore compared the caller's lexical path. The alias case failed with the expected logical-path rejection before the repair. Both sides now use the existing canonical identity resolver.
- **Real absent-credentials regression:** complete independent review found a valid shared-without-local-credentials capsule that failed during rebinding. The actual create/restore case failed before the fix. Rebinding now requires the local image declared by the admitted manifest, not a filesystem existence guess.
- **Earlier offline integration:** all **5 cases pass** through actual archive/capture/restore owners and native SQLite, including queued delivery intent, daemon pins, private socket credentials, workspace bytes, promoted credential admission, state/output aliases, missing local credentials, and artifact/manifest tampering before target creation. Wrapper 388.99s including worker preparation and cleanup. The two physical PostgreSQL-refusal cases also passed, including the stopped-store fast path.
- **Landed prerequisite integration:** the pinned main commit containing #189638 was merged to provide a clean base for the dependent quiesced PR. No conflicts or feature production edits were needed; the three production modules and their existing owner contracts remain byte-identical, with matching feature patch ID. All **9 tests across three files** pass on the combined tree: five capsule cases, WAL/DELETE source-preservation cases, and both physical PostgreSQL-refusal cases; complete wrapper 53.50s. Core typecheck passes. The live CLI result remains explicitly bound to its earlier clean source, not relabeled as a new-head run.
- **Checks:** core production and commands/services test typechecks passed; final repair's commands-test typecheck and source-backed lint passed. Production/test formatting and diff checks passed. Documentation link validation checked 16,194 links with zero broken. That earlier revision allocated 292 governed lines; the combined candidate's exact 354-line allocation is verified above.
- **Review:** full committed-context independent review included the unchanged credential owner and identified the missing-local issue. Fresh repair review completed source verification with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Earlier incomplete reviews are not credited as clean. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable, so the documented local-autoreview/hosted-review fallback applies.
- **Real built CLI proof:** runtime build completed at clean source `3710860d6c54c01eae89b4479bf9aad55b9c7e5b`. A disposable, uniquely profiled instance exercised capabilities → ordinary backup creation/verification → exact capsule capture → staging restore → exact witness-row read and promoted credential-owner admission → tamper refusal before target creation. All four stage markers passed; 1/1 proof test passed in 11.455s, with the full test wrapper and joined cleanup finishing in 50.50s. The build and runtime-postbuild stamps both bind the executing source; no installed Gateway or user database was accessed. The disposable proof harness was removed after settlement.
- **Prior setup failures retained:** the first CLI attempt selected the default service during runtime preparation; the corrected-profile attempt then exhausted its unchanged 600-second command deadline while building bundled plugins. Neither was product proof. Separate standard runtime preparation completed successfully before the passing run; no publication guard, heartbeat, or product deadline was weakened.

Historical cold Node runs hit startup/no-output or outer command limits. Later Bun passes do not establish fixes for those timing failures. No live installation or real user database was used.

prs.title: fix(agents): preserve fractional millisecond timestamps
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: message timestamps supplied as fractional millisecond strings are interpreted as seconds, producing dates 1,000 times too far in the future.

## User Impact

Slack, Discord, and other SDK consumers now retain the correct date for millisecond timestamps such as `1700000000000.5`.

## Why This Change Was Made

String timestamps should use the same magnitude-based unit detection as numeric timestamps. The previous string branch treated every decimal string as seconds, while numeric inputs already distinguished seconds from milliseconds by magnitude.

## Evidence

### Final behavior proof

The Slack plugin's `ChannelMessageActionAdapter.handleAction` `read` entrypoint received a provider message from the real `@slack/web-api` client over a local loopback Slack API fixture. The fixture returned a fractional millisecond string and a seconds-scale Slack control. The test passed on head `400cba6aa1c95c122937e1f49b2ab1ee5c608ca0` in [the exact GitHub CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40378689884/job/121769577090).

Input and returned channel-action payload asserted by the test:

```json
{
  "ts": "1700000000000.5",
  "timestampMs": 1700000000001,
  "timestampUtc": "2023-11-14T22:13:20.001Z"
}
```

The same result retained the seconds-scale control `1712345678.123456` as `timestampMs: 1712345678123`. The CI log reports the named Slack channel-action test passed; the Slack changed-extension shard completed with 163 tests passed.

### Supporting checks

- `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-2`: Slack channel-action/Web API test passed.
- `check-test-types`: passed for the changed Slack action test.
- `check-prod-types`, `check-lint`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Autoreview reported no actionable findings for the test change and its fixture correction.

### Proof boundary

The channel action and Slack Web API client are production code; only the Slack HTTP service is a local fixture. This proves the returned action payload without contacting a Slack workspace or sending an external message. No credentials or private channel data were used.

Exact head: `400cba6aa1c95c122937e1f49b2ab1ee5c608ca0`

prs.title: fix(gateway): retain full plugin commands without a default workspace
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In a multi-agent Gateway without `agents.defaults.workspace`, command registration from the admitting Gateway must remain available to the prepared reply registry. The regression is user-visible when a plugin registers its command only during `registerFull` and the text command instead falls through to the model.

## User Impact

The prepared reply path retains full-mode plugin commands for agents in a multi-agent configuration without a default workspace. The regression exercises the real command dispatcher and verifies that the command produces a reply and stops further handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep borrowing eligibility in the existing per-plugin loader, which owns source, activation, and workspace-inventory decisions. prs.title: feat(nodes): show recorded contact ages in nodes describe
prs.body:
Closes #181157

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw nodes describe` cannot answer "when did this node last talk to the Gateway?" for a node that is offline, so an operator investigating a stopped node has to switch to `nodes status` and scan for the matching row, or decode `--json` timestamps by hand — exactly when the timestamp matters most.

## User Impact

`nodes describe` now reports two recorded contact rows next to the existing `Last input` row:

- `Last seen` — the newest recorded Gateway contact for the node.
- `Connection` — `connected <age>` while the node is live, `last connected <age>` from stored connection history once it is offline.

No behavior change for `--json` consumers, and gateways that record no contact facts keep today's output: a row is only rendered when its field is present.

## Why This Change Was Made

Presentation only, inside the describe renderer; the facts are the ones `node.describe` already returns.

- `lastSeenAtMs` is the newest of the live connection time, the stored pairing `lastSeenAtMs`, the stored `lastConnectedAtMs`, and the device-pairing `lastSeenAtMs` (`resolveEffectiveLastSeen` in `src/gateway/node-catalog-read.ts`). Because stored pairing history feeds it, it still renders for a disconnected node, where the live `connectedAtMs` is already gone.
- The connection row uses `connectedAtMs` while live and `lastConnectedAtMs ?? connectedAtMs` when offline; the fallback keeps older gateways without the stored field working.
- The three labels stay distinct, per the conflation risk in the earlier review: `Last input` is user interaction (`lastActiveAtMs`), `Last seen` is Gateway contact, `Connection` is connection age. Nothing new is collected, persisted, or exposed: `node.describe` already spreads the catalog entry (`src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.read.ts`), so this is rendering plus docs plus tests.

The describe action also used `Date.now()` twice per render; it now takes one `now` so every age in one table shares a clock.

## Evidence

### Shipped CLI against a live Gateway (isolated state)

Setup, no production state touched: Gateway `openclaw gateway run --port 47860` under an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, then a real Linux node host joined it with `openclaw connect <setup-code> --display-name proof-node`.

Connected node — `openclaw nodes describe --node proof-node` (unrelated rows trimmed):

```text
│ Client     │ node-host/node                                                                                          │
│ Version    │ core v2026.10.7                                                                                         │
│ Stats      │ load 6.3/8 · mem 18/24 GB · disk 152 GB free                                                            │
│ Last seen  │ 3m ago                                                                                                  │
│ Connection │ connected 3m ago                                                                                        │
│ Status     │ paired · connected                                                                                      │
```

Same node after the node-host process is stopped, `node.describe` now served from stored pairing facts:

```text
│ Stats      │ load 8.3/8 · mem 16/24 GB · disk 152 GB free (last known 1m ago)                                        │
│ Last seen  │ 5m ago                                                                                                  │
│ Connection │ last connected 5m ago                                                                                   │
│ Status     │ paired · disconnected                                                                                   │
│ Approval   │ approved                                                                                                │
```

That is the operator case from the issue: the offline row keeps the recorded contact and connection ages instead of printing no timestamp at all.

### `--json` is untouched

The action returns `writeJson(result)` before any of the new code runs, so the JSON payload is the Gateway's `node.describe` result verbatim. Live check with both states: the payload keys differ only in gateway-owned presence fields (`connectedAtMs`, `lastDisconnectedAtMs`, `pathEnv`, `nodePluginTools`), none of which this diff reads or writes.

### Red on base, green on head

```sh
git checkout HEAD^ -- src/cli/nodes-cli/register.status.ts   # base renderer, new tests present
pnpm test src/cli/nodes-cli/register.status.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

```text
× renders the last Gateway contact and the live connection age
× keeps the stored connection age for a disconnected node
  AssertionError: expected 'Node\n┌────────────┬─────────────────…' to contain 'Last seen'
Tests  2 failed | 9 passed (11)
```

With the PR head restored the same file is 11 passed (3.6 s warm, 7.8 s cold). The third new case asserts the rows are absent when the Gateway records no contact facts, so it passes on base by design.

### Checks run

`pnpm exec oxlint` on both touched files: 0 warnings, 0 errors. `node scripts/run-format.mts --check`: clean. `scripts/format-docs.mts --check`: clean. Line-cap / max-lines / test-lines ratchets: OK. CI on this head: no failing check.

### Not tested

- `pnpm tsgo:core` cannot run in this environment (the pinned `tsrs` binary needs GLIBC 2.29); CI typecheck covers the touched files.
- The live run above used a locally built CLI from this head; no macOS/Windows node host was available, so the host-stats/last-known variants come from the existing test fixtures rather than a second real device.
---

### ClawSweeper verdict

Diff: production +17/−2 (`src/cli/nodes-cli/register.status.ts`) | tests +56/−0 | docs +7/−0 → **+80/−2 across 3 files**.

| Dimension | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Overall readiness | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** — capped only by the unresolved product-direction decision |
| Proof confidence | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** — "Sufficient (live_output): … shipped CLI against an isolated live Gateway and real Linux node host … resolves the previous review's proof request." |
| Patch quality | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** — "No actionable review findings were identified." |

[ClawSweeper re-review (2026-10-26)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184758#issuecomment-6420509686) — labels `proof: sufficient`, `rating: 🦐 gold shrimp`, `status: ⏳ waiting on maintainer`.


---

## Decision requested (not an approval claim)

The ClawSweeper `Recommendation` quoted above is an **advisory design suggestion, not a contract approval** — it was written by the review bot, and no maintainer has recorded a decision on this direction. This PR adds two diagnostic rows (`Last seen`, `Connection`) to the `nodes describe` renderer using facts `node.describe` already returns, and it is waiting on an owner decision before merge.

| Option | Effect | Cost if chosen |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Accept (this PR)** | `nodes describe` reports when an offline node last talked to the Gateway and its connection age, next to the existing `Last input` row. | Two rows rendered only when their recorded fields are present; `--json` consumers and gateways without contact facts are unchanged. |
| **Decline and close** | Operators keep switching to `nodes status` or decoding `--json` timestamps to answer the same question. | Nothing from this PR is lost; the labels stay distinct from `Last input`. |

prs.title: fix: parent sessions miss child approvals with a custom session store
prs.body:
Closes #189823

## What Problem This Solves

Parent sessions miss child approval events and reconnect replay when `session.store` points to a custom store.

## User Impact

Authorized parent subscribers receive their child's approval updates with custom stores. Existing recipient authorization and registry-parent precedence remain unchanged; no configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The audience resolver used the metadata reader without its configured store locator. Pass the existing per-agent store resolver into that reader. The production change is two lines; the remaining changes prove the configured-store, registry and actual Gateway boundaries.

## Evidence

### Shipped Gateway runtime capture — outside Vitest

The missing shipped-entry gate is now exercised through the **normal package binary**, built independently from the parent and current PR commits. No Vitest, test-helper server startup, mocked audience/authorization, source imports or server-constructor calls were used. A separate Node observer imports the **built public** `dist/plugin-sdk/gateway-runtime.js` `GatewayClient` and uses real authenticated WebSocket connections and public RPCs.

| Run | Source/build identity | Observed parent pending / pending replay / denied terminal |
|---|---|---|
| Original failure | `4fb684e294e27aed927548aaf64d2a7b8ba4696f`; `2026.10.9-4fb684e294e2-2026-10-31T23-19-58.960Z` | `false / false / false`, after all setup and positive controls passed |
| Patched success | `50381fbe3d4bd39942d42fcbc32069f230916ff3`; `2026.10.9-50381fbe3d4b-2026-10-31T23-16-17.896Z` | `true / true / true` |

Each run has its own private0700 HOME, config, client credentials, Gateway state, workspace, caches and loopback listener. Normal token authentication and device pairing remain enabled. Configuration is admitted by the normal CLI validator before launch; `session.store` points to `<RUN_ROOT>/custom-{agentId}/sessions.json`. Three equal-authority CLI clients isolate session routing. Public `sessions.create` and `sessions.describe` establish the actual stored child→parent metadata before approval registration. The unrelated subscription first receives its **own** pending and denied-terminal approval, then excludes the child's live events and pending replay while the child request remains pending. All resolutions are `deny`; no executor RPC, model call or external provider send is made. This is ordinary session projection proof, not separate-user resource authorization.

<details>
<summary>Exact build/launch commands and normal RPC flow</summary>

Paths and ephemeral endpoints below are placeholders for the task-owned builds and private per-run directories; no operator Gateway/service or production configuration is used.

# Observer preflight (artifact-local scripts, outside product source)

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p "$PROOF/observer.tsconfig.json"

# Actual invocations, with sanitized output captured
python3 "$PROOF/launch-proof.py" patched "$PATCHED"
python3 "$PROOF/launch-proof.py" baseline "$BASELINE"

# Each launcher creates a fresh private0700 /tmp tree and an allowlisted environment.
# Its normal config preflight and actual separate-process Gateway command are:
/usr/bin/node "$BUILD/openclaw.mjs" config validate --json
/usr/bin/node "$BUILD/openclaw.mjs" gateway run --port "$PORT" --bind loopback

The launcher supplies only an allowlisted environment (`PATH`, private `HOME`/`TMPDIR`/XDG directories, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, private client `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `NODE_ENV=production`, `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, `NO_COLOR=1`, `TERM=dumb`). The Gateway child's `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` selects its own private Gateway directory. No inherited model/API/service credentials or test flags are passed. Browser, cron, external hooks, mDNS, telemetry and update checks are disabled using supported disposable configuration; there are no configured external channel accounts. No admission or approval authorization callback is overridden.

Public flow: create parent/unrelated/child (`parentSessionKey` on child), describe child, subscribe all three with `includeApprovals:true`, register unrelated positive, deny it, register child approval, request parent and unrelated pending replay, then deny child. The approval request uses `host:"local"`, `ask:"always"`, `twoPhase:true`, `requireDeliveryRoute:false`, and a synthetic `printf shipped-proof-never-executed` command; the flow never invokes execution. prs.title: fix(macos): don't check Off in Thinking/Verbose menu for sessions inheriting the agent default
prs.body:
Fixes #187607

## What Problem This Solves

In the macOS status-bar menu, a session that has not set its own Thinking/Verbose level inherits the agent default. The menu previously manufactured an "Off" checkmark for such sessions, misrepresenting the effective level.

## Why This Change Was Made

`StatusMenuSessions.swift` had two places that fell back a `nil` override to `"off"` when building or updating the Thinking/Verbose submenus. A `nil` value means "inherit the agent default", not "off", so this produced an incorrect check. Both paths are repaired: `buildPreferenceMenu` (fresh submenu) and `updatePreferenceMenu` (reused submenu).

## User Impact

Sessions inheriting the agent default now show no item selected in their Thinking/Verbose submenus instead of a misleading "Off" check. Explicitly configured sessions are unaffected.

## Evidence

**Asserted AppKit menu state on macOS, head vs base.** `StatusMenuProbe` drives the shipped `StatusMenuSessions` against a real `NSMenuItem`/`NSMenu` tree using the repository's own `GatewayTestWebSocketSession` fixture (the same transport double as the committed tests below) and asserts the expected checkmarks. The workflow no longer tolerates failures: the probe fails when its expectation does not hold, the regression step asserts its exit code per mode, and base mode fails loudly if its revert patch stops applying.

| scenario | path | head | base (fallback restored) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| inherited (`thinkingLevel`/`verboseLevel` nil) | fresh | no item checked | **Off checked** |
| inherited | reuse | no item checked | **Off checked** |
| explicit `off` | fresh + reuse | Off checked | — |
| explicit `high` | fresh + reuse | High checked | — |
| explicit verbose `off` | fresh + reuse | Off checked (Verbose) | — |

Head run [`41197714308`](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/actions/runs/41197714308) prints
`CHECK inherited path=fresh thinking=[] verbose=[]` / `path=reuse` `[]`, asserts `REGRESSION_EXIT=0`, 10 tests passed.

Base run [`41197720414`](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/actions/runs/41197720414) prints
`CHECK inherited path=fresh thinking=["Off"] verbose=["Off"]` / `path=reuse` `["Off"]`, asserts `REGRESSION_EXIT=1`
with `Expectation failed: submenu.items.allSatisfy { $0.state != .on }`.

**Committed regression** in `apps/macos/Tests/OpenClawIPCTests/StatusMenuSummariesTests.swift`:
`Thinking and Verbose submenus show no check when the session inherits the agent default` — green on head, red on base (both exit codes asserted above).

**On screenshots:** this environment is Linux-only, and GitHub's macOS runners cannot capture menu pixels. Verified on `macos-latest`: `screencapture` returns the menu window frame with no item text or checkmark content (Screen Recording is not granted, and NSMenu content is drawn by WindowServer); the popup window is visible in `NSApp.windows` but `cacheDisplay` renders it blank; `CGWindowListCreateImage` and `CGDisplayCreateImage` are obsoleted in the macOS 15 SDK. The menu-state table above is therefore the strongest evidence obtainable here — a before/after app screenshot needs a Mac and can be supplied by a maintainer if required.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): show reconnect feedback only for real connection delays
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The original campaign measured 14 visible startup states over about 15 seconds on a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link. This PR addresses one remaining warm-reload artifact.

An ordinary signed-in warm reload of a chat or dashboard deep link flashed “Saved conversation · Reconnecting…” despite a healthy connection. Cached history and pending route resolution manufactured this status independently of the Gateway owner.

## User Impact

Normal warm reloads retain their cached content without a connection-status flash. Slow and failed connections show feedback inside the header without moving its controls or covering conversation rows. Real socket loss produces feedback immediately and retains it through retries until hello succeeds.

Identity and action hydration remain separate follow-up work. The fully offline dashboard screenshot shows the HTML widget's connection-waiting view; cached transcript, sidebar and chrome remain visible. This PR does not claim the broader cached-page campaign is complete.

## Why This Change Was Made

The header now consumes shared Gateway status and its existing two-second initial grace. An observed socket close ends that grace immediately. Cached messages only qualify the label; they no longer invent connection state. The existing action region retains its flexible width and holds feedback in its available gap. Desktop controls stay mounted during recovery.

No new timer, config option, transport/backoff/liveness policy, Gateway protocol or durable state change. The existing grace comfortably covers the normal sub-second handshake. An inexpensive connected check also keeps transcript projection out of connected header rendering.

Release-note context: Control UI warm reloads no longer flash reconnect feedback during an ordinary initial handshake; slow or failed connections remain visible without displacing header controls.

## Evidence

Head: `b7f9de1604be6c4f7580377ff4dc18e397712455`; pinned main: `9e3b867810d470abf8b39af2eafa1a56dd7b49c3`.

Real outage proof and remaining validation continued on the same retained lease and unchanged head, with clean-tree assertions and active-conversation persistence verified through the existing cache owner.

### Production and test cost

UI runtime net **+13 lines**, reusable diagnostic **+10**. The requested non-test/non-doc stat is **144 additions / 118 deletions, net +26**, including the two-line allocation and one added narrow browser fixture line. Runtime/diagnostic source growth is +23 lines. The small growth reserves the flexible feedback slot and makes observed failure immediate while deleting the competing cached-history status fallback and desktop menu-hiding policy. Existing late-action reservation remains covered in Chromium and WebKit.

The exact test allocation is **155 net LF lines**, with no slack or shared scalar bump: owner normal/slow/failed grace regression, updated status table, and native two-route lifecycle/geometry/containment regression, plus offline feedback in the existing narrow desktop fixture. The diagnostic stays because `bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts` calls it through `--pane-chrome-probe`; indicator frames and identity attribution are reusable by the follow-up lane.

prs.title: docs(i18n): expand Russian glossary (250 entries) and add ru navigation (12 tabs / 55 groups)
prs.body:
## What

Russian docs localization is wired up but nearly empty: `docs/.i18n/glossary.ru.json` was 21 entries (1.2 KB) against 107 KB for `zh-CN`, and `ru-navigation.json` did not exist at all, so the Russian sidebar fell back to English while the pages themselves were already 75% translated.

This PR fills in the two files that drive the Russian locale:

- `glossary.ru.json`: **21 → 250 entries** (1.2 KB → 18.6 KB). Existing entries and their order are preserved; 6 target terms were corrected for consistency with the pages: Compaction → Сжатие контекста, Gateway → Шлюз, Node → Нода, Plugin → Плагин, Skills → Скиллы, Webhook → Вебхук. Deliberately kept in English: Active Memory, Cron, Dreaming, Heartbeat, Loopback, Markdown, Self-hosted.
- `ru-navigation.json`: **created from scratch — 12 tabs, 55 groups** (8.6 KB), mirroring the English navigation structure.

No page content, no build scripts, no English strings touched: two data files only.

## Verification

- Every path in `ru-navigation.json` was checked against the repository tree (1,385 `.md` files): 0 broken links, 55 unique anchors.
- Rendered through the real `composeDocsConfig()` from `scripts/docs-sync-publish.mjs`: 12/12 Russian tabs, 55/55 groups, pages resolve as `ru/index…`.
- `glossary.ru.json` parses as valid JSON and keeps the original key order (`json.load` round-trip diff on the untouched prefix).
- Note: `check-docs-i18n-glossary.mts` only validates `zh-CN` today, so this file is not CI-gated — I verified it manually as described above.

## Why

The Russian locale is the largest non-English audience for OpenClaw docs and currently has English headings over Russian text. These two files are the smallest, highest-leverage change: no translation work, but the sidebar and the inline glossary switch to Russian immediately.

## Visual proof

Rendered through the real `composeDocsConfig()` from `scripts/docs-sync-publish.mjs`, locale `ru`, same tree, only `docs/.i18n/ru-navigation.json` added.

| Before (`main` — no ru overlay) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adamant064/openclaw/docs/ru-i18n-proof/proof/ru-sidebar-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adamant064/openclaw/docs/ru-i18n-proof/proof/ru-sidebar-after.png) |

Behavioural comparison of the two composed configs:

```
before: tabs 12, groups 55, pages 308
after : tabs 12, groups 55, pages 308      # page inventory identical
before tabs: Get started | Install | Channels | Agents | Capabilities | Models |
             Platforms | Gateway & Ops | Reference | Releases | Contributing | Help
after  tabs: Начало работы | Установка | Каналы | Агенты | Возможности | Модели |
             Платформы | Шлюз и эксплуатация | Справочник | Релизы | Участие в разработке | Помощь
```

Only labels change; every route and its order is preserved, which is the guarantee the overlay functions (`applyLocaleNavLabelOverlay`) are supposed to give. Screenshots are generated from the composed `docs.json` (sidebar label tree), not from a live docs host, so nothing is redacted and no endpoint is involved.
