prs.title: perf(gateway): share equivalent session publication preparation
prs.body:
## Final tail qualification and disposition

**Decision: close unmerged.** The lead withdrew the arbitrary 5x allocation target and accepted the measured allocation/CPU gains and +92 production LOC, conditional on tails fitting timing A/A noise. All 20 requested control windows completed, with five fresh-boot windows in each of A1/A2 (baseline) and B1/B2 (candidate), on the fixed interleaved schedule. No window was excluded or retried; the original full fixture was restored. Both loop statistics passed the predeclared rule. Both GC statistics failed for the original and contemporaneous comparisons. The conditional acceptance statement does not apply.

| Cohort (5 windows each) | Loop maximum: median [min–max], ms | GC-p99: median [min–max], ms |
|---|---:|---:|
| A1 (baseline) | 171.311 [146.276–251.265] | 27.646 [25.342–28.286] |
| A2 (baseline) | 301.728 [131.990–394.789] | 29.822 [27.390–30.590] |
| B1 (candidate) | 181.273 [124.977–525.337] | 32.254 [25.726–80.382] |
| B2 (candidate) | 142.475 [127.140–224.264] | 28.926 [24.958–35.838] |

| Tail statistic | Original increase | New A/B signed change | Baseline noise ceiling | Candidate noise ceiling | Original within both | New within both |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| medianLoopMax | 24.501% | -22.761% | 76.398% | 74.414% | True | True |
| medianGcP99 | 26.668% | 9.886% | 7.871% | 26.514% | False | False |
| p95LoopP99 | 21.562% | 32.586% | 68.408% | 161.459% | True | True |
| p95GcP99 | 29.080% | 162.772% | 8.145% | 130.890% | False | False |

The original and fresh A/B increases were compared with each version's predeclared empirical ceiling: all 252 balanced five-versus-five splits, nearest-rank 95th percentile of absolute log statistic ratios, transformed back to a percentage. Both versions' ceilings had to cover each positive change. This is a measured qualification for this workload/host, not proof of a source-code regression or statistical equivalence. The fresh median GC-p99 was 27.838→30.590ms (+9.886%); across-window p95 was 30.590→80.382ms (+162.772%). The slow candidate B1 window is retained.

The retention audit found no new publication-state edge into queued sends or connection history. Projectors/runtime WeakMaps stay publication-owned; the transport receives encoded bytes, and connection history retains existing bounded fingerprints/certificates. One additional bounded unfiltered child view can occur for restricted audiences, but the all-admin fixture already used that view before this patch. No clearing change is justified by that ownership trace.

Fresh post-GC old-space medians were 569.815→570.284MB; post-GC heap medians 672.990→673.371MB. These short fresh-process bursts show no large persistent retained-cache increase, but cannot rule out a long-lived production leak. Fewer GC events also change the all-GC p99 rank; the retained summaries cannot reconstruct raw pause sequences or establish that mixture explains the increase. The slow B1 window contained minor max 137.552ms and major max 156.615ms, and coincided with window-matched host load 44.779 versus 17.131/19.226 in adjacent baselines. Coincidence is not causal proof, so host load is not used to waive the failed gate.

Code remained unchanged at 7e959fc6efc7 throughout the controls. Focused security/regression tests, changed-file checks, Codex autoreview, and exact-head CI remain green. Native review retains NEEDS DISCUSSION; no prepare/merge request is submitted. The 5x target is not a closure reason. The independent GC-log reporter repair in this branch also remains unmerged; the pre-existing main tooling regression introduced by f5b87c5f8228/#178075 still needs separate disposition.

## What Problem This Solves

Session event fan-out repeatedly prepares identical display rows and envelopes for distinct signed-in viewers, allocating far more than the delta delivered to each dashboard.

## User Impact

Reduces repeated preparation during concurrent session streaming while preserving live recipient permissions, row-delta history, and negotiated compression. No protocol, configuration, or database schema change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Permission decisions remain recipient-local. Once those decisions produce identical immutable rows and ancestor visibility, the publication shares envelope preparation and delivery plans. Publication-wide runtime display facts are prepared once, and role resolution reads membership only when membership can affect its answer.

## Lead-directed tail acceptance follow-up (declared before controls)

The lead explicitly accepts the measured 3.1x broadcaster-allocation reduction, approximately 27% whole allocation/s reduction, approximately 13% CPU reduction and +92 production LOC; the earlier arbitrary 5x requirement is withdrawn. Landing is now conditional on tail behavior against timing A/A controls. The historical measurements and original rule below remain provenance, not the current landing threshold.

Run 20 independent fresh-boot timing windows: baseline cohorts A1/A2 and candidate cohorts B1/B2, five windows each. Interleave four windows per block, alternating A1,B1,A2,B2 and B2,A2,B1,A1 for five blocks. Keep the prior full synthetic fixture, warmup, 70 viewers, 20 streams, list polling, tools, compression and runtime overlays unchanged. Use diagnostics only; no heap profiler, CPU sampler, wire observer or broadcast timer. Preserve counts, host load, major/minor GC and all raw results; do not retry failing windows automatically.

Report each labeled cohort's median, nearest-rank p95 and range for loop maximum, loop-p99 and GC-p99, plus paired same-version differences. To make “within A/A noise” precise before seeing outcomes, enumerate all 252 balanced five-versus-five splits of each version's ten windows. For each of the four flagged statistics (median loop maximum, median GC-p99, p95 loop-p99, p95 GC-p99), the version's noise ceiling is exp(nearest-rank 95th percentile of absolute log statistic ratios)−1. Both the original positive A/B change and any positive contemporaneous A/B change must lie inside BOTH versions' ceilings; decreases pass. The contemporaneous statistic uses all ten windows per version. These empirical A/A bounds describe this host/workload; they do not prove statistical equivalence in general.

If that predeclared rule passes, the lead authorizes landing through scripts/pr with the exact statement “lead accepted: tails within A/A noise”. Otherwise inspect retention ownership, fix a demonstrated lifetime defect and remeasure, or close with evidence. The completed controls did not pass; the final disposition above supersedes this prospective statement.

## Evidence

The original campaign did not establish tail acceptance; the lead-directed A/A follow-up above now determines landing. All twelve full-fixture untraced timing passes completed (two independent baseline controls and five interleaved A/B pairs). Median whole-workload main-thread CPU improved 650.218→566.456 ms/s (−12.88%) and 0.727704→0.621317 ms/delivery (−14.62%), but four aggregate tail statistics worsened by >20%: median per-window loop maximum +24.50%, median GC-p99 +26.67%, across-window p95 loop-p99 +21.56%, and across-window p95 GC-p99 +29.08%. These remain acceptance flags; host variation and improved medians do not waive them. With five windows, nearest-rank p95 is the observed maximum, not a pooled percentile.

## Controlled full-fixture allocation: five pairs plus A/A

All twelve allocation windows are accounted for: two independent baseline controls, five baseline comparisons and five candidate comparisons. Candidate4 is explicitly recovered from its intact raw heap profile after the reporting failure described below. Independent readers and disjoint self-byte accounting reconcile all profiles.

| Sampled main-isolate allocation | Baseline median [min,max] | Candidate median [min,max] | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Whole workload, B/delivery | 318,369.04 [309,548.29,340,530.42] | 231,927.80 [224,687.97,250,698.77] | 1.373× |
| Broadcaster, B/delivery | 111,067.52 [110,752.82,116,449.71] | 35,608.20 [35,223.74,36,485.73] | 3.119× |
| Outside broadcaster, B/delivery | 205,446.31 [198,480.77,229,777.59] | 196,319.59 [189,464.22,215,208.50] | 1.046× |
| Whole workload, MB/s | 283.790 [270.063,305.147] | 206.726 [204.415,215.610] | 1.373× |
| Broadcaster, MB/s | 99.354 [99.161,101.825] | 32.046 [30.523,32.932] | 3.100× |

With five windows, nearest-rank p95 is the maximum shown. These independent medians are not additive. The following table instead pools raw self bytes over the same total delivery denominator within each arm; its categories add exactly.

| Disjoint owner | Baseline pooled B/delivery | Candidate pooled B/delivery | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| projection | 50,727.46 | 8,802.07 | 5.763× |
| row presentation | 43,299.86 | 15,239.55 | 2.841× |
| serialization | 4,521.97 | 856.99 | 5.277× |
| reference history | 3,960.66 | 1,826.27 | 2.169× |
| sharing | 3,407.73 | 3,548.23 | 0.960× |
| compression | 2,994.59 | 2,268.99 | 1.320× |
| other broadcast | 3,450.99 | 3,250.75 | 1.062× |
| **Broadcaster total** | 112,363.26 | 35,792.85 | 3.139× |
| Outside broadcaster | 212,678.82 | 199,032.37 | 1.069× |
| **Whole workload** | 325,042.08 | 234,825.22 | 1.384× |

Projection and serialization exceed 5× individually; broadcaster 3.119× and whole 1.373× median reductions miss the requested 5×. Sharing slightly increases in the pooled attribution; recipient authority remains live. The full-fixture A/A controls measured333,484/316,304 whole B/delivery (−5.15%) and112,319/110,335 broadcaster B/delivery (−1.77%). Their whole rates were325.189/292.205 MB/s. Controls are not mixed into the comparison medians.

Outside broadcaster, the largest nearest-source allocations in the candidate are session-list-view-cache18.44KB/delivery, row-projection-materialize8.90KB, session-active-runs7.23KB, session-utils-list6.38KB and row-presentation6.07KB; the remainder spans many producer, transport and runtime sites. These are attributed sampled allocation, not claims of independently removable waste. The real-Gateway workload and polling schedule were preserved.


The separate populated-35-GiB wire probe completed both arms with exactly 70 deliveries per publication and no missing wire-size observations. Events already contain individual row patches and ancestor references, not full sidebar arrays. Baseline roster session-change frames averaged 927 compressed payload bytes (1,813 decompressed bytes); transcript message bodies went only to the four exact-session viewers. The fixture's full 200-row list polling remains unchanged between arms.

The initial thirty focused runtime tests and six tooling tests passed, including distinct-principal isolation, immediate grant revocation, and regression assertions that fail on the baseline. CI then caught a mid-fanout permission-pending freshness regression, presenter identity regressions in diagnostics, and a parameter-reassignment lint failure. These were candidate failures, not inherited reds. The repair rechecks the existing live row-facts identity and preserves presenter identity while its shared runtime stays current. All eight selected repair/authority cases pass, including all four failing assertions, with unchanged test expectations. Fresh Codex autoreview of base `4cc56385a57783587fa756c55220dddb4e78d880` and full candidate tree `af410a1de47e5082f02938b96a254669e3a74cb1` found no actionable P0–P2 issues. `pnpm check:changed --base 4cc56385a57783587fa756c55220dddb4e78d880` passes after the repair; runtime-head CI for `2ab953fc34240e53346a1db4b2678806b80125e6` is green ([CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41232777847), [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41233533208)).

A newly encountered pre-existing main tooling regression stopped report generation after allocation candidate4: native GC JSON interleaved with worker/application output. The identical raw log fails on the exact base; the parser assumption originated in `f5b87c5f8228923c1d9499c72f577814ed78162b` ([#178075](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178075)). The reporter fix preserves strict parsing for other callers and marks corrupt broadcast GC totals unavailable, without discarding independent profiles. Candidate4 allocation was independently reconciled from its intact heap profile; whole-window CPU and promotion are unavailable for that allocation pass. The original exit1 remains recorded. Only the final pair ran on the repaired reporter; all runtime overlay hashes and workload stayed unchanged. Reporter regression red/green, targeted checks, full-candidate Codex review and `pnpm check:changed --base 2ab953fc34240e53346a1db4b2678806b80125e6` pass. Current head `7e959fc6efc7ba59d068f3f600930df9a931a163` is green: [CI 41244262150](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41244262150), [Darwin tooling 41244262199](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41244262199), [aggregate gate 41244919575](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41244919575). Exact-head rollup: 77 successful, 61 skipped, 1 neutral; no pending/failing checks. This is a main tooling regression, not a noise exemption.

The separate one-window-per-arm CPU diagnostic attributes 122.571→53.191 sampled stack-ms/s to broadcaster source frames, using each V8 profile's own duration. This is sampled stack time, not actual CPU usage or untraced acceptance. Instrumented whole main-thread CPU was 646.064→664.263 ms/s. Mean synchronous changed-event broadcast time fell 7.433→3.281 ms/call and message time 7.730→3.453; changed-event p99 worsened 12.030→14.782 ms, and message maximum worsened 12.831→34.565 ms. These diagnostic tails are not waived.

The diagnostic extractor exited 1 on an invalid boundary-equality assertion: candidate timers counted 406 broadcast calls while the narrower received-event window counted 405 publications. Every one of 70 clients received 279 changed+126 message events. Diagnostics begins before receipt measurement and ends afterward; the timer includes targeted/retained/early-return calls. The exact extra call is unidentified. The intact RESULT/profile were SHA-verified and retained, the original wrapper failure is preserved, and timer means use observed call counts. No workload was rerun to chase a passing extraction. The original fixture is restored; measured Gateways exited, the temporary staging volume was ejected/removed, and the test lease is closed. Local APFS proof does not establish btrfs behavior.

Runtime changes add 92 net lines for publication-local output grouping and shared display-fact preparation. They add no retained cross-event authority cache. Tests add 142 net lines. The existing three-producer regression now covers distinct principals with identical output; it fails on the baseline with three filtered envelopes instead of two.

The acceptance rule below was declared before new load measurements. A reduction beneath the broadcaster is not a claim that all mixed-workload allocation improved by the same factor.
# Lane 2058 runtime-fix acceptance, declared before new measurements

Pin baseline 4cc56385a57783587fa756c55220dddb4e78d880 and candidate exact commit. Reuse the committed real-Gateway transcript broadcast memory-soak workload: 70 distinct authenticated administrator connections, 20 primary streaming sessions, deltas and tools, 2-second sidebar polling/filter churn, row deltas/envelope refs enabled, compression enabled. Warm each pristine synthetic fixture at its same absolute path before measurement. Full proof uses 5,000 sessions, 2,000 settled runs, 20 projects, populated 35 GiB database and 62,000 synthetic files (~1.1 GB). No production data.

The requested 5x target is assessed on whole-workload sampled main-isolate bytes per delivered session publication (<=20% baseline). A 5x reduction beneath the broadcaster is an intermediate owner milestone, not permission to claim the whole-workload target met. Report both, plus MB/s and allocation per source publication; do not claim mixed-workload denominators are exclusive event cost. Preserve event delivery counts per publication, payload meaning, ordering, current permissions and immediate revocation. A target miss is a miss, not an exception inferred from another metric.

Collect untraced timing and collected-object allocation separately, five serial interleaved A/B samples per arm, with A/A controls and host load. Report median, p95, range; distinguish whole main-thread CPU counters from owner CPU/profile attribution. No user-facing >20% regression in CPU, p99, GC, or frame bytes is acceptable without explanation/owner acceptance. Diagnostic source observers report compressed payload bytes, decompressed message bytes, patch/full/ancestor shape, and projection work counts in separate excluded runs.

A small fixture pilot (same session/connection/event cardinality; 16 MiB starter transcript) may reject ineffective candidates before expensive full-scale proof. Pilot numbers are never substituted for the required production-shaped result. Keep clock/platform and warm/cold qualification explicit. Prior A/A is retained independently; this campaign does not relabel it as candidate evidence.

prs.title: improve(ui): truncate session hovercard commentary with an ellipsis
prs.body: Related: #189630 ## What Problem This Solves Long Task progress notes need a clear three-line preview. CSS clipping alone left the full note and its hidden links in the hovercard, allowing keyboard focus to reach content outside the preview. ## User Impact The hovercard renders only the content that fits within three lines, with an ellipsis when truncated. Omitted text and links are absent from the rendered preview. Visible links remain usable, and updating the note preserves focus. ## Implementation The existing Markdown owner measures a balanced prefix of sanitized content at the actual width and line height. The existing reconciler commits that prefix directly. Resize and font changes refresh the measurement. Complete Markdown views keep their existing behavior. The last-message excerpt and other hovercard rows retain their current presentation. ## Validation - The omitted-link regression fails on the previous head and passes with the correction. - Eight production-bundle Chromium hovercard E2Es passed for the preview implementation. The focused commentary case passed again after the final content-callback correction. - The flow covers retained links, refresh/focus, narrow viewport resizing, prose, lists, long code and a short note without an ellipsis. - Focused Markdown and hovercard tests passed. The final correction also passed 40 affected unit cases, the browser provider case, production/test typechecks, typed lint, formatting and the line-cap check. Existing ownership, access-denial and control-cleanup assertions remain intact. - Fresh independent review and final source inspection found no remaining actionable issue in the corrected projection. Browser evidence uses the existing controlled Gateway fixture and ordinary UI interactions, without injected styles or forced component state. It is not a live model run. ## Risk and coverage Full preview behavior was exercised in Chromium. The existing WebKit unit covers lifecycle/focus, not the complete measured preview flow. prs.title: fix(ui): keep PDF readers open when file metadata refreshes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an open PDF reader resets when session-file metadata refreshes, even though the selected file and its contents have not changed.

## User Impact

Users can keep reading the same PDF across metadata refreshes without the reader being destroyed and recreated. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The preview lifetime included the file download callback, which metadata refreshes can recreate independently of file identity. Keep that callback in the existing reactive byte-read path, but remove it from the reader lifetime key. Identity, size, and source availability still retire the reader; failed reads and byte limits retain their existing behavior.

This is a focused lifecycle fix, not a reader redesign. Related: #183854 (session-file PDF previews). No separate issue was filed for this small bug fix.

## Evidence

- Regression exercised through the registered chat detail panel: with the new test on base `1a2eb9f0da9`, the refreshed callback removes the iframe (1 failed, 14 passed).
- With the fix, the complete PDF preview suite passes: **15/15**, including replacement/closure cleanup, failed reads, limits, ticket revalidation, and local Blob handling.
- Command: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config ui/vitest.config.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-pdf-preview.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Formatting, targeted oxlint, UI typecheck, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Real Chromium native PDF layout test passes (**1/1**): `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config ui/vitest.config.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-pdf-preview.browser.test.ts --project browser --maxWorkers=1`.
- Simplification pass: removed the callback from the existing lifetime key; no new state or production owner. Two files, 36 insertions and 2 deletions, including one regression test.
- Proof boundary: the refresh regression is jsdom component integration with the real PDF worker program in a test realm; the existing layout test also ran in Chromium. No manual PDF scroll-position session or screenshots captured. This change only alters reader lifecycle, not layout or styling. Existing Solid untracked-read warnings are emitted by the panel bridge.
- Local autoreview was unavailable: the installed skill could not be read (`Resource deadlock avoided`). No automated local review is claimed.

- Exact candidate: `a066927fdc29b51eb2d12665c18dbfb053a0b520`. Hosted CI is pending.

prs.title: improve(ui): shimmer the running tool call narration
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

While a tool call runs, its narration line (for example "Search sessions for release notes") stays static. Only rows that show a file verb or a raw command had the running shimmer, so a call with a stated purpose looked no different from a finished one.

## User Impact

User impact: while a call runs, its narration line carries the shimmer. When it finishes or fails, the shimmer stops and the line returns to its current resting look. Copy, icons and layout do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

This reuses the running tool row's existing treatment: the shared `text-shimmer` keyframes, its 2.2s timing and the same `--text` / `--bg` gradient. No new animation or tokens.

- **Rows:** the running row rule now also covers the stated purpose and the tool name fallback.
- **Group headline:** from the second call on, the line becomes the group headline, so the headline gets a running state tied to that operation's status. It keeps its existing enter motion.
- **Forced colors:** the rule now also requires `forced-colors: none`, matching the other text shimmers. This applies to the existing verb and command rows too.
- **WebKit:** the rule sets `-webkit-text-fill-color: transparent`, matching the other text shimmers.

A settled headline keeps its dim-until-hover behavior. A running headline now shows the shimmer instead, like running rows already did, and hovering it does not change it.

## Evidence

### Recording

One continuous normal run in Chromium, nothing paused: the message is typed and sent, the first call shimmers and stops, the second call becomes the group headline and does the same, and the reply arrives with nothing animating. Absolutely dark, then light.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2ff902c7-664d-4e14-a8a1-55e5a7bdd648

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e256edd-4917-43fe-a9c1-733e3087f9fa

Events go through the mock Gateway layer in the order the runner emits them: the item then the tool event to open a call, the tool result then the item to close it. Items are built with the real `projectAgentToolActivity`. Tool durations are chosen for the recording.

### Absolutely dark

Top to bottom: Before while running, After while running, After when done.

![Absolutely dark Before, After running and After done](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/92d3c634-783b-49d0-981b-36c25f78f210)

Consecutive live frames while running, then done:

![Absolutely dark live frames](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c52bffd2-fffa-49d5-b8e9-7a675e72b2bc)

### Absolutely light

![Absolutely light Before, After running and After done](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4862a054-7c77-4aa7-8b4b-931d4cf9af5f)

![Absolutely light live frames](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/551a8e7b-98a7-4d7b-963a-b5d2124b4f45)

### CRT and Beacon

Two live frames while running, then done. CRT dark and light:

![CRT dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1321272f-62c2-45db-9402-168b48f21954)

![CRT light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/baadae86-aa18-4277-b82f-9f05a79a7de0)

Beacon dark and light:

![Beacon dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad674cc9-141b-475a-8ae3-7620ddf864bf)

![Beacon light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d863910-c6fd-40f9-8d98-eb5ede066163)

### Measurements

Six themes (Absolutely, CRT, Beacon, each dark and light), Chromium:

- **Layout:** the row and its text keep the same width and height while running and when done.
- **Stops animating:** after a call finishes or fails no shimmer animation remains on it, and none remains after the run ends.
- **Reduced motion and forced colors:** no shimmer animation and the text keeps its resting color.
- **Off screen:** with 80 history messages, scrolling away unmounts the running row and no animation remains; scrolling back resumes it. On another route the retained row runs no animation.
- **Performance:** Chromium traced no layout invalidation from the narration, the same as the existing command row. Like that row, it animates `background-position`, so style recalculates on each frame while a call runs.

Lowest painted glyph contrast against the page across live samples, compared with the resting look:

| Theme | Sweep | Resting |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Absolutely dark | 3.7 | 5.3 |
| Absolutely light | 2.7 | 3.6 |
| CRT dark | 3.2 | 4.7 |
| CRT light | 2.5 | 3.5 |
| Beacon dark | 5.0 | 7.4 |
| Beacon light | 3.9 | 5.7 |

The low point sits only in the moving band, and the rest of the line is at full `--text` then. It comes from the existing gradient, which running verb and command rows already use, so it was kept as it is.

### Tests

- Added: `ui/src/styles/shimmer.browser.test.ts`, `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-activity-headline.test.tsx`, `ui/src/e2e/chat-tool-turn-outcome.e2e.test.ts`.
- Updated: `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-disclosure.browser.test.tsx` now checks dim-until-hover on a settled headline, since a running one shows the shimmer.
- Passing locally: those files, `chat-run-lifecycle` E2E, `chat-tool-cards`, `chat-tool-purpose`, `chat-view.activity-headline`, stylelint, oxfmt, oxlint and `tsgo:ui`.
- `ui:check-performance:base`: passes. Total CSS gzip +42 B (308593 B, ceiling 309366 B), total CSS raw +423 B (1592630 B, ceiling 1599319 B).

### Gaps

- **Safari has no visual proof here.** In one run in the Safari app (27.0.1), the page reported the shimmer animation on the running line at each step and none after each call finished or the reply arrived. Other windows covered the recording, so no Safari image or video is included.
- The existing "…" on a running headline is still removed when it finishes, so that line changes by one glyph as it did before.
- When a second call starts, the single row is still replaced by the group headline as it was before, which moves the line about 4 px.
- A subagent row that links to its session keeps its static link text.
- Calls running at the same time are not shown in the images or recording.
- Returning to chat mid-run was not proved: the mock's history does not carry the live row, so it is gone on return.
- Images and recordings come from the source dev server, not the production bundle.

prs.title: fix: prevent context overflow during long tool turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long tool-heavy turns can exceed the model window before turn-end maintenance runs. In the Contributor PRs cron incident on 2026-10-31 20:28–20:30Z, request 7 reached **1,000,188 tokens against a 1,000,000-token window**. The surfaced “Auto-compaction failed” label did not establish that compaction had run.

## User Impact

Hard context-window admission now runs by default at provider request boundaries, using conservative projected context and the existing 20,000-token reserve floor (capped for small windows). The optional soft threshold retains its disabled default and configured reserve. Unsafe replay or unsettled tools still prevent recovery compaction; surfaced overflow messages now identify a mid-turn window overflow. Manual compaction is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Lead policy decision: a request already projected beyond the model window guarantees a 400 and cannot advance the turn. Reuse the existing provider-bound estimator, boundary signal, and compaction/retry owner instead of sending that request. The recovery safety gate remains authoritative, including parked Code Mode handling.

No new compactor, configuration option, state owner, or test-line allocation. Simplification consolidated duplicated retry fixtures and removed redundant fixture casts/identity overrides. Whole-PR production delta: **+4 lines**; tests and case fixtures: **−13 lines** (ratchet-scoped tests: **0**).

## Evidence

- Red on rebased base `75d8b08f450d`: the real Responses reply/session/attempt flow sent an over-window request to the deterministic local provider (HTTP 400).
- Green: the same tool-loop boundary compacts before the next request, completes the turn with zero over-window submissions, and answers the next turn without repeating compaction. The existing completions summary-timeout case remains covered.
- Focused Bun runs, timeout-wrapped, one worker: boundary guards, measured/opaque provider accounting, unsafe replay/Code Mode recovery, overflow presentation, prompt-prefix stability, and attempt siblings passed. The presentation cases use supported source-only E2E mode and make no built-runtime claim.

- CI repair: regenerated the help-text hash with the canonical generator, preserved real exports in the shared settings mock, and supplied the existing 8,192-token model window to four tool-flow fixtures. The cache-prefix fixture uses a 192k window so eight conservatively priced truncated results fit; its 32k result cap is unchanged. Dedicated small-window budget tests remain unchanged; all tool assertions remain intact.

Cold source preparation is included where reported; CI-repair rows show Vitest time (wrapper totals: 13.17s, 40.32s, 43.92s, 14.82s, 17.63s). Exact-head CI completed successfully; see the run below.

prs.body:
Supersedes #140357, thanks @NianJiuZst.

Related: #140295.

## What Problem This Solves

Image generation reports requested size, quality, and format as applied even when the provider returns different settings or leaves them unknown.

## User Impact

Completed image results now separate `details.requested` hints from per-image `details.outputs`. issues.title: Recovery: persist completed tool results at execution-batch boundaries

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
### Problem / Motivation

The current runtime checkpoint has a crash-consistency window during multi-tool responses. If tool A completes, tool B starts, and the gateway crashes before tool C runs, the durable checkpoint may still record all calls as pending. After restart, recovery cannot distinguish completed work (and its external side effects) from unfinished or uncertain work.

This makes recovery unnecessarily lose completed tool results and evidence that a side-effecting tool already ran. The existing recovery policy should remain conservative: a restart must not implicitly resume model/tool work, and pending calls must still require explicit user confirmation.

### Proposed Solution

Advance the existing runtime checkpoint at completed tool-execution batch boundaries. A partial checkpoint could record:

    assistant tool calls = [A, B, C]
    completed_tool_results = [A_result]
    pending_tool_calls = [B, C]

Maintain the invariant: completed_ids union pending_ids == assistant_tool_call_ids; completed_ids intersect pending_ids == empty. Reuse the existing runtime_checkpoint, completed_tool_results, pending_tool_calls, tool batching logic, and recovery materialization path. Recovery should preserve A's real result, materialize interrupted results for B and C, discard provider-native conversation state for partial/uncertain checkpoints as it does today, and continue waiting for explicit confirmation without replaying pending tools.

### Alternatives Considered

Persisting every internal tool event would add unnecessary checkpoint churn. Introducing a new task ledger, scheduler, or recovery subsystem would be broader than needed. Batch boundaries are a focused durability boundary because read-only/concurrency-safe tools already run in batches, while side-effecting tools run as singleton batches.

### Related Component

Other

### Additional Context

Suggested regression tests:

1. Partial sequential completion: A completes while B remains pending; after simulated interruption, assert A is in completed_tool_results and B is in pending_tool_calls.
2. Partial recovery: preserve A's real result and give B an interrupted-tool result.
3. No implicit replay: recovery waits for explicit confirmation and does not execute B.
4. Partition validation: reject overlapping IDs, incomplete unions, and duplicate IDs.
5. Legacy compatibility: keep all-pending awaiting_tools and all-completed tools_completed checkpoints valid.

Non-goals: no automatic replay, new task ledger, new scheduler, exactly-once guarantee, change to ordinary agent behavior, or new public configuration. This follows the general durability principle used by workflow runtimes such as LangGraph and DeerFlow, while keeping the implementation within nanobot's existing checkpoint primitives.

prs.title: fix(channels): deliver provider retry waits through an opt-in hook
prs.body:
Fixes #5585

## Problem
When a provider call backs off, core publishes `RetryWaitEvent` ("Model request failed, retry in {n}s (attempt {k}).") but `ChannelManager._dispatch_outbound_loop` dropped it unconditionally, before any channel hook and outside the `sendProgress` gate. Only the interactive CLI ever rendered it, so chat channels looked hung for the whole backoff.

## Change
I went with the less intrusive option from the issue: a default no-op `BaseChannel.send_retry_wait(...)` hook, following the same pattern as `send_delta` / `send_reasoning*`.
- `ChannelManager` now forwards `RetryWaitEvent` to `send_retry_wait` and never falls through to `send()`. Channels that don't override the hook stay silent, so there's no new config key and no extra chat messages by default.
- I didn't route it through `sendProgress`: that defaults to on, so every progress-enabled channel would get a permanent chat line. This matches the precedent in #5799 (compaction notices).
- Linear already built an ephemeral thought for this event inside `send()`, but that code was unreachable because of the drop. It now lives in `LinearChannel.send_retry_wait`, and `send()` delegates to it, so direct sends behave the same.
- WebSocket/WebUI is unchanged (it uses the structured `RetryStatusEvent`).
- `docs/channel-package-guide.md` documents the hook.

## Tests
- New `tests/channels/test_channel_manager_retry_wait.py` covers two cases: a channel that implements the hook receives the notice even with `send_progress` false, and default channels don't get it through `send()`. The hook test failed before the fix.
- A Linear test covers the ephemeral thought and direct `send()` delegation.

## Verification (Linux, Python 3.11, GH tokens unset)
- `uv sync --all-extras --dev`, channel dependency install, `uv pip check`: exit 0
- `uv run --no-sync ruff check nanobot tests conftest.py`: exit 0
- `uv run --no-sync basedpyright`: exit 0 (0 errors)
- `uv run --no-sync python -m pytest -n 2 --dist loadfile --ignore=tests/cli/test_commands.py`: exit 0 (9220 passed, 48 skipped)
- `uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/cli/test_commands.py`: exit 0 (160 passed)
- Not run locally: the Python 3.14 coverage cell, Windows, and Docker.

This change was prepared with help from an AI coding assistant and reviewed by me.

prs.title: fix(api): release idle session locks
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #4883.

Completed API requests with distinct `session_id` values leave their locks in the application's registry indefinitely. Store these locks in a `WeakValueDictionary` so idle entries can be collected, while request handlers and streaming tasks keep strong references to locks that are held or awaited.

The production change updates the registry's typed `AppKey`, local annotation, and initialization. The refreshed branch incorporates main `8b37976d36c2812c62b464321e729a88872b60f9` and preserves its routing and cleanup changes in the runner tests.

## Tests

- Exercise completed requests with 20 distinct session IDs through the real HTTP endpoint in both streaming and non-streaming modes, then verify that no idle locks remain.
- Cover default and custom sessions in both modes, including garbage collection while one request holds the lock and another waits. Request arrival is synchronized with an event, and the requests must still execute serially.
- Allow runner shutdown tests to finish durable cleanup, and verify that verbose Docker smoke status output does not trigger the `grep -q` / `pipefail` failure.

## Validation

Current revision, macOS arm64, Python 3.11.15:

- **163 passed** across API endpoints, API session/stream/attachment handling, API runtime integration, AgentLoop lock lifecycle, runner injections, and Docker smoke-script contract tests. No cases skipped in this focused run.
- Repository Ruff checks, Python import boundaries, dependency consistency, and strict BasedPyright pass: **0 type errors, 0 type warnings**. Dependencies include all extras and channel manifests, matching the documented CI setup.
- `bash -n tests/test_docker.sh` and whitespace checks pass.
- A test-only strong-registry control makes both HTTP cleanup regressions fail with **20 retained idle locks**. The production sources are unchanged by this probe; the normal weak-registry tests pass for both response modes.

HTTP tests use a mocked agent. The Docker script tests use a fake Docker boundary; an image build, the complete repository suite, and Windows/Linux execution were not run locally for this refreshed revision. Fresh CI remains to be evaluated on the updated head.

## Related work

PR #4890 uses the same weak-reference approach. This proposal preserves typed application keys and adds streaming cleanup/serialization coverage.

## Summary

Replace the JEV-specific client and configuration with a reusable structured-decision client. The client exposes typed questions and results through a provider/protocol abstraction; OpenRouter with the System One protocol is the initial registered backend.

- OpenRouter is the only registered provider, and System One is the only supported protocol.

- Provider fallback, telemetry, and caller-specific confidence thresholds are out of scope.

## Verification

issues.title: TUI prompt drops lone spaces from live display (buffer intact at submit)
issues.body:
## What happens

Typing a space in the `hermes chat` prompt sometimes doesn't show up: the live prompt line renders e.g. `qq` while typing `q q`. The space **is** in the buffer — submitting sends `q q` (the model quotes it back with the space).

## Repro

Spawn `hermes -p default chat` in a pty with echo disabled, wait for the prompt, then write the bytes `q`, ` `, `q` as three separate writes (~0.5s apart):

- live prompt line never shows the space (`qq`-looking line),
- on Enter the submitted message contains `q q`.

Writing the same bytes in one write (`q q` at once) renders fine. Bare prompt_toolkit 3.0.52 keeps lone spaces, so it's in the CLI's input/display path, not the parser (parser emits `(' ', ' ')` correctly).

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.22.5 (2026.9.24), stable channel
- prompt_toolkit 3.0.52, Python 3.14
- Linux, TERM=xterm-256color (also reproduced inside bubblewrap and through a second pty hop, so it's not terminal-specific)

Happy to run any debug build or provide pty transcripts.

issues.title: [Bug]: Desktop - model dropdown (w-72) truncates long provider and model names
issues.body:
**Version:** Hermes Desktop v0.22.2+ (Windows 11)

**What happens**
The composer model dropdown (`[data-slot="dropdown-menu-content"].w-72` containing the model groups) is fixed at 288 px. With custom providers or long model ids (for example `claude-subscription-...: claude-opus-...[1m]`), names truncate, and similar entries can't be told apart.

**Expected**
The menu grows to fit its content, up to a sensible maximum.

**Workaround we use (CSS plugin)**
```css
[data-slot="dropdown-menu-content"].w-72.p-0:has([class~="group/model"]) { width: min(420px, calc(100vw - 24px)) !important; max-width: calc(100vw - 24px) !important; }
```
Fonts, prices and controls are unchanged; only the width differs.

issues.title: [Perf]: Desktop on Windows - opening a menu toggles body pointer-events and takes about 280 ms
issues.body:
**Version:** Hermes Desktop v0.22.x (Windows 11, packaged build, long sessions open in several panes)

**What happens**
Opening a Radix dropdown or popup sets `pointer-events: none` on `body` (scroll lock). With several large transcripts mounted, that style change took 272-294 ms per toggle on our machine, so every menu open and close lagged.

**Measured**
A live A/B in the same window: 272-294 ms per toggle before, about 6 ms after these CSS rules:
```css
[data-pane-hidden]{content-visibility:hidden;contain:strict;}
#root{pointer-events:auto;}
body[data-scroll-locked]::before,body[style*='pointer-events: none']::before{content:'';position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:49;pointer-events:auto;}
```
(The overlay at z-index 49 keeps outside-click blocking under Radix menus, which sit at z-index 50.) Hidden panes being fully laid out and style-recalculated looks like the main cost.

**Expected**
Menus open without a style recalculation of every hidden pane. Two possible fixes: apply `content-visibility: hidden` to hidden panes natively, or avoid the body-wide pointer-events toggle.

We ship this today as a local CSS plugin.

issues.title: [Bug]: Desktop - composer mic button shifts, so clicks land on Start voice conversation
issues.body:
**Version:** Hermes Desktop v0.22.5 (Windows 11)

**What happens**
The composer's right-hand control row is right-aligned (`justify-end`). The right-most control changes width depending on state:
- Send and Stop: one circle, 26 px.
- Start voice conversation (idle, empty composer): circle plus the voice-engine chevron (`w-5`), about 46 px total.

When a chat goes from busy to idle with an empty composer, the dictation mic (`fan-menu-anchor`) slides left by about 20 px. Start voice conversation then sits exactly where the mic was, so a click aimed at dictation starts a voice conversation. The Queue message button (shown when busy and the composer has text) is inserted between the mic and Send, and shifts the mic the same way.

Measured on a 1x display: mic at x=2137 with Stop showing, x=2117 with Start voice showing.

**Expected**
The mic keeps a fixed position in every state. Two options: reserve the right-most slot at the width of the widest variant, or put the Queue button somewhere that doesn't move the mic.

**Workaround we use (CSS-only plugin)**
```css
div:has(> [data-slot="fan-menu-anchor"]) > button[type="submit"] { margin-left: 1.25rem; } /* chevron width */
div:has(> [data-slot="fan-menu-anchor"]) > button[aria-label="Queue message"] { order: -1; }
```
Source: `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/controls.tsx` (showQueueButton / showVoicePrimary) and `start-voice-button.tsx`.

issues.title: [Bug]: Desktop - reading position jumps when a reply finishes while scrolled up
issues.body:
**Version:** Hermes Desktop v0.22.5 (Windows 11, packaged build)

**What happens**
When I scroll up in a chat to read older messages (`data-following="false"` on `[data-slot="aui_thread-viewport"]`), the text I'm reading moves when the current reply finishes. Sometimes the view also snaps all the way to the bottom.

**Measured (live renderer, a row in the middle of the viewport tracked each frame, no user input within 400 ms):**
- At reply completion: the row moved about 400 px. In that frame `scrollTop` changed by +800 while `scrollHeight` grew by 396. Mutations in the same frame: `-aui_response-group` / `+aui_response-group` under `aui_turn-pair`, `-aui_turn-activity`, `+aui_turn-duration`, `+timeline-timestamp`. So the finished reply's group is remounted, and the scroll offset is rewritten during the swap.
- A separate shift of 1,163 px happened in another scrolled-up chat during a redraw. No input was involved.

**Expected**
If the reader has escaped stick-to-bottom, the row on screen stays at the same y position through any redraw (reply finalizing, tool rows collapsing, budget backfill or unmount), and the view never snaps to the bottom without a user action.

**Workaround we use**
A desktop plugin. While `data-following="false"`, it records a reference element's `getBoundingClientRect().top`. If that element moves with no recent wheel, touch, pointer or navigation-key input, it adds the difference back to `scrollTop` (in rAF, a ResizeObserver and a scroll listener). It also undoes a follow=true flip that no input caused. This removes the jumps, but the fix belongs in `list.tsx` (the response-group remount and the scroll writes around it).

Related but different: #65714 (setting to disable auto-scroll), #73990 (preserve position when sending).

issues.title: Memory provider stays 'activated' after initialize() fails — half-built provider crashes every hook for the process lifetime
issues.body:
## Bug Description

When a memory provider's `initialize()` raises, `MemoryManager.initialize()` logs `Memory provider '<name>' initialize failed: <exc>` and swallows the exception (`_each_provider`), but the provider stays in `_providers` and is reported as "activated". The provider is half-initialized — attributes assigned late in its `initialize()` body never exist — so **every subsequent lifecycle hook and tool call crashes** on those missing attributes for the entire lifetime of the process. There is no drop, no disable, and no retry.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a memory provider whose `initialize()` can fail partway (e.g. `qdrant-memory` 0.2.2: two Hermes processes on the same profile — the second one's `WriterLease` raises `WriterBusyError: Another writer still owns this profile destination` before `self.ledger` is assigned).
2. Start the second process/session; observe `initialize failed` warning followed by `Memory provider 'qdrant-memory' activated`.
3. Chat a few turns, end a session, and call one of the provider's tools.

## Actual Behavior

Every turn logs:

```
WARNING agent.memory_manager: Memory provider 'qdrant-memory' sync_turn failed: 'QdrantMemoryProvider' object has no attribute 'ledger'
```

Session end logs `on_session_end failed: Provider is shut down`, and tool calls return `{"error": {"type": "AttributeError", "retryable": false}}`. Observed 94 `sync_turn` failures + 14 `on_session_end` failures in one errors.log, repeating every turn with no recovery until process restart.

## Expected Behavior

A provider whose `initialize()` raised should not remain active. Either:
- drop/disable it the same way `claim_instance` failure triggers `_drop_provider`, and surface a user-facing warning (related: #32495 asks for user-facing errors on dead tools), or
- mark it degraded and retry `initialize()` with backoff on the next session/turn.

Silently keeping a half-built provider guarantees a warning per turn and dead tools for hours.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.22.5 (2026.9.24), stable channel, macOS
- qdrant-memory plugin 0.2.2 (community catalog)
- Same pattern applies to any provider that assigns state late in `initialize()`; `agent/memory_provider.py` base class does not require or enforce an "initialized" flag.

Related (distinct triggers): #32495, #47954, #145889

issues.title: Dashboard Chat sidebar cannot resume login-owned GUI sessions: PTY child loses authenticated identity
issues.body:
## Summary

The dashboard Chat sidebar lists historical authenticated GUI-client conversations, but selecting them fails with `session.resume` returning `not_found`. Their transcripts still exist in state.db. The observed client was Hermex on iOS; the dashboard was opened in Chromium on Linux using the same Basic-auth username.

A synthetic reproduction isolates two independent ownership/restoration problems and a transport gate. This is a compatibility/identity-propagation bug report, not a claim of an authentication bypass or confirmed security vulnerability.

## Environment / verification scope

- Repository: NousResearch/hermes-agent
- Investigated checkout: `daec3cd4c6d34f5befbc8f25a8af3e3b84b94f06`
- Linux 6.12.107+deb13-amd64; Python 3.13.14
- Default-profile, bound dashboard; password/Basic authentication enabled
- Historical rows: `source='gui'`, `user_id='basic:alice'` (synthetic example), no session_key/chat_id/origin_json
- Latest upstream main/release has NOT been reproduced. The installed checkout has unrelated local modifications in model metadata/timeouts/catalog and messaging code; they were not changed for this investigation. The relevant auth/restoration files were not locally modified.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a historical GUI conversation through an authenticated client such that its row records `source='gui'` and the verified login label `basic:alice`.
2. Open the Hermes dashboard in Chromium and authenticate as the same Basic-auth user, alice.
3. Select that conversation in the Chat sidebar (not the read-only Sessions detail view).
4. The embedded TUI attempts `session.resume` and receives:

```json
{"error":{"code":4001,"message":"not_found","data":{"reason":"not_found"}}}
```

Expected: the verified owner can open/resume their existing conversation, retaining its transcript; otherwise the UI should explain the unsupported restoration rather than imply the conversation is absent.

Actual: the sidebar lists the conversation, but resuming fails although its messages remain stored.

## Source trace on the investigated checkout

1. `web/src/components/ChatSessionList.tsx` sets the resume query parameter. The Chat page starts `/api/pty` for that target.
2. `hermes_cli/web_server_chat.py:_ws_auth_reason` correctly authenticates the incoming PTY websocket as Basic-auth alice.
3. `hermes_cli/web_routers/chat_ws.py:pty_ws` does not forward that verified identity into the child launcher.
4. In the bound default-dashboard branch, `web_server_chat.py:_resolve_chat_argv` obtains `HERMES_TUI_GATEWAY_URL` via `_build_gateway_ws_url` / `_server_internal_ws_url`.
5. That URL uses the process-wide internal credential. `dashboard_auth/ws_tickets.py:consume_internal_credential` resolves it to `server-internal/server-internal`, not alice.
6. The child therefore reaches the authority as `auth:v1:["server-internal","","server-internal"]`. It is not a registered native legacy transport.
7. `gateway/session_controls.py:resume` routes historical gui rows through `resolve_local_target` and `adopt_legacy_session`. `gateway/session_local_migration.py:adopt_legacy_session` rejects that transport with `not_found`.
8. Independently, even if the correct authenticated subject `auth:v1:["basic","","alice"]` is supplied, `hermes_state_local_migration.py:login_owned_by` only recognizes `source='desktop'`, so `validate_legacy_row` rejects the same owner's `gui` row.

Thus only broadening the GUI-source check, or only forwarding the login, is insufficient.

## Isolated reproduction evidence

The existing `tests/gateway/test_session_follow_profile_config.py` `_owner` / `_profile` fixtures were used to construct real SessionStore / SessionAuthority / AuthorityConnection objects, dispatch actual `session.resume` requests, and use scratch-only SQLite databases. Three synthetic gui/basic-auth-owned rows reproduced the same failure. No real transcripts, credentials, or production resume calls were used.

Checks independently rerun:

- Verified PTY ticket authenticates as the login, while the current generated child gateway URL authenticates as server-internal.
- Current resume dispatch returns `not_found` for all three synthetic rows.
- Even the correct login subject fails the current GUI-row eligibility check.
- A desired-success regression intentionally fails on current code.
- Evaluating candidate adoption-policy edits only in memory allows the exact owner, with a non-operator connection, to resume all three rows and retain their synthetic messages; another ordinary login is denied before and after adoption.

Result: **1 intentionally failing acceptance regression, 3 passing diagnostic/candidate-policy tests**. Existing legacy ownership and Desktop login-stamping tests also passed: **9 passed**.

The candidate owner-policy portion was tested; a full credential-forwarding implementation was NOT built or end-to-end tested. No production fix is claimed.

## Suggested fix direction / acceptance criteria

- Propagate only the server-verified PTY login into the child gateway connection through a server-issued, scoped delegation mechanism. Do not trust client-supplied principal/provider/capability parameters.
- Keep delegated owner connections distinct from privileged operator connections; do not widen operator privileges as a shortcut.
- Scope PTY keepalive/reattachment and cleanup to the verified owner/profile; support reconnect and credential revocation.
- Recognize exact login ownership for both desktop and gui historical rows, preserving issuer and profile checks.
- Permit the verified login to adopt its own labelled history without pretending it is a native OS transport; retain capability checks and transactional validation.
- Regression tests should cover same-owner success, different ordinary user denial before/after adoption and cold restoration, wrong issuer/profile/purpose, identityless/internal/native callers on labelled rows, and reconnect/reattachment behavior.
- Preserve existing intentional operator semantics and native adoption of genuinely unowned history. No bulk ownership rewrite or schema migration is suggested.

## Related reports

- #144814 describes dashboard-login mobile history failing from native Desktop because its OS-UID identity differs from the login. This report concerns the **browser dashboard Chat sidebar**, where the incoming request already has the correct Basic-auth login but the PTY child receives the fixed server-internal identity. It also covers `gui` rows excluded by `login_owned_by`.
- #142942 concerns `webui` rows missing canonical routing/policy receipts; the synthetic rows here use `source='gui'` and a stored authenticated login label.

## Privacy

Usernames in this report are synthetic. No actual hostnames, account identifiers, chat titles, session IDs, transcript content, cookies, tokens, or configuration files are included.

## Summary
In Hermes Desktop, hovering the mouse over a session (window/tile/pane) changes the focused session. Focus should only change on an intentional click — e.g. the input/composer or a neutral area of that session — not on hover.

## Why this is a problem
- Host-level / OS speech-to-text follows the focused window. Hover-driven focus switches puts dictation into the wrong session.
- Moving the mouse toward the bottom bar (e.g. to change a folder) can cross another session and change focus/status UI without any click.
- This is unintuitive compared to normal desktop apps, where activation requires a click.

## Expected behavior
- Hover may show visual highlight only.
- Hover must not change the focused session, keyboard/OS focus target, or bottom bar / status context.
- Focus changes only when the user clicks the session’s input bar or another neutral area (etc.) of that session.

## Actual behavior
Hover alone switches session focus and related UI.

## Environment
- Hermes Desktop (version: v0.22.5)
- OS: Fedora

prs.title: feat: /model reset returns a pinned session to the configured default (CLI, TUI, Desktop, gateway; salvage #74899)
prs.body:
`/model reset` takes a pinned session back to the configured default model — classic CLI, Ink TUI, Desktop and messaging gateway — without losing the conversation. Before this, the only way off a session `/model` pick (which survives gateway restarts and `session.resume`) was `/new`, which also drops the history; and typing `/model reset` switched to a model literally named `reset`.

## Before / after (real runs, fake loopback provider, no spend)

Provider column = the `model` field the provider actually received on the next turn. Config default `cfg-default-model`; the session was first switched to `other-model`.

| Surface (real process) | `origin/main` c419cf7 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Messaging gateway (`python -m gateway.run` + fake platform), `/model other-model` → **gateway restart** → `/model reset` | reply `Model switched to \`reset\` … not found in this custom endpoint's model listing`; provider got `reset` | reply `Session model override cleared — now using \`cfg-default-model\` (the channel/global default). Conversation history kept.`; provider got `cfg-default-model` |
| same, `/model reset` again | switches to `reset` again | `No session model override is active — already using \`cfg-default-model\` …` |
| Ink TUI legacy path (`tui_gateway.entry`, `config.set model reset`) | value `reset`; provider got `reset` | value `cfg-default-model`; provider got `cfg-default-model` |
| Desktop legacy path (`slash.exec "/model reset"`: CLI worker + session mirror) | `✓ Model switched: reset`; provider got `reset` | `✓ Model switched: cfg-default-model`; provider got `cfg-default-model`; a second reset prints `Already on the configured default (cfg-default-model) — nothing to reset.` |
| TUI session resumed in a fresh process after the reset | provider got `reset` | provider got `cfg-default-model` (history kept: 6 messages) |
| **Ink TUI, default canonical path** (`hermes --tui` attached to a `gateway run` owner; `session.mutate model`) `/model other-model` → `/model reset` | `model → reset`, status bar `reset`; provider got `reset` | `model → cfg-default-model`; provider got `cfg-default-model` |
| same, `/model reset` again | `model → reset`; provider still got `reset` | `Already on the configured default (cfg-default-model) — nothing to reset.`; provider got `cfg-default-model` |
| Control: `/model other-model` after reset | provider got `other-model` | provider got `other-model` |

## Root cause
No surface had a way to clear a session's `/model` pin: the shared parser handed `reset` to `switch_model` as a model name, and on the canonical path (TUI, Desktop, attached CLI) the session owner froze `reset` into the session policy as the model.

## Changes
- `hermes_cli/model_switch.py`: `reset` is its own request (`ModelSwitchRequest.is_reset`); `reset` with any flag (`--global`, `--once`, `--session`, `--provider`, `--reasoning`) is refused with `MODEL_SWITCH_ERR_RESET_WITH_FLAGS`. Not aliased to `default` (MoA's preset name); a model whose bare id is `reset` stays reachable as `vendor/reset`.
- Messaging gateway (`gateway/slash_commands_model.py`): rehydrates a store-only override (after a restart), then clears it in memory and in the session store, drops an armed `--once` restore, evicts the cached agent, leaves a next-turn model note, and updates the dashboard row. `channel_overrides` > config.yaml applies again, read from the owning profile's config. A local (Desktop-owned) session has no override tier, so there reset is a session-scoped pick of the configured default through the normal commit path.
- TUI gateway (`tui_gateway/model_switch.py`, reached by `config.set model` and Desktop's slash mirror): drops the pin and one-turn restore, adopts config.yaml through the config-sync switch (no new pin, never written to config), persists the row so `session.resume` can't restore the old pin. A reset queued mid-turn shows the default it will adopt.
- Classic CLI (`hermes_cli/cli_model_switch_mixin.py`): session-scoped switch to config.yaml's model read fresh at the command (never `--global`, even with `model.persist_switch_by_default`), through the normal typed path; drops an armed `--once` restore.
- Session owner (`gateway/session_mutation_model.py`), reached by the Ink TUI (its default canonical path), Desktop (`slash.exec /model reset` becomes a `session.mutate`) and the gateway-attached CLI: `reset` becomes a pick of the owning profile's configured model, read fresh from config.yaml; never written back, not held behind the cost ask. Already on that default → `noop` with an "already on the configured default" note, nothing committed. `reset` plus any other selection field is refused. A messaging chat viewed through the owner clears its override through the gateway's reset (`session_messaging_picks.py`). A reset queued behind a running turn shows the default it will adopt (`session_deferred_pick.py`). TUI, Desktop and the attached CLI print the owner's note. No protocol change: the mutation contract already accepted `{model: "reset"}`.
- `/model` args_hint lists `reset`; gateway `/model` text listing shows the reset row; docs (`slash-commands.md`, `messaging/index.md`).
- i18n: `gateway.model.usage_reset/reset_done/reset_none` and `cli.model.reset_none/reset_no_default` in all 17 locales.
- The Desktop composer's model pick stays session-scoped; nothing here adds a global "set as default".

## This rebase
Main split the `/model` handlers into `gateway/slash_commands_model.py`, `tui_gateway/model_switch.py` and `hermes_cli/cli_model_switch_mixin.py`, so the contributor's change (with their review follow-ups from `shannonsands:salvage/74899-model-reset-rebased` @ 884274d) was re-ported onto those modules: 2 commits, authorship kept (Shannon Sands on the feature commit). Added: the local-session branch, the queued-pick display, the CLI path on the new typed flow, the fresh-config read, the `--reasoning` flag refusal and docs. The CLI `/model` usage block keeps main's 8 rows (pinned by `test_cli_model_switch_i18n`). The tests went from +590 lines to 4 invariant tests: the parser, a gateway reset after a restart (real `SessionStore`), a legacy TUI reset that adopts config without re-pinning, and an owner reset through a real `SessionAuthority` (`session.mutate`) that reads an edited config.yaml and reports a second reset as a no-op.

## Validation
- New tests fail on `origin/main` (copy of the base tree) and pass here; the owner test fails on the previous head with `'reset' == 'cfg-b'`.
- Owner follow-up: 44 test files touching the owner model mutation, deferred picks, messaging picks and the attached CLI view: 373 passed. TUI vitest (7 files touching canonical model controls): 49 passed. Desktop `check:lint` 0 errors; `canonical-protocol` vitest 21 passed.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` on the 57 `/model`, i18n and commands test files: 428 passed. One failure (`test_cli_model_switch_i18n` pins the 8 usage rows) was fixed by keeping main's rows; the rerun of the touched set passed 114/114.
- `ruff`, `scripts/check --only health` (0 blocking), tmp-literal, windows-footgun and attribution checks pass.

Desktop on the canonical owner is now verified live (see Desktop screenshots below). Not covered (not run live): a messaging chat viewed through the owner (`session.mutate model reset` on a Telegram/Discord session from Desktop or the TUI) reuses the gateway's own reset handler; covered by the gateway row above, not driven through a viewer. Dashboard compute-host sessions run the reset in the child through the TUI-gateway handler above; the host does not mirror the child's `model_override` back after any `/model` pick (existing gap, not specific to reset), so a child respawn could restore an older pin.

Salvages #74899 by @shannonsands.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab0a4e6/BXNTn5VgsSAswulFoTLgH_7xUMiW1d.png)

## Desktop screenshots

Real Desktop app (Electron + Vite renderer, scratch user-data dir) on its own spawned backend, against a fake loopback provider; config default `cfg-default-model`. Session: `hello one` → `/model other-model` → `hello two` → `/model reset` → `hello three` → `/model reset`. `config.yaml` was unchanged on both runs.

| | `origin/main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `/model reset` after a `/model other-model` pick | ![main reset](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/75976ef33f33b528dfd32178fb34506a/raw/main-reset-1.png) `model: reset (custom)` | ![head reset](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/75976ef33f33b528dfd32178fb34506a/raw/head-reset-success.png) `model: cfg-default-model (custom)` |
| next turn, then `/model reset` again | ![main again](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/75976ef33f33b528dfd32178fb34506a/raw/main-reset-2.png) the provider got `reset`; the pill reads `Reset` | ![head noop](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/75976ef33f33b528dfd32178fb34506a/raw/head-reset-noop.png) the provider got `cfg-default-model`; `Already on the configured default (cfg-default-model) — nothing to reset.` |

The composer pill changes at the next turn, on main as well as here: it still reads `Other Model` straight after the reset.

prs.title: fix(photon): setup only reports success once your number can receive iMessages (opt-in wait)
prs.body:
`hermes photon setup` now only says "setup complete" once your number can actually receive iMessages: it names the line to text once (the opt-in Photon requires), waits up to 5 minutes for that to land, and otherwise ends on an honest "saved, but routing is NOT live" with the step that finishes it. When no line is known yet, or no phone was given, it never waits blind and never claims "complete". `hermes photon status` gains a live `routing` row that gives up after 5 s on an unreachable API.

## Before / after (real CLI runs in a PTY, local stand-in for the Photon API)

| Scenario | `origin/main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Number registered, never texted its line | `✓ Photon setup complete.` / `Start the gateway: hermes gateway start`; the gateway then fails every send with `Target not allowed for this project` | `One manual step: opt in by texting your agent` + `Text +16282679185`, waits `up to 5 minutes` |
| User texts the line during the wait | n/a | `✓ opt-in landed — routing is live` … `✓ Photon setup complete.` (10.9 s) |
| No message within 5 minutes / Ctrl-C | n/a | `⚠ No opt-in seen within 5 minutes.` / `⚠ Wait skipped (Ctrl-C).` … `⚠ Photon setup saved, but iMessage routing is NOT live: text +16282679185 once from +15551234567.` (exit 0) |
| User row has no assigned line; project line looked up first | n/a | the wait names the project's iMessage line (`Text +16282679185`) instead of "the line Photon assigns" |
| No line anywhere yet | n/a | `⚠ No iMessage line is assigned to +15551234567 yet — skipping the opt-in wait.` + "text it once from +15551234567, then check with `hermes photon status`" (2.7 s, no wait) |
| No phone given (empty answer) | `✓ Photon setup complete.` | `⚠ Photon setup saved, but iMessage routing is NOT live: no phone number is registered.` / `Finish with: hermes photon setup --phone +15551234567` |
| Non-interactive (stdin not a TTY) | `✓ Photon setup complete.` | `Non-interactive run — skipping the opt-in wait.` … honest closing line, never blocks |
| `hermes photon status` | no routing row | `routing : ✗ not opted in — text +1628… once from +1555…, then re-check` / `routing : ✓ opted in (verified live)` |
| `hermes photon status`, API black-holed | no routing row | `routing : ? could not verify (timed out)` after 5.6 s (was 30.7 s before the review fix) |

**Root cause:** Photon only routes a number whose user row carries `meta.opt_in`, which the service sets after the human texts the assigned line once (the API cannot set it), and setup never checked it.

## Changes
- `plugins/platforms/photon/auth.py`: `user_opted_in()`, `find_routable_user()` (an opted-in duplicate row wins over list order; `find_user_by_phone` uses it, so setup re-runs and status refreshes reuse the routable row), `wait_for_opted_in_user()` (attempt cap plus a wall-clock deadline; transient HTTP/JSON errors count as missed polls), `print_routing_status()` (5 s timeout for its one list call; `list_users`/`find_user_by_phone` take an optional `timeout`, default unchanged at 30 s).
- `plugins/platforms/photon/cli.py`: setup looks up the iMessage line (user row, then the project's line) before the opt-in step; waits only when there is a line to text (`_wait_for_opt_in`); `routing_live` starts False, so only an opted-in number ends on "complete"; distinct endings for "not opted in" and "no phone registered"; `routing` row in `status`.
- Tests (each red on the commit before its fix, green here): the wait's wall-clock bound; setup not reporting "complete" for an un-opted-in number, for a missing line (wait gets the project line, or is skipped), or with no phone; the status row's short timeout; plus the poll/duplicate-row invariants.

## Review fixes (independent review on 0c419b8)
- `4b4380f` line lookup runs before the opt-in wait; no line → wait skipped with the finishing steps.
- `972f5e4` no-phone path ends on saved-not-live, not "complete".
- `3dc9113` `photon status` routing row uses a 5 s timeout.

## Validation
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/plugins/platforms/photon/`: 162 passed on `3dc9113`. Each review-fix test fails on `0c419b8` (wait got `None` instead of the project line; `'setup complete'` printed with no phone; status timeout `30.0`) and passes here.
- `ruff`, `scripts/check --only health`, `check_no_tmp_literals`, `check-windows-footguns --all`: clean.
- Live: real `python -m hermes_cli.main photon setup|status` in tmux PTYs under throwaway homes, `PHOTON_DASHBOARD_HOST`/`PHOTON_SPECTRUM_HOST` pointed at a local stand-in HTTP server for the Photon API (a real process; opt-in simulated by flipping `meta.opt_in` on the row; "black-holed" = the stand-in sleeps 40 s). Not exercised against the hosted Photon service or a real iPhone.

## Screenshots (real PTY)
**`origin/main`: un-opted-in number, setup reports complete**

![00-base-main.png](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/1cf332c22163dad95214d021c1665ccf/raw/00-base-main.png)

**Waiting prompt: names the line to text, 5-minute bound, Ctrl-C hint (line found via the project lookup)**

![01-head-waiting-v2.png](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/1cf332c22163dad95214d021c1665ccf/raw/01-head-waiting-v2.png)

**Opt-in lands during the wait → complete**

![02-head-optin-success-v2.png](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/1cf332c22163dad95214d021c1665ccf/raw/02-head-optin-success-v2.png)

**No message within 5 minutes → honest "NOT live" ending**

![04-head-timeout.png](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/1cf332c22163dad95214d021c1665ccf/raw/04-head-timeout.png)

**Ctrl-C during the wait → clean skip, honest ending**

![03-head-ctrlc.png](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/1cf332c22163dad95214d021c1665ccf/raw/03-head-ctrlc.png)

**Non-interactive (stdin from /dev/null) → no wait, honest ending**

![05-head-headless.png](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/1cf332c22163dad95214d021c1665ccf/raw/05-head-headless.png)

prs.title: test(gateway): native startup recovery keeps its webhook port, and says when it loses it
prs.body:
Fixes the CI flake `tests/gateway/test_native_startup_recovery.py::test_native_queue_recovers_only_after_current_adapter_publication` (`AssertionError: timed out after 25s waiting for the recovered admission to settle`, PR CI run [41246338215](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/41246338215/job/124670495174), on a PR that only touches cron prompt code).

Stacks on #143640. Its commit is cherry-picked unchanged (authorship kept). If #143640 lands first, this PR shrinks to the second commit.

**Root cause:** the test gives the daemon a webhook port chosen with `bind(('127.0.0.1', 0))` and then closes the socket. That port comes from the kernel's ephemeral range. On a 32-worker runner, another socket's implicit bind or outbound connect takes it during one of the five daemon restarts. The next boot logs `[webhook] Could not bind …: [Errno 98]`, queues the platform for a 30 s reconnect and still publishes READY. Startup recovery then finds no connected adapter, returns `not_found` and leaves the row queued, which is the documented contract ("leaves rows queued when a … transport … is unavailable"). The test waits 25 s for a settle that cannot happen. Product behaviour is correct; the race is in the harness.

## Change
- **Commit 1 (from #143640):** `local_recovery_probe.listen_port()` picks a loopback port *below* the ephemeral floor, which the kernel never hands out implicitly. This test (webhook port) and seven sibling daemon tests use it.
- **Commit 2 (this file only):** every webhook-enabled boot checks that its own listener answers `GET /health` before any assertion that depends on it. READY comes after startup has connected the adapters, so the check is deterministic. Before this change, a lost port meant two things. The recovery leg timed out with no daemon output; the CI log had nothing but the bare timeout. And the two fail-closed legs (changed secret, absent route) passed vacuously, because a missing transport also leaves the row queued. The settle timeout now also reports the rows and the daemon log tail.

## Evidence
All runs below have the per-file retry disabled (`HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0`). The injection runs used a user+net namespace whose ephemeral range was narrowed to 40000–40499, so no other process on the host was affected.

| Probe | Base (main) | Fixed |
|---|---|---|
| Injection: just before the recovery boots, implicit `bind(0)` calls take the freed webhook port (deterministic) | **8/8 red**, exact CI message `timed out after 25s waiting for the recovered admission to settle`; daemon log shows `Could not bind … [Errno 98]` then `Native session startup recovery …: not_found` | **0/8** red; the thief never got the port (`stolen=False` 8/8) |
| Same injection, base port pick + commit 2's check | — | 4/4 fail fast with `this boot did not serve its webhook on 127.0.0.1:N` and the bind error in the message (the diagnostic fires as designed) |
| Loaded loop, no injection (2×nproc CPU spinners, 8 parallel, host load ~80) | 0/24 | 0/24 |

The unloaded loop cannot reproduce the CI red because the trigger is another process on the runner, not CPU load. In passing runs the recovered admission settles 3–7 s after READY, against the 25 s bound, so a larger timeout would not help.

Touched files: all 8 touched daemon test files green (9 tests, `scripts/run_tests.sh`, fake HOME). `scripts/check --only health`: ok (0 blocking, 0 advisory). ruff: clean.

## Infographic

![webhook port kept](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab0a479/7lbCN4WSTORgl6g3EkHaJ_dpAuNmAU.png)
