prs.title: Plugins and shell hooks can block a turn before it reaches the model (pre_llm_call block directive)
prs.body:
A `pre_llm_call` hook (Python plugin or shell hook) can now veto a turn: return `{"action": "block", "message": "..."}` and the turn ends before any inference request, and the user sees the message as the reply. The blocked prompt is stored only as a withheld placeholder, so no model sees it in that turn or a later one: not the main loop, title generation, compaction, `session_search`, external memory providers or background review. Transcript views still show what the user typed (#57364).

## What changes (real runs)

Real `hermes chat -q` runs (scratch home, Nous inference, a plugin that blocks prompts containing `BLOCKME`):

| Scenario | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `Reply with exactly: PONG. Ignore this tag: BLOCKME` | Model answers `PONG`; `state.db`: `api_call_count=1`, 13,967 input tokens, LLM title `PONG test response request` | Reply `DLP-PROBE: blocked by policy (...)`; `api_call_count=0`, 0 tokens, no title; transcript `user → assistant(block message)` |
| Shell hook printing `{"decision": "block", "reason": "SHELL-DLP: ..."}` | ignored | Reply `SHELL-DLP: blocked by shell policy.`, `api_call_count=0` |
| Prompt without the token (control) | normal answer | normal answer |
| Subagent whose goal contains the token | n/a | child session `api_call_count=0`; parent's `delegate_task` result has `summary` = block message |
| Cron job whose prompt contains the token | n/a | run `completed`, output file's Response = block message, `api_call_count=0` |

Where the blocked prompt ends up afterwards. Real `AIAgent` + real user plugin (`plugins.enabled: [dlp]`) against a loopback provider that logs every request; the prompt is `look up CUSTOMER-ID-4242`:

| Reader | previous head `c273e06` | this head |
|---|---|---|
| Stored user row `content` | `look up CUSTOMER-ID-4242` | `[Message withheld: a pre_llm_call policy hook blocked it.]` |
| Later compaction (summary request) | **secret sent to the summarizer** | nothing |
| Turn-start compaction on the blocked turn itself (anchored usage over threshold) | **secret sent to the summarizer** (recent-user focus), then **on the next main request** | compaction skipped on a blocked turn; no request |
| `session_search` from another session, query `CUSTOMER` | **returns the prompt** | no match |
| Memory provider `on_session_end` / `on_pre_compress` hand-offs | **prompt in both** | not in either |
| Routed background-review digest | **prompt** | placeholder |
| TUI/Desktop submit-time row (written before the agent runs) | prompt stays in `content` | rewritten in place to the placeholder |
| Post-turn micro-compaction on the blocked turn (`micro_compact: true`) | 1 auxiliary request | none |
| Transcript views (CLI `--resume` recap, TUI/Desktop history, dashboard) | typed text | typed text (unchanged) |
| Next turn's wire, in memory and reloaded from `state.db` | placeholder | placeholder |

## Changes

- `agent/turn_context.py`: `pre_llm_call` results may carry `{"action": "block", "message": ...}`; the first one with a message wins (one without a message is ignored, as for `pre_tool_call`). The hook now runs before turn-start compaction, which a blocked turn skips, along with titling and external-memory prefetch. The blocked user row's `content` becomes the placeholder (also the persist override, so no flush restores the typed text). What the user typed goes into `display_metadata.withheld_prompt`. A row the TUI/Desktop already wrote at submit time is rewritten in place.
- `agent/message_metadata.py`: the `withheld_prompt` key plus two helpers, one that reads it for transcript views and one that drops it from memory-provider hand-offs.
- Transcript views render the typed text: `hermes_cli/cli_agent_setup_mixin.py` (resume recap), `tui_gateway/session_history.py` (TUI/Desktop `session.resume`), `hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py` (`display_content`, which the desktop app and dashboard already prefer).
- `SessionDB.set_user_message_content` (and the managed-worker store op) take an optional `display_metadata`. No schema change.
- `agent/conversation_loop.py`: a blocked turn goes straight to `finalize_turn` (`turn_exit_reason="blocked_by_plugin_pre_llm_call"`, `api_calls=0`, not failed).
- `agent/turn_finalizer.py`: a blocked turn gets no memory sync, background review, micro-compaction or prepare-ahead summary.
- `agent/memory_manager.py`: transcript hand-offs to memory providers drop the display-only key.
- `agent/shell_hooks.py`: `pre_llm_call` stdout accepts both block shapes (`action`/`message` and `decision`/`reason`), same as `pre_tool_call`.
- Docs: the hooks reference, the plugin guide and `observer-hooks.md` cover the return shape, what gets stored and the fail-open rule below.

Root cause: `pre_llm_call` could only add context, so a DLP / policy plugin had no supported way to stop a prompt from reaching the model. The first version of this PR then kept the prompt as the row's `content`, which every transcript reader except the main-loop replay uses.

Known limits (documented):
- **Only a returned block blocks.** A callback that raises, or runs past `plugins.hook_callback_timeout` (30 s by default), is skipped, and the turn goes ahead. This is deliberate: failing closed would block every turn for users with a buggy context hook.
- A model-metadata lookup (such as a `/models` context-length probe on a fresh session) can run before the hook. It carries no message content.
- The `/goal` judge still sees the goal text the user typed.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/agent/test_pre_llm_block_hook.py` | 5 passed. Two end-to-end tests against an in-process provider: (1) the blocked turn makes zero chat requests, the stored row is the placeholder, `session_search` misses, and the next turn's wire carries the placeholder; (2) compacting a history that holds the blocked turn keeps the prompt out of the summary request and the compacted history. Plus 3 shell-dialect cases. |
| Red on the previous head `c273e06` | both end-to-end tests fail (stored content, summary request) |
| Suites that call the touched functions (turn context, compaction, api_content sidecar, memory provider, session history / resume projections, submit-row, worker store, finalizer, micro/prepared compaction, shell hooks, plugins) | 98 files: 1,933 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped (`scripts/run_tests.sh`); `test_plugins_cmd_catalog.py` errors in the scratch test home only (`the worker contract requires real uv`) |
| `scripts/check --only health`, ruff, `/tmp` literals, Windows footguns, attribution | pass |
| Live spend for this round | $0 (loopback provider) |

## Infographic

![pre_llm_call block directive](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aa573c6/2gT0TEYNNFso8rpzmnL_3_ch5YHTdx.png)

prs.title: fix(desktop): drop a finished turn's journal on reopen instead of replaying it
prs.body:
![Stale-journal fix infographic: the bug, why recovery missed it, the owner pending-list rule, the reopen race, proof and limits](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af809d0c-c153-42fe-a282-d92ab234f206)

## What does this PR do?

I hit this in the Webapp on Firefox for Android. A tab closed while a turn was streaming. When I reopened the chat later, that old prompt and its half-streamed reply showed up below the newest reply, and they came back after every reload. The server transcript was fine: the extra copy came from the tab's in-flight turn journal in `localStorage`.

**Root cause.** On reopen, `recoverInFlightTurnJournal` decides whether the journaled turn finished by finding its completed reply in the loaded transcript. When the loaded rows don't hold the journaled prompt, `mergeInFlightMessages` appends the whole journaled tail, which it has done since the journal landed in 8d8d1d61fe. The loaded rows miss the prompt in several cases:
- a long tool-heavy turn, or newer turns from another device, push the prompt out of the newest 120-row page;
- compaction re-stored the rows;
- the last throttled snapshot differs from the final text, which is #136335's case.

The idle re-persist then refreshes the journal, so it never ages out.

**Approach: ask the owner instead of inferring.** The canonical reopen snapshot already lists every admission the owner has not finished (`queued`, `started`, or `unknown` after a crash) under the client's submission id. A send's optimistic prompt id is `user-<submission id>`, so the journal can be checked against that list directly:

| Owner's pending list | Journal |
|---|---|
| lists the journaled turn as `started` or `queued` | folded live, as today |
| lists it as `unknown` (lost in a crash) | recovered, as today; this is what the journal is for |
| doesn't list it | the turn finished: cleared before any transcript matching |
| journal prompt names no admission (tile action, first-message id) | cleared only when the list is empty |
| no list at all (owners without an admission ledger, failed-resume fallback) | unchanged from `main` |

The second commit closes a race this opens. A cold reopen reads the newest REST page alongside `session.resume` and normally omits the snapshot's history, so the page can be read before a turn commits its final reply. Until now the stale journal stood in for that reply; once it's cleared, nothing would. `rereadPageAfterResumeBarrier` now re-reads the page once whenever the journal holds a turn the owner no longer lists. That holds even when the owner isn't idle, because a queued successor may already be running. The re-read is safe because `settle_session_input` marks an admission terminal only after the agent wrote the turn's rows. Owners without a list never trigger it.

Approaches I tried and dropped before this one:
- **Ordering by row id.** It passed unit tests, but a live send's journaled prompt has no row id: the `prompt.submit` admission receipt carries no `user_row_id`.
- **Comparing the send time against server row timestamps with a clock-skew margin.** It still replayed the old turn whenever the chat was reopened within the margin.
- **Paging back until the prompt is found.** Unbounded.

## Related Issue

Refs #136335: the same mechanism, a stale journal re-folded below a finished reply after long tool-heavy turns. I'm not marking it fixed, because the reporter later saw one occurrence with no journal keys stored, which this change doesn't explain.

#77584 (open) also edits `inflight-turn-journal.ts` and `use-session-actions/index.ts`, but for retention and deletion. It doesn't cover this replay.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

Two commits:

- `147ec5a92d` **fix(desktop): drop a finished turn's journal on reopen instead of replaying it**
  - `apps/desktop/src/lib/inflight-turn-journal.ts`: `ownerPendingTurns()` reads `info.pending_submissions`. `recoverInFlightTurnJournal` takes an `owner` option and clears a journaled turn the owner has finished before any transcript matching.
  - `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/index.ts`: the reopen path passes the snapshot's pending list. The comment above the call was shortened to keep the file at its code-health size cap.
  - `apps/desktop/src/lib/inflight-turn-journal.test.ts`: retire cases (prompt outside the loaded page, another turn running), plus controls (`unknown` recovered, `started` keeps folding, no list keeps today's transcript check, and the prompt-without-admission cases).
  - `apps/desktop/e2e/core/webapp-stale-journal.spec.ts` (new, Linux like the other Webapp journeys): a real gateway and Webapp build with two tests.
    - **Stale turn:** a tab dies mid-turn, the turn finishes, and another browser runs a tool-heavy turn (4 × 32 terminal calls) and then a newer one. The reopened and reloaded chat must end at the newest reply, with the journal cleared.
    - **Crash:** the gateway is SIGKILLed mid-turn and restarted. The owner lists the turn as `unknown`, and the reopened chat must still show the streamed reply that only the journal held.
- `19c46310b3` **fix(desktop): re-read the reopen page when a journaled turn has finished**
  - `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/resume-barrier-reread.ts`: re-reads once when the journal holds a finished turn, idle or not.
  - `apps/desktop/src/lib/inflight-turn-journal.ts`: `journaledTurnFinished()` helper.
  - `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/resume-settled-journal-reread.test.tsx` (new): drives the real `resumeSession` with a page read before the final reply.

## How to Test

1. E2E: `npm run build:webapp`, then `npx playwright test -c e2e/core/playwright.config.ts webapp-stale-journal` from `apps/desktop`.
   - On `main`, the stale-turn test fails with the old prompt and its partial reply after the newest prompt. On this branch, both tests pass.
2. Units: `npx vitest run --project ui src/lib/inflight-turn-journal.test.ts src/app/session/hooks/resume-settled-journal-reread.test.tsx`.
3. By hand in the Webapp:
   1. Send a prompt and close the tab while the reply streams.
   2. Let the turn finish, then run a few more turns from another browser.
   3. Reopen the chat. It should end at the newest reply. `hermes.desktop.inflightTurnJournal.v2:*` should be gone from `localStorage`.

## Verification

Run on head `19c46310b3` against base `9a76ac8e4f`. Linux arm64, Node 26.12.1, Playwright Chromium 1248 and Firefox 157.

| Check | `main` (`9a76ac8e4f`) | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| E2E, Chromium | stale-turn test **fails** (old prompt and partial reply after the newest prompt); crash test passes | both pass, 4/4 over 2 repeats |
| E2E, Firefox 157 (Gecko) | stale-turn test **fails** the same way; crash test passes | both pass, 2/2 |
| `resume-settled-journal-reread.test.tsx` | both race cases **fail**, showing the stale partial "Reading the issue" where the final reply "There are four open issues." should be; the read-once control passes | 3/3 pass |
| `inflight-turn-journal.test.ts` | the 7 new tests can't run on `main` (`ownerPendingTurns is not a function`), so their red isn't behavioural; the behavioural red is the three rows above | all pass |
| Commit `147ec5a92d` on its own | | 27 files, 440 tests pass; `tsc` clean; code-health clean |
| Full desktop `test:ui` | | 1,490 files, 12,601 tests pass |
| `python scripts/check` | | 14/14 checks pass |
| `tsc` (src and e2e), eslint | | clean |

**Before/after**, 34 seconds, recorded at the same time on the two builds: real Webapp and gateway, a scripted mock model, headed Chromium, and a real X pointer. The left side is `main`; the right side is this branch.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9883fe72-1c02-441e-94ff-0fd7326df2ee

| | After reopening | After reload |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | the old prompt and "Reading" sit below the newest reply; journal still stored | same |
| this branch | ends at "Here is the note for the team."; journal cleared | same |

**Not covered.**
- Owners that send no pending list keep `main`'s behaviour, so the replay can still happen there:
  - the legacy JSON-RPC backends, including Desktop remote;
  - the failed-resume fallback.
- Forwarded owners (`tui_gateway/owner_forward.py`) publish their list only as a `session.info` event, which this doesn't read.
- I haven't re-tested on Firefox for Android, where I first saw this. Desktop Firefox 157 passes the e2e.
- Prettier flags two lines in `use-session-actions/index.ts` that I didn't touch and that `main` already has. I left them alone because reformatting would push the file past its size cap.

## Checklist

### Code

prs.title: fix(local-runtime): size unified-memory launches from free RAM, refuse what it cannot hold
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

On Apple Silicon and Linux integrated GPUs the launch budget is 80% of *total* RAM, so the planner picks context windows that free memory cannot hold. On an 18 GB Mac with ~2.2 GiB free, Bonsai-27B was planned at 221K (~14 GiB); a 4B load on the same machine pushed swap from 7 to 11.8 GB.

RAM-backed budgets are now priced against the RAM free at launch. Windows keeps the existing commit-room logic and NVIDIA unified memory is unchanged. When even the 64K floor does not fit, the model is refused with how much it needs and how much is free, instead of being started into swap. If free RAM cannot be measured (guessed reading), the existing capacity plan is kept.

## Related Issue

Related: #133261, #136164. Touches the same planner code as open #144250 and #136173; happy to rebase onto either.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/local_runtime/hardware.py`: free-RAM reading with a measured/guessed flag; `ram_backed` budgets on macOS and Linux iGPU
- `hermes_cli/local_runtime/estimator.py`, `context_policy.py`, `bootstrap.py`: size from the launch budget, refuse below the floor; 1 GiB re-plan step so free-RAM drift does not re-read headers every pass
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_local_launch_budget.py`: launch-budget cases; OS-specific cases use `platforms(...)` markers
- `website/docs/user-guide/local-models.md`: one line

## How to Test

2. On a RAM-backed machine with little free memory, regenerate presets: a large model is refused with a reason instead of getting a 221K window.

prs.title: feat(desktop): make bare file paths and URLs in chat clickable
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Agents hand over paths and URLs as plain text far more often than as markdown links - `Report: /Users/me/report.md`, or `` `/tmp/out.md` `` and `` `http://localhost:8931/` `` inside a code span. Authored links (`[report](/path)`) already open in the preview pane. The unwrapped shapes stayed dead text: copyable, never clickable.

This makes those unwrapped shapes inline links so the sentence stays a sentence (not a block PreviewAttachment card):

- Left-click a path → existing sandboxed preview tab (resolved at click time against session cwd / backend).
- Left-click a URL that filled a code span → same in-app browser routing as a prose URL.
- Appearance setting **Require ⌘/Ctrl-click to open chat links** (default off, matching current upstream). When on, a regular click selects text; ⌘-click on Mac / Ctrl-click elsewhere opens; Enter on a focused link still opens. Cursor is `default` until the modifier is held, then `pointer`. Settings, plugins, artifacts and other chrome stay single-click (`applyInlineOpenPreference` is opt-in on chat markdown only).

Renderer-only. No new IPC. Default-app / reveal stay out of this PR (see the stacked follow-up).

## Related Issue

Fixes #48313 (clickable chat paths). Also covers the URL / code-span part called out as missing from #48859 / #48947.

Related duplicates of the same ask: #58854, #51239.

## Not a duplicate of open PRs

| PR | Why this is different |
|---|---|
| #86976 (open) | Opt-in config key; prose absolute paths become `#media:` links that open with the OS default app. No code-span targets, no URLs, no in-app preview. This PR opens paths in the existing preview pane, linkifies code-span paths **and** URLs, and keeps OS-open as a later right-click verb. |
| #48859 / #48947 (drafts) | New hardened `hermes:openPath` IPC and a different `#file/` door. This PR reuses the existing preview + `hermes:openExternal` path and does not add main-process surface. |
| #91664 (open) | Artifact filename download / reveal. Adjacent file UX, not chat prose linkify. |

If #86976 or #48859 land first, `markdown-text.tsx` / preprocess will need a mechanical rebase. No file overlap with current `main` at preparation time.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/lib/path-refs.ts` - pure detector, sibling of `session-refs.ts`. Bare absolute / `~/` / `file://` paths with a known extension in prose become a `#path/` fragment href (same sanitisation-safe trick as `#session/`). Relative paths, directories, unknown extensions, and paths already inside a markdown link or autolink are left alone; sentence punctuation is re-emitted after the link.
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/markdown-preprocess.ts` - `linkifyBarePaths` runs after `routeFileLinksToPreview` and before `autoLinkRawUrls`.
- `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/markdown-text.tsx` - `#path/` renders as `InlinePathLink`. The `inlineCode` override wraps a code span that **is** a single path or URL in the same link (code styling kept). Chat markdown URLs pass `applyInlineOpenPreference`.
- `apps/desktop/src/components/chat/inline-path-link.tsx` - click resolves via `normalizeOrLocalPreviewTarget`; raw path is the `href` so the existing app context menu can resolve a right-click.
- `apps/desktop/src/store/inline-link-open.ts` - desktop-local appearance preference + document flags for cursor (one window listener, not per link).
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/external-link.tsx` - optional `applyInlineOpenPreference` (default off).
- Appearance toggle + i18n for en, zh, zh-hant, ja, ar, ru.

Windows drive paths (`C:\…`) are excluded on purpose: the backslash is an escape in markdown and needs its own treatment.

## How to Test

```bash
cd apps/desktop
npx vitest run --project ui --environment jsdom \
  src/lib/path-refs.test.ts \
  src/components/assistant-ui/markdown-text.barepaths.test.tsx \
  src/lib/external-link.test.tsx \
  src/store/inline-link-open.test.ts
npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit
```

2. A URL that fills a code span should open like a prose link.
3. `git checkout -- index.html` and relative `css/file.css` in code spans stay plain code. Fenced blocks stay inert.
4. Authored `[report](/path)` stays the PreviewAttachment card (no double wrap).
5. Appearance → enable **Require ⌘/Ctrl-click to open chat links**. Regular click selects; modifier-click opens; chrome links outside chat still open on a regular click. Cursor is an arrow until the modifier is held.

prs.title: fix(local_runtime): size upstream ggml Q1_0 (41) and Q2_0 (42) tensors
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The local-runtime planner refuses GGUFs that use the upstream ggml **Q1_0 (41)** and **Q2_0 (42)** types with `unknown ggml tensor type 41`, even though the pinned engine serves them. `_GGML_TYPE_SIZES` in `hermes_cli/local_runtime/gguf.py` stops at MXFP4 (39).

Block layouts are taken from upstream `ggml/src/ggml-common.h`: fp16 scale + 128 one-bit quants (Q1_0) or 64 two-bit quants (Q2_0), both 18-byte blocks. Type ids are from `ggml/include/ggml.h`.

Real-world case: PrismML's 1-bit `Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf` (Apache-2.0).

Fork-only types (e.g. PrismML's 142/143 used by Ternary-Bonsai-2) are unaffected and still refused.

## How to test

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_local_runtime_gguf.py`: the new test sizes a one-tensor GGUF of each type. It fails without the fix and passes with it. Neighbouring local-runtime suites: 69 passed.
- Live (macOS arm64, engine b10964 metal, 18 GB):
  - `Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf` (sha256 `17ef842e…819aa0`) now parses (3.53 GiB tensors), and the planner records a launchable preset.
  - The same engine serves it directly at 8K context and passes a two-turn tool-call test: correct `calibration_lookup` call, correct value reported; ~63 tok/s prefill, ~18.5 tok/s decode.

## Note

On this 18 GB machine the planner picked a 221K window for this model, and loading it there drove memory pressure to 5% before I aborted the load. That window-sizing question is separate and is not addressed here.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

prs.title: feat(google-workspace): named Google accounts with --account
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Lets one Hermes profile use more than one Google account (personal + work) through the bundled `google-workspace` skill. Today the skill reads a single `<HERMES_HOME>/google_token.json`, so the only way to reach a second account is a whole second Hermes profile, which also splits memory, sessions and config.

`--account EMAIL` on `setup.py`, `google_api.py` and `gws_bridge.py` selects a token of its own at `<HERMES_HOME>/google_tokens/<email>.json`. Leaving the flag out changes nothing: same token path, same output, same gws environment.

This is deliberately the small core the triage on #15602 asked for when it pointed at the closed #30686 ("split out the core multi-account token resolution and CLI plumbing that can be reviewed independently"): no migration, no default-account pointer, no aliases, no new env var, no new scope logic.

### Design decisions

- **No fallback for a named account.** `--account work@x.com` with no token for it exits 1 with the setup command to run. It never reads the default token, because that would answer a request about one account with another account's mail (the data-boundary concern raised in #15602).
- **Wrong-account guard at consent time.** `--auth-url` passes `login_hint`, and `--auth-code` asks Google which account actually granted the token (Gmail `users.getProfile`, or the primary Calendar id when only Calendar was granted). If it differs from `--account`, the token is not written and the message names both accounts. If the granted scopes can't reveal the account, the token is saved with a warning.
- **Separate gws config dir per named account.** gws caches access tokens per config dir without keying on `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLI_CREDENTIALS_FILE` (googleworkspace/cli#572, #134966), so two accounts sharing the default dir would silently run as whichever filled the cache first. Named accounts get `<HERMES_HOME>/google_tokens/gws/<email>` (0700); an explicit `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLI_CONFIG_DIR` from the caller wins. The default-token path is untouched, so this doesn't conflict with #134967's fix for that path.
- **Account names are validated as plain email addresses** (lowercased, no path separators), so `--account` can't escape `google_tokens/`.
- **No new `HERMES_*` env var**, per the contribution rubric; selection is by flag only.

## Related Issue

Fixes #15602

Related: #30686 (closed, larger version of this), #44057 (auth contexts: broader, overlaps in intent), #134967 (gws cache for the default token).

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `skills/productivity/google-workspace/scripts/_google_account.py` (new): account validation, `--account` argument, per-account token / pending-session / gws config paths, `list_accounts()`.
- `scripts/setup.py`: `--account` for `--check`, `--check-live`, `--auth-url`, `--auth-code`, `--revoke`; `--list-accounts`; `login_hint`; identity check before saving a named token.
- `scripts/google_api.py`: global `--account` (before the service); per-account gws config dir; setup hint names the account.
- `scripts/gws_bridge.py`: optional leading `--account EMAIL`; refreshes and writes only that account's token.
- `SKILL.md`: "More than one Google account" section, agent rule to ask which account when ambiguous, remote-backend note (`terminal.credential_files`); version 1.3.0. Website page regenerated with `website/scripts/generate-skill-docs.py`.
- `tests/skills/test_google_workspace_accounts.py` (new): 10 behaviour tests.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills/test_google_workspace_accounts.py tests/skills/test_google_workspace_api.py tests/skills/test_google_workspace_setup.py tests/skills/test_google_workspace_setup_deps.py tests/skills/test_google_workspace_credential_files.py -q` → 28 passed.
2. Manual, with a second Google account added as a test user on the OAuth client:
   ```bash
   setup.py --account work@example.com --auth-url      # consent screen pre-selects work@example.com
   setup.py --account work@example.com --auth-code "<redirect URL>"
   setup.py --list-accounts
   google_api.py --account work@example.com gmail search "is:unread" --max 3
   google_api.py gmail search "is:unread" --max 3      # still the default account
   ```
3. Approve with the wrong account on step 1 → `--auth-code` prints `ERROR: You authorized ..., but --account is ...` and writes no token.

The tests cover: named account uses its own token and gws cache; omitting `--account` leaves the env exactly as before; a missing named token fails instead of using the default; path-like `--account` values are rejected before anything is created; the bridge refreshes only the named token; `--auth-url` hints the account and keeps the default pending session untouched; a token granted by a different account is never saved.

prs.title: fix(cli): stop the /goal loop after a failed provider turn
prs.body:
This stops the classic CLI `/goal` loop from judging and re-queuing after a failed provider turn.

## What does this PR do?

On main, a credit cap hit mid-goal (HTTP 402) spends the whole turn budget on 402s plus one judge call per failed turn.

A failed turn has no model reply. `_maybe_continue_goal_after_turn` still reads the newest assistant row, which is the `FAILED_TURN_NOTICE` boundary row on main ("Your request was not processed...") and the previous turn's reply on v0.20.0. The judge reads that as progress, says continue, and the next turn fails the same way. The TUI already gates this with `_is_successful_goal_turn`. The CLI hook never reads `_last_turn_result`.

This came from production use of Hermes on my fleet of unattended `hermes chat` goal agents (v0.20.0, custom provider behind a daily credit cap). Across the fleet's tmux panes, the goal event right after a billing-failed turn was 91 continuations, 87 parks and 7 "goal achieved" verdicts, all judged on text the failed turn never produced. One pane logged "402, Continuing toward goal (n/20)" in a loop until the judge-error pause fired.

## Related Issue

Related to #63180, the gateway twin of this bug. #63187, #63203, #64337 and #74974 touch only `gateway/`. No open issue or PR covers the classic CLI hook. #118705 edits the empty-response check a few lines below and composes with this change.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/cli_loops_mixin.py` adds `_goal_turn_failed`. It applies the TUI contract to `_last_turn_result` and skips the judge. The contract is failed, interrupted, or `completed is False` that is not a max-iterations handoff, so #102213 keeps working.
- For `failure_reason` billing, auth or auth_permanent the hook also pauses the goal, because those repeat on every retry until the user acts.

- `locales/*.yaml` adds `cli.goal.paused_provider_failure` to all 17 catalogs (parity test).

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_goal_interrupt.py` adds 5 cases. Billing, auth and auth_permanent pause with no judge call and nothing queued. A transient server error skips the judge, spends no goal turn and leaves the goal active, while a max-iterations handoff still goes to the judge as before.

## How to Test

1. Run `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_goal_interrupt.py -q` on main code with the new tests. The 4 failure cases fail because the judge runs on the failed-turn notice, and on this branch all 8 pass.

```
E   AssertionError: Expected 'judge_goal' to not have been called. Called 1 times.
E   Calls: [call('build a thing', 'Your request was not processed. Send it again if you still want me to carry it out.', ...)]
```

2. End to end, I drove the real `HermesCLI` (`chat()` plus the post-turn goal hook that `process_loop` runs) against a local fake OpenAI server. The `/goal` kickoff turn succeeds and every continuation turn gets the Nous 402 "Insufficient available credits" body. The judge always answers continue.

|---|---|---|
| turns run | 20 | 2 |
| POSTs answered 402 | 19 | 1 |
| judge calls on failed turns | 19 | 0 |
| final goal state | paused, turn budget exhausted (20/20) | paused, provider turn failed (billing) |

3. The 15 goal, loop, i18n and TUI goal test files give 322 passed, 1 skipped on main and 327 passed, 1 skipped on this branch.

prs.title: Anthropic streams cut before stop_reason continue the reply instead of ending the turn (port MiniMax-AI/minimax-code#566)
prs.body:
An Anthropic Messages stream that is cut after the text but before `stop_reason` now continues the reply instead of saving the half answer as the final one.

## What changes

| Stream shape (anthropic_messages wire) | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `message_start` → text → `message_stop`, **no `message_delta`** (no `stop_reason`) | half answer saved as the final reply, turn ends, no warning | `⚠️ Response truncated — server ended the stream without ever sending finish_reason …` → `↻ requesting continuation (1/4)` → full answer |
| normal stream with `message_delta` (`stop_reason=end_turn`) | finishes | finishes (unchanged) |
| no `message_stop` at all / tool_use with no `stop_reason` / empty | EmptyStreamError retry (#121535, #80498) | unchanged |

**Root cause:** `stop_reason=None` mapped to `"stop"`. The chat_completions wire already treats the same shape (text, no `finish_reason`, clean EOF) as a drop (#32086); the Anthropic wire did not.

- `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py::_StreamingCall._call_anthropic` records whether `message_delta` arrived; a final message with no `stop_reason` and no `message_delta` comes back as the existing Anthropic-shaped clean-EOF partial stub, so `turn_truncation.recover_from_truncation` runs its normal bounded continuation.
- The completion checks (`check_anthropic_message`, moved unchanged, plus the new `completed_or_drop_stub`) live in the new sibling `agent/chat_completion_helpers_anthropic.py`, which keeps the facade under its FILE_LINES ratchet (4001 → 3986).
- 1 invariant test in `tests/agent/test_anthropic_message_stop.py` (red on `origin/main`, green here). The existing "message_stop + stop_reason=end_turn accepted without retry" test still passes.

Port from MiniMax-AI/minimax-code#566 (0.7.2: "report a truncated Anthropic stream without a stop_reason"). They surface it as a model-service error; Hermes reuses its existing continuation path for the same shape on the other wire, so the content received so far is kept and the model finishes.

## Live repro

Real `AIAgent.run_conversation` (`api_mode=anthropic_messages`, real `anthropic` SDK) against a loopback Anthropic SSE stand-in whose first main request sends `message_stop` without `message_delta`; later requests complete normally. Same driver, both trees.

| arm | final_response | provider requests (main) |
|---|---|---|
| `origin/main` 9a76ac8e4f6 | `PART-ONE of the answer, cut here` (truncated, accepted) | 1 |
| this PR | `PART-ONE of the answer, cut here\nPART-TWO done.` | 2 (second is the continuation prompt) |

Loopback stand-in, not a real provider: no real endpoint produces this shape on demand. Not covered: the auxiliary (non-loop) `anthropic_adapter._stream_final_message` path, which has no continuation machinery; it keeps its current behaviour.

## Tests

`scripts/run_tests.sh` over `test_anthropic_message_stop`, `test_anthropic_mid_tool_call_drop`, `test_anthropic_stream_fallbacks`, `test_partial_stream_finish_reason`, `test_stream_runaway_repetition`, `test_stream_stale_abandon`, `test_run_agent`: 334 passed, 0 failed. `scripts/check --only health` passes.

prs.title: fix(kanban): end a worker's turn on the terminal board call it just landed
prs.body:
## Problem

A dispatcher-owned Kanban worker's turn must **end** on the terminal board call that hands the card on (`kanban_complete`, `kanban_block`, `kanban_request_review`, `kanban_request_changes`, and now `kanban_schedule`). The stop gate only covered the mirror direction: a turn that exits with **no** terminal call is nudged to make one. The landed direction had no guard at all, so the loop kept iterating after the handoff.

Measured 2026-09-23: run 2666 called `kanban_block`, the dispatcher respawned a fresh worker, and the original live process went on to implement the card under a run id it no longer held — its own board writes landed on someone else's run. This is the in-process half of #98750 ("a successful terminal transition does not end the turn"); #69116 describes the same authority boundary on the Codex app-server transport.

## What changed

`agent/kanban_stop.py`

- New `terminal_handoff_status(messages, tool_calls) -> str | None`: returns the status landed by a terminal board call **in the round that just ran**, else `None`.
  - Result rows are read from the tail of `messages` — the block after the newest assistant row carrying tool calls, i.e. this round's results, never an earlier round's.
  - Results are matched to a terminal call **by call id** (`tool_call_id_variants`, the existing single pairing policy), **not by tool name**: the mixed-invalid-batch path appends an error row under the terminal tool's own name, so a name match would read a refused call as a handoff.
  - Only a success payload (`{"ok": true, ...}` from `tools/kanban_tools._ok` / `_ok_landed`) counts. A `tool_error` row, a spilled/stubbed result, or anything unparseable yields `None` — no evidence, no handoff.
  - The terminal set is read from `_TERMINAL_KANBAN_TOOLS`, so the guard covers `kanban_schedule` (added upstream after this branch was cut) without a code change.

`agent/turn_tool_round.py`

- `run_tool_round` breaks immediately after tool execution when this round's terminal call returned a success payload, synthesizing a non-empty `final_response` (`Task handed off: <status>.`) so the turn finalizes as completed rather than failed.
- Scope is `kanban_stop_nudge_enabled()` — the dispatcher-owned worker only, which excludes delegated children and cron runs.
- Exit reason `kanban_terminal_handoff` is deliberately **not** in `turn_failure_copy._EXIT_REASON_FAILURES`, so a landed handoff is never reported as a turn failure (verified: the token appears nowhere in `agent/turn_failure_copy.py` at this tip).

A refused call, a non-terminal Kanban tool, or an earlier round's result therefore never ends the turn — the worker stays alive and retries, which is what #136843 and #138607 are about.

## Tests

`tests/agent/test_kanban_terminal_handoff.py` — 9 tests / 15 cases:

- parametrized over the four terminal tools for **both** the landed and the refused payload (the parametrization is `sorted(_TERMINAL_KANBAN_TOOLS)`, so it picks up `kanban_schedule` on rebase);
- non-terminal Kanban tool, no-owned-task and delegated-child scope gates;
- call-id matching (an error row under the terminal tool's name does not hand off) and "only this round's result" ;
- the exit-reason contract and the payload parser (`{"ok": true}` with/without status; unparseable and non-success payloads).

Branch-carried receipt recorded at this tip: with the base blobs of `agent/kanban_stop.py` and `agent/turn_tool_round.py` swapped back in, the new test file fails to collect, and the same scenario driven through `run_tool_round` returns `action=continue` (worker keeps iterating) against `action=break` on the fixed tree. Targeted suite: 23 files / 202 tests passed.

## Scope / risk

Policy-only: no board access, no state, no schema. The break is limited to the dispatcher-owned worker path and to a call whose own result row proves it landed, so a worker that is refused or that calls a non-terminal Kanban tool is unaffected. Behaviour for every non-Kanban agent (CLI, gateway chat, cron, delegated children) is unchanged.

## Relation to existing work

- Closes the in-process half of #98750. It does **not** add the run-existence check before a mid-stream continuation resumes a worker — that is the other half of #98750 and remains open.
- Prior art #98769 (suppress the mid-stream continuation stub) targeted the same symptom from the stub side and closed unmerged.
- Not a duplicate of #91220 (require one durable terminal handoff — the missing-handoff direction), #138654 (plugin terminal handoff tools), #138607/#136843 (refused-call nudge), or #104721 / #103457 (run-identity checks before board writes): those are separate defects on the same lifecycle.

## Rebase note

Cut from upstream `main` at `65d01a7c` on 2026-09-24; upstream has moved a long way since, so the two touched files are expected to need a trivial rebase. `agent/kanban_stop.py` diff against current `main` is one added frozenset member (`kanban_schedule`); `agent/turn_tool_round.py` has drifted in the tool-batch normalization region only. Happy to rebase on request.

prs.title: fix(desktop): require explicit session focus selection
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Require an explicit click or keyboard selection to change the active Desktop chat. Moving across another transcript on the way to Files currently changes the composer recipient, native typing focus and workspace context, in both docked and floating composer modes.

This deliberately replaces the existing documented focus-follows-mouse interaction. Selecting a pane now costs a click or keyboard action; pointer transit does not select it. Hover-first **tab shortcut targeting** remains unchanged.

## Related Issue

Fixes #145453

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `floating-target.ts`: remove pointer-move selection; hand off on explicit pointer/focus events while preserving controls, transcript selection, inline editing, IME and capture ownership. Plain Tab/Shift+Tab cancels a pending delayed pane-focus request so a later mount cannot steal newer focus.
- `pane-shell/pane-focus.ts`, tab actions and session focus: keep explicit tab shortcuts and already-open session navigation aligned with the visible pane, composer recipient and Files context. Generic background pane activation does not request typing focus.
- Keep the two over-limit stores below their current line counts by moving their existing event-to-group lookup and open-tile focus block into the focus modules; no ratchet exceptions or threshold changes.
- Update the Desktop interaction contract and add regression coverage for both composer placements, cross-group tab selection, prevented-default reaction clicks and delayed mounting.

## How to Test

1. Open two chat panes with different working directories and unsent drafts. Click the right pane's editor, then move the mouse across the left transcript to Files without clicking. The right pane remains the recipient; its draft, caret and Files directory remain selected.
2. Click the other transcript or editor, or navigate there with the keyboard. The selected chat changes. Clicked buttons/inputs, transcript text selection and inline editors retain normal focus.
3. Repeat with the composer popped out. Its recipient changes only on explicit selection. During active dictation/voice capture, microphone ownership remains pinned until capture ends; a clicked control can still focus another pane and Files follows that pane.
4. With multiple tabs in another group, use the existing tab-slot/cycle shortcuts. The visible selected chat and typing recipient agree. Request a delayed tab and then Tab/Shift+Tab to another control before it mounts: the later mount must not override the newer selection.

### Executed validation

- Linux, Node 26.12.1, production module imports with the repository's registered Vitest `ui` project: **23 files / 358 unique tests passed**. This includes composer focus, Files/CWD, session sidebar/open-pane navigation, shortcut targeting, stale IME flags, reactions and inline editing.

prs.title: Plugin catalog: hermes-band — local music composition and rendering (4 tools, skill)
prs.body:
Adds the `hermes-band` entry to the plugin catalog, pinned to `c7a104f9a3d4daf28f507fbf0e054871bc1489c9` (v0.2.0).

**What it does.** Composes and renders original music locally. An arrangement is data — tempo, key, chord progression, parts — rendered deterministically through fluidsynth and a mastering chain into an exact-length wav plus mp3, which is what makes it usable for scoring to picture. Registers `band_render`, `band_validate_score`, `band_list_presets`, `band_doctor` and the bundled `hermes-band` skill.

**Disclosure.** This one shells out. It runs the host's `fluidsynth` and `ffmpeg` binaries against a local General MIDI soundfont (path override: `HERMES_BAND_SF2`), and writes the wav, mp3 and per-part midi/wav stems into `~/hermes-band-out/<name>/` — configurable through the plugin's `output_dir` setting. A render takes tens of seconds and runs in the foreground of the tool call; nothing is downloaded and no background process is left behind. `band_doctor` reports a missing binary/soundfont instead of failing the render. No network calls, no credentials, no self-updater.

**Dependency.** `numpy>=1.24,<3` (floor plus ceiling, per rule 10) — the mixing and mastering code is plain numpy DSP.

**Checks at the pinned commit:**

- `hermes plugins validate . --install-deps` → **passed** (manifest, declared capabilities, security scan, no core override)
- `hermes plugins doctor .` → runtime discovery, import and registration OK
- `scripts/scan_plugin_payloads.py` → no findings (no binaries, no committed bytecode, no archives)
  The security scan reports one `caution`: `sudo_usage` in `SKILL.md`, because the setup instructions include `sudo apt install fluidsynth fluid-soundfont-gm ffmpeg`. It is documentation for the human installing host packages — the plugin itself never invokes sudo.
- End-to-end smoke test in a throwaway `HERMES_HOME`: a one-shot agent session ran `band_doctor` (`ready: true`, fluidsynth 2.3.4, soundfont 148 MB, ffmpeg present) and then `band_render` with the bundled `bed` preset, producing `bed.wav` + `bed.mp3` (33.4 s, 192 kbps, peak -0.97 dB) and five per-part stems, verified with ffprobe.

**Catalog rules.** Exact 40-hex SHA pin, owner submission (the repo is ours), no binaries in the tree, no self-update, no credential access, declared capabilities match registrations exactly.

prs.title: fix(agent): scope auxiliary semaphores to event loops (salvage #93880)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #93772. `_acquire_async_aux_semaphore` caches one `asyncio.Semaphore` per `(home, task, id(loop))`, and `id()` is only unique while the loop is alive. CPython hands a collected loop's address to the next one, so a new event loop can receive a dead loop's semaphore — with its permits exhausted, or already bound to the old loop. The cache also keeps one entry per loop for the life of the process. This only bites when `auxiliary.<task>.max_concurrency` is set, on paths that run auxiliary calls on short-lived loops (`async_call_llm` from separately created loops, e.g. trajectory compression).

Repro for the `needs-repro` label, stdlib only (Python 3.14):

```python
import asyncio, gc
ids = []
for _ in range(50):
    async def f(): return id(asyncio.get_running_loop())
    ids.append(asyncio.run(f())); gc.collect()
print(len(set(ids)))           # 3 — fifty loops, three addresses

sem = asyncio.Semaphore(1)
async def main():
    async def hold():
        async with sem: await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
    await asyncio.gather(*(hold() for _ in range(3)))
asyncio.run(main())
asyncio.run(main())            # RuntimeError: <Semaphore ... [locked]> is bound to a different event loop
```

The fix keys the cache by the loop object in a `weakref.WeakKeyDictionary` and drops closed loops on each acquire, because a semaphore that has been waited on references its loop and would otherwise keep the weak key alive.

**Salvage of #93880** by @JoaoMarcos44 (closed by its author, never merged), cherry-picked so the authorship survives, then adapted to current `main`:
- kept main's per-profile `(hermes_home_key(), task)` key and the shared `_cached_semaphore` helper (both landed after #93880);
- prune closed loops across all tasks instead of per task, so loops whose task never fires again do not linger (the review note on #93880);
- moved `_get_task_max_concurrency` into a new sibling `agent/auxiliary_concurrency.py` (it late-imports `_get_auxiliary_task_config` from the facade, so existing `patch("agent.auxiliary_client._get_auxiliary_task_config")` seams still apply) to offset the growth, per the FILE_LINES ratchet: `agent/auxiliary_client.py` ends one line shorter than on `main`.

## Related Issue

Fixes #93772

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/auxiliary_client.py`: `_aux_async_semaphores` is a `WeakKeyDictionary` of loop → `{(home, task): (limit, semaphore)}`; `_acquire_async_aux_semaphore` prunes closed loops and looks up by the loop object.
- `agent/auxiliary_concurrency.py`: `_get_task_max_concurrency`, moved unchanged apart from the late facade import.
- `tests/agent/test_auxiliary_concurrency.py`: from #93880 — two loops whose `id()` collides (patched to a constant) must not share a semaphore.

## How to Test

2. On `main`, `test_async_cache_does_not_alias_distinct_loops_with_same_address` fails (`sem1 is sem2`).

prs.title: fix(tool_search): 合并 tool_call 字符串 slip 修复（括号 + 缺 name）/ combine stringified tool_call slip repairs
prs.body:
## 中文
把两个相邻的 `tool_call` 字符串化 slip 修复合并成一个 PR（原 #131399 + #143966），rebase 到当前 main。二者都是长 Qwen3.8-27B 回合把 `tool_call` 批发成 JSON 字符串时的尾部小模型 slip，都作用于同一个 `normalize_tool_call_entries`，本就该在一起：

- **括号 slip（原 #131399）**：相邻闭合括号错序、多余一个闭合括号、尾部缺 1–2 个闭合括号、单字符/转义漂移/漏逗号。`_repair_malformed_calls_string` 五类有界修复 + `_is_valid_calls_batch` 语义守卫——只有能重解析成合法 calls 批才接受，真实损坏绝不静默吞掉。
- **缺 name（原 #143966）**：单条 entry 丢掉 `"name"` 字段 + 闭合 `}`（10-24 实测 8/8 失败）。`_recover_missing_name_entry` 在尾部闭合位插入一个 `}`，`_resolve_entry_name_from_args` 用参数 schema 唯一指纹反推 name——要求恰好一个注册 deferrable 工具匹配，绝不猜；猜不出就给一条教会模型正确形态的定向错误。

`normalize_tool_call_entries` 统一两条恢复路径：字符串批先试括号修复（entry name 保留），不行再落到缺 name 恢复；per-entry 循环先解析 `arguments` 再按指纹恢复缺失的 `name`。

rebase 到当前 main 的冲突已解：上游把签名改成小写 generic（`dict`/`list`）并在 4 处现代化，两个 PR 的修复函数按各自有界策略并入、无重复。

## English
Merges two adjacent stringified-`tool_call` slip repairs into one PR (formerly #131399 + #143966), rebased onto current main. Both fix small-model tail slips when a long Qwen3.8-27B turn emits the batch as a JSON string, in the same `normalize_tool_call_entries` — they belong together:
- **bracket slips** (`_repair_malformed_calls_string` + `_is_valid_calls_batch` guard): out-of-order / surplus / missing-tail closers, single-char / escape / comma drift; accepted only when the repair re-parses to a valid calls batch.
- **missing `name`** (`_recover_missing_name_entry` + `_resolve_entry_name_from_args`): the entry dropped its `"name"` field and closing `}`; recover the name by a UNIQUE argument-schema fingerprint (never guessed — otherwise a targeted error teaches the correct shape).

The unified `normalize_tool_call_entries` tries the bracket repair first (entries keep their names), then falls back to missing-name recovery; the per-entry loop parses `arguments` before recovering a dropped `name`.

## Tests
`tests/tools/test_connector_bridge_wiring.py`: **49/49 pass** (both PRs' 19 new cases + 30 existing, no regression). py_compile clean, ruff pre-commit passes.

prs.title: fix(tool_search): recover stringified tool_call entries that dropped "name" / 修复 tool_call 字符串化批次丢 name 字段的不可恢复错误
prs.body:
## Bug Description / 问题描述

When a smaller model (measured: Qwen3.8-27B) invokes a deferred MCP tool through the `tool_call` bridge, it can emit the batch envelope as a JSON **string** whose single entry drops both the `"name"` field and the entry's closing `}`. The call then dies with an opaque error the model cannot learn from:

```
tool_call 'calls' is not valid JSON: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 1 column 882
```

In the measured session (2026-10-24), this pattern caused **8 consecutive failures** of the same task-card update while the model retried with byte-identical payloads — it had no signal about what was actually wrong.

当小模型（实测 Qwen3.8-27B）经 `tool_call` 桥调用 deferred MCP 工具时，可能把批次信封输出成 JSON **字符串**，且其中唯一的 entry 同时丢掉 `"name"` 字段和 entry 的闭合 `}`。调用随后报一个模型学不到的晦涩错误：`Expecting ',' delimiter`。实测会话（2026-10-24）中同一任务卡更新**连续 8 次失败**，模型用字节相同的 payload 重试，得不到任何有效纠错信号。

## Root Cause / 根因

The stringified-batch tolerance path (`normalize_tool_call_entries`) only recovers *bracket* slips. A dropped `"name"` key is not recoverable by any bracket edit — and the previous policy was to deliberately never guess a tool name, leaving the failure to a model retry. But the retry error was the raw JSON parse error, which tells the model nothing about the missing field; with no new information, the model reproduces the identical slip (8/8 in the measured session).

字符串化批次的容错路径只恢复**括号**类 slip。丢失的 `"name"` 键不是任何括号编辑能恢复的——旧策略是"绝不猜工具名"，把失败留给模型重试。但重试看到的错误是原始 JSON 解析错误，对缺失字段毫无提示；模型得不到新信息，就重复同样的错误（实测 8/8）。

## Fix / 修复

Two bounded, unique-solution mechanisms in `tools/tool_search_validation.py` (same conservative philosophy as the existing stringified-batch repairs):

1. **Unique-schema name inference** (`_resolve_entry_name_from_args`): when a batch entry has no `name`, infer it from its argument keys — accepted **only** when exactly one registered deferrable tool's parameter schema fits the fingerprint (`required ⊆ keys ⊆ properties`). Tools without required parameters never match (an empty fingerprint fits everything). Ambiguous or unmatched fingerprints are never guessed.
   无 `name` 的 entry 用参数键做指纹推断——**仅当**恰好一个已注册可 defer 工具的参数 schema 精确匹配（`required ⊆ keys ⊆ properties`）才接受；无 required 参数的工具永不匹配；歧义或无匹配绝不猜。
2. **Bounded tail-closer recovery** (`_recover_missing_name_entry`): for the string-broken variant (tail reads `...<arguments>}]}]`), insert one `}` at each trailing closer position; accept only when every parse canonicalizes to the same single-entry batch.
   字符串破损变体（尾部 `...}]}]`）：在尾部闭合位有界插入一个 `}`，所有解析结果必须归一化为同一批次才接受。
3. **Teaching errors**: when recovery cannot apply, the error now states the required entry shape (`{"name": "<tool name>", "arguments": {...}}`) and names the closest candidate tools, so the model's retry is one mechanical edit instead of a blind repeat.
   救不了时报错直接给出正确的 entry 形状并列出最接近的候选工具名，重试变成一次机械修正。

## How to Verify / 验证方法

1. `tests/tools/test_connector_bridge_wiring.py` — 5 new tests, including the **exact 882-char payload** from the measured session as a regression fixture:
   `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_connector_bridge_wiring.py` → all green (42 passed on this branch).
2. Red on base: the 5 new tests fail on `upstream/main` without this change (verified).
3. Behavior boundary: entries with an ambiguous fingerprint are rejected with candidates named; the existing "requires a 'name'" contract is preserved for the no-match case.

## Test Plan / 测试计划

- [x] Added regression tests for this bug (5: rescue broken-tail, rescue valid-JSON, ambiguity rejection, no-match teaching error, real-payload fixture)
- [x] Existing tests still pass (42/42 in the file; tool_search suite unmodified)
- [x] Measured real-world payloads: 8/8 previously-failing task-card updates now recover with their plan steps intact

## Risk Assessment / 风险评估

**Low** — recovery is gated on a *unique* schema fingerprint across the whole registered tool set, so the only way a wrong tool could be inferred is if two registered tools are exact argument-key twins of each other; in that case the call is rejected (with both names shown) rather than guessed. All other paths (proper arrays, named entries, existing bracket repairs) are untouched. The error-text change is additive to the existing `requires a 'name'` message, preserving the contract existing tests check.

prs.title: fix(tool_search): repair mis-ordered close brackets in stringified tool_call "calls" / 修复字符串化 tool_call 参数里错位的闭括号
prs.body:
## 问题 / Problem

小模型（实测 Qwen3.8-27B）在长对话 turn 里经 `tool_call` 桥更新任务卡时，会把批次参数 `calls` 编码成 JSON **字符串**，且字符串尾部的两个相邻闭括号**顺序错位**：把 `[{"name":...,"arguments":{...}}]` 写成尾部 `"..."}]}`（数组的 `]` 提前到了 arguments 对象的 `}` 之前）。括号计数仍平衡，所以严格 `json.loads` 在错位的 `]` 处报 `Expecting ',' delimiter`，harness 拒绝，模型重试仍是同形错——实测一个 turn 内 **5/5 全部失败**。

A small model (measured on Qwen3.8-27B) emitting a task-card `update_plan` via the `tool_call` bridge, in a long turn, stringifies the `calls` batch and mis-orders two adjacent close brackets at the tail: it writes `"..."}]}` instead of `"...}}]"` (the array's `]` lands ahead of the arguments object's `}`). Bracket counts stay balanced, so strict `json.loads` fails at the misplaced `]` with `Expecting ',' delimiter`, the harness rejects it, and the model retries the *identical* shape — **5/5 failures measured in a single turn**.

This is the same small-model-output class already handled for a *stringified* envelope (#114484); this PR adds the missing *mis-ordered closer* variant.

## 证据 / Evidence

- 5 条真实损坏 payload（会话 `mumnbxl4ekd7nw`，`messages.tool_calls` 原始输出）：每条 tail 均为 `"...""]}]}`，`json.loads` 失败位置恰在错位的 `]`。
- 修复后 5/5 全部还原（正确 tool name / context_id / 完整 plan）。

- 5 real corrupted payloads (session `mumnbxl4ekd7nw`, raw `messages.tool_calls` output): every tail is `"..."}]}` and `json.loads` fails exactly at the misplaced `]`.
- After the fix all 5/5 recover (correct tool name, context_id, full plan).

## 修法 / Fix

`tools/tool_search_validation.py`：新增 `_repair_swapped_close_brackets()`——单遍严格扫描（尊重 JSON 字符串字面量），在**第一个**不匹配的闭括号处，若其相邻下一字符恰好能匹配栈顶，则交换两者并继续；任何其它失败形态返回 `None` 走原错误路径。

这是**有界单类修复**，不是宽松 JSON 解析器：只有"相邻两个闭括号顺序颠倒"这一种明确形态会被纠正，其它畸形（缺逗号、深度不平衡等）一律照旧报错，避免掩盖真实损坏。

Add `_repair_swapped_close_brackets()`: one strict single-pass scan (string literals respected); at the first unmatched closer, if the very next character is the closer that *would* match the stack top, swap the two and resume; any other failure shape returns `None` and the original parse error is surfaced.

This is a **bounded, single-class repair, not a lenient JSON parser**: only the one well-defined shape "two adjacent close brackets swapped" is corrected; every other malformation (missing comma, unbalanced nesting, ...) still errors out, so real corruption is never silently masked.

## 测试 / Tests

- 2 个新回归测试：可修复形态（swap 后还原）+ 两类不可修复形态（仍被拒）。
- `test_connector_bridge_wiring.py` + `test_tool_search*.py`：**115 passed**（含既有的 #114484 字符串包络与 malformed 拒绝用例，全部不回归）。

- 2 new regression tests: the repairable shape (recovers after swap) + two unrepairable shapes (still rejected).
- `test_connector_bridge_wiring.py` + `test_tool_search*.py`: **115 passed** (incl. existing #114484 string-envelope and malformed-rejection cases, no regressions).

## 范围 / Scope

仅 `tools/tool_search_validation.py` + 其测试。不动工具列表 pin / deferred 机制（那是有意的 prompt-cache 设计）。2 files, +104/-1.

prs.title: fix(context): release context-engine resources at agent teardown and detach the closed session DB
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Context engines have `on_session_start` / `on_session_end` / `on_session_reset`, but nothing tells an engine that the agent holding it is being torn down, so an engine that opened its own resources (a connection, a worker thread) has no place to release them before process exit.

This adds an optional, no-op `ContextEngine.shutdown()` hook and calls it once per agent from `AIAgent.shutdown_memory_provider()`, after the existing memory-provider and session-end teardown. The call sits in a `finally`, so an earlier teardown step that raises does not skip it; a failing `shutdown()` is logged at debug and never breaks close.

The contract is written for how engines are actually shared. Teardown happens many times per process (per-message gateway agents, delegate children, side-question forks, TUI session close), every agent gets `clone_for_agent()` of the one registered engine (which the plugin guide tells uncopyable engines to implement by sharing the durable backend), and a directory engine may hand the same object to every agent. So `shutdown()` must release only what that instance opened itself and never a backend shared with the registered instance or other agents' clones. The docstring, the module lifecycle line and the plugin developer guide (methods table + lifecycle list) all say this.

It also folds in #111138 (same author): after `close()` releases an owned session DB, `self._session_db` is cleared, so a second `close()` no longer calls `end_session` through the released handle.

## Related Issue

Supersedes #111138 (same author), now included here.

Third-party #79575 proposes a broader lifecycle (`create_runtime()` plus an idempotent `close()`) at the same teardown point; it is an alternative to this hook, not a complement. This PR keeps to a single no-op method so it stays small, and I'm happy to close it or rebase onto #79575's shape if maintainers prefer that design.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] 📝 Documentation update (context-engine plugin guide)

## Changes Made

- `agent/context_engine.py`: `ContextEngine.shutdown()` (no-op default) with the sharing contract; `shutdown_context_engine(agent)` selects the engine once under a per-agent lock and calls it outside the lock; lifecycle line in the module docstring.
- `agent/agent_init.py`: per-agent lock and once-flag in `_CONTROL_STATE` (a duplicated adjacent comment is dropped to stay within the file-size ratchet).
- `run_agent.py`: `shutdown_memory_provider()` runs engine shutdown in a `finally` after the existing order; `close()` clears `_session_db` after an owned release.
- `website/docs/developer-guide/context-engine-plugin.md`: `shutdown()` row in the overridable-methods table and step 7 in the lifecycle list.
- `tests/agent/test_agent_resource_teardown.py`: shutdown called exactly once across `close()` + gateway cleanup + repeated calls; called even when an earlier teardown step raises; a raising `shutdown()` does not break close; a real SQLite double close does not call `end_session` on the released handle.

Paths that reach `shutdown()`: `close()`, gateway cleanup (including per-message and temporary slash-command agents), CLI exit and one-shot, TUI session close, delegate-child close, side-question fork cleanup. Paths that do not (unchanged, soft release via `release_clients()` only): gateway cache eviction, background-review forks, CLI agent retirement.

## How to Test

1. On base `e1fdf003a6` with only the new test file added: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_agent_resource_teardown.py` → 6 failures, each on the missing behaviour (no hook call / `end_session` called twice), no import errors.
2. On this branch, same command → 6 passed.
3. `python scripts/check --base e1fdf003a6` → all checks pass, no code-health findings; `git diff --check` clean.

Tested on macOS 27.0 (26A428). Full suite left to CI.

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] Conventional Commits
- [x] Searched for duplicates (#79575 discussed above)
- [x] Only changes related to this fix
- [ ] Full `pytest tests/ -q` — left to CI; focused tests via `scripts/run_tests.sh`
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes
- [x] Tests added
- [x] Documentation updated (plugin guide)

## What this PR does NOT change

No plugin engine implementation, no new required methods, no config keys, no change to memory-provider behaviour or order, no change to shared (non-owned) session DB handles. Behaviour shifts from clearing `_session_db`: readers that already guard on it now skip a released handle instead of using it; a late, guarded persistence write after close is skipped rather than written through a released handle.

issues.title: [BUG] picoclaw-launcher: `-public` 与 `-host` 同时设置会自撞（crash loop）；`-public` 单独使用时只绑 IPv6，IPv4 客户端连不上
issues.body:
## 环境

- PicoClaw Launcher **v0.5.0**（`picoclaw-launcher`，arm64 静态二进制）
- OpenWrt aarch64（GL-BE6500），内核 dual-stack（`net.ipv6.bindv6only = 0`）
- 以 procd 服务方式常驻，`-host 0.0.0.0`

## 症状 A：`-public` 单独使用时**只绑 IPv6**，IPv4 客户端连不上

```
$ picoclaw-launcher -public
$ netstat -lntp | grep 18800
tcp   0  0  :::18800   :::*   LISTEN   <pid>/picoclaw-laun

本机自测（同一进程监听期间）：
  wget http://[::1]:18800/     → ✅ OK
  wget http://127.0.0.1:18800/ → ❌ FAIL
  wget http://192.168.8.1:18800/ → ❌ FAIL   ← 局域网浏览器用的就是这个
```

`--help` 里写的是：

```
-public   Listen on all interfaces (dual-stack) instead of localhost only
```

**文档说 dual-stack，实际只绑了 `[::]`（且该 socket 显然带 `IPV6_V6ONLY`）**，
所以 IPv4 一律连不上 —— 与文档不符。

## 症状 B：`-public` + `-host 0.0.0.0` 同时给 → **自撞 → crash loop**

```
$ picoclaw-launcher -public -host 0.0.0.0
… fatal … "Failed to open launcher listener(s): listen tcp4 0.0.0.0:18800: bind: address already in use"
```

**关键点：此刻 `netstat` / `/proc/net/tcp` 里 18800 是空的** —— 占用者就是它自己：
先绑了 `[::]:18800`（dual-stack 内核下**同时占住了 IPv4 端口**），再去绑 `tcp4 0.0.0.0:18800` → EADDRINUSE → fatal。

在 procd 下表现为无限重启：

```
procd: Instance picoclaw-launcher::instance1 s in a crash loop 7 crashes, 0 seconds since last crash
```

## 症状 C：`launcher-config.json` 里的 `"public": true` 同样触发

即使命令行**只**给 `-host 0.0.0.0`，只要 `launcher-config.json` 里是

```json
{ "port": 18800, "public": true, "allowed_cidrs": ["192.168.8.0/24", "10.10.10.0/24"] }
```

启动时依然会去做那套 dual-stack 绑定 → 同样 fatal / crash loop。

## 当前可用的绕过（workaround）

```json
{ "port": 18800, "public": false, "allowed_cidrs": [...] }
```

```
picoclaw-launcher -host 0.0.0.0      # 不传 -public
```

→ 只做单次 `tcp4 0.0.0.0:18800` 绑定，服务稳定，局域网 IPv4 正常访问。

## 建议

1. **监听顺序去重**：若 `[::]`（或 v4-mapped）已绑成功，就**跳过** `0.0.0.0` 的绑定（或反之），
   不要把"同一个端口"绑两次；绑失败也应降级而不是 fatal。
2. **`-public` 的行为对齐文档**：要么真的 dual-stack 且 IPv4 可达（`IPV6_V6ONLY=0`），
   要么把 `--help` 改成"IPv6 全接口"，别让使用者按文档配置却连不上。
3. `-host` 与 `launcher-config.json` 的 `public` 之间的关系，建议在文档里写清楚（目前是"都会生效并互相打架"）。

## 说明

我是把这套跑在 OpenWrt 上的用户（PicoClaw 装在路由器上做家用助手），
以上都在实机复现；日志和 `netstat` 输出都是原文。
没有提交修复 PR，按维护者习惯先报 issue。

prs.title: fix(telegram): escape link labels and blockquote text in MarkdownV2
prs.body:
Fixes #3426.

**Problem:** With Telegram MarkdownV2 enabled, reserved characters in link labels (e.g. the `.` in `[picoclaw.io]`) and blockquote text caused Telegram to reject the reply, falling back to plain text and losing all formatting. The converter treated complete `[label](url)` links and `> quote` lines as verbatim entities, bypassing the escaping required inside their displayed text.

**Fix:** In `pkg/channels/telegram/parse_markdown_to_md_v2.go`:
- Links `[label](url)`: the label is now recursively processed (specials escaped, nested entities kept) while the URL stays verbatim.
- Blockquotes `>` / `**>`: the quoted text is now recursively processed instead of passed through untouched. A trailing `||` expandable-blockquote terminator is preserved verbatim (it's syntactic, not content).
- Removed `[`, `>`, `**>` from `verbatimEntities` (code blocks and custom emoji remain verbatim).

**Tests:** Added the issue's two examples as test cases (`link label with period gets escaped`, `blockquote with link gets escaped`). Full `Test_markdownToTelegramMarkdownV2` suite passes (12/12). New cases proven red on base.

prs.title: fix(cron): propagate job failures to lastStatus instead of always ok
prs.body:
Fixes #3423.

**Problem:** Cron jobs always recorded `"lastStatus": "ok"` in `cron/jobs.json`, even when the run failed. Two compounding causes:

1. `CronTool.ExecuteJob` (`pkg/tools/cron.go`) returned the literal string `"ok"` on failure paths: when command execution was disabled, and when the exec tool reported `result.IsError`. Only the agent-error path returned an `"Error: ..."` string.
2. The gateway's `SetOnJob` callback (`pkg/gateway/gateway.go`) wrapped the result as `(result, nil)` — always a nil error — so `CronService` never took its `LastStatus = "error"` branch.

**Fix:**
- `ExecuteJob` now returns `"Error: ..."` strings on all failure paths (exec disabled, exec tool error). The agent-error path already did.
- The gateway callback converts any non-`"ok"` result into a non-nil error, so the cron service records `lastStatus: "error"` with the failure message in `LastError`.

**Tests:** Updated `TestCronTool_ExecuteJobPublishesErrorWhenExecDisabled` (it had codified the buggy `"ok"` expectation) to assert the `"Error:"` prefix. All `TestCronTool_ExecuteJob*` tests pass (6/6), `go build` succeeds for the touched packages. The updated test was proven red on base.

issues.title: Codex WebSocket idle retry is hidden until NanoClaw’s 10-minute turn timeout

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
### Summary

  A simple Telegram request can remain silent for ten minutes when the Codex Responses WebSocket stalls.

  Codex CLI detects its own five-minute WebSocket idle timeout and retries internally, but `codex app-server` does
  not surface that failure to NanoClaw. NanoClaw therefore waits until its fixed ten-minute `TURN_TIMEOUT_MS`
  expires.

  ## Environment

  - NanoClaw v2
  - Provider: `codex`
  - Codex CLI: `0.138.0`
  - Model: `gpt-5.4`, reasoning effort `high`
  - Authentication: API key through OneCLI
  - Channel: Telegram
  - Linux/systemd
  - Upstream checked: `main` at `53ea1e8b`, `providers` at `efc8eff4`

  ## Reproduction observed

  1. Send a simple Telegram request requiring a small workspace edit.
  2. NanoClaw starts/resumes the Codex thread successfully.
  3. Codex sends `response.create` successfully.
  4. No WebSocket response events arrive for five minutes.
  5. Codex logs:

 ```text
     stream error: idle timeout waiting for websocket
     stream disconnected - retrying sampling request (1/5 ...)
```
  6. The retry remains inside Codex CLI and is not emitted as an app-server error.
  7. At ten minutes, NanoClaw emits:
```
     Error: Turn timed out after 600000ms
```
  No model output or tool call occurred before the timeout.

  Follow-up Telegram messages sent while the turn was stalled were steered into the same active turn, making the bot
  appear completely stuck.

  ## Relevant implementation

  container/agent-runner/src/providers/codex.ts uses:

  const TURN_TIMEOUT_MS = 10 * 60 * 1000;

  The timeout is fixed wall-clock time. It is not aware of Codex’s internal WebSocket idle timeout or retry state.
  Timeout errors are also currently emitted with retryable: false.

  ## Expected behavior

  NanoClaw should not remain silent for ten minutes after Codex’s transport has already stalled.

  Ideally it should:

  1. Detect prolonged app-server turn inactivity.
  2. Interrupt the stalled Codex turn.
  3. Notify the messaging channel promptly.
  4. Replay automatically only when no assistant output, tool call, or other side effect occurred.
  5. Queue follow-up messages separately instead of steering them into a stalled turn.

  At minimum, the error should explain that the Codex transport stalled and that the original request may need
  retrying.

  ## Additional context

  This appears related to OpenAI Codex issue #19821, where Responses WebSocket failures consume the stream retry
  budget before HTTP fallback:

  https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/19821

  A possible short-term mitigation may be disabling WebSocket transport for Codex, but NanoClaw should still have its
  own activity watchdog and safe recovery behavior.

prs.title: ncl: warn when group scope overrides an explicit auto-fill arg (#2464)
prs.body:
Fixes #2464

## Summary

Under group scope, `dispatch()` auto-fills `agent_group_id`, `group`, and
`id` from the caller's locked context (and, for `wirings-get`/
`wirings-update`, from the resolved wiring for the current conversation).
When a caller explicitly passes a differing value for one of these keys,
nothing on stderr told them their value was overridden — the operator had
no signal that their write target changed.

This adds a single stderr warning, gated strictly on `provided !== undefined
&& provided !== locked`, at each auto-fill point:

- `agent_group_id`
- `group`
- `id` (groups/destinations resources, locked to the caller's own group)
- `id` (wirings-get/wirings-update, locked to the resolved wiring id for the
  current conversation — the case most likely to be missed, since it's a
  second, unconditional override a few lines below the general auto-fill
  block)

Matching-value passes stay silent, per the issue's guidance, so the warning
doesn't get trained out by redundant flags.

Note: for `agent_group_id`/`group`, a differing value is already denied by
the guard's cross-group check (`src/cli/guard.ts`) added in #2986, so those
two no longer reach the handler with the wrong value — but the caller
previously got no stderr signal explaining *why*, only a generic
`forbidden` JSON error. The wirings id case has no such guard check and was
a genuine silent override with no signal at all. This PR adds the warning
uniformly across all four auto-fill points so the operator sees the
mismatch immediately in every case.

## Test plan

- [x] Added 6 new tests to `src/cli/dispatch.test.ts` covering: warn on
      differing `--agent_group_id`, differing `--group`, differing `--id`
      (groups/destinations), differing `--id` (wirings-get resolved-wiring
      override), no warning on a matching value, no warning when the arg
      isn't passed at all.
- [x] `npx vitest run src/cli/dispatch.test.ts` — 64/64 passed.
- [x] `npx vitest run` (full suite) — 156 files / 1986 tests passed.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- [x] `npx eslint src/cli/dispatch.ts src/cli/dispatch.test.ts` — 0 errors (3
      pre-existing unrelated warnings in `dispatch.ts`, untouched by this
      change).
