prs.title: feat(telegram): bot-to-bot admission gate (doorman) behind TELEGRAM_BOT_INBOUND
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 draft payload. Branch: feat/telegram-bot-admission, cut from the upstream/main tip. -->

## Summary

Stops other Telegram bots from waking a NanoClaw agent into unbounded reply loops once Bot-to-Bot Communication Mode is enabled.

- **Problem**: with BotFather B2B on, every other bot's group message reaches the gateway and engages like a human mention. The Chat SDK skips only self-messages, so two bots sharing a group wake each other endlessly, and unregistered bot senders flood the unknown-sender path (#3235).
- **Fix**: a bridge-level admission policy for `channelType: 'telegram'` (built on the `registerBridgeInboundPolicy` seam), gated by `TELEGRAM_BOT_INBOUND`. It admits bot-authored inbound only from an allowlisted channel (`chatId` means anywhere in that chat, `chatId:topic` means one forum topic) and only when the message is addressed: the text opens with `/command@<botname>` or `@<botname>`, or it replies to the bot's own message content (forum-topic anchor replies excluded). Mid-text quotes, in prose or code spans, do not address. A per-peer throttle allows one admitted turn per peer per 30 s, and every decision logs one line.
- **Out of scope**: the unknown-sender gate itself (#3446 covers it), per-wiring topic engagement, and an `/add-b2b-peer` setup skill (follow-up).

## Related work

- #3235: bot senders generate unbounded approval cards, and this policy complements the gate-layer fix. Traffic dropped at the bridge never reaches the sender gate. PR #3446 fixes the gate layer itself; the two compose and are merge-order independent (this PR's only bridge hunks are two optional `ReplyContext` fields). Its auto-drop denies at the gate; this policy prevents earlier with a positive allowlist.
- #3600 / #3601: adapter and router reply-to-bot mention semantics. This policy does not consume `isMention` for bot-authored messages; it derives addressing itself and stamps `isMention` on admits, so it is unaffected either way. A note for #3601: its proposed `isReplyToBot` (a username match) counts forum-topic anchor service messages as "reply to bot". The anchor exclusion this PR adds to `ReplyContext` (`replyToForumTopicAnchor`) is that finding, expressed as a field.
- No open issue asks for an admission policy directly; #3235 is the closest pain. This change is safe to review directly as defense-in-depth.

## Change kind

<!-- Check exactly one. -->
- [x] `kind/hardening`
- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`

Hardening rationale: CONTRIBUTING routes new capabilities to skills; this PR uses the hardening kind instead. It adds a missing admission boundary (loop containment against bot-authored traffic on a stock install), is dormant by default, and exposes no capability surface. If maintainers read it as a capability, the payload converts to a channels-branch skill delivery; only the two `ReplyContext` fields are core.

## Validation

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/telegram-bot-admission.test.ts` returns 27/27 on a fresh `upstream/main` worktree (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`), and `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` passes. The 27 tests cover every drop reason, both addressing legs, anchor exclusion, bare-chatId entries, per-peer throttle isolation, and real-bridge integration (an admitted reply reaches the host mention-stamped; the firehose never does; humans flow untouched).
- Live fire in a production two-bot deployment: 5 drops, 1 admit (a raw `/ping@bot`), and an agent reply after 9 s. The chain ended human-addressed. The peer agent found the anchor-overload bug during this test; we fixed and re-verified it.

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change, release note below
- [ ] Breaking change, release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Telegram: new opt-in bot-to-bot admission gate (TELEGRAM_BOT_INBOUND="chatId" or "chatId:topic"). Bot-authored messages are dropped unless they address the bot (start-anchored command or mention, or a reply to its messages) in an allowlisted channel. Per-peer 30 s throttle; every decision is logged. Inert unless set; human traffic is unaffected.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- Adds an admission boundary for untrusted bot-authored input. Only allowlisted channels pass. This policy derives addressing itself and does not trust the adapter's substring `isMention` for bots. Admitted messages are stamped and forwarded to the existing router gates unchanged.
- Gated channels are default-deny. Drops are silent in chat and each writes one audit line (reason, sender id, chat, topic) to the host log; admits log at INFO. No new credentials, egress, or runtime changes.
- Human-message handling is untouched on every path. Rollback is removing the env var and restarting; nothing registers without it.

## Skill delivery

- [x] Not a skill
- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

This is the trunk hardening piece. The companion Telegram-adapter registration ships as a small patch on the `channels` branch, delivered through the channel-skill flow once the trunk change lands.

## AI assistance

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change
- [x] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

<!-- The attestation box above is deliberately unchecked. It is the operator's to tick after reviewing the diff (compare/files tab). Required by CONTRIBUTING regardless of the disclosure box. -->

<details>
<summary>Appendix: install DX, scaling, two-target split</summary>

**Install (post-merge)**

1. In BotFather, enable B2B for the bot pair and add both bots to the group.
2. Update NanoClaw. The policy ships inert.
3. Add `TELEGRAM_BOT_INBOUND="-1001234567"` (whole group) or `"-1001234567:42"` (topic only) to `.env`, then restart the host. To roll back, remove the line and restart.
4. Register the peer: `ncl members add --user telegram:<peerBotId> --group <agentGroupId>`.
5. The peer addresses the agent at message start (`/cmd@bot`) or by replying to the agent's messages. Every admission decision is auditable in the host log.

**Scaling**

Comma-separate env entries for more channels or topics, and run `ncl members add` for more peers. The throttle is per peer, so one chatty bot cannot starve the others.

**Two-target split**

Trunk ships channel-adapter infrastructure; the Telegram adapter lives on the `channels` branch. This PR (trunk) adds `src/channels/telegram-bot-admission.ts` with tests that compile standalone, plus the two optional `ReplyContext` fields. The `channels` branch gets a 66-line patch that exports and extends the adapter's `extractReplyContext` and registers the policy at module load (a no-op without the env var). Upstream `chat-sdk-bridge.ts` has moved past some forks; this PR's hunks touch only the `ReplyContext` interface and apply cleanly on the current tip.

</details>

prs.title: fix(host): propagate operational errors from AnchoredDir callers instead of treating them as unsafe paths
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops three `AnchoredDir` call sites from treating disk and permission errors as unsafe-path refusals.

- **Problem**: `AnchoredDir`'s deliberate refusal (a segment is a symlink or not a directory) and operational failures (ENOSPC, EACCES, EMFILE) reach the same catch blocks, and every catch downgrades every error to "unsafe path": the inbox catch accepts the message without its attachment files and never retries it; the outbox catch returns no files and delivery proceeds without them; the template-skill catch lets the spawn continue after the old skill was deleted and its replacement only partly copied. The log lines name the wrong cause in each case. Regression from #4063.
- **Fix**: `anchored-dir.ts` exports `isAnchoredRefusal(err)`, true only for the wrapped refusal whose `cause` carries ELOOP or ENOTDIR. The inbox, outbox and template-skill catches rethrow anything else, so operational failures reach the existing failure paths: the inbound write throws before the message is stored, delivery retries and eventually marks the message failed, and the spawn realization throws.
- **Out of scope**: the same catch shape in `src/provider-contracts/realize.ts` (`syncSharedSkillLinks`) and `src/modules/agent-to-agent/agent-route.ts` — separate subsystems with their own callers and semantics, not changed here. `clearOutbox`'s swallow-all catch is deliberate and documented (the message is already delivered) and is untouched.

## Related work

Closes #4134

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

- Tests were written first and fail without the fix; they pass with it, and reverting only the three source files makes them fail again: `src/anchored-dir.test.ts` (`isAnchoredRefusal` against real ELOOP/ENOTDIR refusals raised by `AnchoredDir.open`, plus operational, plain and wrapped non-refusal errors classified false), `src/session-manager.attachments.test.ts` (ENOSPC while opening the inbox propagates out of `writeSessionMessage` instead of the message being accepted without its files), `src/session-manager.outbox.test.ts` (EACCES while opening the outbox propagates out of `readOutboxFiles` instead of silently returning no files), `src/group-skills.test.ts` (ENOSPC mid-copy fails `materializeTemplateSkills` after the old skill was deleted and the replacement file created empty).
- `vitest run src/anchored-dir.test.ts src/session-manager.attachments.test.ts src/session-manager.outbox.test.ts src/group-skills.test.ts` -> 4 files, 49 tests, all passed.
- `vitest run src/session-manager.test.ts src/session-manager.feeds.test.ts src/host-core.test.ts src/delivery.test.ts src/delivery-poll.test.ts` -> 5 files, 75 tests, all passed.
- Full suite (`vitest run`, 312 files): 4232 passed / 22 failed with the fix, against 4208 passed / 40 failed on unmodified `main` in the same sandbox. The 22 failures are a strict subset of the baseline's — all pre-existing environment failures in `scripts/` and `setup/` suites (sqlite CLI wrapper, update/uninstall rollback e2e, gateway detection); the 18 that did not recur are flaky rollback e2e tests. No failure is in or near the touched modules.
- `tsc --noEmit` -> clean. `eslint` on the seven touched files -> 0 errors (10 warnings, the same count as on the unmodified files). `prettier --check` on the touched files -> clean.
- Refusal behavior is unchanged, still covered by the pre-existing tests: symlinked inbox root, symlinked outbox root, symlinked source and destination skills dirs, and the full-path traversal refusals all still warn and skip. In `group-skills.ts` the full-path anchor refusal keeps its own catch and the same log line — it is a warn-and-skip by contract (pinned by the existing tests) and is not an `AnchoredDir` error, so it is resolved before the classified catch.

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Host no longer mistakes disk or permission errors for unsafe paths: an attachment save that fails operationally now fails the inbound write instead of silently dropping the files, and a template-skill copy that fails mid-way now fails the spawn instead of starting with a half-copied skill set.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

The refusal path itself is unchanged: a segment that is a symlink or not a directory is still refused before anything is read, written or deleted through it, and still downgraded to a warning. Only the classification of errors that are not refusals changes — they fail loudly instead of being reported as unsafe paths. No new input surface, no permission or credential change.

## Skill delivery

- [x] Not a skill
- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

prs.title: fix(telegram): escape `$` and keep line breaks in rich messages
prs.body:
**What:** Adapter 4.41.1 (the rc.2 bump) sends agent replies as Telegram rich messages. Any reply with two dollar amounts renders the text between them as a math formula, and bullet lines separated by single newlines merge into one paragraph. This adds `fixTelegramRichText` as the bridge's `transformOutboundText`. It escapes `$` and turns single newlines into hard breaks, skipping code spans, fenced blocks and lines that start a block.

**Why here:** it's a stopgap until the adapter fixes it (vercel/chat#1109). Remove the hook when it does.

**Validation:** unit tests (6 cases). Sent through `sendRichMessage` before and after the fix: before, the prices rendered as a formula; after, they render as plain text.

Targets the `channels` branch, where `src/channels/telegram.ts` lives.

issues.title: web_search: Exa rejects requests because Content-Type is sent twice (exa:InvalidResponse)
issues.body:
## Description

`web_search` with `search_provider: "exa"` fails on every call with `web_search (exa) request failed ...: error.InvalidResponse`, and the agent answers without search results.

The request reaches Exa with two `Content-Type: application/json` headers, and Exa replies:

```
HTTP 400
{"error":"Invalid request body | Validation error: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined","tag":"INVALID_REQUEST_BODY"}
```

The provider sees no `results` array and reports `InvalidResponse`, which hides the 400.

Cause: `exa.zig` (also tavily, firecrawl, perplexity, weixin) passes `Content-Type: application/json` in its headers, and `curlRequestWithProxy` sets its own as well. Both the std.http fallback and the curl path send both.

## Expected behavior

One `Content-Type` per request; Exa searches return results.

## Steps to reproduce

Plain curl shows the same 400:

```sh
echo '{"query":"Binance","numResults":1}' | curl -s -H "x-api-key: $EXA_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @- https://api.exa.ai/search
```

With a single `-H 'Content-Type: ...'` it returns results.

## Version

v2026.5.29; `main` at 5f1cade0 has the same code.

## OS

Linux

prs.title: fix(http): send a single Content-Type when callers pass their own
prs.body:
Closes #1085.

`curlRequestWithProxy` sets `Content-Type` and then appends the caller headers, so the search providers (which pass `Content-Type: application/json` themselves) sent it twice. Exa answers 400 and `web_search` with Exa never works.

The fix skips a caller `Content-Type` when `content_type` is set, in both `httpRequestWithStatusAndHeaders` and `secureCurlRequestWithStatusAndHeaders`. Without `content_type` the caller header still goes out. Done in the http layer rather than in the five callers so it cannot come back.

Validation: `zig fmt --check src/http_util.zig` clean; `zig build test --summary all` 7496 passed / 14 skipped, no leaks (baseline 5f1cade0: 7493 / 14). The two new regression tests fail with `expected 1, found 2` when the fix is reverted. Checked on an aarch64 device: Exa searches work again.

issues.title: [Bug]: server/discover 返回 HTTP 404 + JSON-RPC -32601 被当现代协议硬失败，老协议 MCP 服务器无法回退 legacy 握手
issues.body:
**TL;DR (EN)**
`server/discover` returning **HTTP 404 + JSON-RPC -32601** is hard-failed inside `_negotiate()` as "modern server, unknown method", so the client never falls back to the legacy `initialize` handshake. Legacy-only MCP servers that answer unknown methods with `404 {"code":-32601,"data":"api not found"}` therefore can never connect. Related: #8047 (422), #7728 (500), #7827 (500 empty), #7620/#7627 (401).

---

### 环境

- QwenPaw `2.2.2.post1`（镜像 `agentscope/qwenpaw:latest`，Docker 部署）
- 对端 MCP 服务器：ezBookkeeping `2.1.0`（Go 实现，`POST /mcp`，Bearer token）
- 接入方式：`drivers/mcp/ezbookkeeping.yaml`，`transport: streamable_http`

### 现象

驱动每次启动都构建失败，Agent 拿不到该 MCP 的 7 个工具：

```
WARNING | qwenpaw/drivers/manager.py:159 | Failed to build Driver 'ezbookkeeping':
MCP JSON-RPC error for 'server/discover': code=-32601 message=Method not found
...
File ".../drivers/handlers/mcp_streamable_http.py", line 759, in _negotiate
    raise _discover_rpc_error(exc) from exc
RuntimeError: MCP JSON-RPC error for 'server/discover': code=-32601 message=Method not found
```

10-19 到 10-26 每天启动都失败（同一台机器上的 anki MCP 因为返回 400，能正常回退 legacy，只有这个不行）。

### 对端实际响应（实测，curl/urllib 直打）

```
POST /mcp  {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"server/discover","params":{}}
→ HTTP 404
  {"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32601,"message":"Method not found","data":"api not found"},"id":1}

POST /mcp  {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"probe","version":"1.0"}}}
→ HTTP 200
  {"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{"tools":{"listChanged":false}},
   "serverInfo":{"name":"ezBookkeeping-mcp","title":"ezBookkeeping","version":"2.1.0"}},"id":1}

POST /mcp  {"method":"tools/list"}
→ HTTP 200，返回 7 个工具（add_transaction / query_transactions / query_all_accounts /
  query_all_accounts_balance / query_all_transaction_categories / query_all_transaction_tags /
  query_latest_exchange_rates）
```

也就是说：**这个服务器完全支持老协议，握手能成功、工具能列出**，只是没实现 `server/discover`，并且把"未知方法"按 Web 框架的习惯返回成了 `404 + -32601`。

### 根因（源码定位）

`qwenpaw/drivers/handlers/mcp_streamable_http.py` 的 `_negotiate()`：

```python
if exc.code == _JSONRPC_METHOD_NOT_FOUND:
    # HTTP 404 + -32601 is the modern unknown-method shape.
    if exc.http_status == 404:
        raise _discover_rpc_error(exc) from exc      # ← 直接判死，不回退
    raise _LegacyProtocolError(str(exc)) from exc    # ← 非 404 才回退 legacy
```

而 `_is_legacy_protocol_evidence()` 只有在 `status_code in {400,404,405}` **且不是 -32601 时**才认作旧协议证据（-32601 被单独提前排除）。

问题在于：**老协议的 Web 服务器对"未知方法"最常见的应答恰恰就是 `404 + -32601`**（Spring/Go/gin 的默认路由未命中行为）。把这种组合一律当成"现代服务器不支持该方法"，会让 dual-era 客户端失去它最重要的兼容场景。

### 期望行为

`-32601`（尤其 `data` 里带 `api not found` / `not found` 之类文本时）应当被当作**旧协议证据**，或者至少像 #7627 处理 401 那样——**先回退一次，让 legacy `initialize` 握手去裁决**。modern 服务器真的不支持 discover 时，legacy initialize 一样会失败，代价只是多一次请求，远小于"整类服务器接不进来"。

### 临时绕过（已验证可行，供其他用户参考）

在 MCP 前面加一层极小的垫片，只把 `server/discover` 的 `404` 改写成 `400`，其余请求原样透传，即可触发原有的 legacy 回退：

```python
if jrpc_method == "server/discover" and status == 404:
    status = 400
```

实测日志立刻变成正常：

```
INFO | mcp_streamable_http.py:981 | MCP client 'ezbookkeeping' falling back to legacy: ...
INFO | mcp_stateful_client.py:251  | MCP client connected: ezbookkeeping
```

7 个工具全部可用，`query_all_accounts_balance` 能正常返回 8 个账户余额。（同时给该驱动补了 `policy` 段，否则默认 `default_effect: deny` 会拒绝调用——这点也顺便提一下，新建驱动卡如果不写 policy 就是全拒，容易让人误以为"工具坏了"。）

### 建议

1. `-32601` + `404` 归入 `_LegacyProtocolError`（最小改动，直接修复本 case）；
2. 或者更稳妥：discover 探测出现任何"-32601/未知方法"信号时，都走一次 legacy 回退，由 `initialize` 结果裁决（与 #7627 的思路一致）；
3. 顺带给"新建 MCP 驱动卡不写 policy 就全拒"加个显式提示或默认 `ask`。

感谢维护，QwenPaw 整体体验很好，这是升级到 2.2.x 之后唯一挡住我日常使用的问题。

issues.title: [Bug] Auto-Dream silently drops memory: unusable extract receipt still gets checkpointed, files never retried
issues.body:
## Description

Auto-Dream silently discards a whole day of memory when the extract step cannot parse the agent's reply, and then **checkpoints those files anyway** — so they are never retried. The run still reports `success=True`, and nothing user-visible indicates that the content was dropped.

The affected content never reaches `digest/`, so downstream `memory_search` keeps returning stale older knowledge, and the agent behaves as if the newer facts never existed.

## Environment

- QwenPaw: v2.2.2 (Docker on NAS)
- Memory backend: `remelight` (default)
- Config: `dream_cron_enabled: true`, `dream_cron: "0 23 * * *"`, `auto_memory_interval: 5`
- OS: Linux 5.19.17

## Reproduction / evidence

Real run on 2026-10-28 at 23:00 and 23:05, from the agent log:

```
[DreamExtractStep] agent done has_result=True
[DreamExtractStep] extract attempt 1 returned an unusable receipt; retrying once
[DreamExtractStep] dream extract skipped unusable agent receipt after retry; expected units and topics lists
[DreamExtractStep] parse done keys=(none)
[DreamExtractStep] Extracted 0 unit(s), 0 topic(s) from 9 changed file(s) across 2 day(s)
[DreamIntegrateStep] skip no units
[DreamFinishStep] start changed=9 failed_paths=0 checkpoint=9 ...
[DreamFinishStep] finish success=True checkpointed=9 failed_units=0 errors=0
```

Note `changed=9` but `Extracted 0 unit(s)` yet `checkpoint=9` and `success=True`.

## Root cause

Three pieces combine into a permanent, silent data loss:

1. **Extract failure does not mark files as failed.**
   In `reme/steps/evolve/dream/extract.py` (~L148-160), when the agent reply cannot be parsed into `units` + `topics` lists, after one retry the code deliberately takes a warning-only path instead of raising:

   ```python
   # Keep the warning-only result checkpointable after one retry so a bad source cannot loop forever.
   warning = "dream extract skipped unusable agent receipt after retry; expected units and topics lists"
   state.warnings.append(warning)
   ```

   The anti-infinite-loop intent is reasonable, but `state.failed_paths` is **never populated** on this path.

2. **Finish checkpoints everything not in `failed_paths`.**
   In `reme/steps/evolve/dream/finish.py`:

   ```python
   failed_paths = set(state.failed_paths)
   checkpoint = [p for p in state.changed_paths if p not in failed_paths]
   ```

   Since `failed_paths` is empty, `checkpoint` == all 9 changed files, and their current mtimes are written into the file catalog.

3. **"Changed" is computed by mtime comparison against the catalog.**
   In `extract.py`:

   ```python
   changed = [rel for rel, mt in existing.items() if indexed.get(rel) != mt]
   ```

   Because those 9 files were just cataloged with their current mtimes, every subsequent Dream run sees them as **unchanged** and skips them forever. The content is never retried unless the file itself is modified again.

**Net effect: one unusable model reply permanently drops a day of memory, silently, with `success=True`.**

## Impact

- Whole day of memory never enters `digest/` (in my case: a music-library consolidation and tag-rewrite session).
- `memory_search` continues to return the **older, now-incorrect** digest nodes, so the agent confidently answers with stale facts (observed: it reported a stale path convention and stale playback constraints).
- Not self-healing: this is not a transient failure that the next scheduled run fixes.
- No visibility: the only trace is a `WARNING` line in the log; `response.success` is `True`, and the Inbox push treats it as a successful no-op.

## Suggested fix

1. On the warning-only (unusable receipt) path, also do `state.failed_paths = list(state.changed_paths)` so `DreamFinishStep` does **not** checkpoint them, allowing the next run to retry. A small retry counter / backoff is fine to avoid infinite loops on genuinely unparsable input.
2. Alternatively/additionally: when `len(changed) > 0` and `len(state.units) == 0`, do not report a plain success. Set `success=False` or emit an explicit Inbox warning such as "dream skipped N files: unusable receipt".
3. Consider logging the parse failure with the reply prefix (truncated) so the failure mode (e.g. model returned prose instead of a JSON receipt) is diagnosable.

## Additional context

Same "false success" family as #8184 (cron records false success after gate termination) and related to #6116 (doom loop / missing budget gates), but the root cause here is distinct: **parse failure → warning-only path → full checkpoint → permanent skip**.

Happy to test a patch in my deployment (v2.2.2, 29 cron jobs, daily Dream runs) and report back.

issues.title: [Bug] Doom-loop gate kills legitimate task-authorized polling; cron records false success after termination
issues.body:
## Description

The doom-loop gate terminated a **legitimate, task-authorized polling pattern** while the awaited background task was genuinely progressing. The gate cannot distinguish "agent stuck repeating itself" from "agent waiting for a long-running background task exactly as its task instructions require".

Additionally, the cron scheduler recorded `last_status: "success"` for the killed run — the termination is invisible to operators.

## Reproduction (real production case, 2026-10-12 08:00 Asia/Shanghai)

A daily cron job (`6e7d12f7`, 08:00, agent-type) runs a ~12-minute report script in the background (`nohup ... &`), then polls for a completion marker (`---CHARTS---` in an output file) every 30 seconds, exactly as the job's task text instructs.

Observed sequence (from `history.db` of session `5ff775cf`, seq 33987–33994):

1. Agent issues, four times in a row, the **identical** tool call:
   `sleep 30 && (ps -p 18280 > /dev/null && echo "PID 18280 存活" || echo "PID 18280 已退出") && tail -c 300 /tmp/morning_output.txt`
2. Each result was byte-identical and showed **real external progress**: the background script advanced from "连接数据库..." to "腾讯新闻 AI 详摘 42 条" between polls.
3. After the 4th identical call the gate fired: `Doom loop: agent stuck after 4 consecutive repetitions` and killed the session at 08:02:38.
4. The background script (PID 18280) was completely healthy and finished on its own at ~08:12. Nothing was stuck — only the *waiting pattern* matched the repetition heuristic.
5. `qwenpaw cron state 6e7d12f7` afterwards: `{"last_run_at": "2026-10-12T08:02:38+08:00", "last_status": "success", "last_error": null}` — a killed run reported as success. The failure only became visible by manually inspecting session files.

## Root cause discussion

The repetition gate compares tool calls for similarity (and after PRs #7919/#7906, requires new evidence to escalate — good). What it still ignores:

1. **Intent context**: the repeated call is explicitly instructed by the task text ("poll every 30 seconds until marker X appears"). Within a cron/agent task, periodic `sleep + check` is a *waiting* idiom, not a stuck loop.
2. **External progress**: the awaited world state (log file content, process liveness) *was* changing between calls. A stuck loop has static observed state; a poll has evolving observed state.
3. **Inter-call spacing**: 30s between identical calls is not the tight-fire behavior the gate was designed for (sub-second or back-to-back regeneration).

The combined effect: any task instruction that says "wait for a background job by polling" is a guaranteed gate trip after N polls, and the operator gets a false success.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Recognize wait/poll morphology** (e.g. `sleep N && check-same-target`, or same tool+args with N-second spacing): exclude from repetition accounting, or place in a separate slower-escalation track, while the awaited condition (marker file / process) can still change.
2. **State-change awareness**: if the observed environment between identical calls changed (file grew, process still alive, log advanced), treat as polling-with-progress, not repetition.
3. **First-class wait primitive**: a `wait_for`-style tool (wait for file marker / process exit / condition, with timeout) removes the need for agents to hand-roll polling loops entirely.
4. **Cron truthfulness**: when a run is terminated by the doom-loop gate (or any loop gate), record it distinctly — e.g. `last_status: "terminated"` with `last_error` naming the gate — instead of `success`.

Longer term, a `script`-type cron task (see our feature request #4963 — direct shell execution without agent inference) would structurally eliminate this class: no agent in the loop means no polling loop to misclassify.

## Related

- #6116 — original doom-loop report (closed as wontfix; today's case is a *different* failure mode: authorized polling, not model repetition)
- #4963 — feature request: script-type cron tasks (structural avoidance)
- #7919 / #7906 — doom-loop gate accounting fixes (merged; today's case survives them)
- #7420 — different mechanism (runtime re-dispatch after `write_file`)

## Environment

- QwenPaw: 2.2.1 (Docker, Linux x86_64)
- Channel: Feishu; session `5ff775cf`; cron job `6e7d12f7` (daily 08:00 Asia/Shanghai, agent type, runtime timeout 1800s)
- Models routed via self-hosted gateway (free-pool small models on this job)
- We mitigated on our side by rewriting the task text to use a single blocking wait command instead of repeated polling; the gate/cron behaviors above remain unfixed framework-side.

---
*Tooling disclosure (per #4333): this report was prepared with AI assistance under human direction. All timestamps, commands, and state outputs come from a real live deployment.*

issues.title: [Bug] Feishu channel fails with 426 Upgrade Required when HTTP(S)_PROXY is injected without NO_PROXY for feishu.cn
issues.body:
## Summary

When QwenPaw runs in an environment where `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` are injected but `NO_PROXY` does **not** include `feishu.cn`, the Feishu channel cannot connect at all:

- The WebSocket long-connection thread fails repeatedly
- Outbound `tenant_access_token` requests fail
- Every HTTP call to `open.feishu.cn` returns `426 Upgrade Required` from the proxy

## Environment

- QwenPaw 2.1.0 (installed package), Python 3.11
- Containerized Linux deployment
- `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` (and lowercase variants) injected into the process environment
- `NO_PROXY` does not contain `feishu.cn`

## Symptoms

`app.err.log` fills with:

```
urllib3.exceptions.MaxRetryError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='open.feishu.cn', port=443):
Max retries exceeded with url: /callback/ws/endpoint
(Caused by ProxyError('Unable to connect to proxy', OSError('Tunnel connection failed: 426 Upgrade Required')))

requests.exceptions.ProxyError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='open.feishu.cn', port=443): ...
```

Counters over roughly one day: `ProxyError` 14,570 / `426 Upgrade Required` 14,561 / `feishu WebSocket thread failed` 3,647.

The process itself looks healthy (`/api/version` returns 200), so the failure is silent from a monitoring standpoint.

## Root cause

`lark_oapi` uses `requests` internally, and `requests` honours `HTTP(S)_PROXY` / `NO_PROXY` from the environment. Two calls are affected:

1. `POST https://open.feishu.cn/callback/ws/endpoint` — WS endpoint negotiation
2. `POST https://open.feishu.cn/open-apis/auth/v3/tenant_access_token/internal`

Note that `lark_oapi`'s WebSocket transport already passes `proxy=None` when building the connection (`_ws_connect_kwargs()`), so the WS socket itself bypasses the proxy — but the HTTP calls that precede it do not.

QwenPaw's own client is also proxy-aware by default, in `app/channels/feishu/channel.py`:

```python
self._http_client = httpx.AsyncClient(
    timeout=30.0,
)                                   # trust_env defaults to True

self._client = (
    lark.Client.builder()
    .app_id(self.app_id)
    .app_secret(self.app_secret)
    .domain(sdk_domain)
    ...
    .build()
)
```

## Suggested fixes

1. Build the Feishu-bound httpx client with `trust_env=False` (or explicit `proxies=None`):
   ```python
   self._http_client = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=30.0, trust_env=False)
   ```
2. For the `lark_oapi` client, propagate a proxy/`NO_PROXY` setting if the SDK supports it; otherwise document that `NO_PROXY` must include `.feishu.cn`.
3. Document required `NO_PROXY` entries (`feishu.cn`, `.feishu.cn`, `larksuite.com`) for containerized deployments behind a proxy.
4. Optionally add a config switch such as `channels.feishu.bypass_env_proxy` (default `true`), so a misconfigured platform proxy does not silently kill the channel.

## Workaround

Adding `.feishu.cn` to `NO_PROXY` in the process environment fixes both the WS connection and outbound messages (verified by exporting `no_proxy` / `NO_PROXY` in the supervisor command that launches the app).

## Additional suggestion

A startup health check that probes `open.feishu.cn` and logs a clear, actionable error would make this much easier to diagnose — currently the channel simply stays silent while the error log fills up.

issues.title: Feishu channel: intermittent `ProviderError: No active model configured` when a new message arrives while the agent is still processing the previous one
issues.body:
### Environment
- QwenPaw Desktop: v2.3.0-beta.1 (also reproduced on v2.2.2 - NOT introduced by the beta)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro 64-bit
- Channel: Feishu (channel message -> feishu:sw:<session>)

### Symptoms
- Intermittent "Internal error" shown in the Feishu chat when the user sends a new message while the agent is still processing the previous one in the SAME session.
- Retrying the same message succeeds immediately - no data loss, but frequent enough to be disruptive.
- Backend log (both versions):

```
ERROR | qwenpaw/runtime/runtime.py:193 | runtime: unhandled error session=...: No active model configured
qwenpaw.exceptions.ProviderError: No active model configured
ERROR | qwenpaw/app/channels/base.py:1038 | channel _stream_with_tracker failed: No active model configured, session=feishu:sw:..., agent=...
```

### Evidence that it is a concurrency race, not a config loss
- `active_model` is present the whole time (agent.json `active_model=kexin_token/glm-5.3-flash`; provider registry intact, 41 providers, all enabled).
- Timeline strictly correlates with concurrent sends: e.g. 18:24:33 fail -> 18:25:34 success; 18:25:49/18:25:53/18:26:02/18:26:15 four consecutive fails -> 18:26:21 success. Every failed attempt coincides with the previous message still being processed.
- Occurrence counts: 4 errors on 10-29 23:57 (still on v2.2.2, before upgrade), 28 errors 18:24-18:27, 1 error 19:19:11 (on v2.3.0-beta.1).
- Network/model API verified healthy at failure time (model API reachable in 0.04-0.12s) - rules out connectivity.

### Root cause (speculation)
When a new message arrives while the session's previous run is still active, the message handler builds the request before the model/session state is (re)bound, so it fails with "No active model configured" instead of being queued.

### Expected behavior
- Same-session concurrent messages should be queued (serialized) rather than rejected, or
- Fail with a clear, retryable "session busy" error instead of `ProviderError: No active model configured`.

### Suggested fix direction
Queue incoming channel messages per session while busy (or acquire the session lock before reading active model config).

issues.title: [Bug]: Hub Docker runtime fails to start with Permission denied on working/config.json when Hub runs as non-root
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

The deployed package version and Docker image tag/digest were not captured in the available report.

Source analysis below was checked against upstream commit [c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/commit/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df). This is the reviewed source revision, not a claim that the affected server runs that exact revision.

## Description

A QwenPaw Hub running as a regular Ubuntu user starts successfully, but starting an existing personal Docker runtime fails with:

```text
[Errno 13] Permission denied: '/data/qwenpaw/hub/runtimes/<runtime-id>/working/config.json'
```

The observed failure is a host-side access failure on a runtime's shared configuration. Source review suggests an ownership mismatch between the non-root Hub and the root application in the Docker image. Actual file ownership/mode and Docker user-namespace settings on the affected server have not yet been collected, so this cause still needs runtime verification.

**Security considerations:** A fix should preserve restrictive configuration/secret permissions and avoid requiring the Hub itself to run as root.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (Hub runtime lifecycle, configuration persistence)
- [x] Scripts / Deploy (Docker entrypoint and Supervisor)

## Environment

- **OS:** Ubuntu server; release not captured
- **Hub process user:** Non-root user `ubuntu`
- **Python:** 3.12, according to the installed-package log path
- **Install method:** Hub runs from a Python environment on the host; managed runtime uses the Docker backend
- **Docker image tag/digest, Engine version, rootless/userns mode:** Not captured

## Steps to Reproduce

Observed trigger:

1. Run the Hub as the regular `ubuntu` user with an existing personal Docker runtime.
2. Start the Hub with:

   ```bash
   qwenpaw hub \
     --host 0.0.0.0 \
     --port 8080 \
     --force-public \
     --config hub.yaml
   ```

3. A runtime start operation fails while accessing that runtime's `working/config.json`.

Suggested focused reproduction to verify the suspected cause (not yet independently executed):

1. Use a non-root Hub with a standard Linux Docker Engine and the current runtime image.
2. Initialize a Docker runtime, then cause the container application to save configuration in the bind-mounted working directory.
3. Record ownership and mode of `config.json` and `workspaces/*/agent.json`, then stop/start the runtime.
4. Check whether host-side configuration preparation fails after the container has written root-owned, owner-only files.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** The Hub HTTP server starts, but the personal runtime start operation fails with `EACCES` on its shared configuration.
- **Expected:** Runtime initialization and later configuration writes remain accessible to the Hub across runtime and Hub restarts, while keeping sensitive files private.

## Logs / Screenshots

Relevant output from the affected Ubuntu host; the runtime ID has been redacted:

```text
INFO:     Application startup complete.
INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:8080 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
WARNING lib/python3.12/site-packages/qwenpaw/hub/service.py:531 | 2026-10-30 20:37:56 | Runtime <runtime-id> start operation failed: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/data/qwenpaw/hub/runtimes/<runtime-id>/working/config.json'
```

## Additional Notes

### Source evidence and suspected failure mechanism

All links below refer to the same upstream revision, `c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df`:

- [DockerRuntimeProvisioner.start](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df/src/qwenpaw/hub/docker_provisioner.py#L219-L245) creates read/write bind mounts for working, secrets, and backups without specifying a container user.
- [entrypoint.sh](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df/deploy/entrypoint.sh) runs `qwenpaw init` before starting Supervisor, without dropping privileges.
- [Supervisor configuration](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df/deploy/config/supervisord.conf.template) sets `[supervisord] user=root`; the application has no separate `user=`.
- [RuntimeService._start_locked](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df/src/qwenpaw/hub/service.py#L266-L270) calls `prepare_workspace_paths` before `provisioner.start`.
- [prepare_workspace_paths](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df/src/qwenpaw/hub/runtime_paths.py#L58-L68) reads `config.json` and workspace `agent.json` files on the host.
- [write_text_atomic](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df/src/qwenpaw/utils/io_utils.py#L280-L320) defaults new internal files to `0600` and uses a sibling temporary file plus `os.replace`. Existing permission bits are preserved, but ownership is not explicitly preserved. A root writer can therefore replace a Hub-owned configuration with a root-owned inode.

### Possible fix direction

Align the host-visible identity used for runtime initialization and subsequent application writes with the Hub's shared-data access requirements.

Simply adding a hard-coded `user="1000:1000"` to the provisioner is insufficient for the current image: Supervisor configuration generation, logs/PID/socket paths, system D-Bus, and desktop processes also need appropriate handling. A smaller approach could retain a privileged bootstrap/Supervisor while dropping initialization and application processes to the intended identity, with explicit HOME/environment setup.

Rootless Docker, userns-remap, and Docker Desktop require platform-aware identity handling rather than blindly copying the host UID/GID.

Existing root-owned data also needs a controlled one-time ownership migration while the affected runtime is stopped. Changing the image alone will not repair a file the Hub cannot read before container startup.

### Workaround and validation status

A targeted ownership repair on the affected instance has been suggested, but success has not yet been confirmed. No deployed code fix or independent reproduction is claimed here.

Useful regression coverage would include first initialization, subsequent application configuration writes, runtime stop/start, Hub restart, and continued Hub access to configuration without weakening file permissions.

### Duplicate search

Searched open and closed issues for Hub/config.json permission failures, Docker permissions, UID, and Hub root ownership. #7612 concerns CLI authentication inside local sandboxes and appears to be a different issue.

issues.title: [Feature]: Display per-reply latency in the Console chat UI
issues.body:
# Feature request: display per-reply latency in the Console chat UI

## Problem

QwenPaw has no built-in way to see how long a reply took.

What exists today:

- **Console → Settings → Token 消耗**: token totals by date and model (no timing).
- **`/history`**: message list + token statistics (no timing).
- **TUI status bar**: agent, model, session id, live token counters, busy/ready (no timing).
- **Console chat**: message bubbles with collapsible thinking / tool-call panels (no timing).

The only latency instrumentation shipped with QwenPaw is the `Tracing Middleware`
demo plugin (`plugins/middleware-demo/tracing-middleware/`), which measures
**tool call** duration and writes to a file. It does not measure the reply
itself, does not surface anything in the UI, and requires installing a plugin
plus setting `QWENPAW_TRACE`.

For users, "how long did that take?" is a basic question when tuning prompts,
choosing models, or debugging a slow agent. Today the only answer is reading
server logs or writing a plugin.

## Proposal

Add an optional per-message latency indicator to the Console chat UI.

### 1. Per-message timing

Show the elapsed time for each assistant reply, e.g. below the message bubble:

```
⏱ 12.4s · 3 model calls · 2 tool calls
```

Suggested placement: a small, muted line under the assistant message, aligned
with the existing metadata row (model name / token count, if any).

### 2. Breakdown on hover / expand

Optionally expose a breakdown so the user can tell *what* was slow:

| Phase | Time |
|---|---|
| Model call 1 | 8.1s |
| Tool: read_file | 41ms |
| Model call 2 | 4.2s |

This distinction matters: in practice most of the wall-clock time is model
generation, and tool time is usually negligible. A single total hides that.

### 3. Configurable display

A toggle in **Settings → 运行配置** (or Console settings), e.g.:

- `显示回复耗时`: off / on
- maybe `显示耗时明细` (breakdown): off / on

Default: **off**, so existing users see no UI change.

### 4. Where the timing should come from

AgentScope already emits the events needed to compute this:

- `ReplyStartEvent` / `ReplyEndEvent` — reply boundaries (`reply_id`).
- `ModelCallStartEvent` / `ModelCallEndEvent` — per-model-call boundaries, and
  `ModelCallEndEvent` already carries `input_tokens` / `output_tokens`.
- `ToolCallStartEvent` / `ToolResultEndEvent` — per-tool boundaries.

So the backend work is mostly plumbing these into the existing console event
stream that the frontend already consumes, rather than new instrumentation.

## Alternative / interim solution

If a full UI feature is too large, exposing the same data through the existing
plugin API would already unblock users. A `on_reply` / `on_model_call` /
`on_acting` middleware can measure all three levels — I have a working
implementation (~150 lines, `AgentScope` `MiddlewareBase` subclass) that writes
JSONL to `<workspace>/.qwenpaw/timing/timing.jsonl`. Happy to contribute it as
an official example plugin (`plugins/middleware-demo/agent-timing/`) if that is
easier to accept, or to upstream it if the maintainers prefer a first-class
feature.

## Environment

- QwenPaw v2.2.2.post1
- Checked: Console chat UI, `/history`, TUI status bar, Settings → Token 消耗
- Official docs consulted: `console`, `tui`, `commands`, `plugins`

## Notes

- The per-reply time should be measured server-side. The frontend already
  receives streaming events with `reply_id`, so the timestamp can be attached
  to the events and never depend on client clock.
- `on_model_call` returns an **async generator** for streaming models, so any
  implementation must time the full stream consumption, not just the call to
  the model. (Getting this wrong under-reports model time by ~1000×.)

issues.title: [Bug]: /api/console/chat SSE missing X-Accel-Buffering: no — first event buffered behind nginx reverse proxy

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
# [Bug] /api/console/chat SSE missing X-Accel-Buffering: no — first event buffered behind nginx reverse proxy

---

## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2.post1 (pip). Same behavior on 2.2.2.

## Description

When QwenPaw is deployed behind an nginx reverse proxy (default `proxy_buffering on`), the `/api/console/chat` SSE stream is buffered: the first SSE event is not forwarded to the browser until the nginx buffer fills or the model emits its first token. As a result, in the Console UI the "accepted / start of reply" state only appears **after the first token arrives**, instead of immediately. Direct access (no proxy) is unaffected — the stream arrives immediately.

Root cause: `/api/console/chat` SSE responses (`src/qwenpaw/app/routers/console.py`) do **not** set `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, while every other SSE endpoint does (`backup.py`, `portability_imports.py`, `project_directory.py`, `skills_stream.py`, `workspace.py`). nginx therefore buffers only this stream.

Suggested fix: add `"X-Accel-Buffering": "no"` to the two SSE `headers` in `console.py` (consistent with the other endpoints), and/or document that reverse proxies need `proxy_buffering off` / `X-Accel-Buffering: no`.

**Related PR(s):** #6843 (middleware SSE buffering — different layer)

**Security considerations:** None.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI) — symptom surfaces here; root cause is in the backend router

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2.post1
- **OS:** Linux (Debian-based, fnOS), x86_64
- **Install method:** pip
- **Python version (if applicable):** 3.12

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install QwenPaw (pip) and put it behind an nginx reverse proxy with default `proxy_buffering on` (`proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:<port>`).
2. Open Console through the proxied URL and send any message.
3. Observe the assistant bubble stays empty; "accepted / start of reply" only appears after the first token is generated.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** Through nginx, the first SSE event is delayed until the buffer fills / the first token is emitted.
- **Expected:** The first SSE event is forwarded immediately, like direct (non-proxied) access.

## Logs / Screenshots

No errors on the server; events arrive normally — only the proxy holds the first event. Timing measurements:

```
Direct  GET /api/version :  TTFB ≈ 0.002 s
Via     GET /api/version :  TTFB ≈ 0.55 s / 0.81 s / 1.20 s   (default proxy_buffering on)
Direct  GET /api/workspace/watch (SSE, already sends X-Accel-Buffering: no): first event = 0.011 s
```

## Additional Notes

- Workaround (verified on 2.2.2.post1): set `proxy_buffering off;` on the `/api/console/chat` location in nginx.
- Related: #6820 (same symptom), #6843 (middleware buffering — different layer; Starlette 1.9.0's `BaseHTTPMiddleware` uses a rendezvous stream and no longer buffers), #7642 (Chrome-specific frontend issue).
- Suggested code fix: `headers={ ..., "X-Accel-Buffering": "no" }` in both SSE `StreamingResponse`s in `console.py`.

---

# [Bug] /api/console/chat 的 SSE 缺少 X-Accel-Buffering: no，经 nginx 反代时首事件被缓冲

## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2.post1（pip）。2.2.2 表现相同。

## Description

QwenPaw 部署在 nginx 反向代理后（默认 `proxy_buffering on`）时，`/api/console/chat` 的 SSE 流会被缓冲：首个 SSE 事件要等 nginx 缓冲区满或模型吐出第一个 token 才转发到浏览器。结果在 Console UI 里，要**等首个 token 到达**才显示「已接受/开始回复」，而非立即。直连（不经反代）不受影响，流会立即到达。

根因：`/api/console/chat` 的 SSE 响应（`src/qwenpaw/app/routers/console.py`）**没有**设置 `X-Accel-Buffering: no`，而其他所有 SSE 端点都设置了（`backup.py`、`portability_imports.py`、`project_directory.py`、`skills_stream.py`、`workspace.py`）。因此 nginx 只缓冲了这一个流。

建议修复：给 `console.py` 两处 SSE `headers` 补上 `"X-Accel-Buffering": "no"`（与其他端点一致）；和/或在部署文档注明反代需 `proxy_buffering off` / `X-Accel-Buffering: no`。

**Related PR(s):** #6843（中间件 SSE 缓冲——不同层）

**Security considerations:** 无。

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI) — 现象在此呈现，根因在后端路由

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2.post1
- **OS:** Linux（Debian 系，fnOS），x86_64
- **Install method:** pip
- **Python version (if applicable):** 3.12

## Steps to Reproduce

1. 用 pip 安装 QwenPaw，置于 nginx 反代之后（默认 `proxy_buffering on`，`proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:<port>`）。
2. 通过反代地址打开 Console，发送任意消息。
3. 观察气泡长时间空白；「已接受/开始回复」要等首个 token 生成后才出现。

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** 经 nginx 时，首个 SSE 事件延迟到缓冲区满/首个 token 才转发。
- **Expected:** 首个 SSE 事件立即转发，与直连（不经反代）一致。

## Logs / Screenshots

服务端无报错，事件正常到达，仅代理憋住了首事件。计时测量：

```
直连  GET /api/version :  TTFB ≈ 0.002 秒
反代  GET /api/version :  TTFB ≈ 0.55 秒 / 0.81 秒 / 1.20 秒   （默认 proxy_buffering on）
直连  GET /api/workspace/watch（SSE，自带 X-Accel-Buffering: no）：首事件 0.011 秒
```

## Additional Notes

- 已验证的 workaround（2.2.2.post1）：在 nginx 的 `/api/console/chat` location 配 `proxy_buffering off;`。
- 相关：#6820（相同症状）、#6843（中间件缓冲——不同层；Starlette 1.9.0 的 `BaseHTTPMiddleware` 使用会合通道流，已不再缓冲）、#7642（Chrome 特有前端问题）。
- 建议代码修复：在 `console.py` 两处 SSE `StreamingResponse` 的 `headers` 加 `"X-Accel-Buffering": "no"`。

Fixes #8516

prs.title: fix(providers): bound inline media per request, not just per file
prs.body:
## Summary

The per-file inline cap (`MAX_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES`, 2 MB) does not bound the
**request body**. Media counts ~0 tokens, so token-based context eviction
never fires, and a session that accumulates many *in-spec* images keeps
sending a multi-megabyte body on every turn. Once a gateway's byte limit
answers 413 the session is unusable until the history is stripped by hand.

This adds a cumulative inline-media budget to the shared capping
formatters, so the request body is bounded independently of tokens.

Refs #7671

## What Problem This Solves

The reporter's incident: a design-review session accumulated ~20 MB of
inline base64 screenshots — every one *under* the 2 MB per-file cap — and
every subsequent turn failed with provider 413 until the session JSON was
surgically stripped. A 2,979,813-byte PNG also became
`[Image unavailable: ... exceeds the 2097152-byte image limit.]`, i.e. an
image marginally over the line was dropped even though a slightly smaller
version would have been fine.

PR #7965 fixed the Scroll-side half (reclaim historical media, fold media
into the existing compression flow) and explicitly listed this as remaining:

> **Out of scope / TODO** — HTTP request-body limits: accumulated media can
> still exceed a gateway's byte limit without exceeding the token threshold.

This PR closes that TODO.

## Changes

`src/qwenpaw/providers/capping_formatter.py`:

- New `max_total_bytes` field (default `MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` = 8 MB
  = 4× the per-file cap; `0` disables it, restoring per-file-only behaviour).
  The field is **derived from the instance's per-file cap** when it is not
  set explicitly: `max(8 MiB, 4 × max_bytes)`. A raised per-file cap is
  therefore no longer undercut by a fixed total — with a 16 MiB per-file cap
  a 10 MiB file reaches the wire instead of being dropped by the total — and
  a lowered per-file cap never tightens the total below the 8 MiB default.
  An explicitly configured `max_total_bytes` always wins.
- The budget is spent in two passes. A **measuring** pass records the size of
  every media block in wire order; only when the measured total exceeds the
  budget does an **enforcing** pass run, replacing the oldest media (a byte
  prefix of the wire order) with placeholders. The newest media is what the
  request keeps.
- `_cap_media` runs the per-file cap first, so a file that is already a
  placeholder is never charged to the budget.
- `inline_media_size()` also sizes inline `data:` URLs, and the OpenAI Chat /
  Responses formatters route PDF attachments through `_format_file_source()`,
  so `data:` URLs and PDFs count toward the budget like any other media.
- The per-request media **dedup scope** lives next to the budget policy
  (`SEEN_MEDIA_KEYS`) and is reset between the measuring and the enforcing
  pass — both passes have to observe the same media, otherwise the enforcing
  pass sees every source as "already shown above" and drops all media,
  including the newest one the budget keeps.

`src/qwenpaw/agents/model_factory.py`:

- The Anthropic formatter now only remembers a media source as *seen* once it
  has actually reached the wire. A source the budget dropped is not part of
  the request, so a later copy of it stays eligible: with **A → B → A**
  (512 bytes each, 900-byte budget) the request keeps the newest **A**
  instead of folding it as "already shown above" while the dropped copy is
  nowhere in the request.
- A folded duplicate still occupies a slot in the wire order, but it is never
  sent, so it costs the budget nothing: the plan drops oldest occurrences only
  until the *deduplicated* payload — the distinct sources that actually reach
  the wire — fits the budget, and a folded copy is re-inlined when the budget
  dropped every earlier copy of its source (so A → B → A still keeps the
  newest A).
- **Video is bounded by the budget too.** Video never reaches a media hook:
  Anthropic routes it through `_format_anthropic_video_data_block`, and the
  OpenAI Chat / Responses / DashScope paths substitute it into the request
  around the formatter's `format()` call. The Anthropic path now caps the
  video before formatting it, and the OpenAI-family paths *mark* the video
  block (its `name` becomes the substitution placeholder) instead of
  replacing it, so the formatter's media hook still sees it and the budget
  can account for it at its own position in the wire order. A marked block is
  rendered as the substitution placeholder and resolved to the video wire
  dict afterwards, exactly as before. Assistant-role video is unaffected (it
  was never substituted and still is not).

Because formatting walks the conversation oldest-first, spending the budget
as it is spent **keeps the newest media and drops the oldest** — the
direction the issue asks for.

A `ContextVar` rather than instance state, because formatter instances are
shared across concurrent requests and a running total on the instance would
let one session spend another's allowance
(`test_concurrent_requests_do_not_share_a_budget` pins this).

Placeholder wording distinguishes the two causes, and every provider shape
is preserved: Chat Completions / Anthropic / DashScope `{"type":"text"}`,
Gemini `{"text"}`, Responses API `{"type":"input_text"}`.

## Evidence

```
$ pytest tests/unit/providers/test_capping_formatter.py -q
77 passed
```

`TestCumulativeBudgetEndToEnd` drives the **real** formatters (OpenAI,
Anthropic, Gemini, DashScope, and the Responses formatter) over a
three-image conversation with a budget that fits only one:

```
[media omitted from model context: this request already inlines 513 bytes
 of media, exceeds the 900-byte per-request limit]     <- oldest, dropped
[media omitted from model context: ... 900-byte ...]   <- middle, dropped
{"inline_data": {...}}                                 <- newest, inlined
```

`TestCumulativeBudgetThroughProductionWrapper` drives the same scenario
through the production formatter wrapper, and
`TestRepeatedMediaSurvivesTheBudget` pins the repeated-source case through
the Anthropic wrapper, the same case with the newest copy arriving in a tool
result, and the OpenAI Chat / Responses paths:

```
A (512 B) -> B (512 B) -> A (512 B), 900-byte budget
  before:  A dropped by the budget, B inlined, newest A folded as
           "[Image omitted - already shown above]"
  after:   A dropped by the budget, B dropped by the budget,
           newest A inlined
```

The two Anthropic cases fail without the fix (verified by reverting the
`model_factory.py` change):

```
FAILED TestRepeatedMediaSurvivesTheBudget::test_anthropic_wrapper_keeps_the_newest_repeated_media
FAILED TestRepeatedMediaSurvivesTheBudget::test_anthropic_wrapper_keeps_the_newest_repeated_tool_media
2 failed, 62 passed
```

`TestVideoUnderThePerRequestBudget` pins the video case on all five provider
paths through the production wrapper (three 312-byte `video/mp4` blocks, a
900-byte budget → two videos inlined, one dropped):

```
$ pytest tests/unit/providers/test_capping_formatter.py -q -k TestVideoUnderThePerRequestBudget
9 passed
```

Wider runs — no regressions. The failure below is pre-existing in this
environment (a file-permission assertion that depends on the process umask)
and is identical on the unmodified head commit:

```
$ pytest tests/unit/providers tests/unit/agents -q
# this branch:        1 failed, 5108 passed, 3 skipped
# unmodified head:    1 failed, 5098 passed, 3 skipped   (+10 = the new tests)

$ pytest tests/unit -q
# this branch:        4 failed, 18629 passed, 25 skipped
# unmodified head:    the same 4 failures (file mode, docker, sandbox paths)

$ black --line-length=79 / flake8 / pylint (10.00) / mypy   # clean
```

### The 8 MiB budget is raw media, not wire bytes

`MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` counts the **decoded** media bytes; base64
encoding expands them by 4/3 on the wire. An 8 MiB raw budget therefore
becomes roughly **10.7 MiB** of base64 in the request body — still above the
**6 MiB** limit of the `dash_anthropic` gateway. To stay inside that gateway
the raw budget has to stay at or below ~4.5 MiB (6 MiB x 3/4).

This is deliberate: the budget bounds the *media a request carries*, in the
same unit as the per-file cap and the file sizes reported to the user. The
alternative — budgeting encoded bytes — would mean the limit no longer
matches the number a user sees for a file, and it would still not track the
provider's own overhead on top of the media.

The default is therefore a bound on the request body, not a guarantee that
every gateway accepts it: deployments behind a 6 MiB gateway should lower
`MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` (or set `max_total_bytes` explicitly on the
model) to match their gateway limit.

## Notes for review

- **The default changes behaviour**: a request that used to inline ~20 MB of
  media now inlines 8 MB and placeholders the rest. If you would rather this
  be opt-in, set `MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES = 0` and I will drop the
  default; the plumbing and tests are unaffected.
- The per-request budget now covers **video** as well, on all five provider
  paths. One path is still outside it: the OpenAI-family / Gemini
  **tool-result video promotion** (`_promote_tool_result_videos`) injects the
  video after formatting, so it is capped per file but not per request. The
  Anthropic tool-result video goes through the media hook and is covered.
  Covering the promotion would mean moving it inside the budget's scope —
  worth a follow-up if you want one budget for both paths.
- The issue's other asks (auto-downscale an oversized attachment instead of
  dropping it, and making the cap configurable per provider) are not
  included; the cap is already a provider field, so only the downscale is
  new work.

prs.title: feat(providers): let custom gateways declare OpenAI prompt cache params
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #8058.

Since #7899, request parameters pass through `cache_request()` in
`providers/adapters/cache_policy.py`, which rejects
`prompt_cache_key` / `prompt_cache_retention` unless the provider's cache
capabilities include `openai` / `openai_explicit`.
`OpenAIProvider.cache_capabilities()` only returns those modes for
`api.openai.com`, so a custom provider pointing at an OpenAI-compatible
Responses gateway fails **before sending anything** with
`ValueError: Unsupported cache control: prompt_cache_key` — including when the
key is only in `extra_body`, which `cache_request()` lifts out and re-validates.

Users had no way to declare the capability: `cache_modes` is a class
attribute, so `"cache_modes": ["openai"]` in the provider JSON is ignored and
dropped on the next save. Losing `prompt_cache_key` measurably lowers cache
hit rates on long agent sessions that share a prefix.

## Change

New persisted provider field (backend-only, default off):

```json
"supports_openai_prompt_cache": true
```

`OpenAIProvider.cache_capabilities()` now opens **only** the explicit prompt
cache parameters for a non-`api.openai.com` base URL when this flag is set —
i.e. it adds the `openai` mode, which is exactly what gates
`prompt_cache_key` / `prompt_cache_retention` in `cache_policy.py`.

Deliberately still gated (`openai_explicit` is not granted): `prompt_cache_options`,
`enable_prompt_cache_breakpoint` and `cache_control` keep raising, so the opt-in
cannot be used to unlock TTL/breakpoint controls that a host model may not have.

Why a config flag instead of forwarding unconditionally for custom providers
(the issue's option 2): the wire-level gate is intentionally fail-closed for
unverified services, and this keeps it that way while giving operators a
declared, reviewable escape hatch. Because it is a real pydantic field, it is
no longer discarded on save (the `cache_modes` class attribute was), and
`update_config()` only touches keys present in the request, so console-driven
provider updates do not clobber it.

## Evidence

- `tests/unit/providers/test_openai_provider.py`:
  - `test_custom_gateway_rejects_prompt_cache_key_by_default` — the issue's
    minimal repro (both `prompt_cache_key` in kwargs and in `extra_body`)
    still raises before this flag is set.
  - `test_declared_capability_forwards_prompt_cache_parameters` — with the
    flag, both forms forward a single `prompt_cache_key`, and
    `prompt_cache_retention` too.
  - `test_declaration_does_not_unlock_explicit_cache_controls` —
    `prompt_cache_options` and `enable_prompt_cache_breakpoint` still raise.
  - `test_official_host_capabilities_are_unaffected` — `api.openai.com`
    routing is unchanged, `gpt-5.6` still gets `openai_explicit`.
- `tests/unit/providers/test_provider_manager.py`:
  - `test_custom_provider_prompt_cache_declaration_from_json` — a custom
    provider JSON with the flag loads through `_init_from_storage`, exposes the
    capability, and `prepare_request()` forwards the key end to end.
  - `test_custom_provider_without_declaration_keeps_gate_closed` — a legacy
    custom JSON (no key) still rejects, so upgrades change no behavior.
- Full runs: `pytest tests/unit/providers/` → 895 passed.
- Lint: `add-trailing-comma` before `black --line-length=79`, `flake8` clean;
  `pylint` 8.49/10 with only pre-existing message categories (f-string style,
  module length) — nothing new beyond the two that already fire on `main`.

prs.title: fix(token-usage): count Anthropic cache tokens in the live context meter
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #8057.

For Anthropic Messages providers, `usage.input_tokens` counts only the
uncached part of the prompt; cache reads (`cache_read_input_tokens`) and
cache writes (`cache_creation_input_tokens`) are reported separately. On a
long cached turn An example from the issue: `input_tokens=3000`,
`cache_read=120000`, `cache_write=5000` on a 200k window showed as 3k/200k
(1.5%) in the console context meter instead of 128k/200k (64%).

`TokenRecordingModelWrapper._record_usage()` set `last_prompt_tokens` to the
raw `input_tokens`, even though the same method already computes the correct
input denominator in `cache_eligible_input_tokens` (the value used for the
cache hit rate).

## Change

`last_prompt_tokens` — the per-request value the console channel sends as
`context_usage.estimated_tokens` in the live `turn_usage` event
(`app/channels/console/channel.py:440`) — now uses the cache-aware
denominator:

- Anthropic: `input_tokens + cache_read + cache_write` (cache reads/writes
  really are part of the prompt the model processed).
- OpenAI Chat / Responses: unchanged, their `prompt_tokens` / `input_tokens`
  already include cached tokens, and `_cache_usage_metrics()` returns
  `cache_eligible == prompt_tokens` for them.
- Providers without verifiable cache semantics: unchanged
  (`cache_observed` is False, so the raw input tokens are kept and the cache
  counters are zeroed by the existing guard).

Session totals (`prompt_tokens`, the usage event) deliberately still carry
the uncached input tokens, so billing/statistics input accounting is not
affected — only the live per-request context meter.

## Evidence

- `tests/unit/token_usage/test_token_usage.py`:
  - `test_last_prompt_tokens_counts_anthropic_cache_tokens` — the issue's
    numbers (3000 / 120000 / 5000) now produce `last_prompt_tokens == 128000`
    while `prompt_tokens` stays 3000. Fails on `main` (asserted 128000 == 3000).
  - `test_last_prompt_tokens_keeps_openai_input_tokens` — an OpenAI adapter
    with `cache_input_tokens=3000` inside a 4000-token prompt keeps
    `last_prompt_tokens == 4000` (no double counting).
  - `test_last_prompt_tokens_ignores_unverifiable_cache_tokens` — an unknown
    adapter keeps raw input tokens and drops the cache counters.
- Full runs: `pytest tests/unit/token_usage/ tests/unit/channels/test_console.py`
  → 142 passed.
- Lint: `add-trailing-comma` + `black --line-length=79` clean,
  `flake8` clean on the changed lines (the one B017 hit is pre-existing at
  `tests/unit/token_usage/test_token_usage.py:439`), `pylint` 9.48/10 with the
  pre-existing import-outside-toplevel note only.

prs.title: test: stop leaking unawaited coroutines from scheduling mocks
prs.body:
## Summary

Six unit tests leak a coroutine: a scheduling mock replaces the scheduler
without consuming what production handed it, or a test runs a production
path in the wrong execution context. The tests pass, but the
`RuntimeWarning: coroutine ... was never awaited` noise hides real async
lifecycle defects (the issue cites #7857) and makes a clean test run
impossible to certify.

This fixes all six and tightens each test so it asserts the behaviour it
claims to cover.

Refs #7858

## What Problem This Solves

Running the affected files with `-X tracemalloc=5` emits **7**
unawaited-coroutine warnings. Six come from tests that pass for the wrong
reason, so a genuine async defect introduced nearby would be invisible in
the noise — the warnings are attributed to whichever test happens to
trigger the delayed GC, not the one that leaked.

Concretely, `test_download_attachment_exception` patched
`qq_channel._loop.run_coroutine_threadsafe` while production calls the
module-level `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe`, so the mock never fired
and the "returns None on failure" assertion was never exercising the
intended exception path. Similarly, `test_run_stream_forever` called the
sync thread entry point from inside a test coroutine, where `asyncio.run`
raises and the entry point's `except Exception` swallowed it — the test
asserted nothing about the stream loop at all.

## Changes

| Test | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `test_proactive_trigger_logic.py::TestEnableDisable::test_enable_stores_config_and_workspace` | `create_task` mock returned a stub task and left `_run_trigger_loop` unawaited | close the coroutine in the stub scheduler |
| `test_hub.py::TestClientLifecycle::test_aclose_hub_client_drain_timeout_warns` | fake `wait_for` raised `TimeoutError` without consuming the `Event.wait` coroutine | close it, and assert the warning the timeout path is supposed to log (was: `# must not raise`) |
| `test_dingtalk.py::TestDingTalkStreamMode::test_run_stream_forever` | async test called the sync thread entry point; `asyncio.run` failed inside the running loop and was swallowed | run it in a real thread and assert the stream loop actually executed |
| `test_qq.py::TestDownloadAttachmentSync::test_download_attachment_exception` | patched the loop's method; production uses the module-level function | patch `qwenpaw.app.channels.qq.channel.asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe`, assert it was scheduled on the channel's loop |
| `test_telegram.py::TestTelegramTypingIndicators::test_start_typing_creates_task` | `create_task` mock left `_typing_loop` unawaited | close the coroutine in the stub scheduler |
| `test_telegram.py::TestTelegramTypingIndicators::test_start_typing_replaces_existing` | same | same |

No production code is touched — every defect here is in the tests.

## Evidence

The issue's reproduction command, before and after:

```
$ python -X tracemalloc=5 -m pytest -q \
    tests/unit/agents/acp/test_acp_service.py \
    tests/unit/agents/memory/test_proactive_trigger_logic.py \
    tests/unit/agents/skill_system/test_hub.py \
    tests/unit/channels/test_dingtalk.py \
    tests/unit/channels/test_qq.py \
    tests/unit/channels/test_telegram.py

# before: 755 passed, 38 warnings   → 7 unawaited-coroutine warnings
# after:  755 passed, 33 warnings   → 1 unawaited-coroutine warning
```

The one remaining warning is `ACPService.close_all_sessions`, which is the
separate production defect tracked in #7857 — the issue's acceptance
criteria explicitly asks for this PR to land before that one.

Wider runs (no new failures; the single failure is a pre-existing
network-dependent one):

```
$ pytest tests/unit/channels tests/unit/agents -q
1 failed, 5864 passed, 4 skipped
# tests/unit/agents/utils/test_file_handling.py::TestDownloadFileFromUrl::test_remote_download
# fails on clean main too (needs network)

$ black --line-length=79 / flake8 / pylint (10.00)   # clean
```

prs.title: feat(browser): let config drop Playwright default launch arguments
prs.body:
## Summary

With `identity: "avatar"` and a real `user_data_dir`, extensions installed in
that persistent profile never load, because Playwright injects
`--disable-extensions` into the Chromium command line and QwenPaw has no way
to remove it.

`BrowserConfig.args` can only **append** switches, and Chromium treats a
boolean switch as "present means on", so re-appending
`--disable-extensions` does not cancel it. Playwright's only supported way
to drop a default is `ignore_default_args`, which QwenPaw never forwarded —
the only workaround was byte-patching
`playwright/driver/package/lib/server/chromium/chromiumSwitches.js` inside
`site-packages`, which a Playwright upgrade silently reverts.

This adds `browser.ignore_default_args` and forwards it end to end.

Refs #7984

## What Problem This Solves

A user running QwenPaw Desktop 2.2.1 on Windows configured the Browser SDK
with `backend: "launch"`, `identity: "avatar"` and a real `user_data_dir`,
then installed the SwitchyOmega proxy extension in that profile. The
extension never loaded: `chrome://extensions` was empty and the main
`chrome.exe` command line contained `--disable-extensions` (verified with
`Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`). Without the extension, sites only
reachable through the proxy failed with
`Page.goto: net::ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT`.

Because `browser.args` can only append and Chromium boolean switches are
"present means on", there was no configuration-level fix — the user had to
edit Playwright's compiled driver JS.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/qwenpaw/config/config.py` | `BrowserConfig.ignore_default_args: List[str]` (default `[]`) |
| `src/qwenpaw/browser/runtime/launch_resolve.py` | include it in the resolved launch spec |
| `src/qwenpaw/browser/runtime/ownership_adapter.py` | forward it in the `open_session` request |
| `src/qwenpaw/browser/control_link/playwright/adapter.py` | `_build_launch_kwargs` passes it to Playwright when non-empty |
| `website/public/docs/browser.{en,zh}.md` | document the field |

`_build_launch_kwargs` is the single choke point for launch kwargs, and both
`chromium.launch` and `chromium.launch_persistent_context` receive
`**launch_kwargs`, so one change covers the incognito and profile paths.

## Usage

```json
{
  "browser": {
    "backend": "launch",
    "identity": "avatar",
    "user_data_dir": "path\\to\\User Data",
    "ignore_default_args": ["--disable-extensions"]
  }
}
```

Scope: `backend: "launch"` only. `managed_cdp` / `connect_cdp` attach to an
already-running browser and have no launch command line to adjust (the CDP
adapter builds its own argv and does not use Playwright's default list).

## Evidence

The switch is traced from config to the Playwright launch call:

```
$ pytest tests/unit/browser tests/unit/config -q
403 passed

$ pytest tests/unit/browser/control_link/test_playwright_adapter_gate.py -q
13 passed
```

`test_open_session_reaches_playwright_with_ignore_default_args` drives
`_m_open_session` for real (with a stubbed Playwright) and asserts the value
reaches `chromium.launch`:

```
captured.get("ignore_default_args") == ["--disable-extensions"]
captured.get("executable_path")    == "/usr/bin/chromium"
```

Each forwarding test was verified to fail when its corresponding change is
reverted:

```
# adapter.py change reverted:
FAILED test_launch_kwargs_forward_ignore_default_args
FAILED test_launch_kwargs_copy_ignore_default_args
FAILED test_open_session_reaches_playwright_with_ignore_default_args
3 failed, 9 passed
```

Other checks:

```
$ pytest tests/integration/test_browser_module.py   # 17 passed
$ black --line-length=79 / flake8 / pylint (10.00)   # clean
```

`tests/integration/browser/*e2e*` has 7 failures on clean `main` here too —
they need a real Playwright/Chromium install, which this environment does not
have. Unrelated to this change.

prs.title: fix(security): flag inline Office COM automation in shell commands
prs.body:
## Summary

On Windows with approval level `auto` and the sandbox off, an agent-authored
inline Office COM command runs instead of being stopped.
`PowerPoint.Application`, `Excel.Application`, `Word.Application` and
`Outlook.Application` are single-instance COM servers, so attaching to one
binds to the **user's** already-open app and `Quit()` on that object
terminates the user's document — not a private automation instance.

The command matched no detection rule, so `GovernancePolicy.evaluate`
classified it as `SANDBOX_FALLBACK`, and `ResourceGovernor` rewrites that
decision to `ALLOW` whenever the sandbox is unavailable
(`running unsandboxed`). Nothing sat between the model and the user's
Office process.

This adds a `CRITICAL` rule that matches the COM construction itself, so
the call lands on the approval path instead of the unsandboxed one.

Refs #8002

## What Problem This Solves

A user had PowerPoint open on a real file. With approval level `auto` and
the security sandbox off, the agent emitted an Office COM self-check such as
`New-Object -ComObject PowerPoint.Application` followed by `Quit()`, and the
shell tool ran it. PowerShell attached to the **running** PowerPoint COM
server and `Quit()` closed the user's presentation — with data loss and no
warning, because the decision path never asked.

The root cause is not a missing sandbox rule but the fallback rewrite: an
unmatched shell command is `SANDBOX_FALLBACK`, and when the sandbox is
unusable `ResourceGovernor` turns that into `ALLOW`. Any command no rule
recognises is therefore executed unsandboxed and unguarded.

## Changes

`src/qwenpaw/security/tool_guard/rules/dangerous_shell_commands.yaml` —
new `TOOL_CMD_OFFICE_COM_AUTOMATION` rule (`category: resource_abuse`,
`severity: CRITICAL`) with three patterns:

1. a COM construction verb (`New-Object`, `GetActiveObject`, `GetObject`,
   `CreateObject`, `CreateInstance`, `GetTypeFromProgID`, `Dispatch`,
   `DispatchEx`) followed by an Office `*.Application` ProgID — catches
   `New-Object -ComObject PowerPoint.Application`,
   `[Activator]::CreateInstance([Type]::GetTypeFromProgID("Word.Application"))`,
   `win32com.client.Dispatch("Excel.Application")`
2. the same pairing in the other order, for the split
   `$t = GetTypeFromProgID(...); CreateInstance($t)` spelling
3. `.Quit()` invoked on an attached Office server

## Behaviour

| command | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `New-Object -ComObject PowerPoint.Application; $ppt.Quit()` | `sandbox_fallback` → `ALLOW` (sandbox off) | `ask` |
| `echo hello` | `sandbox_fallback` | `sandbox_fallback` |
| `python render_deck.py --out deck.pptx` | `sandbox_fallback` | `sandbox_fallback` |
| `git commit -m 'document Word.Application'` | `sandbox_fallback` | `sandbox_fallback` |

Mere mentions of the ProgID do not match, so built-in scripts that only
`Close()` a private temp presentation are unaffected (verified: no
occurrence of these ProgIDs or `ComObject`/`win32com` anywhere in `src/`,
`tests/`, `scripts/`, `plugins/` or `e2e/`).

Note the rule escalates to `ask`, not `deny`: `execution_level=off` is
documented as "tool guard completely disabled", so nothing fires there by
design and this change does not alter that.

## Evidence

End-to-end through `GovernancePolicy.evaluate` with the bundled rules
loaded (before → after):

```
$ python - <<'PY'
pol = _create_default_policy()
spec = ToolCallSpec(tool_name="Bash",
    target='New-Object -ComObject PowerPoint.Application; $ppt.Quit()',
    agent_id="a", session_id="s")
for level in ("auto", "smart", "strict", "off"):
    pol.execution_level = level
    d = pol.evaluate(spec)
    print(level, "->", d.action.value, d.source)
PY
# before: auto -> sandbox_fallback  smart -> sandbox_fallback  strict -> ask  off -> sandbox_fallback
auto     -> ask              source=detection_rules
smart    -> ask              source=detection_rules
strict   -> ask              source=STRICT mode
off      -> sandbox_fallback source=sandbox

benign auto     -> sandbox_fallback source=sandbox
benign smart    -> sandbox_fallback source=sandbox
benign off      -> sandbox_fallback source=sandbox
```

Full validation:

```
$ pytest tests/unit/governance tests/unit/security/tool_guard   # 842 passed
$ pytest tests/unit -k "tool_guard or governance or detector"   # 874 passed
$ black --line-length=79 / flake8 / pylint (10.00)              # clean
```
