prs.title: fix(mcp): confine SSE endpoints and redirects to the server origin
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Validate each resolved SSE message endpoint before a write starts. A server can no longer send configured headers or JSON-RPC content to another origin through an endpoint event.
- Bind SSE GET and POST redirects to the same origin. Reject URL credentials and report sanitized origins without query strings or userinfo.
- **Scope boundary:** SSE transport destination validation and its documentation. HTTP transport, stdio, CA trust, tool authorization, DNS pinning and gateway admin authorization retain their existing behavior.
- **Blast radius:** Remote MCP servers configured with `transport = "sse"`. Same-origin relative/absolute endpoints and redirects remain supported.
- Fixes #12146. #12129 merged as f87368a6aa53d16b0bd7411b002331a22622c2a7. This branch now contains that dependency repair through a single true rebase onto master 4c9edcf33716381b2c3455649cbd0f3e6b3a38b1; its two-file patch is unchanged.

### What this does, simply

An MCP server can tell the client where to send its next message. The client now checks that address against the server URL the operator configured. A different scheme, host or effective port is refused. HTTP redirects cannot bypass this check. The refusal happens before credentials or content reach the other destination.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Local HTTP fixtures exercise the production transport and record requests at the destination; no real server or credential is needed. The commands below run these checks.

### How I tested

Rebased revision: d8199da11070690344d3ca3e0e0d02ec638d979a. Fresh local validation on Windows x86-64, Rust 1.97.1, 2026-11-01. Exactly one own commit, with parent 4c9edcf33716381b2c3455649cbd0f3e6b3a38b1. `git range-diff` reports the original repair and this rebased commit as equivalent. No source edits followed validation.

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib mcp_transport::tests::
87 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

cargo fmt --all -- --check
exit 0

cargo clippy --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
exit 0 (no tools-crate warnings)

npx --yes markdownlint-cli2@0.20.0 docs/book/src/tools/mcp.md
Summary: 0 error(s)
```

The changed-link collector also passed: zero added links in the edited document. Test/dev debug info and incremental compilation were disabled; builds used two jobs.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** On d8199da11070690344d3ca3e0e0d02ec638d979a, [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41262135860/job/124719523203) and [Security](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41262135860/job/124717381898) pass. [Run 41262135860](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41262135860) also passes Test, Lint, MSRV, Linux build, Windows compilation and targeted Clippy, macOS compilation, Docs Style and Installer Drift. Path-gated skips are not runtime execution evidence. The old b09f760f72 run is historical evidence only. Independent Core Team/CODEOWNER security review remains required; reviewers have been requested.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The hosted required gate is complete and passes; independent security review remains pending. The local tests use loopback HTTP fixtures; no live external MCP service or native macOS execution was performed. A macOS compile job does not establish runtime execution.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Two adversarial self-review passes and a final reread covered endpoint-to-write ordering, redirects, URL normalization, error privacy, the constructor policy and non-SSE compatibility. The checks happen before headers, pending-sender registration and the write outcome marker. These passes are not independent approval. Historical negative control on b09f760f72: removing the two new guards made both capture tests fail because a foreign server received a request; restoring them passed all 87 tests. That mutation control was not repeated on the unchanged rebased patch; the 87-test result above is fresh on this head.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No CLI, TUI or web rendering or interaction code changed; the network boundary is exercised directly.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** The revision above; `SharedMcpTransportConn::send_and_recv` through real loopback HTTP servers, with synthetic `Authorization` and `X-Api-Key` headers. Tests are in `mcp_transport.rs`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Test summaries above. Five new tests cover origin rules, refused endpoint/redirect destinations, and accepted same-origin endpoint/redirect controls.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Foreign destinations received zero requests with the fix. Accepted destinations received the configured headers and returned the JSON-RPC result. Refused endpoints left no pending sender or post-write outcome marker.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No full workspace or live-service run; the focused transport module includes existing TLS, cancellation, fallback and response-limit controls. The locked test run fetched missing cached dependencies; Clippy then used offline resolution.

Two existing Windows warnings remain in unchanged `zeroclaw-config` files: `resolved_launcher` in `platform/docker.rs` and `resolved_shell` in `platform/native.rs`. Their reads are Unix-only. No warning suppression was added.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.**
- New external network calls? **No.**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** SSE credentials and payloads stay on the configured origin. Redirects receive the same check; URLs with credentials are refused. Errors name only sanitized origins.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.** This validates server-controlled transport metadata.

This changes a network credential boundary. Independent Core Team/CODEOWNER security review is required; this submission is not self-approval.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No** for servers that advertise another origin or use URL credentials. Same-origin endpoints and redirects remain supported.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No.**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Lifecycle-directory refusals print a pasteable `rm` / `chmod 700` / `sudo chown -R …` fix.
  - A relative config/data path whose first component starts with `-` (for example `ZEROCLAW_CONFIG_DIR=-install`) made those commands look like options to `rm` and GNU `chmod`/`chown`.

- **Blast radius:** Only the remediation command string shown in refusal errors for `.lifecycle` (and the matching owner-refusal `chown` command). Runtime behavior when the directory is already valid is unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11952

### What this does, simply

When ZeroClaw refuses to start because `.lifecycle` is wrong, it prints a command you can paste to fix it. If your config directory itself starts with a dash (unusual but legal), that printed command used to look like an option flag and failed. This PR makes those printed paths start with `./` so pasting them works. Normal absolute paths and ordinary relative paths look the same as before.

prs.title: fix(security): require administrator authority for SOP execution
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Require current administrator authority for `sops/run` and every `sops/decide` decision, including when a non-admin has wildcard selectors and `tools:execute`. SOP steps and their descendants do not carry a scoped caller's principal limits.
  - Retain that authority through synchronous start/approval storage effects after decision-model and engine waits; a contended store refuses immediately rather than holding authority while waiting for a writer.
  - Withhold `sop_execute`, `sop_approve`, `sop_advance`, `sop_workshop`, and their skill aliases from non-admin RPC sessions. Also withhold `spawn_subagent`, `execute_pipeline`, and delegate aliases that cannot carry the restriction.
  - Keep direct delegation for callers with unrestricted selectors, binding bounded, independent, background, parallel, and nested child builders to the originating credential's live authority resolver. The canonical policy remains `RpcInboundAuth`; no copied grant decision authorizes a child registry.
- **Scope boundary:** Cross-credential steering and combined permission checks with credential renewal remain separate work under RFC #12131, pending repository disposition; this branch does not implement them. This is interim containment, not principal propagation inside SOP steps; RPC SOP authoring and non-RPC triggers retain their existing policies. The cumulative diff includes the session-authority prerequisite from #11234 and current master; unrelated session-data and cron repairs from the supplemental drafts are not imported.
- **Blast radius:** Non-admin SOP execution, approval, workshop use, and unsafe nested tool exposure; administrators and the shared operator retain configured access, and ordinary admitted tools remain usable.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11123. Depends on #11234. Related #11408, #11410, #11230, and #11169.

### What this does, simply

A user could reach a procedure through a tool alias or an allowed agent and then run work outside that user's permissions. Until procedures can carry those permissions into every step, only administrators may start or decide them, and non-admin sessions do not receive tools that bypass that restriction.

```text
RPC run / decision ── current admin authority ── guarded storage effect
                         │ no
                         └───────────────────── FORBIDDEN

non-admin session ── ordinary tools / controlled delegate
                         └─ child registry rechecks live authority
                            └─ SOP entry tools and unsafe builders absent
```

The [earlier review](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11220#pullrequestreview-5364022889) identifies the tool-entry and descendant gaps; this carries the SOP-specific repairs from [#11408](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11408) and workshop regressions from [#11410](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11410), retaining their authorship and adapting their delegate propagation pattern to live resolution.

### Landing and shared-helper reconciliation

Land #11234 before this PR; the supplemental drafts must drop the SOP changes carried here when they refresh. #11169 must rebase onto this admission contract: one `SopAdmissionCheck` returns a held `SopEffectGuard`, and execution must keep the administrator predicate and nonblocking storage boundary rather than restoring its older wildcard predicate or a check returning `()`.

An integration probe against #11169 at `908a035d3f6b3734fcdf471785def4f6c3a1ad00` reports conflicts in `rpc/dispatch.rs`, `sop/dispatch.rs`, `sop/executor.rs`, and `sop/mod.rs`; its new ingress/cancel methods and authenticated approver changes still require that rebase and combined validation before landing.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes: compare the same scenarios with the previous head `ec5fc1c28760c63c9da9ea4d74e18379c146a2a8`.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Local authenticated JSON-RPC and Chat/ACP tool dispatch used by CLI/TUI clients; model providers in the regressions are synthetic.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A non-admin roster principal with `sops:execute`, `tools:execute`, wildcard selectors, and an approval-gated procedure; retain an administrator control.
- **Steps to run:** Request `sops/run` and an approval/denial through `sops/decide`; ask the session to invoke the direct SOP tools and a built-in skill alias, then repeat as administrator. The `sop_principal` tests also exercise a queued admin demotion and workshop persistence.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Non-admin RPC effects return `FORBIDDEN`; withheld tool calls return `Unknown tool` and leave runs/proposals unchanged; administrator controls and ordinary tools succeed.
- **Prior behavior (before):** Wildcard non-admins could pass the RPC guard, and model-facing SOP tools could enter procedures without the caller's principal ceiling.

### How I tested

#### Current revision: 0ddaef7c1a65aa9a934c03bbfbcef52591a4b65d

The latest change brings the existing writer-then-hook locks from #11234 into the copied deferred-approval log-capture test, keeping both guards through its asynchronous waits. It then additively merges master `f87368a6aa53d16b0bd7411b002331a22622c2a7`, including #12129. The owned production code is unchanged by this update; both dependency files exactly match master.

On this exact revision, all five selected tests passed together with `--test-threads=8`: deferred approval recheck, immediate approval refusal, provider payload capture, Chat state-write retry, and ACP checkpoint failure. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed. The test command was `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- deferred_approval_install_rechecks_after_agent_wait immediate_approval_install_refusal_fails_session_resume llm_request_payload_redacts_truncates_and_off_omits chat_running_state_write_failure_preserves_session_for_retry checkpoint_start_failure_notifies_once_and_releases_session --test-threads=8`.

The four-line repair and master integration were independently checked. New-head hosted checks remain required; the previous Wasmtime failure is addressed by the now-merged #12129 dependency files. The plugin feature matrix was not rerun locally; [#12129's successful run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41119606972) is inherited dependency evidence. The full local workspace and live two-provider acceptance were not rerun. Shared-execution authority/renewal is the separate RFC #12131, pending repository disposition; #11169 integration remains a prerequisite.

#### Earlier integration: f09b08f749cba368959ae05cbbdf8a264b3f033f

This head incorporates the #11234 session-error repair and an additive merge of master at 1c1cd118ac536a1dd1bc79b9cce69cbdc04e4f29. Immediate approval-channel installation errors now fail the request; deferred installation remains nonblocking and logs a sanitized refusal. A Chat state-write failure preserves the live session for retry, while ACP checkpoint failure retains its recovery eviction. The Fluent merge preserves all SOP and turn-recovery entries.

Historical local validation on that exact combined revision:

```sh
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- sop immediate_approval_install_refusal_fails_session_resume deferred_approval_install_rechecks_after_agent_wait chat_running_state_write_failure_preserves_session_for_retry checkpoint_start_failure_notifies_once_and_releases_session
# 853 passed; 0 failed; 1 existing live-model test ignored.
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
# Both passed.
```

[Hosted CI for that earlier head](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41097867322) provides the remaining platform/workspace matrix. Security reports five inherited Wasmtime 48.0.7 advisories (RUSTSEC-2026-0420 through 0424); the merged lockfile is identical to the pinned master. The hosted run is complete: Security and its aggregate required gate failed; the other required checks passed or were skipped as configured. A later metadata-only advisory risk-report job was cancelled; it is not source-validation evidence. The repair and merge were independently checked, but this is not whole-stack approval or resolution of the steering design and #11169 integration.

#### Earlier local validation: 137ae093935d1d216d0c62d6f53d22dea48a2cf2

The following results are preserved for this earlier revision, not attributed to the current head.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The historical local run below preceded hosted CI; current-revision evidence is listed above.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local validation is macOS with Rust/Cargo 1.97.1; cross-platform and full-workspace coverage remain with CI.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
  exit 0
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
  Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo]
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- rpc:: sop:: tools::sop_ tools::delegate:: live_config_authority::
  1883 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib live::
  8 passed; 0 failed
BASE_SHA=4d0d22b9771064827eaa25f2a2d2b56a860fd499 DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/security/authentication.md bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  Summary: 0 error(s)
BASE_SHA=4d0d22b9771064827eaa25f2a2d2b56a860fd499 DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/security/authentication.md bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
  6 tests OK; no added links
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Reviewed the registry/factory wiring and the #11169 merge probe; automated controls exercise real run/proposal persistence, SQLite writer contention, queued demotion, credential expiry/revocation, aliases, and all supported delegate construction paths. No external identity-provider or interactive TUI smoke test was performed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no layout or rendering change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `137ae093935d1d216d0c62d6f53d22dea48a2cf2`, local JSON-RPC/tool regressions; local logs in `tmp/oidc-11220-validation/` in the implementation worktree.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Runtime assertions verify `FORBIDDEN` or `Unknown tool: <name>` and unchanged durable/in-memory SOP state, with successful administrator controls.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** A queued principal demotion prevents SOP/workshop effects; a queued config writer cannot deadlock a nested read; busy SQLite refuses before start/resume mutation.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full-workspace/all-feature tests were not duplicated locally; the selected suites cover the changed boundaries. The existing two ignored runtime cases remain ignored.

The runtime test linker emits the pre-existing macOS `__eh_frame section too large (max 16MB)` warning; the same diagnostic was reproduced on clean master `ceb1e11176b7ee86ca3007cb7f6110ae94ff6ecb` during prerequisite validation, and both builds completed successfully.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**; this restricts existing access.
- New external network calls? **No**.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes**; delegate builders retain the originating connection's non-secret authentication evidence in a live resolver, so current revocation/expiry and grants are checked rather than a stored admission decision; no bearer is retained.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**; fixtures are synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**; unsafe tool capabilities are removed from the executable registry and its advertised surface.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: A descendant must not inherit another later caller's authority; each child retains its originating resolver while current policy remains canonical in the auth layer.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No**; non-admin wildcard SOP access is intentionally removed, including deny/amend/revise, and unsafe nested builders/aliases are withheld.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No** new setting, flag, or wire method; existing methods have stricter authorization and localized refusal text.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**.
- Exact upgrade steps: Use a trusted administrator/shared operator for SOP execution and decisions; adding `tools:execute` alone no longer restores access. Parent session tools narrow at the next prompt admission; recreate a session after promotion to regain removed tools, and retry busy-store requests once contention clears.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's eventual merge/squash commit while retaining the #11234 prerequisite; no data migration is required, but reverting restores the unsafe non-admin paths.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None; the restriction is deliberate and fails closed.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `FORBIDDEN` on SOP run/decision, `Unknown tool` for withheld names, localized SOP storage-busy refusals, and matching RPC authorization-denied records.

prs.title: fix(runtime): withhold session-data tools from non-admin principals
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Depends on #11225 and #11234. This is the cumulative recut, including adopted containment and steering repairs; review its full owned delta, not only the latest test commit. The separately scoped SOP containment is #11220.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Withhold `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, and `sessions_send` from every non-admin RPC session, including wildcard selectors, because these tools do not enforce principal ownership. Keep `sessions_current`, which accepts no foreign target.
  - Withhold principal-unaware cron, schedule, peer-messaging and nested-executor paths, including captured skill aliases. Retained delegates carry the narrowing into bounded, parallel and independent descendants; an Agent without the concrete delegate handle drops that entry. The canonical delegate remains available only when its selectors and retained handle permit it.
  - Apply one complete tool posture to prompt admission and steering. Steering resolves authority when consumed and again after memory writes, so the next accepted steering applies current withholding. This does not add continuous revocation between every action. Narrowing is monotonic: a later grant does not restore withdrawn tools to that live Agent.
  - Authorize cron patches against the actual stored row after acquiring its SQLite write transaction, and retain current authority through the synchronous commit. A queued demotion, revoked grant, changed owner or changed job type cannot reuse an earlier decision.
  - Retain #11234's session-authority and error-handling repairs: immediate approval-channel refusal propagates, deferred installation logs a sanitized refusal, and a Chat running-state write failure preserves the session for retry while ACP checkpoint failure retains its recovery behavior. The latest commit serializes the deferred test's process-wide log capture using the existing writer-then-hook locks.
- **Source of truth:** current grants come from the existing authorization authority. The posture is derived at each applicable boundary; registry removal and shared delegate withholding are narrowing effects, not a second live grant policy.
- **Scope boundary:** this contains principal-unaware tools; it does not make their stores principal-aware, add shared-execution credential renewal, or propagate principal ceilings into SOP runs. #11220 owns the SOP entry/workshop containment. Scheduled work, channels, CLI turns and existing independent triggers are not converted into principal-owned execution by this PR. The #11225 routing integration and full current-parent integration remain separate gates.
- **Blast radius:** RPC Chat/ACP construction, prompts and steering, aliases and delegate descendants, cron patch commits, and the inherited session-authority/storage boundary. Non-admin sessions lose the listed tools even with wildcard selectors.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11127; its containment closure also requires #11220 to land. Depends on #11225. Depends on #11234. Related #11220, #11410, #12046, #8290 and #12131.

### What this does, simply

Two people can use the same agent without owning each other's conversations. Until the cross-session tools check that ownership themselves, non-admin sessions cannot use them or regain them through the named contained cron, peer-message or nested-executor entry points exposed by that session. SOP entry and workshop containment remains in #11220. The same restrictions apply when a former administrator steers an existing turn after demotion. Ordinary tools and the current-session tool remain available when the caller's grants allow them.

The headless tool set withheld here is `cron_add`, `cron_update`, `cron_run`, `cron_list`, `cron_runs`, `cron_remove`, `schedule` and `send_message_to_peer`. The session tools, `spawn_subagent`, `execute_pipeline`, and aliases of the withheld tools or `delegate` are also removed. These restrictions are interim containment, not a claim that the OIDC isolation milestone is complete.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A for an additional manual setup: dispatcher tests drive real session/store boundaries with synthetic principals, controlled demotion and competing writes. Live provider acceptance remains a separate milestone gate.

### How I tested

- **Current repair revision:** `0efa2558924e60fc3397720ffdf4f12e4459ec0a`. This retains the additive four-line log-test fix `9684cf3b5008fb64a17a2b3fc71650f4578f279d` and merges master `f87368a6aa53d16b0bd7411b002331a22622c2a7`, including #12129. The merge required no manual resolutions; the owned patch is unchanged, while the incoming master changes include persisted-log access containment. Both dependency files exactly match master.
- **Exact-revision local results:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passed. `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- rpc::dispatch:: agent::turn::provider_call:: steering principal_scope principal_memory withhold --test-threads=8` passed all 642 selected tests with no failures or ignored tests. `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed. These ran on macOS with jobs=2, incremental=0, debug=0 and an isolated Cargo target.
- **Validation retry:** the initial attempt reused another worktree's Cargo target and failed to see PR-specific trait methods already present in this source. The unchanged head passed after rebuilding in its own target directory; no source suppression or test bypass was added.
- **Current hosted evidence:** new-head checks remain required. The merge and test repair were independently checked. The unchanged dependency files adopt #12129's [successful Security and plugin matrix](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41119606972); those feature suites were not repeated locally.
- **Historical hosted evidence on the preceding PR head:** d69f99d77c6f0b659d1714b44b90de1601107158 passes [Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41096212634/job/124202534955), [Parallel Runtime Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41096212634/job/124202737438), [Lint](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41096212634/job/124202534799) and [Docs Style](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41096212634/job/124202723889). Test reports 19,572 passed and 42 skipped in its main group. The source-confirmed shared-log race was not an observed failure in this run.
- **Earlier failed gate:** [Security](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41096212634/job/124202534613) and the [aggregate gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41096212634/job/124212229592) fail on the inherited Wasmtime 48.0.7 advisories, RUSTSEC-2026-0420 through 0424. #12129 has merged the dependency repair; it was not integrated into this preceding head. These failures are not waived.
- **Boundary evidence:** hosted tests cover same-agent foreign-history/append refusal; wildcard and named selectors; canonical and aliased headless tools; descendant withholding; cron transaction contention; prompt admission after waits; and steering demotion both before consumption and during a memory write. Positive controls retain the caller's own session, allowed ordinary tools and unchanged administrator behavior.
- **Steering repair provenance:** dfe06dcf76b20533e622ba7a74b5b02b70335f65 is in the branch. [Its adoption check](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11230#pullrequestreview-5706814602) links the exact earlier hosted steering regressions. The [session-error update](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11230#issuecomment-6528701580) records four passing focused tests, formatting and runtime all-target Clippy on d69f99d77c6f0b659d1714b44b90de1601107158.
- **Beyond CI:** the earlier repair reports include negative controls; they are historical evidence on their named revisions, not new executions on this test-only commit.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: authorization/tool availability and error propagation are proved at dispatcher/store boundaries; this PR introduces no presentation-sensitive interface change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** the linked hosted run covers d69f99d77c6f0b659d1714b44b90de1601107158. Current integrated-head local results are recorded above; historical hosted results are not attributed to it.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the linked Test log records the named boundary regressions and their passing results.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** demotion or revocation during the tested waits denies the affected operation and preserves foreign data; unchanged permitted controls succeed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full workspace, native Windows runtime suite and live IdP flows have not been rerun locally for this four-line test repair. Complete provider, migration and rollback acceptance is not claimed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The owned containment narrows tools and rechecks existing authority.
- New external network calls? No. The inherited #11225 slice places principal-scoped private recall in the existing provider context and restores private autosave; this containment slice adds no new payload type.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No in this slice; the existing authority supplies current decisions.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No; fixtures use synthetic roster identities.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes in inherited #11225: private recall reaches provider context under the existing provenance and owner/tenant/namespace/agent filters. This containment slice narrows the tool registry and adds no new text source.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: recalled memory remains untrusted context and must retain its ownership and provenance filtering. The containment risk is an omitted tool or a missed revocation boundary; foreign-data refusal, mutation preservation and allowed controls cover the specified paths. Related execution and storage work remains explicitly separate.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No. Non-admin RPC sessions, including wildcard accounts, lose the tools named above and their aliases. Previously narrowed live Agents do not regain tools on a later grant; a new or rehydrated session is needed after an authorized policy change. The inherited #11225 slice also refuses owned-background delegation and its task-management operations for owned principals, including named administrators.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new configuration or CLI option in this containment slice.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No toolchain-floor change. The public Rust `SteeringPosture` gains `withhold_principal_unaware_session_tools`; callers constructing it with struct literals must derive that field from their admission policy; the all-false default is unscoped. The inherited #11225 API requires former `AllToolsResult` struct-literal callers to use `AllToolsResult::from_prebuilt_tools`. The cumulative branch also carries the separately reviewed APIs from #11225 and #11234.
- Exact upgrade steps: operators must account for the restricted non-admin tool set and coordinate #11220's SOP containment and the declared parents. Single-operator and currently authorized administrator sessions retain their ordinary allowed tools. Principal-aware replacements and shared-execution renewal remain follow-up work; granting administrator access is a broad authority change, not an equivalent scoped replacement.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** after landing, `git revert <landed-PR-squash-commit>`, reconciling dependent PRs. There is no persisted migration in the owned containment slice. Reverting containment reopens the described foreign-session/headless access; keep affected tools unavailable through existing agent policy until a safe replacement is deployed. Reverting only 9684cf3b5008fb64a17a2b3fc71650f4578f279d restores the test race and does not undo containment.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** no new toggle. Existing agent tool policy can retain restrictions during rollback.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** non-admin `Unknown tool` responses for withheld capabilities are expected. A foreign transcript read/append, a queued cron mutation after revoked authority, or missing ordinary tools for an unchanged permitted control is a regression.

## Supersede Attribution

This is not a replacement PR. Adopted repairs from @Aarlington and @JordanTheJet retain their commit authorship and the prerequisite history. No contributor branch or published history was rewritten.

prs.title: fix(rpc): judge queued session ownership by current authority
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Current head: `021ace3df17b12e359b643eb2c41dc2b785830d7`, including an additive merge of master `f87368a6aa53d16b0bd7411b002331a22622c2a7`. The latest merge leaves the reviewed eight-file owned patch unchanged. The [prepared canonical repair](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/commit/677961e7d73f17c36a7d21742095ea0292d605d8) and contributor commits remain in the ancestry, including the remote-TUI transcript fence and merged #10246/#11222 behavior.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Session operations that wait (for the session admission permit, the config writer gate, a pending provider binding or the provider-update lock) decided ownership with the administrator bypass stamped on the connection before the wait. `recheck_authority_after_admission` re-resolved the grants afterwards but never updated that stamp, so an administrator demoted while queued still reached another principal's session. A new `scoped_principal_id_from(grants)` derives the ownership scope from a given grant set; `scoped_principal_id()` delegates to it with the stamped grants and remains the pre-wait check. `revalidate_admitted_session`, `authorize_session_owner_for_mode` and `resolve_session_record_for_mode` now take the scope as a parameter instead of reading the stamp, so those post-admission ownership decisions and refusals use freshly resolved grants.
  - `session/close`, `session/kill` and `session/delete` recheck authority right after the permit and revalidate with the scope those grants give. Kill and delete also fall back to the durable record when a hard-cancelled turn removed the live incarnation during the wait; that fallback now requires the record to be the caller's under the same scope. Without it, a demoted administrator whose target's live incarnation disappeared while it waited still tombstoned or deleted another principal's durable row.
  - `session/prompt` derives ownership from fresh grants after admission and provider waits. Final preparation runs inside the execution task after it acquires the canonical Agent lock. It checks the exact Agent and current owner/binding/environment permissions, narrows tools, and authorizes the checkpoint or running-state write under the storage lock before execution. Refused preparation ends the client turn through `refuse_admitted_prompt` without calling the provider. Rehydration uses guarded recovery and seed-trim persistence so a storage-lock wait cannot retain earlier authority.
  - `session/new`: `SessionStore::resume_existing_authorized` hands the session's owner to its authorize closure, and the new `authorize_resumed_incarnation` judges that owner with the same authority it resolves for the agent/workspace binding and the retained environment, under the store lock. A connection whose stamp still carries a revoked bypass therefore cannot rebind another principal's live session. After the permit, authority is re-resolved before anything else and the scope derived from it judges the record found under the permit (so a demoted administrator no longer leaves a cross-principal audit record for a request refused a few lines later, and a principal promoted while waiting is honoured), the post-admission resume, the cross-mode replacement and the ACP restore preload. After the config writer gate wait it is re-derived again: the owner of the session being restored or replaced must match, and whether a failed owner-stamp write aborts creation follows that scope.
  - `session/configure` and the queued (reaped) branch of `session/messages` also act after a wait and call `revalidate_admitted_session`, so they recheck authority and pass the fresh scope as well.
  - The covered close/kill/delete cancellation effects, publication and deferred approval-channel installation reauthorize under the live-session boundary. `session/messages` and plan replay reserve outbound capacity before their final ownership/authority check and send synchronously while guarded. The shared plan helper covers live resume, restored `session/new`, and prompt rehydration.
  - `session/append` passes the current ownership scope into its admitted lookup, then resolves authority again after that awaited lookup and before either transcript write. Its regression covers a demoted administrator targeting a foreign session, an owner whose update grant was revoked, and a demoted owner whose update grant remains valid.
  - Approval-channel installation errors propagate on the immediate path; deferred installation logs a sanitized refusal after its wait. A failed Chat running-state write preserves the session for retry, while ACP checkpoint failure retains its recovery behavior. The deferred log-capture regression holds the existing writer-then-hook locks for the entire test.
- **Scope boundary:** The request gate, durable owner identity (`owner_principal_id`), wire, config and CLI shapes are unchanged. Ownership after the covered waits follows current authority. The guards authorize individual effects; this does not add continuous revocation of an already-admitted running turn or roll back effects authorized before demotion.
- **Blast radius:** RPC dispatch, execution-task preparation, live-session synchronization, outbound frame reservation, and guarded ACP/Chat persistence. New authorization callbacks run after storage locks or transactions are acquired and retain authority through synchronous effects. History helpers acquire the Agent before the session map and recheck incarnation identity. Unsupported guarded backend reads and deletes fail closed. Permitted own-session operations retain positive-control coverage.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11126. Related #11222 (merged prerequisite). Related #10412.

### What this does, simply

Named local principals can hold an administrator bypass that lets them act on other principals' sessions. Several session requests wait before they act: behind a turn that holds the session, behind a configuration change, or behind a provider update. The daemon did recheck the caller's permissions after that wait, but it kept deciding who owns what from the administrator flag recorded when the request arrived. If an administrator lost that role while their request waited, the request still went through: it could delete another person's saved session, kill it, send it a prompt, change its settings, read it, or restore it.

After this change, the covered effects decide ownership from the permissions in force after their final wait. A demoted administrator receives the same "not found or not owned" refusal as any other principal before that effect executes, changes saved data, or discloses a foreign transcript or plan. Permitted operations on the caller's own sessions keep working.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: reproducing it needs a principal roster and a demotion that lands while a request is queued, which the dispatcher-level regressions below drive deterministically.

### How I tested

#### Current integration: `021ace3df17b12e359b643eb2c41dc2b785830d7`

On this exact revision, formatting passed; 21 focused runtime authority/error regressions passed together at `--test-threads=8`; three guarded-effect infrastructure tests passed; and strict all-target Clippy passed for `zeroclaw-api`, `zeroclaw-infra` and `zeroclaw-runtime`. A separate four-test run combined both persisted-log access tests from master with the deferred approval capture and provider payload capture; all four passed (two overlap the first set).

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- queued_operations_lose_the_admin_bypass queued_prompt_rechecks_ownership demoted_administrator_cannot_resume final_prompt_effect_waits removal_effect_waits restore_effect_waits messages_frame_capacity_wait resume_plan_capacity_wait resume_plan_empty_and_closed remote_resume_admission_wait remote_resume_rechecks_channels immediate_approval_install deferred_approval_install chat_running_state_write_failure checkpoint_start_failure_notifies append_rechecks_authority_after_admitted history_wait_releases_map backend_effect_refusal sqlite_effect_callbacks llm_request_payload_redacts_truncates_and_off_omits --test-threads=8
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-infra --lib -- guarded_effects_reauthorize guarded_state_and_delete no_state_backend_admits
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- persisted_log_reads deferred_approval_install llm_request_payload_redacts_truncates_and_off_omits --test-threads=8
```

The automatic merge and preserved owned patch were independently checked. The lockfile and plugin manifest are byte-identical to master, adopting merged #12129. Its [successful Security/plugin matrix](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41119606972) is inherited dependency evidence; those feature suites were not repeated locally. Hosted checks on this new revision remain required. Full-workspace local and live-provider acceptance were not rerun.

#### Earlier validation

The following results are historical evidence for their explicitly named revisions.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** On `90baa4e0b822dbee54e51d870e3f902c1143f073`, [Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914/job/121823900690), [Parallel Runtime Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914/job/121824145930), [Lint](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914/job/121823900780) and the [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914/job/121833369379) pass in [Quality Gate run 40394518914](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914). Test covers the RPC and storage regressions, including the remote-TUI transcript fence; Parallel Runtime Test checks concurrent runtime execution, and the required gate aggregates the selected jobs. [Windows compile](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914/job/121824410202), [Windows Service Smoke](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914/job/121824410236), [macOS compile](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914/job/121823900711), [MSRV](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914/job/121825752013) and [plugin runtime](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914/job/121823901145) checks also pass. The check runs and the re-read PR head match this exact commit.

- **Earlier local validation (2026-10-26):** Tested `90baa4e0b822dbee54e51d870e3f902c1143f073` (tree `36d89052034e3d2e1230835aa09da6146bb678c8`) on macOS arm64 with rustc/cargo 1.97.1, default crate features and default test threading. The isolated checkout used its own `target/` directory with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0` and `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0`. All 1,549 selected tests passed; formatting and strict Clippy exited 0.

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0; no output
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra --lib
# zeroclaw-api: 321 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
# zeroclaw-infra: 319 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::
# 870 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 5023 filtered out
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib live_config_authority::
# 39 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 5854 filtered out
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
# exit 0; no Clippy diagnostics
# Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized] target(s) in 1m 54s
```

- **Historical hosted validation (not current-head evidence):** On `1688a026cb7dff7c8ef9a54a9e73128c3258cb8a`, [Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39728651042/job/119658338409), [Parallel Runtime Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39728651042/job/119658474359), [Lint](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39728651042/job/119658338391) and the [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39728651042/job/119661634575) pass. Test runs the RPC regressions listed below, including the transcript remote-TUI recheck.
- **Transcript remote-TUI recheck (68c8228891, b350fcec00):** `commit_session_messages` also checks the remote TUI owner after reserving writer capacity, under the same session-map guard as the send, as `replay_session_plan` does. `messages_frame_capacity_wait_rechecks_remote_tui_owner` rebinds the owner through a trusted-local `session/new` during the capacity wait and asserts that the old remote TUI gets no transcript; current-owner and trusted-local controls still read it. The test fails without the fix.
- **Historical local validation (not current-head evidence):** `d72bab13cd71f1fa31e0028668a2ee471a88f9fc` (tree `0cb5396b9b114b24801ab91e4a87f00e433c7974`), macOS arm64, rustc 1.97.1; default crate features and eight test threads. All 1,094 focused tests passed, with no Clippy diagnostics.

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0; no output
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc:: -- --test-threads=8
# 862 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 4919 filtered out
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-infra --lib session -- --test-threads=8
# 207 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 107 filtered out
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib live_config_authority:: -- --test-threads=8
# 25 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 5756 filtered out
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
# Finished dev profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 19s
```

- **Earlier local linker diagnostic and historical baseline:** That runtime test link emitted `ld: __eh_frame section too large (max 16MB) to encode dwarf unwind offsets in compact unwind table, performance of exception handling might be affected`; the binary linked and all selected tests passed. The warning concerns the large test binary's unwind table. Earlier validation reproduced the same diagnostic on clean master `ceb1e11176b7ee86ca3007cb7f6110ae94ff6ecb` with `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --no-run` (exit 0). That is historical baseline evidence; the current pinned master was not separately rebuilt for this warning.

- **Historical CI on the previous PR head (not current-head evidence):** On `d5df4214cad96bfc6bfbdea13a64767b116ac1df`, [Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36751197781/job/110009962176), [Parallel Runtime Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36751197781/job/110010144453), Lint, the plugin-backend Check legs, and the [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36751197781/job/110014127332) pass. The Test log explicitly records the admission/provider, final-effect, storage-lock and outbound-backpressure regressions below passing; its main suite reports 19,059 passed and 39 skipped. These results cover only that older revision; the refreshed head has a separate run.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local evidence exercises synthetic principals, in-process RPC handlers, existing local/WSS transport tests and real session stores on macOS; no live daemon against a real identity provider was tested. Hosted Windows compile and service-smoke jobs passed, but the advisory Windows nextest workflow and targeted Windows Clippy job were skipped by workflow selection. Full Windows runtime-suite coverage is not claimed.
- **Regression coverage:**
  - `append_rechecks_authority_after_admitted_lookup` (prepared-repair regression): demotion cannot preserve a foreign-session append, and revoking an owner's update grant prevents both durable and live writes; a demoted owner who retains update authority can still append.
  - `queued_operations_lose_the_admin_bypass_when_the_administrator_is_demoted` (new): alice holds `member` session grants plus an `administrator` profile, and bob owns an ACP session. For each of prompt, close, delete and kill against bob's live session, delete and kill when its live incarnation is reaped during the wait, and prompt (the rehydration path) and messages against the reaped session, alice's request passes its pre-check as administrator and parks on the admission permit; the profile loses `admin` (her `member` grants stay) and the permit is released. Each request gets `FORBIDDEN` with the uniform denial, each refused prompt ends the client's turn with a failed `TurnComplete` on alice's connection, bob's live generation is unchanged (or the session stays reaped, not revived), and his durable row still exists, is not killed, keeps his owner and gains no messages. Configure parked on the provider-update lock is refused the same way and bob's overrides are unchanged. Positive control: alice, demoted while her delete of her own session waits, deletes it.
  - `queued_prompt_rechecks_ownership_after_its_provider_waits` (new): alice's prompt on bob's live session passes the post-admission ownership check as administrator and then parks, once on the provider-update lock and once on a pending provider binding; she is demoted and the wait is released. Both prompts get `FORBIDDEN` with the uniform denial and a failed `TurnComplete`, bob's provider receives no call, and his incarnation and durable row are unchanged.
  - `demoted_administrator_cannot_resume_a_foreign_session_with_a_stale_stamp` (new): `handle_session_new_for_test` skips the gate, so alice's connection keeps its administrator stamp after the demotion; `session/new` naming bob's live session is refused and his generation is unchanged, while the same stale connection still rebinds a session of her own. Resumes of bob's reaped ACP and chat sessions queued behind the permit when the demotion lands are refused and nothing is restored; bob's ACP row keeps an interrupted-turn checkpoint unrecovered and his chat row keeps its owner. Positive control: her own reaped ACP session, resumed the same way, is restored.
  - The direct `resume_existing_authorized` tests accept the owner argument and returned authorization guard.
  - `final_prompt_effect_waits_recheck_current_authority`, `removal_effect_waits_preserve_foreign_session_after_demotion`, `restore_effect_waits_preserve_retained_checkpoint_after_demotion`, and `deferred_approval_install_rechecks_after_agent_wait` cover the later execution, mutation and channel-install boundaries.
  - `messages_frame_capacity_wait_rechecks_authority_before_disclosure` and `resume_plan_capacity_wait_rechecks_authority_and_incarnation` exercise actual dispatcher responses and backpressure. The plan test covers live/restored resume, prompt rehydration, demotion, replacement, own-session and unchanged-administrator controls. Empty-plan and closed-writer cases also pass.
  - `guarded_effects_reauthorize_after_store_lock_without_partial_writes` and `guarded_state_and_delete_recheck_owner_and_authority_after_connection_wait` verify post-lock authorization and preserved durable data on denial. `history_wait_releases_map_and_refuses_replaced_incarnation` covers the changed history lock order.
  - `remote_resume_admission_wait_uses_current_principal` covers remote demotion with an own-session control. `remote_resume_rechecks_channels_at_final_agent_install` checks capability changes during the final Agent wait. The plan-backpressure matrix now includes remote live and cross-mode resume and checks their intended admission-permit lifetimes.
- **Commands run and tail output** (author-reported historical local evidence on b0879527d3, macOS arm64, rustc 1.98.0; not a claim of new local runs on the integrated head):
  - `cargo nextest run -p zeroclaw-runtime -E 'test(/admitted|demot|owner|resume|queued/)'`: `114 tests run: 114 passed, 5169 skipped`.
  - `TMPDIR=/private/tmp cargo nextest run -p zeroclaw-runtime -E 'test(/rpc::/)'`: `660 tests run: 660 passed, 4623 skipped`.
  - `./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh --strict`: fmt passes; clippy stops on its only error, `unused import: std::sync::mpsc` at `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/service/mod.rs:15`, which unmodified `master` also reports on macOS (the import is used only by Windows and Linux code). The script's provider-dispatch section, run on its own: `provider dispatch gate clean`.
  - `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings -A unused_imports`: `Finished`, no diagnostics.
  - `cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`: `Finished`, no warnings.
  - `./scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh`: `Comment hygiene gate passed.`
  - `cargo test --no-run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`: every test target builds; its only warnings are the two macOS-only ones unmodified `master` emits (the `std::sync::mpsc` import and the `ld: __eh_frame section too large` linker note), so allowing `unused_imports` above hides nothing new.
  - `TMPDIR=/private/tmp ZEROCLAW_PARALLEL_TEST_RUNS=1 ./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh`: `zeroclaw-runtime` `5231 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored`, `zeroclaw-channels` `1957 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored`.
  - Plugin-backend commands from `check-plugin-backends`, run as written (the change filter reports `true` for this diff). The two `zeroclaw-runtime` legs ran on this commit; the rest ran on the previous revision of it, which differs only in `rpc/dispatch.rs`:
    - `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features` `plugins-wasm-cranelift` / `plugins-wasm-pulley` / `plugins-wasmtime`: all `Finished`.
    - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test channel_plugin_e2e --test egress_plugin_e2e --test tool_plugin_timeout_e2e --test reference_plugin --test reference_plugin_e2e --test tool_plugin_e2e`: every binary `ok`, 43 passed, 0 failed.
    - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib`: `260 passed; 0 failed`.
    - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib agent::plugin_live_config`: `2 passed; 0 failed`.
    - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib -- plugin_runtime:: tools::tests::shared_ceiling tools::tests::repeated_loader tools::tests::auto_discover tools::tests::colliding_plugin`: `22 passed; 0 failed`.
    - `cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test plugin_channel_runtime_e2e`: `4 passed; 0 failed`.
    - `cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test channel_egress_e2e`: `3 passed; 0 failed`.
    - `cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --bin zeroclaw`: `551 passed; 0 failed`.
    - `cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test component -- plugin_info_cli`: `4 passed; 0 failed`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Historical author verification on b0879527d3 and the earlier revisions noted below (not newly repeated on the integrated head): confirmed the regressions fail without the fix by mutating one path at a time and rerunning them. Removing only the ownership check after the prompt's provider waits lets the demoted administrator's prompt complete a turn on bob's session (`"turn finished"` from his provider), once parked on the provider-update lock and once on the pending binding. Judging every scope by the stamp again fails the other two: the queued prompt runs a turn on bob's session (it reaches his provider), and the stale stamp rebinds bob's live session. Removing only the post-lock owner check restores bob's reaped chat session; judging only the ACP restore preload by the stamp recovers bob's interrupted turn into his history before the refusal; removing only the owner check in the resume closure rebinds bob's live session; judging only rehydration by the stamp revives bob's reaped session; removing only the scope from kill's durable fallback tombstones bob's session (`killed: true`), and from delete's fallback deletes it. The delete, kill and rehydration mutations ran on an earlier revision of these tests that lacked only the liveness precondition assertions. At that time, `git merge-tree --write-tree` with #10412 and `master` completed without conflicts; that historical check does not establish their current integration state. Did not run a live daemon against a real principal roster.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: no rendered interface or presentation changed. The existing RPC denial shape is asserted by the handler regressions.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Earlier local and hosted validation: `90baa4e0b822dbee54e51d870e3f902c1143f073` (tree `36d89052034e3d2e1230835aa09da6146bb678c8`), using the commands above and [Quality Gate run 40394518914](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914). Older local and hosted revisions are historical only. The tests exercise handler and JSON-RPC dispatcher behavior, outbound frames, and storage effects. No live deployment or rendered-interface run is claimed.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** The queued administrator-demotion tests assert `FORBIDDEN` (`-32012`) and the uniform denial `Session not found or not owned by this principal`. The remote-TUI rebind regression asserts `SESSION_NOT_OWNED` and that the private transcript marker is not sent. These are distinct refusal paths; no claim is made that every regression has the same message.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** A demoted administrator's queued prompt, close, delete, kill, configure, messages or resume of another principal's session is refused at the covered waits, with the foreign session's state preserved. Positive controls explicitly cover deletion and live/reaped resume of the caller's own sessions.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace and platform/feature matrices were not repeated locally; the focused local commands cover the changed RPC, storage/API and authority boundaries. The historical hosted runs above supply the broader Linux tests, Windows compile/service smoke, macOS compile and selected plugin checks named above. The older local plugin skips remain historical. No live identity-provider/deployment test was run. Docs gates were not run because this PR changes no documentation.

Current-head hosted checks remain required; historical hosted coverage is not attributed to this integration.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The change only narrows access: after a wait, cross-principal access requires the administrator bypass under the policy in force at that moment. Fixtures use the existing fake roster principals (`user:alice`, `user:bob`, uids 4242 and 4343).

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Wire/config shapes remain compatible; requests that lose authority while waiting are refused. Rust APIs add guarded `SessionBackend` methods and a generation field to `ResumedRpcSession`. The changed `resume_existing_authorized` callback is crate-private, not a public closure API.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- Backend compatibility: the new guarded disclosure and deletion defaults return `Unsupported`; custom persistent backends must implement them to support those RPC operations. The guarded state default has no persistent effect and authorizes the locked live owner; a backend that persists state must override it and read the stored owner under its mutation lock. In-tree SQLite and JSONL behavior is covered by the added tests. No wire or config migration is required.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's eventual squash commit; this reopens the reported bypass, so prefer a forward fix.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** session requests from principals whose authority did not change being refused after a wait: `FORBIDDEN` "Session not found or not owned by this principal" on their own sessions, or WARN "RPC authorization denied" for `session/close`, `session/kill`, `session/delete`, `session/configure` or `session/messages`.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.
