prs.title: fix(install): verify Windows prebuilt release checksums
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`, at `1c1cd118ac536a1dd1bc79b9cce69cbdc04e4f29`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Resolve one release tag, then download the Windows archive and `SHA256SUMS` from that tag. Require one exact asset entry and a matching SHA256 before extraction.
  - Use one PowerShell helper for `setup.bat --prebuilt` and the generated Windows guide. Missing, malformed, duplicate or mismatched checksums stop installation. A failed download also stops this mode.
  - Add offline tests under PowerShell 5.1 and 7 to the existing required Windows job. Helper-only changes now select that job.
- **Scope boundary:** Windows x86_64 prebuilt installation only. No change to Unix installers, release publishing, signing, PATH policy or the existing Rust prerequisite check in `setup.bat`.
- **Blast radius:** The Windows batch entrypoint, its shared helper, the generated PowerShell guide and Windows CI selection.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12122.

### What this does, simply

The Windows installers currently extract a downloaded archive without checking its release checksum. This checks the checksum first. If it fails, the archive is not extracted and the existing install is left alone. Both files come from the same resolved release, so a change to `latest` between requests cannot mix releases.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A for additional manual checksum testing: the checked-in offline fixtures exercise the hash and extraction path, the complete documented failure path and the real batch entrypoint. A live release installation and binary startup are not claimed.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Run 41233505537](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41233505537) is complete on this head. [Installer Drift](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41233505537/job/124632380150) passed the full generator check. The [required Windows job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41233505537/job/124632524247) passed both PowerShell suites and the build checks. Lint, Test, targeted Windows Clippy and Docs Style also passed. The [Security job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41233505537/job/124632380072) and resulting required gate are the only failed jobs: five inherited Wasmtime 48.0.7 advisories, RUSTSEC-2026-0420 through 0424, addressed by #12129. This PR leaves the dependency manifest and lockfile unchanged. The red gate still blocks merge; no waiver is requested.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The full generator and required Windows job now have completed hosted passes. The checksum suites use synthetic archives and mocked downloads. They do not run an installed ZeroClaw binary or persist a user PATH change.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
powershell.exe -NoProfile -File scripts/ci/windows_prebuilt.test.ps1
pwsh.exe -NoProfile -File scripts/ci/windows_prebuilt.test.ps1
# Each shell:
PASS setup.bat --prebuilt: checksum mismatch, exit 1, no extraction, source fallback or PATH write
PASS 22 checksum cases, explicit tag and 3 invalid tags; all network calls mocked

bash scripts/ci/windows_test_scope.test.sh
Required Windows package ownership: pass
Required Windows gate consistency: pass
windows test scope contract tests: pass

rustfmt --edition 2024 --check xtask/src/generate/docs.rs
git diff --check
bash -n install.sh
# exit 0

bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
Summary: 0 error(s)
```

  The link gate's six unit tests and changed-link collector passed under Linux. No invalid local targets were found. Optional `lychee` validation was unavailable. The repository comment-hygiene filter passed on the changed supported source files.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Two adversarial passes checked same-tag URLs, exact and duplicate manifest entries, fail-before-extraction behavior, temporary-file cleanup, batch error propagation, generator/helper parity and CI selection. Two disposable mutation controls failed as intended: removing the hash comparison and changing the archive URL back to `latest`. The current v0.8.7 release lists both the Windows archive and `SHA256SUMS`; neither asset was executed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output. No layout or rendering change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `6c257aa66d6c1d7f7f2f4f2dbdc0d3b6c80a4520`; Windows, PowerShell 5.1 and 7; `scripts/ci/windows_prebuilt.test.ps1`. The tested installer, generated PowerShell block and test code are unchanged; later prose only clarifies the source-archive and fallback requirements. English assertions do not depend on terminal width.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** The output above includes the observed batch failure and fixture results. The helper prints `SHA256 verified: zeroclaw-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip (v1.2.3)` for a valid synthetic archive.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** A valid archive replaces the fixture payload. Corrupt or unverifiable input leaves the existing fixture unchanged, removes temporary downloads and stops before PATH or Quickstart. The batch process returns 1.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The full workspace generator, Cargo tests and Clippy were not run locally: disk exhaustion required a sparse source checkout. The guide was mechanically materialized from the canonical Rust raw template and shared helper. The completed hosted run now verifies Installer Drift, Test, Lint and targeted Windows Clippy. The Linux-only link and selector tests were moved from Windows to Linux after path-format failures; their source is unchanged except for the new selector case. No live installation or new private CI job was run.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.** Downloads use a unique temporary directory; the install destination is unchanged.
- New external network calls? **Yes.** Both routes fetch the manifest. The batch route resolves the release through the public GitHub API instead of the previous `gh`/mutable-URL fallback. Asset URLs use one validated version tag.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.** No credentials are required or added.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.**
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Downloads stay on the existing GitHub release boundary. Missing or invalid verification data fails closed. A checksum is not a signature: this does not protect against an attacker who can replace both the archive and its manifest.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No for the former automatic fallback and standalone copies of `setup.bat`.** Valid prebuilt archives install as before.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No new installer flags or application configuration.**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- Exact upgrade steps: Keep `setup.bat` with `scripts/install_windows_prebuilt.ps1` from the same checkout or unpacked source archive, or use the self-contained PowerShell guide. If a prebuilt download or checksum fails, select `--dist` explicitly to build from source. The existing `setup.bat` Rust prerequisite is unchanged.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the landed commit through a reviewed PR. This restores the unverified Windows extraction paths; use a source build while a replacement fix is reviewed.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `SHA256 mismatch`, a missing/invalid `SHA256SUMS` entry, a download error or a missing helper causes an error before installation. `setup.bat` prints `Setup failed` and returns 1.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A. This does not supersede another PR.

prs.title: feat(runtime): let the operator override an exceeded cost limit
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `cost.allow_override` was documented but read by nothing, so an exceeded shared limit always failed the turn and the only way on was a daemon restart. With it on, the main tool loop now pauses before a provider call that would exceed the shared daily or monthly limit and asks through the turn's approval channel (`tool_name = cost_limit_override`, exported as `COST_LIMIT_OVERRIDE_APPROVAL`). Deny, no answer within 10 minutes, or a channel that cannot ask stops the turn exactly as before. ZeroCode and Telegram wait the full 10 minutes; ACP waits the shorter of 10 minutes and `acp.session_timeout_secs`, because the ACP channel uses the trait's default timeout; other chat channels keep their own `approval_timeout_secs` (300 s by default), so there the shorter wait applies.
  - Approval calls `CostTracker::grant_override`, which records the override for the current UTC day or month on state shared by every derived tracker, so one answer covers every session and delegation of the daemon. `check_budget` skips that limit (and its warning) while the stored period matches, so it expires on its own at rollover. Per-hop and per-agent ceilings still bind, and `grant_override` refuses when `allow_override` is off.
  - The grant is kept in memory only. It ends at the next UTC day or month rollover, or when the daemon restarts, and a restart restores enforcement. Nothing is written to `state/cost-overrides.json`; a file left by an earlier build is ignored.
  - A turn waiting on its own prompt also watches for a grant from another session (a `watch` channel on the tracker). When one arrives it drops its request and continues. `RpcApprovalChannel` sends a new `session/update` type, `approval_withdrawn` (`request_id`), for any approval that ends without an answer from its client, and ZeroCode takes that prompt down. Before this, approving in one session left the same prompt up in the other, and that turn stopped at the 10-minute timeout although the limit was already lifted.
  - `RpcApprovalChannel` and `AskUserApprovalBridge` now implement `request_approval_attributed_with_timeout`. The trait default wrapped `request_approval_attributed`, whose own 120 s deadline fired first, so the 10-minute wait would have been cut short.
  - ZeroCode renders a `cost_limit_override` approval as a centred, bold red notice with Override and Stop buttons instead of the tool card. Only Override or Stop (key or click) closes it. If the daemon refuses the answer (for example `FORBIDDEN`), the notice comes back with the error so the user can answer again; a timeout shows the error without bringing the notice back, because the daemon may already have the answer.
- **Scope boundary:** no warning at `warn_at_percent` (#10950) and no notice for a turn that stops with no override possible; both need a daemon-to-client budget event this PR does not add. `cost.enforcement.mode` stays unread. Applying `config/set` limit changes to the live tracker is #11587.
- **Holding-crate exception:** the #11589 row in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` covers `src/agent/{approval_bridge,cost}.rs`, `src/agent/turn/{approval_gate,mod,provider_call}.rs`, `src/rpc/approval_channel.rs` and `locales/en/cli.ftl`. It doesn't yet cover the RPC enforcement adapter in `src/rpc/{context,dispatch,local}.rs`, or the attribution-only edits in `src/agent/agent.rs`, `src/daemon/mod.rs` and `src/integrations/registry.rs`. The ancestry, admission and binding rules themselves live in `zeroclaw-config` (`cost::override_grant`). A row amendment that covers these files and states the memory-only grant is drafted on fork branch `docs/runtime-exception-11589` (`e7868ca2a`, on `master` `1c1cd118a`). Like #11697, it needs its own Core Team-approved PR; this PR can't grant it.
- **Blast radius:** turns that hit a shared limit with `allow_override = true` now wait for an answer instead of failing, on any channel that answers approvals (ZeroCode, ACP, Telegram inline buttons). The approval bridge's timeout plumbing is used only by callers that pass a budget; tool approvals are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11585
- **Labels:** (set after open)

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can stop the agent when spending passes a daily or monthly limit. There was a setting meant to let you go past the limit, but nothing used it: once the limit tripped, every message failed, and the only way to continue was to raise the limit and restart, which closes every open session.

Now, with that setting on, the agent pauses when it reaches the limit and ZeroCode shows a red box asking whether to keep going. Say yes and the same task carries on, and the limit stays lifted until the day (or month) ends or the daemon restarts. If several sessions were waiting at the limit, one yes lets all of them continue. Say no, or leave it for ten minutes, and the task stops as it does today. Chat apps that cannot show the question, and scheduled jobs, still stop at the limit.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` `tui` (ZeroCode Code tab over RPC)
- **Setup / preconditions:** `[cost] enabled = true`, `allow_override = true`, `daily_limit_usd` just above today's recorded spend.
- **Steps to run:** in ZeroCode, run a prompt that makes a few model calls until spend passes the limit. When the red notice appears, click Override. Then open a second session and send a prompt. Separately: get two sessions waiting on the notice at once and Override in one; and restart the daemon after an Override and send a prompt.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the first turn pauses on the red notice and continues after Override; the second session is not asked again; with two waiting, the other notice closes and its turn continues; after a daemon restart the limit is enforced again and the next turn asks again. With Stop instead, the turn ends with the budget error.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the turn fails with `Budget exceeded: ... Cannot make further API calls until the budget resets.`, there is no prompt, and every later turn fails until a restart.

### How I tested

- **Authority recheck after the peer lookup (head `5d2ca670b747`):** `session/approve` for a cost-override prompt now rechecks the admitted session, the caller's current `SessionApprove` grants and ownership, and the pending request's session binding after the peer-process lookup. It holds the authority lease through delivery, so no await sits between the last check and `resolve_from_operator`. A caller who lost `sessions:update` during the lookup gets `FORBIDDEN`, the prompt stays pending and no override is granted. New tests: `rpc::dispatch::tests::cost_override_approve_rechecks_authority_after_peer_lookup` pauses the lookup, revokes the grant and checks for no approval and no grant. `cost_override_approve_accepts_unchanged_authority_after_peer_lookup` is the control: the approval is acknowledged and the real budget gate grants the override. With only the test commit applied to `ab919d606c`, the revocation test fails (the old handler answers `acknowledged: true`) and the control passes. On this head, through the local cargo wrapper: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib` → `5902 passed; 2 failed`, the two being the `relay::local_dial_tests` loopback-stall tests that also fail on the base; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --test '*'` → all 15 integration binaries pass.
```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check   # rustfmt --edition 2024 on the changed files
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib cost::tracker
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib budget_override
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib approval_
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- budget_override_tests rpc::approval_channel
cargo test -p zerocode --bins -- approval parse_approval cost_limit

cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode approval

```

Clippy `-D warnings` clean on `zeroclaw-channels` and `zeroclaw-runtime`; channels `approval_typing abandoned_approval approval_wait_resumes unsupported_approval_resumes` 5 passed; rustfmt and the comment hygiene gate pass.

Older local runs on `225c52bb636f` (master `f12da7462a0f`, remote macOS arm64 builder). ## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (grants are memory-only; no new file is written)
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The override is off by default and only an operator answer grants it; a runtime timeout or unreachable client does not.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. With `allow_override = false` (the default) behaviour is unchanged.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: one new key, `channels.telegram.<alias>.cost_override_operators` (numeric Telegram user IDs allowed to override in group chats; defaults to empty, which denies group overrides; no wildcards or usernames). Also one new RPC `session/update` type, `approval_withdrawn`, which older clients ignore; `allow_override` now does what its docs say, and the docs are corrected.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): reopen open sessions when zerocode restarts
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - zerocode's sidebar list of open sessions lived only in memory. The daemon keeps every transcript, but quitting zerocode lost which sessions were open, so each launch started from an empty sidebar.
  - The list (session ids, agent aliases, order, focus, and the last Chat/Code pane on screen) is now saved whenever it changes, as an owner-only JSON file per connection target under `<config-dir>/open-sessions/`.
  - At launch the saved list goes to the existing reconnect resume path (`set_resume_sessions`), so restored sessions reattach by id exactly as they do after a daemon reconnect: focused first, the rest in the background.
  - On by default (`[sidebar] restore_sessions = true`). `zerocode --fresh` starts one launch with an empty sidebar and still saves its own list.
  - Each zerocode window on a daemon keeps its own list in a numbered slot, held by an OS file lock. A window takes the lowest free slot, so closing a second window and opening it again while the first runs reopens the second window's sessions. At restore, sessions another running window has in its list are skipped with a notice. Without that, two windows would reattach the same live session, and either window could cancel the other's turn. That stale-session and multi-tab hazard is why #8911 (silent auto-resume, for #8653) was closed in favour of the #8922 picker. The lock is released when the owning window exits, including on a crash.
  - Each window publishes the list it is about to reopen before its panes start (an empty list on `--fresh`), so other windows never judge by the previous occupant's stale list.
  - Saved Code sessions the daemon no longer lists, and saved Chat sessions with no stored history (for example deleted), are dropped with one notice.
  - When the daemon refuses to reattach a restored session because this terminal's environment differs from the one the session started in (FORBIDDEN `-32012`, "Session environment differs" or "Session retains a local operator environment"), the entry stays where it was, with the same order and focus. Its pane shows a translated notice that the saved session can't be reattached from this terminal environment and that the daemon still keeps the old conversation, plus an explicit "start a new conversation" action (the existing new-session key, Ctrl+N by default). Only that action opens a fresh session in the same slot, with the same agent and mode, and the saved list then tracks the new id. If creating it fails, the refused entry and its notice stay. Switching from the notice to another session moves the refused entry to the background, and closing it while a live session is focused closes only that row, so the live session stays on screen. Nothing is replaced automatically, other errors behave as before, and the daemon's environment check is unchanged.
  - Fully resuming the old conversation in that case is left to upstream #11921 (history persistence so tasks can resume after restart).
  - Local daemon connections only. Over WSS the daemon admits a resume only from the client identity that owns the session (`capture_session_access`), and a relaunched window connects with a new one, so a saved remote list could only produce failed rows. Reclaiming a remote identity per window slot is a follow-up.
- **Scope boundary:** Local connections only; remote (`--connect`) windows are unchanged. Client only (`apps/zerocode`); no daemon, RPC or runtime change. Queued messages, unsent drafts and attachments are not saved. A turn that was running when zerocode quit is not resumed or rerun.
- **Blast radius:** zerocode startup (one extra `session/list-acp` call and/or one `session/messages` probe per saved Chat session on a local connection when a saved list exists) and the per-frame sidebar derivation (a cheap comparison; the file is written only when the list changes, and never while disconnected).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8653, #8911, #8922.

### What this does, simply

When you quit zerocode and start it again, the sessions you had open in the sidebar come back: same order, same one focused, on the pane you were using. The conversations themselves were always kept by the daemon. What was lost was the list of which ones you had open. If a saved session has since been deleted, it is skipped with a short notice. If a saved session can't be reattached from the terminal you relaunched in, it stays in its place with a notice and an option to start a new conversation there. Each zerocode window keeps its own list: close a second window and open it again, and it gets its own sessions back. A session already open in another window is not opened twice. Use `zerocode --fresh` to start one launch with an empty sidebar, or set `restore_sessions = false` under `[sidebar]` to turn the feature off.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `tui` (zerocode Chat and Code panes)
- **Setup / preconditions:** A local daemon with at least two agents.
- **Steps to run:** Open two Code sessions and one Chat session from the sidebar, focus the second Code session, quit zerocode, start it again. Then quit and start once more with `zerocode --fresh`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** With one `zerocode` open, open a second window, add a session there, close it and reopen it: it comes back with that session, and the first window is unchanged. The second launch opens on the Code pane with the same three sidebar rows in the same order and the second Code session focused, transcripts loaded. The `--fresh` launch starts with an empty sidebar.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Every launch starts with an empty sidebar (or the recent-session picker); the previous launch's open sessions must be reopened one by one.

### How I tested

- **Current head:** `214a73cc5` (`8628b342c` plus the fix for Greptile 4429702542: if switching from a refused restore notice to another retained session fails, the refused entry stays focused, so its notice and "start a new conversation" still work). Linux x86_64, rustc 1.98.0, in its own target dir (the log shows zerocode compiled from this tree): `cargo test --locked -p zerocode --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4` → library 52 passed; binary 1,599 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored, including the new `chat::tests::a_failed_switch_from_a_refused_notice_keeps_the_refused_entry_focused` (Chat and Code panes). `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` are clean.
- **Previous head:** `8628b342c` (the fix for Greptile 4429144032: closing a refused restore row after switching to a live session no longer replaces that session; test `closing_a_refused_entry_after_switching_away_keeps_the_working_session`).
- **Previous head:** `b8f816f436`, a merge of master `1c1cd118a` into `d05cdf055c`. The merge conflicted only in `apps/zerocode/src/chat.rs`: master added `cleanup_notice` to `ResumeEntry` and this branch added `environment_refused`, so the struct and its constructors keep both fields. On a Linux x86_64 build host (rustc 1.99.1): `cargo test --locked -p zerocode -- --test-threads=4` → library 52 passed; binary 1,596 passed, 1 failed (the known `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`); `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passed.
- **Previous tested revision:** `d05cdf055cb2a9a61f343643619abe730dc78b4c` on the Mac mini, with the results below.
- **Formatting:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passed.
- **Clippy:** `cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
- **Package suite:** `cargo test -p zerocode`, through `zc-cargo-narrow` with `-j2` for compilation and two test threads: library 54 passed; binary 1,600 passed, 1 failed (the known failure below). The TestBackend evidence-frame tests were removed in this revision; the behaviour tests stay.
- **Deleted-Chat regressions (new or updated, all pass):** `open_sessions::tests::deleted_chat_session_is_skipped_at_restore`, `open_sessions::tests::chat_sessions_survive_startup_without_a_complete_daemon_listing`, `open_sessions::tests::chat_restore_drops_only_the_specific_missing_session_refusal`, `open_sessions::tests::mixed_restore_prunes_code_by_list_and_chat_by_history_in_order`. Each saved Chat entry is probed with `session/messages` (limit 1): no stored history, or the daemon's "Session not found or not owned by this principal" refusal, drops it with the existing notice; any other error keeps it for the normal resume path. I ran the first test against `409b7725ef` and it fails there (`dropped` is 0, expected 1), because that head kept every saved Chat ID.
- **Environment-refusal regressions (all pass):** `chat::tests::focused_restored_environment_refusal_keeps_slot_focus_and_notice`, `chat::tests::background_restored_environment_refusal_keeps_slot_and_opens_notice_on_focus`, `chat::tests::restored_environment_refusal_new_conversation_replaces_only_the_selected_slot`, `chat::tests::failed_refused_session_replacement_keeps_saved_id_and_notice`, `chat::tests::unrelated_forbidden_restore_keeps_existing_error_behaviour`, `chat::tests::session_picker_environment_refusal_keeps_selected_entry_and_notice`, `chat::tests::chat_entry_retry_adopts_restored_environment_refusal_action`, `chat::tests::restored_environment_refusal_requires_typed_code_and_specific_message`. On `c4f45eb508` the focused-refusal case promotes the background session over the refused one and shows no notice, so the first test's focus and notice assertions fail there.
- **Known failures:** `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` also fails on clean master `f2b432db` on this Mini (it passes when run alone). `app::tests::input_wait_returns_early_for_pending_transport_events` is a known timing flake (it passed in this run).

prs.title: feat(runtime): show a foreground delegate's tool calls in the parent turn
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A foreground agentic delegate ran its tool loop with an inert observer, so while it worked the parent turn, the RPC stream and ZeroCode showed nothing until the child answered. A long delegate looked the same whether it was working, looping or stuck.
  - Each tool execution in a turn that streams events now scopes the turn's event sender and the call id (`agent/tool_execution.rs`, next to #11298's cancellation scope). A foreground agentic delegate gives its child loop an observer (`tools/delegate_activity.rs`) that turns each child tool start and finish into one new live turn event, `TurnEvent::DelegateActivity` in `zeroclaw-api`: the tool name, a secret-redacted argument summary (`approval::summarize_args`), and a 400-character output preview of the already-scrubbed result. Parallel workers carry the scope across their spawn. A delegate inside the child reports one level deeper (`depth`) against the same parent call.
  - The observer sends with `try_send`, so a full parent channel drops activity instead of slowing the child or the parent turn.
  - RPC forwards it as a `delegate_activity` `session/update` (`rpc/{dispatch,types}.rs`). ZeroCode shows a child-call count and the running tool under the delegate card, and the call list when the card is expanded.
  - A tool's own `approved` input is left out of child summaries: under a successful call, `approved: false` read as a refusal.
  - While the delegate's turn runs, its card's Response line now says "Waiting for response" instead of "Result not recorded". The card only says that for a call this pane saw start in the running turn; restored history and calls a finished or cancelled turn left without a result keep the neutral wording from #11446.
- **Scope boundary:** no persistence: the event isn't written to the turn checkpoint or session history, so restored sessions look as before. Background delegates don't forward (their turn may be gone; #11292's `check_result` progress covers them). The child's text, reasoning, usage and approvals aren't forwarded. No config key and no opt-in. Other channels (ACP server, gateway WS, chat channels) ignore the new variant through their existing fall-through arms.
- **Blast radius:** the tool-execution scope wraps every tool's `execute` when the turn streams events, but only the delegate tool reads it. Foreground agentic delegates now run with a forwarding observer instead of the no-op one. RPC clients get a new `session/update` type; older ZeroCode builds ignore it.
- **Linked issue(s):** Part of #10531 (its observer-forwarding piece; #11292 shipped the first piece). Related #8763 (live half of the ZeroCode subagent view), #11446 (the neutral wording kept for restored cards). Holding-crate exception row: #11697 (merged).

### What this does, simply

When one agent hands work to a helper agent and waits for the answer, you used to see nothing until the helper was done. Now the waiting card in ZeroCode shows how many tools the helper has used and which one it's running right now, and expanding the card lists each of them. Only the tool names and a short, secret-stripped summary of each call are shown, never the helper's full inputs or outputs. Nothing is saved; reopening the session shows the card as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`: I ran it live in the experiment build; the tests below drive the delegate path end to end with a scripted provider.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Chat with an agent that has an agentic delegate target.

### How I tested

```bash
zc-cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings
zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- tools::delegate agent::tool_execution rpc::dispatch::tests::delegate rpc::types
zc-cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" zc-cargo doc -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-runtime --no-deps
rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <changed files>
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Test and Parallel Runtime Test run the new runtime and ZeroCode tests; Lint covers clippy, rustdoc and comment hygiene; Docs Style covers the `rpc-socket.md` addition.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no test drives a real daemon and ZeroCode together; the RPC mapping and the ZeroCode handler are tested on each side of the wire.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Latest local run on `9f3090ee37` (the head `db3d91e2f9` since then only removes TestBackend evidence tests): fmt and clippy clean; `zeroclaw-runtime` + `zerocode` suites 7916 passed, 3 failed: `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` and two `relay::local_dial_tests` tests, which fail on master on the same machine. CI Required Gate green on `db3d91e2f9`. @tidux's points are fixed in `563ed8555` (id-less results paired by arguments), `c6fb85a71` (reused child ids, neutral unfinished rows) and `035aa48f4` (checkpoint-exclusion test, `output_preview` documented in `rpc-socket.md`). Earlier run: clippy clean (exit 0). Runtime filter: `318 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored`. ZeroCode: `1459 passed; 1 failed` — the failure is `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, which also fails on master on the machine I ran it on. Rustdoc exit 0, fmt clean, hygiene gate passed, docs gate `0 error(s)`.
- New tests:
  - `foreground_agentic_delegate_reports_child_tool_calls_to_the_parent_turn`: a scripted agentic child calls `echo_tool`; the parent sink gets exactly one start and one finish with the parent call id, agent, child call id, a summary and an `echo:` preview.
  - `background_delegate_does_not_report_to_the_parent_turn`: same child with a progress sink (the background shape) runs its tool and sends nothing to the parent.
  - `tools_see_the_parent_event_sink_only_in_a_streaming_turn`: the scope is visible inside `execute` with the call id, absent without an event sender, and gone afterwards.
  - `delegate_activity::tests`: secret argument redacted, preview bounded, id-less calls get one id shared by start and finish, a full parent channel drops instead of blocking.
  - `delegate_activity_notification_is_flat_and_round_trips` (RPC), `parses_delegate_activity_update` and `delegate_card_shows_child_activity_while_running_and_keeps_it_after` (ZeroCode).
  - `subagent_card_says_waiting_only_while_its_turn_runs`: a live delegate card says "Waiting for response"; after its turn settles without a result it says "Result not recorded". The existing `subagent_card_restored_missing_result_does_not_claim_live_work` passes unchanged.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Swapping the forwarder back to the no-op observer makes the foreground test fail and leaves the background one passing; forcing the card's waiting flag off makes the waiting test fail. Both restored afterwards. Live run in the experiment build ([branch](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d), dogfood base `0341618f9d69`): a foreground delegate to another agent running four slow read-only tool calls; the parent's card counted the calls, showed the running one, said "Waiting for response" until the child answered, and kept the list afterwards.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Screenshot`: real macOS Terminal.app captures of the current head `db3d91e2f9`, at https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11730#issuecomment-6534712777
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Tests: `9f3090ee37` (above) and CI on `db3d91e2f9`. Interface: ZeroCode TUI, debug build of `db3d91e2f9` (daemon and ZeroCode from the same build), captured in https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11730#issuecomment-6534712777. Earlier captures from experiment build [20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d) are in 6232092560.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11730#issuecomment-6534712777 (current head `db3d91e2f9`; earlier: 6232092560)
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** asked the agent to delegate in the foreground to a helper agent that runs several slow tool calls. While it runs, the card shows the call count, the running tool and "Waiting for response"; expanded, it lists each call with its redacted summary; after the helper answers, the list stays and the result replaces the waiting line.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full `zeroclaw-runtime` suite; I ran the delegate, tool-execution and RPC-type filters, which hold every test touching the changed code.

### Screenshots

Real screenshots of the current head `db3d91e2f9`: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11730#issuecomment-6534712777 (the delegate is running with live child-call counts, and the card expands to the child call list). Earlier captures from the experiment build: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11730#issuecomment-6232092560.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. Child arguments go through the same redacting summarizer as approval prompts, and the output preview comes from the result the loop has already credential-scrubbed. Tested with an `api_key` argument.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The activity goes to the client only; it never enters a model request. ZeroCode renders it through the existing terminal-safe text path.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: n/a

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. The `session/update` type is additive; older clients fall through their unknown-type arms.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

prs.title: feat(tools): add opt-in subprocess memory watchdog
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add `runtime_profiles.<alias>.shell_max_memory_mb`, measured in MiB and disabled by default, for native shell and skill subprocesses.
  - Sample the command's resident memory plus its visible descendants. Stop the owned command group or Windows Job Object when a sample exceeds the threshold, and return a failed `ToolResult` with the threshold and observed memory.
  - Share the existing capped-output execution path between shell and skill tools. Stop the command on monitoring failure, preserve capped partial output with truncation markers, and bound cleanup waiting after timeout or failure.
  - Check zero RSS readings through the operating system's process API. Accept a confirmed zero for the same observed process identity and skip descendants confirmed to have exited after the snapshot. Unreadable live processes and incomplete responses remain monitoring errors.
  - Carry the threshold through the existing runtime-profile policy. Explicit child policies cannot raise or disable a finite parent threshold.
- **Scope boundary:** No `RLIMIT_AS`, default memory cap, hard allocation ceiling, cgroup implementation, or guarantee against host OOM. Detached or reparented processes can escape sampling. Docker keeps its existing container memory controls.
- **Blast radius:** Native shell and skill execution, runtime-profile policy construction, explicit child-policy validation, and Windows process ownership. Existing tool admission, environment filtering, and sandbox authorization remain in place.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #6916. The original strict OOM-prevention requirements remain open. #7937 introduced the earlier implementation, which #8417 reverted; this PR uses resident-memory sampling instead of restoring it.
- **Runtime placement:** The bounded native shell/skill RSS scope was approved by @tidux and recorded in merged #11436. Merged #11697 widens its catalogue coverage to all five locale files used here.

### What this does, simply

The shell and skill tools let an agent run programs on your machine. Their timeout and output cap limit how long a command runs and how much text ZeroClaw stores, but they do not limit the memory used by the program itself.

This adds an optional watcher. You choose a memory threshold in the agent's runtime profile. While its command runs, ZeroClaw samples the physical memory used by that command and its visible children. If the total crosses the threshold, ZeroClaw stops the owned command group and tells the agent why it failed. A zero reading is checked directly with the operating system so an unavailable measurement is not mistaken for no memory use. A child that exits between the snapshot and that check no longer causes an otherwise healthy command to be stopped. If output was capped before a command failed, its partial output says it was truncated.

The watcher is off unless configured. It reacts after observing memory use, so a command can exceed the threshold between samples. It does not reserve memory, impose a kernel allocation ceiling, or guarantee that an out-of-memory event cannot happen. Virtual-address reservations alone do not count, avoiding the earlier virtual-memory-limit approach.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

Both tool entry points need the same child ownership, bounded output capture, timeout, and memory-failure handling. Sharing the existing shell runner avoids implementing those lifecycles twice. The new sampler uses the existing `sysinfo` dependency; Windows containment and failed-spawn cleanup reuse the existing `process-wrap` dependency and service guard.

The essential new work is per-command process ancestry and RSS sampling, plus platform-specific ownership on Windows. Three small native readers resolve zero readings without adding another process cache or dependency. They compare the returned process identity at the existing whole-second precision; this does not eliminate every descendant PID-reuse race. There is no global process cache, new dependency, polling scheduler, or sandbox backend. Sampling runs about every 100 ms plus observation time. Its metadata work scales with host process count and concurrent monitored commands; disabled monitoring starts no sampler. Shared resident pages may count more than once.

Monitoring follows the root command's lifetime. On Windows, dropping the enabled command's owner explicitly terminates its Job Object before closing the handle, stopping remaining job descendants even after root completion. Non-native runtimes, Docker sandboxes, and unsupported operating systems reject an enabled watchdog before spawning; Docker deployments should use their existing container memory limits.

The bounded runtime placement exception is recorded by merged #11436.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Focused tests spawn real subprocesses and exercise resident allocation, descendant aggregation, virtual reservation, and tool-result conversion without requiring a provider or changing a live agent's configuration.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Required CI](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38010558146) passes on `73db3b5cae818a5d45d9f5676f69643d8ee48007`, including Linux Test, Parallel Runtime Test, Lint, Format, Windows compilation and task-owner recovery. The same head ran in [hosted macOS](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39163181716/job/117780719339) and [hosted Windows](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39163181716/job/117780719366) jobs. All 12 macOS and 11 Windows subprocess-memory tests passed, including `descendant_departure_after_snapshot_is_not_a_monitor_failure` and `failed_native_read_does_not_accept_sysinfo_zero` on both platforms, the complete native-record check on macOS, and `root_exit_closes_owned_job_descendants` on Windows. Both platforms also pass the resident-memory tool diagnostic, shell/skill container rejection and policy non-escalation tests. macOS passes terminal detachment, timeout/cancellation descendant cleanup and all three truncation tests. Both hosted jobs ran `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-fail-fast`.
- **Current head `de78ac7c0f81`** (`73db3b5ca`, a clean merge of `master` `1c1cd118a`, and `de78ac7c0`): the new commit is documentation only. It adds one sentence to the `shell_max_memory_mb` doc comment and to `docs/book/src/tools/python-skills.md`. The sentence says that on macOS a command that starts a descendant under another user (`sudo`, a setuid helper) is stopped with a monitoring failure, because that process's memory can't be read. On Linux x86_64, `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-config --lib` gave `5910 passed; 0 failed; 9 ignored` for runtime and `1819 passed; 0 failed` for config. `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-api --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean. CI for this head is pending. The Security job may fail on the new wasmtime advisories (RUSTSEC-2026-0420 to 0424) until #12129 lands.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The new departure regression has now executed on both macOS and Windows at the current head. The full platform suites remain red: macOS ran 19,490 tests with 19,484 passed, six failed and 39 skipped; Windows ran 19,043 tests with 19,034 passed, nine failed and 36 skipped. The six macOS failures exactly match the [earlier macOS run](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38000741090/job/114058025862), covering Telegram prompt timing, a filesystem spelling fixture, Hailo-Ollama and Serply connection classification, RPC session-method grants and Tailscale probe timing. No clean-master macOS execution baseline was run. The nine Windows failures exactly match both the [earlier Windows run](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38000741090/job/114058025868) and the [clean-master Windows run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37880263821/job/113658218149). The previously identified fixes in #11361, #11362, #11363, #11365, #11366 and #11630 remain separate from this branch.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

The integrated head `73db3b5cae818a5d45d9f5676f69643d8ee48007` passes the focused macOS watchdog, terminal-detachment and descendant-cleanup checks:

```text
cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -E 'test(tools::subprocess_memory::tests) | test(shell_child_cannot_open_owners_controlling_terminal) | test(shell_reaps_descendants_after_timeout_or_cancellation)' --test-threads=1
Summary: 14 tests run, 14 passed.

cargo fmt --all -- --check
Passed.

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.

git diff --check
Passed.
```

The departure repair at `a42774653cd4f1458707854863228f3e5d6594ef` passes the focused macOS watchdog suite, formatting, diff integrity and comment hygiene:

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::subprocess_memory::tests -- --test-threads=1
12 passed; 0 failed on macOS, including descendant departure and live read-failure controls.

```

The following results are from earlier implementation and repair candidates:

```text

11 passed; 0 failed on the repaired candidate.

cargo fmt --all
Passed on the repaired candidate.

Earlier implementation validation:
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- from_profiles_ ensure_no_escalation_
27 passed; 0 failed.

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- tools::subprocess_memory:: tools::shell::tests:: tools::skill_tool::tests::
110 passed; 0 failed; completed in 2.86 seconds after compilation.

cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime
Passed.

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.

git diff --check
Passed.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source comparison confirms that shell and skill tools use the same runner, enabled monitoring is rejected before unsupported execution, and bounded delegates retain their parent-owned tool policy. No real-account or live-agent exercise was needed for the subprocess contract.
- **Build warning:** The macOS linker reported that the debug test executable's `__eh_frame` section exceeds its 16 MiB compact-unwind encoding limit. All selected tests completed. Existing clean-master validation also records this linker warning; no new source warning was reported.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. This changes subprocess enforcement rather than visual presentation. The shell regression observes the returned failed tool result and memory diagnostic.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Head `de78ac7c0f81` (the macOS evidence below ran at `73db3b5ca`, and later commits change only docs and the `master` merge); native subprocess execution and `ToolResult`, exercised by `tools::subprocess_memory::tests`, `tools::shell::tests`, `tools::skill_tool::tests`, and the config policy tests.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `shell_memory_failure_surfaces_resident_cause` checks that the failed tool result identifies the resident-memory threshold.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The process fixtures distinguish touched resident pages from a large untouched virtual reservation, aggregate two descendants, and preserve completion when monitoring is disabled or memory stays below the threshold. Focused regressions distinguish successful zero measurements from failed reads and identity changes, and confirm truncation markers on both captured streams after a timeout. The departure regression discovers a live child, deliberately kills and reaps it before the native fallback, and confirms that sampling continues; its live-process read-denial control remains an error. The integrated master regressions confirm the child cannot open its owner's controlling terminal and descendants stop after timeout or cancellation. Policy tests parse the setting and reject child escalation.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No duplicate local full-workspace run. Hosted macOS and Windows execution now covers the changed native process paths on the current head, alongside the focused local macOS checks and required Linux CI. The remaining full-platform failures are recorded above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Memory failure adds a localized diagnostic to the existing tool result. Its threshold and RSS values are numeric, and it grants no authority. Existing command output remains untrusted and capped.
- **Risk and mitigation:** A configured watchdog can stop a legitimate memory-heavy command. Shared pages can inflate the total, and polling can miss short spikes. Only owned process groups or Job Objects are signaled; sampled descendant PIDs are never termination targets. Samples remain in memory for the invocation and are not persisted.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for existing configuration. The new setting defaults to `0`. Sharing the shell runner also bounds skill output during collection and applies owned-process cleanup on skill timeout or cancellation.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. Adds `runtime_profiles.<alias>.shell_max_memory_mb`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Set the selected runtime profile's `shell_max_memory_mb` to `0` and recreate the affected agent/session. Revert the merge commit to remove the implementation and shared skill-runner change entirely.

N/A. This does not supersede an open PR or incorporate contributor code from the reverted implementation.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): refresh the focused session without cancellation
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Add F5 to refresh the focused Code or Chat session through the existing read-only session APIs. Keep local drafts, attachments, queues and interactions instead of invoking cancel-first recovery. Retain selection and reading position when their transcript entries still match; refuse replacement when they do not.
- **Scope boundary:** No polling, cancellation, automatic retries, cross-client streaming, new RPC method, authorization change or persistence migration.
- **Blast radius:** Shared ZeroCode Chat/ACP key handling, transcript projection and cached rendering. The daemon and other clients are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Refs #10695. This implements the manual-refresh slice.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `risk:medium`, `size:XL`, `zerocode`, `docs`.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode lets you keep several agent conversations open. Another authorized client can send a message to one of those sessions, but the already-open pane can keep showing its older transcript. Closing and reopening the session reloads it, at the cost of disrupting the local view.

With this change, press F5 in Code or Chat to read the focused session again. A completed exchange returned by the daemon is added to the view without sending another prompt or cancelling a turn. Your unsent draft, attachments and queued messages stay in the pane. If the session is busy, the read fails, or selected content cannot be matched safely, the existing view stays available with a notice.

This is an explicit, point-in-time refresh. It does not stream another client's response or keep the pane synchronized in the background.

Refresh rebuilds the stored transcript. Local-only transcript rows, such as notices, can disappear.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The daemon remains the history owner. Both panes use the existing shared Chat action and history projection. Most of the remaining client work matches transcript entries and preserves reading/selection anchors; calling recovery or resetting the pane would discard state that #10695 requires retaining. The diff also includes focused preservation regressions. Append-only histories reuse the existing rendered prefix. No new runtime or transport owner is introduced.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. I ran the two-client smoke myself (below); an independent run is welcome.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, Code/ACP and Chat.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Run this branch's ZeroCode against a compatible daemon. Open a harmless dedicated session and keep it focused. A second authorized RPC client must be able to resume that same session.
- **Steps to run:** Leave an unsent draft and a paused queued message in the pane. From the second client, submit a harmless prompt to the same session and wait for completion. Select unchanged text in the existing pane, then press F5. Also press F5 once while the second client still has a turn running.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The completed exchange appears after refresh; the local draft, attachment ownership, paused queue, selection and reading position remain. Refresh during a running turn reports busy without cancellation.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** F5 has no focused-session refresh action. The already-open transcript can remain stale until the session is reopened.

### How I tested

Run on head `204ca052d` (Linux x86_64, Rust 1.98.0, the CI toolchain):

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                   ok
cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings   ok
cargo test --locked -p zerocode
  zerocode (lib)       52 passed; 0 failed
  zerocode (bin)       1566 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored  (10 session_refresh tests pass)
  terminal_disconnect  3 passed
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh          Comment hygiene gate passed.
bash scripts/ci/zerocode_no_zeroclaw_dep_gate.sh zerocode gate passed: no zeroclaw-* implementation dependencies.
```

The one failure, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, also fails on clean `master` on these machines and is not touched by this PR.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [`CI Required Gate`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40932393331) passed on the current head `204ca052d`: Formatting, Lint, workspace Test, ZeroCode RPC-only, MSRV and platform checks.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** The focused suite drives the real Chat action, RPC request sequence, asynchronous result application and production renderer with controlled daemon responses. It does not submit a turn through a second real client or exercise daemon persistence.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** A live two-client run on the current head `204ca052d` (Linux, daemon and both clients from one debug build, local stub provider; [manifest](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/blob/evidence-screenshots/pr-11457/live-204ca052d/MANIFEST.txt)). Client B resumed client A's session and completed a turn. F5 in A then imported that exchange and kept the unsent draft and the `notes.txt` attachment. F5 while B's slow turn was running showed the busy notice and left the transcript unchanged. That turn completed without being cancelled, and a second F5 imported it. Earlier, a two-client smoke on the experiment build [`20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d`](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d) ([commit](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/af67956b5e9d1b9a9f0521dab4a1f48c999d6e71); dogfood base [`0341618f9d69`](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/0341618f9d69e31bf38300d134ba86e98491d49d), which carries this change). A second client submitted a prompt to the focused session; F5 in the open pane imported the completed exchange and kept the unsent draft and attachment. F5 while the second client's turn was running showed the busy notice, and that turn completed normally without cancellation. I did not separately exercise the paused-queue or selection/reading-position cases live; the automated tests cover them. The tests cover preserved draft attachments, paused queue and selection, busy/failed/stale reads, pending interactions, removed or inserted selected rows, ACP enrichment and sent attachments, first-plan visibility, durable ACP recovery-notice anchors, and an append to 900 transcript entries.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real captures of the current head: [before refresh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11457/live-204ca052d/R03-clientA-before-F5.png), [after F5](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11457/live-204ca052d/R04-clientA-after-F5-imports-exchange-keeps-draft.png), [busy notice](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11457/live-204ca052d/R06-clientA-F5-while-busy-notice.png), [second client's turn not cancelled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11457/live-204ca052d/R07-clientB-turn-completed-uncancelled.png), and [after a second F5](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11457/live-204ca052d/R08-clientA-F5-after-completion.png). All eight are listed in the [manifest](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/blob/evidence-screenshots/pr-11457/live-204ca052d/MANIFEST.txt). The earlier experiment-build screenshots are in [this comment](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11457#issuecomment-6232350070).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Current head `204ca052d1a975cfe0269fc43b010539b93de2c9`: the tests above, plus the live two-client Chat run over local RPC (xfce4-terminal at 120×34, ffmpeg x11grab captures of the real windows).
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** See Visual interface evidence. After F5, the status line reads "Session refreshed. Local draft and queued messages were kept." While the other client's turn runs, it reads "This session is busy. Nothing was cancelled. Refresh again when the turn finishes."
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The automated F5 test imports a controlled completed exchange and observes its answer after final rendering while retaining local transient state.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Broad local workspace tests and platform builds are deferred to exact-head CI. Documentation translation refresh is deferred to the normal catalog pass; new application keys fall back to embedded English.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No new endpoint or destination; refresh invokes existing authorized read-only session calls.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. Refresh does not submit transcript content to the model.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Uses existing `session/state` and `session/messages` responses.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? The TUI adds the remappable `chat.refresh_session` keybinding action, bound to F5 by default. No environment or CLI change.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: No migration or daemon restart required for this client-only change; run the updated ZeroCode binary.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this commit or run the previous ZeroCode binary.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Refresh runs only when its action is invoked.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** F5 fails to import a completed exchange, loses local state, changes selected text, or reports a refresh error. The refusal path keeps the previous transcript. Refresh sends only existing session-read requests; it does not submit prompts or cancellation requests.

## Supersede Attribution

Not applicable. No PR is superseded.

prs.title: fix(zerocode): answer dropped elicitations and record them in the transcript
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A pending `ask_user` / `poll` prompt could be cleared on the client with no reply. The daemon then waited out the tool's own timeout (600 s for `ask_user`) while the user saw nothing. Every clear that isn't the user's answer now goes through `withdraw_pending_elicitation`. `Chat::answer_withdrawn_elicitations` (run each transport tick, after the resync drain) sends the `cancel` and notes it in the transcript.
  - A modal that outlives its turn is closed on `TurnComplete` and recorded as expired.
  - The `ask_user` / `poll` tool card now leads with `question:` and lists the choices. Before, the collapsed card showed the first 120 bytes of key-sorted input JSON, so `channel` and `choices` came first and the question was cut off. The card is the one record of the question.
  - The expanded (`Full`) `ask_user` / `poll` card shows each choice whole, inside the card's shared byte and line limits. Multi-line choices continue indented under their bullet, and the list stops with the usual show-less footer when the shared limit is reached. The collapsed card keeps the 200-byte, one-line preview per choice.
  - The card's `result:` is the record of the outcome. For `ask_user` / `poll`, the pick (or the `DISMISSED` marker from #11815) is shown in the warn colour the old outcome line used. An outcome line (answered, dismissed, withdrawn, expired) is written only when no matching `ask_user` / `poll` card is on screen, such as an older history or a card that never arrived. In dogfooding, a line under the card repeated its `result:`. That fallback line names the question (`<outcome> (Question: <question>)`, new key `zc-chat-elicitation-outcome-note` in all five catalogues), because no card shows it.
- **Scope boundary:** Client only (`apps/zerocode`). No daemon or wire change. Overlay placement and the sidebar needs-input dot are unchanged; the dot already exists (`ChatState::sidebar_status`). Free-form `ask_user` on the Code tab is still unsupported.
- **Blast radius:** The ZeroCode Code and Chat panes' elicitation path, and how the `ask_user` / `poll` tool cards render. A dropped prompt now gets a `cancel` reply where before it got none. The daemon already handles `cancel` (`Ok(None)` → "user cancelled").
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11623. Related #11117 (durable human-question primitive; it scopes ACP elicitation out). Companion #11815 makes `ask_user` return a `DISMISSED` result rather than an error when the user presses Esc, so the card's `result:` reads as a dismissal.

### What this does, simply

When an agent asks you a multiple-choice question in ZeroCode, a box pops up with the options. If the pane reloaded while that box was up (which happens when the client falls behind the live stream) or you started a new session in place, the box disappeared and nobody told the agent. The agent sat waiting for up to ten minutes and then failed with a timeout. Nothing about the question stayed on screen either, so afterwards you couldn't tell what had been asked.

Now the agent is told "cancelled" right away whenever the box goes away without your answer. The `ask_user` tool card shows the question, its options and what happened. A separate note appears only if the card isn't on screen.

**Why the record is client-side.** The prompt asked whether the record belongs in the daemon so it survives reload. It already partly does: the daemon persists the `ask_user` tool call with its full input, and with this change that card shows the question and choices. So after a reload the question is still on screen. The card's `result:` carries the answer or the cancel, and it is persisted with the card. Making the outcome durable means a new daemon event and storage, which is the job of the #11117 durable-question primitive. I kept this PR to the client.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The failing path needs a notification-lag reload to land while a prompt is up, which is hard to trigger by hand. The regression test drives it directly.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (ZeroCode Code pane)

### How I tested

**Current head `b28702328`** (`8c7f6f54de` plus the fallback-note fix for Greptile 4429142227), on a Linux x86_64 build host with rustc 1.98.0, in its own target dir (the log shows zerocode compiled from this tree):

- `cargo test --locked -p zerocode --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4` → library `52 passed; 0 failed`; binary `1570 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored`. The one failure is the known `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` (see below). The four tests that check a fallback note now expect the question in it. The reload-withdrawal test also asserts that the withdrawn line contains `Pick one`.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → `Finished`, no warnings. `cargo fmt -p zerocode -- --check` → clean.

**Previous head `8c7f6f54de`** (`59b0cd500` on `7996a8193b`, then a clean merge of master `1c1cd118a`), on a Linux x86_64 build host with rustc 1.99.1:

- `cargo test --locked -p zerocode -- --test-threads=4` → library `52 passed; 0 failed`; binary `1570 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored`. The one failure is the known `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` (see below). The two new tests pass: `expanded_ask_user_card_shows_whole_choices_within_shared_limits` (a 300-byte choice and a two-line choice render whole when expanded, with the second line indented under its bullet, and the collapsed card still cuts both) and `expanded_ask_user_choices_stop_at_the_shared_line_limit` (a poll with 100 two-line options renders 100 choice rows and then the show-less footer).
- `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → `Finished`, no warnings. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → clean.

Earlier commits, all through the remote wrapper (`scripts/zc-cargo`) on the build host:

- `zc-cargo test -p zerocode elicitation` → `test result: ok. 19 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1410 filtered out` (at the third commit)
- `zc-cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → `Finished `dev` profile`, no warnings
- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check apps/zerocode/src/chat.rs` → clean
- Full `zc-cargo test -p zerocode` → `1426 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored` at the second and third commits (first commit: 1425/1). The one failure is `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` ("SIGINT was swallowed while the insecure-TLS prompt was blocked", `main.rs`). It fails the same way on unmodified `origin/master` 05f9fe95d4 on the same host (`0 passed; 1 failed; 1422 filtered out`), so it's environmental on that host, not this change.

**Mutation check, third commit.** `elicitation_question_choices_and_answer_are_recorded` now applies the card's result and asserts no outcome line; `elicitation_with_a_card_adds_no_outcome_line` (renamed from `elicitation_outcome_sits_under_its_card_inside_the_agent_turn`) asserts the entries stay `agent, tool:ask_user, tool:shell` after Esc and the browse cursor is untouched. Writing the line even when a card exists: `17 passed; 2 failed`, both tests. Restored → 19 passed.

**Mutation check, second commit (placement since superseded by the third).** `elicitation_question_choices_and_answer_are_recorded` now streams the agent turn and asserts no line on arrival, one outcome line, and the question exactly once in the rendered transcript. The new `elicitation_outcome_sits_under_its_card_inside_the_agent_turn` delivers the request before the turn streams in (the router order), adds a parallel `shell` call, presses Esc, and asserts the entry order `agent, tool:ask_user, system:dismissed, tool:shell`, the rendered order agent label < `question:` < outcome < shell card, and that the browse cursor follows the shift.
- Asked line restored on arrival: `18 passed; 2 failed`. Both tests fail; the order assertion shows `["system:The agent asked: Pick one…", "agent", "tool:ask_user", …]`, which is what my screenshot shows.
- Outcome appended instead of placed: `19 passed; 1 failed`, with `["agent", "tool:ask_user", "tool:shell", "system:You dismissed…"]`.
- Index shift removed: fails with "the browse cursor stays on the shell card" (`Some(2)` vs `Some(3)`).
Restored → 20 passed.

**Mutation check, first commit.** I reverted each piece of the fix in one mutant (reload clears silently again, no asked-record, no `TurnComplete` close, card arm disabled, `reset_for_session` clears silently): `14 passed; 5 failed`. All five new tests failed:
`elicitation_installed_during_reload_is_answered_not_dropped`, `reset_for_session_queues_a_cancel_for_the_dropped_elicitation`, `elicitation_question_choices_and_answer_are_recorded`, `turn_complete_closes_a_stale_elicitation_and_records_it`, `ask_user_card_leads_with_the_question_and_lists_choices`. Restored → 19 passed.

- **CI checks relied on:** the zerocode test and clippy jobs.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** none for this surface.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real screenshots: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11624#issuecomment-6233889542 (experiment build, picked result and dismissed). Real screenshots of the current head pending. I dogfooded the second commit on 2026-10-17: the question showed once, but the answer was repeated, which the third commit fixes.
- **Not verified:** a live reproduction of the lag-reload race against a daemon.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The question text was already rendered (in the modal); it's now also rendered in the transcript through the same terminal-safe path as tool input. Nothing new reaches the model.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert the squash commit. The change is client-only, with no config, state or wire change to undo.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** none.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** an `ask_user` / `poll` prompt that disappears without a `cancel` reaching the daemon (the turn then waits out the tool's timeout), a prompt answered twice, or an `ask_user` card missing its question, choices or `result:`.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.
